mula_pali: 1. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā campāyaṃ viharati gaggarāya pokkharaṇiyā tīre mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ. Atha kho pesso peyo (ka.) ca hatthārohaputto kandarako ca paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā pesso hatthārohaputto bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Kandarako pana paribbājako bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ sārāṇīyaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ pī.) vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho kandarako paribbājako tuṇhībhūtaṃ tuṇhībhūtaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ anuviloketvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘acchariyaṃ , bho gotama, abbhutaṃ, bho gotama, yāvañcidaṃ bhotā gotamena sammā bhikkhusaṅgho paṭipādito! Yepi te, bho gotama, ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā tepi bhagavanto etaparamaṃyeva sammā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṭipādesuṃ – seyyathāpi etarahi bhotā gotamena sammā bhikkhusaṅgho paṭipādito. Yepi te, bho gotama, bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā tepi bhagavanto etaparamaṃyeva sammā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṭipādessanti – seyyathāpi etarahi bhotā gotamena sammā bhikkhusaṅgho paṭipādito’’ti.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was staying near Campā on the banks of the Gaggarā Lake together with a large Saṅgha of monks.

Then Pessa, the elephant driver's son, and Kandaraka the wanderer, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, Pessa, the elephant driver's son, paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side.

Then Kandaraka the wanderer exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. Having engaged in courteous, amiable talk, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, Kandaraka the wanderer surveyed the Saṅgha of monks, who were utterly silent, and said this to the Blessed One: "It is wonderful, venerable Gotama! It is amazing, venerable Gotama, how well the Saṅgha of monks has been guided by venerable Gotama! Those Blessed Ones, perfected ones, fully awakened Buddhas who existed in the past also guided the Saṅgha of monks to the highest attainment, just as the Saṅgha of monks is now guided by venerable Gotama. And those Blessed Ones, perfected ones, fully awakened Buddhas who will exist in the future will also guide the Saṅgha of monks to the highest attainment, just as the Saṅgha of monks is now guided by venerable Gotama."
commentary_pali:
1.Evaṃme sutanti kandarakasuttaṃ. Tattha campāyanti evaṃnāmake nagare. Tassa hi nagarassa ārāmapokkharaṇīādīsu tesu tesu ṭhānesu campakarukkhāva ussannā ahesuṃ, tasmā campāti saṅkhamagamāsi. Gaggarāya pokkharaṇiyā tīreti tassa campānagarassa avidūre gaggarāya nāma rājamahesiyā khaṇitattā gaggarāti laddhavohārā pokkharaṇī atthi. Tassā tīre samantato nīlādipañcavaṇṇakusumapaṭimaṇḍitaṃ mahantaṃ campakavanaṃ. Tasmiṃ bhagavā kusumagandhasugandhe campakavane viharati. Taṃ sandhāya ‘‘gaggarāya pokkharaṇiyā tīre’’ti vuttaṃ. Mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhinti adassitaparicchedena mahantena bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ. Pessoti tassa nāmaṃ. Hatthārohaputtoti hatthācariyassa putto. Kandarakoca paribbājakoti kandarakoti evaṃnāmo channaparibbājako. Abhivādetvāti chabbaṇṇānaṃ ghanabuddharasmīnaṃ antaraṃ pavisitvā pasannalākhārase nimujjamāno viya, siṅgīsuvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ dussavaraṃ pasāretvā sasīsaṃ pārupamāno viya, vaṇṇagandhasampannacampakapupphāni sirasā sampaṭicchanto viya, sinerupādaṃ upagacchanto puṇṇacando viya bhagavato cakkalakkhaṇapaṭimaṇḍite alattakavaṇṇaphullapadumasassirike pāde vanditvāti attho. Ekamantaṃ nisīdīti chanisajjadosavirahite ekasmiṃ okāse nisīdi.

Tuṇhībhūtaṃ tuṇhībhūtanti yato yato anuviloketi, tato tato tuṇhībhūtamevāti attho. Tattha hi ekabhikkhussāpi hatthakukkuccaṃ vā pādakukkuccaṃ vā natthi, sabbe bhagavato ceva gāravena attano ca sikkhitasikkhatāya aññamaññaṃ vigatasallāpā antamaso ukkāsitasaddampi akarontā sunikhātaindakhīlā viya nivātaṭṭhāne sannisinnaṃ mahāsamuddaudakaṃ viya kāyenapi niccalā manasāpi avikkhittā rattavalāhakā viya sinerukūṭaṃ bhagavantaṃ parivāretvā nisīdiṃsu. Paribbājakassa evaṃ sannisinnaṃ parisaṃ disvā mahantaṃ pītisomanassaṃ uppajji. Uppannaṃ pana antohadayasmiṃyeva sannidahituṃ asakkonto piyasamudāhāraṃ samuṭṭhāpesi. Tasmā acchariyaṃ bhotiādimāha.

Tuṇhībhū taṃ tuṇhībhūta acchariyaṃ bho

Tattha andhassa pabbatārohanaṃ viya niccaṃ na hotīti acchariyaṃ. Ayaṃ tāva saddanayo. Ayaṃ pana aṭṭhakathānayo , accharāyogganti acchariyaṃ. Accharaṃ paharituṃ yuttanti attho. Abhūtapubbaṃ bhūtanti abbhutaṃ. Ubhayampetaṃ vimhayassevādhivacanaṃ. Taṃ panetaṃ garahaacchariyaṃ, pasaṃsāacchariyanti duvidhaṃ hoti. Tattha acchariyaṃ moggallāna abbhutaṃ moggallāna, yāva bāhāgahaṇāpi nāma so moghapuriso āgamessatīti (cūḷava. 383; a. ni. 8.20), idaṃ garahaacchariyaṃ nāma. ‘‘Acchariyaṃ nandamāte abbhutaṃ nandamāte, yatra hi nāma cittuppādampi parisodhessasīti (a. ni. 7.53) idaṃ pasaṃsāacchariyaṃ nāma. Idhāpi idameva adhippetaṃ’’ ayañhi taṃ pasaṃsanto evamāha.

acchariyaṃ acchariyaṃ abbhutaṃ

Yāvañcidanti ettha idanti nipātamattaṃ. Yāvāti pamāṇaparicchedo, yāva sammā paṭipādito, yattakena pamāṇena sammā paṭipādito, na sakkā tassa vaṇṇe vattuṃ, atha kho acchariyamevetaṃ abbhutamevetanti vuttaṃ hoti. Etaparamaṃyevāti evaṃ sammā paṭipādito eso bhikkhusaṅgho tassāpi bhikkhusaṅghassa paramoti etaparamo, taṃ etaparamaṃ yathā ayaṃ paṭipādito, evaṃ paṭipāditaṃ katvā paṭipādesuṃ, na ito bhiyyoti attho. Dutiyanaye evaṃ paṭipādessanti, na ito bhiyyoti yojetabbaṃ. Tattha paṭipāditoti ābhisamācārikavattaṃ ādiṃ katvā sammā apaccanīkapaṭipattiyaṃ yojito. Atha kasmā ayaṃ paribbājako atītānāgate buddhe dasseti, kimassa tiyaddhajānanañāṇaṃ atthīti. Natthi, nayaggāhe pana ṭhatvā ‘‘yenākārena ayaṃ bhikkhusaṅgho sannisinno danto vinīto upasanto, atītabuddhāpi etaparamaṃyeva katvā paṭipajjāpesuṃ, anāgatabuddhāpi paṭipajjāpessanti, natthi ito uttari paṭipādanā’’ti maññamāno anubuddhiyā evamāha.

Yāvañcida ida Yāvā Etaparamaṃyevā paṭipādito
commentary_english:
1. Thus have I heard: The Kandarakasutta. There, *Campā* means in a city of that name. For in that city, campaka trees grew luxuriantly in those various places, such as parks and ponds; therefore, it came to be called Campā. *On the bank of Gaggara's Pond* means not far from that city of Campā, there is a pond called Gaggarā, which got its name because it was dug by a queen consort named Gaggarā. On its bank [there is] a large campaka grove adorned all around with five-colored flowers, such as blue ones, etc. In that campaka grove, fragrant with the scent of flowers, the Blessed One was staying. Referring to that, it was said, "On the bank of Gaggara's Pond." *Together with a large Saṅgha of monks* means together with a large Saṅgha of monks, the extent of which was not indicated. *Pesso* is his name. *The son of Hatthāroha* means the son of a teacher of elephant-lore. *Kandaraka the wanderer* means Kandaraka by name, a clothed wanderer. *Having paid homage* means having entered into the midst of the dense Buddha-rays of six colors, as if submerging in refined lac-dye, as if spreading out an excellent cloth of gold color, completely covering [himself] head and all, as if receiving upon his head campaka flowers endowed with color and fragrance, like the full moon approaching the foot of Mount Meru, [he] paid homage to the Blessed One's feet, adorned with wheel-marks and lovely like full-blown lotuses, the color of lac-dye—this is the meaning. *He sat down to one side* means he sat down in a certain place devoid of the faults of being covered with grass. *Being silent, that silent one* means wherever he looked, he was only silent—this is the meaning. For there, even a single monk did not have hand-restlessness or foot-restlessness; all, both out of respect for the Blessed One and because of their own well-learned training, were without conversation with each other, not even making a sound of clearing the throat, like well-driven-in posts, like the ocean water settled in a windless place, motionless even in body, unscattered even in mind, like red clouds surrounding the peak of Mount Meru, they sat surrounding the Blessed One. Having seen the assembly thus seated, great joy and happiness arose in the wanderer. But being unable to contain what had arisen only in his heart, he brought forth an agreeable utterance. Therefore, he said, "It's wonderful, good sir," and so on. *It's wonderful, good sir* There, *wonderful* [means] it does not happen constantly, like a blind man climbing a mountain. This, first of all, is the verbal method. But this is the commentary method: *wonderful* [means] suitable for [uttering] a verse. The meaning is: suitable for uttering a verse. *Marvelous* [means] something that has come to be that never was before. Both of these are synonyms for astonishment. But that is twofold: reproach-wonder and praise-wonder. There, "It's wonderful, Moggallāna! It's marvelous, Moggallāna! That this empty man would come even as far as being taken by the arm!" (Cūḷava. 383; A. Ni. 8. 20)—this is called reproach-wonder. "It's wonderful, Nandamātā! It's marvelous, Nandamātā! That you will purify even a thought!" (A. Ni. 7. 53) This is called *pasaṃsāacchariyaṃ*. Here too, this very thing is intended,” for, praising him, he said thus: *Acchariyaṃ* Acchariyaṃ abbhutaṃ “*yāvañcida*nti ettha *ida*nti is merely a particle. yāvāti [means] the delimitation of measure; to the extent that it is well established, with whatever measure it is well established, it is not possible to express its quality; thus it is said that it is truly marvelous and wonderful. etaparamaṃyevāti thus this Saṃgha of monks is well established. For that Saṃgha of monks, *parama* is *etaparama*; that *etaparama* as this is well established, having done thus it was well established; there is no more than this, [is] the meaning. In the second way, they will thus establish [it]; it should be connected [that] there is no more than this. There, *paṭipādito*ti, having made the *ābhisamācārikavatta* the beginning, is joined to right and non-adversarial practice. Now, why does this wandering ascetic show the Buddhas of the past and future? Does he have knowledge of knowing the three times? There is not. But standing in the acceptance of a principle, “In whatever manner this Saṃgha of monks is assembled, tamed, disciplined, and peaceful, the Buddhas of the past also, having done just this much, attained [liberation], the Buddhas of the future will also attain [liberation], there is no further attainment than this,” thinking thus, with understanding, he said thus.

yāvañcida ida yāvā etaparamaṃyevā paṭipādito

mula_pali:
2. ‘‘Evametaṃ , kandaraka, evametaṃ, kandaraka. Yepi te, kandaraka, ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā tepi bhagavanto etaparamaṃyeva sammā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṭipādesuṃ – seyyathāpi etarahi mayā sammā bhikkhusaṅgho paṭipādito. Yepi te, kandaraka, bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā tepi bhagavanto etaparamaṃyeva sammā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṭipādessanti – seyyathāpi etarahi mayā sammā bhikkhusaṅgho paṭipādito.

‘‘Santi hi, kandaraka, bhikkhū imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe arahanto khīṇāsavā vusitavanto katakaraṇīyā ohitabhārā anuppattasadatthā parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanā sammadaññā vimuttā. Santi hi, kandaraka, bhikkhū imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe sekkhā santatasīlā santatavuttino nipakā nipakavuttino; te catūsu nipakavuttino catūsu (sī.) satipaṭṭhānesu suppatiṭṭhitacittā supaṭṭhitacittā (sī. pī. ka.) viharanti. Katamesu catūsu? Idha, kandaraka, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; citte cittānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassa’’nti.

nipakavuttino catūsu (sī.) supaṭṭhitacittā (sī. pī. ka.)
mula_english:
2. "So it is, Kandaraka, so it is, Kandaraka. Those who were the Blessed Ones, accomplished and fully enlightened in the past, at most only led the *bhikkhu-saṃgha* (community of monks) to practise the right way as is done by me now. And those who will be the Blessed Ones, accomplished and fully enlightened in the future, at most will only lead the *bhikkhu-saṃgha* to practise the right way as is done by me now."

"Indeed, Kandaraka, in this *bhikkhu-saṃgha* there are *arhats* (worthy ones) with taints destroyed, who have lived the holy life, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, reached the true goal, destroyed the fetters of being, and who are completely liberated through final knowledge. Indeed, Kandaraka, in this *bhikkhu-saṃgha* there are those in higher training (*sekkhā*), of constant virtue, living a life of constant virtue, sagacious, living a life of constant sagacity; they abide with their minds well established in the four foundations of mindfulness (*satipaṭṭhānesu*). What are the four? Here, Kandaraka, a *bhikkhu* abides contemplating body as body (*kāye kāyānupassī*), ardent, clearly aware and mindful, having put aside hankering and fretting for the world; he abides contemplating feelings as feelings (*vedanāsu vedanānupassī*), ardent, clearly aware and mindful, having put aside hankering and fretting for the world; he abides contemplating mind as mind (*citte cittānupassī*), ardent, clearly aware and mindful, having put aside hankering and fretting for the world; he abides contemplating mind-objects as mind-objects (*dhammesu dhammānupassī*), ardent, clearly aware and mindful, having put aside hankering and fretting for the world."
commentary_pali:
2.Evametaṃ kandarakāti pāṭiekko anusandhi. Bhagavā kira taṃ sutvā ‘‘kandaraka tvaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ upasantoti vadasi, imassa pana bhikkhusaṅghassa upasantakāraṇaṃ tuyhaṃ apākaṭaṃ, na hi tvaṃ samatiṃsa pāramiyā pūretvā kusalamūlaṃ paripācetvā bodhipallaṅke sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ paṭivijjhi, mayā pana pāramiyo pūretvā ñātatthacariyaṃ lokatthacariyaṃ buddhatthacariyañca koṭiṃ pāpetvā bodhipallaṅke sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ paṭividdhaṃ, mayhaṃ etesaṃ upasantakāraṇaṃ pākaṭa’’nti dassetuṃ imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi.

Santi hi kandarakāti ayampi pāṭiekko anusandhi. Bhagavato kira etadahosi – ‘‘ayaṃ paribbājako imaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ upasantoti vadati, ayañca bhikkhusaṅgho kappetvā pakappetvā kuhakabhāvena iriyāpathaṃ saṇṭhapento cittena anupasanto na upasantākāraṃ dasseti. Ettha pana bhikkhusaṅghe paṭipadaṃ pūrayamānāpi paṭipadaṃ pūretvā matthakaṃ patvā ṭhitabhikkhūpi atthi, tattha paṭipadaṃ pūretvā matthakaṃ pattā attanā paṭividdhaguṇeheva upasantā, paṭipadaṃ pūrayamānā uparimaggassa vipassanāya upasantā, ito muttā pana avasesā catūhi satipaṭṭhānehi upasantā. Taṃ nesaṃ upasantakāraṇaṃ dassessāmī’’ti ‘‘iminā ca iminā ca kāraṇena ayaṃ bhikkhusaṅgho upasanto’’ti dassetuṃ ‘‘santi hi kandarakā’’tiādimāha.

Santi hi kandarakā

Tattha arahanto khīṇāsavātiādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ mūlapariyāyasuttavaṇṇanāyameva vuttaṃ. Sekhapaṭipadampi tattheva vitthāritaṃ. Santatasīlāti satatasīlā nirantarasīlā. Santatavuttinoti tasseva vevacanaṃ, santatajīvikā vātipi attho. Tasmiṃ santatasīle ṭhatvāva jīvikaṃ kappenti, na dussīlyaṃ maraṇaṃ pāpuṇantīti attho.

arahanto khīṇāsavā Santatasīlā Santatavuttino

Nipakāti nepakkena samannāgatā paññavanto. Nipakavuttinoti paññāya vuttino, paññāya ṭhatvā jīvikaṃ kappenti. Yathā ekacco sāsane pabbajitvāpi jīvitakāraṇā chasu agocaresu carati, vesiyāgocaro hoti, vidhavathullakumārikapaṇḍakapānāgārabhikkhunigocaro hoti. Saṃsaṭṭho viharati rājūhi rājamahāmattehi titthiyehi titthiyasāvakehi ananulomikena gihisaṃsaggena (vibha. 514), vejjakammaṃ karoti, dūtakammaṃ karoti, pahiṇakammaṃ karoti, gaṇḍaṃ phāleti, arumakkhanaṃ deti, uddhaṃvirecanaṃ deti, adhovirecanaṃ deti, natthutelaṃ pacati, pivanatelaṃ pacati, veḷudānaṃ, pattadānaṃ, pupphadānaṃ, phaladānaṃ, sinānadānaṃ, dantakaṭṭhadānaṃ, mukhodakadānaṃ, cuṇṇamattikadānaṃ deti, cāṭukamyaṃ karoti, muggasūpiyaṃ, pāribhaṭuṃ, jaṅghapesaniyaṃ karotīti ekavīsatividhāya anesanāya jīvikaṃ kappento anipakavutti nāma hoti, na paññāya ṭhatvā jīvikaṃ kappeti, tato kālakiriyaṃ katvā samaṇayakkho nāma hutvā ‘‘tassa saṅghāṭipi ādittā hoti sampajjalitā’’ti vuttanayena mahādukkhaṃ anubhoti. Evaṃvidhā ahutvā jīvitahetupi sikkhāpadaṃ anatikkamanto catupārisuddhisīle patiṭṭhāya yathābalaṃ buddhavacanaṃ uggaṇhitvā rathavinītapaṭipadaṃ, mahāgosiṅgapaṭipadaṃ, mahāsuññatapaṭipadaṃ, anaṅgaṇapaṭipadaṃ, dhammadāyādapaṭipadaṃ, nālakapaṭipadaṃ, tuvaṭṭakapaṭipadaṃ, candopamapaṭipadanti imāni ariyapaṭipadāni pūrento catupaccaya-santosa-bhāvanārāma-ariyavaṃsapaṭipattiyaṃ kāyasakkhino hutvā anīkā nikkhantahatthī viya yūthā vissaṭṭhasīho viya nipacchābandhamahānāvā viya ca gamanādīsu ekavihārino vipassanaṃ paṭṭhapetvā ajjaajjeva arahattanti pavattaussāhā viharantīti attho.

Nipakā Nipakavuttino samaṇayakkho

Suppatiṭṭhitacittāti catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu suṭṭhapitacittā hutvā. Sesā satipaṭṭhānakathā heṭṭhā vitthāritāva. Idha pana lokiyalokuttaramissakā satipaṭṭhānā kathitā, ettakena bhikkhusaṅghassa upasantakāraṇaṃ kathitaṃ hoti.

Suppatiṭṭhitacittā
commentary_english:
2. "Thus it is, Kandaraka," is a phrase that links to the preceding context.

The Blessed One, hearing this, said, "Kandaraka, you say that the *bhikkhu-saṃgha* is peaceful (*upasantoti*), but the reason for this *bhikkhu-saṃgha*'s peacefulness is unknown to you. You have not fulfilled the thirty perfections (*pāramitā*), ripened the roots of good (*kusalamūla*), or penetrated all-knowing wisdom (*sabbaññutaññāṇa*) at the *bodhi*-seat. But I have fulfilled the perfections, brought the practice for the benefit of relatives (*ñātatthacariya*), the practice for the benefit of the world (*lokatthacariya*), and the practice for the benefit of the Buddha (*buddhatthacariya*) to completion, attained all-knowing wisdom (*sabbaññutaññāṇa*) at the *bodhi*-seat, and the reason for their peacefulness is known to me." To demonstrate this, he began this discourse.

"The presence of Kandaraka" is another phrase that links to the preceding context.

The Blessed One thought, "This wandering ascetic (*paribbājaka*) says that this *bhikkhu-saṃgha* is peaceful, but this *bhikkhu-saṃgha*, having only fashioned and conceived the appearance of peace through hypocrisy (*kuhakabhāvena*), does not show the nature of peace with their minds, being unpeaceful."

Here in the *bhikkhu-saṃgha* are *bhikkhus* who are fulfilling the practice (*paṭipadaṃ pūrayamānāpi*), *bhikkhus* who have completed the practice (*paṭipadaṃ pūretvā*) and attained the summit (*matthakaṃ patvā*), and *ṭhitabhikkhūpi*. Of those, those who have completed the practice (*paṭipadaṃ pūretvā*) and attained the summit (*matthakaṃ pattā*) are peaceful through the qualities they have penetrated themselves (*attanā paṭividdhaguṇeheva upasantā*), those who are fulfilling the practice (*paṭipadaṃ pūrayamānā*) are peaceful through insight (*vipassanāya*) into the higher path (*uparimaggassa*), and those who are liberated (*muttā*) from this, the remaining ones, are peaceful through the four establishments of mindfulness (*catūhi smṛtyupasthānehi upasantā*).

"I will show them the reason for this peacefulness (*upasantakāraṇaṃ dassessāmī*)," he said, "Because of this and this reason, this *bhikkhu-saṃgha* is peaceful (*upasanto*)," to show this, he began with "The presence of Kandaraka" (*santi hi kandarakā*).

"The presence of Kandaraka"

There, what should be said in the *ādi*s "Arahants, those who have destroyed the āsavas (influxes)" (*arahanto khīṇāsavā*), has already been said in the commentary on the Mūlapariyāyasutta.

The practice of a *śaikṣa* (learner) has also been extensively explained there.

"*Santatasīlā*" means constant *śīla*, uninterrupted *śīla*.

"*Santatavuttino*" <pb ed="p" n="3.0005"/> is <pb ed="v" n="3.0004"/> a synonym for that, or it also means continuous livelihood (*santatajīvikā*).

Living in that continuous *śīla*, they maintain their livelihood; that is, they do not reach death through bad *śīla* (*dussīlyaṃ maraṇaṃ pāpuṇanti*).

*Arahants*, those who have destroyed the *āsavas*, those with constant *śīla*, those with continuous conduct, <pb ed="p" n="3.0005"/> <pb ed="v" n="3.0004"/>

"*Nipakā*" means endowed with wisdom (*nepakkena samannāgatā*) and possessing understanding (*paññavanto*).

"*Nipakavuttino*" means conduct based on wisdom (*paññāya vuttino*), they maintain their livelihood by relying on wisdom (*paññāya ṭhatvā jīvikaṃ kappenti*).

Just as some, even having gone forth in the *śāsana* (teaching), <pb ed="m" n="3.0004"/> wander for the sake of livelihood among the six improper resorts (*chasu agocaresu carati*), are a resort for prostitutes (*vesiyāgocaro hoti*), are a resort for widows, old maids, *paṇḍakas* (eunuchs), taverns, and nuns (*vidhavathullakumārikapaṇḍakapānāgārabhikkhunigocaro hoti*).

They dwell in association (*saṃsaṭṭho viharati*) with kings, royal ministers (*rājamahāmattehi*), adherents of other sects (*titthiyehi*), disciples of adherents of other sects (*titthiyasāvakehi*) through unseemly association with householders (*ananulomikena gihisaṃsaggena*) (Vibha.

514), perform medical work (*vejjakammaṃ karoti*), perform the work of a messenger (*dūtakammaṃ karoti*), perform the work of an errand-runner (*pahiṇakammaṃ karoti*), lance tumors (*gaṇḍaṃ phāleti*), give *arumakkhanas*, give upward-purging medicines (*uddhaṃvirecanaṃ deti*), give downward-purging medicines (*adhovirecanaṃ deti*), cook nasal oil (*natthutelaṃ pacati*), cook drinking oil (*pivanatelaṃ pacati*), [give] bamboo offerings (*veḷudānaṃ*), leaf offerings (*pattadānaṃ*), flower offerings (*pupphadānaṃ*), fruit offerings (*phaladānaṃ*), bathing offerings (*sinānadānaṃ*), tooth-stick offerings (*dantakaṭṭhadānaṃ*), mouth-washing offerings (*mukhodakadānaṃ*), powder-earth offerings (*cuṇṇamattikadānaṃ deti*), perform flattery (*cāṭukamyaṃ karoti*), [perform] bean-soupery (*muggasūpiyaṃ*), are fondlers (*pāribhaṭuṃ*), are errand-runners (*jaṅghapesaniyaṃ karotīti*), maintaining their livelihood through twenty-one kinds of improper searches (*ekavīsatividhāya anesanāya jīvikaṃ kappento*) are called those with unwise conduct (*anipakavutti nāma hoti*), they do not maintain their livelihood by relying on wisdom (*paññāya ṭhatvā jīvikaṃ kappeti*), then, having made a timely end (*tato kālakiriyaṃ katvā*), becoming a *śramaṇa-yakṣa* (*samaṇayakkho*) named [so and so], they experience great suffering (*mahādukkhaṃ anubhoti*) in the manner described: "even his robe is kindled and blazing" (*tassa saṅghāṭipi ādittā hoti sampajjalitā*).

Not being like that, not transgressing the precepts (*sikkhāpadaṃ anatikkamanto*) even for the sake of livelihood (*jīvitahetupi*), being established in the fourfold purity of *śīla* (*catupārisuddhisīle patiṭṭhāya*), learning the Buddha's word to the best of their ability (*yathābalaṃ buddhavacanaṃ uggaṇhitvā*), <pb ed="p" n="3.0006"/> fulfilling these noble practices (*imāni ariyapaṭipadāni pūrento*): the Rathavinīta-practice, the Mahāgosiṅga-practice, the Mahāsuññata-practice, the Anaṅgaṇa-practice, the Dhammadāyāda-practice, the Nālaka-practice, the Tuvaṭṭaka-practice, the Candopama-practice, being bodily witnesses (*kāyasakkhino hutvā*) to the practice of the noble lineage, delighting in cultivating contentment with the four requisites (*catupaccaya-santosa-bhāvanārāma-ariyavaṃsapaṭipattiyaṃ*), like an elephant that has emerged from the herd without a chain (*anīkā nikkhantahatthī viya*), like a lion that has emerged from the pack (*yūthā vissaṭṭhasīho viya*), like a great ship released from its mooring (*nipacchābandhamahānāvā viya ca*), establishing insight (*vipassanāṃ paṭṭhapetvā*) in going and so on (*gamanādīsu ekavihārino*), striving to attain Arhatship here and now (*ajjaajjeva arahattanti pavattaussāhā viharanti*), this is the meaning.

The wise, those with wise conduct, <pb ed="m" n="3.0004"/> the *śramaṇa-yakṣa*, <pb ed="p" n="3.0006"/>

"*Suppatiṭṭhitacittā*" means having a well-established mind (*suṭṭhapitacittā hutvā*) in the four *smṛtyupasthānas* (establishments of mindfulness).

The remaining discussion of the *smṛtyupasthānas* has already been extensively explained below.

Here, however, the *smṛtyupasthānas* that are a mixture of mundane and supramundane (*lokiyalokuttaramissakā*) have been spoken of; by this much, the reason for the *bhikkhu-saṃgha*'s peacefulness (*upasantakāraṇaṃ*) has been spoken of.

Those with well-established minds

mula_pali: 3. Evaṃ vutte, pesso hatthārohaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante! Yāva supaññattā cime, bhante, bhagavatā cattāro satipaṭṭhānā sattānaṃ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṃ sokapariddavānaṃ (sī. pī.) samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya. Mayampi hi, bhante, gihī odātavasanā kālena kālaṃ imesu catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu suppatiṭṭhitacittā viharāma. Idha mayaṃ, bhante, kāye kāyānupassino viharāma ātāpino sampajānā satimanto, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; vedanāsu vedanānupassino viharāma ātāpino sampajānā satimanto, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; citte cittānupassino viharāma ātāpino sampajānā satimanto, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; dhammesu dhammānupassino viharāma ātāpino sampajānā satimanto, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante! Yāvañcidaṃ, bhante, bhagavā evaṃ manussagahane evaṃ manussakasaṭe evaṃ manussasāṭheyye vattamāne sattānaṃ hitāhitaṃ jānāti. Gahanañhetaṃ, bhante, yadidaṃ manussā; uttānakañhetaṃ, bhante, yadidaṃ pasavo. Ahañhi, bhante, pahomi hatthidammaṃ sāretuṃ. Yāvatakena antarena campaṃ gatāgataṃ karissati sabbāni tāni sāṭheyyāni kūṭeyyāni vaṅkeyyāni jimheyyāni pātukarissati. Amhākaṃ pana, bhante, dāsāti vā pessāti vā kammakarāti vā aññathāva kāyena samudācaranti aññathāva vācāya aññathāva nesaṃ cittaṃ hoti. Acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante! Yāvañcidaṃ, bhante, bhagavā evaṃ manussagahane evaṃ manussakasaṭe evaṃ manussasāṭheyye vattamāne sattānaṃ hitāhitaṃ jānāti. Gahanañhetaṃ, bhante, yadidaṃ manussā; uttānakañhetaṃ, bhante, yadidaṃ pasavo’’ti.
mula_english:
3. When this was said, the elephant trainer's son said to the Blessed One: "Wonderful, venerable sir, amazing, venerable sir! How well the four foundations of mindfulness have been made known by the Blessed One: for the purification of beings, for the surmounting of sorrow and lamentation, for the disappearance of pain and grief, for the attainment of the true way, for the realisation of *Nibbāna*.

Indeed, venerable sir, we householders wearing white robes also abide from time to time with minds well-established in these four foundations of mindfulness. Here, venerable sir, we abide contemplating the body as a body, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world; we abide contemplating feelings as feelings, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world; we abide contemplating mind as mind, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world; we abide contemplating phenomena as phenomena, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world. Wonderful, venerable sir, amazing, venerable sir! How amid man’s tangle, corruption, and deceptions, the Blessed One knows the welfare and harm of beings. For humankind is a tangle but the animal is open enough. Venerable sir, I can drive an elephant to be tamed, and in the time it takes to make a trip back and forth in Campa, that elephant will show every kind of deception, duplicity, crookedness, and fraud he is capable of. But those who are called our slaves, messengers, and servants behave in one way with the body, in another way by speech, while their minds work in still another way. Wonderful, venerable sir, amazing, venerable sir! How amid man’s tangle, corruption, and deceptions, the Blessed One knows the welfare and harm of beings. For humankind is a tangle but the animal is open enough."
commentary_pali:
3.Yāva supaññattāti yāva suṭṭhapitā sudesitā. Mayampi hi, bhanteti iminā esa attano kārakabhāvaṃ dasseti, bhikkhusaṅghañca ukkhipati. Ayañhettha adhippāyo, mayampi hi, bhante, gihi…pe… suppatiṭṭhitacittā viharāma, bhikkhusaṅghassa pana ayameva kasi ca bījañca yuganaṅgalañca phālapācanañca, tasmā bhikkhusaṅgho sabbakālaṃ satipaṭṭhānaparāyaṇo, mayaṃ pana kālena kālaṃ okāsaṃ labhitvā etaṃ manasikāraṃ karoma, mayampi kārakā, na sabbaso vissaṭṭhakammaṭṭhānāyevāti. Manussagahaneti manussānaṃ ajjhāsayagahanena gahanatā, ajjhāsayassāpi nesaṃ kilesagahanena gahanatā veditabbā. Kasaṭasāṭheyyesupi eseva nayo. Tattha aparisuddhaṭṭhena kasaṭatā, kerāṭiyaṭṭhena sāṭheyyatā veditabbā. Sattānaṃ hitāhitaṃ jānātīti evaṃ gahanakasaṭakerāṭiyānaṃ manussānaṃ hitāhitapaṭipadaṃ yāva suṭṭhu bhagavā jānāti. Yadidaṃ pasavoti ettha sabbāpi catuppadajāti pasavoti adhippetā. Pahomīti sakkomi. Yāvatakena antarenāti yattakena khaṇena. Campaṃ gatāgataṃ karissatīti assamaṇḍalato yāva campānagaradvārā gamanañca āgamanañca karissati. Sāṭheyyānīti saṭhattāni. Kūṭeyyānīti kūṭattāni. Vaṅkeyyānīti vaṅkattāni. Jimheyyānīti jimhattāni. Pātukarissatīti pakāsessati dassessati. Na hi sakkā tena tāni ettakena antarena dassetuṃ.

Tattha yassa kismiñcideva ṭhāne ṭhātukāmassa sato yaṃ ṭhānaṃ manussānaṃ sappaṭibhayaṃ, purato gantvā vañcetvā ṭhassāmīti na hoti, tasmiṃ ṭhātukāmaṭṭhāneyeva nikhātatthambho viya cattāro pāde niccale katvā tiṭṭhati, ayaṃ saṭho nāma. Yassa pana kismiñcideva ṭhāne avacchinditvā khandhagataṃ pātetukāmassa sato yaṃ ṭhānaṃ manussānaṃ sappaṭibhayaṃ, purato gantvā vañcetvā pātessāmīti na hoti, tattheva avacchinditvā pāteti, ayaṃ kūṭo nāma. Yassa kismiñcideva ṭhāne maggā ukkamma nivattitvā paṭimaggaṃ ārohitukāmassa sato yaṃ ṭhānaṃ manussānaṃ sappaṭibhayaṃ, purato gantvā vañcetvā evaṃ karissāmīti na hoti, tattheva maggā ukkamma nivattitvā paṭimaggaṃ ārohati, ayaṃ vaṅko nāma. Yassa pana kālena vāmato kālena dakkhiṇato kālena ujumaggeneva gantukāmassa sato yaṃ ṭhānaṃ manussānaṃ sappaṭibhayaṃ, purato gantvā vañcetvā evaṃ karissāmīti na hoti, tattheva kālena vāmato kālena dakkhiṇato kālena ujumaggaṃ gacchati, tathā laṇḍaṃ vā passāvaṃ vā vissajjetukāmassa sato idaṃ ṭhānaṃ susammaṭṭhaṃ ākiṇṇamanussaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ, imasmiṃ ṭhāne evarūpaṃ kātuṃ na yuttaṃ, purato gantvā paṭicchannaṭhāne karissāmīti na hoti, tattheva karoti, ayaṃ jimho nāma. Iti imaṃ catubbidhampi kiriyaṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Sabbāni tāni sāṭheyyāni kūṭeyyāni vaṅkeyyāni jimheyyāni pātukarissatīti evaṃ karontāpi te saṭhādayo tāni sāṭheyyādīni pātukaronti nāma.

saṭho kūṭo vaṅko jimho

Evaṃ pasūnaṃ uttānabhāvaṃ dassetvā idāni manussānaṃ gahanabhāvaṃ dassento amhākaṃ pana, bhantetiādimāha. Tattha dāsāti antojātakā vā dhanakkītā vā karamarānītā vā sayaṃ vā dāsabyaṃ upagatā. Pessāti pesanakārakā. Kammakarāti bhattavetanabhatā. Aññathāva kāyenāti aññenevākārena kāyena samudācaranti, aññenevākārena vācāya, aññena ca nesaṃ ākārena cittaṃ ṭhitaṃ hotīti dasseti. Tattha ye sammukhā sāmike disvā paccuggamanaṃ karonti, hatthato bhaṇḍakaṃ gaṇhanti, imaṃ vissajjetvā imaṃ gaṇhantā sesānipi āsana-paññāpana-tālavaṇṭabījana-pādadhovanādīni sabbāni kiccāni karonti, parammukhakāle pana telampi uttarantaṃ na olokenti, satagghanakepi sahassagghanakepi kamme parihāyante nivattitvā oloketumpi na icchanti, ime aññathā kāyena samudācaranti nāma. Ye pana sammukhā ‘‘amhākaṃ sāmi amhākaṃ ayyo’’tiādīni vatvā pasaṃsanti, parammukhā avattabbaṃ nāma natthi, yaṃ icchanti, taṃ vadanti, ime aññathā vācāya samudācaranti nāma.

amhākaṃ pana, bhante dāsā Pessā Kammakarā Aññathāva kāyenā
commentary_english:
3. " *yāva supaññattā* " means as long as it is well established, well taught. " *mayampi hi, bhante* " by this, he shows his being a performer and elevates the monastic community ( *bhikkhusaṅgha* ). Here is the meaning: We too, venerable sir ( *bhante* ), as householders…pe… abide with well-established minds, but for the monastic community, this itself is cultivation, seed, yoke, plough, and hoe. Therefore, the monastic community is always devoted to mindfulness, we, however, from time to time, having obtained an opportunity, direct our minds to this; we too are performers, not entirely abandoning the grounds of ascetic practice." " *manussagahane* " on being deeply attached to human beings, there is attachment, it should be understood that even with attachment to intentions, there is attachment through defilements ( *kilesa* ). In corruptness and deceitfulness, this is the method. There, due to impurity, there is corruptness ( *kasaṭatā* ), due to trickery, there is deceitfulness ( *sāṭheyyatā* ), it should be understood. " *sattānaṃ hitāhitaṃ jānātī* " thus the Blessed One ( *bhagavā* ) knows well the beneficial and unbeneficial conduct of human beings who are deeply attached, corrupt, and deceitful. " *yadidaṃ pasavo* " here all four-footed creatures are meant by the word 'animals' ( *pasavo* ). " *pahomī* " means I am able ( *sakkomi* ). " *yāvatakena antarenā* " means in whatever moment. " *campaṃ gatāgataṃ karissatī* " means he will go and come to Campā from the boundary of the hermitage, he will make going and coming. " *sāṭheyyānī* " means deceitful things ( *saṭhattāni* ). " *kūṭeyyānī* " means dishonest things ( *kūṭattāni* ). " *vaṅkeyyānī* " means crooked things ( *vaṅkattāni* ). " *jimheyyānī* " means bent things ( *jimhattāni* ). " *pātukarissatī* " means he will reveal, he will show. It is not possible to show those things with such a great interval. There, whatever place is frightening to people for one who desires to stand still in some place, if it doesn't occur to him that "having gone forward, having deceived, I will stand," but he stands in that very place where he desires to stand, making his four feet motionless, like a stake that has been driven into the ground, this is called "deceitful" ( *saṭho* ). Moreover, whatever place is frightening to people for one who desires to cut off and drop his burden in some place, if it doesn't occur to him that "having gone forward, having deceived, I will drop it," but he cuts off and drops it right there, this is called "dishonest" ( *kūṭo* ). Whatever place is frightening to people for one who desires to leave the road in some place, turn back, and climb on a side road, if it doesn't occur to him that "having gone forward, having deceived, I will do thus," but right there he leaves the road, turns back, and climbs on a side road, this is called "crooked" ( *vaṅko* ). Moreover, whatever place is frightening to people for one who desires to go sometimes to the left, sometimes to the right, sometimes straight ahead, if it doesn't occur to him that "having gone forward, having deceived, I will do thus," but right there he goes sometimes to the left, sometimes to the right, sometimes straight ahead; likewise, when he desires to excrete feces or urine, if it doesn't occur to him that "this place is well-swept, crowded with people, and delightful, it is not proper to do such a thing in this place, having gone forward, I will do it in a hidden place," but he does it right there, this is called "bent" ( *jimho* ). Thus, this fourfold action has been spoken with reference to that. All those deceitful things, dishonest things, crooked things, bent things, he will reveal, thus even while doing, those deceitful ones reveal those deceitful things, and so forth. Deceitful ( *saṭho* ), dishonest ( *kūṭo* ), crooked ( *vaṅko* ), bent ( *jimho* ). Thus, having shown the open state of the animals, now showing the state of attachment of human beings, he says, "But for us, venerable sir ( *bhante* )," and so on. There, "slaves" ( *dāsā* ) means those born in the house, or bought with wealth, or brought by force, or who have themselves entered into slavery. "Messengers" ( *pessā* ) means those who carry messages. "Workers" ( *kammakarā* ) means those who are hired for food and wages. "Differently by body" ( *aññathāva kāyenā* ) means they conduct themselves differently by body, differently by speech, and their minds are established differently, thus he shows. There, those who, having seen the master face to face, rise to greet him, take the goods from his hand, release this, take that, perform all the remaining duties such as arranging a seat, providing water for washing the feet, and so forth; but when the master is not present, they do not even look at the oil rising, even if the work is worth a hundred or a thousand, they turn away, and do not even want to look at it, these conduct themselves differently by body. Those who, to our face, praise us, saying, "You are our master, you are our lord," but behind our backs, there is nothing they won't say; they say what they want. These people behave differently with their words (*vācāya*).

Furthermore, venerable sir, our slaves (*dāsā*), servants (*pessā*), and workers (*kammakarā*) [act] differently with their bodies (*kāyena*).

mula_pali:
4. ‘‘Evametaṃ, pessa, evametaṃ, pessa. Gahanañhetaṃ , pessa, yadidaṃ manussā; uttānakañhetaṃ, pessa, yadidaṃ pasavo. Cattārome, pessa, puggalā santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ. Katame cattāro? Idha, pessa, ekacco puggalo attantapo hoti attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto; idha pana, pessa, ekacco puggalo parantapo hoti paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto; idha pana, pessa, ekacco puggalo attantapo ca hoti attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto, parantapo ca paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto ; idha pana, pessa, ekacco puggalo nevattantapo hoti nāttaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto na parantapo na paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto. So anattantapo aparantapo diṭṭheva dhamme nicchāto nibbuto sītībhūto sītibhūto (sī. pī. ka.) sukhappaṭisaṃvedī brahmabhūtena attanā viharati. Imesaṃ, pessa, catunnaṃ puggalānaṃ katamo te puggalo cittaṃ ārādhetī’’ti?

‘‘Yvāyaṃ, bhante, puggalo attantapo attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto, ayaṃ me puggalo cittaṃ nārādheti. Yopāyaṃ, bhante, puggalo parantapo paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto , ayampi me puggalo cittaṃ nārādheti. Yopāyaṃ, bhante, puggalo attantapo ca attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto parantapo ca paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto, ayampi me puggalo cittaṃ nārādheti. Yo ca kho ayaṃ, bhante, puggalo nevattantapo nāttaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto na parantapo na paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto, so anattantapo aparantapo diṭṭheva dhamme nicchāto nibbuto sītībhūto sukhappaṭisaṃvedī brahmabhūtena attanā viharati – ayameva ayaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) me puggalo cittaṃ ārādhetī’’ti.

ayaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)
mula_english:
4. So it is, Pessa, so it is.

This is profound, Pessa, that is, human beings; this is obvious, Pessa, that is, animals.

There are these four kinds of persons to be found existing in the world, Pessa. What are the four? Here, Pessa, a certain person torments himself and is devoted to the practice of torturing himself; here, Pessa, a certain person torments others and is devoted to the practice of torturing others; here, Pessa, a certain person torments himself and is devoted to the practice of torturing himself, and he also torments others and is devoted to the practice of torturing others; here, Pessa, a certain person neither torments himself nor is devoted to the practice of torturing himself, and he neither torments others nor is devoted to the practice of torturing others.

Since he torments neither himself nor others, he dwells in the here and now free of hunger, extinguished, cooled, sensitive to pleasure, with a mind like Brahmā.

Which of these four types of individuals satisfies your mind the most?”

“Venerable sir, the person who torments himself and is devoted to the practice of torturing himself does not satisfy my mind.

Venerable sir, the person who torments others and is devoted to the practice of torturing others does not satisfy my mind.

Venerable sir, the person who torments himself and is devoted to the practice of torturing himself and also torments others and is devoted to the practice of torturing others does not satisfy my mind.

Venerable sir, the person who neither torments himself nor is devoted to the practice of torturing himself and neither torments others nor is devoted to the practice of torturing others, who, since he torments neither himself nor others, is here and now hungerless, extinguished, and cooled, and abides experiencing bliss, having himself become like Brahmā – that person satisfies my mind the most.”
commentary_pali:
4.Cattārome pessapuggalāti ayampi pāṭiekko anusandhi. Ayañhi pesso ‘‘yāvañcidaṃ, bhante, bhagavā evaṃ manussagahaṇe evaṃ manussakasaṭe evaṃ manussasāṭheyye vattamāne sattānaṃ hitāhitaṃ jānātī’’ti āha. Purime ca tayo puggalā ahitapaṭipadaṃ paṭipannā, upari catuttho hitapaṭipadaṃ, evamahaṃ sattānaṃ hitāhitaṃ jānāmīti dassetuṃ imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi. Heṭṭhā kandarakassa kathāya saddhiṃ yojetumpi vaṭṭati. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘yāvañcidaṃ bhotā gotamena sammā bhikkhusaṅgho paṭipādito’’ti. Athassa bhagavā ‘‘purime tayo puggale pahāya upari catutthapuggalassa hitapaṭipattiyaṃyeva paṭipādemī’’ti dassentopi imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi. Santoti idaṃ saṃvijjamānāti padasseva vevacanaṃ. ‘‘Santā honti samitā vūpasantā’’ti (vibha. 542) ettha hi niruddhā santāti vuttā. ‘‘Santā ete vihārā ariyassa vinaye vuccantī’’ti ettha (ma. ni. 1.82) nibbutā. ‘‘Santo have sabbhi pavedayantī’’ti ettha (jā. 2.21.413) paṇḍitā. Idha pana vijjamānā upalabbhamānāti attho.

Attantapādīsu attānaṃ tapati dukkhāpetīti attantapo. Attano paritāpanānuyogaṃ attaparitāpanānuyogaṃ. Paraṃ tapati dukkhāpetīti parantapo. Paresaṃ paritāpanānuyogaṃ paraparitāpanānuyogaṃ. Diṭṭheva dhammeti imasmiṃyeva attabhāve. Nicchātoti chātaṃ vuccati taṇhā, sā assa natthīti nicchāto. Sabbakilesānaṃ nibbutattā nibbuto. Anto tāpanakilesānaṃ abhāvā sītalo jātoti sītibhūto. Jhānamaggaphalanibbānasukhāni paṭisaṃvedetīti sukhapaṭisaṃvedī. Brahmabhūtena attanāti seṭṭhabhūtena attanā. Cittaṃ ārādhetīti cittaṃ sampādeti, paripūreti gaṇhāti pasādetīti attho.

attantapo attaparitāpanānuyogaṃ parantapo paraparitāpanānuyogaṃ Diṭṭheva dhamme Nicchāto nibbuto sītibhūto sukhapaṭisaṃvedī Brahmabhūtena attanā Cittaṃ ārādhetī
commentary_english:
4. " *Cattārome pessapuggalā* ": this is also a phrase-by-phrase connection.

This messenger said, "Indeed, venerable sir, the Blessed One, while living amidst such human greed, such human miserliness, such human deceitfulness, knows what is beneficial and not beneficial for beings."

The first three individuals were engaged in a course of action that was not beneficial, and the fourth was engaged in a beneficial course of action. Thus, to show that "I know what is beneficial and not beneficial for beings," he began this discourse.

It is also fitting to connect it with the story of Kandāraka further below.

Therefore, it was said, "Indeed, the *bhikkhu-saṅgha* has been well guided by the venerable Gotama."

Then the Blessed One, even while showing that "Having abandoned the first three individuals, I will guide [beings] only in the beneficial course of action of the fourth individual," began this discourse.

*Santo*: this is a synonym for the word *saṃvijjamānāti*, "existing".

For here it is said that those who are stopped are *santā*, "peaceful" (*santo honti samitā vūpasantā*).

Here, *nibbuta*, "quenched" (*santā ete vihārā ariyassa vinaye vuccanti*).

Here, *paṇḍitā*, "wise" (*santo have sabbhi pavedayantī*).

But here, the meaning is "existing, available."

Among those who torture themselves: *attantapo*: one who tortures or causes suffering to oneself. *attaparitāpanānuyogaṃ*: engaging in self-torment. *parantapo*: one who tortures or causes suffering to others. *paraparitāpanānuyogaṃ*: engaging in the torment of others. *Diṭṭheva dhamme*: in this very existence. *nicchāto*: *chātaṃ* means craving; one who does not have that is *nicchāto*, without craving. *Nibbuto*: cooled down through emancipation from all defilements. *Sītibhūto*: one who has become cool because of the absence of the defilements that cause burning. *Sukhapaṭisaṃvedī*: one who experiences the happiness of *jhāna*, the path, the fruit, and *nirvāṇa*. *Brahmabhūtena attanā*: with an excellent self. *Cittaṃ ārādheti*: he pleases the mind; the meaning is that he accomplishes, fulfills, takes hold of, and gladdens the mind.

mula_pali: 5. ‘‘Kasmā pana te, pessa, ime tayo puggalā cittaṃ nārādhentī’’ti? ‘‘Yvāyaṃ, bhante, puggalo attantapo attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto so attānaṃ sukhakāmaṃ dukkhapaṭikkūlaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti – iminā me ayaṃ puggalo cittaṃ nārādheti. Yopāyaṃ, bhante, puggalo parantapo paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto so paraṃ sukhakāmaṃ dukkhapaṭikkūlaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti – iminā me ayaṃ puggalo cittaṃ nārādheti. Yopāyaṃ, bhante, puggalo attantapo ca attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto parantapo ca paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto so attānañca parañca sukhakāmaṃ dukkhapaṭikkūlaṃ sukhakāme dukkhapaṭikkūle (sī. pī.) ātāpeti paritāpeti – iminā me ayaṃ puggalo cittaṃ nārādheti. Yo ca kho ayaṃ, bhante, puggalo nevattantapo nāttaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto na parantapo na paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto so anattantapo aparantapo diṭṭheva dhamme nicchāto nibbuto sītībhūto sukhappaṭisaṃvedī brahmabhūtena attanā viharati. iminā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) viharati; so attānañca parañca sukhakāmaṃ dukkhapaṭikkūlaṃ neva ātāpeti na paritāpeti – iminā viharati. iminā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) me ayaṃ puggalo cittaṃ ārādheti. Handa, ca dāni mayaṃ, bhante, gacchāma; bahukiccā mayaṃ bahukaraṇīyā’’ti. ‘‘Yassadāni tvaṃ, pessa, kālaṃ maññasī’’ti. Atha kho pesso hatthārohaputto bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.
mula_english:
5. "Why then, Pessa, do these three individuals not satisfy your mind?"

"Venerable sir, the kind of person who torments himself (attan tapo) and pursues the practice of torturing himself (atta paritāpana anuyoga manuyutto), torments and tortures himself though he desires pleasure (sukha kāma) and recoils from pain (dukkha patikkūlaṃ) – that is why this kind of person does not satisfy my mind.

And the kind of person who torments others (parantapo) and pursues the practice of torturing others (para paritāpana anuyoga manuyutto), torments and tortures others who desire pleasure (sukha kāma) and recoil from pain (dukkha patikkūlaṃ); that is why this kind of person does not satisfy my mind.

And the kind of person who torments himself (attan tapo) and pursues the practice of torturing himself (atta paritāpana anuyoga manuyutto), and who also torments others (parantapo) and pursues the practice of torturing others (para paritāpana anuyoga manuyutto), torments and tortures himself and others, both of whom desire pleasure (sukha kāma) and recoil from pain (dukkha patikkūlaṃ); that is why this kind of person does not satisfy my mind.

But the kind of person who does not torment himself (nevattan tapo) or pursue the practice of torturing himself (nātta paritāpana anuyoga manuyutto) and who does not torment others (na parantapo) or pursue the practice of torturing others (na para paritāpana anuyoga manuyutto); who, since he torments neither himself (anattan tapo) nor others (aparantapo), is here and now hungerless (nicchāto), extinguished (nibbuto), and cooled (sītībhūto), and abides experiencing bliss (sukha patisaṃvedī), having himself become holy (brahmabhūtena attanā); he does not torment and torture either himself or others, both of whom desire pleasure (sukha kāma) and recoil from pain (dukkha patikkūlaṃ). That is why this kind of person satisfies my mind.

And now, venerable sir, we depart. We are busy and have much to do."

"Now is the time, Pessa, to do as you think fit."

Then Pessa, the elephant driver’s son (hatthārohaputto), having delighted and rejoiced in the Blessed One’s (bhagavato) words (bhāsitaṃ), rose from his seat, and after paying homage to the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ), keeping him on his right (padakkhiṇaṃ katvā), he departed (pakkāmi).
commentary_pali: 5.Dukkhapaṭikkūlanti dukkhassa paṭikūlaṃ, paccanīkasaṇṭhitaṃ dukkhaṃ apatthayamānanti attho.
commentary_english: *duḥkhapaṭikkūla* means adverse to suffering, the opposite state, not desiring suffering—this is the meaning.

mula_pali: 6. Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkante pesse hatthārohaputte bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘paṇḍito, bhikkhave, pesso hatthārohaputto; mahāpañño, bhikkhave, pesso hatthārohaputto. Sace, bhikkhave, pesso hatthārohaputto muhuttaṃ nisīdeyya yāvassāhaṃ ime cattāro puggale vitthārena vibhajissāmi vibhajāmi (sī. pī.), mahatā atthena saṃyutto abhavissa. Api ca, bhikkhave, ettāvatāpi pesso hatthārohaputto mahatā atthena saṃyutto’’ti. ‘‘Etassa, bhagavā, kālo, etassa, sugata, kālo, yaṃ bhagavā ime cattāro puggale vitthārena vibhajeyya. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī’’ti. ‘‘Tena hi, bhikkhave, suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
After that, the Blessed One, soon after Pessa, the elephant driver's son, had left, addressed the *bhikkhus*, saying: "Oh *bhikkhus*, Pessa, the elephant driver’s son, is wise; oh *bhikkhus*, Pessa, the elephant driver’s son, has great wisdom.

"If, oh *bhikkhus*, Pessa, the elephant driver’s son, had sat a while longer until I had expounded in detail these four types of individuals (*pudgala*) , he would have greatly benefited.

Still, oh *bhikkhus*, even as it is, Pessa, the elephant driver’s son, has already greatly benefited."

"Venerable Sir (*bhagavā*), this is the time; oh *Sugata*, this is the time for the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) to expound in detail these four types of individuals (*pudgala*). Having heard it from the Blessed One (*bhagavataḥ*), the *bhikkhus* will remember it."

"Then listen, oh *bhikkhus*, and pay close attention; I will speak."

"As you say, venerable sir (*bhante*)," the *bhikkhus* replied to the Blessed One (*bhagavato*).

The Blessed One (*bhagavā*) said this:
commentary_pali: 6.Paṇḍitoti idha catūhi kāraṇehi paṇḍitoti na vattabbo, satipaṭṭhānesu pana kammaṃ karotīti paṇḍitoti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Mahāpaññoti idampi mahante atthe pariggaṇhātītiādinā mahāpaññalakkhaṇena na vattabbaṃ, satipaṭṭhānapariggāhikāya pana paññāya samannāgatattā mahāpaññoti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Mahatā atthena saṃyutto agamissāti mahatā atthena saṃyutto hutvā gato bhaveyya, sotāpattiphalaṃ pāpuṇeyyāti attho. Kiṃ pana yesaṃ maggaphalānaṃ upanissayo atthi, buddhānaṃ sammukhībhāve ṭhitepi tesaṃ antarāyo hotīti. Āma hoti, na pana buddhe paṭicca, atha kho kiriyaparihāniyā vā pāpamittatāya vā hoti. Tattha kiriyaparihāniyā hoti nāma – sace hi dhammasenāpati dhanañjānissa brāhmaṇassa āsayaṃ ñatvā dhammaṃ adesayissā, so brāhmaṇo sotāpanno abhavissā, evaṃ tāva kiriyaparihāniyā hoti. Pāpamittatāya hoti nāma – sace hi ajātasattu devadattassa vacanaṃ gahetvā pitughātakammaṃ nākarissā, sāmaññaphalasuttakathitadivaseva sotāpanno abhavissā, tassa vacanaṃ gahetvā pitughātakammassa katattā pana na hoti, evaṃ pāpamittatāya hoti. Imassāpi upāsakassa kiriyaparihāni jātā, apariniṭṭhitāya desanāya uṭṭhahitvā pakkanto. Apica, bhikkhave, ettāvatāpi pessohatthārohaputto mahatā atthena saṃyuttoti katarena mahantena atthena? Dvīhi ānisaṃsehi. So kira upāsako saṅghe ca pasādaṃ paṭilabhi, satipaṭṭhānapariggahaṇatthāya cassa abhinavo nayo udapādi. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘mahatā atthena saṃyutto’’ti. Kandarako pana saṅghe pasādameva paṭilabhi. Etassa bhagavā kāloti etassa dhammakkhānassa, catunnaṃ vā puggalānaṃ vibhajanassa kālo.
commentary_english:
6. "Paṇḍito": Here, "paṇḍito" should not be defined by four causes. But it is proper to say "paṇḍito" because one engages in actions in the *smṛtyupasthānas* (mindfulness practices).

"Mahāpañño": Here, "mahāpañño" should not be defined by the characteristics of great wisdom (*mahāpañña-lakkhana*) beginning with the phrase "because it grasps a great meaning" (*mahante atthe pariggaṇhāti*). But it is proper to say "mahāpañño" because wisdom is endowed with the acceptance of mindfulness.

"Mahatā atthena saṃyutto agamissā": "He would have gone being united with a great meaning," meaning, he would have become united with a great meaning and would have gone, he would have attained the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpatti-phala*).

But is there a foundation (*upanissayo*) for the paths and fruits (*maggaphalānaṃ*) of those for whom there is an obstacle (*antarāyo*) even when the Buddhas are present?

Yes, it is. However, not in relation to the Buddha, but because of a decline in practice (*kiriyaparihāniyā*) or because of bad friendship (*pāpamittatāya*).

There, the decline in practice occurs, namely—if the general of the Dharma, *Dhanañjāni*, having known the inclination of the *brāhmaṇa*, were to have taught the Dharma, that *brāhmaṇa* would have become a stream-enterer (*sotāpanna*); thus, there is a decline in practice.

Bad friendship occurs, namely—if Ajātaśatru, not having taken Devadatta's word, had not committed the deed of killing his father, he would have become a stream-enterer on the very day the Fruits of Recluseship were spoken of (*sāmaññaphalasutta*); however, because of his having taken his word and having committed the deed of killing his father, it did not happen; thus, there is bad friendship.

A decline in practice has occurred for this lay follower (*upāsaka*) as well; having arisen from the teaching which was not completed, he departed.

"Furthermore, *bhikkhus*, even to this extent, the son of the elephant trainer (*hatthārohaputto*) is united with a great meaning (*mahatā atthena saṃyutto*)": With what great meaning? With two benefits (*ānisaṃsehi*).

It is said that that lay follower obtained confidence in the *saṃgha*, and a new method (*naya*) arose for him for the sake of accepting the applications of mindfulness.

Therefore, it was said: "united with a great meaning."

But Kandaraka only obtained confidence in the *saṃgha*.

"This is the time, Blessed One (*bhagavā kālo*)": This is the time for this teaching of the Dharma (*dharmakkhānassa*), [or] the time for the distribution of four individuals (*puggalānaṃ*).

mula_pali: 7. ‘‘Katamo ca, bhikkhave, puggalo attantapo attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo acelako hoti muttācāro hatthāpalekhano hatthāvalekhano (syā. kaṃ.) naehibhaddantiko natiṭṭhabhaddantiko naehibhadantiko, natiṭṭhabhadantiko (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.); nābhihaṭaṃ na uddissakataṃ na nimantanaṃ sādiyati; so na kumbhimukhā paṭiggaṇhāti na kaḷopimukhā khaḷopimukho (sī.) paṭiggaṇhāti na eḷakamantaraṃ na daṇḍamantaraṃ na musalamantaraṃ na dvinnaṃ bhuñjamānānaṃ na gabbhiniyā na pāyamānāya na purisantaragatāya na saṅkittīsu na yattha sā upaṭṭhito hoti na yattha makkhikā saṇḍasaṇḍacārinī; na macchaṃ na maṃsaṃ na suraṃ na merayaṃ na thusodakaṃ pivati. So ekāgāriko vā hoti ekālopiko, dvāgāriko vā hoti dvālopiko…pe… sattāgāriko vā hoti sattālopiko; ekissāpi dattiyā yāpeti, dvīhipi dattīhi yāpeti…pe… sattahipi dattīhi yāpeti; ekāhikampi āhāraṃ āhāreti, dvīhikampi āhāraṃ āhāreti…pe… sattāhikampi āhāraṃ āhāreti – iti evarūpaṃ aḍḍhamāsikaṃ pariyāyabhattabhojanānuyogamanuyutto viharati. So sākabhakkho vā hoti, sāmākabhakkho vā hoti, nīvārabhakkho vā hoti, daddulabhakkho vā hoti, haṭabhakkho vā hoti, kaṇabhakkho vā hoti, ācāmabhakkho vā hoti, piññākabhakkho vā hoti, tiṇabhakkho vā hoti, gomayabhakkho vā hoti; vanamūlaphalāhāro yāpeti pavattaphalabhojī. So sāṇānipi dhāreti, masāṇānipi dhāreti, chavadussānipi dhāreti, paṃsukūlānipi dhāreti, tirīṭānipi dhāreti, ajinampi dhāreti, ajinakkhipampi dhāreti, kusacīrampi dhāreti, vākacīrampi dhāreti, phalakacīrampi dhāreti, kesakambalampi dhāreti, vāḷakambalampi dhāreti, ulūkapakkhampi dhāreti; kesamassulocakopi hoti, kesamassulocanānuyogamanuyutto, ubbhaṭṭhakopi hoti āsanapaṭikkhitto, ukkuṭikopi hoti ukkuṭikappadhānamanuyutto, kaṇṭakāpassayikopi hoti kaṇṭakāpassaye seyyaṃ kappeti passa ma. ni. 1.155 mahāsīhanādasutte; sāyatatiyakampi udakorohanānuyogamanuyutto viharati – iti evarūpaṃ anekavihitaṃ kāyassa ātāpanaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, puggalo attantapo attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto.
mula_english:
7. Monks, what is the person who torments himself and is devoted to the practice of torturing himself? Here, monks, a certain person goes naked, rejecting conventions, licking his hands, not coming when asked, not stopping when asked; he does not accept food brought or food specially made or an invitation to a meal; he receives nothing from a pot, from a bowl, across a threshold, across a stick, across a pestle, from two eating together, from a pregnant woman, from a woman giving suck, from a woman lying with a man, from where food is advertised to be distributed, from where a dog is waiting, from where flies are swarming. He eats no fish or meat and drinks no rum or spirits or fermented rice-gruel.

He is a one-house man or a one-morsel man, a two-house man or a two-morsel man… a seven-house man or a seven-morsel man. He lives on one saucerful a day, on two saucerfuls a day…on seven saucerfuls a day. He takes food once a day, once every two days…once every seven days; thus he dwells pursuing the practice of taking food at stated intervals, every half month.

He is an eater of greens or millet or wild rice or hide-parings or moss or rice-bran or rice-scum or sesamum flour or grass or cow dung; he lives on forest roots and fruits, he feeds on fallen fruits.

He wears coarse hemp or mixed material, shrouds from corpses, rags from the dust-heap, garments of bark-fibre, antelope-skins, grass, bark, shavings, blankets of human hair or horse-hair, the wings of owls. He is a plucker-out of hair and beard, devoted to this practice; he is one who squats continuously, devoted to maintaining the squatting position. He is one who uses a mattress of spikes; he makes a mattress of spikes his bed; he dwells pursuing the practice of bathing in water three times daily including the evening - thus in such a variety of ways he dwells pursuing the practice of tormenting and mortifying the body.

This is called the kind of person who torments himself and pursues the practice of torturing himself.

mula_pali: 8. ‘‘Katamo ca, bhikkhave, puggalo parantapo paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo orabbhiko hoti sūkariko sākuṇiko māgaviko luddo macchaghātako coro coraghātako goghātako bandhanāgāriko ye vā panaññepi keci kurūrakammantā. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, puggalo parantapo paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto.
mula_english:
Here, bhikkhus, which individual is a tormentor of others, one who is devoted to torturing others? Here, bhikkhus, a certain individual is a butcher of sheep (*orabbhiko*), a butcher of pigs (*sūkariko*), a fowler (*sākuṇiko*), a hunter (*māgaviko*), a cruel hunter (*luddo*), a fisherman (*macchaghātako*), a thief (*coro*), an executioner (*coraghātako*), a cattle slaughterer (*goghātako*), a prison warden (*bandhanāgāriko*), or one who follows any other such cruel occupation (*kurūrakammantā*).

This, bhikkhus, is called an individual who torments others (*parantapo*) and is devoted to the practice of torturing others (*paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto*).
commentary_pali: 8.Orabbhikādīsu urabbhā vuccanti eḷakā, urabbhe hanatīti orabbhiko. Sūkarikādīsupi eseva nayo. Luddoti dāruṇo kakkhaḷo. Macchaghātakoti macchabandhakevaṭṭo. Bandhanāgārikoti bandhanāgāragopako. Kururakammantāti dāruṇakammantā.
commentary_english:
In *orabbhikā* etc., *urabbhā* means goats; *orabbhiko* means one who kills goats.

The same method applies in *sūkarikā* etc.

*luddo* means cruel, harsh.

*macchaghātako* means a fisherman.

*bandhanāgāriko* means a prison guard.

*kururakammantā* means cruel actions.

mula_pali: 9. ‘‘Katamo ca, bhikkhave, puggalo attantapo ca attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto parantapo ca paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo rājā vā hoti khattiyo muddhāvasitto brāhmaṇo vā mahāsālo. So puratthimena nagarassa navaṃ santhāgāraṃ sandhāgāraṃ (ṭīkā) kārāpetvā kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kharājinaṃ nivāsetvā sappitelena kāyaṃ abbhañjitvā magavisāṇena piṭṭhiṃ kaṇḍuvamāno navaṃ santhāgāraṃ pavisati saddhiṃ mahesiyā brāhmaṇena ca purohitena. So tattha anantarahitāya bhūmiyā haritupalittāya seyyaṃ kappeti. Ekissāya gāviyā sarūpavacchāya yaṃ ekasmiṃ thane khīraṃ hoti tena rājā yāpeti, yaṃ dutiyasmiṃ thane khīraṃ hoti tena mahesī yāpeti, yaṃ tatiyasmiṃ thane khīraṃ hoti tena brāhmaṇo purohito yāpeti , yaṃ catutthasmiṃ thane khīraṃ hoti tena aggiṃ juhati, avasesena vacchako yāpeti. So evamāha – ‘ettakā usabhā haññantu yaññatthāya, ettakā vacchatarā haññantu yaññatthāya, ettakā vacchatariyo haññantu yaññatthāya, ettakā ajā haññantu yaññatthāya, ettakā urabbhā haññantu yaññatthāya, (ettakā assā haññantu yaññatthāya) ( ) natthi sī. pī. potthakesu, ettakā rukkhā chijjantu yūpatthāya, ettakā dabbhā lūyantu barihisatthāyā’ti parihiṃ satthāya (ka.). Yepissa te honti dāsāti vā pessāti vā kammakarāti vā tepi daṇḍatajjitā bhayatajjitā assumukhā rudamānā parikammāni karonti. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, puggalo attantapo ca attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto parantapo ca paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto.
mula_english: Bhikkhus, what is the individual who torments himself and is devoted to the practice of torturing himself, and who torments others and is devoted to the practice of torturing others? Here, some person is a head-anointed noble king ( *kṣatriyo mūrddhāvasikto* ) or a well-to-do Brahmin (*brāhmaṇo mahāsālo*). Having had a new sacrificial temple built to the east of the city, and having shaved off his hair and beard, dressed himself in rough hide, and greased his body with ghee (*sarpi*) and oil, scratching his back with a deer’s horn, he enters the new sacrificial temple together with his chief queen (*mahesiyā*) and his brahmin high priest (*brāhmaṇena ca purohitena*). There he lies down on the bare ground with the grass on it. The king lives on the milk in the first teat of a cow with a calf of the same colour while the chief queen lives on the milk in the second teat and the brahmin high priest lives on the milk in the third teat; the milk in the fourth teat they pour onto the fire ( *aggiṃ juhoti* ), and the calf lives on what is left. He says thus: ‘Let so many bulls (*usabhā*) be slaughtered for sacrifice ( *yaññatthāya*), let so many bullocks (*vacchatarā*) be slaughtered for sacrifice, let so many heifers (*vacchatarīyo*) be slaughtered for sacrifice, let so many goats (*ajā*) be slaughtered for sacrifice, let so many sheep (*urabbhā*) be slaughtered for sacrifice, let so many trees (*rukkha*) be felled for the sacrificial posts (*yūpatthāya*), let so much grass (*dabbhā*) be cut for the sacrificial grass (*barihisatthāya*) .’ And those who are his slaves or messengers or workers, they too, being threatened with sticks, being threatened with fear, with tearful faces, weeping, do their work. This is called, bhikkhus, an individual who torments himself and is devoted to the practice of torturing himself, and who torments others and is devoted to the practice of torturing others.
commentary_pali:
9.Muddhāvasittoti khattiyābhisekena muddhani abhisitto. Puratthimena nagarassāti nagarato puratthimadisāya. Santhāgāranti yaññasālaṃ. Kharājinaṃ nivāsetvāti sakhuraṃ ajinacammaṃ nivāsetvā. Sappitelenāti sappinā ca telena ca. Ṭhapetvā hi sappiṃ avaseso yo koci sneho telanti vuccati. Kaṇḍūvamānoti nakhānaṃ chinnattā kaṇḍūvitabbakāle tena kaṇḍūvamāno. Anantarahitāyāti asanthatāya. Sarūpavacchāyāti sadisavacchāya. Sace gāvī setā hoti, vacchopi setakova. Sace gāvī kabarā vā rattā vā, vacchopi tādiso vāti evaṃ sarūpavacchāya. So evamāhāti so rājā evaṃ vadeti. Vacchatarāti taruṇavacchakabhāvaṃ atikkantā balavavacchā. Vacchatarīsupi eseva nayo. Barihisatthāyāti parikkhepakaraṇatthāya ceva yaññabhūmiyaṃ attharaṇatthāya ca. Sesaṃ heṭṭhā tattha tattha vitthāritattā uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Kandarakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
9. *muddhāvasitto* means *abhiṣikta* (anointed) at the head with the *kṣatriyābhiseka* (anointment of a kṣatriya).

*puratthimena nagarassā* means *puratthimadisāya* (eastern direction) from the city.

*santhāgāra* means *yajñasālā* (hall for sacrifice).

*kharājinaṃ nivāsetvā* means *nivāsetvā* (having covered) the *ajinacammaṃ* (deer skin) with its hair.

*sappitelenā* means with *sappinā* (ghee) and with *telena* (oil).

Having set aside ghee, any remaining *sneha* (oil) is called *tela* (oil).

*kaṇḍūvamāno* means because of the cutting of the nails, he scratches at the time for scratching.

*anantarahitāyā* means *asanthatāya* (undisturbed).

*sarūpavacchāyā* means *sadisavacchāya* (similar shadow).

If a cow is white, the calf is also white.

If a cow is speckled or red, the calf is also of that kind; thus, the shadow is similar.

*so evamāhā* means the king speaks thus.

*vacchatarā* means having passed the state of a young calf; a strong calf.

Even with a *vacchatarī* (older female calf), this is the same method.

*barihisatthāyā* means both for the purpose of making a boundary and for the purpose of spreading on the *yajñabhūmi* (sacrificial ground).

The rest is expanded below there; thus, it is spread out.

The *papañcasūdanī* commentary on the *majjhimanikāya* is finished.

The *kandarakasuttavaṇṇanā* (commentary on the Kandarakasutta) is finished.

mula_pali: 10. ‘‘Katamo ca, bhikkhave, puggalo nevattantapo nāttaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto na parantapo na paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto, so anattantapo aparantapo diṭṭheva dhamme nicchāto nibbuto sītībhūto sukhappaṭisaṃvedī brahmabhūtena attanā viharati? Idha, bhikkhave, tathāgato loke uppajjati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā. So imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti. So dhammaṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāseti. Taṃ dhammaṃ suṇāti gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā aññatarasmiṃ vā kule paccājāto. So taṃ dhammaṃ sutvā tathāgate saddhaṃ paṭilabhati. So tena saddhāpaṭilābhena samannāgato iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘sambādho gharāvāso rajāpatho, abbhokāso pabbajjā. Nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ ekantaparisuddhaṃ saṅkhalikhitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajeyya’nti . So aparena samayena appaṃ vā bhogakkhandhaṃ pahāya, mahantaṃ vā bhogakkhandhaṃ pahāya, appaṃ vā ñātiparivaṭṭaṃ pahāya , mahantaṃ vā ñātiparivaṭṭaṃ pahāya, kesamassuṃ ohāretvā, kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati.
mula_english:
“And what kind of person, mendicants, neither torments himself, nor is intent on the practice of torturing himself, neither torments others, nor is intent on the practice of torturing others; but, not tormenting himself or others, is without craving in this very life, extinguished, cooled, experiencing pleasure, having become Brahman? Here, mendicants, a *Tathāgata* arises in the world, a worthy one, a rightly self-awakened one, perfect in knowledge and conduct, a *Sugata*, a knower of the world, unsurpassed, a trainer of those persons ready to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed. He makes known this world—with its gods, *Māras*, and *Brahmās*, its ascetics and Brahmins, its princes and people—having realized it with his own insight through direct knowledge (*abhiññā*). He teaches the *Dhamma* that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing. He reveals the spiritual life (*brahmacariya*) that is perfectly complete and pure. A householder or a householder’s son or someone reborn in another family hears that *Dhamma*. Having heard this *Dhamma*, he gains faith (*saddhā*) in the *Tathāgata*. Possessing that faith (*saddhā*), he reflects: ‘The household life is confining, a dusty path; going forth is the open air. It’s not easy to live the spiritual life (*brahmacariya*) perfectly complete, perfectly pure, like a polished shell, while living at home. Why don’t I shave off my hair and beard, dress in orange robes, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness?’

Later, he gives up a small or large amount of wealth; he abandons a small or large circle of relatives. He shaves off his hair and beard, puts on the orange robes, and goes forth from the household life into homelessness.

mula_pali:
11. ‘‘So evaṃ pabbajito samāno bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāsājīvasamāpanno pāṇātipātaṃ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho, lajjī dayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharati. Adinnādānaṃ pahāya adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti dinnādāyī dinnapāṭikaṅkhī, athenena sucibhūtena attanā viharati. Abrahmacariyaṃ pahāya brahmacārī hoti ārācārī virato methunā gāmadhammā. Musāvādaṃ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato hoti saccavādī saccasandho theto paccayiko avisaṃvādako lokassa. Pisuṇaṃ vācaṃ pahāya pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, ito sutvā na amutra akkhātā imesaṃ bhedāya, amutra vā sutvā na imesaṃ akkhātā amūsaṃ bhedāya – iti bhinnānaṃ vā sandhātā sahitānaṃ vā anuppadātā samaggārāmo samaggarato samagganandī samaggakaraṇiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti. Pharusaṃ vācaṃ pahāya pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, yā sā vācā nelā kaṇṇasukhā pemanīyā hadayaṅgamā porī bahujanakantā bahujanamanāpā tathārūpiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti. Samphappalāpaṃ pahāya samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti kālavādī bhūtavādī atthavādī dhammavādī vinayavādī, nidhānavatiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā kālena sāpadesaṃ pariyantavatiṃ atthasaṃhitaṃ. So bījagāmabhūtagāmasamārambhā paṭivirato hoti, ekabhattiko hoti rattūparato virato vikālabhojanā; naccagītavāditavisūkadassanā paṭivirato hoti; mālāgandhavilepanadhāraṇamaṇḍanavibhūsanaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti; uccāsayanamahāsayanā paṭivirato hoti; jātarūparajatapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti; āmakadhaññapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti; āmakamaṃsapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti; itthikumārikapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti; dāsidāsapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti; ajeḷakapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti; kukkuṭasūkarapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti; hatthigavassavaḷavapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti; khettavatthupaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti; dūteyyapahiṇagamanānuyogā paṭivirato hoti; kayavikkayā paṭivirato hoti; tulākūṭakaṃsakūṭamānakūṭā paṭivirato hoti; ukkoṭanavañcananikatisāciyogā sāviyogā (syā. kaṃ. ka.) sāci kuṭilapariyāyo paṭivirato hoti; chedanavadhabandhanaviparāmosaālopasahasākārā paṭivirato hoti passa ma. ni. 1.293 cūḷahatthipadopame.

‘‘So santuṭṭho hoti kāyaparihārikena cīvarena kucchiparihārikena piṇḍapātena. So yena yeneva pakkamati, samādāyeva pakkamati. Seyyathāpi nāma pakkhī sakuṇo yena yeneva ḍeti, sapattabhārova ḍeti; evameva bhikkhu santuṭṭho hoti kāyaparihārikena cīvarena kucchiparihārikena piṇḍapātena. So yena yeneva pakkamati, samādāyeva pakkamati . So iminā ariyena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato ajjhattaṃ anavajjasukhaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti.
mula_english:
11. “Having thus gone forth and possessing the *bhikkhus’* training and way of life, abandoning the killing of living beings (*prāṇātipāta*), he abstains from killing living beings; with rod and weapon laid aside (*nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho*), gentle and kindly, he abides compassionate to all living beings.

Abandoning the taking of what is not given (*adinnādāna*), he abstains from taking what is not given; taking only what is given, expecting only what is given, by not stealing he abides in purity.

Abandoning unchastity (*abrahmacariya*), he observes celibacy (*brahmacārī*), living apart (*ārācārī*), abstaining from the vulgar practice of sexual intercourse (*methunā gāmadhammā*).

Abandoning false speech (*musāvāda*), he abstains from false speech; he speaks truth (*saccavādī*), adheres to truth (*saccasandha*), is trustworthy (*theto*) and reliable (*paccayiko*), one who is no deceiver of the world (*avisaṃvādako lokassa*).

Abandoning malicious speech (*pisuṇā vācā*), he abstains from malicious speech; he does not repeat elsewhere what he has heard here in order to divide those people from these, nor does he repeat to these people what he has heard elsewhere in order to divide these people from those; thus he is one who reunites those who are divided, a promoter of friendships, who enjoys concord, rejoices in concord, delights in concord, a speaker of words that promote concord (*samaggakaraṇiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti*).

Having abandoned harsh speech (*pharusaṃ vācaṃ*), he abstains from harsh speech; he speaks only such words as are gentle, pleasing to the ear (*kaṇṇasukhā*), endearing (*pemanīyā*), going to the heart (*hadayaṅgamā*), polite (*porī*), amiable (*bahujanakantā*) and agreeable to the manyfolk (*bahujanamanāpā*).

Having abandoned idle chatter (*samphappalāpa*), he abstains from idle chatter. He speaks at the right time (*kālavādī*), speaks what is factual (*bhūtavādī*) and beneficial (*atthavādī*), speaks on the *dharma* (*dhammavādī*) and the *Vinaya* (*vinayavādī*). His words are worth treasuring; they are timely, backed by reasons, measured, and connected with the good (*atthasaṃhitaṃ*).

He abstains from injuring seeds and plants. He practises eating only in one part of the day (*ekabhattiko*), abstaining from eating at night (*rattūparato*) and outside the proper time (*vikālabhojanā*). He abstains from dancing, singing, music, and theatrical shows. He abstains from wearing garlands, smartening himself with scent, and embellishing himself with unguents. He abstains from high and large couches (*uccāsayanamahāsayanā*). He abstains from accepting gold and silver (*jātarūparajatapaṭiggahaṇā*). He abstains from accepting raw grain (*āmakadhaññapaṭiggahaṇā*). He abstains from accepting raw meat (*āmakamaṃsapaṭiggahaṇā*). He abstains from accepting women and girls (*itthikumārikapaṭiggahaṇā*). He abstains from accepting male and female slaves (*dāsidāsapaṭiggahaṇā*). He abstains from accepting goats and sheep (*ajeḷakapaṭiggahaṇā*). He abstains from accepting fowl and pigs (*kukkuṭasūkarapaṭiggahaṇā*). He abstains from accepting elephants, cattle, horses, and mares (*hatthigavassavaḷavapaṭiggahaṇā*). He abstains from accepting fields and land (*khettavatthupaṭiggahaṇā*). He abstains from going on errands and messages (*dūteyyapahiṇagamanānuyogā*). He abstains from buying and selling (*kayavikkayā*).

He abstains from false balances, false metalware, and false measures. He abstains from scheming, deception, trickery, and crooked ways. He abstains from mutilation, killing, binding, robbery, slander, and violent acts.

“He is content with robes to protect his body and with almsfood to maintain his stomach.

Wherever he goes, he sets out taking only these with him.

Just as a bird, wherever it flies, flies with its wings as its only burden, so too, the *bhikkhu* is content with robes to protect his body and with almsfood to maintain his stomach.

Wherever he goes, he sets out taking only these with him.

Possessing this aggregate of noble virtue (*ariyena sīlakkhandhena*), he experiences within himself a bliss that is blameless (*anavajjasukhaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti*).

mula_pali:
12. ‘‘So cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ tassa saṃvarāya paṭipajjati, rakkhati cakkhundriyaṃ, cakkhundriye saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā…pe… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā…pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā…pe… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ manindriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ tassa saṃvarāya paṭipajjati, rakkhati manindriyaṃ, manindriye saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. So iminā ariyena indriyasaṃvarena samannāgato ajjhattaṃ abyāsekasukhaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti.

‘‘So abhikkante paṭikkante sampajānakārī hoti, ālokite vilokite sampajānakārī hoti, samiñjite pasārite sampajānakārī hoti, saṅghāṭipattacīvaradhāraṇe sampajānakārī hoti, asite pīte khāyite sāyite sampajānakārī hoti, uccārapassāvakamme sampajānakārī hoti, gate ṭhite nisinne sutte jāgarite bhāsite tuṇhībhāve sampajānakārī hoti.
mula_english:
12.
Having seen a form with the eye (cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā), he does not grasp at its signs (nimitta) and features (anubyañjana).

Since, if he were to dwell without restraint over the eye faculty (cakkhundriya) --evil, unskillful qualities such as greed (abhijjhā) or distress (domanassa) might assail him. He practices with restraint (saṃvarāya paṭipajjati). He guards the eye faculty (cakkhundriyaṃ, rakkhati). He achieves restraint (saṃvaraṃ āpajjati) with regard to the eye faculty (cakkhundriye).

On hearing a sound with the ear (sotena saddaṃ sutvā)…pe… on smelling an odour with the nose (ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā)…pe… on tasting a flavour with the tongue (jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā)…pe… on touching a tangible object with the body (kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā)…pe… on cognizing a mind-object with the mind (manasā dhammaṃ viññāya), he does not grasp at the sign (nimitta) or the details (anubyañjana).

Since, if he were to dwell without restraint over the mind faculty (manindriya) unskillful qualities such as greed (abhijjhā) or distress (domanassa) might assail him. He practices with restraint (saṃvarāya paṭipajjati). He guards the mind faculty (manindriyaṃ, rakkhati). He achieves restraint (saṃvaraṃ āpajjati) with regard to the mind faculty (manindriye).

Possessing this noble (ariyena) restraint (saṃvarena) of the faculties (indriya), he experiences within himself (ajjhattaṃ) a bliss (sukhaṃ) that is unsullied (abyāseka).

He acts with clear awareness (sampajānakārī hoti) in going forward (abhikkante) and returning (paṭikkante), in looking ahead (ālokite) and looking aside (vilokite), in bending (samiñjite) and stretching (pasārite), in wearing his robes (cīvara) and cloak (saṅghāṭi) and using his almsbowl (patta), in eating (asite), drinking (pīte), chewing (khāyite), and tasting (sāyite), in defecating (uccāra) and urinating (passāva), in going (gate), standing (ṭhite), sitting (nisinne), lying down (sutte), waking up (jāgarite), speaking (bhāsite) and in keeping silent (tuṇhībhāve).

mula_pali:
13. ‘‘So iminā ca ariyena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato, (imāya ca ariyāya santuṭṭhiyā samannāgato,) passa ma. ni. 1.296 cūḷahatthipadopame iminā ca ariyena indriyasaṃvarena samannāgato, iminā ca ariyena satisampajaññena samannāgato vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati araññaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ susānaṃ vanapatthaṃ abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ. So pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. So abhijjhaṃ loke pahāya vigatābhijjhena cetasā viharati, abhijjhāya cittaṃ parisodheti, byāpādapadosaṃ pahāya abyāpannacitto viharati sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī, byāpādapadosā cittaṃ parisodheti; thīnamiddhaṃ pahāya vigatathīnamiddho viharati ālokasaññī sato sampajāno, thīnamiddhā cittaṃ parisodheti; uddhaccakukkuccaṃ pahāya anuddhato viharati ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacitto, uddhaccakukkuccā cittaṃ parisodheti; vicikicchaṃ pahāya tiṇṇavicikiccho viharati akathaṃkathī kusalesu dhammesu, vicikicchāya cittaṃ parisodheti.

‘‘So ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe, vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati ; sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati.
mula_english:
13.
