There, the Blessed One, seated in the midst of the monks and lay followers, having been bathed with scented water, having wiped [himself] with a fine cloth, having been anointed with cinnabar, shone forth exceedingly, like a golden image placed on a red blanket-covered seat.

This is the ancient way of praising:

"<hi rend="bold">Having placed the Blessed One in front</hi>"

"Having gone to the palace courtyard, with the gait of a serpent-king;

Illuminating the world's chief, he sat on the excellent seat.

There, seated, the charioteer of men to be tamed,

The god above the gods, marked with a hundred meritorious signs;

In the Buddha-seat, in the middle, he shines,

Like a golden necklace on a russet blanket.

A necklace of gold, placed on a russet blanket;

He shines, stainless, like a jewel, a radiant gem.

Like a great *sāla* tree in full bloom, adorned like Mount Meru;

Like a golden pillar, a lotus, like a red lotus.

Blazing like a lamp-tree, like a flame on a mountain peak;

Like the gods' *pāricchatta* tree, fully blossomed, he shines."

"<hi rend="bold">In Kapilavatthu</hi>, <hi rend="bold">among the Sakyans, much divine talk at night, about the Dhamma</hi>"—here, *dhammī kathā* means mixed talk connected with rejoicing in the assembly hall, it should be understood.

Then, indeed, the Blessed One, as if descending the Ganges of the sky, as if drawing the strength of the earth, as if holding the great *jambu* tree on his shoulder and shaking it, as if pressing the *yojanika* honey jar with a wheel-machine, as if giving honey-drink to drink, spoke talk that brought benefit and happiness to the Sakyans of Kapilavatthu.

"This gift of a dwelling, O great king, is great, your dwelling is enjoyed by me, is enjoyed by the Sangha of monks, is enjoyed by me and by the Sangha of monks, but it is enjoyed by the jewel of the Dhamma, thus it is said to be enjoyed by the three jewels.

For in giving the gift of a dwelling, all gifts are given."
It is impossible to estimate the benefit of a ground-level leaf hut or a branch-covered pavilion." Having said this, he related a great deal of *dhamma*-talk of varied and diverse methods to Kapilavatthu.

In the Sakyas, during the night, with much talk about the *dhamma*.

‘‘Cold and heat it keeps away, and from wild beasts, too;

creeping things and gnats it wards, and rains in the cold season.

It keeps away the wind and burning sun,

When those awful things arise.

It’s for the sake of shelter and happiness,

To attain absorption and to see clearly.

Giving dwellings to the *Saṅgha*

Is praised as the best by the Buddha.

Therefore the wise man,

Seeing what is beneficial for himself,

Should have delightful dwellings built, and lodge the very learned there;

He should give them food and drink, clothes, and lodgings.

He should give to the upright, with a clear heart;

they teach him the *dhamma* that dispels all suffering;

knowing which *dhamma* in this life, he is extinguished, free from *āsavas*."

(Cūḷava. 295) –

Thus, this too is a benefit of a dwelling, and that too is a benefit.’ He related a talk on the benefit of a dwelling for a very great length of the night to the *bahudevas*, exceeding one and a half watches.

There, only these verses were included in the compilation, but scattered *dhammadesanā* was not included in the compilation.

*Sandassesīti*, etc., in the same place as stated before.

*Sandassesī*, *“The venerable Ānanda I will ask,"* he made it known, being desirous to cause him to tell a *dhamma*-talk.

Then why, with Sāriputta, Mahāmoggallāna, Mahākassapa, and the rest of the eighty great elders being present, did the Blessed One place the burden on the venerable Ānanda?

Because of his disposition for training.

For the venerable Ānanda is the foremost of the very learned, he is able to relate a sweet *dhamma*-talk with rounded phrases and expressions.’ He was known and renowned in the Sakyan territory.

A *dhammatalk* had been heard before even by the Sakyan kings having gone to the *vihāra*, but the women of the inner chambers do not obtain to go to the *vihāra* according to their own pleasure. It occurred to them, “Oh, if only the Blessed One, having told just a little *dhammatalk*, would place the burden on Ānanda, the best of our relatives."

Because of their disposition, the Blessed One placed the burden on him.

*“The venerable Ānanda I will ask,"* *Sekho pāṭipado*, one who has entered on the path, a trainee monk.

‘May he appear to you, may he attend upon you; teach him the practice’ thus, having restricted the individual to the practice, he showed (it).

But why did the Blessed One restrict this practice? Because of many reasons.

These Sakyas, for now, hope for good fortune and desire growth in the auspicious hall; and this trainee practice is an auspicious practice, a practice leading to growth in my Dispensation.’ Therefore, he restricted this practice.

And in that assembly many trainees are sitting; they, when a place attained by themselves is being spoken about, will easily understand without tiring.’ Therefore, he restricted this practice.

And the venerable Ānanda is one who has attained the discriminations proper to a trainee; he, speaking about a place directly known by himself, not tiring, will be able to inform (them).’ Therefore, he restricted this practice.

And in the practice of a trainee the three trainings are comprised as well, there, when the complete training in higher virtue is spoken of, the entire *Vinaya Piṭaka* is spoken of indeed, when the training in higher mind is spoken of, the entire *Suttanta Piṭaka* is spoken of, when the training in higher wisdom is spoken of, the entire *Abhidhamma Piṭaka* is spoken of, and Ānanda is very learned, a bearer of the three *Piṭakas*, he is able to tell the three trainings with the three *Piṭakas*, thus, when it is spoken of, good fortune and growth itself will happen for the Sakyas.’ Therefore, he restricted this practice.

*Sekho pāṭipado*

*“My back is aching,”* why is it aching? For the Blessed One, indeed, while striving for six years, there was great bodily suffering, then in the latter part of his life, in old age, wind in the back arose.

Or it is without cause.

For the Blessed One is able, having suppressed the arisen feeling, to sit down for one or two weeks in a single posture.

But he was desirous of enjoying the hall of assembly with the four postures; there, from the place for washing his feet to the *dhammāsana* he went, that much going was accomplished.

Having reached the *dhammāsana*, having stood a little, he sat down, that much (was the) place.He sat on the Dharma seat for one and a half *yāmas*. The sitting and lying down were accomplished in this place.

Now, he desired to use the four postures, saying, "The bed will be prepared if I lie down for a little while on my right side."

It should not be said that the body made of grasping does not ache. Therefore, having taken even a slight ache that arose from sitting for a long time, he spoke thus:

My back aches.

"Having spread out the *saṃghāṭi*": It seems those kings, on one side of the assembly hall, had a silk cloth stretched around, had a suitable couch arranged, had it covered with a suitable covering, and having hung above it a canopy adorned with golden stars, garlands of scents, and strings, they raised up a lamp with fragrant oil, saying, "Perhaps the Teacher, having risen from the Dharma seat, might rest here for a little while; thus, this assembly hall, used by the Blessed One with the four postures, will be for a long time for our benefit and happiness."

The Teacher, too, intending that very thing, having spread out the *saṃghāṭi* there, lay down.

"*Uṭṭhānasaññaṃ manasi karitvā*": Having placed the sign of rising in his mind, thinking, "Having passed this much time, I will get up," having established the perception of rising in his mind.

Having spread out the *saṃghāṭi*.

*Uṭṭhānasaññaṃ manasi karitvā*

mula_pali: 23. Atha kho āyasmā ānando mahānāmaṃ sakkaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘idha , mahānāma, ariyasāvako sīlasampanno hoti, indriyesu guttadvāro hoti, bhojane mattaññū hoti, jāgariyaṃ anuyutto hoti, sattahi saddhammehi samannāgato hoti, catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī.
mula_english: Then the venerable Ānanda addressed Mahānāma the Sakyan thus: “Mahānāma, here a noble disciple is possessed of virtue (śīlasampanno hoti), guards the doors of his sense faculties (indriyesu guttadvāro hoti), is moderate in eating (bhojane mattaññū hoti), and devoted to wakefulness (jāgariyaṃ anuyutto hoti); he possesses seven good qualities (sattahi saddhammehi samannāgato hoti); and he is one who obtains at will, without trouble or difficulty, the four *jhānas* (catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ) that constitute the higher mind and provide a pleasant abiding here and now (diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī).
commentary_pali: 23.Mahānāmaṃ sakkaṃ āmantesīti so kira tasmiṃ kāle tassaṃ parisati jeṭṭhako pāmokkho, tasmiṃ saṅgahite sesaparisā saṅgahitāva hotīti thero tameva āmantesi. Sīlasampannoti sīlena sampanno, sampannasīlo paripuṇṇasīloti attho. Saddhammehīti sundaradhammehi, sataṃ vā sappurisānaṃ dhammehi.
commentary_english: "23. *Mahānāmaṃ sakkaṃ āmantesī*—he addressed Mahānāma, the Sakyan. He, it seems, at that time in that assembly was the eldest, the chief. When he was included, the rest of the assembly was included. Therefore, the Elder addressed him. *Sīlasampanno*—endowed with virtue, accomplished in virtue, perfectly complete in virtue, is the meaning. *Saddhammehī*—with beautiful teachings, or with the teachings of good people."

mula_pali:
24. ‘‘Kathañca, mahānāma , ariyasāvako sīlasampanno hoti? Idha, mahānāma, ariyasāvako sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu. Evaṃ kho, mahānāma, ariyasāvako sīlasampanno hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, mahānāma, ariyasāvako indriyesu guttadvāro hoti? Idha, mahānāma, ariyasāvako cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ tassa saṃvarāya paṭipajjati, rakkhati cakkhundriyaṃ, cakkhundriye saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā…pe… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā…pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā…pe… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī. Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṃ manindriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ tassa saṃvarāya paṭipajjati, rakkhati manindriyaṃ, manindriye saṃvaraṃ āpajjati . Evaṃ kho, mahānāma, ariyasāvako indriyesu guttadvāro hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, mahānāma, ariyasāvako bhojane mattaññū hoti? Idha, mahānāma, ariyasāvako paṭisaṅkhā yoniso āhāraṃ āhāreti – ‘neva davāya na madāya na maṇḍanāya na vibhūsanāya; yāvadeva imassa kāyassa ṭhitiyā yāpanāya vihiṃsūparatiyā brahmacariyānuggahāya . Iti purāṇañca vedanaṃ paṭihaṅkhāmi, navañca vedanaṃ na uppādessāmi, yātrā ca me bhavissati anavajjatā ca phāsuvihāro cā’ti. Evaṃ kho, mahānāma, ariyasāvako bhojane mattaññū hoti.

‘‘Kathañca, mahānāma, ariyasāvako jāgariyaṃ anuyutto hoti? Idha, mahānāma, ariyasāvako divasaṃ caṅkamena nisajjāya āvaraṇīyehi dhammehi cittaṃ parisodheti, rattiyā paṭhamaṃ yāmaṃ caṅkamena nisajjāya āvaraṇīyehi dhammehi cittaṃ parisodheti, rattiyā majjhimaṃ yāmaṃ dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṃ kappeti, pāde pādaṃ accādhāya, sato sampajāno, uṭṭhānasaññaṃ manasi karitvā, rattiyā pacchimaṃ yāmaṃ paccuṭṭhāya caṅkamena nisajjāya āvaraṇīyehi dhammehi cittaṃ parisodheti. Evaṃ kho, mahānāma, ariyasāvako jāgariyaṃ anuyutto hoti.
mula_english:
24. “And how, Mahānāma, is a noble disciple possessed of virtue (śīlasampanno)? Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple is virtuous (śīlavā), dwells restrained with the restraint of the Pāṭimokkha (pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto), is perfect in conduct and resort (ācāragocarasampanno), and seeing fear in the slightest fault, trains by undertaking the training precepts (sikkhāpadesu). This is how, Mahānāma, a noble disciple is possessed of virtue (śīlasampanno).

“And how, Mahānāma, does a noble disciple guard the doors of his senses (indriyesu guttadvāro)? Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple, on seeing a form (rūpaṃ) with the eye (cakkhunā), does not grasp at its signs (na nimittaggāhī) and features (nānubyañjanaggāhī). Since, if he were to dwell without restraint over the faculty of the eye (cakkhundriyaṃ), evil unwholesome states such as covetousness (abhijjhā) and grief (domanassā) might assail him, he practises restraint (saṃvarāya paṭipajjati), guards the faculty of the eye (cakkhundriyaṃ), and achieves restraint over the faculty of the eye (cakkhundriye saṃvaraṃ āpajjati). On hearing a sound (saddaṃ) with the ear (sotena)…On smelling an odour (gandhaṃ) with the nose (ghānena)…On tasting a flavour (rasaṃ) with the tongue (jivhāya)…On touching a tangible object (phoṭṭhabbaṃ) with the body (kāyena)…On cognizing a mind-object (dhammaṃ) with the mind (manasā), he does not grasp at its major signs (nimittaggāhī) or secondary characteristics (nānubyañjanaggāhī). Since, if he were to dwell without restraint over the faculty of the intellect (manindriyaṃ), unskillful qualities such as greed (abhijjhā) or distress (domanassā) might assail him. He practices with restraint (saṃvarāya paṭipajjati). He guards the faculty of the intellect (manindriyaṃ). He achieves restraint with regard to the faculty of the intellect (manindriye saṃvaraṃ āpajjati). This is how, Mahānāma, a noble disciple guards the doors of his sense faculties (indriyesu guttadvāro).

“And how, Mahānāma, is a noble disciple moderate in eating (bhojane mattaññū)? Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple, reflecting wisely (paṭisaṅkhā yoniso), partakes of food (āhāraṃ āhāreti) neither for amusement (neva davāya) nor for intoxication (na madāya) nor for the sake of physical beauty (na maṇḍanāya) and attractiveness (na vibhūsanāya), but only for the endurance (ṭhitiyā) and continuance (yāpanāya) of this body (kāyassa), for ending discomfort (vihiṃsūparatiyā), and for assisting the holy life (brahmacariyānuggahāya), considering: ‘Thus I shall terminate old feelings (purāṇañca vedanaṃ paṭihaṅkhāmi) without arousing new feelings (navañca vedanaṃ na uppādessāmi) and I shall be healthy (yātrā ca me bhavissati) and blameless (anavajjatā ca) and shall live in comfort (phāsuvihāro ca).’ This is how, Mahānāma, a noble disciple is moderate in eating (bhojane mattaññū).

“And how, Mahānāma, is a noble disciple devoted to wakefulness (jāgariyaṃ anuyutto)? Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple during the day (divasaṃ) purifies his mind (cittaṃ parisodheti) of obstructive states (āvaraṇīyehi dhammehi) while walking back and forth (caṅkamena) and sitting (nisajjāya). In the first watch (paṭhamaṃ yāmaṃ) of the night (rattiyā), he purifies his mind (cittaṃ parisodheti) of obstructive states (āvaraṇīyehi dhammehi) while walking back and forth (caṅkamena) and sitting (nisajjāya). In the middle watch (majjhimaṃ yāmaṃ) of the night (rattiyā) he assumes the lion’s pose (sīhaseyyaṃ kappeti) on his right side (dakkhiṇena passena), placing one foot (pāde) over the other (pādaṃ accādhāya), mindful (sato) and fully aware (sampajāno), after noting in his mind (manasi karitvā) the time for rising (uṭṭhānasaññaṃ). In the last watch (pacchimaṃ yāmaṃ) of the night (rattiyā), after rising (paccuṭṭhāya), he purifies his mind (cittaṃ parisodheti) of obstructive states (āvaraṇīyehi dhammehi) while walking back and forth (caṅkamena) and sitting (nisajjāya). This is how, Mahānāma, a noble disciple is devoted to wakefulness (jāgariyaṃ anuyutto).
commentary_pali: 24.Kathañca mahānāmāti iminā ettakena ṭhānena sekhapaṭipadāya mātikaṃ ṭhapetvā paṭipāṭiyā vitthāretukāmo evamāha. Tattha sīlasampannotiādīni ‘‘sampannasīlā, bhikkhave, viharathā’’ti ākaṅkheyyasuttādīsu vuttanayeneva veditabbāni.
commentary_english:
How then does the name *mahānāma* arise? Having established the framework (mātikaṃ) for the path of the *śaikṣa* (one under training) in such a manner and to such an extent, he desires to elaborate it step by step and thus he speaks.

There, the terms beginning with *śīlasampanno* (endowed with virtue) are to be understood in the same way as explained in the *Ākaṅkheyyasutta* and other sūtras, [where it is said:] “Endowed with virtue, monks, abide.”

mula_pali: 25. ‘‘Kathañca, mahānāma, ariyasāvako sattahi saddhammehi samannāgato hoti? Idha, mahānāma, ariyasāvako saddho hoti, saddahati tathāgatassa bodhiṃ – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. Hirimā hoti, hirīyati kāyaduccaritena vacīduccaritena manoduccaritena, hirīyati pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samāpattiyā. Ottappī hoti, ottappati kāyaduccaritena vacīduccaritena manoduccaritena, ottappati pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samāpattiyā. Bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo. Ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthā sabyañjanā kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā bahū sutā (?) honti dhātā dhatā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā. Āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu. Satimā hoti, paramena satinepakkena samannāgato, cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā anussaritā. Paññavā hoti, udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato, ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā. Evaṃ kho, mahānāma, ariyasāvako sattahi saddhammehi samannāgato hoti.
mula_english:
"And how, Mahānāma, does a noble disciple possess seven good qualities? Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple has faith (saddho hoti), he has faith in the Tathāgata’s awakening (bodhiṃ) – ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is an *arahaṃ*, a *sammāsambuddho* (perfectly enlightened one), perfect in knowledge and conduct (*vijjācaraṇasampanno*), the Well-Farer (*sugato*), Knower of the worlds (*lokavidū*), unsurpassed trainer of those who can be trained (*anuttaro purisadammasārathi*), teacher of gods and humans (*satthā devamanussānaṃ*), the Awakened One (*buddho*), the Blessed One (*bhagavā*)’.

He has shame (hirimā hoti); he is ashamed of misconduct in body (*kāyaduccaritena*), speech (*vacīduccaritena*), and mind (*manoduccaritena*); ashamed of engaging in evil unwholesome deeds.

He has fear of wrongdoing (ottappī hoti); he is afraid of misconduct in body (*kāyaduccaritena*), speech (*vacīduccaritena*), and mind (*manoduccaritena*); afraid of engaging in evil unwholesome deeds.

He has learned much (*bahussuto hoti*), remembers what he has learned (*sutadharo*), and consolidates what he has learned (*sutasannicayo*).

Those teachings which are good in the beginning (*ādikalyāṇā*), good in the middle (*majjhekalyāṇā*), and good in the end (*pariyosānakalyāṇā*), with the right meaning (*sātthā*) and phrasing (*sabyañjanā*), and which affirm a holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) that is utterly perfect and pure (*kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ*), such teachings he has learned much of (*bahussutā honti*), remembered (*dhātā*), mastered verbally (*vacasā paricitā*), investigated with the mind (*manasānupekkhitā*), and penetrated well by view (*diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā*).

He dwells with aroused energy (*āraddhavīriyo viharati*) for abandoning unwholesome qualities (*akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya*) and undertaking wholesome qualities (*kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadāya*); he is strong (*thāmavā*), firm in exertion (*daḷhaparakkamo*), not shirking his duties (*anikkhittadhuro*) with regard to wholesome qualities (*kusalesu dhammesu*).

He has mindfulness (*satimā hoti*); he possesses the highest mindfulness and skill (*paramena satinepakkena samannāgato*); he recalls and recollects what was done long ago and spoken long ago (*cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā anussaritā*).

He is wise (*paññavā hoti*); he possesses wisdom regarding rise and disappearance (*udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato*) that is noble (*ariyāya*) and penetrative (*nibbedhikāya*) and leads to the complete destruction of suffering (*sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā*).

That is how, Mahānāma, a noble disciple possesses seven good qualities."
commentary_pali:
25.Kāyaduccaritenātiādīsu upayogatthe karaṇavacanaṃ, hiriyitabbāni kāyaduccaritādīni hiriyati jigucchatīti attho. Ottappaniddese hetvatthe karaṇavacanaṃ, kāyaduccaritādīhi ottappassa hetubhūtehi ottappati bhāyatīti attho. Āraddhavīriyoti paggahitavīriyo anosakkitamānaso. Pahānāyāti pahānatthāya. Upasampadāyāti paṭilābhatthāya. Thāmavāti vīriyathāmena samannāgato. Daḷhaparakkamoti thiraparakkamo. Anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesūti kusalesu dhammesu anoropitadhuro anosakkitavīriyo. Paramenāti uttamena. Satinepakkenāti satiyā ca nipakabhāvena ca. Kasmā pana satibhājaniye paññā āgatāti? Satiyā balavabhāvadīpanatthaṃ. Paññāvippayuttā hi sati dubbalā hoti, sampayuttā balavatīti.

Cirakatampīti attanā vā parena vā kāyena cirakataṃ cetiyaṅgaṇavattādi asīti mahāvattapaṭipattipūraṇaṃ. Cirabhāsitampīti attanā vā parena vā vācāya cirabhāsitaṃ sakkaccaṃ uddisana-uddisāpana-dhammosāraṇa-dhammadesanā-upanisinnakathā-anumodaniyādivasena pavattitaṃ vacīkammaṃ. Saritā anussaritāti tasmiṃ kāyena cirakate ‘‘kāyo nāma kāyaviññatti, cirabhāsite vācā nāma vacīviññatti. Tadubhayampi rūpaṃ, taṃsamuṭṭhāpikā cittacetasikā arūpaṃ. Iti ime rūpārūpadhammā evaṃ uppajjitvā evaṃ niruddhā’’ti sarati ceva anussarati ca, satisambojjhaṅgaṃ samuṭṭhāpetīti attho. Bojjhaṅgasamuṭṭhāpikā hi sati idha adhippetā. Tāya satiyā esa sakimpi saraṇena saritā, punappunaṃ saraṇena anussaritāti veditabbā.

Cirakatampī Cirabhāsitampī Saritā anussaritā

Udayatthagāminiyāti pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ udayavayagāminiyā udayañca vayañca paṭivijjhituṃ samatthāya. Ariyāyāti vikkhambhanavasena ca samucchedavasena ca kilesehi ārakā ṭhitāya parisuddhāya. Paññāya samannāgatoti vipassanāpaññāya ceva maggapaññāya ca samaṅgībhūto. Nibbedhikāyāti sāyeva nibbijjhanato nibbedhikāti vuccati, tāya samannāgatoti attho. Tattha maggapaññāya samucchedavasena anibbiddhapubbaṃ apadālitapubbaṃ lobhakkhandhaṃ dosakkhandhaṃ mohakkhandhaṃ nibbijjhati padāletīti nibbedhikā. Vipassanāpaññāya tadaṅgavasena nibbedhikāya maggapaññāya paṭilābhasaṃvattanato cāti vipassanā ‘‘nibbedhikā’’ti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyāti idhāpi maggapaññā ‘‘sammā hetunā nayena vaṭṭadukkhaṃ khepayamānā gacchatīti sammā dukkhakkhayagāminī nāma. Vipassanā tadaṅgavasena vaṭṭadukkhañca kilesadukkhañca khepayamānā gacchatīti dukkhakkhayagāminī. Dukkhakkhayagāminiyā vā maggapaññāya paṭilābhasaṃvattanato esā dukkhakkhayagāminī’’ti veditabbā.

Udayatthagāminiyā Ariyāyā Paññāya samannāgato Nibbedhikāyā Sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā
commentary_english:
25. In *kāyaduccaritenā*tiādīsu, the instrumental case is used in the sense of application, meaning that the immoralities of body etc. are those to be ashamed of, that one shrinks from, feels disgust for.

In the analysis of *ottappa*, the instrumental case is used in the sense of the cause, meaning that through the immoralities of the body etc., which are the cause of *ottappa*, one fears.

*āraddhavīriyo*ti: one who has aroused energy, whose mind does not waver.

*pahānāyā*ti: for the sake of abandoning.

*upasampadāyā*ti: for the sake of attainment.

*thāmavā*ti: endowed with the strength of energy.

*daḷhaparakkamo*ti: one of firm exertion.

*anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesū*ti: one who has not laid down the burden in wholesome things, whose energy does not waver.

*paramenā*ti: with the highest.

*satinepakkenā*ti: with mindfulness and skill.

But why has wisdom (*paññā*) come into the receptacle of mindfulness? To illuminate the powerful state of mindfulness. Mindfulness disconnected from wisdom is weak, connected it is strong.

*cirakatampī*ti: a long-standing practice of the duties relating to a *cetiya*, such as the courtyard etc., done by oneself or another, fulfilling the eighty great duties.

*cirabhāsitampī*ti: a long-standing act of speech done by oneself or another, respectfully reciting, causing to recite, reciting the Dhamma, teaching the Dhamma, stories for those who are seated nearby, things to be rejoiced over, etc.

*saritā anussaritā*ti: in that long-standing practice done by the body, "[This] body is merely a physical expression, in that long-standing speech, speech is merely a verbal expression. Both of these are form, and the mind and mental factors that arise from them are formless. Thus these phenomena of form and formlessness arise and cease in this way," he both remembers and recollects, he arouses the awakening factor of mindfulness. Here, mindfulness that arouses the awakening factors is intended. Through that mindfulness, it should be understood that he has once remembered through remembering, and repeatedly recollected through recollection.

*cirakatampī* *cirabhāsitampī* *saritā anussaritā*

*udayatthagāminiyā*ti: going to the arising and passing away of the five aggregates, capable of penetrating both arising and passing away.

*ariyāyā*ti: standing far from defilements, pure, by way of dispelling and by way of cutting off.

*paññāya samannāgato*ti: united with both insight wisdom (*vipassanāpaññā*) and path wisdom (*maggapaññā*).

*nibbedhikāyā*ti: that same [wisdom] is called *nibbedhikā* because of penetrating, the meaning is endowed with that. There, path wisdom penetrates and cuts off the aggregate of greed, the aggregate of hatred, the aggregate of delusion, which have never been penetrated or cut off before, by way of cutting off. Insight wisdom, by way of being a part of penetrating path wisdom and by way of leading to the attainment of path wisdom, it is fitting to say that insight is "penetrating."

*sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā*ti: here also path wisdom is called "rightly going to the destruction of suffering" because it goes rightly destroying the round of suffering by way of the cause and the method. Insight, by way of being a part of that, goes destroying the round of suffering and the suffering of defilements, thus [it is] going to the destruction of suffering. Or, this [wisdom] should be understood to be going to the destruction of suffering by way of leading to the attainment of path wisdom which goes to the destruction of suffering.

*udayatthagāminiyā* *ariyāyā* *paññāya samannāgato* *nibbedhikāyā* *sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā*

mula_pali: 26. ‘‘Kathañca , mahānāma, ariyasāvako catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī? Idha, mahānāma, ariyasāvako vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi, savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Evaṃ kho, mahānāma, ariyasāvako catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī.
mula_english:
26. How, Mahānāma, is a noble disciple one who obtains at will, without trouble or difficulty, the four *jhānas* (*jhānānam*) that constitute the higher mind (*ābhicetasikānam*) and provide a pleasant abiding here and now (*diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānam*)? Here, Mahānāma, quite secluded from sensual pleasures (*kāmehi*), secluded from unwholesome states (*akusalehi dhammehi*), a noble disciple enters upon (*upasampajja*) and abides in (*viharati*) the first *jhāna* (*paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ*), which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought (*savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ*), with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion (*vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ*); With the stilling (*vūpasamā*) of applied and sustained thought (*vitakkavicārānaṃ*), internal assurance (*ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ*)… he enters upon and abides in the second *jhāna* (*dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati*); With the fading away as well of rapture (*pītiyā ca virāgā*)… he enters upon and abides in the third *jhāna* (*tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati*); With the abandoning (*pahānā*) of pleasure (*sukha*) and the abandoning of pain (*dukkhassa ca pahānā*), as well as with the previous disappearance of joy and sorrow (*pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā*)… he enters upon and abides in the fourth *jhāna* (*catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati*).

That is how, Mahānāma, a noble disciple is one who obtains at will, without trouble or difficulty, the four *jhānas* (*jhānānam*) that constitute the higher mind (*ābhicetasikānam*) and provide a pleasant abiding here and now (*diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānam*).
commentary_pali: 26.Abhicetasikānanti abhicittaṃ seṭṭhacittaṃ sitānaṃ nissitānaṃ. Diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānanti appitappitakkhaṇe sukhapaṭilābhahetūnaṃ. Nikāmalābhīti icchiticchitakkhaṇe samāpajjitā. Akicchalābhīti nidukkhalābhī. Akasiralābhīti vipulalābhī. Paguṇabhāvena eko icchiticchitakkhaṇe samāpajjituṃ sakkoti, samādhipāripanthikadhamme pana akilamanto vikkhambhetuṃ na sakkoti, so attano anicchāya khippameva vuṭṭhāti, yathāparicchedavasena samāpattiṃ ṭhapetuṃ na sakkoti ayaṃ kicchalābhī kasiralābhī nāma. Eko icchiticchitakkhaṇe ca samāpajjituṃ sakkoti, samādhipāripanthikadhamme ca akilamanto vikkhambheti, so yathāparicchedavaseneva vuṭṭhātuṃ sakkoti, ayaṃ akicchalābhī akasiralābhī nāma.
commentary_english:
26. *abhicetasikāna* means with a superior mind, the best mind, sharpened, relied upon.

*diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārāna* means having as their cause the attainment of happiness in the moment of application.

*nikāmalābhī* means attained at the moment of wishing.

*akicchalābhī* means attained without difficulty, attained without suffering.

*akasiralābhī* means attained abundantly.

Through the power of virtue, one is able to attain at the moment of wishing, but if without striving, one is not able to resist the opposing forces to *samādhi* (concentration), one quickly departs against one's will, one is not able to maintain the attainment according to the measure; this is called attaining with difficulty, attaining with trouble.

One is able to attain at the moment of wishing, and striving, one resists the opposing forces to *samādhi* (concentration), one is able to depart only according to the measure; this is called attaining without difficulty, attaining without trouble.

mula_pali: 27. ‘‘Yato kho, mahānāma, ariyasāvako evaṃ sīlasampanno hoti, evaṃ indriyesu guttadvāro hoti, evaṃ bhojane mattaññū hoti, evaṃ jāgariyaṃ anuyutto hoti, evaṃ sattahi saddhammehi samannāgato hoti, evaṃ catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī, ayaṃ vuccati, mahānāma, ariyasāvako sekho pāṭipado apuccaṇḍatāya samāpanno, bhabbo abhinibbhidāya, bhabbo sambodhāya, bhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya. Seyyathāpi, mahānāma, kukkuṭiyā aṇḍāni aṭṭha vā dasa vā dvādasa vā tānāssu kukkuṭiyā sammā adhisayitāni sammā pariseditāni sammā paribhāvitāni, kiñcāpi tassā kukkuṭiyā na evaṃ icchā uppajjeyya – ‘aho vatime kukkuṭapotakā pādanakhasikhāya vā mukhatuṇḍakena vā aṇḍakosaṃ padāletvā sotthinā abhinibbhijjeyyu’nti, atha kho bhabbāva te kukkuṭapotakā pādanakhasikhāya vā mukhatuṇḍakena vā aṇḍakosaṃ padāletvā sotthinā abhinibbhijjituṃ. Evameva kho, mahānāma, yato ariyasāvako evaṃ sīlasampanno hoti, evaṃ indriyesu guttadvāro hoti, evaṃ bhojane mattaññū hoti, evaṃ jāgariyaṃ anuyutto hoti, evaṃ sattahi saddhammehi samannāgato hoti, evaṃ catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī, ayaṃ vuccati, mahānāma, ariyasāvako sekho pāṭipado apuccaṇḍatāya samāpanno , bhabbo abhinibbhidāya, bhabbo sambodhāya, bhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya.
mula_english:
27. “So too, Mahānāma, when a noble disciple (ariyasāvako) is virtuous (sīlasampanno), guards the doors of his senses (indriyesu guttadvāro), is moderate in eating (bhojane mattaññū), is devoted to wakefulness (jāgariyaṃ anuyutto), possesses seven good qualities (sattahi saddhammehi samannāgato), obtains at will, without trouble or difficulty, the four *jhānas* (jhānānaṃ), that constitute the higher mind (ābhicetasikānaṃ) and provide a pleasant abiding here and now (diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī akicchalābhī akasiralābhī), he is called one in higher training (sekho) who has entered upon the way (pāṭipado). His eggs are unspoiled (apuccaṇḍatāya samāpanno); he is capable of breaking out (bhabbo abhinibbhidāya), capable of enlightenment (bhabbo sambodhāya), capable of attaining the supreme security from bondage (anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya).

“Suppose, Mahānāma, there were a hen with eight or ten or twelve eggs (aṇḍāni), which she had covered (adhisayitāni), incubated (pariseditāni), and nurtured properly (paribhāvitāni). Even though she did not wish: ‘Oh, that my chicks (kukkuṭapotakā) might pierce their shells (aṇḍakosaṃ) with the points of their claws (pādanakhasikhāya) and beaks (mukhatuṇḍakena) and hatch out safely (sotthinā abhinibbhijjeyyu)!’ yet the chicks (kukkuṭapotakā) are capable of piercing their shells (aṇḍakosaṃ) with the points of their claws (pādanakhasikhāya) and beaks (mukhatuṇḍakena) and hatching out safely (sotthinā abhinibbhijjituṃ).

“So too, Mahānāma, when a noble disciple (ariyasāvako) is virtuous (sīlasampanno), guards the doors of his senses (indriyesu guttadvāro), is moderate in eating (bhojane mattaññū), is devoted to wakefulness (jāgariyaṃ anuyutto), possesses seven good qualities (sattahi saddhammehi samannāgato), obtains at will, without trouble or difficulty, the four *jhānas* (jhānānaṃ), that constitute the higher mind (ābhicetasikānaṃ) and provide a pleasant abiding here and now (diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī akicchalābhī akasiralābhī), he is called one in higher training (sekho) who has entered upon the way (pāṭipado). His eggs are unspoiled (apuccaṇḍatāya samāpanno); he is capable of breaking out (bhabbo abhinibbhidāya), capable of enlightenment (bhabbo sambodhāya), capable of attaining the supreme security from bondage (anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya).
commentary_pali: 27.Ayaṃvuccati mahānāma ariyasāvako sekho pāṭipadoti mahānāma ariyasāvako sekho pāṭipado vipassanāgabbhāya vaḍḍhamānakapaṭipadāya samannāgatoti vuccatīti dasseti. Apuccaṇḍatāyāti apūtiaṇḍatāya. Bhabbo abhinibbhidāyāti vipassanādiñāṇappabhedāya bhabbo. Sambodhāyāti ariyamaggāya. Anuttarassa yogakkhemassāti arahattaṃ anuttaro yogakkhemo nāma, tadabhigamāya bhabboti dasseti. Yā panāyamettha atthadīpanatthaṃ upamā āhaṭā, sā cetokhilasutte vuttanayeneva veditabbā. Kevalañhi tattha ‘‘tassā kukkuṭiyā aṇḍesu tividhakiriyakaraṇaṃ viya hi imassa bhikkhuno ussoḷhipannarasehi aṅgehi samannāgatabhāvo’’ti yaṃ evaṃ opammasaṃsandanaṃ āgataṃ, taṃ idha evaṃ sīlasampanno hotītiādivacanato ‘‘tassā kukkuṭiyā aṇḍesu tividhakiriyakaraṇaṃ viya imassa bhikkhuno sīlasampannatādīhi pannarasehi dhammehi samaṅgibhāvo’’ti. Evaṃ yojetvā veditabbaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbattha vuttasadisameva.
commentary_english:
27. *Ayaṃ vuccati mahānāma ariyasāvako sekho pāṭipado* means it shows that the noble disciple Mahānāma, a learner on the path, is endowed with the practice that increases insight.

*Apuccaṇḍatāyā* means *apūti-aṇḍatāya*.

*Bhabbo abhinibbhidāya* means capable of the distinction of insight-knowledge and so forth.

*Sambodhāya* means for the noble path (ariyamaggāya).

*Anuttarassa yogakkhemassā* means Arahantship is called unsurpassed rest from the yoke; it shows [him] capable of attaining that.

Now, the simile that has been brought here to reveal the meaning should be understood just in the way it was stated in the Cetokila Sutta.

For there, only the comparison that came, "Just as the hen performs a threefold action with respect to the eggs, so this bhikkhu is possessed of the fifteen limbs of zeal," from the statement here beginning "He is accomplished in morality," [should be understood] as "Just as the hen performs a threefold action with respect to the eggs, so this bhikkhu is endowed with the fifteen qualities beginning with accomplishment in morality."

It should be understood having construed it thus.

The remainder is just as stated everywhere.

mula_pali:
28. ‘‘Sa kho so, mahānāma, ariyasāvako imaṃyeva anuttaraṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ āgamma anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, ayamassa paṭhamābhinibbhidā hoti kukkuṭacchāpakasseva aṇḍakosamhā.

‘‘Sa kho so, mahānāma, ariyasāvako imaṃye anuttaraṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ āgamma dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate…pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti, ayamassa dutiyābhinibbhidā hoti kukkuṭacchāpakasseva aṇḍakosamhā.

‘‘Sa kho so, mahānāma, ariyasāvako imaṃyeva anuttaraṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ āgamma āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati, ayamassa tatiyābhinibbhidā hoti kukkuṭacchāpakasseva aṇḍakosamhā.
mula_english:
“Again, Mahānāma, having arrived at that same supreme mindfulness whose purity is due to equanimity, a noble disciple recollects his manifold past lives, that is, one birth, two births… Thus with their aspects and particulars he recollects his manifold past lives. This is his first breaking out like that of the hen’s chicks from their shells.

“Again, Mahānāma, having arrived at that same supreme mindfulness whose purity is due to equanimity, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, this noble disciple sees beings passing away and reappearing… he understands how beings pass on according to their actions. This is his second breaking out like that of the hen’s chicks from their shells.

“Again, Mahānāma, having arrived at that same supreme mindfulness whose purity is due to equanimity, by realizing for himself with direct knowledge, this noble disciple here and now enters upon and abides in the deliverance of mind (*ceto-vimutti*) and deliverance by wisdom (*paññā-vimutti*) that are taintless with the destruction of the taints (āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ). This is his third breaking out like that of the hen’s chicks from their shells.
commentary_pali: 28.Imaṃyeva anuttaraṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhinti imaṃ paṭhamādijjhānehi asadisaṃ uttamaṃ catutthajjhānikaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ. Paṭhamābhinibbhidāti paṭhamo ñāṇabhedo. Dutiyādīsupi eseva nayo. Kukkuṭacchāpako pana ekavāraṃ mātukucchito ekavāraṃ aṇḍakosatoti dve vāre jāyati. Ariyasāvako tīhi vijjāhi tāyo vāre jāyati. Pubbenivāsacchādakaṃ tamaṃ vinodetvā pubbenivāsañāṇena paṭhamaṃ jāyati, sattānaṃ cutipaṭisandhicchādakaṃ tamaṃ vinodetvā dibbacakkhuñāṇena dutiyaṃ jāyati, catusaccapaṭicchādakaṃ tamaṃ vinodetvā āsavakkhayañāṇena tatiyaṃ jāyati.
commentary_english:
"*"imaṃyeva anuttaraṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhi*"" means this unequalled, supreme purity of mindfulness and equanimity of the fourth *dhyāna*, unlike the first *dhyānas*, etc.

"*"paṭhamābhinibbhidā*"" means the first breakthrough of knowledge.

And the same rule applies in the case of the second etc.

A chick, however, is born twice, once from its mother's womb, and once from the eggshell.

A noble disciple is born three times through the three kinds of knowledge.

Having dispelled the darkness that obscures previous existences, he is born the first time through the knowledge of previous existences; having dispelled the darkness that obscures the decease and rebirth of beings, he is born the second time through the divine eye knowledge; having dispelled the darkness that obscures the four noble truths, he is born the third time through the knowledge of the destruction of the *āsavas*.

mula_pali:
29. ‘‘Yampi yampi kho (ka.), mahānāma, ariyasāvako sīlasampanno hoti, idampissa hoti caraṇasmiṃ; yampi, mahānāma, ariyasāvako indriyesu guttadvāro hoti, idampissa hoti caraṇasmiṃ; yampi, mahānāma, ariyasāvako bhojane mattaññū hoti, idampissa hoti caraṇasmiṃ; yampi, mahānāma, ariyasāvako jāgariyaṃ anuyutto hoti, idampissa hoti caraṇasmiṃ; yampi, mahānāma, ariyasāvako sattahi saddhammehi samannāgato hoti, idampissa hoti caraṇasmiṃ; yampi, mahānāma, ariyasāvako catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī, idampissa hoti caraṇasmiṃ.

‘‘Yañca kho, mahānāma, ariyasāvako anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, idampissa hoti vijjāya; yampi, mahānāma, ariyasāvako dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate…pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti, idampissa hoti vijjāya. Yampi, mahānāma, ariyasāvako āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati, idampissa hoti vijjāya.

‘‘Ayaṃ vuccati, mahānāma, ariyasāvako vijjāsampanno itipi caraṇasampanno itipi vijjācaraṇasampanno itipi.
mula_english:
29. “When, Mahānāma, a noble disciple is possessed of virtue ( *śīlasampanna*), that too is part of his conduct (*caraṇa*); when, Mahānāma, a noble disciple guards the doors of his senses ( *indriyesu guttadvāro*), that too is part of his conduct; when, Mahānāma, a noble disciple is moderate in eating ( *bhojane mattaññū*), that too is part of his conduct; when, Mahānāma, a noble disciple is devoted to wakefulness ( *jāgariyaṃ anuyutto*), that too is part of his conduct; when, Mahānāma, a noble disciple possesses seven good qualities (*sattahi saddhammehi samannāgato*), that too is part of his conduct; when, Mahānāma, a noble disciple obtains at will, without trouble or difficulty, the four *jhānas* ( *catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ*) that constitute the higher mind and provide a pleasant abiding here and now (*diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī*), that too is part of his conduct.

“And when, Mahānāma, a noble disciple recollects his manifold past lives ( *anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati*)… with their aspects and particulars, that too is part of his true knowledge (*vidyā*); when, Mahānāma, with the divine eye (*dibbena cakkhunā*)… he sees beings passing away and reappearing, and understands how beings pass on according to their actions (*yathākammūpage satte pajānāti*), that too is part of his true knowledge. When, Mahānāma, by realizing for himself with direct knowledge, he here and now enters upon and abides in the deliverance of mind (*cetovimutti*) and deliverance by wisdom (*paññāvimutti*) that are taintless with the destruction of the taints (*āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ*), that too is part of his true knowledge (*vidyā*).

“This, Mahānāma, is said to be a noble disciple who is perfect in true knowledge (*vijjāsampanno*), perfect in conduct (*caraṇasampanno*), and perfect in true knowledge and conduct (*vijjācaraṇasampanno*).
commentary_pali:
29.Idampissa hoti caraṇasminti idampi sīlaṃ assa bhikkhuno caraṇaṃ nāma hotīti attho. Caraṇaṃ nāma bahu anekavidhaṃ, sīlādayo pannarasadhammā, tattha idampi ekaṃ caraṇanti attho. Padattho pana carati tena agatapubbaṃ disaṃ gacchatīti caraṇaṃ. Esa nayo sabbattha.

Idampissa hoti vijjāyāti idaṃ pubbenivāsañāṇaṃ tassa vijjā nāma hotīti attho. Vijjā nāma bahu anekavidhā, vipassanañāṇādīni aṭṭha ñāṇāni, tattha idampi ñāṇaṃ ekā vijjātipi attho. Padattho pana vinivijjhitvā etāya jānātīti vijjā. Esa nayo sabbattha. Vijjāsampanno itipīti tīhi vijjāhi vijjāsampanno itipi. Caraṇasampanno itipīti pañcadasahi dhammehi caraṇasampanno itipi. Tadubhayena pana vijjācaraṇasampanno itipīti.

Idampissa hoti vijjāyā vijjā Vijjāsampanno itipī Caraṇasampanno itipī
commentary_english:
29. “*Idampissa hoti caraṇasmi*” means: this is the *sīla* whose conduct is named for that monk.
"*Caraṇaṃ*" means much and various. *Sīla*, etc., are the fifteen qualities; and this, there, is one aspect of conduct.
Furthermore, *padattho* means: one conducts oneself, and by that one goes to a place never gone before; that is *caraṇaṃ*.
This method [applies] everywhere.

“*Idampissa hoti vijjāyā*” means: this is the knowledge of previous existences; *vijjā* is its name.
*Vijjā* means much and various. *Vipassanāñāṇa*, etc., are the eight *ñāṇas*; this *ñāṇa* is also one aspect of *vidyā*.
Furthermore, *padattho* means: having pierced through, one knows by this; that is *vijjā*.
This method [applies] everywhere.
"*Vijjāsampanno itipī*" means: one is endowed with *vidyā* by these three *vidyās*.
"*Caraṇasampanno itipī*" means: one is endowed with conduct by these fifteen qualities (*dhammas*).
Therefore, by both, one is endowed with both *vidyā* and *caraṇa*.

"*Idampissa hoti vijjāyā, vijjā, vijjāsampanno itipī, caraṇasampanno itipī*."

mula_pali:
30. ‘‘Brahmunāpesā, mahānāma, sanaṅkumārena gāthā bhāsitā –

‘Khattiyo seṭṭho janetasmiṃ, ye gottapaṭisārino;

Vijjācaraṇasampanno, so seṭṭho devamānuse’ti.

‘‘Sā kho panesā, mahānāma, brahmunā sanaṅkumārena gāthā sugītā no duggītā, subhāsitā no dubbhāsitā, atthasaṃhitā no anatthasaṃhitā, anumatā bhagavatā’’ti.

Atha kho bhagavā uṭṭhahitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘sādhu sādhu, ānanda, sādhu kho tvaṃ, ānanda, kāpilavatthavānaṃ sakyānaṃ sekhaṃ pāṭipadaṃ abhāsī’’ti.

Idamavocāyasmā ānando. Samanuñño satthā ahosi. Attamanā kāpilavatthavā sakyā āyasmato ānandassa bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Sekhasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.
mula_english:
30. “Mahānāma, this verse was spoken by the Brahmā Sanankumāra:

‘The kṣatriya is the best among people who value lineage;
But he who is accomplished in knowledge and conduct is the best among gods and humans.’

“Now that stanza was well sung by the Brahmā Sanankumāra, not ill-sung; it was well spoken, not ill-spoken; it has a meaning, and is not meaningless; and it was approved by the Blessed One.”

Then the Blessed One rose and addressed the venerable Ānanda thus: “Good, good, Ānanda! It is good that you have spoken to the Śākyans of Kapilavatthu about the disciple in higher training who has entered upon the way.”

This is what the venerable Ānanda said. The Teacher approved of it, and the Śākyans of Kapilavatthu were satisfied and delighted in the venerable Ānanda’s words.

The Third Sekhasutta is finished.
commentary_pali:
30.Sanaṅkumārenāti porāṇakakumārena, cirakālato paṭṭhāya kumāroti paññātena. So kira manussapathe pañcacūḷakakumārakakāle jhānaṃ nibbattetvā aparihīnajjhāno brahmaloke nibbatti, tassa so attabhāvo piyo ahosi manāpo, tasmā tādiseneva attabhāvena carati, tena naṃ sanaṅkumāroti sañjānanti. Janetasminti janitasmiṃ, pajāyāti attho. Ye gottapaṭisārinoti ye janetasmiṃ gottaṃ paṭisaranti ‘‘ahaṃ gotamo, ahaṃ kassapo’’ti, tesu loke gottapaṭisārīsu khattiyo seṭṭho. Anumatā bhagavatāti mama pañhabyākaraṇena saddhiṃ saṃsanditvā desitāti ambaṭṭhasutte buddhena bhagavatā ‘‘ahampi, ambaṭṭha, evaṃ vadāmi –

‘Khattiyo seṭṭho janetasmiṃ, ye gottapaṭisārino;

Vijjācaraṇasampanno, so seṭṭho devamānuse’ti’’. (dī. ni. 1.277) –

Evaṃ bhāsantena anuññātā anumoditā. Sādhu sādhu ānandāti, bhagavā kira ādito paṭṭhāya niddaṃ anokkamantova imaṃ suttaṃ sutvā ānandena sekhapaṭipadāya kūṭaṃ gahitanti ñatvā uṭṭhāya pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā nisinno sādhukāraṃ adāsi. Ettāvatā ca pana idaṃ suttaṃ jinabhāsitaṃ nāma jātaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Sādhu sādhu ānandā

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Sekhasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
30. “*Sanaṅkumārenā*” means by the ancient youth (*porāṇakakumāra*), he is known as a youth since a long time (*cirakālato paṭṭhāya kumāroti paññātena*). It is said that he, having developed *jhāna* in the human realm (*manussapathe*) at the time of being a five-crested youth (*pañcacūḷakakumārakakāle jhānaṃ nibbattetvā*), and being of unfaded *jhāna* (*aparihīnajjhāno*), was reborn in the Brahma world (*brahmaloke nibbatti*). That state (*attabhāvo*) was dear and pleasing to him (*piyo ahosi manāpo*), therefore he lives with that same state (*tasmā tādiseneva attabhāvena carati*), therefore they recognize him as "*Sanaṅkumāra*" (*tena naṃ sanaṅkumāroti sañjānanti*).

"*Janetasmi*nti" means in the one who is born (*janitasmiṃ*), it means offspring (*pajāyāti attho*).

"*Ye gottapaṭisārino*ti" means those who, in the one who is born (*ye janetasmiṃ*), recall the lineage (*gottaṃ paṭisaranti*) "I am a Gotama, I am a Kassapa," among those who recall lineage in the world (*tesu loke gottapaṭisārīsu*), a *kṣatriya* is the best (*khattiyo śreṣṭho*).

"*Anumatā bhagavatā*ti" means it was taught having agreed and discussed with my question and answer (*mama pañhabyākaraṇena saddhiṃ saṃsanditvā desitāti*) in the Ambaṭṭha Sutta (*ambaṭṭhasutte*) by the Buddha, the Blessed One (*buddhena bhagavatā*): "I too, Ambaṭṭha, say thus:

'A *kṣatriya* is the best in the one who is born (*khattiyo śreṣṭho janetasmiṃ*), those who recall lineage (*ye gottapaṭisārino*);

Endowed with knowledge and conduct (*vijjācaraṇasampanno*), he is the best among gods and humans (*so śreṣṭho devamānuse'ti*.'"

(Dīgha Nikāya 1.277) - Thus, it was approved and rejoiced over by the one who was speaking (*evaṃ bhāsantena anuññātā anumoditā*).

"*Sādhu sādhu ānandā*ti," it is said that the Blessed One (*bhagavā kira*), from the beginning onwards (*ādito paṭṭhāya*), having heard this Sutta (*imaṃ suttaṃ sutvā*) while not yet emerging from sleep (*niddaṃ anokkamantova*), knowing that Ānanda had grasped the essence in the practice of a trainee (*ānandena sekhapaṭipadāya kūṭaṃ gahitanti ñatvā*), arose, arranged his seat, and sitting down (*uṭṭhāya pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā nisinno*), gave approval (*sādhukāraṃ adāsi*).

By this much, this Sutta became known as the speech of the Victor (*ettāvatā ca pana idaṃ suttaṃ jinabhāsitaṃ nāma jātaṃ*).

The rest is clear throughout (*sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti*).

*Sādhu sādhu ānandā*

The Sekha Sutta Commentary, from the Papañcasūdanī Commentary to the Majjhima Nikāya, is finished (*sekhasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā*).

mula_pali: 31. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā aṅguttarāpesu viharati āpaṇaṃ nāma aṅguttarāpānaṃ nigamo. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya āpaṇaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Āpaṇe piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yenaññataro vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāya. Taṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ ajjhogāhetvā ajjhogahetvā (sī. syā. kaṃ.), ajjhogāhitvā (pī. ka.) aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi. Potaliyopi kho gahapati sampannanivāsanapāvuraṇo pāpuraṇo (sī. syā. kaṃ.) chattupāhanāhi chattupāhano (ka.) jaṅghāvihāraṃ anucaṅkamamāno anuvicaramāno yena so vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ ajjhogāhetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ kho potaliyaṃ gahapatiṃ bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘saṃvijjanti kho, gahapati, āsanāni; sace ākaṅkhasi nisīdā’’ti. Evaṃ vutte, potaliyo gahapati ‘‘gahapativādena maṃ samaṇo gotamo samudācaratī’’ti kupito anattamano tuṇhī ahosi. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā…pe… tatiyampi kho bhagavā potaliyaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘saṃvijjanti kho, gahapati, āsanāni; sace ākaṅkhasi nisīdā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ vutte, potaliyo gahapati gahapativādena maṃ samaṇo gotamo samudācaratī’’ti kupito anattamano bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘tayidaṃ, bho gotama, nacchannaṃ, tayidaṃ nappatirūpaṃ, yaṃ maṃ tvaṃ gahapativādena samudācarasī’’ti. ‘‘Te hi te, gahapati, ākārā, te liṅgā , te nimittā yathā taṃ gahapatissā’’ti. ‘‘Tathā hi pana me, bho gotama, sabbe kammantā paṭikkhittā, sabbe vohārā samucchinnā’’ti. ‘‘Yathā kathaṃ pana te, gahapati, sabbe kammantā paṭikkhittā, sabbe vohārā samucchinnā’’ti? ‘‘Idha me, bho gotama, yaṃ ahosi dhanaṃ vā dhaññaṃ vā rajataṃ vā jātarūpaṃ vā sabbaṃ taṃ puttānaṃ dāyajjaṃ niyyātaṃ, tatthāhaṃ anovādī anupavādī ghāsacchādanaparamo viharāmi. Evaṃ kho me evañca me (syā.), evaṃ me (ka.), bho gotama, sabbe kammantā paṭikkhittā, sabbe vohārā samucchinnā’’ti. ‘‘Aññathā kho tvaṃ, gahapati, vohārasamucchedaṃ vadasi, aññathā ca pana ariyassa vinaye vohārasamucchedo hotī’’ti. ‘‘Yathā kathaṃ pana, bhante, ariyassa vinaye vohārasamucchedo hoti? Sādhu me, bhante , bhagavā tathā dhammaṃ desetu yathā ariyassa vinaye vohārasamucchedo hotī’’ti. ‘‘Tena hi, gahapati, suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho potaliyo gahapati bhagavato paccassosi.
mula_english:
31. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was living in the country of the Aṅguttarāpas at a town of theirs named Āpaṇa, a market town of the Aṅguttarāpas.

Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed, and taking his bowl and robe, went into Āpaṇa for alms.

When he had wandered for alms in Āpaṇa and had returned from his almsround, after his meal he went to a certain grove (*vanasaṇḍa*) for the day’s abiding.

Having entered that grove (*vanasaṇḍa*), he sat down at the foot of a tree for the day's abiding.

Potaliya the householder, while walking and wandering for exercise, wearing full dress with parasol and sandals, also went to the grove (*vanasaṇḍa*), and having entered the grove, he went to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.

After an exchange of friendly greetings & courtesies, he stood to one side.

The Blessed One said to Potaliya the householder as he stood to one side: “There are seats, householder (*gahapati*), sit down if you like.”

When this was said, the householder Potaliya thought: “The recluse Gotama addresses me as ‘householder (*gahapati*)’,” and angry and displeased, he remained silent.

A second time the Blessed One…pe… A third time the Blessed One said to Potaliya the householder: “There are seats, householder (*gahapati*), sit down if you like.”

When this was said, the householder Potaliya thought: “The recluse Gotama addresses me as ‘householder (*gahapati*)’,” and angry and displeased, he said to the Blessed One: “Master Gotama, it is neither fitting nor proper that you address me as ‘householder (*gahapati*)’.”

“Householder (*gahapati*), you have the aspects, marks (*liṅga*), and signs of a householder (*gahapati*).”

“Nevertheless, Master Gotama, I have given up all my works and cut off all my affairs.”

“But how, householder (*gahapati*), have you given up all your works and cut off all your affairs?” “Here, Master Gotama, whatever wealth or grain or silver or gold I had, all that I have bequeathed to my sons, and there I live without admonishing, without reproving, devoted to food and clothing.

That is how I have given up all my works and cut off all my affairs.”

“Householder (*gahapati*), the cutting off of affairs as you describe it is one thing, but in the Noble One’s Discipline the cutting off of affairs is different.”

“But how, venerable sir (*bhante*), does the cutting off of affairs occur in the Noble One’s Discipline? It would be good, venerable sir (*bhante*), if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in such a way that the cutting off of affairs occurs in the Noble One’s Discipline.”

“Then listen, householder (*gahapati*), and attend closely to what I shall say.”

“Yes, venerable sir (*bhante*),” Potaliya the householder replied.
commentary_pali:
31.Evaṃme sutanti potaliyasuttaṃ. Tattha aṅguttarāpesūti aṅgāyeva so janapado, mahiyā panassa uttarena yā āpo, tāsaṃ avidūrattā uttarāpotipi vuccati. Kataramahiyā uttarena yā āpoti, mahāmahiyā. Tatthāyaṃ āvibhāvakathā – ayaṃ kira jambudīpo dasasahassayojanaparimāṇo. Tattha ca catusahassayojanappamāṇo padeso udakena ajjhotthaṭo samuddoti saṅkhaṃ gato . Tisahassayojanappamāṇe manussā vasanti. Tisahassayojanappamāṇe himavā patiṭṭhito ubbedhena pañcayojanasatiko caturāsītikūṭasahassapaṭimaṇḍito samantato sandamānapañcasatanadīvicitto, yattha āyāmavitthārena ceva gambhīratāya ca paṇṇāsapaṇṇāsayojanā diyaḍḍhayojanasataparimaṇḍalā anotattadaho kaṇṇamuṇḍadaho rathakāradaho chaddantadaho kuṇāladaho mandākinīdaho sīhapapātadahoti satta mahāsarā patiṭṭhitā. Tesu anotattadaho sudassanakūṭaṃ citrakūṭaṃ kāḷakūṭaṃ gandhamādanakūṭaṃ kelāsakūṭanti imehi pañcahi pabbatehi parikkhitto.

Tattha sudassanakūṭaṃ sovaṇṇamayaṃ dviyojanasatubbedhaṃ antovaṅkaṃ kākamukhasaṇṭhānaṃ tameva saraṃ paṭicchādetvā ṭhitaṃ. Citrakūṭaṃ sabbaratanamayaṃ. Kāḷakūṭaṃ añjanamayaṃ. Gandhamādanakūṭaṃ sānumayaṃ abbhantare muggavaṇṇaṃ, mūlagandho sāragandho pheggugandho tacagandho papaṭikagandho rasagandho pattagandho pupphagandho phalagandho gandhagandhoti imehi dasahi gandhehi ussannaṃ nānappakāraosadhasañchannaṃ, kāḷapakkhauposathadivase ādittamiva aṅgāraṃ jalantaṃ tiṭṭhati. Kelāsakūṭaṃ rajatamayaṃ. Sabbāni sudassanena samānubbedhasaṇṭhānāni, tameva saraṃ paṭicchādetvā ṭhitāni. Tāni sabbāni devānubhāvena nāgānubhāvena ca vassanti, nadiyo ca tesu sandanti. Taṃ sabbampi udakaṃ anotattameva pavisati. Candimasūriyā dakkhiṇena vā uttarena vā gacchantā pabbatantarena tattha obhāsaṃ karonti, ujuṃ gacchantā na karonti, tenevassa anotattanti saṅkhā udapādi.

Tattha manoharasilātalāni nimmacchakacchapāni phalikasadisanimmaludakāni nhānatitthāni supaṭiyattāni honti, yesu buddhapaccekabuddhakhīṇāsavā ca iddhimanto ca isayo nhāyanti, devayakkhādayo uyyānakīḷakaṃ kīḷanti.

Tassa catūsu passesu sīhamukhaṃ hatthimukhaṃ assamukhaṃ usabhamukhanti cattāri mukhāni honti, yehi catasso nadiyo sandanti. Sīhamukhena nikkhantanadītīre sīhā bahutarā honti. Hatthimukhādīhi hatthiassausabhā. Puratthimadisato nikkhantanadī anotattaṃ tikkhattuṃ padakkhiṇaṃ katvā itarā tisso nadiyo anupagamma pācīnahimavanteneva amanussapathaṃ gantvā mahāsamuddaṃ pavisati. Pacchimadisato ca uttaradisato ca nikkhantanadiyopi tatheva padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pacchimahimavanteneva uttarahimavanteneva ca amanussapathaṃ gantvā mahāsamuddaṃ pavisanti. Dakkhiṇadisato nikkhantanadī pana taṃ tikkhattuṃ padakkhiṇaṃ katvā dakkhiṇena ujukaṃ pāsāṇapiṭṭheneva saṭṭhiyojanāni gantvā pabbataṃ paharitvā vuṭṭhāya parikkhepena tigāvutappamāṇā udakadhārā ca hutvā ākāsena saṭṭhiyojanāni gantvā tiyaggaḷe nāma pāsāṇe patitā, pāsāṇo udakadhārāvegena bhinno. Tattha paññāsayojanappamāṇā tiyaggaḷā nāma pokkharaṇī jātā, pokkharaṇiyā kūlaṃ bhinditvā pāsāṇaṃ pavisitvā saṭṭhiyojanāni gatā. Tato ghanapathaviṃ bhinditvā umaṅgena saṭṭhiyojanāni gantvā viñjhuṃ nāma tiracchānapabbataṃ paharitvā hatthatale pañcaṅgulisadisā pañcadhārā hutvā pavattanti. Sā tikkhattuṃ anotattaṃ padakkhiṇaṃ katvā gataṭṭhāne āvaṭṭagaṅgāti vuccati. Ujukaṃ pāsāṇapiṭṭhena saṭṭhiyojanāni gataṭṭhāne kaṇhagaṅgāti, ākāsena saṭṭhiyojanāni gataṭṭhāne ākāsagaṅgāti, tiyaggaḷapāsāṇe paññāsayojanokāse ṭhitā tiyaggaḷapokkharaṇīti, kūlaṃ bhinditvā pāsāṇaṃ pavisitvā saṭṭhiyojanāni gataṭṭhāne bahalagaṅgāti, umaṅgena saṭṭhiyojanāni gataṭṭhāne umaṅgagaṅgāti vuccati. Viñjhuṃ nāma tiracchānapabbataṃ paharitvā pañcadhārā hutvā pavattaṭṭhāne pana gaṅgā yamunā aciravatī sarabhū mahīti pañcadhā saṅkhaṃ gatā. Evametā pañca mahānadiyo himavantato pabhavanti. Tāsu yā ayaṃ pañcamī mahī nāma, sā idha mahāmahīti adhippetā. Tassā uttarena yā āpo, tāsaṃ avidūrattā so janapado aṅguttarāpoti veditabbo. Tasmiṃ aṅguttarāpesu janapade.

Āpaṇaṃnāmāti tasmiṃ kira nigame vīsati āpaṇamukhasahassāni vibhattāni ahesuṃ. Iti so āpaṇānaṃ ussannattā āpaṇantveva saṅkhaṃ gato. Tassa ca nigamassa avidūre nadītīre ghanacchāyo ramaṇīyo bhūmibhāgo mahāvanasaṇḍo, tasmiṃ bhagavā viharati. Tenevettha vasanaṭṭhānaṃ na niyāmitanti veditabbaṃ. Yenaññataro vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkamīti bhikkhusaṅghaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ pesetvā ekakova upasaṅkami potaliyaṃ gahapatiṃ sandhāya. Potaliyopi kho gahapatīti potaliyoti evaṃnāmako gahapati. Sampannanivāsanapāvuraṇoti paripuṇṇanivāsanapāvuraṇo , ekaṃ dīghadasaṃ sāṭakaṃ nivattho ekaṃ pārutoti attho. Chattupāhanāhīti chattaṃ gahetvā upāhanā āruyhāti attho. Āsanānīti pallaṅkapīṭhapalālapīṭhakādīni. Antamaso sākhābhaṅgampi hi āsananteva vuccati. Gahapativādenāti gahapatīti iminā vacanena. Samudācaratīti voharati.

Āpaṇaṃ nāmā Yenaññataro vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkamī Potaliyopi kho gahapatī Sampannanivāsanapāvuraṇo Chattupāhanāhī Āsanānī Gahapativādenā Samudācaratī

Bhagavantaṃ etadavocāti tatiyaṃ gahapatīti vacanaṃ adhivāsetuṃ asakkonto bhagavantametaṃ ‘‘tayidaṃ, bho, gotamā’’tiādivacanaṃ avoca. Tattha nacchannanti na anucchavikaṃ. Nappatirūpanti na sāruppaṃ. Ākārātiādīni sabbāneva kāraṇavevacanāni. Dīghadasavatthadhāraṇa-kesamassunakhaṭhapanādīni hi sabbāneva gihibyañjanāni tassa gihibhāvaṃ pākaṭaṃ karontīti ākārā, gihisaṇṭhānena saṇṭhitattā liṅgā, gihibhāvassa sañjānananimittatāya nimittāti vuttā. Yathā taṃ gahapatissāti yathā gahapatissa ākāraliṅganimittā bhaveyyuṃ, tatheva tuyhaṃ. Tena tāhaṃ evaṃ samudācarāmīti dasseti. Atha so yena kāraṇena gahapativādaṃ nādhivāseti, taṃ pakāsento ‘‘tathā hi pana me’’tiādimāha.

Bhagavantaṃ etadavocā nacchanna Nappatirūpa Ākārā ākārā, liṅgā, nimittā Yathā taṃ gahapatissā

Niyyātanti niyyātitaṃ. Anovādī anupavādīti ‘‘tātā, kasatha, vapatha, vaṇippathaṃ payojethā’’tiādinā hi nayena ovadanto ovādī nāma hoti. ‘‘Tumhe na kasatha, na vapatha, na vaṇippathaṃ payojetha, kathaṃ jīvissatha, puttadāraṃ vā bharissathā’’tiādinā nayena pana upavadanto upavādī nāma hoti. Ahaṃ pana ubhayampi taṃ na karomi. Tenāhaṃ tattha anovādī anupavādīti dasseti. Ghāsacchādanaparamoviharāmīti ghāsamattañceva acchādanamattañca paramaṃ katvā viharāmi, tato paraṃ natthi, na ca patthemīti dīpeti.

Niyyāta Anovādī anupavādī Ghāsacchādanaparamo viharāmī
commentary_english:
Thus have I heard. This is the *Potaliyasutta*.

Here, *aṅguttarāpesū* means that district is indeed Aṅga. But because the waters that are to the north of that land are not far away, it is called Uttarāpotipi.

Which land has waters to the north? The great land.

Here is the story of its manifestation: This *Jambudvīpa* is approximately ten thousand *yojanas*.

There, approximately four thousand *yojanas* of the region are covered with water, which has the designation "ocean."

Humans live in approximately three thousand *yojanas*.

The *Himavā* is established in approximately three thousand *yojanas*, and is a hundred leagues in height; it is adorned with eighty-four thousand peaks; it is characterized all around by a continuous flow of five hundred rivers. There, with a length and width, and also with a depth of fifty by fifty *yojanas*, and one and a half hundred *yojanas* in circumference, are the *Anotatta* lake, the *Kaṇṇamuṇḍa* lake, the *Rathakāra* lake, the *Chaddanta* lake, the *Kuṇāla* lake, the *Mandākinī* lake, and the *Sīhapapāta* lake, which are the seven great lakes that are established.

Among those, the *Anotatta* lake is surrounded by these five mountains: the *Sudassana* peak, the *Citrakūṭa* peak, the *Kāḷakūṭa* peak, the *Gandhamādana* peak, and the *Kelāsa* peak.

There, the *Sudassana* peak is made of gold, two hundred *yojanas* in height, with a concave interior, with a crow-mouth shape, and stands covering that very lake.

The *Citrakūṭa* peak is made of all gems.

The *Kāḷakūṭa* peak is made of *añjana*.

The *Gandhamādana* peak is made of summits, with the color of *mudga* beans on the interior. From these ten smells—root smell, core smell, *pheggu* smell, bark smell, *papaṭika* smell, sap smell, leaf smell, flower smell, fruit smell, and fragrance smell—it is overgrown and covered over with various kinds of medicinal herbs, and on the day of the black-fortnight *uposatha*, it stands like a burning coal that is blazing.

The *Kelāsa* peak is made of silver.

All are of equal height and shape to the *Sudassana* peak, and stand covering that very lake.

All of those are raining down by the power of the gods and by the power of the *nāgas*, and rivers flow down in those.

That entire water enters only the *Anotatta*.

The moon and sun, going either to the south or to the north, make light there through the mountain interior; they do not make [light] going straight, and so its name, *Anotatta*, arose.

There, the delightful stone surfaces, free from flies and turtles, bathing places with pure water like crystal, are well-prepared; there, Buddhas, *Pratyekabuddhas*, *Khīṇāsavas*, powerful ones, and *ṛṣis* bathe, and gods, *yakṣas*, and others play garden sports.

On its four sides are the lion-mouth, elephant-mouth, horse-mouth, and bull-mouth, these are the four mouths from which the four rivers flow.

On the river bank issuing from the lion-mouth, there are many lions.

Elephants, horses, and bulls [are on the banks issuing] from the elephant-mouth and the others.

The river issuing from the eastern direction, having circumambulated the *Anotatta* three times, without going to the other three rivers, having gone to the path of non-humans by means of the eastern *Himavant*, enters the great ocean.

The rivers issuing from the western direction and from the northern direction also, having circumambulated in that way and having gone to the path of non-humans by means of the western *Himavant* and by means of the northern *Himavant*, enter the great ocean.

But the river issuing from the southern direction, having circumambulated that three times, and going directly south by means of a stone surface, having gone sixty *yojanas*, having struck the mountain, rising up and becoming a stream of water approximately three *gāvutas* in circumference, and having gone sixty *yojanas* through the sky, fell upon a stone named *Tiyaggaḷa*; the stone was broken by the force of the water stream.

There, a pond named *Tiyaggaḷā*, approximately fifty *yojanas* in extent, arose; having broken the bank of the pond, having entered the stone, it went sixty *yojanas*.

From there, having broken the solid earth, having gone sixty *yojanas* by means of a tunnel, having struck the mountain named *Viñjhuṃ*, five streams similar to fingers in the palm of the hand, flow out.

That, having circumambulated the *Anotatta* three times, in the place it went, is called *Āvaṭṭagaṅgā*.

In the place where it went sixty *yojanas* directly by means of a stone surface, [it is called] *Kaṇhagaṅgā*; in the place where it went sixty *yojanas* through the sky, [it is called] *Ākāsagaṅgā*; the *Tiyaggaḷapokkharaṇī*, standing in a fifty-*yojana* space on the *Tiyaggaḷa* stone; having broken the bank, having entered the stone, in the place where it went sixty *yojanas*, [it is called] *Bahalagaṅgā*; in the place where it went sixty *yojanas* by means of a tunnel, [it is called] *Umaṅgagaṅgā*.

But in the place where, having struck the mountain named *Viñjhuṃ*, having become five streams, it flowed out, it has the designation fivefold, as the *Gaṅgā*, *Yamunā*, *Aciravatī*, *Sarabhū*, and *Mahī*.

Thus, these five great rivers originate from the *Himavant*.
Among them, that which is called the fifth earth (pañcamī mahī) is what is intended here as the great earth (mahāmahī).

To the north of that are the waters (āpo), and not far from them is that district (janapada), which should be known as Aṅguttarāpa.

In that district of Aṅguttarāpa.

 

 āpaṇaṃ: nāmā means in that town (nigama), twenty thousand shop fronts (āpaṇamukhasahassāni) were divided.

Thus, because of the thriving of the shops (āpaṇānaṃ), it went to the designation of shop (āpaṇaṃ).

And not far from that town, on the bank of the river, is a delightful land area with dense shade, a great forest thicket (mahāvanasaṇḍo), in which the Blessed One (bhagavā) dwells (viharati).

Therefore, it should be understood that the location of the dwelling (vasanaṭṭhānaṃ) is not fixed (niyāmitanti).

yenaññataro vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkamīti: Having sent the monastic community (bhikkhusaṅghaṃ) to the dwelling place (vasanaṭṭhānaṃ), he went alone to Potaliya concerning the householder (gahapatiṃ sandhāya).

potaliyopi kho gahapatīti: potaliyoti is a householder (gahapati) of such a name.

sampannanivāsanapāvuraṇoti: paripuṇṇanivāsanapāvuraṇo, meaning wearing a single long cloak (sāṭakaṃ) and a single covering (pārutoti).

chattupāhanāhīti: chattaṃ gahetvā upāhanā āruyhāti, meaning taking an umbrella and wearing shoes (upāhanā).

āsanānīti: pallaṅkapīṭhapalālapīṭhakādīni, meaning couches (pallaṅka), chairs (pīṭha), straw chairs (palālapīṭhaka), and so on.

Even a branch breaking (sākhābhaṅgampi) is called a seat (āsananteva).

gahapativādenāti: gahapatīti iminā vacanena, meaning by this word, householder (gahapati).

samudācaratīti: voharati, meaning he speaks.

 

 āpaṇaṃ nāmā yenaññataro vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkamī potaliyopi kho gahapatī sampannanivāsanapāvuraṇo chattupāhanāhī āsanānī gahapativādenā samudācaratī bhagavantaṃ etadavocāti: Having failed to convince the third householder to accept the word gahapati, he said this to the Blessed One, "This is yours, Gotama."

tattha nacchannanti: na anucchavikaṃ, meaning not suitable.

nappatirūpanti: na sāruppaṃ, meaning not conforming.

ākārātiādīni sabbāneva kāraṇavevacanāni: ākārātiādīni are all words for cause.

dīghadasavatthadhāraṇa-kesamassunakhaṭhapanādīni hi sabbāneva gihibyañjanāni tassa gihibhāvaṃ pākaṭaṃ karontīti ākārā, gihisaṇṭhānena saṇṭhitattā liṅgā, gihibhāvassa sañjānananimittatāya nimittāti vuttā: Because the wearing of long-fringed robes, the keeping of hair, beards, and nails, and so on, are all characteristics of a householder, they make his state as a householder apparent; therefore, they are called form (ākārā), sign (liṅgā) because they are arranged in the manner of a householder, and cause (nimittā) because they are the cause of the arising of the state of being a householder.

yathā taṃ gahapatissāti: yathā gahapatissa ākāraliṅganimittā bhaveyyuṃ, tatheva tuyhaṃ, meaning just as a householder has form, sign, and cause, so do you.

tena tāhaṃ evaṃ samudācarāmīti dasseti, thereby he shows that he behaves thus.

atha so yena kāraṇena gahapativādaṃ nādhivāseti, taṃ pakāsento tathā hi pana me'tiādimāha: Then, revealing the reason why he does not accept the householder's words, he said, "Thus, indeed, for me..."

 bhagavantaṃ etadavocā nacchanna nappatirūpa ākārā ākārā, liṅgā, nimittā yathā taṃ gahapatissā niyyātanti niyyātitaṃ.

anovādī anupavādīti: ‘‘tātā, kasatha, vapatha, vaṇippathaṃ payojethā’’tiādinā hi nayena ovadanto ovādī nāma hoti: He who advises, saying, "Fathers, cultivate, sow, engage in trade," is called an advisor (ovādī).

‘‘tumhe na kasatha, na vapatha, na vaṇippathaṃ payojetha, kathaṃ jīvissatha, puttadāraṃ vā bharissathā’’tiādinā nayena pana upavadanto upavādī nāma hoti: But he who censures, saying, "You do not cultivate, you do not sow, you do not engage in trade, how will you live, or support your children and wife?" is called a censurer (upavādī).

ahaṃ pana ubhayampi taṃ na karomi: But I do not do either of those things.

tenāhaṃ tattha anovādī anupavādīti dasseti: Therefore, he shows that he is neither an advisor nor a censurer there.

ghāsacchādanaparamo viharāmīti: ghāsamattañceva acchādanamattañca paramaṃ katvā viharāmi, tato paraṃ natthi, na ca patthemīti dīpeti: He lives with only food and clothing as the highest goal, and he reveals that there is nothing beyond that, nor does he desire anything.

 niyyāta anovādī anupavādī ghāsacchādanaparamo viharāmī

mula_pali: 32. Bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘aṭṭha kho ime, gahapati, dhammā ariyassa vinaye vohārasamucchedāya saṃvattanti. Katame aṭṭha? Apāṇātipātaṃ nissāya pāṇātipāto pahātabbo; dinnādānaṃ nissāya adinnādānaṃ pahātabbaṃ; saccavācaṃ saccaṃ vācaṃ (syā.) nissāya musāvādo pahātabbo; apisuṇaṃ vācaṃ nissāya pisuṇā vācā pahātabbā; agiddhilobhaṃ nissāya giddhilobho pahātabbo; anindārosaṃ nissāya nindāroso pahātabbo; akkodhūpāyāsaṃ nissāya kodhūpāyāso pahātabbo; anatimānaṃ nissāya atimāno pahātabbo. Ime kho, gahapati, aṭṭha dhammā saṃkhittena vuttā, vitthārena avibhattā, ariyassa vinaye vohārasamucchedāya saṃvattantī’’ti. ‘‘Ye me ye me pana (syā. ka.), bhante, bhagavatā aṭṭha dhammā saṃkhittena vuttā, vitthārena avibhattā, ariyassa vinaye vohārasamucchedāya saṃvattanti, sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā ime aṭṭha dhamme vitthārena vitthāretvā (ka.) vibhajatu anukampaṃ upādāyā’’ti. ‘‘Tena hi, gahapati, suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho potaliyo gahapati bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
The Blessed One said this: “Householder, there are these eight things in the Noble One’s Discipline that lead to the cutting off of affairs.

Which eight? With the support of the non-killing of living beings, the killing of living beings is to be abandoned. With the support of taking only what is given, the taking of what is not given is to be abandoned. With the support of truthful speech, false speech is to be abandoned. With the support of unmalicious speech, malicious speech is to be abandoned. With the support of refraining from rapacious greed, rapacious greed is to be abandoned. With the support of refraining from spiteful scolding, spiteful scolding is to be abandoned. With the support of refraining from anger and despair, anger and despair are to be abandoned. With the support of refraining from excessive pride, excessive pride is to be abandoned. These are the eight things, stated in brief without being expounded in detail, that lead to the cutting off of affairs in the Noble One’s Discipline.”

“Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would expound in detail these eight things that you have stated in brief without being expounded in detail, which lead to the cutting off of affairs in the Noble One’s Discipline, out of compassion.”

“Then listen, householder, and attend closely to what I shall say.”

“Yes, venerable sir,” Potaliya the householder replied.

The Blessed One said:
commentary_pali:
32.Giddhilobhopahātabboti gedhabhūto lobho pahātabbo. Anindārosanti anindābhūtaṃ aghaṭṭanaṃ. Nindārosoti nindāghaṭṭanā. Vohārasamucchedāyāti ettha vohāroti byavahāravohāropi paṇṇattipi vacanampi cetanāpi. Tattha –

‘‘Yo hi koci manussesu, vohāraṃ upajīvati;

Evaṃ vāseṭṭha jānāhi, vāṇijo so na brāhmaṇo’’ti. (ma. ni. 2.457) –

Ayaṃ byavahāravohāro nāma. ‘‘Saṅkhā samaññā paññatti vohāro’’ti (dha. sa. 1313-1315) ayaṃ paṇṇattivohāro nāma. ‘‘Tathā tathā voharati aparāmasa’’nti (ma. ni. 3.332) ayaṃ vacanavohāro nāma. ‘‘Aṭṭha ariyavohārā aṭṭha anariyavoharā’’ti (a. ni. 8.67) ayaṃ cetanāvohāro nāma, ayamidhādhippeto. Yasmā vā pabbajitakālato paṭṭhāya gihīti cetanā natthi, samaṇoti cetanā hoti. Gihīti vacanaṃ natthi, samaṇoti vacanaṃ hoti. Gihīti paṇṇatti natthi, samaṇoti paṇṇatti hoti. Gihīti byavahāro natthi, samaṇoti vā pabbajitoti vā byavahāro hoti. Tasmā sabbepete labbhanti.

mula_pali: 33. ‘‘‘Apāṇātipātaṃ nissāya pāṇātipāto pahātabbo’ti iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ ? Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘yesaṃ kho ahaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ hetu pāṇātipātī assaṃ, tesāhaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ pahānāya samucchedāya paṭipanno. Ahañceva ahañce (?) kho pana pāṇātipātī assaṃ, attāpi maṃ upavadeyya pāṇātipātapaccayā, anuviccāpi maṃ viññū anuvicca viññū (sī. syā. pī.) garaheyyuṃ pāṇātipātapaccayā, kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā duggati pāṭikaṅkhā pāṇātipātapaccayā. Etadeva kho pana saṃyojanaṃ etaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ yadidaṃ pāṇātipāto. Ye ca pāṇātipātapaccayā uppajjeyyuṃ āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, pāṇātipātā paṭiviratassa evaṃsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti’. ‘Apāṇātipātaṃ nissāya pāṇātipāto pahātabbo’ti – iti yantaṃ vuttaṃ idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.
mula_english: 33. “‘With the support of non-killing (apāṇātipātaṃ), the killing of living beings (pāṇātipāto) is to be abandoned (pahātabbo)’—so it was said. And with reference to what was this said? Here, householder (gahapati), a noble disciple (ariyasāvako) considers thus: ‘I am practicing the way to the abandoning and cutting off of those fetters (saṃyojanānaṃ) because of which I might kill living beings (pāṇātipātī). If I were to kill living beings (pāṇātipātī), I would blame myself (attāpi) for doing so; the wise (viññū), having investigated, would censure me for doing so; and on the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), an unhappy destination (duggati) would be expected because of killing living beings (pāṇātipātapaccayā). But this killing of living beings (pāṇātipāto) is itself a fetter (saṃyojanaṃ) and a hindrance (nīvaraṇaṃ). And while taints (āsavā), vexation (vighāta), and fever (pariḷāhā) might arise through the killing of living beings (pāṇātipātapaccayā), there are no taints (āsavā), vexation (vighāta), and fever (pariḷāhā) in one who abstains from killing living beings (pāṇātipātā paṭiviratassa).’ ‘With the support of non-killing (apāṇātipātaṃ), the killing of living beings (pāṇātipāto) is to be abandoned (pahātabbo)’—so it was said. So it is with reference to this that it was said.
commentary_pali: 33.Yesaṃ kho ahaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ hetu pāṇātipātīti ettha pāṇātipātova saṃyojanaṃ. Pāṇātipātasseva hi hetu pāṇātipātapaccayā pāṇātipātī nāma hoti. Pāṇātipātānaṃ pana bahutāya ‘‘yesaṃ kho aha’’nti vuttaṃ. Tesāhaṃsaṃyojanānanti tesaṃ ahaṃ pāṇātipātabandhanānaṃ. Pahānāya samucchedāya paṭipannoti iminā apāṇātipātasaṅkhātena kāyikasīlasaṃvarena pahānatthāya samucchedanatthāya paṭipanno. Attāpi maṃ upavadeyyāti kunthakipillikampi nāma jīvitā avoropanakasāsane pabbajitvā pāṇātipātamattatopi oramituṃ na sakkomi, kiṃ mayhaṃ pabbajjāyāti evaṃ attāpi maṃ upavadeyya. Anuviccāpi maṃ viññū garaheyyunti evarūpe nāma sāsane pabbajitvā pāṇātipātamattatopi oramituṃ na sakkoti, kiṃ etassa pabbajjāyāti evaṃ anuvicca tulayitvā pariyogāhetvā aññepi viññū paṇḍitā garaheyyuṃ. Etadeva kho pana saṃyojanametaṃ nīvaraṇanti dasasu saṃyojanesu pañcasu ca nīvaraṇesu apariyāpannampi ‘‘aṭṭha nīvaraṇā’’ti desanāvasenetaṃ vuttaṃ. Vaṭṭabandhanaṭṭhena hi hitapaṭicchādanaṭṭhena ca saṃyojanantipi nīvaraṇantipi vuttaṃ. Āsavāti pāṇātipātakāraṇā eko avijjāsavo uppajjati. Vighātapariḷāhāti vighātā ca pariḷāhā ca. Tattha vighātaggahaṇena kilesadukkhañca vipākadukkhañca gahitaṃ, pariḷāhaggahaṇenapi kilesapariḷāho ca vipākapariḷāho ca gahito. Iminā upāyena sabbattha attho veditabbo.
commentary_english:
33. "Because of what *saṃyojanas* [fetters] am I a killer of living beings (pāṇātipātī)?" Here, killing of living beings is itself a *saṃyojana*.

Indeed, it is because of the cause of killing living beings, due to the condition of killing living beings, that one is called a killer of living beings.

But it is said, "Because of what *saṃyojanas* am I?" with reference to the abundance of killing living beings.

"Of those *saṃyojanas*" means of those bonds of killing living beings.

"Committed to abandoning and destroying" means committed to abandoning and destroying through this restraint of bodily morality (kāyikasīlasaṃvara) known as abstaining from killing living beings (apāṇātipāta).

"Even myself would reproach me," [thinking,] "Even someone as insignificant as a *kunthakipillika* [ant] cannot, after going forth in a teaching that prevents the taking of life, refrain even from the smallest act of killing living beings. What is the use of my going forth?" Thus, even myself would reproach me.

"Even the wise would despise me," [thinking,] "Having gone forth in such a teaching, he cannot refrain even from the smallest act of killing living beings. What is the use of his going forth?" Thus, having investigated, weighed, and examined, other wise and learned people would despise him.

"This very thing is a *saṃyojana*, this is a *nīvaraṇa* [hindrance]"—although not included among the ten *saṃyojanas* and the five *nīvaraṇas*, this was said in the context of the teaching, "Eight *nīvaraṇas*."

Indeed, it is said to be both a *saṃyojana* and a *nīvaraṇa* by way of binding together and by way of concealing what is beneficial.

"*Āsavas* [influxes]"—because of the cause of killing living beings, one *avijjāsava* [influx of ignorance] arises.

"*Vighāta* [affliction] and *pariḷāha* [torment]" means affliction and torment.

There, by the term "*vighāta*," both the suffering of defilements (kilesadukkha) and the suffering of consequences (vipākadukkha) are included; and by the term "*pariḷāha*," both the torment of defilements (kilesapariḷāha) and the torment of consequences (vipākapariḷāha) are included.
