*micchādiṭṭhī* means, taking what is the path going to a non-god realm (*adevaloka*) alone as the path going to a god realm (*devaloka*), because of the arisen nature, that is called wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhi*).
*aññataraṃ gatiṃ vadāmī* means, for him, another destination other than hell (*niraya*) or the animal realm (*tiracchānayoni*) does not exist; therefore, he speaks thus.
*sampajjamāna* means lying down, not mixed with views (*diṭṭhi*).

*nāhaṃ, bhante, etaṃ rodāmi, yaṃ maṃ bhagavā evamāhā* means, "I, venerable sir (*bhante*), do not weep for this that the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) has said to me," is the meaning.
Thus, the meaning here should be understood in terms of karmic agency, not merely by the shedding of tears.

*nāhaṃ, bhante, etaṃ rodāmi, yaṃ maṃ bhagavā evamāhā* "Mothers weep for the dead, or for those living who are not seen;

Why, mother, do you weep for me who am living and seen?"
(Saṃ.
Ni.
1.
239) –

This is the application here.
*apica me idaṃ, bhante* means, "Moreover, this to me, venerable sir (*bhante*)," moreover, this dog-vow (*kukkuravata*) has been undertaken by me for a long time (*dīgharattaṃ*), even when fulfilled, there is no growth, even when ruined.
Thus, "For so long, the karma done by me has become useless," thus, considering his own misfortune (*vipatti*), he weeps, venerable sir (*bhante*).

*apica me idaṃ, bhante*

mula_pali:
80. ‘‘Addhā kho te ahaṃ, seniya, na labhāmi. Alaṃ, seniya, tiṭṭhatetaṃ; mā maṃ etaṃ pucchīti; api ca tyāhaṃ byākarissāmi. Idha, seniya, ekacco govataṃ bhāveti paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ, gosīlaṃ bhāveti paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ, gocittaṃ bhāveti paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ, gavākappaṃ gvākappaṃ (ka.) bhāveti paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ. So govataṃ bhāvetvā paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ, gosīlaṃ bhāvetvā paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ, gocittaṃ bhāvetvā paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ, gavākappaṃ bhāvetvā paripuṇṇaṃ abbokiṇṇaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā gunnaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Sace kho panassa evaṃdiṭṭhi hoti – ‘imināhaṃ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti , sāssa hoti micchādiṭṭhi. Micchādiṭṭhissa kho ahaṃ, seniya, dvinnaṃ gatīnaṃ aññataraṃ gatiṃ vadāmi – nirayaṃ vā tiracchānayoniṃ vā. Iti kho, seniya, sampajjamānaṃ govataṃ gunnaṃ sahabyataṃ upaneti, vipajjamānaṃ niraya’’nti. Evaṃ vutte, puṇṇo koliyaputto govatiko parodi, assūni pavattesi.

Atha kho bhagavā acelaṃ seniyaṃ kukkuravatikaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘etaṃ kho te ahaṃ, seniya , nālatthaṃ. Alaṃ, seniya, tiṭṭhatetaṃ; mā maṃ etaṃ pucchī’’ti. ‘‘Nāhaṃ, bhante, etaṃ rodāmi yaṃ maṃ bhagavā evamāha; api ca me idaṃ, bhante, govataṃ dīgharattaṃ samattaṃ samādinnaṃ. Evaṃ pasanno ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati; pahoti bhagavā tathā dhammaṃ desetuṃ yathā ahaṃ cevimaṃ govataṃ pajaheyyaṃ, ayañceva acelo seniyo kukkuravatiko taṃ kukkuravataṃ pajaheyyā’’ti. ‘‘Tena hi, puṇṇa, suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho puṇṇo koliyaputto govatiko bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
80. “Well, Seniya, since I certainly cannot persuade you when I say:

‘Enough, Seniya, let that be. Do not ask me that.’ I shall therefore answer you.

“Here, Seniya, someone develops the ox-duty (govataṃ) fully and uninterruptedly; he develops the ox-habit (gosīlaṃ) fully and uninterruptedly; he develops the ox-mind (gocittaṃ) fully and uninterruptedly; he develops ox-behaviour (gavākappaṃ) fully and uninterruptedly.
Having done so, on the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), he reappears in the company of oxen (gunnaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati).
If he has such a view: ‘By this moral discipline (sīlena), or vow (vatena), or asceticism (tapena), or living the holy life (brahmacariyena), may I become a god (devo) or one among the gods (devaññataro vā)’, that is wrong view (micchādiṭṭhi).
Now there are two destinations for one with wrong view (micchādiṭṭhissa), I say: hell (nirayaṃ) or the animal realm (tiracchānayoniṃ).
So, Seniya, if his ox-duty (govataṃ) succeeds (sampajjamānaṃ), it will lead him to the company of oxen (gunnaṃ sahabyataṃ upaneti); if it fails (vipajjamānaṃ), it will lead him to hell (nirayaṃ).”

When this was said, Puṇṇa, son of the Koliyas, the ox-duty ascetic cried out and burst into tears (assūni pavattesi).

Then the Blessed One (bhagavā) told Seniya the naked dog-duty ascetic (kukkuravatikaṃ): “Seniya, I could not persuade you when I said:

‘Enough, Seniya, let that be. Do not ask me that.’”

Then Puṇṇa the ox-duty ascetic said: “Venerable sir (bhante), I am not crying because the Blessed One (bhagavā) has said this about me, but because I have long taken up and practised this ox-duty (govataṃ).
Venerable sir (bhante), I have confidence in the Blessed One (bhagavati) thus: ‘The Blessed One (bhagavā) is capable of teaching me the Dhamma in such a way that I can abandon this ox-duty (govataṃ) and that this Seniya the naked dog-duty ascetic (kukkuravatiko) can abandon that dog-duty (kukkuravataṃ).’”

“Well then, Puṇṇa, listen (suṇāhi) and attend carefully to what I shall say (bhāsissāmī).”

“Yes, venerable sir (bhante),” he replied.
The Blessed One (bhagavā) said:
commentary_pali: 80.Govatantiādīni kukkuravatādīsu vuttanayeneva veditabbāni. Gavākappanti goākappaṃ. Sesaṃ kukkurākappe vuttasadisameva. Yathā pana tattha aññe kukkure disvā dante vivaritvā gamanākāro, evamidha aññe gāvo disvā kaṇṇe ukkhipitvā gamanākāro veditabbo. Sesaṃ tādisameva.
commentary_english: 80. *Govata*nti and the rest should be understood just by the method already stated in *kukkuravatādi*. *Gavākappa*nti [means the same as] *goākappaṃ*. The remainder is just like what has been stated in the case of *kukkurākappa*. Just as there, on seeing other dogs, the manner of going is [with] teeth bared, so here, on seeing other cows, the manner of going is to be understood [with] ears raised. The rest is just the same as that.

mula_pali:
81. ‘‘Cattārimāni, puṇṇa, kammāni mayā sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā paveditāni. Katamāni cattāri? Atthi, puṇṇa, kammaṃ kaṇhaṃ kaṇhavipākaṃ; atthi, puṇṇa, kammaṃ sukkaṃ sukkavipākaṃ; atthi, puṇṇa, kammaṃ kaṇhasukkaṃ kaṇhasukkavipākaṃ; atthi, puṇṇa, kammaṃ akaṇhaṃ asukkaṃ akaṇhaasukkavipākaṃ, kammakkhayāya saṃvattati .

‘‘Katamañca, puṇṇa, kammaṃ kaṇhaṃ kaṇhavipākaṃ? Idha, puṇṇa, ekacco sabyābajjhaṃ sabyāpajjhaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.) kāyasaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti, sabyābajjhaṃ vacīsaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti, sabyābajjhaṃ manosaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti. So sabyābajjhaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā, sabyābajjhaṃ vacīsaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā, sabyābajjhaṃ manosaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā, sabyābajjhaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. Tamenaṃ sabyābajjhaṃ lokaṃ upapannaṃ samānaṃ sabyābajjhā phassā phusanti. So sabyābajjhehi phassehi phuṭṭho samāno sabyābajjhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti ekantadukkhaṃ, seyyathāpi sattā nerayikā . Iti kho, puṇṇa, bhūtā bhūtassa upapatti hoti; yaṃ karoti tena upapajjati, upapannamenaṃ phassā phusanti. Evaṃpāhaṃ, puṇṇa, ‘kammadāyādā sattā’ti vadāmi. Idaṃ vuccati, puṇṇa, kammaṃ kaṇhaṃ kaṇhavipākaṃ.

sabyāpajjhaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.)

‘‘Katamañca, puṇṇa, kammaṃ sukkaṃ sukkavipākaṃ? Idha, puṇṇa, ekacco abyābajjhaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti, abyābajjhaṃ vacīsaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti, abyābajjhaṃ manosaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti. So abyābajjhaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā, abyābajjhaṃ vacīsaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā, abyābajjhaṃ manosaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā abyābajjhaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. Tamenaṃ abyābajjhaṃ lokaṃ upapannaṃ samānaṃ abyābajjhā phassā phusanti. So abyābajjhehi phassehi phuṭṭho samāno abyābajjhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti ekantasukhaṃ, seyyathāpi devā subhakiṇhā. Iti kho , puṇṇa, bhūtā bhūtassa upapatti hoti; yaṃ karoti tena upapajjati, upapannamenaṃ phassā phusanti. Evaṃpāhaṃ, puṇṇa, ‘kammadāyādā sattā’ti vadāmi. Idaṃ vuccati, puṇṇa, kammaṃ sukkaṃ sukkavipākaṃ.

‘‘Katamañca, puṇṇa, kammaṃ kaṇhasukkaṃ kaṇhasukkavipākaṃ? Idha, puṇṇa, ekacco sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi kāyasaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti, sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi vacīsaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti, sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi manosaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti. So sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi kāyasaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā, sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi vacīsaṅkhāraṃ abhiṅkharitvā, sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi manosaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi lokaṃ upapajjati. Tamenaṃ sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi lokaṃ upapannaṃ samānaṃ sabyābajjhāpi abyābajjhāpi phassā phusanti. So sabyābajjhehipi abyābajjhehipi phassehi phuṭṭho samāno sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi vedanaṃ vedeti vokiṇṇasukhadukkhaṃ, seyyathāpi manussā ekacce ca devā ekacce ca vinipātikā. Iti kho, puṇṇa, bhūtā bhūtassa upapatti hoti; yaṃ karoti tena upapajjati. Upapannamenaṃ phassā phusanti. Evaṃpāhaṃ, puṇṇa, ‘kammadāyādā sattā’ti vadāmi. Idaṃ vuccati, puṇṇa, kammaṃ kaṇhasukkaṃ kaṇhasukkavipākaṃ.

‘‘Katamañca , puṇṇa, kammaṃ akaṇhaṃ asukkaṃ akaṇhaasukkavipākaṃ, kammakkhayāya saṃvattati? Tatra, puṇṇa, yamidaṃ kammaṃ kaṇhaṃ kaṇhavipākaṃ tassa pahānāya yā cetanā, yamidaṃ yampidaṃ (sī. pī.) kammaṃ sukkaṃ sukkavipākaṃ tassa pahānāya yā cetanā, yamidaṃ yampidaṃ (sī. pī.) kammaṃ kaṇhasukkaṃ kaṇhasukkavipākaṃ tassa pahānāya yā cetanā – idaṃ vuccati, puṇṇa, kammaṃ akaṇhaṃ asukkaṃ akaṇhaasukkavipākaṃ, kammakkhayāya saṃvattatīti. Imāni kho, puṇṇa, cattāri kammāni mayā sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā paveditānī’’ti.

yampidaṃ (sī. pī.) yampidaṃ (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
81. “Puṇṇa, there are these four kinds of *kamma* proclaimed by me after realizing them for myself with direct knowledge.

What are the four? There is, Puṇṇa, dark action (*kamma*) with dark result; there is, Puṇṇa, bright action with bright result; there is, Puṇṇa, dark-and-bright action with dark-and-bright result; and there is, Puṇṇa, action that is neither dark nor bright with neither-dark-nor-bright result, action that leads to the destruction of action.

“And what, Puṇṇa, is dark action with dark result? Here, someone generates an afflictive (*sabyābajjhaṃ*) bodily formation (*kāyasaṅkhāraṃ*), an afflictive verbal formation (*vacīsaṅkhāraṃ*), an afflictive mental formation (*manosaṅkhāraṃ*). Having generated an afflictive bodily formation, an afflictive verbal formation, an afflictive mental formation, he reappears in an afflictive world. When he has reappeared in an afflictive world, afflictive contacts touch him. Being touched by afflictive contacts, he feels afflictive feelings, extremely painful, as in the case of the beings in hell. Thus a being’s reappearance is due to a being; one reappears through the actions one has performed. When one has reappeared, contacts touch one. Thus I say beings are the heirs to their actions. This is called dark action with dark result.

“And what, Puṇṇa, is bright action with bright result? Here, someone generates an unafflictive bodily formation (*abyābajjhaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ*), an unafflictive verbal formation (*abyābajjhaṃ vacīsaṅkhāraṃ*), an unafflictive mental formation (*abyābajjhaṃ manosaṅkhāraṃ*). Having generated an unafflictive bodily formation, an unafflictive verbal formation, an unafflictive mental formation, he reappears in an unafflictive world. When he has reappeared in an unafflictive world, unafflictive contacts touch him. Being touched by unafflictive contacts, he feels unafflictive feelings, extremely pleasant, as in the case of the gods of Refulgent Glory (*subhakiṇhā*). Thus a being’s reappearance is due to a being; one reappears through the actions one has performed. When one has reappeared, contacts touch one. Thus I say beings are the heirs to their actions. This is called bright action with bright result.

“And what, Puṇṇa, is dark-and-bright action with dark-and-bright result? Here, someone generates a bodily formation that is both afflictive and unafflictive (*sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi kāyasaṅkhāraṃ*), a verbal formation that is both afflictive and unafflictive (*sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi vacīsaṅkhāraṃ*), a mental formation that is both afflictive and unafflictive (*sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi manosaṅkhāraṃ*). Having generated a bodily formation, a verbal formation, a mental formation that is both afflictive and unafflictive, he reappears in a world that is both afflictive and unafflictive. When he has reappeared in a world that is both afflictive and unafflictive, both afflictive and unafflictive contacts touch him. Being touched by both afflictive and unafflictive contacts, he feels both afflictive and unafflictive feelings, mingled pleasure and pain (*vokiṇṇasukhadukkhaṃ*), as in the case of human beings and some gods and some beings in the lower worlds (*vinipātikā*). Thus a being’s reappearance is due to a being; one reappears through the actions one has performed. When one has reappeared, contacts touch one. Thus I say beings are the heirs to their actions. This is called dark-and-bright action with dark-and-bright result.
What, Puṇṇa, is the karma that is neither dark nor bright with neither dark nor bright result, [but] leads to the destruction of karma (kammakkhayāya)? Therein, Puṇṇa, the intention (cetanā) in abandoning that karma which is dark with dark result (kṛṣṇa-kṛṣṇa-vipāka), the intention in abandoning that karma which is bright with bright result (śukla-śukla-vipāka), and the intention in abandoning that karma which is dark and bright with dark and bright result (kṛṣṇaśukla-kṛṣṇaśukla-vipāka) – this is called, Puṇṇa, karma that is neither dark nor bright with neither dark nor bright result, [but] leads to the destruction of karma.

These, Puṇṇa, are the four kinds of karma proclaimed by me after realizing them for myself with direct knowledge."
commentary_pali:
81.Cattārimānipuṇṇa kammānīti kasmā imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi? Ayañhi desanā ekaccakammakiriyavasena āgatā, imasmiñca kammacatukke kathite imesaṃ kiriyā pākaṭā bhavissatīti imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi. Apica imaṃ kammacatukkameva desiyamānaṃ ime sañjānissanti , tato eko saraṇaṃ gamissati, eko pabbajitvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇissatīti ayameva etesaṃ sappāyāti ñatvāpi imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi.

Tattha kaṇhanti kāḷakaṃ dasaakusalakammapathakammaṃ. Kaṇhavipākanti apāye nibbattanato kāḷakavipākaṃ. Sukkanti paṇḍaraṃ dasakusalakammapathakammaṃ. Sukkavipākanti sagge nibbattanato paṇḍaravipākaṃ. Kaṇhasukkanti vomissakakammaṃ. Kaṇhasukkavipākanti sukhadukkhavipākaṃ. Missakakammañhi katvā akusalena tiracchānayoniyaṃ maṅgalahatthiṭṭhānādīsu uppanno kusalena pavatte sukhaṃ vediyati. Kusalena rājakulepi nibbatto akusalena pavatte dukkhaṃ vediyati. Akaṇhaṃ asukkanti kammakkhayakaraṃ catumaggacetanākammaṃ adhippetaṃ. Tañhi yadi kaṇhaṃ bhaveyya, kaṇhavipākaṃ dadeyya. Yadi sukkaṃ bhaveyya, sukkavipākaṃ dadeyya. Ubhayavipākassa pana adānato akaṇhāsukkavipākattā ‘‘akaṇhaṃ asukka’’nti vuttaṃ. Ayaṃ tāva uddese attho.

kaṇha Kaṇhavipāka Sukka Sukkavipāka Kaṇhasukka Kaṇhasukkavipāka Akaṇhaṃ asukka

Niddese pana sabyābajjhanti sadukkhaṃ. Kāyasaṅkhārādīsu kāyadvāre gahaṇādivasena copanappattā dvādasa akusalacetanā sabyābajjhakāyasaṅkhāro nāma. Vacīdvāre hanusañcopanavasena vacībhedapavattikā tāyeva dvādasa vacīsaṅkhāro nāma. Ubhayacopanaṃ appattā raho cintayantassa manodvāre pavattā manosaṅkhāro nāma. Iti tīsupi dvāresu kāyaduccaritādibhedā akusalacetanāva saṅkhārāti veditabbā. Imasmiñhi sutte cetanā dhuraṃ, upālisutte kammaṃ. Abhisaṅkharitvāti saṅkaḍḍhitvā, piṇḍaṃ katvāti attho. Sabyābajjhaṃ lokanti sadukkhaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Sabyābajjhā phassā phusantīti sadukkhā vipākaphassā phusanti. Ekantadukkhanti nirantaradukkhaṃ. Bhūtāti hetvatthe nissakkavacanaṃ, bhūtakammato bhūtassa sattassa uppatti hoti. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – yathābhūtaṃ kammaṃ sattā karonti, tathābhūtena kammena kammasabhāgavasena tesaṃ upapatti hoti. Tenevāha ‘‘yaṃ karoti tena upapajjatī’’ti. Ettha ca tenāti kammena viya vuttā, upapatti ca nāma vipākena hoti. Yasmā pana vipākassa kammaṃ hetu, tasmā tena mūlahetubhūtena kammena nibbattatīti ayamettha attho. Phassā phusantīti yena kammavipākena nibbatto, taṃkammavipākaphassā phusanti. Kammadāyādāti kammadāyajjā kammameva nesaṃ dāyajjaṃ santakanti vadāmi.

sabyābajjha sabyābajjhakāyasaṅkhāro vacīsaṅkhāro manosaṅkhāro Abhisaṅkharitvā Sabyābajjhaṃ loka Sabyābajjhā phassā phusantī Ekantadukkha Bhūtā tenā Phassā phusantī Kammadāyādā

Abyābajjhanti niddukkhaṃ . Imasmiṃ vāre kāyadvāre pavattā aṭṭha kāmāvacarakusalacetanā kāyasaṅkhāro nāma. Tāyeva vacīdvāre pavattā vacīsaṅkhāro nāma. Manodvāre pavattā tāyeva aṭṭha, tisso ca heṭṭhimajhānacetanā abyābajjhamanosaṅkhāro nāma. Jhānacetanā tāva hotu, kāmāvacarā kinti abyābajjhamanosaṅkhāro nāma jātāti. Kasiṇasajjanakāle ca kasiṇāsevanakāle ca labbhanti. Kāmāvacaracetanā paṭhamajjhānacetanāya ghaṭitā, catutthajjhānacetanā tatiyajjhānacetanāya ghaṭitā. Iti tīsupi dvāresu kāyasucaritādibhedā kusalacetanāva saṅkhārāti veditabbo. Tatiyavāro ubhayamissakavasena veditabbā.

Abyābajjha kāyasaṅkhāro vacīsaṅkhāro abyābajjhamanosaṅkhāro

Seyyathāpi manussātiādīsu manussānaṃ tāva kālena sukhaṃ kālena dukkhaṃ pākaṭameva, devesu pana bhummadevatānaṃ, vinipātikesu vemānikapetānaṃ kālena sukhaṃ kālena dukkhaṃ hotīti veditabbaṃ. Hatthiādīsu tiracchānesupi labbhatiyeva.

Seyyathāpi manussā

Tatrāti tesu tīsu kammesu. Tassa pahānāya yā cetanāti tassa pahānatthāya maggacetanā. Kammaṃ patvāva maggacetanāya añño paṇḍarataro dhammo nāma natthi. Idaṃ pana kammacatukkaṃ patvā dvādasa akusalacetanā kaṇhā nāma, tebhūmakakusalacetanā sukkā nāma, maggacetanā akaṇhā asukkāti āgatā.

Tatrā Tassa pahānāya yā cetanā
commentary_english:
81. Why did the Blessed One begin this discourse, "[There are] these four *karmas*"? This discourse came about due to a certain act of *karma*, and having spoken on this set of four *karmas*, the action of these will become evident; [therefore,] he began this discourse. Moreover, if this very set of four *karmas* is taught, they will understand these, then one will go to refuge, one will renounce and attain *arhatship*; knowing that this itself is suitable for them, he also began this discourse.

There, *kaṇha* means black, the ten paths of unwholesome action. *Kaṇhavipāka* means black result, because it is produced in the states of loss. *Sukka* means white, the ten paths of wholesome action. *Sukkavipāka* means white result, because it is produced in heaven. *Kaṇhasukka* means mixed *karma*. *Kaṇhasukkavipāka* means result of pleasure and pain. Having performed mixed *karma*, produced by unwholesome [karma] in the animal womb in places such as the elephant stables, he experiences pleasure when wholesome [karma] prevails. Produced by wholesome [karma] even in a royal family, he experiences pain when unwholesome [karma] prevails. *Akaṇhaṃ asukka* means the *karma* of the four paths of consciousness that destroys *karma* is intended. If that were black, it would give a black result. If it were white, it would give a white result. However, since it does not give both results, it is called “*akaṇhaṃ asukka*” because of being *akaṇhāsukkavipāka*. This, for the time being, is the meaning in the summary.

*Kaṇha*, *kaṇhavipāka*, *sukka*, *sukkavipāka*, *kaṇhasukka*, *kaṇhasukkavipāka*, *akaṇhaṃ asukka*.

In the explanation, however, *sabyābajjha* means with suffering. Among the bodily fabrications, etc., the twelve unwholesome consciousnesses that are obtained in the body-door by way of grasping, etc., are called *sabyābajjhakāyasaṅkhāro*. The twelve that occur in the speech-door by way of the movement of the jaws, which are the cause of the breaking up of speech, are called *vacīsaṅkhāro*. The *manosaṅkhāro* is that which occurs in the mind-door of one who is thinking in private, not having obtained both kinds of movement. Thus, in all three doors, only unwholesome consciousnesses with the distinction of bodily misconduct, etc., are to be understood as *saṅkhāra*. In this *sutta*, consciousness is the chief thing; in the Upāli *sutta*, *karma* [is the chief thing]. *Abhisaṅkharitvā* means having tightened, having made a lump. *Sabyābajjhaṃ loka* means they are reborn in a world with suffering. *Sabyābajjhā phassā phusantī* means painful result-contacts touch. *Ekantadukkha* means uninterrupted suffering. *Bhūtā* is a word of certainty in the sense of a cause; the arising of a being is from past *karma*. This has been said: beings perform *karma* according to what has come to be; their rebirth is by way of the similarity of *karma* with *karma* that has come to be. Therefore, he said, "what one does, by that one is reborn." And here, *tenā* is said as if it were by *karma*; and rebirth is by result. However, since *karma* is the cause of result, therefore it is that it is produced by the original causal *karma*; this is the meaning here. *Phassā phusantī* means by whatever result of *karma* one is produced, those result-contacts of *karma* touch. *Kammadāyādā* means *kammadāyajjā*, I say that *karma* itself is their inheritance, their own property.

*Sabyābajjha*, *sabyābajjhakāyasaṅkhāro*, *vacīsaṅkhāro*, *manosaṅkhāro*, *abhisaṅkharitvā*, *sabyābajjhaṃ loka*, *sabyābajjhā phassā phusantī*, *ekantadukkha*, *bhūtā*, *tenā*, *phassā phusantī*, *kammadāyādā*.

mula_pali:
82. Evaṃ vutte, puṇṇo koliyaputto govatiko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante! Seyyathāpi, bhante…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata’’nti. Acelo pana seniyo kukkuravatiko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante! Seyyathāpi, bhante…pe… pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Labheyyāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada’’nti. ‘‘Yo kho, seniya , aññatitthiyapubbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhati pabbajjaṃ, ākaṅkhati upasampadaṃ so cattāro māse parivasati. Catunnaṃ māsānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājenti, upasampādenti bhikkhubhāvāya. Api ca mettha puggalavemattatā viditā’’ti.

‘‘Sace, bhante, aññatitthiyapubbā imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhantā pabbajjaṃ ākaṅkhantā upasampadaṃ te cattāro māse parivasanti catunnaṃ māsānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājenti upasampādenti bhikkhubhāvāya, ahaṃ cattāri vassāni parivasissāmi. Catunnaṃ vassānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājentu, upasampādentu bhikkhubhāvāyā’’ti. Alattha kho acelo seniyo kukkuravatiko bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampadaṃ. Acirūpasampanno kho panāyasmā seniyo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro kho panāyasmā seniyo arahataṃ ahosīti.

Kukkuravatikasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.
mula_english:
82. When this was said, Puṇṇa Koliyaputta the cow-vow ascetic said this to the Blessed One: “Magnificent, venerable sir! Magnificent, venerable sir! Just as, venerable sir… may the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from today onward for as long as life lasts.”

But Seniya the naked dog-duty ascetic said to the Blessed One: “Magnificent, venerable sir! Magnificent, venerable sir! Just as, venerable sir… it has been revealed. I go to the Blessed One for refuge, and to the Dhamma and to the Saṅgha of monks. May I receive the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence? May I receive admission?”

“Seniya, one who formerly belonged to another sect and desires the going forth and the full admission in this Dhamma and Discipline lives on probation for four months. At the end of four months, if the bhikkhus are satisfied with him, they give him the going forth and the full admission to the bhikkhus’ state. But I recognise individual differences in this matter.”

“Venerable sir, if those who formerly belonged to another sect and desire the going forth and the full admission in this Dhamma and Discipline live on probation for four months, and if at the end of the four months the bhikkhus being satisfied with them give them the going forth and the full admission to the bhikkhus’ state, then I will live on probation for four years. At the end of the four years if the bhikkhus are satisfied with me, let them give me the going forth and the full admission to the bhikkhus’ state.”

Then Seniya the naked dog-duty ascetic received the going forth under the Blessed One, and he received the full admission. And soon, not long after his full admission, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute, the venerable Seniya, by realizing for himself with direct knowledge, here and now entered upon and abided in that supreme goal of the holy life for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness. He directly knew: “Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more coming to any state of being.” And the venerable Seniya became one of the arahants.

The Kukuravatika Sutta, the seventh, is finished.
commentary_pali:
82.‘‘Labheyyāhaṃ, bhante’’ti idaṃ so ‘‘ciraṃ vata me aniyyānikapakkhe yojetvā attā kilamito, ‘sukkhanadītīre nhāyissāmī’ti samparivattentena viya thuse koṭṭentena viya ca na koci attho nipphādito, handāhaṃ attānaṃ yoge yojemī’’ti cintetvā āha. Atha bhagavā yonena khandhake titthiyaparivāso paññatto, yaṃ aññatitthiyapubbo sāmaṇerabhūmiyaṃ ṭhito – ‘‘ahaṃ, bhante, itthannāmo aññatitthiyapubbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhāmi upasampadaṃ, svāhaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ cattāro māse parivāsaṃ yācāmī’’tiādinā (mahāva. 86) nayena samādiyitvā parivasati, taṃ sandhāya ‘‘yo kho, seniya, aññatitthiyapubbo’’tiādimāha.

Tattha pabbajjanti vacanasiliṭṭhatāvaseneva vuttaṃ. Aparivasitvāyeva hi pabbajjaṃ labhati. Upasampadatthikena pana nātikālena gāmappavesanādīni aṭṭha vattāni pūrentena parivasitabbaṃ . Āraddhacittāti aṭṭhavattapūraṇena tuṭṭhacittā. Ayamettha saṅkhepo. Vitthārato panesa titthiyaparivāso samantapāsādikāya vinayaṭṭhakathāya pabbajjakhandhakavaṇṇanāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 86) vuttanayeneva veditabbo . Apica metthāti apica me ettha. Puggalavemattatā viditāti puggalanānattaṃ viditaṃ. Ayaṃ puggalo parivāsāraho, ayaṃ na parivāsārahoti idaṃ mayhaṃ pākaṭanti dasseti.

pabbajja Āraddhacittā samantapāsādikāya vinayaṭṭhakathāya Apica metthā Puggalavemattatā viditā

Tato seniyo cintesi – ‘‘aho acchariyaṃ buddhasāsanaṃ, yattha evaṃ ghaṃsitvā koṭṭetvā yuttameva gaṇhanti, ayuttaṃ chaḍḍentī’’ti. Tato suṭṭhutaraṃ pabbajjāya sañjātussāho sace, bhantetiādimāha. Atha bhagavā tassa tibbacchandataṃ viditvā na seniyo parivāsaṃ arahatīti aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantesi – ‘‘gaccha tvaṃ, bhikkhu, seniyaṃ nhāpetvā pabbājetvā ānehī’’ti. So tathā katvā taṃ pabbājetvā bhagavato santikaṃ ānayi. Bhagavā gaṇe nisīditvā upasampādesi. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘alattha kho acelo seniyo bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ alattha upasampada’’nti.

sace, bhante

Acirūpasampannoti upasampanno hutvā nacirameva. Vūpakaṭṭhoti vatthukāmakilesakāmehi kāyena ca cittena ca vūpakaṭṭho. Appamattoti kammaṭṭhāne satiṃ avijahanto. Ātāpīti kāyikacetasikasaṅkhātena vīriyātāpena ātāpī. Pahitattoti kāye ca jīvite ca anapekkhatāya pesitatto vissaṭṭhaattabhāvo. Yassatthāyāti yassa atthāya. Kulaputtāti ācārakulaputtā. Sammadevāti hetunāva kāraṇeneva. Tadanuttaranti taṃ anuttaraṃ. Brahmacariyapariyosānanti maggabrahmacariyapariyosānabhūtaṃ arahattaphalaṃ. Tassa hi atthāya kulaputtā pabbajanti. Diṭṭheva dhammeti imasmiṃyeva attabhāve. Sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvāti attanāyeva paññāya paccakkhaṃ katvā, aparappaccayaṃ ñatvāti attho. Upasampajja vihāsīti pāpuṇitvā sampādetvā vihāsi. Evaṃ viharantova khīṇā jāti…pe… abbhaññāsi.

Acirūpasampanno Vūpakaṭṭho Appamatto Ātāpī Pahitatto Yassatthāyā Kulaputtā Sammadevā Tadanuttara Brahmacariyapariyosāna Diṭṭheva dhamme Sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā Upasampajja vihāsī khīṇā jāti…pe… abbhaññāsi

Evamassa paccavekkhaṇabhūmiṃ dassetvā arahattanikūṭeneva desanaṃ niṭṭhāpetuṃ ‘‘aññataro kho panāyasmā seniyo arahataṃ ahosī’’ti vuttaṃ. Tattha aññataroti eko. Arahatanti arahantānaṃ, bhagavato sāvakānaṃ arahantānaṃ abbhantaro ahosīti ayamevattha adhippāyo. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

aññataro Arahata

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Kukkuravatikasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
82. "I would receive it, venerable sir," thinking, "For a long time, indeed, I have exhausted myself by applying [my] self to what leads to no release, just like someone agitating at a pile of husks, or like someone pounding at husks, with no purpose accomplished by someone thinking, 'I will bathe at the bank of a dried-up river,' now I will apply myself to the practice," he said.

Then, in the section on types, the Blessed One established the probationary period for those formerly of other sects. Someone formerly of another sect, standing on the level of a novice, having undertaken it in the manner of "I, venerable sir, named thus-and-so, formerly of another sect, desire the higher ordination in this Doctrine and Discipline; I, venerable sir, ask the Saṅgha for the probationary period of four months," (Mahāva. 86) lives on probation. With reference to that, he said, "Whoever, Seniya, was formerly of another sect," and so on.

There, *pabbajja* (going forth) is mentioned merely by way of verbal embellishment. For he obtains the going forth without having lived on probation. But by one seeking the higher ordination, having fulfilled the eight duties such as not entering a village at an unseasonable time, the probationary period should be lived through. *āraddhacittā* means with mind pleased by the fulfillment of the eight duties. This is a brief explanation here. But this probationary period for those of other sects should be understood in detail in the same way as stated in the section on the going forth in the commentary on the Vinaya, the *Samantapāsādikā* (Mahāva. aṭṭha. 86). *apica metthā* means *apica me ettha* (moreover, to me here). *puggalavemattatā viditā* means *puggalanānattaṃ viditaṃ* (the distinction of individuals is known). It shows that "This individual is fit for the probationary period, this one is not fit for the probationary period; this is plain to me."

*pabbajja*
*āraddhacittā*
*Samantapāsādikāya vinayaṭṭhakathāya*
*apica metthā*
*puggalavemattatā viditā*

Then Seniya thought: "How wonderful is the Buddha's Dispensation, where, having scrubbed and pounded, they accept what is fitting and reject what is unfitting!" Then, with enthusiasm for the going forth arisen even better, he said, *sace, bhante* (if, venerable sir), and so on. Then, the Blessed One, knowing his intense desire, since Seniya was not fit for the probationary period, addressed a certain bhikkhu: "Go, bhikkhu, having bathed Seniya and having him go forth, bring him here." He, having done so, having had him go forth, brought him to the Blessed One. The Blessed One, sitting in the assembly, conferred the higher ordination. Therefore it was said: "Then Seniya the naked dog-duty ascetic received the going forth under the Blessed One, and he received the higher ordination."

*sace, bhante*

*acirūpasampanno* means having been ordained, not long after. *vūpakaṭṭho* means secluded by body and also by mind from sense-desires relating to the objects [of sense] and to defilements. *appamatto* means not abandoning mindfulness in the meditation subject. *ātāpī* means ardent with the heat of effort consisting of what is bodily and mental. *pahitatto* means with self sent forth, with essence of self dismissed, through not being attached to body and life. *yassatthāyā* means *yassa atthāya* (for the sake of which). *kulaputtā* means sons of good families in terms of conduct. *sammadevā* means just by reason, just by cause. *tadanuttara* means that unsurpassed. *brahmacariyapariyosāna* means the fruit of arahantship that is the culmination of the holy life of the path. Indeed, for that benefit young men of good families become monks. *diṭṭheva dhamme* means in this very existence. *sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā* means having directly experienced with his own wisdom, having known without reliance on another.
Having attained and accomplished, he dwelt.
Thus, as he lived, destroyed was birth...and he directly knew.

Newly ordained, secluded, diligent, ardent, with self-controlled, for which the sons of good family rightly go forth from home to homelessness, that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life, in this very life, having directly known by himself with higher knowledge, he dwells, attained. Destroyed is birth...and he directly knew.

Having shown the ground for reflection, in order to complete the teaching with the pinnacle of Arahatship, it was said, "A certain venerable Seniya was among the Arahats."

There, "a certain one" means one.

"Of the Arahats" means he was among the inner circle of the Arahats, disciples of the Blessed One; this is the meaning.

The rest is clear throughout.

A certain one, of the Arahats.

The Commentary to the Majjhima Nikāya, the Papañcasūdanī.

The Commentary on the Kukuravatika Sutta is complete.

mula_pali: 83. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha kho abhayo rājakumāro yena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho abhayaṃ rājakumāraṃ nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto etadavoca – ‘‘ehi tvaṃ, rājakumāra, samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṃ āropehi. Evaṃ te kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggacchissati – ‘abhayena rājakumārena samaṇassa gotamassa evaṃ mahiddhikassa evaṃ mahānubhāvassa vādo āropito’’’ti. ‘‘Yathā kathaṃ panāhaṃ, bhante, samaṇassa gotamassa evaṃ mahiddhikassa evaṃ mahānubhāvassa vādaṃ āropessāmī’’ti? ‘‘Ehi tvaṃ, rājakumāra, yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ vadehi – ‘bhāseyya nu kho, bhante, tathāgato taṃ vācaṃ yā sā vācā paresaṃ appiyā amanāpā’ti? Sace te samaṇo gotamo evaṃ puṭṭho evaṃ byākaroti – ‘bhāseyya, rājakumāra, tathāgato taṃ vācaṃ yā sā vācā paresaṃ appiyā amanāpā’ti, tamenaṃ tvaṃ evaṃ vadeyyāsi – ‘atha kiñcarahi te, bhante, puthujjanena nānākaraṇaṃ? Puthujjanopi hi taṃ vācaṃ bhāseyya yā sā vācā paresaṃ appiyā amanāpā’ti. Sace pana te samaṇo gotamo evaṃ puṭṭho evaṃ byākaroti – ‘na, rājakumāra, tathāgato taṃ vācaṃ bhāseyya yā sā vācā paresaṃ appiyā amanāpā’ti, tamenaṃ tvaṃ evaṃ vadeyyāsi – ‘atha kiñcarahi te, bhante, devadatto byākato – ‘‘āpāyiko devadatto, nerayiko devadatto, kappaṭṭho devadatto, atekiccho devadatto’’ti? Tāya ca pana te vācāya devadatto kupito ahosi anattamano’ti. Imaṃ kho te, rājakumāra, samaṇo gotamo ubhatokoṭikaṃ pañhaṃ puṭṭho samāno neva sakkhiti uggilituṃ na sakkhiti ogilituṃ. Seyyathāpi nāma purisassa ayosiṅghāṭakaṃ kaṇṭhe vilaggaṃ, so neva sakkuṇeyya uggilituṃ na sakkuṇeyya ogilituṃ; evameva kho te, rājakumāra, samaṇo gotamo imaṃ ubhatokoṭikaṃ pañhaṃ puṭṭho samāno neva sakkhiti uggilituṃ na sakkhiti ogilitu’’nti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho abhayo rājakumāro nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Rajagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary.

Then Prince Abhaya went to the *Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta*, and after paying homage to him, sat down at one side.

Seated to one side, Prince Abhaya was addressed by the *Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta* thus: “Come, prince, refute the doctrine of the *śramaṇa* Gotama (Śramaṇassa Gotamassa vādaṃ āropehi).

Thus a good report of you will be spread to this effect: ‘Prince Abhaya has refuted the doctrine of the *śramaṇa* Gotama, who is so powerful and mighty.’”

“How, venerable sir (*bhante*), can I refute the doctrine of the *śramaṇa* Gotama, who is so powerful and mighty?” “Go, prince, to where the *śramaṇa* Gotama is, and on arrival ask the *śramaṇa* Gotama: ‘Venerable sir (*bhante*), would the *Tathāgata* utter speech that would be unwelcome and disagreeable to others?’ If the *śramaṇa* Gotama, on being asked thus, answers: ‘The *Tathāgata*, prince, would utter speech that would be unwelcome and disagreeable to others,’ then say to him: ‘Then why, venerable sir (*bhante*), is there any distinction from an ordinary person (*puthujjanena nānākaraṇaṃ*)? For even an ordinary person (*puthujjanopi*) would utter speech that would be unwelcome and disagreeable to others.’

But if the *śramaṇa* Gotama, on being asked thus, answers: ‘No, prince, the *Tathāgata* would not utter speech that would be unwelcome and disagreeable to others,’ then say to him: ‘Then why, venerable sir (*bhante*), has Devadatta been declared: “Devadatta is destined for the states of deprivation (*āpāyiko devadatto*), Devadatta is destined for hell (*nerayiko devadatto*), Devadatta will remain in hell for the aeon (*kappaṭṭho devadatto*), Devadatta is incorrigible (*atekiccho devadatto*)”? And by that speech Devadatta was angered and displeased.’

When the *śramaṇa* Gotama is posed this two-horned question by you, he will not be able either to gulp it down or to throw it up.

If an iron spike were stuck in a man’s throat, he would not be able either to gulp it down or to throw it up; so too, prince, when the *śramaṇa* Gotama is posed this two-horned question by you, he will not be able either to gulp it down or to throw it up.”

“Yes, venerable sir (*evaṃ bhante*),” Prince Abhaya replied, and he rose from his seat, and after paying homage to the *Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta*, keeping him on his right, he left and went to the Blessed One.
commentary_pali:
83.Evaṃme sutanti abhayasuttaṃ. Tattha abhayoti tassa nāmaṃ. Rājakumāroti bimbisārassa orasaputto. Vādaṃ āropehīti dosaṃ āropehi. Nerayikoti niraye nibbattako. Kappaṭṭhoti kappaṭṭhitiko. Atekicchoti buddhasahassenāpi tikicchituṃ na sakkā. Uggilitunti dve ante mocetvā kathetuṃ asakkonto uggilituṃ bahi nīharituṃ na sakkhiti. Ogilitunti pucchāya dosaṃ datvā hāretuṃ asakkonto ogilituṃ anto pavesetuṃ na sakkhiti.

Evaṃ, bhanteti nigaṇṭho kira cintesi – ‘‘samaṇo gotamo mayhaṃ sāvake bhinditvā gaṇhāti, handāhaṃ ekaṃ pañhaṃ abhisaṅkharomi, yaṃ puṭṭho samaṇo gotamo ukkuṭiko hutvā nisinno uṭṭhātuṃ na sakkhissatī’’ti. So abhayassa gehā nīhaṭabhatto siniddhabhojanaṃ bhuñjanto bahū pañhe abhisaṅkharitvā – ‘‘ettha samaṇo gotamo imaṃ nāma dosaṃ dassessati, ettha imaṃ nāmā’’ti sabbe pahāya cātumāsamatthake imaṃ pañhaṃ addasa. Athassa etadahosi – ‘‘imassa pañhassa pucchāya vā vissajjane vā na sakkā doso dātuṃ, ovaṭṭikasāro ayaṃ, ko nu kho imaṃ gahetvā samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṃ āropessatī’’ti. Tato ‘‘abhayo rājakumāro paṇḍito, so sakkhissatīti taṃ uggaṇhāpemī’’ti niṭṭhaṃ gantvā uggaṇhāpesi. So vādajjhāsayatāya tassa vacanaṃ sampaṭicchanto ‘‘evaṃ, bhante,’’ti āha.

Evaṃ, bhante
commentary_english:
83.
evaṃ, bhante

Thus I have heard: the Abhayasuttaṃ.

There, *abhayo* means his name.

rājakumāro means Bimbisāra's legitimate son.

vādaṃ āropehī means attribute fault.

nerayiko means one who is reborn in hell.

kappaṭṭho means kappaṭṭhitiko.

atekiccho means it is not possible to cure even with a thousand Buddhas.

uggilitu means being unable to loosen the two ends and speak, being unable to expel it, to bring it out.

ogilitu means being unable, when asked a question, to give a fault and defeat [the opponent], being unable to swallow it, to cause it to enter within.

evaṃ, bhante

nigaṇṭho reflected: "The renunciate Gotama breaks up my disciples and takes them. Come, let me concoct a question such that, when asked, the renunciate Gotama, squatting, sitting, will not be able to arise."

He, having had the rice removed from Abhaya's house, while enjoying smooth food, having concocted many questions - "Here the renunciate Gotama will show this fault by name, here this by name" - having abandoned all, at the end of four months, saw this question.

Then it occurred to him: "It is not possible to give a fault either by asking or by answering this question. This is a rolling essence. Who now, having taken this, will attribute fault to the renunciate Gotama?"

Then, "Abhayo is a wise prince; he will be able," having gone to the conclusion, he taught [it].

He, agreeing with his words due to his inclination towards debate, said, "evaṃ, bhante."

evaṃ, bhante

mula_pali: 84. Ekamantaṃ nisinnassa kho abhayassa rājakumārassa sūriyaṃ suriyaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) ulloketvā etadahosi – ‘‘akālo kho ajja bhagavato vādaṃ āropetuṃ . Sve dānāhaṃ sake nivesane bhagavato vādaṃ āropessāmī’’ti bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya attacatuttho bhatta’’nti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho abhayo rājakumāro bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena abhayassa rājakumārassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho abhayo rājakumāro bhagavantaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi. Atha kho abhayo rājakumāro bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ aññataraṃ nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi.
mula_english:
84. Then, Prince Abhaya, having sat down to one side, looked up at the sun (note: *sūriyaṃ* (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)) and thought: "This is not the right time to refute the Blessed One's doctrine. Tomorrow, I shall refute the Blessed One’s doctrine in my own house." Then he said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, let the Blessed One with three others consent to accept tomorrow's meal from me." The Blessed One assented by silence ( *tuṇhībhāvena*).

Then, Prince Abhaya, knowing that the Blessed One had consented ( *adhivāsanaṃ viditvā*), rose from his seat, and after paying homage to him ( *abhivādetvā*), circumambulating him ( *padakkhiṇaṃ katvā*), he departed.

Then, when the night had ended, it being morning, the Blessed One dressed, and taking his bowl and outer robe (*pattacīvaramādāya*), he went to Prince Abhaya’s house and sat down on the seat made ready ( *paññatte āsane nisīdi*).

Then, Prince Abhaya served and satisfied the Blessed One with his own hands ( *sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi*) with choice hard and soft food (*paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena*).

Then, Prince Abhaya, when the Blessed One had finished eating (*bhuttāviṃ*) and had withdrawn his hand from the bowl (*onītapattapāṇiṃ*), took a low seat (*nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā*) and sat down to one side (*ekamantaṃ nisīdi*).
commentary_pali: 84.Akālokho ajjāti ayaṃ pañho catūhi māsehi abhisaṅkhato, tattha idaṃ gahetvā idaṃ vissajjiyamāne divasabhāgo nappahossatīti maññanto evaṃ cintesi. So dānīti sve dāni. Attacatutthoti kasmā bahūhi saddhiṃ na nimantesi? Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘bahūsu nisinnesu thokaṃ datvā vadantassa aññaṃ suttaṃ aññaṃ kāraṇaṃ aññaṃ tathārūpaṃ vatthuṃ āharitvā dassessati, evaṃ sante kalaho vā kolāhalameva vā bhavissati. Athāpi ekakaṃyeva nimantessāmi, evampi me garahā uppajjissati ‘yāvamaccharī vāyaṃ abhayo, bhagavantaṃ divase divase bhikkhūnaṃ satenapi sahassenapi saddhiṃ carantaṃ disvāpi ekakaṃyeva nimantesī’’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ pana doso na bhavissatī’’ti aparehi tīhi saddhiṃ attacatutthaṃ nimantesi.
commentary_english:
84. *akālo*
*kho ajjā* this question was interrupted by four months. Thinking, "If I take this and dismiss this, even a part of the day won't suffice," he thought thus.
*so dānī* tomorrow then.
*attacatuttho* Why didn't he invite [more] together with many? It occurred to him thus: "When many are seated, having given a little, while one is speaking, he will bring forth another *sūtra*, another cause, another such thing. Thus, there will be strife or even an uproar."
Even so, I will invite only one. Even so, blame will arise for me: 'This *abhayo* is stingy! Even having seen the Blessed One going about together with a hundred or even a thousand *bhikkhus* every day, he invites only one!'
 nimantesī.
"In this way, there will be no fault," having said thus, he invited *attacatuttha* together with the other three.

mula_pali: 85. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho abhayo rājakumāro bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘bhāseyya nu kho, bhante, tathāgato taṃ vācaṃ yā sā vācā paresaṃ appiyā amanāpā’’ti? ‘‘Na khvettha, rājakumāra, ekaṃsenā’’ti. ‘‘Ettha, bhante, anassuṃ nigaṇṭhā’’ti. ‘‘Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, rājakumāra, evaṃ vadesi – ‘ettha , bhante, anassuṃ nigaṇṭhā’’’ti? ‘‘Idhāhaṃ, bhante, yena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho maṃ, bhante, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto etadavoca – ‘ehi tvaṃ, rājakumāra, samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṃ āropehi. Evaṃ te kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggacchissati – abhayena rājakumārena samaṇassa gotamassa evaṃ mahiddhikassa evaṃ mahānubhāvassa vādo āropito’ti. Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhante, nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘yathā kathaṃ panāhaṃ , bhante, samaṇassa gotamassa evaṃ mahiddhikassa evaṃ mahānubhāvassa vādaṃ āropessāmī’ti? ‘Ehi tvaṃ, rājakumāra, yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ vadehi – bhāseyya nu kho, bhante, tathāgato taṃ vācaṃ yā sā vācā paresaṃ appiyā amanāpāti? Sace te samaṇo gotamo evaṃ puṭṭho evaṃ byākaroti – bhāseyya, rājakumāra, tathāgato taṃ vācaṃ yā sā vācā paresaṃ appiyā amanāpāti, tamenaṃ tvaṃ evaṃ vadeyyāsi – atha kiñcarahi te, bhante, puthujjanena nānākaraṇaṃ? Puthujjanopi hi taṃ vācaṃ bhāseyya yā sā vācā paresaṃ appiyā amanāpāti. Sace pana te samaṇo gotamo evaṃ puṭṭho evaṃ byākaroti – na, rājakumāra, tathāgato taṃ vācaṃ bhāseyya yā sā vācā paresaṃ appiyā amanāpāti, tamenaṃ tvaṃ evaṃ vadeyyāsi – atha kiñcarahi te, bhante, devadatto byākato – āpāyiko devadatto, nerayiko devadatto, kappaṭṭho devadatto, atekiccho devadattoti? Tāya ca pana te vācāya devadatto kupito ahosi anattamanoti. Imaṃ kho te, rājakumāra, samaṇo gotamo ubhatokoṭikaṃ pañhaṃ puṭṭho samāno neva sakkhiti uggilituṃ na sakkhiti ogilituṃ. Seyyathāpi nāma purisassa ayosiṅghāṭakaṃ kaṇṭhe vilaggaṃ, so neva sakkuṇeyya uggilituṃ na sakkuṇeyya ogilituṃ; evameva kho te, rājakumāra, samaṇo gotamo imaṃ ubhatokoṭikaṃ pañhaṃ puṭṭho samāno neva sakkhiti uggilituṃ na sakkhiti ogilitu’’’nti.
mula_english:
85. Having sat down to one side, Prince Abhaya said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, would the *Tathāgata* utter speech that is unwelcome and disagreeable to others?”

“Prince, there is no categorical answer to that.”

“Then, venerable sir, the *Nigaṇṭhas* have lost in this.”

“Why do you say this, prince: ‘Then, venerable sir, the *Nigaṇṭhas* have lost in this’?”

“Venerable sir, I went to where the *Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta* was; having gone there, I greeted the *Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta*, and sat down to one side.

Having sat down to one side, the *Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta* said this to me: ‘Come, prince, refute the doctrine of the *Śramaṇa Gotama*.

In this way, a good report of you will be spread: ‘Prince Abhaya has refuted the doctrine of the *Śramaṇa Gotama*, who is so powerful and mighty.’

When this was said, I said this to the *Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta*: ‘But how, venerable sir, could I refute the doctrine of the *Śramaṇa Gotama*, who is so powerful and mighty?’ ‘Come, prince, go to where the *Śramaṇa Gotama* is; having gone there, say this to the *Śramaṇa Gotama*: ‘Venerable sir, would the *Tathāgata* utter speech that is unwelcome and disagreeable to others?’ If the *Śramaṇa Gotama*, being asked thus, answers thus: ‘The *Tathāgata*, prince, would utter speech that is unwelcome and disagreeable to others,’ then you should say this to him: ‘Then in what way, venerable sir, is there any distinction for you from an ordinary person ( *pṛthagjana*)? For an ordinary person ( *pṛthagjana*) also would utter speech that is unwelcome and disagreeable to others.’

But if the *Śramaṇa Gotama*, being asked thus, answers thus: ‘No, prince, the *Tathāgata* would not utter speech that is unwelcome and disagreeable to others,’ then you should say this to him: ‘Then why, venerable sir, was Devadatta declared by you to be destined for the states of deprivation ( *āpāyika*), destined for hell ( *nerayika*), destined to remain in hell for the aeon ( *kappaṭṭha*), incorrigible ( *atekiccha*)?’ And Devadatta was angered and displeased by that speech of yours.

This two-horned question, prince, the *Śramaṇa Gotama*, being asked it, will not be able either to gulp it down or to throw it up.

Just as if an iron spike were stuck in a man’s throat, he would not be able either to gulp it down or to throw it up; so too, prince, the *Śramaṇa Gotama*, being asked this two-horned question, will not be able either to gulp it down or to throw it up.”
commentary_pali: 85.Na khvettha, rājakumāra, ekaṃsenāti na kho, rājakumāra, ettha pañhe ekaṃsena vissajjanaṃ hoti. Evarūpañhi vācaṃ tathāgato bhāseyyāpi na bhāseyyāpi. Bhāsitapaccayena atthaṃ passanto bhāseyya, apassanto na bhāseyyāti attho. Iti bhagavā mahānigaṇṭhena catūhi māsehi abhisaṅkhataṃ pañhaṃ asanipātena pabbatakūṭaṃ viya ekavacaneneva saṃcuṇṇesi. Anassuṃ nigaṇṭhāti naṭṭhā nigaṇṭhā.
commentary_english:
“There is no one-sided answer to that, prince.” ( *na khvettha, rājakumāra, ekaṃsenā* ti ) That is, prince, there is no one-sided answer to this question ( *pañha* ).

For the *tathāgata* might speak such words, and might not speak them.

The meaning is that one who, through the condition of what is spoken, sees the meaning ( *attha* ) might speak; one who does not see it might not speak.

Thus, the Blessed One ( *bhagavā* ) crushed the question ( *pañha* ) that Mahānigaṇṭha had pondered for four months with a single word, like a thunderbolt ( *asanipāta* ) [crushing] a mountain peak.

“The *nigaṇṭhas* were destroyed” ( *anassuṃ nigaṇṭhā* ti ): the *nigaṇṭhas* were ruined.

mula_pali: 86. Tena kho pana samayena daharo kumāro mando uttānaseyyako abhayassa rājakumārassa aṅke nisinno hoti. Atha kho bhagavā abhayaṃ rājakumāraṃ etadavoca – ‘‘taṃ kiṃ maññasi, rājakumāra, sacāyaṃ kumāro tuyhaṃ vā pamādamanvāya dhātiyā vā pamādamanvāya kaṭṭhaṃ vā kaṭhalaṃ kathalaṃ (ka.) vā mukhe āhareyya, kinti naṃ kareyyāsī’’ti? ‘‘Āhareyyassāhaṃ, bhante. Sace, bhante, na sakkuṇeyyaṃ ādikeneva āhattuṃ āharituṃ (syā. kaṃ.), vāmena hatthena sīsaṃ pariggahetvā paggahetvā (sī.) dakkhiṇena hatthena vaṅkaṅguliṃ karitvā salohitampi āhareyyaṃ. Taṃ kissa hetu? Atthi me, bhante, kumāre anukampā’’ti. ‘‘Evameva kho, rājakumāra, yaṃ tathāgato vācaṃ jānāti abhūtaṃ atacchaṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ sā ca paresaṃ appiyā amanāpā, na taṃ tathāgato vācaṃ bhāsati. Yampi tathāgato vācaṃ jānāti bhūtaṃ tacchaṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ sā ca paresaṃ appiyā amanāpā, tampi tathāgato vācaṃ na bhāsati. Yañca kho tathāgato vācaṃ jānāti bhūtaṃ tacchaṃ atthasaṃhitaṃ sā ca paresaṃ appiyā amanāpā, tatra kālaññū tathāgato hoti tassā vācāya veyyākaraṇāya. Yaṃ tathāgato vācaṃ jānāti abhūtaṃ atacchaṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ sā ca paresaṃ piyā manāpā, na taṃ tathāgato vācaṃ bhāsati. Yampi tathāgato vācaṃ jānāti bhūtaṃ tacchaṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ sā ca paresaṃ piyā manāpā tampi tathāgato vācaṃ na bhāsati. Yañca tathāgato vācaṃ jānāti bhūtaṃ tacchaṃ atthasaṃhitaṃ sā ca paresaṃ piyā manāpā, tatra kālaññū tathāgato hoti tassā vācāya veyyākaraṇāya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Atthi, rājakumāra, tathāgatassa sattesu anukampā’’ti.
mula_english:
Now on that occasion, a young, tender infant was lying prone on Prince Abhaya’s lap.

Then the Blessed One said to Prince Abhaya: “What do you think, prince? If, while you or your nurse were not attending to him, this child were to put a stick or a pebble in his mouth, what would you do to him?”

“I would take it out, venerable sir. If I could not take it out at once, I would take his head in my left hand, and crooking a finger of my right hand, I would take it out even if it meant drawing blood. Why is that? Because I have compassion for the child, venerable sir.”

“So too, prince, such speech as the *Tathāgata* knows to be untrue, incorrect, and unbeneficial, and which is also unwelcome and disagreeable to others: such speech the *Tathāgata* does not utter. Such speech as the *Tathāgata* knows to be true and correct but unbeneficial, and which is also unwelcome and disagreeable to others: such speech the *Tathāgata* does not utter. Such speech as the *Tathāgata* knows to be true, correct, and beneficial, but which is unwelcome and disagreeable to others: the *Tathāgata* knows the time to use such speech. Such speech as the *Tathāgata* knows to be untrue, incorrect, and unbeneficial, but which is welcome and agreeable to others: such speech the *Tathāgata* does not utter. Such speech as the *Tathāgata* knows to be true and correct but unbeneficial, and which is welcome and agreeable to others: such speech the *Tathāgata* does not utter. Such speech as the *Tathāgata* knows to be true, correct, and beneficial, and which is welcome and agreeable to others: the *Tathāgata* knows the time to use such speech. Why is that? Because the *Tathāgata* has compassion for beings, prince.”
commentary_pali:
86.Aṅke nisinno hotīti ūrūsu nisinno hoti. Lesavādino hi vādaṃ paṭṭhapentā kiñcideva phalaṃ vā pupphaṃ vā potthakaṃ vā gahetvā nisīdanti. Te attano jaye sati paraṃ ajjhottharanti, parassa jaye sati phalaṃ khādantā viya pupphaṃ ghāyantā viya potthakaṃ vācentā viya vikkhepaṃ dassenti. Ayaṃ pana cintesi – ‘‘sammāsambuddho esa osaṭasaṅgāmo paravādamaddano. Sace me jayo bhavissati, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce bhavissati, dārakaṃ vijjhitvā rodāpessāmi. Tato passatha, bho, ayaṃ dārako rodati, uṭṭhahatha tāva, pacchāpi jānissāmā’’ti tasmā dārakaṃ gahetvā nisīdi. Bhagavā pana rājakumārato sahassaguṇenapi satasahassaguṇenapi vādīvarataro, ‘‘imamevassa dārakaṃ upamaṃ katvā vādaṃ bhindissāmī’’ti cintetvā ‘‘taṃ kiṃ maññasi rājakumārā’’tiādimāha.

Tattha mukhe āhareyyāti mukhe ṭhapeyya. Āhareyyassāhanti apaneyyaṃ assa ahaṃ. Ādikenevāti paṭhamapayogeneva. Abhūtanti abhūtatthaṃ. Atacchanti na tacchaṃ. Anatthasaṃhitanti na atthasaṃhitaṃ na vaḍḍhinissitaṃ. Appiyā amanāpāti neva piyā na manāpā. Iminā nayeneva sabbattha attho daṭṭhabbo.

mukhe āhareyyā Āhareyyassāha Ādikenevā Abhūta Ataccha Anatthasaṃhita Appiyā amanāpā

Tattha appiyapakkhe paṭhamavācā acoraṃyeva coroti, adāsaṃyeva dāsoti, aduppayuttaṃyeva duppayuttoti pavattā. Na taṃ tathāgato bhāsati. Dutiyavācā coraṃyeva coro ayantiādivasena pavattā. Tampi tathāgato na bhāsati. Tatiyavācā ‘‘idāni akatapuññatāya duggato dubbaṇṇo appesakkho , idha ṭhatvāpi puna puññaṃ na karosi, dutiyacittavāre kathaṃ catūhi apāyehi na muccissasī’’ti evaṃ mahājanassa atthapurekkhārena dhammapurekkhārena anusāsanīpurekkhārena ca vattabbavācā. Tatra kālaññū tathāgatoti tasmiṃ tatiyabyākaraṇe tassā vācāya byākaraṇatthāya tathāgato kālaññū hoti, mahājanassa ādānakālaṃ gahaṇakālaṃ jānitvāva byākarotīti attho.

paṭhamavācā Dutiyavācā Tatiyavācā Tatra kālaññū tathāgato

Piyapakkhe paṭhamavācā aṭṭhāniyakathā nāma. Sā evaṃ veditabbā – evaṃ kira gāmavāsimahallakaṃ nagaraṃ āgantvā pānāgāre pivantaṃ vañcetukāmā sambahulā dhuttā pītaṭṭhāne ṭhatvā tena saddhiṃ suraṃ pivantā ‘‘imassa nivāsanapāvuraṇampi hatthe bhaṇḍakampi sabbaṃ gaṇhissāmā’’ti cintetvā katikaṃ akaṃsu – ‘‘ekekaṃ attapaccakkhakathaṃ kathema, yo ‘abhūta’nti kathesi, kathitaṃ vā na saddahati, taṃ dāsaṃ katvā gaṇhissāmā’’ti. Tampi mahallakaṃ pucchiṃsu ‘‘tumhākampi tāta ruccatī’’ti. Evaṃ hotu tātāti.

Eko dhutto āha – mayhaṃ, bho mātu, mayi kucchigate kapiṭṭhaphaladohalo ahosi. Sā aññaṃ kapiṭṭhahārakaṃ alabbhamānā maṃyeva pesesi. Ahaṃ gantvā rukkhaṃ abhiruhituṃ asakkonto attanāva attānaṃ pāde gahetvā muggaraṃ viya rukkhassa upari khipiṃ; atha sākhato sākhaṃ vicaranto phalāni gahetvā otarituṃ asakkonto gharaṃ gantvā nisseṇiṃ āharitvā oruyha mātu santikaṃ gantvā phalāni mātuyā adāsiṃ; tāni pana mahantāni honti cāṭippamāṇāni. Tato me mātarā ekāsane nisinnāya samasaṭṭhiphalāni khāditāni. Mayā ekucchaṅgena ānītaphalesu sesakāni kulasantake gāme khuddakamahallakānaṃ ahesuṃ. Amhākaṃ gharaṃ soḷasahatthaṃ, sesaparikkhārabhaṇḍakaṃ apanetvā kapiṭṭhaphaleheva yāva chadanaṃ pūritaṃ. Tato atirekāni gahetvā gehadvāre rāsiṃ akaṃsu. So asītihatthubbedho pabbato viya ahosi. Kiṃ īdisaṃ, bho sakkā, saddahitunti?

Gāmikamahallako tuṇhī nisīditvā sabbesaṃ kathāpariyosāne pucchito āha – ‘‘evaṃ bhavissati tātā, mahantaṃ raṭṭhaṃ, raṭṭhamahantatāya sakkā saddahitu’’nti. Yathā ca tena, evaṃ sesehipi tathārūpāsu nikkāraṇakathāsu kathitāsu āha – mayhampi tātā suṇātha, na tumhākaṃyeva kulāni, amhākampi kulaṃ mahākulaṃ, amhākaṃ pana avasesakhettehi kappāsakhettaṃ mahantataraṃ . Tassa anekakarīsasatassa kappāsakhettassa majjhe eko kappāsarukkho mahā asītihatthubbedho ahosi. Tassa pañca sākhā, tāsu avasesasākhā phalaṃ na gaṇhiṃsu, pācīnasākhāya ekameva mahācāṭimattaṃ phalaṃ ahosi. Tassa cha aṃsiyo, chasu aṃsīsu cha kappāsapiṇḍiyo pupphitā. Ahaṃ massuṃ kāretvā nhātavilitto khettaṃ gantvā tā kappāsapiṇḍiyo pupphitā disvā ṭhitakova hatthaṃ pasāretvā gaṇhiṃ. Tā kappāsapiṇḍiyo thāmasampannā cha dāsā ahesuṃ. Te sabbe maṃ ekakaṃ ohāya palātā. Ettake addhāne te na passāmi, ajja diṭṭhā, tumhe te cha janā. Tvaṃ nando nāma, tvaṃ puṇṇo nāma, tvaṃ vaḍḍhamāno nāma, tvaṃ citto nāma tvaṃ maṅgalo nāma, tvaṃ poṭṭhiyo nāmāti vatvā uṭṭhāya nisinnakeyeva cūḷāsu gahetvā aṭṭhāsi. Te ‘‘na mayaṃ dāsā’’tipi vattuṃ nāsakkhiṃsu. Atha ne kaḍḍhanto vinicchayaṃ netvā lakkhaṇaṃ āropetvā yāvajīvaṃ dāse katvā paribhuñji. Evarūpiṃ kathaṃ tathāgato na bhāsati.

Dutiyavācā āmisahetucāṭukamyatādivasena nānappakārā paresaṃ thomanavācā ceva, corakathaṃ rājakathanti ādinayappavattā tiracchānakathā ca. Tampi tathāgato na bhāsati. Tatiyavācā ariyasaccasannissitakathā, yaṃ vassasatampi suṇantā paṇḍitā neva tittiṃ gacchanti. Iti tathāgato neva sabbampi appiyavācaṃ bhāsati na piyavācaṃ. Tatiyaṃ tatiyameva pana bhāsitabbakālaṃ anatikkamitvā bhāsati. Tattha tatiyaṃ appiyavācaṃ sandhāya heṭṭhā daharakumāraupamā āgatāti veditabbaṃ.

Dutiyavācā Tatiyavācā
commentary_english:
86. "Sitting on the lap" means he sits on the thighs.

Fraudulent debaters, indeed, establishing a debate, taking some flower, fruit, or book, sit down.

They, when they themselves are victorious, boast, but when another is victorious, they show distraction as if eating fruit, smelling a flower, or reading a book.

Then he thought, "The *sammāsambuddha* is skilled in ending conflict, a destroyer of others' doctrines.

If victory is mine, that will be skillful.

If it is not, having pierced the boy, I will make him cry.

Then look, sirs, this boy is crying, get up quickly, later we will know" thus, having taken the boy, he sat down.

The Blessed One, however, is much more skilled in debate than the prince, even by a thousand qualities, even by a hundred thousand qualities, thinking, "Having made this boy an example, I will break the debate," he said, beginning with, "What do you think, prince?"

There, "*mukhe āhareyyā*" means he should place it in his mouth.

"*āhareyyassāha*" means I would remove it from him.

"*ādikenevā*" means with the first effort.

"*abhūta*" means untrue.

"*ataccha*" means not true.

"*anatthasaṃhita*" means not connected with benefit, not dependent on increase.

"*appiyā amanāpā*" means neither dear nor pleasing.

In this way, the meaning should be seen everywhere.

*mukhe āhareyyā āhareyyassāha ādikenevā abhūta ataccha anatthasaṃhita appiyā amanāpā*

There, on the unpleasant side, "*paṭhamavācā*" the first speech, is current, saying "He is a thief even though he is not a thief, he is a slave even though he is not a slave, he is misused even though he is not misused."

The *Tathāgata* does not speak that.

"*dutiyavācā*" the second speech, is current, with the phrase "He is a thief, indeed, who comes."

The *Tathāgata* does not speak that either.

"*tatiyavācā*" the third speech, "'Now, because of not doing merit, he is wretched, ugly, and of little power, even having stayed here, again you do not do merit; in the second thought moment, how will you not be freed from the four woeful courses?'" Thus, that is speech worthy of being spoken with regard to the benefit of the multitude, with regard to *dharma*, and with regard to instruction.

"*tatra kālaññū tathāgato*" means in that third explanation, for the sake of the explanation of that speech, the *Tathāgata* is timely, that is, knowing the time of the multitude's receiving and the time of grasping, he speaks.

*paṭhamavācā dutiyavācā tatiyavācā tatra kālaññū tathāgato*

On the pleasant side, the first speech is called the "base of establishment" (*aṭṭhāniyakathā*).

That should be understood thus – thus, it is said that many rogues, having come to a city, desiring to deceive an old villager drinking in a tavern, having stayed in a drinking place, drinking liquor with him, thinking, "We will take all of this one's dwelling, cloak, and goods in his hand," they made an agreement – "Let us each tell a story seen by ourselves; whoever says 'untrue', or does not believe what is said, having made him a slave, we will take him."

They asked that old man, "Does this please you, sir?"

Let it be so, sir.

One rogue said – "Sir, when my mother was pregnant with me, she had a craving for *kapiṭṭha* fruit.

She, not obtaining another *kapiṭṭha* gatherer, sent me myself.

I, having gone, being unable to climb the tree, taking myself by my feet, threw myself above the tree like a mallet; then, wandering from branch to branch, having taken the fruits, being unable to descend, having gone home, having brought a ladder, having descended, having gone to my mother's presence, I gave the fruits to my mother; those, however, were large, of the size of cooking pots.

Then, my mother, having sat down on one seat, ate sixty fruits together.

The remainder of the fruits brought by me in one lap, were for the small old people in the village belonging to the family.
Our house was sixteen *hattha*s, filled up to the roof with *kapittha* fruits after removing the remaining paraphernalia and goods.
Then, taking the surplus, they made a pile at the door of the house.
It was like a mountain eighty *hattha*s high.
"Is this believable, sir Sakkā?"

The village elder, sat silently and, at the end of the conversation of all those asked, said: "Yes, father, it will be. It is a large kingdom; because of the greatness of the kingdom, it is possible to believe."
As with him, so also with the others, when such groundless stories were told, he said: "Listen to me too, fathers. It is not only your families [that are great]; our family too is a great family. But our cotton field is much larger than the remaining fields."

In the middle of that cotton field of many hundreds of *karīsa*s, there was one great cotton tree, eighty *hattha*s high.
It had five branches; the remaining branches did not bear fruit, but the eastern branch had only one fruit, the size of a large bowl.
It had six filaments, and on the six filaments, six cotton bolls had flowered.
Having had my beard trimmed and anointed after bathing, I went to the field and, seeing those cotton bolls in bloom, stood there and stretched out my hand and took them.
Those cotton bolls, endowed with strength, became six slaves.
All of them deserted me alone and fled.
In so much time I did not see them, today they are seen, you are those six people.
You are named Nanda, you are named Puṇṇa, you are named Vaḍḍhamāna, you are named Citta, you are named Maṅgala, you are named Poṭṭhiya," he said, and rising up, having grabbed the hair knots of the ones who were still sitting, he stood there.
They could not even say, "We are not slaves."
Then, dragging them along, bringing them to a judgment, branding them with a mark, he made them slaves for life and enjoyed [their services].
How could the *Tathāgata* not speak such a thing?

The second speech, the speech of praise of others, of various kinds, based on greed for gifts, flattery, and so on, and also animal talk, which proceeds according to the principle beginning with thief talk, king talk, and so on.
That too, the *Tathāgata* does not speak.
The third speech [is] talk based on the Noble Truths; wise people never get tired of listening to it even for a hundred years.
Thus, the *Tathāgata* does not speak all unpleasant speech, nor pleasant speech.
The *Tathāgata* speaks the third [kind of speech] at the very time when it should be spoken, without transgressing the [proper] time for speaking.
There, it should be understood that the simile of the young boy has come down with reference to the third unpleasant speech.

Second speech, third speech

mula_pali:
87. ‘‘Yeme, bhante, khattiyapaṇḍitāpi brāhmaṇapaṇḍitāpi gahapatipaṇḍitāpi samaṇapaṇḍitāpi pañhaṃ abhisaṅkharitvā tathāgataṃ upasaṅkamitvā pucchanti, pubbeva nu kho, etaṃ, bhante , bhagavato cetaso parivitakkitaṃ hoti ‘ye maṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ pucchissanti tesāhaṃ evaṃ puṭṭho evaṃ byākarissāmī’ti, udāhu ṭhānasovetaṃ tathāgataṃ paṭibhātī’’ti?

‘‘Tena hi, rājakumāra, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi, yathā te khameyya tathā naṃ byākareyyāsi. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, rājakumāra, kusalo tvaṃ rathassa aṅgapaccaṅgāna’’nti?

‘‘Evaṃ, bhante, kusalo ahaṃ rathassa aṅgapaccaṅgāna’’nti.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, rājakumāra, ye taṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘kiṃ nāmidaṃ rathassa aṅgapaccaṅga’nti? Pubbeva nu kho te etaṃ cetaso parivitakkitaṃ assa ‘ye maṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ pucchissanti tesāhaṃ evaṃ puṭṭho evaṃ byākarissāmī’ti, udāhu ṭhānasovetaṃ paṭibhāseyyā’’ti?

‘‘Ahañhi, bhante, rathiko saññāto kusalo rathassa aṅgapaccaṅgānaṃ. Sabbāni me rathassa aṅgapaccaṅgāni suviditāni. Ṭhānasovetaṃ maṃ paṭibhāseyyā’’ti .

‘‘Evameva kho, rājakumāra, ye te khattiyapaṇḍitāpi brāhmaṇapaṇḍitāpi gahapatipaṇḍitāpi samaṇapaṇḍitāpi pañhaṃ abhisaṅkharitvā tathāgataṃ upasaṅkamitvā pucchanti, ṭhānasovetaṃ tathāgataṃ paṭibhāti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Sā hi, rājakumāra, tathāgatassa dhammadhātu suppaṭividdhā yassā dhammadhātuyā suppaṭividdhattā ṭhānasovetaṃ tathāgataṃ paṭibhātī’’ti.

Evaṃ vutte, abhayo rājakumāro bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante…pe… ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata’’nti.

Abhayarājakumārasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.
mula_english:
“Venerable sir, when learned nobles (*khattiya*), learned Brahmins (*brāhmaṇa*), learned householders (*gahapati*), and learned renunciates (*samaṇa*), after formulating a question (*pañhaṃ abhisaṅkharitvā*), then go to the *Tathāgata* and pose it, has there already been in the Blessed One’s (*bhagavato*) mind the thought (*parivitakkitaṃ hoti*): ‘If they come to me and ask me thus, I shall answer thus’? Or does that answer occur to the *Tathāgata* on the spot (*ṭhānasovetaṃ tathāgataṃ paṭibhātī*)?”

“Therefore, prince (*rājakumāra*), I will question you in return about that very thing here. You should explain it as it suits you. What do you think, prince? Are you skilled in the parts of a chariot (*rathassa aṅgapaccaṅgānaṃ*)?”

“Yes, venerable sir (*bhante*), I am skilled in the parts of a chariot (*rathassa aṅgapaccaṅgānaṃ*).”

“What do you think, prince? If they were to come to you and ask thus: ‘What is the name of this part of the chariot (*rathassa aṅgapaccaṅgaṃ*)?’ Has that already been thought out in your mind: ‘If they come to me and ask me thus, I shall answer thus,’ or would the answer occur to you on the spot (*ṭhānasovetaṃ paṭibhāseyyā*)?”

“Venerable sir, I am known as a chariot-maker (*rathiko*), skilled in the parts of a chariot (*rathassa aṅgapaccaṅgānaṃ*). All the parts of a chariot (*rathassa aṅgapaccaṅgāni*) are well known to me (*suviditāni*). The answer would occur to me on the spot (*ṭhānasovetaṃ maṃ paṭibhāseyyā*).”

“So too, prince (*rājakumāra*), when those learned nobles (*khattiya*), learned Brahmins (*brāhmaṇa*), learned householders (*gahapati*), and learned renunciates (*samaṇa*), after formulating a question (*pañhaṃ abhisaṅkharitvā*), then come to the *Tathāgata* and pose it, the answer occurs to the *Tathāgata* on the spot (*ṭhānasovetaṃ tathāgataṃ paṭibhāti*). Why is this so (*taṃ kissa hetu*)? That element of things (*dhammadhātu*) has been fully penetrated (*suppaṭividdhā*) by the *Tathāgata*, through the full penetration of which (*dhammadhātuyā suppaṭividdhattā*) the answer occurs to the *Tathāgata* on the spot (*ṭhānasovetaṃ tathāgataṃ paṭibhātī*).”

When this was said, Prince Abhaya said this to the Blessed One (*bhagavantaṃ*): “Excellent, venerable sir (*bhante*), excellent, venerable sir (*bhante*)… from today, I go to the Blessed One (*bhagavantaṃ*) for refuge (*saraṇaṃ gata*), taking refuge for life (*pāṇupetaṃ*).”

The Abhayarājakumārasutta, the eighth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
87.Udāhu ṭhānasovetanti udāhu ṭhānuppattikañāṇena taṅkhaṇaṃyeva taṃ tathāgatassa upaṭṭhātīti pucchati. Saññātoti ñāto paññāto pākaṭo. Dhammadhātūti dhammasabhāvo. Sabbaññutaññāṇassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ . Taṃ bhagavatā suppaṭividdhaṃ, hatthagataṃ bhagavato. Tasmā so yaṃ yaṃ icchati, taṃ taṃ sabbaṃ ṭhānasova paṭibhātīti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānameva. Ayaṃ pana dhammadesanā neyyapuggalavasena pariniṭṭhitāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Abhayarājakumārasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
87. "udāhu ṭhānasoveta" means, does it arise for the Tathāgata at that very moment through the knowledge of the arising of the basis? This is a question.

"saññāto" means known, understood, manifest.

"dhammadhātū" means the nature of the Dhamma (dharma).

This is a designation for the knowledge of omniscience. It is well-penetrated by the Blessed One, it is in the hand of the Blessed One. Therefore, whatever he wishes, all of that appears to him as a basis.

The rest is clear throughout.

This teaching of the Dhamma, however, is concluded in accordance with persons who need to be led (neyya-puggala).

The commentary on the Abhayarājakumāra Sutta in the Papañcasūdanī, the commentary on the Majjhima Nikāya, is finished.

mula_pali: 88. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho pañcakaṅgo thapati yenāyasmā udāyī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho pañcakaṅgo thapati āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘kati nu kho, bhante udāyi, vedanā vuttā bhagavatā’’ti? ‘‘Tisso kho, thapati gahapati (syā. kaṃ. pī.), vedanā vuttā bhagavatā. Sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā – imā kho, thapati, tisso vedanā vuttā bhagavatā’’ti. Evaṃ vutte, pañcakaṅgo thapati āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘na kho, bhante udāyi, tisso vedanā vuttā bhagavatā; dve vedanā vuttā bhagavatā – sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā. Yāyaṃ, bhante, adukkhamasukhā vedanā santasmiṃ esā paṇīte sukhe vuttā bhagavatā’’ti. Dutiyampi kho āyasmā udāyī pañcakaṅgaṃ thapatiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘na kho, gahapati, dve vedanā vuttā bhagavatā; tisso vedanā vuttā bhagavatā. Sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā – imā kho, thapati, tisso vedanā vuttā bhagavatā’’ti. Dutiyampi kho pañcakaṅgo thapati āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘na kho, bhante udāyi, tisso vedanā vuttā bhagavatā; dve vedanā vuttā bhagavatā – sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā. Yāyaṃ, bhante , adukkhamasukhā vedanā santasmiṃ esā paṇīte sukhe vuttā bhagavatā’’ti. Tatiyampi kho āyasmā udāyī pañcakaṅgaṃ thapatiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘na kho, thapati, dve vedanā vuttā bhagavatā; tisso vedanā vuttā bhagavatā. Sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā – imā kho, thapati, tisso vedanā vuttā bhagavatā’’ti. Tatiyampi kho pañcakaṅgo thapati āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘na kho, bhante udāyi, tisso vedanā vuttā bhagavatā, dve vedanā vuttā bhagavatā – sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā. Yāyaṃ, bhante, adukkhamasukhā vedanā santasmiṃ esā paṇīte sukhe vuttā bhagavatā’’ti. Neva kho sakkhi āyasmā udāyī pañcakaṅgaṃ thapatiṃ saññāpetuṃ na panāsakkhi pañcakaṅgo thapati āyasmantaṃ udāyiṃ saññāpetuṃ.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī (Śrāvastī) in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s (Anāthapiṇḍada's) monastery.

Then the carpenter Pañcakaṅga (Pāñcakaṅga) went to the venerable Udāyī; having approached, having greeted the venerable Udāyī, he sat down at a respectful distance.

Seated at a respectful distance, the carpenter Pañcakaṅga said this to the venerable Udāyī: "How many kinds of feeling (*vedanā*) have been stated by the Blessed One (bhagavat)?"

"There are three feelings, householder, stated by the Blessed One: pleasant feeling (*sukhā vedanā*), painful feeling (*duḥkhā vedanā*), and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (*adukkhamasukhā vedanā*). These, householder, are the three feelings stated by the Blessed One."

When this was said, the carpenter Pañcakaṅga said this to the venerable Udāyī: "Not three feelings have been stated by the Blessed One, venerable Udāyī; two feelings have been stated by the Blessed One: pleasant feeling and painful feeling.

That which is neither painful nor pleasant feeling, venerable sir, that peaceful and sublime pleasure has been stated by the Blessed One."

And a second time the venerable Udāyī said this to the carpenter Pañcakaṅga: "Not two feelings have been stated by the Blessed One, householder; three feelings have been stated by the Blessed One: pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. These, householder, are the three feelings stated by the Blessed One."

And a second time the carpenter Pañcakaṅga said this to the venerable Udāyī: "Not three feelings have been stated by the Blessed One, venerable Udāyī; two feelings have been stated by the Blessed One: pleasant feeling and painful feeling.

That which is neither painful nor pleasant feeling, venerable sir, that peaceful and sublime pleasure has been stated by the Blessed One."

And a third time the venerable Udāyī said this to the carpenter Pañcakaṅga: "Not two feelings have been stated by the Blessed One, householder; three feelings have been stated by the Blessed One: pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. These, householder, are the three feelings stated by the Blessed One."

And a third time the carpenter Pañcakaṅga said this to the venerable Udāyī: "Not three feelings have been stated by the Blessed One, venerable Udāyī; two feelings have been stated by the Blessed One: pleasant feeling and painful feeling.

That which is neither painful nor pleasant feeling, venerable sir, that peaceful and sublime pleasure has been stated by the Blessed One."

The venerable Udāyī was not able to convince the carpenter Pañcakaṅga, nor was the carpenter Pañcakaṅga able to convince the venerable Udāyī.
commentary_pali: 88.Evaṃme sutanti bahuvedanīyasuttaṃ. Tattha pañcakaṅgo thapatīti pañcakaṅgoti tassa nāmaṃ. Vāsipharasunikhādanadaṇḍamuggarakāḷasuttanāḷisaṅkhātehi vā aṅgehi samannāgatattā so pañcaṅgoti paññāto. Thapatīti vaḍḍhakījeṭṭhako. Udāyīti paṇḍitaudāyitthero.
commentary_english:
88.
Thus, I have heard: the Bahuvedanīya Sūtra.
There, Pañcakaṅga Thapatī: Pañcakaṅga is his name.
Because he is endowed with limbs known as a carpenter's axe, shield, sunikhādana, staff, club, black thread, and pipe, therefore he is known as Pañcaṅga.
Thapatī means the chief carpenter.
Udāyī means Paṇḍitaudāyitthera.

mula_pali: 89. Assosi kho āyasmā ānando āyasmato udāyissa pañcakaṅgena thapatinā saddhiṃ imaṃ kathāsallāpaṃ. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando yāvatako ahosi āyasmato udāyissa pañcakaṅgena thapatinā saddhiṃ kathāsallāpo taṃ sabbaṃ bhagavato ārocesi. Evaṃ vutte, bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘santaññeva kho, ānanda, pariyāyaṃ pañcakaṅgo thapati udāyissa nābbhanumodi, santaññeva ca pana pariyāyaṃ udāyī pañcakaṅgassa thapatissa nābbhanumodi. Dvepānanda, vedanā vuttā mayā pariyāyena , tissopi vedanā vuttā mayā pariyāyena, pañcapi vedanā vuttā mayā pariyāyena, chapi vedanā vuttā mayā pariyāyena, aṭṭhārasapi vedanā vuttā mayā pariyāyena, chattiṃsapi vedanā vuttā mayā pariyāyena, aṭṭhasatampi vedanā vuttā mayā pariyāyena. Evaṃ pariyāyadesito kho, ānanda, mayā dhammo. Evaṃ pariyāyadesite kho, ānanda, mayā dhamme ye aññamaññassa subhāsitaṃ sulapitaṃ na samanujānissanti na samanumaññissanti na samanumodissanti tesametaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharissanti. Evaṃ pariyāyadesito kho, ānanda, mayā dhammo. Evaṃ pariyāyadesite kho, ānanda, mayā dhamme ye aññamaññassa subhāsitaṃ sulapitaṃ samanujānissanti samanumaññissanti samanumodissanti tesametaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā khīrodakībhūtā aññamaññaṃ piyacakkhūhi sampassantā viharissanti’’.
mula_english:
The venerable Ānanda heard this conversation between the venerable Udāyi and the carpenter Pañcakaṅga.

Then the venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One; having approached, he respectfully greeted the Blessed One and sat down to one side.

Seated to one side, the venerable Ānanda reported to the Blessed One the entire conversation between the venerable Udāyi and the carpenter Pañcakaṅga.

When this was said, the Blessed One said to the venerable Ānanda: "Ānanda, the carpenter Pañcakaṅga did not approve of Udāyi's approach, and Udāyi did not approve of the carpenter Pañcakaṅga's approach.

"Ānanda, feeling (vedanā) has been explained by me in two ways, in three ways, in five ways, in six ways, in eighteen ways, in thirty-six ways, and in one hundred and eight ways.

Ānanda, the Dhamma has been shown by me in different presentations (pariyāyadesito).

Ānanda, when the Dhamma has thus been shown by me in different presentations, it may be expected of those who will not concede, allow, and accept what is well stated and well spoken by others that they will take to quarreling, brawling, and disputing, stabbing each other with verbal daggers.

Ānanda, the Dhamma has been shown by me in different presentations (pariyāyadesito).

Ānanda, when the Dhamma has thus been shown by me in different presentations, it may be expected of those who will concede, allow, and accept what is well stated and well spoken by others that they will live in concord, rejoicing, without dispute, like milk and water, regarding each other with loving eyes."
commentary_pali: 89.Pariyāyanti kāraṇaṃ. Dvepānandāti dvepi, ānanda. Pariyāyenāti kāraṇena. Ettha ca kāyikacetasikavasena dve veditabbā. Sukhādivasena tisso, indriyavasena sukhindriyādikā pañca, dvāravasena cakkhusamphassajādikā cha, upavicāravasena ‘‘cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā somanassaṭṭhāniyaṃ rūpaṃ upavicaratī’’tiādikā aṭṭhārasa, cha gehassitāni somanassāni, cha nekkhammasitāni somanassāni, cha gehassitāni domanassāni, cha nekkhammasitāni domanassāni, cha gehassitā upekkhā, cha nekkhammasitāti evaṃ chattiṃsa, tā atīte chattiṃsa, anāgate chattiṃsa, paccuppanne chattiṃsāti evaṃ aṭṭhavedanāsataṃ veditabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
89. *pariyāya* means cause.

*dvepānandā* means dvepi, Ānanda.

*pariyāyenā* means *kāraṇena*.

Here, two (*dve*) should be understood in terms of physical and mental.

Three (*tisso*) in terms of pleasure, etc., five (*pañca*) in terms of the senses, such as the pleasure faculty, six (*cha*) in terms of the gateways, such as those born of eye-contact (*cakṣusamphassajādikā*), eighteen (*aṭṭhārasa*) in terms of investigation (*upavicāravasena*), such as "having seen a form with the eye, he investigates a form that is a cause for joy (*somanassaṭṭhāniyaṃ rūpaṃ upavicarati*)," six joys (*somanassāni*) dependent on the household, six joys dependent on renunciation, six displeasures (*domanassāni*) dependent on the household, six displeasures dependent on renunciation, six neutral feelings (*upekkhā*) dependent on the household, six dependent on renunciation, thus thirty-six (*chattiṃsa*), those thirty-six in the past, thirty-six in the future, thirty-six in the present, thus one hundred and eight feelings (*aṭṭhavedanāsataṃ*) should be understood.

mula_pali:
90. ‘‘Pañca kho ime, ānanda, kāmaguṇā. Katame pañca? Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā, sotaviññeyyā saddā…pe… ghānaviññeyyā gandhā…pe… jivhāviññeyyā rasā…pe… kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā – ime kho, ānanda, pañca kāmaguṇā. Yaṃ kho, ānanda, ime pañca kāmaguṇe paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ idaṃ vuccati kāmasukhaṃ.

‘‘Yo kho, ānanda, evaṃ vadeyya – ‘etaparamaṃ sattā sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedentī’ti, idamassa nānujānāmi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Atthānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca. Katamañcānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca?
