Idhānanda, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati . Idaṃ kho, ānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca.

‘‘Yo kho, ānanda, evaṃ vadeyya – ‘etaparamaṃ sattā sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedentī’ti, idamassa nānujānāmi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Atthānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca. Katamañcānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca? Idhānanda, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca.

‘‘Yo kho, ānanda, evaṃ vadeyya…pe…. Katamañcānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca? Idhānanda, bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca.

‘‘Yo kho, ānanda, evaṃ vadeyya…pe…. Katamañcānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca? Idhānanda, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca.

‘‘Yo kho, ānanda, evaṃ vadeyya…pe…. Katamañcānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca ? Idhānanda, bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā, paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā, nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca.

‘‘Yo kho, ānanda, evaṃ vadeyya…pe…. Katamañcānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca? Idhānanda, bhikkhu sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca.

‘‘Yo kho, ānanda, evaṃ vadeyya…pe…. Katamañcānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca? Idhānanda, bhikkhu sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca.

‘‘Yo kho, ānanda, evaṃ vadeyya…pe…. Katamañcānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca? Idhānanda, bhikkhu sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca.

‘‘Yo kho, ānanda, evaṃ vadeyya – ‘etaparamaṃ sattā sukhaṃ somanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedentī’ti, idamassa nānujānāmi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Atthānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca. Katamañcānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca? Idhānanda, bhikkhu sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, etamhā sukhā aññaṃ sukhaṃ abhikkantatarañca paṇītatarañca.
mula_english:
90. “Ānanda, there are these five cords of sensual pleasure.

Which five? Forms cognizable by the eye that are wished for, desired, agreeable, and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust. Sounds cognizable by the ear… Odours cognizable by the nose…Flavours cognizable by the tongue… Tangibles cognizable by the body that are wished for, desired, agreeable, and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust. These are the five cords of sensual pleasure. Now the pleasure and joy that arise dependent on these five cords of sensual pleasure are called sensual pleasure (*kāmasukha*).

“Should anyone say: ‘That is the utmost pleasure and joy that beings experience.’ I would not concede that to him.

Why is that? Because, Ānanda, there is another kind of pleasure loftier and more sublime than that pleasure.

And what is that other kind of pleasure? Here, Ānanda, a monk, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states of mind, enters and abides in the first *jhāna*, which is accompanied by thought and investigation, born of seclusion, and filled with joy (*prīti*) and pleasure (*sukha*).

This is that other kind of pleasure loftier and more sublime than the previous pleasure.

“Should anyone say…

And what is that other kind of pleasure? Here, Ānanda, a monk, with the stilling of thought and investigation… enters and abides in the second *jhāna*.

This is that other kind of pleasure loftier and more sublime than the previous pleasure.

“Should anyone say…

And what is that other kind of pleasure? Here, Ānanda, a monk, with the fading away of joy (*prīti*)… enters and abides in the third *jhāna*.

This is that other kind of pleasure loftier and more sublime than the previous pleasure.

“Should anyone say…

And what is that other kind of pleasure? Here, Ānanda, a monk, with the giving up of pleasure (*sukha*)… enters and abides in the fourth *jhāna*.

This is that other kind of pleasure loftier and more sublime than the previous pleasure.

“Should anyone say…

And what is that other kind of pleasure? Here, Ānanda, a monk, by completely transcending all perceptions of form, by the disappearance of the perceptions of sense-reaction, and by giving no attention to diversity-perceptions, aware that ‘Space is infinite,’ attains to and abides in the sphere of infinite space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*).

This is that other kind of pleasure loftier and more sublime than the previous pleasure.

“Should anyone say…

And what is that other kind of pleasure? Here, Ānanda, a monk, by completely transcending the sphere of infinite space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*), aware that ‘Consciousness is infinite,’ attains to and abides in the sphere of infinite consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatana*).

This is that other kind of pleasure loftier and more sublime than the previous pleasure.

“Should anyone say…

And what is that other kind of pleasure? Here, Ānanda, a monk, by completely transcending the sphere of infinite consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatana*), aware that ‘There is nothing,’ attains to and abides in the sphere of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*).

This is that other kind of pleasure loftier and more sublime than the previous pleasure.

“Should
“Should anyone say… Ānanda, if anyone should say…
And what, Ānanda, is that other kind of pleasure loftier and more sublime than that pleasure? Here, Ānanda, a *bhikṣu*, by completely transcending the dimension of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*) enters upon and abides in the dimension of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*).
This is that other kind of pleasure loftier and more sublime than the previous pleasure.

“Ānanda, if anyone should say: ‘That is the utmost pleasure (*sukha*) and joy (*somanassa*) that beings experience.’ I would not concede that to him.
And what is the reason for that? Because, Ānanda, there is another kind of pleasure loftier and more sublime than that pleasure.
And what, Ānanda, is that other kind of pleasure loftier and more sublime than that pleasure? Here, Ānanda, a *bhikṣu*, by completely surmounting the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*), enters upon and abides in the cessation of perception and feeling (saññāvedayitanirodha).
This is that other kind of pleasure loftier and more sublime than the previous pleasure.
commentary_pali:
90.Pañca kho ime, ānanda, kāmaguṇāti ayaṃ pāṭiekko anusandhi. Na kevalampi dve ādiṃ katvā vedanā bhagavatā paññattā, pariyāyena ekāpi vedanā kathitā. Taṃ dassento pañcakaṅgassa thapatino vādaṃ upatthambhetuṃ imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi.

Abhikkantataranti sundarataraṃ. Paṇītataranti atappakataraṃ. Ettha ca catutthajjhānato paṭṭhāya adukkhamasukhā vedanā, sāpi santaṭṭhena paṇītaṭṭhena ca sukhanti vuttā. Cha gehassitāni sukhanti vuttāni. Nirodho avedayitasukhavasena sukhaṃ nāma jāto. Pañcakāmaguṇavasena hi aṭṭhasamāpattivasena ca uppannaṃ vedayitasukhaṃ nāma. Nirodho avedayitasukhaṃ nāma. Iti vedayitasukhaṃ vā hotu avedayitasukhaṃ vā, taṃ niddukkhabhāvasaṅkhātena sukhaṭṭhena ekantasukhameva jātaṃ.

Abhikkantatara Paṇītatara
commentary_english:
90. “Ānanda, there are these five cords of sensual pleasure (kāmaguṇā).” This is a connected account.

Not only were two kinds of feeling (vedanā) described by the Blessed One by making a beginning, but one kind of feeling was also spoken of by a method. Showing that, he began this teaching in order to support the master carpenter's statement about the five factors.

"More lovely (abhikkantatara)" means more beautiful.

"More exquisite (paṇītatara)" means more unheated.

And here, from the fourth *dhyāna* onward, there is a feeling of neither-pain-nor-pleasure (adukkhamasukhā vedanā); that, too, is called pleasure in the sense of contentment and in the sense of exquisiteness.

Six kinds of domestic pleasures are called pleasure.

Cessation (nirodho), by means of pleasure without feeling (*avedayitasukha*), is known as bliss (sukhaṃ nāma jāto).

Indeed, by means of the five cords of sensual pleasure (*pañcakāmaguṇavasena*), and by means of the attainment of the eight attainments (*aṭṭhasamāpattivasena*), what arises is known as pleasure with feeling (*vedayitasukhaṃ nāma*).

Cessation (*nirodho*) is known as pleasure without feeling (*avedayitasukhaṃ nāma*).

Thus, whether it is pleasure with feeling (*vedayitasukhaṃ*) or pleasure without feeling (*avedayitasukhaṃ*), that, by the designation of a state without suffering (*niddukkhabhāvasaṅkhātena*), is truly known as one-sided pleasure (*ekantasukhameva jātaṃ*), in the sense of happiness (*sukhaṭṭhena*).

More lovely (abhikkantatara). More exquisite (paṇītatara).

mula_pali:
91. ‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, ānanda, vijjati yaṃ aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samaṇo gotamo āha; tañca sukhasmiṃ paññapeti. Tayidaṃ kiṃsu, tayidaṃ kathaṃsū’ti? Evaṃvādino, ānanda, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evamassu vacanīyā – ‘na kho, āvuso, bhagavā sukhaṃyeva vedanaṃ sandhāya sukhasmiṃ paññapeti; api ca, āvuso, yattha yattha sukhaṃ upalabbhati yahiṃ yahiṃ taṃ taṃ tathāgato sukhasmiṃ paññapetī’’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā ānando bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Bahuvedanīyasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.
mula_english:
“It is possible, Ānanda, that wanderers of other sects might speak thus: ‘The recluse Gotama speaks of the cessation of perception and feeling (saññāvedayitanirodha) and he describes that as pleasure (sukha). What is this? How is this?’ Ānanda, wanderers of other sects who speak thus should be told: ‘Friends, the Blessed One (bhagavā) describes pleasure (sukha) not only with reference to pleasant feeling; rather, friends, the *Tathāgata* describes as pleasure any kind of pleasure wherever and in whatever way it is found.’”

The Blessed One (bhagavā) spoke thus.

The venerable Ānanda, being pleased, rejoiced in the Blessed One’s (bhagavato) words (bhāsitaṃ).

The *Bahuvedanīya Sutta*, the ninth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
91.Yatthayatthāti yasmiṃ yasmiṃ ṭhāne. Sukhaṃ upalabbhatīti vedayitasukhaṃ vā avedayitasukhaṃ vā upalabbhati. Taṃ taṃ tathāgato sukhasmiṃ paññapetīti taṃ sabbaṃ tathāgato niddukkhabhāvaṃ sukhasmiṃyeva paññapetīti. Idha bhagavā nirodhasamāpattiṃ sīsaṃ katvā neyyapuggalavasena arahattanikūṭeneva desanaṃ niṭṭhāpesīti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Bahuvedanīyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

mula_pali: 92. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosalesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena sālā nāma kosalānaṃ brāhmaṇagāmo tadavasari. Assosuṃ kho sāleyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā – ‘‘samaṇo khalu bho gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito kosalesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ sālaṃ anuppatto. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. So imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti. So dhammaṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāseti. Sādhu kho pana tathārūpānaṃ arahataṃ dassanaṃ hotī’’ti. Atha kho sāleyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā appekacce bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu; sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce bhagavato santike nāmagottaṃ sāvetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce tuṇhībhūtā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu.
mula_english:
92. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was wandering in the Kosala country with a large Saṅgha of monks, and he arrived at a town of Brahmins in Kosala, called Sāla.

The householders who were Brahmins of Sāla heard, "The ascetic Gotama, the son of the Sakyans, who went forth from the Sakyan clan, is wandering in the Kosala country with a large Saṅgha of monks, and has arrived at Sāla."

Now a good report of that Blessed Gotama has spread to this effect: 'Indeed, the Blessed One is an *arhat*, a perfectly enlightened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, a Well-Farer, knower of the worlds, unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, enlightened, blessed.' ( *arahant* = worthy one)

He, having realized it by his own super-knowledge, proclaims this world with its gods ( *devas*), Māras, and Brahmās, its ascetics and Brahmins, its princes and people.

He teaches the Dhamma ( *dharma*) that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing; he reveals the spiritual life ( *brahmacariya*) that is utterly perfect and pure.

"It is good to see such *arahants*."

Then the householders of Sāla, who were Brahmins, went to the Blessed One. On arrival, some bowed down to the Blessed One and sat to one side. Some exchanged greetings with the Blessed One, and when this courteous and amiable talk was finished, sat down to one side. Some extended their hands in reverential salutation towards the Blessed One and sat down to one side.

Some announced their name and clan in the Blessed One's presence and sat down to one side. Some kept silent and sat down to one side.
commentary_pali: 92.Evaṃme sutanti apaṇṇakasuttaṃ. Tattha cārikanti aturitacārikaṃ.
commentary_english: 92. *evaṃ me suta* is the Apaṇṇaka Sutta. There, *cārika* means unhurried wandering.

mula_pali: 93. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho sāleyyake brāhmaṇagahapatike bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘atthi pana vo, gahapatayo, koci manāpo satthā yasmiṃ vo ākāravatī saddhā paṭiladdhā’’ti? ‘‘Natthi kho no, bhante, koci manāpo satthā yasmiṃ no ākāravatī saddhā paṭiladdhā’’ti. ‘‘Manāpaṃ vo, gahapatayo, satthāraṃ alabhantehi ayaṃ apaṇṇako dhammo samādāya vattitabbo. Apaṇṇako hi, gahapatayo, dhammo samatto samādinno, so vo bhavissati dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya. Katamo ca, gahapatayo, apaṇṇako dhammo’’?
mula_english:
93. As the Blessed One was sitting to one side with the householders and Brahmins of Sāleyyaka, he said to them: “Householders, is there any teacher agreeable to you in whom you have found grounded conviction (ākāravatī śraddhā)?” “No, venerable sir, there is no agreeable teacher in whom we have found grounded conviction.”

“As you have not found an agreeable teacher, you should adopt and practice this safe-bet teaching (apaṇṇako dharma),
for this safe-bet teaching (apaṇṇako dharma)—when accepted and adopted—will be to your long-term welfare and happiness (hitāya sukhāya).
And what is the safe-bet teaching (apaṇṇako dharma)?”
commentary_pali: 93.Atthi pana vo gahapatayoti kasmā āha? So kira gāmo aṭavidvāre niviṭṭho. Nānāvidhā samaṇabrāhmaṇā divasaṃ maggaṃ gantvā sāyaṃ taṃ gāmaṃ vāsatthāya upenti, tesaṃ te manussā mañcapīṭhāni pattharitvā pāde dhovitvā pāde makkhetvā kappiyapānakāni datvā punadivase nimantetvā dānaṃ denti. Te pasannacittā tehi saddhiṃ sammantayamānā evaṃ vadanti ‘‘atthi pana vo gahapatayo kiñci dassanaṃ gahita’’nti? Natthi, bhanteti. ‘‘Gahapatayo vinā dassanena loko na niyyāti, ekaṃ dassanaṃ ruccitvā khamāpetvā gahetuṃ vaṭṭati, ‘sassato loko’ti dassanaṃ gaṇhathā’’ti vatvā pakkantā. Aparadivase aññe āgatā. Tepi tatheva pucchiṃsu. Te tesaṃ ‘‘āma, bhante, purimesu divasesu tumhādisā samaṇabrāhmaṇā āgantvā ‘sassato loko’ti amhe idaṃ dassanaṃ gāhāpetvā gatā’’ti ārocesuṃ. ‘‘Te bālā kiṃ jānanti? ‘Ucchijjati ayaṃ loko’ti ucchedadassanaṃ gaṇhathā’’ti evaṃ tepi ucchedadassanaṃ gaṇhāpetvā pakkantā. Etenupāyena aññe ekaccasassataṃ, aññe antānantaṃ , aññe amarāvikkhepanti evaṃ dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhiyo uggaṇhāpesuṃ. Te pana ekadiṭṭhiyampi patiṭṭhātuṃ nāsakkhiṃsu. Sabbapacchā bhagavā agamāsi. So tesaṃ hitatthāya pucchanto ‘‘atthi pana vo gahapatayo’’tiādimāha. Tattha ākāravatīti kāraṇavatī sahetukā. Apaṇṇakoti aviraddho advejjhagāmī ekaṃsagāhiko.
commentary_english:
93. Why did he say, "Are there householders present?" It seems that the village was situated at the Aṭavī gate.

Various *śramaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas* went on the road during the day, and in the evening they approached that village for lodging. Those people spread out seats and benches for them, washed their feet, anointed their feet, gave them suitable drinks, and invited them for the next day, giving alms.

Those with pleased minds, consulting with them, said thus: "Is there any doctrine accepted by you householders?" "No, venerable sirs."

"Householders, without a doctrine, the world does not proceed. It is fitting to accept one doctrine, having approved and condoned it. Accept the doctrine, 'The world is eternal!'" So saying, they departed.

On the next day, others came.

They asked the same way.

They told them, "Yes, venerable sirs, on previous days, *śramaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas* like you came and made us accept this doctrine, 'The world is eternal!' and left."

"What do those fools know? Accept the doctrine of annihilation, 'This world is annihilated!'" Thus, they too, having made [them] accept the doctrine of annihilation, departed.

In this way, some [taught] eternalism in some respects, others [taught] the infinity of the end, others [taught] the sport of the immortals. Thus, they taught sixty-two views.

But they were not able to be established in even one view.

The Blessed One came last of all.

He, asking for their benefit, spoke, beginning with "Are there householders?"

There, *ākāravatī* means having a cause (*kāraṇavatī*), having a reason (*sahetukā*).

*Apaṇṇaka* means non-erroneous (*aviraddha*), going to the non-dual (*advejjhagāmī*), grasping the one aspect (*ekaṃsagāhiko*).

mula_pali: 94. ‘‘Santi , gahapatayo, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ, natthi hutaṃ; natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ sukaṭadukkaṭānaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko, natthi ayaṃ loko, natthi paro loko; natthi mātā, natthi pitā; natthi sattā opapātikā; natthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā samaggatā (ka.) sammā paṭipannā ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti. Tesaṃyeva kho, gahapatayo, samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā ujuvipaccanīkavādā. Te evamāhaṃsu – ‘atthi dinnaṃ, atthi yiṭṭhaṃ, atthi hutaṃ; atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko; atthi ayaṃ loko, atthi paro loko; atthi mātā, atthi pitā; atthi sattā opapātikā; atthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammā paṭipannā ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, gahapatayo – ‘nanume samaṇabrāhmaṇā aññamaññassa ujuvipaccanīkavādā’’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’.
mula_english:
94. Householders, there are some ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* who maintain the following doctrine and view: ‘There is nothing given, nothing offered, nothing sacrificed. There is no fruit or result of good or bad actions. There is no this world, no next world, no mother, no father; there are no spontaneously reborn beings; there are no ascetics or *brāhmaṇas* in the world who have rightly attained and practice rightly, and who after having directly known and realized this world and the next, proclaim them.’

However, householders, there are other ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* who hold directly opposing views. They say: ‘There is what is given, what is offered, what is sacrificed. There are fruits and results of good and bad actions. There is this world and the next world. There is mother and father. There are spontaneously reborn beings; there are ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* in the world who have rightly attained and practice rightly, and who after having directly known and realized this world and the next, proclaim them.’

What do you think, householders? Are not the assertions of these ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* directly opposed to one another?" "Yes, venerable sir."
commentary_pali: 94.Natthi dinnantiādi dasavatthukā micchādiṭṭhi heṭṭhā sāleyyakasutte vitthāritā. Tathā tabbipaccanīkabhūtā sammādiṭṭhi.
commentary_english: "natthi dinna" etc., the ten-factored wrong view, is extensively explained in the Sāleyyaka Sutta below. Likewise, the opposite of that, the right view (sammādiṭṭhi).

mula_pali:
95. ‘‘Tatra, gahapatayo, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ…pe… ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti tesametaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ? Yamidaṃ yadidaṃ (ka.) kāyasucaritaṃ, vacīsucaritaṃ, manosucaritaṃ – ime tayo kusale dhamme abhinivajjetvā abhinibbajjetvā (syā. kaṃ.), abhinibbijjitvā (ka.) yamidaṃ yadidaṃ (ka.) kāyaduccaritaṃ, vacīduccaritaṃ, manoduccaritaṃ – ime tayo akusale dhamme samādāya vattissanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Na hi te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā passanti akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ vodānapakkhaṃ. Santaṃyeva pana paraṃ lokaṃ ‘natthi paro loko’ tissa diṭṭhi hoti; sāssa hoti micchādiṭṭhi. Santaṃyeva kho pana paraṃ lokaṃ ‘natthi paro loko’ti saṅkappeti; svāssa hoti micchāsaṅkappo. Santaṃyeva kho pana paraṃ lokaṃ ‘natthi paro loko’ti vācaṃ bhāsati; sāssa hoti micchāvācā. Santaṃyeva kho pana paraṃ lokaṃ ‘natthi paro loko’ti āha; ye te arahanto paralokaviduno tesamayaṃ paccanīkaṃ karoti. Santaṃyeva kho pana paraṃ lokaṃ ‘natthi paro loko’ti paraṃ saññāpeti paññāpeti (ka.); sāssa hoti asaddhammasaññatti assaddhammapaññatti (ka.). Tāya ca pana asaddhammasaññattiyā attānukkaṃseti, paraṃ vambheti. Iti pubbeva kho panassa susīlyaṃ pahīnaṃ hoti, dussīlyaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ – ayañca micchādiṭṭhi micchāsaṅkappo micchāvācā ariyānaṃ paccanīkatā asaddhammasaññatti attukkaṃsanā paravambhanā. Evamassime evaṃ’si’me’ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti micchādiṭṭhipaccayā.

‘‘Tatra , gahapatayo, viññū puriso iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘sace kho natthi paro loko evamayaṃ bhavaṃ purisapuggalo kāyassa bhedā sotthimattānaṃ karissati; sace kho atthi paro loko evamayaṃ bhavaṃ purisapuggalo kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjissati. Kāmaṃ kho pana māhu paro loko, hotu nesaṃ bhavataṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ saccaṃ vacanaṃ; atha ca panāyaṃ bhavaṃ purisapuggalo diṭṭheva dhamme viññūnaṃ gārayho – dussīlo purisapuggalo micchādiṭṭhi natthikavādo’ti. Sace kho attheva paro loko, evaṃ imassa bhoto purisapuggalassa ubhayattha kaliggaho – yañca diṭṭheva dhamme viññūnaṃ gārayho, yañca kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjissati. Evamassāyaṃ apaṇṇako dhammo dussamatto samādinno, ekaṃsaṃ pharitvā tiṭṭhati, riñcati kusalaṃ ṭhānaṃ.
mula_english:
95.   “Now, householders, those ascetics and Brahmins who speak thus, who hold such views—’There is nothing given, there is nothing offered’…and so on… ‘those who declare this world and the next, having directly known and realized them by themselves with higher knowledge’—what is to be expected of them? That is, good bodily conduct *kāyasucarita*, good verbal conduct *vacīsucarita*, good mental conduct *manosucarita*—having abandoned these three wholesome dharmas, and having adopted bad bodily conduct *kāyaduccarita*, bad verbal conduct *vacīduccarita*, bad mental conduct *manoduccarita*—they will live according to these three unwholesome dharmas.

What is the reason for this? It is because those venerable ascetics and Brahmins do not see the danger, inferiority, and defilement in unwholesome dharmas, and the benefit, the cleansing side of renunciation in wholesome dharmas.

Indeed, while there is another world *paraṃ lokaṃ*, the view arises in him that ‘there is no other world *paro loko*’; that is his wrong view *micchādiṭṭhi*.

Indeed, while there is another world *paraṃ lokaṃ*, he resolves that ‘there is no other world *paro loko*’; that is his wrong resolve *micchāsaṅkappo*.

Indeed, while there is another world *paraṃ lokaṃ*, he utters the speech that ‘there is no other world *paro loko*’; that is his wrong speech *micchāvācā*.

Indeed, while there is another world *paraṃ lokaṃ*, he says that ‘there is no other world *paro loko*’; he makes himself an opponent of those ascetics (arahants) who know the other world *paralokaviduno*.

Indeed, while there is another world *paraṃ lokaṃ*, he persuades another that ‘there is no other world *paro loko*’; that is persuasion in what is not true Dhamma *asaddhammasaññatti*.

And through that persuasion in what is not true Dhamma *asaddhammasaññattiyā*, he exalts himself and disparages others.

Thus, even earlier his good morality *susīlyaṃ* is abandoned, and bad morality *dussīlyaṃ* arises. And this wrong view *micchādiṭṭhi*, wrong resolve *micchāsaṅkappo*, wrong speech *micchāvācā*, opposition to the noble ones (ariyānaṃ), persuasion in what is not true Dhamma *asaddhammasaññatti*, self-exaltation *attukkaṃsanā*, and disparagement of others *paravambhanā*—

Thus, in him, these many evil unwholesome dharmas arise, conditioned by wrong view *micchādiṭṭhipaccayā*.

“Now, householders, a wise person reflects thus: ‘If there is no other world *paro loko*, then this good person, this individual, at the breaking up of the body, will keep himself in safety; but if there is another world *paro loko*, then this good person, this individual, at the breaking up of the body, after death, will go to a state of loss (apāyaṃ), a bad destiny (duggatiṃ), a downfall (vinipātaṃ), hell (nirayaṃ).

Even if there is no other world *paro loko*, let the word of those ascetics and Brahmins be true; nevertheless, this good person, this individual, is still censured in this very life by the wise: ‘A person of bad character (dussīlo), a person of wrong view (micchādiṭṭhi), an annihilationist (natthikavādo).’

And if indeed there is another world *paro loko*, then for this good person, this individual, there is a losing throw in both respects: in that he is censured in this very life by the wise, and in that, at the breaking up of the body, after death, he will go to a state of loss (apāyaṃ), a bad destiny (duggatiṃ), a downfall (vinipātaṃ), hell (nirayaṃ).

Thus, this sure teaching (apaṇṇako dhammo), when badly undertaken and adopted, only touches one side, and leaves aside the possibility of the wholesome (kusalaṃ ṭhānaṃ).
commentary_pali:
95.Nekkhamme ānisaṃsanti yo nesaṃ akusalato nikkhantabhāve ānisaṃso, yo ca vodānapakkho visuddhipakkho, taṃ na passantīti attho. Asaddhammasaññattīti abhūtadhammasaññāpanā . Attānukkaṃsetīti ṭhapetvā maṃ ko añño attano dassanaṃ pare gaṇhāpetuṃ sakkotīti attānaṃ ukkhipati. Paraṃ vambhetīti ettakesu janesu ekopi attano dassanaṃ pare gaṇhāpetuṃ na sakkotīti evaṃ paraṃ heṭṭhā khipati. Pubbeva kho panāti pubbe micchādassanaṃ gaṇhantasseva susīlyaṃ pahīnaṃ hoti, dussīlabhāvo paccupaṭṭhito. Evamassimeti evaṃ assa ime micchādiṭṭhiādayo satta. Aparāparaṃ uppajjanavasena pana teyeva micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā uppajjanti nāma.

Tatrāti tāsu tesaṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ laddhīsu. Kaliggahoti parājayaggāho. Dussamatto samādinnoti duggahito dupparāmaṭṭho. Ekaṃsaṃ pharitvā tiṭṭhatīti ekantaṃ ekakoṭṭhāsaṃ sakavādameva pharitvā adhimuccitvā tiṭṭhati, ‘‘sace kho natthi paro loko’’ti evaṃ santeyeva sotthibhāvāvaho hoti. Riñcatīti vajjeti.

Tatrā Kaliggaho Dussamatto samādinno Ekaṃsaṃ pharitvā tiṭṭhatī Riñcatī
commentary_english:
95. *Nekkhamme ānisaṃsa* means the benefit in their having gone forth from the unwholesome, and it means they do not see the purification side, the side of cleansing.

*Asaddhammasaññattī* means misperceptions of false Dharma.

*Attānukkaṃsetī* means that having set me aside, who else is able to make others accept their views? He exalts himself.

*Paraṃ vambhetī* means that among so many people, not even one is able to make others accept their views. Thus, he puts others down.

*Pubbeva kho panā* means that even before, as soon as he grasps wrong views, his good morality is lost, and immorality is present.

*Evamassime* means thus, these seven—wrong view, and so forth—belong to him. Furthermore, through the force of the arising of one thing after another, indeed, through the condition of wrong view, many evil, unwholesome *dharmas* arise.

*Tatrā* means among those doctrines of those ascetics and Brahmins.

*Kaliggaho* means seizing quarrels.

*Dussamatto samādinno* means badly grasped, poorly comprehended.

*Ekaṃsaṃ pharitvā tiṭṭhatī* means he dwells having thoroughly pervaded only one aspect, one part, his own doctrine, having fixated on it, thinking, "If there is no other world," thus, even in that case, he is the bringer of well-being.

*Riñcatī* means he avoids.

There, seizing quarrels, badly grasped, poorly comprehended, dwelling having thoroughly pervaded only one aspect, he avoids.

mula_pali:
96. ‘‘Tatra , gahapatayo, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘atthi dinnaṃ…pe… ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti tesametaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ? Yamidaṃ kāyaduccaritaṃ, vacīduccaritaṃ, manoduccaritaṃ – ime tayo akusale dhamme abhinivajjetvā yamidaṃ kāyasucaritaṃ, vacīsucaritaṃ, manosucaritaṃ – ime tayo kusale dhamme samādāya vattissanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Passanti hi te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ vodānapakkhaṃ. Santaṃyeva kho pana paraṃ lokaṃ ‘atthi paro loko’ tissa diṭṭhi hoti; sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi. Santaṃyeva kho pana paraṃ lokaṃ ‘atthi paro loko’ti saṅkappeti; svāssa hoti sammāsaṅkappo. Santaṃyeva kho pana paraṃ lokaṃ ‘atthi paro loko’ti vācaṃ bhāsati; sāssa hoti sammāvācā. Santaṃyeva kho pana paraṃ lokaṃ ‘atthi paro loko’ti āha; ye te arahanto paralokaviduno tesamayaṃ na paccanīkaṃ karoti. Santaṃyeva kho pana paraṃ lokaṃ ‘atthi paro loko’ti paraṃ saññāpeti; sāssa hoti saddhammasaññatti. Tāya ca pana saddhammasaññattiyā nevattānukkaṃseti, na paraṃ vambheti. Iti pubbeva kho panassa dussīlyaṃ pahīnaṃ hoti, susīlyaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ – ayañca sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā ariyānaṃ apaccanīkatā saddhammasaññatti anattukkaṃsanā aparavambhanā. Evamassime aneke kusalā dhammā sambhavanti sammādiṭṭhipaccayā.

‘‘Tatra, gahapatayo, viññū puriso iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘sace kho atthi paro loko , evamayaṃ bhavaṃ purisapuggalo kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjissati. Kāmaṃ kho pana māhu paro loko, hotu nesaṃ bhavataṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ saccaṃ vacanaṃ; atha ca panāyaṃ bhavaṃ purisapuggalo diṭṭheva dhamme viññūnaṃ pāsaṃso – sīlavā purisapuggalo sammādiṭṭhi atthikavādo’ti. Sace kho attheva paro loko, evaṃ imassa bhoto purisapuggalassa ubhayattha kaṭaggaho – yañca diṭṭheva dhamme viññūnaṃ pāsaṃso, yañca kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjissati. Evamassāyaṃ apaṇṇako dhammo susamatto samādinno, ubhayaṃsaṃ pharitvā tiṭṭhati, riñcati akusalaṃ ṭhānaṃ.
mula_english:
96. It is said, "Therein, householders, those ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* who speak thus, who hold such views, namely, ‘There is what is given…pe… those who, having directly experienced this world and the next with their own higher knowledge, make them known’—this is to be expected of them: that they, having completely avoided these three unwholesome things—bodily misconduct (*kāyaduccarita*), verbal misconduct (*vacīduccarita*), and mental misconduct (*manoduccarita*)—will undertake and maintain these three wholesome things (*kusala dhamma*)—bodily good conduct (*kāyasucarita*), verbal good conduct (*vacīsucarita*), and mental good conduct (*manosucarita*)."

What is the reason for this? Because those venerable ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* see drawbacks (*ādīnava*), degradation (*okāra*), and defilement (*saṃkilesa*) in unwholesome qualities (*akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ*), and they see the rewards (*ānisaṃsaṃ*) of renunciation (*nekkhamme*), resembling cleansing (*vodānapakkhaṃ*), in wholesome qualities (*kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ*).

Because there actually is the next world (*paraṃ lokaṃ*), the view (*diṭṭhi*) of one who thinks, ‘There is a next world (*atthi paro loko*)’ is his right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*).

Because there actually is the next world (*paraṃ lokaṃ*), when he is resolved that ‘There is a next world (*atthi paro loko*)’, that is his right resolve (*sammāsaṅkappo*).

Because there actually is the next world (*paraṃ lokaṃ*), when he speaks the statement, ‘There is a next world (*atthi paro loko*)’, that is his right speech (*sammāvācā*).

Because there actually is the next world (*paraṃ lokaṃ*), when he says that ‘There is a next world (*atthi paro loko*)’, he doesn’t make himself an opponent to those *arahants* who know the next world (*paralokaviduno*).

Because there actually is the next world (*paraṃ lokaṃ*), when he persuades another that ‘There is a next world (*atthi paro loko*)’, that is persuasion in what is true *dharma* (*saddhammasaññatti*).

And in that persuasion in what is true *dharma* (*saddhammasaññattiyā*), he doesn’t exalt himself (*nevattānukkaṃseti*) or disparage others (*na paraṃ vambheti*).

Whatever bad habituation (*dussīlyaṃ*) he previously had is abandoned (*pahīnaṃ hoti*), while good habituation (*susīlyaṃ*) is manifested (*paccupaṭṭhitaṃ*). And this right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*), right resolve (*sammāsaṅkappo*), right speech (*sammāvācā*), non-opposition to the *ariyas*, persuasion in what is true *dharma* (*saddhammasaññatti*), non-exaltation of self (*anattukkaṃsanā*), & non-disparagement of others (*aparavambhanā*):

These many skillful activities (*kusalā dhammā*) come into play (*sambhavanti*), in dependence on right view (*sammādiṭṭhipaccayā*).

“Therein, householders, an observant person considers thus: ‘If there actually is the next world (*atthi paro loko*), then this venerable person (*bhavaṃ purisapuggalo*)—on the breakup of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*paraṃ maraṇā*)—will reappear in a good destination (*sugatiṃ*), a heavenly world (*saggaṃ lokaṃ*)’.”

Even if we didn’t speak of the next world (*paro loko*), and there weren’t the true statement (*saccaṃ vacanaṃ*) of those venerable ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* (*samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ*), this venerable person (*bhavaṃ purisapuggalo*) is still praised in the here & now (*diṭṭheva dhamme*) by the observant (*viññūnaṃ pāsaṃso*) as a person of good habits (*sīlavā purisapuggalo*) & right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*): one who holds to a doctrine of existence (*atthikavādo*).’

If there really is a next world (*paro loko*), then this venerable person (*bhoto purisapuggalassa*) has made a good throw twice (*ubhayattha kaṭaggaho*): in that he is praised by the observant (*viññūnaṃ pāsaṃso*) here & now (*diṭṭheva dhamme*); and in that—with the breakup of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*paraṃ maraṇā*)—he will reappear in a good destination (*sugatiṃ*), a heavenly world (*saggaṃ lokaṃ*).

Thus this safe-bet teaching (*apaṇṇako dhammo*), when well grasped (*susamatto*) & adopted (*samādinno*) by him, covers both sides (*ubhayaṃsaṃ pharitvā tiṭṭhati*), and leaves behind the possibility of the unskillful (*riñcati akusalaṃ ṭhānaṃ*).
commentary_pali:
96.Saddhammasaññattīti bhūtadhammasaññāpanā.

Kaṭaggahoti jayaggāho. Susamatto samādinnoti suggahito suparāmaṭṭho. Ubhayaṃsaṃpharitvā tiṭṭhatīti ubhayantaṃ ubhayakoṭṭhāsaṃ sakavādaṃ paravādañca pharitvā adhimuccitvā tiṭṭhati ‘‘sace kho atthi paro loko’’ti evaṃ santepi ‘‘sace kho natthi paro loko’’ti evaṃ santepi sotthibhāvāvaho hoti. Paratopi ekaṃsaubhayaṃsesu imināva nayena attho veditabbo.

Kaṭaggaho Susamatto samādinno Ubhayaṃsaṃ pharitvā tiṭṭhatī
commentary_english:
96. *Saddhammasaññattī* means declaration of the real dharma.

*Kaṭaggaho* means gaining victory.
*Susamatto samādinno* means well grasped, well considered.
*Ubhayamsaṃ*, having pervaded, he remains; *ubhayantaṃ ubhayakoṭṭhāsaṃ sakavādaṃ paravādañca pharitvā adhimuccitvā tiṭṭhati* "If there is another world," even while he exists thus, "If there is not another world," even while he exists thus, he brings about a state of well-being.
Moreover, in *ekaṃsaubhayaṃsesu*, the meaning should be understood by this method.

*Kaṭaggaho, susamatto samādinno, ubhayamsaṃ, pharitvā tiṭṭhatī*.

mula_pali: 97. ‘‘Santi, gahapatayo, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘karoto kārayato, chindato chedāpayato, pacato pācāpayato, socayato socāpayato, kilamato kilamāpayato, phandato phandāpayato, pāṇamatipātayato pāṇamatimāpayato (sī. pī.), pāṇamatipātāpayato (syā. kaṃ.), pāṇamatipāpayato (ka.), adinnaṃ ādiyato, sandhiṃ chindato, nillopaṃ harato, ekāgārikaṃ karoto, paripanthe tiṭṭhato, paradāraṃ gacchato, musā bhaṇato; karoto na karīyati pāpaṃ. Khurapariyantena cepi cakkena yo imissā pathaviyā pāṇe ekaṃ maṃsakhalaṃ ekaṃ maṃsapuñjaṃ kareyya, natthi tatonidānaṃ pāpaṃ, natthi pāpassa āgamo. Dakkhiṇañcepi gaṅgāya tīraṃ gaccheyya hananto ghātento, chindanto chedāpento, pacanto pācento; natthi tatonidānaṃ pāpaṃ, natthi pāpassa āgamo. Uttarañcepi gaṅgāya tīraṃ gaccheyya dadanto dāpento, yajanto yajāpento; natthi tatonidānaṃ puññaṃ, natthi puññassa āgamo. Dānena damena saṃyamena saccavajjena saccavācena (ka.) natthi puññaṃ, natthi puññassa āgamo’ti. Tesaṃyeva kho, gahapatayo, samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā ujuvipaccanīkavādā te evamāhaṃsu – ‘karoto kārayato, chindato chedāpayato, pacato pācāpayato, socayato socāpayato, kilamato kilamāpayato, phandato phandāpayato, pāṇamatipātayato, adinnaṃ ādiyato, sandhiṃ chindato, nillopaṃ harato, ekāgārikaṃ karoto, paripanthe tiṭṭhato, paradāraṃ gacchato, musā bhaṇato; karoto karīyati pāpaṃ. Khurapariyantena cepi cakkena yo imissā pathaviyā pāṇe ekaṃ maṃsakhalaṃ ekaṃ maṃsapuñjaṃ kareyya, atthi tatonidānaṃ pāpaṃ, atthi pāpassa āgamo. Dakkhiṇañcepi gaṅgāya tīraṃ gaccheyya hananto ghātento, chindanto chedāpento, pacanto pācento; atthi tatonidānaṃ pāpaṃ, atthi pāpassa āgamo. Uttarañcepi gaṅgāya tīraṃ gaccheyya dadanto dāpento, yajanto yajāpento; atthi tatonidānaṃ puññaṃ, atthi puññassa āgamo. Dānena damena saṃyamena saccavajjena atthi puññaṃ, atthi puññassa āgamo’ti. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, gahapatayo, nanume samaṇabrāhmaṇā aññamaññassa ujuvipaccanīkavādā’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’.
mula_english:
97. “There are, householders, some ascetics and Brahmins who hold such views and doctrines: ‘In acting or getting others to act, in mutilating or getting others to mutilate, in torturing or getting others to torture, in inflicting sorrow or getting others to inflict sorrow, in tormenting or getting others to torment, in intimidating or getting others to intimidate, in taking life, in taking what is not given, in breaking into houses, in plundering, in committing burglary, in lying in wait on the roads, in going to another’s wife, in speaking falsehood, no evil is done by the doer.

If with a razor-sharp wheel one were to make of this earth one single mass of flesh, one single heap of flesh, there would be no evil resulting from that, no coming of evil.

Even if one were to go along the south bank of the Gaṅgā, killing and slaughtering, mutilating and making others mutilate, torturing and making others torture, there would be no evil resulting from that, no coming of evil.

Even if one were to go along the north bank of the Gaṅgā giving and causing to give, sacrificing and causing to sacrifice, there would be no merit resulting from that, no coming of merit.

Through generosity ( *dāna*), self-control (*dama*), restraint (*saṃyama*), and truthful speech (*saccavajja*), there is no merit, there is no coming of merit.’

There are, householders, some ascetics and Brahmins who hold directly opposing views to those ascetics and Brahmins. They say: ‘In acting or getting others to act, in mutilating or getting others to mutilate, in torturing or getting others to torture, in inflicting sorrow or getting others to inflict sorrow, in tormenting or getting others to torment, in intimidating or getting others to intimidate, in taking life, in taking what is not given, in breaking into houses, in plundering, in committing burglary, in lying in wait on the roads, in going to another’s wife, in speaking falsehood, evil *is* done by the doer.

If with a razor-sharp wheel one were to make of this earth one single mass of flesh, one single heap of flesh, there *would* be evil resulting from that, there *would* be a coming of evil.

Even if one were to go along the south bank of the Gaṅgā killing and slaughtering, mutilating and making others mutilate, torturing and making others torture, there *would* be evil resulting from that, there *would* be a coming of evil.

Even if one were to go along the north bank of the Gaṅgā giving and causing to give, sacrificing and causing to sacrifice, there *would* be merit resulting from that, there *would* be a coming of merit.

Through generosity (*dāna*), self-control (*dama*), restraint (*saṃyama*), and truthful speech (*saccavajja*), there *is* merit, there *is* a coming of merit.’

What do you think, householders, don’t these ascetics and Brahmins hold directly opposing views to each other?” “Yes, venerable sir.”
commentary_pali:
97.Karototi sahatthā karontassa. Kārayatoti āṇattiyā kārentassa. Chindatoti paresaṃ hatthādīni chindantassa. Pacatoti daṇḍena pīḷentassa vā tajjentassa vā. Socayatoti parassa bhaṇḍaharaṇādīhi sokaṃ sayaṃ karontassapi parehi kārentassapi. Kilamatoti āhārūpaccheda-bandhanāgārappavesanādīhi sayaṃ kilamantassāpi parehi kilamāpentassāpi. Phandato phandāpayatoti paraṃ phandantaṃ phandanakāle sayampi phandato parampi phandāpayato. Pāṇamatipātayatoti pāṇaṃ hanantassapi hanāpentassapi. Evaṃ sabbattha karaṇakārāpanavaseneva attho veditabbo.

Sandhinti gharasandhiṃ. Nillopanti mahāvilopaṃ. Ekāgārikanti ekameva gharaṃ parivāretvā vilumpanaṃ. Paripanthetiṭṭhatoti āgatāgatānaṃ acchindanatthaṃ magge tiṭṭhato. Karoto na karīyati pāpanti yaṃkiñci pāpaṃ karomīti saññāya karotopi pāpaṃ na karīyati, natthi pāpaṃ. Sattā pana karomāti evaṃsaññino hontīti attho. Khurapariyantenāti khuraneminā, khuradhārasadisapariyantena vā. Ekaṃ maṃsakhalanti ekaṃ maṃsarāsiṃ. Puñjanti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Tatonidānanti ekamaṃsakhalakaraṇanidānaṃ. Dakkhiṇatīre manussā kakkhaḷā dāruṇā, te sandhāya hanantotiādi vuttaṃ. Uttaratīre saddhā honti pasannā buddhamāmakā dhammamāmakā saṅghamāmakā, te sandhāya dadantotiādi vuttaṃ.

Sandhi Nillopa Ekāgārika Paripanthe tiṭṭhato Karoto na karīyati pāpa Khurapariyantenā Ekaṃ maṃsakhala Puñja Tatonidāna hananto dadanto

Tattha yajantoti mahāyāgaṃ karonto. Damenāti indriyadamena uposathakammena. Saṃyamenāti sīlasaṃyamena. Saccavajjenāti saccavacanena. Āgamoti āgamanaṃ, pavattīti attho. Sabbathāpi pāpapuññānaṃ kiriyameva paṭikkhipanti. Sukkapakkhopi vuttanayeneva veditabbo. Sesamettha purimavāre vuttasadisameva.

yajanto Damenā Saṃyamenā Saccavajjenā Āgamo
commentary_english:
97. *karoto* means one doing with his own hand.
*kārayato* means one causing to do by command.
*chindato* means one cutting off the hands etc. of others.
*pacato* means one oppressing or threatening with a stick.
*socayato* means one causing sorrow to another by taking away goods etc., or one causing sorrow to himself and also causing others to do so.
*kilamato* means one fatiguing himself or causing fatigue to others by means of cutting off food, imprisonment etc.
*phandato phandāpayato* means one trembling himself and causing others to tremble, or one causing others to tremble at the time of trembling himself.
*pāṇamatipātayato* means one killing a living being himself or causing others to kill.
Thus, in all cases, the meaning should be understood through the force of doing and causing to do.

*sandhi* means housebreaking.
*nillopa* means great plundering.
*ekāgārika* means plundering after surrounding just one house.
*paripanthe tiṭṭhato* means standing on the road for the purpose of intercepting those who come and go.
*karoto na karīyati pāpa* means even though one does something with the idea "I am doing evil," evil is not done; there is no evil.
*sattā pana karomāti evaṃsaññino hontīti attho* means beings have the idea "We are doing evil."
*khurapariyantenā* means by the edge of a razor, or by an edge similar to the blade of a razor.
*ekaṃ maṃsakhala* means a heap of meat.
*puñja* means a synonym of that itself.
*tatonidāna* means having as its cause the making of a heap of meat.
On the southern bank, humans are rough and cruel; referring to them, *hananto tiādi* was said.
On the northern bank, there are faithful, serene people who consider the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṃgha as their own; referring to them, *dadanto tiādi* was said.

*sandhi*, *nillopa*, *ekāgārika*, *paripanthe*, *tiṭṭhato*, *karoto na karīyati pāpa*, *khurapariyantenā*, *ekaṃ maṃsakhala*, *puñja*, *tatonidāna*, *hananto*, *dadanto*

There, *yajanto* means one performing a great sacrifice.
*damenā* means by self-restraint of the senses, by the uposatha act.
*saṃyamenā* means by moral restraint.
*saccavajjenā* means by truthful speech.
*āgamo* means coming, it means continuity.
In every case, they reject the doing of evil and merit.
The bright fortnight, too, should be understood in the way already stated.
The remainder here is just like what was stated in the previous turn.

*yajanto*, *damenā*, *saṃyamenā*, *saccavajjenā*, *āgamo*

mula_pali:
98. ‘‘Tatra, gahapatayo, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘karoto kārayato, chindato chedāpayato, pacato pācāpayato, socayato socāpayato, kilamato kilamāpayato, phandato phandāpayato, pāṇamatipātayato, adinnaṃ ādiyato, sandhiṃ chindato, nillopaṃ harato, ekāgārikaṃ karoto, paripanthe tiṭṭhato, paradāraṃ gacchato, musā bhaṇato; karoto na karīyati pāpaṃ. Khurapariyantena cepi cakkena yo imissā pathaviyā pāṇe ekaṃ maṃsakhalaṃ ekaṃ maṃsapuñjaṃ kareyya, natthi tatonidānaṃ pāpaṃ, natthi pāpassa āgamo. Dakkhiṇañcepi gaṅgāya tīraṃ gaccheyya hananto ghātento…pe… dānena damena saṃyamena saccavajjena natthi puññaṃ, natthi puññassa āgamo’ti tesametaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ? Yamidaṃ kāyasucaritaṃ, vacīsucaritaṃ, manosucaritaṃ – ime tayo kusale dhamme abhinivajjetvā yamidaṃ kāyaduccaritaṃ, vacīduccaritaṃ, manoduccaritaṃ – ime tayo akusale dhamme samādāya vattissanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Na hi te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā passanti akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ vodānapakkhaṃ. Santaṃyeva kho pana kiriyaṃ ‘natthi kiriyā’ tissa diṭṭhi hoti; sāssa hoti micchādiṭṭhi. Santaṃyeva kho pana kiriyaṃ ‘natthi kiriyā’ti saṅkappeti; svāssa hoti micchāsaṅkappo. Santaṃyeva kho pana kiriyaṃ ‘natthi kiriyā’ti vācaṃ bhāsati; sāssa hoti micchāvācā. Santaṃyeva kho pana kiriyaṃ ‘natthi kiriyā’ti āha, ye te arahanto kiriyavādā tesamayaṃ paccanīkaṃ karoti. Santaṃyeva kho pana kiriyaṃ ‘natthi kiriyā’ti paraṃ saññāpeti; sāssa hoti asaddhammasaññatti. Tāya ca pana asaddhammasaññattiyā attānukkaṃseti, paraṃ vambheti. Iti pubbeva kho panassa susīlyaṃ pahīnaṃ hoti, dussīlyaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ – ayañca micchādiṭṭhi micchāsaṅkappo micchāvācā ariyānaṃ paccanīkatā asaddhammasaññatti attukkaṃsanā paravambhanā. Evamassime aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti micchādiṭṭhipaccayā.

‘‘Tatra, gahapatayo, viññū puriso iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘sace kho natthi kiriyā, evamayaṃ bhavaṃ purisapuggalo kāyassa bhedā sotthimattānaṃ karissati; sace kho atthi kiriyā evamayaṃ bhavaṃ purisapuggalo kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjissati. Kāmaṃ kho pana māhu kiriyā, hotu nesaṃ bhavataṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ saccaṃ vacanaṃ; atha ca panāyaṃ bhavaṃ purisapuggalo diṭṭheva dhamme viññūnaṃ gārayho – dussīlo purisapuggalo micchādiṭṭhi akiriyavādo’ti. Sace kho attheva kiriyā, evaṃ imassa bhoto purisapuggalassa ubhayattha kaliggaho – yañca diṭṭheva dhamme viññūnaṃ gārayho, yañca kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjissati. Evamassāyaṃ apaṇṇako dhammo dussamatto samādinno, ekaṃsaṃ pharitvā tiṭṭhati, riñcati kusalaṃ ṭhānaṃ.
mula_english:
98. “Now, householders, of those contemplatives and *brāhmaṇas* who hold this doctrine, hold this view: ‘In acting or getting others to act, in mutilating or getting others to mutilate, in torturing or getting others to torture, in inflicting sorrow or in getting others to inflict sorrow, in tormenting or getting others to torment, in intimidating or getting others to intimidate, in taking life, taking what is not given, breaking into houses, plundering wealth, committing burglary, ambushing highways, committing adultery and telling lies; in acting, no evil is done.’

If with a razor-sharp wheel one were to make of this earth one single mass and heap of flesh, there would be no evil as a result of that, no evil would accrue.

If one were to go to the bank of the river Gaṅgā, killing and slaughtering…pe…there is no merit in giving, taming, restraining, speaking the truth, there is no coming of merit.’ Is this their expectation? Rejecting this bodily good conduct (kāyasucarita), verbal good conduct (vacīsucarita), and mental good conduct (manosucarita) – these three wholesome qualities (kusala dhamma), they will live embracing this bodily bad conduct (kāyaduccarita), verbal bad conduct (vacīduccarita), and mental bad conduct (manoduccarita) – these three unwholesome qualities (akusala dhamma).

Why is that? Those venerable contemplatives and *brāhmaṇas* do not see the misery, the fault, the corruption in unwholesome qualities, nor the advantage, the side of purity in the renunciation of wholesome qualities.

Because there actually is action (kiriya), the view of one who thinks, ‘There is no action (kiriya)’ is his wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhi*).

Because there actually is action (kiriya), when he conceives that ‘There is no action (kiriya),’ that is his wrong resolve (*micchāsaṅkappa*).

Because there actually is action (kiriya), when he speaks the statement, ‘There is no action (kiriya),’ that is his wrong speech (*micchāvācā*).

Because there actually is action (kiriya), when he says that ‘There is no action (kiriya),’ he makes himself an opponent to those *arahants* who teach action (kiriyavāda).

Because there actually is action (kiriya), when he persuades another that ‘There is no action (kiriya),’ that is persuasion in what is not true Dhamma (*asaddhammasaññatti*).

And in that persuasion in what is not true Dhamma (*asaddhammasaññatti*), he exalts himself and disparages others.

Whatever good habituation he previously had is abandoned, while bad habituation is manifested. And this wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhi*), wrong resolve (*micchāsaṅkappa*), wrong speech (*micchāvācā*), opposition to the *arahants*, persuasion in what is not true Dhamma (*asaddhammasaññatti*), exaltation of self, & disparagement of others:

Thus these many evil, unskillful activities come into play, in dependence on wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhipaccayā*).

“With regard to this, householders, an observant person considers thus: ‘If there is no action (kiriya), then—with the breakup of the body, after death—this venerable person has made himself safe. But if there is action (kiriya), then this venerable person—on the breakup of the body, after death—will reappear in a plane of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell.

Even if we didn’t speak of action (kiriya), and there weren’t the true statement of those venerable contemplatives and *brāhmaṇas*, this venerable person is still criticized in the here and now by the observant as a person of bad habits and wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhi*): one who holds to a doctrine of non-action (*akiriyavādo*).

If there really is action (kiriya), then this venerable person has made a bad throw twice: in that he is criticized by the observant here and now; and in that—with the breakup of the body, after death—he will reappear in a plane of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell.

Thus this safe-bet teaching (*apaṇṇako dhammo*), when poorly grasped and poorly adopted by him, covers one side and leaves behind the possibility of the skillful.

mula_pali:
99. ‘‘Tatra, gahapatayo, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘karoto kārayato, chindato chedāpayato, pacato pācāpayato, socayato socāpayato, kilamato kilamāpayato, phandato phandāpayato, pāṇamatipātayato, adinnaṃ ādiyato, sandhiṃ chindato, nillopaṃ harato, ekāgārikaṃ karoto, paripanthe tiṭṭhato, paradāraṃ gacchato, musā bhaṇato; karoto karīyati pāpaṃ. Khurapariyantena cepi cakkena yo imissā pathaviyā pāṇe ekaṃ maṃsakhalaṃ ekaṃ maṃsapuñjaṃ kareyya, atthi tatonidānaṃ pāpaṃ, atthi pāpassa āgamo. Dakkhiṇañcepi gaṅgāya tīraṃ gaccheyya hananto ghātento, chindanto chedāpento, pacanto pācento, atthi tatonidānaṃ pāpaṃ, atthi pāpassa āgamo. Uttarañcepi gaṅgāya tīraṃ gaccheyya dadanto dāpento, yajanto yajāpento, atthi tatonidānaṃ puññaṃ, atthi puññassa āgamo. Dānena damena saṃyamena saccavajjena atthi puññaṃ, atthi puññassa āgamo’ti tesametaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ? Yamidaṃ kāyaduccaritaṃ, vacīduccaritaṃ , manoduccaritaṃ – ime tayo akusale dhamme abhinivajjetvā yamidaṃ kāyasucaritaṃ, vacīsucaritaṃ, manosucaritaṃ – ime tayo kusale dhamme samādāya vattissanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Passanti hi te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ vodānapakkhaṃ. Santaṃyeva kho pana kiriyaṃ ‘atthi kiriyā’ tissa diṭṭhi hoti; sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi. Santaṃyeva kho pana kiriyaṃ ‘atthi kiriyā’ti saṅkappeti; svāssa hoti sammāsaṅkappo. Santaṃyeva kho pana kiriyaṃ ‘atthi kiriyā’ti vācaṃ bhāsati; sāssa hoti sammāvācā. Santaṃyeva kho pana kiriyaṃ ‘atthi kiriyā’ti āha; ye te arahanto kiriyavādā tesamayaṃ na paccanīkaṃ karoti. Santaṃyeva kho pana kiriyaṃ ‘atthi kiriyā’ti paraṃ saññāpeti; sāssa hoti saddhammasaññatti. Tāya ca pana saddhammasaññattiyā nevattānukkaṃseti, na paraṃ vambheti. Iti pubbeva kho panassa dussīlyaṃ pahīnaṃ hoti, susīlyaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ – ayañca sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā ariyānaṃ apaccanīkatā saddhammasaññatti anattukkaṃsanā aparavambhanā. Evamassime aneke kusalā dhammā sambhavanti sammādiṭṭhipaccayā.

‘‘Tatra, gahapatayo, viññū puriso iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘sace kho atthi kiriyā, evamayaṃ bhavaṃ purisapuggalo kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjissati. Kāmaṃ kho pana māhu kiriyā, hotu nesaṃ bhavataṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ saccaṃ vacanaṃ; atha ca panāyaṃ bhavaṃ purisapuggalo diṭṭheva dhamme viññūnaṃ pāsaṃso – sīlavā purisapuggalo sammādiṭṭhi kiriyavādo’ti. Sace kho attheva kiriyā, evaṃ imassa bhoto purisapuggalassa ubhayattha kaṭaggaho – yañca diṭṭheva dhamme viññūnaṃ pāsaṃso, yañca kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjissati. Evamassāyaṃ apaṇṇako dhammo susamatto samādinno, ubhayaṃsaṃ pharitvā tiṭṭhati, riñcati akusalaṃ ṭhānaṃ.
mula_english:
99. “Now, householders, of those ascetics and Brahmins who hold such views and opinions: ‘In acting or getting others to act, in mutilating or getting others to mutilate, in torturing or getting others to torture, in inflicting sorrow or getting others to inflict sorrow, in tormenting or getting others to torment, in intimidating or getting others to intimidate, in taking life, taking what is not given, breaking into houses, plundering wealth, committing burglary, ambushing highways, committing adultery and telling lies, in doing so, evil is done.

If with a razor-edged disk one were to turn all the living beings on this earth into a single mass of flesh, a single pile of flesh, there would be evil from that cause, there would be a coming of evil.

If one were to go along the right bank of the Ganges, killing and getting others to kill, mutilating and getting others to mutilate, torturing and getting others to torture, there would be evil from that cause, there would be a coming of evil.

If one were to go along the north bank of the Ganges giving gifts and inducing others to give gifts, making offerings and inducing others to make offerings, there would be merit from that cause, there would be a coming of merit.

Is this what they expect: ‘Through generosity (dāna), self-control (dama), restraint (saṃyama), and speaking the truth (saccavajjena) there is merit (puñña), there is an outcome of merit?' Whereas, bad bodily conduct (kāyaduccarita), bad verbal conduct (vacīduccarita), and bad mental conduct (manoduccarita) – having turned away from these three unwholesome qualities (akusale dhamme), they will engage in good bodily conduct (kāyasucarita), good verbal conduct (vacīsucarita), and good mental conduct (manosucarita) – these three wholesome qualities (kusale dhamme).

What is the reason for that? Because those venerable ascetics and Brahmins see the drawbacks (ādīnava), degradation (okāra), and defilement (saṃkilesa) in unwholesome qualities (akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ); and in wholesome qualities (kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ) they see the rewards of renunciation (nekkhamma), resembling cleansing (vodānapakkhaṃ).

Because there actually is action (kiriya), the view of one who thinks, ‘There is action (atthi kiriyā)’ is his right view (sammādiṭṭhi).

Because there actually is action (kiriya), when he is resolved that ‘There is action (atthi kiriyā),’ that is his right resolve (sammāsaṅkappo).

Because there actually is action (kiriya), when he speaks the statement, ‘There is action (atthi kiriyā),’ that is his right speech (sammāvācā).

Because there actually is action (kiriya), when he says that ‘There is action (atthi kiriyā),’ he doesn’t make himself an opponent to those *arhats* (arahanto) who teach action (kiriyavādā).

Because there actually is action (kiriya), when he persuades another that ‘There is action (atthi kiriyā),’ that is persuasion in what is true Dhamma (saddhammasaññatti).

And in that persuasion in what is true Dhamma (saddhammasaññattiyā), he doesn’t exalt himself or disparage others.

Thus, whatever bad habituation (dussīlyaṃ) he previously had is abandoned (pahīnaṃ), while good habituation (susīlyaṃ) is manifested (paccupaṭṭhitaṃ). And this right view (sammādiṭṭhi), right resolve (sammāsaṅkappo), right speech (sammāvācā), non-opposition to the *aryas* (ariyānaṃ), persuasion in what is true Dhamma (saddhammasaññatti), non-exaltation of self (anattukkaṃsanā), and non-disparagement of others (aparavambhanā):

These many wholesome qualities (kusalā dhammā) come into play, in dependence on right view (sammādiṭṭhipaccayā).

“Now, householders, an observant person (viññū puriso) considers thus: ‘If there is action (atthi kiriyā), then this venerable person (bhavaṃ purisapuggalo)—on the breakup of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā)—will reappear in a good destination (sugati), a heavenly world (saggaṃ lokaṃ).’

Even if we didn’t speak of action (kiriya), and there weren’t the true statement of those venerable ascetics and Brahmins (samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ), this venerable person (bhavaṃ purisapuggalo) is still praised in the here and now by the observant (viññūnaṃ pāsaṃso) as a person of good habits and right view: one who holds to a doctrine of action (kiriyavādo).’

If there really is action (atthi kiriyā), then this venerable person (bhoto purisapuggalassa) has made a good throw twice, in that he is praised by the observant here and now; and in that—with the breakup of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā)—he will reappear in a good destination (sugati), a heavenly world (saggaṃ lokaṃ).

Thus, this safe-bet teaching (apaṇṇako dhammo), when well grasped and adopted (susamatto samādinno) by him, covers both sides (ubhayaṃsaṃ pharitvā), and leaves behind the possibility of the unskillful (akusalaṃ ṭhānaṃ).

mula_pali: 100. ‘‘Santi , gahapatayo, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘natthi hetu, natthi paccayo sattānaṃ saṃkilesāya; ahetū appaccayā sattā saṃkilissanti. Natthi hetu, natthi paccayo sattānaṃ visuddhiyā; ahetū appaccayā sattā visujjhanti. Natthi balaṃ, natthi vīriyaṃ viriyaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), natthi purisathāmo, natthi purisaparakkamo; sabbe sattā sabbe pāṇā sabbe bhūtā sabbe jīvā avasā abalā avīriyā niyatisaṃgatibhāvapariṇatā chasvevābhijātīsu sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedentī’ti. Tesaṃyeva kho, gahapatayo, samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā ujuvipaccanīkavādā. Te evamāhaṃsu – ‘atthi hetu, atthi paccayo sattānaṃ saṃkilesāya; sahetū sappaccayā sattā saṃkilissanti. Atthi hetu, atthi paccayo sattānaṃ visuddhiyā; sahetū sappaccayā sattā visujjhanti. Atthi balaṃ, atthi vīriyaṃ, atthi purisathāmo, atthi purisaparakkamo; na sabbe sattā sabbe pāṇā sabbe bhūtā sabbe jīvā avasā abalā avīriyā atthi purisaparakkamo, sabbe sattā… savasā sabalā savīriyā (syā. kaṃ. ka.) niyatisaṃgatibhāvapariṇatā chasvevābhijātīsu sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedentī’ti. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, gahapatayo, nanume samaṇabrāhmaṇā aññamaññassa ujuvipaccanīkavādā’ti? ‘Evaṃ, bhante’.
mula_english:
“There are some contemplatives and Brahmins, householders, who hold this doctrine, hold this view: ‘There is no cause (hetu), no requisite condition (paccaya), for the defilement (saṃkilesa) of beings (sattānaṃ). Beings are defiled without causality, without requisite condition. There is no cause, no condition, for the purification (visuddhiyā) of beings; beings are purified without cause or condition. There is no strength (balaṃ), there is no effort (vīriyaṃ), there is no human energy (purisathāmo), there is no human endeavor (purisaparakkamo). All living beings (sabbe sattā), all life (sabbe pāṇā), all beings (sabbe bhūtā), all souls (sabbe jīvā) are powerless (avasā), devoid of strength (abalā), devoid of effort (avīriyā). Subject to the changes of fate (niyati), serendipity (saṃgati), and nature (bhāva), they experience pleasure (sukha) and pain (dukkha) in the six great classes of birth (abhijātīsu.’

“Some contemplatives and Brahmins, householders, speak in direct opposition to those contemplatives and Brahmins. They say this: ‘There is causality (hetu), there is requisite condition (paccayo), for the defilement of beings (sattānaṃ). Beings are defiled with causality, with requisite condition. There is causality, there is requisite condition, for the purification of beings; beings are purified with causality, with requisite condition. There is strength (balaṃ), there is effort (vīriyaṃ), there is human energy (purisathāmo), there is human endeavor (purisaparakkamo). It’s not the case that all living beings, all life, all beings, all souls are powerless, devoid of strength, devoid of effort; or that subject to the changes of fate, serendipity, and nature, they experience pleasure and pain in the six great classes of birth.’

“What do you think, householders? Are these contemplatives and Brahmins speaking in direct opposition to one another?”

“Yes, venerable sir.”
commentary_pali:
100.Natthi hetu natthi paccayoti ettha paccayo hetuvevacanaṃ. Ubhayenāpi vijjamānakameva kāyaduccaritādisaṃkilesapaccayaṃ kāyasucaritādivisuddhipaccayaṃ paṭikkhipanti. Natthibalaṃ, natthi vīriyaṃ, natthi purisathāmo, natthi purisaparakkamoti sattānaṃ saṃkilesituṃ vā visujjhituṃ vā balaṃ vā vīriyaṃ vā purisena kātabbo nāma purisathāmo vā purisaparakkamo vā natthi.

Sabbe sattāti oṭṭhagoṇagadrabhādayo anavasese nidassenti. Sabbe pāṇāti ekindriyo pāṇo dvindriyo pāṇoti ādivasena vadanti. Sabbe bhūtāti aṇḍakosavatthikosesu bhūte sandhāya vadanti. Sabbe jīvāti sāliyavagodhumādayo sandhāya vadanti. Tesu hete viruhanabhāvena jīvasaññino. Avasā abalā avīriyāti tesaṃ attano vaso vā balaṃ vā vīriyaṃ vā natthi. Niyatisaṅgatibhāvapariṇatāti ettha niyatīti niyatatā. Saṅgatīti channaṃ abhijātīnaṃ tattha tattha gamanaṃ. Bhāvoti sabhāvoyeva. Evaṃ niyatiyā ca saṅgatiyā ca bhāvena ca pariṇatā nānappakārataṃ pattā. Yena hi yathā bhavitabbaṃ, so tatheva bhavati. Yena no bhavitabbaṃ, so na bhavatīti dassenti. Chasvevābhijātīsūti chasu eva abhijātīsu ṭhatvā sukhañca dukkhañca paṭisaṃvedenti, aññā sukhadukkhabhūmi natthīti dassenti.

Sabbe sattā Sabbe pāṇā Sabbe bhūtā Sabbe jīvā Avasā abalā avīriyā Niyatisaṅgatibhāvapariṇatā niyatī Saṅgatī Bhāvo Chasvevābhijātīsū

Tattha cha abhijātiyo nāma kaṇhābhijāti nīlābhijāti lohitābhijāti haliddābhijāti sukkābhijāti paramasukkābhijātīti. Tattha sākuṇiko sūkariko luddo macchaghātako coro coraghātako, ye vā panaññepi keci kurūrakammantā, ayaṃ kaṇhābhijāti nāma. Bhikkhū nīlābhijātīti vadanti. Te kira catūsu paccayesu kaṇṭake pakkhipitvā khādanti. ‘‘Bhikkhū ca kaṇṭakavuttino’’ti ayañhi nesaṃ pāḷiyeva. Atha vā kaṇṭakavuttikā evaṃ nāma eke pabbajitāti vadanti. ‘‘Samaṇakaṇṭakavuttikā’’tipi hi nesaṃ pāḷi. Lohitābhijāti nāma nigaṇṭhā ekasāṭakāti vadanti. Ime kira purimehi dvīhi paṇḍaratarā. Gihī acelakasāvakā haliddābhijātīti vadanti. Iti attano paccayadāyake nigaṇṭhehipi jeṭṭhakatare karonti. Nando, vaccho, saṅkicco, ayaṃ sukkābhijātīti vadanti. Te kira purimehi catūhi paṇḍaratarā. Ājīvake pana paramasukkābhijātīti vadanti. Te kira sabbehi paṇḍaratarā.

Tattha sabbe sattā paṭhamaṃ sākuṇikādayova honti, tato visujjhamānā sakyasamaṇā honti, tato visujjhamānā nigaṇṭhā, tato ājīvakasāvakā, tato nandādayo, tato ājīvakāti ayametesaṃ laddhi. Sukkapakkho vuttapaccanīkena veditabbo. Sesamidhāpi purimavāre vuttasadisameva.

Imāsu pana tīsu diṭṭhīsu natthikadiṭṭhi vipākaṃ paṭibāhati, akiriyadiṭṭhi kammaṃ paṭibāhati, ahetukadiṭṭhi ubhayampi paṭibāhati. Tattha kammaṃ paṭibāhantenāpi vipāko paṭibāhito hoti, vipākaṃ paṭibāhantenāpi kammaṃ paṭibāhitaṃ. Iti sabbepete atthato ubhayapaṭibāhakā natthikavādā ceva ahetukavādā akiriyavādā ca honti. Ye pana tesaṃ laddhiṃ gahetvā rattiṭṭhāne divāṭṭhāne nisinnā sajjhāyanti vīmaṃsanti, tesaṃ – ‘‘natthi dinnaṃ natthi yiṭṭhaṃ, karoto na kariyati pāpaṃ, natthi hetu natthi paccayo’’ti tasmiṃ ārammaṇe micchāsati santiṭṭhati , cittaṃ ekaggaṃ hoti, javanāni javanti, paṭhamajavane satekicchā honti, tathā dutiyādīsu. Sattame buddhānampi atekicchā anivattino ariṭṭhakaṇṭakasadisā.

Tattha koci ekaṃ dassanaṃ okkamati, koci dve, koci tīṇipi, ekasmiṃ okkantepi dvīsu tīsu okkantesupi niyatamicchādiṭṭhikova hoti, patto saggamaggāvaraṇañceva mokkhamaggāvaraṇañca, abhabbo tassa attabhāvassa anantaraṃ saggampi gantuṃ, pageva mokkhaṃ. Vaṭṭakhāṇu nāmesa satto pathavīgopako. Kiṃ panesa ekasmiṃyeva attabhāve niyato hoti, udāhu aññasmimpīti? Ekasmiññeva niyato, āsevanavasena pana bhavantarepi taṃ taṃ diṭṭhiṃ rocetiyeva. Evarūpassa hi yebhuyyena bhavato vuṭṭhānaṃ nāma natthi.

Tasmā akalyāṇajanaṃ, āsīvisamivoragaṃ;

Ārakā parivajjeyya, bhūtikāmo vicakkhaṇoti.
commentary_english:
100. "[They say that] there is no cause (*hetu*), there is no condition (*pratyaya*)," here *pratyaya* is a synonym for *hetu*. By both [statements], they reject the condition for defilement, such as bad conduct of the body, and the condition for purification, such as good conduct of the body, even when they exist. "[They say that] there is no strength (*balam*), there is no vigor (*vīryam*), there is no manly strength (*purisathāmo*), there is no manly valor (*purisaparakkamo*)," it is not that strength, vigor, manly strength or manly valor should be done by a person to defile or purify beings.

All beings (*sabbe sattā*)' refers to showing without remainder camels, cows, donkeys, etc.
'All living beings (*sabbe pāṇā*)' means creatures having one faculty (*ekindriyo pāṇo*), two faculties (*dvindriyo pāṇo*), and so forth, they say this by way of beginning.
'All existents (*sabbe bhūtā*)' refers to existents in the egg, womb, placenta, etc. they say this intending [that].
'All life (*sabbe jīvā*)' refers to rice, barley, wheat, etc.; they say this intending [that].
Among these, these have the designation of life because of the nature of growth.
"Helpless (*avasā*), powerless (*abalā*), devoid of energy (*avīriyā*)" means that they do not have self-control (*vaso*), power (*balam*), or energy (*vīriyam*).
"Subject to destiny, association, and becoming (*niyatisaṅgatibhāvapariṇatā*)" here "destiny (*niyatī*)" means definiteness.
"Association (*saṅgatī*)' means going here and there of the six classes (*abhijātīnaṃ*).
"Becoming (*bhāvo*)" means just nature itself (*sabhāvoyeva*).
Thus, subject to destiny, association, and becoming, they have attained to various kinds of forms (*nānappakārataṃ pattā*).
Whatever will be will be (*yena hi yathā bhavitabbaṃ, so tatheva bhavati*).
Whatever will not be will not be (*yena no bhavitabbaṃ, so na bhavatīti*), they show.
"Only in the six classes (*chasvevābhijātīsū*)" means that having stood in just the six classes, they experience pleasure and pain, and they show that there is no other ground of pleasure and pain (*sukhadukkhabhūmi*).

All beings, all living beings, all existents, all life, helpless, powerless, devoid of energy, subject to destiny, association, and becoming, destiny, association, becoming, only in the six classes, there are six classes, namely the black class (*kaṇhābhijāti*), the blue class (*nīlābhijāti*), the red class (*lohitābhijāti*), the yellow class (*haliddābhijāti*), the white class (*sukkābhijāti*), and the ultimate white class (*paramasukkābhijāti*).
There, the fowler, the swine-butcher, the hunter, the fisherman, the thief, the executioner, or any other cruel occupations, this is called the black class.
The monks are called the blue class.
They, it is said, eat having thrown thorns into the four requisites.
"And the monks are thorny in conduct," this is just their *pāḷi*.
Or alternatively, some who have gone forth are called thorny in conduct.
"The mendicants are thorny in conduct," this too is their *pāḷi*.
The red class is made up of the one-robed Nigaṇṭhas.
These are purer than the former two.
Lay followers of the *acelakas* are called the yellow class.
Thus, they make their own lay supporters superior even to the Nigaṇṭhas.
Nanda, Vaccha, Saṅkicca, this is what they call the white class.
They, it is said, are purer than the previous four.
The Ājīvakas, however, are called the ultimate white class.
They, it is said, are the purest of all.

There, all beings are first just fowlers, etc., then, being purified, they are Śākya mendicants, then, being purified, they are Nigaṇṭhas, then they are followers of the Ājīvakas, then they are Nandas, etc., then they are Ājīvakas, this is their doctrine.
The bright side should be understood in the opposite way.

The remainder here is just like what was said previously.

Among these three views, the nihilistic view (natthikadiṭṭhi) denies the result (*vipāka*), the doctrine of the inefficacy of action (*akiriyadiṭṭhi*) denies action (*karma*), and the acausalist view (*ahetukadiṭṭhi*) denies both.

There, by denying action (*karma*), one also denies its result (*vipāka*); by denying the result (*vipāka*), one also denies action (*karma*).

Thus, all these thinkers, in effect, deny both and espouse nihilism (*natthikavāda*), acausalism (*ahetukavāda*), and the doctrine of the inefficacy of action (*akiriyavāda*).

But those who, having adopted their views, sit in a secluded place at night or during the day, reciting and pondering, their wrong mindfulness is established on this object, thinking, "There is no gift, no sacrifice, no sin is committed by the one who acts, there is no cause (*hetu*), no condition (*pratyaya*),"

the mind (*citta*) becomes one-pointed, impulses rush forth, in the first impulse there are tendencies, likewise in the second, etc.

In the seventh, even for the Buddhas, there are irreversible tendencies like the *ariṣṭa* thorn.

There, someone adopts one view, another two, another three. But whether one adopts one, two, or three views, one is certainly a holder of wrong views (*niyatamicchādiṭṭhika*), obstructed from the path to heaven (*svargamārga-āvaraṇa*) and the path to liberation (*mokṣamārga-āvaraṇa*), incapable of going to heaven (*svarga*) immediately after this existence (*attabhāva*), much less to liberation (*mokṣa*).

This being is called a stump in the round of existence, a watchman of the earth.

Is this person fixed in just one existence (*attabhāva*), or also in another? He is fixed in just one. However, through the force of habituation, he approves of that same view in another existence (*bhavāntara*).

Indeed, for one of this sort, there is generally no emergence from existence.

Therefore, one should avoid an unwholesome person, like a poisonous snake;

one who desires prosperity should avoid them from afar, [such a one is] discerning.

mula_pali:
101. ‘‘Tatra , gahapatayo, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘natthi hetu, natthi paccayo sattānaṃ saṃkilesāya; ahetū appaccayā sattā saṃkilissanti. Natthi hetu, natthi paccayo sattānaṃ visuddhiyā; ahetū appaccayā sattā visujjhanti. Natthi balaṃ, natthi vīriyaṃ, natthi purisathāmo, natthi purisaparakkamo; sabbe sattā sabbe pāṇā sabbe bhūtā sabbe jīvā avasā abalā avīriyā niyatisaṃgatibhāvapariṇatā chasvevābhijātīsu sukhadukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedentī’ti tesametaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ? Yamidaṃ kāyasucaritaṃ, vacīsucaritaṃ, manosucaritaṃ – ime tayo kusale dhamme abhinivajjetvā yamidaṃ kāyaduccaritaṃ, vacīduccaritaṃ, manoduccaritaṃ – ime tayo akusale dhamme samādāya vattissanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Na hi te bhonto samaṇabrāhmaṇā passanti akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ vodānapakkhaṃ. Santaṃyeva kho pana hetuṃ ‘natthi hetū’ tissa diṭṭhi hoti; sāssa hoti micchādiṭṭhi. Santaṃyeva kho pana hetuṃ ‘natthi hetū’ti saṅkappeti ; svāssa hoti micchāsaṅkappo. Santaṃyeva kho pana hetuṃ ‘natthi hetū’ti vācaṃ bhāsati; sāssa hoti micchāvācā. Santaṃyeva kho pana hetuṃ ‘natthi hetū’ti āha; ye te arahanto hetuvādā tesamayaṃ paccanīkaṃ karoti. Santaṃyeva kho pana hetuṃ ‘natthi hetū’ti paraṃ saññāpeti; sāssa hoti asaddhammasaññatti. Tāya ca pana asaddhammasaññattiyā attānukkaṃseti, paraṃ vambheti. Iti pubbeva kho panassa susīlyaṃ pahīnaṃ hoti, dussīlyaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ – ayañca micchādiṭṭhi micchāsaṅkappo micchāvācā ariyānaṃ paccanīkatā asaddhammasaññatti attānukkaṃsanā paravambhanā. Evamassime aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti micchādiṭṭhipaccayā.

‘‘Tatra, gahapatayo, viññū puriso iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘sace kho natthi hetu, evamayaṃ bhavaṃ purisapuggalo kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sotthimattānaṃ karissati; sace kho atthi hetu, evamayaṃ bhavaṃ purisapuggalo kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjissati. Kāmaṃ kho pana māhu hetu, hotu nesaṃ bhavataṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ saccaṃ vacanaṃ; atha ca panāyaṃ bhavaṃ purisapuggalo diṭṭheva dhamme viññūnaṃ gārayho – dussīlo purisapuggalo micchādiṭṭhi ahetukavādo’ti. Sace kho attheva hetu, evaṃ imassa bhoto purisapuggalassa ubhayattha kaliggaho – yañca diṭṭheva dhamme viññūnaṃ gārayho, yañca kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjissati. Evamassāyaṃ apaṇṇako dhammo dussamatto samādinno, ekaṃsaṃ pharitvā tiṭṭhati, riñcati kusalaṃ ṭhānaṃ.
mula_english:
101. It is said, "There, householders, are some ascetics and Brahmins who hold this doctrine and view: 'There is no cause (*hetu*), no condition (*pratyaya*) for the defilement (*saṃkilesa*) of beings (*sattva*); beings are defiled without a cause, without a condition. There is no cause, no condition for the purification (*visuddhi*) of beings; beings are purified without a cause or condition. There is no strength (*bala*), no energy (*vīriya*), no manly strength (*purisathāma*), no manly endurance (*purisaparakrama*); all beings (*sattva*), all living things (*pāṇa*), all creatures (*bhūta*), all souls (*jīva*) are without mastery (*avasā*), powerless (*abalā*), without energy (*avīriyā*); molded by destiny (*niyati*), circumstance (*saṃgati*), and nature (*bhāva*), they experience pleasure (*sukha*) and pain (*dukkha*) in the six great classes of birth (*abhijāti*)'. Is this what they anticipate? Abandoning this bodily good conduct (*kāyasucarita*), verbal good conduct (*vacīsucarita*), and mental good conduct (*manosucarita*) – these three skillful (*kusala*) qualities (*dhamma*) – they will undertake and maintain this bodily misconduct (*kāyaduccarita*), verbal misconduct (*vacīduccarita*), and mental misconduct (*manoduccarita*) – these three unskillful (*akusala*) qualities (*dhamma*).

Why is that? Because those venerable ascetics and Brahmins do not see in unskillful (*akusala*) qualities (*dhamma*) the drawbacks (*ādīnava*), the degradation (*okāra*), and the defilement (*saṃkilesa*); and in skillful (*kusala*) qualities (*dhamma*) the rewards of renunciation (*nekkhamma*), resembling cleansing (*vodānapakkha*).

Because there actually is causality (*hetu*), the view of one who thinks, ‘There is no cause (*hetu*)’ is his wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhi*). Because there actually is causality, when he intends that ‘There is no cause,’ that is his wrong intention (*micchāsaṅkappo*). Because there actually is causality, when he speaks the statement, ‘There is no cause,’ that is his wrong speech (*micchāvācā*). Because there actually is causality, when he says that ‘There is no cause,’ he makes himself an opponent to those *arhats* (*arahanto*) who teach causality (*hetuvādā*). Because there actually is causality, when he persuades another that ‘There is no cause,’ that is persuasion in what is not true Dhamma (*asaddhammasaññatti*). And in that persuasion in what is not true Dhamma, he exalts himself and disparages others.

Whatever good habituation (*susīlya*) he previously had is abandoned, while bad habituation (*dussīlya*) is manifested. And this wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhi*), wrong resolve (*micchāsaṅkappo*), wrong speech (*micchāvācā*), opposition (*paccanīkatā*) to the *arhats* (*ariyānaṃ*), persuasion in what is not true Dhamma (*asaddhammasaññatti*), exaltation of self (*attānukkaṃsanā*), & disparagement (*paravambhanā*) of others: Thus numerous bad unwholesome qualities (*pāpakā akusalā dhammā*) come into play, in dependence on wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhipaccayā*).

“There, householders, an observant person (*viññū puriso*) considers thus: ‘If there is no cause (*hetu*), then—with the breakup of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*paraṃ maraṇā*)—this venerable person (*bhavaṃ purisapuggalo*) has made himself safe (*sotthimattānaṃ karissati*). But if there is a cause (*hetu*), then this venerable person—on the breakup of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*paraṃ maraṇā*)—will reappear in a plane of deprivation (*apāyaṃ*), a bad destination (*duggatiṃ*), a lower realm (*vinipātaṃ*), hell (*nirayaṃ upapajjissati*).

Even if we didn’t speak of causality (*hetu*), and there weren’t the true statement of those venerable ascetics (*samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ*) & Brahmins, this venerable person (*bhavaṃ purisapuggalo*) is still criticized in the here & now by the observant (*viññūnaṃ gārayho*) as a person of bad habits (*dussīlo purisapuggalo*) & wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhi*): one who holds to a doctrine of non-causality (*ahetukavādo*)'.

If there actually is a cause (*hetu*), in this way, this venerable person (*purisapuggalassa*) will have a clinging to contention (*kaliggaho*) in both ways (*ubhayattha*)—both here & now being criticized by the observant (*diṭṭheva dhamme viññūnaṃ gārayho*), and also on the breakup of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*paraṃ maraṇā*), reappearing in a plane of deprivation (*apāyaṃ*), a bad destination (*duggatiṃ*), a lower realm (*vinipātaṃ*), hell (*nirayaṃ upapajjissati*).

Thus this safe-bet teaching (*apaṇṇako dhammo*), when poorly grasped & poorly adopted (*dussamatto samādinno*) by him, covers one side (*ekaṃsaṃ pharitvā tiṭṭhati*), and leaves behind the possibility of the skillful (*kusalaṃ ṭhānaṃ riñcati*).

mula_pali:
102. ‘‘Tatra, gahapatayo, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘atthi hetu, atthi paccayo sattānaṃ saṃkilesāya; sahetū sappaccayā sattā saṃkilissanti.
