Then the venerable Rāhula considered thus: “Who would go into the town for alms today, having been personally admonished by the Blessed One?” Thus, he turned back and sat down at the root of a certain tree, folding his legs crosswise, setting his body erect, and establishing mindfulness in front of him.

The venerable Sāriputta (Śāriputra) saw the venerable Rāhula sitting at the root of a certain tree, folding his legs crosswise, setting his body erect, and establishing mindfulness in front of him. Having seen him, he addressed the venerable Rāhula: "Rāhula, develop mindfulness of breathing (ānāpānasmṛti). Mindfulness of breathing, Rāhula, when developed and cultivated, is of great fruit and great benefit."
commentary_pali:
113.Evaṃme sutanti mahārāhulovādasuttaṃ. Tattha piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhīti dassanaṃ avijahitvā gamanaṃ abbocchinnaṃ katvā pacchato pacchato iriyāpathānubandhanena anubandhi. Tadā hi bhagavā pade padaṃ nikkhipanto vilāsitagamanena purato purato gacchati, rāhulatthero dasabalassa padānupadiko hutvā pacchato pacchato.

Tattha bhagavā supupphitasālavanamajjhagato subhūmiotaraṇatthāya nikkhantamattavaravāraṇo viya virocittha, rāhulabhaddo ca varavāraṇassa pacchato nikkhantagajapotako viya. Bhagavā sāyanhasamaye maṇiguhato nikkhamitvā gocaraṃ paṭipanno kesarasīho viya, rāhulabhaddo ca sīhamigarājānaṃ anubandhanto nikkhantasīhapotako viya. Bhagavā maṇipabbatasassirikavanasaṇḍato dāṭhabalo mahābyaggho viya, rāhulabhaddo ca byaggharājānaṃ anubandhabyagghapotako viya. Bhagavā simbalidāyato nikkhantasupaṇṇarājā viya, rāhulabhaddo ca supaṇṇarājassa pacchato nikkhantasupaṇṇapotako viya. Bhagavā cittakūṭapabbatato gaganatalaṃ pakkhandasuvaṇṇahaṃsarājā viya, rāhulabhaddo ca haṃsādhipatiṃ anupakkhandahaṃsapotako viya. Bhagavā mahāsaraṃ ajjhogāḷhā suvaṇṇamahānāvā viya, rāhulabhaddo ca suvaṇṇanāvaṃ pacchā anubandhanāvāpotako viya. Bhagavā cakkaratanānubhāvena gaganatale sampayātacakkavattirājā viya, rāhulabhaddo ca rājānaṃ anusampayātapariṇāyakaratanaṃ viya. Bhagavā vigatavalāhakaṃ nabhaṃ paṭipannatārakarājā viya, rāhulabhaddo ca tārakādhipatino anumaggapaṭipannā parisuddhaosadhitārakā viya.

Bhagavāpi mahāsammatapaveṇiyaṃ okkākarājavaṃse jāto, rāhulabhaddopi. Bhagavāpi saṅkhe pakkhittakhīrasadiso suparisuddhajātikhattiyakule jāto, rāhulabhaddopi. Bhagavāpi rajjaṃ pahāya pabbajito, rāhulabhaddopi. Bhagavatopi sarīraṃ dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇapaṭimaṇḍitaṃ devanagaresu samussitaratanatoraṇaṃ viya sabbapāliphullo pāricchattako viya ca atimanoharaṇaṃ, rāhulabhaddassāpi. Iti dvepi abhinīhārasampannā, dvepi rājapabbajitā, dvepi khattiyasukhumālā, dvepi suvaṇṇavaṇṇā, dvepi lakkhaṇasampannā ekamaggaṃ paṭipannā paṭipāṭiyā gacchantānaṃ dvinnaṃ candamaṇḍalānaṃ dvinnaṃ sūriyamaṇḍalānaṃ dvinnaṃ sakkasuyāmasantusitasunimmitavasavattimahābrahmādīnaṃ siriyā siriṃ abhibhavamānā viya virociṃsu.

Tatrāyasmā rāhulo bhagavato piṭṭhito piṭṭhito gacchantova pādatalato yāva upari kesantā tathāgataṃ ālokesi. So bhagavato buddhavesavilāsaṃ disvā ‘‘sobhati bhagavā dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇavicittasarīro byāmappabhāparikkhittatāya vippakiṇṇasuvaṇṇacuṇṇamajjhagato viya, vijjulatāparikkhitto kanakapabbato viya, yantasuttasamākaḍḍhitaratanavicittaṃ suvaṇṇaagghikaṃ viya, rattapaṃsukūlacīvarapaṭicchannopi rattakambalaparikkhittakanakapabbato viya, pavāḷalatāpaṭimaṇḍitaṃ suvaṇṇaagghikaṃ viya , cīnapiṭṭhacuṇṇapūjitaṃ suvaṇṇacetiyaṃ viya, lākhārasānulitto kanakayūpo viya, rattavalāhakantarato taṅkhaṇabbhuggatapuṇṇacando viya, aho samatiṃsapāramitānubhāvasajjitassa attabhāvassa sirīsampattī’’ti cintesi. Tato attānampi oloketvā – ‘‘ahampi sobhāmi. Sace bhagavā catūsu mahādīpesu cakkavattirajjaṃ akarissā, mayhaṃ pariṇāyakaṭṭhānantaraṃ adassā. Evaṃ sante ativiya jambudīpatalaṃ asobhissā’’ti attabhāvaṃ nissāya gehassitaṃ chandarāgaṃ uppādesi.

Bhagavāpi purato gacchantova cintesi – ‘‘paripuṇṇacchavimaṃsalohito dāni rāhulassa attabhāvo. Rajanīyesu rūpārammaṇādīsu hi cittassa pakkhandanakālo jāto, kiṃ bahulatāya nu kho rāhulo vītināmetī’’ti. Atha sahāvajjaneneva pasannaudake macchaṃ viya, parisuddhe ādāsamaṇḍale mukhanimittaṃ viya ca tassa taṃ cittuppādaṃ addasa. Disvāva – ‘‘ayaṃ rāhulo mayhaṃ atrajo hutvā mama pacchato āgacchanto ‘ahaṃ sobhāmi, mayhaṃ vaṇṇāyatanaṃ pasanna’nti attabhāvaṃ nissāya gehassitachandarāgaṃ uppādeti, atitthe pakkhando uppathaṃ paṭipanno agocare carati, disāmūḷhaaddhiko viya agantabbaṃ disaṃ gacchati. Ayaṃ kho panassa kileso abbhantare vaḍḍhanto attatthampi yathābhūtaṃ passituṃ na dassati, paratthampi, ubhayatthampi. Tato nirayepi paṭisandhiṃ gaṇhāpessati, tiracchānayoniyampi, pettivisayepi, asurakāyepi, sambādhepi mātukucchisminti anamatagge saṃsāravaṭṭe paripātessati. Ayañhi –

Anatthajanano lobho, lobho cittappakopano;

Bhayamantarato jātaṃ, taṃ jano nāvabujjhati.

Luddho atthaṃ na jānāti, luddho dhammaṃ na passati;

Andhatamaṃ tadā hoti, yaṃ lobho sahate naraṃ. (itivu. 88) –

Yathā kho pana anekaratanapūrā mahānāvā bhinnaphalakantarena udakaṃ ādiyamānā muhuttampi na ajjhupekkhitabbā hoti, vegenassā vivaraṃ pidahituṃ vaṭṭati, evamevaṃ ayampi na ajjhupekkhitabbo. Yāvassa ayaṃ kileso abbhantare sīlaratanādīni na vināseti, tāvadeva naṃ niggaṇhissāmī’’ti ajjhāsayamakāsi. Evarūpesu pana ṭhānesu buddhānaṃ nāgavilokanaṃ nāma hoti. Tasmā yantena parivattitasuvaṇṇapaṭimā viya sakalakāyeneva parivattetvā ṭhito rāhulabhaddaṃ āmantesi. Taṃ sandhāya ‘‘atha kho bhagavā apaloketvā’’tiādi vuttaṃ.

Tattha yaṃkiñci rūpantiādīni sabbākārena visuddhimagge khandhaniddese vitthāritāni. Netaṃ mamātiādīni mahāhatthipadopame vuttāni. Rūpameva nu kho bhagavāti kasmā pucchati? Tassa kira – ‘‘sabbaṃ rūpaṃ netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi na meso attā’’ti sutvā – ‘‘bhagavā sabbaṃ rūpaṃ vipassanāpaññāya evaṃ daṭṭhabbanti vadati, vedanādīsu nu kho kathaṃ paṭipajjitabba’’nti nayo udapādi. Tasmā tasmiṃ naye ṭhito pucchati. Nayakusalo hesa āyasmā rāhulo, idaṃ na kattabbanti vutte idampi na kattabbaṃ idampi na kattabbamevāti nayasatenapi nayasahassenapi paṭivijjhati. Idaṃ kattabbanti vuttepi eseva nayo.

yaṃkiñci rūpa visuddhimagge Netaṃ mamā Rūpameva nu kho bhagavā

Sikkhākāmo hi ayaṃ āyasmā, pātova gandhakuṭipariveṇe patthamattaṃ vālikaṃ okirati – ‘‘ajja sammāsambuddhassa santikā mayhaṃ upajjhāyassa santikā ettakaṃ ovādaṃ ettakaṃ paribhāsaṃ labhāmī’’ti. Sammāsambuddhopi naṃ etadagge ṭhapento – ‘‘etadaggaṃ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhākāmānaṃ yadidaṃ rāhulo’’ti (a. ni. 1.209) sikkhāyameva aggaṃ katvā ṭhapesi. Sopi āyasmā bhikkhusaṅghamajjhe tameva sīhanādaṃ nadi –

‘‘Sabbametaṃ abhiññāya, dhammarājā pitā mama;

Sammukhā bhikkhusaṅghassa, etadagge ṭhapesi maṃ.

Sikkhākāmānahaṃ aggo, dhammarājena thomito;

Saddhāpabbajitānañca, sahāyo pavaro mama.

Dhammarājā pitā mayhaṃ, dhammārakkho ca pettiyo;

Sāriputto upajjhāyo, sabbaṃ me jinasāsana’’nti.

Athassa bhagavā yasmā na kevalaṃ rūpameva, vedanādayopi evaṃ daṭṭhabbā, tasmā rūpampi rāhulātiādimāha. Ko najjāti ko nu ajja. Therassa kira etadahosi ‘‘sammāsambuddho mayhaṃ attabhāvanissitaṃ chandarāgaṃ ñatvā ‘samaṇena nāma evarūpo vitakko na vitakkitabbo’ti neva pariyāyena kathaṃ kathesi, gaccha bhikkhu rāhulaṃ vadehi ‘mā puna evarūpaṃ vitakkaṃ vitakkesī’ti na dūtaṃ pesesi. Maṃ sammukkhe ṭhatvāyeva pana sabhaṇḍakaṃ coraṃ cūḷāya gaṇhanto viya sammukhā sugatovādaṃ adāsi. Sugatovādo ca nāma asaṅkheyyehipi kappehi dullabho. Evarūpassa buddhassa sammukhā ovādaṃ labhitvā ko nu viññū paṇḍitajātiko ajja gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pavisissatī’’ti. Athesa āyasmā āhārakiccaṃ pahāya yasmiṃ nisinnaṭṭhāne ṭhitena ovādo laddho, tatova paṭinivattetvā aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisīdi. Bhagavāpi taṃ āyasmantaṃ nivattamānaṃ disvā na evamāha – ‘‘mā nivatta tāva, rāhula, bhikkhācārakālo te’’ti. Kasmā? Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘ajja tāva kāyagatāsatiamatabhojanaṃ bhuñjatū’’ti.

rūpampi rāhulā Ko najjā

Addasā kho āyasmā sāriputtoti bhagavati gate pacchā gacchanto addasa. Etassa kirāyasmato ekakassa viharato aññaṃ vattaṃ, bhagavatā saddhiṃ viharato aññaṃ. Yadā hi dve aggasāvakā ekākino vasanti, tadā pātova senāsanaṃ sammajjitvā sarīrapaṭijagganaṃ katvā samāpattiṃ appetvā sannisinnā attano cittaruciyā bhikkhācāraṃ gacchanti. Bhagavatā saddhiṃ viharantā pana therā evaṃ na karonti. Tadā hi bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaparivāro paṭhamaṃ bhikkhācāraṃ gacchati. Tasmiṃ gate thero attano senāsanā nikkhamitvā – ‘‘bahūnaṃ vasanaṭṭhāne nāma sabbeva pāsādikaṃ kātuṃ sakkonti vā, na vā sakkontī’’ti tattha tattha gantvā asammaṭṭhaṃ ṭhānaṃ sammajjati. Sace kacavaro achaḍḍito hoti, taṃ chaḍḍeti. Pānīyaṭṭhapetabbaṭṭhānamhi pānīyakūṭe asati pānīyaghaṭaṃ ṭhapeti. Gilānānaṃ santikaṃ gantvā, ‘‘āvuso, tumhākaṃ kiṃ āharāmi, kiṃ vo icchitabba’’nti? Pucchati. Avassikadaharānaṃ santikaṃ gantvā – ‘‘abhiramatha, āvuso, mā ukkaṇṭhittha, paṭipattisārakaṃ buddhasāsana’’nti ovadati. Evaṃ katvā sabbapacchā bhikkhācāraṃ gacchati. Yathā hi cakkavatti kuhiñci gantukāmo senāya parivārito paṭhamaṃ nikkhamati, pariṇāyakaratanaṃ senaṅgāni saṃvidhāya pacchā nikkhamati, evaṃ saddhammacakkavatti bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaparivāro paṭhamaṃ nikkhamati, tassa bhagavato pariṇāyakaratanabhūto dhammasenāpati imaṃ kiccaṃ katvā sabbapacchā nikkhamati. So evaṃ nikkhanto tasmiṃ divase aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisinnaṃ rāhulabhaddaṃ addasa. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘pacchā gacchanto addasā’’ti.

Addasā kho āyasmā sāriputto

Atha kasmā ānāpānassatiyaṃ niyojesi? Nisajjānucchavikattā. Thero kira ‘‘etassa bhagavatā rūpakammaṭṭhānaṃ kathita’’nti anāvajjitvāva yenākārena ayaṃ acalo anobaddho hutvā nisinno, idamassa etissā nisajjāya kammaṭṭhānaṃ anucchavikanti cintetvā evamāha. Tattha ānāpānassatinti assāsapassāse pariggahetvā tattha catukkapañcakajjhānaṃ nibbattetvā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā arahattaṃ gaṇhāhīti dasseti.

ānāpānassati

Mahapphalā hotīti kīvamahapphalā hoti? Idha bhikkhu ānāpānassatiṃ anuyutto ekāsane nisinnova sabbāsave khepetvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, tathā asakkonto maraṇakāle samasīsī hoti, tathā asakkonto devaloke nibbattitvā dhammakathikadevaputtassa dhammaṃ sutvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, tato viraddho anuppanne buddhuppāde paccekabodhiṃ sacchikaroti, taṃ asacchikaronto buddhānaṃ sammukhībhāve bāhiyattherādayo viya khippābhiñño hoti, evaṃ mahapphalā. Mahānisaṃsāti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Vuttampi cetaṃ –

Mahapphalā hotī Mahānisaṃsā

‘‘Ānāpānassatī yassa, paripuṇṇā subhāvitā;

Anupubbaṃ paricitā, yathā buddhena desitā;

Somaṃ lokaṃ pabhāseti, abbhā muttova candimā’’ti. (theragā. 548; paṭi. ma. 1.1.60) –

Imaṃ mahapphalataṃ sampassamāno thero saddhivihārikaṃ tattha niyojeti.

Iti bhagavā rūpakammaṭṭhānaṃ, thero ānāpānassatinti ubhopi kammaṭṭhānaṃ ācikkhitvā gatā, rāhulabhaddo vihāreyeva ohīno. Bhagavā tassa ohīnabhāvaṃ jānantopi neva attanā khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ gahetvā agamāsi, na ānandattherassa hatthe pesesi, na pasenadimahārājaanāthapiṇḍikādīnaṃ saññaṃ adāsi. Saññāmattakañhi labhitvā te kājabhattaṃ abhihareyyuṃ. Yathā ca bhagavā, evaṃ sāriputtattheropi na kiñci akāsi. Rāhulatthero nirāhāro chinnabhatto ahosi. Tassa panāyasmato – ‘‘bhagavā maṃ vihāre ohīnaṃ jānantopi attanā laddhapiṇḍapātaṃ nāpi sayaṃ gahetvā āgato, na aññassa hatthe pahiṇi , na manussānaṃ saññaṃ adāsi, upajjhāyopi me ohīnabhāvaṃ jānanto tatheva na kiñci akāsī’’ti cittampi na uppannaṃ, kuto tappaccayā omānaṃ vā atimānaṃ vā janessati. Bhagavatā pana ācikkhitakammaṭṭhānameva purebhattampi pacchābhattampi – ‘‘itipi rūpaṃ aniccaṃ, itipi dukkhaṃ, itipi asubhaṃ, itipi anattā’’ti aggiṃ abhimatthento viya nirantaraṃ manasikatvā sāyanhasamaye cintesi – ‘‘ahaṃ upajjhāyena ānāpānassatiṃ bhāvehīti vutto , tassa vacanaṃ na karissāmi. Ācariyupajjhāyānañhi vacanaṃ akaronto dubbaco nāma hoti. ‘Dubbaco rāhulo, upajjhāyassapi vacanaṃ na karotī’ti ca garahuppattito kakkhaḷatarā pīḷā nāma natthī’’ti bhāvanāvidhānaṃ pucchitukāmo bhagavato santikaṃ agamāsi. Taṃ dassetuṃ atha kho āyasmā rāhulotiādi vuttaṃ.

atha kho āyasmā rāhulo
commentary_english:
113. Thus have I heard: the Great Rāhula Instruction Discourse. There, "following closely behind" means following closely behind with continuous gait, not abandoning the sight, making no break in the going, but pursuing in the rear. Then, indeed, the Blessed One, placing foot after foot, walks in front, in front, with graceful gait. The venerable Rāhula follows closely behind, step by step, of the Ten-Powered One. There, the Blessed One, in the middle of a Sāla forest with very beautiful blossoms, shone forth like a magnificent, just-emerged elephant, come forth for the sake of descending to an excellent ground. And Rāhulabhadra [shone forth] like a young elephant calf, come forth behind the magnificent elephant. The Blessed One, having emerged from the jewel cave at evening time and set out for alms, [was] like a lion with a flowing mane. And Rāhulabhadra, following the lion-king, [was] like a lion cub that has just emerged. The Blessed One, from the jewel mountain with a forest grove abounding in beauty, [was] like a powerful, great tiger. And Rāhulabhadra [was] like a tiger cub following the tiger-king. The Blessed One, from the Simali tree, [was] like a Garuda king who has just emerged. And Rāhulabhadra [was] like a Garuda chick that has just emerged behind the Garuda king. The Blessed One, from Mount Citrakūṭa to the surface of the sky, [was] like a golden swan-king soaring up. And Rāhulabhadra [was] like a swan chick soaring up after the swan lord. The Blessed One, plunging into the great lake, [was] like a great golden ship. And Rāhulabhadra [was] like a ship-calf following behind the golden ship. The Blessed One, by the power of the wheel-jewel, on the surface of the sky, [was] like a wheel-turning king who has just set forth. And Rāhulabhadra [was] like the guide-jewel that has set forth afterwards the king. The Blessed One, to the cloudless sky, [was] like a star-king who has just set out. And Rāhulabhadra [was] like a pure medicinal star who has set out on the path following the star lord. The Blessed One, too, was born in the Okkāka royal lineage of the Great Appointed Lineage; Rāhulabhadra too. The Blessed One, too, like milk poured into a conch shell, was born in a very pure, high-born Kṣatriya family; Rāhulabhadra too. The Blessed One, too, having abandoned kingship, went forth; Rāhulabhadra too. The Blessed One's body, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, [was] like a jewel arch raised up in a city of gods, and, with every branch fully blossoming, [was] like a *pāricchattaka* tree, and was exceedingly delightful; Rāhulabhadra's too. Thus, both were accomplished in resolution, both were royal renunciates, both were Kṣatriyas [and] tender, both were of golden hue, both were accomplished in marks, having set out on the one path. As they went along in due order, they shone forth like two moon-orbs, two sun-orbs, overcoming the glory of two Sakka, Suyāma, Santuṣita, Sunirmita, Vasavatti, Great Brahmā, and others. There, the venerable Rāhula, walking behind, behind, the Blessed One, gazed upon the Tathāgata from the soles of his feet up to the tips of his hair. Seeing the Blessed One's display of the Buddha's vesture, he thought, "The Blessed One is beautiful, his body, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, with a variegated body, because it is encompassed by a fathom's radiance, [is] like one who has entered into the midst of scattered gold dust, [is] like a golden mountain encircled by a lightning flash, [is] like a golden altar adorned with variegated jewels drawn together with a machine-thread, even though covered with a robe made of rags taken from a dust heap, [is] like a golden mountain encircled by a red blanket, [is] like a golden altar adorned with coral vines, [is] like a golden *cetiya* honored with Chinese flour powder, [is] like a golden sacrificial post smeared with lac-resin, [is] like a full moon that has just risen up from the midst of a red cloud bank. O, the prosperity and success of the glory of the being of one who is endowed with the power of the surpassing perfections!" Then, having looked at himself, too, [he thought]: "I, too, am beautiful. If the Blessed One were to rule as a wheel-turning monarch in the four great continents, he would give me the position of guide-jewel. Thus being the case, this surface of Jambudvīpa would be exceedingly beautiful." Relying on his own being, he generated desire-passion connected with the household life. The Blessed One, too, walking in front, thought, "Now, Rāhula's being is full of complexion, flesh, and blood. Indeed, this is a time for the mind to rush forth in regard to desirable objects such as forms. Will Rāhula spend his time with much diligence, or not?" Then, just as a fish in clear water, just as a reflection of a face in a very pure mirror, so, with his very mindfulness, he saw that thought that had arisen in him. Having seen [it], he said, "This Rāhula, having become my own son, coming behind me, relying on his own being, generates desire-passion connected with the household life, [thinking,] 'I am beautiful, my sphere of color is pleasing.' He rushes forth to an improper place, sets out on a wrong path, conducts himself in an improper pasture. [He is] like a wayfarer confused as to direction, he goes to a direction that should not be gone to. This defilement of his, growing inside, will not allow [him] to see even his own welfare as it actually is, much less [the welfare] of others, [or the welfare] of both. From that, it will cause [him] to take rebirth even in hell, and in the animal womb, and in the realm of ghosts, and in the Asura body, and even in the crowded mother's womb. Thus, in this cycle of existence with no known beginning, he will fall down." This indeed – Lust, generating what is detrimental, is a disturber of the mind; Fear born from within, that, people do not understand. The greedy person does not know the meaning; The greedy person does not see the *dharma*; Then there is utter darkness, which greed overpowers the person. (Thus it was said. 88) – Just as a great ship filled with many treasures, taking in water through a broken plank, should not be neglected even for a moment, but it is fitting to quickly stop up its opening, just so, this too should not be neglected. As long as this defilement does not destroy the moral jewels, etc., within, just so long will I restrain it," he made an intention. In such places, the *nāga*-glance of the Buddhas is called a name. Therefore, like a golden statue turned by a machine, having turned around with his whole body, he addressed Rāhula Bhadda. With reference to that, it was said, "Then, indeed, the Blessed One, having looked around," etc. There, whatever form, etc., in all ways, in the *Visuddhimagga*, in the section on the aggregates, have been extensively taught. "This is not mine," etc., in the simile of the great elephant footprint, were stated. "Is it just form, Blessed One?" Why does he ask? For him, it is said – having heard, "All form is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self" – "The Blessed One says that all form should be seen thus with the wisdom of insight, but how should one practice with regard to feeling, etc.?" an understanding arose. Therefore, standing in that way, he asks. Skillful in understanding, indeed, is the venerable Rāhula. Having been told, "This should not be done," this too should not be done, this too should not be done, thus he discerns with hundreds of ways, even thousands of ways. Even having been told, "This should be done," just this is the way. Whatever form, in the *Visuddhimagga*, "This is not mine," "Is it just form, Blessed One?" The venerable one is desirous of training, early in the morning in the vicinity of the Perfumed Chamber Monastery, he sprinkles a measure of sand – "Today, from the presence of the Perfectly Awakened One, from the presence of my preceptor, I will receive this much advice, this much instruction." The Perfectly Awakened One also, establishing him in this foremost position – "This is foremost, monks, of my disciples, monks, who are desirous of training, that is, Rāhula" (A. Ni. 1. 209), having made training itself foremost, he established him. That venerable one also, in the midst of the community of monks, uttered that same lion's roar – "All this, for direct knowledge, the *dharma*-king is my father; In front of the community of monks, he established me in this foremost position. Desirous of training, I am foremost, praised by the *dharma*-king; And of those who have gone forth in faith, I am an excellent companion. The *dharma*-king is my father, *dharma*-protection also is paternal; Sāriputta is my preceptor, all this is the Buddha's Dispensation." Then, the Blessed One, because not only form, but also feeling, etc., should be seen thus, therefore, he spoke, beginning with, "Form too, Rāhula." "*Ko najjā*," who now today? To the elder, this occurred: "The Perfectly Awakened One, knowing my desire-passion based on self-regard, 'Such a thought should not be thought by a renunciate,' thus, not even in a roundabout way, did he tell a story. Go, monk, tell Rāhula, 'Do not again think such a thought!'” he did not send a messenger. Standing in front of me, as if seizing a thief with goods and hair, face to face he gave the Sugata's teaching. And the Sugata's teaching, by name, is difficult to obtain even in countless *aeons*. Having obtained advice in the presence of such a Buddha, who now, a discerning one, of wise birth, today would enter the village for alms?" Then, the venerable one, having given up the business of eating and drinking, sat down at the foot of a certain tree, after returning from the place where he had received the instruction while standing. The Blessed One also, seeing the venerable one returning, did not say this: "Do not return yet, Rāhula, it is your time for collecting alms." Why? It occurred to him thus: "Let him enjoy the ambrosial food of mindfulness immersed in the body today."

rūpampi rāhulā ko najjā

"The venerable Sāriputta saw," that is, he saw [him] walking behind after the Blessed One had gone. It seems the venerable one has one kind of behavior when dwelling alone, and another when dwelling with the Blessed One. When two chief disciples dwell alone, early in the morning, having swept the lodging, having attended to the body, having averted [mental] dullness, being seated, according to their own inclination, they go for alms. But the elders, dwelling with the Blessed One, do not do thus. For then the Blessed One, surrounded by a retinue of monks, goes for alms first. Having gone, the elder, after leaving his lodging, thinking, "Indeed, in a dwelling place for many, all are able to make [the place] pleasing or not able to make [it] pleasing," going here and there, sweeps the place that is unswept. If there is any rubbish thrown away, he throws it away. In a place where water should be placed, if there is no water pot, he places a water pot. Going to the sick, he asks, "Friend, what shall I bring for you? What do you desire?" Going to the young novices, he exhorts them, "Take delight, friends, do not be discontented, the Buddha's teaching is conducive to practice." Having done thus, he goes for alms last of all. Just as a wheel-turning monarch, wishing to go anywhere, surrounded by his army, goes forth first, and the guiding jewel, having arranged the divisions of the army, goes forth afterwards, so too, the Blessed One, the righteous wheel-turning monarch, surrounded by a retinue of monks, goes forth first, and the general of the Dhamma, who is like a guiding jewel of that Blessed One, having done this task, goes forth last of all. So, having gone forth thus, on that day, he saw Rāhulabhadra seated at the foot of a certain tree. Therefore it was said, "He saw [him] walking behind."

The venerable Sāriputta saw

Then why did he direct him to mindfulness of breathing? Because sitting was suitable for him. It seems the elder, without reflecting, "The Blessed One has spoken of a meditation subject concerning form for this one," thinking, "In whatever manner this one is seated, being unmoving, unperturbed, this meditation subject is suitable for this sitting of his," spoke thus. There, mindfulness of breathing means, having grasped the in-breath and out-breath there, having produced the fourfold or fivefold jhāna, having developed insight, it shows [the way] to attain Arhatship.

Mindfulness of breathing

is of great fruit means, how great is the fruit? Here, a monk, devoted to mindfulness of breathing, seated in one seat, having destroyed all the āsavas, attains Arhatship; so too, if he is unable, at the time of death, he becomes of equanimity; so too, if he is unable, having been reborn in the deva world, having heard the Dhamma from a deva son who is a preacher of the Dhamma, he attains Arhatship; then, having been deprived, in a time when no Buddha has arisen, he realizes individual enlightenment; if he does not realize that, in the presence of Buddhas, like the elders beginning with Bāhiya, he becomes swift in understanding; thus it is of great fruit. Of great benefit is a synonym for that itself. This also was said –

Is of great fruit is of great benefit

"Mindfulness of breathing for whom, is fully perfected, well cultivated;

practiced in due order, as taught by the Buddha;

illumines this world, like the moon freed from a cloud." (Theragā. 548; Paṭi. Ma. 1. 1. 60) –

Seeing this great fruitfulness, the elder directs his co-resident monk to that. iti *bhagavā* rūpakammaṭṭhānaṃ, thero ānāpānassatinti ubhopi kammaṭṭhānaṃ ācikkhitvā gatā, rāhulabhaddo vihāreyeva ohīno. Then the Blessed One [gave instruction on] the meditation subject (kammaṭṭhāna) of rūpa (form), the Elder gave instruction on mindfulness of breathing (*ānāpānassati*); both of them having given instruction on the *kammaṭṭhāna*, departed. Rāhulabhadra remained in the *vihāra*. bhagavā tassa ohīnabhāvaṃ jānantopi neva attanā khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ gahetvā agamāsi, na ānandattherassa hatthe pesesi, na pasenadimahārājaanāthapiṇḍikādīnaṃ saññaṃ adāsi. Though the Blessed One knew of his decline, he neither personally went, taking fresh or cooked food, nor did he send it in the hand of Ānanda, nor did he give a sign to Pasenadi, Mahārāja, Anāthapiṇḍika, and the others. saññāmattakañhi labhitvā te kājabhattaṃ abhihareyyuṃ. "For having obtained just a sign, they would bring him suitable food." yathā ca bhagavā, evaṃ sāriputtattheropi na kiñci akāsi. Just as the Blessed One, so also Sāriputta did nothing. rāhulatthero nirāhāro chinnabhatto ahosi. Rāhula, the Elder, became without nourishment, deprived of food. tassa panāyasmato – ‘‘bhagavā maṃ vihāre ohīnaṃ jānantopi attanā laddhapiṇḍapātaṃ nāpi sayaṃ gahetvā āgato, na aññassa hatthe pahiṇi , na manussānaṃ saññaṃ adāsi, upajjhāyopi me ohīnabhāvaṃ jānanto tatheva na kiñci akāsī’’ti cittampi na uppannaṃ, kuto tappaccayā omānaṃ vā atimānaṃ vā janessati. Then to that venerable one [occurred the thought]: "Though the Blessed One knows that I am declining in the *vihāra*, he neither himself, having taken the alms-food he had received, came, nor did he send it in the hand of another, nor did he give a sign to men. My preceptor also, knowing of my declining state, likewise did nothing." Even the thought did not arise: "Why will he generate conceit or disdain on account of that cause?" bhagavatā pana ācikkhitakammaṭṭhānameva purebhattampi pacchābhattampi – ‘‘itipi rūpaṃ aniccaṃ, itipi dukkhaṃ, itipi asubhaṃ, itipi anattā’’ti aggiṃ abhimatthento viya nirantaraṃ manasikatvā sāyanhasamaye cintesi – ‘‘ahaṃ upajjhāyena ānāpānassatiṃ bhāvehīti vutto , tassa vacanaṃ na karissāmi. But constantly reflecting on the meditation subject that the Blessed One had taught, both before and after the meal—"Thus also form is impermanent, thus also suffering, thus also impure, thus also not-self," like one kindling a fire, he thought in the evening: "I was told by my preceptor, 'Develop mindfulness of breathing,' [but] I will not do that instruction. ācariyupajjhāyānañhi vacanaṃ akaronto dubbaco nāma hoti. For one who does not follow the instruction of the teacher and preceptor is called 'difficult to speak to.' ‘dubbaco rāhulo, upajjhāyassapi vacanaṃ na karotī’ti ca garahuppattito kakkhaḷatarā pīḷā nāma natthī’’ti bhāvanāvidhānaṃ pucchitukāmo bhagavato santikaṃ agamāsi. There is no suffering more severe than blame arising from 'Rāhula is difficult to speak to; he does not follow even the instruction of his preceptor.'" Desiring to ask about the method of meditation, he went to the Blessed One. taṃ dassetuṃ atha kho āyasmā rāhulo tiādi vuttaṃ. To show that, it was said, "Then, indeed, the venerable Rāhula," and so forth.

mula_pali: 114. Atha kho āyasmā rāhulo sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rāhulo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘kathaṃ bhāvitā nu kho, bhante, ānāpānassati, kathaṃ bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā’’ti? ‘‘Yaṃ kiñci, rāhula, ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ kakkhaḷaṃ kharigataṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – kesā lomā nakhā dantā taco maṃsaṃ nhāru nahāru (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) aṭṭhi aṭṭhimiñjaṃ vakkaṃ hadayaṃ yakanaṃ kilomakaṃ pihakaṃ papphāsaṃ antaṃ antaguṇaṃ udariyaṃ karīsaṃ, yaṃ vā panaññampi kiñci ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ kakkhaḷaṃ kharigataṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, rāhula, ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu paṭhavīdhātu (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). Yā ceva kho pana ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu yā ca bāhirā pathavīdhātu, pathavīdhāturevesā. Taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā pathavīdhātuyā nibbindati, pathavīdhātuyā cittaṃ virājeti’’.
mula_english:
Then, when it was evening, the venerable Rāhula rose from meditation and went to the Blessed One. After approaching, paying homage to the Blessed One, he sat down at one side.

Seated to one side, the venerable Rāhula said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, how is mindfulness of breathing developed and cultivated, so that it is of great fruit and great benefit?"

"Whatever, Rāhula, is internal, belonging to oneself, is solid, solidified, and clung-to, that is, head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys (vakkaṃ), heart (hadayaṃ), liver (yakanaṃ), diaphragm, spleen, lungs, large intestines, small intestines, contents of the stomach, feces, or whatever else internally, belonging to oneself, is solid, solidified, and clung-to: this is called, Rāhula, the internal earth element (ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu). Now both the internal earth element and the external earth element are simply the earth element (pathavīdhātu). That, 'this is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’—thus should it be seen as it actually is with proper wisdom (sammappaññāya). When one sees it thus as it actually is with proper wisdom, one becomes disenchanted with the earth element and makes the mind dispassionate towards the earth element."
commentary_pali:
114. Tattha paṭisallānāti ekībhāvato. Yaṃkiñci rāhulāti kasmā? Bhagavā ānāpānassatiṃ puṭṭho rūpakammaṭṭhānaṃ kathetīti. Rūpe chandarāgappahānatthaṃ. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘rāhulassa attabhāvaṃ nissāya chandarāgo uppanno, heṭṭhā cassa saṅkhepena rūpakammaṭṭhānaṃ kathitaṃ. Idānissāpi dvicattālīsāya ākārehi attabhāvaṃ virājetvā visaṅkharitvā taṃnissitaṃ chandarāgaṃ anuppattidhammataṃ āpādessāmī’’ti. Atha ākāsadhātuṃ kasmā vitthāresīti? Upādārūpadassanatthaṃ. Heṭṭhā hi cattāri mahābhūtāneva kathitāni, na upādārūpaṃ. Tasmā iminā mukhena taṃ dassetuṃ ākāsadhātuṃ vitthāresi. Apica ajjhattikena ākāsena paricchinnarūpampi pākaṭaṃ hoti.

Ākāsena paricchinnaṃ, rūpaṃ yāti vibhūtataṃ;

Tassevaṃ āvibhāvatthaṃ, taṃ pakāsesi nāyako.

Ettha pana purimāsu tāva catūsu dhātūsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ mahāhatthipadopame vuttameva.
commentary_english:
114. There, *paṭisallānā* means due to unification.

*yaṃkiñci rāhulā*—why [is this said]? [It is] because the Blessed One, being questioned about mindfulness of breathing, is teaching the subject of form.

[It is] for the sake of abandoning desire and lust for form.

Thus, it occurred to him: “Desire and lust arose in Rāhula relying on the self; and for him the subject of form was taught concisely below.

Even now, having eliminated and disintegrated the self with forty-two characteristics, I will bring the desire and lust dependent on that to the state of non-arising.”

Then, why did he expand on the space element? [It is] for the sake of showing derived form (*upādārūpa*).

For below, only the four great elements were spoken of, not derived form.

Therefore, with this approach, in order to show that, he expanded on the space element.

Moreover, even defined form becomes manifest by internal space.

Defined by space, form attains distinctness;

The leader revealed that, for the sake of its manifestation.

Here, however, what should be said about the first four elements has already been said in the *Mahāhatthipadopama*.

mula_pali: 115. ‘‘Katamā ca, rāhula, āpodhātu? Āpodhātu siyā ajjhattikā, siyā bāhirā. Katamā ca, rāhula, ajjhattikā āpodhātu ? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ āpo āpogataṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – pittaṃ semhaṃ pubbo lohitaṃ sedo medo assu vasā kheḷo siṅghāṇikā lasikā muttaṃ, yaṃ vā panaññampi kiñci ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ āpo āpogataṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, rāhula, ajjhattikā āpodhātu. Yā ceva kho pana ajjhattikā āpodhātu yā ca bāhirā āpodhātu āpodhāturevesā. Taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā āpodhātuyā nibbindati, āpodhātuyā cittaṃ virājeti.
mula_english:
115. And what, Rāhula, is the *āpo-dhātu*, the water element? The water element (*āpo-dhātu*) may be internal (*ajjhattikā*), or it may be external (*bāhirā*).

And what, Rāhula, is the internal (*ajjhattikā*) water element (*āpo-dhātu*)? Whatever internally (*ajjhattaṃ*), belonging to oneself (*paccattaṃ*), is water (*āpo*), watery (*āpogataṃ*), and clung-to (*upādinnaṃ*), that is, bile (*pittaṃ*), phlegm (*semhaṃ*), pus (*pubbo*), blood (*lohitaṃ*), sweat (*sedo*), fat (*medo*), tears (*assu*), grease (*vasā*), spittle (*kheḷo*), snot (*siṅghāṇikā*), synovial fluid (*lasikā*), urine (*muttaṃ*), or whatever else internally (*ajjhattaṃ*), belonging to oneself (*paccattaṃ*), is water (*āpo*), watery (*āpogataṃ*), and clung-to (*upādinnaṃ*): this is called the internal (*ajjhattikā*) water element (*āpo-dhātu*), Rāhula.

Now both the internal (*ajjhattikā*) water element (*āpo-dhātu*) and the external (*bāhirā*) water element (*āpo-dhātu*) are simply water element (*āpodhāturevesā*).

And that should be seen as it actually is (*yathābhūtaṃ*) with proper wisdom (*sammappaññāya*) thus: ‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā’ti*).’

When one sees it thus as it actually is (*yathābhūtaṃ*) with proper wisdom (*sammappaññāya*), one becomes disenchanted (*nibbindati*) with the water element (*āpodhātuyā*) and makes the mind dispassionate (*virājeti*) towards the water element (*āpodhātuyā*).

mula_pali: 116. ‘‘Katamā ca, rāhula, tejodhātu? Tejodhātu siyā ajjhattikā, siyā bāhirā. Katamā ca, rāhula, ajjhattikā tejodhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ tejo tejogataṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – yena ca santappati yena ca jīrīyati yena ca pariḍayhati yena ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ sammā pariṇāmaṃ gacchati, yaṃ vā panaññampi kiñci ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ tejo tejogataṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, rāhula, ajjhattikā tejodhātu. Yā ceva kho pana ajjhattikā tejodhātu yā ca bāhirā tejodhātu tejodhāturevesā. Taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā tejodhātuyā nibbindati, tejodhātuyā cittaṃ virājeti.
mula_english:
“What, Rāhula, is the *tejodhātu* (fire element)? The *tejodhātu* (fire element) may be internal (*ajjhattikā*), or may be external (*bāhirā*).

“What, Rāhula, is the internal (*ajjhattikā*) *tejodhātu* (fire element)? Whatever internally, belonging to oneself (*paccattaṃ*), is fire (*tejo*), fiery (*tejogataṃ*), and clung-to (*upādinnaṃ*), that is, that by which one is warmed (*santappati*), ages (*jīrīyati*), and is consumed (*pariḍayhati*), and that by which what is eaten (*asitaṃ*), drunk (*pītaṃ*), consumed (*khāyitaṃ*), and tasted (*sāyitaṃ*) gets completely digested (*sammā pariṇāmaṃ gacchati*), or whatever else internally, belonging to oneself, is fire, fiery, and clung-to: this is called the internal fire element.

Now both the internal fire element and the external fire element are simply fire element.

And that should be seen as it actually is with proper wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā*)’

When one sees it thus as it actually is with proper wisdom, one becomes disenchanted with the fire element and makes the mind dispassionate towards the fire element.

mula_pali: 117. ‘‘Katamā ca, rāhula, vāyodhātu? Vāyodhātu siyā ajjhattikā, siyā bāhirā. Katamā ca, rāhula, ajjhattikā vāyodhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – uddhaṅgamā vātā, adhogamā vātā, kucchisayā vātā, koṭṭhāsayā koṭṭhasayā (sī. pī.) vātā , aṅgamaṅgānusārino vātā, assāso passāso, iti yaṃ vā panaññampi kiñci ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ upādinnaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, rāhula, ajjhattikā vāyodhātu. Yā ceva kho pana ajjhattikā vāyodhātu yā ca bāhirā vāyodhātu vāyodhāturevesā. Taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi , na meso attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā vāyodhātuyā nibbindati, vāyodhātuyā cittaṃ virājeti.
mula_english:
117.
’’And what, Rāhula, is the *vāyodhātu* (wind element)? The *vāyodhātu* may be internal (*ajjhattikā*), or may be external (*bāhirā*).

And what, Rāhula, is the internal *ajjhattikā vāyodhātu*? Whatever internally, belonging to oneself, is *vāyu* (air), airy (*vāyugata*), and clung-to (*upādinnaṃ*), that is, up-going winds (*uddhaṅgamā vātā*), down-going winds (*adhogamā vātā*), winds in the belly (*kucchisayā vātā*), winds in the bowels (*koṭṭhāsayā vātā*), winds that course through the limbs (*aṅgamaṅgānusārino vātā*), in-breath (*assāso*) and out-breath (*passāso*), or whatever else internally, belonging to oneself, is *vāyu* (air), airy (*vāyogata*), and clung-to (*upādinnaṃ*): this is called the internal *ajjhattikā vāyodhātu*.

Now both the internal *ajjhattikā vāyodhātu* and the external *bāhirā vāyodhātu* are simply *vāyodhātu*.

That ‘this is not mine (netaṃ mama), this I am not (nesohamasmi), this is not my self (na meso attā)’—so it is with this to be seen as it actually is (*yathābhūtaṃ*) with proper wisdom (*sammappaññāya*).

When one sees it thus as it actually is (*yathābhūtaṃ*) with proper wisdom (*sammappaññāya*), one becomes disenchanted (*nibbindati*) with the *vāyodhātu* and makes the mind dispassionate (*virājeti*) toward the *vāyodhātu*.

mula_pali: 118. ‘‘Katamā ca, rāhula, ākāsadhātu? Ākāsadhātu siyā ajjhattikā, siyā bāhirā. Katamā ca, rāhula, ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu? Yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ ākāsaṃ ākāsagataṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – kaṇṇacchiddaṃ nāsacchiddaṃ mukhadvāraṃ, yena ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ ajjhoharati, yattha ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ santiṭṭhati, yena ca asitapītakhāyitasāyitaṃ adhobhāgaṃ adhobhāgā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) nikkhamati, yaṃ vā panaññampi kiñci ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ ākāsaṃ ākāsagataṃ, aghaṃ aghagataṃ, vivaraṃ vivaragataṃ, asamphuṭṭhaṃ, maṃsalohitehi upādinnaṃ ākāsagataṃ upādinnaṃ (sī. pī.) – ayaṃ vuccati, rāhula, ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu. Yā ceva kho pana ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu yā ca bāhirā ākāsadhātu ākāsadhāturevesā. Taṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya disvā ākāsadhātuyā cittaṃ nibbindati, ākāsadhātuyā cittaṃ virājeti.
mula_english:
118. And what, Rāhula, is the space element (*ākāśadhātu*)? The space element (*ākāśadhātu*) may be internal (*ajjhattikā*), or may be external (*bāhirā*).

And what, Rāhula, is the internal space element (*ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu*)? Whatever internally (*ajjhattaṃ*), belonging to oneself (*paccattaṃ*), is space (*ākāsaṃ*), spatial (*ākāsagataṃ*), and clung-to (*upādinnaṃ*), that is, the holes of the ears (*kaṇṇacchiddaṃ*), the nostrils (*nāsacchiddaṃ*), the door of the mouth (*mukhadvāraṃ*), and that aperture whereby what is eaten (*asita*), drunk (*pīta*), consumed (*khāyita*), and tasted (*sāyita*) gets swallowed (*ajjhoharati*), and where what is eaten, drunk, consumed, and tasted collects (*santiṭṭhati*), and whereby what is eaten, drunk, consumed, and tasted is excreted (*nikkhamati*) from below (*adhobhāgaṃ*), or whatever else internally, belonging to oneself, is space, spatial, the bad, related to the bad, a hole, related to a hole, unimpinged, and clung-to by flesh and blood (*maṃsalohitehi upādinnaṃ*): that, Rāhula, is called the internal space element (*ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu*).

Now both the internal space element (*ajjhattikā ākāsadhātu*) and the external space element (*bāhirā ākāsadhātu*) are simply space element (*ākāsadhāturevesā*).

That should be seen as it actually is (*yathābhūtaṃ*) with proper wisdom (*sammappaññāya*) thus: ‘This is not mine (*netaṃ mama*), this I am not (*nesohamasmi*), this is not my self (*na meso attā*.’)

When one sees it thus as it actually is with proper wisdom, one becomes disenchanted (*nibbindati*) with the space element (*ākāsadhātuyā*) and makes the mind (*cittaṃ*) dispassionate (*virājeti*) towards the space element.
commentary_pali: 118. Ākāsadhātuyaṃ ākāsagatanti ākāsabhāvaṃ gataṃ. Upādinnantiādinnaṃ gahitaṃ parāmaṭṭhaṃ, sarīraṭṭhakanti attho. Kaṇṇacchiddanti maṃsalohitādīhi asamphuṭṭhakaṇṇavivaraṃ. Nāsacchiddādīsupi eseva nayo. Yenacāti yena chiddena. Ajjhoharatīti anto paveseti, jivhābandhanato hi yāva udarapaṭalā manussānaṃ vidatthicaturaṅgulaṃ chiddaṭṭhānaṃ hoti. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Yattha cāti yasmiṃ okāse. Santiṭṭhatīti patiṭṭhāti. Manussānañhi mahantaṃ paṭaparissāvanamattañca udarapaṭalaṃ nāma hoti. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Adhobhāgaṃ nikkhamatīti yena heṭṭhā nikkhamati. Dvattiṃsahatthamattaṃ ekavīsatiyā ṭhānesu vaṅkaṃ antaṃ nāma hoti. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Yaṃ vā panaññampīti iminā sukhumasukhumaṃ cammamaṃsādiantaragatañceva lomakūpabhāvena ca ṭhitaṃ ākāsaṃ dasseti. Sesametthāpi pathavīdhātuādīsu vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
118. *ākāśadhātūyaṃ*, *ākāsagata*nti ākāśabhāvaṃ gataṃ.

*upādinna*ntiādinnnaṃ, gahitam, parāmaṭṭhaṃ, *śarīraṭṭhakanti attho*.

*kaṇṇacchidda*nti *maṃsa-lohitādīhi asamphuṭṭha-kaṇṇa-vivaraṃ*.

*nāsacchiddādīsupi eseva nayo*.

*yena cā*ti yena chiddena.

*ajjhoharatī*ti anto paveseti, *jivhābandhanato hi yāva udarapaṭalā manussānaṃ vidatthicaturaṅgulaṃ chiddaṭṭhānaṃ hoti*.

*taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ*.

*yattha cā*ti yasmiṃ okāse.

*santiṭṭhatī*ti patiṭṭhāti.

*manussānañhi mahantaṃ paṭaparissāvanamattañca udarapaṭalaṃ nāma hoti*.

*taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ*.

*adhobhāgaṃ nikkhamatī*ti yena heṭṭhā nikkhamati.

*dvattiṃsahatthamattaṃ ekavīsatiyā ṭhānesu vaṅkaṃ antaṃ nāma hoti*.

*taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ*.

*yaṃ vā panaññampī*ti iminā sukhumasukhumaṃ cammamaṃsādiantaragatañceva lomakūpabhāvena ca ṭhitaṃ ākāsaṃ dasseti.

sesametthāpi *pṛthivīdhātu*-ādīsu vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.

mula_pali:
119. ‘‘Pathavīsamaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Pathavīsamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassanti. Seyyathāpi, rāhula, pathaviyā sucimpi nikkhipanti, asucimpi nikkhipanti, gūthagatampi nikkhipanti, muttagatampi nikkhipanti, kheḷagatampi nikkhipanti, pubbagatampi nikkhipanti, lohitagatampi nikkhipanti, na ca tena pathavī aṭṭīyati vā harāyati vā jigucchati vā; evameva kho tvaṃ, rāhula, pathavīsamaṃ bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Pathavīsamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassanti.

‘‘Āposamaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Āposamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassanti. Seyyathāpi, rāhula, āpasmiṃ sucimpi dhovanti, asucimpi dhovanti, gūthagatampi dhovanti, muttagatampi dhovanti, kheḷagatampi dhovanti, pubbagatampi dhovanti, lohitagatampi dhovanti, na ca tena āpo aṭṭīyati vā harāyati vā jigucchati vā; evameva kho tvaṃ, rāhula, āposamaṃ bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Āposamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassanti.

‘‘Tejosamaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Tejosamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassanti. Seyyathāpi, rāhula, tejo sucimpi dahati, asucimpi dahati, gūthagatampi dahati, muttagatampi dahati, kheḷagatampi dahati, pubbagatampi dahati, lohitagatampi dahati, na ca tena tejo aṭṭīyati vā harāyati vā jigucchati vā; evameva kho tvaṃ, rāhula, tejosamaṃ bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Tejosamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassanti.

‘‘Vāyosamaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Vāyosamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassanti. Seyyathāpi, rāhula, vāyo sucimpi upavāyati, asucimpi upavāyati, gūthagatampi upavāyati, muttagatampi upavāyati, kheḷagatampi upavāyati, pubbagatampi upavāyati, lohitagatampi upavāyati, na ca tena vāyo aṭṭīyati vā harāyati vā jigucchati vā; evameva kho tvaṃ, rāhula, vāyosamaṃ bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Vāyosamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassanti.

‘‘Ākāsasamaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Ākāsasamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassanti. Seyyathāpi, rāhula, ākāso na katthaci patiṭṭhito; evameva kho tvaṃ, rāhula, ākāsasamaṃ bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Ākāsasamañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato uppannā manāpāmanāpā phassā cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassanti.
commentary_pali:
119. Idānissa tādibhāvalakkhaṇaṃ ācikkhanto pathavīsamantiādimāha. Iṭṭhāniṭṭhesu hi arajjanto adussanto tādī nāma hoti. Manāpāmanāpāti ettha aṭṭha lobhasahagatacittasampayuttā manāpā nāma, dve domanassacittasampayuttā amanāpā nāma. Cittaṃ na pariyādāya ṭhassantīti ete phassā uppajjitvā tava cittaṃ antomuṭṭhigataṃ karonto viya pariyādāya gahetvā ṭhātuṃ na sakkhissanti ‘‘ahaṃ sobhāmi, mayhaṃ vaṇṇāyatanaṃ pasanna’’nti puna attabhāvaṃ nissāya chandarāgo nuppajjissati. Gūthagatantiādīsu gūthameva gūthagataṃ. Evaṃ sabbattha.

Na katthaci patiṭṭhitoti pathavīpabbatarukkhādīsu ekasmimpi na patiṭṭhito, yadi hi pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhito bhaveyya, pathaviyā bhijjamānāya saheva bhijjeyya, pabbate patamāne saheva pateyya, rukkhe chijjamāne saheva chijjeyya.

Na katthaci patiṭṭhito
commentary_english:
119. Now, explaining its nature, he begins with "like the earth" (pathavīsama).

Indeed, one who is not attached to the agreeable and disagreeable, who is not hateful, is called "such a one."

"Agreeable and disagreeable": Here, the eight that are associated with greed-related thoughts are called agreeable (manāpa), the two that are associated with displeasure-related thoughts are called disagreeable (amanāpa).

"Thoughts will not overwhelm": These contacts, arising, will not be able to stand, overwhelming and seizing your mind as if making it fist-closed, [thinking,] "I am beautiful, my complexion is clear," desire and passion will not arise again, relying on self-regard.

"Gone to excrement": In these and other cases, excrement is just gone to excrement (gūthagata).

Thus, in each case.

"Not established anywhere": He is not established in even one of the earth, mountains, trees, etc. If he were established on the earth, he would be broken together when the earth is broken; when the mountain falls, he would fall together; when the tree is cut, he would be cut together.

Not established anywhere.

mula_pali: 120. ‘‘Mettaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Mettañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato yo byāpādo so pahīyissati. Karuṇaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Karuṇañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato yā vihesā sā pahīyissati. Muditaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Muditañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato yā arati sā pahīyissati. Upekkhaṃ , rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Upekkhañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato yo paṭigho so pahīyissati. Asubhaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Asubhañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato yo rāgo so pahīyissati. Aniccasaññaṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Aniccasaññañhi te, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvayato yo asmimāno so pahīyissati.
mula_english:
120. “Rāhula, develop meditation on loving-kindness ( *maitrī* ); for, Rāhula, from developing the meditation that is friendliness, any ill will (*byāpāda*) will be abandoned.

“Rāhula, develop meditation on compassion (*karuṇā*); for when you develop meditation on compassion, any cruelty (*vihimsā*) will be abandoned.

“Rāhula, develop meditation on appreciative joy (*muditā*); for when you develop meditation on appreciative joy, any discontent (*arati*) will be abandoned.

“Rāhula, develop meditation on equanimity (*upekṣā*); for when you develop meditation on equanimity, any aversion (*pratigha*) will be abandoned.

“Rāhula, develop meditation on foulness (*aśubha*); for when you develop meditation on foulness, any lust (*rāga*) will be abandoned.

“Rāhula, develop meditation on the perception of impermanence (*anitya-saṃjñā*); for when you develop meditation on the perception of impermanence, the conceit ‘I am’ (*asmimāna*) will be abandoned.
commentary_pali:
120.Mettaṃrāhulāti kasmā ārabhi? Tādibhāvassa kāraṇadassanatthaṃ. Heṭṭhā hi tādibhāvalakkhaṇaṃ dassitaṃ, na ca sakkā ahaṃ tādī homīti akāraṇā bhavituṃ, napi ‘‘ahaṃ uccākulappasuto bahussuto lābhī, maṃ rājarājamahāmattādayo bhajanti, ahaṃ tādī homī’’ti imehi kāraṇehi koci tādī nāma hoti, mettādibhāvanāya pana hotīti tādibhāvassa kāraṇadassanatthaṃ imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi.

Tattha bhāvayatoti upacāraṃ vā appanaṃ vā pāpentassa. Yo byāpādoti yo satte kopo, so pahīyissati. Vihesāti pāṇiādīhi sattānaṃ vihiṃsanaṃ. Aratīti pantasenāsanesu ceva adhikusaladhammesu ca ukkaṇṭhitatā. Paṭighoti yattha katthaci sattesu saṅkhāresu ca paṭihaññanakileso. Asubhanti uddhumātakādīsu upacārappanaṃ. Uddhumātakādīsu asubhabhāvanā ca nāmesā vitthārato visuddhimagge kathitāva. Rāgoti pañcakāmaguṇikarāgo. Aniccasaññanti aniccānupassanāya sahajātasaññaṃ. Vipassanā eva vā esā asaññāpi saññāsīsena saññāti vuttā. Asmimānoti rūpādīsu asmīti māno.

bhāvayato Yo byāpādo Vihesā Aratī Paṭigho Asubha visuddhimagge Rāgo Aniccasañña Asmimāno
commentary_english:
120.
*Mettaṃ* — why did he begin with *Rāhulā*? [It is] to show the cause of such a state.

Below, the characteristic of such a state has been shown. It is not possible to become like that without a cause. Also, it is not that someone becomes like that due to these reasons: "I am born in a high family, learned, a gainer, and kings, great ministers, etc., attend on me." But it happens through the cultivation of loving-kindness, etc.; therefore, he began this teaching to show the cause of such a state.

There, *bhāvayato* means for one causing approach or absorption.

*Yo byāpādo* means whatever anger [kopa] towards beings, that will be abandoned (pahīyissati).

*Vihesā* means harming beings with hands, etc.

*Aratī* means disgust in remote forest dwellings and also in wholesome things.

*Paṭigho* means the defilement [kileso] of repulsion [paṭihaññana] in whatever beings and compounded things.

*Asubha* means approach to the repulsive [uddhumātaka], etc.

Furthermore, meditation on the repulsive in the blown-up corpse [uddhumātaka], etc., has been spoken of extensively in the *Visuddhimagga*.

*Rāgo* means attachment consisting of the five strands of sense desire (pañcakāmaguṇikarāgo).

*Aniccasañña* means the perception (saññaṃ) that is co-born with the contemplation of impermanence (*aniccānupassanā*).

Or, indeed, this insight (*vipassanā*) is called perception (*saññā*) by the head of perception, even without perception (*asaññāpi*).

*Asmimāno* means the conceit of “I am” in forms [rūpa], etc.

*bhāvayato*, *yo byāpādo*, *vihesā*, *aratī*, *paṭigho*, *asubha*, *Visuddhimagge*, *rāgo*, *aniccasañña*, *asmimāno*

mula_pali:
121. ‘‘Ānāpānassatiṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi. Ānāpānassati hi te, rāhula, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Kathaṃ bhāvitā ca, rāhula, ānāpānassati, kathaṃ bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā ? Idha, rāhula, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. So satova assasati satova sato (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) passasati.

‘‘Dīghaṃ vā assasanto ‘dīghaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, dīghaṃ vā passasanto ‘dīghaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti; rassaṃ vā assasanto ‘rassaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, rassaṃ vā passasanto ‘rassaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti. ‘Sabbakāyappaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘sabbakāyappaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati.

‘‘‘Pītippaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘pītippaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘sukhappaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘sukhappaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘cittasaṅkhārappaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘cittasaṅkhārappaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘passambhayaṃ cittasaṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘passambhayaṃ cittasaṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati.

‘‘‘Cittappaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘cittappaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati ; ‘abhippamodayaṃ cittaṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘abhippamodayaṃ cittaṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘samādahaṃ cittaṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘samādahaṃ cittaṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘vimocayaṃ cittaṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘vimocayaṃ cittaṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati.

‘‘‘Aniccānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘aniccānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘virāgānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘virāgānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘nirodhānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘nirodhānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘paṭinissaggānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘paṭinissaggānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati.

‘‘Evaṃ bhāvitā kho, rāhula, ānāpānassati, evaṃ bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Evaṃ bhāvitāya, rāhula, ānāpānassatiyā, evaṃ bahulīkatāya yepi te carimakā assāsā tepi viditāva nirujjhanti no aviditā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā rāhulo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Mahārāhulovādasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.
mula_english:
121. “Rāhula, develop mindfulness of breathing (*ānāpānasmṛtiṃ, rāhula, bhāvanaṃ bhāvehi*).

When mindfulness of breathing is developed and cultivated (*ānāpānassati hi te, rāhula, bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā*), it is of great fruit and great benefit.

And how is mindfulness of breathing developed (*kathaṃ bhāvitā ca, rāhula, ānāpānassati*) and cultivated, so that it is of great fruit and great benefit (*kathaṃ bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā*)? Here, Rāhula, a monk, gone to the forest or to the root of a tree or to an empty hut, sits down; having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and established mindfulness in front of him (*idha, rāhula, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā*).

Simply mindful, he breathes in; mindful, he breathes out (*so satova assasati satova passasati*).

“Breathing in long, he understands: ‘I breathe in long’ (*dīghaṃ vā assasanto ‘dīghaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti*); or breathing out long, he understands: ‘I breathe out long’ (*dīghaṃ vā passasanto ‘dīghaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti*). Breathing in short, he understands: ‘I breathe in short’ (*rassaṃ vā assasanto ‘rassaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti*); or breathing out short, he understands: ‘I breathe out short’ (*rassaṃ vā passasanto ‘rassaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti*).

He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in experiencing the whole body of breath’ (*sabbakāyappaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati*); he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out experiencing the whole body of breath’ (*sabbakāyappaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati*). He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in tranquillising the bodily formation’ (*passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati*); he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out tranquillising the bodily formation’ (*passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati*).

“He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in experiencing rapture’ (*pītippaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati*); he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out experiencing rapture’ (*pītippaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati*). He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in experiencing pleasure’ (*sukhappaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati*); he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out experiencing pleasure’ (*sukhappaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati*). He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in experiencing the mental formation’ (*cittasaṅkhārappaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati*); he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out experiencing the mental formation’ (*cittasaṅkhārappaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati*). He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in tranquillising the mental formation’ (*passambhayaṃ cittasaṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati*); he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out tranquillising the mental formation’ (*passambhayaṃ cittasaṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati*).

“He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in experiencing the mind’ (*cittappaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati*); he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out experiencing the mind’ (*cittappaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati*). He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in gladdening the mind’ (*abhippamodayaṃ cittaṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati*); he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out gladdening the mind’ (*abhippamodayaṃ cittaṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati*). He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in concentrating the mind’ (*samādahaṃ cittaṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati*); he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out concentrating the mind’ (*samādahaṃ cittaṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati*). He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in liberating the mind’ (*vimocayaṃ cittaṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati*); he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out liberating the mind’ (*vimocayaṃ cittaṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati*).

He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in contemplating impermanence’ (*aniccānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati*); he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out contemplating impermanence’ (*aniccānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati*). He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in contemplating detachment’ (*virāgānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati*); he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out contemplating detachment’ (*virāgānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati*). He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in contemplating cessation’ (*nirodhānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati*); he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out contemplating cessation’ (*nirodhānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati*). He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in contemplating relinquishment’ (*paṭinissaggānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati*); he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out contemplating relinquishment’ (*paṭinissaggānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati*).

“Rāhula, that is how mindfulness of breathing is developed (*evaṃ bhāvitā kho, rāhula, ānāpānassati*) and cultivated, so that it is of great fruit and great benefit (*evaṃ bahulīkatā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā*). Rāhula, when mindfulness of breathing is thus developed (*evaṃ bhāvitāya, rāhula, ānāpānassatiyā*) and cultivated, even the final in-breaths and out-breaths are known as they cease, not unknown (*evaṃ bahulīkatāya yepi te carimakā assāsā tepi viditāva nirujjhanti no aviditā’’ti*).”

Thus spoke the Lord (*idamavoca bhagavā*). The venerable Rāhula was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words (*attamano āyasmā rāhulo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti*).

The Great Rāhula Instruction Discourse, the Second, is finished. (*mahārāhulovādasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ*).
commentary_pali:
121. Idāni therena pucchitaṃ pañhaṃ vitthārento ānāpānassatintiādimāha. Tattha idaṃ kammaṭṭhānañca kammaṭṭhānabhāvanā ca pāḷiattho ca saddhiṃ ānisaṃsakathāya sabbo sabbākārena visuddhimagge anussatiniddese vitthāritoyeva. Imaṃ desanaṃ bhagavā neyyapuggalavaseneva pariniṭṭhāpesīti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Māhārāhulovādasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
Now, while elaborating on the question asked by the Elder, he begins with "**ānāpānassati**" and so forth.

There, this meditation subject (kammaṭṭhāna), the cultivation of this meditation subject (kammaṭṭhānabhāvanā), and the meaning of the Pāli [text], along with the discourse on its benefits, have all been extensively explained in every way in the section on mindfulness (*anussati*) in the **Visuddhimagga**.

The Blessed One concluded this discourse solely based on those capable of being guided (*neyyapuggala*).

*Papañcasūdanīyā Majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya*

*Māhārāhulovādasuttavaṇṇanā Niṭṭhitā.*

mula_pali: 122. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āyasmato mālukyaputtassa māluṅkyaputtassa (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘‘yānimāni diṭṭhigatāni bhagavatā abyākatāni ṭhapitāni paṭikkhittāni – ‘sassato loko’tipi, ‘asassato loko’tipi, ‘antavā loko’tipi, ‘anantavā loko’tipi, ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’ntipi, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’ntipi, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi – tāni me bhagavā na byākaroti. Yāni me bhagavā na byākaroti taṃ me na ruccati, taṃ me nakkhamati. Sohaṃ bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ pucchissāmi. Sace me bhagavā byākarissati – ‘sassato loko’ti vā ‘asassato loko’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā – evāhaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ carissāmi; no ce me bhagavā byākarissati – ‘sassato loko’ti vā ‘asassato loko’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā – evāhaṃ sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissāmī’’ti.
mula_english:
122. Thus have I heard:

On one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

Then, while the venerable Mālukyaputta was alone in meditation, the following thought arose in his mind: “These speculative views have been undeclared by the Blessed One, set aside and rejected by him, namely: ‘the world is eternal’ (śāśvato lokaḥ) and ‘the world is not eternal’ (aśāśvato lokaḥ); ‘the world is finite’ (antavā lokaḥ) and ‘the world is infinite’ (anantavā lokaḥ); ‘the soul is the same as the body’ and ‘the soul is one thing and the body another’; and ‘after death a Tathāgata exists’ (hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā) and ‘after death a Tathāgata does not exist’ (na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā) and ‘after death a Tathāgata both exists and does not exist’ and ‘after death a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist’ – these the Blessed One does not declare to me.

The Blessed One does not declare these to me, and I do not approve of and accept the fact that he does not declare these to me,

so I shall go to the Blessed One and ask him the meaning of this.

If he declares to me either ‘the world is eternal’ (śāśvato lokaḥ) or ‘the world is not eternal’ (aśāśvato lokaḥ)…or ‘after death a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist,’ then I will lead the holy life under him; if he does not declare these to me, then I will abandon the training and return to the low life.”
commentary_pali: 122.Evaṃme sutanti mālukyasuttaṃ. Tattha mālukyaputtassāti evaṃnāmakassa therassa. Ṭhapitāni paṭikkhittānīti diṭṭhigatāni nāma na byākātabbānīti evaṃ ṭhapitāni ceva paṭikkhittāni ca. Tathāgatoti satto. Taṃ me na ruccatīti taṃ abyākaraṇaṃ mayhaṃ na ruccati. Sikkhaṃpaccakkhāyāti sikkhaṃ paṭikkhipitvā.
commentary_english:
122. Thus, "I have heard" is the Mālukya Sūtra.

There, "of Mālukyaputta" refers to a *thera* of such a name.

"Established and rejected" means that views are not to be explained as things established and rejected in this way.

"*Tathāgata*" means a being.

"That does not please me" means that non-explanation does not please me.

"Training," having rejected the training, means having rejected it.

mula_pali: 123. Atha kho āyasmā mālukyaputto sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā mālukyaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –
mula_english: Then, when it was evening, the venerable Mālunkyaputta rose from meditation and went to the Blessed One. After paying homage to the Blessed One he sat down at one side. As he was sitting there, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One,

mula_pali: 124. ‘‘Idha mayhaṃ, bhante, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – yānimāni diṭṭhigatāni bhagavatā abyākatāni ṭhapitāni paṭikkhittāni – ‘sassato loko’tipi, ‘asassato loko’tipi…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’tipi – tāni me bhagavā na byākaroti. Yāni me bhagavā na byākaroti taṃ me na ruccati, taṃ me nakkhamati. Sohaṃ bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ pucchissāmi. Sace me bhagavā byākarissati – ‘sassato loko’ti vā, ‘asassato loko’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā – evāhaṃ bhagavati, brahmacariyaṃ carissāmi. No ce me bhagavā byākarissati – ‘sassato loko’ti vā, ‘asassato loko’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā – evāhaṃ sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissāmīti. Sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘sassato loko’ti, ‘sassato loko’ti me bhagavā byākarotu; sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘asassato loko’ti, ‘asassato loko’ti me bhagavā byākarotu. No ce bhagavā jānāti – ‘sassato loko’ti vā, ‘asassato loko’ti vā, ajānato kho pana apassato etadeva ujukaṃ hoti yadidaṃ – ‘na jānāmi, na passāmī’ti. Sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘antavā loko’ti, ‘anantavā loko’ti me bhagavā byākarotu; sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘anantavā loko’ti, ‘anantavā loko’ti me bhagavā byākarotu. No ce bhagavā jānāti – ‘antavā loko’ti vā, ‘anantavā loko’ti vā, ajānato kho pana apassato etadeva ujukaṃ hoti yadidaṃ – ‘na jānāmi, na passāmī’ti. Sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’nti, ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’nti me bhagavā byākarotu; sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’nti, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’nti me bhagavā byākarotu. No ce bhagavā jānāti – ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’nti vā, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’nti vā, ajānato kho pana apassato etadeva ujukaṃ hoti yadidaṃ – ‘na jānāmi, na passāmī’ti. Sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti me bhagavā byākarotu; sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti me bhagavā byākarotu. No ce bhagavā jānāti – ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ajānato kho pana apassato etadeva ujukaṃ hoti yadidaṃ – ‘na jānāmi na passāmī’ti. Sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti me bhagavā byākarotu; sace bhagavā jānāti – ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti me bhagavā byākarotu. No ce bhagavā jānāti – ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ajānato kho pana apassato etadeva ujukaṃ hoti yadidaṃ – ‘na jānāmi, na passāmī’’’ti.
mula_english:
124. Here, venerable sir (bhante), while I was alone in meditation (rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa), the following thought arose in my mind (cetaso parivitakko udapādi): “These speculative views (diṭṭhigatāni) have been undeclared (abyākatāni) by the Blessed One (bhagavatā), set aside (ṭhapitāni) and rejected (paṭikkhittāni), namely: ‘the world is eternal’ (sassato loko) and ‘the world is not eternal’ (asassato loko)...pe... ‘after death a *Tathāgata* neither exists nor does not exist’ (neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā)”—the Blessed One (bhagavā) does not declare these to me (tāni me bhagavā na byākaroti).

The Blessed One (bhagavā) does not declare these to me (yāni me bhagavā na byākaroti), and I do not approve of it (taṃ me na ruccati), I do not accept it (taṃ me nakkhamati).

So (sohaṃ), I shall go to the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā) and ask him the meaning of this (etamatthaṃ pucchissāmi).

If (sace) the Blessed One (bhagavā) declares to me (byākarissati): ‘the world is eternal’ (sassato loko) or ‘the world is not eternal’ (asassato loko)...pe... ‘after death a *Tathāgata* neither exists nor does not exist’ (neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā)—then (eva) I will lead the holy life (brahmacariyaṃ carissāmi) under the Blessed One (bhagavati).

If (no ce) the Blessed One (bhagavā) does not declare to me (byākarissati): ‘the world is eternal’ (sassato loko) or ‘the world is not eternal’ (asassato loko)...pe... ‘after death a *Tathāgata* neither exists nor does not exist’ (neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā)—then (eva) I will abandon the training (sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya) and return to the lower life (hīnāyāvattissāmīti).

If (sace) the Blessed One (bhagavā) knows (jānāti): ‘the world is eternal’ (sassato loko), let the Blessed One (bhagavā) declare to me (byākarotu): ‘the world is eternal’ (sassato loko); if (sace) the Blessed One (bhagavā) knows (jānāti): ‘the world is not eternal’ (asassato loko), let the Blessed One (bhagavā) declare to me (byākarotu): ‘the world is not eternal’ (asassato loko).

If (no ce) the Blessed One (bhagavā) does not know (jānāti): ‘the world is eternal’ (sassato loko) or ‘the world is not eternal’ (asassato loko), then it is straightforward (etadeva ujukaṃ hoti) for one who does not know (ajānato) and does not see (apassato) to say (yadidaṃ): ‘I do not know (na jānāmi), I do not see (na passāmī)’.

If (sace) the Blessed One (bhagavā) knows (jānāti): ‘the world is finite’ (antavā loko) or ‘the world is infinite’ (anantavā loko), let the Blessed One (bhagavā) declare to me (byākarotu): ‘the world is finite’ (antavā loko) or ‘the world is infinite’ (anantavā loko).

If (no ce) the Blessed One (bhagavā) does not know (jānāti): ‘the world is finite’ (antavā loko) or ‘the world is infinite’ (anantavā loko), then it is straightforward (etadeva ujukaṃ hoti) for one who does not know (ajānato) and does not see (apassato) to say (yadidaṃ): ‘I do not know (na jānāmi), I do not see (na passāmī)’.

If (sace) the Blessed One (bhagavā) knows (jānāti): ‘the soul is the same as the body’ (taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ), let the Blessed One (bhagavā) declare to me (byākarotu): ‘the soul is the same as the body’ (taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ); if (sace) the Blessed One (bhagavā) knows (jānāti): ‘the soul is one thing and the body another’ (aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ), let the Blessed One (bhagavā) declare to me (byākarotu): ‘the soul is one thing and the body another’ (aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ).

If (no ce) the Blessed One (bhagavā) does not know (jānāti): ‘the soul is the same as the body’ (taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ) or ‘the soul is one thing and the body another’ (aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ), then it is straightforward (etadeva ujukaṃ hoti) for one who does not know (ajānato) and does not see (apassato) to say (yadidaṃ): ‘I do not know (na jānāmi), I do not see (na passāmī)’.

If (sace) the Blessed One (bhagavā) knows (jānāti): ‘after death a *Tathāgata* exists’ (hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā), let the Blessed One (bhagavā) declare to me (byākarotu): ‘after death a *Tathāgata* exists’ (hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā); if (sace) the Blessed One (bhagavā) knows (jānāti): ‘after death a *Tathāgata* does not exist’ (na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā), let the Blessed One (bhagavā) declare to me (byākarotu): ‘after death a *Tathāgata* does not exist’ (na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā).

If (no ce) the Blessed One (bhagavā) does not know (jānāti): ‘after death a *Tathāgata* exists’ (hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā) or ‘after death a *Tathāgata* does not exist’ (na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā), then it is straightforward (etadeva ujukaṃ hoti) for one who does not know (ajānato) and does not see (apassato) to say (yadidaṃ): ‘I do not know (na jānāmi), I do not see (na passāmī)’.

If (sace) the Blessed One (bhagavā) knows (jānāti): ‘after death a *Tathāgata* both exists and does not exist’ (hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā), let the Blessed One (bhagavā) declare to me (byākarotu): ‘after death a *Tathāgata* both exists and does not exist’ (hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā); if (sace) the Blessed One (bhagavā) knows (jānāti): ‘after death a *Tathāgata* neither exists nor does not exist’ (neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā), let the Blessed One (bhagavā) declare to me (byākarotu): ‘after death a *Tathāgata* neither exists nor does not exist’ (neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā).

If (no ce) the Blessed One (bhagavā) does not know (jānāti): ‘after death a *Tathāgata* both exists and does not exist’ (hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā) or ‘after death a *Tathāgata* neither exists nor does not exist’ (neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā), then it is straightforward (etadeva ujukaṃ hoti) for one who does not know (ajānato) and does not see (apassato) to say (yadidaṃ): ‘I do not know (na jānāmi), I do not see (na passāmī)’.

mula_pali: 125. ‘‘Kiṃ nu kiṃ nu kho (syā. kaṃ. ka.) tāhaṃ, mālukyaputta, evaṃ avacaṃ – ‘ehi tvaṃ, mālukyaputta, mayi brahmacariyaṃ cara, ahaṃ te byākarissāmi – ‘sassato loko’ti vā, ‘asassato loko’ti vā, ‘antavā loko’ti vā, ‘anantavā loko’ti vā, ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’nti vā, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’nti vā, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Tvaṃ vā pana maṃ evaṃ avaca – ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ carissāmi , bhagavā me byākarissati – ‘sassato loko’ti vā, ‘asassato loko’ti vā, ‘antavā loko’ti vā, ‘anantavā loko’ti vā, ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’nti vā, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’nti vā, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Iti kira, mālukyaputta, nevāhaṃ taṃ vadāmi – ehi tvaṃ, mālukyaputta, mayi brahmacariyaṃ cara, ahaṃ te byākarissāmi – ‘sassato loko’ti vā, ‘asassato loko’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇāti vā’ti; napi kira maṃ tvaṃ vadesi – ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ carissāmi, bhagavā me byākarissati – ‘sassato loko’ti vā ‘asassato loko’ti vā…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā’’ti. Evaṃ sante, moghapurisa, ko santo kaṃ paccācikkhasi?
mula_english:
“125. How then, Mālunkyaputta, did I ever say to you: ‘Come, Mālunkyaputta, lead the holy life under me, and I will declare to you: ‘The world is eternal’ (śāśvato loko’ti vā), or ‘The world is not eternal,’ (aśāśvato loko’ti vā) or ‘The world is finite,’ (antavā loko’ti vā) or ‘The world is infinite,’ (anantavā loko’ti vā) or ‘The soul is the same as the body,’ (taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ śarīraṃ) or ‘The soul is one thing and the body another,’ (aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ śarīraṃ) or ‘After death a Tathāgata exists,’ (hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā) or ‘After death a Tathāgata does not exist,’ (na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā) or ‘After death a Tathāgata both exists and does not exist,’ (hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā) or ‘After death a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist’ (neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā)?”

“No, Bhante.”

“Or did you ever tell me: ‘I will lead the holy life under the Blessed One, and the Blessed One will declare to me: ‘The world is eternal’ (śāśvato loko’ti vā), or ‘The world is not eternal,’ (aśāśvato loko’ti vā) or ‘The world is finite,’ (antavā loko’ti vā) or ‘The world is infinite,’ (anantavā loko’ti vā) or ‘The soul is the same as the body,’ (taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ śarīraṃ) or ‘The soul is one thing and the body another,’ (aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ śarīraṃ) or ‘After death a Tathāgata exists,’ (hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā) or ‘After death a Tathāgata does not exist,’ (na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā) or ‘After death a Tathāgata both exists and does not exist,’ (hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā) or ‘After death a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist’ (neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā)?”

“No, Bhante.”

“So it seems, Mālunkyaputta, that I do not say that you should come, Mālunkyaputta, lead the holy life under me, and I will declare to you: ‘The world is eternal’ (śāśvato loko’ti vā), or ‘The world is not eternal’ (aśāśvato loko’ti vā)...or...'After death a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist’ (neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā). Nor do you say to me: ‘I, Bhante, will lead the holy life under the Blessed One, and the Blessed One will declare to me: ‘The world is eternal’ (śāśvato loko’ti vā), or ‘The world is not eternal’ (aśāśvato loko’ti vā)...or... ‘After death a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist’ (neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā).”

Such being the case, you foolish man (moghapurisa), who are you, and what are you giving up (kaṃ paccācikkhasi)?
commentary_pali: 125.Ko santo kaṃ paccācikkhasīti yācako vā hi yācitakaṃ paccācikkheyya, yācitako vā yācakaṃ. Tvaṃ neva yācako na yācitako, so dāni tvaṃ ko santo kaṃ paccācikkhasīti attho.
commentary_english:
Who, being, refuses whom? If a beggar refuses a borrower, or a borrower a beggar.
You are neither a beggar nor a borrower; so now, who are you, being, [that] you refuse whom? This is the meaning.

mula_pali: 126. ‘‘Yo kho, mālukyaputta, evaṃ vadeyya – ‘na tāvāhaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ carissāmi yāva me bhagavā na byākarissati – ‘‘sassato loko’’ti vā, ‘‘asassato loko’’ti vā…pe… ‘‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’’ti vāti, abyākatameva taṃ, mālukyaputta, tathāgatena assa, atha so puggalo kālaṃ kareyya. Seyyathāpi, mālukyaputta, puriso sallena viddho assa savisena gāḷhapalepanena. Tassa mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā bhisakkaṃ sallakattaṃ upaṭṭhapeyyuṃ. So evaṃ vadeyya – ‘na tāvāhaṃ imaṃ sallaṃ āharissāmi yāva na taṃ purisaṃ jānāmi yenamhi viddho, khattiyo vā brāhmaṇo vā vesso vā suddo vā’ti; so evaṃ vadeyya – ‘na tāvāhaṃ imaṃ sallaṃ āharissāmi yāva na taṃ purisaṃ jānāmi yenamhi viddho, evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto iti vā’ti; so evaṃ vadeyya – ‘na tāvāhaṃ imaṃ sallaṃ āharissāmi yāva na taṃ purisaṃ jānāmi yenamhi viddho, dīgho vā rasso vā majjhimo vā’ti; so evaṃ vadeyya – ‘na tāvāhaṃ imaṃ sallaṃ āharissāmi yāva na taṃ purisaṃ jānāmi yenamhi viddho, kāḷo vā sāmo vā maṅguracchavī vā’ti; so evaṃ vadeyya – ‘na tāvāhaṃ imaṃ sallaṃ āharissāmi yāva na taṃ purisaṃ jānāmi yenamhi viddho, amukasmiṃ gāme vā nigame vā nagare vā’ti; so evaṃ vadeyya – ‘na tāvāhaṃ imaṃ sallaṃ āharissāmi yāva na taṃ dhanuṃ jānāmi yenamhi viddho, yadi vā cāpo yadi vā kodaṇḍo’ti; so evaṃ vadeyya – ‘na tāvāhaṃ imaṃ sallaṃ āharissāmi yāva na taṃ jiyaṃ jānāmi yāyamhi viddho , yadi vā akkassa yadi vā saṇhassa saṇṭhassa (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) yadi vā nhārussa yadi vā maruvāya yadi vā khīrapaṇṇino’ti; so evaṃ vadeyya – ‘na tāvāhaṃ imaṃ sallaṃ āharissāmi yāva na taṃ kaṇḍaṃ jānāmi yenamhi viddho, yadi vā gacchaṃ yadi vā ropima’nti; so evaṃ vadeyya – ‘na tāvāhaṃ imaṃ sallaṃ āharissāmi yāva na taṃ kaṇḍaṃ jānāmi yenamhi viddho, yassa pattehi vājitaṃ vākhittaṃ (ka.) yadi vā gijjhassa yadi vā kaṅkassa yadi vā kulalassa yadi vā morassa yadi vā sithilahanuno’ti; so evaṃ vadeyya – ‘na tāvāhaṃ imaṃ sallaṃ āharissāmi yāva na taṃ kaṇḍaṃ jānāmi yenamhi viddho, yassa nhārunā parikkhittaṃ yadi vā gavassa yadi vā mahiṃsassa yadi vā bheravassa roruvassa (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) yadi vā semhārassā’ti; so evaṃ vadeyya – ‘na tāvāhaṃ imaṃ sallaṃ āharissāmi yāva na taṃ sallaṃ jānāmi yenamhi viddho, yadi vā sallaṃ yadi vā khurappaṃ yadi vā vekaṇḍaṃ yadi vā nārācaṃ yadi vā vacchadantaṃ yadi vā karavīrapatta’nti – aññātameva taṃ, mālukyaputta, tena purisena assa, atha so puriso kālaṃ kareyya. Evameva kho, mālukyaputta, yo evaṃ vadeyya – ‘na tāvāhaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ carissāmi yāva me bhagavā na byākarissati – ‘‘sassato loko’’ti vā ‘‘asassato loko’’ti vā…pe… ‘‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’’ti vāti – abyākatameva taṃ, mālukyaputta, tathāgatena assa, atha so puggalo kālaṅkareyya.
mula_english:
