126.
"If someone should say thus, Mālukyaputta: 'I will not lead the holy life under the Blessed One until the Blessed One declares to me: "The world is eternal" or "The world is not eternal"... or "after death a *Tathāgata* neither exists nor does not exist,"' that would still remain undeclared by the *Tathāgata*, Mālukyaputta, and meanwhile that person would die.

Suppose, Mālukyaputta, a man were wounded by an arrow thickly smeared with poison, and his friends and companions, his kinsmen and relatives, brought a surgeon to treat him.

The man would say: 'I will not let the surgeon pull out this arrow until I know whether the man who wounded me was a noble (*kṣatriya*) or a *brāhmin* (*brāhmaṇa*) or a merchant (*vaiśya*) or a worker (*śūdra*).' And he would say: 'I will not let the surgeon pull out this arrow until I know the name and clan of the man who wounded me,' or 'until I know whether the man who wounded me was tall or short or of middle height,' or 'until I know whether the man who wounded me was dark or brown or golden-skinned,' or 'until I know whether the man who wounded me lives in such and such a village or town or city.' And he would say: 'I will not let the surgeon pull out this arrow until I know the bow with which I was wounded, whether it was a *cāpa* or a *kodaṇḍa*.' And he would say: 'I will not let the surgeon pull out this arrow until I know the bowstring with which I was wounded, whether of *akka* or of *saṇha*, whether of *nhāru* or of *maruva* or of *khīrapaṇṇin*.' And he would say: 'I will not let the surgeon pull out this arrow until I know the arrow with which I was wounded, whether it was *gaccha* or *ropima*.' And he would say: 'I will not let the surgeon pull out this arrow until I know with whose feathers it was winged, whether of vulture (*gijjha*) or of heron (*kaṅka*) or of osprey (*kulala*) or of peacock (*mora*) or of *sithilahanu*.' And he would say: 'I will not let the surgeon pull out this arrow until I know with whose sinews it was bound, whether of cow (*gava*) or of buffalo (*mahiṃsa*) or of *bherava* or of *semhāra*.' And he would say: 'I will not let the surgeon pull out this arrow until I know the arrow with which I was wounded, whether it was a *salla* or a *khurappa* or a *vekaṇḍa* or a *nārāca* or a *vacchadanta* or a *karavīrapatta*.' That would still remain unknown to that man, Mālukyaputta, and meanwhile that man would die.

So too, Mālukyaputta, if anyone should say thus: ‘I will not lead the holy life under the Blessed One until the Blessed One declares to me: "The world is eternal" or "The world is not eternal"... or "a *Tathāgata* neither exists nor does not exist after death,"' that would still remain undeclared by the *Tathāgata*, Mālukyaputta, and meanwhile that person would die."
commentary_pali: 126.Viddhoassāti parasenāya ṭhitena viddho bhaveyya. Gāḷhapalepanenāti bahalalepanena. Bhisakkanti vejjaṃ. Sallakattanti sallakantanaṃ sallakantiyasuttavācakaṃ. Akkassāti akkavāke gahetvā jiyaṃ karonti. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘akkassā’’ti. Saṇhassāti veṇuvilīvassa. Maruvākhīrapaṇṇīnampi vākehiyeva karonti. Tena vuttaṃ yadi vā maruvāya yadi vā khīrapaṇṇinoti. Gacchanti pabbatagacchanadīgacchādīsu jātaṃ. Ropimanti ropetvā vaḍḍhitaṃ saravanato saraṃ gahetvā kataṃ. Sithilahanunoti evaṃnāmakassa pakkhino. Bheravassāti kāḷasīhassa. Semhārassāti makkaṭassa. Evaṃ noti etāya diṭṭhiyā sati na hotīti attho.
commentary_english:
126.
*Viddho*: he might be struck by one standing in the enemy's army.
*Gāḷhapalepanenā*: by thick plastering.
*Bhisakka* means physician (*vejjaṃ*).
*Sallakatta* means *sallakantanaṃ*, a reciter of the *sallakantiyasutta*.
*Akkassā*: having taken an *akkavāke*, they make a bowstring (*jiyaṃ karonti*).
Therefore it was said, "*akkassā*."
*Saṇhassā*: of *veṇuvilīva*.
They make even *maruvākhīrapaṇṇī* with *vākehiyeva*.
Therefore it was said, "*yadi vā maruvāya yadi vā khīrapaṇṇino*."
*Gaccha* means born in mountain trees, river trees, etc. (*pabbatagacchanadīgacchādīsu jātaṃ*).
*Ropima* means having planted and grown it, having taken the essence from the *saravana* forest, it is made.
*Sithilahanuno* is the name of a bird.
*Bheravassā* means of a black lion (*kāḷasīhassa*).
*Semhārassā* means of a monkey (*makkaṭassa*).
*Evaṃ no* means with this view, it is not, such is the meaning (*etāya diṭṭhiyā sati na hotīti attho*).

mula_pali: 127. ‘‘‘Sassato loko’ti, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso abhavissāti , evaṃ ‘no asassato loko’ti, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso abhavissāti, evampi ‘no sassato loko’ti vā, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhiyā sati, ‘asassato loko’ti vā diṭṭhiyā sati attheva jāti, atthi jarā, atthi maraṇaṃ, santi sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā; yesāhaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme nighātaṃ paññapemi . ‘Antavā loko’ti, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso abhavissāti, evaṃ ‘no anantavā loko’ti, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso abhavissāti, evampi ‘no antavā loko’ti vā, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhiyā sati, ‘anantavā loko’ti vā diṭṭhiyā sati attheva jāti, atthi jarā, atthi maraṇaṃ, santi sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā; yesāhaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme nighātaṃ paññapemi. ‘Taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’nti, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso abhavissāti, evaṃ ‘no aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’nti, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso abhavissāti, evampi ‘no taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’nti vā, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhiyā sati, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’nti vā diṭṭhiyā sati attheva jāti…pe… nighātaṃ paññapemi. ‘Hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso abhavissāti, evaṃ ‘no na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso abhavissāti, evampi ‘no hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhiyā sati, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā diṭṭhiyā sati attheva jāti…pe… yesāhaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme nighātaṃ paññapemi. ‘Hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso abhavissāti, evaṃ ‘no neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāso abhavissāti, evampi ‘no hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti, mālukyaputta, diṭṭhiyā sati, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā diṭṭhiyā sati attheva jāti…pe… yesāhaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme nighātaṃ paññapemi.
mula_english:
127. “Mālukyaputta, if there is the view ‘the world is eternal’ (*śāśvataḥ lokaḥ*), the holy life (*brahmacariyavāsa*) cannot be lived; and if there is the view ‘the world is not eternal’ (*aśāśvataḥ lokaḥ*), the holy life (*brahmacariyavāsa*) cannot be lived. Whether there is the view ‘the world is eternal’ or the view ‘the world is not eternal,’ there is birth (*jāti*), there is ageing (*jarā*), there is death (*maraṇaṃ*), there are sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, the destruction of which I prescribe here and now.

‘The world is finite’ (*antavā lokaḥ*), Mālukyaputta, if there is the view, the holy life (*brahmacariyavāsa*) cannot be lived; and if there is the view ‘the world is not finite’ (*anantavā lokaḥ*), Mālukyaputta, if there is the view, the holy life (*brahmacariyavāsa*) cannot be lived. Whether there is the view ‘the world is finite’ or the view ‘the world is not finite,’ there is birth (*jāti*), there is ageing (*jarā*), there is death (*maraṇaṃ*), there are sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, the destruction of which I prescribe here and now.

'The soul is the same as the body' (*taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ śarīra*), Mālukyaputta, if there is the view, the holy life (*brahmacariyavāsa*) cannot be lived; and if there is the view 'the soul is one thing and the body another' (*aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ śarīra*), Mālukyaputta, if there is the view, the holy life (*brahmacariyavāsa*) cannot be lived. Whether there is the view 'the soul is the same as the body' or the view 'the soul is one thing and the body another,' there is birth (*jāti*)…pe… the destruction of which I prescribe here and now.

‘After death a *tathāgata* exists’ (*tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā*), Mālukyaputta, if there is the view, the holy life (*brahmacariyavāsa*) cannot be lived; and if there is the view ‘after death a *tathāgata* does not exist’ (*na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā*), Mālukyaputta, if there is the view, the holy life (*brahmacariyavāsa*) cannot be lived. Whether there is the view ‘after death a *tathāgata* exists’ or the view ‘after death a *tathāgata* does not exist,’ there is birth (*jāti*)…pe… the destruction of which I prescribe here and now.

If there is the view ‘after death a *tathāgata* both exists and does not exist’ (*hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā*), Mālukyaputta, if there is the view, the holy life (*brahmacariyavāsa*) cannot be lived; and if there is the view ‘after death a *tathāgata* neither exists nor does not exist’ (*neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā*), Mālukyaputta, if there is the view, the holy life (*brahmacariyavāsa*) cannot be lived. Whether there is the view ‘after death a *tathāgata* both exists and does not exist’ or the view ‘after death a *tathāgata* neither exists nor does not exist,’ there is birth (*jāti*)…pe… the destruction of which I prescribe here and now.
commentary_pali: 127.Attheva jātīti etāya diṭṭhiyā sati brahmacariyavāsova natthi, jāti pana atthiyeva. Tathā jarāmaraṇādīnīti dasseti. Yesāhanti yesaṃ ahaṃ. Nighātanti upaghātaṃ vināsaṃ. Mama sāvakā hi etesu nibbinnā idheva nibbānaṃ pāpuṇantīti adhippāyo.
commentary_english:
127. *attheva jātī* means that with this view, there is no living of the holy life, but there is indeed birth.

Similarly, it indicates aging, death, and so on.

*yesāha* means "of whom am I?"

*nighāta* means injury and destruction ( *upaghātaṃ vināsaṃ*).

The meaning is: "My disciples, having become disgusted with these things, will attain *nirvāṇa* right here ( *nibbānaṃ pāpuṇanti*)."

mula_pali:
128. ‘‘Tasmātiha, mālukyaputta, abyākatañca me abyākatato dhāretha; byākatañca me byākatato dhāretha. Kiñca, mālukyaputta, mayā abyākataṃ? ‘Sassato loko’ti mālukyaputta, mayā abyākataṃ; ‘asassato loko’ti – mayā abyākataṃ; ‘antavā loko’ti – mayā abyākataṃ; ‘anantavā loko’ti – mayā abyākataṃ; ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’nti – mayā abyākataṃ; ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’nti – mayā abyākataṃ; ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti – mayā abyākataṃ; ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti – mayā abyākataṃ; ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti – mayā abyākataṃ; ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti – mayā abyākataṃ. Kasmā cetaṃ, mālukyaputta, mayā abyākataṃ? Na hetaṃ, mālukyaputta, atthasaṃhitaṃ na ādibrahmacariyakaṃ na netaṃ (sī.) nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattati. Tasmā taṃ mayā abyākataṃ. Kiñca, mālukyaputta, mayā byākataṃ? ‘Idaṃ dukkha’nti, mālukyaputta, mayā byākataṃ; ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti – mayā byākataṃ; ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti – mayā byākataṃ; ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti – mayā byākataṃ. Kasmā cetaṃ, mālukyaputta, mayā byākataṃ? Etañhi, mālukyaputta, atthasaṃhitaṃ etaṃ ādibrahmacariyakaṃ nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Tasmā taṃ mayā byākataṃ. Tasmātiha, mālukyaputta , abyākatañca me abyākatato dhāretha; byākatañca me byākatato dhārethā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā mālukyaputto bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Cūḷamālukyasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.
mula_english:
“Therefore, Mālunkyaputta, remember what I have left undeclared as undeclared, and remember what I have declared as declared.

Furthermore, Mālunkyaputta, what have I left undeclared? ‘The world is eternal (śāśvato lokaḥ)’— I have left undeclared. ‘The world is not eternal (aśāśvato lokaḥ)’— I have left undeclared. ‘The world is finite (antavā loko)’— I have left undeclared. ‘The world is infinite (anantavā loko)’— I have left undeclared. ‘The soul is the same as the body (taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ śarīraṃ)’— I have left undeclared. ‘The soul is one thing and the body another (aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ śarīraṃ)’— I have left undeclared. ‘After death a *Tathāgata* exists (hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā)’— I have left undeclared. ‘After death a *Tathāgata* does not exist (na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā)’— I have left undeclared. ‘After death a *Tathāgata* both exists and does not exist (hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā)’— I have left undeclared. ‘After death a *Tathāgata* neither exists nor does not exist (neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā)’— I have left undeclared.

Why have I left that undeclared, Mālunkyaputta? Because it is unbeneficial, Mālunkyaputta, it does not belong to the fundamentals of the holy life, it does not lead to disenchantment (*nirbidā*), to dispassion (*virāga*), to cessation (*nirodha*), to peace (*upaśama*), to direct knowledge (*abhijñā*), to enlightenment (*saṃbodha*), to *Nirvāṇa* (*nirbāṇa*). That is why I have left it undeclared.

Furthermore, Mālunkyaputta, what have I declared? ‘This is suffering (idaṃ duḥkhaṃ)’— I have declared. ‘This is the origin of suffering (ayaṃ duḥkhasamudayo)’— I have declared. ‘This is the cessation of suffering (ayaṃ duḥkhanirodho)’— I have declared. ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering (ayaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipadā)’— I have declared.

Why have I declared that, Mālunkyaputta? Because it is beneficial, Mālunkyaputta, it belongs to the fundamentals of the holy life, it leads to disenchantment (*nirbidā*), to dispassion (*virāga*), to cessation (*nirodha*), to peace (*upaśama*), to direct knowledge (*abhijñā*), to enlightenment (*saṃbodha*), to *Nirvāṇa* (*nirbāṇa*). That is why I have declared it.

Therefore, Mālunkyaputta, remember what I have left undeclared as undeclared, and remember what I have declared as declared.”

This is what the Blessed One said. The venerable Mālunkyaputta was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

The *Cūḷamālunkya-sūtra*, the third [sūtra], is finished.
commentary_pali:
128.Tasmātihāti yasmā abyākatametaṃ, catusaccameva mayā byākataṃ, tasmāti attho. Na hetaṃ mālukyaputta atthasaṃhitanti etaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ vā etaṃ byākaraṇaṃ vā kāraṇanissitaṃ na hoti. Na ādibrahmacariyakanti brahmacariyassa ādimattampi pubbabhāgasīlamattampi na hoti. Na nibbidāyātiādīsu vaṭṭe nibbindanatthāya vā virajjhanatthāya vā vaṭṭanirodhāya vā rāgādivūpasamanatthāya vā abhiññeyye dhamme abhijānanatthāya vā catumaggasaṅkhātasambodhatthāya vā asaṅkhatanibbānasacchikiriyatthāya vā na hoti. Etaṃ hīti etaṃ catusaccabyākaraṇaṃ. Ādibrahmacariyakanti brahmacariyassa ādibhūtaṃ pubbapadaṭṭhānaṃ. Sesaṃ vuttapaṭivipakkhanayena veditabbaṃ. Imampi desanaṃ bhagavā neyyapuggalavasena niṭṭhāpesīti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Cūḷamālukyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
128. Therefore, that means: because this is unrevealed, but the Four Noble Truths are revealed by me, therefore it means that.

"Not indeed, Mālukyaputta, is this connected with the goal," meaning this is either a matter of (wrong) view, or this is a grammar, or it is based on a cause, it is not.

"Not the beginning of the holy life," meaning there is not even the slightest beginning of the holy life, nor even just a preliminary virtue.

"Not for disenchantment," etc., meaning in the cycle [of rebirth], it is not for the purpose of disenchantment, or for the purpose of detachment, or for the cessation of the cycle, or for the appeasement of passions and so forth, or for thoroughly knowing knowable things, or for the sake of the enlightenment consisting of the four paths, or for the sake of realizing the unconditioned *nirvāṇa*.

"This indeed," means this is the explanation of the Four Noble Truths.

"The beginning of the holy life," means it is the first element, the preliminary foundation of the holy life.

The remainder should be understood by the method of the opposite of what has been said.

The Blessed One brought even this teaching to a conclusion in accordance with the disposition of one who needs guidance.

The commentary to the Cūḷamālukya Sūtra in the Papañcasūdanī, commentary to the *Majjhimanikāya*, is finished.

mula_pali:
129. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘dhāretha no tumhe, bhikkhave, mayā desitāni pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanānī’’ti?

Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā mālukyaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘ahaṃ kho, bhante, dhāremi bhagavatā desitāni pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanānī’’ti. ‘‘Yathā kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, mālukyaputta, dhāresi mayā desitāni pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanānī’’ti? ‘‘Sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ desitaṃ dhāremi; vicikicchaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ desitaṃ dhāremi; sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ desitaṃ dhāremi; kāmacchandaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ desitaṃ dhāremi; byāpādaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ desitaṃ dhāremi. Evaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, dhāremi bhagavatā desitāni pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanānī’’ti.

‘‘Kassa kho nāma tvaṃ, mālukyaputta, imāni evaṃ pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni desitāni dhāresi? Nanu, mālukyaputta , aññatitthiyā paribbājakā iminā taruṇūpamena upārambhena upārambhissanti? Daharassa hi, mālukyaputta, kumārassa mandassa uttānaseyyakassa sakkāyotipi na hoti, kuto panassa uppajjissati sakkāyadiṭṭhi? Anusetvevassa anuseti tvevassa (sī. pī.) sakkāyadiṭṭhānusayo. Daharassa hi, mālukyaputta, kumārassa mandassa uttānaseyyakassa dhammātipi na hoti, kuto panassa uppajjissati dhammesu vicikicchā? Anusetvevassa vicikicchānusayo. Daharassa hi, mālukyaputta, kumārassa mandassa uttānaseyyakassa sīlātipi na hoti, kuto panassa uppajjissati sīlesu sīlabbataparāmāso? Anusetvevassa sīlabbataparāmāsānusayo . Daharassa hi, mālukyaputta, kumārassa mandassa uttānaseyyakassa kāmātipi na hoti, kuto panassa uppajjissati kāmesu kāmacchando? Anusetvevassa kāmarāgānusayo. Daharassa hi, mālukyaputta, kumārassa mandassa uttānaseyyakassa sattātipi na hoti, kuto panassa uppajjissati sattesu byāpādo? Anusetvevassa byāpādānusayo. Nanu, mālukyaputta, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā iminā taruṇūpamena upārambhena upārambhissantī’’ti? Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘etassa, bhagavā, kālo, etassa, sugata, kālo yaṃ bhagavā pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni deseyya. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī’’ti. ‘‘Tena hānanda, suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –

anuseti tvevassa (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Savatthi in the Jetavana in Anathapindika’s park.

There the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: “Monks!”

“Venerable sir,” those monks replied.

The Blessed One said this: “Monks, do you remember the five lower fetters (*pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni*) as taught by me?”

When this was said, the venerable Mälunkyaputta replied: “Venerable sir, I remember the five lower fetters (*pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni*) as taught by the Blessed One.”

“In what way, Mälunkyaputta, do you remember the five lower fetters (*pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni*) as taught by me?”

“Venerable sir, I remember personality view (*sakkāyadiṭṭhi*) as a lower fetter (*orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ*) taught by the Blessed One. I remember doubt (*vicikicchā*) as a lower fetter (*orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ*) taught by the Blessed One. I remember adherence to rules and observances (*sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ*) as a lower fetter (*orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ*) taught by the Blessed One. I remember sensual desire (*kāmacchandaṃ*) as a lower fetter (*orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ*) taught by the Blessed One. I remember ill will (*byāpādaṃ*) as a lower fetter (*orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ*) taught by the Blessed One. In this way, venerable sir, I remember the five lower fetters (*pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni*) as taught by the Blessed One.”

“Mälunkyaputta, to whom do you remember my having taught these five lower fetters (*pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni*) in that way? Mälunkyaputta, will not other ascetics and wanderers ridicule you with this youthful simile? A young, tender infant lying prone does not even have the notion ‘personality,’ so how could personality view (*sakkāyadiṭṭhi*) arise in him? Yet the underlying tendency to personality view (*sakkāyadiṭṭhānusayo*) lies within him. A young, tender infant lying prone does not even have the notion ‘teachings,’ so how could doubt (*vicikicchā*) about teachings arise in him? Yet the underlying tendency to doubt (*vicikicchānusayo*) lies within him. A young, tender infant lying prone does not even have the notion ‘rules,’ so how could adherence to rules and observances (*sīlabbataparāmāso*) arise in him? Yet the underlying tendency to adherence to rules and observances (*sīlabbataparāmāsānusayo*) lies within him. A young, tender infant lying prone does not even have the notion ‘sensual pleasures,’ so how could sensual desire (*kāmacchando*) arise in him? Yet the underlying tendency to sensual passion (*kāmarāgānusayo*) lies within him. A young, tender infant lying prone does not even have the notion ‘beings,’ so how could ill will (*byāpādo*) towards beings arise in him? Yet the underlying tendency to ill will (*byāpādānusayo*) lies within him. Mälunkyaputta, will not other ascetics and wanderers ridicule you with this youthful simile?”

When this was said, the venerable Ananda said to the Blessed One: “Lord, it is time for that! Well-Farer, it is time for that! If the Lord would teach about the five lower fetters (*pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni*), the monks would listen and remember it.”

“Then listen, Ananda, and attend closely to what I shall say.”

“So be it, O Lord.” the venerable Ananda replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said:
commentary_pali:
129.Evaṃme sutanti mahāmālukyasuttaṃ. Tattha orambhāgiyānīti heṭṭhā koṭṭhāsikāni kāmabhave nibbattisaṃvattanikāni. Saṃyojanānīti bandhanāni. Kassakho nāmāti kassa devassa vā manussassa vā desitāni dhāresi, kiṃ tvameveko assosi, na añño kocīti? Anusetīti appahīnatāya anuseti. Anusayamāno saṃyojanaṃ nāma hoti.

Ettha ca bhagavatā saṃyojanaṃ pucchitaṃ, therenapi saṃyojanameva byākataṃ. Evaṃ santepi tassa vāde bhagavatā doso āropito. So kasmāti ce? Therassa tathāladdhikattā. Ayañhi tassa laddhi ‘‘samudācārakkhaṇeyeva kilesehi saṃyutto nāma hoti, itarasmiṃ khaṇe asaṃyutto’’ti. Tenassa bhagavatā doso āropito. Athāyasmā ānando cintesi – ‘‘bhagavatā bhikkhusaṅghassa dhammaṃ desessāmīti attano dhammatāyeva ayaṃ dhammadesanā āraddhā, sā iminā apaṇḍitena bhikkhunā visaṃvāditā. Handāhaṃ bhagavantaṃ yācitvā bhikkhūnaṃ dhammaṃ desessāmī’’ti. So evamakāsi. Taṃ dassetuṃ ‘‘evaṃ vutte āyasmā ānando’’tiādi vuttaṃ.

Tattha sakkāyadiṭṭhipariyuṭṭhitenāti sakkāyadiṭṭhiyā gahitena abhibhūtena. Sakkāyadiṭṭhiparetenāti sakkāyadiṭṭhiyā anugatena. Nissaraṇanti diṭṭhinissaraṇaṃ nāma nibbānaṃ, taṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Appaṭivinītāti avinoditā anīhaṭā. Orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojananti heṭṭhābhāgiyasaṃyojanaṃ nāma hoti. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Sukkapakkho uttānatthoyeva. ‘‘Sānusayā pahīyatī’’ti vacanato panettha ekacce ‘‘aññaṃ saṃyojanaṃ añño anusayo’’ti vadanti. ‘‘Yathā hi sabyañjanaṃ bhatta’’nti vutte bhattato aññaṃ byañjanaṃ hoti, evaṃ ‘‘sānusayā’’ti vacanato pariyuṭṭhānasakkāyadiṭṭhito aññena anusayena bhavitabbanti tesaṃ laddhi. Te ‘‘sasīsaṃ pārupitvā’’tiādīhi paṭikkhipitabbā. Na hi sīsato añño puriso atthi. Athāpi siyā – ‘‘yadi tadeva saṃyojanaṃ so anusayo, evaṃ sante bhagavatā therassa taruṇūpamo upārambho duāropito hotī’’ti. Na duāropito, kasmā? Evaṃladdhikattāti vitthāritametaṃ. Tasmā soyeva kileso bandhanaṭṭhena saṃyojanaṃ, appahīnaṭṭhena anusayoti imamatthaṃ sandhāya bhagavatā ‘‘sānusayā pahīyatī’’ti evaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ.

sakkāyadiṭṭhipariyuṭṭhitenā Sakkāyadiṭṭhiparetenā Nissaraṇa Appaṭivinītā Orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojana
commentary_english:
129. Thus I have heard: the Mahāmālukyasutta.

There, *orambhāgiyāni* means the lower, portion-belonging attachments, pertaining to arising in the desire realm. *Saṃyojanāni* means bindings. *Kassa kho nāmā* means to whom, to what god or human, were [these teachings] taught and preserved? Did only you hear it, and no one else? *Anusetī* means it clings because it has not been abandoned. One who clings is called a *saṃyojana*.

Here, the Blessed One asked about *saṃyojana*, and the Elder also explained *saṃyojana*. Even so, the Blessed One found fault with his view. Why is that? Because the Elder held such a view. For this is his view: "One is only connected with the defilements at the moment of habitual practice, and unconnected at other moments." Therefore, the Blessed One found fault with him.

Then Āyasmā Ānanda thought: "This teaching of the Dharma has been begun by the Blessed One according to his own nature, thinking 'I will teach the Dharma to the Saṅgha of monks,' but it has been contradicted by this unwise monk. I will ask the Blessed One to teach the Dharma to the monks." So he did. To show this, it is said, "When this was said, Āyasmā Ānanda," etc.

There, *sakkāyadiṭṭhipariyuṭṭhitenā* means seized and overcome by *sakkāyadiṭṭhi* [personality belief]. *Sakkāyadiṭṭhiparetena* means followed by *sakkāyadiṭṭhi*. *Nissaraṇa* means that *nibbāna* is the escape from [wrong] views; he does not understand it as it really is. *Appaṭivinītā* means not removed, not driven away. *Orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojana* means it is called a lower-portion-belonging *saṃyojana*. The same method applies to the other clauses as well. The bright side is easy to understand. Because it is said that "it is abandoned together with the anusaya," some here say, "One *saṃyojana* is different, and one *anusaya* is different." Just as when it is said, "rice with curry," the curry is different from the rice, so because of the saying "with *anusaya*", it must be that the *anusaya* is different from *pariyuṭṭhāna-sakkāyadiṭṭhi* [personality belief in manifestation]; this is their view. They should be rejected by [passages beginning] "covering the head," etc. For there is no person other than the head.

But even if it were so – "if that same thing is the *saṃyojana* and the *anusaya*, then in that case, the Blessed One's rebuke of the Elder would be wrongly applied" – it is not wrongly applied. Why? Because he held such a view; this has been explained in detail. Therefore, it should be understood that the Blessed One said "it is abandoned together with the *anusaya*", intending to convey this meaning: that same defilement is a *saṃyojana* in the sense of a binding, and an *anusaya* in the sense of not being abandoned.

*Sakkāyadiṭṭhipariyuṭṭhitenā, sakkāyadiṭṭhiparetena, nissaraṇa, appaṭivinītā, orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojana.*

mula_pali: 130. ‘‘Idhānanda , assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṃ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto sakkāyadiṭṭhipariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati sakkāyadiṭṭhiparetena; uppannāya ca sakkāyadiṭṭhiyā nissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Tassa sā sakkāyadiṭṭhi thāmagatā appaṭivinītā orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ. Vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati vicikicchāparetena; uppannāya ca vicikicchāya nissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Tassa sā vicikicchā thāmagatā appaṭivinītā orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ. Sīlabbataparāmāsapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati sīlabbataparāmāsaparetena; uppannassa ca sīlabbataparāmāsassa nissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Tassa so sīlabbataparāmāso thāmagato appaṭivinīto orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ. Kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati kāmarāgaparetena ; uppannassa ca kāmarāgassa nissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Tassa so kāmarāgo thāmagato appaṭivinīto orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ. Byāpādapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati byāpādaparetena; uppannassa ca byāpādassa nissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Tassa so byāpādo thāmagato appaṭivinīto orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ.
mula_english: “Here, Ānanda, an untaught ordinary person who has no regard for noble ones and is unskilled and undisciplined in their Dhamma, who has no regard for true men and is unskilled and undisciplined in their Dhamma, abides with a mind obsessed and enslaved by personality view (*satkāyadṛṣṭi*), and he does not understand as it actually is the escape from the arisen personality view (*satkāyadṛṣṭi*); and when that personality view (*satkāyadṛṣṭi*) has become habitual and is uneradicated in him, it is a lower fetter (*orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ*). He abides with a mind obsessed and enslaved by doubt (*vicikicchā*), and he does not understand as it actually is the escape from arisen doubt (*vicikicchā*); and when that doubt (*vicikicchā*) has become habitual and is uneradicated in him, it is a lower fetter (*orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ*). He abides with a mind obsessed and enslaved by adherence to rules and observances (*śīlavrataparāmāśa*), and he does not understand as it actually is the escape from arisen adherence to rules and observances (*śīlavrataparāmāśa*); and when that adherence to rules and observances (*śīlavrataparāmāśa*) has become habitual and is uneradicated in him, it is a lower fetter (*orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ*). He abides with a mind obsessed and enslaved by sensual lust (*kāmarāga*), and he does not understand as it actually is the escape from arisen sensual lust (*kāmarāga*); and when that sensual lust (*kāmarāga*) has become habitual and is uneradicated in him, it is a lower fetter (*orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ*). He abides with a mind obsessed and enslaved by ill will (*vyāpāda*), and he does not understand as it actually is the escape from arisen ill will (*vyāpāda*); and when that ill will (*vyāpāda*) has become habitual and is uneradicated in him, it is a lower fetter (*orambhāgiyaṃ saṃyojanaṃ*).

mula_pali: 131. ‘‘Sutavā ca kho, ānanda, ariyasāvako ariyānaṃ dassāvī ariyadhammassa kovido ariyadhamme suvinīto, sappurisānaṃ dassāvī sappurisadhammassa kovido sappurisadhamme suvinīto na sakkāyadiṭṭhipariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati na sakkāyadiṭṭhiparetena; uppannāya ca sakkāyadiṭṭhiyā nissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Tassa sā sakkāyadiṭṭhi sānusayā pahīyati. Na vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati na vicikicchāparetena; uppannāya ca vicikicchāya nissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Tassa sā vicikicchā sānusayā pahīyati. Na sīlabbataparāmāsapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati na sīlabbataparāmāsaparetena; uppannassa ca sīlabbataparāmāsassa nissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Tassa so sīlabbataparāmāso sānusayo pahīyati. Na kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati na kāmarāgaparetena; uppannassa ca kāmarāgassa nissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Tassa so kāmarāgo sānusayo pahīyati . Na byāpādapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati na byāpādaparetena; uppannassa ca byāpādassa nissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Tassa so byāpādo sānusayo pahīyati.
mula_english:
131.
“Indeed, Ānanda, a well-taught noble disciple (ariyasāvako) who has regard for noble ones (ariyānaṃ dassāvī) and is skilled in the Dhamma of the noble ones (ariyadhammassa kovido), who is well-disciplined in the Dhamma of the noble ones (ariyadhamme suvinīto), who has regard for true men (sappurisānaṃ dassāvī) and is skilled in the Dhamma of true men (sappurisadhammassa kovido), who is well-disciplined in the Dhamma of true men (sappurisadhamme suvinīto), does not abide with a mind obsessed by personality view (sakkāyadiṭṭhi) nor enslaved by personality view (sakkāyadiṭṭhi); and he understands as it actually is the escape (nissaraṇaṃ) from the arisen personality view (sakkāyadiṭṭhi).
And personality view (sā sakkāyadiṭṭhi) together with the underlying tendency to it (sānusayā) is abandoned (pahīyati) in him.
He does not abide with a mind obsessed by doubt (vicikicchā) nor enslaved by doubt (vicikicchā); and he understands as it actually is the escape (nissaraṇaṃ) from arisen doubt (vicikicchāya).
And doubt (sā vicikicchā) together with the underlying tendency to it (sānusayā) is abandoned (pahīyati) in him.
He does not abide with a mind obsessed by clinging to rules and observances (sīlabbataparāmāsa) nor enslaved by clinging to rules and observances (sīlabbataparāmāsa); and he understands as it actually is the escape (nissaraṇaṃ) from arisen clinging to rules and observances (sīlabbataparāmāsassa).
And clinging to rules and observances (so sīlabbataparāmāso) together with the underlying tendency to it (sānusayo) is abandoned (pahīyati) in him.
He does not abide with a mind obsessed by sensual lust (kāmarāga) nor enslaved by sensual lust (kāmarāga); and he understands as it actually is the escape (nissaraṇaṃ) from arisen sensual lust (kāmarāgassa).
And sensual lust (so kāmarāgo) together with the underlying tendency to it (sānusayo) is abandoned (pahīyati) in him.
He does not abide with a mind obsessed by ill will (byāpāda) nor enslaved by ill will (byāpāda); and he understands as it actually is the escape (nissaraṇaṃ) from arisen ill will (byāpādassa).
And ill will (so byāpādo) together with the underlying tendency to it (sānusayo) is abandoned (pahīyati) in him.

mula_pali:
132. ‘‘Yo, ānanda, maggo yā paṭipadā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ pahānāya taṃ maggaṃ taṃ paṭipadaṃ anāgamma pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni ñassati vā dakkhati vā pajahissati vāti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, mahato rukkhassa tiṭṭhato sāravato tacaṃ acchetvā phegguṃ acchetvā sāracchedo bhavissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati; evameva kho, ānanda, yo maggo yā paṭipadā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ pahānāya taṃ maggaṃ taṃ paṭipadaṃ anāgamma pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni ñassati vā dakkhati vā pajahissati vāti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

‘‘Yo ca kho, ānanda, maggo yā paṭipadā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ pahānāya taṃ maggaṃ taṃ paṭipadaṃ āgamma pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni ñassati vā dakkhati vā pajahissati vāti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, mahato rukkhassa tiṭṭhato sāravato tacaṃ chetvā phegguṃ chetvā sāracchedo bhavissatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati; evameva kho, ānanda, yo maggo yā paṭipadā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ pahānāya taṃ maggaṃ taṃ paṭipadaṃ āgamma pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni ñassati vā dakkhati vā pajahissati vāti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, gaṅgā nadī pūrā udakassa samatittikā kākapeyyā. Atha dubbalako puriso āgaccheyya – ‘ahaṃ imissā gaṅgāya nadiyā tiriyaṃ bāhāya sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ gacchissāmī’ti gacchāmīti (sī. pī.); so na sakkuṇeyya gaṅgāya nadiyā tiriyaṃ bāhāya sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ gantuṃ. Evameva kho, ānanda, yesaṃ kesañci yassa kassaci (sabbattha) sakkāyanirodhāya dhamme desiyamāne cittaṃ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati; seyyathāpi so dubbalako puriso evamete daṭṭhabbā. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, gaṅgā nadī pūrā udakassa samatittikā kākapeyyā. Atha balavā puriso āgaccheyya – ‘ahaṃ imissā gaṅgāya nadiyā tiriyaṃ bāhāya sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ gacchissāmī’ti; so sakkuṇeyya gaṅgāya nadiyā tiriyaṃ bāhāya sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ gantuṃ. Evameva kho, ānanda, yesaṃ kesañci sakkāyanirodhāya dhamme desiyamāne cittaṃ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati; seyyathāpi so balavā puriso evamete daṭṭhabbā.

gacchāmīti (sī. pī.) yassa kassaci (sabbattha)
mula_english:
“There is a path, Ānanda, a way to the abandoning of the five lower fetters; that anyone, without coming to that path, to that way, shall know or see or abandon the five lower fetters - this is not possible.

Just as when there is a great tree standing possessed of heartwood, it is not possible that anyone shall cut out its heartwood without cutting through its bark and sapwood, so too, there is a path …this is not possible.

“There is a path, Ānanda, a way to the abandoning of the five lower fetters; that someone, by coming to that path, to that way, shall know and see and abandon the five lower fetters - this is possible.

Just as, when there is a great tree standing possessed of heartwood, it is possible that someone shall cut Out its heartwood by cutting through its bark and sapwood, so too, there is a path… this is possible.

“Suppose, Ānanda, the river Gaṅgā were full of water right up to the brim so that crows could drink from it.

and then a feeble man came thinking: ‘By swimming across the stream with my arms, I shall get safely across to the further shore of this river Gaṅgā’; yet he would not be able to get safely across.

So too, when the *dharma* is being taught to someone for the cessation of personality (*satkāya-nirodha*), if his mind does not enter into it and acquire confidence, steadiness, and decision, then he can be regarded as like the strong man.

“Suppose, Ānanda, the river Gaṅgā were full of water right up to the brim so that crows could drink from it.

and then a strong man came thinking: ‘By swimming across the stream with my arms, I shall get safely across to the further shore of this river Gaṅgā’; and he would be able to get safely across.

So too, when the *dharma* is being taught to someone for the cessation of personality (*satkāya-nirodha*), if his mind enters into it and acquires confidence, steadiness, and decision, then he can be regarded as like the strong man.
commentary_pali: 132.Tacaṃ chetvātiādīsu idaṃ opammasaṃsandanaṃ – tacacchedo viya hi samāpatti daṭṭhabbā, pheggucchedo viya vipassanā, sāracchedo viya maggo. Paṭipadā pana lokiyalokuttaramissakāva vaṭṭati. Evamete daṭṭhabbāti evarūpā puggalā evaṃ daṭṭhabbā.
commentary_english: In " *tacaṃ chetvā* tiādīsu," this is a connection made through simile: the attainment (*samāpatti*) should be seen like cutting the bark (*tacacchedo*), insight (*vipassanā*) is like cutting the sapwood (*pheggucchedo*), the path (*maggo*) is like cutting the heartwood (*sāracchedo*). However, the practice (*paṭipadā*) is suitable as a mixture of mundane and supramundane. " *evamete daṭṭhabbā* ti," such individuals should be seen in this way.

mula_pali:
133. ‘‘Katamo cānanda, maggo, katamā paṭipadā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ pahānāya? Idhānanda, bhikkhu upadhivivekā akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānā sabbaso kāyaduṭṭhullānaṃ paṭippassaddhiyā vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. So yadeva tattha hoti rūpagataṃ vedanāgataṃ saññāgataṃ saṅkhāragataṃ viññāṇagataṃ te dhamme aniccato dukkhato rogato gaṇḍato sallato aghato ābādhato parato palokato suññato anattato samanupassati. So tehi dhammehi cittaṃ paṭivāpeti paṭipāpeti (syā.), patiṭṭhāpeti (ka.). So tehi dhammehi cittaṃ paṭivāpetvā amatāya dhātuyā cittaṃ upasaṃharati – ‘etaṃ santaṃ etaṃ paṇītaṃ yadidaṃ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo virāgo nirodho nibbāna’nti. So tattha ṭhito āsavānaṃ khayaṃ pāpuṇāti; no ce āsavānaṃ khayaṃ pāpuṇāti teneva dhammarāgena tāya dhammanandiyā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko hoti, tattha parinibbāyī, anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā. Ayampi kho, ānanda, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ pahānāya.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. So yadeva tattha hoti rūpagataṃ vedanāgataṃ saññāgataṃ saṅkhāragataṃ viññāṇagataṃ… anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā. Ayampi kho, ānanda, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ pahānāya.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. So yadeva tattha hoti vedanāgataṃ saññāgataṃ saṅkhāragataṃ viññāṇagataṃ…pe… anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā. Ayampi kho, ānanda, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ pahānāya.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. So yadeva tattha hoti vedanāgataṃ saññāgataṃ saṅkhāragataṃ viññāṇagataṃ…pe… anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā. Ayampi kho, ānanda, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ pahānāya.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. So yadeva tattha hoti vedanāgataṃ saññāgataṃ saṅkhāragataṃ viññāṇagataṃ…pe… anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā. Ayampi kho, ānanda, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ pahānāyā’’ti.

‘‘Eso ce, bhante, maggo esā paṭipadā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ pahānāya, atha kiñcarahi idhekacce bhikkhū cetovimuttino ekacce bhikkhū paññāvimuttino’’ti? ‘‘Ettha kho panesāhaṃ ettha kho tesāhaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), ānanda, indriyavemattataṃ vadāmī’’ti.

ettha kho tesāhaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā ānando bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Mahāmālukyasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.
mula_english:
133. "And what, Ānanda, is the path, what is the way to the abandoning of the five lower fetters (*orambhāgiya-saṃyojana*)? Here, Ānanda, a *bhikkhu*, quite secluded from sense-desires, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and abides in the first *jhāna*, which is accompanied by thought and examination, born of seclusion, filled with rapture and joy, having abandoned attachment to the acquisitions, abandoning unwholesome *dharmas*, and with the stilling of all bodily distress.

Whatever exists therein of material form (*rūpa*), feeling (*vedanā*), perception (*saṃjñā*), formations (*saṃskāra*), and consciousness (*vijñāṇa*), he sees those states as impermanent, as suffering, as a disease, as a tumour, as a barb, as a calamity, as an affliction, as alien, as disintegrating, as void, as not self.

He turns his mind away from those states.

He turns his mind away from those states and directs it towards the deathless element thus: ‘This is the peaceful, this is the sublime, that is, the stilling of all formations, the relinquishing of all acquisitions, the destruction of craving (*taṇhā*), dispassion (*virāga*), cessation (*nirodha*), *Nirvāṇa*.’

Standing upon that, he attains the destruction of the taints (*āsava*). But if he does not attain the destruction of the taints, then because of that desire for the Dharma, that delight in the Dharma, with the destruction of the five lower fetters he becomes one due to reappear spontaneously, and there attain final *Nirvāṇa* without ever returning from that world.

This is the path, Ānanda, the way to the abandoning of the five lower fetters.

“Again, Ānanda, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought…he enters upon and abides in the second *jhāna*… the third *jhāna*… the fourth *jhāna*.

Whatever exists therein of material form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness… he does not return from that world.

This is the path, Ānanda, the way to the abandoning of the five lower fetters.

“Again, Ānanda, with the complete surmounting of perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of sensory impact, with non-attention to perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite,’ a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the base of infinite space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*).

Whatever exists therein of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness… he does not return from that world.

This is the path, Ānanda, the way to the abandoning of the five lower fetters.

“Again, Ānanda, by completely surmounting the base of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite,’ a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the base of infinite consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatana*).

Whatever exists therein of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness… he does not return from that world.

This is the path, Ānanda, the way to the abandoning of the five lower fetters.

“Again, Ānanda, by completely surmounting the base of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing,’ a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*).

Whatever exists therein of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness… he does not return from that world.

This is the path, Ānanda, the way to the abandoning of the five lower fetters.”

“Venerable sir, if this is the path, this is the way to the abandoning of the five lower fetters, then how is it that some *bhikkhus* here are said to gain deliverance of mind (*cetovimutti*) and some are said to gain deliverance by wisdom (*paññāvimutti*)?”

Ānanda, I speak of variety of faculties."
Here, indeed, concerning these...

The Bhagavān said this.

The venerable Ānanda, being pleased, rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words.

The Mahāmālukyasūtra, the fourth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
133.Upadhivivekāti upadhivivekena. Iminā pañcakāmaguṇaviveko kathito. Akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāti iminā nīvaraṇappahānaṃ kathitaṃ. Kāyaduṭṭhullānaṃ paṭippassaddhiyāti iminā kāyālasiyapaṭippassaddhi kathitā. Vivicceva kāmehīti upadhivivekena kāmehi vinā hutvā. Vivicca akusalehīti akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānena kāyaduṭṭhullānaṃ paṭippassaddhiyā ca akusalehi vinā hutvā. Yadeva tattha hotīti yaṃ tattha antosamāpattikkhaṇeyeva samāpattisamuṭṭhitañca rūpādidhammajātaṃ hoti. Tedhammeti te rūpagatantiādinā nayena vutte rūpādayo dhamme. Aniccatoti na niccato. Dukkhatoti na sukhato. Rogatotiādīsu ābādhaṭṭhena rogato, antodosaṭṭhena gaṇḍato, anupaviddhaṭṭhena dukkhajananaṭṭhena ca sallato, dukkhaṭṭhena aghato, rogaṭṭhena ābādhato, asakaṭṭhena parato, palujjanaṭṭhena palokato, nissattaṭṭhena suññato, na attaṭṭhena anattato. Tattha aniccato, palokatoti dvīhi padehi aniccalakkhaṇaṃ kathitaṃ, dukkhatotiādīhi chahi dukkhalakkhaṇaṃ, parato suññato anattatoti tīhi anattalakkhaṇaṃ.

So tehi dhammehīti so tehi evaṃ tilakkhaṇaṃ āropetvā diṭṭhehi antosamāpattiyaṃ pañcakkhandhadhammehi. Cittaṃ paṭivāpetīti cittaṃ paṭisaṃharati moceti apaneti. Upasaṃharatīti vipassanācittaṃ tāva savanavasena thutivasena pariyattivasena paññattivasena ca etaṃ santaṃ nibbānanti evaṃ asaṅkhatāya amatāya dhātuyā upasaṃharati. Maggacittaṃ nibbānaṃ ārammaṇakaraṇavaseneva etaṃ santametaṃ paṇītanti na evaṃ vadati, iminā pana ākārena taṃ paṭivijjhanto tattha cittaṃ upasaṃharatīti attho. So tattha ṭhitoti tāya tilakkhaṇārammaṇāya vipassanāya ṭhito. Āsavānaṃ khayaṃ pāpuṇātīti anukkamena cattāro magge bhāvetvā pāpuṇāti . Teneva dhammarāgenāti samathavipassanādhamme chandarāgena. Samathavipassanāsu hi sabbaso chandarāgaṃ pariyādātuṃ sakkonto arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, asakkonto anāgāmī hoti.

So tehi dhammehī Cittaṃ paṭivāpetī Upasaṃharatī So tattha ṭhito Āsavānaṃ khayaṃ pāpuṇātī Teneva dhammarāgenā

Yadevatattha hoti vedanāgatanti idha pana rūpaṃ na gahitaṃ. Kasmā? Samatikkantattā. Ayañhi heṭṭhā rūpāvacarajjhānaṃ samāpajjitvā rūpaṃ atikkamitvā arūpāvacarasamāpattiṃ samāpannoti samathavasenapinena rūpaṃ atikkantaṃ, heṭṭhā rūpaṃ sammadeva sammasitvā taṃ atikkamma idāni arūpaṃ sammasatīti vipassanāvasenapinena rūpaṃ atikkantaṃ. Arūpe pana sabbasopi rūpaṃ natthīti taṃ sandhāyapi idha rūpaṃ na gahitaṃ.

Yadeva tattha hoti vedanāgata

Atha kiñcarahīti kiṃ pucchāmīti pucchati? Samathavasena gacchato cittekaggatā dhuraṃ hoti, so cetovimutto nāma. Vipassanāvasena gacchato paññā dhuraṃ hoti, so paññāvimutto nāmāti ettha therassa kaṅkhā natthi. Ayaṃ sabhāvadhammoyeva, samathavaseneva pana gacchantesu eko cetovimutto nāma hoti, eko paññāvimutto. Vipassanāvasena gacchantesupi eko paññāvimutto nāma hoti, eko cetovimuttoti ettha kiṃ kāraṇanti pucchati.

Atha kiñcarahī

Indriyavemattataṃ vadāmīti indriyanānattataṃ vadāmi. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti, na tvaṃ, ānanda, dasa pāramiyo pūretvā sabbaññutaṃ paṭivijjhi, tena te etaṃ apākaṭaṃ. Ahaṃ pana paṭivijjhiṃ, tena me etaṃ pākaṭaṃ. Ettha hi indriyanānattatā kāraṇaṃ. Samathavaseneva hi gacchantesu ekassa bhikkhuno cittekaggatā dhuraṃ hoti, so cetovimutto nāma hoti. Ekassa paññā dhuraṃ hoti, so paññāvimutto nāma hoti. Vipassanāvaseneva ca gacchantesu ekassa paññā dhuraṃ hoti, so paññāvimutto nāma hoti. Ekassa cittekaggatā dhuraṃ hoti, so cetovimutto nāma hoti. Dve aggasāvakā samathavipassanādhurena arahattaṃ pattā. Tesu dhammasenāpati paññāvimutto jāto, mahāmoggallānatthero cetovimutto. Iti indriyavemattamettha kāraṇanti veditabbaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Indriyavemattataṃ vadāmī

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Mahāmālukyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
133. *Upadhivivekā* means by discrimination of the basis.

By this, discrimination of the five strands of sense desire is spoken of.

*Akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānā* means by the abandonment of unwholesome factors, by this, abandonment of the hindrances is spoken of.

*Kāyaduṭṭhullānaṃ paṭippassaddhiyā* means by tranquilization of bodily unruliness, by this, tranquilization of bodily sloth and torpor is spoken of.

*Vivicceva kāmehī* means having become without desires by discrimination of the basis.

*Vivicca akusalehī* means having become without unwholesome [factors] by the abandonment of unwholesome factors and by tranquilization of bodily unruliness.

*Yadeva tattha hotī* means whatever exists there, that is, whatever phenomena ( *rūpādi-dhamma-jātaṃ*) exist there at the very moment of inner attainment (*antosaṃāpatti*), and which arise together with the attainment.

*Te dhamme* means those factors, that is, the factors like form, etc., which are spoken of in the manner beginning with "they have gone to form".

*Aniccato* means not permanent.

*Dukkhato* means not pleasurable.

*Rogato* etc. means in the case of diseases, *rogato* is due to the condition of being afflicted, *gaṇḍato* is due to the condition of internal affliction, *sallato* is due to the condition of not being rejected and the condition of producing suffering, *aghato* is due to the condition of suffering, *ābādhato* is due to the condition of disease, *parato* is due to the condition of being unsustained, *palokato* is due to the condition of perishing, *suññato* is due to the condition of being without substance, *anattato* is due to the condition of not being self.

There, by the two terms *aniccatas* and *palokato*, the characteristic of impermanence is spoken of; by the six, beginning with *dukkhato*, the characteristic of suffering; by the three, *parato*, *suññato*, *anattato*, the characteristic of not-self.

*So tehi dhammehī* means he, by those factors, that is, by the five aggregates (*pañcakkhandha*) as seen by superimposing the three characteristics (*tilakkhaṇa*) in this way in inner attainment (*antosaṃāpatti*).

*Cittaṃ paṭivāpetī* means he turns back the mind, withdraws it, releases it, removes it.

*Upasaṃharatī* means he leads [the mind] near; he leads the mind of insight near to the unconditioned (*asaṅkhata*) deathless (*amata*) element (*dhātu*), that is, *nirvāṇa*, by way of praise, by way of learning, by way of designation, [thinking,] "This is peace, this is *nirvāṇa*."

However, the path-mind does not speak thus, [saying,] "This is peace, this is excellent," merely through the force of making *nirvāṇa* its object. But in this way, while penetrating that, he leads the mind near there, is the meaning.

*So tattha ṭhito* means he stands in that insight (*vipassanā*) which has the three characteristics (*tilakkhaṇa*) as its object (*ārammaṇa*).

*Āsavānaṃ khayaṃ pāpuṇātī* means he attains the destruction of the āsavas by developing the four paths in due order.

*Teneva dhammarāgenā* means by interest (*chandarāga*) in the states of serenity and insight (*samatha-vipassanā-dhamma*).

For one who, in those states of serenity and insight, is able to completely consume interest, attains arhatship; one who is unable to, becomes a non-returner (anāgāmī).

So, by those factors, he turns back the mind; he leads [the mind] near; he stands in that place; he attains the destruction of the āsavas; by that very interest in the Dharma; whatever there is there, sensation-gone-to-that-place, here, however, form is not taken.

Why? Because of having transcended [it].

For here, having attained to the *rūpāvacara-jhāna* below, having transcended form, he attains to the *arūpāvacara-samāpatti*. Thus, by way of serenity, form is transcended. Below, having properly experienced form, having transcended that, now he experiences the formless. Thus, by way of insight, form is transcended.

However, in the formless, since form does not exist at all, with reference to that also, form is not taken here.

Whatever sensation gone to that place exists there. Now what? He asks, "What shall I ask?" For one going by way of serenity, singleness of mind is the prominent feature; he is called mind-liberated.

For one going by way of insight, wisdom is the prominent feature; he is called wisdom-liberated. Here, there is no doubt for the elder.

This is just the nature of the phenomena. However, among those going by way of serenity, one is called mind-liberated, one is called wisdom-liberated.

Even among those going by way of insight, one is called wisdom-liberated, one is called mind-liberated. Here, he asks, what is the reason?

Now what? I will speak of the diversity of the faculties means I will speak of the difference of the faculties.

This has been said: "It is not you, Ānanda, who, having fulfilled the ten perfections, penetrated omniscience; therefore, this is not clear to you."

"But I penetrated [it]; therefore, this is clear to me."

Here, the diversity of the faculties is the reason.
Indeed, while going by way of tranquility, if a *bhikkhu* has one-pointedness of mind ( *cittekaggatā*) as his chief concern (*dhuraṃ*), he is called liberated in mind (*cetovimutto*).

If one has wisdom (*paññā*) as their chief concern, they are called liberated by wisdom (*paññāvimutto*).

And while going by way of insight (*vipassanā*), if one has wisdom (*paññā*) as their chief concern (*dhuraṃ*), he is called liberated by wisdom (*paññāvimutto*).

If one has one-pointedness of mind (*cittekaggatā*) as his chief concern, he is called liberated in mind (*cetovimutto*).

Two foremost disciples attained *arahatta* by means of tranquility (*samatha*) and insight (*vipassanā*) as their chief concern (*dhurena*).

Among them, the general of the Dharma (*dhammasenāpati*) was born liberated by wisdom (*paññāvimutto*), and the great *thera* Moggallana (*mahāmoggallānatthero*) was liberated in mind (*cetovimutto*).

Thus, the difference in faculties (*indriyavemattamettha*) should be understood as the reason.

The rest is clear throughout.

I speak of the difference in faculties (*indriyavemattataṃ vadāmī*).

The commentary on the *Majjhimanikāya*, the *Papañcasūdanī*, is finished.

The exposition of the Mahāmālukya Sutta (*mahāmālukyasuttavaṇṇanā*) is finished.

mula_pali: 134. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhadante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘ahaṃ kho, bhikkhave, ekāsanabhojanaṃ bhuñjāmi; ekāsanabhojanaṃ kho, ahaṃ, bhikkhave, bhuñjamāno appābādhatañca sañjānāmi appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañca. Etha, tumhepi, bhikkhave, ekāsanabhojanaṃ bhuñjatha; ekāsanabhojanaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tumhepi bhuñjamānā appābādhatañca sañjānissatha appātaṅkatañca lahuṭṭhānañca balañca phāsuvihārañcā’’ti. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā bhaddāli bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘ahaṃ kho, bhante, na ussahāmi ekāsanabhojanaṃ bhuñjituṃ; ekāsanabhojanañhi me, bhante, bhuñjato siyā kukkuccaṃ, siyā vippaṭisāro’’ti. ‘‘Tena hi tvaṃ, bhaddāli, yattha nimantito assasi tattha ekadesaṃ bhuñjitvā ekadesaṃ nīharitvāpi bhuñjeyyāsi. Evampi kho tvaṃ, bhaddāli, bhuñjamāno ekāsano yāpessasī’’ti bhuñjamāno yāpessasīti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). ‘‘Evampi kho ahaṃ, bhante, na ussahāmi bhuñjituṃ; evampi hi me, bhante, bhuñjato siyā kukkuccaṃ, siyā vippaṭisāro’’ti. Atha kho āyasmā bhaddāli bhagavatā sikkhāpade paññāpiyamāne bhikkhusaṅghe sikkhaṃ samādiyamāne anussāhaṃ pavedesi. Atha kho āyasmā bhaddāli sabbaṃ taṃ temāsaṃ na bhagavato sammukhībhāvaṃ adāsi, yathā taṃ satthusāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārī.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One (bhagavā) was staying near Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapindika’s Park (jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme).

There the Blessed One addressed the monks (bhikkhū), saying: “Monks (bhikkhavo)!”

“Venerable sir (bhadante),” those monks replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this: “Monks (bhikkhave), I eat at a single session (ekāsanabhojanaṃ). By eating at a single session (ekāsanabhojanaṃ), monks (bhikkhave), I experience freedom from illness (appābādhatañca), freedom from affliction (appātaṅkatañca), lightness (lahuṭṭhānañca), strength (balañca), and a comfortable abiding (phāsuvihārañca).

Come, monks (bhikkhave), eat at a single session (ekāsanabhojanaṃ). By eating at a single session (ekāsanabhojanaṃ), monks (bhikkhave), you too will experience freedom from illness (appābādhatañca), freedom from affliction (appātaṅkatañca), lightness (lahuṭṭhānañca), strength (balañca), and a comfortable abiding (phāsuvihārañcā).”

When this was said, the venerable Bhaddāli told the Blessed One: “Venerable sir (bhante), I am not willing to eat at a single session (ekāsanabhojanaṃ); for if I were to eat at a single session (ekāsanabhojanaṃ), venerable sir (bhante), I might have worry (kukkuccaṃ) and anxiety (vippaṭisāro) about it.”

“Then, Bhaddāli, eat one part there where you are invited and bring away one part to eat.

Even then, Bhaddāli, while eating, you should maintain the practice of eating one meal a day."

“Even in that way, venerable sir (bhante), I am not willing to eat; for if I were to eat in that way, venerable sir (bhante), I might also have worry (kukkuccaṃ) and anxiety (vippaṭisāro) about it.”

Then, when this training precept (sikkhāpade) was being made known by the Blessed One, the venerable Bhaddāli publicly declared in the Sangha (bhikkhusaṅghe) of monks his unwillingness (anussāhaṃ) to undertake the training (sikkhaṃ samādiyamāne).

Then the venerable Bhaddāli did not present himself to the Blessed One for the whole of that three-month period of the Rains, as he did not fulfil the training in the Teacher’s Dispensation (satthusāsane).
commentary_pali:
134.Evaṃme sutanti bhaddālisuttaṃ. Tattha ekāsanabhojananti ekasmiṃ purebhatte asanabhojanaṃ, bhuñjitabbabhattanti attho. Appābādhatantiādīni kakacopame vitthāritāni. Na ussahāmīti na sakkomi. Siyā kukkuccaṃ siyā vippaṭisāroti evaṃ bhuñjanto yāvajīvaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ sakkhissāmi nu kho, na nu khoti iti me vippaṭisārakukkuccaṃ bhaveyyāti attho. Ekadesaṃ bhuñjitvāti porāṇakattherā kira patte bhattaṃ pakkhipitvā sappimhi dinne sappinā uṇhameva thokaṃ bhuñjitvā hatthe dhovitvā avasesaṃ bahi nīharitvā chāyūdakaphāsuke ṭhāne nisīditvā bhuñjanti. Etaṃ sandhāya satthā āha. Bhaddāli, pana cintesi – ‘‘sace sakiṃ pattaṃ pūretvā dinnaṃ bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā puna pattaṃ dhovitvā odanassa pūretvā laddhaṃ bahi nīharitvā chāyūdakaphāsuke ṭhāne bhuñjeyya, iti evaṃ vaṭṭeyya, itarathā ko sakkotī’’ti. Tasmā evampi kho ahaṃ, bhante, na ussahāmīti āha. Ayaṃ kira atīte anantarāya jātiyā kākayoniyaṃ nibbatti. Kākā ca nāma mahāchātakā honti. Tasmā chātakatthero nāma ahosi. Tassa pana viravantasseva bhagavā taṃ madditvā ajjhottharitvā – ‘‘yo pana bhikkhu vikāle khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā khādeyya vā bhuñjeyya vā pācittiya’’nti (pāci. 248) sikkhāpadaṃ paññapesi. Tena vuttaṃ atha kho āyasmā, bhaddāli,…pe… anussāhaṃ pavedesīti.

Yathātanti yathā aññopi sikkhāya na paripūrakārī ekavihārepi vasanto satthu sammukhībhāvaṃ na dadeyya, tatheva na adāsīti attho. Neva bhagavato upaṭṭhānaṃ agamāsi, na dhammadesanaṭṭhānaṃ na vitakkamāḷakaṃ, na ekaṃ bhikkhācāramaggaṃ paṭipajji. Yasmiṃ kule bhagavā nisīdati, tassa dvārepi na aṭṭhāsi. Sacassa vasanaṭṭhānaṃ bhagavā gacchati, so puretarameva ñatvā aññattha gacchati. Saddhāpabbajito kiresa kulaputto parisuddhasīlo. Tenassa na añño vitakko ahosi, – ‘‘mayā nāma udarakāraṇā bhagavato sikkhāpadapaññāpanaṃ paṭibāhitaṃ, ananucchavikaṃ me kata’’nti ayameva vitakko ahosi. Tasmā ekavihāre vasantopi lajjāya satthu sammukhībhāvaṃ nādāsi.

Yathā ta
commentary_english:
134. Thus have I heard: the *Bhaddālisutta*.

There, *ekāsanabhojana* means eating a meal at one sitting before noon; the meaning is food that should be eaten.

*Appābādhata*, etc., are explained through the simile of a saw.

*Na ussahāmī* means I am not able.

*"Siyā kukkuccaṃ siyā vippaṭisāro"* means, thinking in this way while eating, "Will I be able to practice the *brahmacariya* for as long as I live? Or will I not?" the meaning is that regret and scruples may arise in me.

*Ekadesaṃ bhuñjitvā* means the elder monks of old, having poured food into their bowl and having been given ghee, having eaten only a little while it was still hot with the ghee, having washed their hands, having taken the remainder outside, they would sit down in a place comfortable with shade and water and eat.

With this in mind, the Teacher said:

Bhaddāli, consider this: "If, having filled the bowl once, having eaten the food that was given, having washed the bowl again, having filled it with rice, and having obtained more, he should take it outside, and should eat in a place comfortable with shade and water, in this way it would be proper, otherwise who would be able to do it?"

Therefore, "Even in this way, venerable sir, I am not able," he said.

It is said that in the past, in an uninterrupted birth, he was born in the crow-womb (*kākayoniyaṃ*).

And crows are very greedy.

Therefore, he was named *Chātakathera*.

While he was crying in this way, the Blessed One, having touched him and covered him, laid down the rule of training: "Whoever, monks, should eat or consume any *khādanīyaṃ* or *bhojanīyaṃ* at the wrong time, it is an offense entailing confession" (*pācittiya*).

Therefore it was said: "Then, venerable Bhaddāli...he declared his lack of enthusiasm".

Just as another, though not fulfilling the training, dwelling in one monastery, would not give face to face with the Teacher, just so he did not give. This is the meaning.

He did not go to the Blessed One's presence, nor to the place of teaching the Dharma, nor to the debating hall, nor did he follow a single alms-round path.

In whatever family the Blessed One would sit down, he did not stand even at the door.

When the Blessed One would go to his dwelling place, he, knowing it beforehand, would go elsewhere.

It is said that this son of a good family went forth out of faith, with pure morality.

Therefore, no other thought arose in him: "It is I who, for the sake of my belly, have rejected the Blessed One's laying down of a training rule; it is not fitting that this has been done by me." This very thought arose in him.

Therefore, even dwelling in one monastery, out of shame he did not give face to face with the Teacher.

mula_pali:
135. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū bhagavato cīvarakammaṃ karonti – niṭṭhitacīvaro bhagavā temāsaccayena cārikaṃ pakkamissatīti. Atha kho āyasmā bhaddāli yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā tehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ bhaddāliṃ te bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – ‘‘idaṃ kho, āvuso bhaddāli, bhagavato cīvarakammaṃ karīyati karaṇīyaṃ (ka.). Niṭṭhitacīvaro bhagavā temāsaccayena cārikaṃ pakkamissati. Iṅghāvuso bhaddāli, etaṃ dosakaṃ sādhukaṃ manasi karohi, mā te pacchā dukkarataraṃ ahosī’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho āyasmā bhaddāli tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā bhaddāli bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘accayo maṃ, bhante, accagamā yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ, yohaṃ bhagavatā sikkhāpade paññāpiyamāne bhikkhusaṅghe sikkhaṃ samādiyamāne anussāhaṃ pavedesiṃ. Tassa me, bhante, bhagavā accayaṃ accayato paṭiggaṇhātu āyatiṃ saṃvarāyā’’ti.

‘‘Taggha tvaṃ, bhaddāli, accayo accagamā yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ mayā sikkhāpade paññāpiyamāne bhikkhusaṅghe sikkhaṃ samādiyamāne anussāhaṃ pavedesi. Samayopi kho te, bhaddāli, appaṭividdho ahosi – ‘bhagavā kho sāvatthiyaṃ viharati, bhagavāpi maṃ jānissati – bhaddāli nāma bhikkhu satthusāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārī’ti. Ayampi kho te, bhaddāli, samayo appaṭividdho ahosi. Samayopi kho te, bhaddāli, appaṭividdho ahosi – ‘sambahulā kho bhikkhu sāvatthiyaṃ vassaṃ upagatā, tepi maṃ jānissanti – bhaddāli nāma bhikkhu satthusāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārī’ti. Ayampi kho te, bhaddāli, samayo appaṭividdho ahosi. Samayopi kho te, bhaddāli, appaṭividdho ahosi – ‘sambahulā kho bhikkhuniyo sāvatthiyaṃ vassaṃ upagatā, tāpi maṃ jānissanti – bhaddāli nāma bhikkhu satthusāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārī’ti. Ayampi kho te, bhaddāli, samayo appaṭividdho ahosi. Samayopi kho te, bhaddāli, appaṭividdho ahosi – ‘sambahulā kho upāsakā sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasanti, tepi maṃ jānissanti – bhaddāli nāma bhikkhu satthusāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārī’ti. Ayampi kho te, bhaddāli, samayo appaṭividdho ahosi. Samayopi kho te, bhaddāli, appaṭividdho ahosi – ‘sambahulā kho upāsikā sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasanti, tāpi maṃ jānissanti – bhaddāli nāma bhikkhu satthusāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārī’ti. Ayampi kho te, bhaddāli , samayo appaṭividdho ahosi. Samayopi kho te, bhaddāli, appaṭividdho ahosi – ‘sambahulā kho nānātitthiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇā sāvatthiyaṃ vassaṃ upagatā, tepi maṃ jānissanti – bhaddāli nāma bhikkhu samaṇassa gotamassa sāvako theraññataro bhikkhu sāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārī’ti. Ayampi kho te, bhaddāli, samayo appaṭividdho ahosī’’ti.

‘‘Accayo maṃ, bhante, accagamā yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ, yohaṃ bhagavatā sikkhāpade paññāpiyamāne bhikkhusaṅghe sikkhaṃ samādiyamāne anussāhaṃ pavedesiṃ. Tassa me, bhante, bhagavā accayaṃ accayato paṭiggaṇhātu āyatiṃ saṃvarāyā’’ti. ‘‘Taggha tvaṃ, bhaddāli, accayo accagamā yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ mayā sikkhāpade paññāpiyamāne bhikkhusaṅghe sikkhaṃ samādiyamāne anussāhaṃ pavedesi’’.
mula_english:
135. Now on that occasion, a number of *bhikkhus* were engaged in making up a robe for the Blessed One, thinking: “With his robe completed, at the end of the three months of the Rains (*temāsa*), the Blessed One will set out wandering (*cārikaṃ pakkamissatīti*).”

Then the venerable Bhaddāli went to those *bhikkhus* and exchanged greetings with them. When this courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side.

As he was sitting there, these *bhikkhus* said to the venerable Bhaddāli: “Friend Bhaddāli, this robe is being made up for the Blessed One. With his robe completed, at the end of the three months of the rains, the Blessed One will set out wandering.”

“Please, friend Bhaddāli, give proper attention to your declaration. Do not let it become more difficult for you later on.”

“Yes, friends,” he replied, and the venerable Bhaddāli went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side.

As he was sitting there, the venerable Bhaddāli said to the Blessed One, “Venerable sir, a transgression (*accayo*) overcame me, in that like a fool, confused and blundering, when a training precept (*sikkhāpada*) was being made known by the Blessed One, I publicly declared in the *Saṅgha* of *bhikkhus* my unwillingness to undertake the training. May the Lord accept my confession of this fault (*accayaṃ accayato*), that I may restrain myself in future!”

“Surely, Bhaddāli, a transgression overcame you, in that like a fool, confused and blundering, when a training precept was being made known by me, you publicly declared in the *Saṅgha* of *bhikkhus* your unwillingness to undertake the training.

Bhaddāli, this circumstance too was not recognised by you: ‘The Blessed One is living at Sāvatthī, and the Blessed One will know me thus: “The *bhikkhu* named Bhaddāli is one who does not fulfil the training in the Teacher’s Dispensation (*satthusāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārī*)".’ This circumstance too was not recognised by you.

Bhaddāli, this circumstance too was not recognised by you: ‘Many *bhikkhus* have taken up residence at Sāvatthī for the Rains (*vassaṃ upagatā*), and they too will know me thus: “The *bhikkhu* named Bhaddāli is one who does not fulfil the training in the Teacher’s Dispensation (*satthusāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārī*)".’ This circumstance too was not recognised by you.

Bhaddāli, this circumstance too was not recognised by you: ‘Many *bhikkhunis* have taken up residence at Sāvatthī for the Rains (*vassaṃ upagatā*), and they too will know me thus: “The *bhikkhu* named Bhaddāli is one who does not fulfil the training in the Teacher’s Dispensation (*satthusāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārī*)".’ This circumstance too was not recognised by you.

Bhaddāli, this circumstance too was not recognised by you: ‘Many men lay followers (*upāsakā*) are staying at Sāvatthī, and they too will know me thus: “The *bhikkhu* named Bhaddāli is one who does not fulfil the training in the Teacher’s Dispensation (*satthusāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārī*)".’ This circumstance too was not recognised by you.

Bhaddāli, this circumstance too was not recognised by you: ‘Many women lay followers (*upāsikā*) are staying at Sāvatthī, and they too will know me thus: “The *bhikkhu* named Bhaddāli is one who does not fulfil the training in the Teacher’s Dispensation (*satthusāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārī*)".’ This circumstance too was not recognised by you.

Bhaddāli, this circumstance too was not recognised by you: ‘Many recluses and *brāhmaṇas* of other sects have taken up residence at Sāvatthī for the Rains (*vassaṃ upagatā*), and they too will know me thus: “The *bhikkhu* named Bhaddāli, a disciple of the recluse Gotama (*samaṇassa Gotamassa sāvako*), is one who does not fulfil the training in the Teacher’s Dispensation (*satthusāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārī*)".’ This circumstance too was not recognised by you.”

commentary_pali:
135.Cīvarakammaṃ karontīti manussā bhagavato cīvarasāṭakaṃ adaṃsu, taṃ gahetvā cīvaraṃ karonti. Etaṃ dosakanti etaṃ okāsametaṃ aparādhaṃ, satthu sikkhāpadaṃ paññapentassa paṭibāhitakāraṇaṃ sādhukaṃ manasi karohīti attho. Dukkarataranti vassañhi vasitvā disāpakkante bhikkhū kuhiṃ vasitthāti pucchanti, tehi jetavane vasimhāti vutte, ‘‘āvuso, bhagavā imasmiṃ antovasse kataraṃ jātakaṃ kathesi, kataraṃ suttantaṃ, kataraṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññapesī’’ti pucchitāro honti. Tato ‘‘vikālabhojanasikkhāpadaṃ paññapesi, bhaddāli, nāma naṃ eko thero paṭibāhī’’ti vakkhanti. Taṃ sutvā bhikkhū – ‘‘bhagavatopi nāma sikkhāpadaṃ paññapentassa paṭibāhitaṃ ayuttaṃ akāraṇa’’nti vadanti. Evaṃ te ayaṃ doso mahājanantare pākaṭo hutvā duppaṭikārataṃ āpajjissatīti maññamānā evamāhaṃsu. Apica aññepi bhikkhū pavāretvā satthu santikaṃ āgamissanti. Atha tvaṃ ‘‘ethāvuso, mama satthāraṃ khamāpentassa sahāyā hothā’’ti saṅghaṃ sannipātessasi. Tattha āgantukā pucchissanti, ‘‘āvuso, kiṃ imināpi bhikkhunā kata’’nti. Tato etamatthaṃ sutvā ‘‘bhāriyaṃ kataṃ bhikkhunā, dasabalaṃ nāma paṭibāhissatīti ayuttameta’’nti vakkhanti. Evampi te ayaṃ aparādho mahājanantare pākaṭo hutvā duppaṭikārataṃ āpajjissatīti maññamānāpi evamāhaṃsu. Atha vā bhagavā pavāretvā cārikaṃ pakkamissati, atha tvaṃ gatagataṭṭhāne bhagavato khamāpanatthāya saṅghaṃ sannipātessasi. Tatra disāvāsino bhikkhū pucchissanti, ‘‘āvuso, kiṃ iminā bhikkhunā kata’’nti…pe… duppaṭikārataṃ āpajjissatīti maññamānāpi evamāhaṃsu.

Etadavocāti appatirūpaṃ mayā kataṃ, bhagavā pana mahantepi aguṇe alaggitvā mayhaṃ accayaṃ paṭiggaṇhissatīti maññamāno etaṃ ‘‘accayo maṃ, bhante,’’tiādivacanaṃ avoca. Tattha accayoti aparādho. Maṃ accagamāti maṃ atikkamma abhibhavitvā pavatto. Paṭiggaṇhātūti khamatu. Āyatiṃ saṃvarāyāti anāgate saṃvaraṇatthāya, puna evarūpassa aparādhassa dosassa khalitassa akaraṇatthāya. Tagghāti ekaṃsena. Samayopi kho te, bhaddālīti, bhaddāli, tayā paṭivijjhitabbayuttakaṃ ekaṃ kāraṇaṃ atthi, tampi te na paṭividdhaṃ na sallakkhitanti dasseti.

Etadavocā accayo Maṃ accagamā Paṭiggaṇhātū Āyatiṃ saṃvarāyā Tagghā Samayopi kho te, bhaddālī
commentary_english:
135. “*cīvarakammaṃ karontī*”: People gave robe-cloth (*cīvarasāṭakaṃ*) to the Blessed One (Bhagavato), and taking that, they made robes.

“*etaṃ dosaka*”: This is an opportunity, this is an offense, the reason for rejecting the training rule (*sikkhāpadaṃ*) of the Teacher (satthu), carefully bear this in mind, is the meaning.

“*dukkaratara*”: After residing for the rainy season and departing in different directions, the monks ask, "Where did you reside?” If they are told, “We resided in Jetavana,” they would ask, “Friends (āvuso), which *jātakaṃ* did the Blessed One (bhagavā) tell during this rains retreat (*antovasse*)? Which *suttantaṃ*, which training rule (*sikkhāpadaṃ*) did he enact?”

Then they will say, “He enacted the training rule (*sikkhāpadaṃ*) against eating at the wrong time (*vikālabhojana*). Bhaddāli by name was one elder (thero) who rejected it.”

Having heard that, the monks say, “Even for the Blessed One (bhagavato), the training rule (*sikkhāpadaṃ*) that he enacted was rejected, improper, without cause (*akāraṇa*)".

Thinking that this fault (doso) of yours, having become public among the great mass of people (*mahājanantare*), will fall into being difficult to remedy (*duppaṭikārataṃ āpajjissati*), they said this.

Moreover, other monks, having completed the *pavāraṇā*, will come to the Teacher's (satthu) presence.

Then you will convene the *saṃgha*, saying, “Come, friends (āvuso), be companions in appeasing my Teacher (satthāraṃ khamāpentassa)”.

There, newcomers will ask, “Friends (āvuso), what has this monk done?”

Having heard this matter, they will say, “A grave thing has been done by the monk; he will reject the Ten-Powered One (dasabalaṃ), this is improper".

Even so, thinking that this offense (aparādho) of yours, having become public among the great mass of people (*mahājanantare*), will fall into being difficult to remedy (*duppaṭikārataṃ āpajjissati*), they said this.

Or else, the Blessed One (bhagavā), having completed the *pavāraṇā*, will set out on pilgrimage (*cārikaṃ pakkamissati*), then you will convene the *saṃgha* in every place he has gone, for the sake of appeasing the Blessed One (bhagavato khamāpanatthāya).

There, the monks residing in different directions will ask, “Friends (āvuso), what has this monk done?”…pe… Thinking that it will fall into being difficult to remedy (*duppaṭikārataṃ āpajjissati*), they said this.

“*etadavocā*”: An unbefitting thing has been done by me, but the Blessed One (bhagavā), not clinging to even great faults (aguṇe), will accept my transgression (accayaṃ paṭiggaṇhissati),” thinking this, he spoke this saying beginning with, “Transgression to me, O Bhante".

There, "*accayo*" means offense (aparādho).

"*maṃ accagamā*": Having transgressed me (maṃ atikkamma), having overcome (abhibhavitvā), it has arisen (pavatto).

"*paṭiggaṇhātū*": Let him forgive (*khamatu*).

"*āyatiṃ saṃvarāyā*": For restraint (saṃvaraṇatthāya) in the future (*anāgate*), for the sake of not doing again an offense (aparādhassa) of this sort, a fault (dosassa), a transgression (khalitassa).

"*tagghā*": Decidedly (ekaṃsena).

"*samayopi kho te, bhaddālī*": Bhaddāli, there is one reason (ekaṃ kāraṇaṃ atthi) which ought to be understood (paṭivijjhitabbayuttakaṃ) by you, and that too has not been understood (na paṭividdhaṃ), has not been recognized (na sallakkhitanti), this he shows.

*etadavocā accayo maṃ accagamā paṭiggaṇhātū āyatiṃ saṃvarāyā tagghā samayopi kho te, bhaddālī*

mula_pali:
136. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, bhaddāli, idhassa bhikkhu ubhatobhāgavimutto, tamahaṃ evaṃ vadeyyaṃ – ‘ehi me tvaṃ, bhikkhu, paṅke saṅkamo hohī’ti, api nu kho so saṅkameyya vā aññena vā kāyaṃ sannāmeyya, ‘no’ti vā vadeyyā’’ti?

‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, bhaddāli, idhassa bhikkhu paññāvimutto… kāyasakkhi… diṭṭhippatto… saddhāvimutto… dhammānusārī… saddhānusārī, tamahaṃ evaṃ vadeyyaṃ – ‘ehi me tvaṃ, bhikkhu, paṅke saṅkamo hohī’ti, api nu kho so saṅkameyya vā aññena vā kāyaṃ sannāmeyya, ‘no’ti vā vadeyyā’’ti?

‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, bhaddāli, api nu tvaṃ, bhaddāli, tasmiṃ samaye ubhatobhāgavimutto vā hosi paññāvimutto vā kāyasakkhi vā diṭṭhippatto vā saddhāvimutto vā dhammānusārī vā saddhānusārī vā’’ti?

‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Nanu tvaṃ, bhaddāli, tasmiṃ samaye ritto tuccho aparaddho’’ti?

‘‘Evaṃ , bhante. Accayo maṃ, bhante, accagamā yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ, yohaṃ bhagavatā sikkhāpade paññāpiyamāne bhikkhusaṅghe sikkhaṃ samādiyamāne anussāhaṃ pavedesiṃ. Tassa me, bhante, bhagavā accayaṃ accayato paṭiggaṇhātu āyatiṃ saṃvarāyā’’ti. ‘‘Taggha tvaṃ, bhaddāli, accayo accagamā yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ mayā sikkhāpade paññāpiyamāne bhikkhusaṅghe sikkhaṃ samādiyamāne anussāhaṃ pavedesi. Yato ca kho tvaṃ, bhaddāli, accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikarosi, taṃ te mayaṃ paṭiggaṇhāma. Vuddhihesā, bhaddāli, ariyassa vinaye yo accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikaroti, āyatiṃ saṃvaraṃ āpajjati’’.
mula_english:
136. “What do you think, Bhaddāli? Suppose a *bhikkhu* here were one liberated in both ways (*ubhatobhāgavimutto*), and I told him: ‘Come, *bhikkhu*, be a plank (*saṅkamo*) for me to walk across the mud (*paṅke*)’ Would he walk across himself, or would he dispose his body (*kāyaṃ*) otherwise, or would he say ‘No’?”

“No, venerable sir (*bhante*).”

“What do you think, Bhaddāli? Suppose a *bhikkhu* here were one liberated-by-wisdom (*paññāvimutto*)… a body-witness (*kāyasakkhi*)… one attained-to-view (*diṭṭhippatto*)… one liberated-by-faith (*saddhāvimutto*)… a Dhamma-follower (*dhammānusārī*)… a faith-follower (*saddhānusārī*), and I told him: ‘Come, *bhikkhu*, be a plank (*saṅkamo*) for me to walk across the mud (*paṅke*)’ Would he walk across himself, or would he dispose his body (*kāyaṃ*) otherwise, or would he say ‘No’?”

“No, venerable sir (*bhante*).”

“What do you think, Bhaddāli? At that time, were you, Bhaddāli, liberated in both ways (*ubhatobhāgavimutto*), liberated by wisdom (*paññāvimutto*), a body-witness (*kāyasakkhi*), one attained-to-view (*diṭṭhippatto*), liberated by faith (*saddhāvimutto*), a Dhamma-follower (*dhammānusārī*), or a faith-follower (*saddhānusārī*)?”

“No, venerable sir (*bhante*).”

“So, Bhaddāli, at that time were you empty (*ritto*), vain (*tuccho*), and at fault (*aparaddho*)?”

“Yes, venerable sir (*bhante*). A transgression (*accayo*) overcame me, venerable sir, in that like a fool (*yathābālaṃ*), confused (*yathāmūḷhaṃ*) and blundering (*yathāakusalaṃ*), when a training precept (*sikkhāpade*) was being made known by the Blessed One (*bhagavatā*) in the Sangha of *bhikkhus* (*bhikkhusaṅghe*), I publicly declared my unwillingness to undertake the training (*sikkhaṃ samādiyamāne anussāhaṃ pavedesiṃ*). May the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) accept my transgression (*accayaṃ*) as a transgression (*accayato paṭiggaṇhātu*) for the sake of my restraint in the future (*āyatiṃ saṃvarāya*)!”

“Surely, Bhaddāli, a transgression (*accayo*) overcame you, in that like a fool (*yathābālaṃ*), confused (*yathāmūḷhaṃ*) and blundering (*yathāakusalaṃ*), when a training precept (*sikkhāpade*) was being made known by me in the Sangha of *bhikkhus* (*bhikkhusaṅghe*), you publicly declared your unwillingness to undertake the training (*sikkhaṃ samādiyamāne anussāhaṃ pavedesi*).

But since you, Bhaddāli, see your transgression (*accayaṃ*) as such and make amends in accordance with the Dhamma (*yathādhammaṃ paṭikarosi*), we forgive you (*taṃ te mayaṃ paṭiggaṇhāma*).

For it is growth (*vuddhihesā*) in the Noble One’s (*ariyassa*) Discipline (*vinaye*) when one sees one’s transgression (*accayaṃ*) as such and makes amends in accordance with the Dhamma (*yathādhammaṃ paṭikaroti*) by undertaking restraint for the future (*āyatiṃ saṃvaraṃ āpajjati*).”
commentary_pali:
136.Ubhatobhāgavimuttotiādīsu dhammānusārī, saddhānusārīti dve ekacittakkhaṇikā maggasamaṅgipuggalā. Ete pana sattapi ariyapuggale bhagavatāpi evaṃ āṇāpetuṃ na yuttaṃ, bhagavatā āṇatte tesampi evaṃ kātuṃ na yuttaṃ. Aṭṭhānaparikappavasena pana ariyapuggalānaṃ suvacabhāvadassanatthaṃ bhaddālittherassa ca dubbacabhāvadassanatthametaṃ vuttaṃ.

Api nu tvaṃ tasmiṃ samaye ubhatobhāgavimuttoti desanaṃ kasmā ārabhi? Bhaddālissa niggahaṇatthaṃ.
