Ayañhettha adhippāyo – bhaddāli, ime satta ariyapuggalā loke dakkhiṇeyyā mama sāsane sāmino, mayi sikkhāpadaṃ paññapente paṭibāhitabbayutte kāraṇe sati etesaṃ paṭibāhituṃ yuttaṃ. Tvaṃ pana mama sāsanato bāhirako, mayi sikkhāpadaṃ paññapente tuyhaṃ paṭibāhituṃ na yuttanti.

Api nu tvaṃ tasmiṃ samaye ubhatobhāgavimutto

Ritto tucchoti anto ariyaguṇānaṃ abhāvena rittako tucchako, issaravacane kiñci na hoti. Yathādhammaṃ paṭikarosīti yathā dhammo ṭhito, tatheva karosi, khamāpesīti vuttaṃ hoti. Taṃ te mayaṃ paṭiggaṇhāmāti taṃ tava aparādhaṃ mayaṃ khamāma. Vuḍḍhi hesā, bhaddāli, ariyassa vinayeti esā, bhaddāli, ariyassa vinaye buddhassa bhagavato sāsane vuḍḍhi nāma. Katamā? Accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikaritvā āyatiṃ saṃvarāpajjanā. Desanaṃ pana puggalādhiṭṭhānaṃ karonto ‘‘yo accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikaroti, āyatiṃ saṃvaraṃ āpajjatī’’ti āha.

Ritto tuccho Yathādhammaṃ paṭikarosī Taṃ te mayaṃ paṭiggaṇhāmā Vuḍḍhi hesā, bhaddāli, ariyassa vinaye
commentary_english:
136. In the *ubhatobhāgavimutto* etc., <pb ed="v" n="3.0109"/> *dhammānusārī*, *saddhānusārīti dve ekacittakkhaṇikā maggasamaṅgipuggalā.*
Furthermore, it is not fitting that even the Blessed One should command these seven noble individuals in this way, and it is not fitting that they should do so even when commanded by the Blessed One.
Moreover, it was said to demonstrate the ready obedience of noble individuals by way of ungrounded speculation, <pb ed="p" n="3.0152"/> and to demonstrate the disobedience of Bhaddāli the Elder.

Why did he begin the teaching, "<hi rend="bold">api nu tvaṃ tasmiṃ samaye ubhatobhāgavimutto</hi>?" It was to restrain Bhaddāli.
The meaning here is this: "Bhaddāli, these seven noble individuals are worthy of offerings in the world, masters in my dispensation. When I prescribe a training rule, it is fitting for them to reject [it] when there is a justified reason for rejecting it.
But you are external to my dispensation, so it is not fitting for you to reject [it] when I prescribe a training rule for you."

<hi rend="bold">api nu tvaṃ tasmiṃ samaye ubhatobhāgavimutto</hi> <hi rend="bold">ritto tuccho</hi> means empty because of the absence of noble qualities; he is empty and hollow. There is nothing in the word of a lord.
<hi rend="bold">yathādhammaṃ paṭikarosī</hi> means as the Dharma is established, so you do, you ask for forgiveness.
<hi rend="bold">taṃ te mayaṃ paṭiggaṇhāmā</hi> means we forgive that offense of yours.
<hi rend="bold">vuḍḍhi hesā, bhaddāli, ariyassa vinaye</hi> means this, Bhaddāli, is growth in the discipline of the noble ones, in the dispensation of the Buddha, the Blessed One.
What is it? Seeing a transgression as a transgression, making amends according to the Dharma, and achieving restraint in the future.
When giving a teaching based on individuals, he said, "Whoever sees a transgression as a transgression, makes amends according to the Dharma, and achieves restraint in the future."

<hi rend="bold">ritto tuccho</hi> <hi rend="bold">yathādhammaṃ paṭikarosī</hi> <hi rend="bold">taṃ te mayaṃ paṭiggaṇhāmā</hi> <hi rend="bold">vuḍḍhi hesā, bhaddāli, ariyassa vinaye</hi>

mula_pali: 137. ‘‘Idha, bhaddāli, ekacco bhikkhu satthusāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārī hoti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajeyyaṃ araññaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ susānaṃ vanapatthaṃ abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ. Appeva nāmāhaṃ uttari uttariṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ sacchikareyya’nti. So vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati araññaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ susānaṃ vanapatthaṃ abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ. Tassa tathāvūpakaṭṭhassa viharato satthāpi upavadati, anuviccapi viññū sabrahmacārī upavadanti, devatāpi upavadanti, attāpi attānaṃ upavadati. So satthārāpi upavadito, anuviccapi viññūhi sabrahmacārīhi upavadito, devatāhipi upavadito, attanāpi attānaṃ upavadito na uttari manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ sacchikaroti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhi taṃ, bhaddāli, hoti yathā taṃ satthusāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārissa.
mula_english:
“Here, Bhaddali, some *bhikṣu* does not fulfil the training in the Teacher’s Dispensation (satthusāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārī hoti).

He considers thus: ‘Suppose I were to resort to a secluded resting place (*vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ*): the forest (*araññaṃ*), the root of a tree (*rukkhamūlaṃ*), a mountain (*pabbataṃ*), a ravine (*kandaraṃ*), a hillside cave (*giriguhaṃ*), a charnel ground (*susānaṃ*), a jungle thicket (*vanapatthaṃ*), an open space (*abbhokāsaṃ*), a heap of straw (*palālapuñjaṃ*). Perhaps I might realise a superhuman state (*uttari manussadhammā*), a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones (*alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ sacchikareyya*.’

He resorts to a secluded lodging (*vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati*): the forest (*araññaṃ*), the foot of a tree (*rukkhamūlaṃ*), a mountain (*pabbataṃ*), a ravine (*kandaraṃ*), a hillside cave (*giriguhaṃ*), a charnel ground (*susānaṃ*), a jungle highland (*vanapatthaṃ*), the open air (*abbhokāsaṃ*), a heap of straw (*palālapuñjaṃ*).

While he lives thus withdrawn, the Teacher (*satthā*) censures him (*upavadati*), wise companions in the holy life (*viññū sabrahmacārī*) who have made investigation censure him, gods (*devatā*) censure him, and he censures himself (*attāpi attānaṃ upavadati*).

Being censured in this way by the Teacher (*satthārāpi upavadito*), by wise companions in the holy life (*viññūhi sabrahmacārīhi upavadito*), by gods (*devatāhipi upavadito*), and by himself (*attanāpi attānaṃ upavadito*) he realises no superhuman state (*uttari manussadhammā*), no distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones (*alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ sacchikaroti*).

Why [is that]? That is how it is with one who does not fulfil the training in the Teacher’s Dispensation (*satthusāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārissa*).
commentary_pali: 137.Satthāpiupavadatīti ‘‘asukavihāravāsī asukassa therassa saddhivihāriko asukassa antevāsiko itthannāmo nāma bhikkhu lokuttaradhammaṃ nibbattetuṃ araññaṃ paviṭṭho’’ti sutvā – ‘‘kiṃ tassa araññavāsena, yo mayhaṃ pana sāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārī’’ti evaṃ upavadati, sesapadesupi eseva nayo, apicettha devatā na kevalaṃ upavadanti, bheravārammaṇaṃ dassetvā palāyanākārampi karonti. Attanāpi attānanti sīlaṃ āvajjantassa saṃkiliṭṭhaṭṭhānaṃ pākaṭaṃ hoti, cittaṃ vidhāvati, na kammaṭṭhānaṃ allīyati. So ‘‘kiṃ mādisassa araññavāsenā’’ti vippaṭisārī uṭṭhāya pakkamati. Attāpi attānaṃ upavaditoti attanāpi attā upavadito, ayameva vā pāṭho. Sukkapakkho vuttapaccanīkanayena veditabbo. Sovivicceva kāmehītiādi evaṃ sacchikarotīti dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ.
commentary_english:
137. *Satthāpi upavadatī* means, upon hearing that "a certain monk named so-and-so, a resident of such-and-such monastery, a fellow resident of such-and-such elder, a disciple of such-and-such, has entered the forest to achieve supramundane dharma," [one] thus disparages, "What is the use of his forest dwelling, since he is not fulfilling the training in my dispensation?" This is the method in the remaining instances as well. Furthermore, here the deities not only disparage but also, showing frightening objects, make [him] act as if fleeing.

*Attanāpi attāna* means, for one who reflects on morality, a defiled condition becomes evident, the mind runs wild, and it does not adhere to the meditation subject.

He, being remorseful, rises up and departs, [thinking,] "What is the use of forest dwelling for someone like me?"

*Attāpi attānaṃ upavadito* means, the self is disparaged by oneself; or this itself is the reading.

The bright side should be understood in the opposite way.

*So vivicceva kāmehī* etc., is said to show that he thus realizes it.

mula_pali: 138. ‘‘Idha pana, bhaddāli, ekacco bhikkhu satthusāsane sikkhāya paripūrakārī hoti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajeyyaṃ araññaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ susānaṃ vanapatthaṃ abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ. Appeva nāmāhaṃ uttari manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ sacchikareyya’nti. So vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati araññaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ susānaṃ vanapatthaṃ abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ. Tassa tathāvūpakaṭṭhassa viharato satthāpi na upavadati, anuviccapi viññū sabrahmacārī na upavadanti, devatāpi na upavadanti, attāpi attānaṃ na upavadati. So satthārāpi anupavadito , anuviccapi viññūhi sabrahmacārīhi anupavadito, devatāhipi anupavadito, attanāpi attānaṃ anupavadito uttari manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ sacchikaroti. So vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhi taṃ, bhaddāli, hoti yathā taṃ satthusāsane sikkhāya paripūrakārissa.
mula_english:
138. Here, Bhaddāli, some *bhikkhu* (monk) fulfills the training in the Teacher's Dispensation (*satthusāsane sikkhāya paripūrakārī hoti*).

He considers thus: ‘Suppose I were to resort to a secluded dwelling (*vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajeyyaṃ*): the forest (*araññaṃ*), the root of a tree (*rukkhamūlaṃ*), a mountain (*pabbataṃ*), a ravine (*kandaraṃ*), a mountain cave (*giriguhaṃ*), a charnel ground (*susānaṃ*), a jungle thicket (*vanapatthaṃ*), an open space (*abbhokāsaṃ*), a heap of straw (*palālapuñjaṃ*). Perhaps I might realize a superhuman state (*uttari manussadhammā*), a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones (*alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ sacchikareyya*)’.

He resorts to a secluded dwelling: the forest, the root of a tree, a mountain, a ravine, a mountain cave, a charnel ground, a jungle thicket, an open space, a heap of straw.

While he lives thus withdrawn, the Teacher does not censure him, wise companions in the holy life (*viññū sabrahmacārī*) who have made investigation do not censure him, gods (*devatāpi*) do not censure him, and he does not censure himself (*attāpi attānaṃ na upavadati*).

Being uncensured in this way by the Teacher, by wise companions in the holy life, by gods, and by himself, he realizes a superhuman state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones.

Quite secluded from sensual pleasures (*kāmehi vivicca*), secluded from unwholesome states (*akusalehi dhammehi vivicca*), with applied and sustained thought (*savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ*), he enters and abides in the first *jhāna*: rapture and pleasure born of seclusion (*vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati*).

What is the cause for that? That is how it is, Bhaddāli, with one who fulfills the training in the Teacher’s Dispensation.

mula_pali:
139. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhaddāli, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhi taṃ, bhaddāli, hoti yathā taṃ satthusāsane sikkhāya paripūrakārissa.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhaddāli, bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati, sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhi taṃ, bhaddāli, hoti yathā taṃ satthusāsane sikkhāya paripūrakārissa.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhaddāli, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhi taṃ, bhaddāli, hoti yathā taṃ satthusāsane sikkhāya paripūrakārissa.

‘‘So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti. So anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhi taṃ, bhaddāli, hoti yathā taṃ satthusāsane sikkhāya paripūrakārissa.

‘‘So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte sattānaṃ cutūpapātañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti. So dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti – ‘ime vata bhonto sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā…pe… vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannā; ime vā pana bhonto sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā…pe… sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā’ti iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena…pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhi taṃ, bhaddāli, hoti yathā taṃ satthusāsane sikkhāya paripūrakārissa.

‘‘So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti. So ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti; ‘ime āsavā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ āsavasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ āsavanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, bhavāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, avijjāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhi taṃ, bhaddāli, hoti yathā taṃ satthusāsane sikkhāya paripūrakārissā’’ti.
mula_english:
139. “Again, Bhaddāli, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought, a monk enters upon and abides in the second *jhāna*, which has self-confidence and singleness of mind without applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of concentration.
If you ask why, Bhaddāli, that is how it is with one who fulfils the training in the Teacher’s Dispensation.

“Again, Bhaddāli, with the fading away of rapture, he dwells equanimous, mindful and clearly aware, and experiences pleasure with the body; he enters and dwells in the third *jhāna*, about which the noble ones declare: “Equanimous, mindful, [he] dwells in pleasure.”
If you ask why, Bhaddāli, that is how it is with one who fulfils the training in the Teacher’s Dispensation.

“Again, Bhaddāli, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, a monk enters upon and abides in the fourth *jhāna*, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and purity of mindfulness due to equanimity.
If you ask why, Bhaddāli, that is how it is with one who fulfils the training in the Teacher’s Dispensation.

“When his concentrated mind is thus purified and bright, unblemished, rid of imperfection, malleable, wieldy, steady, and attained to imperturbability, he directs it to knowledge of the recollection of past lives.
He recollects his manifold past lives, that is, one birth, two births… Thus with their aspects and particulars he recollects his manifold past lives.
If you ask why, Bhaddāli, that is how it is with one who fulfils the training in the Teacher’s Dispensation.

“When his concentrated mind is thus purified and bright, unblemished, rid of imperfection, malleable, wieldy, steady, and attained to imperturbability, he directs it to knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings.
With the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate. He understands how beings pass on according to their actions thus: ‘These worthy beings who were ill-conducted in body…[and] have reappeared in a state of deprivation, in a bad destination, in the nether world, in hell; these other worthy beings who were well-conducted in body…[and] have reappeared in a good destination, in a heavenly world.’ Thus with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human…he understands how beings pass on according to their actions.
If you ask why, Bhaddāli, that is how it is with one who fulfils the training in the Teacher’s Dispensation.

“When his mind is thus concentrated, purified, cleansed, unblemished, rid of defilement, malleable, wieldy, steady, and attained to imperturbability, he directs it to the knowledge of the destruction of the taints.
He understands as it really is: ‘This is suffering.’ He understands as it really is: ‘This is the origin of suffering.’ He understands as it really is: ‘This is the cessation of suffering.’ He understands as it really is: ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering.’ He undarstands as it really is: ‘These are the taints.’ He understands as it really is: ‘This is the origin of the taints.’ He understands as it really is: ‘This is the cessation of the taints.’ He understands as it really is: ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of the taints.’
When he knows and sees thus, his mind is liberated from the taint of sensual desire, from the taint of existence, and from the taint of ignorance.
When it is liberated there comes the knowledge: ‘It is liberated.’ He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the spiritual life has been lived, what had tobe done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’
If you ask why, Bhaddāli, that is how it is with one who fulfills the training in the Teacher’s Dispensation.”

mula_pali: 140. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā bhaddāli bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena midhekaccaṃ bhikkhuṃ pasayha pasayha pavayha pavayha (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) kāraṇaṃ karonti? Ko pana, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena midhekaccaṃ bhikkhuṃ no tathā pasayha pasayha kāraṇaṃ karontī’’ti? ‘‘Idha, bhaddāli, ekacco bhikkhu abhiṇhāpattiko hoti āpattibahulo. So bhikkhūhi vuccamāno aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmeti, kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti, na sammā vattati, na lomaṃ pāteti, na netthāraṃ vattati, ‘yena saṅgho attamano hoti taṃ karomī’ti nāha. Tatra, bhaddāli, bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu abhiṇhāpattiko āpattibahulo. So bhikkhūhi vuccamāno aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmeti, kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti, na sammā vattati, na lomaṃ pāteti, na netthāraṃ vattati, ‘yena saṅgho attamano hoti taṃ karomī’ti nāha. Sādhu vatāyasmanto imassa bhikkhuno tathā tathā upaparikkhatha yathāssidaṃ yathayidaṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.) adhikaraṇaṃ na khippameva vūpasameyyāti. Tassa kho evaṃ, bhaddāli, bhikkhuno bhikkhū tathā tathā upaparikkhanti yathāssidaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ na khippameva vūpasammati.
mula_english:
140. When this was said, the venerable Bhaddāli said this to the Blessed One: “What, venerable sir, is the cause (hetu), what is the reason (paccaya), why they take action against some *bhikkhu* here by repeatedly admonishing him? And what, venerable sir, is the cause (hetu), what is the reason (paccaya), why they do not repeatedly take action against some *bhikkhu* here by admonishing him?”

“Here, Bhaddāli, a certain *bhikkhu* is frequently transgressing and is full of offences (*abhiṇhāpattiko hoti āpattibahulo*). When he is corrected by the *bhikkhus*, he prevaricates, leads the talk aside, shows disturbance, hate, and bitterness; he does not proceed rightly, he does not comply, he does not clear himself, he does not say: ‘Let me so act that the *saṃgha* will be satisfied.’ There, Bhaddāli, the *bhikkhus* think thus: ‘This venerable *bhikkhu* is frequently transgressing and is full of offences. When he is corrected by the *bhikkhus*, he prevaricates, leads the talk aside, shows disturbance, hate, and bitterness; he does not proceed rightly, he does not comply, he does not clear himself, he does not say: “Let me so act that the *saṃgha* will be satisfied.”’

“It would be good if the venerable ones examine this *bhikkhu* in such a way that this litigation (*adhikaraṇaṃ*) against him is not settled too quickly. And the *bhikkhus* examine that *bhikkhu* in such a way that the litigation (*adhikaraṇaṃ*) against him is not settled too quickly.
commentary_pali:
140.Pasayha pasayha kāraṇaṃ karontīti appamattakepi dose niggahetvā punappunaṃ kārenti. No tathāti mahantepi aparādhe yathā itaraṃ, evaṃ pasayha na kārenti. So kira, ‘‘āvuso, bhaddāli, mā cintayittha, evarūpaṃ nāma hoti, ehi satthāraṃ khamāpehī’’ti bhikkhusaṅghatopi, kañci bhikkhuṃ pesetvā attano santikaṃ pakkosāpetvā, ‘‘bhaddāli, mā cintayittha, evarūpaṃ nāma hotī’’ti evaṃ satthusantikāpi anuggahaṃ paccāsīsati. Tato ‘‘bhikkhusaṅghenāpi na samassāsito, satthārāpī’’ti cintetvā evamāha.

Atha bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghopi satthāpi ovaditabbayuttameva ovadati, na itaranti dassetuṃ idha, bhaddāli, ekaccotiādimāha. Tattha aññenāññantiādīni anumānasutte vitthāritāni. Na sammā vattatīti sammā vattampi na vattati. Na lomaṃ pātetīti anulomavatte na vattati, vilomameva gaṇhāti. Na nitthāraṃ vattatīti nitthāraṇakavattamhi na vattati, āpattivuṭṭhānatthaṃ turitaturito chandajāto na hoti. Tatrāti tasmiṃ tassa dubbacakaraṇe. Abhiṇhāpattikoti nirantarāpattiko. Āpattibahuloti sāpattikakālovassa bahu, suddho nirāpattikakālo appoti attho. Na khippameva vūpasammatīti khippaṃ na vūpasammati, dīghasuttaṃ hoti. Vinayadharā pādadhovanakāle āgataṃ ‘‘gacchāvuso, vattavelā’’ti vadanti. Puna kālaṃ maññitvā āgataṃ ‘‘gacchāvuso, tuyhaṃ vihāravelā, gacchāvuso, sāmaṇerādīnaṃ uddesadānavelā, amhākaṃ nhānavelā, therūpaṭṭhānavelā, mukhadhovanavelā’’tiādīni vatvā divasabhāgepi rattibhāgepi āgataṃ uyyojentiyeva. ‘‘Kāya velāya, bhante, okāso bhavissatī’’ti vuttepi ‘‘gacchāvuso, tvaṃ imameva ṭhānaṃ jānāsi, asuko nāma vinayadharatthero sinehapānaṃ pivati, asuko virecanaṃ kāreti, kasmā turitosī’’tiādīni vatvā dīghasuttameva karonti.

idha, bhaddāli, ekacco aññenāñña Na sammā vattatī Na lomaṃ pātetī Na nitthāraṃ vattatī Tatrā Abhiṇhāpattiko Āpattibahulo Na khippameva vūpasammatī
commentary_english:
140. “*pasayha pasayha kāraṇaṃ karontī*ti” means that they make [someone] do [something] again and again, having rebuked even a minor fault.

“*no tathā*ti” means that they do not compel [someone] in that way even in a major offense like other offenses.

It seems that he anticipates compassion from the Teacher's presence, thinking, "Friend Bhaddāli, do not worry, it is like this," sending a monk from the monastic community, summoning some monk to his presence, and saying, "Friend Bhaddāli, do not worry, it is like this."

Then, thinking, "I have not been consoled even by the monastic community, nor by the Teacher," he says this:

Then, to show that the Blessed One, the monastic community, and the Teacher only advise what is proper to advise, he says, "*idha, bhaddāli, ekacco*," and so on.

There, "*aññenāñña*," and so on, are explained in detail in the *anumāna-sutta*.

"*na sammā vattatī*ti" means that he does not behave properly; he does not even behave with *sammā vattampi*.

"*na lomaṃ pātetī*ti" means that he does not behave according to *anuloma-vatta*; he only grasps the opposite (*vilomameva gaṇhāti*).

"*na nitthāraṃ vattatī*ti" means that he does not behave in *nitthāraṇa-kavatta*; he is not quickly inclined (*turitaturito chandajāto na hoti*) for the sake of rising from an offense (*āpattivuṭṭhāna*).

"*tatrā*ti" means in that act of making it difficult to speak (*tasmiṃ tassa dubbacakaraṇe*).

"*abhiṇhāpattiko*ti" means one who constantly commits offenses (*nirantarāpattiko*).

"*āpattibahulo*ti" means that the time of being in offense (*sāpattikakālo*) is much, and the time of being pure and free from offense (*suddho nirāpattikakālo*) is little; this is the meaning (*attho*).

"*na khippameva vūpasammatī*ti" means that it does not quickly subside (*khippaṃ na vūpasammati*); it is a lengthy matter (*dīghasuttaṃ hoti*).

The Vinaya-holders, when [someone] comes at the time of washing the feet, say, "Go, friend, it is time for service (*vattavelā*)."

Again, thinking it is time, when [someone] comes, they say things like, "Go, friend, it is your time for dwelling (*vihāravelā*); go, friend, it is the time for the novices and others to receive instruction (*uddesadānavelā*); it is our time for bathing (*nhānavelā*), the time for attending to the elders (*therūpaṭṭhānavelā*), the time for washing the face (*mukhadhovanavelā*)," and they send [him] away whether [he] comes during the day or during the night.

Even when it is said, "Venerable sir, when will there be an opportunity (*okāso bhavissatī*)?" they say, "Go, friend, you know only this place; so-and-so is a Vinaya-holder elder who is drinking oil (*sinehapānaṃ pivati*), so-and-so is having a purgative administered (*virecanaṃ kāreti*); why are you in a hurry (*kasmā turitosī*)?" and they make it a lengthy matter (*dīghasuttameva karonti*).

*idha, bhaddāli, ekacco* *aññenāñña* *na sammā vattatī* *na lomaṃ pātetī* *na nitthāraṃ vattatī* *tatrā* *abhiṇhāpattiko* *āpattibahulo* *na khippameva vūpasammatī*

mula_pali: 141. ‘‘Idha pana, bhaddāli, ekacco bhikkhu abhiṇhāpattiko hoti āpattibahulo. So bhikkhūhi vuccamāno nāññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, bahiddhā kathaṃ na apanāmeti, na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti, sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, ‘yena saṅgho attamano hoti taṃ karomī’ti āha. Tatra, bhaddāli, bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu abhiṇhāpattiko āpattibahulo. So bhikkhūhi vuccamāno nāññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, bahiddhā kathaṃ na apanāmeti, na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti, sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, ‘yena saṅgho attamano hoti taṃ karomī’ti āha. Sādhu vatāyasmanto, imassa bhikkhuno tathā tathā upaparikkhatha yathāssidaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ khippameva vūpasameyyāti. Tassa kho evaṃ, bhaddāli, bhikkhuno bhikkhū tathā tathā upaparikkhanti yathāssidaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ khippameva vūpasammati.
mula_english:
“But here, Bhaddāli, some *bhikkhu* is a constant offender (*abhiṇhāpattika*) with many offenses (*āpattibahula*).

When he is corrected by the *bhikkhus*, he does not prevaricate, lead the talk aside, or show disturbance, hate, and bitterness; he proceeds rightly, he complies, he clears himself, he says: ‘Let me so act that the *Saṃgha* will be satisfied.’

In this case, Bhaddāli, *bhikkhus* consider thus: ‘Friends, this *bhikkhu* is a constant offender (*abhiṇhāpattika*) with many offenses (*āpattibahula*).

When he is corrected by the *bhikkhus*, he does not prevaricate, lead the talk aside, or show disturbance, hate, and bitterness; he proceeds rightly, he complies, he clears himself, he says: ‘Let me so act that the *Saṃgha* will be satisfied.’

‘It would be good if the venerable ones examine this *bhikkhu* in such a way that this litigation (*adhikaraṇa*) against him is settled quickly.’

And the *bhikkhus* examine that *bhikkhu*, Bhaddāli, in such a way that the litigation (*adhikaraṇa*) against him is settled quickly.
commentary_pali: 141.Khippameva vūpasammatīti lahuṃ vūpasammati, na dīghasuttaṃ hoti. Ussukkāpannā bhikkhū – ‘‘āvuso, ayaṃ subbaco bhikkhu, janapadavāsino nāma gāmantasenāsane vasanaṭṭhānanisajjanādīni na phāsukāni honti, bhikkhācāropi dukkho hoti, sīghamassa adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamemā’’ti sannipatitvā āpattito vuṭṭhāpetvā suddhante patiṭṭhāpenti.
commentary_english:
141. *khippam eva vūpasammati*—it quickly subsides; *lahum vūpasammati*, it subsides swiftly, it is not a lengthy matter.

Monks who are eager and ready [think]: "Friends, this monk is easy to speak to. For those who dwell in the country, dwelling in village outskirts, lodging places, sitting places, and so on are not comfortable. Also, the alms round is difficult. Let us quickly settle this matter." Having assembled, they raise him from the offense and establish him in purity.

mula_pali: 142. ‘‘Idha, bhaddāli, ekacco bhikkhu adhiccāpattiko hoti anāpattibahulo. So bhikkhūhi vuccamāno aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmeti, kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti, na sammā vattati, na lomaṃ pāteti, na netthāraṃ vattati, ‘yena saṅgho attamano hoti taṃ karomī’ti nāha. Tatra, bhaddāli, bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu adhiccāpattiko anāpattibahulo . So bhikkhūhi vuccamāno aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmeti, kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti, na sammā vattati, na lomaṃ pāteti, na netthāraṃ vattati, ‘yena saṅgho attamano hoti taṃ karomī’ti nāha. Sādhu vatāyasmanto, imassa bhikkhuno tathā tathā upaparikkhatha yathāssidaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ na khippameva vūpasameyyāti. Tassa kho evaṃ, bhaddāli, bhikkhuno bhikkhū tathā tathā upaparikkhanti yathāssidaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ na khippameva vūpasammati.
mula_english:
“Here, Bhaddāli, some *bhikkhu* is a chance offender without many offences.

When he is corrected by the *bhikkhus*, he prevaricates, leads the talk aside, shows disturbance, hate, and bitterness; he does not proceed rightly, he does not comply, he does not clear himself, he does not say: ‘Let me so act that the *saṃgha* will be satisfied.’

There, Bhaddāli, the *bhikkhus* think thus: ‘This *bhikkhu*, reverend sir, is a chance offender without many offences.’

When he is corrected by the *bhikkhus*, he prevaricates, leads the talk aside, shows disturbance, hate, and bitterness; he does not proceed rightly, he does not comply, he does not clear himself, he does not say: ‘Let me so act that the *saṃgha* will be satisfied.’

‘It would be good if the venerable ones examine this *bhikkhu* in such a way that this litigation against him is settled quickly.’

For that *bhikkhu*, Bhaddāli, the *bhikkhus* examine in such a way that this litigation against him is not settled quickly.
commentary_pali: 142.Adhiccāpattikoti kadāci kadāci āpattiṃ āpajjati. So kiñcāpi lajjī hoti pakatatto, dubbacattā panassa bhikkhū tatheva paṭipajjanti.
commentary_english: 142. adhiccāpattikoti: Sometimes, sometimes he commits an offense. Although he is ashamed and of natural character, because of his being difficult to admonish, the monks treat him just the same.

mula_pali: 143. ‘‘Idha pana, bhaddāli, ekacco bhikkhu adhiccāpattiko hoti anāpattibahulo. So bhikkhūhi vuccamāno nāññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, na bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmeti, na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti, sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, ‘yena saṅgho attamano hoti taṃ karomī’ti āha. Tatra, bhaddāli, bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu adhiccāpattiko anāpattibahulo. So bhikkhūhi vuccamāno nāññenaññaṃ paṭicarati, na bahiddhā kathaṃ apanāmeti, na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti, sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, ‘yena saṅgho attamano hoti taṃ karomī’ti āha. Sādhu vatāyasmanto, imassa bhikkhuno tathā tathā upaparikkhatha yathāssidaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ khippameva vūpasameyyāti. Tassa kho evaṃ, bhaddāli, bhikkhuno bhikkhū tathā tathā upaparikkhanti yathāssidaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ khippameva vūpasammati.
mula_english:
“But here, Bhaddāli, some *bhikkhu* is a chance offender without many offenses. When he is corrected by the *bhikkhus*, he does not prevaricate, lead the talk aside, or show disturbance, hate, and bitterness; he proceeds rightly, he complies, he clears himself, he says: ‘Let me so act that the *Saṅgha* will be satisfied.’

In this case, Bhaddāli, *bhikkhus* consider thus: ‘Friends, this *bhikkhu* is a chance offender without many offenses.’ When he is corrected by the *bhikkhus*, he does not prevaricate, lead the talk aside, or show disturbance, hate, and bitterness; he proceeds rightly, he complies, he clears himself, he says: ‘Let me so act that the *Saṅgha* will be satisfied.’

‘It would be good if the venerable ones examine this *bhikkhu* in such a way that this litigation (*adhikaraṇa*) against him is settled quickly.’

And the *bhikkhus* examine that *bhikkhu* in such a way that the litigation (*adhikaraṇa*) against him is settled quickly.

mula_pali: 144. ‘‘Idha , bhaddāli, ekacco bhikkhu saddhāmattakena vahati pemamattakena. Tatra, bhaddāli, bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – ‘ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saddhāmattakena vahati pemamattakena. Sace mayaṃ imaṃ bhikkhuṃ pasayha pasayha kāraṇaṃ karissāma – mā yampissa taṃ saddhāmattakaṃ pemamattakaṃ tamhāpi parihāyī’ti. Seyyathāpi, bhaddāli, purisassa ekaṃ cakkhuṃ, tassa mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā taṃ ekaṃ cakkhuṃ rakkheyyuṃ – ‘mā yampissa taṃ ekaṃ cakkhuṃ tamhāpi parihāyī’ti; evameva kho, bhaddāli, idhekacco bhikkhu saddhāmattakena vahati pemamattakena. Tatra, bhaddāli, bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – ‘ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saddhāmattakena vahati pemamattakena. Sace mayaṃ imaṃ bhikkhuṃ pasayha pasayha kāraṇaṃ karissāma – mā yampissa taṃ saddhāmattakaṃ pemamattakaṃ tamhāpi parihāyī’ti. Ayaṃ kho, bhaddāli, hetu ayaṃ paccayo yena midhekaccaṃ bhikkhuṃ pasayha pasayha kāraṇaṃ karonti. Ayaṃ pana, bhaddāli, hetu ayaṃ paccayo, yena midhekaccaṃ bhikkhuṃ no tathā pasayha pasayha kāraṇaṃ karontī’’ti.
mula_english:
144.
"Here, Bhaddāli, some *bhikkhu* progresses by a measure of faith (*śraddhā*) and love (*prema*).

In this case, Bhaddāli, *bhikkhus* consider thus: 'Friends, this *bhikkhu* progresses by a measure of faith (*śraddhā*) and love (*prema*).

If we take action against this *bhikkhu* by repeatedly admonishing him, let him not lose that measure of faith (*śraddhā*) and love (*prema*), as he may.'

Suppose a man had only one eye; then his friends and companions, his kinsmen and relatives, would guard his eye, thinking: 'Let him not lose his one eye.' So too, some *bhikkhu* progresses by a measure of faith (*śraddhā*) and love (*prema*).

In this case, Bhaddāli, *bhikkhus* consider thus: 'Friends, this *bhikkhu* progresses by a measure of faith (*śraddhā*) and love (*prema*).

If we take action against this *bhikkhu* by repeatedly admonishing him, let him not lose that measure of faith (*śraddhā*) and love (*prema*), as he may.'

This is the cause, Bhaddāli, this is the reason, why they take action against some *bhikkhu* here by repeatedly admonishing him.

This, however, Bhaddāli, is the cause, this is the reason, why they do not take such action against some *bhikkhu* here by repeatedly admonishing him."
commentary_pali: 144.Saddhāmattakena vahati pemamattakenāti ācariyupajjhāyesu appamattikāya gehassitasaddhāya appamattakena gehassitapemena yāpeti. Paṭisandhiggahaṇasadisā hi ayaṃ pabbajjā nāma, navapabbajito pabbajjāya guṇaṃ ajānanto ācariyupajjhāyesu pemamattena yāpeti, tasmā evarūpā saṅgaṇhitabbā. Appamattakampi hi saṅgahaṃ labhitvā pabbajjāya ṭhitā abhiññāpattā mahāsamaṇā bhavissanti. Ettakena kathāmaggena ‘‘ovaditabbayuttakaṃ ovadanti, na itara’’nti imameva bhagavatā dassitaṃ.
commentary_english:
"Because he maintains himself with only a little faith (saddhā) and only a little affection (pema)," means that he lives with his teachers and preceptors with only a small amount of faith associated with household life, and with only a small amount of affection associated with household life.

For this going forth (pabbajjā) is similar to taking rebirth (paṭisandhiggahaṇa). A newly gone forth one (navapabbajito), not knowing the qualities of going forth, lives with his teachers and preceptors with only affection. Therefore, such ones should be taken care of (saṅgaṇhitabbā).

For even those established in going forth, having obtained only a little care, will become great ascetics (mahāsamaṇā) who have attained higher knowledge (abhiññāpattā).

With this much line of talk, the Blessed One (Bhagavat) has shown just this: “They advise those who are fit to be advised; they do not advise others.”

mula_pali: 145. ‘‘‘Ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena pubbe appatarāni ceva sikkhāpadāni ahesuṃ bahutarā ca bhikkhū aññāya saṇṭhahiṃsu? Ko pana, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena etarahi bahutarāni ceva sikkhāpadāni honti appatarā ca bhikkhū aññāya saṇṭhahantī’ti? ‘‘Evametaṃ, bhaddāli, hoti sattesu hāyamānesu, saddhamme antaradhāyamāne, bahutarāni ceva sikkhāpadāni honti appatarā ca bhikkhū aññāya saṇṭhahantīti. Na tāva, bhaddāli, satthā sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññāpeti yāva na idhekacce āsavaṭṭhānīyā dhammā saṅghe pātubhavanti. Yato ca kho, bhaddāli, idhekacce āsavaṭṭhānīyā dhammā saṅghe pātubhavanti, atha satthā sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññāpeti tesaṃyeva āsavaṭṭhānīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ paṭighātāya. Na tāva, bhaddāli, idhekacce āsavaṭṭhānīyā dhammā saṅghe pātubhavanti yāva na saṅgho mahattaṃ patto hoti. Yato ca kho, bhaddāli, saṅgho mahattaṃ patto hoti, atha idhekacce āsavaṭṭhānīyā dhammā saṅghe pātubhavanti. Atha satthā sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññāpeti tesaṃyeva āsavaṭṭhānīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ paṭighātāya. Na tāva, bhaddāli, idhekacce āsavaṭṭhānīyā dhammā saṅghe pātubhavanti yāva na saṅgho lābhaggaṃ patto hoti, yasaggaṃ patto hoti, bāhusaccaṃ patto hoti, rattaññutaṃ patto hoti. Yato ca kho, bhaddāli, saṅgho rattaññutaṃ patto hoti, atha idhekacce āsavaṭṭhānīyā dhammā saṅghe pātubhavanti, atha satthā sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññāpeti tesaṃyeva āsavaṭṭhānīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ paṭighātāya.
mula_english:
145. “What is the cause, what is the reason, venerable sir, why in the past there were fewer training rules and more monks became established in final knowledge? And what is the cause, venerable sir, what is the reason, why at the present time there are more training rules and fewer monks become established in final knowledge?”

“It is because beings are declining, Bhaddāli, and the true Dharma is disappearing that there are more training rules and fewer monks become established in final knowledge. The Teacher does not make known the training rule for disciples until certain things that are the basis for taints (*āsavaṭṭhānīyā dhammā*) become manifest here in the *Saṅgha*; but when certain things that are the basis for taints become manifest here in the *Saṅgha*, then the Teacher makes known the training rule for disciples in order to ward off those things that are the basis for taints.

“Those things that are the basis for taints do not become manifest here in the *Saṅgha* until the *Saṅgha* has reached greatness; but when the *Saṅgha* has reached greatness, then those things that are the basis for taints become manifest here in the *Saṅgha*, and then the Teacher makes known the training rule for disciples in order to ward off those things that are the basis for taints.

“Those things that are the basis for taints do not become manifest here in the *Saṅgha* until the *Saṅgha* has reached the acme of worldly gain, the acme of fame, the acme of great learning, the acme of long-standing renown; but when the *Saṅgha* has reached the acme of long-standing renown, then those things that are the basis for taints become manifest here in the *Saṅgha*, and then the Teacher makes known the training rule for disciples in order to ward off those things that are the basis for taints.
commentary_pali:
145.Aññāyasaṇṭhahiṃsūti arahatte patiṭṭhahiṃsu. Sattesu hāyamānesūti paṭipattiyā hāyamānāya sattā hāyanti nāma. Saddhamme antaradhāyamāneti paṭipattisaddhamme antaradhāyamāne. Paṭipattisaddhammopi hi paṭipattipūrakesu sattesu asati antaradhāyati nāma . Āsavaṭṭhānīyāti āsavā tiṭṭhanti etesūti āsavaṭṭhānīyā. Yesu diṭṭhadhammikasamparāyikā parūpavādavippaṭisāravadhabandhanādayo ceva apāyadukkhavisesabhūtā ca āsavā tiṭṭhantiyeva. Yasmā nesaṃ te kāraṇaṃ hontīti attho. Te āsavaṭṭhānīyā vītikkamadhammā yāva na saṅghe pātubhavanti, na tāva satthā sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññapetīti ayamettha yojanā.

Evaṃ akālaṃ dassetvā puna kālaṃ dassetuṃ yato ca kho, bhaddālītiādimāha. Tattha yatoti yadā, yasmiṃ kāleti vuttaṃ hoti. Sesaṃ vuttānusāreneva veditabbaṃ. Ayaṃ vā ettha saṅkhepattho – yasmiṃ kāle āsavaṭṭhānīyā dhammāti saṅkhaṃ gatā vītikkamadosā saṅghe pātubhavanti, tadā satthā sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññapeti. Kasmā? Tesaṃyeva āsavaṭṭhānīyadhammasaṅkhātānaṃ vītikkamadosānaṃ paṭighātāya.

yato ca kho, bhaddālī yato

Evaṃ āsavaṭṭhānīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppattiṃ sikkhāpadapaññattiyā akālaṃ, uppattiñca kālanti vatvā idāni tesaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppattikālañca uppattikālañca dassetuṃ ‘‘na tāva, bhaddāli, idhekacce’’tiādimāha. Tattha mahattanti mahantabhāvaṃ. Saṅgho hi yāva na theranavamajjhimānaṃ vasena mahattaṃ patto hoti, tāva senāsanāni pahonti, sāsane ekacce āsavaṭṭhānīyā dhammā na uppajjanti. Mahattaṃ patte pana te uppajjanti, atha satthā sikkhāpadaṃ paññapeti. Tattha mahattaṃ patte saṅghe paññattasikkhāpadāni –

‘‘na tāva, bhaddāli, idhekacce’’ mahatta

‘‘Yo pana bhikkhu anupasampannena uttaridvirattatirattaṃ sahaseyyaṃ kappeyya pācittiyaṃ (pāci. 51). Yā pana bhikkhunī anuvassaṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya pācittiyaṃ (pāci. 1171). Yā pana bhikkhunī ekavassaṃ dve vuṭṭhāpeyya pācittiya’’nti (pāci. 1175).

Iminā nayena veditabbāni.

Lābhagganti lābhassa aggaṃ. Saṅgho hi yāva na lābhaggapatto hoti, na tāva lābhaṃ paṭicca āsavaṭṭhānīyā dhammā uppajjanti. Patte pana uppajjanti, atha satthā sikkhāpadaṃ paññapeti –

Lābhagga

‘‘Yo pana bhikkhu acelakassa vā paribbājakassa vā paribbājikāya vā sahatthā khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā dadeyya pācittiya’’nti (pāci. 270).

Idañhi lābhaggapatte saṅghe sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ.

Yasagganti yasassa aggaṃ. Saṅgho hi yāva na yasaggapatto hoti, na tāva yasaṃ paṭicca āsavaṭṭhānīyā dhammā uppajjanti. Patte pana uppajjanti, atha satthā sikkhāpadaṃ paññapeti ‘‘surāmerayapāne pācittiya’’nti (pāci. 327). Idañhi yasaggapatte saṅghe sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ.

Yasagga

Bāhusaccanti bahussutabhāvaṃ. Saṅgho hi yāva na bāhusaccapatto hoti, na tāva āsavaṭṭhānīyā dhammā uppajjanti. Bāhusaccapatte pana yasmā ekaṃ nikāyaṃ dve nikāye pañcapi nikāye uggahetvā ayoniso ummujjamānā puggalā rasena rasaṃ saṃsandetvā uddhammaṃ ubbinayaṃ satthu sāsanaṃ dīpenti, atha satthā – ‘‘yo pana bhikkhu evaṃ vadeyya tathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi (pāci. 418)…pe… samaṇuddesopi ce evaṃ vadeyyā’’tiādinā (pāci. 429) nayena sikkhāpadaṃ paññapeti.

Bāhusacca

Rattaññutaṃ pattoti ettha rattiyo jānantīti rattaññū. Attano pabbajitadivasato paṭṭhāya bahū rattiyo jānanti, cirapabbajitāti vuttaṃ hoti. Rattaññūnaṃ bhāvaṃ rattaññutaṃ. Tatra rattaññutaṃ patte saṅghe upasenaṃ vaṅgantaputtaṃ ārabbha sikkhāpadaṃ paññattanti veditabbaṃ. So hāyasmā ūnadasavasse bhikkhū upasampādente disvā ekavasso saddhivihārikaṃ upasampādesi. Atha bhagavā sikkhāpadaṃ paññapesi – ‘‘na, bhikkhave, ūnadasavassena upasampādetabbo, yo upasampādeyya āpatti dukkaṭassā’’ti (mahāva. 75). Evaṃ paññatte sikkhāpade puna bhikkhū ‘‘dasavassamhā dasavassamhā’’ti bālā abyattā upasampādenti. Atha bhagavā aparampi sikkhāpadaṃ paññapesi – ‘‘na, bhikkhave, bālena abyattena upasampādetabbo, yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena dasavassena vā atirekadasavassena vā upasampādetu’’nti. Iti rattaññutaṃ pattakāle dve sikkhāpadāni paññattāni.

Rattaññutaṃ patto
commentary_english:
145. Having known, *saṇṭhahiṃsū* means they were established in arhatship.

When beings are declining, *sattesu hāyamānesū* means that beings decline when the practice declines.

When the good Dharma is disappearing, *saddhamme antaradhāyamāne* means when the practice's good Dharma is disappearing.

Indeed, the good Dharma of practice also disappears when beings who fulfill the practice are not present.

*Āsavā tiṭṭhanti etesūti āsavaṭṭhānīyā* means that defilements abide in these, therefore they are the places where defilements abide (āsavaṭṭhānīyā).

In which the defilements (āsava) such as visible-dharma-related and future-life-related, the censure of others, remorse, killing, imprisonment, etc., and the specific painful states of deprivation exist.

Because those are their causes, this is the meaning.

Those transgression-dharmas related to the places where defilements abide (āsavaṭṭhānīyā) do not appear in the Saṅgha, so the Teacher does not prescribe the training rule (śikṣāpada) for the disciples; this is the connection here.

Thus, having shown what is untimely, he again says, in order to show what is timely, "When indeed, Bhaddālī..."

There, *yato* means when, it is said to be "at what time."

The remainder should be understood according to what has been said.

Or, this is the concise meaning here: when transgression-faults, called defilement-abiding dharmas, appear in the Saṅgha, then the Teacher prescribes the training rule (śikṣāpada) for the disciples.

Why? It is for the prevention of those very transgression-faults which are enumerated as defilement-abiding dharmas.

When indeed, Bhaddālī... When... Thus, having stated that the non-arising of the defilement-abiding dharmas is untimely for the prescription of the training rule (śikṣāpada), and that their arising is timely, now, in order to show both the time of the non-arising and the time of the arising of those dharmas, he says, "Not so, Bhaddālī, in this case..."

There, *mahatta* means greatness.

Indeed, as long as the Saṅgha has not attained greatness by way of elders, novices, and those in the middle, the dwelling places suffice, and some defilement-abiding dharmas do not arise in the teaching.

But when it has attained greatness, then they arise, and then the Teacher prescribes the training rule (śikṣāpada).

There, these are the prescribed training rules (śikṣāpada) in the Saṅgha which has attained greatness:

"Not so, Bhaddālī, in this case..." Greatness... "If any monk should sleep together with a person who is not fully ordained for more than two or three nights, he commits an offense entailing confession (pācittiya)" (Pācittiya 51).

"If any nun should give full admission every year, she commits an offense entailing confession (pācittiya)" (Pācittiya 1171).

"If any nun should give the full admission to two women in one year, she commits an offense entailing confession (pācittiya)" (Pācittiya 1175).

These should be understood in this way.

*Lābhagga* means the height of gain (lābha).

Indeed, as long as the Saṅgha has not reached the height of gain (lābhagga), defilement-abiding dharmas do not arise in dependence on gain.

But when it has reached [the height of gain], then they arise, and then the Teacher prescribes the training rule (śikṣāpada):

Gain (lābha)... "If any monk should personally give fresh or cooked food to a naked ascetic, to a male wanderer, or to a female wanderer, he commits an offense entailing confession" (Pācittiya 270).

This training rule (śikṣāpada) was prescribed in the Saṅgha which had reached the height of gain (lābhagga).

*Yasagga* means the height of fame (yasa).

Indeed, as long as the Saṅgha has not reached the height of fame (yasagga), defilement-abiding dharmas do not arise in dependence on fame.
But when the circumstances arise, the Teacher laid down the training rule: "It is a *pācittiya* for drinking intoxicants" (Pāci. 327).

This was the laying down of a training rule in the Saṅgha when Yasagga was the instigator.

*Bāhusacca* means being very learned. Because, as long as the Saṅgha has not attained vast learning, then things that are the basis for taints do not arise. But when the Saṅgha has attained vast learning, since individuals, having taken up one school, two schools, or even five schools, and surfacing unwisely, mixing flavor with flavor, illuminating what is not the Dhamma and what is not the Discipline, [and thus] displaying the Teacher’s dispensation, then the Teacher lays down a training rule in this way: "Whatever monk should speak thus: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One…’ (Pāci. 418)…pe… even a novice should speak thus” (Pāci. 429).

Herein, *rattaññutaṃ patto* means: those who know the nights are *rattaññū*. Beginning from the day of their going forth, they know many nights; it is said that they have gone forth for a long time. *Rattaññutaṃ* is the state of those who are *rattaññū*.

Here, it should be understood that a training rule was laid down concerning Upasena Vaṅgantaputta in the Saṅgha that had attained seniority. That venerable one, seeing monks conferring the Going Forth on those who were less than ten years [senior], conferred the Going Forth on a co-resident who was one year [senior]. Then the Blessed One laid down a training rule: “Monks, one who is less than ten years [senior] should not be given the Going Forth. Whoever should confer it incurs an offense of wrong-doing” (Mahāva. 75). Even when this training rule had been laid down, inexperienced and incompetent monks were still conferring the Going Forth, [saying,] “I have ten rains; I have ten rains.” Then the Blessed One laid down another training rule: “Monks, an inexperienced and incompetent person should not be given the Going Forth. Whoever should confer it incurs an offense of wrong-doing. I allow a competent and capable monk who has ten or more years of seniority to give the Going Forth.”

Thus, two training rules were laid down at the time when seniority had been attained.

mula_pali:
146. ‘‘Appakā kho tumhe, bhaddāli, tena samayena ahuvattha yadā vo ahaṃ ājānīyasusūpamaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ desesiṃ. Taṃ sarasi sarasi tvaṃ (sī. pī.), sarasi taṃ (?) bhaddālī’’ti ?

‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Tatra, bhaddāli, kaṃ hetuṃ paccesī’’ti?

‘‘So hi nūnāhaṃ, bhante, dīgharattaṃ satthusāsane sikkhāya aparipūrakārī ahosi’’nti.

‘‘Na kho, bhaddāli, eseva hetu, esa paccayo. Api ca me tvaṃ, bhaddāli, dīgharattaṃ cetasā cetoparicca vidito – ‘na cāyaṃ moghapuriso mayā dhamme desiyamāne aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetaso sabbaṃ cetaso (ka.) samannāharitvā ohitasoto dhammaṃ suṇātī’ti. Api ca te ahaṃ, bhaddāli, ājānīyasusūpamaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ desessāmi. Taṃ suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi ; bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā bhaddāli bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –

sabbaṃ cetaso (ka.)
mula_english:
146. “There were few of you, Bhaddāli, at that time when I taught the *Dhamma* (Law, teaching, doctrine) through the simile of the young thoroughbred colt.

You remember that, Bhaddāli?”

“Certainly not, venerable sir.”

“Then, Bhaddāli, what reason do you see in this?”

“Because, venerable sir, for a long time I have not fulfilled the training in the Teacher’s instruction.”

“That is not the only cause, Bhaddāli, that is not the only reason. But rather, by encompassing your mind with my mind, I have long known you thus: ‘When I am teaching the *Dhamma*, this misguided man does not heed it, does not give it attention, does not engage it with all his mind, does not hear the *Dhamma* with eager ears.’ Still, Bhaddāli, I will teach you the *Dhamma* through the simile of the young thoroughbred colt. Listen & pay close attention; I will speak.”

“Yes, venerable sir,” the venerable Bhaddāli replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this:
commentary_pali: 146.Ājānīyasusūpamaṃdhammapariyāyaṃ desesinti taruṇājānīyaupamaṃ katvā dhammaṃ desayiṃ. Tatrāti tasmiṃ asaraṇe. Na kho, bhaddāli, eseva hetūti na esa sikkhāya aparipūrakārībhāvoyeva eko hetu.
commentary_english:
146.
ājānīyasusūpamaṃ
dhammapariyāyaṃ desesi nti taruṇājānīyaupamaṃ katvā dhammaṃ desayiṃ.
tatrāti tasmiṃ asaraṇe.
na kho, bhaddāli, eseva hetūti na esa sikkhāya aparipūrakārībhāvoyeva eko hetu.

mula_pali:
147. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhaddāli, dakkho assadamako bhadraṃ assājānīyaṃ labhitvā paṭhameneva mukhādhāne kāraṇaṃ kāreti. Tassa mukhādhāne kāraṇaṃ kāriyamānassa hontiyeva visūkāyitāni visevitāni vipphanditāni kānici kānici, yathā taṃ akāritapubbaṃ kāraṇaṃ kāriyamānassa. So abhiṇhakāraṇā anupubbakāraṇā tasmiṃ ṭhāne parinibbāyati. Yato kho, bhaddāli, bhadro assājānīyo abhiṇhakāraṇā anupubbakāraṇā tasmiṃ ṭhāne parinibbuto hoti, tamenaṃ assadamako uttari kāraṇaṃ kāreti yugādhāne. Tassa yugādhāne kāraṇaṃ kāriyamānassa hontiyeva visūkāyitāni visevitāni vipphanditāni kānici kānici, yathā taṃ akāritapubbaṃ kāraṇaṃ kāriyamānassa. So abhiṇhakāraṇā anupubbakāraṇā tasmiṃ ṭhāne parinibbāyati . Yato kho, bhaddāli, bhadro assājānīyo abhiṇhakāraṇā anupubbakāraṇā tasmiṃ ṭhāne parinibbuto hoti, tamenaṃ assadamako uttari kāraṇaṃ kāreti anukkame maṇḍale khurakāse khurakāye (sī. pī.) dhāve davatte ravatthe (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) rājaguṇe rājavaṃse uttame jave uttame haye uttame sākhalye. Tassa uttame jave uttame haye uttame sākhalye kāraṇaṃ kāriyamānassa hontiyeva visūkāyitāni visevitāni vipphanditāni kānici kānici, yathā taṃ akāritapubbaṃ kāraṇaṃ kāriyamānassa. So abhiṇhakāraṇā anupubbakāraṇā tasmiṃ ṭhāne parinibbāyati. Yato kho, bhaddāli, bhadro assājānīyo abhiṇhakāraṇā anupubbakāraṇā tasmiṃ ṭhāne parinibbuto hoti, tamenaṃ assadamako uttari vaṇṇiyañca pāṇiyañca valiyañca (sī. pī.), baliyañca (syā. kaṃ.) anuppavecchati. Imehi kho, bhaddāli, dasahaṅgehi samannāgato bhadro assājānīyo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo rañño aṅganteva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati.

‘‘Evameva kho, bhaddāli, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassa. Katamehi dasahi? Idha, bhaddāli, bhikkhu asekhāya sammādiṭṭhiyā samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāsaṅkappena samannāgato hoti, asekhāya sammāvācāya samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammākammantena samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāājīvena samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāvāyāmena samannāgato hoti , asekhāya sammāsatiyā samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāsamādhinā samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāñāṇena samannāgato hoti, asekhāya sammāvimuttiyā samannāgato hoti – imehi kho, bhaddāli, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā bhaddāli bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Bhaddālisuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.
mula_english:
147. “Bhaddāli, suppose a clever horse-trainer obtains a fine thoroughbred colt. He first makes him get used to wearing the bit.

While the colt is being made to get used to wearing the bit, because he is doing something that he has never done before, he displays some contortion, writhing, and vacillation.

But through constant repetition and gradual practice, he becomes peaceful in those actions.

“When the colt has become peaceful in that action, the horse trainer further makes him get used to wearing the harness (yugādhāne).

While the colt is being made to get used to wearing the harness, because he is doing something that he has never done before, he displays some contortion, writhing, and vacillation.

But through constant repetition and gradual practice, he becomes peaceful in those actions.

“When the colt has become peaceful in that action, the horse trainer further makes him act in keeping in step (anukkame), in running in a circle (maṇḍale), in prancing (khurakāse), in galloping (dhāve), in charging (davatte), in the kingly qualities (rājaguṇe), in the kingly heritage (rājavaṃse), in the highest speed (uttame jave), in the highest fleetness (uttame haye), in the highest gentleness (uttame sākhalye).

While the colt is being made to get used to doing these things, because he is doing something that he has never done before, he displays some contortion, writhing, and vacillation.

But through constant repetition and gradual practice, he becomes peaceful in those actions.

“When the colt has become peaceful in these actions, the horse-trainer further rewards him with a rubbing down (vaṇṇiyañca) and a grooming (pāṇiyañca).

When a fine thoroughbred colt possesses these ten factors (dasahaṅgehi), he is worthy of the king (rājāraho), in the king’s service (rājabhoggo), and considered one of the factors of a king.

“So too, Bhaddāli, when a bhikkhu possesses ten qualities (dasahi dhammehi), he is worthy of gifts (āhuneyyo), worthy of hospitality (pāhuneyyo), worthy of offerings (dakkhiṇeyyo), worthy of reverential salutation (añjalikaraṇīyo), an unsurpassed field of merit (anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ) for the world (lokassa).

Which are the ten? Here, Bhaddali, a *bhikkhu* possesses the right view of one beyond training (asekhāya sammādiṭṭhiyā), the right intention of one beyond training (asekhena sammāsaṅkappena), the right speech of one beyond training (asekhāya sammāvācāya), the right action of one beyond training (asekhena sammākammantena), the right livelihood of one beyond training (asekhena sammāājīvena), the right effort of one beyond training (asekhena sammāvāyāmena), the right mindfulness of one beyond training (asekhāya sammāsatiyā), the right concentration of one beyond training (asekhena sammāsamādhinā), the right knowledge of one beyond training (asekhena sammāñāṇena), and the right deliverance of one beyond training (asekhāya sammāvimuttiyā). When a *bhikkhu* possesses these ten qualities, he is worthy of gifts, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, an unsurpassed field of merit for the world.”

Thus spoke the Lord.

The venerable Bhaddali was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

The Bhaddāli Sutta, the fifth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
147.Mukhādhāne kāraṇaṃ kāretīti khalīnabandhādīhi mukhaṭṭhapane sādhukaṃ gīvaṃ paggaṇhāpetuṃ kāraṇaṃ kāreti. Visūkāyitānītiādīhi visevanācāraṃ kathesi. Sabbāneva hetāni aññamaññavevacanāni. Tasmiṃ ṭhāneti tasmiṃ visevanācāre. Parinibbāyatīti nibbisevano hoti, taṃ visevanaṃ jahatīti attho. Yugādhāneti yugaṭṭhapane yugassa sādhukaṃ gahaṇatthaṃ.

Anukkameti cattāropi pāde ekappahāreneva ukkhipane ca nikkhipane ca. Parasenāya hi āvāṭe ṭhatvā asiṃ gahetvā āgacchantassa assassa pāde chindanti. Tasmiṃ samaye esa ekappahāreneva cattāropi pāde ukkhipissatīti rajjubandhanavidhānena etaṃ kāraṇaṃ karonti. Maṇḍaleti yathā asse nisinnoyeva bhūmiyaṃ patitaṃ āvudhaṃ gahetuṃ sakkoti, evaṃ karaṇatthaṃ maṇḍale kāraṇaṃ kāreti. Khurakāseti aggaggakhurehi pathavīkamane. Rattiṃ okkantakaraṇasmiñhi yathā padasaddo na suyyati, tadatthaṃ ekasmiṃ ṭhāne saññaṃ datvā aggaggakhurehiyeva gamanaṃ sikkhāpenti. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Javeti sīghavāhane. ‘‘Dhāve’’tipi pāṭho. Attano parājaye sati palāyanatthaṃ, paraṃ palāyantaṃ anubandhitvā gahaṇatthañca etaṃ kāraṇaṃ kāreti. Davatteti davattāya, yuddhakālasmiñhi hatthīsu vā koñcanādaṃ karontesu assesu vā hasantesu rathesu vā nighosantesu yodhesu vā ukkuṭṭhiṃ karontesu tassa ravassa abhāyitvā parasenapavesanatthaṃ ayaṃ kāraṇā karīyati.

Anukkame Maṇḍale Khurakāse Jave Davatte

Rājaguṇeti raññā jānitabbaguṇe. Kūṭakaṇṇarañño kira guḷavaṇṇo nāma asso ahosi. Rājā pācīnadvārena nikkhamitvā cetiyapabbataṃ gamissāmīti kalambanadītīraṃ sampatto. Asso tīre ṭhatvā udakaṃ otarituṃ na icchati, rājā assācariyaṃ āmantetvā – ‘‘aho tayā asso sikkhāpito udakaṃ otarituṃ na icchatī’’ti āha. Ācariyo – ‘‘susikkhāpito deva asso, evamassa hi cittaṃ ‘sacāhaṃ udakaṃ otarissāmi, vālaṃ temissati, vāle tinte rañño aṅge udakaṃ pāteyyā’ti evaṃ tumhākaṃ sarīre udakapātanabhayena na otarati, vālaṃ gaṇhāpethā’’ti āha. Rājā tathā kāresi. Asso vegena otaritvā pāraṃ gato. Etadatthaṃ ayaṃ kāraṇā karīyati. Rājavaṃseti assarājavaṃse. Vaṃso ceso assarājānaṃ, tathārūpena pahārena chinnabhinnasarīrāpi assārohaṃ parasenāya apātetvā bahi nīharantiyeva. Etadatthaṃ kāraṇaṃ kāretīti attho.

Rājaguṇe Rājavaṃse

Uttame javeti javasampattiyaṃ, yathā uttamajavo hoti, evaṃ kāraṇaṃ kāretīti attho. Uttame hayeti uttamahayabhāve, yathā uttamahayo hoti, evaṃ kāraṇaṃ kāretīti attho. Tattha pakatiyā uttamahayova uttamahayakāraṇaṃ arahati, na añño. Uttamahayakāraṇāya eva ca hayo uttamajavaṃ paṭipajjati, na aññoti.

Uttame jave Uttame haye

Tatridaṃ vatthu – eko kira rājā ekaṃ sindhavapotakaṃ labhitvā sindhavabhāvaṃ ajānitvāva imaṃ sikkhāpehīti ācariyassa adāsi. Ācariyopi tassa sindhavabhāvaṃ ajānanto taṃ māsakhādakaghoṭakānaṃ kāraṇāsu upaneti. So attano ananucchavikattā kāraṇaṃ na paṭipajjati. So taṃ dametuṃ asakkonto ‘‘kūṭasso ayaṃ mahārājā’’ti vissajjāpesi.

Athekadivasaṃ eko assācariyapubbako daharo upajjhāyassa bhaṇḍakaṃ gahetvā gacchanto taṃ parikhāpiṭṭhe carantaṃ disvā – ‘‘anaggho, bhante, sindhavapotako’’ti upajjhāyassa kathesi. Sace rājā jāneyya, maṅgalassaṃ naṃ kareyyāti. Thero āha – ‘‘micchādiṭṭhiko, tāta, rājā appeva nāma buddhasāsane pasīdeyya rañño kathehī’’ti. So gantvā, – ‘‘mahārāja, anaggho sindhavapotako atthī’’ti kathesi. Tayā diṭṭho , tātāti? Āma, mahārājāti. Kiṃ laddhuṃ vaṭṭatīti? Tumhākaṃ bhuñjanakasuvaṇṇathāle tumhākaṃ bhuñjanakabhattaṃ tumhākaṃ pivanakaraso tumhākaṃ gandhā tumhākaṃ mālāti. Rājā sabbaṃ dāpesi. Daharo gāhāpetvā agamāsi.

Asso gandhaṃ ghāyitvāva ‘‘mayhaṃ guṇajānanakaācariyo atthi maññe’’ti sīsaṃ ukkhipitvā olokento aṭṭhāsi. Daharo gantvā ‘‘bhattaṃ bhuñjā’’ti accharaṃ pahari. Asso āgantvā suvaṇṇathāle bhattaṃ bhuñji, rasaṃ pivi. Atha naṃ gandhehi vilimpitvā rājapiḷandhanaṃ piḷandhitvā ‘‘purato purato gacchā’’ti accharaṃ pahari. So daharassa purato purato gantvā maṅgalassaṭṭhāne aṭṭhāsi. Daharo – ‘‘ayaṃ te, mahārāja, anaggho sindhavapotako, imināva naṃ niyāmena katipāhaṃ paṭijaggāpehī’’ti vatvā nikkhami.

Atha katipāhassa accayena āgantvā assassa ānubhāvaṃ passissasi, mahārājāti. Sādhu ācariya kuhiṃ ṭhatvā passāmāti? Uyyānaṃ gaccha, mahārājāti. Rājā assaṃ gāhāpetvā agamāsi. Daharo accharaṃ paharitvā ‘‘etaṃ rukkhaṃ anupariyāhī’’ti assassa saññaṃ adāsi. Asso pakkhanditvā rukkhaṃ anuparigantvā āgato. Rājā neva gacchantaṃ na āgacchantaṃ addasa. Diṭṭho te, mahārājāti? Na diṭṭho, tātāti. Valañjakadaṇḍaṃ etaṃ rukkhaṃ nissāya ṭhapethāti vatvā accharaṃ pahari ‘‘valañjakadaṇḍaṃ gahetvā ehī’’ti. Asso pakkhanditvā mukhena gahetvā āgato. Diṭṭhaṃ, mahārājāti. Diṭṭhaṃ, tātāti.

Puna accharaṃ pahari ‘‘uyyānassa pākāramatthakena caritvā ehī’’ti. Asso tathā akāsi. Diṭṭho, mahārājāti. Na diṭṭho, tātāti. Rattakambalaṃ āharāpetvā assassa pāde bandhāpetvā tatheva saññaṃ adāsi. Asso ullaṅghitvā pākāramatthakena anupariyāyi. Balavatā purisena āviñchanaalātaggisikhā viya uyyānapākāramatthake paññāyittha. Asso gantvā samīpe ṭhito. Diṭṭhaṃ, mahārājāti. Diṭṭhaṃ, tātāti. Maṅgalapokkharaṇipākāramatthake anupariyāhīti saññaṃ adāsi.

Puna ‘‘pokkharaṇiṃ otaritvā padumapattesu cārikaṃ carāhī’’ti saññaṃ adāsi. Pokkharaṇiṃ otaritvā sabbapadumapatte caritvā agamāsi, ekaṃ pattampi anakkantaṃ vā phālitaṃ vā chinditaṃ vā khaṇḍitaṃ vā nāhosi. Diṭṭhaṃ, mahārājāti. Diṭṭhaṃ, tātāti. Accharaṃ paharitvā taṃ hatthatalaṃ upanāmesi. Dhātūpatthaddho laṅghitvā hatthatale aṭṭhāsi. Diṭṭhaṃ, mahārājāti? Diṭṭhaṃ, tātāti. Evaṃ uttamahayo eva uttamakāraṇāya uttamajavaṃ paṭipajjati.

Uttame sākhalyeti muduvācāya. Muduvācāya hi, ‘‘tāta, tvaṃ mā cintayi, rañño maṅgalasso bhavissasi, rājabhojanādīni labhissasī’’ti uttamahayakāraṇaṃ kāretabbo. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘uttame sākhalye’’ti. Rājabhoggoti rañño upabhogo. Rañño aṅganteva saṅkhaṃ gacchatīti yattha katthaci gacchantena hatthaṃ viya pādaṃ viya anohāyeva gantabbaṃ hoti. Tasmā aṅganti saṅkhaṃ gacchati, catūsu vā senaṅgesu ekaṃ aṅgaṃ hoti.

Uttame sākhalye Rājabhoggo Rañño aṅganteva saṅkhaṃ gacchatī

Asekhāya sammādiṭṭhiyāti arahattaphalasammādiṭṭhiyā. Sammāsaṅkappādayopi taṃsampayuttāva. Sammāñāṇaṃ pubbe vuttasammādiṭṭhiyeva. Ṭhapetvā pana aṭṭha phalaṅgāni sesā dhammā vimuttīti veditabbā. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānameva. Ayaṃ pana desanā ugghaṭitaññūpuggalassa vasena arahattanikūṭaṃ gahetvā niṭṭhāpitāti.

Asekhāya sammādiṭṭhiyā Sammāñāṇaṃ vimuttī

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Bhaddālisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
147. " *Mukhādhāne kāraṇaṃ kāretī*": namely, with the *khalīna* bridle, etc., he makes [the horse] hold its mouth well, and causes it to raise its neck properly.
"*Visūkāyitānī*": namely, he related the *visevana* conduct, and so on.
All these reasons are synonymous with each other.
"*Tasmiṃ ṭhāne*": namely, in that *visevana* conduct.
"*Parinibbāyatī*": namely, one becomes without *visevana*; that is, abandoning that *visevana*.
"*Yugādhāne*": namely, in placing the yoke, for the proper grasping of the yoke.

Following the sequence, with a single strike, all four feet are raised and lowered.
Indeed, for the enemy army, standing in a pit, taking a sword, they cut the feet of the approaching horse.
At that time, this one, with a single strike, will lift all four feet; thus, with the method of binding the rope, they perform this cause.
"*Maṇḍale*": namely, just as the horse, remaining seated, is able to take the weapon that has fallen on the ground; thus, to do so, he makes the cause in the circle.
"*Khurakāse*": namely, the earth movement with the tips of the hooves.
At night, indeed, when the sound of footsteps is not heard in the *okkanta* practice, therefore, giving a signal in one place, they teach movement only with the tips of the hooves.
This was said with reference to that.
"*Jave*": namely, in swift vehicles.
"It should run": this is also a reading.
When there is defeat for oneself, for the purpose of fleeing, and having pursued the fleeing enemy, for the purpose of capturing him, he makes this cause.
"*Davatte*": namely, for the sake of *davatta*; indeed, in the time of war, when elephants are making the sound of *koñca*, or when horses are neighing, or when chariots are rumbling, or when warriors are shouting, not being afraid of that sound, this reason is made for the purpose of entering the enemy's army.

Following the sequence, in the circle, the hoof-mark, in speed, in *davatta*.
"*Rājaguṇe*": namely, qualities to be known by the king.
It is said that there was a horse named *Guḷavaṇṇa* belonging to the king *Kūṭakaṇṇa*.
The king, having departed through the eastern gate, having reached the bank of the *Kalambanadī* River, [thought] "I will go to *Cetiyapabbata*."
The horse, standing on the bank, does not wish to cross the water; the king, having called the horse-trainer, said: "Alas, this horse you have trained does not wish to cross the water."
The trainer said: "O King, the horse has been well trained; indeed, this is its thought: 'If I cross the water, the tail will get wet, and when the tail is wet, water will fall on the king's limbs.' Thus, it does not cross out of fear of water falling on your body. Let it grasp the tail!"
The king did so.
The horse, having crossed swiftly, went to the other side.
For this purpose, this cause is made.
"*Rājavaṃse*": namely, in the lineage of royal horses.
That lineage certainly causes the royal horse, even with a body torn and broken by a strike of that form, without making the horseman fall into the enemy's army, to lead him out.
For this purpose, he makes this reason.

In the king's qualities, in speed, "*Uttame jave*": namely, in the attainment of speed, just as there is supreme speed, so he makes that cause.
"*Uttame haye*": namely, in the state of being an excellent horse, just as there is an excellent horse, so he makes that reason.
There, by nature, only an excellent horse deserves the cause of an excellent horse, not another.
And indeed, it is for the sake of an excellent horse that a horse acquires excellent speed, not another.

**Excellent Speed, Excellent Horse**

There is a story about this: It is said that a king obtained a Sindh thoroughbred foal and, not knowing its Sindh nature, gave it to a teacher, saying, "Train this one!"

The teacher, also not knowing its Sindh nature, placed it among the causes of horses that eat monthly rations.

Due to its being unsuitable for that, it did not take to the cause.

Unable to tame it, he dismissed it, saying, "This king is a cheat!"

Then one day, a young man who had previously been a horse-trainer, while going with his teacher's bag, saw it wandering near the moat and said to the teacher, "Venerable sir, this is a priceless Sindh thoroughbred foal!"

"If the king knew, he would make it a ceremonial horse."

The Elder said, "The king, foolish in his views, might not be pleased with the Buddha's teachings. Tell the king."

So he went and said, "Great King, there is a priceless Sindh thoroughbred foal!"

"Have you seen it, young man?" "Yes, Great King."

"What is it worthy of receiving?" "Your golden plate for eating, your meal for eating, your juice for drinking, your perfumes, your garlands!"

The king had everything given.

The young man took them and left.

The horse, smelling the scents, stood looking around, raising its head, thinking, "I think there is a teacher who knows my qualities."

The young man went and uttered the phrase, "Eat the rice!"

The horse came and ate the rice from the golden plate, drank the juice.

Then, after anointing it with perfumes and dressing it in royal ornaments, he uttered the phrase, "Go forward, forward!"

It went forward, forward of the young man, and stood in the place of the ceremonial horse.

The young man said, "This, Great King, is your priceless Sindh thoroughbred foal. Have it cared for for a few days by this very method." And he left.

After a few days, you will come and see the horse's power, Great King.

"Good, teacher, where shall we stand and watch?" "Go to the park, Great King."

The king had the horse brought and went.

The young man uttered the phrase and gave the horse the sign, "Go around this tree!"

The horse leaped and, having gone around the tree, came back.

The king did not see it going or coming.

"Have you seen it, Great King?" "I have not seen it, young man."

Saying, "Place this walking stick leaning against this tree," he uttered the phrase, "Take the walking stick and come!"

The horse leaped and came, taking it in its mouth.

"Have you seen it, Great King?"

"I have seen it, young man!"

Again, he uttered the phrase, "Go, walking on the top of the park wall!"

The horse did so.

"Have you seen it, Great King?"
He was not seen, father.
Having brought a red blanket, having bound it on the horse's feet, he gave the signal just so.
The horse, having leaped over, went around the top of the wall.
Like a firebrand whirled around by a strong man, it appeared on top of the garden wall.
The horse went and stood nearby.
"It is seen, great king."
"It is seen, father."
He gave the signal, "Go around the top of the auspicious lotus pond wall."

Again, he gave the signal, "Having descended into the lotus pond, wander about on the lotus leaves."
Having descended into the lotus pond, having wandered about on all the lotus leaves, it went away; not even one leaf was trodden on, or split, or cut, or broken.
"It is seen, great king."
"It is seen, father."
Having struck the letter, he presented it on the palm of his hand.
Supported by relics, having leapt, he stood on the palm of his hand.
"It is seen, great king?" "It is seen, father."
Thus, a supreme horse attains supreme speed for a supreme reason.

"<hi rend="bold">In supreme health</hi>" means with gentle speech.
Indeed, with gentle speech, "Dear father, do not worry, you will be the king's auspicious horse; you will obtain the king's food, etc.," a cause for a supreme horse should be made.
Therefore, it was said, "In supreme health."
"<hi rend="bold">Royal enjoyment</hi>" means the king's enjoyment.
"<hi rend="bold">He goes to the count as if he were a limb of the king</hi>" means that wherever he goes, one should go without indifference, like a hand or a foot.
Therefore, a limb goes to the count; one limb is among the four divisions of the army.

<hi rend="bold">In supreme health</hi> <hi rend="bold">Royal enjoyment</hi> <hi rend="bold">He goes to the count as if he were a limb of the king</hi> "<hi rend="bold">By the non- обучения right view</hi>" means by the right view of the fruit of arahantship.
Right thought and the others are connected with that.
<hi rend="bold">Right knowledge</hi> is just the previously mentioned right view.
Having set aside eight, the remaining things, the *dharmas*, are to be understood as <hi rend="bold">liberation</hi>.
The rest is clear throughout.
However, this teaching, taking the arahantship-shortcut by way of the person who understands quickly, is finished.

<hi rend="bold">By the non- обучение right view</hi> <hi rend="bold">Right knowledge</hi> <hi rend="bold">Liberation</hi> The commentary on the Bhaddāli Sutta is finished.

mula_pali: 148. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā aṅguttarāpesu viharati āpaṇaṃ nāma aṅguttarāpānaṃ nigamo. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya āpaṇaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Āpaṇe piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yenaññataro vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāya. Taṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ ajjhogāhetvā aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi. Āyasmāpi kho udāyī pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya āpaṇaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Āpaṇe piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena so vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāya. Taṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ ajjhogāhetvā aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi. Atha kho āyasmato udāyissa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘‘bahūnaṃ bahunnaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) evamīdise aviññāṇakappakaraṇe vata no bhagavā dukkhadhammānaṃ apahattā, bahūnaṃ vata no bhagavā sukhadhammānaṃ upahattā; bahūnaṃ vata no bhagavā akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ apahattā, bahūnaṃ vata no bhagavā kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upahattā’’ti. Atha kho āyasmā udāyī sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi .
mula_english:
148. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was living in the country of the Aṅguttarāpas at a town of theirs named Āpaṇa, a market town of the Aṅguttarāpas.

Then, when it was morning, the Blessed One dressed, and taking his bowl and outer robe, went into Āpaṇa for alms.

When he had wandered for alms in Āpaṇa and had returned from his almsround, after his meal he went to a certain grove (vanasaṇḍa) for the day’s abiding (divāvihāra).

Having entered that grove (vanasaṇḍa), he sat down at the root of a tree for the day’s abiding (divāvihāraṃ nisīdi).

The venerable Udayin also, when it was morning, dressed, and taking his bowl and outer robe, went into Āpaṇa for alms.

When he had wandered for alms in Āpaṇa and had returned from his almsround, after his meal he went to that same grove (vanasaṇḍa) for the day’s abiding (divāvihāra).

Having entered that grove (vanasaṇḍa), he sat down at the root of a tree for the day’s abiding (divāvihāraṃ nisīdi).

Then, while the venerable Udayin was alone in meditation, the following thought arose in his mind: “How many painful states ( *dukkha-dhammā* ) has the Blessed One rid us of! How many pleasant states ( *sukha-dhammā* ) has the Blessed One brought us! How many unwholesome states ( *akusala-dhammā* ) has the Blessed One rid us of! How many wholesome states ( *kusala-dhammā* ) has the Blessed One brought us!”

Then, when it was evening, the venerable Udayin rose from meditation, went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side.
commentary_pali: 148.Evaṃme sutanti laṭukikopamasuttaṃ. Tattha yena so vanasaṇḍoti ayampi mahāudāyitthero bhagavatā saddhiṃyeva piṇḍāya pavisitvā saddhiṃ paṭikkami. Tasmā yena so bhagavatā upasaṅkamanto vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkamīti veditabbo. Apahattāti apahārako. Upahattāti upahārako. Paṭisallānā vuṭṭhitoti phalasamāpattito vuṭṭhito.
commentary_english:
148.

Thus, "me suta" is the Laṭukikopamasutta.

There, "yena so vanasaṇḍo" means that the great Udāyitthera, having entered for alms with the Blessed One, then departed with him.

Therefore, "yena so bhagavatā upasaṅkamanto vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkamīti veditabbo" should be understood.

"apahattā" means apahārako.

"upahattā" means upahārako.

"paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito" means phalasamāpattito vuṭṭhito.

mula_pali: 149. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā udāyī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘idha mayhaṃ, bhante, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘bahūnaṃ vata no bhagavā dukkhadhammānaṃ apahattā, bahūnaṃ vata no bhagavā sukhadhammānaṃ upahattā; bahūnaṃ vata no bhagavā akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ apahattā, bahūnaṃ vata no bhagavā kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upahattā’ti. Mayañhi, bhante, pubbe sāyañceva bhuñjāma pāto ca divā ca vikāle. Ahu kho so, bhante, samayo yaṃ bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘iṅgha tumhe, bhikkhave, etaṃ divāvikālabhojanaṃ pajahathā’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, ahudeva aññathattaṃ, ahudeva ahu (sī. pī.) domanassaṃ – ‘yampi no saddhā gahapatikā divā vikāle paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ denti tassapi no bhagavā pahānamāha, tassapi no sugato paṭinissaggamāhā’ti. Te mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavati pemañca gāravañca hiriñca ottappañca sampassamānā evaṃ taṃ divāvikālabhojanaṃ pajahimhā. Te mayaṃ, bhante, sāyañceva bhuñjāma pāto ca. Ahu kho so, bhante, samayo yaṃ bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘iṅgha tumhe, bhikkhave, etaṃ rattiṃvikālabhojanaṃ pajahathā’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, ahudeva aññathattaṃ ahudeva domanassaṃ – ‘yampi no imesaṃ dvinnaṃ bhattānaṃ paṇītasaṅkhātataraṃ tassapi no bhagavā pahānamāha, tassapi no sugato paṭinissaggamāhā’ti. Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhante, aññataro puriso divā sūpeyyaṃ labhitvā evamāha – ‘handa ca imaṃ nikkhipatha, sāyaṃ sabbeva samaggā bhuñjissāmā’ti. Yā kāci, bhante, saṅkhatiyo sabbā tā rattiṃ, appā divā. Te mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavati pemañca gāravañca hiriñca ottappañca sampassamānā evaṃ taṃ rattiṃvikālabhojanaṃ pajahimhā. Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhante, bhikkhū rattandhakāratimisāyaṃ piṇḍāya carantā candanikampi pavisanti, oligallepi papatanti, kaṇṭakāvāṭampi kaṇṭakavattampi (sī. pī.), kaṇṭakarājimpi (syā. kaṃ.) ārohanti, suttampi gāviṃ ārohanti, māṇavehipi samāgacchanti katakammehipi akatakammehipi, mātugāmopi te tena (ka.) asaddhammena nimanteti. Bhūtapubbāhaṃ, bhante, rattandhakāratimisāyaṃ piṇḍāya carāmi. Addasā kho maṃ, bhante, aññatarā itthī vijjantarikāya bhājanaṃ dhovantī. Disvā maṃ bhītā vissaramakāsi – ‘abhumme abbhumme (sī. pī.) pisāco vata ma’nti! Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhante, taṃ itthiṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘nāhaṃ, bhagini, pisāco; bhikkhu piṇḍāya ṭhito’ti. ‘Bhikkhussa ātumārī, bhikkhussa mātumārī ṭhito’ti. bhikkhussa ātumātumārī (ka.)! Varaṃ te, bhikkhu, tiṇhena govikantanena kucchi parikanto, na tveva varaṃ yaṃ na tveva yā (sī. pī.) rattandhakāratimisāyaṃ kucchihetu piṇḍāya carasī’ti carasāti (sī. pī.). Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, tadanussarato evaṃ hoti – ‘bahūnaṃ vata no bhagavā dukkhadhammānaṃ apahattā, bahūnaṃ vata no bhagavā sukhadhammānaṃ upahattā; bahūnaṃ vata no bhagavā akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ apahattā, bahūnaṃ vata no bhagavā kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upahattā’’’ti.
mula_english:
149. Then the venerable Udayin, being alone in seclusion, this thought arose in his mind: "Indeed, the Blessed One has rid us of many painful states; indeed, the Blessed One has brought us many pleasant states; indeed, the Blessed One has rid us of many unwholesome states; indeed, the Blessed One has brought us many wholesome states."

Venerable sir, formerly we used to eat in the evening, in the morning, and during the day outside the proper time.

Then there was an occasion when the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: 'Come, monks, abandon this eating at the wrong time of day.'

Venerable sir, I was upset and sad, thinking: 'Even though faithful householders give us good food, both hard and soft, at the wrong time of day, the Blessed One tells us to abandon it, the Well-Gone One tells us to relinquish it.'

Then we, venerable sir, seeing love, respect, shame, and fear of wrongdoing in the Blessed One, abandoned that eating at the wrong time of day.

Then we, venerable sir, eat only in the evening and in the morning.

Then there was an occasion when the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: 'Come, monks, abandon this eating at the wrong time of night.'

Venerable sir, I was upset and sad, thinking: 'Even the more delicious of these two meals, the Blessed One tells us to abandon, the Well-Gone One tells us to relinquish.’

Once, venerable sir, a certain man, having obtained a soup during the day, said thus: 'Come, put this aside, and this evening we will all enjoy it together.'

Whatever cooking there is, venerable sir, is mostly done at night, and little by day.

Then we, venerable sir, seeing love, respect, shame, and fear of wrongdoing in the Blessed One, abandoned that eating at the wrong time of night.

Once, venerable sir, monks wandering for alms in the pitch-black darkness of the night enter a charnel ground, fall into a cesspool, climb into a thorn bush, fall over a sleeping cow, meet with young ruffians who have already committed crimes and those planning to do so, and women entice them to unrighteousness.

Once, venerable sir, I was wandering for alms in the pitch-black darkness of the night.

Then a certain woman, washing a pot by the flash of lightning, saw me.

Having seen me, frightened, she exclaimed: 'Is this an earth-bound spirit or a demon?' When this was said, I, venerable sir, said to that woman: 'Sister, I am not a demon, I am a monk standing for alms.'

'It is a bhikkhu whose father is dead, a bhikkhu whose mother is dead!' Better for you, monk, that your belly be cut open with a sharp butcher's knife than to wander for alms in the pitch-black darkness of the night for the sake of your belly!'
