Venerable sir, when I recollect that, it occurs to me: 'Indeed, the Blessed One has rid us of many painful states; indeed, the Blessed One has brought us many pleasant states; indeed, the Blessed One has rid us of many unwholesome states; indeed, the Blessed One has brought us many wholesome states.'
commentary_pali:
149.Yaṃbhagavāti yasmiṃ samaye bhagavā. Iṅghāti āṇattiyaṃ nipāto. Aññathattanti cittassa aññathattaṃ. Tañca kho na bhagavantaṃ paṭicca, evarūpaṃ pana paṇītabhojanaṃ alabhantā kathaṃ yāpessāmāti evaṃ paṇītabhojanaṃ paṭicca ahosīti veditabbaṃ. Bhūtapubbanti iminā rattibhojanassa paṇītabhāvaṃ dasseti. Sūpeyyanti sūpena upanetabbaṃ macchamaṃsakaḷīrādi. Samaggā bhuñjissāmāti ekato bhuñjissāma. Saṅkhatiyoti abhisaṅkhārikakhādanīyāni. Sabbā tā rattinti sabbā tā saṅkhatiyo rattiṃyeva honti, divā pana appā parittā thokikā hontīti. Manussā hi divā yāgukañjiyādīhi yāpetvāpi rattiṃ yathāsatti yathāpaṇītameva bhuñjanti.

Puna bhūtapubbanti iminā ratti vikālabhojane ādīnavaṃ dasseti. Tattha andhakāratimisāyanti bahalandhakāre. Māṇavehīti corehi. Katakammehīti katacorakammehi. Corā kira katakammā yaṃ nesaṃ devataṃ āyācitvā kammaṃ nipphannaṃ, tassa upahāratthāya manusse māretvā galalohitādīni gaṇhanti. Te aññesu manussesu māriyamānesu kolāhalā uppajjissanti, pabbajitaṃ pariyesanto nāma natthīti maññamānā bhikkhū gahetvā mārenti. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Akatakammehīti aṭavito gāmaṃ āgamanakāle kammanipphannatthaṃ puretaraṃ balikammaṃ kātukāmehi. Asaddhammena nimantetīti ‘‘ehi bhikkhu ajjekarattiṃ idheva bhuñjitvā idha vasitvā sampattiṃ anubhavitvā sve gamissasī’’ti methunadhammena nimanteti.

bhūtapubba andhakāratimisāya Māṇavehī Katakammehī Akatakammehī Asaddhammena nimantetī

Puna bhūtapubbanti iminā attanā diṭṭhakāraṇaṃ katheti. Vijjantarikāyāti vijjuvijjotanakkhaṇe . Vissaramakāsīti mahāsaddamakāsi. Abhummeti bhū’ti vaḍḍhi, abhū’ti avaḍḍhi, vināso mayhanti attho. Pisāco vata manti pisāco maṃ khādituṃ āgato vata. Ātumārī mātumārīti ettha ātūti pitā, mātūti mātā. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – yassa pitā vā mātā vā atthi, taṃ mātāpitaro amhākaṃ puttakoti yathā tathā vā uppādetvā yaṃkiñci khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ datvā ekasmiṃ ṭhāne sayāpenti. So evaṃ rattiṃ piṇḍāya na carati. Tuyhaṃ pana mātāpitaro matā maññe, tena evaṃ carasīti.

bhūtapubba Vijjantarikāyā Vissaramakāsī Abhumme Pisāco vata ma Ātumārī mātumārī ātū mātū
commentary_english:
[149]
Yaṃ: At whatever time the Fortunate One...
Iṅghāti: [This is] a particle implying command.
Aññathattanti: It means the otherness of the mind.
Moreover, not relying on the Fortunate One, but not obtaining such excellent food, how would they subsist? Thus, it should be understood that it happened relying on excellent food.
Bhūtapubbanti: By this, he shows the excellence of eating at night.
Sūpeyyanti: With sauce, one should bring near fish, meat, kaḷīra, etc.
Samaggā bhuñjissāmāti: We will eat together.
Saṅkhatiyoti: Prepared edibles.
Sabbā tā ratti: All those prepared things are only at night; during the day, however, they are few, limited, scarce.
Indeed, humans, during the day, having subsisted even on gruel, sour congee, etc., at night they enjoy whatever is available, whatever is excellent.

Furthermore, bhūtapubbanti: By this, he shows the fault in eating at the wrong time at night.
There, andhakāratimisāyanti: In thick darkness.
Māṇavehīti: By thieves.
Katakmehīti: By those who do thieving deeds.
Thieves, it is said, after requesting a deity for the successful completion of a deed, kill humans and take throat-blood, etc., as an offering for that.
When others are being killed, noises will arise; thinking that there is no one seeking renunciants, they take monks and kill [them].
This was said with reference to that.
Akatakmehīti: By those desiring to perform a bali offering beforehand at the time of coming from the forest to the village, for the purpose of the successful completion of a deed.
Asaddhammena nimantetīti: “Come, monk, tonight, having eaten right here, having stayed here, having experienced prosperity, tomorrow you will go," thus, he invites with sexual intercourse.

Bhūtapubba, andhakāratimisāya, māṇavehī, katakmehī, akatakmehī, asaddhammena nimantetī
Furthermore, bhūtapubbanti: By this, he relates a cause seen by himself.
Vijjantarikāyāti: At the moment of lightning flashing.
Vissaramakāsīti: He made a great noise.
Abhummeti: Bhū means growth, abhū means no growth, destruction is mine—this is the meaning.
Pisāco vata ma: A goblin has come to eat me.
Ātumārī mātumārīti: Here, ātū means father, mātū means mother.
This is said: Whomever a father or mother there is, those parents, having somehow or other produced [him, saying] "He is our son," and having given whatever edibles or foods, they cause [him] to lie down in one place.
He thus does not wander for alms at night.
But your parents are dead, I think; therefore, you wander thus.

Bhūtapubba, vijjantarikāyā, vissaramakāsī, abhumme, pisāco vata ma, ātumārī mātumārī, ātū, mātū

mula_pali: 150. ‘‘Evameva panudāyi, idhekacce moghapurisā ‘idaṃ pajahathā’ti mayā vuccamānā te evamāhaṃsu – ‘kiṃ panimassa appamattakassa oramattakassa adhisallikhatevāyaṃ samaṇo’ti. Te tañceva nappajahanti, mayi ca appaccayaṃ upaṭṭhāpenti. Ye ca bhikkhū sikkhākāmā tesaṃ taṃ, udāyi, hoti balavaṃ bandhanaṃ, daḷhaṃ bandhanaṃ, thiraṃ bandhanaṃ, apūtikaṃ bandhanaṃ, thūlo, kaliṅgaro – seyyathāpi, udāyi, laṭukikā sakuṇikā pūtilatāya bandhanena baddhā tattheva vadhaṃ vā bandhaṃ vā maraṇaṃ vā āgameti. Yo nu kho, udāyi, evaṃ vadeyya – ‘yena sā laṭukikā sakuṇikā pūtilatāya bandhanena baddhā tattheva vadhaṃ vā bandhaṃ vā maraṇaṃ vā āgameti, tañhi tassā abalaṃ bandhanaṃ , dubbalaṃ bandhanaṃ, pūtikaṃ bandhanaṃ, asārakaṃ bandhana’nti; sammā nu kho so, udāyi, vadamāno vadeyyā’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante. Yena sā, bhante, laṭukikā sakuṇikā pūtilatāya bandhanena baddhā tattheva vadhaṃ vā bandhaṃ vā maraṇaṃ vā āgameti, tañhi tassā balavaṃ bandhanaṃ, daḷhaṃ bandhanaṃ, thiraṃ bandhanaṃ apūtikaṃ bandhanaṃ, thūlo, kaliṅgaro’’ti. ‘‘Evameva kho, udāyi, idhekacce moghapurisā ‘idaṃ pajahathā’ti mayā vuccamānā te evamāhaṃsu – ‘kiṃ panimassa appamattakassa oramattakassa adhisallikhatevāyaṃ samaṇo’ti? Te tañceva nappajahanti, mayi ca appaccayaṃ upaṭṭhāpenti. Ye ca bhikkhū sikkhākāmā tesaṃ taṃ, udāyi, hoti balavaṃ bandhanaṃ, daḷhaṃ bandhanaṃ, thiraṃ bandhanaṃ, apūtikaṃ bandhanaṃ, thūlo, kaliṅgaro’’.
mula_english:
150. “So too, Udayin, there are certain misguided men here who, when told by me ‘Abandon this’… say: ‘What, such a mere trifle, such a little thing as this? This *samaṇa* is much too exacting!’

And they do not abandon that and they show discourtesy towards me.

as well as towards those *bhikkhus* desirous of training. For them that thing becomes a strong, stout, tough, unrotting tether and a thick yoke. 8. “Suppose, Udayin, a quail were tethered by a rotting creeper and would thereby expect injury, captivity, or death.

Now suppose someone said: ‘The rotting creeper by which that quail is tethered and thereby expects injury, captivity, or death, is for her a feeble, weak, rotting, coreless tether.’ Would he be speaking rightly?”

“For that quail, venerable sir (*bhante*), the rotting creeper by which she is tethered and thereby expects injury, captivity, or death, is a strong, stout, tough, unrotting tether and a thick yoke.”

“So too, Udayin, there are certain misguided men here who, when told by me ‘Abandon this,’ say: ‘What, such a mere trifle, such a little thing as this? This *samaṇa* is much too exacting!’

And they do not abandon that and they show discourtesy towards me.

as well as towards those *bhikkhus* desirous of training. For them that thing becomes a strong, stout, tough, unrotting tether and a thick yoke."
commentary_pali:
150.Evamevāti evameva kiñci ānisaṃsaṃ apassantā nikkāraṇeneva. Evamāhaṃsūti garahanto āha. Tattha āhaṃsūti vadanti. Kiṃ panimassāti imassa appamattakassa hetu kiṃ vattabbaṃ nāma, nanu apassantena viya asuṇantena viya bhavitabbanti. Oramattakassāti parittamattakassa. Adhisallikhatevāyanti ayaṃ samaṇo navanītaṃ pisanto viya padumanāḷasuttaṃ kakacena okkantanto viya atisallekhati, ativāyāmaṃ karoti. Sikkhākāmāti sāriputtamoggallānādayo viya sikkhākāmā, tesu ca appaccayaṃ upaṭṭhapenti. Tesañhi evaṃ hoti ‘‘sace ete ‘appamattakametaṃ, haratha bhagavā’ti vadeyyuṃ, kiṃ satthā na hareyya. Evaṃ pana avatvā bhagavantaṃ parivāretvā nisinnā ‘evaṃ bhagavā, sādhu bhagavā, paññapetha bhagavā’ti atirekataraṃ ussāhaṃ paṭilabhantī’’ti. Tasmā tesu appaccayaṃ upaṭṭhapenti.

Tesanti tesaṃ ekaccānaṃ moghapurisānaṃ. Tanti taṃ appamattakaṃ pahātabbaṃ. Thūlo kaliṅgaroti gale baddhaṃ mahākaṭṭhaṃ viya hoti. Laṭukikā sakuṇikāti cātakasakuṇikā. Sā kira ravasataṃ ravitvā naccasataṃ naccitvā sakiṃ gocaraṃ gaṇhāti. Ākāsato bhūmiyaṃ patiṭṭhitaṃ pana naṃ disvā vacchapālakādayo kīḷanatthaṃ pūtilatāya bandhanti. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Āgametīti upeti. Tañhi tassāti taṃ pūtilatābandhanaṃ tassā appasarīratāya ceva appathāmatāya ca balavabandhanaṃ nāma, mahantaṃ nāḷikerarajju viya ducchijjaṃ hoti. Tesanti tesaṃ moghapurisānaṃ saddhāmandatāya ca paññāmandatāya ca balavaṃ bandhanaṃ nāma, dukkaṭavatthumattakampi mahantaṃ pārājikavatthu viya duppajahaṃ hoti.

Tesa Ta Thūlo kaliṅgaro Laṭukikā sakuṇikā Āgametī Tañhi tassā Tesa
commentary_english:
150. "Just so (evamevāti)" [means:] just so, without seeing any benefit, for no reason at all.

"Thus they said (evamāhaṃsūti)" he says, criticizing.

There, "they said (āhaṃsūti)" means they say.

"What then of this (kiṃ panimassā)" means what should be said about this trifling cause? Surely one should be like one who does not see or hear.

"Of very little (oramattakassā)" means of a very small amount.

"He over-mortifies himself (adhisallikhatevāyaṃ)" means this renunciant mortifies himself excessively, like someone grinding fresh butter, like someone sawing a lotus stalk with a saw; he makes excessive effort.

"Desiring training (sikkhākāmā)" means desiring training, like Sāriputta, Moggallāna, and so on; and they establish no confidence in them. For it occurs to them, "If these were to say, 'This is very little, let the Blessed One accept it,' would the Teacher not accept it? But without speaking thus, surrounding the Blessed One and sitting down, they obtain even greater enthusiasm, [saying,] 'Thus, Blessed One, good, Blessed One, teach, Blessed One.'" Therefore, they establish no confidence in them.

"Of those (tesaṃ)" [means:] of some of those foolish men.

"That (taṃ)" [means:] that trifling thing to be abandoned.

"A thick yoke (thūlo kaliṅgaro)" is like a large log tied around the neck.

"A quail chick (laṭukikā sakuṇikā)" is a cātaka chick. It is said that after chirping a hundred times and dancing a hundred times, it takes its range once. Having seen it settled on the ground from the sky, cowherds and others tie it with a stinking vine for the sake of play. With reference to this, it was said.

"He approaches (āgameti)" means he comes near.

"For that (tañhi tassā)" [means:] that tying with a stinking vine is indeed a strong bond for it, because of its small body and lack of strength, like a large coconut rope; it is difficult to cut.

"Of those (tesaṃ)" [means:] because of the lack of faith and lack of wisdom of those foolish men, it is indeed a strong bond; even a trifling matter of wrong-doing is hard to abandon, like a great matter involving defeat.

tesaṃ, taṃ, thūlo kaliṅgaro, laṭukikā sakuṇikā, āgameti, tañhi tassā, tesaṃ.

mula_pali: 151. ‘‘Idha panudāyi, ekacce kulaputtā ‘idaṃ pajahathā’ti mayā vuccamānā te evamāhaṃsu – ‘kiṃ panimassa appamattakassa oramattakassa pahātabbassa yassa no bhagavā pahānamāha, yassa no sugato paṭinissaggamāhā’ti? Te tañceva pajahanti, mayi ca na appaccayaṃ upaṭṭhāpenti. Ye ca bhikkhū sikkhākāmā te taṃ pahāya appossukkā pannalomā paradattavuttā paradavuttā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) migabhūtena cetasā viharanti. Tesaṃ taṃ, udāyi, hoti abalaṃ bandhanaṃ, dubbalaṃ bandhanaṃ, pūtikaṃ bandhanaṃ, asārakaṃ bandhanaṃ – seyyathāpi, udāyi, rañño nāgo īsādanto urūḷhavā abhijāto saṅgāmāvacaro daḷhehi varattehi bandhanehi baddho īsakaṃyeva kāyaṃ sannāmetvā tāni bandhanāni saṃchinditvā saṃpadāletvā yena kāmaṃ pakkamati. Yo nu kho, udāyi, evaṃ vadeyya – ‘yehi so rañño nāgo īsādanto urūḷhavā abhijāto saṅgāmāvacaro daḷhehi varattehi bandhanehi baddho īsakaṃyeva kāyaṃ sannāmetvā tāni bandhanāni saṃchinditvā saṃpadāletvā yena kāmaṃ pakkamati, tañhi tassa balavaṃ bandhanaṃ, daḷhaṃ bandhanaṃ, thiraṃ bandhanaṃ, apūtikaṃ bandhanaṃ, thūlo, kaliṅgaro’ti; sammā nu kho so, udāyi, vadamāno vadeyyā’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante. Yehi so, bhante, rañño nāgo īsādanto urūḷhavā abhijāto saṅgāmāvacaro daḷhehi varattehi bandhanehi baddho īsakaṃyeva kāyaṃ sannāmetvā tāni bandhanāni saṃchinditvā saṃpadāletvā yena kāmaṃ pakkamati, tañhi tassa abalaṃ bandhanaṃ…pe… asārakaṃ bandhana’’nti. ‘‘Evameva kho, udāyi, idhekacce kulaputtā ‘idaṃ pajahathā’ti mayā vuccamānā te evamāhaṃsu – ‘kiṃ panimassa appamattakassa oramattakassa pahātabbassa yassa no bhagavā pahānamāha, yassa no sugato paṭinissaggamāhā’ti? Te tañceva pajahanti, mayi ca na appaccayaṃ upaṭṭhāpenti. Ye ca bhikkhū sikkhākāmā te taṃ pahāya appossukkā pannalomā paradattavuttā migabhūtena cetasā viharanti. Tesaṃ taṃ, udāyi, hoti abalaṃ bandhanaṃ, dubbalaṃ bandhanaṃ, pūtikaṃ bandhanaṃ, asārakaṃ bandhanaṃ’’.
mula_english:
151. “Here, Udayin, certain clansmen, when told by me ‘Abandon this,’ say thus: ‘What is this trifling, insignificant thing that the Blessed One tells us to abandon, that the Well-Gone One tells us to relinquish?’ They abandon just that, and they do not establish confidence in me.

Or towards those *bhikkhus* desirous of training. Having abandoned it, they live at ease, unruffled, subsisting on others’ gifts, with mind as aloof as a wild deer’s.

For them that thing becomes a feeble ( *abalaṃ*), weak (*dubbalaṃ*), rotting (*pūtikaṃ*), coreless (*asārakaṃ*) tether. Suppose, Udayin, a royal tusker elephant (*nāga*) with tusks as long as chariot-poles (*īsādanta*), full-grown in stature (*urūḷhavā*), high-bred (*abhijāta*) and accustomed to battle (*saṅgāmāvacara*), were tethered by stout leather thongs (*daḷhehi varattehi bandhanehi baddha*), but by simply twisting his body a little he could break and burst the thongs and then go where he likes.

Now suppose someone said: ‘The stout leather thongs by which this royal tusker elephant is tethered…are for him a strong (*balavaṃ*), stout (*daḷhaṃ*), tough (*thiraṃ*), unrotting (*apūtikaṃ*) tether and a thick yoke (*thūlo, kaliṅgaro*)’ Would he be speaking rightly?”

“No, venerable sir.

The stout leather thongs by which that royal tusker elephant (*nāga*) is tethered, which by simply twisting his body a little he could break and burst and then go where he likes, are for him a feeble (*abalaṃ*) tether… coreless (*asārakaṃ*) tether.”

“So too, Udayin, there are certain clansmen here who, when told by me ‘Abandon this,’ say thus: ‘What is this trifling, insignificant thing that the Blessed One tells us to abandon, that the Well-Gone One tells us to relinquish?’ They abandon just that, and they do not establish confidence in me.

Or towards those *bhikkhus* desirous of training. Having abandoned it, they live at ease, unruffled, subsisting on others’ gifts, with mind as aloof as a wild deer’s.

For them that thing becomes a feeble (*abalaṃ*) tether, a weak (*dubbalaṃ*) tether, a rotting (*pūtikaṃ*) tether, a coreless (*asārakaṃ*) tether.”
commentary_pali: 151. Sukkapakkhe pahātabbassāti kiṃ imassa appamattakassa pahātabbassa hetu bhagavatā vattabbaṃ atthi, yassa no bhagavā pahānamāha. Nanu evaṃ bhagavato adhippāyaṃ ñatvāpi pahātabbamevāti attho. Appossukkāti anussukkā. Pannalomāti patitalomā, na tassa pahātabbabhayena uddhaggalomā. Paradattavuttāti parehi dinnavuttino, parato laddhena yāpentāti attho. Migabhūtena cetasā viharantīti apaccāsīsanapakkhe ṭhitā hutvā viharanti. Migo hi pahāraṃ labhitvā manussāvāsaṃ gantvā bhesajjaṃ vā vaṇatelaṃ vā labhissāmīti ajjhāsayaṃ akatvā pahāraṃ labhitvāva agāmakaṃ araññaṃ pavisitvā pahaṭaṭṭhānaṃ heṭṭhā katvā nipatitvā phāsubhūtakāle uṭṭhāya gacchati. Evaṃ migā apaccāsīsanapakkhe ṭhitā. Idaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘‘migabhūtena cetasā viharantī’’ti. Tañhi tassāti taṃ varattabandhanaṃ tassa hatthināgassa mahāsarīratāya ceva mahāthāmatāya ca dubbalabandhanaṃ nāma. Pūtilatā viya suchijjaṃ hoti. Tesaṃ tanti tesaṃ taṃ kulaputtānaṃ saddhāmahantatāya ca paññāmahantatāya ca mahantaṃ pārājikavatthupi dukkaṭavatthumattakaṃ viya suppajahaṃ hoti.
commentary_english: 151. "Because it should be abandoned in the bright half of the month [sukkapakkhe pahātabbassā]," what is the reason [hetu] the Blessed One [bhagavatā] said it should be abandoned in this insignificant [appamattakassa] matter? It should be stated [vattabbaṃ] that the Blessed One [bhagavā] spoke [āha] of abandoning [pahānaṃ] what does not exist [atthi, yassa no]? Indeed [nanu], is the meaning [attho] that even having known [ñatvāpi] the Blessed One's [bhagavato] intention [adhippāyaṃ], it should still be abandoned [pahātabbameva]? "Without eagerness [appossukkā]" means without longing [anussukkā]. "Having fallen hair [pannalomā]" means having hair that has fallen out [patitalomā]; their hair does not stand on end [uddhaggalomā] from the fear [bhayena] of what should be abandoned [pahātabba]. "Living on what is given by others [paradattavuttā]" means those whose livelihood [vuttino] is from what is given by others [parehi dinna], they maintain themselves [yāpentāti] by what is obtained [laddhena] from another [parato]; this is the meaning [attho]. "Living with a mind like a deer [migabhūtena cetasā viharantī]" means abiding [ṭhitā hutvā viharanti] in the state of not expecting favors [apaccāsīsanapakkhe]. For [hi] a deer [migo], having received [labhitvā] a wound [pahāraṃ], having gone [gantvā] to a human dwelling [manussāvāsaṃ], without thinking [akatvā] "I will obtain [labhissāmi] medicine [bhesajjaṃ] or wound oil [vaṇatelaṃ]," having only received [labhitvāva] the wound [pahāraṃ], having entered [pavisitvā] a pathless [agāmakaṃ] forest [araññaṃ], having made [katvā] the wounded [pahaṭaṭṭhānaṃ] place downward [heṭṭhā], having lain down [nipatitvā], when the time is right [phāsubhūtakāle], gets up [uṭṭhāya] and goes [gacchati]. Thus [evaṃ] deer [migā] are abiding [ṭhitā] in the state of not expecting favors [apaccāsīsanapakkhe]. This [idaṃ] was spoken [vuttaṃ] with reference [sandhāya] to "living with a mind like a deer [migabhūtena cetasā viharantī]". "Because it belongs to her [tañhi tassā]" means that rope binding [taṃ varattabandhanaṃ] is called [nāma] a weak binding [dubbalabandhanaṃ] for that elephant-Nāga [tassa hatthināgassa] because of its large body [mahāsarīratāya ceva] and great strength [mahāthāmatāya ca]. It becomes [hoti] easily cut [suchijjaṃ] like a rotten vine [pūtilatā viya]. "Their that [tesaṃ ta]" means that great [mahantaṃ] offense entailing defeat [pārājikavatthupi] is easily abandoned [suppajahaṃ hoti] like a small [mattakaṃ viya] offense of wrong-doing [dukkaṭavatthu] for those sons of good families [tesaṃ taṃ kulaputtānaṃ] because of their great faith [saddhāmahantatāya ca] and great wisdom [paññāmahantatāya ca].

mula_pali: 152. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, udāyi, puriso daliddo assako anāḷhiyo; tassa’ssa ekaṃ agārakaṃ oluggaviluggaṃ kākātidāyiṃ kākātiḍāyiṃ (?) naparamarūpaṃ, ekā khaṭopikā kaḷopikā (ka.) oluggaviluggā naparamarūpā, ekissā kumbhiyā dhaññasamavāpakaṃ naparamarūpaṃ, ekā jāyikā naparamarūpā. So ārāmagataṃ bhikkhuṃ passeyya sudhotahatthapādaṃ manuññaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuttāviṃ sītāya chāyāya nisinnaṃ adhicitte yuttaṃ. Tassa evamassa – ‘sukhaṃ vata, bho, sāmaññaṃ, ārogyaṃ vata, bho, sāmaññaṃ! So vatassaṃ so vatassa (ka.) yohaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajeyya’nti. So na sakkuṇeyya ekaṃ agārakaṃ oluggaviluggaṃ kākātidāyiṃ naparamarūpaṃ pahāya, ekaṃ khaṭopikaṃ oluggaviluggaṃ naparamarūpaṃ pahāya, ekissā kumbhiyā dhaññasamavāpakaṃ naparamarūpaṃ pahāya, ekaṃ jāyikaṃ naparamarūpaṃ pahāya kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ. Yo nu kho, udāyi, evaṃ vadeyya – ‘yehi so puriso bandhanehi baddho na sakkoti ekaṃ agārakaṃ oluggaviluggaṃ kākātidāyiṃ naparamarūpaṃ pahāya, ekaṃ khaṭopikaṃ oluggaviluggaṃ naparamarūpaṃ pahāya, ekissā kumbhiyā dhaññasamavāpakaṃ naparamarūpaṃ pahāya, ekaṃ jāyikaṃ naparamarūpaṃ pahāya kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ; tañhi tassa abalaṃ bandhanaṃ, dubbalaṃ bandhanaṃ, pūtikaṃ bandhanaṃ, asārakaṃ bandhana’nti; sammā nu kho so, udāyi, vadamāno vadeyyā’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante. Yehi so, bhante, puriso bandhanehi baddho, na sakkoti ekaṃ agārakaṃ oluggaviluggaṃ kākātidāyiṃ naparamarūpaṃ pahāya, ekaṃ khaṭopikaṃ oluggaviluggaṃ naparamarūpaṃ pahāya, ekissā kumbhiyā dhaññasamavāpakaṃ naparamarūpaṃ pahāya, ekaṃ jāyikaṃ naparamarūpaṃ pahāya kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ; tañhi tassa balavaṃ bandhanaṃ, daḷhaṃ bandhanaṃ, thiraṃ bandhanaṃ, apūtikaṃ bandhanaṃ, thūlo, kaliṅgaro’’ti. ‘‘Evameva kho, udāyi, idhekacce moghapurisā ‘idaṃ pajahathā’ti mayā vuccamānā te evamāhaṃsu – ‘kiṃ panimassa appamattakassa oramattakassa adhisallikhatevāyaṃ samaṇo’ti? Te tañceva nappajahanti, mayi ca appaccayaṃ upaṭṭhāpenti. Ye ca bhikkhū sikkhākāmā tesaṃ taṃ, udāyi, hoti balavaṃ bandhanaṃ, daḷhaṃ bandhanaṃ, thiraṃ bandhanaṃ, apūtikaṃ bandhanaṃ, thūlo, kaliṅgaro’’.
mula_english:
152. “Suppose, Udayin, there were a poor, penniless, destitute man, and he had one dilapidated hovel open to the crows, not the best kind, and one dilapidated wicker bedstead, not the best kind, and some grain and pumpkin seeds in a pot, not the best kind, and one hag of a wife, not the best kind.

He might see a *bhikṣu* in a monastery park sitting in the shade of a tree, his hands and feet well washed after he had eaten a delicious meal, devoting himself to the higher mind.

He might think: ‘How pleasant the recluse’s state is! How healthy the recluse’s state is! If only I could shave off my hair and beard, put on the yellow robe, and go forth from the home life into homelessness!’

But being unable to abandon his one dilapidated hovel open to the crows, not the best kind, and his one dilapidated wicker bedstead, not the best kind, and his grain and pumpkin seeds in a pot, not the best kind, and his hag of a wife, not the best kind, he is unable to shave off his hair and beard, put on the yellow robe, and go forth from the home life into homelessness.

Now suppose someone said: ‘The tethers by which that man is tethered so that he cannot abandon his one dilapidated hovel…and his hag of a wife, not the best kind, and shave off his hair and beard, put on the yellow robe, and go forth from the home life into homelessness - for him those are a feeble, weak, rotting, coreless tether.’ Would he be speaking rightly?”

“No, venerable sir.

The tethers by which that man is tethered so that he cannot abandon his one dilapidated hovel…and his hag of a wife, not the best kind, and shave off his hair and beard, put on the yellow robe, and go forth from the home life into homelessness - for him those are a strong, stout, tough, unrotting tether and a thick yoke.”

“Just so, Udayin, here some foolish men, when I say to them, ‘Give this up,’ say to me, ‘Why is this ascetic being so extremely scrupulous?’ They do not abandon that, and they show discourtesy towards me.

as well as towards those *bhikṣus* desirous of training. For them that thing becomes a strong, stout, tough, unrotting tether and a thick yoke.”
commentary_pali:
152.Daliddoti dāliddiyena samannāgato. Assakoti nissako. Anāḷhiyoti anaḍḍho. Agārakanti khuddakagehaṃ. Oluggavilugganti yassa gehayaṭṭhiyo piṭṭhivaṃsato muccitvā maṇḍale laggā, maṇḍalato muccitvā bhūmiyaṃ laggā. Kākātidāyinti yattha kiñcideva bhuñjissāmāti anto nisinnakāle visuṃ dvārakiccaṃ nāma natthi, tato tato kākā pavisitvā parivārenti. Sūrakākā hi palāyanakāle ca yathāsammukhaṭṭhāneneva nikkhamitvā palāyanti. Naparamarūpanti na puññavantānaṃ gehaṃ viya uttamarūpaṃ. Khaṭopikāti vilīvamañcako. Oluggaviluggāti oṇatuṇṇatā. Dhaññasamavāpakanti dhaññañca samavāpakañca. Tattha dhaññaṃ nāma kudrūsako. Samavāpakanti lābubījakumbhaṇḍabījakādi bījajātaṃ. Naparamarūpanti yathā puññavantānaṃ gandhasālibījādi parisuddhaṃ bījaṃ, na evarūpaṃ. Jāyikāti kapaṇajāyā. Naparamarūpāti pacchisīsā lambatthanī mahodarā pisācā viya bībhacchā. Sāmaññanti samaṇabhāvo. So vatassaṃ, yohanti so vatāhaṃ puriso nāma assaṃ, yo kesamassuṃ ohāretvā pabbajeyyanti.

So na sakkuṇeyyāti so evaṃ cintetvāpi gehaṃ gantvā – ‘‘pabbajjā nāma lābhagarukā dukkarā durāsadā, sattapi aṭṭhapi gāme piṇḍāya caritvā yathādhoteneva pattena āgantabbampi hoti , evaṃ yāpetuṃ asakkontassa me puna āgatassa vasanaṭṭhānaṃ icchitabbaṃ, tiṇavallidabbasambhārā nāma dussamodhāniyā, kinti karomī’’ti vīmaṃsati. Athassa taṃ agārakaṃ vejayantapāsādo viya upaṭṭhāti. Athassa khaṭopikaṃ oloketvā – ‘‘mayi gate imaṃ visaṅkharitvā uddhanālātaṃ karissanti, puna aṭṭanipādavilīvādīni laddhabbāni honti, kinti karissāmī’’ti cinteti. Athassa sā sirisayanaṃ viya upaṭṭhāti. Tato dhaññakumbhiṃ oloketvā – ‘‘mayi gate ayaṃ gharaṇī imaṃ dhaññaṃ tena tena saddhiṃ bhuñjissati. Puna āgatena jīvitavutti nāma laddhabbā hoti, kinti karissāmī’’ti cinteti. Athassa sā aḍḍhateḷasāni koṭṭhāgārasatāni viya upaṭṭhāti. Tato mātugāmaṃ oloketvā – ‘‘mayi gate imaṃ hatthigopako vā assagopako vā yo koci palobhessati, puna āgatena bhattapācikā nāma laddhabbā hoti, kinti karissāmī’’ti cinteti. Athassa sā rūpinī devī viya upaṭṭhāti. Idaṃ sandhāya ‘‘so na sakkuṇeyyā’’tiādi vuttaṃ.

So na sakkuṇeyyāti
commentary_english:
152. *Daliddo* means associated with poverty (*dāliddiyena samannāgato*).

*Assako* means without possessions (*nissako*).

*Anāḷhiyo* means not rich (*anaḍḍho*).

*Agāraka* means a small house (*khuddakagehaṃ*).

*Oluggavilugga* means when the roof-timbers of a house have become detached from the back-bone [of the roof] and stick in the circle [of the roof], and, having become detached from the circle, stick in the ground (*yassa gehayaṭṭhiyo piṭṭhivaṃsato muccitvā maṇḍale laggā, maṇḍalato muccitvā bhūmiyaṃ laggā*).

*Kākātidāyi* means where there is no separate door-duty at the time when one sits down inside, thinking "I will eat something or other," [but] crows, having entered from here and there, surround [the place] (*yattha kiñcideva bhuñjissāmāti anto nisinnakāle visuṃ dvārakiccaṃ nāma natthi, tato tato kākā pavisitvā parivārenti*).

Brave crows flee, even at the time of fleeing, just by standing face to face and going out (*sūrakākā hi palāyanakāle ca yathāsammukhaṭṭhāneneva nikkhamitvā palāyanti*).

*Naparamarūpa* means not an excellent form like the house of meritorious people (*na puññavantānaṃ gehaṃ viya uttamarūpaṃ*).

*Khaṭopikā* means a shaky couch (*vilīvamañcako*).

*Oluggaviluggā* means being stooped and bent (*oṇatuṇṇatā*).

*Dhaññasamavāpaka* means grain and one who brings [it] together (*dhaññañca samavāpakañca*).

There, *dhaññaṃ* means *kudrūsako* [a kind of grain].

*Samavāpaka* means seeds such as gourd seeds, pumpkin seeds, and the like (*lābubījakumbhaṇḍabījakādi bījajātaṃ*).

*Naparamarūpa* means, just as the seed of fragrant rice and the like of meritorious people is purified, it is not of such a kind (*yathā puññavantānaṃ gandhasālibījādi parisuddhaṃ bījaṃ, na evarūpaṃ*).

*Jāyikā* means a wretched wife (*kapaṇajāyā*).

*Naparamarūpā* means disgusting, like a goblin, with a flattened head, hanging breasts, and a large belly (*pacchisīsā lambatthanī mahodarā pisācā viya bībhacchā*).

*Sāmañña* means the state of being a renunciant (*samaṇabhāvo*).

*"So vatassaṃ, yoha"* means "Would that I were a man, who, having shaved off his hair and beard, might renounce!" (*so vatāhaṃ puriso nāma assaṃ, yo kesamassuṃ ohāretvā pabbajeyyanti*).

"He would not be able," thinking thus, he also went to the house, [thinking]: "Renunciation is indeed difficult, hard to do, difficult to attain, since even having wandered for alms in seven or eight villages, it would be necessary to come back with a bowl just washed out.

If, thus, I am unable to spend [my time], a dwelling-place must be sought again by me when I have come back; the requisite materials of grass, creepers and *dabba* [reeds] are difficult to provide; what shall I do?" Thus he reflects (*evaṃ yāpetuṃ asakkontassa me puna āgatassa vasanaṭṭhānaṃ icchitabbaṃ, tiṇavallidabbasambhārā nāma dussamodhāniyā, kinti karomī’’ti vīmaṃsati*).

Then that house appears to him like the Vejayanta palace (*athassa taṃ agārakaṃ vejayantapāsādo viya upaṭṭhāti*).

Then, having looked at the couch, [he thinks]: "When I am gone, they will take it apart and make a fire-brand, again the legs of the bed and the like must be obtained, what shall I do?" Thus he thinks (*athassa khaṭopikaṃ oloketvā – ‘‘mayi gate imaṃ visaṅkharitvā uddhanālātaṃ karissanti, puna aṭṭanipādavilīvādīni laddhabbāni honti, kinti karissāmī’’ti cinteti*).

Then that sleeping-place appears to him like a fortunate bed (*athassa sā sirisayanaṃ viya upaṭṭhāti*).

Then, having looked at the grain-pot, [he thinks]: "When I am gone, this housewife will enjoy this grain together with this and that person.

When I have come back, a living must be obtained, what shall I do?" Thus he thinks (*tato dhaññakumbhiṃ oloketvā – ‘‘mayi gate ayaṃ gharaṇī imaṃ dhaññaṃ tena tena saddhiṃ bhuñjissati. puna āgatena jīvitavutti nāma laddhabbā hoti, kinti karissāmī’’ti cinteti*).

Then those one and a half times thirteen hundred store-houses appear to him (*athassa sā aḍḍhateḷasāni koṭṭhāgārasatāni viya upaṭṭhāti*).

Then, having looked at the woman, [he thinks]: "When I am gone, either a trainer of elephants or a trainer of horses or anyone will entice her, when I have come back, a cook must be obtained, what shall I do?" Thus he thinks (*tato mātugāmaṃ oloketvā – ‘‘mayi gate imaṃ hatthigopako vā assagopako vā yo koci palobhessati, puna āgatena bhattapācikā nāma laddhabbā hoti, kinti karissāmī’’ti cinteti*).

Then that beautiful woman appears to him like a goddess (*athassa sā rūpinī devī viya upaṭṭhāti*).

Having this in mind, the statement "He would not be able" and the like was said (*idaṃ sandhāya ‘‘so na sakkuṇeyyā’’tiādi vuttaṃ*).

mula_pali: 153. ‘‘Seyyathāpi , udāyi, gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā aḍḍho mahaddhano mahābhogo, nekānaṃ nikkhagaṇānaṃ cayo, nekānaṃ dhaññagaṇānaṃ cayo, nekānaṃ khettagaṇānaṃ cayo, nekānaṃ vatthugaṇānaṃ cayo, nekānaṃ bhariyagaṇānaṃ cayo, nekānaṃ dāsagaṇānaṃ cayo, nekānaṃ dāsigaṇānaṃ cayo; so ārāmagataṃ bhikkhuṃ passeyya sudhotahatthapādaṃ manuññaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuttāviṃ sītāya chāyāya nisinnaṃ adhicitte yuttaṃ. Tassa evamassa – ‘sukhaṃ vata, bho, sāmaññaṃ, ārogyaṃ vata, bho, sāmaññaṃ! So vatassaṃ yohaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajeyya’nti. So sakkuṇeyya nekāni nikkhagaṇāni pahāya, nekāni dhaññagaṇāni pahāya, nekāni khettagaṇāni pahāya, nekāni vatthugaṇāni pahāya, nekāni bhariyagaṇāni pahāya, nekāni dāsagaṇāni pahāya, nekāni dāsigaṇāni pahāya kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ. Yo nu kho, udāyi, evaṃ vadeyya – ‘yehi so gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā bandhanehi baddho, sakkoti nekāni nikkhagaṇāni pahāya, nekāni dhaññagaṇāni pahāya, nekāni khettagaṇāni pahāya, nekāni vatthugaṇāni pahāya, nekāni bhariyagaṇāni pahāya, nekāni dāsagaṇāni pahāya, nekāni dāsigaṇāni pahāya kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ, tañhi tassa balavaṃ bandhanaṃ, daḷhaṃ bandhanaṃ, thiraṃ bandhanaṃ, apūtikaṃ bandhanaṃ, thūlo, kaliṅgaro’ti; sammā nu kho so, udāyi, vadamāno vadeyyā’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante. Yehi so, bhante, gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā bandhanehi baddho, sakkoti nekāni nikkhagaṇāni pahāya, nekāni dhaññagaṇāni pahāya, nekāni khettagaṇāni pahāya, nekāni vatthugaṇāni pahāya, nekāni bhariyagaṇāni pahāya, nekāni dāsagaṇāni pahāya, nekāni dāsigaṇāni pahāya kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ; tañhi tassa abalaṃ bandhanaṃ, dubbalaṃ bandhanaṃ, pūtikaṃ bandhanaṃ, asārakaṃ bandhana’’nti. ‘‘Evameva kho, udāyi, idhekacce kulaputtā ‘idaṃ pajahathā’ti mayā vuccamānā te evamāhaṃsu – ‘kiṃ panimassa appamattakassa oramattakassa pahātabbassa yassa no bhagavā pahānamāha yassa, no sugato paṭinissaggamāhā’ti? Te tañceva pajahanti, mayi ca na appaccayaṃ upaṭṭhāpenti. Ye ca bhikkhū sikkhākāmā te taṃ pahāya appossukkā pannalomā paradattavuttā migabhūtena cetasā viharanti. Tesaṃ taṃ, udāyi, hoti abalaṃ bandhanaṃ, dubbalaṃ bandhanaṃ, pūtikaṃ bandhanaṃ, asārakaṃ bandhanaṃ’’.
mula_english:
“Suppose, Udayin, there were a rich householder or a householder’s son, with great wealth and property (*mahābhoga*), with a vast number of gold ingots (*nikkhagaṇānaṃ cayo*), a vast number of granaries (*dhaññagaṇānaṃ cayo*), a vast number of fields (*khettagaṇānaṃ cayo*), a vast amount of land (*vatthugaṇānaṃ cayo*), a vast number of wives (*bhariyagaṇānaṃ cayo*), and a vast number of men slaves (*dāsagaṇānaṃ cayo*), and a vast number of women slaves (*dāsigaṇānaṃ cayo*). He might see a *bhikkhu* in a monastery park sitting in the shade of a tree, his hands and feet well washed after he had eaten a delicious meal, devoting himself to the higher mind.

He might think: ‘Happy indeed is the ascetic life (*sāmaññaṃ*), healthy indeed is the ascetic life! If only I could shave off my hair and beard (*kesamassuṃ ohāretvā*), put on the yellow robes (*kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā*), and go forth from the household life into homelessness (*agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajeyya*)’.

And being able to abandon his vast number of gold ingots (*nikkhagaṇāni pahāya*), his vast number of granaries (*dhaññagaṇāni pahāya*), his vast number of fields (*khettagaṇāni pahāya*), his vast amount of land (*vatthugaṇāni pahāya*), his vast number of wives (*bhariyagaṇāni pahāya*), and his vast number of men slaves (*dāsagaṇāni pahāya*), and his vast number of women slaves (*dāsigaṇāni pahāya*), he is able to shave off his hair and beard (*kesamassuṃ ohāretvā*), put on the yellow robe (*kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā*), and go forth from the home life into homelessness (*agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ*).

Now suppose someone said: ‘The tethers by which that householder or householder’s son is tethered so that he can abandon his vast number of gold ingots, his vast number of granaries, his vast number of fields, his vast amount of land, his vast number of wives, and his vast number of men slaves, and his vast number of women slaves, and shave off his hair and beard, put on the yellow robe, and go forth from the home life into homelessness - for him those are a strong, stout, tough, unrotting tether.’ Would he be speaking rightly?” “No, venerable sir.

The tethers by which that householder or householder’s son is tethered so that he can abandon his vast number of gold ingots, his vast number of granaries, his vast number of fields, his vast amount of land, his vast number of wives, and his vast number of men slaves, and his vast number of women slaves, and shave off his hair and beard, put on the yellow robe, and go forth from the home life into homelessness - for him those are a feeble, weak, rotting, coreless tether.”

“Just so, Udayin, there are certain clansmen here who, when told by me ‘Abandon this,’ they say: ‘What, such a mere trifle, such a little thing to be abandoned as this, the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) tells us to abandon, the Sublime One (*sugato*) tells us to relinquish.’ They abandon just that, but they do not establish faith in me.

or towards those *bhikkhus* desirous of training. Having abandoned it, they live at ease, unruffled, subsisting on others’ gifts, with mind as aloof as a wild deer’s.

For them that thing becomes a feeble, weak, rotting, coreless tether.”
commentary_pali: 153.Nikkhagaṇānanti suvaṇṇanikkhasatānaṃ. Cayoti santānato katasannicayo. Dhaññagaṇānanti dhaññasakaṭasatānaṃ.
commentary_english: 153. *Nikkhagaṇāna* means one hundred gold *nikkhas*. *Cayo* means an accumulation made through continuity. *Dhaññagaṇāna* means one hundred carts of grain.

mula_pali:
154. ‘‘Cattārome , udāyi, puggalā santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ. Katame cattāro? Idhudāyi, ekacco puggalo upadhipahānāya paṭipanno hoti upadhipaṭinissaggāya. Tamenaṃ upadhipahānāya paṭipannaṃ upadhipaṭinissaggāya upadhipaṭisaṃyuttā sarasaṅkappā samudācaranti. So te adhivāseti, nappajahati, na vinodeti, na byantīkaroti, na anabhāvaṃ gameti. Imaṃ kho ahaṃ, udāyi, puggalaṃ ‘saṃyutto’ti vadāmi no ‘visaṃyutto’. Taṃ kissa hetu? Indriyavemattatā hi me, udāyi, imasmiṃ puggale viditā.

‘‘Idha panudāyi, ekacco puggalo upadhipahānāya paṭipanno hoti upadhipaṭinissaggāya. Tamenaṃ upadhipahānāya paṭipannaṃ upadhipaṭinissaggāya upadhipaṭisaṃyuttā sarasaṅkappā samudācaranti. So te nādhivāseti, pajahati, vinodeti, byantīkaroti, anabhāvaṃ gameti. Imampi kho ahaṃ, udāyi , puggalaṃ ‘saṃyutto’ti vadāmi no ‘visaṃyutto’. Taṃ kissa hetu? Indriyavemattatā hi me, udāyi, imasmiṃ puggale viditā.

‘‘Idha panudāyi, ekacco puggalo upadhipahānāya paṭipanno hoti upadhipaṭinissaggāya. Tamenaṃ upadhipahānāya paṭipannaṃ upadhipaṭinissaggāya kadāci karahaci satisammosā upadhipaṭisaṃyuttā sarasaṅkappā samudācaranti; dandho, udāyi, satuppādo. Atha kho naṃ khippameva pajahati, vinodeti, byantīkaroti, anabhāvaṃ gameti. Seyyathāpi, udāyi, puriso divasaṃsantatte divasasantatte (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) ayokaṭāhe dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni nipāteyya; dandho, udāyi, udakaphusitānaṃ nipāto. Atha kho naṃ khippameva parikkhayaṃ pariyādānaṃ gaccheyya. Evameva kho, udāyi, idhekacco puggalo upadhipahānāya paṭipanno hoti upadhipaṭinissaggāya. Tamenaṃ upadhipahānāya paṭipannaṃ upadhipaṭinissaggāya kadāci karahaci satisammosā upadhipaṭisaṃyuttā sarasaṅkappā samudācaranti; dandho, udāyi, satuppādo. Atha kho naṃ khippameva pajahati, vinodeti, byantīkaroti, anabhāvaṃ gameti. Imampi kho ahaṃ, udāyi, puggalaṃ ‘saṃyutto’ti vadāmi no ‘visaṃyutto’. Taṃ kissa hetu? Indriyavemattatā hi me, udāyi, imasmiṃ puggale viditā.

divasasantatte (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)

‘‘Idha panudāyi, ekacco puggalo ‘upadhi dukkhassa mūla’nti – iti viditvā nirupadhi hoti, upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto. Imaṃ kho ahaṃ, udāyi, puggalaṃ ‘visaṃyutto’ti vadāmi no ‘saṃyutto’ti . Taṃ kissa hetu? Indriyavemattatā hi me, udāyi, imasmiṃ puggale viditā. Ime kho, udāyi, cattāro puggalā santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ.
mula_english:
154. “Udayin, there are these four kinds of persons found existing in the world. Which four? Here, Udayin, some person practises the way to the abandoning of attachment (*upadhi*), to the relinquishing of attachment. When he is practising the way to the abandoning of attachment, to the relinquishing of attachment, memories and intentions associated with attachment beset him. He tolerates them; he does not abandon them, remove them, do away with them, and annihilate them. Such a person I call fettered (*saṃyutto*), not unfettered (*visaṃyutto*). Why is that? Because I have known the particular diversity of faculties (*indriyavemattatā*) in this person. “Here, Udayin, some person practises the way to the abandoning of attachment, to the relinquishing of attachment. When he is practising the way to the abandoning of attachment, to the relinquishing of attachment, memories and intentions associated with attachment beset him. He does not tolerate them; he abandons them, removes them, does away with them, and annihilates them. Such a person too I call fettered (*saṃyutto*), not unfettered (*visaṃyutto*). Why is that? Because I have known the particular diversity of faculties (*indriyavemattatā*) in this person. “Here, Udayin, some person practises the way to the abandoning of attachment, to the relinquishing of attachment. When he is practising the way to the abandoning of attachment, to the relinquishing of attachment, memories and intentions associated with attachment beset him now and then through lapses of mindfulness; his mindfulness may be slow in arising. But he quickly abandons them, removes them, does away with them, and annihilates them. Just as if a man were to let two or three drops of water fall onto an iron plate heated for a whole day, the falling of the water drops might be slow, but they would quickly vaporise and vanish. Just so, Udayin, some person practises the way to the abandoning of attachment, to the relinquishing of attachment. When he is practising the way to the abandoning of attachment, to the relinquishing of attachment, memories and intentions associated with attachment beset him now and then through lapses of mindfulness; his mindfulness may be slow in arising. But he quickly abandons them, removes them, does away with them, and annihilates them. Such a person too I call fettered (*saṃyutto*), not unfettered (*visaṃyutto*). Why is that? Because I have known the particular diversity of faculties (*indriyavemattatā*) in this person. “Here, Udayin, some person, having understood that attachment (*upadhi*) is the root of suffering (*duḥkha*), divests himself of attachment and is liberated with the destruction of attachment. Such a person I call unfettered (*visaṃyutto*), not fettered (*saṃyutto*). 0126"/>. Why is that? Because I have known the particular diversity of faculties ( *indriyavemattatā*) in this person, Udayi. These, Udayi, are the four ( *cattāro*) kinds of persons (*puggalā*) found existing in the world (*lokasmiṃ*).

.
commentary_pali:
154.Cattārome, udāyi, puggalāti idha kiṃ dasseti? Heṭṭhā ‘‘te tañceva pajahanti, te tañceva nappajahantī’’ti pajahanakā ca appajahanakā ca rāsivasena dassitā, na pāṭiyekkaṃ vibhattā. Idāni yathā nāma dabbasambhāratthaṃ gato puriso paṭipāṭiyā rukkhe chinditvā puna nivattitvā vaṅkañca pahāya kamme upanetabbayuttakameva gaṇhāti, evameva appajahanake chaḍḍetvā abbohārike katvā pajahanakapuggalā cattāro hontīti dassetuṃ imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi.

Upadhipahānāyāti khandhupadhikilesupadhiabhisaṅkhārupadhikāmaguṇūpadhīti imesaṃ upadhīnaṃ pahānāya. Upadhipaṭisaṃyuttāti upadhianudhāvanakā. Sarasaṅkappāti ettha saranti dhāvantīti sarā. Saṅkappentīti saṅkappā. Padadvayenapi vitakkāyeva vuttā. Samudācarantīti abhibhavanti ajjhottharitvā vattanti. Saṃyuttoti kilesehi saṃyutto. Indriyavemattatāti indriyanānattatā . Kadāci karahacīti bahukālaṃ vītivattetvā. Satisammosāti satisammosena. Nipātoti ayokaṭāhamhi patanaṃ. Ettāvatā ‘‘nappajahati, pajahati, khippaṃ pajahatī’’ti tayo rāsayo dassitā. Tesu cattāro janā nappajahanti nāma, cattāro pajahanti nāma, cattāro khippaṃ pajahanti nāma.

Upadhipahānāyā Upadhipaṭisaṃyuttā Sarasaṅkappā Samudācarantī Saṃyutto Indriyavemattatā Kadāci karahacī Satisammosā Nipāto

Tattha puthujjano sotāpanno sakadāgāmī anāgāmīti ime cattāro janā nappajahanti nāma. Puthujjanādayo tāva mā pajahantu, anāgāmī kathaṃ na pajahatīti? Sopi hi yāvadevassa bhavalobho atthi, tāva ahosukhaṃ ahosukhanti abhinandati. Tasmā nappajahati nāma. Eteyeva pana cattāro janā pajahanti nāma. Sotāpannādayo tāva pajahantu, puthujjano kathaṃ pajahatīti? Āraddhavipassako hi satisammosena sahasā kilese uppanne ‘‘mādisassa nāma bhikkhuno kileso uppanno’’ti saṃvegaṃ katvā vīriyaṃ paggayha vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā maggena kilese samugghāteti. Iti so pajahati nāma. Teyeva cattāro khippaṃ pajahanti nāma. Tattha imasmiṃ sutte, mahāhatthipadopame (ma. ni. 1.288 ādayo), indriyabhāvaneti (ma. ni. 3.453 ādayo) imesu suttesu kiñcāpi tatiyavāro gahito, pañho pana dutiyavāreneva kathitoti veditabbo.

Upadhidukkhassa mūlanti ettha pañca khandhā upadhi nāma. Taṃ dukkhassa mūlanti iti viditvā kilesupadhinā nirupadhi hoti, niggahaṇo nitaṇhoti attho. Upadhisaṅkhaye vimuttoti taṇhakkhaye nibbāne ārammaṇato vimutto.

Upadhi dukkhassa mūla Upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto
commentary_english:
154. cattārome, udāyi, puggalā: What does this show here? Below, it is shown as a group of those who abandon and those who do not abandon, “*te tañceva pajahanti, te tañceva nappajahantī*," but they are not individually distinguished. Now, just as a man who has gone for the sake of materials for construction, having cut down trees in order, and then returning, having abandoned the crooked ones, takes only those suitable to be brought to the work, just so, having discarded those who do not abandon, having made them unusable, he began this teaching to show that there are four types of persons who abandon.

upadhipahānāyā: for the abandoning of the *upadhi*s, namely, for the abandoning of the aggregate-*upadhi*s, the defilement-*upadhi*s, the *abhisaṅkhāra*-*upadhi*s, and the sensual quality-*upadhi*s, of these *upadhi*s. upadhipaṭisaṃyuttā: those associated with the *upadhi*s are those who run after the *upadhi*s. sarasaṅkappā: here, *sarā* are those that flow and rush. saṅkappentīti saṅkappā. Even by two words, it is spoken as thought. samudācarantī: they overcome, they behave having overwhelmed [them]. saṃyutto: united with defilements (*kilesehi saṃyutto*). indriyavemattatā: variety of faculties (*indriyanānattatā*).. kadāci karahacī: after a long time has passed. satisammosā: by forgetfulness of mindfulness. nipāto: falling into an iron cauldron. patanaṃ. Thus, three groups are shown: “*nappajahati, pajahati, khippaṃ pajahatī*”. Among them, four people do not abandon, four people abandon, four people abandon quickly.

upadhipahānāyā upadhipaṭisaṃyuttā sarasaṅkappā samudācarantī saṃyutto indriyavemattatā kadāci karahacī satisammosā nipāto

There, the ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*), the stream-enterer (*srotāpanna*), the once-returner (*sakṛdāgāmin*), the non-returner (*anāgāmin*): these four people do not abandon. Even if the ordinary people etc. do not abandon, how does the non-returner not abandon? Because even he, as long as he has desire for existence (*bhava*), rejoices, “Oh, happiness! Oh, happiness!” Therefore, he does not abandon. These four people abandon. Even if the stream-enterers etc. abandon, how does the ordinary person abandon? For, the one who has started insight (*vipassanā*), when defilements suddenly arise through forgetfulness of mindfulness (*satisammosena*), making agitation, “Defilement has arisen in a *bhikkhu* like me!”, exerting effort, developing insight (*vipassanā*), he uproots the defilements with the path. Thus, he abandons. Those four abandon quickly. There, in this *sūtra*, in the Great Elephant Footprint Simile (*mahāhatthipadopame*) (M. N. 1. 288 *ādayo*), in the development of the faculties (*indriyabhāvaneti*) (M. N. 3. 453 *ādayo*), in these *sūtra*s, although the third time is taken, it should be understood that the question is spoken only in the second time.

upadhidukkhassa mūla: Here, the five aggregates (*skandha*) are called *upadhi*. Having known that it is the root of suffering (*duḥkha*), by the defilement-*upadhi* he becomes free of *upadhi* (*nirupadhi*), the meaning is *niggahaṇa* and *nitaṇha*. upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto: liberated in the destruction of *upadhi*, liberated from the object in *Nirvāṇa* at the destruction of craving (*taṇhā*). Upadhi. At the root of suffering, liberated by the cessation of *upadhi* (*upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto*).

mula_pali: 155. ‘‘Pañca kho ime, udāyi, kāmaguṇā. Katame pañca? Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā, sotaviññeyyā saddā…pe… ghānaviññeyyā gandhā… jivhāviññeyyā rasā… kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Ime kho, udāyi, pañca kāmaguṇā. Yaṃ kho, udāyi, ime pañca kāmaguṇe paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ idaṃ vuccati kāmasukhaṃ miḷhasukhaṃ mīḷhasukhaṃ (sī. pī.) puthujjanasukhaṃ anariyasukhaṃ, na sevitabbaṃ, na bhāvetabbaṃ, na bahulīkātabbaṃ; ‘bhāyitabbaṃ etassa sukhassā’ti vadāmi.
mula_english:
155. “There are, Udayin, these five cords of sensual pleasure (*kāmaguṇā*).

Which five? Forms (*rūpā*) cognizable by the eye (*cakṣurvijñeyyā*) that are wished for (*iṣṭhā*), desired (*kāntā*), agreeable (*manāpā*), pleasing (*piyarūpā*), connected with sensual desire (*kāmūpasaṃhitā*) and provocative of lust (*rajanīyā*). Sounds (*saddā*) cognizable by the ear (*śotravijñeyyā*)… Odours (*gandhā*) cognizable by the nose (*ghānavijñeyyā*)… Flavours (*rasā*) cognizable by the tongue (*jihvāvijñeyyā*)… Tangibles (*sparśa*) cognizable by the body (*kāyavijñeyyā*) that are wished for, desired, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust.

These, Udayin, are the five cords of sensual pleasure.

Now, Udayin, the pleasure (*sukha*) and joy (*somanassa*) that arise dependent on these five cords of sensual pleasure are called sensual pleasure (*kāmasukha*) - a filthy pleasure (*mīḷhasukha*), a coarse pleasure, an ignoble pleasure (*anariyasukha*). It should not be pursued (*sevitabbaṃ*), it should not be developed (*bhāvetabbaṃ*), it should not be cultivated (*bahulīkātabbaṃ*); I say of this kind of pleasure that it should be feared (*bhāyitabbaṃ*).
commentary_pali: 155. Evaṃ cattāro puggale vitthāretvā idāni ye pajahanti, te ‘‘ime nāma ettake kilese pajahanti’’. Ye nappajahanti, tepi ‘‘ime nāma ettake kilese nappajahantī’’ti dassetuṃ pañca kho ime udāyi kāmaguṇātiādimāha. Tattha miḷhasukhanti asucisukhaṃ. Anariyasukhanti anariyehi sevitasukhaṃ. Bhāyitabbanti etassa sukhassa paṭilābhatopi vipākatopi bhāyitabbaṃ. Nekkhammasukhanti kāmato nikkhantasukhaṃ. Pavivekasukhanti gaṇatopi kilesatopi pavivittasukhaṃ. Upasamasukhanti rāgādivūpasamatthāya sukhaṃ. Sambodhasukhanti maggasaṅkhātassa sambodhassa nibbattanatthāya sukhaṃ. Na bhāyitabbanti etassa sukhassa paṭilābhatopi vipākatopi na bhāyitabbaṃ, bhāvetabbamevetaṃ.
commentary_english:
155. Thus, having explained the four types of individuals, now, those who abandon, they are "these, by name, abandon such afflictions."

Those who do not abandon, in order to show that they "these, by name, do not abandon such afflictions," he said, beginning with, "Five, indeed, are these sensual qualities, Udayi."

There, *miḷhasukha* means impure pleasure (*asucisukhaṃ*).

*anariyasukha* means pleasure enjoyed by the ignoble (*anariyehi sevitasukhaṃ*).

*bhāyitabba* means one should be afraid of the acquisition of this pleasure (*sukhassa paṭilābhatopi*) and also of its result (*vipākatopi*).

*nekkhammasukha* means pleasure that has emerged from sensual desire (*kāmato nikkhantasukhaṃ*).

*pavivekasukha* means pleasure secluded from the multitude and also from the afflictions (*gaṇatopi kilesatopi pavivittasukhaṃ*).

*upasamasukha* means pleasure for the stilling of attachment and the like (*rāgādivūpasamatthāya sukhaṃ*).

*sambodhasukha* means pleasure for the sake of the arising of enlightenment known as the path (*maggasaṅkhātassa sambodhassa nibbattanatthāya sukhaṃ*).

*na bhāyitabba* means one should not be afraid of the acquisition of this pleasure and also of its result; rather, this should be cultivated (*bhāvetabbamevetaṃ*).

mula_pali:
156. ‘‘Idhudāyi , bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, pītiyā ca virāgā… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, sukhassa ca pahānā… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ vuccati nekkhammasukhaṃ pavivekasukhaṃ upasamasukhaṃ sambodhasukhaṃ, āsevitabbaṃ, bhāvetabbaṃ, bahulīkātabbaṃ; ‘na bhāyitabbaṃ etassa sukhassā’ti vadāmi.

‘‘Idhudāyi, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; idaṃ kho ahaṃ, udāyi, iñjitasmiṃ vadāmi. Kiñca tattha iñjitasmiṃ? Yadeva tattha vitakkavicārā aniruddhā honti idaṃ tattha iñjitasmiṃ. Idhudāyi, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; idampi kho ahaṃ, udāyi, iñjitasmiṃ vadāmi. Kiñca tattha iñjitasmiṃ? Yadeva tattha pītisukhaṃ aniruddhaṃ hoti idaṃ tattha iñjitasmiṃ. Idhudāyi, bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; idampi kho ahaṃ, udāyi, iñjitasmiṃ vadāmi. Kiñca tattha iñjitasmiṃ? Yadeva tattha upekkhāsukhaṃ aniruddhaṃ hoti idaṃ tattha iñjitasmiṃ. Idhudāyi, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; idaṃ kho ahaṃ, udāyi, aniñjitasmiṃ vadāmi.

‘‘Idhudāyi , bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati; idaṃ kho ahaṃ, udāyi, ‘anala’nti vadāmi, ‘pajahathā’ti vadāmi, ‘samatikkamathā’ti vadāmi. Ko ca tassa samatikkamo? Idhudāyi, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ tassa samatikkamo; idampi kho ahaṃ, udāyi, ‘anala’nti vadāmi, ‘pajahathā’ti vadāmi, ‘samatikkamathā’ti vadāmi. Ko ca tassa samatikkamo? Idhudāyi, bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ tassa samatikkamo; idampi kho ahaṃ, udāyi, ‘anala’nti vadāmi, ‘pajahathā’ti vadāmi, ‘samatikkamathā’ti vadāmi. Ko ca tassa samatikkamo? Idhudāyi, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ tassa samatikkamo; idampi kho ahaṃ, udāyi, ‘anala’nti vadāmi, ‘pajahathā’ti vadāmi, ‘samatikkamathā’ti vadāmi. Ko ca tassa samatikkamo? Idhudāyi, bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ tassa samatikkamo; idampi kho ahaṃ, udāyi, ‘anala’nti vadāmi, ‘pajahathā’ti vadāmi, ‘samatikkamathā’ti vadāmi. Ko ca tassa samatikkamo? Idhudāyi, bhikkhu sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ tassa samatikkamo ; idampi kho ahaṃ, udāyi, ‘anala’nti vadāmi, ‘pajahathā’ti vadāmi, ‘samatikkamathā’ti vadāmi. Ko ca tassa samatikkamo? Idhudāyi, bhikkhu sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ tassa samatikkamo; idampi kho ahaṃ, udāyi, ‘anala’nti vadāmi, ‘pajahathā’ti vadāmi, ‘samatikkamathā’ti vadāmi. Ko ca tassa samatikkamo? Idhudāyi, bhikkhu sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ tassa samatikkamo; idampi kho ahaṃ, udāyi, ‘anala’nti vadāmi, ‘pajahathā’ti vadāmi, ‘samatikkamathā’ti vadāmi. Ko ca tassa samatikkamo? Idhudāyi, bhikkhu sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ tassa samatikkamo; iti kho ahaṃ, udāyi, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassapi pahānaṃ vadāmi. Passasi no tvaṃ, udāyi, taṃ saṃyojanaṃ aṇuṃ vā thūlaṃ vā yassāhaṃ no pahānaṃ vadāmī’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā udāyī bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Laṭukikopamasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.
mula_english:
156. Here, Udayin, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the first *jhāna*… With the stilling of applied and sustained thought, he enters upon and abides in the second *jhāna*… With the fading away as well of rapture… he enters upon and abides in the third *jhāna*…With the abandoning of pleasure and pain… he enters upon and abides in the fourth *jhāna*.

This is called the bliss of renunciation (*nekkhammasukhaṃ*), the bliss of seclusion (*pavivekasukhaṃ*), the bliss of peace (*upasamasukhaṃ*), the bliss of enlightenment (*sambodhasukhaṃ*). I say of this kind of pleasure that it should be pursued (*āsevitabbaṃ*), that it should be developed (*bhāvetabbaṃ*), that it should be cultivated (*bahulīkātabbaṃ*), and that it should not be feared (*na bhāyitabbaṃ etassa sukhassā’ti vadāmi*).

Here, Udayin, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the first *jhāna*; Now this, I say, belongs to the perturbable (*iñjitasmiṃ*).

And what belongs to the perturbable (*iñjitasmiṃ*) therein? The applied thought (*vitakka*) and sustained thought (*vicāra*) that have not ceased therein, that is what belongs to the perturbable (*iñjitasmiṃ*).

Here, Udayin, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought, a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the second *jhāna*… Now this, I say, also belongs to the perturbable (*iñjitasmiṃ*).

And what belongs to the perturbable (*iñjitasmiṃ*) therein? The rapture and pleasure (*pītisukhaṃ*) that have not ceased therein, that is what belongs to the perturbable (*iñjitasmiṃ*).

Here, Udayin, with the fading away as well of rapture…a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the third *jhāna*…Now this, I say, also belongs to the perturbable (*iñjitasmiṃ*).

And what belongs to the perturbable (*iñjitasmiṃ*) therein? The equanimity and pleasure (*upekkhāsukhaṃ*) that have not ceased therein, that is what belongs to the perturbable (*iñjitasmiṃ*).

Here, Udayin, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain… a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the fourth *jhāna*… Now this, I say, belongs to the imperturbable (*aniñjitasmiṃ*).

Here, Udayin, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the first *jhāna*… That, I say, is not enough (*anala*). Abandon it (*pajahatha*), I say; surmount it (*samatikkamatha*), I say.

And what surmounts it (*samatikkama*)? Here, Udayin, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought, a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the second *jhāna*… That surmounts it (*samatikkama*). But that too, I say, is not enough (*anala*). Abandon it (*pajahatha*), I say; surmount it (*samatikkamatha*), I say.

And what surmounts it (*samatikkama*)? Here, Udayin, with the fading away as well of rapture…a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the third *jhāna*…That surmounts it (*samatikkama*). But that too, I say, is not enough (*anala*). Abandon it (*pajahatha*), I say; surmount it (*samatikkamatha*), I say.

And what surmounts it (*samatikkama*)? Here, Udayin, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain…a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the fourth *jhāna*… That surmounts it (*samatikkama*). But that too, I say, is not enough (*anala*). Abandon it (*pajahatha*), I say; surmount it (*samatikkamatha*), I say.

And what surmounts it (*samatikkama*)? Here, Udayin, by completely surmounting all perceptions of form (*rūpasaññānaṃ*), with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance (*paṭighasaññānaṃ*), and not attending to perceptions of diversity (*nānattasaññānaṃ*), aware that ‘there is infinite space,’ a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the base of infinite space (*ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ*). That surmounts it (*samatikkama*). But that too, I say, is not enough (*anala*). Abandon it (*pajahatha*), I say; surmount it (*samatikkamatha*), I say.

And what surmounts it (*samatikkama*)? Here, Udayin, by completely surmounting the base of infinite space (*ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ*), aware that ‘there is infinite consciousness,’ a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the base of infinite consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ*). That surmounts it (*samatikkama*). But that too, I say, is not enough (*anala*). Abandon it (*pajahatha*), I say; surmount it (*samatikkamatha*), I say.

And what surmounts it (*samatikkama*)? Here, Udayin, by completely surmounting the base of infinite consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ*), aware that ‘there is nothing,’ a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ*). That surmounts it (*samatikkama*). But that too, I say, is not enough (*anala*). Abandon it (*pajahatha*), I say; surmount it (*samatikkamatha*), I say.

And what surmounts it (*samatikkama*)? Here, Udayin, by completely surmounting the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ*), a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ*). That surmounts it (*samatikkama*). But that too, I say, is not enough (*anala*). Abandon it (*pajahatha*), I say; surmount it (*samatikkamatha*), I say.

And what surmounts it (*samatikkama*)? Here, Udayin, by completely surmounting the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ*), a *bhikkhu* enters and abides in the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ*). That surmounts it (*samatikkama*). Thus I speak of the abandoning even of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassapi pahānaṃ vadāmi*).

Do you see, Udayin, any fetter (*saṃyojanaṃ*), small or great, of whose abandoning I do not speak?” “No, venerable sir.”

Thus spoke the Lord. The venerable Udayin was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

The Laṭukikopama Sutta is finished, the sixth.
commentary_pali:
156.Iñjitasmiṃvadāmīti iñjanaṃ calanaṃ phandananti vadāmi. Kiñca tattha iñjitasminti kiñca tattha iñjitaṃ. Idaṃ tattha iñjitasminti ye ete aniruddhā vitakkavicārā, idaṃ tattha iñjitaṃ. Dutiyatatiyajjhānesupi eseva nayo. Aniñjitasmiṃ vadāmīti idaṃ catutthajjhānaṃ aniñjanaṃ acalanaṃ nipphandananti vadāmi.

Analanti vadāmīti akattabbaālayanti vadāmi, taṇhālayo ettha na uppādetabboti dasseti. Atha vā analaṃ apariyattaṃ, na ettāvatā alametanti sanniṭṭhānaṃ kātabbanti vadāmi. Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassāpīti evarūpāyapi santāya samāpattiyā pahānameva vadāmi. Aṇuṃ vā thūlaṃ vāti khuddakaṃ vā mahantaṃ vā appasāvajjaṃ vā mahāsāvajjaṃ vā. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānameva. Desanā pana neyyapuggalassa vasena arahattanikūṭeneva niṭṭhāpitāti.

Analanti vadāmī Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassāpī Aṇuṃ vā thūlaṃ vā

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Laṭukikopamasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
156. *iñjitasmiṃ* I say, is agitation, movement, tremor.

*kiñca tattha iñjitasmiṃ* means what is agitated there.

*idaṃ tattha iñjitasmiṃ* means these applied thought and sustained thought that have not ceased, this is what is agitated there.

And the same rule applies to the second and third *jhānas*.

*aniñjitasmiṃ vadāmī* means this fourth *jhāna* is non-agitation, non-movement, non-tremor.

*analanti vadāmī* means non-attachment, I say; craving is attachment, here, it shows that it should not be produced.

Or, *analaṃ* is not enough, not complete, not that much is enough, I say that ascertainment should be done.

*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassāpī* means even for such attainment of the realm of neither perception nor non-perception, I speak only of abandoning.

*aṇuṃ vā thūlaṃ vā* means whether small or large, minor offence or major offence.

The rest is clear throughout.

But the teaching is concluded with its culmination in arahatship for the person who needs guidance.

*analanti vadāmī*
*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassāpī* *aṇuṃ vā thūlaṃ vā*

The *Papañcasūdanī*, commentary on the *Majjhimanikāya*

The commentary on the *Laṭukikopamasutta* is finished.

mula_pali: 157. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā cātumāyaṃ viharati āmalakīvane. Tena kho pana samayena sāriputtamoggallānappamukhāni pañcamattāni bhikkhusatāni cātumaṃ anuppattāni honti bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Te ca āgantukā bhikkhū nevāsikehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ paṭisammodamānā senāsanāni paññāpayamānā pattacīvarāni paṭisāmayamānā uccāsaddā mahāsaddā ahesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ke panete, ānanda, uccāsaddā mahāsaddā, kevaṭṭā maññe macchavilope’’ti? ‘‘Etāni, bhante, sāriputtamoggallānappamukhāni pañcamattāni bhikkhusatāni cātumaṃ anuppattāni bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Te āgantukā bhikkhū nevāsikehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ paṭisammodamānā senāsanāni paññāpayamānā pattacīvarāni paṭisāmayamānā uccāsaddā mahāsaddā’’ti. ‘‘Tenahānanda, mama vacanena te bhikkhū āmantehi – ‘satthā āyasmante āmantetī’’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca – ‘‘satthā āyasmante āmantetī’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato ānandassa paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho te bhikkhū bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘kiṃ nu tumhe, bhikkhave, uccāsaddā mahāsaddā, kevaṭṭā maññe macchavilope’’ti? ‘‘Imāni, bhante, sāriputtamoggallānappamukhāni pañcamattāni bhikkhusatāni cātumaṃ anuppattāni bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Teme āgantukā bhikkhū nevāsikehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ paṭisammodamānā senāsanāni paññāpayamānā pattacīvarāni paṭisāmayamānā uccāsaddā mahāsaddā’’ti. ‘‘Gacchatha, bhikkhave, paṇāmemi vo, na vo mama santike vatthabba’’nti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā senāsanaṃ saṃsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya pakkamiṃsu.
mula_english:
THUS HAVE I HEARD. On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Catuma in a myrobalan (*āmalakī*) grove.

Now on that occasion five hundred *bhikkhus* headed by the venerable *Sāriputta* and *Mahā Moggallāna* had come to Catuma to see the Blessed One.

And these visiting *bhikkhus*, while exchanging greetings with the resident *bhikkhus*, preparing resting places, and putting away their bowls and outer robes (*pattacīvara*), were very loud and noisy.

Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable *Ānanda*, “Ānanda, who are these making a great noise, so loud, like fishermen haggling over fish?”

“[They are], venerable sir, five hundred *bhikkhus* headed by *Sāriputta* and *Moggallāna* who have arrived at Catuma to see the Blessed One. These visiting *bhikkhus*, while exchanging greetings with the resident *bhikkhus*, preparing resting places and putting away their bowls and outer robes (*pattacīvara*), are very loud and noisy.”

“In that case, Ānanda, tell those *bhikkhus* in my name, ‘The Teacher summons the venerable ones.’”

“As you say, venerable sir,” replied the venerable Ānanda to the Blessed One. He then went to those *bhikkhus* and said, “The Teacher summons the venerable ones.”

“Very well, friend,” those *bhikkhus* replied to the venerable Ānanda. They then went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, sat down at one side.

As they were sitting to one side, the Blessed One said to the *bhikkhus*, “Why are you making such a loud and great noise, like fishermen haggling over fish?”

“Venerable sir, [they are] these five hundred *bhikkhus* headed by *Sāriputta* and *Moggallāna* who have arrived at Catuma to see the Blessed One. And it was while we visiting *bhikkhus* were exchanging greetings with the resident *bhikkhus*, preparing resting places, and putting away our bowls and outer robes (*pattacīvara*) that we were very loud and noisy.”

“Go away, *bhikkhus*, I dismiss you. You are not to stay in my vicinity.”

“As you say, venerable sir,” those *bhikkhus* replied to the Blessed One. They rose from their seats, and after paying homage to the Blessed One, keeping him on their right, they put away the things in their resting places, and taking their bowls and outer robes (*pattacīvara*), they departed.
commentary_pali:
157.Evaṃme sutanti cātumasuttaṃ. Tattha cātumāyanti evaṃnāmake gāme. Pañcamattāni bhikkhusatānīti adhunā pabbajitānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pañca satāni. Therā kira cintesuṃ – ‘‘ime kulaputtā dasabalaṃ adisvāva pabbajitā, etesaṃ bhagavantaṃ dassessāma, bhagavato santike dhammaṃ sutvā attano attano yathāupanissayena patiṭṭhahissantī’’ti. Tasmā te bhikkhū gahetvā āgatā. Paṭisammodamānāti ‘‘kaccāvuso, khamanīya’’ntiādiṃ paṭisanthārakathaṃ kurumānā. Senāsanāni paññāpayamānāti attano attano ācariyupajjhāyānaṃ vasanaṭṭhānāni pucchitvā dvāravātapānāni vivaritvā mañcapīṭhakaṭasārakādīni nīharitvā papphoṭetvā yathāṭṭhāne saṇṭhāpayamānā. Pattacīvarāni paṭisāmayamānāti, bhante, idaṃ me pattaṃ ṭhapetha, idaṃ cīvaraṃ, idaṃ thālakaṃ, idaṃ udakatumbaṃ, imaṃ kattarayaṭṭhinti evaṃ samaṇaparikkhāre saṅgopayamānā.

Uccāsaddā mahāsaddāti uddhaṃ uggatattā uccaṃ, patthaṭattā mahantaṃ avinibbhogasaddaṃ karontā. Kevaṭṭā maññe macchavilopeti kevaṭṭānaṃ macchapacchiṭhapitaṭṭhāne mahājano sannipatitvā – ‘‘idha aññaṃ ekaṃ macchaṃ dehi, ekaṃ macchaphālaṃ dehi, etassa te mahā dinno, mayhaṃ khuddako’’ti evaṃ uccāsaddaṃ mahāsaddaṃ karonti. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Macchagahaṇatthaṃ jāle pakkhittepi tasmiṃ ṭhāne kevaṭṭā ceva aññe ca ‘‘paviṭṭho na paviṭṭho, gahito na gahito’’ti mahāsaddaṃ karonti. Tampi sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Paṇāmemīti nīharāmi. Na vo mama santike vatthabbanti tumhe mādisassa buddhassa vasanaṭṭhānaṃ āgantvā evaṃ mahāsaddaṃ karotha, attano dhammatāya vasantā kiṃ nāma sāruppaṃ karissatha, tumhādisānaṃ mama santike vasanakiccaṃ natthīti dīpeti. Tesu ekabhikkhupi ‘‘bhagavā tumhe mahāsaddamattakena amhe paṇāmethā’’ti vā aññaṃ vā kiñci vattuṃ nāsakkhi, sabbe bhagavato vacanaṃ sampaṭicchantā ‘‘evaṃ, bhante,’’ti vatvā nikkhamiṃsu. Evaṃ pana tesaṃ ahosi ‘‘mayaṃ satthāraṃ passissāma, dhammakathaṃ sossāma, satthu santike vasissāmāti āgatā. Evarūpassa pana garuno satthu santikaṃ āgantvā mahāsaddaṃ karimhā, amhākameva dosoyaṃ, paṇāmitamhā, na no laddhaṃ bhagavato santike vatthuṃ, na suvaṇṇavaṇṇasarīraṃ oloketuṃ, na madhurassarena dhammaṃ sotu’’nti. Te balavadomanassajātā hutvā pakkamiṃsu.

Uccāsaddā mahāsaddā Kevaṭṭā maññe macchavilope Paṇāmemī Na vo mama santike vatthabba
commentary_english:
157. Thus I have heard (evaṃ me suta) – the Cātuma Sutta.

There, "in Cātumā" means in a village of that name.

"Five hundred monks" (pañcamattāni bhikkhusatānī) means five hundred monks who had recently gone forth.

The elders considered, "These young men have gone forth without seeing the Ten-Powered One. We will show them the Blessed One. Having heard the Dharma in the presence of the Blessed One, they will be established according to their potential."

Therefore, those monks came, having taken [them].

“Exchanging greetings” (paṭisammodamānā) means making polite conversation, such as, “Is it alright, friend? Is it bearable?”

“Preparing lodgings" (senāsanāni paññāpayamānā) means asking about the dwelling places of their respective teachers and preceptors, opening the doors and windows, taking out couches, chairs, and the like, shaking them off, and setting them up in their proper places.

“Putting away bowls and robes” (pattacīvarāni paṭisāmayamānā) means, “Venerable sir, put my bowl here, this is my robe, this is my dish, this is my water pot, this is my needle case,” thus gathering the requisites of a renunciate.

“Loud noises, great noises” (uccāsaddā mahāsaddā) means making a loud, great, unrestrained noise because it rises up on high and spreads out.

"Fishermen, I think, at a fish market" (kevaṭṭā maññe macchavilope) means that in a place where fishermen have set up a fish stall, a great crowd gathers and makes loud noises, saying, "Give me another fish, give me a piece of fish, this one is big for you, mine is small."

This was said with reference to that.

Even when a net has been cast in that place for catching fish, the fishermen and others make a loud noise, saying, "Entered or not entered, caught or not caught."

This too was said with reference to that.

"I drive them away" (paṇāmemī) means I send them out.

"You should not live in my presence" (na vo mama santike vatthabba) means, "Having come to the dwelling place of a Buddha like me, you make such a loud noise. While living according to your own nature, what kind of seemliness would you do? There is no need for people like you to live in my presence," he indicates.

Even one monk among them could not say anything, "The Blessed One is driving us away with just a loud noise", and all, accepting the word of the Blessed One, said, "Yes, venerable sir," and departed.

Thus, it occurred to them, "We have come thinking, 'We will see the Teacher, we will hear the Dharma talk, we will live in the presence of the Teacher.'

Having come into the presence of such a revered Teacher, we have made a loud noise. This is our own fault; we have been driven away. We have not obtained to live in the presence of the Blessed One, to behold his body of golden hue, to hear the Dharma with its sweet voice."

Having become greatly dejected, they departed.

Loud noises, great noises. Fishermen, I think, at a fish market. I drive them away. You should not live in my presence.

mula_pali: 158. Tena kho pana samayena cātumeyyakā sakyā santhāgāre sandhāgāre (ka.) sannipatitā honti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Addasaṃsu kho cātumeyyakā sakyā te bhikkhū dūratova āgacchante; disvāna yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – ‘‘handa, kahaṃ pana tumhe āyasmanto gacchathā’’ti? ‘‘Bhagavatā kho, āvuso, bhikkhusaṅgho paṇāmito’’ti. ‘‘Tenahāyasmanto muhuttaṃ nisīdatha, appeva nāma mayaṃ sakkuṇeyyāma bhagavantaṃ pasādetu’’nti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho te bhikkhū cātumeyyakānaṃ sakyānaṃ paccassosuṃ. Atha kho cātumeyyakā sakyā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho cātumeyyakā sakyā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘abhinandatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ; abhivadatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhante , bhagavatā pubbe bhikkhusaṅgho anuggahito, evameva bhagavā etarahi anuggaṇhātu bhikkhusaṅghaṃ. Santettha, bhante, bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ. Tesaṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya alabhantānaṃ siyā aññathattaṃ, siyā vipariṇāmo. Seyyathāpi, bhante, bījānaṃ taruṇānaṃ udakaṃ alabhantānaṃ siyā aññathattaṃ siyā vipariṇāmo; evameva kho, bhante, santettha bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ, tesaṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya alabhantānaṃ siyā aññathattaṃ, siyā vipariṇāmo. Seyyathāpi, bhante, vacchassa taruṇassa mātaraṃ apassantassa siyā aññathattaṃ, siyā vipariṇāmo; evameva kho, bhante, santettha bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ, tesaṃ bhagavantaṃ apassantānaṃ siyā aññathattaṃ, siyā vipariṇāmo. Abhinandatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ; abhivadatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhante, bhagavatā pubbe bhikkhusaṅgho anuggahito; evameva bhagavā etarahi anuggaṇhātu bhikkhusaṅgha’’nti.
mula_english:
158. At that time, the Śākyas of Cātumā, having gathered in the assembly hall for some business or other (kenacideva karaṇīyena), saw those monks coming from afar. Seeing them, they approached them. Approaching the monks, they said this: “Well, where are you venerable ones going?” “The Blessed One has set out with the *bhikṣusaṃgha* (community of monks), friend.”

“Then, venerable ones, be seated for a moment. Perhaps we shall be able to restore the Blessed One’s confidence.”

“Yes, friends,” those monks replied to the Śākyas of Cātumā.

Then the Śākyas of Cātumā approached the Blessed One. Having approached the Blessed One, they paid homage and sat down on one side. Seated on one side, the Śākyas of Cātumā said this to the Blessed One: “May the Blessed One delight in the *bhikkhusaṃgha*; may the Blessed One welcome the *bhikkhusaṃgha*.

“Just as, venerable sir, the *bhikkhusaṃgha* was shown compassion by the Blessed One in the past, so too may the Blessed One show compassion towards the *bhikkhusaṃgha* now.

“Venerable sir, there are new *bhikkhus* here, recently gone forth, recently come to this Dharma and Discipline (dhammavinaya). If they do not get to see the Blessed One, there may take place in them some change or alteration.

“Just as, venerable sir, when young seedlings get no water there may take place in them some change or alteration, so too, venerable sir, there are new *bhikkhus* here, recently gone forth, recently come to this Dharma and Discipline. If they do not get to see the Blessed One, there may take place in them some change or alteration.

“Just as, venerable sir, when a young calf does not see its mother there may take place in it some change or alteration, so too, venerable sir, there are new *bhikkhus* here, recently gone forth, recently come to this Dharma and Discipline. If they do not get to see the Blessed One, there may take place in them some change or alteration.

“May the Blessed One delight in the *bhikkhusaṃgha*; may the Blessed One welcome the *bhikkhusaṃgha*. Just as, venerable sir, the *bhikkhusaṃgha* was shown compassion by the Blessed One in the past; so too may the Blessed One show compassion towards the *bhikkhusaṃgha* now.”
commentary_pali: 158.Tenupasaṅkamiṃsūti te kira sakyā āgamanasamayepi te bhikkhū tattheva nisinnā passiṃsu. Atha nesaṃ etadahosi – ‘‘kiṃ nu kho ete bhikkhū pavisitvāva paṭinivattā, jānissāma taṃ kāraṇa’’nti cintetvā yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Handāti vavassaggatthe nipāto. Kahaṃ pana tumheti tumhe idāneva āgantvā kahaṃ gacchatha, kiṃ tumhākaṃ koci upaddavo, udāhu dasabalassāti? Tesaṃ pana bhikkhūnaṃ, – ‘‘āvuso, mayaṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya āgatā, diṭṭho no bhagavā, idāni attano vasanaṭṭhānaṃ gacchāmā’’ti kiñcāpi evaṃ vacanaparihāro atthi, evarūpaṃ pana lesakappaṃ akatvā yathābhūtameva ārocetvā bhagavatā kho, āvuso, bhikkhusaṅgho paṇāmitoti āhaṃsu. Te pana rājāno sāsane dhuravahā, tasmā cintesuṃ – ‘‘dvīhi aggasāvakehi saddhiṃ pañcasu bhikkhusatesu gacchantesu bhagavato pādamūlaṃ vigacchissati, imesaṃ nivattanākāraṃ karissāmā’’ti. Evaṃ cintetvā tena hāyasmantotiādimāhaṃsu. Tesupi bhikkhūsu ‘‘mayaṃ mahāsaddamattakena paṇāmitā, na mayaṃ jīvituṃ asakkontā pabbajitā’’ti ekabhikkhupi paṭippharito nāma nāhosi, sabbe pana samakaṃyeva, ‘‘evamāvuso,’’ti sampaṭicchiṃsu.
commentary_english:
158. "Because they approached": it seems that the Śākyas saw those monks sitting right there, even at the time of their arrival. Then it occurred to them: "Why have these monks entered and returned? Let us find out the reason," and having thought this, they approached those monks.

"Indeed": [this] is a particle [used] in the sense of encouragement.

"Where are you going?": Where are you going, having just arrived now? What trouble is yours, or is it the power of the Ten? Then, those monks [replied]: "Friends, we have come to see the Blessed One (Bhagavat). We have seen the Blessed One. Now we are going to our own dwelling place." Although there was such circumlocution, having told the truth as it was, without doing anything deceptive, they said, "Friends, the community of monks (bhikkhusaṃgha) has been dismissed by the Blessed One (Bhagavat)."

Those kings, however, were bearers of the burden in the teaching (śāsana), therefore they thought: "When the five hundred monks, together with the two foremost disciples (agga-sāvaka), are going, [their respect] will disappear at the feet of the Blessed One (Bhagavat). We will make a way to turn them back."

Having thought thus, they said, "Then, venerable sirs..." and so on.

Even among those monks, not even one named [so-and-so] was offended [by the fact that] "we were dismissed by a mere great noise; we did not go forth being unable to live." But all together, they accepted, "Yes, friend."

mula_pali: 159. Atha kho brahmā sahampati bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ sammiñjitaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva – brahmaloke antarahito bhagavato purato pāturahosi. Atha kho brahmā sahampati ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘abhinandatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ; abhivadatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhante, bhagavatā pubbe bhikkhusaṅgho anuggahito; evameva bhagavā etarahi anuggaṇhātu bhikkhusaṅghaṃ. Santettha, bhante, bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ, tesaṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya alabhantānaṃ siyā aññathattaṃ, siyā vipariṇāmo. Seyyathāpi, bhante, bījānaṃ taruṇānaṃ udakaṃ alabhantānaṃ siyā aññathattaṃ, siyā vipariṇāmo; evameva kho, bhante, santettha bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ, tesaṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya alabhantānaṃ siyā aññathattaṃ, siyā vipariṇāmo. Seyyathāpi bhante, vacchassa taruṇassa mātaraṃ apassantassa siyā aññathattaṃ, siyā vipariṇāmo; evameva kho, bhante, santettha bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ, tesaṃ bhagavantaṃ apassantānaṃ siyā aññathattaṃ, siyā vipariṇāmo. Abhinandatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ; abhivadatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhante, bhagavatā pubbe bhikkhusaṅgho anuggahito; evameva bhagavā etarahi anuggaṇhātu bhikkhusaṅgha’’nti.
mula_english:
159. Then Brahmā Sahampati, knowing with his mind the thought in the Blessed One’s mind, just as quickly as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm, vanished from the Brahmā world and appeared before the Blessed One.

Then Brahmā Sahampati, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, extended his joined palms towards the Blessed One and said this to him: “Venerable sir, may the Blessed One delight in the *bhikṣu-saṃgha*; venerable sir, may the Blessed One welcome the *bhikṣu-saṃgha*.
