Just as, venerable sir, the *bhikṣu-saṃgha* was previously favored by the Blessed One, so too, may the Blessed One show compassion towards the *bhikṣu-saṃgha* now. Venerable sir, there are new *bhikṣus* here, recently gone forth, newly come to this *dharma-vinaya*, if they do not have the opportunity to see the Blessed One, there may take place in them some change or alteration.

Just as, venerable sir, when young seedlings do not get water there may take place in them some change or alteration; so too, venerable sir, there are new *bhikṣus* here, recently gone forth, newly come to this *dharma-vinaya*, if they do not have the opportunity to see the Blessed One, there may take place in them some change or alteration.

Just as, venerable sir, when a young calf does not see its mother there may take place in it some change or alteration; so too, venerable sir, there are new *bhikṣus* here, recently gone forth, newly come to this *dharma-vinaya*, if they do not have the opportunity to see the Blessed One, there may take place in them some change or alteration.

Venerable sir, may the Blessed One delight in the *bhikṣu-saṃgha*; venerable sir, may the Blessed One welcome the *bhikṣu-saṃgha*. Just as, venerable sir, the *bhikṣu-saṃgha* was previously favored by the Blessed One, so too, may the Blessed One show compassion towards the *bhikṣu-saṃgha*.”
commentary_pali: 159.Abhinandatūti bhikkhusaṅghassa āgamanaṃ icchanto abhinandatu. Abhivadatūti etu bhikkhusaṅghoti evaṃ cittaṃ uppādento abhivadatu. Anuggahitoti āmisānuggahena ca dhammānuggahena ca anuggahito. Aññathattanti dasabalassa dassanaṃ na labhāmāti pasādaññathattaṃ bhaveyya. Vipariṇāmoti pasādaññathattena vibbhamantānaṃ vipariṇāmaññathattaṃ bhaveyya. Bījānaṃ taruṇānanti taruṇasassānaṃ. Siyā aññathattanti udakavārakāle udakaṃ alabhantānaṃ milātabhāvena aññathattaṃ bhaveyya, sussitvā milātabhāvaṃ āpajjanena vipariṇāmo bhaveyya. Vacchakassa pana khīrapipāsāya sussanaṃ aññathattaṃ nāma, sussitvā kālakiriyā vipariṇāmo nāma.
commentary_english:
159. “*Abhinandatū*”: Wishing for the coming of the *bhikkhu-saṅgha*, let him rejoice.

"*Abhivadatū*": "Let the *bhikkhu-saṅgha* come!" Thus, generating the thought, let him address them.

"*Anuggahito*": Being supported by material support (*āmisānuggahena*) and being supported by Dharma support (*dhammānuggahena*), he is supported.

"*Aññathatta*": Not obtaining the sight (*dassana*) of the Ten Powers (*dasabalassa*), there would be a change in faith (*pasādaññathattaṃ*).

"*Vipariṇāmo*": Through a change in faith (*pasādaññathattena*) for those who are bewildered (*vibbhamantānaṃ*), there would be a change of change (*vipariṇāmaññathattaṃ*).

"*Bījānaṃ taruṇāna*": [This refers to] young crops (*taruṇasassānaṃ*).

"*Siyā aññathatta*": At the time of the water turn (*udakavārakāle*), not obtaining water (*udakaṃ alabhantānaṃ*), there would be a change due to a withered state (*milātabhāvena aññathattaṃ*); having withered, by approaching a withered state (*milātabhāvaṃ āpajjanena*), there would be change (*vipariṇāmo*).

For a calf (*vacchakassa*), with thirst for milk (*khīrapipāsāya*), drying up (*sussanaṃ*) is called change (*aññathattaṃ nāma*), having dried up, death (*kālakiriyā*) is called transformation (*vipariṇāmo nāma*).

mula_pali: 160. Asakkhiṃsu kho cātumeyyakā ca sakyā brahmā ca sahampati bhagavantaṃ pasādetuṃ bījūpamena ca taruṇūpamena ca. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘uṭṭhethāvuso, gaṇhatha pattacīvaraṃ. Pasādito bhagavā cātumeyyakehi ca sakyehi brahmunā ca sahampatinā bījūpamena ca taruṇūpamena cā’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pattacīvaramādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘kinti te, sāriputta, ahosi mayā bhikkhusaṅghe paṇāmite’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ kho me, bhante, ahosi – ‘bhagavatā bhikkhusaṅgho paṇāmito. Appossukko dāni bhagavā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ anuyutto viharissati, mayampi dāni appossukkā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāramanuyuttā viharissāmā’’’ti. ‘‘Āgamehi tvaṃ, sāriputta, āgamehi tvaṃ, sāriputta, diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāra’’nti. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘kinti te, moggallāna, ahosi mayā bhikkhusaṅghe paṇāmite’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ kho me, bhante, ahosi – ‘bhagavatā bhikkhusaṅgho paṇāmito. Appossukko dāni bhagavā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ anuyutto viharissati, ahañca dāni āyasmā ca sāriputto bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pariharissāmā’’’ti. ‘‘Sādhu sādhu, moggallāna! Ahaṃ vā hi, moggallāna , bhikkhusaṅghaṃ parihareyyaṃ sāriputtamoggallānā vā’’ti.
mula_english:
160. The Sakyans of Catuma and the Brahma Sahampati were able to restore the Blessed One’s confidence with the similes of the seedlings (*bījūpamena*) and the young calf (*taruṇūpamena*).

Then the venerable Mahā Moggallāna addressed the bhikkhus thus: “Get up, friends, take your bowls (*pattacīvaraṃ*) and outer robes (*pattacīvaraṃ*). The Blessed One’s confidence has been restored by the Sakyans of Catuma and the Brahma Sahampati with the similes of the seedlings and the young calf.”

“Yes, friend,” they replied, and taking their bowls and outer robes, they went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, sat down at one side.

The Blessed One then said to the venerable Sariputta, who was sitting to one side: “What was your thought, Sariputta, when I dismissed the Saṅgha of bhikkhus?”

“This was my thought, lord: ‘The Saṅgha of bhikkhus has been dismissed by the Blessed One. The Blessed One will now abide inactive, devoted to pleasant abiding here and now (*diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ*); and we too shall now abide inactive, devoted to pleasant abiding here and now.’”

“Hold on, Sāriputta. Hold on, Sāriputta, to pleasant abiding here and now (*diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ*).”

Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Mahā Moggallāna: “What was your thought, Moggallāna, when I dismissed the Saṅgha of bhikkhus?”

“This was my thought, lord: ‘The Saṅgha of bhikkhus has been dismissed by the Blessed One. The Blessed One will now abide inactive, devoted to pleasant abiding here and now (*diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ*). Now the venerable Sariputta and I shall lead the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.’”

“Good, good, Moggallāna! Either I shall lead the Saṅgha of bhikkhus or else Sariputta and Moggallana shall lead it.”
commentary_pali: 160.Pasādito bhagavāti thero kira tattha nisinnova dibbacakkhunā brahmānaṃ āgataṃ addasa , dibbāya sotadhātuyā ca āyācanasaddaṃ suṇi, cetopariyañāṇena bhagavato pasannabhāvaṃ aññāsi. Tasmā – ‘‘kañci bhikkhuṃ pesetvā pakkosiyamānānaṃ gamanaṃ nāma na phāsukaṃ, yāva satthā na peseti, tāvadeva gamissāmā’’ti maññamāno evamāha. Appossukkoti aññesu kiccesu anussukko hutvā. Diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāranti phalasamāpattivihāraṃ anuyutto maññe bhagavā viharitukāmo, so idāni yathāruciyā viharissatīti evaṃ me ahosīti vadati. Mayampidānīti mayaṃ paraṃ ovadamānā vihārato nikkaḍḍhitā, kiṃ amhākaṃ parovādena. Idāni mayampi diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāreneva viharissāmāti dīpeti. Thero imasmiṃ ṭhāne viraddho attano bhārabhāvaṃ na aññāsi. Ayañhi bhikkhusaṅgho dvinnampi mahātherānaṃ bhāro, tena naṃ paṭisedhento bhagavā āgamehītiādimāha. Mahāmoggallānatthero pana attano bhārabhāvaṃ aññāsi. Tenassa bhagavā sādhukāraṃ adāsi.
commentary_english: 160. pasādito bhagavāti: The elder, it seems, while sitting there, saw the arriving Brahmā with his divine eye. 0125"/>, he heard the sound of requesting with his divine ear-element, and he knew the state of serenity of the Blessed One with his mind-penetrating knowledge. Therefore, thinking, "Going when some monk has been sent to call us is not comfortable; we will only go when the Teacher sends for us," he said thus. appossukkoti: Having become unzealous in other tasks. diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāranti: "The Blessed One, I think, is intent on the dwelling in the bliss of the here-and-now and wishes to dwell in the attainment of fruition; now he will dwell as he pleases," thus he speaks, saying, "Thus it occurred to me." mayampidānīti: "We, being those who admonish others, are driven out of the monastery; what is the use of our admonishing others?" Now, he reveals, "We too will dwell just in the dwelling in the bliss of the here-and-now." The elder, being corrupt in this place, did not know his own burden. Indeed, this monastic community is a burden to both the great elders, therefore, as he was preventing him, the Blessed One said, "āgamehīti," and so on. But Mahāmoggallānatthero knew his own burden. Therefore, the Blessed One gave him approval.

mula_pali: 161. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘cattārimāni, bhikkhave, bhayāni udakorohante pāṭikaṅkhitabbāni. Katamāni cattāri? Ūmibhayaṃ ummībhayaṃ (syā. kaṃ.), kumbhīlabhayaṃ, āvaṭṭabhayaṃ, susukābhayaṃ – imāni, bhikkhave, cattāri bhayāni udakorohante pāṭikaṅkhitabbāni. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, cattārimāni bhayāni idhekacce puggale imasmiṃ dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajite pāṭikaṅkhitabbāni. Katamāni cattāri? Ūmibhayaṃ, kumbhīlabhayaṃ, āvaṭṭabhayaṃ, susukābhayaṃ.
mula_english:
Then the Blessed One addressed the *bhikṣus* (monks) thus: "These four fears are to be expected by those who go down to the water. What are the four? The fear of waves (*ūmibhaya*), the fear of crocodiles (*kumbhīlabhaya*), the fear of whirlpools (*āvaṭṭabhaya*), and the fear of sharks (*susukābhaya*) - these are the four fears to be expected by those who go down to the water.

"Just so, *bhikṣus*, these four fears are to be expected in this *dharma* and *vinaya* (doctrine and discipline) by certain individuals who have gone forth from the household life into homelessness. What are the four? The fear of waves (*ūmibhaya*), the fear of crocodiles (*kumbhīlabhaya*), the fear of whirlpools (*āvaṭṭabhaya*), and the fear of sharks (*susukābhaya*)."
commentary_pali: 161.Cattārimāni, bhikkhaveti kasmā ārabhi? Imasmiṃ sāsane cattāri bhayāni. Yo tāni abhīto hoti, so imasmiṃ sāsane patiṭṭhātuṃ sakkoti. Itaro pana na sakkotīti dassetuṃ imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha udakorohanteti udakaṃ orohante puggale. Kumbhīlabhayanti suṃsumārabhayaṃ. Susukābhayanti caṇḍamacchabhayaṃ.
commentary_english:
161. Why did he begin with, "<hi rend="bold">Cattārimāni bhikkhave</hi> (Monks, these four)"? [It is because] in this Dispensation, there are four fears.

He who is fearless regarding these, is able to be established in this Dispensation.

But the other is not able - in order to show this, he began this teaching.

There, <hi rend="bold">udakorohante</hi> means people descending into the water.

<hi rend="bold">Kumbhīlabhaya</hi> means the fear of crocodiles.

<hi rend="bold">Susukābhaya</hi> means the fear of fierce fish.

mula_pali: 162. ‘‘Katamañca, bhikkhave, ūmibhayaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco kulaputto saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti – ‘otiṇṇomhi jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi dukkhotiṇṇo dukkhapareto; appeva nāma imassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa antakiriyā paññāyethā’ti. Tamenaṃ tathā pabbajitaṃ samānaṃ sabrahmacārī ovadanti, anusāsanti – ‘evaṃ te abhikkamitabbaṃ, evaṃ te paṭikkamitabbaṃ, evaṃ te ālokitabbaṃ, evaṃ te vilokitabbaṃ, evaṃ te samiñjitabbaṃ, evaṃ te pasāritabbaṃ, evaṃ te saṅghāṭipattacīvaraṃ dhāretabba’nti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘mayaṃ kho pubbe agāriyabhūtā samānā aññe ovadāma, anusāsāma ovadāmapi anusāsāmapi (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). Ime panamhākaṃ puttamattā maññe, nattamattā maññe, amhe evaṃ (ka.) ovaditabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ maññantī’ti. So sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ūmibhayassa bhīto sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvatto. ‘Ūmibhaya’nti kho, bhikkhave, kodhupāyāsassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ.
mula_english:
162.
“And what, monks, is the fear of waves (ūmibhayā)? Here, monks, some clansman goes forth out of faith from the householder's life into homelessness, considering: ‘I am overwhelmed by birth (*jāti*), aging (*jarā*), and death (*maraṇa*), by sorrow (*śoka*), lamentation (*parideva*), pain (*dukkha*), grief (*domanassa*), and despair (*upāyāsa*); I am overwhelmed by suffering, a prey to suffering. Surely an ending of this whole mass of suffering (*dukkhakkhandha*) can be known.’

Then, after he has gone forth thus, his companions in the holy life (sabrahmacārī) advise and instruct him thus: ‘You should move to and fro thus; you should look ahead and look away thus; you should flex and extend the limbs thus; you should wear the patched cloak (*saṅghāṭi*), bowl (*patta*), and robes (*cīvara*) thus.’

He thinks thus: ‘When we were formerly householders, we used to advise and instruct others.’

'And now these monks, who seem like they might be our sons or our grandsons, think that they can advise and instruct us.'

And so he forsakes the training (*śikṣā*) and reverts to the low life.

He is called one who has forsaken the training and reverted to the low life because he was frightened by the fear of waves.

‘The fear of waves (ūmibhayā)’ stands for anger and despair (krodha *upāyāsa*).
commentary_pali: 162.Kodhupāyāsassetaṃ adhivacananti yathā hi bāhiraṃ udakaṃ otiṇṇo ūmīsu osīditvā marati, evaṃ imasmiṃ sāsane kodhupāyāse osīditvā vibbhamati. Tasmā kodhupāyāso ‘‘ūmibhaya’’nti vutto.
commentary_english: 162. "kodhupāyāsassetaṃ adhivacana" means: just as an outside water-dweller, having entered, sinks in the waves and dies, so too in this teaching, one sinks in kodhupāyāsa and is bewildered. Therefore, kodhupāyāsa is called "fear of the waves."

mula_pali: 163. ‘‘Katamañca, bhikkhave, kumbhīlabhayaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco kulaputto saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti – ‘otiṇṇomhi jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi dukkhotiṇṇo dukkhapareto; appeva nāma imassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa antakiriyā paññāyethā’ti. Tamenaṃ tathā pabbajitaṃ samānaṃ sabrahmacārī ovadanti anusāsanti – ‘idaṃ te khāditabbaṃ, idaṃ te na khāditabbaṃ; idaṃ te bhuñjitabbaṃ, idaṃ te na bhuñjitabbaṃ; idaṃ te sāyitabbaṃ, idaṃ te na sāyitabbaṃ; idaṃ te pātabbaṃ, idaṃ te na pātabbaṃ; kappiyaṃ te khāditabbaṃ, akappiyaṃ te na khāditabbaṃ; kappiyaṃ te bhuñjitabbaṃ, akappiyaṃ te na bhuñjitabbaṃ; kappiyaṃ te sāyitabbaṃ, akappiyaṃ te na sāyitabbaṃ ; kappiyaṃ te pātabbaṃ, akappiyaṃ te na pātabbaṃ; kāle te khāditabbaṃ, vikāle te na khāditabbaṃ; kāle te bhuñjitabbaṃ, vikāle te na bhuñjitabbaṃ; kāle te sāyitabbaṃ, vikāle te na sāyitabbaṃ; kāle te pātabbaṃ, vikāle te na pātabba’nti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘mayaṃ kho pubbe agāriyabhūtā samānā yaṃ icchāma taṃ khādāma, yaṃ na icchāma na taṃ khādāma; yaṃ icchāma taṃ bhuñjāma, yaṃ na icchāma na taṃ bhuñjāma; yaṃ icchāma taṃ sāyāma, yaṃ na icchāma na taṃ sāyāma; yaṃ icchāma taṃ pivāma pipāma (sī. pī.), yaṃ na icchāma na taṃ pivāma; kappiyampi khādāma, akappiyampi khādāma; kappiyampi bhuñjāma, akappiyampi bhuñjāma; kappiyampi sāyāma, akappiyampi sāyāma; kappiyampi pivāma, akappiyampi pivāma; kālepi khādāma, vikālepi khādāma; kālepi bhuñjāma vikālepi bhuñjāma; kālepi sāyāma, vikālepi sāyāma; kālepi pivāma, vikālepi pivāma. Yampi no saddhā gahapatikā divā vikāle paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ denti tatthapime mukhāvaraṇaṃ maññe karontī’ti. So sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, kumbhīlabhayassa bhīto sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvatto. ‘Kumbhīlabhaya’nti kho, bhikkhave, odarikattassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ.
mula_english:
163. Furthermore, what is the fear of crocodiles ( *kumbhīlabhaya* )? Here, some clansman goes forth out of faith from the house life into homelessness, considering: ‘I am a victim of birth ( *jāti* ), aging ( *jarā* ), and death ( *maraṇa* ), of sorrow ( *śoka* ), lamentation ( *parideva* ), pain ( *dukkha* ), grief ( *daumanasya* ), and despair ( *upāyāsa* ); I am a victim of suffering ( *dukkha* ), a prey to suffering ( *dukkha* ). Surely an ending of this whole mass of suffering ( *dukkhakkhandha* ) can be known.’

Then, after he has gone forth thus, his companions in the holy life advise and instruct him thus: ‘This can be consumed by you, this cannot be consumed by you; this can be eaten by you, this cannot be eaten by you; this can be tasted by you, this cannot be tasted by you; this can be drunk by you, this cannot be drunk by you. You can consume what is allowable ( *kappiya* ), you cannot consume what is not allowable ( *akappiya* ); you can eat what is allowable ( *kappiya* ), you cannot eat what is not allowable ( *akappiya* ); you can taste what is allowable ( *kappiya* ), you cannot taste what is not allowable ( *akappiya* ); you can drink what is allowable ( *kappiya* ), you cannot drink what is not allowable ( *akappiya* ). You can consume at the proper time ( *kāla* ), you cannot consume at the improper time ( *vikāla* ); you can eat at the proper time ( *kāla* ), you cannot eat at the improper time ( *vikāla* ); you can taste at the proper time ( *kāla* ), you cannot taste at the improper time ( *vikāla* ); you can drink at the proper time ( *kāla* ), you cannot drink at the improper time ( *vikāla* ).’

Then he thinks: ‘Formerly, when we were in the home life, we consumed what we liked and did not consume what we did not like; we ate what we liked and did not eat what we did not like; we tasted what we liked and did not taste what we did not like; we drank what we liked and did not drink what we did not like. We consumed what was allowable ( *kappiya* ) and what was not allowable ( *akappiya* ); we ate what was allowable ( *kappiya* ) and what was not allowable ( *akappiya* ); we tasted what was allowable ( *kappiya* ) and what was not allowable ( *akappiya* ); we drank what was allowable ( *kappiya* ) and what was not allowable ( *akappiya* ). We consumed at the proper time ( *kāla* ) and at the improper time ( *vikāla* ); we ate at the proper time ( *kāla* ) and at the improper time ( *vikāla* ); we tasted at the proper time ( *kāla* ) and at the improper time ( *vikāla* ); we drank at the proper time ( *kāla* ) and at the improper time ( *vikāla* ).

Now, when faithful householders give us good food ( *khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ* ) of various kinds during the day ( *divā* ) outside the proper time ( *vikāla* ), it seems these monks put a muzzle on our mouths.’

And so he forsakes the training ( *śikṣā* ) and reverts to the low life. He is called one who has forsaken the training ( *śikṣā* ) and reverted to the low life because he was frightened by the fear of crocodiles ( *kumbhīlabhaya* ).

Now ‘crocodiles ( *kumbhīlabhaya* )’ is a term for gluttony ( *odarikatta* ).
commentary_pali: 163.Odarikattassetaṃ adhivacananti yathā hi bāhiraṃ udakaṃ otiṇṇo kumbhīlena khādito marati, evaṃ imasmiṃ sāsane odarikattena khādito vibbhamati. Tasmā odarikattaṃ ‘‘kumbhīlabhaya’’nti vuttaṃ.
commentary_english: This is a designation for voracity. Just as an external body of water overwhelms, a crocodile devours and kills, likewise in this teaching (śāsana), one devoured by voracity is destroyed. Therefore, voracity is said to be "fear of the crocodile".

mula_pali: 164. ‘‘Katamañca, bhikkhave, āvaṭṭabhayaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco kulaputto saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti – ‘otiṇṇomhi jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi dukkhotiṇṇo dukkhapareto; appeva nāma imassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa antakiriyā paññāyethā’ti. So evaṃ pabbajito samāno pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā piṇḍāya pavisati. Arakkhiteneva kāyena arakkhitāya vācāya anupaṭṭhitāya satiyā asaṃvutehi indriyehi so tattha passati gahapatiṃ vā gahapatiputtaṃ vā pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitaṃ samaṅgībhūtaṃ paricārayamānaṃ paricāriyamānaṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.). Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘mayaṃ kho pubbe agāriyabhūtā samānā pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitā samaṅgībhūtā paricārimhā. Saṃvijjanti kho pana me kule saṃvijjanti kho kule (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) bhogā. Sakkā bhoge ca bhuñjituṃ puññāni ca kātu’nti. So sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, āvaṭṭabhayassa bhīto sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvatto. ‘Āvaṭṭabhaya’nti kho, bhikkhave, pañcannetaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ adhivacanaṃ.
mula_english:
164. Now, what is the whirlpool-fear (āvaṭṭabhayaṃ)? Here, some clansman goes forth out of faith from the home life into homelessness, considering: ‘I am a victim of birth, ageing, and death, of sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; I am a victim of suffering, a prey to suffering. Surely an ending of this whole mass of suffering can be known.’

Then, after he has gone forth thus, when it is morning he dresses, and taking his bowl and outer robe, he goes into a village or town for alms.

In the morning, he dresses, takes his robe and bowl, and enters that village or town for alms with body unguarded, with speech unguarded, with mindfulness unestablished, and with sense faculties unrestrained. He sees some householder there or householder’s son furnished and endowed with the five cords of sensual pleasure (pañcahi kāmaguṇehi) enjoying himself with them.

He considers thus: ‘Formerly, when we were in the home life, we were furnished and endowed with the five cords of sensual pleasure (pañcahi kāmaguṇehi) and we enjoyed ourselves with them.

My family has wealth (bhogā); It might be possible to enjoy the possessions (bhoge) and to do good (puññāni).’

And so he forsakes the training (sikkhaṃ) and reverts to the low life (hīnāya āvattati).

He is called one who has forsaken the training (sikkhaṃ) and reverted to the low life (hīnāya āvatto) because he was frightened by the fear of whirlpools (āvaṭṭabhayassa bhīto).

Now ‘whirlpool-fear’ (āvaṭṭabhaya) is a term for the five cords of sensual pleasure (pañcannetaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ adhivacanaṃ).
commentary_pali: 164.Arakkhiteneva kāyenāti sīsappacālakādikaraṇena arakkhitakāyo hutvā. Arakkhitāya vācāyāti duṭṭhullabhāsanādivasena arakkhitavāco hutvā. Anupaṭṭhitāyasatiyāti kāyagatāsatiṃ anupaṭṭhāpetvā. Asaṃvutehīti apihitehi. Pañcannetaṃkāmaguṇānaṃ adhivacananti yathā hi bāhiraṃ udakaṃ otiṇṇo āvaṭṭe nimujjitvā marati, evaṃ imasmiṃ sāsane pabbajito pañcakāmaguṇāvaṭṭe nimujjitvā vibbhamati. Tasmā pañca kāmaguṇā ‘‘āvaṭṭabhaya’’nti vuttā.
commentary_english:
164.
" *Arakkhiteneva kāyenā* ": having an unprotected body (*arakkhitakāyo hutvā*) because of actions beginning with thoughtlessness.
" *Arakkhitāya vācāyā* ": having unprotected speech (*arakkhitavāco hutvā*) because of coarse language and the like (*duṭṭhullabhāsanādivasena*).
" *Anupaṭṭhitāya satiyā* ": not establishing mindfulness regarding the body (*kāyagatāsatiṃ anupaṭṭhāpetvā*).
" *Asaṃvutehī* ": with the unguarded ones (*apihitehi*).
" *Pañcannetaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ adhivacana* ": just as someone having entered an external body of water drowns and dies after diving into a whirlpool, likewise, someone who has gone forth (*pabbajito*) in this teaching (*sāsane*) becomes bewildered after diving into the whirlpool of the five sense pleasures (*pañcakāmaguṇāvaṭṭe nimujjitvā vibbhamati*).
Therefore, the five desirable sense qualities (*pañca kāmaguṇā*) are called a "whirlpool of fear" (*‘‘āvaṭṭabhaya’’nti vuttā*).

mula_pali:
165. ‘‘Katamañca , bhikkhave, susukābhayaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco kulaputto saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti – ‘otiṇṇomhi jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi dukkhotiṇṇo dukkhapareto; appeva nāma imassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa antakiriyā paññāyethā’ti. So evaṃ pabbajito samāno pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā piṇḍāya pavisati. Arakkhiteneva kāyena arakkhitāya vācāya anupaṭṭhitāya satiyā asaṃvutehi indriyehi so tattha passati mātugāmaṃ dunnivatthaṃ vā duppārutaṃ vā. Tassa mātugāmaṃ disvā dunnivatthaṃ vā duppārutaṃ vā rāgo cittaṃ anuddhaṃseti. So rāgānuddhaṃsena anuddhastena (sī. pī.) cittena sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati . Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, susukābhayassa bhīto sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvatto. ‘Susukābhaya’nti kho, bhikkhave, mātugāmassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri bhayāni, idhekacce puggale imasmiṃ dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajite pāṭikaṅkhitabbānī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Cātumasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.
mula_english:
165. "And what, bhikkhus, is the fear of sharks? Here, bhikkhus, some clansman goes forth out of faith from the home life into homelessness, considering: ‘I am a victim of birth, ageing, and death, of sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair; I am a victim of suffering, a prey to suffering. Surely an ending of this whole mass of suffering can be known.’

Then, after he has gone forth thus, when it is morning he dresses, and taking his bowl and outer robe, he goes into a village or town for alms.

with his body unguarded, with his speech unguarded, with mindfulness unestablished, and with sense faculties unrestrained. He sees a woman there lightly clothed, lightly dressed.

When he sees them, *rāga* (lust) invades his mind.

With his mind invaded by *rāga* (lust), he forsakes the training and reverts to the low life.

He is called one who has forsaken the training and reverted to the low life because he was frightened by the fear of sharks.

Now ‘sharks’ is a term for women.

“Bhikkhus, these are the four kinds of fears to be expected by certain persons who have gone forth from the home life into homelessness in this *Dhamma* and Discipline.”

This is what the *Bhagavā* (Blessed One) said.

Elated, those *bhikkhus* delighted in the *Bhagavā’s* (Blessed One's) statement.

The Cātuma Sutta, the seventh, is finished.
commentary_pali:
165.Anuddhaṃsetīti kilameti milāpeti. Rāgānuddhaṃsenāti rāgānuddhaṃsitena. Mātugāmassetaṃ adhivacananti yathā hi bāhiraṃ udakaṃ otiṇṇo caṇḍamacchaṃ āgamma laddhappahāro marati, evaṃ imasmiṃ sāsane mātugāmaṃ āgamma uppannakāmarāgo vibbhamati. Tasmā mātugāmo ‘‘susukābhaya’’nti vutto.

Imāni pana cattāri bhayāni bhāyitvā yathā udakaṃ anorohantassa udakaṃ nissāya ānisaṃso natthi, udakapipāsāya pipāsito ca hoti rajojallena kiliṭṭhasarīro ca, evamevaṃ imāni cattāri bhayāni bhāyitvā sāsane apabbajantassāpi imaṃ sāsanaṃ nissāya ānisaṃso natthi, taṇhāpipāsāya pipāsito ca hoti kilesarajena saṃkiliṭṭhacitto ca. Yathā pana imāni cattāri bhayāni abhāyitvā udakaṃ orohantassa vuttappakāro ānisaṃso hoti, evaṃ imāni abhāyitvā sāsane pabbajitassāpi vuttappakāro ānisaṃso hoti. Thero panāha – ‘‘cattāri bhayāni bhāyitvā udakaṃ anotaranto sotaṃ chinditvā paratīraṃ pāpuṇituṃ na sakkoti, abhāyitvā otaranto sakkoti, evamevaṃ bhāyitvā sāsane apabbajantopi taṇhāsotaṃ chinditvā nibbānapāraṃ daṭṭhuṃ na sakkoti, abhāyitvā pabbajanto pana sakkotī’’ti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānameva. Ayaṃ pana desanā neyyapuggalassa vasena niṭṭhāpitāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Cātumasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
165. *Anuddhaṃseti* means he stirs up, he mixes. *Rāgānuddhaṃsenā* means by stirring up passion. *Mātugāmassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ* means this is a designation for woman. Just as an aggressive fish, having come upon water that has receded outside, dies having received a blow; so too, in this Dispensation, one whose lust has arisen, having come upon a woman, is destroyed. Therefore, woman is called "a terror to the easygoing."

If one is afraid of these four fears, just as there is no benefit relying on water for one who does not descend into the water; and he is thirsty from thirst for water, and his body is soiled with the dirt of dust; even so, there is no benefit relying on this Dispensation for one who, being afraid of these four fears, does not go forth in the Dispensation; and he is thirsty from thirst for craving, and his mind is soiled with the dirt of defilement. Just as there is a benefit of the kind stated above for one who, not being afraid of these four fears, descends into the water, even so there is a benefit of the kind stated above for one who, not being afraid of these, goes forth in the Dispensation. But the Elder said: "One who, being afraid of the four fears, does not cross over the water is not able to cut off the stream and reach the far shore; one who crosses over without being afraid is able. Even so, one who, being afraid, does not go forth in the Dispensation is not able to cut off the stream of craving and see the further shore of *nirvāṇa*; one who goes forth without being afraid is able." The rest is clear throughout. This exposition, however, is concluded in relation to a person who needs guidance.

The Commentary on the Cātumā Sutta in the Papañcasūdanī, the Commentary to the Middle Length Discourses, is finished.

mula_pali: 166. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosalesu viharati naḷakapāne palāsavane. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā abhiññātā abhiññātā kulaputtā bhagavantaṃ uddissa saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā honti – āyasmā ca anuruddho, āyasmā ca bhaddiyo nandiyo (sī. pī.) vinaye ca ma. ni. 1 cūḷagosiṅge ca, āyasmā ca kimilo kimbilo (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), āyasmā ca bhagu, āyasmā ca koṇḍañño kuṇḍadhāno (sī. pī.), āyasmā ca revato, āyasmā ca ānando, aññe ca abhiññātā abhiññātā kulaputtā. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto abbhokāse nisinno hoti. Atha kho bhagavā te kulaputte ārabbha bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘ye te, bhikkhave, kulaputtā mamaṃ uddissa saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, kacci te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū abhiratā brahmacariye’’ti? Evaṃ vutte, te bhikkhū tuṇhī ahesuṃ. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā te kulaputte ārabbha bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘ye te, bhikkhave, kulaputtā mamaṃ uddissa saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, kacci te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū abhiratā brahmacariye’’ti? Dutiyampi kho te bhikkhū tuṇhī ahesuṃ. Tatiyampi kho bhagavā te kulaputte ārabbha bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘ye te, bhikkhave, kulaputtā mamaṃ uddissa saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā , kacci te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū abhiratā brahmacariye’’ti? Tatiyampi kho te bhikkhū tuṇhī ahesuṃ.
mula_english:
166. Thus have I heard:

At one time the Blessed One (bhagavā) was dwelling in the Kosala country at Naḷakapāna in the Palāsa forest.

Now at that time, many well-known clansmen had gone forth from the household life into homelessness out of faith in the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ). These were the venerable Anuruddha, the venerable Bhaddiya (Nandiya), the venerable Kimila (Kimbila), the venerable Bhagu, the venerable Koṇḍañña (Kuṇḍadhāna), the venerable Revata, the venerable Ānanda, and other well-known clansmen.

Then, on that occasion, the Blessed One (bhagavā), surrounded by the community of monks (bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto), was seated in the open air (abbhokāse nisinno hoti).

Then the Blessed One (bhagavā), concerning those clansmen, addressed the monks (bhikkhū) saying: "Those clansmen who have gone forth from the household life into homelessness out of faith in me (mamaṃ uddissa saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā), are those monks delighting in the holy life (brahmacariye)?" When this was said, those monks were silent (tuṇhī ahesuṃ).

A second time, the Blessed One (bhagavā), concerning those clansmen, addressed the monks (bhikkhū) saying: "Those clansmen who have gone forth from the household life into homelessness out of faith in me (mamaṃ uddissa saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā), are those monks delighting in the holy life (brahmacariye)?" A second time, those monks were silent (tuṇhī ahesuṃ).

A third time, the Blessed One (bhagavā), concerning those clansmen, addressed the monks (bhikkhū) saying: "Those clansmen who have gone forth from the household life into homelessness out of faith in me (mamaṃ uddissa saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā), are those monks delighting in the holy life (brahmacariye)?" A third time, those monks were silent (tuṇhī ahesuṃ).
commentary_pali:
166.Evaṃme sutanti naḷakapānasuttaṃ. Tattha naḷakapāneti evaṃnāmake gāme. Pubbe kira amhākaṃ bodhisatto vānarayoniyaṃ nibbatto, mahākāyo kapirājā anekavānarasahassaparivuto pabbatapāde vicarati. Paññavā kho pana hoti mahāpuñño. So parisaṃ evaṃ ovadati – ‘‘imasmiṃ pabbatapāde tātā, visaphalāni nāma honti, amanussapariggahitā pokkharaṇiyo nāma honti, tumhe pubbe khāditapubbāneva phalāni khādatha, pītapubbāneva pānīyāni ca pivatha, ettha vo maṃ paṭipucchitabbakiccaṃ natthi, akhāditapubbāni pana phalāni apītapubbāni ca pānīyāni maṃ apucchitvā mā khādittha mā pivitthā’’ti.

Te ekadivasaṃ caramānā aññaṃ pabbatapādaṃ gantvā gocaraṃ gahetvā pānīyaṃ olokentā ekaṃ amanussapariggahitaṃ pokkharaṇiṃ disvā sahasā apivitvā samantā parivāretvā mahāsattassa āgamanaṃ olokayamānā nisīdiṃsu. Mahāsatto āgantvā ‘‘kiṃ tātā pānīyaṃ na pivathā’’ti āha. Tumhākaṃ āgamanaṃ olokemāti. Sādhu tātāti samantā padaṃ pariyesamāno otiṇṇapadaṃyeva addasa, na uttiṇṇapadaṃ, disvā saparissayāti aññāsi. Tāvadeva ca tattha abhinibbattaamanusso udakaṃ dvedhā katvā uṭṭhāsi setamukho nīlakucchi rattahatthapādo mahādāṭhiko vaṅkadāṭho virūpo bībhaccho udakarakkhaso. So evamāha – ‘‘kasmā pānīyaṃ na pivatha, madhuraṃ udakaṃ pivatha, kiṃ tumhe etassa vacanaṃ suṇāthā’’ti? Mahāsatto āha – ‘‘tvaṃ idha adhivattho amanusso’’ti? Āmāhanti. Tvaṃ idha otiṇṇe labhasīti? Āma labhāmi, tumhe pana sabbe khādissāmīti. Na sakkhissasi, yakkhāti. Pānīyaṃ pana pivissathāti? Āma pivissāmāti. Evaṃ sante ekopi vo na muccissatīti. Pānīyañca pivissāma, na ca te vasaṃ gamissāmāti ekanaḷaṃ āharāpetvā koṭiyaṃ gahetvā dhami, sabbo ekacchiddo ahosi, tīre nisīditvāva pānīyaṃ pivi, sesavānarānaṃ pāṭiyekke naḷe āharāpetvā dhamitvā adāsi. Sabbe yakkhassa passantasseva pānīyaṃ piviṃsu. Vuttampi cetaṃ –

‘‘Disvā padamanuttiṇṇaṃ, disvāno’ taritaṃ padaṃ;

Naḷena vāriṃ pissāma, neva maṃ tvaṃ vadhissasī’’ti. (jā. 1.1.20);

Tato paṭṭhāya yāva ajjadivasā tasmiṃ ṭhāne naḷā ekacchiddāva honti. Iminā hi saddhiṃ imasmiṃ kappe cattāri kappaṭṭhiyapāṭihāriyāni nāma – cande sasabimbaṃ , vaṭṭakajātakamhi saccakiriyaṭṭhāne aggissa gamanupacchedo, ghaṭikārakumbhakārassa mātāpitūnaṃ vasanaṭṭhāne devassa avassanaṃ, tassā pokkharaṇiyā tīre naḷānaṃ ekacchiddabhāvoti. Iti sā pokkharaṇī naḷena pānīyassa pītattā naḷakapānāti nāmaṃ labhi. Aparabhāge taṃ pokkharaṇiṃ nissāya gāmo patiṭṭhāsi, tassāpi naḷakapānanteva nāmaṃ jātaṃ. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘‘naḷakapāne’’ti. Palāsavaneti kiṃsukavane.

cattāri kappaṭṭhiyapāṭihāriyāni naḷakapānā naḷakapānanteva Palāsavane
commentary_english:
166. Thus have I heard: the *Naḷakapāna Sutta*.

There, *Naḷakapāna* is the name of a village.

Long ago, it seems, our bodhisattva was born in a monkey's womb. A great-bodied monkey king, surrounded by many thousands of monkeys, wandered at the foot of a mountain.

He was wise, moreover, and of great merit.

He advised the assembly thus: “At this mountain foot, fathers, there are fruits that are poison, and pools that are haunted by non-humans. You should eat only those fruits that you have eaten before, and drink only those waters that you have drunk before. Here, you should not have any need to ask me about what to do. But, without asking me, do not eat those fruits that you have not eaten before, and do not drink those waters that you have not drunk before.”

Then, one day, while wandering, they went to another mountain foot. After fetching their food, while looking for water, they saw a pool haunted by non-humans. Without drinking any of it suddenly, they surrounded it on all sides, watching for the great being's arrival.

The great being arrived and said, “Why do you not drink the water, fathers?”

“We are watching for your arrival.”

“Good, fathers!” Searching all around for a footprint, he saw only a footprint leading down, not a footprint leading up. Having seen this, he understood, “It is dangerous!”

At that very moment, a non-human that had arisen there, having split the water in two, arose. He had a white face, a blue belly, red hands and feet, great fangs, crooked teeth, a deformed and repulsive appearance, an aquatic demon.

He said thus: “Why do you not drink the water? Drink the sweet water! Why do you listen to this fellow's word?” The great being said, “You are a non-human dwelling here?” “Yes.”

“Are you able to catch those who have gone down into it here?” “Yes, I am able. But I will eat all of you!”

“You will not be able to, *yakṣa*!”

“Then will you drink the water?” “Yes, we will drink!”

“If that is so, not even one of you will escape!”

“We will drink the water, and we will not come under your control!” Having had a single reed brought, having taken it at the tip, he blew on it. It all became one-holed. Sitting on the bank, he drank the water. Having had individual reeds brought for the remaining monkeys, having blown on them, he gave them out.

All drank the water while the *yakṣa* looked on.

This was also said:

“Having seen the un-ascended footprint, having seen the un-crossed footprint;

We will drink the water with a reed, and you will never kill me.”

(Jā. 1.1.20);

From then on, up to this present day, in that place the reeds are one-holed.

Along with this, in this *kalpa* there are four marvels that are fixed for the *kalpa*: the hare-image on the moon, the uninterrupted journey of fire in the *Vaṭṭaka Jātaka* at the place of the act of truth, the raining down of the god at the dwelling place of the potter Ghaṭikāra's parents, and the one-holed-ness of the reeds on the bank of that pool.

Thus, that pool, because the water was drunk with a reed, obtained the name *Naḷakapāna*.

In another part, relying on that pool, a village was established. That too obtained the name *Naḷakapananteva*.

With reference to that, it was said, “*Naḷakapāna*”.

*Palāsa Forest* is the *Kiṃsuka* Forest.

Four wonders fixed for the *kalpa*, *Naḷakapāna*, *Naḷakapananteva*, *Palāsa Forest*.

mula_pali:
167. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – ‘‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ te kulaputte puccheyya’’nti! Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘kacci tumhe, anuruddhā, abhiratā brahmacariye’’ti? ‘‘Taggha mayaṃ, bhante, abhiratā brahmacariye’’ti. ‘‘Sādhu sādhu, anuruddhā! Etaṃ kho, anuruddhā, tumhākaṃ patirūpaṃ kulaputtānaṃ saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitānaṃ yaṃ tumhe abhirameyyātha brahmacariye. Yena tumhe anuruddhā, bhadrena yobbanena samannāgatā paṭhamena vayasā susukāḷakesā kāme paribhuñjeyyātha tena tumhe, anuruddhā, bhadrenapi yobbanena samannāgatā paṭhamena vayasā susukāḷakesā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā. Te ca kho pana tumhe, anuruddhā, neva rājābhinītā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, na corābhinītā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, na iṇaṭṭā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, na bhayaṭṭā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, nājīvikāpakatā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā. Api ca khomhi otiṇṇo jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, dukkhotiṇṇo dukkhapareto; appeva nāma imassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa antakiriyā paññāyethāti – nanu tumhe, anuruddhā, evaṃ saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Evaṃ pabbajitena ca pana, anuruddhā, kulaputtena kimassa karaṇīyaṃ? Vivekaṃ, anuruddhā, kāmehi vivekaṃ akusalehi dhammehi pītisukhaṃ nādhigacchati aññaṃ vā aññaṃ ca (ka.) tato santataraṃ, tassa abhijjhāpi cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, byāpādopi cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, thīnamiddhampi thīnamiddhampi (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati uddhaccakukkuccampi cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, vicikicchāpi cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, aratīpi cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, tandīpi cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhati. Vivekaṃ, anuruddhā, kāmehi vivekaṃ akusalehi dhammehi pītisukhaṃ nādhigacchati aññaṃ vā tato santataraṃ’’.

‘‘Vivekaṃ, anuruddhā, kāmehi vivekaṃ akusalehi dhammehi pītisukhaṃ adhigacchati aññaṃ vā tato santataraṃ, tassa abhijjhāpi cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, byāpādopi cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, thīnamiddhampi cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, uddhaccakukkuccampi cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, vicikicchāpi cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, aratīpi cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati, tandīpi cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati. Vivekaṃ, anuruddhā, kāmehi vivekaṃ akusalehi dhammehi pītisukhaṃ adhigacchati aññaṃ vā tato santataraṃ.

167. Then it occurred to the Blessed One: “Why don't I question those young men of good family?” Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Anuruddha: “Anuruddha, do you all delight in the holy life (brahmacariye)?” “Yes, venerable sir, we delight in the holy life (brahmacariye).”

“Good, good, Anuruddha! It is fitting for you, Anuruddha, young men of good family, who have gone forth from the house life into homelessness out of faith (saddhā), that you delight in the holy life (brahmacariye).

As you, Anuruddha, are endowed with the blessing of youth, black-haired young men in the prime of life, you could have indulged in sensual pleasures (kāme), yet you have gone forth from the home life into homelessness.

And it is not because you have been driven by kings that you have gone forth from the home life into homelessness, or because you have been driven by thieves, or owing to debt, fear, or want of a livelihood.

Rather, I am immersed in birth (jātiyā), aging (jarāya), and death (maraṇena), in sorrow (sokehi), lamentation (paridevehi), pain (dukkhehi), grief (domanassehi), and despair (upāyāsehi), I am a victim of suffering (dukkha), a prey to suffering (dukkha). Surely an ending of this whole mass of suffering (dukkhakkhandhassa) can be known’?” “Indeed, Anuruddha, it is out of such faith (saddhā) that you have gone forth from the house life into homelessness?” “Yes, venerable sir.”

“So, Anuruddha, what should be done by a young man of good family who has gone forth? He still does not attain the rapture (pīti) and pleasure (sukhaṃ) that are secluded from sensual pleasures (kāmehi) and secluded from unwholesome states (dhammehi), or to something more peaceful than that. Covetousness (abhijjhā) invades his mind (cittaṃ) and remains, ill will (byāpādopi) invades his mind (cittaṃ) and remains, sloth and torpor (thīnamiddhampi) invade his mind (cittaṃ) and remain, restlessness and remorse (uddhaccakukkuccampi) invade his mind (cittaṃ) and remain, doubt (vicikicchāpi) invades his mind (cittaṃ) and remains, discontent (aratīpi) invades his mind (cittaṃ) and remains, weariness (tandīpi) invades his mind (cittaṃ) and remains.

commentary_pali:
167.Tagghamayaṃ, bhanteti ekaṃseneva mayaṃ, bhante, abhiratā. Aññepi ye tumhākaṃ sāsane abhiramanti, te amhehi sadisāva hutvā abhiramantīti dīpenti.

Neva rājābhinītātiādīsu eko rañño aparādhaṃ katvā palāyati. Rājā kuhiṃ, bho, asukoti? Palāto devāti. Palātaṭṭhānepi me na muccissati, sace pana pabbajeyya, mucceyyāti vadati. Tassa kocideva suhado gantvā taṃ pavattiṃ ārocetvā tvaṃ sace jīvitumicchasi, pabbajāhīti. So pabbajitvā jīvitaṃ rakkhamāno carati. Ayaṃ rājābhinīto nāma.

Neva rājābhinītā rājābhinīto

Eko pana corānaṃ mūlaṃ chindanto carati. Corā sutvā ‘‘purisānaṃ atthikabhāvaṃ na jānāti, jānāpessāma na’’nti vadanti. So taṃ pavattiṃ sutvā palāyati. Corā palātoti sutvā ‘‘palātaṭṭhānepi no na muccissati, sace pana pabbajeyya, mucceyyā’’ti vadanti. So taṃ pavattiṃ sutvā pabbajati. Ayaṃ corābhinīto nāma.

corābhinīto

Eko pana bahuṃ iṇaṃ khāditvā tena iṇena aṭṭo pīḷito tamhā gāmā palāyati. Iṇasāmikā sutvā ‘‘palātaṭṭhānepi no na muccissati, sace pana pabbajeyya, mucceyyā’’ti vadanti. So taṃ pavattiṃ sutvā pabbajati. Ayaṃ iṇaṭṭo nāma.

iṇaṭṭo

Rājabhayādīnaṃ pana aññatarena bhayena bhīto aṭṭo āturo hutvā nikkhamma pabbajito bhayaṭṭo nāma. Dubbhikkhādīsu jīvituṃ asakkonto pabbajito ājīvikāpakato nāma, ājīvikāya pakato abhibhūtoti attho. Imesu pana ekopi imehi kāraṇehi pabbajito nāma natthi, tasmā ‘‘neva rājābhinīto’’tiādimāha.

bhayaṭṭo ājīvikāpakato

Vivekanti vivicca vivitto hutvā. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – yaṃ kāmehi ca akusaladhammehi ca vivittena paṭhamadutiyajjhānasaṅkhātaṃ pītisukhaṃ adhigantabbaṃ, sace taṃ vivicca kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi pītisukhaṃ nādhigacchati, aññaṃ vā upari dvinnaṃ jhānānaṃ catunnañca maggānaṃ vasena santataraṃ sukhaṃ nādhigacchati, tassa ime abhijjhādayo cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhantīti. Tattha aratīti adhikusalesu dhammesu ukkaṇṭhitatā. Tandīti ālasiyabhāvo. Evaṃ yo pabbajitvā pabbajitakiccaṃ kātuṃ na sakkoti, tassa ime satta pāpadhammā uppajjitvā cittaṃ pariyādiyantīti dassetvā idāni yassa te dhammā cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhanti, soyeva samaṇakiccampi kātuṃ na sakkotīti puna vivekaṃ anuruddhā…pe… aññaṃ vā tato santataranti āha.

Viveka aratī Tandī vivekaṃ anuruddhā…pe… aññaṃ vā tato santatara

Evaṃ kaṇhapakkhaṃ dassetvā idāni teneva nayena sukkapakkhaṃ dassetuṃ puna vivekantiādimāha. Tassattho vuttanayeneva veditabbo.

viveka
commentary_english:
167.
“Indeed, we, venerable sir, delight in oneness.” Thus, they reveal that others too who delight in your dispensation delight having become similar to us.

“Not brought near by the king,” etc.—one commits an offense against the king and flees.

“Where is the king, sir, so-and-so?” “He has fled, good sir.”

He thinks, “Even in a place of flight, he will not release me; if, however, I were to go forth, I would be released.”

Having gone to him, a certain well-wisher, having announced that event, [says,] “If you wish to live, go forth!”

Having gone forth, he lives protecting his life.

This is called *rājābhinītaḥ* (brought near by the king).

*neva rājābhinītā* *rājābhinīto* (not brought near by the king, brought near by the king)—but one goes about destroying the root of thieves.

Having heard, the thieves say, “He does not know the state of being property-holders of men; we will make [him] know.”

Having heard that event, he flees.

Having heard, “He has fled,” the thieves say, “Even in a place of flight, he will not release us; if, however, he were to go forth, he would be released.”

Having heard that event, he goes forth.

This is called *corābhinīto* (brought near by thieves).

*corābhinīto* (brought near by thieves)—but one, having eaten much debt, oppressed, afflicted by that debt, flees from that village.

Having heard, the debt-owners say, “Even in a place of flight, he will not release us; if, however, he were to go forth, he would be released.”

Having heard that event, he goes forth.

This is called *iṇaṭṭo* (afflicted by debt).

*iṇaṭṭo* (afflicted by debt)—but one, frightened by some other fear, such as fear of the king, afflicted, sick, having gone out, gone forth, is called *bhayaṭṭo* (afflicted by fear).

Unable to live in times of famine, etc., one goes forth. This is called *ājīvikāpakato* (caused by livelihood); *ājīvikāya pakato* (caused by livelihood) means overcome.

But even one among these is not one gone forth by these causes; therefore, he said, “*neva rājābhinīto* (not brought near by the king),” etc.

*bhayaṭṭo* *ājīvikāpakato* (afflicted by fear, caused by livelihood)—*viveka* (discrimination) means having discriminated, having become solitary.

This is said—the *pītisukhaṃ* (joy and happiness) counted as the first and second *dhyānas* which should be attained by one secluded from desires and unwholesome dharmas; if, having discriminated, he does not attain that *pītisukhaṃ* (joy and happiness) by desires, having discriminated from unwholesome *dharmas*, or he does not attain another, more peaceful *sukhaṃ* (happiness), higher by way of the two *dhyānas* and the four paths, these covetousnesses, etc., stand pervading his mind.

There, *aratī* (dissatisfaction) means being disgusted with superior wholesome *dharmas*.

*tandī* (languor) means the state of laziness.

Thus, one who, having gone forth, is not able to do the business of one gone forth, these seven evil *dharmas*, having arisen, showing that they pervade his mind, now, he alone by whom those *dharmas* stand pervading his mind, is not able to do even the business of a *śramaṇa* (ascetic). Again, he said “*vivekaṃ anuruddhā…pe… aññaṃ vā tato santatara*” (adhering to discrimination…etc… or another, more peaceful than that).

*viveka* *aratī* *tandī* (discrimination, dissatisfaction, languor)—*vivekaṃ anuruddhā…pe… aññaṃ vā tato santatara* (adhering to discrimination…etc… or another, more peaceful than that)—thus, having shown the dark side, now, in order to show the bright side by that same method, again, he said "*viveka*nti (discrimination)," etc.

Its meaning should be understood by the method stated.

*viveka* (discrimination).

mula_pali:
168. ‘‘Kinti vo, anuruddhā, mayi hoti – ‘ye āsavā saṃkilesikā ponobbhavikā ponobhavikā (sī. pī.) sadarā dukkhavipākā āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyā, appahīnā te tathāgatassa; tasmā tathāgato saṅkhāyekaṃ paṭisevati, saṅkhāyekaṃ adhivāseti, saṅkhāyekaṃ parivajjeti, saṅkhāyekaṃ vinodetī’’’ti? ‘‘Na kho no, bhante, bhagavati evaṃ hoti – ‘ye āsavā saṃkilesikā ponobbhavikā sadarā dukkhavipākā āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyā, appahīnā te tathāgatassa; tasmā tathāgato saṅkhāyekaṃ paṭisevati, saṅkhāyekaṃ adhivāseti, saṅkhāyekaṃ parivajjeti, saṅkhāyekaṃ vinodetī’ti. Evaṃ kho no, bhante, bhagavati hoti – ‘ye āsavā saṃkilesikā ponobbhavikā sadarā dukkhavipākā āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyā, pahīnā te tathāgatassa; tasmā tathāgato saṅkhāyekaṃ paṭisevati, saṅkhāyekaṃ adhivāseti, saṅkhāyekaṃ parivajjeti, saṅkhāyekaṃ vinodetī’’’ti. ‘‘Sādhu sādhu, anuruddhā! Tathāgatassa, anuruddhā, ye āsavā saṃkilesikā ponobbhavikā sadarā dukkhavipākā āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyā, pahīnā te ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Seyyathāpi, anuruddhā, tālo matthakacchinno abhabbo punavirūḷhiyā; evameva kho, anuruddhā , tathāgatassa ye āsavā saṃkilesikā ponobbhavikā sadarā dukkhavipākā āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyā, pahīnā te ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā; tasmā tathāgato saṅkhāyekaṃ paṭisevati, saṅkhāyekaṃ adhivāseti, saṅkhāyekaṃ parivajjeti, saṅkhāyekaṃ vinodeti’’.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, anuruddhā, kaṃ atthavasaṃ sampassamāno tathāgato sāvake abbhatīte kālaṅkate upapattīsu byākaroti – ‘asu amutra upapanno; asu amutra upapanno’’’ti? ‘‘Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā bhagavaṃnettikā bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā. Sādhu vata, bhante, bhagavantaṃyeva paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī’’ti . ‘‘Na kho, anuruddhā, tathāgato janakuhanatthaṃ na janalapanatthaṃ na lābhasakkārasilokānisaṃsatthaṃ na ‘iti maṃ jano jānātū’ti sāvake abbhatīte kālaṅkate upapattīsu byākaroti – ‘asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno’ti. Santi ca kho, anuruddhā, kulaputtā saddhā uḷāravedā uḷārapāmojjā. Te taṃ sutvā tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharanti. Tesaṃ taṃ, anuruddhā, hoti dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya’’.
mula_english:
168. “What do you think, Anuruddha? Do you think this of me: ‘The taints (āsava) that defile (saṃkilesika), bring renewal of being (ponobbhavika), give trouble (sadara), ripen in suffering (duḥkhavipāka), and lead to future birth, aging, and death (jātijarāmaraṇiya), those have not been abandoned by the *Tathāgata*’? Therefore, the *Tathāgata* uses one thing after reflecting (saṅkhāyekaṃ paṭisevati), endures another thing after reflecting (saṅkhāyekaṃ adhivāseti), avoids another thing after reflecting (saṅkhāyekaṃ parivajjeti), and removes another thing after reflecting (saṅkhāyekaṃ vinodeti)?"

“No, venerable sir (bhante), we do not think of the Blessed One (bhagavati) in that way: ‘The taints (āsava) that defile (saṃkilesika), bring renewal of being (ponobbhavika), give trouble (sadara), ripen in suffering (duḥkhavipāka), and lead to future birth, aging, and death (jātijarāmaraṇiya), those have not been abandoned by the *Tathāgata*’; therefore, the *Tathāgata* uses one thing after reflecting, endures another thing after reflecting, avoids another thing after reflecting, and removes another thing after reflecting.”

We think of the Blessed One in this way: ‘The taints (āsava) that defile (saṃkilesika), bring renewal of being (ponobbhavika), give trouble (sadara), ripen in suffering (duḥkhavipāka), and lead to future birth, aging, and death (jātijarāmaraṇiya), those have been abandoned by the *Tathāgata*; therefore, the *Tathāgata* uses one thing after reflecting, endures another thing after reflecting, avoids another thing after reflecting, and removes another thing after reflecting.’”

“Good, good, Anuruddha! Anuruddha, the *Tathāgata* has abandoned the taints (āsava) that defile (saṃkilesika), bring renewal of being (ponobbhavika), give trouble (sadara), ripen in suffering (duḥkhavipāka), and lead to future birth, aging, and death (jātijarāmaraṇiya); he has cut them off at the root (ucchinnamūla), made them like a palm stump (tālāvatthukata), done away with them so that they are no longer subject to future arising (anabhāvaṃkata āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā).

Just as a palmyra tree (tāla) with its crown cut off (matthakacchinno) is incapable of growing again (abhabbo punavirūḷhiyā); so too, Anuruddha, the *Tathāgata* has abandoned the taints (āsava) that defile (saṃkilesika), bring renewal of being (ponobbhavika), give trouble (sadara), ripen in suffering (duḥkhavipāka), and lead to future birth, aging, and death (jātijarāmaraṇiya); he has cut them off at the root (ucchinnamūla), made them like a palm stump (tālāvatthukata), done away with them so that they are no longer subject to future arising (anabhāvaṃkata āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā). Therefore, the *Tathāgata* uses one thing after reflecting, endures another thing after reflecting, avoids another thing after reflecting, and removes another thing after reflecting.”

“What do you think, Anuruddha? What purpose (attha) does the *Tathāgata* see that when a disciple (sāvake) has died (abbhatīte kālaṅkate), he declares his reappearance (upapattīsu byākaroti) thus: ‘So-and-so (asu) has reappeared in such-and-such a place (amutra upapanno); so-and-so (asu) has reappeared in such-and-such a place (amutra upapanno’?”

“Venerable sir (bhante), our teachings (dhamma) are rooted in the Blessed One (bhagavaṃmūlakā), guided by the Blessed One (bhagavaṃnettikā), have the Blessed One as their resort (bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā).

It would be good (sādhu vata), venerable sir, if the Blessed One would clarify (paṭibhātu) the meaning (attha) of that statement (bhāsitassa). Having heard (sutvā) it from the Blessed One (bhagavato), the *bhikkhus* will remember it (dhāressantī).”

“So, Anuruddha, it is not for the purpose of scheming to deceive people (janakuhanatthaṃ) or for the purpose of flattering people (janalapanatthaṃ) or for the purpose of gain, honor, and renown (lābhasakkārasilokānisaṃsatthaṃ), or with the thought, ‘Let people know me to be thus (iti maṃ jano jānātū),’ that when a disciple has died, the *Tathāgata* declares his reappearance thus: ‘So-and-so has reappeared in such-and-such a place; so-and-so has reappeared in such-and-such a place.’

Rather, it is because there are faithful (saddhā) clansmen (kulaputtā) inspired and gladdened (uḷārapāmojjā) by what is lofty (uḷāravedā). When they hear that (te taṃ sutvā), they direct their minds to such a state (tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharanti). And that leads to their welfare and happiness for a long time (tesaṃ taṃ hoti dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya).”
commentary_pali:
168.Saṅkhāyāti jānitvā. Ekanti ekaccaṃ. Paṭisevatīti sevitabbayuttakaṃ sevati. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Upapattīsu byākarotīti sappaṭisandhike tāva byākarotu, appaṭisandhike kathaṃ byākarotīti. Appaṭisandhikassa puna bhave paṭisandhi natthīti vadanto upapattīsu byākaroti nāma.

Janakuhanatthanti janavimhāpanatthaṃ. Janalapanatthanti mahājanassa upalāpanatthaṃ. Na iti maṃ jano jānātūti evaṃ maṃ mahājano jānissati, evaṃ me mahājanassa antare kittisaddo uggacchissatīti imināpi kāraṇena na byākarotīti attho. Uḷāravedāti mahantatuṭṭhino.

Janakuhanattha Janalapanattha Na iti maṃ jano jānātū Uḷāravedā
commentary_english:
168. *saṅkhāyā* ti, having known.

*eka* nti, a certain one.

*paṭisevatī* ti, he cultivates what is worth cultivating.

The same method applies to the remaining clauses as well.

*upapattīsu byākarotī* ti, in regard to suitable conditions, he explains. To the one with rebirth, he may explain, but how does he explain to the one without rebirth?

Declaring that for one without rebirth, there is no rebirth in a future existence, he explains in regard to suitable conditions.

*janakuhanattha* nti, for the purpose of deceiving people.

*janalapanattha* nti, for the purpose of coaxing the great multitude of people.

*na iti maṃ jano jānātū* ti, in this way the great multitude of people will know me, in this way the sound of my fame will rise up among the great multitude of people; thus, for this reason, he does not explain—that is the meaning.

*uḷāravedā* ti, those of great satisfaction.

*janakuhanattha*, *janalapanattha*, *na iti maṃ jano jānātū*, *uḷāravedā*

mula_pali:
169. ‘‘Idhānuruddhā, bhikkhu suṇāti – ‘itthannāmo bhikkhu kālaṅkato kālakato (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.); so bhagavatā byākato – aññāya saṇṭhahī’ti. So kho panassa āyasmā sāmaṃ diṭṭho vā hoti anussavassuto vā – ‘evaṃsīlo so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃdhammo so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃpañño so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃvihārī so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃvimutto so āyasmā ahosi itipī’ti. So tassa saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussaranto tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati. Evampi kho, anuruddhā, bhikkhuno phāsuvihāro hoti.

‘‘Idhānuruddhā , bhikkhu suṇāti – ‘itthannāmo bhikkhu kālaṅkato; so bhagavatā byākato – pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā’ti. So kho panassa āyasmā sāmaṃ diṭṭho vā hoti anussavassuto vā – ‘evaṃsīlo so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃdhammo…pe… evaṃpañño… evaṃvihārī… evaṃvimutto so āyasmā ahosi itipī’ti. So tassa saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussaranto tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati. Evampi kho, anuruddhā, bhikkhuno phāsuvihāro hoti.

‘‘Idhānuruddhā, bhikkhu suṇāti – ‘itthannāmo bhikkhu kālaṅkato; so bhagavatā byākato – tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmī sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissatī’ti. So kho panassa āyasmā sāmaṃ diṭṭho vā hoti anussavassuto vā – ‘evaṃsīlo so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃdhammo…pe… evaṃpañño… evaṃvihārī… evaṃvimutto so āyasmā ahosi itipī’ti. So tassa saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussaranto tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati. Evampi kho, anuruddhā, bhikkhuno phāsuvihāro hoti.

‘‘Idhānuruddhā, bhikkhu suṇāti – ‘itthannāmo bhikkhu kālaṅkato; so bhagavatā byākato – tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’ti. So kho panassa āyasmā sāmaṃ diṭṭho vā hoti anussavassuto vā – ‘evaṃsīlo so āyasmā ahosi itipi, evaṃdhammo…pe… evaṃpañño… evaṃvihārī… evaṃvimutto so āyasmā ahosi itipī’ti. So tassa saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussaranto tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati. Evampi kho, anuruddhā, bhikkhuno phāsuvihāro hoti.
mula_english:
169. “Here, Anuruddha, a *bhikkhu* hears thus: ‘The *bhikkhu* named so-and-so has died; the Blessed One has declared of him: “He was established in final knowledge (aññāya saṇṭhahi).”’

And he has either seen that venerable one for himself or heard it said of him: ‘That venerable one’s virtue (*śīla*) was thus, his state of concentration (*dharma*) was thus, his wisdom (*prajñā*) was thus, his abiding in attainments (*vihārī*) was thus, his deliverance (*vimutti*) was thus.’

Recollecting his faith (*śraddhā*), virtue (*śīla*), learning (*śruta*), generosity (*tyāga*), and wisdom (*prajñā*), he directs his mind (*citta*) to such a state.

In this way too, Anuruddha, a *bhikkhu* has a comfortable abiding (*phāsuvihāra*).

“Here, Anuruddha, a *bhikkhu* hears thus: ‘The *bhikkhu* named so-and-so has died; the Blessed One has declared of him: “With the destruction of the five lower fetters (*pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā*) he has reappeared spontaneously (*opapātika*) in the Pure Abodes and there will attain final *nirvāṇa* (*parinirvāyī*) without ever returning from that world (anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā).”’

And he has either seen that venerable one for himself or heard it said of him: ‘That venerable one’s virtue (*śīla*) was thus... his wisdom (*prajñā*) was thus... his abiding in attainments (*vihārī*) was thus... his deliverance (*vimutti*) was thus.’

Recollecting his faith (*śraddhā*), virtue (*śīla*), learning (*śruta*), generosity (*tyāga*), and wisdom (*prajñā*), he directs his mind (*citta*) to such a state.

In this way too, Anuruddha, a *bhikkhu* has a comfortable abiding (*phāsuvihāra*).

“Here, Anuruddha, a *bhikkhu* hears thus: ‘The *bhikkhu* named so-and-so has died; the Blessed One has declared of him: “With the destruction of three fetters (*tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā*) and with the attenuation of lust (*rāga*), hate (*dveṣa*), and delusion (*moha*), he has become a once-returner (*sakadāgāmī*), returning once to this world (*imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā*) to make an end of suffering (dukkhassantaṃ karissatī).”’

And he has either seen that venerable one for himself or heard it said of him: ‘That venerable one’s virtue (*śīla*) was thus... his wisdom (*prajñā*) was thus... his abiding in attainments (*vihārī*) was thus... his deliverance (*vimutti*) was thus.’

Recollecting his faith (*śraddhā*), virtue (*śīla*), learning (*śruta*), generosity (*tyāga*), and wisdom (*prajñā*), he directs his mind (*citta*) to such a state.

In this way too, Anuruddha, a *bhikkhu* has a comfortable abiding (*phāsuvihāra*).

“Here, Anuruddha, a *bhikkhu* hears thus: ‘The *bhikkhu* named so-and-so has died; the Blessed One has declared of him: “With the destruction of three fetters (*tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā*) he has become a stream-enterer (*sotāpanna*), no longer subject to perdition (*avinipātadhamma*), bound for deliverance, headed for enlightenment (*niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo*).”’

And he has either seen that venerable one for himself or heard it said of him: ‘That venerable one’s virtue (*śīla*) was thus... his wisdom (*prajñā*) was thus... his abiding in attainments (*vihārī*) was thus... his deliverance (*vimutti*) was thus.’

Recollecting his faith (*śraddhā*), virtue (*śīla*), learning (*śruta*), generosity (*tyāga*), and wisdom (*prajñā*), he directs his mind (*citta*) to such a state.

In this way too, Anuruddha, a *bhikkhu* has a comfortable abiding (*phāsuvihāra*).
commentary_pali:
169.So kho panassa āyasmāti so parinibbuto āyasmā imassa ṭhitassa āyasmato. Evaṃsīlotiādīsu lokiyalokuttaramissakāva sīlādayo veditabbo. Evaṃdhammoti ettha pana samādhipakkhikā dhammā dhammāti adhippetā. Phāsuvihāro hotīti tena bhikkhunā pūritapaṭipattiṃ pūrentassa arahattaphalaṃ sacchikatvā phalasamāpattivihārena phāsuvihāro hoti, arahattaṃ pattumasakkontassa paṭipattiṃ pūrayamānassa caratopi phāsuvihāroyeva nāma hoti. Iminā nayena sabbavāresu attho veditabboti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Naḷakapānasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
169. So kho panassa āyasmā: That venerable one, so parinibbuto āyasmā: that venerable one who has attained final nirvāṇa, imassa ṭhitassa āyasmato: of this abiding venerable one.

Evaṃsīlo tiādīsu lokiyalokuttaramissakāva sīlādayo veditabbo: In evaṃsīlo, etc., the qualities of moral conduct, etc., should be understood as mixed with the mundane and supramundane.

Evaṃdhammo ti ettha pana samādhipakkhikā dhammā dhammāti adhippetā: Here, in evaṃdhammo, the qualities pertaining to concentration (*samādhi*) are intended by the term qualities (*dharma*).

Phāsuvihāro hotī ti tena bhikkhunā pūritapaṭipattiṃ pūrentassa arahattaphalaṃ sacchikatvā phalasamāpattivihārena phāsuvihāro hoti, arahattaṃ pattumasakkontassa paṭipattiṃ pūrayamānassa caratopi phāsuvihāroyeva nāma hoti: "There is a dwelling in comfort," means that by that *bhikṣu* who fulfills the practice that has been fulfilled, having realized the fruit of *arhatship*, there is a dwelling in comfort by means of the dwelling in the attainment of the fruit. Even for one who, while practicing, is unable to attain *arhatship*, it is still called a dwelling in comfort.

Iminā nayena sabbavāresu attho veditabbo ti: The meaning in all cases should be understood in this way.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya: The *Papañcasūdanī*, commentary on the *Majjhimanikāya*.

Naḷakapānasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā: The commentary on the Naḷakapānasutta is finished.

171.
“Here, Anuruddha, a lay follower hears: ‘The lay follower named so-and-so has passed away; the Blessed One has declared of him: “With the destruction of the five lower fetters, he has been reborn spontaneously, and there he will attain nirvāṇa, not liable to return from that world.”’

172. ‘‘Idhānuruddhā , upāsikā suṇāti – ‘itthannāmā upāsikā kālaṅkatā; sā bhagavatā byākatā – pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyinī anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā’ti. Sā kho panassā bhaginī sāmaṃ diṭṭhā vā hoti anussavassutā vā – ‘evaṃsīlā sā bhaginī ahosi itipi, evaṃdhammā… evaṃpaññā… evaṃvihārinī… evaṃvimuttā sā bhaginī ahosi itipī’ti. Sā tassā saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussarantī tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati. Evampi kho, anuruddhā, upāsikāya phāsuvihāro hoti.

Sā tassā saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussarantī tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati. Evampi kho, anuruddhā, upāsikāya phāsuvihāro hoti.

‘‘Iti kho, anuruddhā, tathāgato na janakuhanatthaṃ na janalapanatthaṃ na lābhasakkārasilokānisaṃsatthaṃ na ‘iti maṃ jano jānātū’ti sāvake abbhatīte kālaṅkate upapattīsu byākaroti – ‘asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno’ti.
