Evaṃ te pañcaviññāṇasamaṅgīpi lokuttaradhammasamaṅgīyeva bhavissati. Sace panetaṃ sampaṭicchasi, satthārā saddhiṃ paṭivirujjhasi. Satthārā hi pañcaviññāṇakāyā ekantaṃ abyākatāva vuttā, taṃsamaṅgissa kusalākusalaṃ paṭikkhittaṃ, lokuttaramaggo ca ekantakusalo. Tasmā pajahetaṃ vāda’’nti paññapetabbo. Sace paññattiṃ na upagacchati, ‘‘gaccha pātova vihāraṃ pavisitvā yāguṃ pivāhī’’ti uyyojetabbo.
commentary_english:
182. . sattime, bhikkhave, puggalā: Here, what is indicated? It indicates this meaning: those for whom there is nothing to be done through diligence are two; those for whom there is something to be done are five; thus, all these are the seven types of persons.

There, *ubhatobhāgavimutto*: liberated through both aspects. He is liberated from the material body (*rūpakāya*) through the immaterial attainments (*arūpasamāpatti*), and from the mental body (*nāmakāya*) through the path (*magga*). He is fivefold by way of the four who, having arisen from each of the four immaterial attainments, contemplate formations and attain Arhatship, and the Anāgāmins who attain Arhatship having arisen from cessation. Here is a passage from the Pāli canon: "And what individual is liberated in both ways (*ubhatobhāgavimutto*)? Here, some individual dwells having contacted the eight liberations (*aṭṭha vimokkha*) with the body, and his cankers are destroyed by seeing with wisdom." (Pu. Pa. 208) Thus, it comes in the Abhidhamma by way of the one who has gained the eight liberations (*aṭṭhavimokkhalābhino*).

ubhatobhāgavimutto

paññāvimutto: liberated through wisdom (*prajñā*). He is fivefold by way of the *śuklavipaśyaka* (one who has bare insight), and the four who, having arisen from the four *dhyānas*, attain Arhatship. Here, in the Pāli canon, it comes only by way of rejecting the eight liberations. As he said: "He does not dwell having contacted the eight liberations with the body, but his cankers are destroyed by seeing with wisdom. This individual is called liberated through wisdom (*paññāvimutto*)."

paññāvimutto

The one who realizes by touching is called a kāyasakkhī (body-witness). He who first contacts the bliss of *dhyāna* and afterwards realizes cessation (*nirodha*) and *nirvāṇa*, should be understood as sixfold, starting with the one established in the fruit of Stream-Entry (*sotāpattiphala*) up to the one established in the path of Arhatship (*arahattamagga*). Therefore, he said: "Here, some individual dwells having contacted the eight liberations with the body, and some of his cankers are destroyed by seeing with wisdom. This individual is called a body-witness (*kāyasakkhī*)."

kāyasakkhī

The one who has attained vision is called a diṭṭhippatto (one attained to vision). Here is a concise characteristic of that: "Formations are painful, cessation is bliss" - it is known, seen, recognized, realized, and experienced with understanding; thus, he is one attained to vision (*diṭṭhippatto*). But in detail, he is also sixfold like the *kāyasakkhī*. Therefore, he said: "Here, some individual understands in accordance with reality, 'This is suffering'...pe... 'This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering,' and the teachings proclaimed by the Tathāgata have been reviewed and examined with wisdom...pe... This individual is called one attained to vision (*diṭṭhippatto*)." (Pu. Pa. 208).

diṭṭhippatto

saddhāvimutto: liberated through faith (*śraddhā*). He is also sixfold in the manner stated above. Therefore, he said: "Here, some individual understands in accordance with reality, 'This is suffering'...pe... 'This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.' The teachings proclaimed by the Tathāgata have been reviewed and examined with wisdom...pe... but not like the one attained to vision. This individual is called liberated through faith (*saddhāvimutto*)." (Pu. Pa. 208). Among these, for the one liberated through faith, at the moment of the preliminary path, the destruction of defilements (*kilesa*) occurs as if he is believing, as if he is approving, as if he is deciding. For the one attained to vision (*diṭṭhippatto*), at the moment of the preliminary path, the knowledge that cuts off defilements proceeds unhesitatingly, sharply, and bravely. Therefore, just as when someone cuts a banana tree with a not-too-sharp knife, the cut place is not smooth, the knife does not proceed quickly, a sound is heard, and a stronger effort must be made, such is the preliminary path cultivation (*pubbabhāgamaggabhāvanā*) of the one liberated through faith (*saddhāvimutta*). Just as, when someone cuts a banana tree with a sharp sword, the place where it was cut becomes smooth, the sword cuts quickly, no sound is heard, and there is no need for strenuous effort, so the preliminary practice of the path of one liberated by wisdom (paññāvimutto) should be understood. One liberated by faith (saddhāvimutto). Dharmaṃ anussaratīti *dhammānusārī*. One who remembers the Dhamma is a *dhammānusārī* (one who follows the Dhamma). The Dhamma is wisdom (paññā); the meaning is that he cultivates the path preceded by wisdom (paññāpubbaṅgamaṃ maggaṃ bhāvetīti attho). In the same way is the method for the *saddhānusārī* (one who follows faith). Both of these are only standing on the path to stream-entry (sotāpatti). It was said, "For a person who has undertaken the realization of the fruit of stream-entry (sotāpatti-phala), the faculty of wisdom is excessive; he cultivates the noble path (ariyamagga) that leads with wisdom, carrying wisdom.” This person is called a *dhammānusārī*. So too, "For a person who has undertaken the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, the faculty of faith is excessive; he cultivates the noble path that leads with faith, carrying faith." This person is called a *saddhānusārī*. This is a brief explanation. In detail, the talk about the Ubhatobhāgavimutta and so on is spoken of in the *Visuddhimagga* in the section on the cultivation of wisdom. Therefore, it should be understood in the way it is spoken of there. Since this Pāḷi comes here for the purpose of showing the distinction between these, since there is no attainment of the Formless (arūpa-samāpattiyo) without the attainment of form (rūpa-samāpattiyā), therefore, even when the Formless is spoken of, it should be understood that the eight liberations (vimokkha) are spoken of. *Dhammānusārī*, in the *saddhānusārimhi*, in the *Visuddhimagga*: *kāyena phusitvā*: having touched with the body, that is, having touched with the body consisting of name and form that is born together. *paññāya cassa disvā*: having seen it with wisdom, that is, having seen the Noble Truths with wisdom. *ekacce āsavā*: some āsavas, that is, some defilements are to be abandoned by the first path and so on. *tathāgatappaveditā*: proclaimed by the Tathāgata, that is, the four Noble Truths proclaimed by the Tathāgata. *paññāya vodiṭṭhā hontī*: they are well seen with wisdom, that is, in this place, morality (sīla) is spoken of, in this place concentration (samādhi), in this place insight (vipassanā), in this place the path (magga), in this place the fruit (phala); thus, through meaning in meaning, through cause in cause, because of habitual conduct, they are well seen with the wisdom of the path. *vocaritā*: wandered. *saddhā niviṭṭhā hotī*: faith is established, that is, resolute faith is established. *mattaso nijjhānaṃ khamantī*: they endure reflection in moderation, that is, they endure looking in moderation. *saddhāmatta* means just faith; the other is a synonym of that. Thus, among these people who should be diligent, three are learners (sekhā) who have penetrated the path and fruit. Living in agreeable lodgings, frequenting virtuous friends, harmonizing their senses, they gradually attain Arhatship. Therefore, for them, the meaning of the Pāḷi is as it stands. Finally, there are two who are endowed with the path to stream-entry. By them, agreeable lodgings are frequented for that path, virtuous friends are frequented, the senses are harmonized. Furthermore, for the sake of the three paths above, frequenting, consorting, harmonizing, they will gradually attain Arhatship; this is the meaning of the Pāḷi here. However, a quibbler, taking this very Pāḷi, says: "The supramundane path (lokuttaramaggo) is not of a single moment of consciousness (ekacittakkhaṇiko), it is of many moments of consciousness." He should be told: "If with one thought he frequents lodgings, with another... He associates with a *kalyāṇamitta* (good friend), he brings together the *indriya*s (senses) with another, and with the intention of another *maggacitta* (path-consciousness) you say, “The path is not of one mind-moment, but of many mind-moments." In this case, one frequenting a dwelling place sees a blue-tinged mountain, sees a forest, hears the sound of beasts and birds, smells the fragrance of flowers and fruits, tastes flavor while drinking water, and touches touch while sitting and lying down. Thus, one endowed with the five consciousnesses will be endowed with the supramundane *dhamma*s. But if you accept this, you contradict the Teacher. For the Teacher has said that the aggregates of the five consciousnesses are definitely indeterminate; the skillful and unskillful are rejected for one endowed with them, and the supramundane path is definitely skillful. Therefore, this view should be abandoned,’ he should be instructed. If he does not accept the instruction, he should be dismissed, saying, “Go, early in the morning enter the *vihāra* (monastery) and drink rice-gruel.”

mula_pali: 183. ‘‘Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ādikeneva aññārādhanaṃ vadāmi; api ca, bhikkhave, anupubbasikkhā anupubbakiriyā anupubbapaṭipadā aññārādhanā hoti. Kathañca, bhikkhave, anupubbasikkhā anupubbakiriyā anupubbapaṭipadā aññārādhanā hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, saddhājāto upasaṅkamati, upasaṅkamanto payirupāsati, payirupāsanto sotaṃ odahati, ohitasoto dhammaṃ suṇāti, sutvā dhammaṃ dhāreti, dhatānaṃ dhātānaṃ (ka.) dhammānaṃ atthaṃ upaparikkhati, atthaṃ upaparikkhato dhammā nijjhānaṃ khamanti, dhammanijjhānakkhantiyā sati chando jāyati, chandajāto ussahati, ussāhetvā tuleti, tulayitvā padahati, pahitatto samāno kāyena ceva paramasaccaṃ sacchikaroti, paññāya ca naṃ ativijjha passati. Sāpi nāma, bhikkhave, saddhā nāhosi; tampi nāma, bhikkhave, upasaṅkamanaṃ nāhosi; sāpi nāma, bhikkhave, payirupāsanā nāhosi; tampi nāma, bhikkhave, sotāvadhānaṃ nāhosi ; tampi nāma, bhikkhave, dhammassavanaṃ nāhosi; sāpi nāma, bhikkhave, dhammadhāraṇā nāhosi; sāpi nāma, bhikkhave, atthūpaparikkhā nāhosi; sāpi nāma, bhikkhave, dhammanijjhānakkhanti nāhosi; sopi nāma, bhikkhave, chando nāhosi; sopi nāma, bhikkhave, ussāho nāhosi; sāpi nāma, bhikkhave, tulanā nāhosi; tampi nāma, bhikkhave, padhānaṃ nāhosi. Vippaṭipannāttha, bhikkhave, micchāpaṭipannāttha, bhikkhave. Kīva dūrevime, bhikkhave, moghapurisā apakkantā imamhā dhammavinayā.
mula_english:
183. “I do not, monks, speak of attaining (aññārādhana) at the very beginning. But, monks, gradual training (anupubbasikkhā), gradual practice (anupubbakiriyā), gradual progress (anupubbapaṭipadā) leads to attainment (aññārādhanā).

And how, monks, does gradual training (anupubbasikkhā), gradual practice (anupubbakiriyā), gradual progress (anupubbapaṭipadā) lead to attainment (aññārādhanā)? Here, monks, a person with faith (saddhājāta) approaches a teacher; approaching, he attends upon him; attending upon him, he gives ear; giving ear, he hears the Dhamma; having heard the Dhamma, he remembers it; he examines the meaning of the teachings (dhammānaṃ atthaṃ) he has remembered; examining the meaning, the teachings find acceptance through reflection (dhammā nijjhānaṃ khamanti); with acceptance of the teachings through reflection, zeal (chando) is born; with zeal born, he strives; having strived, he weighs (the teachings); having weighed, he makes an effort, being one who has exerted himself, he realizes the ultimate truth (paramasaccaṃ) with his body, and with wisdom, he sees it by penetrating it.

That faith, monks, was not (true) faith (saddhā nāhosi); that approaching, monks, was not (true) approaching (upasaṅkamanaṃ nāhosi); that attending, monks, was not (true) attending (payirupāsanā nāhosi); that giving ear, monks, was not (true) giving ear (sotāvadhānaṃ nāhosi); that hearing of the Dhamma, monks, was not (true) hearing of the Dhamma (dhammassavanaṃ nāhosi); that remembering of the Dhamma, monks, was not (true) remembering of the Dhamma (dhammadhāraṇā nāhosi); that examination of the meaning, monks, was not (true) examination of the meaning (atthūpaparikkhā nāhosi); that acceptance of the teachings through reflection, monks, was not (true) acceptance of the teachings through reflection (dhammanijjhānakkhanti nāhosi); that zeal, monks, was not (true) zeal (chando nāhosi); that striving, monks, was not (true) striving (ussāho nāhosi); that weighing, monks, was not (true) weighing (tulanā nāhosi); that effort, monks, was not (true) effort (padhānaṃ nāhosi).

You have lost your way, monks; you have been practising the wrong way, monks.

How far you have strayed, monks, misguided men, from this Dhamma and Discipline (dhammavinayā)!
commentary_pali:
183.Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ādikenevāti ahaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭhamameva maṇḍūkassa uppatitvā gamanaṃ viya aññārādhanaṃ arahatte patiṭṭhānaṃ na vadāmi. Anupubbasikkhāti karaṇatthe paccattavacanaṃ. Parato padadvayepi eseva nayo. Saddhājātoti okappaniyasaddhāya jātasaddho. Upasaṅkamatīti garūnaṃ samīpaṃ gacchati. Payirupāsatīti santike nisīdati. Dhāretīti sādhukaṃ katvā dhāreti. Chando jāyatīti kattukamyatākusalacchando jāyati. Ussahatīti vīriyaṃ karoti. Tuletīti aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattāti tulayati. Tulayitvā padahatīti evaṃ tīraṇavipassanāya tulayanto maggapadhānaṃ padahati. Pahitattoti pesitacitto. Kāyena ceva paramasaccanti nāmakāyena nibbānasaccaṃ sacchikaroti. Paññāya cāti nāmakāyasampayuttāya maggapaññāya paṭivijjhati passati.

Idāni yasmā te satthu āgamanaṃ sutvā paccuggamanamattampi na akaṃsu, tasmā tesaṃ cariyaṃ garahanto sāpi nāma, bhikkhave, saddhā nāhosītiādimāha. Tattha kīvadūrevimeti kittakaṃ dūre ṭhāne. Yojanasatampi yojanasahassampi apakkantāti vattuṃ vaṭṭati, na pana kiñci āha. Catuppadaṃ veyyākaraṇanti catusaccabyākaraṇaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

sāpi nāma, bhikkhave, saddhā nāhosī kīvadūrevime Catuppadaṃ veyyākaraṇa
commentary_english:
183.
"""I am not,""" monks, """saying that the attainment of the state of an *arhat* is like a frog jumping and going, through another's grace, from the very beginning."""
*Anupubbasikkhā* means a word expressing individuality in the sense of instrumentality.
The same method [applies] even to the two words after *parato*.
*Saddhājāto* means one whose faith has arisen through faith based on conviction.
*Upasaṅkamatī* means he goes near the teachers.
*Payirupāsatī* means he sits near.
*Dhāretī* means having done well, he maintains.
*Chando jāyatī* means desire for doing wholesome things arises.
*Ussahatī* means he exerts energy (*vīryaṃ karoti*).
*Tuletī* means he weighs [thus]: impermanent (*aniccaṃ*), suffering (*dukkhaṃ*), not-self (*anattā*).
*Tulayitvā padahatī* means thus, weighing with insight that ascertains, he applies the exertion of the path (*maggapadhānaṃ padahati*).
*Pahitatto* means one whose mind is sent forth.
*Kāyena ceva paramasacca*nti means with the group of names, he realizes the truth of extinction (*nibbānasaccaṃ sacchikaroti*).
*Paññāya cā*ti means with the wisdom of the path (*maggapaññāya*) associated with the group of names, he penetrates and sees.

Now, because they did not even rise to greet the Teacher when they heard of his arrival, therefore, disparaging their conduct, he said, """Was there even faith, monks?""" etc.
There, *kīvadūrevime* means how far away in distance.
It is fitting to say that they have gone away a hundred *yojanas* or a thousand *yojanas*, but he did not say anything at all.
*Catuppadaṃ veyyākaraṇa*nti means it was said with reference to the exposition of the four truths (*catusaccabyākaraṇaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ*).

"""Was there even faith, monks?""" """How far away?""" """Four-footed grammar."""

mula_pali:
184. ‘‘Atthi , bhikkhave, catuppadaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ yassuddiṭṭhassa viññū puriso nacirasseva paññāyatthaṃ ājāneyya. Uddisissāmi vo uddiṭṭhassāpi (ka.), bhikkhave, ājānissatha me ta’’nti? ‘‘Ke ca mayaṃ, bhante, ke ca dhammassa aññātāro’’ti? Yopi so, bhikkhave, satthā āmisagaru āmisadāyādo āmisehi saṃsaṭṭho viharati tassa pāyaṃ evarūpī paṇopaṇaviyā na upeti – ‘evañca no assa atha naṃ kareyyāma, na ca no evamassa na naṃ kareyyāmā’ti, kiṃ pana, bhikkhave, yaṃ tathāgato sabbaso āmisehi visaṃsaṭṭho viharati. Saddhassa, bhikkhave, sāvakassa satthusāsane pariyogāhiya pariyogāya (sī. pī. ka.), pariyogayha (syā. kaṃ.) vattato ayamanudhammo hoti – ‘satthā bhagavā, sāvakohamasmi; jānāti bhagavā, nāhaṃ jānāmī’ti. Saddhassa, bhikkhave, sāvakassa satthusāsane pariyogāhiya vattato ruḷhanīyaṃ rumhaniyaṃ (sī. pī.) satthusāsanaṃ hoti ojavantaṃ. Saddhassa, bhikkhave, sāvakassa satthusāsane pariyogāhiya vattato ayamanudhammo hoti – ‘kāmaṃ taco ca nhāru ca aṭṭhi ca avasissatu, sarīre upasussatu upasussatu sarīre (sī.), sarīre avasussatu (ka.) maṃsalohitaṃ, yaṃ taṃ purisathāmena purisavīriyena purisaparakkamena pattabbaṃ na taṃ apāpuṇitvā vīriyassa saṇṭhānaṃ santhānaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) bhavissatī’ti. Saddhassa, bhikkhave, sāvakassa satthusāsane pariyogāhiya vattato dvinnaṃ phalānaṃ aññataraṃ phalaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – diṭṭheva dhamme aññā, sati vā upādisese anāgāmitā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Kīṭāgirisuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

Bhikkhuvaggo niṭṭhito dutiyo.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Kuñjara-rāhula-sassataloko, mālukyaputto ca bhaddāli-nāmo;

Khudda-dijātha-sahampatiyācaṃ, nāḷaka-raññikiṭāgirināmo.
mula_english:
“Bhikkhus, there is a four-phrased statement, and when it is recited a wise man would quickly understand it. I will recite it to you, bhikkhus; listen to me.”

“But who are we, venerable sir, and who are the knowers of the Dhamma?”

“Bhikkhus, even with a teacher who is concerned with material things, an heir to material things, attached to material things, such haggling by his disciples would not be proper: ‘If we get this, we will do it; if we don’t get this, we won’t do it’; so what should be said when the teacher is the *Tathāgata*, who is utterly detached from material things?

“Bhikkhus, for a faithful disciple who is intent on fathoming the Teacher’s Dispensation, it is proper that he conduct himself thus: ‘The Blessed One is the Teacher, I am a disciple; the Blessed One knows, I do not know.’

“Bhikkhus, for a faithful disciple who is intent on fathoming the Teacher’s Dispensation, the Teacher’s Dispensation is nourishing and refreshing.

“Bhikkhus, for a faithful disciple who is intent on fathoming the Teacher’s Dispensation, it is proper that he conduct himself thus: ‘Let skin, sinew, and bone remain, and let the flesh and blood in the body dry up; but I will not give up my efforts until I have attained whatever can be attained by manly strength, manly energy, and manly exertion.’

“Bhikkhus, for a faithful disciple who is intent on fathoming the Teacher’s Dispensation, one of two fruits may be expected: either final knowledge here and now or, if there is a trace of clinging left, non-return.”

The Blessed One said this. Elated, those *bhikkhus* delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The Kīṭāgiri Sutta, the tenth, is finished.

The Second Chapter for Monks is finished.

Its summary:

Kuñjara, Rāhula, Sassataloka,
Mālukyaputta and Bhaddāli-nāma;
Khudda, Dijātha, and Sahampatiyācaṃ,
Nāḷaka, Raññi, Kīṭāgiri-nāma.
commentary_pali:
184.Yassuddiṭṭhassāti yassa uddiṭṭhassa. Yopiso, bhikkhave, satthāti bāhirakasatthāraṃ dasseti. Evarūpīti evaṃjātikā. Paṇopaṇaviyāti paṇaviyā ca opaṇaviyā ca . Na upetīti na hoti. Kayavikkayakāle viya agghavaḍḍhanahāpanaṃ na hotīti attho. Ayaṃ goṇo kiṃ agghati, vīsati agghatīti bhaṇanto paṇati nāma. Na vīsati agghati, dasa agghatīti bhaṇanto opaṇati nāma. Idaṃ paṭisedhento āha ‘‘paṇopaṇaviyā na upetī’’ti. Idāni taṃ paṇopaṇaviyaṃ dassetuṃ evañca no assa, atha naṃ kareyyāma, na ca no evamassa, na naṃ kareyyāmāti āha.

Kiṃ pana, bhikkhaveti, bhikkhave, yaṃ tathāgato sabbaso āmisehi visaṃsaṭṭho viharati, evaṃ visaṃsaṭṭhassa satthuno evarūpā paṇopaṇaviyā kiṃ yujjissati? Pariyogāhiya vattatoti pariyogāhitvā ukkhipitvā gahetvā vattantassa. Ayamanudhammoti ayaṃ sabhāvo. Jānāti bhagavā, nāhaṃ jānāmīti bhagavā ekāsanabhojane ānisaṃsaṃ jānāti, ahaṃ na jānāmīti mayi saddhāya divasassa tayo vāre bhojanaṃ pahāya ekāsanabhojanaṃ bhuñjati. Ruḷahanīyanti rohanīyaṃ. Ojavantanti sinehavantaṃ. Kāmaṃ taco cāti iminā caturaṅgavīriyaṃ dasseti. Ettha hi taco ekaṃ aṅgaṃ, nhāru ekaṃ, aṭṭhi ekaṃ, maṃsalohitaṃ ekanti evaṃ caturaṅgasamannāgataṃ vīriyaṃ adhiṭṭhahitvā arahattaṃ appatvā na vuṭṭhahissāmīti evaṃ paṭipajjatīti dasseti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānameva. Desanaṃ pana bhagavā neyyapuggalassa vasena arahattanikūṭena niṭṭhāpesīti.

Kiṃ pana, bhikkhave Pariyogāhiya vattato Ayamanudhammo Jānāti bhagavā, nāhaṃ jānāmī Ruḷahanīya Ojavanta Kāmaṃ taco cā

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Kīṭāgirisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Dutiyavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
184. *Yassuddiṭṭhassā* means "of whom it was pointed out."

*Yopi so, bhikkhave, satthā* means "he shows a teacher who is an outsider, O monks."

*Evarūpī* means "of such a kind."

*Paṇopaṇaviyā* means "selling dear and cheap."

*Na upetī* means "does not approach," that is, it is without meaning when increasing or decreasing the price during a time of buying and selling.

"This ox, how much is it worth? Twenty is what it is worth," saying this, it is called *paṇati*.

"Not twenty is what it is worth, ten is what it is worth," saying this, it is called *opaṇati*.

Rejecting this, he said, "He does not approach selling dear and cheap."

Now, to show that selling dear and cheap, he said, "Thus it will not be for us, and what should we do? It will not be thus for us, and we should not do it."

*Kiṃ pana, bhikkhave* means, "O monks, since the *Tathāgata* dwells completely detached from sensual pleasures, how could such selling dear and cheap be fitting for a teacher who is thus detached?" *Pariyogāhiya vattato* means "for one speaking after having investigated, lifted up, and taken hold of."

*Ayamanudhammo* means "this is the nature."

*Jānāti bhagavā, nāhaṃ jānāmī* means "the Blessed One knows the advantages of eating a single meal, but I do not know," and because of faith in me, he abandons three meals of the day and eats a single meal.

*Ruḷahanīya* means *rohanīyaṃ*.

*Ojavanta* means *sinehavantaṃ*.

*Kāmaṃ taco cā* means "by this, he shows the vigor of the four components."

Here, skin is one component, sinew is one, bone is one, and flesh and blood are one; thus, having undertaken the vigor endowed with the four components, he shows that, not having attained *arhatship*, he will not get up.

The rest is clear throughout.

However, the Blessed One brought the teaching to completion in accordance with a person who is to be guided, with the pinnacle of *arhatship*.

*Kiṃ pana, bhikkhave, pariyogāhiya vattato, ayamanudhammo, jānāti bhagavā, nāhaṃ jānāmī, ruḷahanīya, ojavanta, kāmaṃ taco cā.*

Commentary on the Kīṭāgiri Sūtra, from the *Papañcasūdanī*, commentary on the *Majjhimanikāya*, is finished.

Commentary on the Second Vagga is finished.

mula_pali: 185. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena vacchagotto paribbājako ekapuṇḍarīke paribbājakārāme paṭivasati. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya vesāliṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – ‘‘atippago kho tāva vesāliyaṃ piṇḍāya carituṃ; yaṃnūnāhaṃ yena ekapuṇḍarīko paribbājakārāmo yena vacchagotto paribbājako tenupasaṅkameyya’’nti. Atha kho bhagavā yena ekapuṇḍarīko paribbājakārāmo yena vacchagotto paribbājako tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘etu kho, bhante, bhagavā. Svāgataṃ sāgataṃ (sī. pī.), bhante, bhagavato. Cirassaṃ kho, bhante, bhagavā imaṃ pariyāyamakāsi yadidaṃ idhāgamanāya. Nisīdatu, bhante, bhagavā idamāsanaṃ paññatta’’nti. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Vacchagottopi kho paribbājako aññataraṃ nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante – ‘samaṇo gotamo sabbaññū sabbadassāvī, aparise+saṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paṭijānāti, carato ca me tiṭṭhato ca suttassa ca jāgarassa ca satataṃ samitaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paccupaṭṭhita’nti. Ye te, bhante, evamāhaṃsu – ‘samaṇo gotamo sabbaññū sabbadassāvī, aparisesaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paṭijānāti, carato ca me tiṭṭhato ca suttassa ca jāgarassa ca satataṃ samitaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paccupaṭṭhita’nti, kacci te, bhante, bhagavato vuttavādino, na ca bhagavantaṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhanti, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākaronti, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchatī’’ti? ‘‘Ye te, vaccha, evamāhaṃsu – ‘samaṇo gotamo sabbaññū sabbadassāvī, aparisesaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paṭijānāti, carato ca me tiṭṭhato ca suttassa ca jāgarassa ca satataṃ samitaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paccupaṭṭhita’nti, na me te vuttavādino, abbhācikkhanti ca pana maṃ asatā abhūtenā’’ti.
mula_english:
Thus I have heard.

On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Vesālī in the Great Wood in the Hall with the Peaked Roof.

Now at that time the wanderer Vacchagotta was staying in the Wanderers’ Park of the Single White-lotus Mango Tree.

Then, early in the morning, the Blessed One dressed, and taking his bowl and outer robe, went into Vesālī for alms.

Then the Blessed One thought: “It is still too early to wander for alms in Vesālī. Suppose I went to the wanderer Vacchagotta in the Wanderers’ Park of the Single White-lotus Mango Tree.”

Then the Blessed One went to the wanderer Vacchagotta in the Wanderers’ Park of the Single White-lotus Mango Tree.

The wanderer Vacchagotta saw the Blessed One coming in the distance.

Seeing the Blessed One, he said to him: “Come, venerable sir, Blessed One.

Welcome, venerable sir, to the Blessed One!

It is long since the Blessed One found an opportunity to come here.

Be seated, venerable sir, Blessed One. This seat has been prepared.”

The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat.

Then the wanderer Vacchagotta, taking a low seat, sat down at one side.

Seated to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Blessed One: “I have heard this, venerable sir: ‘The *śramaṇa* Gotama claims to be all-knowing *sarvajñū* and all-seeing *sarvadassāvī*, to have complete *aparisesaṃ* knowledge and vision *ñāṇadassanaṃ*: “Whether I am walking or standing or sleeping or awake, continuous and constant *satataṃ samitaṃ* knowledge and vision *ñāṇadassanaṃ* are present to me.’”

Those who say this, venerable sir: ‘The *śramaṇa* Gotama claims to be all-knowing *sarvajñū* and all-seeing *sarvadassāvī*, to have complete *aparisesaṃ* knowledge and vision *ñāṇadassanaṃ*: “Whether I am walking or standing or sleeping or awake, continuous and constant *satataṃ samitaṃ* knowledge and vision *ñāṇadassanaṃ* are present to me”’—do they speak what has been said by the Blessed One, and not misrepresent him with what is contrary to fact? Do they explain in accordance with the *dharma* in such a way that nothing which provides a ground for censure can be legitimately deduced from their assertion?”

“Those who say this, Vaccha: ‘The *śramaṇa* Gotama claims to be all-knowing *sarvajñū* and all-seeing *sarvadassāvī*, to have complete *aparisesaṃ* knowledge and vision *ñāṇadassanaṃ*: “Whether I am walking or standing or sleeping or awake, continuous and constant *satataṃ samitaṃ* knowledge and vision *ñāṇadassanaṃ* are present to me”’—they do not speak what has been said by me, and they misrepresent me with what is false and contrary to fact.”
commentary_pali: 185.Evaṃme sutanti tevijjavacchasuttaṃ. Tattha ekapuṇḍarīketi puṇḍarīko vuccati setambarukkho, so tasmiṃ ārāme eko puṇḍarīko atthīti ekapuṇḍarīko. Etadahosīti tattha pavisitukāmatāya ahosi. Cirassaṃ kho, bhanteti pakatiyā āgatapubbataṃ upādāya. Dhammassa cānudhammanti idha sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ dhammo nāma, mahājanassa byākaraṇaṃ anudhammo nāma. Sesaṃ jīvakasutte (ma. ni. 2.51 ādayo) vuttanayameva. Na me teti ananuññāya ṭhatvā anuññampi paṭikkhipati. ‘‘Sabbaññū sabbadassāvī aparisesaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paṭijānātī’’ti hi idaṃ anujānitabbaṃ siyā, – ‘‘carato ca me…pe… paccupaṭṭhita’’nti idaṃ pana nānujānitabbaṃ. Sabbaññutaññāṇena hi āvajjitvā pajānāti. Tasmā ananuññāya ṭhatvā anuññampi paṭikkhipanto evamāha.
commentary_english:
185.
Thus, I have heard: the Tevijjavacchasuttaṃ.

Herein, *ekapuṇḍarīke* means *puṇḍarīka* is said to be a white mango tree; so in that monastery, because there is one *puṇḍarīka*, it is *ekapuṇḍarīka*.

*Etadahosī* means it was because of a desire to enter there.

*"Cirassaṃ kho, bhante"* means by taking up the state of having previously come by nature.

*"Dhammassa cānudhamma"* means here, omniscience-knowledge is called *dharma*, the explanation of the great multitude is called *anudhamma*.

The rest is like what was said in the Jīvakasutta (Ma.
Ni.
2.
51 ff.).

*"Na me te"* means having stood without permission, he rejects even permission.

"The all-knowing, all-seeing one claims complete knowledge and vision," this, indeed, should be permitted, – "While wandering, he is ever-present to me…" This, however, should not be permitted.

For he knows by considering it with omniscience-knowledge.

Therefore, having stood without permission, rejecting even permission, he said thus.

mula_pali:
186. ‘‘Kathaṃ byākaramānā pana mayaṃ, bhante, vuttavādino ceva bhagavato assāma, na ca bhagavantaṃ abhūtena abbhācikkheyyāma, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākareyyāma, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgaccheyyā’’ti?

‘‘‘Tevijjo samaṇo gotamo’ti kho, vaccha, byākaramāno vuttavādī ceva me assa, na ca maṃ abhūtena abbhācikkheyya, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākareyya, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgaccheyya. Ahañhi, vaccha, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarāmi, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarāmi. Ahañhi, vaccha, yāvadeva ākaṅkhāmi dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passāmi cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate…pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāmi. Ahañhi, vaccha, āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmi.

‘‘‘Tevijjo samaṇo gotamo’ti kho, vaccha, byākaramāno vuttavādī ceva me assa, na ca maṃ abhūtena abbhācikkheyya, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākareyya, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgaccheyyā’’ti.

Evaṃ vutte, vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘atthi nu kho, bho gotama, koci gihī gihisaṃyojanaṃ appahāya kāyassa bhedā dukkhassantakaro’’ti? ‘‘Natthi kho, vaccha, koci gihī gihisaṃyojanaṃ appahāya kāyassa bhedā dukkhassantakaro’’ti.

‘‘Atthi pana, bho gotama, koci gihī gihisaṃyojanaṃ appahāya kāyassa bhedā saggūpago’’ti? ‘‘Na kho, vaccha, ekaṃyeva sataṃ na dve satāni na tīṇi satāni na cattāri satāni na pañca satāni, atha kho bhiyyova ye gihī gihisaṃyojanaṃ appahāya kāyassa bhedā saggūpagā’’ti ‘‘atthi kho vaccha koci gihī gihisaṃyojanaṃ appahāya kāyassa bhedā saggūpagoti’’. (ka.).

‘‘atthi kho vaccha koci gihī gihisaṃyojanaṃ appahāya kāyassa bhedā saggūpagoti’’. (ka.)

‘‘Atthi nu kho, bho gotama, koci ājīvako ājīviko (ka.) kāyassa bhedā dukkhassantakaro’’ti? ‘‘Natthi kho, vaccha, koci ājīvako kāyassa bhedā dukkhassantakaro’’ti.

ājīviko (ka.)

‘‘Atthi pana, bho gotama, koci ājīvako kāyassa bhedā saggūpago’’ti? ‘‘Ito kho so, vaccha, ekanavuto kappo ito ko vaccha ekanavute kappe (ka.) yamahaṃ anussarāmi, nābhijānāmi kañci ājīvakaṃ saggūpagaṃ aññatra ekena; sopāsi kammavādī kiriyavādī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ sante, bho gotama, suññaṃ aduṃ titthāyatanaṃ antamaso saggūpagenapī’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ, vaccha, suññaṃ aduṃ titthāyatanaṃ antamaso saggūpagenapī’’ti.

ito ko vaccha ekanavute kappe (ka.)

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Tevijjavacchasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.
mula_english:
186. How, when we explain, Venerable Sir, might we be speakers of what has been said by the Blessed One, and not misrepresent the Blessed One with what is contrary to fact; and might we explain in accordance with the Dhamma, so that no reasonable consequence of our assertion would give ground for criticism?”

“'Gotama the recluse has the threefold knowledge ( *tevijja* )'—Vaccha, if one explains in this way, one would be stating what has been said by me and would not misrepresent me with what is contrary to fact; one would explain in accordance with the Dhamma, and no reasonable consequence of one’s assertion would give ground for criticism.

“For in so far as I wish, Vaccha, I recollect my manifold past lives, that is, one birth, two births… with their aspects and particulars I recollect my manifold past lives.

“And in so far as I wish, Vaccha, with the divine eye ( *dibbaṃ cakkhuṃ* ), which is purified and surpasses the human, I see beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, and I understand how beings pass on according to their actions.

“And by realizing for myself with direct knowledge, Vaccha, I here and now enter upon and abide in the deliverance of mind ( *cetovimuttiṃ* ) and deliverance by wisdom ( *paññāvimuttiṃ* ) that are taintless with the destruction of the taints ( *āsavānaṃ khayā* ).”

“'Gotama the recluse has the threefold knowledge'—Vaccha, if one explains in this way, one would be stating what has been said by me and would not misrepresent me with what is contrary to fact; one would explain in accordance with the Dhamma, and no reasonable consequence of one’s assertion would give ground for criticism.”

When this was said, Vacchagotta the wanderer said to the Blessed One: “Master Gotama, is there any householder who, without abandoning the fetter of householdership (*gihisaṃyojanaṃ*), on the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*) has made an end of suffering (*dukkhassantakaro*)?”

“Vaccha, there is no householder who, without abandoning the fetter of householdership, on the dissolution of the body, has made an end of suffering.”

“But, Master Gotama, is there any householder who, without abandoning the fetter of householdership, on the dissolution of the body has gone to heaven (*saggūpago*)?”

“Vaccha, there are not only one hundred or two or three or four or five hundred, but far more householders who, without abandoning the fetter of householdership, on the dissolution of the body have gone to heaven.”

“Master Gotama, is there any *Ājīvaka* who, on the dissolution of the body, has made an end of suffering?”

“Vaccha, there is no *Ājīvaka* who, on the dissolution of the body, has made an end of suffering.”

“But, Master Gotama, is there any *Ājīvaka* who, on the dissolution of the body, has gone to heaven?”

“When I recollect the past ninety-one aeons, Vaccha, I do not recall any *Ājīvaka* who, on the dissolution of the body, went to heaven, with one exception, and he held the doctrine of the moral efficacy of action (*kammavādī*), the doctrine of the moral efficacy of deeds (*kiriyavādī*).”

“So, Master Gotama, is the *Tīrthāyatana* empty of even those who go to heaven?”

“Yes, Vaccha, the *Tīrthāyatana* is empty of even those who go to heaven.”

This the Blessed One said.

Vacchagotta the wanderer was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

The *Tevijjavacchasutta* is finished, the first.
commentary_pali:
186.Āsavānaṃ khayāti ettha sakiṃ khīṇānaṃ āsavānaṃ puna khepetabbābhāvā yāvadevāti na vuttaṃ. Pubbenivāsañāṇena cettha bhagavā atītajānanaguṇaṃ dasseti, dibbacakkhuñāṇena paccuppannajānanaguṇaṃ, āsavakkhayañāṇena lokuttaraguṇanti. Iti imāhi tīhi vijjāhi sakalabuddhaguṇe saṃkhipitvā kathesi.

Gihisaṃyojananti gihibandhanaṃ gihiparikkhāresu nikantiṃ. Natthi kho vacchāti gihisaṃyojanaṃ appahāya dukkhassantakaro nāma natthi. Yepi hi santatimahāmatto uggaseno seṭṭhiputto vītasokadārakoti gihiliṅge ṭhitāva arahattaṃ pattā, tepi maggena sabbasaṅkhāresu nikantiṃ sukkhāpetvā pattā. Taṃ patvā pana na tena liṅgena aṭṭhaṃsu, gihiliṅgaṃ nāmetaṃ hīnaṃ, uttamaguṇaṃ dhāretuṃ na sakkoti. Tasmā tattha ṭhito arahattaṃ patvā taṃdivasameva pabbajati vā parinibbāti vā. Bhūmadevatā pana tiṭṭhanti. Kasmā? Nilīyanokāsassa atthitāya. Sesakāmabhave manussesu sotāpannādayo tayo tiṭṭhanti, kāmāvacaradevesu sotāpannā sakadāgāmino ca, anāgāmikhīṇāsavā panettha na tiṭṭhanti. Kasmā? Tañhi ṭhānaṃ laḷitajanassa āvāso, natthi tattha tesaṃ pavivekārahaṃ paṭicchannaṭṭhānañca. Iti tattha khīṇāsavo parinibbāti, anāgāmī cavitvā suddhāvāse nibbattati. Kāmāvacaradevato upari pana cattāropi ariyā tiṭṭhanti.

Gihisaṃyojana Natthi kho vacchā

Sopāsi kammavādīti sopi kammavādī ahosi, kiriyampi na paṭibāhittha. Tañhi ekanavutikappamatthake attānaṃyeva gahetvā katheti. Tadā kira mahāsatto pāsaṇḍapariggaṇhanatthaṃ pabbajito tassapi pāsaṇḍassa nipphalabhāvaṃ jānitvā vīriyaṃ na hāpesi, kiriyavādī hutvā sagge nibbattati. Tasmā evamāha. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Sopāsi kammavādī

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Tevijjavacchasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
186. *Āsavānaṃ khayā* means that it is not stated that the *āsavas* that are destroyed once should be destroyed again, because there is no possibility of destroying them again.

Here, the Blessed One reveals the quality of knowing the past by means of the knowledge of former existences (*pubbenivāsañāṇa*), the quality of knowing the present by means of the divine eye knowledge (*dibbacakkhuñāṇa*), and the quality of supramundane knowledge by means of the knowledge of the destruction of the *āsavas* (*āsavakkhayañāṇa*).

Thus, he has spoken concisely of all the qualities of the Buddha by these three knowledges (*vijjā*).

*Gihisaṃyojana* means the bond of a householder, attachment to the possessions of a householder.

*"Natthi kho vacchā"* means there is no one who makes an end to suffering without abandoning the bond of a householder (*gihisaṃyojana*).

Even those, such as Santati Mahāmatta, Uggasena the merchant's son, and Vītasoka Dāraka, who, while remaining in the guise of householders (*gihiliṅga*), attained *arahatta*, attained the drying up of attachment in all conditioned things (*sabbasankhāresu nikantiṃ sukkhāpetvā pattā*) by means of the path (*magga*).

Having attained that, they did not stand by that guise, for the guise of a householder is base (*hīnaṃ*), it is not capable of bearing the highest qualities (*uttamaguṇaṃ dhāretuṃ na sakkoti*).

Therefore, having attained *arahatta* while staying there, he either goes forth or attains final *nirvāṇa* on that very day.

But the earth deities remain.

Why? Because of the existence of a place of concealment (*nilīyanokāsassa atthitāya*).

In the remaining realm of desire (*sesakāmabhave*), the *sotāpannas* and the others remain, but in the desire-realm heavens (*kāmāvacaradevesu*) the *sotāpannas*, the *sakadāgāminos*, and the *anāgāmikhīṇāsavas* do not remain.

Why? Because that place is the dwelling of frivolous people (*laḷitajanassa āvāso*), there is no place fit for seclusion (*pavivekārahaṃ*) and concealment for them there.

Thus, there the *khīṇāsava* attains final *nirvāṇa*, the *anāgāmī* is reborn in the pure abodes (*suddhāvāse nibbattati*) after dying.

Above the *kāmāvacaradevato*, however, even the four *ariyas* remain.

*Gihisaṃyojana Natthi kho vacchā*

*Sopāsi kammavādī* means that he was also a *kammavādī*, and he did not reject action either.

He says that he took himself at the head of ninety-one aeons (*ekanavutikappamatthake attānaṃyeva gahetvā katheti*).

Then, it is said that the great being (*mahāsatto*), having gone forth for the purpose of embracing the heretics (*pāsaṇḍapariggaṇhanatthaṃ pabbajito*), having known the fruitlessness of that heresy (*tassapi pāsaṇḍassa nipphalabhāvaṃ jānitvā*) did not diminish his vigor (*vīriyaṃ na hāpesi*), having become a proponent of action (*kiriyavādī hutvā*) is reborn in heaven (*sagge nibbattati*).

Therefore, he spoke thus.

The rest is clear throughout.

*Sopāsi kammavādī*

The commentary on the *Tevijjavacchasutta* is finished.

mula_pali:
187. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

‘‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, ‘sassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi evaṃdiṭṭhī (sī. syā. kaṃ. ka.) bhavaṃ gotamo’’ti? ‘‘Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘sassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’’’nti.

evaṃdiṭṭhī (sī. syā. kaṃ. ka.)

‘‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, ‘asassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’’ti? ‘‘Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘asassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’’’nti.

‘‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, ‘antavā loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’’ti? ‘‘Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘antavā loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’’’nti.

‘‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, ‘anantavā loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’’ti? ‘‘Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘anantavā loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’’’nti.

‘‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’’ti? ‘‘Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’’’nti.

‘‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’’ti? ‘‘Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’’’nti.

‘‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’’ti? ‘‘Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’’’nti.

‘‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’’ti? ‘‘Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’’’nti.

‘‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’’ti ? ‘‘Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’’’nti.

‘‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’’ti? ‘‘Na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’’’nti.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard: On one occasion the Blessed One (bhagavā) was living near Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Wood, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

Then Vacchagotta the wanderer approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One (bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi).

When this courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side.

Seated at one side, Vacchagotta the wanderer said this to the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ etadavoca):

“How is it, Master Gotama, when Master Gotama is asked if he holds the view ‘The cosmos is eternal, only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless’ (sassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña)?

“No, Vaccha, I do not hold the view that ‘The cosmos is eternal, only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless’ (sassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña).”

“Then does Master Gotama hold the view: ‘The cosmos is not eternal: only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless’ (asassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña)?” “No, Vaccha, I do not hold that view.”

“Then does Master Gotama hold the view: ‘The cosmos is finite: only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless’ (antavā loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña)?” “No, Vaccha, I do not hold that view.”

“Then does Master Gotama hold the view: ‘The cosmos is infinite: only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless’ (anantavā loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña)?” “No, Vaccha, I do not hold that view.”

“Then does Master Gotama hold the view: ‘The soul & the body are the same: only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless’ (taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña)?” “No, Vaccha, I do not hold that view.”

“Then does Master Gotama hold the view: ‘The soul & the body are different: only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless’ (aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña)?” “No, Vaccha, I do not hold that view.”

“Then does Master Gotama hold the view: ‘After death a Tathāgata exists: only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless’ (hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña)?” “No, Vaccha, I do not hold that view.”

“Then does Master Gotama hold the view: ‘After death a Tathāgata does not exist: only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless’ (na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña)?” “No, Vaccha, I do not hold that view.”

“Then does Master Gotama hold the view: ‘After death a Tathāgata both exists & does not exist: only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless’ (hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña)?” “No, Vaccha, I do not hold that view.”

“Then does Master Gotama hold the view: ‘After death a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist: only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless’ (neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña)?” “No, Vaccha, I do not hold that view.”
commentary_pali: 187.Evaṃme sutanti aggivacchasuttaṃ. Tattha na kho ahanti paṭhamavāre nāhaṃ sassatadiṭṭhikoti vadati, dutiye nāhaṃ ucchedadiṭṭhikoti. Evaṃ antānantikādivasena sabbavāresu paṭikkhepo veditabbo. Hoti ca na ca hotīti ayaṃ panettha ekaccasassatavādo. Neva hoti na na hotīti ayaṃ amarāvikkhepoti veditabbo.
commentary_english:
187. Thus, I have heard (evaṃ me sutaṃ): the Aggivacchasutta.

There, "No, indeed, I am not (na kho ahaṃ)"—in the first instance, he says, "I am not one who holds the eternalist view (nāhaṃ sassatadiṭṭhiko)"; in the second, "I am not one who holds the annihilationist view (nāhaṃ ucchedadiṭṭhiko)."

Thus, the rejection (paṭikkhepo) in all instances (sabbavāresu) should be understood (veditabbo) by way of [affirming or denying] end, endlessness, and so forth (antānantikādivasena).

"It is (hoti), and it is not (na ca hoti)"—this is the partial eternalism (ekaccasassatavādo) here.

"Neither is it (neva hoti) nor is it not (na na hoti)"—this should be understood as the eel-wriggler's evasion (amarāvikkhepoti veditabbo).

mula_pali:
188. ‘‘‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, sassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – sassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi moghamaññantīti vadesi (sī.), moghamaññanti iti vadesi (?). ‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, asassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṃ, vaccha , evaṃdiṭṭhi – asassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, antavā loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – antavā loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, anantavā loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – anantavā loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi.

‘‘‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi. ‘Kiṃ pana, bho gotama, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhi bhavaṃ gotamo’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na kho ahaṃ, vaccha, evaṃdiṭṭhi – neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti vadesi.

‘‘Kiṃ pana bho gotamo ādīnavaṃ sampassamāno evaṃ imāni sabbaso diṭṭhigatāni anupagato’’ti?
mula_english:
188. “‘Then, Master Gotama, is the cosmos eternal? Is only this true, and anything else worthless?’—when asked this, are you of such a view?”

“No, Vatsa, I am not of such a view. The cosmos is eternal; only this is true, and anything else worthless.”

“Then, Master Gotama, is the cosmos not eternal? Is only this true, and anything else worthless?’—when asked this, are you of such a view?”

“No, Vatsa, I am not of such a view. The cosmos is not eternal; only this is true, and anything else worthless.”

“Then, Master Gotama, is the cosmos finite? Is only this true, and anything else worthless?’—when asked this, are you of such a view?”

“No, Vatsa, I am not of such a view. The cosmos is finite; only this is true, and anything else worthless.”

“Then, Master Gotama, is the cosmos infinite? Is only this true, and anything else worthless?’—when asked this, are you of such a view?”

“No, Vatsa, I am not of such a view. The cosmos is infinite; only this is true, and anything else worthless.”

“Then, Master Gotama, is the soul the same as the body? Is only this true, and anything else worthless?’—when asked this, are you of such a view?”

“No, Vatsa, I am not of such a view. The soul is the same as the body; only this is true, and anything else worthless.”

“Then, Master Gotama, is the soul different from the body? Is only this true, and anything else worthless?’—when asked this, are you of such a view?”

“No, Vatsa, I am not of such a view. The soul is different from the body; only this is true, and anything else worthless.”

“Then, Master Gotama, does the *Tathāgata* exist after death? Is only this true, and anything else worthless?’—when asked this, are you of such a view?”

“No, Vatsa, I am not of such a view. The *Tathāgata* exists after death; only this is true, and anything else worthless.”

“Then, Master Gotama, does the *Tathāgata* not exist after death? Is only this true, and anything else worthless?’—when asked this, are you of such a view?”

“No, Vatsa, I am not of such a view. The *Tathāgata* does not exist after death; only this is true, and anything else worthless.”

“Then, Master Gotama, does the *Tathāgata* both exist and not exist after death? Is only this true, and anything else worthless?’—when asked this, are you of such a view?”

“No, Vatsa, I am not of such a view. The *Tathāgata* both exists and does not exist after death; only this is true, and anything else worthless.”

“Then, Master Gotama, does the *Tathāgata* neither exist nor not exist after death? Is only this true, and anything else worthless?’—when asked this, are you of such a view?”

“No, Vatsa, I am not of such a view. The *Tathāgata* neither exists nor does not exist after death; only this is true, and anything else worthless.”

“Master Gotama, seeing what drawback do you thus entirely avoid all these speculative views?”

mula_pali:
189. ‘‘‘Sassato loko’ti kho, vaccha, diṭṭhigatametaṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhikantāraṃ (sī. pī.) diṭṭhivisūkaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ sadukkhaṃ savighātaṃ saupāyāsaṃ sapariḷāhaṃ, na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattati . ‘Asassato loko’ti kho, vaccha…pe… ‘antavā loko’ti kho, vaccha…pe… ‘anantavā loko’ti kho, vaccha…pe… ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’nti kho, vaccha…pe… ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’nti kho, vaccha…pe… ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti kho, vaccha …pe… ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti kho, vaccha…pe… ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti kho, vaccha…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti kho, vaccha, diṭṭhigatametaṃ diṭṭhigahanaṃ diṭṭhikantāro diṭṭhivisūkaṃ diṭṭhivipphanditaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ sadukkhaṃ savighātaṃ saupāyāsaṃ sapariḷāhaṃ, na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattati. Imaṃ kho ahaṃ, vaccha, ādīnavaṃ sampassamāno evaṃ imāni sabbaso diṭṭhigatāni anupagato’’ti.

‘‘Atthi pana bhoto gotamassa kiñci diṭṭhigata’’nti? ‘‘Diṭṭhigatanti kho, vaccha, apanītametaṃ tathāgatassa. Diṭṭhañhetaṃ, vaccha, tathāgatena – ‘iti rūpaṃ, iti rūpassa samudayo, iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo; iti vedanā, iti vedanāya samudayo, iti vedanāya atthaṅgamo; iti saññā, iti saññāya samudayo, iti saññāya atthaṅgamo; iti saṅkhārā, iti saṅkhārānaṃ samudayo, iti saṅkhārānaṃ atthaṅgamo; iti viññāṇaṃ, iti viññāṇassa samudayo, iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo’ti. Tasmā tathāgato sabbamaññitānaṃ sabbamathitānaṃ sabbaahaṃkāramamaṃkāramānānusayānaṃ khayā virāgā nirodhā cāgā paṭinissaggā anupādā vimuttoti vadāmī’’ti.
mula_english:
189. “'The cosmos is eternal (sassato loko)'—this, Vaccha, is a theoretical position, a theoretical thicket, a theoretical desert, a theoretical trick, a theoretical writhing, a theoretical fetter; it is accompanied by pain, torment, distress, & fever; it does not lead to disenchantment, dispassion, cessation; to calm, direct knowledge, self-awakening, unbinding.

‘The cosmos is not eternal (asassato loko)’…pe…

‘The cosmos is finite (antavā loko)’…pe…

‘The cosmos is infinite (anantavā loko)’…pe…

‘The soul & the body are the same (taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ)’…pe…

‘The soul is one thing and the body another (aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ)’…pe…

‘After death a Tathāgata exists (hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā)’…pe…

…pe… ‘After death a Tathāgata does not exist (na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā)’…pe…

‘After death a Tathāgata both exists & does not exist (hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā)’…pe…

‘After death a Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist (neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā)’—this, Vaccha, is a theoretical position, a theoretical thicket, a theoretical desert, a theoretical trick, a theoretical writhing, a theoretical fetter; it is accompanied by pain, torment, distress, & fever; it does not lead to disenchantment, dispassion, cessation; to calm, direct knowledge, self-awakening, unbinding.

Seeing thus this drawback in these theoretical positions, I remain detached from all of them."

"But does Master Gotama have any theoretical position?"

"A theoretical position (diṭṭhigata), Vaccha, has been abandoned by the Tathāgata.

What a Tathāgata sees is this: 'Such is form (rūpaṃ), such its origination (samudayo), such its disappearance (atthaṅgamo); such is feeling (vedanā), such its origination, such its disappearance; such is perception (saññā), such its origination, such its disappearance; such are fabrications (saṅkhārā), such their origination, such their disappearance; such is consciousness (viññāṇaṃ), such its origination, such its disappearance.'

Because of this, I say, a Tathāgata—with the ending (khayā), fading away (virāgā), cessation (nirodhā), renunciation (cāgā), & relinquishment (paṭinissaggā) of all suppositions (sabbamaññitānaṃ), all excogitations (sabbamathitānaṃ), all I-making & mine-making & obsessions with conceit (sabbaahaṃkāramamaṃkāramānānusayānaṃ)—is, through lack of clinging/sustenance (anupādā), released (vimutto)"
commentary_pali:
189.Sadukkhanti kilesadukkhena ceva vipākadukkhena ca sadukkhaṃ. Savighātanti tesaṃyeva dvinnaṃ vasena saupaghātakaṃ. Saupāyāsanti tesaṃyeva vasena saupāyāsaṃ. Sapariḷāhanti tesaṃyeva vasena sapariḷāhaṃ.

Kiñci diṭṭhigatanti kāci ekā diṭṭhipi ruccitvā khamāpetvā gahitā atthīti pucchati. Apanītanti nīhaṭaṃ apaviddhaṃ. Diṭṭhanti paññāya diṭṭhaṃ. Tasmāti yasmā pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ udayavayaṃ addasa, tasmā. Sabbamaññitānanti sabbesaṃ tiṇṇampi taṇhādiṭṭhimānamaññitānaṃ. Mathitānanti tesaṃyeva vevacanaṃ. Idāni tāni vibhajitvā dassento sabbaahaṃkāra-mamaṃkāra-mānānusayānanti āha. Ettha hi ahaṃkāro diṭṭhi, mamaṃkāro taṇhā, mānānusayo māno. Anupādā vimuttoti catūhi upādānehi kañci dhammaṃ anupādiyitvā vimutto.

Kiñci diṭṭhigata Apanīta Diṭṭha Tasmā Sabbamaññitāna Mathitāna sabbaahaṃkāra-mamaṃkāra-mānānusayāna Anupādā vimutto
commentary_english:
189. *Sadukkha* means *sadukkha* due to the suffering of defilements (*kilesadukkha*) and the suffering of result (*vipākadukkha*).

*Savighāta* means having destruction (*saupaghātaka*) in terms of those same two.

*Saupāyāsa* means having distress (*saupāyāsa*) in terms of those same [two].

*Sapariḷāha* means having burning (*sapariḷāha*) in terms of those same [two].

*Kiñci diṭṭhigata* means he asks if there is any view (*diṭṭhi*) that was liked, accepted, and taken up.

*Apanīta* means removed, rejected.

*Diṭṭha* means seen with wisdom (*paññāya*).

*Tasmā* means because he saw the arising and passing away of the five aggregates (*pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ udayavayaṃ*), therefore.

*Sabbamaññitāna* means of all the conceits (*maññitāna*) of craving (*taṇhā*), views (*diṭṭhi*), and pride (*māna*), all three.

*Mathitāna* means a synonym of those same.

Now, showing them by dividing them, he says *sabbaahaṃkāra-mamaṃkāra-mānānusayāna*.

Here, self-conceit (*ahaṃkāro*) is view (*diṭṭhi*), possessiveness (*mamaṃkāro*) is craving (*taṇhā*), the underlying tendency of pride (*mānānusayo*) is pride (*māno*).

*Anupādā vimutto* means liberated without clinging (*anupādiyitvā vimutto*), not clinging to any thing (*dhammaṃ*) with the four kinds of clinging (*catūhi upādānehi*).

*Kiñci diṭṭhigata apanīta diṭṭha tasmā sabbamaññitāna mathitāna sabbaahaṃkāra-mamaṃkāra-mānānusayāna anupādā vimutto*

mula_pali:
190. ‘‘Evaṃ vimuttacitto pana, bho gotama, bhikkhu kuhiṃ upapajjatī’’ti? ‘‘Upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upeti’’. ‘‘Tena hi, bho gotama, na upapajjatī’’ti? ‘‘Na upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upeti’’. ‘‘Tena hi, bho gotama, upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatī’’ti? ‘‘Upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upeti’’. ‘‘Tena hi, bho gotama, neva upapajjati na na upapajjatī’’ti? ‘‘Neva upapajjati na na upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upeti’’.

‘‘‘Evaṃ vimuttacitto pana, bho gotama, bhikkhu kuhiṃ upapajjatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upetī’ti vadesi. ‘Tena hi, bho gotama, na upapajjatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘na upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upetī’ti vadesi. ‘Tena hi, bho gotama, upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upetī’ti vadesi. ‘Tena hi, bho gotama, neva upapajjati na na upapajjatī’ti iti puṭṭho samāno ‘neva upapajjati na na upapajjatīti kho, vaccha, na upetī’ti vadesi. Etthāhaṃ, bho gotama, aññāṇamāpādiṃ, ettha sammohamāpādiṃ. Yāpi me esā bhoto gotamassa purimena kathāsallāpena ahu pasādamattā sāpi me etarahi antarahitā’’ti. ‘‘Alañhi te, vaccha, aññāṇāya, alaṃ sammohāya. Gambhīro hāyaṃ, vaccha, dhammo duddaso duranubodho santo paṇīto atakkāvacaro nipuṇo paṇḍitavedanīyo. So tayā dujjāno aññadiṭṭhikena aññakhantikena aññarucikena aññatrayogena aññatrāyogena (dī. ni. 1.420) aññatrācariyakena’’ aññatthācariyakena (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.).

aññatrāyogena (dī. ni. 1.420) aññatthācariyakena (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)
mula_english:
190. “But, Master Gotama, the monk whose mind is thus released: Where does he reappear?” “He reappears…doesn’t apply, Vaccha.”

“In that case, Master Gotama, he does not reappear.” “He does not reappear…doesn’t apply, Vaccha.”

“…both does & does not reappear.” “…both does & does not reappear…doesn’t apply, Vaccha.”

“…neither does nor does not reappear.” “…neither does nor does not reappear…doesn’t apply, Vaccha.”

“But, Master Gotama, the monk whose mind is thus released: Where does he reappear?” Thus asked, he says, ‘He reappears…doesn’t apply, Vaccha.’

‘In that case, Master Gotama, he does not reappear.’ Thus asked, he says, ‘He does not reappear…doesn’t apply, Vaccha.’

‘‘…both does & does not reappear.’ Thus asked, he says, ‘…both does & does not reappear…doesn’t apply, Vaccha.’

‘…neither does nor does not reappear.’ Thus asked, he says, ‘…neither does nor does not reappear…doesn’t apply, Vaccha.’

At this point, Master Gotama, I am befuddled; at this point, confused.

And that little bit of clarity I had from my conversation with Master Gotama has now disappeared.”

“Of course you’re befuddled, Vaccha. Of course you’re confused.

Deep, Vaccha, is this *dharma*, hard to see, hard to realize, tranquil, refined, beyond the scope of conjecture, subtle, to-be-experienced by the wise.

For those with other views, other practices, other satisfactions, other aims, other teachers, it is difficult to know.”
commentary_pali: 190.Na upetīti na yujjati. Ettha ca ‘‘na upapajjatī’’ti idaṃ anujānitabbaṃ siyā. Yasmā pana evaṃ vutte so paribbājako ucchedaṃ gaṇheyya, upapajjatīti pana sassatameva, upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatīti ekaccasassataṃ, neva upapajjati na na upapajjatīti amarāvikkhepaṃ, tasmā bhagavā – ‘‘ayaṃ appatiṭṭho anālambo hotu, sukhapavesanaṭṭhānaṃ mā labhatū’’ti ananuññāya ṭhatvā anuññampi paṭikkhipi. Alanti samatthaṃ pariyattaṃ . Dhammoti paccayākāradhammo. Aññatrayogenāti aññattha payogena. Aññatrācariyakenāti paccayākāraṃ ajānantānaṃ aññesaṃ ācariyānaṃ santike vasantena.
commentary_english:
190. *na upetī* *ti* *na yujjati*.

Here, *"na upapajjati"* *iti* should be permitted.

Because when this is said, that wandering ascetic would grasp annihilation (*ucchedaṃ gaṇheyya*), and *"upapajjati"* *iti* indeed [would be] permanence (*sassatameva*); *"upapajjati ca na ca upapajjati"* *iti* [would be] partial permanence (*ekaccasassataṃ*), *"neva upapajjati na na upapajjati"* *iti* [would be] an evasive answer (*amarāvikkhepaṃ*). Therefore, the Blessed One – "May this be without a foundation (*appatiṭṭho*), without support (*anālambo*), may [they] not obtain a place for easy entrance (*sukhapavesanaṭṭhānaṃ mā labhatū*)" – having stood not permitting (*ananuññāya ṭhatvā*) rejected the permission (*anuññampi paṭikkhipi*).

*alaṃ* *ti* means capable (*samatthaṃ*), complete (*pariyattaṃ*).

*dhammo* *ti* means the *dhamma* consisting of conditions (*paccayākāradhammo*).

*aññatrayogenā* *ti* means by another application (*aññattha payogena*).

*aññatrācariyakenā* *ti* means dwelling near other teachers who do not know the nature of conditions (*paccayākāraṃ ajānantānaṃ aññesaṃ ācariyānaṃ santike vasantena*).

mula_pali:
191. ‘‘Tena hi, vaccha, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi; yathā te khameyya tathā naṃ byākareyyāsi. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, vaccha, sace te purato aggi jaleyya, jāneyyāsi tvaṃ – ‘ayaṃ me purato aggi jalatī’’’ti? ‘‘Sace me, bho gotama, purato aggi jaleyya, jāneyyāhaṃ – ‘ayaṃ me purato aggi jalatī’’’ti.

‘‘Sace pana taṃ, vaccha, evaṃ puccheyya – ‘yo te ayaṃ purato aggi jalati ayaṃ aggi kiṃ paṭicca jalatī’ti, evaṃ puṭṭho tvaṃ, vaccha, kinti byākareyyāsī’’ti? ‘‘Sace maṃ, bho gotama, evaṃ puccheyya – ‘yo te ayaṃ purato aggi jalati ayaṃ aggi kiṃ paṭicca jalatī’ti, evaṃ puṭṭho ahaṃ, bho gotama, evaṃ byākareyyaṃ – ‘yo me ayaṃ purato aggi jalati ayaṃ aggi tiṇakaṭṭhupādānaṃ paṭicca jalatī’’’ti.

‘‘Sace te, vaccha, purato so aggi nibbāyeyya, jāneyyāsi tvaṃ – ‘ayaṃ me purato aggi nibbuto’’’ti? ‘‘Sace me, bho gotama, purato so aggi nibbāyeyya, jāneyyāhaṃ – ‘ayaṃ me purato aggi nibbuto’’’ti.

‘‘Sace pana taṃ, vaccha, evaṃ puccheyya – ‘yo te ayaṃ purato aggi nibbuto so aggi ito katamaṃ disaṃ gato – puratthimaṃ vā dakkhiṇaṃ vā pacchimaṃ vā uttaraṃ vā’ti, evaṃ puṭṭho tvaṃ, vaccha, kinti byākareyyāsī’’ti? ‘‘Na upeti, bho gotama, yañhi so, bho gotama, aggi tiṇakaṭṭhupādānaṃ paṭicca ajali jalati (syā. kaṃ. ka.) tassa ca pariyādānā aññassa ca anupahārā anāhāro nibbuto tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchatī’’ti.

jalati (syā. kaṃ. ka.)
mula_english:
That being the case, Vaccha, I will cross-question you on this very point. Answer as you see fit.

What do you think, Vaccha? If a fire were burning in front of you, would you know that ‘This fire is burning in front of me’?”

“…I would reply, ‘This fire burning in front of me is burning dependent on grass and timber as its sustenance.’”

If the fire burning in front of you were to go out, would you know that, ‘This fire burning in front of me has gone out’?”

“If he were to ask, ‘The fire that was burning in front of you, when it has gone out, which direction has that fire gone? East, South, West, or North?’ what would you say, Vaccha?”
“It doesn’t go anywhere, Master Gotama. Since that fire burned dependent on grass and timber, when that is all used up, and there is no more fuel, then, because it is without sustenance, it is simply extinguished ( *nirvṛta*).”
commentary_pali: 191.Tena hi vacchāti yasmā tvaṃ sammohamāpādinti vadasi, tasmā taṃyevettha paṭipucchissāmi. Anāhāronibbutoti appaccayo nibbuto.
commentary_english:
Therefore, Vacchā, because you say you are causing bewilderment, therefore I will question you right here about that very thing.

*Anāhāro*, *nibbuto* means without conditions, extinguished.

mula_pali:
192. ‘‘Evameva kho, vaccha, yena rūpena tathāgataṃ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya taṃ rūpaṃ tathāgatassa pahīnaṃ ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṃkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhammaṃ. Rūpasaṅkhayavimutto rūpasaṅkhāvimutto (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) evaṃ vedanāsaṅkhayādīsupi kho, vaccha, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāḷho – seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo. Upapajjatīti na upeti, na upapajjatīti na upeti, upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatīti na upeti, neva upapajjati na na upapajjatīti na upeti.

‘‘Yāya vedanāya tathāgataṃ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya sā vedanā tathāgatassa pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Vedanāsaṅkhayavimutto kho, vaccha, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāḷho – seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo. Upapajjatīti na upeti, na upapajjatīti na upeti, upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatīti na upeti, neva upapajjati na na upapajjatīti na upeti.

‘‘Yāya saññāya tathāgataṃ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya sā saññā tathāgatassa pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Saññāsaṅkhayavimutto kho, vaccha, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāḷho – seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo. Upapajjatīti na upeti, na upapajjatīti na upeti, upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatīti na upeti, neva upapajjati na na upapajjatīti na upeti.

‘‘Yehi saṅkhārehi tathāgataṃ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya te saṅkhārā tathāgatassa pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Saṅkhārasaṅkhayavimutto kho, vaccha, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāḷho – seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo. Upapajjatīti na upeti , na upapajjatīti na upeti, upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatīti na upeti, neva upapajjati na na upapajjatīti na upeti.

‘‘Yena viññāṇena tathāgataṃ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya taṃ viññāṇaṃ tathāgatassa pahīnaṃ ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṃkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhammaṃ. Viññāṇasaṅkhayavimutto kho, vaccha, tathāgato gambhīro appameyyo duppariyogāḷho – seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo. Upapajjatīti na upeti, na upapajjatīti na upeti, upapajjati ca na ca upapajjatīti na upeti, neva upapajjati na na upapajjatīti na upeti’’.

Evaṃ vutte, vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘seyyathāpi, bho gotama, gāmassa vā nigamassa vā avidūre mahāsālarukkho. Tassa aniccatā sākhāpalāsā palujjeyyuṃ sākhāpalāsaṃ palujjeyya, tacapapaṭikā palujjeyyuṃ, pheggū palujjeyyuṃ pheggu palujjeyya (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.); so aparena samayena apagatasākhāpalāso apagatatacapapaṭiko apagataphegguko suddho assa, sāre patiṭṭhito; evameva bhoto gotamassa pāvacanaṃ apagatasākhāpalāsaṃ apagatatacapapaṭikaṃ apagatapheggukaṃ suddhaṃ, sāre patiṭṭhitaṃ. Abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata’’nti.

sākhāpalāsaṃ palujjeyya pheggu palujjeyya (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)

Aggivacchasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.
mula_english:
192. In the same way, Vaccha, any form by which one describing the *Tathāgata* would describe him: That form the *Tathāgata* has abandoned, its root destroyed, made like a palmyra stump, deprived of the conditions of development, not destined for future arising.

Freed from the classification of form, Vaccha, the *Tathāgata* is deep, boundless, hard to fathom, like the sea.

‘Reappears’ doesn’t apply. ‘Does not reappear’ doesn’t apply. ‘Both does & does not reappear’ doesn’t apply. ‘Neither reappears nor does not reappear’ doesn’t apply.

“Any feeling by which one describing the *Tathāgata* might describe him: That feeling the *Tathāgata* has abandoned, its root destroyed, made like a palmyra stump, deprived of the conditions of development, not destined for future arising.

Freed from the classification of feeling, Vaccha, the *Tathāgata* is deep, boundless, hard to fathom, like the sea.

‘Reappears’ doesn’t apply. ‘Does not reappear’ doesn’t apply. ‘Both does & does not reappear’ doesn’t apply. ‘Neither reappears nor does not reappear’ doesn’t apply.

“Any perception by which one describing the *Tathāgata* might describe him: That perception the *Tathāgata* has abandoned, its root destroyed, made like a palmyra stump, deprived of the conditions of development, not destined for future arising.

Freed from the classification of perception, Vaccha, the *Tathāgata* is deep, boundless, hard to fathom, like the sea.

‘Reappears’ doesn’t apply. ‘Does not reappear’ doesn’t apply. ‘Both does & does not reappear’ doesn’t apply. ‘Neither reappears nor does not reappear’ doesn’t apply.

“Those volitional formations by which one describing the *Tathāgata* might describe him: Those volitional formations the *Tathāgata* has abandoned, its root destroyed, made like a palmyra stump, deprived of the conditions of development, not destined for future arising.

Freed from the classification of volitional formations, Vaccha, the *Tathāgata* is deep, boundless, hard to fathom, like the sea.

‘Reappears’ doesn’t apply. ‘Does not reappear’ doesn’t apply. ‘Both does & does not reappear’ doesn’t apply. ‘Neither reappears nor does not reappear’ doesn’t apply.

“Any consciousness by which one describing the *Tathāgata* might describe him: That consciousness the *Tathāgata* has abandoned, its root destroyed, made like a palmyra stump, deprived of the conditions of development, not destined for future arising.

Freed from the classification of consciousness, Vaccha, the *Tathāgata* is deep, boundless, hard to fathom, like the sea.

‘Reappears’ doesn’t apply. ‘Does not reappear’ doesn’t apply. ‘Both does & does not reappear’ doesn’t apply. ‘Neither reappears nor does not reappear’ doesn’t apply.

When this was said, *Vacchagotta* the wanderer said this to the Blessed One: “Just as, Master *Gotama*, not far from a village or town there might be a great *sāla* tree.

From inconstancy, its branches and leaves would decay, its bark would wear away, its sapwood would wear away, so that on a later occasion—divested of branches, leaves, bark, & sapwood—it would stand as pure heartwood. In the same way, Master *Gotama’s* words are divested of branches, leaves, bark, & sapwood and stand as pure heartwood.

Magnificent, Master *Gotama*! … Please accept me as a lay follower who’s gone for refuge for life.”
pī (reduplication for pyāy).
[Footnote/Note:] [p.1.
0489]
Aggivacchasuttaṃ is completed for the second time.
commentary_pali:
192.Yena rūpenāti yena rūpena sattasaṅkhātaṃ tathāgataṃ rūpīti paññāpeyya. Gambhīroti guṇagambhīro. Appameyyoti pamāṇaṃ gaṇhituṃ na sakkuṇeyyo. Duppariyogāḷhoti duogāho dujjāno. Seyyathāpi mahāsamuddoti yathā mahāsamuddo gambhīro appameyyo dujjāno, evameva khīṇāsavopi. Taṃ ārabbha upapajjatītiādi sabbaṃ na yujjati. Kathaṃ? Yathā parinibbutaṃ aggiṃ ārabbha puratthimaṃ disaṃ gatotiādi sabbaṃ na yujjati, evaṃ.

Aniccatāti aniccatāya. Sāre patiṭṭhitanti lokuttaradhammasāre patiṭṭhitaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Aniccatā Sāre patiṭṭhita

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Aggivacchasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
192. “*Yena rūpeṇa*”: by whatever form one might designate the *Tathāgata* as having form.

“*Gambhīro*”: deep in qualities (*guṇagambhīro*).

“*Appameyyo*”: it is not possible to take a measure (*pamāṇaṃ gaṇhituṃ na sakkuṇeyyo*).

“*Duppariyogāḷho*”: difficult to fathom, difficult to know (*duogāho dujjāno*).

"*Seyyathāpi mahāsamuddo*": Just as the great ocean is deep (*gambhīro*), immeasurable (*appameyyo*), and difficult to know (*dujjāno*), even so is the one whose *āsavas* are destroyed (*khīṇāsavopi*).

It is not fitting to start with that, saying "it arises" etc. (*taṃ ārabbha upapajjatītiādi sabbaṃ na yujjati*).

How so? Just as it is not fitting to say, starting with a fire that has been extinguished (*parinibbutaṃ aggiṃ ārabha*), "it has gone to the eastern direction" etc. (*puratthimaṃ disaṃ gatotiādi sabbaṃ na yujjati*), so too.

“*Aniccatā*”: because of impermanence (*aniccatāya*).

“*Sāre patiṭṭhita*”: established in the essence of the supramundane Dharma (*lokuttaradhammasāre patiṭṭhitaṃ*).

The rest is clear throughout (*sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti*).

Impermanence. Established in essence. The *Papañcasūdanī*, commentary on the *Majjhimanikāya*.

The commentary on the *Aggivacchasutta* is finished.

mula_pali: 193. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘dīgharattāhaṃ bhotā gotamena sahakathī. Sādhu me bhavaṃ gotamo saṃkhittena kusalākusalaṃ desetū’’ti. ‘‘Saṃkhittenapi kho te ahaṃ, vaccha, kusalākusalaṃ deseyyaṃ, vitthārenapi kho te ahaṃ, vaccha, kusalākusalaṃ deseyyaṃ; api ca te ahaṃ, vaccha, saṃkhittena kusalākusalaṃ desessāmi. Taṃ suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bho’’ti kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
193. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One (bhagavā) was living at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary (veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe).

Then the wanderer Vacchagotta approached the Blessed One (bhagavā) and exchanged greetings with him. When this courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side.

Seated to one side, the wanderer Vacchagotta said to the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ): "I have had conversations with Master Gotama for a long time. It would be good if Master Gotama would teach me in brief the wholesome (kusala) and the unwholesome (akusala)."

"I can teach you the wholesome (kusala) and the unwholesome (akusala) in brief, Vaccha, and I can teach you the wholesome (kusala) and the unwholesome (akusala) at length. Still I will teach you the wholesome (kusala) and the unwholesome (akusala) in brief. Listen to that and attend closely, I will speak."

"As you say, lord," (evaṃ, bho) the wanderer Vacchagotta replied to the Blessed One (bhagavato).

The Blessed One (bhagavā) said this:
commentary_pali: 193.Evaṃme sutanti mahāvacchasuttaṃ. Tattha sahakathīti saddhiṃvādo, bahuṃ mayā tumhehi saddhiṃ kathitapubbanti kathaṃ sāreti mettiṃ ghaṭeti. Purimāni hi dve suttāni etasseva kathitāni, saṃyuttake abyākatasaṃyuttaṃ (saṃ. ni. 4.416 ādayo) nāma etasseva kathitaṃ – ‘‘kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, sassato loko idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti abyākatameta’’nti evaṃ ekuttaranikāyepi iminā saddhiṃ kathitaṃ atthiyeva. Tasmā evamāha. Sammāsambuddhopi tassa āgatāgatassa saṅgahaṃ katvā okāsamakāsiyeva. Kasmā? Ayañhi sassatadiṭṭhiko, sassatadiṭṭhikā ca sīghaṃ laddhiṃ na vissajjenti, vasātelamakkhitapilotikā viya cirena sujjhanti. Passati ca bhagavā – ‘‘ayaṃ paribbājako kāle gacchante gacchante laddhiṃ vissajjetvā mama santike pabbajitvā cha abhiññāyo sacchikatvā abhiññātasāvako bhavissatī’’ti. Tasmā tassa āgatāgatassa saṅgahaṃ katvā okāsamakāsiyeva. Idaṃ panassa pacchimagamanaṃ. So hi imasmiṃ sutte taraṇaṃ vā hotu ataraṇaṃ vā, yaṭṭhiṃ otaritvā udake patamāno viya samaṇassa gotamassa santikaṃ gantvā pabbajissāmīti sanniṭṭhānaṃ katvā āgato. Tasmā dhammadesanaṃ yācanto sādhu me bhavaṃ gotamotiādimāha. Tassa bhagavā mūlavasena saṃkhittadesanaṃ, kammapathavasena vitthāradesanaṃ desesi. Mūlavasena cettha atisaṃkhittā desanā, kammapathavasena saṃkhittā vitthārasadisā. Buddhānaṃ pana nippariyāyena vitthāradesanā nāma natthi. Catuvīsatisamantapaṭṭhānampi hi sattapakaraṇe abhidhammapiṭake ca sabbaṃ saṃkhittameva. Tasmā mūlavasenāpi kammapathavasenāpi saṃkhittameva desesīti veditabbo.
commentary_english:
193. It is like this.

"Thus I have heard" is the Mahāvacchasutta.

There, *sahakathī* means friendly discourse. How does he remember the affection, saying, "I have spoken much with you before"?

Indeed, the previous two sūtras were spoken to him. In the *Saṃyutta*, the *abyākatasaṃyutta* (Saṃ. Ni. 4.416 and so on) is said to him - "What now, venerable Gotama, is the world eternal, is this alone true, is the rest worthless?" Aabyākatameta’* thus, in the *Ekuttaranikāya* also it is said together with this that there is meaning.

Therefore, he spoke thus.

The Sammāsambuddha also, having taken up the coming and going, made an opportunity.

Why? Because he is a sassatadiṭṭhiko, and sassatadiṭṭhikas do not quickly abandon their views, they are cleansed slowly like a wick smeared with sesame oil.

The Blessed One sees: "This wanderer, as time goes on, having abandoned his views, having gone forth near me, having realized the six higher knowledges, will become a well-known disciple."

Therefore, having taken up his coming and going, he made an opportunity.

This, however, was his last journey.

He, indeed, in this sūtra, whether there be a crossing or no crossing, having descended from the staff, falling into the water, as it were, having gone to the presence of the Samaṇa Gotama, having made the determination, "I will go forth," has come.

Therefore, asking for a teaching of the Dharma, he said, "Good for me, venerable Gotama," and so on.

To him, the Blessed One taught a concise teaching based on the root, and a detailed teaching based on the path of action (karmapatha).

Here, the teaching based on the root is extremely concise, the teaching based on the path of action is concise and similar to detail.

For the Buddhas, there is no detailed teaching by an indirect method.

Indeed, in the twenty-four conditioned relations (*catuvīsatisamantapaṭṭhāna*) also, in the seven treatises (*sattapakaraṇa*) and in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, everything is concise.

Therefore, it should be understood that he taught concisely based on the root and also based on the path of action.

mula_pali:
194. ‘‘Lobho kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, alobho kusalaṃ; doso kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, adoso kusalaṃ; moho kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, amoho kusalaṃ. Iti kho, vaccha, ime tayo dhammā akusalā, tayo dhammā kusalā.
