‘‘Pāṇātipāto kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, pāṇātipātā veramaṇī kusalaṃ; adinnādānaṃ kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, adinnādānā veramaṇī kusalaṃ; kāmesumicchācāro kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī kusalaṃ; musāvādo kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, musāvādā veramaṇī kusalaṃ; pisuṇā vācā kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ , pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī kusalaṃ; pharusā vācā kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī kusalaṃ; samphappalāpo kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, samphappalāpā veramaṇī kusalaṃ; abhijjhā kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, anabhijjhā kusalaṃ; byāpādo kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ, abyāpādo kusalaṃ; micchādiṭṭhi kho, vaccha, akusalaṃ sammādiṭṭhi kusalaṃ. Iti kho, vaccha, ime dasa dhammā akusalā, dasa dhammā kusalā.

‘‘Yato kho, vaccha, bhikkhuno taṇhā pahīnā hoti ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā, so hoti bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto’’ti.
mula_english:
194. "Vaccha, greed (*lobha*) is unwholesome (*akuśala*), non-greed (*alobha*) is wholesome (*kuśala*); hate (*dosa*) is unwholesome, non-hate (*adosa*) is wholesome; delusion (*moha*) is unwholesome, non-delusion (*amoha*) is wholesome. In this way, Vaccha, these three things are unwholesome, and these three things are wholesome.

“Killing living beings (*pāṇātipāta*) is unwholesome, abstaining from killing living beings (*pāṇātipātā veramaṇī*) is wholesome; taking what is not given (*adinnādāna*) is unwholesome, abstaining from taking what is not given (*adinnādānā veramaṇī*) is wholesome; misconduct in sensual pleasures (*kāmesumicchācāra*) is unwholesome, abstaining from misconduct in sensual pleasures (*kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī*) is wholesome; false speech (*musāvāda*) is unwholesome, abstaining from false speech (*musāvādā veramaṇī*) is wholesome; malicious speech (*pisuṇā vācā*) is unwholesome, abstaining from malicious speech (*pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī*) is wholesome; harsh speech (*pharusā vācā*) is unwholesome, abstaining from harsh speech (*pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī*) is wholesome; idle chatter (*samphappalāpa*) is unwholesome, abstaining from idle chatter (*samphappalāpā veramaṇī*) is wholesome; covetousness (*abhijjhā*) is unwholesome, non-covetousness (*anabhijjhā*) is wholesome; ill will (*byāpāda*) is unwholesome, non-ill will (*abyāpāda*) is wholesome; wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhi*) is unwholesome, right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*) is wholesome. In this way, Vaccha, these ten things are unwholesome, and these ten things are wholesome.

“When, Vaccha, a *bhikkhu* has abandoned craving (*taṇhā*), cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, done away with it so that it is no longer subject to future arising, then that *bhikkhu* is an *arahaṃ*, one with taints destroyed (*khīṇāsava*), one who has lived the holy life (*vusitavā*), done what had to be done (*katakaraṇīyo*), laid down the burden (*ohitabhāro*), reached the true goal (*anuppattasadattho*), destroyed the fetters of being (*parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano*), and is completely liberated through final knowledge (*sammadāññā vimutto*).”
commentary_pali:
194. Tattha pāṇātipātā veramaṇī kusalantiādīsu paṭipāṭiyā sattadhammā kāmāvacarā, anabhijjhādayo tayo catubhūmikāpi vaṭṭanti.

Yatokho, vaccha, bhikkhunoti kiñcāpi aniyametvā vuttaṃ, yathā pana jīvakasutte ca caṅkīsutte ca, evaṃ imasmiṃ sutte ca attānameva sandhāyetaṃ bhagavatā vuttanti veditabbaṃ.

Yato kho, vaccha, bhikkhuno
commentary_english:
194. Furthermore, refraining from killing living beings is wholesome, etc. The seven *dharma*s pertaining to the desire realm (*kāmāvacara*), and the three (*trayo*) such as non-covetousness (*anabhijjhādayo*) belonging to the four planes of existence (*catubhūmikāpi*) are valid.

Since, O Vatsa (vaccha), it is said "of a *bhikkhu*," although it is said without restriction, just as in the Jīvaka Sutta and the Caṅkī Sutta, so in this Sutta too, it should be understood that the Blessed One (*bhagavatā*) spoke with reference to himself (*attānameva sandhāya*).

Since, O Vatsa (vaccha), [it is said] "of a *bhikkhu*."

mula_pali:
195. ‘‘Tiṭṭhatu bhavaṃ gotamo. Atthi pana te bhoto gotamassa ekabhikkhupi sāvako yo āsavānaṃ khayā sāvako āsavānaṃ khayā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) evamuparipi anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī’’ti? ‘‘Na kho, vaccha, ekaṃyeva sataṃ na dve satāni na tīṇi satāni na cattāri satāni na pañca satāni, atha kho bhiyyova ye bhikkhū mama sāvakā āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī’’ti.

‘‘Tiṭṭhatu bhavaṃ gotamo, tiṭṭhantu bhikkhū. Atthi pana bhoto gotamassa ekā bhikkhunīpi sāvikā yā āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī’’ti? ‘‘Na kho, vaccha, ekaṃyeva sataṃ na dve satāni na tīṇi satāni na cattāri satāni na pañca satāni, atha kho bhiyyova yā bhikkhuniyo mama sāvikā āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī’’ti.

‘‘Tiṭṭhatu bhavaṃ gotamo, tiṭṭhantu bhikkhū, tiṭṭhantu bhikkhuniyo. Atthi pana bhoto gotamassa ekupāsakopi sāvako gihī odātavasano brahmacārī yo pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā’’ti? ‘‘Na kho, vaccha, ekaṃyeva sataṃ na dve satāni na tīṇi satāni na cattāri satāni na pañca satāni, atha kho bhiyyova ye upāsakā mama sāvakā gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā’’ti.

‘‘Tiṭṭhatu bhavaṃ gotamo, tiṭṭhantu bhikkhū, tiṭṭhantu bhikkhuniyo, tiṭṭhantu upāsakā gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino. Atthi pana bhoto gotamassa ekupāsakopi sāvako gihī odātavasano kāmabhogī sāsanakaro ovādappaṭikaro yo tiṇṇavicikiccho vigatakathaṃkatho vesārajjappatto aparappaccayo satthusāsane viharatī’’ti? ‘‘Na kho, vaccha, ekaṃyeva sataṃ na dve satāni na tīṇi satāni na cattāri satāni na pañca satāni , atha kho bhiyyova ye upāsakā mama sāvakā gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino sāsanakarā ovādappaṭikarā tiṇṇavicikicchā vigatakathaṃkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane viharantī’’ti.

‘‘Tiṭṭhatu bhavaṃ gotamo, tiṭṭhantu bhikkhū, tiṭṭhantu bhikkhuniyo, tiṭṭhantu upāsakā gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino, tiṭṭhantu upāsakā gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino. Atthi pana bhoto gotamassa ekupāsikāpi sāvikā gihinī odātavasanā brahmacārinī yā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyinī anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā’’ti? ‘‘Na kho, vaccha, ekaṃyeva sataṃ na dve satāni na tīṇi satāni na cattāri satāni na pañca satāni, atha kho bhiyyova yā upāsikā mama sāvikā gihiniyo odātavasanā brahmacāriniyo pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyiniyo anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā’’ti.

‘‘Tiṭṭhatu bhavaṃ gotamo, tiṭṭhantu bhikkhū, tiṭṭhantu bhikkhuniyo, tiṭṭhantu upāsakā gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino, tiṭṭhantu upāsakā gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino, tiṭṭhantu upāsikā gihiniyo odātavasanā brahmacāriniyo. Atthi pana bhoto gotamassa ekupāsikāpi sāvikā gihinī odātavasanā kāmabhoginī sāsanakarā ovādappaṭikarā yā tiṇṇavicikicchā vigatakathaṃkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane viharatī’’ti? ‘‘Na kho, vaccha, ekaṃyeva sataṃ na dve satāni na tīṇi satāni na cattāri satāni na pañca satāni, atha kho bhiyyova yā upāsikā mama sāvikā gihiniyo odātavasanā kāmabhoginiyo sāsanakarā ovādappaṭikarā tiṇṇavicchikicchā vigatakathaṃkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane viharantī’’ti.
mula_english:
195. “Apart from Master Gotama.

Is there any one bhikkhu, Master Gotama’s disciple, who, through the destruction of the āsavas, has realized for himself with direct knowledge, here and now, the deliverance of mind and deliverance by wisdom that are taintless?”

“There are not only one hundred, Vaccha, or two or three or four or five hundred, but far more bhikkhus, my disciples, who by realising for themselves with direct knowledge here and now enter upon and abide in the deliverance of mind and deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the destruction of the taints.”

“Apart from Master Gotama, and the bhikkhus.

Is there any one bhikkhuni, Master Gotama’s disciple, who, through the destruction of the *āsavas*, has realized for herself with direct knowledge, here and now, the deliverance of mind and deliverance by wisdom that are taintless?”

“There are not only one hundred, Vaccha, or two or three or four or five hundred, but far more bhikkhunis, my disciples, who by realising for themselves with direct knowledge here and now enter upon and abide in the deliverance of mind and deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the destruction of the taints.”

“Apart from Master Gotama, the bhikkhus and the bhikkhunis.

Is there any one male lay follower, Master Gotama’s disciple, a householder clothed in white, leading a life of celibacy, who, through the destruction of the five lower fetters (*orambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni*), has arisen spontaneously (*opapātiko*), will attain final Emancipation there, and will not return from that world?”

“There are not only one hundred, Vaccha, or two or three or four or five hundred, but far more male lay followers, my disciples, householders clothed in white, leading lives of celibacy, who, through the destruction of the five lower fetters, have arisen spontaneously, will attain final Emancipation there, and will not return from that world.”

“Apart from Master Gotama, the bhikkhus, the bhikkhunis, and the male lay followers who are householders clothed in white, leading lives of celibacy.

Is there any one male lay follower, Master Gotama’s disciple, a householder clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, who carries out the instruction, responds to the advice, has gone beyond doubt, become free from perplexity, gained intrepidity, and become independent of others in the Teacher’s Dispensation?”

“There are not only one hundred, Vaccha, or two or three or four or five hundred, but far more male lay followers, my disciples, householders clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, who carry out my instruction, respond to my advice, have gone beyond doubt, become free from perplexity, gained intrepidity, and become independent of others in the Teacher’s Dispensation.”

“Apart from Master Gotama, the *bhikkhus*, the *bhikkhunis*, and the male lay followers who are householders clothed in white, leading lives of celibacy, and the male lay followers who are householders clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures.

Is there any one female lay follower, Master Gotama’s disciple, a householder clothed in white, leading a life of celibacy, who, through the destruction of the five lower fetters (*orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ*), has arisen spontaneously (*opapātikā*), will attain final *Nirvāṇa* there, and will not return from that world?”

“There are not only one hundred, Vaccha, or two or three or four or five hundred, but far more female lay followers, my disciples, householders clothed in white, leading lives of celibacy, who, through the destruction of the five lower fetters, have arisen spontaneously, will attain final Emancipation there, and will not return from that world.”

“Apart from Master Gotama, the *bhikkhus*, the *bhikkhunis*, the male lay followers who are householders clothed in white, leading lives of celibacy, the male lay followers who are householders clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, and the female lay followers who are householders clothed in white, leading lives of celibacy.

Is there any one female lay follower, Master Gotama’s disciple, a householder clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, who carries out my instruction, responds to my advice, has gone beyond doubt, become free from perplexity, gained intrepidity, and become independent of others in the Teacher’s Dispensation?”

“There are not only one hundred, Vaccha, or two or three or four or five hundred, but far more female lay followers, my disciples, householders clothed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, who carry out my instruction, respond to my advice, have gone beyond doubt, become free from perplexity, gained intrepidity, and become independent of others in the Teacher’s Dispensation.”
commentary_pali: 195.Atthipanāti kiṃ pucchāmīti pucchati? Ayaṃ kirassa laddhi – ‘‘tasmiṃ tasmiṃ sāsane satthāva arahā hoti, sāvako pana arahattaṃ pattuṃ samattho natthi. Samaṇo ca gotamo ‘yato kho, vaccha, bhikkhuno’ti ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ kathento viya katheti, atthi nu kho samaṇassa gotamassa sāvako arahattappatto’’ti. Etamatthaṃ pucchissāmīti pucchati. Tattha tiṭṭhatūti bhavaṃ tāva gotamo tiṭṭhatu, bhavañhi loke pākaṭo arahāti attho. Tasmiṃ byākate uttari bhikkhunīādīnaṃ vasena pañhaṃ pucchi, bhagavāpissa byākāsi.
commentary_english:
195.
Is there? Why do I ask "what?" He asks. This is indeed his view: "In that very teaching, only the teacher is an *arhat* (arhan), but a disciple is not capable of attaining *arhatship* (arahattva)."
And the ascetic Gotama speaks as if telling one *bhikṣu* (monk), "Because, Vaccha, of a *bhikṣu* (monk)," is there now a disciple of the ascetic Gotama who has attained *arhatship* (arahattva)?
He asks, "I will ask about this matter."
There, let him remain! The venerable Gotama should remain, for the venerable one is known in the world as an *arhat* (arhan)—this is the meaning.
When that was explained, he further asked a question by means of the nuns and so forth, and the Blessed One explained it to him.

mula_pali:
196. ‘‘Sace hi, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavaṃyeva gotamo ārādhako abhavissa, no ca kho bhikkhū ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu ; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ aparipūraṃ abhavissa tenaṅgena. Yasmā ca kho, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako bhikkhū ca ārādhakā; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ paripūraṃ tenaṅgena.

‘‘Sace hi, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako abhavissa, bhikkhū ca ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, no ca kho bhikkhuniyo ārādhikā abhavissaṃsu; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ aparipūraṃ abhavissa tenaṅgena. Yasmā ca kho, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako, bhikkhū ca ārādhakā, bhikkhuniyo ca ārādhikā; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ paripūraṃ tenaṅgena.

‘‘Sace hi, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako abhavissa, bhikkhū ca ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, bhikkhuniyo ca ārādhikā abhavissaṃsu, no ca kho upāsakā gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ aparipūraṃ abhavissa tenaṅgena. Yasmā ca kho, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako, bhikkhū ca ārādhakā, bhikkhuniyo ca ārādhikā, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino ārādhakā; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ paripūraṃ tenaṅgena.

‘‘Sace hi, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako abhavissa, bhikkhū ca ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, bhikkhuniyo ca ārādhikā abhavissaṃsu, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, no ca kho upāsakā gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ aparipūraṃ abhavissa tenaṅgena. Yasmā ca kho, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako, bhikkhū ca ārādhakā, bhikkhuniyo ca ārādhikā, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino ārādhakā, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino ārādhakā; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ paripūraṃ tenaṅgena.

‘‘Sace hi, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako abhavissa, bhikkhū ca ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, bhikkhuniyo ca ārādhikā abhavissaṃsu, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, no ca kho upāsikā gihiniyo odātavasanā brahmacāriniyo ārādhikā abhavissaṃsu; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ aparipūraṃ abhavissa tenaṅgena. Yasmā ca kho, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako, bhikkhū ca ārādhakā, bhikkhuniyo ca ārādhikā, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino ārādhakā, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino ārādhakā , upāsikā ca gihiniyo odātavasanā brahmacāriniyo ārādhikā; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ paripūraṃ tenaṅgena.

‘‘Sace hi, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako abhavissa, bhikkhū ca ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, bhikkhuniyo ca ārādhikā abhavissaṃsu, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino ārādhakā abhavissaṃsu, upāsikā ca gihiniyo odātavasanā brahmacāriniyo ārādhikā abhavissaṃsu, no ca kho upāsikā gihiniyo odātavasanā kāmabhoginiyo ārādhikā abhavissaṃsu; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ aparipūraṃ abhavissa tenaṅgena. Yasmā ca kho, bho gotama, imaṃ dhammaṃ bhavañceva gotamo ārādhako, bhikkhū ca ārādhakā, bhikkhuniyo ca ārādhikā, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino ārādhakā, upāsakā ca gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino ārādhakā, upāsikā ca gihiniyo odātavasanā brahmacāriniyo ārādhikā, upāsikā ca gihiniyo odātavasanā kāmabhoginiyo ārādhikā; evamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ paripūraṃ tenaṅgena.
mula_english:
196. “Master Gotama, if only Master Gotama were accomplished in this *dharma*, but no *bhikkhus* were accomplished, then this holy life (*brahmacarya*) would be deficient in that respect; but because Master Gotama and *bhikkhus* are accomplished in this *dharma*, this holy life (*brahmacarya*) is thus complete in that respect.

“Master Gotama, if only Master Gotama, *bhikkhus*, and *bhikkhunis* were accomplished in this *dharma*, but no *bhikkhunis* were accomplished, then this holy life (*brahmacarya*) would be deficient in that respect; but because Master Gotama, *bhikkhus*, and *bhikkhunis* are accomplished in this *dharma*, this holy life (*brahmacarya*) is thus complete in that respect.

“Master Gotama, if only Master Gotama, *bhikkhus* and *bhikkhunis*, and men lay followers clothed in white observing *brahmacarya* were accomplished in this *dharma*, but no men lay followers clothed in white observing *brahmacarya* were accomplished, then this holy life (*brahmacarya*) would be deficient in that respect; but because Master Gotama, *bhikkhus* and *bhikkhunis*, men lay followers clothed in white observing *brahmacarya* are accomplished in this *dharma*, this holy life (*brahmacarya*) is thus complete in that respect.

“Master Gotama, if only Master Gotama, *bhikkhus* and *bhikkhunis*, men lay followers clothed in white observing *brahmacarya*, and men lay followers clothed in white enjoying sensual pleasures were accomplished in this *dharma*, but no men lay followers clothed in white enjoying sensual pleasures were accomplished, then this holy life (*brahmacarya*) would be deficient in that respect; but because Master Gotama, *bhikkhus* and *bhikkhunis*, men lay followers clothed in white observing *brahmacarya*, and men lay followers clothed in white enjoying sensual pleasures are accomplished in this *dharma*, this holy life (*brahmacarya*) is thus complete in that respect.

“Master Gotama, if only Master Gotama, *bhikkhus* and *bhikkhunis*, men lay followers clothed in white observing *brahmacarya*, men lay followers clothed in white enjoying sensual pleasures, and women lay followers clothed in white observing *brahmacarya* were accomplished in this *dharma*, but no women lay followers clothed in white observing *brahmacarya* were accomplished, then this holy life (*brahmacarya*) would be deficient in that respect; but because Master Gotama, *bhikkhus* and *bhikkhunis*, men lay followers clothed in white observing *brahmacarya*, men lay followers clothed in white enjoying sensual pleasures, and women lay followers clothed in white observing *brahmacarya* are accomplished in this *dharma*, this holy life (*brahmacarya*) is thus complete in that respect.

“Master Gotama, if only Master Gotama, *bhikkhus* and *bhikkhunis*, men lay followers clothed in white observing *brahmacarya*, men lay followers clothed in white enjoying sensual pleasures, women lay followers clothed in white observing *brahmacarya*, and women lay followers clothed in white enjoying sensual pleasures were accomplished in this *dharma*, but no women lay followers clothed in white enjoying sensual pleasures were accomplished, then this holy life (*brahmacarya*) would be deficient in that respect; but because Master Gotama, *bhikkhus* and *bhikkhunis*, men lay followers clothed in white observing *brahmacarya*, men lay followers clothed in white enjoying sensual pleasures, women lay followers clothed in white observing *brahmacarya*, and women lay followers clothed in white enjoying sensual pleasures are accomplished in this *dharma*, this holy life (*brahmacarya*) is thus complete in that respect.
commentary_pali: 196.Ārādhakoti sampādako paripūrako.
commentary_english: 196. ārādhakoti *sampādako paripūrako*.

mula_pali:
197. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, gaṅgā nadī samuddaninnā samuddapoṇā samuddapabbhārā samuddaṃ āhacca tiṭṭhati, evamevāyaṃ bhoto gotamassa parisā sagahaṭṭhapabbajitā nibbānaninnā nibbānapoṇā nibbānapabbhārā nibbānaṃ āhacca tiṭṭhati. Abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… esāhaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Labheyyāhaṃ bhoto gotamassa santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada’’nti . ‘‘Yo kho, vaccha, aññatitthiyapubbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhati pabbajjaṃ, ākaṅkhati upasampadaṃ, so cattāro māse parivasati. Catunnaṃ māsānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājenti upasampādenti bhikkhubhāvāya; api ca mettha puggalavemattatā viditā’’ti. ‘‘Sace, bhante, aññatitthiyapubbā imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhantā pabbajjaṃ, ākaṅkhantā upasampadaṃ cattāro māse parivasanti, catunnaṃ māsānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājenti upasampādenti bhikkhubhāvāya; ahaṃ cattāri vassāni parivasissāmi. Catunnaṃ vassānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājentu upasampādentu bhikkhubhāvāyā’’ti. Alattha kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ alattha upasampadaṃ.

Acirūpasampanno kho panāyasmā vacchagotto addhamāsūpasampanno yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā vacchagotto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘yāvatakaṃ, bhante, sekhena ñāṇena sekhāya vijjāya pattabbaṃ, anuppattaṃ taṃ mayā; uttari ca me uttariṃ me (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) bhagavā dhammaṃ desetū’’ti. ‘‘Tena hi tvaṃ, vaccha, dve dhamme uttari bhāvehi – samathañca vipassanañca. Ime kho te, vaccha, dve dhammā uttari bhāvitā – samatho ca vipassanā ca – anekadhātupaṭivedhāya saṃvattissanti.

uttariṃ me (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)
mula_english:
197. Just as the river Gaṅgā (Ganges) inclines towards the sea (*samuddaninnā*), slopes towards the sea (*samuddapoṇā*), flows towards the sea (*samuddapabbhārā*), and merges with the sea (*samudraṃ āhacca tiṭṭhati*), so too, Gotama, Master Gotama's assembly with its householders (*sagahaṭṭha*) and homeless ones (*pabbajitā*) inclines towards *Nibbāna*, slopes towards *Nibbāna*, flows towards *Nibbāna*, and merges with *Nibbāna*.

Magnificent, Master Gotama!…

I go for refuge to the Blessed Lord Gotama, to the *Dhamma* (Doctrine) and to the *Bhikkhusaṅgha* (Community of Monks).

May I receive the going forth (*pabbajjaṃ*) in the presence of Master Gotama; may I receive the full ordination (*upasampadaṃ*).

Vaccha, one who formerly belonged to another sect (*aññatitthiyapubbo*) and desires the going forth (*pabbajjaṃ*) and the full admission (*upasampadaṃ*) in this *Dhamma* and *Vinaya* (Discipline) lives on probation for four months.

At the end of four months, if the *bhikkhus* (monks) are satisfied with him, they give him the going forth (*pabbājenti*) and the full admission (*upasampādenti*) to the *bhikkhus’ bhāva* (state of a monk); but I recognize individual differences in this matter.

Venerable sir (*bhante*), if those who formerly belonged to another sect (*aññatitthiyapubbā*) and desire the going forth (*pabbajjaṃ*), desiring the full admission (*upasampadaṃ*), in this *Dhamma* and *Vinaya* live on probation for four months, and at the end of the four months the *bhikkhus* being satisfied with them give them the going forth (*pabbājenti*) and the full admission (*upasampādenti*) to the *bhikkhus’ bhāva* (state of a monk); I will live on probation for four years.

At the end of the four years if the *bhikkhus* are satisfied with me, let them give me the going forth (*pabbājentu*) and the full admission (*upasampādentu*) to the *bhikkhus’ bhāva* (state of a monk).

Then the wanderer Vacchagotta received the going forth (*pabbajjaṃ*) in the presence of the Blessed One (*bhagavato santike*), and he received the full admission (*upasampadaṃ*).

Not long after his full admission (*acirūpasampanno*), a half-month after his full admission (*addhamāsūpasampanno*), the venerable Vacchagotta went to the Blessed One (*bhagavā*), and after paying homage (*abhivādetvā*) to him, he sat down at one side (*ekamantaṃ nisīdi*).

Seated to one side (*ekamantaṃ nisinno*), the venerable Vacchagotta said this to the Blessed One (*bhagavantaṃ etadavoca*) – “Venerable sir (*bhante*), I have attained whatever can be attained by the knowledge (*ñāṇena*) of a disciple in higher training (*sekhena*), by the true knowledge (*vijjāya*) of a disciple in higher training (*sekhāya*). Let the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) teach me the *Dhamma* (Doctrine) further.”

In that case, Vaccha, develop further two things (*dve dhamme*): *samatha* (serenity) and *vipassanā* (insight).

When these two things (*dve dhammā*) are developed further (*uttari bhāvitā*)—*samatha* (serenity) and *vipassanā* (insight)—they will lead to the penetration of many elements (*anekadhātupaṭivedhāya saṃvattissanti*).
commentary_pali:
197.Sekhāya vijjāya pattabbanti heṭṭhimaphalattayaṃ pattabbaṃ. Taṃ sabbaṃ mayā anuppattanti vadati. Vitaṇḍavādī panāha – ‘‘katame dhammā sekkhā? Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā heṭṭhimāni ca tīṇi sāmaññaphalānī’’ti (dha. sa. 1023) vacanato arahattamaggopi anena pattoyeva. Phalaṃ pana apattaṃ, tassa pattiyā uttari yogaṃ kathāpetīti. So evaṃ saññāpetabbo –

‘‘Yo ve kilesāni pahāya pañca,

Paripuṇṇasekho aparihānadhammo;

Cetovasippatto samāhitindriyo,

Sa ve ṭhitattoti naro pavuccatī’’ti. (a. ni. 4.5);

Anāgāmipuggalo hi ekantaparipuṇṇasekho. Taṃ sandhāya ‘‘sekhāya vijjāya pattabba’’nti āha. Maggassa pana ekacittakkhaṇikattā tattha ṭhitassa pucchā nāma natthi. Iminā suttena maggopi bahucittakkhaṇiko hotūti ce. Etaṃ na buddhavacanaṃ, vuttagāthāya ca attho virujjhati. Tasmā anāgāmiphale ṭhatvā arahattamaggassa vipassanaṃ kathāpetīti veditabbo. Yasmā panassa na kevalaṃ suddhaarahattasseva upanissayo, channampi abhiññānaṃ upanissayo atthi, tasmā bhagavā – ‘‘evamayaṃ samathe kammaṃ katvā pañca abhiññā nibbattessati , vipassanāya kammaṃ katvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇissati. Evaṃ chaḷabhiñño mahāsāvako bhavissatī’’ti vipassanāmattaṃ akathetvā samathavipassanā ācikkhi.
commentary_english:
197. "What is to be attained by the training knowledge (sekhāya vijjāya pattabba)?" means the three lower fruits are to be attained. He says, "All that I have attained."

But the quibbler says: "Which things are in training (sekkhā)? The four paths not included, and the three lower fruits of the life of a recluse (sāmaññaphalānī)" (Dhs. 1023). According to that statement, the path of Arahantship is also attained by him. But the fruit is not attained, for he is making an additional effort for the attainment of that.

He should be made to understand thus:

"That man is said to be established who, having abandoned the five defilements, is fully trained, not subject to decline, has attained mastery of mind, and whose senses are composed." (A.N. 4.5)

The non-returner (anāgāmi-puggalo) is indeed perfectly trained. Referring to that, he said, "What is to be attained by the training knowledge." But since the path lasts only for a single moment of consciousness, there is no question of one standing on it. If it is asked, "Should the path also be of many moments of consciousness, according to this sutta?" That is not the word of the Buddha, and the meaning contradicts the verse quoted. Therefore, it should be understood that, standing in the fruit of non-return, he causes insight (vipassanā) into the path of Arahantship.

Since for him there is a basis (upanissayo) not only for pure Arahantship, but also a basis for the six superknowledges (abhiññā), therefore the Blessed One, without mentioning only insight, taught both serenity and insight, saying: "Thus, having done work in serenity, he will produce the five superknowledges, having done work in insight, he will attain Arahantship. Thus, he will be a great disciple with the six superknowledges."

mula_pali:
198. ‘‘So tvaṃ, vaccha, yāvadeva yāvade (pī.) ākaṅkhissasi – ‘anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhaveyyaṃ – ekopi hutvā bahudhā assaṃ, bahudhāpi hutvā eko assaṃ; āvibhāvaṃ, tirobhāvaṃ; tirokuṭṭaṃ tiropākāraṃ tiropabbataṃ asajjamāno gaccheyyaṃ, seyyathāpi ākāse; pathaviyāpi ummujjanimujjaṃ kareyyaṃ, seyyathāpi udake; udakepi abhijjamāne gaccheyyaṃ, seyyathāpi pathaviyaṃ; ākāsepi pallaṅkena kameyyaṃ, seyyathāpi pakkhī sakuṇo; imepi candimasūriye evaṃmahiddhike evaṃmahānubhāve pāṇinā parimaseyyaṃ, parimajjeyyaṃ; yāvabrahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vatteyya’nti, tatra tatreva sakkhibhabbataṃ pāpuṇissasi, sati satiāyatane.

‘‘So tvaṃ, vaccha, yāvadeva ākaṅkhissasi – ‘dibbāya sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya ubho sadde suṇeyyaṃ – dibbe ca mānuse ca, ye dūre santike cā’ti, tatra tatreva sakkhibhabbataṃ pāpuṇissasi, sati satiāyatane.

‘‘So tvaṃ, vaccha, yāvadeva ākaṅkhissasi – ‘parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajāneyyaṃ – sarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ sarāgaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, vītarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ vītarāgaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; sadosaṃ vā cittaṃ sadosaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, vītadosaṃ vā cittaṃ vītadosaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; samohaṃ vā cittaṃ samohaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, vītamohaṃ vā cittaṃ vītamohaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; saṃkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ saṃkhittaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, vikkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ vikkhittaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; mahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ mahaggataṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, amahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ amahaggataṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; sauttaraṃ vā cittaṃ sauttaraṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, anuttaraṃ vā cittaṃ anuttaraṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; samāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ samāhitaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, asamāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ asamāhitaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ; vimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ vimuttaṃ cittanti pajāneyyaṃ, avimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ avimuttaṃ cittanti pajāneyya’nti, tatra tatreva sakkhibhabbataṃ pāpuṇissasi, sati satiāyatane.

‘‘So tvaṃ, vaccha, yāvadeva ākaṅkhissasi – ‘anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussareyyaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṃsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi jātisatasahassampi; anekepi saṃvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe – amutrāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṃ; tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapannoti; iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussareyya’nti, tatra tatreva sakkhibhabbataṃ pāpuṇissasi, sati satiāyatane.

‘‘So tvaṃ, vaccha, yāvadeva ākaṅkhissasi – ‘dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passeyyaṃ cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajāneyyaṃ – ime vata bhonto sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannā; ime vā pana bhonto sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā vacīsucaritena samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannāti; iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passeyyaṃ cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajāneyya’nti, tatra tatreva sakkhibhabbataṃ pāpuṇissasi, sati satiāyatane.

‘‘So tvaṃ, vaccha, yāvadeva ākaṅkhissasi – ‘āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyya’nti, tatra tatreva sakkhibhabbataṃ pāpuṇissasi, sati satiāyatane’’ti.
mula_english:
198. “To the extent that you may wish: ‘May I wield the various kinds of supernormal power ( *iddhi-vidha* ): having been one, may I become many; having been many, may I become one; may I appear (*āvibhāva*) and vanish (*tirobhāva* ); may I go unhindered through a wall (*tirokuṭṭa* ), through an enclosure (*tiropākāra* ), through a mountain (*tiropabbata* ), as though through space (*ākāśa* ); may I dive in and out of the earth (*pṛthivī*) as though it were water (*udaka* ); may I walk on water (*udaka*) without sinking as though it were earth (*pṛthivī* ); seated crosslegged (*pallaṅka* ), may I travel in space (*ākāśa*) like a bird (*pakṣī sakuṇo* ); with my hand may I touch and stroke the moon (*candi-masūriya*) and sun so powerful and mighty; may I wield power in the body (*kāya*) as far as the Brahma world (*brahmaloka*)’—you will attain the ability to witness any aspect therein, there being a suitable basis.

“To the extent that you may wish: ‘May I, with the divine ear element (*dibbāya sotadhātuyā*), which is purified (*visuddhāya*) and surpasses the human (*atikkantamānusikāya*), hear both kinds of sounds (*sadda*), the divine (*dibbe*) and the human (*mānuse*), those that are far (*dūre*) as well as near (*santike*)’—you will attain the ability to witness any aspect therein, there being a suitable basis.

“To the extent that you may wish: ‘May I understand the minds (*cetasā ceto paricca pajāneyyaṃ*) of other beings (*parasattānaṃ*) and persons (*parapuggalānaṃ*). May I understand a mind (*cittaṃ*) with lust (*sarāgaṃ*) as a mind (*cittaṃ*) with lust (*sarāgaṃ*), and a mind (*cittaṃ*) without lust (*vītarāgaṃ*) as a mind (*cittaṃ*) without lust (*vītarāgaṃ*); a mind (*cittaṃ*) with hatred (*sadosaṃ*) as a mind (*cittaṃ*) with hatred (*sadosaṃ*), and a mind (*cittaṃ*) without hatred (*vītadosaṃ*) as a mind (*cittaṃ*) without hatred (*vītadosaṃ*); a mind (*cittaṃ*) with delusion (*samohaṃ*) as a mind (*cittaṃ*) with delusion (*samohaṃ*), and a mind (*cittaṃ*) without delusion (*vītamohaṃ*) as a mind (*cittaṃ*) without delusion (*vītamohaṃ*); a contracted mind (*saṃkhittaṃ*) as contracted (*saṃkhittaṃ*), and a distracted mind (*vikkhittaṃ*) as distracted (*vikkhittaṃ*); an exalted mind (*mahaggataṃ*) as exalted (*mahaggataṃ*), and an unexalted mind (*amahaggataṃ*) as unexalted (*amahaggataṃ*); a surpassed mind (*sauttaraṃ*) as surpassed (*sauttaraṃ*), and an unsurpassed mind (*anuttaraṃ*) as unsurpassed (*anuttaraṃ*); a concentrated mind (*samāhitaṃ*) as concentrated (*samāhitaṃ*), and an unconcentrated mind (*asamāhitaṃ*) as unconcentrated (*asamāhitaṃ*); a liberated mind (*vimuttaṃ*) as liberated (*vimuttaṃ*), and an unliberated mind (*avimuttaṃ*) as unliberated (*avimuttaṃ*)’—you will attain the ability to witness any aspect therein, there being a suitable basis.

“To the extent that you may wish: ‘May I recollect my manifold past lives (*anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussareyyaṃ*), that is, one birth (*ekaṃ jātiṃ*), two births (*dve jātiyo*)...... Thus with their aspects and particulars may I recollect my manifold past lives (*anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussareyyaṃ*)’—you will attain the ability to witness any aspect therein, there being a suitable basis.

“To the extent that you may wish: ‘May I, with the divine eye (*dibbena cakkhunā*), which is purified (*visuddhena*) and surpasses the human (*atikkantamānusakena*), see beings (*satte*) passing away (*cavamāne*) and reappearing (*upapajjamāne*), inferior (*hīne*) and superior (*paṇīte*), fair (*suvaṇṇe*) and ugly (*dubbaṇṇe*), fortunate (*sugate*) and unfortunate (*duggate*), and may I understand how beings fare in accordance with their kamma (*yathākammūpage satte pajāneyyaṃ*) thus: “These worthy beings (*bhonto sattā*) who were ill-conducted in body (*kāyaduccaritena*), speech (*vacīduccaritena*), and mind (*manoduccaritena*), revilers of noble ones (*ariyānaṃ upavādakā*), wrong in their views (*micchādiṭṭhikā*), giving effect to wrong view in their actions (*micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā*), on the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*paraṃ maraṇā*), have reappeared in a state of deprivation (*apāyaṃ*), in a bad destination (*duggatiṃ*), in the lower realms (*vinipātaṃ*), in hell (*nirayaṃ upapannā*). But these worthy beings (*bhonto sattā*) who were well-conducted in body (*kāyasucaritena*), speech (*vacīsucaritena*), and mind (*manosucaritena*), non-revilers of noble ones (*ariyānaṃ anupavādakā*), right in their views (*sammādiṭṭhikā*), giving effect to right view in their actions (*sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā*), on the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*paraṃ maraṇā*), have reappeared in a good destination (*sugatiṃ*), in a heavenly world (*saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannāti*)”’—you will attain the ability to witness any aspect therein, there being a suitable basis.

“To the extent that you may wish: ‘May I, by realising for myself with direct knowledge (*sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā*), here and now enter upon and abide in the deliverance of mind (*cetovimuttiṃ*) and deliverance by wisdom (*paññāvimuttiṃ*) that are taintless (*anāsavaṃ*) with the destruction of the taints (*āsavānaṃ khayā*)’—you will attain the ability to witness any aspect therein, there being a suitable basis.”
commentary_pali: 198.Satisatiāyataneti sati satikāraṇe. Kiñcettha kāraṇaṃ? Abhiññā vā abhiññāpādakajjhānaṃ vā avasāne pana arahattaṃ vā kāraṇaṃ arahattassa vipassanā vāti veditabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
198. *smṛti* (sati), because of mindfulness (*smṛti*, *sati*), there is the cause of mindfulness (*satikāraṇe*).

Furthermore, what is the cause here? Is it direct knowledge (*abhijñā*) or the *dhyāna* that is the basis of direct knowledge (*abhijñāpādakajjhānaṃ*)? Or, in the end, is it *arhattva*? It should be understood that the cause of *arhattva* is *vipaśyanā*.

mula_pali: 199. Atha kho āyasmā vacchagotto bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho āyasmā vacchagotto eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro kho panāyasmā vacchagotto arahataṃ ahosi.
mula_english:
Then the venerable Vacchagotta, having delighted and rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words (bhāsitaṃ), rose from his seat, and after paying homage to the Blessed One, keeping him on his right (padakkhiṇaṃ katvā), he departed.

Then the venerable Vacchagotta, dwelling alone, withdrawn (vūpakaṭṭho), diligent (appamatto), ardent (ātāpī), and resolute (pahitatto), before long – by realising for himself with direct knowledge (sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā) here and now entered upon and abided in that supreme goal (anuttaraṃ) of the holy life (brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ) for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life (agārasmā) into homelessness (anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti).

He directly knew: “Birth is destroyed (khīṇā jāti), the holy life has been lived (vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ), what had to be done has been done (kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ), there is no more coming to any state of being (nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti abbhaññāsi).”

And the venerable Vacchagotta became one of the *arhats* (arahataṃ ahosi).

mula_pali:
200. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ dassanāya gacchanti. Addasā kho āyasmā vacchagotto te bhikkhū dūratova āgacchante. Disvāna yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca – ‘‘handa! Kahaṃ pana tumhe āyasmanto gacchathā’’ti? ‘‘Bhagavantaṃ kho mayaṃ, āvuso, dassanāya gacchāmā’’ti . ‘‘Tenahāyasmanto mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatha, evañca vadetha – ‘vacchagotto, bhante, bhikkhu bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati, evañca vadeti – pariciṇṇo me bhagavā, pariciṇṇo me sugato’’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato vacchagottassa paccassosuṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘āyasmā, bhante, vacchagotto bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati, evañca vadeti – ‘pariciṇṇo me bhagavā, pariciṇṇo me sugato’’’ti. ‘‘Pubbeva me, bhikkhave, vacchagotto bhikkhu cetasā ceto paricca vidito – ‘tevijjo vacchagotto bhikkhu mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo’ti. Devatāpi me etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ – ‘tevijjo, bhante, vacchagotto bhikkhu mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo’’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Mahāvacchasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.
mula_english:
Now at that time a number of monks were going to see the Blessed One.

The venerable Vacchagotta saw them coming in the distance.

He approached those monks and said to them, "Well, where are you venerable ones going?"

"We are going to see the Blessed One, friend."

"In that case, venerable ones, pay homage with your head at the Blessed One’s feet in my name, saying: ‘Venerable sir, the monk Vacchagotta pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet.’ And say: ‘The Blessed One has been worshipped by me, the Well-Gone One has been worshipped by me.’"

"Yes, friend," those monks replied to the venerable Vacchagotta.

Then those monks went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, sat down at one side.

Sitting to one side, those monks said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, the venerable Vacchagotta pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet, and he says: ‘The Blessed One has been worshipped by me, the Well-Gone One has been worshipped by me.’"

"Monks, even before this, Vacchagotta the monk was known to me, having encompassed his mind with my own mind: ‘The monk Vacchagotta has the threefold knowledge, is powerful and mighty.’

Deities also told me this: ‘Venerable sir, the monk Vacchagotta has the threefold knowledge, is powerful and mighty.’"

This is what the Buddha said.

Elated, those monks delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The Great Vacchagotta Discourse is finished, the third.
commentary_pali:
200.Pariciṇṇo me bhagavāti satta hi sekhā bhagavantaṃ paricaranti nāma, khīṇāsavena bhagavā pariciṇṇo hoti. Iti saṅkhepena arahattaṃ byākaronto thero evamāha. Te pana bhikkhū tamatthaṃ na jāniṃsu, ajānantāva tassa vacanaṃ sampaṭicchitvā. Bhagavato ārocesuṃ. Devatāti tesaṃ guṇānaṃ lābhī devatā. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Mahāvacchasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
200. "The Blessed One attends to me," because seven trainees attend to the Blessed One, and the Blessed One is attended to by one whose outflows are ended.

Thus, in brief, the elder spoke, explaining Arhatship in this way.

Those monks did not understand that meaning; not understanding, they accepted his word.

They told the Blessed One.

*Devatā* means that the *devatā* is the gainer of those qualities (*guṇas*).

The rest is clear throughout.

The *Papañcasūdanī* commentary on the *Majjhimanikāya*

The *Mahāvacchasutta* commentary is concluded.

mula_pali: 201. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate sūkarakhatāyaṃ. Atha kho dīghanakho paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho dīghanakho paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘ahañhi, bho gotama, evaṃvādī evaṃdiṭṭhi – ‘sabbaṃ me nakkhamatī’’’ti. ‘‘Yāpi kho te esā, aggivessana, diṭṭhi – ‘sabbaṃ me nakkhamatī’ti, esāpi te diṭṭhi nakkhamatī’’ti? ‘‘Esā ce esāpi (ka.) me, bho gotama, diṭṭhi khameyya, taṃpassa tādisameva, taṃpassa tādisamevā’’ti. ‘‘Ato kho te, aggivessana, bahū hi bahutarā lokasmiṃ ye evamāhaṃsu – ‘taṃpassa tādisameva, taṃpassa tādisamevā’ti. Te tañceva diṭṭhiṃ nappajahanti aññañca diṭṭhiṃ upādiyanti. Ato kho te, aggivessana, tanū hi tanutarā lokasmiṃ ye evamāhaṃsu – ‘taṃpassa tādisameva, taṃpassa tādisamevā’ti. Te tañceva diṭṭhiṃ pajahanti aññañca diṭṭhiṃ na upādiyanti. Santaggivessana, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘sabbaṃ me khamatī’ti; santaggivessana, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘sabbaṃ me nakkhamatī’ti; santaggivessana , eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘ekaccaṃ me khamati, ekaccaṃ me nakkhamatī’ti. Tatraggivessana, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘sabbaṃ me khamatī’ti tesamayaṃ diṭṭhi sārāgāya santike, saññogāya santike, abhinandanāya santike ajjhosānāya santike upādānāya santike; tatraggivessana ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘sabbaṃ me nakkhamatī’ti tesamayaṃ diṭṭhi asārāgāya santike, asaññogāya santike, anabhinandanāya santike, anajjhosānāya santike, anupādānāya santike’’ti.
mula_english:
201. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Rājagaha in the Boar’s Cave on the mountain Vulture Peak.

Then the wanderer Dīghanakha went to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.

After an exchange of friendly greetings & courtesies, he stood to one side.

Standing to one side, the wanderer Dīghanakha said to the Blessed One: “Master Gotama, my doctrine and view is this: ‘Nothing is acceptable to me.’”

“This view of yours, Aggivessana, ‘Nothing is acceptable to me’ - is not at least that view acceptable to you?” “If that view were acceptable to me, Master Gotama, then look at that, it is just the same, look at that, it is just the same."

“Well, Aggivessana, there are plenty in the world who say: ‘It too would be the same, it too would be the same,’

yet they do not abandon that view and they take up still some other view.

Those are few in the world who say: ‘It too would be the same, it too would be the same,’

and who abandon that view and do not take up some other view.

Aggivessana, there are some *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s whose doctrine and view is this: ‘Everything is acceptable to me.’ Aggivessana, there are some *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s whose doctrine and view is this: ‘Nothing is acceptable to me.’ Aggivessana, there are some *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s whose doctrine and view is this: ‘Something is acceptable to me, something is not acceptable to me.’

Among these, the view of those *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s who hold the doctrine and view ‘Everything is acceptable to me’ is close to lust (*sārāga*), close to bondage (*saṃyoga*), close to delighting (*abhinandana*), close to holding (*ajjhosāna*), close to clinging (*upādāna*). The view of those *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s who hold the doctrine and view ‘Nothing is acceptable to me’ is close to non-lust (*asārāga*), close to non-bondage (*asaṃyoga*), close to non-delighting (*anabhinandana*), close to non-holding (*anajjhosāna*), close to non-clinging (*anupādāna*).”
commentary_pali:
201.Evaṃme sutanti dīghanakhasuttaṃ. Tattha sūkarakhatāyanti sūkarakhatāti evaṃnāmake leṇe. Kassapabuddhakāle kira taṃ leṇaṃ ekasmiṃ buddhantare pathaviyā vaḍḍhamānāya antobhūmigataṃ jātaṃ. Athekadivasaṃ eko sūkaro tassa chadanapariyantasamīpe paṃsuṃ khaṇi. Deve vuṭṭe paṃsudhoto chadanapariyanto pākaṭo ahosi. Eko vanacarako disvā – ‘‘pubbe sīlavantehi paribhuttaleṇena bhavitabbaṃ, paṭijaggissāmi na’’nti samantato paṃsuṃ apanetvā leṇaṃ sodhetvā kuṭṭaparikkhepaṃ katvā dvāravātapānaṃ yojetvā supariniṭṭhita-sudhākammacittakammarajatapaṭṭasadisāya vālukāya santhatapariveṇaṃ leṇaṃ katvā mañcapīṭhaṃ paññāpetvā bhagavato vasanatthāya adāsi. Leṇaṃ gambhīraṃ ahosi otaritvā abhiruhitabbaṃ. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ.

Dīghanakhoti tassa paribbājakassa nāmaṃ. Upasaṅkamīti kasmā upasaṅkami? So kira there aḍḍhamāsapabbajite cintesi – ‘‘mayhaṃ mātulo aññaṃ pāsaṇḍaṃ gantvā na ciraṃ tiṭṭhati, idāni panassa samaṇassa gotamassa santikaṃ gatassa aḍḍhamāso jāto. Pavattimpissa na suṇāmi, ojavantaṃ nu kho sāsanaṃ, jānissāmi na’’nti gantukāmo jāto. Tasmā upasaṅkami. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitoti tasmiṃ kira samaye thero bhagavantaṃ bījayamāno ṭhito hoti, paribbājako mātule hirottappena ṭhitakova pañhaṃ pucchi. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘ekamantaṃ ṭhito’’ti.

Dīghanakho Upasaṅkamī Ekamantaṃ ṭhito

Sabbaṃ me nakkhamatīti sabbā me upapattiyo nakkhamanti, paṭisandhiyo nakkhamantīti adhippāyena vadati. Ettāvatānena ‘‘ucchedavādohamasmī’’ti dīpitaṃ hoti. Bhagavā panassa adhippāyaṃ muñcitvā akkhare tāva dosaṃ dassento yāpi kho tetiādimāha. Tattha esāpi te diṭṭhi nakkhamatīti esāpi te paṭhamaṃ ruccitvā khamāpetvā gahitadiṭṭhi nakkhamatīti. Esā ce me, bho gotama, diṭṭhi khameyyāti mayhañhi sabbaṃ nakkhamatīti diṭṭhi, tassa mayhaṃ yā esā sabbaṃ me nakkhamatīti diṭṭhi, esā me khameyya. Yaṃ taṃ ‘‘sabbaṃ me nakkhamatī’’ti vuttaṃ, tampissa tādisameva. Yathā sabbagahaṇena gahitāpi ayaṃ diṭṭhi khamati, evamevaṃ tampi khameyya . Evaṃ attano vāde āropitaṃ dosaṃ ñatvā taṃ pariharāmīti saññāya vadati, atthato panassa ‘‘esā diṭṭhi na me khamatī’’ti āpajjati. Yassa panesā na khamati na ruccati, tassāyaṃ tāya diṭṭhiyā sabbaṃ me na khamatīti diṭṭhi rucitaṃ. Tena hi diṭṭhiakkhamena arucitena bhavitabbanti sabbaṃ khamatīti ruccatīti āpajjati. Na panesa taṃ sampaṭicchati, kevalaṃ tassāpi ucchedadiṭṭhiyā ucchedameva gaṇhāti. Tenāha bhagavā ato kho te, aggivessana,…pe… aññañca diṭṭhiṃ upādiyantīti. Tattha atoti pajahanakesu nissakkaṃ, ye pajahanti, tehi ye nappajahantīti vucciyanti, teva bahutarāti attho. Bahū hi bahutarāti ettha hikāro nipātamattaṃ, bahū bahutarāti attho. Parato tanū hi tanutarāti padepi eseva nayo. Ye evamāhaṃsūti ye evaṃ vadanti. Tañceva diṭṭhiṃ nappajahanti, aññañca diṭṭhiṃ upādiyantīti mūladassanaṃ nappajahanti, aparadassanaṃ upādiyanti.

Sabbaṃ me nakkhamatī yāpi kho te esāpi te diṭṭhi nakkhamatī Esā ce me, bho gotama, diṭṭhi khameyyā ato kho te, aggivessana,…pe… aññañca diṭṭhiṃ upādiyantī ato Bahū hi bahutarā tanū hi tanutarā Ye evamāhaṃsū Tañceva diṭṭhiṃ nappajahanti, aññañca diṭṭhiṃ upādiyantī

Ettha ca sassataṃ gahetvā tampi appahāya ucchedaṃ vā ekaccasassataṃ vā gahetuṃ na sakkā, ucchedampi gahetvā taṃ appahāya sassataṃ vā ekaccasassataṃ vā na sakkā gahetuṃ, ekaccasassatampi gahetvā taṃ appahāya sassataṃ vā ucchedaṃ vā na sakkā gahetuṃ. Mūlasassataṃ pana appahāya aññaṃ sassatameva sakkā gahetuṃ. Kathaṃ? Ekasmiñhi samaye ‘‘rūpaṃ sassata’’nti gahetvā aparasmiṃ samaye ‘‘na suddharūpameva sassataṃ, vedanāpi sassatā, viññāṇampi sassata’’nti gaṇhāti. Ucchedepi ekaccasassatepi eseva nayo. Yathā ca khandhesu, evaṃ āyatanesupi yojetabbaṃ. Idaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘tañceva diṭṭhiṃ nappajahanti, aññañca diṭṭhiṃ upādiyantī’’ti.

Dutiyavāre atoti appajahanakesu nissakkaṃ, ye nappajahanti, tehi, ye pajahantīti vucciyanti, teva tanutarā appatarāti attho. Tañceva diṭṭhiṃ pajahanti, aññañca diṭṭhiṃ na upādiyantīti tañca mūladassanaṃ pajahanti, aññañca dassanaṃ na gaṇhanti. Kathaṃ? Ekasmiñhi samaye ‘‘rūpaṃ sassata’’nti gahetvā aparasmiṃ samaye tattha ādīnavaṃ disvā ‘‘oḷārikametaṃ mayhaṃ dassana’’nti pajahati ‘‘na kevalañca rūpaṃ sassatanti dassanameva oḷārikaṃ, vedanāpi sassatā…pe… viññāṇampi sassatanti dassanaṃ oḷārikamevā’’ti vissajjeti . Ucchedepi ekaccasassatepi eseva nayo. Yathā ca khandhesu, evaṃ āyatanesupi yojetabbaṃ. Evaṃ tañca mūladassanaṃ pajahanti, aññañca dassanaṃ na gaṇhanti.

ato Tañceva diṭṭhiṃ pajahanti, aññañca diṭṭhiṃ na upādiyantī

Santaggivessanāti kasmā ārabhi? Ayaṃ ucchedaladdhiko attano laddhiṃ nigūhati, tassā pana laddhiyā vaṇṇe vuccamāne attano laddhiṃ pātukarissatīti tisso laddhiyo ekato dassetvā vibhajituṃ imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi.

Santaggivessanā

Sārāgāya santiketiādīsu rāgavasena vaṭṭe rajjanassa āsannā taṇhādiṭṭhisaṃyojanena vaṭṭasaṃyojanassa santike. Abhinandanāyāti taṇhādiṭṭhivaseneva gilitvā pariyādiyanassa gahaṇassa ca āsannāti attho. Asārāgāya santiketiādīsu vaṭṭe arajjanassa āsannātiādinā nayena attho veditabbo.

Sārāgāya santike Abhinandanāyā Asārāgāya santike

Ettha ca sassatadassanaṃ appasāvajjaṃ dandhavirāgaṃ, ucchedadassanaṃ mahāsāvajjaṃ khippavirāgaṃ. Kathaṃ? Sassatavādī hi idhalokaṃ paralokañca atthīti jānāti, sukatadukkaṭānaṃ phalaṃ atthīti jānāti, kusalaṃ karoti, akusalaṃ karonto bhāyati, vaṭṭaṃ assādeti, abhinandati. Buddhānaṃ vā buddhasāvakānaṃ vā sammukhībhūto sīghaṃ laddhiṃ jahituṃ na sakkoti. Tasmā taṃ sassatadassanaṃ appasāvajjaṃ dandhavirāganti vuccati. Ucchedavādī pana idhalokaparalokaṃ atthīti jānāti, sukatadukkaṭānaṃ phalaṃ atthīti jānāti, kusalaṃ na karoti, akusalaṃ karonto na bhāyati, vaṭṭaṃ na assādeti, nābhinandati, buddhānaṃ vā buddhasāvakānaṃ vā sammukhībhāve sīghaṃ dassanaṃ pajahati. Pāramiyo pūretuṃ sakkonto buddho hutvā, asakkonto abhinīhāraṃ katvā sāvako hutvā parinibbāyati. Tasmā ucchedadassanaṃ mahāsāvajjaṃ khippavirāganti vuccati.
commentary_english:
201. Thus I have heard: the Dīghanakha Sūtra.

There, *sūkarakhatāya* means in a cave named Sūkarakhatā.

It is said that in the time of the Buddha Kassapa, that cave became located inside the earth as the earth grew during one Buddha-interval.

Then, one day, a certain pig dug the earth near the edge of its roof.

When it rained, the edge of the roof, cleansed by the rain, became visible.

A certain forester saw it and thought, “It must have been a cave frequented by virtuous people in the past. I will take care of it.” Having removed the earth from all around, cleaned the cave, made a wall enclosure, connected the door and window, made the cave a seat-enclosure with sand like a very well-finished stucco work, a painting, a silver plate, prepared a bed and seat, and gave it to the Blessed One for residence.

The cave was deep; one had to descend and ascend.

This was said with reference to that.

*Dīghanakha* means the name of that wanderer.

Why did [he] approach? A month after he had renounced [the world], he thought: “My maternal uncle, having gone to another sect, does not stay long. Now, a half-month has passed since he went to the presence of the ascetic Gotama.

I do not hear of his conduct. Is the teaching substantial? I will know," he became desirous of going.

Therefore, he approached.

*Ekamantaṃ ṭhito* means that at that time, the elder, fanning the Blessed One, was standing, [and] the wanderer, being respectfully and humbly [approached] the maternal uncle, asked a question.

Therefore, it was said, “Standing to one side.”

*Sabbaṃ me nakkhamatī* means all my upapattis do not please me, all my rebirths do not please me, [thus] he speaks with that intention.

By this much, it is made known “I am an annihilationist."

The Blessed One, having released his intention, while showing the fault in the letters themselves, said, “Whatever, Aggivessana,…”

There, *esāpi te diṭṭhi nakkhamatī* means this view also does not please you; this view which was first liked by you, having been caused to be forgiven, was taken; that view does not please you.

*Esā ce me, bho Gotama, diṭṭhi khameyya* means all does not please me; that view, whatever view of mine [says] all does not please me, may that please me.

That which was said, “All does not please me,” that too is just like that.

Just as this view, though taken with all grasping, is pleasing, even so may that please.

Thus, knowing the fault attributed to his own statement, he speaks with the perception, “I will avoid that.” In reality, however, he incurs, “This view does not please me.”

For whomever this is not pleasing, nor delights [him], for him, by that view, the view that all is not pleasing to me is pleasing.

Therefore, it should be that by the unpleasant, disagreeable view, all is pleasing; thus, he incurs delight.

But he does not accept that, but only grasps only annihilation by that annihilationist view.

Therefore, the Blessed One said: “Therefore, Aggivessana,…pe… they undertake another view.”

There, *ato* means without firmness in those to be abandoned. Those who abandon, and by those who are said not to abandon, they are more numerous, is the meaning.

*Bahū hi bahutarā*ti here the *hi* sound is merely a particle; many are more numerous, is the meaning.

After that, *tanū hi tanutarā*ti this is also the same method in that phrase.

*Ye evamāhaṃsū*ti means those who say thus.

*Tañceva diṭṭhiṃ nappajahanti, aññañca diṭṭhiṃ upādiyantī*ti they do not abandon the root view, they undertake another view.
Everything is not pleasing to me. Indeed, that view is not pleasing to you either. If that view were pleasing to me, O Gotama...

Therefore, O Aggivessana,… and who take up some other view. Therefore, many indeed are far more numerous.

Thin indeed, thinner still are those who have said thus, and who do not abandon that very view, and who take up some other view.

Herein, having taken permanence and without abandoning that, it is not possible to take annihilation or partial permanence; and having taken annihilation, without abandoning that, it is not possible to take permanence or partial permanence; and having taken partial permanence, without abandoning that, it is not possible to take permanence or annihilation.

But without abandoning fundamental permanence, it is only possible to take another permanence.

How? At one time, having taken, “Form is permanent,” at another time he takes, “Not only is form permanent, feeling too is permanent, consciousness too is permanent.”

In the case of annihilation and partial permanence too, the same method applies.

Just as with the aggregates, so too it should be connected with the sense-bases.

This was said with reference to, "and who do not abandon that very view, and who take up some other view."

In the second utterance, therefore, "because" means certainty with regard to those who do not abandon. Those who do not abandon, by them, those who are said to abandon, their meaning is that they are thinner, fewer.

"And who abandon that very view, and who do not take up some other view" means they abandon that fundamental view, and do not take up some other view.

How? At one time, having taken, "Form is permanent," at another time, having seen the fault therein, he abandons, "This view of mine is coarse." "Not only is form permanent, but the view itself is coarse, feeling too is permanent… consciousness too is permanent, so the view is coarse," he discards.

In the case of annihilation and partial permanence too, the same method applies.

Just as with the aggregates, so too it should be connected with the sense-bases.

Thus, they abandon that fundamental view, and do not take up some other view.

Therefore.

"Contentious Aggivessana"

Why was it begun? This annihilationist conceals his own view, but when the good qualities of that view are being spoken of, he will reveal his own view. Therefore, having shown the three views together, he began this teaching in order to distinguish them.

"Contentious Aggivessana"

"Near to passion," and so forth, means near to the attachment of passion, near to the attachment of the cycle, through the fetter of craving and views.

"For rejoicing" means near to the seizing and devouring and consuming, precisely through the power of craving and views, is the meaning.

"Near to non-passion," and so forth, the meaning should be understood by the method beginning with near to the non-attachment of the cycle.

Near to passion, for rejoicing, near to non-passion.

Herein, the view of permanence is of little fault, of slow fading away, the view of annihilation is of great fault, of rapid fading away.

How? The proponent of permanence knows, "There is this world and the next world," he knows, "There is fruit of good and bad actions," he does good, fearing when doing bad, he savors the cycle, he rejoices.

Being face to face with the Buddhas or the Buddha's disciples, he is not able to quickly abandon his view.

Therefore, that view of permanence is said to be of little fault, of slow fading away.

But the proponent of annihilation knows, "There is this world and the next world," he knows, "There is fruit of good and bad actions," he does not do good, not fearing when doing bad, he does not savor the cycle, he does not rejoice, in the presence of the Buddhas or the Buddha's disciples, he quickly abandons his view.

Being able to fulfill the perfections, he becomes a Buddha, not being able, having made an aspiration, he becomes a disciple and attains final nirvāṇa.

Therefore, the view of annihilation is said to be of great fault, of rapid fading away.

mula_pali: 202. Evaṃ vutte, dīghanakho paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘ukkaṃseti ukkaṃsati (sī. pī. ka.) me bhavaṃ gotamo diṭṭhigataṃ, samukkaṃseti sampahaṃsati (ka.) me bhavaṃ gotamo diṭṭhigata’’nti. ‘‘Tatraggivessana, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘ekaccaṃ me khamati, ekaccaṃ me nakkhamatī’ti. Yā hi tesaṃ khamati sāyaṃ diṭṭhi sārāgāya santike, saññogāya santike, abhinandanāya santike, ajjhosānāya santike, upādānāya santike; yā hi tesaṃ nakkhamati sāyaṃ diṭṭhi asārāgāya santike, asaññogāya santike, anabhinandanāya santike, anajjhosānāya santike, anupādānāya santike. Tatraggivessana, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘sabbaṃ me khamatī’ti tattha viññū puriso iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘yā kho me ayaṃ diṭṭhi – sabbaṃ me khamatīti, imañce ahaṃ diṭṭhiṃ thāmasā parāmāsā abhinivissa vohareyyaṃ – idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti; dvīhi me assa viggaho – yo cāyaṃ samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃvādī evaṃdiṭṭhi – sabbaṃ me nakkhamatīti, yo cāyaṃ samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃvādī evaṃdiṭṭhi – ekaccaṃ me khamati, ekaccaṃ me nakkhamatīti – imehi assa dvīhi viggaho. Iti viggahe sati vivādo, vivāde sati vighāto, vighāte sati vihesā’. Iti so viggahañca vivādañca vighātañca vihesañca attani sampassamāno tañceva diṭṭhiṃ pajahati aññañca diṭṭhiṃ na upādiyati. Evametāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ pahānaṃ hoti, evametāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ paṭinissaggo hoti.
mula_english: 202. When this was said, the wanderer Dīghanakha addressed the Blessed One, saying: “Reverend Gotama, you commend my point of view (*dṛṣṭigata*), Reverend Gotama, you highly commend my point of view.” “Aggivessana, as to those *śramaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas* who hold this doctrine and this view: ‘Something is acceptable to me, something is not acceptable to me,’ - the view of theirs as to what is acceptable is close to lust (*sārāga*), close to bondage (*saṃyoga*), close to delighting (*abhinandana*), close to holding (*ajjhosāna*), close to clinging (*upādāna*), while the view of theirs as to what is not acceptable is close to non-lust (*asārāga*), close to non-bondage (*asaṃyoga*), close to non-delighting (*anabhinandana*), close to non-holding (*anajjhosāna*), close to non-clinging (*anupādāna*). “Now, Aggivessana, a wise man among those *śramaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas* who hold the doctrine and view ‘Everything is acceptable to me’ considers thus: ‘If I obstinately adhere to my view “Everything is acceptable to me” and declare: “Only this is true, anything else is wrong,” then I may clash with the two others: with a *śramaṇa* or *brāhmaṇa* who holds the doctrine and view “Nothing is acceptable to me” and with a *śramaṇa* or *brāhmaṇa* who holds the doctrine and view “Something is acceptable to me, something is not acceptable to me.” When there is a clash (*vigraha*), there are disputes (*vivāda*); when there are disputes, there are quarrels (*vighāta*); when there are quarrels, there is vexation (*vihesā*)’. Foreseeing for himself clashes, disputes, quarrels, and vexation, he abandons that view (*dṛṣṭi*) and does not take up some other view. This is how there comes to be the abandoning (*pahāna*) of these views; this is how there comes to be the relinquishing (*pratinissagga*) of these views.
commentary_pali:
202. So pana paribbājako etamatthaṃ asallakkhetvā – ‘‘mayhaṃ dassanaṃ saṃvaṇṇeti pasaṃsati, addhā me sundaraṃ dassana’’nti sallakkhetvā ukkaṃseti me bhavantiādimāha.

Idāni yasmā ayaṃ paribbājako kañjiyeneva tittakālābu, ucchedadassaneneva pūrito, so yathā kañjiyaṃ appahāya na sakkā lābumhi telaphāṇitādīni pakkhipituṃ, pakkhittānipi na gaṇhāti, evamevaṃ taṃ laddhiṃ appahāya abhabbo maggaphalānaṃ lābhāya, tasmā laddhiṃ jahāpanatthaṃ tatraggivessanātiādi āraddhaṃ. Viggahoti kalaho. Evametāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ pahānaṃ hotīti evaṃ viggahādiādīnavaṃ disvā tāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ pahānaṃ hoti. So hi paribbājako ‘‘kiṃ me iminā viggahādinā’’ti taṃ ucchedadassanaṃ pajahati.

tatraggivessanā Viggaho Evametāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ pahānaṃ hotī
commentary_english:
202. Then, that wandering ascetic, not considering this matter, thinking, "My appearance is praised and extolled; truly my appearance is beautiful," inflates himself, saying, "May there be existence for me!" and so on.

Now, because this wandering ascetic is filled with mere sour gruel, like a bitter bottle gourd, filled with the view of annihilation, therefore, just as it is not possible to put oil, molasses, and so on into a bottle gourd without removing the sour gruel, and even if they are put in, it does not hold them, just so, without abandoning that view, he is incapable of gaining the fruits of the path. Therefore, to cause the abandonment of that view, the *tatrāggivessanā* and so on were begun.

*Viggaho* means strife or quarrel (kalaho).

*Evametāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ pahānaṃ hotī* means, having seen the wretchedness of strife and so on in this way, the abandonment of those views occurs.

That wandering ascetic abandons that view of annihilation, [thinking,] "What is the use to me of this strife and so on?"

*tatrāggivessanā*, *viggaho*, *evametāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ pahānaṃ hotī*

mula_pali: 203. ‘‘Tatraggivessana, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘sabbaṃ me nakkhamatī’ti tattha viññū puriso iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘yā kho me ayaṃ diṭṭhi – sabbaṃ me nakkhamatī’ti, imañce ahaṃ diṭṭhiṃ thāmasā parāmāsā abhinivissa vohareyyaṃ – idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti; dvīhi me assa viggaho – yo cāyaṃ samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃvādī evaṃdiṭṭhi – sabbaṃ me khamatīti, yo cāyaṃ samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃvādī evaṃdiṭṭhi – ekaccaṃ me khamati ekaccaṃ me nakkhamatīti – imehi assa dvīhi viggaho. Iti viggahe sati vivādo, vivāde sati vighāto, vighāte sati vihesā’. Iti so viggahañca vivādañca vighātañca vihesañca attani sampassamāno tañceva diṭṭhiṃ pajahati aññañca diṭṭhiṃ na upādiyati. Evametāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ pahānaṃ hoti, evametāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ paṭinissaggo hoti.
mula_english:
“Now, Aggivessana, a wise man among those *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s who hold the doctrine and view ‘Nothing is acceptable to me’ considers thus: ‘If I obstinately adhere to my view “Nothing is acceptable to me” and declare: “Only this is true, anything else is wrong,” then I may clash with the two others: with a *śramaṇa* or *brāhmaṇa* who holds the doctrine and view “Everything is acceptable to me” and with a *śramaṇa* or *brāhmaṇa* who holds the doctrine and view “Something is acceptable to me, something is not acceptable to me.”’

"When there is a clash (*viggaha*), there are disputes (*vivāda*); when there are disputes, there are quarrels (*vighāta*); when there are quarrels, there is vexation (*vihesā*)’."

Foreseeing for himself clashes (*viggaha*), disputes (*vivāda*), quarrels (*vighāta*), and vexation (*vihesā*), he abandons that view (*dṛṣṭi*) and does not take up some other view.

This is how there comes to be the abandoning (*pahāna*) of these views; this is how there comes to be the relinquishing (*pratinissagga*) of these views.

mula_pali: 204. ‘‘Tatraggivessana, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘ekaccaṃ me khamati, ekaccaṃ me nakkhamatī’ti tattha viññū puriso iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘yā kho me ayaṃ diṭṭhi – ekaccaṃ me khamati, ekaccaṃ me nakkhamatīti, imañce ahaṃ diṭṭhiṃ thāmasā parāmāsā abhinivissa vohareyyaṃ – idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti; dvīhi me assa viggaho – yo cāyaṃ samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃvādī evaṃdiṭṭhi – sabbaṃ me khamatīti, yo cāyaṃ samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃvādī evaṃdiṭṭhi – sabbaṃ me nakkhamatīti – imehi assa dvīhi viggaho. Iti viggahe sati vivādo, vivāde sati vighāto, vighāte sati vihesā’. Iti so viggahañca vivādañca vighātañca vihesañca attani sampassamāno tañceva diṭṭhiṃ pajahati aññañca diṭṭhiṃ na upādiyati. Evametāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ pahānaṃ hoti, evametāsaṃ diṭṭhīnaṃ paṭinissaggo hoti.
mula_english:
204. “Now, Aggivessana, a wise man among those recluses and *brāhmaṇas* who hold the doctrine and view ‘Something is acceptable to me, something is not acceptable to me’ considers thus: ‘If I obstinately adhere to my view “Something is acceptable to me, something is not acceptable to me” and declare: “Only this is true, anything else is wrong,” then I may clash with the two others: with a recluse or *brāhmaṇa* who holds the doctrine and view “Everything is acceptable to me” and with a recluse or *brāhmaṇa* who holds the doctrine and view “Nothing is acceptable to me.”’

and when there is a *viggaha*, there are disputes (*vivāda*); when there are disputes, there are quarrels (*vighāta*); when there are quarrels, there is vexation (*vihesā*)’."

Foreseeing for himself clashes, disputes, quarrels, and vexation, he abandons that view and does not take up some other view.

This is how there comes to be the abandoning of these views; this is how there comes to be the relinquishing of these views.

mula_pali:
205. ‘‘Ayaṃ kho panaggivessana, kāyo rūpī cātumahābhūtiko cātummahābhūtiko (sī. syā.) mātāpettikasambhavo odanakummāsupacayo aniccucchādanaparimaddanabhedanaviddhaṃsanadhammo, aniccato dukkhato rogato gaṇḍato sallato aghato ābādhato parato palokato suññato anattato samanupassitabbo . Tassimaṃ kāyaṃ aniccato dukkhato rogato gaṇḍato sallato aghato ābādhato parato palokato suññato anattato samanupassato yo kāyasmiṃ kāyachando kāyasneho kāyanvayatā sā pahīyati.

‘‘Tisso kho imā, aggivessana, vedanā – sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā. Yasmiṃ, aggivessana, samaye sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti , neva tasmiṃ samaye dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti, na adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti; sukhaṃyeva tasmiṃ samaye vedanaṃ vedeti. Yasmiṃ, aggivessana, samaye dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti, neva tasmiṃ samaye sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti, na adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti; dukkhaṃyeva tasmiṃ samaye vedanaṃ vedeti. Yasmiṃ, aggivessana, samaye adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti, neva tasmiṃ samaye sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti, na dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti; adukkhamasukhaṃyeva tasmiṃ samaye vedanaṃ vedeti. Sukhāpi kho, aggivessana, vedanā aniccā saṅkhatā paṭiccasamuppannā khayadhammā vayadhammā virāgadhammā nirodhadhammā; dukkhāpi kho, aggivessana, vedanā aniccā saṅkhatā paṭiccasamuppannā khayadhammā vayadhammā virāgadhammā nirodhadhammā; adukkhamasukhāpi kho, aggivessana, vedanā aniccā saṅkhatā paṭiccasamuppannā khayadhammā vayadhammā virāgadhammā nirodhadhammā. Evaṃ passaṃ, aggivessana, sutavā ariyasāvako sukhāyapi vedanāya nibbindati, dukkhāyapi vedanāya nibbindati, adukkhamasukhāyapi vedanāya nibbindati ; nibbindaṃ virajjati, virāgā vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ, vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti. Evaṃ vimuttacitto kho, aggivessana, bhikkhu na kenaci saṃvadati, na kenaci vivadati, yañca loke vuttaṃ tena voharati, aparāmasa’’nti.
mula_english:
205. Now, Aggivessana, this body (*kāya*), made of material form (*rūpī*), consisting of the four great elements (*cātumahābhūtika*), procreated by a mother and father (*mātāpettikasambhava*), and built up out of boiled rice and porridge (*odanakummāsupacaya*), is subject to impermanence, to being worn and rubbed away, to dissolution and disintegration (*aniccucchādanaparimaddanabhedanaviddhaṃsanadhamma*). It should be regarded as impermanent, as suffering (*dukkha*), as a disease (*roga*), as a tumor (*gaṇḍa*), as a dart (*salla*), as a calamity (*agha*), as an affliction (*ābādha*), as alien, as disintegrating, as void (*śūnyatā*), as not self (*anatta*).

When one regards this body (*kāya*) as impermanent, as suffering (*dukkha*), as a disease (*roga*), as a tumor (*gaṇḍa*), as a dart (*salla*), as a calamity (*agha*), as an affliction (*ābādha*), as alien, as disintegrating, as void (*śūnyatā*), as not self (*anatta*), one abandons desire for the body (*kāyachanda*), affection for the body (*kāyasneha*), subservience to the body (*kāyanvayatā*).

There are, Aggivessana, three kinds of feeling (*vedanā*): pleasant feeling (*sukhā vedanā*), painful feeling (*dukkha vedanā*), and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (*adukkhamasukhā vedanā*).

On the occasion when one feels pleasant feeling (*sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti*), Aggivessana, one does not feel painful feeling (*dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti*) or neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (*adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti*); on that occasion one feels only pleasant feeling (*sukhaṃyeva tasmiṃ samaye vedanaṃ vedeti*).

On the occasion when one feels painful feeling (*dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti*), Aggivessana, one does not feel pleasant feeling (*sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti*) or neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (*adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti*); on that occasion one feels only painful feeling (*dukkhaṃyeva tasmiṃ samaye vedanaṃ vedeti*).

On the occasion when one feels neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (*adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti*), Aggivessana, one does not feel pleasant feeling (*sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti*) or painful feeling (*dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vedeti*); on that occasion one feels only neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (*adukkhamasukhaṃyeva tasmiṃ samaye vedanaṃ vedeti*).

Pleasant feeling (*sukhā vedanā*), Aggivessana, is impermanent (*aniccā*), conditioned (*saṅkhatā*), dependently arisen (*paṭiccasamuppannā*), subject to destruction (*khayadhammā*), vanishing (*vayadhammā*), fading away (*virāgadhammā*), and ceasing (*nirodhadhammā*). Painful feeling (*dukhā vedanā*) too, Aggivessana, is impermanent (*aniccā*), conditioned (*saṅkhatā*), dependently arisen (*paṭiccasamuppannā*), subject to destruction (*khayadhammā*), vanishing (*vayadhammā*), fading away (*virāgadhammā*), and ceasing (*nirodhadhammā*). Neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (*adukkhamasukhā vedanā*) too, Aggivessana, is impermanent (*aniccā*), conditioned (*saṅkhatā*), dependently arisen (*paṭiccasamuppannā*), subject to destruction (*khayadhammā*), vanishing (*vayadhammā*), fading away (*virāgadhammā*), and ceasing (*nirodhadhammā*).

Seeing thus, Aggivessana, a well-taught noble disciple (*ariyasāvako*) becomes disenchanted (*nibbindati*) with pleasant feeling (*sukhāya vedanāya*), disenchanted (*nibbindati*) with painful feeling (*dukhāyapi vedanāya*), disenchanted (*nibbindati*) with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (*adukkhamasukhāyapi vedanāya*); being disenchanted (*nibbindaṃ*), he becomes dispassionate (*virajjati*); through dispassion (*virāgā*) his mind is liberated (*vimuccati*).

When it is liberated (*vimuttasmiṃ*), there comes the knowledge (*ñāṇaṃ hoti*): ‘It is liberated (*vimuttamiti*)’. He understands (*pajānāti*): ‘Destroyed is birth (*khīṇā jāti*), the spiritual life has been lived (*vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ*), what had to be done has been done (*kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ*), there is no more coming back to any state of being (*nāparaṃ itthattāyā*)’.

A *bhikkhu* whose mind is liberated (*vimuttacitto*) thus, Aggivessana, sides with none and disputes with none; he employs the speech currently used in the world without adhering to it."
commentary_pali:
205. Athassa bhagavā vamitakañjiye lābumhi sappiphāṇitādīni pakkhipanto viya hadaye amatosadhaṃ pūressāmīti vipassanaṃ ācikkhanto ayaṃ kho pana, aggivessana, kāyotiādimāha. Tassattho vammikasutte vutto. Aniccatotiādīnipi heṭṭhā vitthāritāneva. Yo kāyasmiṃ kāyachandoti yā kāyasmiṃ taṇhā. Snehoti taṇhāsnehova. Kāyanvayatāti kāyānugamanabhāvo, kāyaṃ anugacchanakakilesoti attho.

Evaṃ rūpakammaṭṭhānaṃ dassetvā idāni arūpakammaṭṭhānaṃ dassento tisso khotiādimāha. Puna tāsaṃyeva vedanānaṃ asammissabhāvaṃ dassento yasmiṃ, aggivessana, samayetiādimāha. Tatrāyaṃ saṅkhepattho – yasmiṃ samaye sukhādīsu ekaṃ vedanaṃ vedayati, tasmiṃ samaye aññā vedanā attano vāraṃ vā okāsaṃ vā olokayamānā nisinnā nāma natthi, atha kho anuppannāva honti bhinnaudakapupphuḷā viya ca antarahitā vā. Sukhāpi khotiādi tāsaṃ vedanānaṃ cuṇṇavicuṇṇabhāvadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ.

tisso kho yasmiṃ, aggivessana, samaye Sukhāpi kho

Na kenaci saṃvadatīti tassataṃ gahetvā ‘‘sassatavādī aha’’nti ucchedavādināpi saddhiṃ na saṃvadati, tameva gahetvā ‘‘sassatavādī aha’’nti ekaccasassatavādinā saddhiṃ na vivadati. Evaṃ tayopi vādā parivattetvā yojetabbā. Yañca loke vuttanti yaṃ loke kathitaṃ voharitaṃ, tena voharati aparāmasanto kiñci dhammaṃ parāmāsaggāhena aggaṇhanto. Vuttampi cetaṃ –

Na kenaci saṃvadatī Yañca loke vutta

‘‘Yo hoti bhikkhu arahaṃ katāvī,

Khīṇāsavo antimadehadhārī;

Ahaṃ vadāmītipi so vadeyya,

Mamaṃ vadantītipi so vadeyya;

Loke samaññaṃ kusalo viditvā,

Vohāramattena so vohareyyā’’ti. (saṃ. ni. 1.25);

Aparampi vuttaṃ – ‘‘imā kho citta lokasamaññā lokaniruttiyo lokavohārā lokapaññattiyo, yāhi tathāgato voharati aparāmasa’’nti (dī. ni. 1.440).
commentary_english:
205. Then, the Blessed One, while explaining the *vipassanā*, as if pouring ghee, sugar candy, and so on into a *lābu* gourd in Vamitakañji, said, "This body, Aggivessana," and so on.

That meaning is stated in the Vammika Sūtra.

"Because of impermanence" and so on, these have already been extensively explained below.

"*Yo kāyasmiṃ kāyachando*," means craving (*tṛṣṇā*) in relation to the body.

"*Sneho*" means craving-affection (*tṛṣṇāsneha*).

"*Kāyanvayatā*" means the state of following the body; it means defilements that follow the body.

Thus, after showing the *rūpakammaṭṭhāna*, now, while showing the *arūpakammaṭṭhāna*, he said, "*Tisso kho*," and so on.

Again, while showing the state of non-mixing of those feelings, he said, "*Yasmiṃ, aggivessana, samaye*," and so on.

Here, this is the meaning in brief: When one experiences one feeling among pleasant feelings, and so on, at that time, another feeling, waiting for its turn or opportunity, is not present, but rather, they are unarisen, like bubbles on disturbed water, and are vanished.

"*Sukhāpi kho*," and so on, was said in order to show the state of those feelings being crushed and pulverized.

"*Tisso kho* *yasmiṃ, aggivessana, samaye*"

"*Sukhāpi kho* *Na kenaci saṃvadatī*," means having taken that truth, he does not agree with the annihilationist, saying, "I am an eternalist." Having taken that same [truth], he does not dispute with a certain eternalist, saying, "I am an eternalist."

Thus, those three assertions are to be transformed and connected.

"*Yañca loke vutta*," means that which is spoken and expressed in the world; by that, he expresses without clinging, not grasping any *dharma* with the grasping of clinging.

And this was said:

"*Na kenaci saṃvadatī* *yañca loke vutta*"

"The monk who is an *arahaṃ*, a doer,
With extinguished *āsava*s, bearing his last body;
'I speak'—thus might he speak,
'I speak of 'mine'—thus might he speak;
Knowing the convention in the world,
He would express himself with mere usage."

(Saṃ. Ni. 1.25);

And furthermore, it was said: "These, O Citta, are worldly designations, worldly expressions, worldly usages, worldly concepts, with which the Tathāgata expresses himself without clinging" (Dī. Ni. 1.440).

mula_pali:
206. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā sāriputto bhagavato piṭṭhito ṭhito hoti bhagavantaṃ bījayamāno vījayamāno (sī. pī.). Atha kho āyasmato sāriputtassa etadahosi – ‘‘tesaṃ tesaṃ kira no bhagavā dhammānaṃ abhiññā pahānamāha, tesaṃ tesaṃ kira no sugato dhammānaṃ abhiññā paṭinissaggamāhā’’ti. Iti hidaṃ āyasmato sāriputtassa paṭisañcikkhato anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimucci. Dīghanakhassa pana paribbājakassa virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – ‘‘yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma’’nti. Atha kho dīghanakho paribbājako diṭṭhadhammo pattadhammo viditadhammo pariyogāḷhadhammo tiṇṇavicikiccho vigatakathaṃkatho vesārajjappatto aparappaccayo satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama!
