Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti – evameva kho bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata’’nti.

Dīghanakhasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.
mula_english:
At that time, the venerable Śāriputra was standing behind the Blessed One, fanning the Blessed One.

Then the venerable Śāriputra thought to himself: "Indeed, the Blessed One speaks of abandoning such and such things through direct knowledge. Indeed, the Well-Gone One speaks of relinquishing such and such things through direct knowledge."

As the venerable Śāriputra contemplated this, his mind was liberated from the taints, without clinging.

Then, to the wanderer Dīghanakha, the stainless, immaculate Dhamma-eye arose: "Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of ceasing."

Then the wanderer Dīghanakha, who had seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, understood the Dhamma, fathomed the Dhamma, transcended doubt, dispelled uncertainty, attained confidence, become independent of others in the Teacher's Dispensation, said this to the Blessed One: "Excellent, venerable Gotama, excellent, venerable Gotama! Just as, venerable Gotama, one might turn upright what has been overthrown, reveal what has been hidden, show the way to one who is lost, or hold up an oil lamp in the dark so that those with eyes might see forms—just so has the Dhamma been made clear by venerable Gotama in many ways.

"I go to the venerable Gotama for refuge, and to the Dharma and to the monastic Saṅgha (bhikkhusaṅgha). May the venerable Gotama remember me as a lay follower (upāsaka) who has gone for refuge from this day forward, for as long as life lasts."

The Dīghanakha Sūtra, the fourth [sūtra], is completed.
commentary_pali:
206.Abhiññāpahānamāhāti sassatādīsu tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ sassataṃ abhiññāya jānitvā sassatassa pahānamāha, ucchedaṃ, ekaccasassataṃ abhiññāya ekaccasassatassa pahānaṃ vadati. Rūpaṃ abhiññāya rūpassa pahānaṃ vadatītiādinā nayenettha attho veditabbo.

Paṭisañcikkhatoti paccavekkhantassa. Anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimuccīti anuppādanirodhena niruddhehi āsavehi aggahetvāva cittaṃ vimucci. Ettāvatā cesa parassa vaḍḍhitaṃ bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā khudaṃ vinodento viya parassa āraddhāya dhammadesanāya ñāṇaṃ pesetvā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā arahattañceva patto, sāvakapāramīñāṇassa ca matthakaṃ, soḷasa ca paññā paṭivijjhitvā ṭhito. Dīghanakho pana sotāpattiphalaṃ patvā saraṇesu patiṭṭhito.

Paṭisañcikkhato Anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimuccī

Bhagavā pana imaṃ desanaṃ sūriye dharamāneyeva niṭṭhāpetvā gijjhakūṭā oruyha veḷuvanaṃ gantvā sāvakasannipātamakāsi, caturaṅgasamannāgato sannipāto ahosi. Tatrimāni aṅgāni – māghanakkhattena yutto puṇṇamauposathadivaso, kenaci anāmantitāni hutvā attanoyeva dhammatāya sannipatitāni aḍḍhatelasāni bhikkhusatāni, tesu ekopi puthujjano vā sotāpanna-sakadāgāmi-anāgāmi-sukkhavipassaka-arahantesu vā aññataro natthi, sabbe chaḷabhiññāva, ekopi cettha satthakena kese chinditvā pabbajito nāma natthi, sabbe ehibhikkhunoyevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Dīghanakhasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
206. "Abhiññāpahānamāhā": Among things such as the eternal (sassata), having known each and every quality as eternal (sassataṃ abhiññāya jānitvā), it says to abandon the eternal. (pahānamāha) Cutting off (ucchedaṃ), having known the partially eternal, it speaks of abandoning the partially eternal. (ekaccasassataṃ abhiññāya ekaccasassatassa pahānaṃ vadati.)

Having known form (rūpaṃ abhiññāya), it speaks of abandoning form (rūpassa pahānaṃ vadatīti)—in this way, the meaning here should be understood (atthena veditabbo).

"Paṭisañcikkhato": of one who reflects. (paccavekkhantassa.)

"Anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimuccī": The mind is liberated from the āsavas without clinging due to the cessation of arising; the mind is liberated since the āsavas are blocked without grasping (anuppādanirodhena niruddhehi āsavehi aggahetvāva cittaṃ vimucci).

Thus, having enjoyed food increased by another (parassa vaḍḍhitaṃ bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā), as if dispelling hunger, having sent forth wisdom toward the teaching of the Dharma that was begun by another (āraddhāya dhammadesanāya ñāṇaṃ pesetvā), having increased insight (vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā), he attained arahantship (arahattañceva patto), the summit of the knowledge of a disciple's perfections (sāvakapāramīñāṇassa ca matthakaṃ), and stood having pierced through the sixteen knowledges (soḷasa ca paññā paṭivijjhitvā ṭhito).

But Dīghanakha, having attained the fruit of stream-entry (sotāpattiphalaṃ patvā), was established in the refuges (saraṇesu patiṭṭhito).

"Paṭisañcikkhato"

"Anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimuccī"

The Blessed One, indeed, having completed this teaching right when the sun was holding [its place], having descended from Vulture Peak (gijjhakūṭā oruyha), having gone to the Bamboo Grove (veḷuvanaṃ gantvā), made an assembly of disciples (sāvakasannipātamakāsi); the assembly was endowed with four factors (caturaṅgasamannāgato sannipāto ahosi).

These are the factors (aṅgāni): it was a full-moon uposatha day joined with the Māgha constellation (māghanakkhattena yutto puṇṇamauposathadivaso), one thousand two hundred fifty monks assembled on their own by nature, without being invited by anyone (kenaci anāmantitāni hutvā attanoyeva dhammatāya sannipatitāni aḍḍhatelasāni bhikkhusatāni), among them there was not even one ordinary person, or one of the stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, dry-insight practitioners or arahants, all had the six abhiññās (tesu ekopi puthujjano vā sotāpanna-sakadāgāmi-anāgāmi-sukkhavipassaka-arahantesu vā aññataro natthi, sabbe chaḷabhiññāva), there was not even one here who had gone forth having cut off his hair with a razor (ekopi cettha satthakena kese chinditvā pabbajito nāma natthi), all were "come, monks!" (ehibhikkhunoyevāti).

The Dīghanakhasutta Commentary in the Papañcasūdanī of the Majjhimanikāya is finished (dīghanakhasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā).

mula_pali: 207. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kurūsu viharati kammāsadhammaṃ nāma kurūnaṃ nigamo, bhāradvājagottassa brāhmaṇassa agyāgāre tiṇasanthārake tiṇasantharake (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya kammāsadhammaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Kammāsadhammaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena aññataro vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāya. Taṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ ajjhogāhetvā aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi. Atha kho māgaṇḍiyo māgandiyo (sī. pī.) paribbājako jaṅghāvihāraṃ anucaṅkamamāno anuvicaramāno yena bhāradvājagottassa brāhmaṇassa agyāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho māgaṇḍiyo paribbājako bhāradvājagottassa brāhmaṇassa agyāgāre tiṇasanthārakaṃ paññattaṃ. Disvāna bhāradvājagottaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘kassa nvayaṃ bhoto bhāradvājassa agyāgāre tiṇasanthārako paññatto, samaṇaseyyānurūpaṃ samaṇaseyyārūpaṃ (sī. pī.) maññe’’ti? ‘‘Atthi, bho māgaṇḍiya, samaṇo gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. Tassesā bhoto gotamassa seyyā paññattā’’ti. ‘‘Duddiṭṭhaṃ vata, bho bhāradvāja, addasāma; duddiṭṭhaṃ vata, bho bhāradvāja, addasāma! Ye mayaṃ tassa bhoto gotamassa bhūnahuno bhūnahanassa (syā. kaṃ.) seyyaṃ addasāmā’’ti. ‘‘Rakkhassetaṃ, māgaṇḍiya, vācaṃ; rakkhassetaṃ , māgaṇḍiya, vācaṃ. Bahū hi tassa bhoto gotamassa khattiyapaṇḍitāpi brāhmaṇapaṇḍitāpi gahapatipaṇḍitāpi samaṇapaṇḍitāpi abhippasannā vinītā ariye ñāye dhamme kusale’’ti. ‘‘Sammukhā cepi mayaṃ, bho bhāradvāja, taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ passeyyāma, sammukhāpi naṃ vadeyyāma – ‘bhūnahu bhūnahano (syā. kaṃ.) samaṇo gotamo’ti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhi no sutte ocaratī’’ti. ‘‘Sace taṃ bhoto māgaṇḍiyassa agaru āroceyyāmi taṃ āroceyyametaṃ (sī. pī.), ārocessāmi tassa (syā. kaṃ.) samaṇassa gotamassā’’ti. ‘‘Appossukko bhavaṃ bhāradvājo vuttova naṃ vadeyyā’’ti.
mula_english:
207. Thus have I heard.

Once the Blessed One was staying in the Kuru country at a town of the Kurus named Kammasadhamma, on a spread of grass in the fire chamber of a *brāhmaṇa* belonging to the Bhāradvāja clan.

Then, when it was morning, the Blessed One dressed, and taking his bowl and outer robe, went into Kammasadhamma for alms.

When he had wandered for alms in Kammasadhamma and had returned from his almsround, after his meal he went to a certain grove for the day’s abiding.

Having entered the grove, he sat down at the root of a tree for the day’s abiding.

Then the wanderer Māgaṇḍiya, while walking and wandering for exercise, went to the fire chamber of the *brāhmaṇa* belonging to the Bhāradvāja clan.

The wanderer Māgaṇḍiya saw that a spread of grass had been prepared in the fire chamber of the *brāhmaṇa* belonging to the Bhāradvāja clan.

Having seen this, he said to the *brāhmaṇa* of the Bhāradvāja clan: “For whom has this spread of grass been prepared in Master Bhāradvāja’s fire chamber? It seems like a recluse’s bed.”

“Master Māgaṇḍiya, there is the recluse Gotama, the son of the Śākyans, who went forth from a Śākyan clan.

And concerning that Blessed Gotama, such a good report has spread about: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is an *arahaṃ*, perfectly enlightened, accomplished in true knowledge and conduct (*vijjācaraṇasampanno*), well-gone (*sugato*), knower of the world (*lokavidū*), unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed (*purisadammasārathi*), teacher of gods and humans (*devamanussānaṃ*), the Awakened One (*buddho*), the Blessed One (*bhagavā*)’.

This bed has been prepared for that Master Gotama.”

“It is ill-seen, Master Bhāradvāja, what we have seen; it is ill-seen, Master Bhāradvāja, what we have seen! That we have seen the bed of that Master Gotama, a destroyer of growth (*bhūnahuno*)!”

“Be careful what you say, Māgaṇḍiya, be careful what you say!

Many learned nobles (*khattiyapaṇḍitā*), learned *brāhmaṇas* (*brāhmaṇapaṇḍitā*), learned householders (*gahapatipaṇḍitā*), and learned recluses (*samaṇapaṇḍitā*) have full confidence in that Master Gotama, and have been disciplined by him in the noble true way (*ariye ñāye*), in the Dhamma (*dhamme*) that is wholesome (*kusale*)".

“Even face to face, Master Bhāradvāja, we would see that Master Gotama, even face to face we would say to him: ‘The recluse Gotama is a destroyer of growth (*bhūnahu*)!’

Why is this? Because that is how it occurs in our teachings (*sutte*).”

“If Master Māgaṇḍiya has no objection, may I tell this to the recluse Gotama?”

“Let Master Bhāradvāja be at ease. Tell him just what I have said.”
commentary_pali:
207.Evaṃme sutanti māgaṇḍiyasuttaṃ. Tattha agyāgāreti aggihomasālayaṃ. Tiṇasanthāraketi dve māgaṇḍiyā mātulo ca bhāgineyyo ca. Tesu mātulo pabbajitvā arahattaṃ patto, bhāgineyyopi saupanissayo nacirasseva pabbajitvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇissati. Athassa bhagavā upanissayaṃ disvā ramaṇīyaṃ devagabbhasadisaṃ gandhakuṭiṃ pahāya tattha chārikatiṇakacavarādīhi uklāpe agyāgāre tiṇasanthārakaṃ paññāpetvā parasaṅgahakaraṇatthaṃ katipāhaṃ vasittha. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Tenupasaṅkamīti na kevalaṃ taṃdivasameva, yasmā pana taṃ agyāgāraṃ gāmūpacāre dārakadārikāhi okiṇṇaṃ avivittaṃ, tasmā bhagavā niccakālampi divasabhāgaṃ tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe vītināmetvā sāyaṃ vāsatthāya tattha upagacchati.

Addasākho…pe… tiṇasanthārakaṃ paññattanti bhagavā aññesu divasesu tiṇasanthārakaṃ saṅgharitvā saññāṇaṃ katvā gacchati, taṃdivasaṃ pana paññapetvāva agamāsi. Kasmā? Tadā hi paccūsasamaye lokaṃ oloketvāva addasa – ‘‘ajja māgaṇḍiyo idhāgantvā imaṃ tiṇasanthārakaṃ disvā bhāradvājena saddhiṃ tiṇasanthārakaṃ ārabbha kathāsallāpaṃ karissati, athāhaṃ āgantvā dhammaṃ desessāmi, so dhammaṃ sutvā mama santike pabbajitvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇissati. Paresaṃ saṅgahakaraṇatthameva hi mayā pāramiyo pūritā’’ti tiṇasanthārakaṃ paññapetvāva agamāsi.

Addasā kho…pe… tiṇasanthārakaṃ paññatta

Samaṇaseyyānurūpaṃ maññeti imaṃ tiṇasanthārakaṃ ‘‘samaṇassa anucchavikā seyyā’’ti maññāmi. Na ca asaññatasamaṇassa nivutthaṭṭhānametaṃ. Tathāhettha hatthena ākaḍḍhitaṭṭhānaṃ vā pādena ākaḍḍhitaṭṭhānaṃ vā sīsena pahaṭaṭṭhānaṃ vā na paññāyati, anākulo anākiṇṇo abhinno chekena cittakārena tūlikāya paricchinditvā paññatto viya. Saññatasamaṇassa vasitaṭṭhānaṃ, kassa bho vasitaṭṭhānanti pucchati. Bhūnahunoti hatavaḍḍhino mariyādakārakassa. Kasmā evamāha? Chasu dvāresu vaḍḍhipaññāpanaladdhikattā. Ayañhi tassa laddhi – cakkhu brūhetabbaṃ vaḍḍhetabbaṃ, adiṭṭhaṃ dakkhitabbaṃ, diṭṭhaṃ samatikkamitabbaṃ. Sotaṃ brūhetabbaṃ vaḍḍhetabbaṃ, asutaṃ sotabbaṃ, sutaṃ samatikkamitabbaṃ. Ghānaṃ brūhetabbaṃ vaḍḍhetabbaṃ, aghāyitaṃ ghāyitabbaṃ, ghāyitaṃ samatikkamitabbaṃ. Jivhā brūhetabbā vaḍḍhetabbā, assāyitaṃ sāyitabbaṃ, sāyitaṃ samatikkamitabbaṃ. Kāyo brūhetabbo vaḍḍhetabbo, aphuṭṭhaṃ phusitabbaṃ, phuṭṭhaṃ samatikkamitabbaṃ. Mano brūhetabbo vaḍḍhetabbo, aviññātaṃ vijānitabbaṃ, viññātaṃ samatikkamitabbaṃ. Evaṃ so chasu dvāresu vaḍḍhiṃ paññapeti. Bhagavā pana –

Samaṇaseyyānurūpaṃ maññe Bhūnahuno

‘‘Cakkhunā saṃvaro sādhu, sādhu sotena saṃvaro;

Ghānena saṃvaro sādhu, sādhu jivhāya saṃvaro.

Kāyena saṃvaro sādhu, sādhu vācāya saṃvaro;

Manasā saṃvaro sādhu, sādhu sabbattha saṃvaro;

Sabbattha saṃvuto bhikkhu, sabbadukkhā pamuccatī’’ti. (dha. pa. 360-361) –

Chasu dvāresu saṃvaraṃ paññapeti. Tasmā so ‘‘vaḍḍhihato samaṇo gotamo mariyādakārako’’ti maññamāno ‘‘bhūnahuno’’ti āha.

Ariye ñāye dhamme kusaleti parisuddhe kāraṇadhamme anavajje. Iminā kiṃ dasseti? Evarūpassa nāma uggatassa paññātassa yasassino upari vācaṃ bhāsamānena vīmaṃsitvā upadhāretvā mukhe ārakkhaṃ ṭhapetvā bhāsitabbo hoti. Tasmā mā sahasā abhāsi, mukhe ārakkhaṃ ṭhapehīti dasseti. Evañhi no sutte ocaratīti yasmā amhākaṃ sutte evaṃ āgacchati, na mayaṃ mukhāruḷhicchāmattaṃ vadāma, sutte ca nāma āgataṃ vadamānā kassa bhāyeyyāma, tasmā sammukhāpi naṃ vadeyyāmāti attho. Appossukkoti mama rakkhanatthāya anussukko avāvaṭo hutvāti attho. Vuttova naṃ vadeyyāti mayā vuttova hutvā apucchitova kathaṃ samuṭṭhāpetvā ambajambūādīni gahetvā viya apūrayamāno mayā kathitaniyāmena bhavaṃ bhāradvājo vadeyya, vadassūti attho.

Ariye ñāye dhamme kusale Evañhi no sutte ocaratī Appossukko Vuttova naṃ vadeyyā
commentary_english:
207. Thus have I heard: the Māgaṇḍiya Sūtra.

Here, *agyāgāre* means in the fire-hall for burnt offerings.

*tiṇasanthārake* means two Māgaṇḍiyas, an uncle and a nephew.

Of these, the uncle, having gone forth, attained arhatship; the nephew, with the right support, not long after going forth, will attain arhatship.

Then, the Blessed One, having seen his support, and having abandoned the beautiful, deva-chamber-like Perfume Chamber, laid out a straw mat (*tiṇasanthāraka*) in the fire-hall (*agyāgāre*) with grass, chaff, rubbish, and so forth, and dwelt there for a few days for the purpose of helping others.

This was said regarding this.

*tenupasaṅkamī* means not only on that day, but because that fire-hall (*agyāgāra*) was crowded with boys and girls in the vicinity of the village, and was not secluded, the Blessed One always spent the day in that forest grove, and in the evening went there to stay.

*addasā kho…pe… tiṇasanthārakaṃ paññatta* means on other days the Blessed One would sweep together the straw mat (*tiṇasanthārakam*) and leave, making a sign, but on that day he went only after laying it out.

Why? Because then, at dawn, having looked upon the world, he saw – “Today, Māgaṇḍiya, having come here and seen this straw mat (*tiṇasanthārakam*), will engage in conversation with Bhāradvāja about the straw mat (*tiṇasanthārakam*), then I will come and teach the Dharma, and having heard the Dharma, he will go forth in my presence and attain arhatship.

For I have fulfilled the perfections only for the purpose of helping others,"—having laid out the straw mat (*tiṇasanthārakam*), he left.

*addasā kho…pe… tiṇasanthārakaṃ paññatta*

*"samaṇaseyyānurūpaṃ maññe"* means I think that this straw mat (*tiṇasanthārakaṃ*) is a suitable bed for a renunciant (*samaṇa*).

And this is not a place for an unrestrained renunciant (*samaṇa*) to live.

For here, a place pulled by hand, or a place pulled by foot, or a place struck by the head is not evident; it is undisturbed, uncrowded, unbroken, as if laid out by a clever painter, having marked it off with a brush.

It is a place for a restrained renunciant (*saññatasamaṇa*) to live; whose dwelling place is it, sir, he asks.

*"bhūnahuno"* means of the destroyer of growth, the maker of boundaries.

Why does he say this? Because he has gained the doctrine of the establishment of growth in the six sense-spheres.

For this is his doctrine – the eye should be strengthened and increased; what has not been seen should be seen; what has been seen should be transcended.

The ear should be strengthened and increased; what has not been heard should be heard; what has been heard should be transcended.

The nose should be strengthened and increased; what has not been smelled should be smelled; what has been smelled should be transcended.

The tongue should be strengthened and increased; what has not been tasted should be tasted; what has been tasted should be transcended.

The body should be strengthened and increased; what has not been touched should be touched; what has been touched should be transcended.

The mind should be strengthened and increased; what has not been cognized should be cognized; what has been cognized should be transcended.

Thus, he establishes growth in the six sense-spheres.

But the Blessed One –

*"samaṇaseyyānurūpaṃ maññe bhūnahuno"*

“Restraint of the eye is good, good is restraint of the ear;

Restraint of the nose is good, good is restraint of the tongue.

Restraint of the body is good, good is restraint of speech;

Restraint of the mind is good, good is restraint everywhere;

The renunciant restrained everywhere is freed from all suffering.”

(Dhp. 360-361) –

establishes restraint in the six sense-spheres.

Therefore, thinking, "The renunciant Gotama is one whose growth has been destroyed, a maker of boundaries," he said, "bhūnahuno."
"**ariye ñāye dhamme kusale**" means in pure causal states, faultless.

What does this indicate by this? It indicates that when speaking about someone renowned, learned, and famous, one should speak after having reflected, considered, and kept watch over one's mouth. Therefore, it shows: "Don't speak hastily, keep watch over your mouth."

"**evañhi no sutte ocaratī**" Because it comes thus in our sūtra, we don't speak merely out of what we have picked up by mouth. And since we speak according to what has come in the sūtra, why should we fear anyone? Therefore, [it means] we can speak even face to face.

"**appossukko**" means not being eager, not being distracted, for the sake of protecting me.

"**vuttova naṃ vadeyyā**" means Bhava Bharadvaja should speak according to the rule spoken by me, as if not asking but setting forth, not filling up like taking mangoes, jambu fruits, etc.; he should speak, let him speak, according to what I have said.

mula_pali: 208. Assosi kho bhagavā dibbāya sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya bhāradvājagottassa brāhmaṇassa māgaṇḍiyena paribbājakena saddhiṃ imaṃ kathāsallāpaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena bhāradvājagottassa brāhmaṇassa agyāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā nisīdi bhagavā paññatte tiṇasanthārake. Atha kho bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho bhāradvājagottaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘ahu pana te, bhāradvāja, māgaṇḍiyena paribbājakena saddhiṃ imaṃyeva tiṇasanthārakaṃ ārabbha kocideva kathāsallāpo’’ti? Evaṃ vutte, bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo saṃviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘etadeva kho pana mayaṃ bhoto gotamassa ārocetukāmā. Atha ca pana bhavaṃ gotamo anakkhātaṃyeva akkhāsī’’ti. Ayañca hi ayañca hidaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) bhagavato bhāradvājagottena brāhmaṇena saddhiṃ antarākathā vippakatā hoti. Atha kho māgaṇḍiyo paribbājako jaṅghāvihāraṃ anucaṅkamamāno anuvicaramāno yena bhāradvājagottassa brāhmaṇassa agyāgāraṃ yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho māgaṇḍiyaṃ paribbājakaṃ bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
208. The Blessed One heard with his divine ear element—purified, surpassing the human—this conversation between the brahmin of the Bharadvaja clan and the wanderer Magandiya.

Then, in the evening, the Blessed One arose from seclusion and went to the fire chamber of the brahmin of the Bharadvaja clan; having arrived, the Blessed One sat down on the spread of grass made ready.

Then the brahmin of the Bharadvaja clan went to where the Blessed One was; having arrived, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One.

Having concluded the courteous and amiable talk, he sat down at one side.

As he was sitting to one side, the Blessed One said to the brahmin of the Bharadvaja clan: “Bharadvaja, did you have any conversation with the wanderer Magandiya about this very spread of grass?” When this was said, the brahmin of the Bharadvaja clan, agitated and with his hair standing on end, said to the Blessed One: “We wanted to tell Master Gotama about that very thing. But Master Gotama has anticipated us.”

And this discussion between the Blessed One and the brahmin of the Bharadvaja clan was left unfinished.

Then the wanderer Magandiya, while walking and wandering for exercise, went to the fire chamber of the brahmin of the Bharadvaja clan, where the Blessed One was; having arrived, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One.

Having concluded the courteous and amiable talk, he sat down at one side.

As he was sitting to one side, the Blessed One said to the wanderer Magandiya:
commentary_pali: 208.Assosikhoti satthā ālokaṃ vaḍḍhetvā dibbacakkhunā māgaṇḍiyaṃ tattha āgataṃ addasa, dvinnaṃ janānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ dibbasotena saddampi assosi. Paṭisallānā vuṭṭhitoti phalasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhito. Saṃviggoti pītisaṃvegena saṃviggo calito kampito. Tassa kira etadahosi – ‘‘neva māgaṇḍiyena samaṇassa gotamassa ārocitaṃ, na mayā. Amhe muñcitvā añño ettha tatiyopi natthi, suto bhavissati amhākaṃ saddo tikhiṇasotena purisenā’’ti. Athassa abbhantare pīti uppajjitvā navanavutilomakūpasahassāni uddhaggāni akāsi. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘saṃviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto’’ti. Athakho māgaṇḍiyo paribbājakoti paribbājakassa pabhinnamukhaṃ viya bījaṃ paripākagataṃ ñāṇaṃ, tasmā sannisīdituṃ asakkonto āhiṇḍamāno puna satthu santikaṃ āgantvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Taṃ dassetuṃ ‘‘atha kho māgaṇḍiyo’’tiādi vuttaṃ.
commentary_english:
208.
assosi
kho: The teacher, having increased the light with divine vision, saw Māgaṇḍiya who had come there. With divine hearing, he heard the sound of two people speaking.
paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito: [It means] one who has arisen from the fruition attainment (phalasamāpatti).
saṃviggo: Saṃviggo, shaken and agitated by the joy of agitation (pītisaṃvega).
The thought then occurred to him: "It was not announced to the ascetic Gotama by Māgaṇḍiya, nor by me.
Having released us, there is no other third person here; our voice will be heard by a man with sharp hearing."
Then joy arose within him, causing ninety-nine hundred thousand hairs in his pores to stand on end.
Therefore it was said, "Saṃviggo, with hair standing on end."
atha
kho māgaṇḍiyo paribbājako: The wandering ascetic Māgaṇḍiyo, whose knowledge (ñāṇa) was like a seed with a broken surface that had reached maturity (paripākagata). Unable to sit down, he wandered around and again came to the Teacher's presence and sat down to one side.
To show that, it was said, "atha kho māgaṇḍiyo," and so forth.

mula_pali: 209. ‘‘Cakkhuṃ kho, māgaṇḍiya, rūpārāmaṃ rūparataṃ rūpasammuditaṃ. Taṃ tathāgatassa dantaṃ guttaṃ rakkhitaṃ saṃvutaṃ, tassa ca saṃvarāya dhammaṃ deseti. Idaṃ nu te etaṃ, māgaṇḍiya, sandhāya bhāsitaṃ – ‘bhūnahu samaṇo gotamo’’’ti? ‘‘Etadeva kho pana me, bho gotama, sandhāya bhāsitaṃ – ‘bhūnahu samaṇo gotamo’ti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhi no sutte ocaratī’’ti. ‘‘Sotaṃ kho, māgaṇḍiya, saddārāmaṃ…pe… ghānaṃ kho, māgaṇḍiya gandhārāmaṃ… jivhā kho, māgaṇḍiya, rasārāmā rasaratā rasasammuditā. Sā tathāgatassa dantā guttā rakkhitā saṃvutā, tassā ca saṃvarāya dhammaṃ deseti. Idaṃ nu te etaṃ, māgaṇḍiya, sandhāya bhāsitaṃ – ‘bhūnahu samaṇo gotamo’’’ti? ‘‘Etadeva kho pana me, bho gotama, sandhāya bhāsitaṃ – ‘bhūnahu samaṇo gotamo’ti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhi no sutte ocaratī’’ti. ‘‘Kāyo kho, māgaṇḍiya, phoṭṭhabbārāmo phoṭṭhabbarato…pe… mano kho, māgaṇḍiya, dhammārāmo dhammarato dhammasammudito. So tathāgatassa danto gutto rakkhito saṃvuto, tassa ca saṃvarāya dhammaṃ deseti. Idaṃ nu te etaṃ, māgaṇḍiya, sandhāya bhāsitaṃ – ‘bhūnahu samaṇo gotamo’’’ti? ‘‘Etadeva kho pana me, bho gotama, sandhāya bhāsitaṃ – ‘bhūnahu samaṇo gotamo’ti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhi no sutte ocaratī’’ti.
mula_english:
209. The eye, Māgaṇḍiya, delights in forms ( *rūpa*), takes delight in forms, rejoices in forms.

That has been tamed by the *Tathāgata*, guarded, protected, and restrained, and he teaches the *Dharma* for its restraint.

Was it with reference to this that you said: “The recluse Gotama is a destroyer of growth’?” “It was with reference to this, Master Gotama, that I said: ‘The recluse Gotama is a destroyer of growth.’

Why is this so? It is just in this way that it occurs in our *sutta*."

The ear, Māgaṇḍiya, delights in sounds (*śabda*)…pe… The nose, Māgaṇḍiya, delights in odors (*gandha*)… The tongue, Māgaṇḍiya, delights in flavors (*rasa*), takes delight in flavors, rejoices in flavors.

That has been tamed by the *Tathāgata*, guarded, protected, and restrained, and he teaches the *Dharma* for its restraint.

Was it with reference to this that you said: “The recluse Gotama is a destroyer of growth’?” “It was with reference to this, Master Gotama, that I said: ‘The recluse Gotama is a destroyer of growth.’

Why is this so? It is just in this way that it occurs in our *sutta*."

The body (*kāya*), Māgaṇḍiya, delights in tangibles (*sparśa*), takes delight in tangibles…pe… The mind, Māgaṇḍiya, delights in mind-objects (*dharma*), takes delight in mind-objects, rejoices in mind-objects.

That has been tamed by the *Tathāgata*, guarded, protected, and restrained, and he teaches the *Dharma* for its restraint.

Was it with reference to this that you said: “The recluse Gotama is a destroyer of growth’?” “It was with reference to this, Master Gotama, that I said: ‘The recluse Gotama is a destroyer of growth.’

Why is this so? It is just in this way that it occurs in our *sutta*."
commentary_pali: 209. Satthā – ‘‘evaṃ kira tvaṃ, māgaṇḍiya, maṃ avacā’’ti avatvāva cakkhuṃ kho, māgaṇḍiyāti paribbājakassa dhammadesanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha vasanaṭṭhānaṭṭhena rūpaṃ cakkhussa ārāmoti cakkhu rūpārāmaṃ. Rūpe ratanti rūparataṃ. Rūpena cakkhu āmoditaṃ pamoditanti rūpasamuditaṃ. Dantanti nibbisevanaṃ. Guttanti gopitaṃ. Rakkhitanti ṭhapitarakkhaṃ. Saṃvutanti pihitaṃ. Saṃvarāyāti pidhānatthāya.
commentary_english:
The teacher said: "Māgaṇḍiya, without even saying, 'It seems that you spoke to me in this way,' he began teaching the Dharma to the wanderer, saying, "Māgaṇḍiya, it is the eye."

There, *rūpaṃ cakkhussa ārāmoti cakkhu rūpārāmaṃ*: because form is a delightful place, a dwelling place for the eye, therefore the eye is "delighted with form" (*rūpārāmaṃ*).

*rūpe ratanti rūparataṃ*: Being delighted in forms is "fond of form" (*rūparataṃ*).

*rūpena cakkhu āmoditaṃ pamoditanti rūpasamuditaṃ*: Because the eye is pleased and gladdened by form, it is "prosperous with form" (*rūpasamuditaṃ*).

*danta*nti *nibbisevanaṃ*: "*danta*" means "non-indulgence."

*gutta*nti *gopitaṃ*: "*gutta*" means "protected."

*rakkhita*nti *ṭhapitarakkhaṃ*: "*rakkhita*" means "establishing protection."

*saṃvuta*nti *pihitaṃ*: "*saṃvuta*" means "covered."

*saṃvarāyā*ti *pidhānatthāya*: "*saṃvarāyā*" is for the purpose of "covering."

mula_pali: 210. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, māgaṇḍiya – ‘idhekacco cakkhuviññeyyehi rūpehi paricāritapubbo assa iṭṭhehi kantehi manāpehi piyarūpehi kāmūpasaṃhitehi rajanīyehi, so aparena samayena rūpānaṃyeva samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ viditvā rūpataṇhaṃ pahāya rūpapariḷāhaṃ paṭivinodetvā vigatapipāso ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacitto vihareyya. Imassa pana te, māgaṇḍiya, kimassa vacanīya’’’nti? ‘‘Na kiñci, bho gotama’’. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, māgaṇḍiya – ‘idhekacco sotaviññeyyehi saddehi…pe… ghānaviññeyyehi gandhehi… jivhāviññeyyehi rasehi… kāyaviññeyyehi phoṭṭhabbehi paricāritapubbo assa iṭṭhehi kantehi manāpehi piyarūpehi kāmūpasaṃhitehi rajanīyehi, so aparena samayena phoṭṭhabbānaṃyeva samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ viditvā phoṭṭhabbataṇhaṃ pahāya phoṭṭhabbapariḷāhaṃ paṭivinodetvā vigatapipāso ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacitto vihareyya. Imassa pana te, māgaṇḍiya, kimassa vacanīya’’’nti? ‘‘Na kiñci, bho gotama’’.
mula_english:
“What do you think, Magandiya? Here someone may have formerly enjoyed himself with forms cognizable by the eye that are wished for, desired, agreeable, and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust. On a later occasion, having understood as they actually are the origin (*samudaya*), the disappearance (*atthaṅgama*), the gratification (*assāda*), the danger (*ādīnava*), and the escape (*nissaraṇa*) in the case of forms (*rūpa*), he might abandon craving for forms (*rūpataṇhā*), remove fever for forms (*rūpapariḷāha*), and abide without thirst, with a mind inwardly at peace. What would you have to say about that?”

“Nothing, Master Gotama.”

“What do you think, Magandiya? Here someone may have formerly enjoyed himself with sounds cognizable by the ear…with odours cognizable by the nose…with flavours cognizable by the tongue…with tangibles cognizable by the body that are wished for, desired, agreeable, and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust. On a later occasion, having understood as they actually are the origin, the disappearance, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of tangibles, he might abandon craving for tangibles, remove fever for tangibles, and abide without thirst, with a mind inwardly at peace. What would you have to say about that?”

“Nothing, Master Gotama.”
commentary_pali: 210.Paricāritapubboti abhiramitapubbo. Rūpapariḷāhanti rūpaṃ ārabbha uppajjanapariḷāhaṃ. Imassa pana te, māgaṇḍiya, kimassa vacanīyanti imassa rūpaṃ pariggaṇhitvā arahattappattassa khīṇāsavassa tayā kiṃ vacanaṃ vattabbaṃ assa, vuḍḍhihato mariyādakārakoti idaṃ vattabbaṃ, na vattabbanti pucchati. Na kiñci, bho gotamāti, bho gotama, kiñci vattabbaṃ natthi. Sesadvāresupi eseva nayo.
commentary_english:
"Paricāritapubbo" means previously delighted in.

"Rūpapariḷāha" means the torment that arises in relation to form (rūpa).

"Imassa pana te, Māgaṇḍiya, kimassa vacanīya" means: Māgaṇḍiya, what statement should be made by you regarding this person who, having apprehended form, has attained arahantship and is a *khīṇāsava* (one who has destroyed the āsavas)? Should it be said, "He is ruined by old age and is a maker of boundaries (mariyādakārako)," or should it not be said? He asks.

"Na kiñci, bho Gotamā" means: "Nothing, venerable Gotama. Nothing needs to be said."

The same method applies to the remaining doors (sesadvāresupi eseva nayo).

mula_pali: 211. ‘‘Ahaṃ kho pana, māgaṇḍiya, pubbe agāriyabhūto samāno pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāresiṃ cakkhuviññeyyehi rūpehi iṭṭhehi kantehi manāpehi piyarūpehi kāmūpasaṃhitehi rajanīyehi, sotaviññeyyehi saddehi…pe… ghānaviññeyyehi gandhehi… jivhāviññeyyehi rasehi… kāyaviññeyyehi phoṭṭhabbehi iṭṭhehi kantehi manāpehi piyarūpehi kāmūpasaṃhitehi rajanīyehi. Tassa mayhaṃ, māgaṇḍiya, tayo pāsādā ahesuṃ – eko vassiko, eko hemantiko, eko gimhiko. So kho ahaṃ, māgaṇḍiya, vassike pāsāde vassike cattāro vassike pāsāde cattāro (syā. kaṃ.) māse nippurisehi tūriyehi turiyehi (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) paricārayamāno paricāriyamāno (sabbattha) na heṭṭhāpāsādaṃ orohāmi. So aparena samayena kāmānaṃyeva samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ viditvā kāmataṇhaṃ pahāya kāmapariḷāhaṃ paṭivinodetvā vigatapipāso ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacitto viharāmi. So aññe satte passāmi kāmesu avītarāge kāmataṇhāhi khajjamāne kāmapariḷāhena pariḍayhamāne kāme paṭisevante. So tesaṃ na pihemi, na tattha abhiramāmi . Taṃ kissa hetu? Yāhayaṃ, māgaṇḍiya, rati, aññatreva kāmehi aññatra akusalehi dhammehi – api dibbaṃ sukhaṃ samadhigayha tiṭṭhati – tāya ratiyā ramamāno hīnassa na pihemi, na tattha abhiramāmi.
mula_english:
211. “Magandiya, formerly, when I was living the household life, I lived supplied and endowed with the five cords of sensual pleasure (*pañcahi kāmaguṇehi*): with forms cognizable by the eye that were wished for, desired, agreeable, and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust; with sounds cognizable by the ear…with odours cognizable by the nose…with flavours cognizable by the tongue…with tangibles cognizable by the body that were wished for, desired, agreeable, and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust.

I had three palaces, Magandiya, one for the rainy season (*vassiko*), one for the winter (*hemantiko*), and one for the summer (*gimhiko*).

Then, Magandiya, during the rainy season, I lived in the rains’ palace (*vassike pāsāde*), enjoying myself for the four months with musicians who were all female, and I did not go down to the lower palace.

On a later occasion, having understood as they actually are the origination (*samudayañca*), the passing away (*atthaṅgamañca*), the gratification (*assādañca*), the danger (*ādīnavañca*), and the escape (*nissaraṇañca*) in the case of sensual pleasures, I abandoned craving for sensual pleasures (*kāmataṇhaṃ pahāya*), I removed fever for sensual pleasures (*kāmapariḷāhaṃ paṭivinodetvā*), and I abide without thirst, with a mind inwardly at peace (*ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacitto viharāmi*).

I see other beings who are not free from lust for sensual pleasures being devoured by craving for sensual pleasures, burning with fever for sensual pleasures, indulging in sensual pleasures.

I do not envy them, nor do I delight therein.

Why is that? Because, Magandiya, that pleasure which I attain apart from sensual pleasures, apart from unwholesome states—even divine bliss— I abide having attained it. Enjoying that pleasure, I do not envy inferior pleasures, nor do I delight therein.
commentary_pali:
211. Idāni yasmā tayā pañcakkhandhe pariggahetvā arahattappattassa khīṇāsavassa kiñci vattabbaṃ natthi, ahañca pañcakkhandhe pariggahetvā sabbaññutaṃ patto, tasmā ahampi te na kiñci vattabboti dassetuṃ ahaṃ kho panātiādimāha. Tassa mayhaṃ māgaṇḍiyāti gihikāle attano sampattiṃ dassento āha. Tattha vassikotiādīsu yattha sukhaṃ hoti vassakāle vasituṃ, ayaṃ vassiko. Itaresupi eseva nayo. Ayaṃ panettha vacanattho – vassaṃ vāso vassaṃ, vassaṃ arahatīti vassiko. Itaresupi eseva nayo.

Tattha vassiko pāsādo nātiucco hoti nātinīco, dvāravātapānānipissa nātitanūni nātibahūni, bhūmattharaṇapaccattharaṇakhajjabhojjānipettha missakāneva vaṭṭanti. Hemantike thambhāpi bhittiyopi nīcā honti, dvāravātapānāni tanukāni sukhumacchiddāni. Uṇhapavesanatthāya bhittiniyūhāni nīharīyanti. Bhūmattharaṇapaccattharaṇanivāsanapārupanāni panettha uṇhavīriyāni kambalādīni vaṭṭanti. Khajjabhojjaṃ siniddhaṃ kaṭukasannissitañca. Gimhike thambhāpi bhittiyopi uccā honti. Dvāravātapānāni panettha bahūni vipulajālāni bhavanti. Bhūmattharaṇādīni dukūlamayāni vaṭṭanti, khajjabhojjāni madhurarasasītavīriyāni. Vātapānasamīpesu cettha nava cāṭiyo ṭhapetvā udakassa pūretvā nīluppalādīhi sañchādenti. Tesu tesu padesesu udakayantāni karonti, yehi deve vassante viya udakadhārā nikkhamanti.

Bodhisattassa pana aṭṭhasatasuvaṇṇaghaṭe ca rajataghaṭe ca gandhodakassa pūretvā nīluppalagacchake katvā sayanaṃ parivāretvā ṭhapayiṃsu. Mahantesu lohakaṭāhesu gandhakalalaṃ pūretvā nīluppalapadumapuṇḍarīkāni ropetvā utuggahaṇatthāya tattha tattha ṭhapesuṃ. Sūriyarasmīhi pupphāni pupphanti. Nānāvidhā bhamaragaṇā pāsādaṃ pavisitvā pupphesu rasaṃ gaṇhantā vicaranti. Pāsādo atisugandho hoti. Yamakabhittiyā antare lohanāḷiṃ ṭhapetvā navabhūmikapāsādassa upari ākāsaṅgaṇe ratanamaṇḍapamatthake sukhumacchiddakaṃ jālaṃ baddhaṃ ahosi. Ekasmiṃ ṭhāne sukkhamahiṃsacammaṃ pasāreti. Bodhisattassa udakakīḷanavelāya mahiṃsacamme pāsāṇaguḷe khipanti, meghathanitasaddo viya hoti. Heṭṭhā yantaṃ parivattenti, udakaṃ abhiruhitvā jālamatthake patati, vassapatanasalilaṃ viya hoti. Tadā bodhisatto nīlapaṭaṃ nivāseti, nīlapaṭaṃ pārupati, nīlapasādhanaṃ pasādheti. Parivārāpissa cattālīsanāṭakasahassāni nīlavatthābharaṇāneva nīlavilepanāni hutvā mahāpurisaṃ parivāretvā ratanamaṇḍapaṃ gacchanti. Divasabhāgaṃ udakakīḷaṃ kīḷanto sītalaṃ utusukhaṃ anubhoti.

Pāsādassa catūsu disāsu cattāro sarā honti. Divākāle nānāvaṇṇasakuṇagaṇā pācīnasarato vuṭṭhāya viravamānā pāsādamatthakena pacchimasaraṃ gacchanti. Pacchimasarato vuṭṭhāya pācīnasaraṃ, uttarasarato dakkhiṇasaraṃ, dakkhiṇasarato uttarasaraṃ gacchanti, antaravassasamayo viya hoti. Hemantikapāsādo pana pañcabhūmiko ahosi, vassikapāsādo sattabhūmiko.

Nippurisehīti purisavirahitehi. Na kevalañcettha tūriyāneva nippurisāni, sabbaṭṭhānānipi nippurisāneva . Dovārikāpi itthiyova, nhāpanādiparikammakarāpi itthiyova. Rājā kira – ‘‘tathārūpaṃ issariyasukhasampattiṃ anubhavamānassa purisaṃ disvā parisaṅkā uppajjati, sā me puttassa mā ahosī’’ti sabbakiccesu itthiyova ṭhapesi. Tāya ratiyā ramamānoti idaṃ catutthajjhānikaphalasamāpattiratiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

Nippurisehī Tāya ratiyā ramamāno
commentary_english:
Now, since there is nothing to be said to her, who, having grasped the five aggregates, has attained *arhatship*, is rid of taints, and I, having grasped the five aggregates, have attained omniscience, therefore, to show that there is nothing to be said by me to you, he said, "I, indeed,..." etc.

"*Tassa mayhaṃ māgaṇḍiyā*," he said, indicating his own prosperity at the time of his householder life.

There, in "*vassiko*," etc., "*vassiko*" [means]: this is *vassiko* because it is a place where there is happiness to dwell in the rainy season.

The same method applies in the other cases as well.

Here, the meaning of the statement is this: *vassaṃ vāso vassaṃ, vassaṃ arahatīti vassiko*—"dwelling during the rains, dwelling during the rains, because it is fitting for the rains, [it is called] *vassiko*."

The same method applies in the other cases as well.

There, the *vassiko* palace is neither too high nor too low; its door windows are neither too thin nor too many; floor coverings, spread coverings, edibles, and foods exist there in a mixed state.

In the winter season, the pillars and walls are low, the door windows are thin, [and] have subtle openings.

Wall projections are removed for the purpose of allowing warmth to enter.

Floor coverings, spread coverings, cloths for wear, and outer garments, warm and vigorous woolen blankets, etc., exist here.

The edibles and foods are oily and mixed with pungent flavors.

In the summer season, the pillars and walls are high.

The door windows are many [and] have wide nets.

Floor coverings, etc., are made of *dukūla* cloth, [and] the edibles and foods are sweet in taste and cooling.

Near the windows, nine bowls are placed, filled with water, and covered with blue lotuses, etc.

In those places, they make water contraptions, from which streams of water emerge as if the gods were raining.

Furthermore, they filled eight hundred gold jars and silver jars with scented water for the *bodhisattva*, and, having made bouquets of blue lotuses, they surrounded the bed and set them in place.

Having filled large iron caldrons with fragrant paste and having planted blue lotuses, lotuses, and white lotuses, they placed them here and there for the sake of seasonal enjoyment.

The flowers blossom with the sun's rays.

Various groups of bees enter the palace, and, taking the nectar in the flowers, they roam about.

The palace is exceedingly fragrant.

Having placed an iron pipe in between double walls, a subtle latticework of openings was fixed on top of the jeweled pavilion at the summit of the nine-storied palace.

In one place, they spread out a dry antelope hide.

At the time of the *bodhisattva*'s water sports, they toss stones onto the antelope hide, [and] it is as if there is the sound of thunder clouds.

They turn a mechanism below, [and] the water rises up and falls on top of the latticework; it is as if there is rainfall.

Then, the *bodhisattva* puts on a blue cloth, wears a blue cloth, [and] arranges blue adornments.

His retinue of forty thousand actors, having become blue in clothing, ornaments, and unguents, surround the great man and go to the jeweled pavilion.

While sporting and playing water games during the day, he experiences cool seasonal happiness.

There are four lakes in the four directions of the palace.

During the daytime, groups of birds of various colors rise up from the eastern lake, and, chirping, they go to the western lake by way of the top of the palace.

Having risen up from the western lake, [they go] to the eastern lake; from the northern lake to the southern lake; from the southern lake to the northern lake; it is as if it were the time between rains.

The winter palace, however, was five-storied, [and] the rainy season palace was seven-storied.
nippurisehī means "by those who are without men," that is, deserted by men.

Not only here are the musical instruments without men, but all the places are also without men.

The doorkeeper was also a woman, and the bath attendant and other service workers were also women.

The king, it is said, [thought]: "When I see a man enjoying such royal happiness and prosperity, suspicion arises. May that not happen to my son." Therefore, he appointed only women to all duties.

tāya ratiyā ramamāno means "enjoying that pleasure," which is said with reference to the pleasure of attaining the fruition of the fourth *jhāna*.

mula_pali:
212. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, māgaṇḍiya, gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā aḍḍho mahaddhano mahābhogo pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāreyya cakkhuviññeyyehi rūpehi…pe… phoṭṭhabbehi iṭṭhehi kantehi manāpehi piyarūpehi kāmūpasaṃhitehi rajanīyehi. So kāyena sucaritaṃ caritvā vācāya sucaritaṃ caritvā manasā sucaritaṃ caritvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyya devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sahabyataṃ. So tattha nandane vane accharāsaṅghaparivuto dibbehi pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāreyya. So passeyya gahapatiṃ vā gahapatiputtaṃ vā pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitaṃ samaṅgībhūtaṃ paricārayamānaṃ.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, māgaṇḍiya, api nu so devaputto nandane vane accharāsaṅghaparivuto dibbehi pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricārayamāno amussa gahapatissa vā gahapatiputtassa vā piheyya, mānusakānaṃ vā pañcannaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ mānusakehi vā kāmehi āvaṭṭeyyā’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’. Taṃ kissa hetu? Mānusakehi, bho gotama, kāmehi dibbakāmā abhikkantatarā ca paṇītatarā cā’’ti. ‘‘Evameva kho ahaṃ, māgaṇḍiya, pubbe agāriyabhūto samāno pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāresiṃ cakkhuviññeyyehi rūpehi iṭṭhehi kantehi manāpehi piyarūpehi kāmūpasaṃhitehi rajanīyehi, sotaviññeyyehi saddehi…pe… ghānaviññeyyehi gandhehi… jivhāviññeyyehi rasehi… kāyaviññeyyehi phoṭṭhabbehi iṭṭhehi kantehi manāpehi piyarūpehi kāmūpasaṃhitehi rajanīyehi. So aparena samayena kāmānaṃyeva samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ viditvā kāmataṇhaṃ pahāya kāmapariḷāhaṃ paṭivinodetvā vigatapipāso ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacitto viharāmi. So aññe satte passāmi kāmesu avītarāge kāmataṇhāhi khajjamāne kāmapariḷāhena pariḍayhamāne kāme paṭisevante, so tesaṃ na pihemi, na tattha abhiramāmi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Yāhayaṃ, māgaṇḍiya, rati aññatreva kāmehi aññatra akusalehi dhammehi – api dibbaṃ sukhaṃ samadhigayha tiṭṭhati – tāya ratiyā ramamāno hīnassa na pihemi, na tattha abhiramāmi.
mula_english:
“Suppose, Magandiya, a householder or a householder’s son was rich, with great wealth and property, and being provided and endowed with the five cords of sensual pleasure, he might enjoy himself with forms cognizable by the eye…with tangibles cognizable by the body that are wished for, desired, agreeable, and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust.

Having conducted himself well in body (*kāyena sucaritaṃ caritvā*), speech, and mind, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he might reappear in a happy destination, in the heavenly world in the retinue of the gods of the Thirty-three;

and there, surrounded by a group of nymphs in the Nandana Grove, he would enjoy himself, provided and endowed with the five cords of divine sensual pleasure.

Suppose he saw a householder or a householder’s son enjoying himself, provided and endowed with the five cords of human sensual pleasure.

”What do you think, Magandiya? Would that young god surrounded by the group of nymphs in the Nandana Grove, enjoying himself, provided and endowed with the five cords of divine sensual pleasure, envy the householder or the householder’s son for the five cords of human sensual pleasure or would he return to human sensual pleasures? “ “No indeed, Blessed One.”

What is the reason for that? “Because, Gotama, divine sensual pleasures are more surpassing and more exquisite than human sensual pleasures.”

“So too, Magandiya, formerly when I lived the home life, I enjoyed myself, provided and endowed with the five cords of sensual pleasure: with forms cognizable by the eye…with sounds cognizable by the ear…with odours cognizable by the nose…with flavours cognizable by the tongue…with tangibles cognizable by the body that are wished for, desired, agreeable, and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust.

On a later occasion, having understood as they actually are the origination (*samudaya*) , the disappearance (*atthaṅgama*) , the gratification (*assāda*) , the danger (*ādīnava*) , and the escape (*nissaraṇa*) in the case of sensual pleasures, I abandoned craving for sensual pleasures, I removed fever for sensual pleasures, and I abide without thirst, with a mind inwardly at peace.

I see other beings who are not free from lust for sensual pleasures being devoured by craving for sensual pleasures, burning with fever for sensual pleasures, indulging in sensual pleasures, and I do not envy them nor do I delight therein.

What is the reason for that? Because there is, Magandiya, a delight apart from sensual pleasures, apart from unwholesome states, which surpasses divine bliss. Since I take delight in that, I do not envy what is inferior, nor do I delight therein.
commentary_pali:
212.Gahapati vā gahapatiputto vāti ettha yasmā khattiyānaṃ setacchattasmiṃyeva patthanā hoti, mahā ca nesaṃ papañco, brāhmaṇā mantehi atittā mante gavesantā vicaranti, gahapatino pana muddāgaṇanamattaṃ uggahitakālato paṭṭhāya sampattiṃyeva anubhavanti, tasmā khattiyabrāhmaṇe aggahetvā ‘‘gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā’’ti āha. Āvaṭṭeyyāti mānusakakāmahetu āvaṭṭo bhaveyyāti attho. Abhikkantatarāti visiṭṭhatarā. Paṇītatarāti atappakatarā. Vuttampi cetaṃ –

‘‘Kusaggenudakamādāya, samudde udakaṃ mine;

Evaṃ mānusakā kāmā, dibbakāmāna santike’’ti. (jā. 2.21.389) –

Samadhigayha tiṭṭhatīti dibbasukhaṃ gaṇhitvā tato visiṭṭhatarā hutvā tiṭṭhati.

Samadhigayha tiṭṭhatī

Opammasaṃsandanaṃ panettha evaṃ veditabbaṃ – gahapatissa pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samaṅgībhūtakālo viya bodhisattassa tīsu pāsādesu cattālīsasahassaitthimajjhe modanakālo, tassa sucaritaṃ pūretvā sagge nibbattakālo viya bodhisattassa abhinikkhamanaṃ katvā bodhipallaṅke sabbaññutaṃ paṭividdhakālo , tassa nandanavane sampattiṃ anubhavanakālo viya tathāgatassa catutthajjhānikaphalasamāpattiratiyā vītivattanakālo, tassa mānusakānaṃ pañcannaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ apatthanakālo viya tathāgatassa catutthajjhānikaphalasamāpattiratiyā vītināmentassa hīnajanasukhassa apatthanakāloti.
commentary_english:
212. “*Gahapati* or *gahapatiputto vā*”: Here, the aspiration of the *khattiyas* is only for the white umbrella; and their proliferation [of desires] is great. The *brāhmaṇas*, being unsatiated with mantras, go about seeking mantras. But the *gahapati* experiences prosperity from the time he learns only the counting of money. Therefore, without including *khattiyas* and *brāhmaṇas*, he said, “*gahapati* or *gahapatiputto vā*.”

"*Āvaṭṭeyyā*": because of human desire, there would be a turning back; this is the meaning.

"*Abhikkantatarā*": more excellent.

"*Paṇītatarā*": more refined; less coarse.

This was said:

“Taking water with a blade of *kuśa* grass, one might measure the water in the ocean;

Thus are human sensual pleasures, compared to divine sensual pleasures."

(Jā. 2.21.389) –

"*Samadhigayha tiṭṭhati*": having taken divine happiness, having become more excellent than that, he remains.

*Samadhigayha tiṭṭhati*:

Herein, the connection of the simile should be understood thus: The time of enjoying the five sensual qualities by the householder is like the time of rejoicing of the *bodhisattva* in the three palaces amidst forty thousand women; the time of completing his good conduct and being reborn in heaven is like the time when the *bodhisattva*, having renounced the world and attained omniscience at the *bodhi* seat, <pb ed="p" n="3.0217"/>, the time of experiencing prosperity in the Nandana grove is like the time of the *tathāgata* passing the night in the fruition attainment of the fourth *jhāna*; the time of not desiring the five sensual qualities of humans <pb ed="v" n="3.0156"/> is like the time of the *tathāgata* who has passed the night in the fruition attainment of the fourth *jhāna*, not desiring the happiness of inferior beings.

mula_pali:
213. ‘‘Seyyathāpi , māgaṇḍiya, kuṭṭhī puriso arugatto pakkagatto kimīhi khajjamāno nakhehi vaṇamukhāni vippatacchamāno aṅgārakāsuyā kāyaṃ paritāpeyya. Tassa mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā bhisakkaṃ sallakattaṃ upaṭṭhāpeyyuṃ. Tassa so bhisakko sallakatto bhesajjaṃ kareyya. So taṃ bhesajjaṃ āgamma kuṭṭhehi parimucceyya, arogo assa sukhī serī sayaṃvasī yena kāmaṃ gamo. So aññaṃ kuṭṭhiṃ purisaṃ passeyya arugattaṃ pakkagattaṃ kimīhi khajjamānaṃ nakhehi vaṇamukhāni vippatacchamānaṃ aṅgārakāsuyā kāyaṃ paritāpentaṃ.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, māgaṇḍiya, api nu so puriso amussa kuṭṭhissa purisassa piheyya aṅgārakāsuyā vā bhesajjaṃ paṭisevanāya vā’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama. Taṃ kissa hetu? Roge hi, bho gotama, sati bhesajjena karaṇīyaṃ hoti, roge asati na bhesajjena karaṇīyaṃ hotī’’ti. ‘‘Evameva kho ahaṃ, māgaṇḍiya, pubbe agāriyabhūto samāno pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāresiṃ, cakkhuviññeyyehi rūpehi iṭṭhehi kantehi manāpehi piyarūpehi kāmūpasaṃhitehi rajanīyehi, sotaviññeyyehi saddehi…pe… ghānaviññeyyehi gandhehi… jivhāviññeyyehi rasehi… kāyaviññeyyehi phoṭṭhabbehi iṭṭhehi kantehi manāpehi piyarūpehi kāmūpasaṃhitehi rajanīyehi. So aparena samayena kāmānaṃyeva samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ viditvā kāmataṇhaṃ pahāya kāmapariḷāhaṃ paṭivinodetvā vigatapipāso ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacitto viharāmi. So aññe satte passāmi kāmesu avītarāge kāmataṇhāhi khajjamāne kāmapariḷāhena pariḍayhamāne kāme paṭisevante. So tesaṃ na pihemi, na tattha abhiramāmi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Yāhayaṃ, māgaṇḍiya, rati, aññatreva kāmehi aññatra akusalehi dhammehi – api dibbaṃ sukhaṃ samadhigayha tiṭṭhati – tāya ratiyā ramamāno hīnassa na pihemi, na tattha abhiramāmi.
mula_english:
213. Suppose, Magandiya, there was a leper (*kuṭṭhī puriso*) with sores and blisters on his limbs (*arugatto pakkagatto*), being devoured by worms (*kimīhi khajjamāno*), scratching the scabs off the openings of his wounds with his nails (*nakhehi vaṇamukhāni vippatacchamāno*), cauterising his body over a burning charcoal pit (*aṅgārakāsuyā kāyaṃ paritāpeyya*).

Then his friends and companions (*mittāmaccā*), his kinsmen and relatives (*ñātisālohitā*), would bring a physician (*bhisakkaṃ*) and a surgeon (*sallakattaṃ*) to treat him (*upaṭṭhāpeyyuṃ*).

The physician (*bhisakko sallakatto*) would make a medicine (*bhesajjaṃ kareyya*) for him.

And by means of that medicine (*bhesajjaṃ āgamma*) the man would be cured of his leprosy (*kuṭṭhehi parimucceyya*) and would become well (*arogo assa*) and happy (*sukhī*), independent (*serī*), master of himself (*sayaṃvasī*), able to go where he likes (*yena kāmaṃ gamo*).

Then he might see another leper (*kuṭṭhiṃ purisaṃ passeyya*) with sores and blisters on his limbs (*arugattaṃ pakkagattaṃ*), being devoured by worms (*kimīhi khajjamānaṃ*), scratching the scabs off the openings of his wounds with his nails (*nakhehi vaṇamukhāni vippatacchamānaṃ*), cauterising his body over a burning charcoal pit (*aṅgārakāsuyā kāyaṃ paritāpentaṃ*).

What do you think, Magandiya? Would that man envy that leper for his burning charcoal pit or his use of medicine? “

“No, Master Gotama.

What is the reason for that? Because when there is sickness (*roge sati*), medicine (*bhesajjaṃ*) has to be made (*karaṇīyaṃ hoti*), and when there is no sickness (*roge asati*) medicine (*bhesajjaṃ*) does not have to be made (*karaṇīyaṃ hoti*)”.

“So too, Magandiya, formerly when I lived the home life (*pubbe agāriyabhūto samāno*), I enjoyed myself, provided and endowed with the five cords of sensual pleasure (*pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāresiṃ*): with forms cognizable by the eye (*cakkhuviññeyyehi rūpehi*) that are wished for (*iṭṭhehi*), desired (*kantehi*), agreeable (*manāpehi*), and likeable (*piyarūpehi*), connected with sensual desire (*kāmūpasaṃhitehi*) and provocative of lust (*rajanīyehi*), with sounds cognizable by the ear (*sotaviññeyyehi saddehi*)…with odours cognizable by the nose (*ghānaviññeyyehi gandhehi*)…with flavours cognizable by the tongue (*jivhāviññeyyehi rasehi*)…with tangibles cognizable by the body (*kāyaviññeyyehi phoṭṭhabbehi*) that are wished for (*iṭṭhehi*), desired (*kantehi*), agreeable (*manāpehi*), and likeable (*piyarūpehi*), connected with sensual desire (*kāmūpasaṃhitehi*) and provocative of lust (*rajanīyehi*).

On a later occasion, having understood as they actually are (*yathābhūtaṃ viditvā*) the gratification (*samudayañca*), the cessation (*atthaṅgamañca*), the satisfaction (*assādañca*), the danger (*ādīnavañca*), and the escape (*nissaraṇañca*) in the case of sensual pleasures (*kāmānaṃyeva*), I abandoned craving for sensual pleasures (*kāmataṇhaṃ pahāya*), I removed fever for sensual pleasures (*kāmapariḷāhaṃ paṭivinodetvā*), and I abide without thirst (*vigatapipāso*), with a mind inwardly at peace (*ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacitto viharāmi*).

I see other beings (*aññe satte passāmi*) who are not free from lust for sensual pleasures (*kāmesu avītarāge*) being devoured by craving for sensual pleasures (*kāmataṇhāhi khajjamāne*), burning with fever for sensual pleasures (*kāmapariḷāhena pariḍayhamāne*), indulging in sensual pleasures (*kāme paṭisevante*),

and I do not envy them (*na pihemi*), nor do I delight therein (*na tattha abhiramāmi*).

What is the reason for that? Because there is, Magandiya, a delight (*rati*) apart from sensual pleasures (*aññatreva kāmehi*), apart from unwholesome states (*aññatra akusalehi dhammehi*)—which surpasses divine bliss (*api dibbaṃ sukhaṃ samadhigayha tiṭṭhati*)—Since I take delight in that (*tāya ratiyā ramamāno*), I do not envy what is inferior (*hīnassa na pihemi*), nor do I delight therein (*na tattha abhiramāmi*).
commentary_pali:
213.Sukhīti paṭhamaṃ dukkhito pacchā sukhito assa. Serīti paṭhamaṃ vejjadutiyako pacchā serī ekako bhaveyya. Sayaṃvasīti paṭhamaṃ vejjassa vase vattamāno vejjena nisīdāti vutte nisīdi, nipajjāti vutte nipajji, bhuñjāti vutte bhuñji, pivāti vutte pivi, pacchā sayaṃvasī jāto. Yena kāmaṃgamoti paṭhamaṃ icchiticchitaṭṭhānaṃ gantuṃ nālattha, pacchā roge vūpasante vanadassana-giridassana-pabbatadassanādīsupi yenakāmaṃ gamo jāto, yattha yattheva gantuṃ icchati, tattha tattheva gaccheyya.

Etthāpi idaṃ opammasaṃsandanaṃ – purisassa kuṭṭhikālo viya hi bodhisattassa agāramajjhe vasanakālo, aṅgārakapallaṃ viya ekaṃ kāmavatthu, dve kapallāni viya dve vatthūni, sakkassa pana devarañño aḍḍhateyyakoṭiyāni aṅgārakapallāni viya aḍḍhatiyanāṭakakoṭiyo, nakhehi vaṇamukhāni tacchetvā aṅgārakapalle paritāpanaṃ viya vatthupaṭisevanaṃ, bhesajjaṃ āgamma arogakālo viya kāmesu ādīnavaṃ nekkhamme ca ānisaṃsaṃ disvā nikkhamma buddhabhūtakāle catutthajjhānikaphalasamāpattiratiyā vītivattanakālo, aññaṃ kuṭṭhipurisaṃ disvā apatthanakālo viya tāya ratiyā vītināmentassa hīnajanaratiyā apatthanakāloti.
commentary_english:
213. *Sukhī:* Initially distressed, later he may be happy.

*Serī:* Initially in the care of a doctor, later free, he may be alone.

*Sayaṃvasī:* Initially, while under the control of a doctor, when told by the doctor, "Sit down," he sat; when told, "Lie down," he lay down; when told, "Eat," he ate; when told, "Drink," he drank; later, he became independent ( *sayaṃvasī jāto*).

*Yena kāmaṃ gamo:* Initially, he was unable to go to any place he desired, but later, when the illness subsided, he was able to go wherever he wished—to see forests, mountains, hills, and so on. Wherever he wished to go, he could go.

Here also, this is a comparison: A time of skin disease is like the bodhisattva's time dwelling in a household; a single charcoal ember is like a single object of desire (*kāmavatthu*); two embers are like two objects; embers amounting to two and a half crores, like two and a half crores of dramatic performances; scraping wounds with fingernails and heating them on a charcoal ember is like indulging in objects of desire; coming upon medicine and a time of health is like seeing the drawbacks in desires (*kāmesu ādīnavaṃ*) and the advantages in renunciation (*nekkhamme ca ānisaṃsaṃ*), going forth, and, at the time of being a Buddha, the time of experiencing the bliss of the fourth *jhāna* attainment; seeing another person with skin disease is like the time of aversion to that delight due to delighting in inferior people and the time of aversion.

mula_pali:
214. ‘‘Seyyathāpi , māgaṇḍiya, kuṭṭhī puriso arugatto pakkagatto kimīhi khajjamāno nakhehi vaṇamukhāni vippatacchamāno aṅgārakāsuyā kāyaṃ paritāpeyya. Tassa mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā bhisakkaṃ sallakattaṃ upaṭṭhāpeyyuṃ. Tassa so bhisakko sallakatto bhesajjaṃ kareyya. So taṃ bhesajjaṃ āgamma kuṭṭhehi parimucceyya, arogo assa sukhī serī sayaṃvasī yena kāmaṃ gamo. Tamenaṃ dve balavanto purisā nānābāhāsu gahetvā aṅgārakāsuṃ upakaḍḍheyyuṃ.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, māgaṇḍiya, api nu so puriso iti citiceva kāyaṃ sannāmeyyā’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bho gotama’’. ‘‘Taṃ kissa hetu’’? ‘‘Asu hi, bho gotama, aggi dukkhasamphasso ceva mahābhitāpo ca mahāpariḷāho cā’’ti. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, māgaṇḍiya, idāneva nu kho so aggi dukkhasamphasso ceva mahābhitāpo ca mahāpariḷāho ca udāhu pubbepi so aggi dukkhasamphasso ceva mahābhitāpo ca mahāpariḷāho cā’’ti ? ‘‘Idāni ceva, bho gotama, so aggi dukkhasamphasso ceva mahābhitāpo ca mahāpariḷāho ca, pubbepi so aggi dukkhasamphasso ceva mahābhitāpo ca mahāpariḷāho ca. Asu ca asu hi ca (sī. pī.), bho gotama, kuṭṭhī puriso arugatto pakkagatto kimīhi khajjamāno nakhehi vaṇamukhāni vippatacchamāno upahatindriyo dukkhasamphasseyeva aggismiṃ sukhamiti viparītasaññaṃ paccalatthā’’ti. ‘‘Evameva kho, māgaṇḍiya, atītampi addhānaṃ kāmā dukkhasamphassā ceva mahābhitāpā ca mahāpariḷāhā ca, anāgatampi addhānaṃ kāmā dukkhasamphassā ceva mahābhitāpā ca mahāpariḷāhā ca, etarahipi paccuppannaṃ addhānaṃ kāmā dukkhasamphassā ceva mahābhitāpā ca mahāpariḷāhā ca. Ime ca, māgaṇḍiya, sattā kāmesu avītarāgā kāmataṇhāhi khajjamānā kāmapariḷāhena pariḍayhamānā upahatindriyā dukkhasamphassesuyeva kāmesu sukhamiti viparītasaññaṃ paccalatthuṃ.

asu hi ca (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
214. Suppose, Magandiya, there was a leper (*kuṭṭhī puriso*) with sores and blisters on his limbs (*arugatto pakkagatto*), being devoured by worms (*kimīhi khajjamāno*), scratching the scabs off the openings of his wounds with his nails (*nakhehi vaṇamukhāni vippatacchamāno*), cauterising his body over a burning charcoal pit (*aṅgārakāsuyā kāyaṃ paritāpeyya*).

Then his friends and companions, kinsmen and relatives (*mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā*), brought a physician (*bhisakkaṃ sallakattaṃ upaṭṭhāpeyyuṃ*).

The physician (*bhisakko sallakatto*) would make a medicine (*bhesajjaṃ kareyya*) for him.

And by means of that medicine (*taṃ bhesajjaṃ āgamma*) the man would be cured of his leprosy (*kuṭṭhehi parimucceyya*) and would become well (*arogo assa*) and happy (*sukhī*), independent (*serī*), master of himself (*sayaṃvasī*), able to go where he likes (*yena kāmaṃ gamo*).

Then two strong men (*dve balavanto purisā*) would seize him by both arms (*nānābāhāsu gahetvā*) and drag him towards a burning charcoal pit (*aṅgārakāsuṃ upakaḍḍheyyuṃ*).

“What do you think, Magandiya? Would that man contort his body like this?” “Yes, Master Gotama.”

“Why is this so (*taṃ kissa hetu*)?” “Because that fire (*aggi*) is indeed painful to touch (*dukkhasamphasso*), hot (*mahābhitāpo*), and scorching (*mahāpariḷāho*).”

“What do you think, Magandiya? Is it only now that that fire (*aggi*) is painful to touch (*dukkhasamphasso*), hot (*mahābhitāpo*), and scorching (*mahāpariḷāho*), or previously too was that fire painful to touch, hot, and scorching?” "Master Gotama, that fire (*aggi*) is now painful to touch (*dukkhasamphasso*), hot (*mahābhitāpo*), and scorching (*mahāpariḷāho*), and previously too that fire was painful to touch, hot, and scorching."

And because when that man (*kuṭṭhī puriso*) was a leper with sores and blisters on his limbs (*arugatto pakkagatto*), being devoured by worms (*kimīhi khajjamāno*), scratching the scabs off the openings of his wounds with his nails (*nakhehi vaṇamukhāni vippatacchamāno*), his faculties were impaired (*upahatindriyo*); thus, though the fire was actually painful to touch (*dukkhasamphasseyeva*), he mistakenly perceived it as pleasant (*aggismiṃ sukhamiti viparītasaññaṃ paccalatthā*).”

“So too, Magandiya, in the past sensual pleasures (*kāmā*) were painful to touch (*dukkhasamphassā*), hot (*mahābhitāpā*), and scorching (*mahāpariḷāhā*); in the future sensual pleasures will be painful to touch, hot, and scorching; and now at present sensual pleasures are painful to touch, hot, and scorching.

But these beings (*sattā*) who are not free from lust (*avītarāgā*) for sensual pleasures (*kāmesu*), who are devoured by craving for sensual pleasures (*kāmataṇhāhi khajjamānā*), who burn with fever for sensual pleasures (*kāmapariḷāhena pariḍayhamānā*), have faculties that are impaired (*upahatindriyā*); thus, though sensual pleasures are actually painful to touch (*dukkhasamphassesuyeva*), they acquire a mistaken perception of them as pleasant (*kāmesu sukhamiti viparītasaññaṃ paccalatthuṃ*).
commentary_pali: 214.Upahatindriyoti kimirakuṭṭhena nāma upahatakāyappasādo. Upahatindriyāti upahatapaññindriyā. Te yathā so upahatakāyindriyo kuṭṭhī dukkhasamphassasmiṃyeva aggismiṃ sukhamiti viparītasaññaṃ paccalattha, evaṃ paññindriyassa upahatattā dukkhasamphassesveva kāmesu sukhamiti viparītasaññaṃ paccalatthuṃ.
commentary_english:
214.
*Upahatindriyo* means *upahatakāyappasāda* by name of *kimirakuṭṭha*.
*Upahatindriyā* means *upahatapaññindriya*.
Just as that *upahatakāyindriya* leper found pleasure in the painful touch of fire, so too, due to the afflicted state of the faculty of wisdom, they find pleasure in the painful touches of desires, thus having a reversed perception.

mula_pali:
215. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, māgaṇḍiya, kuṭṭhī puriso arugatto pakkagatto kimīhi khajjamāno nakhehi vaṇamukhāni vippatacchamāno aṅgārakāsuyā kāyaṃ paritāpeti. Yathā yathā kho, māgaṇḍiya, asu kuṭṭhī puriso arugatto pakkagatto kimīhi khajjamāno nakhehi vaṇamukhāni vippatacchamāno aṅgārakāsuyā kāyaṃ paritāpeti tathā tathā’ssa tathā tathā tasseva (syā. kaṃ. ka.) tāni vaṇamukhāni asucitarāni ceva honti duggandhatarāni ca pūtikatarāni ca , hoti ceva kāci sātamattā assādamattā – yadidaṃ vaṇamukhānaṃ kaṇḍūvanahetu; evameva kho, māgaṇḍiya, sattā kāmesu avītarāgā kāmataṇhāhi khajjamānā kāmapariḷāhena ca pariḍayhamānā kāme paṭisevanti. Yathā yathā kho, māgaṇḍiya, sattā kāmesu avītarāgā kāmataṇhāhi khajjamānā kāmapariḷāhena ca pariḍayhamānā kāme paṭisevanti tathā tathā tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ kāmataṇhā ceva pavaḍḍhati, kāmapariḷāhena ca pariḍayhanti, hoti ceva sātamattā assādamattā – yadidaṃ pañcakāmaguṇe paṭicca.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, māgaṇḍiya, api nu te diṭṭho vā suto vā rājā vā rājamahāmatto vā pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricārayamāno kāmataṇhaṃ appahāya kāmapariḷāhaṃ appaṭivinodetvā vigatapipāso ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacitto vihāsi vā viharati vā viharissati vā’’ti ? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’. ‘‘Sādhu, māgaṇḍiya! Mayāpi kho etaṃ, māgaṇḍiya, neva diṭṭhaṃ na sutaṃ rājā vā rājamahāmatto vā pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricārayamāno kāmataṇhaṃ appahāya kāmapariḷāhaṃ appaṭivinodetvā vigatapipāso ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacitto vihāsi vā viharati vā viharissati vā. Atha kho, māgaṇḍiya, ye hi keci samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā vigatapipāsā ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacittā vihāsuṃ vā viharanti vā viharissanti vā sabbe te kāmānaṃyeva samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ viditvā kāmataṇhaṃ pahāya kāmapariḷāhaṃ paṭivinodetvā vigatapipāsā ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacittā vihāsuṃ vā viharanti vā viharissanti vā’’ti. Atha kho bhagavā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

‘‘Ārogyaparamā lābhā, nibbānaṃ paramaṃ sukhaṃ;

Aṭṭhaṅgiko ca maggānaṃ, khemaṃ amatagāmina’’nti.
mula_english:
215. “Suppose, Māgaṇḍiya, there was a leper, *kuṭṭhī*, with sores and blisters on his limbs, being devoured by worms, scratching the scabs off the openings of his wounds *vaṇamukhāni* with his nails, cauterising his body *kāyaṃ* over a burning charcoal pit *aṅgārakāsuyā*; the more he scratches the scabs and cauterises his body *kāyaṃ*, the fouler, more evilsmelling and more infected the openings of his wounds *vaṇamukhāni* would become, yet he would find a certain measure of satisfaction and enjoyment in scratching the openings of his wounds *vaṇamukhānaṃ kaṇḍūvanahetu*. So too, Māgaṇḍiya, beings who are not free from lust *avītarāgā* for sensual pleasures *kāmesu*, who are devoured by craving for sensual pleasures *kāmataṇhāhi*, who burn with fever for sensual pleasures *kāmapariḷāhena*, still indulge in sensual pleasures *kāme paṭisevanti*; the more such beings indulge in sensual pleasures *kāme*, the more their craving for sensual pleasures *kāmataṇhā* increases and the more they are burned by their fever for sensual pleasures *kāmapariḷāhena*, yet they find a certain measure of satisfaction and enjoyment in dependence on the five cords of sensual pleasure *pañcakāmaguṇe*.

“What do you think, Māgaṇḍiya? Have you ever seen or heard of a king *rājā* or a king’s minister *rājamahāmatto* enjoying himself, provided and endowed with the five cords of sensual pleasure *pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto*, who, without abandoning craving for sensual pleasures *kāmataṇhaṃ appahāya*, without removing fever for sensual pleasures *kāmapariḷāhaṃ appaṭivinodetvā*, was able to abide free from thirst *vigatapipāso*, with a mind inwardly at peace *ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacitto*, or who is able or who will be able to so abide?”

“No, Master Gotama.”

“Good, Māgaṇḍiya! I too have never seen or heard of a king *rājā* or a king’s minister *rājamahāmatto* enjoying himself, provided and endowed with the five cords of sensual pleasure *pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto*, who, without abandoning craving for sensual pleasures *kāmataṇhaṃ appahāya*, without removing fever for sensual pleasures *kāmapariḷāhaṃ appaṭivinodetvā*, was able to abide free from thirst *vigatapipāso*, with a mind inwardly at peace *ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacitto*, or who is able or who will be able to so abide.

On the contrary, Māgaṇḍiya, those recluses *samaṇā* or brahmins *brāhmaṇā* who abided or abide or will abide free from thirst *vigatapipāsā*, with a mind inwardly at peace *ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacittā*, all do so after having understood as they actually are *yathābhūtaṃ* the origin *samudayaṃ*, the disappearance *atthaṅgamaṃ*, the gratification *assādaṃ*, the danger *ādīnavaṃ*, and the escape *nissaraṇaṃ* in the case of sensual pleasures *kāmānaṃ*, and it is after abandoning craving for sensual pleasures *kāmataṇhaṃ pahāya* and removing fever for sensual pleasures *kāmapariḷāhaṃ paṭivinodetvā* that they abided or abide or will abide free from thirst *vigatapipāsā*, with a mind inwardly at peace *ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacittā*.”

Then the Blessed One *bhagavā*, on that occasion, uttered this verse of uplift:

“Health is the highest gain, nirvāṇa *nibbānaṃ* is the highest bliss *sukhaṃ*;

the eightfold path *aṭṭhaṅgiko* is the best of paths, leading to the deathless *amatagāminaṃ* security *khemaṃ*.”
commentary_pali:
215.Asucitarāni cevātiādīsu pakatiyāva tāni asucīni ca duggandhāni ca pūtīni ca, idāni pana asucitarāni ceva duggandhatarāni ca pūtitarāni ca honti. Kācīti tassa hi paritāpentassa ca kaṇḍūvantassa ca pāṇakā anto pavisanti, duṭṭhalohitaduṭṭhapubbā paggharanti. Evamassa kāci assādamattā hoti.

Ārogyaparamāti gāthāya ye keci dhanalābhā vā yasalābhā vā puttalābhā vā atthi, ārogyaṃ tesaṃ paramaṃ uttamaṃ, natthi tato uttaritaro lābhoti, ārogyaparamā lābhā. Yaṃkiñci jhānasukhaṃ vā maggasukhaṃ vā phalasukhaṃ vā atthi, nibbānaṃ tattha paramaṃ, natthi tato uttaritaraṃ sukhanti nibbānaṃ paramaṃ sukhaṃ. Aṭṭhaṅgiko maggānanti pubbabhāgamaggānaṃ pubbabhāgagamaneneva amatagāmīnaṃ aṭṭhaṅgiko khemo, natthi tato khemataro añño maggo. Atha vā khemaṃ amatagāminanti ettha khemantipi amatantipi nibbānasseva nāmaṃ. Yāvatā puthusamaṇabrāhmaṇā parappavādā khemagāmino ca amatagāmino cāti laddhivasena gahitā, sabbesaṃ tesaṃ khemaamatagāmīnaṃ maggānaṃ aṭṭhaṅgiko paramo uttamoti ayamettha attho.

Ārogyaparamā Aṭṭhaṅgiko maggāna khemaṃ amatagāmina
commentary_english:
215. In the *asucitarāni cevā* etc., those are naturally impure, foul-smelling, and putrid; now, however, they are even more impure, even more foul-smelling, and even more putrid.

*kācī* means that maggots enter him as he is scorched and itches, and corrupted blood and pus ooze out.

Thus, he has some slight taste.

In the verse *ārogyaparamā* [verse begins at page break 3.0157], whatever gains of wealth, fame, or children there may be, health is the most excellent of these; there is no gain higher than that; health is the highest gain.

Whatever happiness of jhāna, the path, or the fruit there may be, nirvāṇa is the highest of these; there is no happiness higher than that; nirvāṇa is the supreme happiness.

*aṭṭhaṅgiko maggāna* means that of the preliminary paths, the eightfold path is the secure one for those going to the deathless through the preliminary path itself; there is no path more secure than that [verse begins at page break 3.0153].

Or alternatively, *khemaṃ amatagāmina* means that here, *khemaṃ* and *amataṃ* are names for nirvāṇa itself.

Insofar as the various wandering ascetics and Brahmins who are proponents of other doctrines are regarded as having taken up the attainment in terms of secure and deathless destinations, the eightfold path is the supreme and highest of all those paths to secure and deathless destinations; this is the meaning here.

*ārogyaparamā* [verse begins at page break 3.0157] *aṭṭhaṅgiko maggāna* [verse begins at page break 3.0153] *khemaṃ amatagāmina*

mula_pali: 216. Evaṃ vutte, māgaṇḍiyo paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘acchariyaṃ, bho gotama, abbhutaṃ, bho gotama! Yāva subhāsitaṃ cidaṃ bhotā gotamena – ‘ārogyaparamā lābhā, nibbānaṃ paramaṃ sukha’nti. Mayāpi kho etaṃ, bho gotama, sutaṃ pubbakānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘ārogyaparamā lābhā, nibbānaṃ paramaṃ sukha’nti; tayidaṃ, bho gotama, sametī’’ti. ‘‘Yaṃ pana te etaṃ, māgaṇḍiya, sutaṃ pubbakānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘ārogyaparamā lābhā, nibbānaṃ paramaṃ sukha’nti, katamaṃ taṃ ārogyaṃ, katamaṃ taṃ nibbāna’’nti? Evaṃ vutte, māgaṇḍiyo paribbājako sakāneva sudaṃ gattāni pāṇinā anomajjati – ‘‘idantaṃ, bho gotama, ārogyaṃ, idantaṃ nibbānaṃ. Ahañhi, bho gotama, etarahi arogo sukhī, na maṃ kiñci ābādhatī’’ti.
mula_english:
When this was said, the wanderer Māgaṇḍiya said this to the Bhagavān: "Amazing, Master Gotama, wonderful, Master Gotama! How well this has been expressed by Master Gotama: ‘The greatest of all gains is health (*ārogyaparamā* *lābhā*), *Nirvāṇa* (*nibbānaṃ*) is the greatest bliss (*paramaṃ* *sukhaṃ*)’.
We too have heard this said by earlier wanderers in the tradition of the teachers: ‘The greatest of all gains is health, *Nirvāṇa* is the greatest bliss; and it agrees, Master Gotama.”
“But that which you have heard, Māgaṇḍiya, from earlier wanderers in the tradition of the teachers: ‘The greatest of all gains is health, *Nirvāṇa* is the greatest bliss,’ what is that health (*ārogyaṃ*)? What is that *Nirvāṇa* (*nibbānaṃ*)?” When this was said, the wanderer Māgaṇḍiya massaged his limbs with his hand and said: “This, Master Gotama, is health, this is *Nirvāṇa*.
For I am now healthy (*arogo*) and happy (*sukhī*), and nothing afflicts me.”
commentary_pali: 216.Ācariyapācariyānanti ācariyānañceva ācariyācariyānañca. Sametīti ekanāḷiyā mitaṃ viya ekatulāya tulitaṃ viya sadisaṃ hoti ninnānākaraṇaṃ. Anomajjatīti pāṇiṃ heṭṭhā otārento majjati – ‘‘idaṃ taṃ, bho gotama, ārogyaṃ, idaṃ taṃ nibbāna’’nti kālena sīsaṃ kālena uraṃ parimajjanto evamāha.
commentary_english:
216. ācariyapācariyānanti means of teachers and teachers of teachers.

Sametīti, page 3.0219, like measured with a single tube, like weighed with a single balance, it is similar, making no distinction.

Anomajjatīti, lowering his hand downwards, he immerses himself, saying, "This is health, Gotama, this is nirvāṇa," stroking his head and chest in due course, he speaks thus.

mula_pali:
217. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, māgaṇḍiya, jaccandho puriso; so na passeyya kaṇhasukkāni rūpāni, na passeyya nīlakāni rūpāni, na passeyya pītakāni rūpāni, na passeyya lohitakāni rūpāni, na passeyya mañjiṭṭhakāni mañjeṭṭhikāni (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), mañjeṭṭhakāni (ka.) rūpāni, na passeyya samavisamaṃ, na passeyya tārakarūpāni, na passeyya candimasūriye. So suṇeyya cakkhumato bhāsamānassa – ‘chekaṃ vata, bho , odātaṃ vatthaṃ abhirūpaṃ nimmalaṃ sucī’ti! So odātapariyesanaṃ careyya. Tamenaṃ aññataro puriso telamalikatena sāhuḷicīrena telamasikatena sāhuḷacīvarena (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) vañceyya – ‘idaṃ te, ambho purisa, odātaṃ vatthaṃ abhirūpaṃ nimmalaṃ sucī’ti. So taṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, paṭiggahetvā pārupeyya, pārupetvā attamano attamanavācaṃ nicchāreyya – ‘chekaṃ vata, bho, odātaṃ vatthaṃ abhirūpaṃ nimmalaṃ sucī’ti!

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, māgaṇḍiya, api nu so jaccandho puriso jānanto passanto amuṃ telamalikataṃ sāhuḷicīraṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, paṭiggahetvā pārupeyya, pārupetvā attamano attamanavācaṃ nicchāreyya – ‘chekaṃ vata, bho, odātaṃ vatthaṃ abhirūpaṃ nimmalaṃ sucī’ti udāhu cakkhumato saddhāyā’’ti? ‘‘Ajānanto hi, bho gotama, apassanto so jaccandho puriso amuṃ telamalikataṃ sāhuḷicīraṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, paṭiggahetvā pārupeyya, pārupetvā attamano attamanavācaṃ nicchāreyya – ‘chekaṃ vata, bho, odātaṃ vatthaṃ abhirūpaṃ nimmalaṃ sucī’ti, cakkhumato saddhāyā’’ti. ‘‘Evameva kho, māgaṇḍiya, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā andhā acakkhukā ajānantā ārogyaṃ, apassantā nibbānaṃ , atha ca panimaṃ gāthaṃ bhāsanti – ‘ārogyaparamā lābhā, nibbānaṃ paramaṃ sukha’nti. Pubbakehesā, māgaṇḍiya, arahantehi sammāsambuddhehi gāthā bhāsitā –

‘Ārogyaparamā lābhā, nibbānaṃ paramaṃ sukhaṃ;

Aṭṭhaṅgiko ca maggānaṃ, khemaṃ amatagāmina’nti.
mula_english:
217. Suppose, Magandiya, there was a man born blind; he could not see dark and light forms, he could not see blue forms, he could not see yellow forms, he could not see red forms, he could not see pink forms, he could not see what was even and uneven, he could not see the stars or the sun and moon.

He might hear a man with good eyesight saying: ‘Good indeed, sirs, is a white cloth, beautiful, spotless, and clean!’ He would seek after a white cloth.

Then a certain man would cheat him with a dirty soiled garment thus: ‘Good man, here is a white cloth for you, beautiful, spotless, and clean.’

And he would accept it and put it on, and being satisfied with it, he would utter words of satisfaction thus: ‘Good indeed, sirs, is a white cloth, beautiful, spotless, and clean!’

What do you think, Magandiya? When that man born blind accepted that dirty soiled garment, put it on, and being satisfied with it, uttered words of satisfaction thus: ‘Good indeed, sirs, is a white cloth, beautiful, spotless, and clean! ‘ - did he do so knowing and seeing, or out of faith in the man with good eyesight?

“Because he does not know, good Gotama, because he does not see. That man born blind accepted that dirty soiled garment, put it on, and being satisfied with it, uttered words of satisfaction thus: ‘Good indeed, sirs, is a white cloth, beautiful, spotless, and clean! ‘ - out of faith in the man with good eyesight.”

“So too, Magandiya, the wanderers of other sects are blind and visionless. They do not know health (ārogya), they do not see *Nirvāṇa*, yet they utter this stanza thus: ‘The greatest of all gains is health (ārogyaparamā lābhā), *Nirvāṇa* (nibbānaṃ) is the greatest bliss (paramaṃ sukha)’.

In the past, Magandiya, this verse was spoken by the *arhats*, the Fully Awakened Ones (sammāsambuddhehi):

‘Health (ārogyaparamā) is the greatest gain (lābhā), *Nirvāṇa* (nibbānaṃ) is the supreme (paramaṃ) bliss (sukhaṃ);

And the eightfold (aṭṭhaṅgiko) path (maggānaṃ) leads to the secure (khemaṃ), the deathless (amatagāmina).’
commentary_pali: 217.Chekanti sampannaṃ. Sāhuḷicīrenāti kāḷakehi eḷakalomehi katathūlacīrena. Saṅkāracoḷakenātipi vadanti. Vācaṃ nicchāreyyāti kālena dasāya kālena ante kālena majjhe parimajjanto nicchāreyya, vadeyyāti attho. Pubbakehesāti pubbakehi esā. Vipassīpi hi bhagavā…pe… kassapopi bhagavā catuparisamajjhe nisinno imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi, ‘‘atthanissitagāthā’’ti mahājano uggaṇhi. Satthari parinibbute aparabhāge paribbājakānaṃ antaraṃ paviṭṭhā. Te potthakagataṃ katvā padadvayameva rakkhituṃ sakkhiṃsu. Tenāha – sā etarahi anupubbena puthujjanagāthāti.
commentary_english:
217. *Cheka* means accomplished.

*Sāhuḷicīrenā* means with a *cīra* made of black goat hair and *kata* cotton.

They say that it is also a dust cover.

*Vācaṃ nicchāreyyā* means that one should investigate, purify, and utter speech at the right time, at the end of the *dasā*, at the end, in the middle, and at the right time; this is its meaning.

*Pubbakehesā* means with earlier hair.

Indeed, Vipassī, the Blessed One… Kassapa, the Blessed One, sitting in the midst of the four assemblies, spoke this verse: "A verse based on meaning," the great assembly learned.

When the Teacher had attained *parinirvāṇa*, wanderers entered into the interval in a subsequent part.

Having made it into a book, they were only able to protect two words.

Therefore he said: *Sā etarahi anupubbena puthujjanagāthā*.

mula_pali: 218. ‘‘Sā etarahi anupubbena puthujjanagāthā puthujjanagatā (sī. pī.). Ayaṃ kho pana, māgaṇḍiya, kāyo rogabhūto gaṇḍabhūto sallabhūto aghabhūto ābādhabhūto, so tvaṃ imaṃ kāyaṃ rogabhūtaṃ gaṇḍabhūtaṃ sallabhūtaṃ aghabhūtaṃ ābādhabhūtaṃ – ‘idantaṃ, bho gotama, ārogyaṃ, idantaṃ nibbāna’nti vadesi. Tañhi te, māgaṇḍiya, ariyaṃ cakkhuṃ natthi yena tvaṃ ariyena cakkhunā ārogyaṃ jāneyyāsi, nibbānaṃ passeyyāsī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ pasanno ahaṃ bhoto gotamassa! Pahoti me bhavaṃ gotamo tathā dhammaṃ desetuṃ yathāhaṃ ārogyaṃ jāneyyaṃ, nibbānaṃ passeyya’’nti.
mula_english:
218. "At the present time, she is gradually [infused with] common worldly talk.
