Pañca ca kammuno satānīti pañca kammasatāni ca, kevalaṃ takkamattakena niratthakaṃ diṭṭhiṃ dīpeti. Pañca ca kammāni tīṇi ca kammānītiādīsupi eseva nayo. Keci panāhu pañca kammānīti pañcindriyavasena bhaṇati. Tīṇīti kāyakammādivasenāti. Kamme ca aḍḍhakamme cāti ettha panassa kāyakammañca vacīkammañca kammanti laddhi, manokammaṃ upaḍḍhakammanti. Dvaṭṭhipaṭipadāti dvāsaṭṭhi paṭipadāti vadati. Dvaṭṭhantarakappāti ekasmiṃ kappe catusaṭṭhi antarakappā nāma honti, ayaṃ pana aññe dve ajānanto evamāha. Chaḷābhijātiyo apaṇṇakasutte vitthāritā.

Pathavīkāyo Tatthā Natthi hantā vā Sattannaṃtveva kāyāna Yonipamukhasatasahassānī Pañca ca kammuno satānī Pañca ca kammāni tīṇi ca kammānī pañca kammānī Tīṇī Kamme ca aḍḍhakamme cā Dvaṭṭhipaṭipadā Dvaṭṭhantarakappā Chaḷābhijātiyo

Aṭṭha purisabhūmiyoti mandabhūmi khiḍḍābhūmi vīmaṃsakabhūmi ujugatabhūmi sekkhabhūmi samaṇabhūmi jinabhūmi pannabhūmīti imā aṭṭha purisabhūmiyoti vadati. Tattha jātadivasato paṭṭhāya sattadivase sambādhaṭṭhānato nikkhantattā sattā mandā honti momūhā. Ayaṃ mandabhūmīti vadati. Ye pana duggatito āgatā honti, te abhiṇhaṃ rodanti ceva viravanti ca. Sugatito āgatā taṃ anussaritvā anussaritvā hasanti. Ayaṃ khiḍḍābhūmi nāma. Mātāpitūnaṃ hatthaṃ vā pādaṃ vā mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā gahetvā bhūmiyaṃ padanikkhipanaṃ vīmaṃsakabhūmi nāma. Padasāva gantuṃ samatthakālo ujugatabhūmi nāma. Sippānaṃ sikkhanakālo sekkhabhūmi nāma. Gharā nikkhamma pabbajanakālo samaṇabhūmi nāma. Ācariyaṃ sevitvā jānanakālo jinabhūmi nāma. Bhikkhu ca pannako jino na kiñci āhāti evaṃ alābhiṃ samaṇaṃ pannabhūmīti vadati.

Aṭṭha purisabhūmiyo

Ekūnapaññāsaājīvasateti ekūnapaññāsa ājīvavuttisatāni. Paribbājakasateti paribbājakapabbajjasatāni. Nāgāvāsasateti nāgamaṇḍalasatāni. Vīse indriyasateti vīsa indriyasatāni. Tiṃse nirayasateti tiṃsa nirayasatāni. Rajodhātuyoti rajaokiraṇaṭṭhānāni. Hatthapiṭṭhipādapiṭṭhādīni sandhāya vadati. Satta saññīgabbhāti oṭṭhagoṇagadrabhaajapasumigamahiṃse sandhāya vadati. Asaññīgabbhāti sāliyavagodhumamuggakaṅguvarakakudrūsake sandhāya vadati. Nigaṇṭhigabbhāti nigaṇṭhimhi jātagabbhā, ucchuveḷunaḷādayo sandhāya vadati. Satta devāti bahū devā, so pana sattāti vadati. Mānusāpi anantā, so sattāti vadati. Satta pisācāti pisācā mahantā, sattāti vadati.

Ekūnapaññāsa ājīvasate Paribbājakasate Nāgāvāsasate Vīse indriyasate Tiṃse nirayasate Rajodhātuyo Satta saññīgabbhā Asaññīgabbhā Nigaṇṭhigabbhā Satta devā Satta pisācā

Sarāti mahāsarā. Kaṇṇamuṇḍa-rathakāra-anotatta-sīhapapātakuḷira-mucalinda-kuṇāladahe gahetvā vadati. Pavuṭāti gaṇṭhikā. Papātāti mahāpapātā. Papātasatānīti khuddakapapātasatāni. Supināti mahāsupinā. Supinasatānīti khuddakasupinasatāni. Mahākappinoti mahākappānaṃ. Ettha ekamhā sarā vassasate vassasate kusaggena ekaṃ udakabinduṃ nīharitvā nīharitvā sattakkhattuṃ tamhi sare nirudake kate eko mahākappoti vadati. Evarūpānaṃ mahākappānaṃ caturāsītisatasahassāni khepetvā bālā ca paṇḍitā ca dukkhassantaṃ karontīti ayamassa laddhi. Paṇḍitopi kira antarā sujjhituṃ na sakkoti, bālopi tato uddhaṃ na gacchati.

Sarā Pavuṭā Papātā Papātasatānī Supinā Supinasatānī Mahākappino

Sīlenāti acelakasīlena vā aññena vā yena kenaci. Vatenāti tādisena vatena. Tapenāti tapokammena. Aparipakkaṃ paripāceti nāma yo ‘‘ahaṃ paṇḍito’’ti antarā visujjhati. Paripakkaṃ phussa phussa byantiṃ karoti nāma yo ‘‘ahaṃ bālo’’ti vuttaparimāṇaṃ kālaṃ atikkamitvā yāti. Hevaṃ natthīti evaṃ natthi. Tañhi ubhayampi na sakkā kātunti dīpeti. Doṇamiteti doṇena mitaṃ viya. Sukhadukkheti sukhadukkhaṃ. Pariyantakateti vuttaparimāṇena kālena katapariyanto. Natthi hāyanavaḍḍhaneti natthi hāyanavaḍḍhanāni. Na saṃsāro paṇḍitassa hāyati, na bālassa vaḍḍhatīti attho. Ukkaṃsāvakaṃseti ukkaṃsāvakaṃsā, hāpanavaḍḍhanānamevetaṃ vevacanaṃ. Idāni tamatthaṃ upamāya sādhento seyyathāpi nāmātiādimāha. Tattha suttaguḷeti veṭhetvā katasuttaguḷaṃ. Nibbeṭhiyamānameva paletīti pabbate vā rukkhagge vā ṭhatvā khittaṃ suttapamāṇena nibbeṭhiyamānaṃ gacchati, sutte khīṇe tattha tiṭṭhati na gacchati. Evamevaṃ vuttakālato uddhaṃ na gacchatīti dasseti.

Sīlenā Vatenā Tapenā Hevaṃ natthī Doṇamite Sukhadukkhe Pariyantakate Natthi hāyanavaḍḍhane Ukkaṃsāvakaṃse seyyathāpi nāmā suttaguḷe Nibbeṭhiyamānameva paletī
commentary_english:
228. " *Akaṭā* " means unmade. " *Akaṭavidhā* " means unmade, unfashioned. “Unfashioned” means that they have not been constructed by anyone who commands them to be made; that is the meaning. " *Animmitā* " means not fashioned even by *iddhi*. " *Animmātā* " means unmade. Some say the reading is *animmitabbāti padaṃ*, but that is not found in the Pāli [canon] or in the commentary. " *Vañjhā* " means barren, like barren animals, barren palm trees, etc., fruitless; it means unproductive for anyone. By this, he denies that the bodies of earth, etc., produce anything such as material form, etc. Like the peak of a mountain, it stands, thus it is "*kūṭaṭṭhā*." "*Īsikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā*" means standing like a reed in *muñja* grass. This is the purport: that which is said to he born emerges as something already existing, like a reed (*īsikā*) that comes out from a sheath of *muñja* grass. " ' *Esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhitā'* " is also a reading; a well-driven stake stands firm; thus it stands, that is the meaning. By both [illustrations] he shows that they do not perish. " *Na iñjantī* " means because of standing like a stake, they do not move. " *Na vipariṇāmentī* " means they do not abandon their nature ( *pakati* ). " *Na aññamaññaṃ byābādhentī* " means they do not injure one another. " *Nāla* " means they are not able. " *Pathavīkāyo* " and so on: The body of earth is the earth itself, or the assemblage of earth. " *Tatthā* " means in those living bodies. " *Natthi hantā vā* " means there is neither slain nor slayer, neither hearer nor proclaimer, neither knower nor causer of knowing; that is what it indicates. " *Sattannaṃtveva kāyāna* " Just as, when one strikes a heap of beans with a sword, the sword enters in between the beans, so the sword enters the space, the interstice, between the seven bodies. Therein he shows: “I am taking his life,” that is only a mere idea. " *Yonipamukhasatasahassānī* " means fourteen hundred thousand of the principal wombs ( *yoni* ), sixty hundred thousand of other wombs, and six hundred thousand of other wombs. " *Pañca ca kammuno satānī* " means five hundred actions, and it reveals a futile view due to mere speculation. " *Pañca ca kammāni tīṇi ca kammānī* " and so on, the same method applies. Some say, " *Pañca kammānī*," speaking in terms of the five faculties. " *Tīṇī* " means according to the body's actions and so forth. " *Kamme ca aḍḍhakamme cā* " Here, indeed, body karma and speech karma are acquired as karma, [while] mind karma is half-karma. " *Dvaṭṭhipaṭipadā* " He says sixty-two pathways. " *Dvaṭṭhantarakappā* " means in one aeon, there are sixty-four sub-aeons, but this one speaks thus without knowing the other two. " *Chaḷābhijātiyo* " are explained in the Apaṇṇaka Sutta. *Pathavīkāyo* *Tatthā* *Natthi hantā vā* *Sattannaṃtveva kāyāna* *Yonipamukhasatasahassānī* *Pañca ca kammuno satānī* *Pañca ca kammāni tīṇi ca kammānī* *Pañca kammānī* *Tīṇī* *Kamme ca aḍḍhakamme cā* *Dvaṭṭhipaṭipadā* *Dvaṭṭhantarakappā* *Chaḷābhijātiyo* *Aṭṭha purisabhūmiyo* means the stage of feebleness, the stage of play, the stage of learning to walk, the erect stage, the stage of training, the recluse stage, the conqueror stage, and the prostrate stage; he declares that these are the eight stages in the life of man. The stage of feebleness: this lasts for seven days following the day of birth; for after coming out from the womb beings are feeble and dull. This one says, "This is a dull place." Those who have come from unfortunate realms weep and cry frequently. Those who have come from fortunate realms, remembering it again and again, laugh. This is called a playground. The stage of learning to walk: this is the stage when the child takes hold of its parents’ hands or feet, or a bed or chair, and places its feet on the ground; it is called the stage of learning. The erect stage: this is the stage when it is able to walk on its feet; it is called the erect stage. The time of learning skills is called the trainable stage. The recluse stage: this is the time when one has renounced the household life and gone forth ;it is called the recluse stage. The conqueror stage: this is the time when, having served a teacher, one knows; it is called the conqueror stage. The *bhikṣu*, the wise one, the conqueror, does not say anything. Thus, he calls the monk who gains nothing, the wise stage. Eight stages of humans. Forty-nine: "livelihood centuries," meaning forty-nine hundreds of ways of earning a living. "Wandering mendicant centuries," meaning hundreds of wandering mendicant renunciations. “Nāga dwelling centuries,” meaning hundreds of Nāga circles. "Twenty faculty centuries," meaning twenty hundreds of faculties. "Thirty hell centuries," meaning thirty hundreds of hells. “Realms of dust”: these are places where dust accumulates. He speaks referring to the backs of the hands, bottom of the feet, etc. “Seven spheres of percipient beings”: he says this referring to camels, oxen, donkeys, goats, cattle, deer, and buffaloes. “Spheres of non-percipient beings”: he says this referring to rice, barley, wheat, millet, beans, and *kudrūsaka*. "Nigantha wombs," meaning those born in a Nigantha, sugar cane, bamboo, reeds, etc., he says this referring to them. “Seven kinds of gods”: there are many kinds of gods, but he says there are seven. Human beings, too, are infinite, but he says there are seven. "Seven goblins": the goblins are numerous, he says there are seven. Forty-nine: livelihood centuries, wandering mendicant centuries, Nāga dwelling centuries, twenty faculty centuries, thirty hell centuries, realms of dust, seven spheres of percipient beings, spheres of non-percipient beings, Nigantha wombs, seven kinds of gods Seven goblins. "Lakes" are great lakes. He speaks having taken Kaṇṇamuṇḍa, chariot-maker, Anotatta, Sīhapapāta, Kuḷira, Mucalinda, Kuṇāladahe. "Pavuṭā" means a knot. "Papātā" means great Papātā. "Papātasatānī" means small Papātasatāni. "Dreams" means great dreams. "Supinasatānī" means small Supinasatāni. "Great aeons" means of great aeons. Here, he says a great aeon is when from one lake, once every hundred years, having taken a single drop of water with the tip of *kuśa* grass, and having removed it, when that lake is made without water seven times, that is one great aeon. When eighty-four hundred thousand of such great aeons have passed, the foolish and the wise make an end to suffering : this is his theory. Even a wise person perhaps cannot purify himself beforehand, nor does a fool go beyond that. Liquids, rains, falls, hundreds of falls, dreams, hundreds of dreams, of a great kalpa. "By moral discipline": by the moral discipline of the naked ascetics (ācelakasīlena) or by any other. "By wind": by such a wind. "By austerity": by ascetic practice (tapokammena). He "ripens the unripe," that is, he who considers himself wise purifies himself beforehand (antarā visujjhati). He "eliminates ripened *karma* whenever it comes up," or that the one who considers himself a fool continues on beyond the stated limits, that is, he goes beyond the time stated to be the limits. "That cannot be (hevaṃ natthi)": it cannot be thus (evaṃ natthi). Indeed, that shows that neither is able to do that (tañhi ubhayampi na sakkā kātunti dīpeti). "Measured by a *doṇa* (doṇamite)": as if measured by a *doṇa* (doṇena mitaṃ viya). "Pleasure and pain (sukhadukkhe)": pleasure and pain (sukhadukkhaṃ). "Limit made (pariyantakate)": limit made by the stated measure and time (vuttaparimāṇena kālena katapariyanto). "There is no decrease or increase (natthi hāyanavaḍḍhane)": there are no decrease or increase (natthi hāyanavaḍḍhanāni). The meaning (attho) is: *Saṃsāra* does not decrease for the wise person, nor does it increase for the fool (na saṃsāro paṇḍitassa hāyati, na bālassa vaḍḍhatīti attho). "Increase and decrease (ukkaṃsāvakaṃse)": increase and decrease (*ukkaṃsāvakaṃsā*); this itself is a synonym for decrease and increase (hāpanavaḍḍhanānaṃ eva etaṃ vevacanaṃ). Now, while establishing that meaning by simile. He says "Just as (seyyathāpi nāmā)," and so forth. There, "*Sutta* ball (suttaguḷe)": having wrapped [thread], a *sutta* ball is made (veṭhetvā katasuttaguḷaṃ). "Unwinding itself, it goes along (nibbeṭhiyamānameva paleti)": having stood on a mountain or at the tip of a tree, when thrown, it goes along unwinding itself by the measure of the thread (suttapamāṇena nibbeṭhiyamānaṃ gacchati); when the thread is exhausted (sutte khīṇe), it stands there (tattha tiṭṭhati), it does not go (na gacchati). Just so, he shows that one does not go beyond the time stated (evamevaṃ vuttakālato uddhaṃ na gacchatīti dasseti).

By moral discipline (sīlenā)

by wind (vatenā) by austerity (tapenā)

that cannot be (hevaṃ natthi) measured by a *doṇa* (doṇamite) pleasure and pain (sukhadukkhe) limit made (pariyantakate) there is no decrease or increase (natthi hāyanavaḍḍhane) increase and decrease (ukkaṃsāvakaṃse)

Just as (seyyathāpi nāmā) *sutta* ball (suttaguḷe) unwinding itself, it goes along (nibbeṭhiyamānameva paleti)

mula_pali: 229. ‘‘Idha, sandaka, ekacco satthā sabbaññū sabbadassāvī aparisesaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paṭijānāti – ‘carato ca me tiṭṭhato ca suttassa ca jāgarassa ca satataṃ samitaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paccupaṭṭhita’nti. So suññampi agāraṃ pavisati, piṇḍampi na labhati, kukkuropi ḍaṃsati, caṇḍenapi hatthinā samāgacchati, caṇḍenapi assena samāgacchati, caṇḍenapi goṇena samāgacchati, itthiyāpi purisassapi nāmampi gottampi pucchati, gāmassapi nigamassapi nāmampi maggampi pucchati. So ‘kimida’nti puṭṭho samāno ‘suññaṃ me agāraṃ pavisitabbaṃ ahosi’, tena pāvisiṃ; ‘piṇḍampi aladdhabbaṃ ahosi’, tena nālatthaṃ ; ‘kukkurena ḍaṃsitabbaṃ ahosi’, tenamhi tena (ka.), tenāsiṃ (?) daṭṭho; ‘caṇḍena hatthinā samāgantabbaṃ ahosi’, tena samāgamiṃ; ‘caṇḍena assena samāgantabbaṃ ahosi’, tena samāgamiṃ; ‘caṇḍena goṇena samāgantabbaṃ ahosi’, tena samāgamiṃ; ‘itthiyāpi purisassapi nāmampi gottampi pucchitabbaṃ ahosi’, tena pucchiṃ; ‘gāmassapi nigamassapi nāmampi maggampi pucchitabbaṃ ahosi’, tena pucchinti. Tatra, sandaka, viññū puriso iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘ayaṃ kho bhavaṃ satthā sabbaññū sabbadassāvī aparisesaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paṭijānāti…pe… ‘gāmassapi nigamassapi nāmampi maggampi pucchitabbaṃ ahosi, tena pucchi’nti . So ‘anassāsikaṃ idaṃ brahmacariya’nti – iti viditvā tasmā brahmacariyā nibbijja pakkamati. Idaṃ kho, sandaka, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena paṭhamaṃ anassāsikaṃ brahmacariyaṃ akkhātaṃ yattha viññū puriso sasakkaṃ brahmacariyaṃ na vaseyya, vasanto ca nārādheyya ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.
mula_english:
229. “Here, Sandaka, some teacher claims to be omniscient ( *sabbaññū*) and all-seeing ( *sabbadassāvī*), to have complete knowledge and vision ( *aparisesaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ*) thus: ‘Whether I am walking or standing or sleeping or awake, knowledge and vision are continuously and uninterruptedly present to me.’

He enters an empty house ( *suññampi agāraṃ pavisati*), he gets no almsfood ( *piṇḍampi na labhati*), a dog bites him, he meets with a wild elephant, a wild horse, a wild bull, he asks the name and clan of a woman or a man, he asks the name of a village or a town, and the way to go there.

When he is questioned: ‘How is this?’ he replies: ‘I had to enter an empty house, that is why I entered it. I had to get no almsfood, that is why I did not get any. I had to be bitten by a dog, that is why I was bitten. I had to meet with a wild elephant, a wild horse, a wild bull, that is why I met with them. I had to ask the name and clan of a woman or a man, that is why I asked. I had to ask the name of a village or a town and the way to go there, that is why I asked.’

About this a wise man considers thus: ‘This good teacher claims to be omniscient and all-seeing, to have complete knowledge and vision…When he is questioned: “How is this?" he replies: “I had to…that is why I asked.”’

So when he finds that this holy life ( *brahmacariya* ) is without consolation ( *anassāsikaṃ*), he turns away from it and leaves it.

This is the first kind of holy life without consolation that has been declared by the Blessed One ( *bhagavatā* ) who knows and sees, accomplished (*arahatā*) and fully enlightened ( *sammāsambuddhena*), wherein a wise man certainly would not live the holy life, or if he should live it, would not attain the true way, the *Dhamma* that is wholesome (*kusalaṃ*).
commentary_pali: 229.Kimidanti kimidaṃ tava aññāṇaṃ, kiṃ sabbaññu nāma tvanti evaṃ puṭṭho samāno niyativāde pakkhipanto suññaṃ me agārantiādimāha.
commentary_english: 229. kimidanti, "What is this?" What is this ignorance of yours? And when asked, "Are you called 'all-knowing'?", while adhering to the doctrine of determinism, he spoke the following, beginning with, "suññaṃ me agāranti," "My house is empty."

mula_pali: 230. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sandaka, idhekacco satthā anussaviko hoti anussavasacco. So anussavena itihitihaparamparāya piṭakasampadāya dhammaṃ deseti. Anussavikassa kho pana, sandaka , satthuno anussavasaccassa sussutampi hoti dussutampi hoti tathāpi hoti aññathāpi hoti. Tatra, sandaka, viññū puriso iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘ayaṃ kho bhavaṃ satthā anussaviko anussavasacco so anussavena itihitihaparamparāya piṭakasampadāya dhammaṃ deseti. Anussavikassa kho pana satthuno anussavasaccassa sussutampi hoti dussutampi hoti tathāpi hoti aññathāpi hoti’. So ‘anassāsikaṃ idaṃ brahmacariya’nti – iti viditvā tasmā brahmacariyā nibbijja pakkamati. Idaṃ kho, sandaka, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dutiyaṃ anassāsikaṃ brahmacariyaṃ akkhātaṃ yattha viññū puriso sasakkaṃ brahmacariyaṃ na vaseyya, vasanto ca nārādheyya ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.
mula_english: “Again, Sandaka, here some teacher is a traditionalist (*anuśravika*), one who regards oral tradition as truth (*anuśravasatya*). He teaches the Dharma by oral tradition (*anuśrava*), by legends handed down (*itihitihaparamparā*), by what has come down in scriptures (*piṭakasampadā*). But when a teacher is a traditionalist, one who regards oral tradition as truth, some is well remembered (*sussuta*) and some is wrongly remembered (*dussuta*), some is true (*tathā*) and some is otherwise (*aññathā*). About this a wise man (*viññū puriso*) considers thus: ‘This good teacher is a traditionalist, one who regards oral tradition as truth. He teaches the Dharma by oral tradition, by legends handed down, by what has come down in scriptures. But when a teacher is a traditionalist, one who regards oral tradition as truth, some is well remembered and some is wrongly remembered, some is true and some is otherwise.’ So when he finds that this holy life (*brahmacariya*) is without consolation (*anassāsikaṃ*), he turns away from it (*nibbijja pakkamati*) and leaves it. This is the second kind of holy life without consolation that has been declared by the Blessed One (*bhagavatā*) who knows (*jānatā*) and sees (*passatā*), accomplished one (*arahatā*) and fully enlightened one (*sammāsambuddhena*), wherein a wise man certainly would not live the holy life, or if he should live it, would not attain the true way (*ñāyaṃ*), the Dharma (*dhammaṃ*) that is wholesome (*kusalaṃ*)."
commentary_pali: 230.Anussaviko hotīti anussavanissito hoti. Anussavasaccoti savanaṃ saccato gahetvā ṭhito. Piṭakasampadāyāti vaggapaṇṇāsakāya piṭakaganthasampattiyā.
commentary_english:
"anussaviko hoti" means he relies on hearsay.
"anussavasacco" means he takes hearsay as truth and stands by it.
"piṭakasampadāya" means with the accomplishment of the collection of texts in sections and fifty sections.

mula_pali: 231. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sandaka, idhekacco satthā takkī hoti vīmaṃsī. So takkapariyāhataṃ vīmaṃsānucaritaṃ sayaṃpaṭibhānaṃ dhammaṃ deseti. Takkissa kho pana, sandaka, satthuno vīmaṃsissa sutakkitampi hoti duttakkitampi hoti tathāpi hoti aññathāpi hoti. Tatra, sandaka, viññū puriso iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘ayaṃ kho bhavaṃ satthā takkī vīmaṃsī. So takkapariyāhataṃ vīmaṃsānucaritaṃ sayaṃpaṭibhānaṃ dhammaṃ deseti. Takkissa kho pana satthuno vīmaṃsissa sutakkitampi hoti duttakkitampi hoti tathāpi hoti aññathāpi hoti’. So ‘anassāsikaṃ idaṃ brahmacariya’nti – iti viditvā tasmā brahmacariyā nibbijja pakkamati. Idaṃ kho, sandaka, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena tatiyaṃ anassāsikaṃ brahmacariyaṃ akkhātaṃ yattha viññū puriso sasakkaṃ brahmacariyaṃ na vaseyya, vasanto ca nārādheyya ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.
mula_english: “Again, Sandaka, here a certain teacher is a reasoner, an inquirer. He teaches a *dhamma* hammered out by reasoning, following a line of inquiry as it occurs to him. But when a teacher is a reasoner, an inquirer, some is well reasoned and some is wrongly reasoned, some is true and some is otherwise. About this a wise man considers thus: ‘This good teacher is a reasoner, an inquirer. He teaches a *dhamma* hammered out by reasoning, following a line of inquiry as it occurs to him. But when a teacher is a reasoner, an inquirer, some is well reasoned and some is wrongly reasoned, some is true and some is otherwise.’ So when he finds that this holy life is without consolation (*anassāsikaṃ brahmacariya*), he turns away from it and leaves it. This is the third kind of holy life without consolation (*anassāsikaṃ brahmacariya*) that has been declared by the Blessed One who knows and sees, accomplished and fully enlightened, wherein a wise man certainly would not live the holy life, or if he should live it, would not attain the true way, the *dhamma* that is wholesome (*kusalaṃ*)."

mula_pali:
232. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sandaka, idhekacco satthā mando hoti momūho. So mandattā momūhattā tattha tattha tathā tathā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) pañhaṃ puṭṭho samāno vācāvikkhepaṃ āpajjati amarāvikkhepaṃ – ‘evantipi evampi (sī. pī.) me no, tathātipi tathāpi (sī. pī.) me no, aññathātipi aññathāpi (sī. pī.) ( ) sabbattha natthi me no, notipi me no, no notipi me no’ti. Tatra, sandaka, viññū puriso iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘ayaṃ kho bhavaṃ satthā mando momūho. So mandattā momūhattā tattha tattha pañhaṃ puṭṭho samāno vācāvikkhepaṃ āpajjati amarāvikkhepaṃ – evantipi me no, tathātipi me no, aññathātipi me no, notipi me no, no notipi me no’ti. So ‘anassāsikaṃ idaṃ brahmacariya’nti – iti viditvā tasmā brahmacariyā nibbijja pakkamati. Idaṃ kho, sandaka, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena catutthaṃ anassāsikaṃ brahmacariyaṃ akkhātaṃ yattha viññū puriso sasakkaṃ brahmacariyaṃ na vaseyya, vasanto ca nārādheyya ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

‘‘Imāni kho, (tāni sandaka, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena cattāri anassāsikāni brahmacariyāni akkhātāni yattha viññū puriso sasakkaṃ brahmacariyaṃ na vaseyya, vasanto ca nārādheyya ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusala’’nti.

‘‘Acchariyaṃ, bho ānanda, abbhutaṃ, bho ānanda! Yāvañcidaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena cattāri anassāsikāneva brahmacariyāni anassāsikāni brahmacariyānīti akkhātāni yattha viññū puriso sasakkaṃ brahmacariyaṃ na vaseyya, vasanto ca nārādheyya ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ. So pana, bho ānanda, satthā kiṃ vādī kiṃ akkhāyī yattha viññū puriso sasakkaṃ brahmacariyaṃ vaseyya, vasanto ca ārādheyya ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusala’’nti.
mula_english:
232. Again, Sandaka, here a certain teacher is dull and confused. Being dull and confused, when asked a question about this or that, he engages in verbal wriggling, in eel-wriggling: ‘I don’t say it is this way, nor do I say it is that way, nor do I say it is otherwise, I do not say it is not so, nor do I say it is not not so.’ About this, Sandaka, a wise man considers thus: ‘This good teacher is dull and confused. Being dull and confused, when asked a question about this or that, he engages in verbal wriggling, in eel-wriggling: I don’t say it is this way, nor do I say it is that way, nor do I say it is otherwise, I do not say it is not so, nor do I say it is not not so.’ So when he finds that ‘this holy life is without consolation (anassāsikaṃ brahmacariyaṃ),’ he turns away from it and leaves it. This, Sandaka, is the fourth kind of holy life without consolation that has been declared by the Blessed One who knows and sees, the worthy one, the fully enlightened one, wherein a wise man certainly would not live the holy life, or if he should live it, would not attain the true way, the Dhamma that is wholesome.

“These, Sandaka, are the four kinds of holy life without consolation that have been declared by the Blessed One who knows and sees, the worthy one, the fully enlightened one, wherein a wise man certainly would not live the holy life, or if he should live it, would not attain the true way, the Dhamma that is wholesome.”

“Wonderful, Master Ānanda, amazing, Master Ānanda! How well these four kinds of holy life without consolation have been declared by the Blessed One who knows and sees, the worthy one, the fully enlightened one, wherein a wise man certainly would not live the holy life, or if he should live it, would not attain the true way, the Dhamma that is wholesome. But, Master Ānanda, what does that teacher assert, what does he declare, wherein a wise man certainly would live the holy life, and while living it would attain the true way, the Dhamma that is wholesome?”
commentary_pali:
232.Mandoti mandapañño. Momūhoti atimūḷho. Vācāvikkhepaṃ āpajjatīti vācāya vikkhepaṃ āpajjati. Kīdisaṃ? Amarāvikkhepaṃ, apariyantavikkhepanti attho. Atha vā amarā nāma macchajāti. Sā ummujjananimmujjanādivasena udake sandhāvamānā gahetuṃ na sakkāti evameva ayampi vādo ito cito ca sandhāvati, gāhaṃ na upagacchatīti amarāvikkhepoti vuccati. Taṃ amarāvikkhepaṃ.

Evantipi me notiādīsu idaṃ kusalanti puṭṭho ‘‘evantipi me no’’ti vadati, tato kiṃ akusalanti vutte ‘‘tathātipi me no’’ti vadati, kiṃ ubhayato aññathāti vutte ‘‘aññathātipi me no’’ti vadati, tato tividhenāpi na hotīti te laddhīti vutte ‘‘notipi me no’’ti vadati, tato kiṃ no noti te laddhīti vutte ‘‘no notipi me no’’ti vikkhepamāpajjati, ekasmimpi pakkhe na tiṭṭhati. Nibbijja pakkamatīti attanopi esa satthā avassayo bhavituṃ na sakkoti, mayhaṃ kiṃ sakkhissatīti nibbinditvā pakkamati. Purimesupi anassāsikesu eseva nayo.

Evantipi me no Nibbijja pakkamatī
commentary_english:
232. *Mando* means of dull wisdom.
*Momūho* means extremely deluded.
*Vācāvikkhepaṃ āpajjatī* means he engages in equivocation in speech.
What kind? Endless equivocation, [which] means endless equivocation.
Or, *amarā* is the name of a kind of fish.
Because they roam about in the water diving in and out, it is impossible to catch hold of them. Analogously, this doctrine roams about here and there and is impossible to catch hold of: therefore it is called endless equivocation.
That is endless equivocation.

In "*evantipi me no* etc.," when asked, "Is this wholesome?", he says, "I do not take it that way." Then, when asked, "What, is it then unwholesome?", he says: “I do not take it that way.” When asked, "What, is it something other than both?", he says, "I do not take it that way.” Asked: “If it is neither of these three, what is your opinion?", he says: “Nor do I say that it is not.” Asked: “In your opinion is it neither this nor that?”, he engages in equivocation, and does not take a stand on any single side.
*Nibbijja pakkamatī*: Even for himself this teacher is not able to be a refuge; thinking, “What will he be able to do for me?”, he departs in disgust.
This same method applies in the preceding cases of those who are without consolation.

*Evantipi me no*, *nibbijja pakkamatī*

mula_pali:
233. ‘‘Idha, sandaka, tathāgato loke uppajjati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā…pe… vitthāro ma. ni. 2.9-10 kandarakasutte so ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Yasmiṃ kho yasmiṃ kho pana (syā. kaṃ. ka.), sandaka, satthari sāvako evarūpaṃ uḷāravisesaṃ adhigacchati tattha viññū puriso sasakkaṃ brahmacariyaṃ vaseyya, vasanto ca ārādheyya ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sandaka, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe... dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Yasmiṃ kho, sandaka, satthari sāvako evarūpaṃ uḷāravisesaṃ adhigacchati tattha viññū puriso sasakkaṃ brahmacariyaṃ vaseyya, vasanto ca ārādheyya ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sandaka, bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Yasmiṃ kho, sandaka, satthari sāvako evarūpaṃ uḷāravisesaṃ adhigacchati tattha viññū puriso sasakkaṃ brahmacariyaṃ vaseyya, vasanto ca ārādheyya ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, sandaka, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Yasmiṃ kho, sandaka, satthari sāvako evarūpaṃ uḷāravisesaṃ adhigacchati tattha viññū puriso sasakkaṃ brahmacariyaṃ vaseyya, vasanto ca ārādheyya ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

‘‘So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti. So anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. Yasmiṃ kho, sandaka, satthari sāvako evarūpaṃ uḷāravisesaṃ adhigacchati tattha viññū puriso sasakkaṃ brahmacariyaṃ vaseyya, vasanto ca ārādheyya ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

‘‘So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte sattānaṃ cutūpapātañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti. So dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate…pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti. Yasmiṃ kho, sandaka, satthari sāvako evarūpaṃ uḷāravisesaṃ adhigacchati tattha viññū puriso sasakkaṃ brahmacariyaṃ vaseyya, vasanto ca ārādheyya ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

‘‘So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti. So ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti; ‘ime āsavā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ āsavasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ āsavanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, bhavāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, avijjāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti. Yasmiṃ kho, sandaka, satthari sāvako evarūpaṃ uḷāravisesaṃ adhigacchati tattha viññū puriso sasakkaṃ brahmacariyaṃ vaseyya, vasanto ca ārādheyya ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusala’’nti.
mula_english:
233. “Here, Sandaka, a *Tathāgata* arises in the world, an *Arhant*, a fully enlightened *Buddha*, endowed with wisdom and conduct (*vijjācaraṇasampanno*), a Well-Farer (*sugato*), a Knower of the worlds (*lokavidū*), an incomparable Trainer of men to be tamed (*anuttaro purisadammasārathi*), a Teacher of gods and humans (*satthā devamanussānaṃ*), enlightened and blessed…pe… So, having abandoned these five hindrances (*pañca nīvaraṇe*), the defilements of the mind that weaken wisdom, quite secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, he enters and remains in the first *jhāna*: rapture and pleasure born of seclusion, accompanied by directed thought and evaluation (*savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati*). A wise man certainly would live the holy life with a teacher under whom a disciple attains such a lofty distinction, and while living it he would attain the true way, the *Dhamma* that is wholesome.

“Again, Sandaka, with the stilling of directed thoughts and evaluations…pe…he enters and remains in the second *jhāna* (*dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati*). A wise man certainly would live the holy life with a teacher under whom a disciple attains such a lofty distinction, and while living it he would attain the true way, the *Dhamma* that is wholesome.

“Again, Sandaka, with the fading away as well of rapture, he remains equanimous…pe…he enters and remains in the third *jhāna* (*tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati*). A wise man certainly would live the holy life with a teacher under whom a disciple attains such a lofty distinction, and while living it he would attain the true way, the *Dhamma* that is wholesome.

“Again, Sandaka, with the abandoning of pleasure…pe…he enters and remains in the fourth *jhāna* (*catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati*). A wise man certainly would live the holy life with a teacher under whom a disciple attains such a lofty distinction, and while living it he would attain the true way, the *Dhamma* that is wholesome.

“When his mind is thus concentrated, purified, and bright, unblemished, rid of imperfection, malleable, wieldy, steady, and attained to imperturbability, he directs it to knowledge of the recollection of past lives (*pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti*). He recollects his manifold past lives, that is, one birth, two births…pe… Thus with their aspects and particulars he recollects his manifold past lives (*anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati*). A wise man certainly would live the holy life with a teacher under whom a disciple attains such a lofty distinction, and while living it he would attain the true way, the *Dhamma* that is wholesome.

“When his mind is thus concentrated, purified, and bright, unblemished, rid of imperfection, malleable, wieldy, steady, and attained to imperturbability, he directs it to knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings (*sattānaṃ cutūpapātañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti*). He sees—by means of the divine eye (*dibbena cakkhunā*), purified and surpassing the human—beings passing away and re-appearing, and he discerns how they are inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate in accordance with their actions (*yathākammūpage satte pajānāti*). A wise man certainly would live the holy life with a teacher under whom a disciple attains such a lofty distinction, and while living it he would attain the true way, the *Dhamma* that is wholesome.

“When his mind is thus concentrated, purified, and bright, unblemished, rid of imperfection, malleable, wieldy, steady, and attained to imperturbability, the monk directs and inclines it to the knowledge of the ending of the effluents (*āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti*). He understands as it really is: ‘This is suffering (*idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti*)’… ‘This is the origin of suffering (*ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti*)’… ‘This is the cessation of suffering (*ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti*)’… ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering (*ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti*)’… ‘These are the taints (*ime āsavā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti*)’… ‘This is the origin of the taints (*ayaṃ āsavasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti*)’… ‘This is the cessation of the taints (*ayaṃ āsavanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti*)’… ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of the taints (*ayaṃ āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti*)’. When he knows and sees thus, his mind is liberated from the taint of sensual desire (*kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati*), from the taint of being (*bhavāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati*), and from taint of ignorance (*avijjāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati*). When it is liberated, there comes the knowledge: ‘It’s liberated (*vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti*)’. He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth (*khīṇā jāti*), the holy life has been lived (*vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ*), what had to be done has been done (*kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ*), there is no more coming back to any state of being (*nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti*)’.
Indeed, Sandaka, a wise person would certainly live the holy life under a teacher in whom a disciple attains such an eminent distinction ( *uḷāra-viśeṣam*), and while living it, he would cultivate the true path (*ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ*), that is wholesome (*kusalaṃ*).

mula_pali: 234. ‘‘Yo pana so, bho ānanda, bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto paribhuñjeyya so kāme’’ti? ‘‘Yo so, sandaka, bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto abhabbo so pañcaṭṭhānāni ajjhācarituṃ. Abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropetuṃ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādātuṃ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevetuṃ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sampajānamusā bhāsituṃ, abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sannidhikārakaṃ kāme paribhuñjituṃ, seyyathāpi pubbe agāriyabhūto. Yo so, sandaka, bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto abhabbo so imāni pañcaṭṭhānāni ajjhācaritu’’nti.
mula_english:
“But, Master Ānanda, when a *bhikkhu* is an *arahaṃ* whose āsavas are destroyed (*khīṇāsavo*), who has lived the holy life (*vusitavā*), done what had to be done (*katakaraṇīyo*), laid down the burden (*ohitabhāro*), reached the true goal (*anuppattasadattho*), destroyed the fetters of being (*parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano*), and is completely liberated through final knowledge (*sammadaññā vimutto*), could he enjoy sensual pleasures (*kāme*)?”

“Sandaka, when a *bhikkhu* is an *arahaṃ* whose āsavas are destroyed (*khīṇāsavo*), who has lived the holy life (*vusitavā*), done what had to be done (*katakaraṇīyo*), laid down the burden (*ohitabhāro*), reached the true goal (*anuppattasadattho*), destroyed the fetters of being (*parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano*), and is completely liberated through final knowledge (*sammadaññā vimutto*), he is incapable of transgression in five cases (*pañcaṭṭhānāni ajjhācarituṃ*).

A *bhikkhu* whose āsavas are destroyed (*khīṇāsavo*) is incapable of deliberately depriving a living being of life (*pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropetuṃ*); he is incapable of taking what is not given, that is, of stealing (*adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādātuṃ*); he is incapable of indulging in sexual intercourse (*methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevetuṃ*); he is incapable of knowingly speaking falsehood (*sampajānamusā bhāsituṃ*); he is incapable of enjoying sensual pleasures by storing them up as he did formerly in lay life (*sannidhikārakaṃ kāme paribhuñjituṃ, seyyathāpi pubbe agāriyabhūto*).

Sandaka, when a *bhikkhu* is an *arahaṃ* whose āsavas are destroyed (*khīṇāsavo*), who has lived the holy life (*vusitavā*), done what had to be done (*katakaraṇīyo*), laid down the burden (*ohitabhāro*), reached the true goal (*anuppattasadattho*), destroyed the fetters of being (*parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano*), and is completely liberated through final knowledge (*sammadaññā vimutto*), he is incapable of transgression in these five cases (*imāni pañcaṭṭhānāni ajjhācarituṃ*).”
commentary_pali: 234.Sannidhikārakaṃ kāme paribhuñjitunti yathā pubbe gihibhūto sannidhiṃ katvā vatthukāme paribhuñjati, evaṃ tilataṇḍulasappinavanītādīni sannidhiṃ katvā idāni paribhuñjituṃ abhabboti attho. Nanu ca khīṇāsavassa vasanaṭṭhāne tilataṇḍulādayo paññāyantīti. No na paññāyanti, na panesa te attano atthāya ṭhapeti, aphāsukapabbajitādīnaṃ atthāya ṭhapeti. Anāgāmissa kathanti. Tassāpi pañca kāmaguṇā sabbasova pahīnā, dhammena pana laddhaṃ vicāretvā paribhuñjati.
commentary_english:
"sannidhikārakaṃ kāme paribhuñjitu" means just as formerly, when one was a householder (gihibhūto), one made a store (sannidhiṃ katvā) and enjoyed (paribhuñjati) objects of desire (vatthukāme), in the same way, now it is not possible to enjoy storing up things like sesame seeds (tila), rice grains (taṇḍula), clarified butter (sappi), fresh butter (navanīta), and so on (ādīni). This is the meaning (attho).

Indeed (nanu ca), aren't sesame seeds (tila), rice grains (taṇḍula), and so on (ādayo) apparent (paññāyanti) in the dwelling place (vasanaṭṭhāne) of one whose āsavas are destroyed (khīṇāsavassa)?

No (no), they are not apparent (na paññāyanti). However (pana), he (esa) does not (na) store (ṭhapeti) them for his own (attano) sake (atthāya), but (ṭhapeti) for the sake (atthāya) of ascetics (pabbajita) and others (ādīnaṃ) who are uncomfortable (aphāsuka).

What about (kathanti) a non-returner (anāgāmissa)?

Even (api) for him (tassa), the five (pañca) sensual qualities (kāmaguṇā) are completely (sabbaso) abandoned (pahīnā); however (pana), having considered (vicāretvā) what is obtained (laddhaṃ) through the Dhamma (dhammena), he enjoys it (paribhuñjati).

mula_pali: 235. ‘‘Yo pana so, bho ānanda, bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto tassa carato ceva tiṭṭhato ca suttassa ca jāgarassa ca satataṃ samitaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ – ‘khīṇā me āsavā’’’ti? ‘‘Tena hi, sandaka, upamaṃ te karissāmi; upamāyapidhekacce viññū purisā bhāsitassa atthaṃ ājānanti. Seyyathāpi, sandaka, purisassa hatthapādā chinnā; tassa carato ceva tiṭṭhato ca suttassa ca jāgarassa ca satataṃ samitaṃ (jānāti – ‘chinnā me hatthapādā’ti, udāhu paccavekkhamāno jānāti – ‘chinnā me hatthapādā’’’ti? ‘‘Na kho, bho ānanda, so puriso satataṃ samitaṃ jānāti – ‘chinnā me hatthapādā’ ti.) (chinnāva hatthapādā,) (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) Api ca kho pana naṃ paccavekkhamāno jānāti – ‘chinnā me hatthapādā’’’ti. ‘‘Evameva kho, sandaka, yo so bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto tassa carato ceva tiṭṭhato ca suttassa ca jāgarassa ca satataṃ samitaṃ (ñāṇadassanaṃ na paccupaṭṭhitaṃ – ‘khīṇā me āsavā’ti;) (khīṇāva āsavā,) (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) api ca kho pana naṃ paccavekkhamāno jānāti – ‘khīṇā me āsavā’’’ti.
mula_english:
235. “But, Master Ānanda, when a *bhikkhu* is an *arahaṃ* with taints destroyed, one who has lived the holy life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own welfare, completely destroyed the fetter of becoming, is liberated by perfect knowledge, is his knowledge and vision that his taints are destroyed (*khīṇā me āsavā*) continuously and uninterruptedly present to him whether he is walking or standing or sleeping or awake?”

“Then, Sandaka, I will make a comparison for you; for through a comparison, some intelligent men understand the meaning of what is spoken. Suppose, Sandaka, a man’s hands and feet were cut off. Would he know ‘My hands and feet are cut off’ continuously and uninterruptedly, whether he is walking or standing or sleeping or awake, or would he know ‘My hands and feet are cut off’ only when he reviews this fact?”

“No, Master Ānanda, that man would not know ‘My hands and feet are cut off’ continuously and uninterruptedly. But when he reviews this fact, he knows ‘My hands and feet are cut off.’”

“In the same way, Sandaka, when a *bhikkhu* is an *arahaṃ* with taints destroyed, one who has lived the holy life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own welfare, completely destroyed the fetter of becoming, is liberated by perfect knowledge, is his knowledge and vision not continuously and uninterruptedly present to him whether he is walking or standing or sleeping or awake that ‘My taints are destroyed (*khīṇā me āsavā*)’? But when he reviews this fact, he knows ‘My taints are destroyed (*khīṇā me āsavā*).’”

mula_pali:
236. ‘‘Kīvabahukā pana, bho ānanda, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye niyyātāro’’ti? ‘‘Na kho, sandaka, ekaṃyeva sataṃ na dve satāni na tīṇi satāni na cattāri satāni na pañca satāni, atha kho bhiyyova ye imasmiṃ dhammavinaye niyyātāro’’ti. ‘‘Acchariyaṃ, bho ānanda, abbhutaṃ, bho ānanda! Na ca nāma sadhammokkaṃsanā bhavissati, na paradhammavambhanā, āyatane ca dhammadesanā tāva bahukā ca niyyātāro paññāyissanti. Ime panājīvakā puttamatāya puttā attānañceva ukkaṃsenti, pare ca vambhenti tayo ceva niyyātāro paññapenti, seyyathidaṃ – nandaṃ vacchaṃ, kisaṃ saṃkiccaṃ, makkhaliṃ gosāla’’nti. Atha kho sandako paribbājako sakaṃ parisaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘carantu bhonto samaṇe gotame brahmacariyavāso. Na dāni sukaraṃ amhehi lābhasakkārasiloke pariccajitu’’nti. Iti hidaṃ sandako paribbājako sakaṃ parisaṃ uyyojesi bhagavati brahmacariyeti.

Sandakasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.
mula_english:
“How many are emancipated in this Dhamma and Discipline?”

“There are not only one hundred, Sandaka, or two hundred, three hundred, four hundred or five hundred, but far more emancipated ones than that in this Dhamma and Discipline.”

“It’s amazing, Ānanda! It’s astonishing, Ānanda! There will not be just praise of the true Dharma, nor disparagement of other doctrines. And in the locations where the Dharma is taught, many emancipated ones will be known.

But these Ājīvakas, those mothers’ dead sons, laud themselves and disparage others, and they recognize only three emancipated ones, namely, Nanda Vaccha, Kisa Sankicca, and Makkhali Gosala.”

Then the wanderer Sandaka addressed his own assembly: “Go, sirs. The holy life (*brahmacariyavāso*) is to be lived under the recluse Gotama.

It is not easy for us now to give up gain, honour (*sakkāra*), and renown.”

That is how the wanderer Sandaka exhorted his own assembly to live the holy life (*brahmacariya*) under the Blessed One (*bhagavati*).

The Sandaka Sutta, the sixth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
236.Puttamatāya puttāti so kira imaṃ dhammaṃ sutvā ājīvakā matā nāmāti saññī hutvā evamāha. Ayañhettha attho – ājīvakā matā nāma, tesaṃ mātā puttamatā hoti, iti ājīvakā puttamatāya puttā nāma honti. Samaṇe gotameti samaṇe gotame brahmacariyavāso atthi, aññattha natthīti dīpeti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Sandakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
236. "Because of the mother of sons ( *puttamatāya puttā* )": Having heard this doctrine, the Ājīvakas, considering themselves "dead mothers," spoke thus.

The meaning here is this: The Ājīvakas are "dead mothers," and their mothers are "mothers of sons." Thus, the Ājīvakas are called "sons because of the mother of sons."

"In the ascetic Gotama ( *samaṇe gotame* )": It indicates that the holy life ( *brahmacariyavāso* ) exists in the ascetic Gotama, but not elsewhere.

The rest is clear throughout.

The commentary on the Sandaka Sutta in the *Papañcasūdanī*, commentary on the *Majjhimanikāya*, is finished.

mula_pali: 237. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā abhiññātā abhiññātā paribbājakā moranivāpe paribbājakārāme paṭivasanti, seyyathidaṃ – annabhāro varadharo sakuludāyī ca paribbājako aññe ca abhiññātā abhiññātā paribbājakā. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – ‘‘atippago kho tāva rājagahe piṇḍāya carituṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ yena moranivāpo paribbājakārāmo yena sakuludāyī paribbājako tenupasaṅkameyya’’nti. Atha kho bhagavā yena moranivāpo paribbājakārāmo tenupasaṅkami. Tena kho pana samayena sakuludāyī paribbājako mahatiyā paribbājakaparisāya saddhiṃ nisinno hoti unnādiniyā uccāsaddamahāsaddāya anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ kathentiyā, seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ corakathaṃ mahāmattakathaṃ senākathaṃ bhayakathaṃ yuddhakathaṃ annakathaṃ pānakathaṃ vatthakathaṃ sayanakathaṃ mālākathaṃ gandhakathaṃ ñātikathaṃ yānakathaṃ gāmakathaṃ nigamakathaṃ nagarakathaṃ janapadakathaṃ itthikathaṃ sūrakathaṃ visikhākathaṃ kumbhaṭṭhānakathaṃ pubbapetakathaṃ nānattakathaṃ lokakkhāyikaṃ samuddakkhāyikaṃ itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vā. Addasā kho sakuludāyī paribbājako bhagavantaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna sakaṃ parisaṃ saṇṭhāpeti – ‘‘appasaddā bhonto hontu; mā bhonto saddamakattha. Ayaṃ samaṇo gotamo āgacchati; appasaddakāmo kho pana so āyasmā appasaddassa vaṇṇavādī. Appeva nāma appasaddaṃ parisaṃ viditvā upasaṅkamitabbaṃ maññeyyā’’ti. Atha kho te paribbājakā tuṇhī ahesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā yena sakuludāyī paribbājako tenupasaṅkami. Atha kho sakuludāyī paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘etu kho, bhante, bhagavā. Svāgataṃ, bhante, bhagavato. Cirassaṃ kho, bhante, bhagavā imaṃ pariyāyamakāsi yadidaṃ idhāgamanāya. Nisīdatu, bhante, bhagavā; idamāsanaṃ paññatta’’nti. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Sakuludāyīpi kho paribbājako aññataraṃ nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho sakuludāyiṃ paribbājakaṃ bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
237. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One (bhagavā) was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove (veḷuvana), the Squirrels’ Sanctuary (kalandakanivāpa).

Now at that time, a number of well-known wanderers (paribbājakā) were staying at the Peacocks’ Sanctuary (moranivāpa), the wanderers’ park (paribbājakārāma), that is to say, Annabhāra, Varadhara, and the wanderer Sakuludāyin, as well as other well-known wanderers (paribbājakā).

Then the Blessed One (bhagavā), having dressed in the morning, taking his bowl (patta) and robe (cīvara), entered Rājagaha for alms (piṇḍa).

Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One (bhagavato): “It is still too early to walk for alms (piṇḍa) in Rājagaha.

Suppose I were to visit the wanderers' park (paribbājakārāma) at the Peacocks’ Sanctuary (moranivāpa), where the wanderer Sakuludāyin is?”

Then the Blessed One (bhagavā) went to the wanderers' park (paribbājakārāma) at the Peacocks’ Sanctuary (moranivāpa).

Now at that time the wanderer Sakuludāyin was seated with a large assembly of wanderers, who were making an uproar, loudly and noisily talking many kinds of pointless talk, such as talk of kings, talk of robbers, talk of ministers, talk of armies, talk of dangers, talk of battles, talk of food, talk of drink, talk of clothing, talk of beds, talk of garlands, talk of perfumes, talk of relatives, talk of vehicles, talk of villages, talk of towns, talk of cities, talk of countries, talk of women, talk of heroes, talk of streets, talk of wells, talk of past ancestors, talk of various things, tales of the world, tales of the sea, talk of what is and what is not.

The wanderer Sakuludāyin saw the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ) coming in the distance.

Seeing him, he quieted his own assembly thus: “Sirs, be quiet; sirs, make no noise.

Here comes the recluse Gotama; that venerable one likes quiet and commends quiet.

Perhaps if he perceives our group as quiet, he will consider it worth his while to come our way.”

Then those wanderers became silent.

Then the Blessed One (bhagavā) went to the wanderer Sakuludāyin.

Then the wanderer Sakuludāyin said this to the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ): “Come, venerable sir, Blessed One (bhagavā).

Welcome, venerable sir, to the Blessed One (bhagavato).

It is long since the Blessed One (bhagavā), venerable sir, found an opportunity to come here.

Be seated, venerable sir, Blessed One (bhagavā); this seat is prepared.”

The Blessed One (bhagavā) sat down on the prepared seat (āsane).

And the wanderer Sakuludāyin also took a low seat and sat down at one side.

When the wanderer Sakuludāyin was seated to one side, the Blessed One (bhagavā) said this to him:
commentary_pali: 237.Evaṃme sutanti mahāsakuludāyisuttaṃ. Tattha moranivāpeti tasmiṃ ṭhāne morānaṃ abhayaṃ ghosetvā bhojanaṃ adaṃsu. Tasmā taṃ ṭhānaṃ moranivāpoti saṅkhaṃ gataṃ. Annabhāroti ekassa paribbājakassa nāmaṃ. Tathā varadharoti. Aññe cāti na kevalaṃ ime tayo, aññepi abhiññātā bahū paribbājakā. Appasaddassa vaṇṇavādīti idha appasaddavinītoti avatvāva idaṃ vuttaṃ. Kasmā? Na hi bhagavā aññena vinītoti.
commentary_english:
237. Thus (evaṃ), “*me suta*” is the Mahāsakuludāyisuttaṃ.

There, "*moranivāpe*": in that place (tasmiṃ ṭhāne), they proclaimed (ghosetvā) safety (abhayaṃ) to the peacocks (morānaṃ) and gave (adaṃsu) food (bhojanaṃ).

Therefore (tasmā), that place (taṃ ṭhānaṃ) went (gataṃ) to the designation (saṅkhaṃ) "*moranivāpo*."

"*annabhāro*" is the name (nāmaṃ) of one (ekassa) wandering ascetic (paribbājakassa).

Likewise (tathā), "*varadharo*."

"*aññe cā*": not (na) only (kevalaṃ) these (ime) three (tayo), [but] other (aññepi) well-known (abhiññātā) wandering ascetics (paribbājakā) [were] many (bahū).

"*appasaddassa vaṇṇavādī*": here (idha), this (idaṃ) was said (vuttaṃ) without saying (avatvāva) "controlled by few sounds (appasaddavinītoti)."

Why (kasmā)? The Blessed One (bhagavā) was not (na hi) controlled (vinīto) by another (aññena).

mula_pali: 238. ‘‘Kāyanuttha , udāyi, etarahi kathāya sannisinnā, kā ca pana vo antarākathā vippakatā’’ti? ‘‘Tiṭṭhatesā, bhante, kathā yāya mayaṃ etarahi kathāya sannisinnā. Nesā, bhante, kathā bhagavato dullabhā bhavissati pacchāpi savanāya. Purimāni, bhante, divasāni purimatarāni nānātitthiyānaṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ kutūhalasālāyaṃ sannisinnānaṃ sannipatitānaṃ ayamantarākathā udapādi – ‘lābhā vata, bho, aṅgamagadhānaṃ, suladdhalābhā vata, bho, aṅgamagadhānaṃ! Tatrime yatthime (sī.) samaṇabrāhmaṇā saṅghino gaṇino gaṇācariyā ñātā yasassino titthakarā sādhusammatā bahujanassa rājagahaṃ vassāvāsaṃ osaṭā. Ayampi kho pūraṇo kassapo saṅghī ceva gaṇī ca gaṇācariyo ca ñāto yasassī titthakaro sādhusammato bahujanassa; sopi rājagahaṃ vassāvāsaṃ osaṭo. Ayampi kho makkhali gosālo…pe… ajito kesakambalo… pakudho kaccāyano… sañjayo belaṭṭhaputto… nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto saṅghī ceva gaṇī ca gaṇācariyo ca ñāto yasassī titthakaro sādhusammato bahujanassa; sopi rājagahaṃ vassāvāsaṃ osaṭo. Ayampi kho samaṇo gotamo saṅghī ceva gaṇī ca gaṇācariyo ca ñāto yasassī titthakaro sādhusammato bahujanassa; sopi rājagahaṃ vassāvāsaṃ osaṭo. Ko nu kho imesaṃ bhavataṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ saṅghīnaṃ gaṇīnaṃ gaṇācariyānaṃ ñātānaṃ yasassīnaṃ titthakarānaṃ sādhusammatānaṃ bahujanassa sāvakānaṃ sakkato garukato mānito pūjito, kañca pana sāvakā sakkatvā garuṃ katvā garukatvā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) upanissāya viharantī’’’ti?
mula_english:
“Just as they are, Udāyi, they are sitting together for a discussion. What is the topic of your conversation?”

“[Please] let that conversation rest, venerable sir, the conversation that we are now sitting together for.

“It won’t be difficult for the Blessed One to hear about that later.

“In the past, venerable sir, a number of ascetics and *brāhmaṇa*s of various sects were sitting together in the debating hall, and this discussion arose among them: ‘A gain, indeed, to the lands of Aṅga and Magadha, a great gain indeed to the lands of Aṅga and Magadha, that these ascetics and *brāhmaṇa*s, heads of orders, heads of groups, teachers of groups, well-known and famous founders of sects regarded by many as saints, have come to spend the Rains at Rājagaha.

“There is also this Pūraṇa Kassapa, the head of an order, the head of a group, the teacher of a group, the well-known and famous founder of a sect regarded by many as a saint: he too has come to spend the Rains at Rājagaha.

“There is also this Makkhali Gosāla… this Ajita Kesakambalin… this Pakudha Kaccāyana… this Sañjaya Belaṭṭhaputta… this Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, the head of an order, the head of a group, the teacher of a group, the well-known and famous founder of a sect regarded by many as a saint: he too has come to spend the Rains at Rājagaha.

“There is also this ascetic Gotama, the head of an order, the head of a group, the teacher of a group, the well-known and famous founder of a sect regarded by many as a saint: he too has come to spend the Rains -at Rājagaha.

“Now among these worthy ascetics and *brāhmaṇa*s, heads of orders… regarded by many as saints, who is honored, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples? And how, honoring and respecting him, do they live in dependence on him?’”
commentary_pali:
238.Purimānīti hiyyodivasaṃ upādāya purimāni nāma honti, tato paraṃ purimatarāni. Kutūhalasālāyanti kutūhalasālā nāma paccekasālā natthi, yattha pana nānātitthiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇā nānāvidhaṃ kathaṃ pavattenti, sā bahūnaṃ – ‘‘ayaṃ kiṃ vadati , ayaṃ kiṃ vadatī’’ti kutūhaluppattiṭṭhānato ‘‘kutūhalasālā’’ti vuccati. ‘‘Kotūhalasālā’’tipi pāṭho. Lābhāti ye evarūpe samaṇabrāhmaṇe daṭṭhuṃ pañhaṃ pucchituṃ dhammakathaṃ vā nesaṃ sotuṃ labhanti, tesaṃ aṅgamagadhānaṃ ime lābhāti attho.

Saṅghinotiādīsu pabbajitasamūhasaṅkhāto saṅgho etesaṃ atthīti saṅghino. Sveva gaṇo etesaṃ atthīti gaṇino. Ācārasikkhāpanavasena tassa gaṇassa ācariyāti gaṇācariyā. Ñātāti paññātā pākaṭā. Yathābhuccaguṇehi ceva ayathābhūtaguṇehi ca samuggato yaso etesaṃ atthīti yasassino. Pūraṇādīnañhi ‘‘appiccho santuṭṭho, appicchatāya vatthampi na nivāsetī’’tiādinā nayena yaso samuggato, tathāgatassa ‘‘itipi so bhagavā’’tiādīhi yathābhūtaguṇehi. Titthakarāti laddhikarā. Sādhusammatāti ime sādhū sundarā sappurisāti evaṃ sammatā. Bahujanassāti assutavato ceva andhabālaputhujjanassa vibhāvino ca paṇḍitajanassa. Tattha titthiyā bālajanassa evaṃ sammatā, tathāgato paṇḍitajanassa. Iminā nayena pūraṇo kassapo saṅghītiādīsu attho veditabbo. Bhagavā pana yasmā aṭṭhatiṃsa ārammaṇāni vibhajanto bahūni nibbānaotaraṇatitthāni akāsi, tasmā ‘‘titthakaro’’ti vattuṃ vaṭṭati.

Saṅghino saṅghino gaṇino gaṇācariyā. Ñātā yasassino Titthakarā Sādhusammatā Bahujanassā pūraṇo kassapo saṅghī

Kasmā panete sabbepi tattha osaṭāti? Upaṭṭhākarakkhaṇatthañceva lābhasakkāratthañca. Tesañhi evaṃ hoti – ‘‘amhākaṃ upaṭṭhākā samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gaccheyyuṃ, te ca rakkhissāma. Samaṇassa ca gotamassa upaṭṭhāke sakkāraṃ karonte disvā amhākampi upaṭṭhākā amhākaṃ sakkāraṃ karissantī’’ti. Tasmā yattha yattha bhagavā osarati, tattha tattha sabbe osaranti.
commentary_english:
238. *Purimānī* means "starting from yesterday, they are called *purimāni*; thereafter, *purimatarāni*."

*Kutūhalasālāya* means a *kutūhalasālā* is not a specific *paccekasālā*. But where various non-Buddhist ascetics and Brahmins engage in diverse discussions, that place is called a *kutūhalasālā* because it is the source of curiosity, [thinking] "What is this person saying?"

There is also the reading *kotūhalasālā*.

*Lābhā* means, those who can obtain the opportunity to see such ascetics and Brahmins, to ask questions, or to hear religious talks, for those Aṅga-Magadhans, this is called *lābhā*, meaning gain.

*Saṅghino* etc., means *saṅgha*, which is the term for a community of renunciates, exists for these people; therefore, they are *saṅghino*.

" *Gaṇino* " means they have a *gaṇa*, a group; therefore, they are *gaṇino*.

"*Gaṇācariyā*" means "teachers of the group," due to their teaching of conduct to that group.

"*Ñātā*" means "known," *paññātā*, "renowned," *pākaṭā*, "manifest."

*Yasassino* means "they have fame (*yasas*) arising from appropriate qualities (*yathābhuccaguṇa*) and inappropriate qualities (*ayathābhūtaguṇa*)."

Because for Pūraṇa and others, fame arises through the principle of "having few desires and being content; not even wearing clothes due to having few desires," and for the *tathāgata*, through appropriate qualities, like "*itipi so bhagavā*," "indeed, that Blessed One."

*Titthakarā* means "those who make gains (*laddhikara*)."

*Sādhusammatā* means "they are regarded thus: 'These are good, beautiful, and noble persons' (*satpuruṣa*)."

*Bahujanassā* means "of many people," both the unlearned, blind, childish common people and discerning, learned people.

There, non-Buddhists are regarded thus by the childish people, while the *tathāgata* is regarded thus by the learned people.

By this principle, the meaning of "*Pūraṇo Kassapo Saṅghī*," and so forth, should be understood.

Moreover, because the Blessed One, dividing the thirty-eight objects of mindfulness, made many places of pilgrimage for descending into nirvāṇa, therefore, it is fitting to say "*titthakaro*."

*Saṅghino, saṅghino, gaṇino, gaṇācariyā. Ñātā, yasassino, titthakarā, sādhusammatā, bahujanassā, Pūraṇo Kassapo Saṅghī.*

Why are all of these gathered there? For the purpose of protecting supporters and for the purpose of gain and honor.

For they think thus: "Our supporters might go to the *samaṇa* Gotama for refuge, and we will protect them. Seeing our supporters honoring the *samaṇa* Gotama, our supporters will also honor us."

Therefore, wherever the Blessed One goes, there all go.

mula_pali:
239. ‘‘Tatrekacce evamāhaṃsu – ‘ayaṃ kho pūraṇo kassapo saṅghī ceva gaṇī ca gaṇācariyo ca ñāto yasassī titthakaro sādhusammato bahujanassa; so ca kho sāvakānaṃ na sakkato na garukato na mānito na pūjito, na ca pana pūraṇaṃ kassapaṃ sāvakā sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharanti. Bhūtapubbaṃ pūraṇo kassapo anekasatāya parisāya dhammaṃ deseti. Tatraññataro pūraṇassa kassapassa sāvako saddamakāsi – ‘‘mā bhonto pūraṇaṃ kassapaṃ etamatthaṃ pucchittha; neso etaṃ jānāti; mayametaṃ jānāma, amhe etamatthaṃ pucchatha; mayametaṃ bhavantānaṃ byākarissāmā’’ti. Bhūtapubbaṃ pūraṇo kassapo bāhā paggayha kandanto na labhati – ‘‘appasaddā bhonto hontu, mā bhonto saddamakattha. Nete, bhavante, pucchanti, amhe ete pucchanti; mayametesaṃ byākarissāmā’’ti. Bahū kho pana pūraṇassa kassapassa sāvakā vādaṃ āropetvā apakkantā – ‘‘na tvaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānāsi, ahaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānāmi , kiṃ tvaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānissasi? Micchāpaṭipanno tvamasi, ahamasmi sammāpaṭipanno, sahitaṃ me, asahitaṃ te, purevacanīyaṃ pacchā avaca, pacchāvacanīyaṃ pure avaca, adhiciṇṇaṃ te viparāvattaṃ, āropito te vādo, niggahitosi, cara vādappamokkhāya, nibbeṭhehi vā sace pahosī’’ti. Iti pūraṇo kassapo sāvakānaṃ na sakkato na garukato na mānito na pūjito, na ca pana pūraṇaṃ kassapaṃ sāvakā sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharanti. Akkuṭṭho ca pana pūraṇo kassapo dhammakkosenā’’’ti.

‘‘Ekacce evamāhaṃsu – ‘ayampi kho makkhali gosālo…pe… ajito kesakambalo… pakudho kaccāyano… sañjayo belaṭṭhaputto… nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto saṅghī ceva gaṇī ca gaṇācariyo ca ñāto yasassī titthakaro sādhusammato bahujanassa; so ca kho sāvakānaṃ na sakkato na garukato na mānito na pūjito, na ca pana nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ sāvakā sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharanti. Bhūtapubbaṃ nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto anekasatāya parisāya dhammaṃ deseti. Tatraññataro nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa sāvako saddamakāsi – mā bhonto nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ etamatthaṃ pucchittha; neso etaṃ jānāti; mayametaṃ jānāma, amhe etamatthaṃ pucchatha; mayametaṃ bhavantānaṃ byākarissāmāti. Bhūtapubbaṃ nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto bāhā paggayha kandanto na labhati – ‘‘appasaddā bhonto hontu, mā bhonto saddamakattha. Nete bhavante pucchanti, amhe ete pucchanti; mayametesaṃ byākarissāmā’’ti. Bahū kho pana nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa sāvakā vādaṃ āropetvā apakkantā – ‘‘na tvaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānāsi, ahaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānāmi. Kiṃ tvaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānissasi? Micchāpaṭipanno tvamasi. Ahamasmi sammāpaṭipanno. Sahitaṃ me asahitaṃ te, purevacanīyaṃ pacchā avaca, pacchāvacanīyaṃ pure avaca, adhiciṇṇaṃ te viparāvattaṃ, āropito te vādo, niggahitosi, cara vādappamokkhāya, nibbeṭhehi vā sace pahosī’’ti. Iti nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto sāvakānaṃ na sakkato na garukato na mānito na pūjito, na ca pana nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ sāvakā sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharanti. Akkuṭṭho ca pana nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto dhammakkosenā’’’ti.
mula_english:
“Thereupon some said this: ‘This Pūraṇa Kassapa is the head of an order, a group leader, the teacher of a group, known, famous, a founder of a school, regarded by many as a saint; yet he is not honoured, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples, nor do his disciples live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.

Once Pūraṇa Kassapa was teaching the Dhamma to an assembly of several hundred followers.

Then a certain disciple of his made a noise thus: “Sirs, do not ask Pūraṇa Kassapa this question. He does not know that. We know that. Ask us that question. We will answer that for you, sirs.”

Once Pūraṇa Kassapa, waving his arms and wailing, did not get his way: “Be quiet, sirs, make no noise, sirs.
They are not asking you, sirs. They are asking us. We will answer them.”

Indeed, many of Pūraṇa Kassapa’s disciples left him after refuting his doctrine thus: “You do not understand this *dharma-vinaya* (Dhamma and Discipline). I understand this Dhamma and Discipline. How could you understand this Dhamma and Discipline? Your way is wrong. My way is right. I am consistent. You are inconsistent. What should have been said first, you said last. What should have been said last, you said first. What you had so carefully thought up has been turned inside out. Your doctrine is refuted. You are proved wrong. Go and learn better, or disentangle yourself if you can!”

Thus Pūraṇa Kassapa is not honoured, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples, nor do his disciples live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.

Indeed, Pūraṇa Kassapa is scorned by the scorn shown to his Dhamma.’

“And some said this: ‘This Makkhali Gosāla… this Ajita Kesakambalin… this Pakudha Kaccāyana… this Sañjaya Belaṭṭhaputta… this Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta is the head of an order, a group leader, the teacher of a group, known, famous, a founder of a school, regarded by many as a saint; yet he is not honoured, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples, nor do his disciples live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.

Once Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta was teaching the Dhamma to an assembly of several hundred followers.

Then a certain disciple of Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta made a noise thus: “Sirs, do not ask Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta this question. He does not know that. We know that. Ask us that question. We will answer that for you, sirs.”

Once Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, waving his arms and wailing, did not get his way: “Be quiet, sirs, make no noise, sirs.
They are not asking you, sirs. They are asking us. We will answer them.”

Indeed, many of Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta’s disciples left him after refuting his doctrine thus: “You do not understand this *dharma-vinaya* (Dhamma and Discipline). I understand this Dhamma and Discipline. How could you understand this Dhamma and Discipline? Your way is wrong.
My way is right.
I am consistent. You are inconsistent. What should have been said first, you said last. What should have been said last, you said first. What you had so carefully thought up has been turned inside out. Your doctrine is refuted. You are proved wrong. Go and learn better, or disentangle yourself if you can!”

Thus Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta is not honoured, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples, nor do his disciples live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.

Indeed, Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta is scorned by the scorn shown to his Dhamma.’
commentary_pali: 239.Vādaṃ āropetvāti vāde dosaṃ āropetvā. Apakkantāti, apagatā, keci disaṃ pakkantā, keci gihibhāvaṃ pattā, keci imaṃ sāsanaṃ āgatā. Sahitaṃ meti mayhaṃ vacanaṃ sahitaṃ siliṭṭhaṃ, atthayuttaṃ kāraṇayuttanti attho. Asahitaṃ teti tuyhaṃ vacanaṃ asahitaṃ. Adhiciṇṇaṃ te viparāvattanti yaṃ tuyhaṃ dīgharattāciṇṇavasena suppaguṇaṃ, taṃ mayhaṃ ekavacaneneva viparāvattaṃ viparivattitvā ṭhitaṃ, na kiñci jātanti attho. Āropito te vādoti mayā tava vāde doso āropito. Cara vādappamokkhāyāti dosamocanatthaṃ cara vicara, tattha tattha gantvā sikkhāti attho. Nibbeṭhehi vā sace pahosīti atha sayaṃ pahosi, idāneva nibbeṭhehi. Dhammakkosenāti sabhāvakkosena.
commentary_english:
239. *vādaṃ āropetvā* means having imposed a fault on the assertion.
*apakkantā* means those who have departed, some having gone to another direction, some having attained the state of householders, some having come to this teaching (*sāsana*).
*sahitaṃ me* means my speech is coherent and lucid, connected to the meaning (*attha*) and connected to the reason (*kāraṇa*).
*asahitaṃ te* means your speech is incoherent.
*adhiciṇṇaṃ te viparāvatta* means that which is well-practiced by you due to long habit, that is reversed by me with a single word, having turned around and remained; it means nothing arose.
*āropito te vādo* means a fault in your assertion has been raised by me.
*cara vādappamokkhāyā* means go wander for the sake of liberation from blame (*dosa*), go wander around in order to release from the fault (*dosamocana*), having gone here and there, train; this is the meaning.
*nibbeṭhehi vā sace pahosī* means if you are able, then immediately refute it yourself.
*dhammakkosenā* means by the voice of Dharma, by the voice of nature (*sabhāva*).

mula_pali: 240. ‘‘Ekacce evamāhaṃsu – ‘ayampi kho samaṇo gotamo saṅghī ceva gaṇī ca gaṇācariyo ca ñāto yasassī titthakaro sādhusammato bahujanassa; so ca kho sāvakānaṃ sakkato garukato mānito pūjito, samaṇañca pana gotamaṃ sāvakā sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharanti. Bhūtapubbaṃ samaṇo gotamo anekasatāya parisāya dhammaṃ desesi. Tatraññataro samaṇassa gotamassa sāvako ukkāsi. Tamenāññataro sabrahmacārī jaṇṇukena jaṇṇuke (sī.) ghaṭṭesi – ‘‘appasaddo āyasmā hotu, māyasmā saddamakāsi, satthā no bhagavā dhammaṃ desesī’’ti. Yasmiṃ samaye samaṇo gotamo anekasatāya parisāya dhammaṃ deseti, neva tasmiṃ samaye samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakānaṃ khipitasaddo vā hoti ukkāsitasaddo vā. Tamenaṃ mahājanakāyo paccāsīsamānarūpo paccāsiṃ samānarūpo (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) paccupaṭṭhito hoti – ‘‘yaṃ no bhagavā dhammaṃ bhāsissati taṃ no sossāmā’’ti. Seyyathāpi nāma puriso cātummahāpathe khuddamadhuṃ khuddaṃ madhuṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) anelakaṃ pīḷeyya uppīḷeyya (sī.). Tamenaṃ mahājanakāyo paccāsīsamānarūpo paccupaṭṭhito assa. Evameva yasmiṃ samaye samaṇo gotamo anekasatāya parisāya dhammaṃ deseti, neva tasmiṃ samaye samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakānaṃ khipitasaddo vā hoti ukkāsitasaddo vā. Tamenaṃ mahājanakāyo paccāsīsamānarūpo paccupaṭṭhito hoti – ‘‘yaṃ no bhagavā dhammaṃ bhāsissati taṃ no sossāmā’’ti. Yepi samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakā sabrahmacārīhi sampayojetvā sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattanti tepi satthu ceva vaṇṇavādino honti, dhammassa ca vaṇṇavādino honti, saṅghassa ca vaṇṇavādino honti, attagarahinoyeva honti anaññagarahino, ‘‘mayamevamhā alakkhikā mayaṃ appapuññā te mayaṃ evaṃ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitvā nāsakkhimhā yāvajīvaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ caritu’’nti. Te ārāmikabhūtā vā upāsakabhūtā vā pañcasikkhāpade samādāya vattanti. Iti samaṇo gotamo sāvakānaṃ sakkato garukato mānito pūjito, samaṇañca pana gotamaṃ sāvakā sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharantī’’’ti.
mula_english:
240. Some said thus: ‘This recluse Gotama is the head of an order (saṅghī), the head of a group (gaṇī), and the teacher of a group (gaṇācariyo), well-known (ñāta), famous (yasassī), founder of a sect (titthakaro), regarded by many as a saint (sādhusammato bahujanassa). He is honored (sakkato), respected (garukato), revered (mānito), and venerated (pūjito) by his disciples (sāvakānaṃ), and his disciples live in dependence on him, honoring and respecting the recluse Gotama (samaṇañca pana gotamaṃ sāvakā sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharanti).

Once, the recluse Gotama was teaching his Dharma (dhammaṃ desesi) to an assembly of several hundred followers (anekasatāya parisāya).

And there a certain disciple of the recluse Gotama (samaṇassa gotamassa sāvako) cleared his throat (ukkāsi).

Thereupon one of his companions in the holy life (sabrahmacārī) nudged him with his knee (jaṇṇukena ghaṭṭesi) to indicate: “Be quiet, venerable sir (appasaddo āyasmā), make no noise (māyasmā saddamakāsi); the Blessed One (bhagavā), the Teacher (satthā), is teaching us the Dhamma (dhammaṃ desesī’ti).”

When the recluse Gotama (samaṇo gotamo) is teaching the Dhamma (dhammaṃ deseti) to an assembly of several hundred followers (anekasatāya parisāya), on that occasion (yasmiṃ samaye) there is no sound of his disciples’ coughing (khipitasaddo) or clearing their throats (ukkāsitasaddo).

For then that large assembly (mahājanakāyo) is poised in expectancy (paccāsīsamānarūpo): “Let us hear the Dhamma (dhammaṃ bhāsissati) the Blessed One (bhagavā) is about to teach (yaṃ no), let us hear it (taṃ no sossāmā’ti).”

Just as if a man should press a small honey-comb (khuddamadhuṃ anelakaṃ pīḷeyya) in a square at a great crossroads (cātummahāpathe).

And a large group of people (tamenaṃ mahājanakāyo) were poised in expectancy (paccāsīsamānarūpo paccupaṭṭhito assa).

So too (evameva), when the recluse Gotama (samaṇo gotamo) is teaching the Dhamma (dhammaṃ deseti) to an assembly of several hundred followers (anekasatāya parisāya), on that occasion (yasmiṃ samaye) there is no sound of his disciples’ coughing (khipitasaddo) or clearing their throats (ukkāsitasaddo).

For then that large assembly (tamenaṃ mahājanakāyo) is poised in expectancy (paccāsīsamānarūpo paccupaṭṭhito hoti): “Let us hear the Dhamma (dhammaṃ bhāsissati) the Blessed One (bhagavā) is about to teach (yaṃ no), let us hear it (taṃ no sossāmā’ti).”

And even those disciples (sāvakā) of the recluse Gotama (samaṇassa gotamassa) who fall out with their companions in the holy life (sabrahmacārīhi sampayojetvā) and abandon the training (sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya) to return to the low life (hīnāyāvattanti)—even they (tepi) praise the Master (satthu) and the Dhamma (dhammassa) and the Saṅgha (saṅghassa); they blame themselves alone (attagarahinoyeva honti), not others (anaññagarahino), saying: “We were unlucky (mayamevamhā alakkhikā), we have little merit (mayaṃ appapuññā); for though we went forth (pabbajitvā) into homelessness in such a well-proclaimed Dhamma-Vinaya (svākkhāte dhammavinaye), we were unable (nāsakkhimhā) to live the perfectly complete and pure holy life (paripuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ caritu’’nti) for the rest of our lives (yāvajīvaṃ.”

Having become monastery attendants (ārāmikabhūtā) or lay followers (upāsakabhūtā), they undertake and observe (samādāya vattanti) the five precepts (pañcasikkhāpade).

Thus (iti) the recluse Gotama (samaṇo gotamo) is honoured (sakkato), respected (garukato), revered (mānito), and venerated (pūjito) by his disciples (sāvakānaṃ), and his disciples live in dependence on him, honoring and respecting (samaṇañca pana gotamaṃ sāvakā sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharanti) the recluse Gotama.’"
commentary_pali: 240.Taṃ no sossāmāti taṃ amhākaṃ desitaṃ dhammaṃ suṇissāma. Khuddamadhunti khuddakamakkhikāhi kataṃ daṇḍakamadhuṃ. Anelakanti niddosaṃ apagatamacchikaṇḍakaṃ. Pīḷeyyāti dadeyya. Paccāsīsamānarūpoti pūretvā nu kho no bhojanaṃ dassatīti bhājanahattho paccāsīsamāno paccupaṭṭhito assa. Sampayojetvāti appamattakaṃ vivādaṃ katvā.
commentary_english:
240. “*Taṃ no sossāmā*” means we will hear that Dharma taught by us.
"*Khuddamadhu*” means *daṇḍakamadhu* made by small bees.
"*Anelaka*" means faultless, without fly-larvae.
"*Pīḷeyyā*" means *dadeyya*.
"*Paccāsīsamānarūpo*" means, thinking, "Having filled [the bowl], will he give us food?" he stands nearby with a bowl in his hand, waiting expectantly.
"*Sampayojetvā*" means, having made a small dispute.

mula_pali:
241. ‘‘Kati pana tvaṃ, udāyi, mayi dhamme samanupassasi, yehi mamaṃ mama (sabbattha) sāvakā sakkaronti garuṃ karonti garukaronti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) mānenti pūjenti, sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharantī’’ti? ‘‘Pañca kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati dhamme samanupassāmi yehi bhagavantaṃ sāvakā sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti, sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharanti. Katame pañca? Bhagavā hi, bhante, appāhāro, appāhāratāya ca vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhante, bhagavā appāhāro, appāhāratāya ca vaṇṇavādī imaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati paṭhamaṃ dhammaṃ samanupassāmi yena bhagavantaṃ sāvakā sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti, sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharanti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhante, bhagavā santuṭṭho itarītarena cīvarena, itarītaracīvarasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhante, bhagavā santuṭṭho itarītarena cīvarena, itarītaracīvarasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī, imaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati dutiyaṃ dhammaṃ samanupassāmi yena bhagavantaṃ sāvakā sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti, sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharanti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhante, bhagavā santuṭṭho itarītarena piṇḍapātena, itarītarapiṇḍapātasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhante, bhagavā santuṭṭho itarītarena piṇḍapātena, itarītarapiṇḍapātasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī, imaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati tatiyaṃ dhammaṃ samanupassāmi yena bhagavantaṃ sāvakā sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti, sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharanti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhante, bhagavā santuṭṭho itarītarena senāsanena, itarītarasenāsanasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhante, bhagavā santuṭṭho itarītarena senāsanena, itarītarasenāsanasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī, imaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati catutthaṃ dhammaṃ samanupassāmi yena bhagavantaṃ sāvakā sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti, sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharanti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhante, bhagavā pavivitto, pavivekassa ca vaṇṇavādī . Yampi, bhante, bhagavā pavivitto, pavivekassa ca vaṇṇavādī, imaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati pañcamaṃ dhammaṃ samanupassāmi yena bhagavantaṃ sāvakā sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti, sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharanti.

‘‘Ime kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati pañca dhamme samanupassāmi yehi bhagavantaṃ sāvakā sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti, sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharantī’’ti.
mula_english:
241. “But how many qualities, Udāyi, do you see in me because of which my disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, honouring, respecting, and living in dependence on me?”

“Venerable sir, I see five qualities in the Blessed One because of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him. What are these five? First, venerable sir, the Blessed One eats little and commends eating little; this I see as the first quality of the Blessed One because of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.

“Again, venerable sir, the Blessed One is content with any kind of robe and commends contentment with any kind of robe; this I see as the second quality of the Blessed One because of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.

“Again, venerable sir, the Blessed One is content with any kind of almsfood and commends contentment with any kind of almsfood; this I see as the third quality of the Blessed One because of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.

“Again, venerable sir, the Blessed One is content with any kind of resting place and commends contentment with any kind of resting place; this I see as the fourth quality of the Blessed One because of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.

“Again, venerable sir, the Blessed One is secluded and commends seclusion; this I see as the fifth quality of the Blessed One because of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.”

“Venerable sir, these are the five qualities I see in the Blessed One because of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, honouring, respecting, and living in dependence on him.”
commentary_pali: 241.Itarītarenāti lāmakalāmakena. Pavivittoti idaṃ paribbājako kāyavivekamattaṃ sandhāya vadati, bhagavā pana tīhi vivekehi vivittova.
commentary_english:
"itarītarenā ti lāmakalāmakena": by this or that inferior and base thing.

"pavivitto ti idaṃ paribbājako kāyavivekamattaṃ sandhāya vadati, bhagavā pana tīhi vivekehi vivittova": "Secluded," the wandering mendicant says this with the idea of physical seclusion, but the Blessed One is secluded by the three seclusions.

mula_pali:
242. ‘‘‘Appāhāro samaṇo gotamo, appāhāratāya ca vaṇṇavādī’ti, iti ce maṃ, udāyi, sāvakā sakkareyyuṃ garuṃ kareyyuṃ māneyyuṃ pūjeyyuṃ, sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya vihareyyuṃ, santi kho pana me, udāyi, sāvakā kosakāhārāpi aḍḍhakosakāhārāpi beluvāhārāpi aḍḍhabeluvāhārāpi.
