Rūpī rūpāni passati, ayaṃ paṭhamo vimokkho; ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī bahiddhā rūpāni passati, ayaṃ dutiyo vimokkho; subhanteva adhimutto hoti, ayaṃ tatiyo vimokkho; sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ catuttho vimokkho; sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ pañcamo vimokkho; sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ chaṭṭho vimokkho; sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ sattamo vimokkho; sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ aṭṭhamo vimokkho. Tatra ca pana me sāvakā bahū abhiññāvosānapāramippattā viharanti.
mula_english:
248. Furthermore, Udayin, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, according to which my disciples develop the eight liberations (aṭṭha vimokkhe).

Possessed of material form, one sees forms: this is the first liberation (paṭhamo vimokkho). Not perceiving form internally, one sees forms externally: this is the second liberation (dutiyo vimokkho). One is resolved only upon the beautiful: this is the third liberation (tatiyo vimokkho). With the complete surmounting of perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of sensory impact, with non-attention to perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite,’ one enters upon and abides in the base of infinite space (ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ): this is the fourth liberation (catuttho vimokkho). With the complete surmounting of the base of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite,’ one enters upon and abides in the base of infinite consciousness (viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ): this is the fifth liberation (pañcamo vimokkho). With the complete surmounting of the base of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing,’ one enters upon and abides in the base of nothingness (ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ): this is the sixth liberation (chaṭṭho vimokkho). With the complete surmounting of the base of nothingness, one enters upon and abides in the base of neither perception nor non-perception (nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ): this is the seventh liberation (sattamo vimokkho). With the complete surmounting of the base of neither perception nor non-perception, one enters upon and abides in the cessation of perception and feeling (saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ): this is the eighth liberation (aṭṭhamo vimokkho).

And thereby many disciples of mine abide having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge (abhiññāvosānapāramippattā).
commentary_pali:
248. Vimokkhakathāyaṃ vimokkheti kenaṭṭhena vimokkhā, adhimuccanaṭṭhena. Ko panāyaṃ adhimuccanaṭṭho nāma? Paccanīkadhammehi ca suṭṭhu muccanaṭṭho, ārammaṇe ca abhirativasena suṭṭhu muccanaṭṭho, pituaṅke vissaṭṭhaṅgapaccaṅgassa dārakassa sayanaṃ viya aniggahitabhāvena nirāsaṅkatāya ārammaṇe pavattīti vuttaṃ hoti. Ayaṃ panattho pacchimavimokkhe natthi, purimesu sabbesu atthi. Rūpī rūpāni passatīti ettha ajjhattakesādīsu nīlakasiṇādivasena uppāditaṃ rūpajjhānaṃ rūpaṃ, tadassa atthīti rūpī. Bahiddhā rūpāni passatīti bahiddhāpi nīlakasiṇādīni rūpāni jhānacakkhunā passati. Iminā ajjhatta bahiddhāvatthukesu kasiṇesu uppāditajjhānassa puggalassa cattāripi rūpāvacarajjhānāni dassitāni.

Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññīti ajjhattaṃ na rūpasaññī, attano kesādīsu anuppāditarūpāvacarajjhānoti attho. Iminā bahiddhā parikammaṃ katvā bahiddhāva uppāditajjhānassa rūpāvacarajjhānāni dassitāni. Subhanteva adhimutto hotīti iminā suvisuddhesu nīlādīsu vaṇṇakasiṇesu jhānāni dassitāni. Tattha kiñcāpi antoappanāyaṃ subhanti ābhogo natthi, yo pana suvisuddhaṃ subhakasiṇaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā viharati, so yasmā subhanti adhimutto hotīti vattabbataṃ āpajjati, tasmā evaṃ desanā katā. Paṭisambhidāmagge pana ‘‘kathaṃ subhanteva adhimutto hotīti vimokkho. Idha bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati…pe… mettāya bhāvitattā sattā appaṭikūlā honti. Karuṇāsahagatena, muditāsahagatena, upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati…pe… upekkhāya bhāvitattā sattā appaṭikūlā honti. Evaṃ subhanteva adhimutto hotīti vimokkho’’ti (paṭi. ma. 1.212) vuttaṃ.

Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī Subhanteva adhimutto hotī

Sabbasorūpasaññānantiādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ visuddhimagge vuttameva. Ayaṃ aṭṭhamo vimokkhoti ayaṃ catunnaṃ khandhānaṃ sabbaso vissaṭṭhattā vimuttattā aṭṭhamo uttamo vimokkho nāma.

Sabbaso rūpasaññāna visuddhimagge Ayaṃ aṭṭhamo vimokkho
commentary_english:
248. In the *vimokkha* discourse, why are the *vimokkhas* called *vimokkhas*? Because of the meaning of "adhimuccana" (deciding, being resolved).

What is this meaning of *adhimuccana*? It is said to be in the sense of freeing thoroughly from the adverse phenomena and in the sense of freeing thoroughly by way of delight in the object. What is meant is: occurrence on the object without constraint, free from apprehension, similar to the way a little boy sleeps in his father’s lap, his body completely relaxed. But the latter meaning applies only to the first seven emancipations, not to the last one.

“One possessing material form sees material forms”: here, the material form (*rūpa*) is the fine-material-sphere *jhāna* aroused through a blue *kasiṇa*, etc., using as the blue *kasiṇa*, etc. something internal such as the hairs of the head, etc. One having that material form is “one possessing material form” (*rūpī*).

“Sees material forms externally”: with the eye of *jhāna* one also sees material forms such as the blue *kasiṇa*, etc. externally. By this the four fine-material-sphere *jhānas* are shown for someone who arouses *jhāna* in the external *kasiṇas* which are internal and external.

“One not perceiving material forms internally”: This means that he does not arouse the fine-material-sphere *jhānas* on his own head hairs, etc. By this the fine-material-sphere *jhānas* are shown for someone who does the preparatory work externally and arouses *jhāna* only externally.

“One is released upon the idea of the beautiful”: by this, *jhānas* are shown in the very pure color *kasiṇas* such as blue, etc. In the meditative absorption itself there is no concern with the idea of the beautiful. But because one who dwells in meditation taking as his object a pure and beautiful *kasiṇa* can be described as “released upon the idea of the beautiful,” the teaching is expounded in those words.

In the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, however, it is said: “'One is released upon the idea of the beautiful'—how is this an emancipation? Herein, a *bhikkhu* dwells pervading one direction, etc. with a mind endowed with loving-kindness; through the development of loving-kindness beings are not repulsive to him. He dwells pervading one direction with a mind endowed with compassion, with a mind endowed with joy, with a mind endowed with equanimity…through the development of equanimity beings are not repulsive to him. Thus, 'one is released upon the idea of the beautiful'—this is an emancipation'” (Paṭi. ma. 1.212).

Regarding all that should be stated in “complete transcendence of perception of material form,” etc., that is stated in the *Visuddhimagga*.

“This is the eighth emancipation”: the eighth emancipation is the highest emancipation, since it is completely purified and liberated from the four aggregates ( *skandha*).

mula_pali:
249. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṃ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā aṭṭha abhibhāyatanāni bhāventi. Ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati parittāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi, passāmī’ti evaṃ saññī hoti. Idaṃ paṭhamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati appamāṇāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi, passāmī’ti evaṃ saññī hoti. Idaṃ dutiyaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati parittāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi, passāmī’ti evaṃ saññī hoti. Idaṃ tatiyaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati appamāṇāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi, passāmī’ti evaṃ saññī hoti. Idaṃ catutthaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati nīlāni nīlavaṇṇāni nīlanidassanāni nīlanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma umāpupphaṃ nīlaṃ nīlavaṇṇaṃ nīlanidassanaṃ nīlanibhāsaṃ, seyyathāpi vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ nīlaṃ nīlavaṇṇaṃ nīlanidassanaṃ nīlanibhāsaṃ; evameva ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati nīlāni nīlavaṇṇāni nīlanidassanāni nīlanibhāsāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi, passāmī’ti evaṃ saññī hoti. Idaṃ pañcamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ .

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati pītāni pītavaṇṇāni pītanidassanāni pītanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma kaṇikārapupphaṃ pītaṃ pītavaṇṇaṃ pītanidassanaṃ pītanibhāsaṃ, seyyathāpi vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ pītaṃ pītavaṇṇaṃ pītanidassanaṃ pītanibhāsaṃ; evameva ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati pītāni pītavaṇṇāni pītanidassanāni pītanibhāsāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi, passāmī’ti evaṃ saññī hoti. Idaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati lohitakāni lohitakavaṇṇāni lohitakanidassanāni lohitakanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma bandhujīvakapupphaṃ lohitakaṃ lohitakavaṇṇaṃ lohitakanidassanaṃ lohitakanibhāsaṃ, seyyathāpi vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ lohitakaṃ lohitakavaṇṇaṃ lohitakanidassanaṃ lohitakanibhāsaṃ; evameva ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati lohitakāni lohitakavaṇṇāni lohitakanidassanāni lohitakanibhāsāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi, passāmī’ti evaṃ saññī hoti. Idaṃ sattamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati odātāni odātavaṇṇāni odātanidassanāni odātanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma osadhitārakā odātā odātavaṇṇā odātanidassanā odātanibhāsā, seyyathāpi vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ odātaṃ odātavaṇṇaṃ odātanidassanaṃ odātanibhāsaṃ; evameva ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati odātāni odātavaṇṇāni odātanidassanāni odātanibhāsāni . ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi , passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ. Tatra ca pana me sāvakā bahū abhiññāvosānapāramippattā viharanti.
mula_english: 249. “Again, Udayin, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way to practice, according to which my disciples develop the eight bases for transcendence (*aṭṭha abhibhāyatanāni*). Perceiving forms internally, one sees forms externally, limited, beautiful and ugly. Mastering them, one is aware that one knows and sees them. This is the first base for transcendence (*paṭhamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ*). Perceiving forms internally, one sees forms externally, immeasurable, beautiful and ugly. Mastering them, one is aware that one knows and sees them. This is the second base for transcendence (*dutiyaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ*). Not perceiving form internally, one sees forms externally, limited, beautiful and ugly. Mastering them, one is aware that one knows and sees them. This is the third base for transcendence (*tatiyaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ*). Not perceiving form internally, one sees forms externally, immeasurable, beautiful and ugly. Mastering them, one is aware that one knows and sees them. This is the fourth base for transcendence (*catutthaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ*). Not perceiving form internally, one sees forms externally, blue, of blue colour, blue in appearance, with blue luminosity. Just as a flax flower is blue, blue in its color, blue in its features, blue in its glow, or just as Vārāṇasī muslin, smooth on both sides, is blue, blue in its color, blue in its features, blue in its glow, so too, not perceiving form internally, one sees forms externally, blue, of blue colour, blue in appearance, with blue luminosity. Mastering them, one is aware that one knows and sees them. This is the fifth base for transcendence (*pañcamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ*). Not perceiving form internally, one sees forms externally, yellow, of yellow colour, yellow in appearance, with yellow luminosity. Just as a *kaṇikāra* flower is yellow, yellow in its color, yellow in its features, yellow in its glow, or just as Vārāṇasī muslin, smooth on both sides, is yellow, yellow in its color, yellow in its features, yellow in its glow, so too, not perceiving form internally, one sees forms externally, yellow, of yellow colour, yellow in appearance, with yellow luminosity. Mastering them, one is aware that one knows and sees them. This is the sixth base for transcendence (*chaṭṭhaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ*). Not perceiving form externally, one sees forms externally, red, of red colour, red in appearance, with red luminosity. Just as a *bandhujīvaka*-flower is red, red in its color, red in its features, red in its glow, or just as Vārāṇasī muslin, smooth on both sides, is red, red in its color, red in its features, red in its glow, in the same way one percipient of the formless internally sees forms externally as red, red in their color, red in their features, red in their glow. Mastering them, one is aware that one knows and sees them. This is the seventh base for transcendence (*sattamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ*). Not perceiving form internally, one sees forms externally, white, of white colour, white in appearance, with white luminosity. Just as the morning star is white, white in its color, white in its features, white in its glow, or just as Vārāṇasī muslin, smooth on both sides, is white, white in its color, white in its features, white in its glow, in the same way one percipient of the formless internally sees forms externally as white, white in their color, white in their features, white in their glow. Mastering them, one is aware that one knows. ...and being master of them, is aware that he perceives and knows them ('*passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti*'). This is the eighth dimension of mastery (*idaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ*). And moreover, many disciples of mine dwell there, having attained the ultimate perfection of direct knowledge (*abhiññāvosānapāramippattā*).
commentary_pali:
249. Abhibhāyatanakathāyaṃ abhibhāyatanānīti abhibhavanakāraṇāni. Kiṃ abhibhavanti? Paccanīkadhammepi ārammaṇānipi. Tāni hi paṭipakkhabhāvena paccanīkadhamme abhibhavanti, puggalassa ñāṇuttaritāya ārammaṇāni. Ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññītiādīsu pana ajjhattarūpe parikammavasena ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī nāma hoti. Ajjhattañca nīlaparikammaṃ karonto kese vā pitte vā akkhitārakāya vā karoti, pītaparikammaṃ karonto mede vā chaviyā vā hatthatalapādatalesu vā akkhīnaṃ pītaṭṭhāne vā karoti, lohitaparikammaṃ karonto maṃse vā lohite vā jivhāya vā akkhīnaṃ rattaṭṭhāne vā karoti, odātaparikammaṃ karonto aṭṭhimhi vā dante vā nakhe vā akkhīnaṃ setaṭṭhāne vā karoti. Taṃ pana sunīlaṃ supītakaṃ sulohitakaṃ suodātaṃ na hoti, asuvisuddhameva hoti.

Eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatīti yassetaṃ parikammaṃ ajjhattaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, nimittaṃ pana bahiddhā, so evaṃ ajjhattaṃ parikammassa bahiddhā ca appanāya vasena – ‘‘ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī’’ti vuccati. Parittānīti avaḍḍhitāni. Suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇānīti suvaṇṇāni vā hontu dubbaṇṇāni vā, parittavaseneva idamabhibhāyatanaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Tāniabhibhuyyāti yathā nāma sampannagahaṇiko kaṭacchumattaṃ bhattaṃ labhitvā ‘‘kimettha bhuñjitabbaṃ atthī’’ti saṅkaḍḍhitvā ekakabaḷameva karoti, evamevaṃ ñāṇuttariko puggalo visadañāṇo – ‘‘kimettha parittake ārammaṇe samāpajjitabbaṃ atthi, nāyaṃ mama bhāro’’ti tāni rūpāni abhibhavitvā samāpajjati, saha nimittuppādenevettha appanaṃ pāpetīti attho. Jānāmi passāmīti iminā panassa ābhogo kathito, so ca kho samāpattito vuṭṭhitassa, na antosamāpattiyaṃ. Evaṃsaññī hotīti ābhogasaññāyapi jhānasaññāyapi evaṃsaññī hoti. Abhibhavasaññā hissa antosamāpattiyaṃ atthi, ābhogasaññā pana samāpattito vuṭṭhitasseva.

Eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī Parittānī Suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇānī Tāni abhibhuyyā Jānāmi passāmī Evaṃsaññī hotī

Appamāṇānīti vaḍḍhitappamāṇāni, mahantānīti attho. Abhibhuyyāti ettha pana yathā mahagghaso puriso ekaṃ bhattavaḍḍhitakaṃ labhitvā ‘‘aññāpi hotu, aññāpi hotu, kimesā mayhaṃ karissatī’’ti taṃ na mahantato passati, evameva ñāṇuttaro puggalo visadañāṇo ‘‘kimettha samāpajjitabbaṃ, nayidaṃ appamāṇaṃ, na mayhaṃ cittekaggatākaraṇe bhāro atthī’’ti tāni abhibhavitvā samāpajjati, saha nimittuppādenevettha appanaṃ pāpetīti attho.

Appamāṇānī Abhibhuyyā

Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññīti alābhitāya vā anatthikatāya vā ajjhattarūpe parikammasaññāvirahito. Ekobahiddhā rūpāni passatīti yassa parikammampi nimittampi bahiddhāva uppannaṃ, so evaṃ bahiddhā parikammassa ceva appanāya ca vasena – ‘‘ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī’’ti vuccati. Sesamettha catutthābhibhāyatane vuttanayameva. Imesu pana catūsu parittaṃ vitakkacaritavasena āgataṃ, appamāṇaṃ mohacaritavasena, suvaṇṇaṃ dosacaritavasena, dubbaṇṇaṃ rāgacaritavasena. Etesañhi etāni sappāyāni. Sā ca nesaṃ sappāyatā vitthārato visuddhimaggecariyaniddese vuttā.

Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī Eko bahiddhā rūpāni passatī visuddhimagge

Pañcamaabhibhāyatanādīsu nīlānīti sabbasaṅgāhikavasena vuttaṃ. Nīlavaṇṇānīti vaṇṇavasena. Nīlanidassanānīti nidassanavasena. Apaññāyamānavivarāni asambhinnavaṇṇāni ekanīlāneva hutvā dissantīti vuttaṃ hoti. Nīlanibhāsānīti idaṃ pana obhāsavasena vuttaṃ, nīlobhāsāni nīlapabhāyuttānīti attho. Etena nesaṃ suvisuddhataṃ dasseti. Visuddhavaṇṇavaseneva hi imāni cattāri abhibhāyatanāni vuttāni. Umāpupphanti etañhi pupphaṃ siniddhaṃ muduṃ dissamānampi nīlameva hoti. Girikaṇṇikapupphādīni pana dissamānāni setadhātukāni honti. Tasmā idameva gahitaṃ, na tāni. Bārāṇaseyyakanti bārāṇasiyaṃ bhavaṃ. Tattha kira kappāsopi mudu, suttakantikāyopi tantavāyāpi chekā, udakampi suci siniddhaṃ, tasmā vatthaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ hoti, dvīsu passesu maṭṭhaṃ mudu siniddhaṃ khāyati. Pītānītiādīsu imināva nayena attho veditabbo. ‘‘Nīlakasiṇaṃ uggaṇhanto nīlasmiṃ nimittaṃ gaṇhāti pupphasmiṃ vā vatthasmiṃ vā vaṇṇadhātuyā vā’’tiādikaṃ panettha kasiṇakaraṇañceva parikammañca appanāvidhānañca sabbaṃ visuddhimagge vitthārato vuttameva.

nīlānī Nīlavaṇṇānī Nīlanidassanānī Nīlanibhāsānī Umāpuppha Bārāṇaseyyaka Pītānī visuddhimagge

Abhiññāvosānapāramippattāti ito pubbesu satipaṭṭhānādīsu te dhamme bhāvetvā arahattappattāva abhiññāvosānapāramippattā nāma honti, imesu pana aṭṭhasu abhibhāyatanesu ciṇṇavasībhāvāyeva abhiññāvosānapāramippattā nāma.

Abhiññāvosānapāramippattā
commentary_english:
249. In the discourse on the spheres of mastery ( *abhibhāyatana*), "*abhibhāyatanāni*" means the causes of mastery.

What do they master? Both the opponent-phenomena (*paccanīkadhammepi*) and the objects (*ārammaṇānipi*).

For they overcome opponent-phenomena by way of opposition, [and they are] objects for the knowledge of an individual, which is supreme.

In "*ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī* " etc., one is called "*ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī*" by way of the inner-form preparatory practice (*parikammavasena*).

And practicing the blue preparatory practice (*nīlaparikammaṃ karonto*) he makes [it] in the hair or in the bile or in the pupil of the eye, practicing the yellow preparatory practice (*pītaparikammaṃ karonto*) he makes [it] in the fat or in the skin or in the palms of the hands and soles of the feet or in the yellow place of the eyes, practicing the red preparatory practice (*lohitaparikammaṃ karonto*) he makes [it] in the flesh or in the blood or in the tongue or in the red place of the eyes, practicing the white preparatory practice (*odātaparikammaṃ karonto*) he makes [it] in the bones or in the teeth or in the nails or in the white place of the eyes.

That, however, is not very blue, very yellow, very red, very white, it is only not very pure.

"*Eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati*" means: Whose preparatory practice (*parikammaṃ*) has arisen internally (*ajjhattaṃ*), but the sign (*nimittaṃ*) is external (*bahiddhā*), thus, by way of the application (*appanāya*) of the internal preparatory practice (*ajjhattaṃ parikammassa*) and external [sign] (*bahiddhā ca*), he is called "*ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati*."

"*Parittānī*" means undeveloped.

"*Suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇānī*" means: Let them be beautiful (*suvaṇṇāni vā hontu*) or ugly (*dubbaṇṇāni vā*), this sphere of mastery (*idamabhibhāyatanaṃ*) should be known to be spoken of only by way of the limited.

Those having overcome (*abhibhuyyā*), just as, for example, an expert cook, having obtained a ladleful of rice (*kaṭacchumattaṃ bhattaṃ*), having gathered [it] together thinking, "What should be eaten here?" makes only one mouthful (*ekakabaḷameva karoti*), just so, the individual (*puggalo*) whose knowledge is supreme (*ñāṇuttariko*), whose knowledge is clear (*visadañāṇo*) – having overcome those forms (*tāni rūpāni*) thinking, "What is to be entered into (*samāpajjitabbaṃ*) in this limited object (*parittake ārammaṇe*)? This is not a burden to me ( *nāyaṃ mama bhāro*)," enters into absorption (*samāpajjati*), together with the arising of the sign (*nimittuppādeneva*) he causes application (*appanaṃ pāpetīti*) here. This is the meaning.

"*Jānāmi passāmī*" by this, its range (*ābhogo*) is spoken of, and that, indeed, [is] of one who has arisen from absorption (*samāpattito vuṭṭhitassa*), not in the midst of absorption (*na antosamāpattiyaṃ*).

"*Evaṃsaññī hotī*" means: he is thus-perceiving (*evaṃsaññī hoti*) even in the range-perception (*ābhogasaññāyapi*) and even in the *jhāna*-perception (*jhānasaññāyapi*).

Overcoming-perception (*abhibhavasaññā*) is, indeed, in the midst of absorption (*antosamāpattiyaṃ atthi*), but range-perception (*ābhogasaññā*) is only of one who has arisen from absorption (*samāpattito vuṭṭhitasseva*).

*Eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati*, *parittānī*, *suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇānī*, *tāni*

Those having overcome (*abhibhuyyā*), I know, I see (*jānāmi passāmī*), he is thus-perceiving (* evaṃsaññī hotī*)

"*Appamāṇānī*" means having increased measure, the meaning is: they are great (*mahantānīti attho*).

"*Abhibhuyyā*" here, just as, for example, a great eater, having obtained one portion of rice (*ekaṃ bhattavaḍḍhitakaṃ labhitvā*) thinking, "Let there be another, let there be another (*aññāpi hoṃtu, aññāpi hoṃtu*), what will this do for me? (*kimesā mayhaṃ karissati*)," does not see that as great (*taṃ na mahantato passati*), just so, the individual (*puggalo*) whose knowledge is supreme (*ñāṇuttaro*), whose knowledge is clear (*visadañāṇo*) – having overcome those (*tāni*) thinking, "What is to be entered into (*samāpajjitabbaṃ*) here? This is not immeasurable (*nayidaṃ appamāṇaṃ*), there is no burden (*na bhāro atthī*) for me in making one-pointedness of mind (*cittekaggatākaraṇe*)," enters into absorption (*samāpajjati*), together with the arising of the sign (*nimittuppādeneva*) he causes application (*appanaṃ pāpetīti*) here. This is the meaning.

Immeasurable (*appamāṇānī*), having overcome (*abhibhuyyā*)

"*Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī*" means: devoid of preparatory-practice-perception (*parikammasaññāvirahito*) in the inner form (*ajjhattarūpe*) due to lack of gain (*alābhitāya vā*) or due to being unprofitable (*anatthikatāya vā*).

*Eko*, *bahiddhā rūpāni passati* means: whose preparatory practice (*parikammampi*) and sign (*nimittampi*) have arisen externally (*bahiddhāva uppannaṃ*), thus, by way of the application (*appanāya*) and the external preparatory practice itself (*bahiddhā parikammassa ceva*) – he is called "*ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati*."

The remainder here [is] just in the manner spoken of in the fourth sphere of mastery (*catutthābhibhāyatane vuttanayameva*).

But in these four (*imesu pana catūsu*) the limited (*parittaṃ*) has come (*āgataṃ*) by way of the discursive temperament (*vitakkacaritavasena*), the immeasurable (*appamāṇaṃ*) by way of the deluded temperament (*mohacaritavasena*), the beautiful (*suvaṇṇaṃ*) by way of the aversive temperament (*dosacaritavasena*), the ugly (*dubbaṇṇaṃ*) by way of the passionate temperament (*rāgacaritavasena*).

For these are suitable for them (*etesañhi etāni sappāyāni*).

And that suitableness (*sappāyatā*) of those is spoken of in detail in the *visuddhimagga* in the conduct-instruction (*cariyaniddese vuttā*).

*Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī* *eko* *bahiddhā rūpāni passati* *visuddhimagge*

Among the fifth sphere of mastery (*pañcamaabhibhāyatanādīsu*), "*nīlānī*" is spoken of by way of all-embracing (*sabbasaṅgāhikavasena vuttaṃ*).

"*Nīlavaṇṇānī*" means by way of colour (*vaṇṇavasena*).

"*Nīlanidassanānī*" means by way of indication (*nidassanavasena*).

It is said that the apertures not appearing, the colours not being mixed, appearing having become just one blue (*ekonīlāneva hutvā dissantīti vuttaṃ*)

"*Nīlanibhāsānī*" means this, however, is spoken by way of radiance (*obhāsavasena vuttaṃ*), *nīlobhāsāni* means possessed of blue light (*nīlapabhāyuttānīti attho*).

By this, he shows their very purity (*nesaṃ suvisuddhataṃ dasseti*).

For, indeed, these four spheres of mastery (*imāni cattāri abhibhāyatanāni*) are spoken of only by way of pure colour (*visuddhavaṇṇavaseneva hi*).

"*umāpuppha*" means: this flower, indeed, being smooth (*siniddhaṃ*), soft (*muduṃ*), even appearing (*dissamānampi*) is only blue (*nīlameva hoti*).

But the *girikaṇṇikapuppha* etc. (*girikaṇṇikapupphādīni pana*) being visible (*dissamānāni*) are of white element (*setadhātukāni honti*).
Therefore, this alone is to be taken, not those.
"Bārāṇaseyyaka" means being in Varanasi (Bārāṇasī).
There, indeed, even the cotton is soft, even the female cotton-spinners are clever, even the weavers are skilled, even the water is pure and smooth; therefore the cloth is rubbed on both sides, on both sides it appears rubbed, soft, and smooth.
In "pītānī" and so on, the meaning should be understood in this way.
“When taking up the blue *kasiṇa* (nīlakasiṇaṃ), one grasps the sign in the blue, either in a flower, or in a cloth, or in the element of color,” and so on; here, all of the *kasiṇa* preparation (kasiṇakaraṇa), the preliminary work (parikamma), and the establishing procedure (appanāvidhāna), is fully described in detail in the *Visuddhimagga*.

Nīlānī, Nīlavaṇṇānī, Nīlanidassanānī, Nīlanibhāsānī, Umāpuppha, Bārāṇaseyyaka, Pītānī, Visuddhimagge, abhiññāvosānapāramippattā, from here, in the previous *satipaṭṭhāna* etc., having developed those *dharmas*, they attained *arahatva*, abhiññāvosānapāramippattā are called. But among these eight abhibhāyatanas, solely through habituation and mastery, they are called abhiññāvosānapāramippattā.

Abhiññāvosānapāramippattā

mula_pali: 250. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṃ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā dasa kasiṇāyatanāni bhāventi. Pathavīkasiṇameko sañjānāti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ advayaṃ appamāṇaṃ; āpokasiṇameko sañjānāti…pe… tejokasiṇameko sañjānāti… vāyokasiṇameko sañjānāti… nīlakasiṇameko sañjānāti… pītakasiṇameko sañjānāti… lohitakasiṇameko sañjānāti… odātakasiṇameko sañjānāti… ākāsakasiṇameko sañjānāti … viññāṇakasiṇameko sañjānāti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ advayaṃ appamāṇaṃ. Tatra ca pana me sāvakā bahū abhiññāvosānapāramippattā viharanti.
mula_english:
250. Again, Udayin, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way to develop the ten *kasiṇa* bases. My disciples, following this path, cultivate the ten *kasiṇāyatanas*.

One contemplates the earth-*kasiṇa* (*pathavīkasiṇa*) above, below, and across, undivided and immeasurable. Another contemplates the water-*kasiṇa* (*āpokasiṇa*)… the fire-*kasiṇa* (*tejokasiṇa*)… the air-*kasiṇa* (*vāyokasiṇa*)… the blue-*kasiṇa* (*nīlakasiṇa*)… the yellow-*kasiṇa* (*pītakasiṇa*)… the red-*kasiṇa* (*lohitakasiṇa*)… the white-*kasiṇa* (*odātakasiṇa*)… the space-*kasiṇa* (*ākāsakasiṇa*)… the consciousness-*kasiṇa* (*viññāṇakasiṇa*) above, below, and across, undivided and immeasurable.

And thereby many disciples of mine abide having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge (*abhiññāvosānapāramippattā*).
commentary_pali: 250. Kasiṇakathāyaṃ sakalaṭṭhena kasiṇāni, tadārammaṇānaṃ dhammānaṃ khettaṭṭhena adhiṭṭhānaṭṭhena vā āyatanāni. Uddhanti upari gaganatalābhimukhaṃ. Adhoti heṭṭhā bhūmitalābhimukhaṃ. Tiriyanti khettamaṇḍalamiva samantā paricchinditvā. Ekacco hi uddhameva kasiṇaṃ vaḍḍheti, ekacco adho, ekacco samantato. Tena tena kāraṇena evaṃ pasāreti ālokamiva rūpadassanakāmo. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘pathavīkasiṇameko sañjānāti uddhaṃadhotiriya’’nti. Advayanti disāanudisāsu advayaṃ. Idaṃ pana ekassa aññabhāvānupagamanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Yathā hi udakaṃ paviṭṭhassa sabbadisāsu udakameva hoti anaññaṃ, evamevaṃ pathavīkasiṇaṃ pathavīkasiṇameva hoti, natthi tassa añño kasiṇasambhedoti. Esa nayo sabbattha. Appamāṇanti idaṃ tassa tassa pharaṇaappamāṇavasena vuttaṃ. Tañhi cetasā pharanto sakalameva pharati, ayamassa ādi, idaṃ majjhanti pamāṇaṃ gaṇhātīti. Viññāṇakasiṇanti cettha kasiṇugghāṭimākāse pavattaṃ viññāṇaṃ. Tattha kasiṇavasena kasiṇugghāṭimākāse, kasiṇugghāṭimākāsavasena tattha pavattaviññāṇe uddhaṃadhotiriyatā veditabbā. Ayamettha saṅkhepo. Kammaṭṭhānabhāvanānayena panetāni pathavīkasiṇādīni vitthārato visuddhimagge vuttāneva. Idhāpi ciṇṇavasibhāveneva abhiññāvosānapāramippattā hontīti veditabbā. Tathā ito anantaresu catūsu jhānesu. Yaṃ panettha vattabbaṃ, taṃ mahāassapurasutte vuttameva.
commentary_english:
250. In the discussion of *kasiṇa*s, the *kasiṇa*s are [understood] in the sense of entirety, the *āyatana*s in the sense of the sphere of the *dhamma*s that have them as their object, or in the sense of foundation.

"Upwards" means facing upwards towards the surface of the sky.

"Downwards" means facing downwards towards the surface of the earth.

"Horizontally" means having completely delimited [it], like a field maṇḍala all around.

For one extends a *kasiṇa* upwards only, another downwards, another all round.

Through that and that cause, thus, he extends [it], like light, desiring to see form.

Therefore, it was said: "One perceives the earth-*kasiṇa* upwards, downwards, horizontally."

"*Advaya*" means non-duality in the directions and intermediate directions.

The word exclusive, however, shows that anyone such state has nothing to do with any other.

Just as there is water and nothing else in all directions for one who is actually in water, so too, the earth *kasiṇa* is the earth *kasiṇa* only; it has nothing in common with any other *kasiṇa*.

This method applies to all the other cases.

"*Appamāṇa*" means it is stated in terms of the measureless aspect of spreading that and that.

Since, indeed, spreading it with his mind, he pervades it entirely, this is his beginning, this the middle, he grasps the measure.

"*Vijñāṇakasiṇa*" means here consciousness which occurs in the space of the *kasiṇa*-opening.

Therein, based on the *kasiṇa*, in the space of the *kasiṇa*-opening, based on the space of the *kasiṇa*-opening, the upwards, downwards, and horizontal nature in the consciousness that occurs there should be understood.

This is in brief here.

But by the method of the practice of meditation, these earth *kasiṇa*s, etc., are stated in detail in the *Visuddhimagga*.

Here too, it should be understood that they attain the perfection of the culmination of direct knowledge through the power of habituation.

Likewise, in the four *jhānas* immediately after this.

Whatever should be stated here, that is stated in the Mahāassapura Sutta itself.

mula_pali:
251. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṃ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā cattāri jhānāni bhāventi. Idhudāyi, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. So imameva kāyaṃ vivekajena pītisukhena abhisandeti parisandeti paripūreti parippharati, nāssa kiñci sabbāvato kāyassa vivekajena pītisukhena apphuṭaṃ hoti. Seyyathāpi, udāyi, dakkho nhāpako nahāpako (sī. pī.) vā nhāpakantevāsī vā kaṃsathāle nhānīyacuṇṇāni nahānīyacuṇṇāni (sī. pī.) ākiritvā udakena paripphosakaṃ paripphosakaṃ sanneyya, sāyaṃ nhānīyapiṇḍi sāssa nahānīyapiṇḍī (sī. syā. kaṃ.) snehānugatā snehapareto santarabāhirā phuṭā snehena na ca pagghariṇī; evameva kho, udāyi, bhikkhu imameva kāyaṃ vivekajena pītisukhena abhisandeti parisandeti paripūreti parippharati, nāssa kiñci sabbāvato kāyassa vivekajena pītisukhena apphuṭaṃ hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, udāyi, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. So imameva kāyaṃ samādhijena pītisukhena abhisandeti parisandeti paripūreti parippharati, nāssa kiñci sabbāvato kāyassa samādhijena pītisukhena apphuṭaṃ hoti . Seyyathāpi, udāyi, udakarahado gambhīro ubbhidodako ubbhitodako (syā. kaṃ. ka.). Tassa nevassa puratthimāya disāya udakassa āyamukhaṃ , na pacchimāya disāya udakassa āyamukhaṃ, na uttarāya disāya udakassa āyamukhaṃ, na dakkhiṇāya disāya udakassa āyamukhaṃ, devo ca na kālena kālaṃ sammā dhāraṃ anuppaveccheyya; atha kho tamhāva udakarahadā sītā vāridhārā ubbhijjitvā tameva udakarahadaṃ sītena vārinā abhisandeyya parisandeyya paripūreyya paripphareyya, nāssa na nesaṃ (sī.) kiñci sabbāvato udakarahadassa sītena vārinā apphuṭaṃ assa. Evameva kho, udāyi, bhikkhu imameva kāyaṃ samādhijena pītisukhena abhisandeti parisandeti paripūreti parippharati, nāssa kiñci sabbāvato kāyassa samādhijena pītisukhena apphuṭaṃ hoti.

ubbhitodako (syā. kaṃ. ka.) na nesaṃ (sī.)

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, udāyi, bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. So imameva kāyaṃ nippītikena sukhena abhisandeti parisandeti paripūreti parippharati, nāssa kiñci sabbāvato kāyassa nippītikena sukhena apphuṭaṃ hoti. Seyyathāpi, udāyi, uppaliniyaṃ vā paduminiyaṃ vā puṇḍarīkiniyaṃ vā appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni udakānuggatāni anto nimuggaposīni, tāni yāva caggā yāva ca mūlā sītena vārinā abhisannāni parisannāni paripūrāni paripphuṭāni, nāssa kiñci sabbāvataṃ, uppalānaṃ vā padumānaṃ vā puṇḍarīkānaṃ vā sītena vārinā apphuṭaṃ assa; evameva kho, udāyi, bhikkhu imameva kāyaṃ nippītikena sukhena abhisandeti parisandeti paripūreti parippharati, nāssa kiñci sabbāvato kāyassa nippītikena sukhena apphuṭaṃ hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, udāyi, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. So imameva kāyaṃ parisuddhena cetasā pariyodātena pharitvā nisinno hoti, nāssa kiñci sabbāvato kāyassa parisuddhena cetasā pariyodātena apphuṭaṃ hoti. Seyyathāpi, udāyi, puriso odātena vatthena sasīsaṃ pārupitvā nisinno assa, nāssa kiñci sabbāvato kāyassa odātena vatthena apphuṭaṃ assa; evameva kho, udāyi, bhikkhu imameva kāyaṃ parisuddhena cetasā pariyodātena pharitvā nisinno hoti, nāssa kiñci sabbāvato kāyassa parisuddhena cetasā pariyodātena apphuṭaṃ hoti. Tatra ca pana me sāvakā bahū abhiññāvosānapāramippattā viharanti.
mula_english:
251. “Again, Udayin, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way to practice, and through having practiced, my disciples develop the four *jhānas*.

Here, Udayin, a *bhikkhu*, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters upon and abides in the first *jhāna*, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion.

He drenches, steeps, saturates, and suffuses his body with this rapture and happiness born of seclusion, so that there is no part of his entire body which is not suffused by this rapture and happiness.

Just as, Udayin, a skilled bath attendant or a bath attendant’s apprentice, having poured bath powder into a metal basin, sprinkles it with water and kneads it gradually, so that the ball of bath powder becomes moistened, saturated, and pervaded inside and out, yet does not trickle; even so, Udayin, a *bhikkhu* drenches, steeps, saturates, and suffuses this body with the rapture and happiness born of seclusion, so that there is no part of his entire body which is not suffused by this rapture and happiness.

“Again, Udayin, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought, a *bhikkhu* enters and abides in the second *jhāna*…

He drenches, steeps, saturates, and suffuses his body with the rapture and happiness born of concentration (*samādhi*), so that there is no part of his entire body which is not suffused by this rapture and happiness.

Just as, Udayin, there might be a deep lake with an upwelling of water.

It would have no inflow from the east, west, north, or south, and the sky would not provide timely showers of rain. Yet a cool stream of water would well up from within that lake, drenching, steeping, saturating, and suffusing it, so that there would be no part of the entire lake not suffused with the cool water.

Even so, Udayin, a *bhikkhu* drenches, steeps, saturates, and suffuses this body with the rapture and happiness born of concentration (*samādhi*), so that there is no part of his entire body which is not suffused by this rapture and happiness.

“Again, Udayin, with the fading away of rapture, a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the third *jhāna*.

He drenches, steeps, saturates, and suffuses his body with happiness free from rapture, so that there is no part of his entire body which is not suffused by this happiness free from rapture.

Just as, Udayin, in a pond of blue lotuses, red lotuses, or white lotuses, some lotuses are born in the water, grow in the water, thrive without rising out of the water, and are nourished from within. Cool water drenches, steeps, saturates, and suffuses them from their tips to their roots, so that there is no part of all those lotuses not suffused by the cool water. Even so, Udayin, a *bhikkhu* drenches, steeps, saturates, and suffuses this body with happiness free from rapture, so that there is no part of his entire body which is not suffused by this happiness free from rapture.

“Again, Udayin, with the abandoning of pleasure and with the abandoning of pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the fourth *jhāna*, which has neither pain nor pleasure and purity of mindfulness due to equanimity (*upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ*).

He sits, having pervaded this body with a pure, bright mind, so that there is no part of his entire body not suffused with the pure, bright mind.

Just as, Udayin, a man might be sitting wrapped from head to foot in a white cloth, so that there would be no part of his entire body not covered by the white cloth.
...unpervaded would be. Just so, Udāyi, a *bhikkhu* pervades this very body with a pure, bright mind (*parisuddhena cetasā pariyodātena*), so that there is no part of his whole body unpervaded by the pure mind.
And thereby many disciples of mine abide having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge (*abhiññāvosānapāramippattā*).

mula_pali: 252. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṃ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā evaṃ pajānanti – ‘ayaṃ kho me kāyo rūpī cātumahābhūtiko mātāpettikasambhavo odanakummāsūpacayo aniccucchādanaparimaddanabhedanaviddhaṃsanadhammo; idañca pana me viññāṇaṃ ettha sitaṃ ettha paṭibaddhaṃ’. Seyyathāpi, udāyi, maṇi veḷuriyo subho jātimā aṭṭhaṃso suparikammakato accho vippasanno sabbākārasampanno; tatridaṃ suttaṃ āvutaṃ nīlaṃ vā pītaṃ vā lohitaṃ vā odātaṃ vā paṇḍusuttaṃ vā. Tamenaṃ cakkhumā puriso hatthe karitvā paccavekkheyya – ‘ayaṃ kho maṇi veḷuriyo subho jātimā aṭṭhaṃso suparikammakato accho vippasanno sabbākārasampanno; tatridaṃ suttaṃ āvutaṃ nīlaṃ vā pītaṃ vā lohitaṃ vā odātaṃ vā paṇḍusuttaṃ vā’ti. Evameva kho, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṃ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā evaṃ pajānanti – ‘ayaṃ kho me kāyo rūpī cātumahābhūtiko mātāpettikasambhavo odanakummāsūpacayo aniccucchādanaparimaddanabhedanaviddhaṃsanadhammo; idañca pana me viññāṇaṃ ettha sitaṃ ettha paṭibaddha’nti. Tatra ca pana me sāvakā bahū abhiññāvosānapāramippattā viharanti.
mula_english:
252. Again, Udayin, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, and having followed that way my disciples understand thus: ‘This body of mine is material (rūpī), composed of the four great elements (cātumahābhūtiko), born of mother and father (mātāpettikasambhavo), built up of rice and porridge (odanakummāsūpacayo), is subject to impermanence, to being worn and rubbed away, to dissolution and disintegration (aniccucchādanaparimaddanabhedanaviddhaṃsanadhammo); and this consciousness (viññāṇaṃ) of mine is supported by it and bound up with it.’

Just as, Udayin, there might be a beautiful beryl gem (maṇi veḷuriyo) of fine quality, eight-faceted (aṭṭhaṃso), well cut (suparikammakato), clear (accho) and transparent (vippasanno), endowed with all good qualities (sabbākārasampanno); and through it a thread (suttaṃ) might be strung, blue (nīlaṃ) or yellow (pītaṃ) or red (lohitaṃ) or white (odātaṃ) or brown (paṇḍusuttaṃ).

A man with good sight, taking it in his hand, might review it thus: “This is a beautiful beryl gem (maṇi veḷuriyo) of fine quality, eight-faceted (aṭṭhaṃso), well cut (suparikammakato), clear (accho) and transparent (vippasanno), endowed with all good qualities (sabbākārasampanno); and through it a thread (suttaṃ) is strung, blue (nīlaṃ) or yellow (pītaṃ) or red (lohitaṃ) or white (odātaṃ) or brown (paṇḍusuttaṃ).”

So too, Udayin, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, and having followed that way my disciples understand thus: ‘This body of mine is material (rūpī), composed of the four great elements (cātumahābhūtiko), born of mother and father (mātāpettikasambhavo), built up of rice and porridge (odanakummāsūpacayo), is subject to impermanence, to being worn and rubbed away, to dissolution and disintegration (aniccucchādanaparimaddanabhedanaviddhaṃsanadhammo); and this consciousness (viññāṇaṃ) of mine is supported by it and bound up with it.’

And thereby many disciples of mine abide having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge (abhiññāvosānapāramippattā).
commentary_pali:
252. Vipassanāñāṇe pana rūpītiādīnamattho vuttoyeva. Ettha sitamettha paṭibaddhanti ettha cātumahābhūtike kāye nissitañca paṭibaddhañca. Subhoti sundaro. Jātimāti suparisuddhaākarasamuṭṭhito. Suparikammakatoti suṭṭhu kataparikammo apanītapāsāṇasakkharo. Acchoti tanucchavi. Vippasannoti suṭṭhu vippasanno. Sabbākārasampannoti dhovana vedhanādīhi sabbehi ākārehi sampanno. Nīlantiādīhi vaṇṇasampattiṃ dasseti. Tādisañhi āvutaṃ pākaṭaṃ hoti.

Evameva khoti ettha evaṃ upamāsaṃsandanaṃ veditabbaṃ – maṇi viya hi karajakāyo. Āvutasuttaṃ viya vipassanāñāṇaṃ. Cakkhumā puriso viya vipassanālābhī bhikkhu. Hatthe karitvā paccavekkhato ‘‘ayaṃ kho maṇī’’ti maṇino āvibhūtakālo viya vipassanāñāṇaṃ abhinīharitvā nisinnassa bhikkhuno cātumahābhūtikakāyassa āvibhūtakālo. ‘‘Tatridaṃ suttaṃ āvuta’’nti suttassa āvibhūtakālo viya vipassanāñāṇaṃ abhinīharitvā nisinnassa bhikkhuno tadārammaṇānaṃ phassapañcamakānaṃ vā sabbacittacetasikānaṃ vā vipassanāñāṇasseva vā āvibhūtakāloti.

Evameva kho

Kiṃ panetaṃ ñāṇassa āvibhūtaṃ, puggalassāti. Ñāṇassa, tassa pana āvibhāvattā puggalassa āvibhūtāva honti. Idañca vipassanāñāṇaṃ maggassa anantaraṃ, evaṃ santepi yasmā abhiññāvāre āraddhe etassa antarāvāro natthi, tasmā idheva dassitaṃ. Yasmā ca aniccādivasena akatasammasanassa dibbāya sotadhātuyā bheravasaddaṃ suṇanto pubbenivāsānussatiyā bherave khandhe anussarato dibbena cakkhunā bheravarūpaṃ passato bhayasantāso uppajjati, na aniccādivasena katasammasanassa, tasmā abhiññāpattassa bhayavinodakahetusampādanatthampi idaṃ idheva dassitaṃ. Idhāpi arahattavaseneva abhiññāvosānapāramippattatā veditabbā.
commentary_english:
252. The meaning of "possessing form," etc., has already been stated in connection with insight knowledge (*vipassanāñāṇa*).

Here, in "[where] it is situated, [where] it is bound," "it is situated and bound" refers to the body composed of the four great elements.

"Beautiful" (*subho*) means lovely.

"Of good birth" (*jātimā*) means arising from a very pure mine.

"Well-prepared" (*suparikammakato*) means well-refined, with gravel and stones removed.

"Clear" (*accho*) means having a thin skin.

"Bright" (*vippasanno*) means very bright.

"Possessing all characteristics" (*sabbākārasampanno*) means possessing all characteristics such as washing and piercing.

With "blue" (*nīla*), etc., it shows the attainment of color.

For such a thread is visible and apparent.

Just as: here, this comparison should be understood—the body produced by karma is like a gem. Insight knowledge is like the thread running through it. The *bhikkhu* who has gained insight is like the man with keen sight. The time when the man takes the gem in his hand, reviews it, and clearly knows, "This is a gem"—this is like the time when the *bhikkhu* is sitting, having directed his mind to insight knowledge, and the body composed of the four great elements becomes clear to him. The time when it becomes clear to the man, "This is a thread running through it"—this is like the time when the *bhikkhu* is sitting, having directed his mind to insight knowledge, and the time when the five aggregates beginning with contact, or all mental states, or even insight knowledge itself, become clear.

Just as, what is it that becomes clear, the knowledge or the person? It is the knowledge; however, because of the manifestation of that, it is as if the person becomes manifest.

And this insight knowledge is immediately after the path. Even so, it is shown here because there would be no intermediate place for it once the section on the direct knowledges (*abhiññā*) has begun.

And because fear and terror arise in one who, not having made a proper determination based on impermanence, etc., hears a terrifying sound with the divine ear-element, or recollects terrifying aggregates with the recollection of former abodes, or sees a terrifying form with the divine eye, but not in one who has made a proper determination based on impermanence, etc., therefore, this is shown here in order to accomplish the cause for dispelling fear in one who has attained direct knowledge.

Here also, it should be understood that perfection in the *pāramī* is attained only by way of *arahatship* at the end of the direct knowledges.

mula_pali: 253. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṃ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā imamhā kāyā aññaṃ kāyaṃ abhinimminanti rūpiṃ manomayaṃ sabbaṅgapaccaṅgiṃ ahīnindriyaṃ. Seyyathāpi, udāyi, puriso muñjamhā īsikaṃ pabbāheyya; tassa evamassa – ‘ayaṃ muñjo, ayaṃ īsikā; añño muñjo, aññā īsikā; muñjamhātveva īsikā pabbāḷhā’ti. Seyyathā vā panudāyi, puriso asiṃ kosiyā pabbāheyya; tassa evamassa – ‘ayaṃ asi, ayaṃ kosi; añño asi aññā kosi; kosiyātveva asi pabbāḷho’ti. Seyyathā vā, panudāyi , puriso ahiṃ karaṇḍā uddhareyya; tassa evamassa – ‘ayaṃ ahi, ayaṃ karaṇḍo; añño ahi, añño karaṇḍo; karaṇḍātveva ahi ubbhato’ti. Evameva kho, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṃ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā imamhā kāyā aññaṃ kāyaṃ abhinimminanti rūpiṃ manomayaṃ sabbaṅgapaccaṅgiṃ ahīnindriyaṃ. Tatra ca pana me sāvakā bahū abhiññāvosānapāramippattā viharanti.
commentary_pali:
253. Manomayiddhiyaṃ ciṇṇavasitāya. Tattha manomayanti manena nibbattaṃ. Sabbaṅgapaccaṅginti sabbehi aṅgehi ca paccaṅgehi ca samannāgataṃ. Ahīnindriyanti saṇṭhānavasena avikalindriyaṃ. Iddhimatā nimmitarūpañhi sace iddhimā odāto, tampi odātaṃ. Sace aviddhakaṇṇo, tampi aviddhakaṇṇanti evaṃ sabbākārehi tena sadisameva hoti. Muñjamhā īsikantiādi upamattayampi taṃ sadisabhāvadassanatthameva vuttaṃ. Muñjasadisā eva hi tassa anto īsikā hoti. Kosasadisoyeva asi, vaṭṭāya kosiyā vaṭṭaṃ asimeva pakkhipanti, patthaṭāya patthaṭaṃ.

Karaṇḍāti idampi ahikañcukassa nāmaṃ, na vilīvakaraṇḍakassa. Ahikañcuko hi ahinā sadisova hoti. Tattha kiñcāpi ‘‘puriso ahiṃ karaṇḍā uddhareyyā’’ti hatthena uddharamāno viya dassito, atha kho cittenevassa uddharaṇaṃ veditabbaṃ. Ayañhi ahi nāma sajātiyaṃ ṭhito, kaṭṭhantaraṃ vā rukkhantaraṃ vā nissāya, tacato sarīranikkaḍḍhanapayogasaṅkhātena thāmena, sarīraṃ khādamānaṃ viya purāṇatacaṃ jigucchantoti imehi catūhi kāraṇehi sayameva kañcukaṃ jahāti, na sakkā tato aññena uddharituṃ. Tasmā cittena uddharaṇaṃ sandhāya idaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Iti muñjādisadisaṃ imassa bhikkhuno sarīraṃ, īsikādisadisaṃ nimmitarūpanti idamettha opammasaṃsandanaṃ. Nimmānavidhānaṃ panettha parato ca iddhividhādipañcaabhiññākathā sabbākārena visuddhimagge vitthāritāti tattha vuttanayeneva veditabbā. Upamāmattameva hi idha adhikaṃ.

Karaṇḍā visuddhimagge

Tattha chekakumbhakārādayo viya iddhividhañāṇalābhī bhikkhu daṭṭhabbo. Suparikammakatamattikādayo viya iddhividhañāṇaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Icchiticchitabhājanavikatiādikaraṇaṃ viya tassa bhikkhuno vikubbanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Idhāpi ciṇṇavasitāvaseneva abhiññāvosānapāramippattatā veditabbā. Tathā ito parāsu catūsu abhiññāsu.
commentary_english:
253. In the case of the mind-madeiddhi, due to the practice of mastery.

There, *manomaya* means produced by the mind.

*Sabbaṅgapaccaṅgi* means complete with all its limbs and secondary limbs.

*Ahīnindriya* means unimpaired faculties through the power of [its] configuration.

For if the possessor of supernormal power is white, then the form he creates will also be white.

If his earlobes are unpierced, the form will also have earlobes which are unpierced. Thus it is similar to him in all respects.

*Muñjamhā Īsika* and so on, even in the simile, that is said only to show the similarity of condition.

For the reed *īsika* inside is similar to the *muñja*.

The sword is similar to its scabbard, since they put a round sword into a round scabbard and a flat sword into a flat scabbard.

*Karaṇḍā* means this is also a name for the snake's slough ( *ahikañcuka*), not for a *vilīvakaraṇḍaka*.

The snake’s slough ( *ahikañcuka*) is similar to the snake.

Though in the text it is said, “Suppose a man were to pull a snake out from its slough ( *karaṇḍā*),” as if he were to pull it out with his hand, we should understand that he extracts it mentally.

For this snake, abiding in its own species, relying on a log or a tree, by its strength, known as the effort of dragging its body out from the skin, feeling disgust towards the old skin as if it were devouring its body, abandons its slough by itself alone, through these four means, no one can pull it out by other means.

Therefore, it should be understood that this is said in reference to the mental extraction of the snake.

Thus, the bhikkhu’s body is similar to the *muñja* etc., and the created form is similar to the reed (*īsika*) etc.; this is the connection of simile here.

The method of creation, moreover, the teaching on the five kinds of direct knowledge, beginning with the modes of supernormal power, has been extensively taught in all ways in the *Visuddhimagga*; it should be understood in accordance with the method stated there.

Here, only the similes are additional.

*Karaṇḍā*

*Visuddhimagga*

There, the bhikkhu who has gained knowledge of the modes of supernormal power should be seen like skilled potters etc.

The well-prepared clay, etc., is like the knowledge of the modes of supernormal power.

The making of whatever kind of vessel, etc., he might desire is like the bhikkhu’s transformations.

Here also, it should be understood that the attainment of the perfection of the exhaustion of direct knowledge is due to the power of mastery through habituation.

Likewise, in the four kinds of direct knowledge beyond this.

mula_pali: 254. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṃ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhonti – ekopi hutvā bahudhā honti, bahudhāpi hutvā eko hoti; āvibhāvaṃ, tirobhāvaṃ; tirokuṭṭaṃ tiropākāraṃ tiropabbataṃ asajjamānā gacchanti, seyyathāpi ākāse; pathaviyāpi ummujjanimujjaṃ karonti, seyyathāpi udake; udakepi abhijjamāne abhijjamānā (ka.) gacchanti, seyyathāpi pathaviyaṃ; ākāsepi pallaṅkena kamanti, seyyathāpi pakkhī sakuṇo; imepi candimasūriye evaṃmahiddhike evaṃmahānubhāve pāṇinā parimasanti parimajjanti, yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vattenti. Seyyathāpi, udāyi, dakkho kumbhakāro vā kumbhakārantevāsī vā suparikammakatāya mattikāya yaṃ yadeva bhājanavikatiṃ ākaṅkheyya taṃ tadeva kareyya abhinipphādeyya; seyyathā vā panudāyi, dakkho dantakāro vā dantakārantevāsī vā suparikammakatasmiṃ dantasmiṃ yaṃ yadeva dantavikatiṃ ākaṅkheyya taṃ tadeva kareyya abhinipphādeyya; seyyathā vā panudāyi, dakkho suvaṇṇakāro vā suvaṇṇakārantevāsī vā suparikammakatasmiṃ suvaṇṇasmiṃ yaṃ yadeva suvaṇṇavikatiṃ ākaṅkheyya taṃ tadeva kareyya abhinipphādeyya. Evameva kho, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṃ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhonti – ekopi hutvā bahudhā honti, bahudhāpi hutvā eko hoti; āvibhāvaṃ, tirobhāvaṃ; tirokuṭṭaṃ tiropākāraṃ tiropabbataṃ asajjamānā gacchanti, seyyathāpi ākāse; pathaviyāpi ummujjanimujjaṃ karonti, seyyathāpi udake; udakepi abhijjamāne gacchanti , seyyathāpi pathaviyaṃ; ākāsepi pallaṅkena kamanti, seyyathāpi pakkhī sakuṇo; imepi candimasūriye evaṃmahiddhike evaṃmahānubhāve pāṇinā parimasanti parimajjanti, yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vattenti. Tatra ca pana me sāvakā bahū abhiññāvosānapāramippattā viharanti.
mula_english:
254. Again, Udayin, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, whereby my disciples, having practiced, experience various kinds of supernormal powers ( *iddhividha*): having been one, they become many; having been many, they become one; they appear and vanish; they go unhindered through walls (*tirokuṭṭaṃ*), through enclosures (*tiropākāraṃ*), through mountains (*tiropabbataṃ*), as though through space (*ākāse*); they dive in and out of the earth (*pathaviyā*) as though it were water (*udake*); they walk on water (*udake*) without sinking as though it were earth (*pathaviyaṃ*); seated cross-legged (*pallaṅkena*), they travel in space (*ākāse*) like a bird (*pakkhī sakuṇo*); with their hands (*pāṇinā*) they touch and stroke the moon and sun (*candimasūriye*), so powerful and mighty; they wield bodily mastery (*kāyena vasaṃ vattenti*) even as far as the Brahma-world (*brahmalokā*).

Just as, Udayin, a skilled potter (*kumbhakāro*) or his apprentice (*kumbhakārantevāsī*) might create and fashion out of well-prepared clay (*mattikāya*) any shape of pot (*bhājanavikatiṃ*) he wished (*ākaṅkheyya*); or just as, Udayin, a skilled ivory-worker (*dantakāro*) or his apprentice (*dantakārantevāsī*) might create and fashion out of well-prepared ivory (*dantasmiṃ*) any ivory work of art (*dantavikatiṃ*) he wished (*ākaṅkheyya*); or just as, Udayin, a skilled goldsmith (*suvaṇṇakāro*) or his apprentice (*suvaṇṇakārantevāsī*) might create and fashion out of well-prepared gold (*suvaṇṇasmiṃ*) any gold work of art (*suvaṇṇavikatiṃ*) he wished (*ākaṅkheyya*).

So too, Udayin, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, whereby my disciples, having practiced, experience various kinds of supernormal powers (*iddhividhaṃ paccanubhonti*): having been one, they become many; having been many, they become one; they appear (*āvibhāvaṃ*) and vanish (*tirobhāvaṃ*); they go unhindered through walls (*tirokuṭṭaṃ*), through enclosures (*tiropākāraṃ*), through mountains (*tiropabbataṃ*) as though through space (*ākāse*); they dive in and out of the earth (*pathaviyā*) as though it were water (*udake*); they walk on water (*udake*) as though it were earth (*pathaviyaṃ*); seated cross-legged (*pallaṅkena*), they travel in space (*ākāse*) like a bird (*pakkhī sakuṇo*); with their hands (*pāṇinā*) they touch and stroke the moon and sun (*candimasūriye*), so powerful and mighty; they wield bodily mastery (*kāyena vasaṃ vattenti*) even as far as the Brahma-world (*brahmalokā*).

And thereby many disciples of mine abide having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge (*abhiññāvosānapāramippattā*).

mula_pali: 255. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṃ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā dibbāya sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya ubho sadde suṇanti – dibbe ca mānuse ca, ye dūre santike ca. Seyyathāpi, udāyi, balavā saṅkhadhamo appakasireneva cātuddisā viññāpeyya; evameva kho, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṃ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā dibbāya sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya ubho sadde suṇanti – dibbe ca mānuse ca, ye dūre santike ca. Tatra ca pana me sāvakā bahū abhiññāvosānapāramippattā viharanti.
mula_english:
255. Again, Udayin, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way whereby, having practiced, my disciples with the divine ear element (dibbāya sotadhātuyā), which is purified (visuddhāya) and surpasses the human (atikkantamānusikāya), hear both kinds of sounds (ubho sadde suṇanti)—the divine and the human (dibbe ca mānuse ca), those that are far as well as near (ye dūre santike ca).

Just as, Udayin, a vigorous trumpeter might make himself heard without difficulty in the four quarters; so too, Udayin, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way whereby, having practiced, my disciples with the divine ear element (dibbāya sotadhātuyā), which is purified (visuddhāya) and surpasses the human (atikkantamānusikāya), hear both kinds of sounds (ubho sadde suṇanti)—the divine and the human (dibbe ca mānuse ca), those that are far as well as near (ye dūre santike ca).

And thereby many disciples of mine abide having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge (abhiññāvosānapāramippattā).
commentary_pali: 255. Tattha dibbasotadhātuupamāyaṃ saṅkhadhamoti saṅkhadhamako. Appakasirenevāti niddukkheneva. Viññāpeyyāti jānāpeyya. Tattha evaṃ cātuddisā viññāpente saṅkhadhamake ‘‘saṅkhasaddo aya’’nti vavatthāpentānaṃ sattānaṃ tassa saṅkhasaddassa āvibhūtakālo viya yogino dūrasantikabhedānaṃ dibbānañceva mānusakānañca saddānaṃ āvibhūtakālo daṭṭhabbo.
commentary_english:
There:
In relation to the simile of the divine ear-element: *saṅkhadhamo* means *saṅkhadhamako*.
*appakasirenevā* means just like *niddukkheneva* (without difficulty).
*viññāpeyyā* means *jānāpeyya* (he should make known).
There, when making known in all four directions to the *saṅkhadhamakas*, the time when the sound of the conch shell becomes manifest to those beings who ascertain "this is the sound of the conch shell," is like the time when the sounds—both divine (*dibbānañceva*) and human (*mānusakānañca*)—of the yogin, distinguished by distance and proximity, become manifest. This should be understood.

mula_pali: 256. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṃ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajānanti – sarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ ‘sarāgaṃ citta’nti pajānanti, vītarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ ‘vītarāgaṃ citta’nti pajānanti; sadosaṃ vā cittaṃ ‘sadosaṃ citta’nti pajānanti, vītadosaṃ vā cittaṃ ‘vītadosaṃ citta’nti pajānanti; samohaṃ vā cittaṃ ‘samohaṃ citta’nti pajānanti, vītamohaṃ vā cittaṃ ‘vītamohaṃ citta’nti pajānanti; saṃkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ ‘saṅkhittaṃ citta’nti pajānanti, vikkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ ‘vikkhittaṃ citta’nti pajānanti; mahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ ‘mahaggataṃ citta’nti pajānanti, amahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ ‘amahaggataṃ citta’nti pajānanti; sauttaraṃ vā cittaṃ ‘sauttaraṃ citta’nti pajānanti, anuttaraṃ vā cittaṃ ‘anuttaraṃ citta’nti pajānanti; samāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ ‘samāhitaṃ citta’nti pajānanti, asamāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ ‘asamāhitaṃ citta’nti pajānanti; vimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ ‘vimuttaṃ citta’nti pajānanti, avimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ ‘avimuttaṃ citta’nti pajānanti. Seyyathāpi, udāyi, itthī vā puriso vā daharo yuvā maṇḍanakajātiko ādāse vā parisuddhe pariyodāte acche vā udakapatte sakaṃ mukhanimittaṃ paccavekkhamāno sakaṇikaṃ vā ‘sakaṇika’nti sakaṇikaṅgaṃ vā sakaṇikaṅganti (sī.) jāneyya , akaṇikaṃ vā ‘akaṇika’nti akaṇikaṅgaṃ vā akaṇikaṅganti (sī.) jāneyya; evameva kho, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṃ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajānanti – sarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ ‘sarāgaṃ citta’nti pajānanti, vītarāgaṃ vā cittaṃ…pe… sadosaṃ vā cittaṃ… vītadosaṃ vā cittaṃ… samohaṃ vā cittaṃ… vītamohaṃ vā cittaṃ… saṅkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ… vikkhittaṃ vā cittaṃ… mahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ… amahaggataṃ vā cittaṃ… sauttaraṃ vā cittaṃ… anuttaraṃ vā cittaṃ… samāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ… asamāhitaṃ vā cittaṃ… vimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ… avimuttaṃ vā cittaṃ ‘avimuttaṃ citta’nti pajānanti. Tatra ca pana me sāvakā bahū abhiññāvosānapāramippattā viharanti.
mula_english:
Again, Udayin, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, according to which my disciples, encompassing with their own minds the minds of other beings and other persons, understand a mind with lust ( *sarāgaṃ citta*) as 'a mind with lust' (*sarāgaṃ cittaṃ*), and a mind without lust ( *vītarāgaṃ citta*) as 'a mind without lust' (*vītarāgaṃ cittaṃ*); they understand a mind with hatred (*sadosaṃ cittaṃ*) as 'a mind with hatred' (*sadosaṃ cittaṃ*), and a mind without hatred (*vītadosaṃ cittaṃ*) as 'a mind without hatred' (*vītadosaṃ cittaṃ*); they understand a mind with delusion (*samohaṃ cittaṃ*) as 'a mind with delusion' (*samohaṃ cittaṃ*), they understand a mind without delusion (*vītamohaṃ cittaṃ*) as 'a mind without delusion' (*vītamohaṃ cittaṃ*); they understand a contracted mind (*saṃkhittaṃ cittaṃ*) as 'a contracted mind' (*saṃkhittaṃ cittaṃ*), and a distracted mind (*vikkhittaṃ cittaṃ*) as 'a distracted mind' (*vikkhittaṃ cittaṃ*); they understand an exalted mind (*mahaggataṃ cittaṃ*) as 'an exalted mind' (*mahaggataṃ cittaṃ*), and an unexalted mind (*amahaggataṃ cittaṃ*) as 'an unexalted mind' (*amahaggataṃ cittaṃ*); they understand a surpassable mind (*sauttaraṃ cittaṃ*) as 'a surpassable mind' (*sauttaraṃ cittaṃ*), and an unsurpassed mind (*anuttaraṃ cittaṃ*) as 'an unsurpassed mind' (*anuttaraṃ cittaṃ*); they understand a concentrated mind (*samāhitaṃ cittaṃ*) as 'a concentrated mind' (*samāhitaṃ cittaṃ*), and an unconcentrated mind (*asamāhitaṃ cittaṃ*) as 'an unconcentrated mind' (*asamāhitaṃ cittaṃ*); they understand a liberated mind (*vimuttaṃ cittaṃ*) as 'a liberated mind' (*vimuttaṃ cittaṃ*), and an unliberated mind (*avimuttaṃ cittaṃ*) as 'an unliberated mind' (*avimuttaṃ cittaṃ*).

Just as, Udayin, a woman or a man, young, youthful, and fond of ornaments, viewing the image of his or her own face in a clean, bright mirror or in a bowl of clear water, would know if there were a spot thus: ‘There is a spot,’ or would know if there were no spot thus: ‘There is no spot’; so too, Udayin, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, according to which my disciples, encompassing with their own minds the minds of other beings and other persons, understand a mind with lust ( *sarāgaṃ citta*) as 'a mind with lust' (*sarāgaṃ cittaṃ*)... they understand a mind with hatred (*sadosaṃ cittaṃ*)... a mind without hatred (*vītadosaṃ cittaṃ*)... a mind with delusion (*samohaṃ cittaṃ*)... a mind without delusion (*vītamohaṃ cittaṃ*)... a contracted mind (*saṃkhittaṃ cittaṃ*)... a distracted mind (*vikkhittaṃ cittaṃ*)... an exalted mind (*mahaggataṃ cittaṃ*)... an unexalted mind (*amahaggataṃ cittaṃ*)... a surpassable mind (*sauttaraṃ cittaṃ*)... an unsurpassed mind (*anuttaraṃ cittaṃ*)... a concentrated mind (*samāhitaṃ cittaṃ*)... an unconcentrated mind (*asamāhitaṃ cittaṃ*)... a liberated mind (*vimuttaṃ cittaṃ*)... and an unliberated mind (*avimuttaṃ cittaṃ*) as 'an unliberated mind' (*avimuttaṃ cittaṃ*).

And thereby many disciples of mine abide having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge (*abhiññāvosānapāramippattā*).
commentary_pali: 256. Cetopariyañāṇa-upamāyaṃ daharoti taruṇo. Yuvāti yobbanena samannāgato. Maṇḍanakajātikoti yuvāpi samāno na alasiyo kiliṭṭhavatthasarīro, atha kho maṇḍanakapakatiko, divasassa dve tayo vāre nhāyitvā suddhavattha-paridahana-alaṅkārakaraṇasīloti attho. Sakaṇikanti kāḷatilakavaṅka-mukhadūsipīḷakādīnaṃ aññatarena sadosaṃ. Tattha yathā tassa mukhanimittaṃ paccavekkhato mukhadoso pākaṭo hoti, evaṃ cetopariyañāṇāya cittaṃ abhinīharitvā nisinnassa bhikkhuno paresaṃ soḷasavidhaṃ cittaṃ pākaṭaṃ hotīti veditabbaṃ. Pubbenivāsaupamādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ mahāassapure vuttameva.
commentary_english: 256. *daharo* means young (*taruṇo*). *yuvā* means endowed with youth (*yobbanena samannāgato*). *maṇḍanakajātiko* means even when young (*yuvāpi samāno*), he is not lazy (*na alasiyo*), with a body [covered by] soiled clothes (*kiliṭṭhavatthasarīro*), but rather (*atha kho*) is one whose nature is to adorn himself (*maṇḍanakapakatiko*), [he is] in the habit of bathing (*nhāyitvā*) two or three times a day (*divasassa dve tayo vāre*), putting on clean clothes (*suddhavattha-paridahana*) and adorning himself (*alaṅkārakaraṇasīloti attho*). *sakaṇika* [means] with blemishes (*sadosaṃ*) by one of the black marks, moles, crooked-faced pustules, etc. (*kāḷatilakavaṅka-mukhadūsipīḷakādīnaṃ aññatarena*). Just as when someone examines the mark on his face (*tattha yathā tassa mukhanimittaṃ paccavekkhato*), the defect in the face becomes evident (*mukhadoso pākaṭo hoti*), so too (*evaṃ*) it should be understood (*veditabbaṃ*) that when a *bhikkhu* sits having directed his mind towards the knowledge of encompassing the minds of others (*cetopariyañāṇāya cittaṃ abhinīharitvā nisinnassa bhikkhuno*), the sixteen kinds of minds of others become evident (*paresam soḷasavidhaṃ cittaṃ pākaṭaṃ hoti iti*). Everything that has to be said about past dwellings and comparisons (*pubbenivāsaupamādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ*), all that (*taṃ sabbaṃ*) has already been said in Mahāassapura (*mahāassapure vuttameva*).

mula_pali: 257. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṃ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussaranti, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṃsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi jātisatasahassampi, anekepi saṃvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe – ‘amutrāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṃ; tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapanno’ti. Iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. Seyyathāpi, udāyi, puriso sakamhā gāmā aññaṃ gāmaṃ gaccheyya, tamhāpi gāmā aññaṃ gāmaṃ gaccheyya; so tamhā gāmā sakaṃyeva gāmaṃ paccāgaccheyya; tassa evamassa – ‘ahaṃ kho sakamhā gāmā aññaṃ gāmaṃ agacchiṃ, tatra evaṃ aṭṭhāsiṃ evaṃ nisīdiṃ evaṃ abhāsiṃ evaṃ tuṇhī ahosiṃ; tamhāpi gāmā amuṃ gāmaṃ agacchiṃ, tatrāpi evaṃ aṭṭhāsiṃ evaṃ nisīdiṃ evaṃ abhāsiṃ evaṃ tuṇhī ahosiṃ, somhi tamhā gāmā sakaṃyeva gāmaṃ paccāgato’ti. Evameva kho, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṃ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussaranti, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussaranti. Tatra ca pana me sāvakā bahū abhiññāvosānapāramippattā viharanti.
mula_english:
257. “Again, Udayin, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way (paṭipadā) whereby, having practiced, my disciples recollect their manifold past lives (anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussaranti), that is, one birth (ekampi jātiṃ), two births (dvepi jātiyo), three births (tissopi jātiyo), four births (catassopi jātiyo), five births (pañcapi jātiyo), ten births (dasapi jātiyo), twenty births (vīsampi jātiyo), thirty births (tiṃsampi jātiyo), forty births (cattālīsampi jātiyo), fifty births (paññāsampi jātiyo), a hundred births (jātisatampi), a thousand births (jātisahassampi), a hundred thousand births (jātisatasahassampi), many aeons of world-contraction (anekepi saṃvaṭṭakappe), many aeons of world-expansion (anekepi vivaṭṭakappe), many aeons of world-contraction and expansion (anekepi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe): ‘There I was so named (evaṃnāmo), of such a clan (evaṃgotto), with such an appearance (evaṃvaṇṇo), such was my food (evamāhāro), such my experience of pleasure and pain (evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī), such my life-term (evamāyupariyanto). Passing away from there (so tato cuto), I arose there (amutra udapādiṃ); there I was so named (evaṃnāmo), of such a clan (evaṃgotto), with such an appearance (evaṃvaṇṇo), such was my food (evamāhāro), such my experience of pleasure and pain (evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī), such my life-term (evamāyupariyanto). Passing away from there, I was reborn here (idhūpapanno).’

Thus he recollects his numerous past lives (anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati) in their modes and their details (sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ).

Just as, Udayin, a man might go from his own village (sakamhā gāmā) to another village (aññaṃ gāmaṃ), and from that village (tamhāpi gāmā) to another village (aññaṃ gāmaṃ); and then from that village (tamhā gāmā) he might return to his own village (sakaṃyeva gāmaṃ paccāgaccheyya); he might think: ‘I went from my own village (sakamhā gāmā) to that other village (aññaṃ gāmaṃ), and there I stood (aṭṭhāsiṃ) in such a way, sat (nisīdiṃ) in such a way, spoke (abhāsiṃ) in such a way, kept silent (tuṇhī ahosiṃ) in such a way; and from that village (tamhāpi gāmā) I went to that other village (amuṃ gāmaṃ), and there too I stood (aṭṭhāsiṃ) in such a way, sat (nisīdiṃ) in such a way, spoke (abhāsiṃ) in such a way, kept silent (tuṇhī ahosiṃ) in such a way, and from that village (tamhā gāmā) I have just returned to my own village (sakaṃyeva gāmaṃ paccāgato.’

So too, Udayin, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way (paṭipadā) whereby, having practiced, my disciples recollect their manifold past lives (anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussaranti), that is, one birth (ekampi jātiṃ)… and so on… Thus he recollects his numerous past lives (anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussaranti) in their modes and their details (sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ).

And thereby many disciples of mine abide having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge (abhiññāvosānapāramippattā viharanti).

mula_pali: 258. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṃ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passanti cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānanti – ‘ime vata bhonto sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannā; ime vā pana bhonto sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā vacīsucaritena samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā’ti. Iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passanti cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānanti. Seyyathāpi, udāyi, dve agārā sadvārā sannadvārā (ka.). Tatra cakkhumā puriso majjhe ṭhito passeyya manusse gehaṃ pavisantepi nikkhamantepi anucaṅkamantepi anuvicarantepi; evameva kho, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṃ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passanti cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānanti…pe… tatra ca pa me sāvakā bahū abhiññāvosānapāramippattā viharanti.
mula_english:
35. Again, Udayin, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way whereby with the divine eye (*dibbena cakkhunā*), which is purified and surpasses the human, they see beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate. They understand how beings pass on according to their actions thus: ‘These worthy beings who were ill-conducted in body (*kāyaduccaritena*), speech, and mind (*manoduccaritena*), revilers of noble ones (*ariyānaṃ upavādakā*), wrong in their views (*micchādiṭṭhikā*), giving effect to wrong view in their actions (*micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā*), on the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*paraṃ maraṇā*), have reappeared in a state of deprivation (*apāyaṃ*), in a bad destination (*duggatiṃ*), in the nether world (*vinipātaṃ*), in hell (*nirayaṃ*); whereas these worthy beings who were well-conducted in body (*kāyasucaritena*), speech, and mind (*manosucaritena*), not revilers of noble ones (*ariyānaṃ anupavādakā*), right in their views (*sammādiṭṭhikā*), giving effect to right view in their actions (*sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā*), on the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*paraṃ maraṇā*), have reappeared in a good destination (*sugatiṃ*), in the heavenly world (*saggaṃ*), in the world (*lokaṃ*)’. Thus, with the divine eye (*dibbena cakkhunā*) which is purified and surpasses the human, they see beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, and they understand how beings pass on according to their actions (*yathākammūpage satte pajānanti*).

Just as, Udayin, if there were two houses with doors. There a man with good sight, standing in the middle, might see people entering the house, leaving, walking back and forth, and wandering about; just so, Udayin, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way whereby with the divine eye which is purified and surpasses the human, they see beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, and they understand how beings pass on according to their actions … and thereby many disciples of mine abide having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge (*abhiññāvosānapāramippattā viharanti*).

mula_pali:
259. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṃ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti. Seyyathāpi, udāyi, pabbatasaṅkhepe udakarahado accho vippasanno anāvilo, tattha cakkhumā puriso tīre ṭhito passeyya sippisambukampi sippikasambukampi (syā. kaṃ. ka.) sakkharakaṭhalampi macchagumbampi carantampi tiṭṭhantampi. Tassa evamassa – ‘ayaṃ kho udakarahado accho vippasanno anāvilo, tatrime sippisambukāpi sakkharakaṭhalāpi macchagumbāpi carantipi tiṭṭhantipī’ti. Evameva kho, udāyi, akkhātā mayā sāvakānaṃ paṭipadā, yathāpaṭipannā me sāvakā āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti. Tatra ca pana me sāvakā bahū abhiññāvosānapāramippattā viharanti. Ayaṃ kho, udāyi, pañcamo dhammo yena mama sāvakā sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti, sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharanti.

‘‘Ime kho, udāyi, pañca dhammā yehi mamaṃ sāvakā sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti, sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharantī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano sakuludāyī paribbājako bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Mahāsakuludāyisuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.
mula_english:
259. Furthermore, Udayin, I have explained to my disciples the practice, whereby my disciples, through the destruction of the taints, having realized here and now, by their own direct knowledge, the taintless deliverance of mind, the deliverance by wisdom, abide in it, having attained it.

Just as, Udayin, in a mountain recess there is a lake of water, clear, limpid, and undisturbed, where a man with good eyesight standing on the bank could see oyster-shells, gravel and pebbles, and shoals of fish moving about and keeping still.

He might think: ‘There is this lake, clear, limpid, and undisturbed, and there are these oyster-shells, gravel, and pebbles, and also these shoals of fish swimming about and resting.’

Even so, Udayin, I have explained to my disciples the practice, whereby my disciples, through the destruction of the *āsavas*, having realized here and now, by their own direct knowledge, the taintless deliverance of mind ( *cetovimutti*), the deliverance by wisdom ( *paññāvimutti*), abide in it, having attained it.

And thereby many disciples of mine abide having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge ( *abhiññāvosānapāramippattā*).

This, Udayin, is the fifth quality because of which my disciples honor, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honoring and respecting me.

“These, Udayin, are the five qualities because of which my disciples honor, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me.”

This is what the Buddha said.

The wanderer Sakuludayin was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

The Great Sakuludayi Sutra, the seventh, is finished.
commentary_pali:
259.Ayaṃ kho udāyi pañcamo dhammoti ekūnavīsati pabbāni paṭipadāvasena ekaṃ dhammaṃ katvā pañcamo dhammoti vutto. Yathā hi aṭṭhakanāgarasutte (ma. ni. 2.17 ādayo) ekādasa pabbāni pucchāvasena ekadhammo kato, evamidha ekūnavīsati pabbāni paṭipadāvasena eko dhammo katoti veditabbāni. Imesu ca pana ekūnavīsatiyā pabbesu paṭipāṭiyā aṭṭhasu koṭṭhāsesu vipassanāñāṇe ca āsavakkhayañāṇe ca arahattavasena abhiññāvosānapāramippattatā veditabbā, sesesu ciṇṇavasibhāvavasena. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Mahāsakuludāyisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
This, Udāyi, is the fifth dhamma—that is, because the nineteen topics, by way of practice, make one dhamma, it is said to be the fifth dhamma.

Just as in the Aṭṭhakanāgara Sutta (M.
N.
2.
17 ff.) eleven topics, by way of questioning, make one dhamma, so here it should be understood that the nineteen topics, by way of practice, make one dhamma.

And in these nineteen topics, in the first eight sections, through the knowledge of insight (*vipassanāñāṇa*) and the knowledge of the destruction of the contaminants (*āsavakkhayañāṇa*), the perfection of the ending in direct knowledge (*abhiññāvosāna-pāramippattatā*) should be understood as being in terms of being an Arhat, and in the remaining ones, as being in terms of the cultivation of mastery (*ciṇṇavasibhāva*).

The rest is clear throughout.

The Mahāsakuludāyi Sutta Commentary in the Papañcasūdanī

is finished.

mula_pali:
260. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena uggāhamāno paribbājako samaṇamuṇḍikāputto samaṇamaṇḍikāputto (sī. pī.) samayappavādake tindukācīre ekasālake mallikāya ārāme paṭivasati mahatiyā paribbājakaparisāya saddhiṃ pañcamattehi paribbājakasatehi. Atha kho pañcakaṅgo thapati sāvatthiyā nikkhami divā divassa bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Atha kho pañcakaṅgassa thapatissa etadahosi – ‘‘akālo kho tāva bhagavantaṃ dassanāya; paṭisallīno bhagavā. Manobhāvaniyānampi bhikkhūnaṃ asamayo dassanāya; paṭisallīnā manobhāvaniyā bhikkhū. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ yena samayappavādako tindukācīro ekasālako mallikāya ārāmo yena uggāhamāno paribbājako samaṇamuṇḍikāputto tenupasaṅkameyya’’nti. Atha kho pañcakaṅgo thapati yena samayappavādako tindukācīro ekasālako mallikāya ārāmo yena uggāhamāno paribbājako samaṇamuṇḍikāputto tenupasaṅkami.

Tena kho pana samayena uggāhamāno paribbājako samaṇamuṇḍikāputto mahatiyā paribbājakaparisāya saddhiṃ nisinno hoti unnādiniyā uccāsaddamahāsaddāya anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ kathentiyā, seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ corakathaṃ mahāmattakathaṃ senākathaṃ bhayakathaṃ yuddhakathaṃ annakathaṃ pānakathaṃ vatthakathaṃ sayanakathaṃ mālākathaṃ gandhakathaṃ ñātikathaṃ yānakathaṃ gāmakathaṃ nigamakathaṃ nagarakathaṃ janapadakathaṃ itthikathaṃ sūrakathaṃ visikhākathaṃ kumbhaṭṭhānakathaṃ pubbapetakathaṃ nānattakathaṃ lokakkhāyikaṃ samuddakkhāyikaṃ itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vā.

Addasā kho uggāhamāno paribbājako samaṇamuṇḍikāputto pañcakaṅgaṃ thapatiṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna sakaṃ parisaṃ saṇṭhāpesi – ‘‘appasaddā bhonto hontu, mā bhonto saddamakattha; ayaṃ samaṇassa gotamassa sāvako āgacchati pañcakaṅgo thapati. Yāvatā kho pana samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakā gihī odātavasanā sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasanti ayaṃ tesaṃ aññataro pañcakaṅgo thapati. Appasaddakāmā kho pana te āyasmanto appasaddavinītā appasaddassa vaṇṇavādino; appeva nāma appasaddaṃ parisaṃ viditvā upasaṅkamitabbaṃ maññeyyā’’ti. Atha kho te paribbājakā tuṇhī ahesuṃ.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapindika’s Park.

Now on that occasion the wanderer Uggāhamāna Samaṇamuṇḍikaputta was staying in Mallikā’s Park, the single-hall Tinduka plantation for philosophical debates, together with a large following of wanderers, with as many as five hundred wanderers. Then the carpenter Pañcakaṅga went out from Sāvatthī at midday in order to see the Blessed One.
