Then, Ānanda, King Kiki of Kasi had excellent carriages prepared, and having mounted an excellent carriage, he set out from Benares with great royal majesty to see the Blessed One Kassapa, accomplished and fully enlightened.

As far as the road was passable for carriages, he went by carriage, and then he got down from the carriage and went forward on foot to where the Blessed One Kassapa, accomplished and fully enlightened was; after paying homage to the Blessed One Kassapa, accomplished and fully enlightened, he sat down at one side.

When King Kiki of Kasi had sat down to one side, the Blessed One Kassapa, accomplished and fully enlightened, instructed, urged, roused, and encouraged him with an exposition of the Dhamma.

Then, Ānanda, King Kiki of Kasi, having been instructed, urged, roused, and encouraged by the Blessed One Kassapa, accomplished and fully enlightened, with an exposition of the Dharma, said this to the Blessed One Kassapa, accomplished and fully enlightened: ‘Venerable sir, may the Blessed One consent to accept a meal from me tomorrow together with the Sangha of monks.’

And the Blessed One Kassapa, accomplished and fully enlightened, accepted in silence.

Then, Ānanda, King Kiki of Kasi, knowing that the Blessed One Kassapa, the Fully Awakened Buddha, had accepted, rose from his seat, and after paying homage to the Blessed One Kassapa, accomplished and fully enlightened, keeping him on his right, he departed.

Then, Ānanda, King Kiki of Kasi, when the night had ended, had good food, hard and soft, prepared in his own dwelling, red rice stored in the sheaf with the dark grains picked out, along with many sauces and curries, and he had the time announced to the Blessed One Kassapa, accomplished and fully enlightened: ‘It is time, venerable sir, the meal is ready.’
commentary_pali:
287.Aḍḍhamāsupasampanneti kuladārakañhi pabbājetvā aḍḍhamāsampi avasitvā gate mātāpitūnaṃ soko na vūpasammati, sopi pattacīvaraggahaṇaṃ na jānāti, daharabhikkhusāmaṇerehi saddhiṃ vissāso na uppajjati, therehi saddhiṃ sineho na patiṭṭhāti, gatagataṭṭhāne anabhirati uppajjati. Ettakaṃ pana kālaṃ nivāse sati mātāpitaro passituṃ labhanti. Tena tesaṃ soko tanubhāvaṃ gacchati, pattacīvaraggahaṇaṃ jānāti, sāmaṇeradaharabhikkhūhi saddhiṃ vissāso jāyati, therehi saddhiṃ sineho patiṭṭhāti, gatagataṭṭhāne abhiramati, na ukkaṇṭhati. Tasmā ettakaṃ vasituṃ vaṭṭatīti aḍḍhamāsaṃ vasitvā pakkāmi.

Paṇḍupuṭakassa sālinoti puṭake katvā sukkhāpitassa rattasālino. Tassa kira sālino vappakālato paṭṭhāya ayaṃ parihāro – kedārā suparikammakatā honti, tattha bījāni patiṭṭhāpetvā gandhodakena siñciṃsu, vappakāle vitānaṃ viya upari vatthakilañjaṃ bandhitvā paripakkakāle vīhisīsāni chinditvā muṭṭhimatte puṭake katvā yottabaddhe vehāsaṃyeva sukkhāpetvā gandhacuṇṇāni attharitvā koṭṭhakesu pūretvā tatiye vasse vivariṃsu. Evaṃ tivassaṃ parivutthassa sugandharattasālino apagatakāḷake suparisuddhe taṇḍule gahetvā khajjakavikatimpi bhattampi paṭiyādiyiṃsu. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ…pe… kālaṃ ārocāpesīti.

Paṇḍupuṭakassa sālino paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ…pe… kālaṃ ārocāpesī
commentary_english:
287. “When endowed with half a month,” means when a young man from a good family has been ordained and has lived [as a monk] for half a month, the parents' grief does not subside, and he does not understand the acceptance of the bowl and robes, he does not develop confidence with young *bhikṣus* and *śrāmaṇeras*, affection does not become established with the elders, and discontent arises in every place he goes. If he lives for such a short time, his parents are not able to see him. Because of that, their grief diminishes, he understands the acceptance of the bowl and robes, confidence arises with *śrāmaṇera*-young *bhikṣus*, affection becomes established with the elders, he delights in every place he goes, and he is not distressed. Therefore, thinking "it is fitting to live for such a short time," he lived for half a month and then departed.

"Rice of *paṇḍupuṭaka*," means red rice that has been dried after being made into a *puṭaka*. It is said that this was the practice for that rice from the time of sowing: the fields were well prepared, and after placing the seeds there, they sprinkled them with fragrant water. At the time of sowing, having tied a cloth mat like an awning above, at the time of ripening, having cut the heads of rice, having made them into *puṭakas* the size of a fist, and having dried them while tied with ropes in the sky itself, having spread fragrant powders, having filled them into storehouses, they opened them in the third year. Having taken the very pure grains of fragrant red rice of one who had lived there for three years, from which the blackness had gone, they prepared various kinds of hard and soft food. In reference to that, it was said, “exquisite food, both that which is to be eaten and that which is to be consumed… *pe*… he announced the time."

Rice of *paṇḍupuṭaka*. Exquisite food, both that which is to be eaten and that which is to be consumed… *pe*… he announced the time.

mula_pali:
288. ‘‘Atha kho, ānanda, kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena kikissa kāsirañño nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho, ānanda, kikī kāsirājā buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi. Atha kho, ānanda, kikī kāsirājā kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ aññataraṃ nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho, ānanda, kikī kāsirājā kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavoca – ‘adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṃ vassāvāsaṃ; evarūpaṃ saṅghassa upaṭṭhānaṃ bhavissatī’ti. ‘Alaṃ, mahārāja. Adhivuttho me vassāvāso’ti. Dutiyampi kho, ānanda… tatiyampi kho, ānanda, kikī kāsirājā kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavoca – ‘adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṃ vassāvāsaṃ; evarūpaṃ saṅghassa upaṭṭhānaṃ bhavissatī’ti. ‘Alaṃ, mahārāja. Adhivuttho me vassāvāso’ti. Atha kho, ānanda, kikissa kāsirañño ‘na me kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho adhivāseti bārāṇasiyaṃ vassāvāsa’nti ahudeva aññathattaṃ , ahu domanassaṃ. Atha kho, ānanda, kikī kāsirājā kassapaṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavoca – ‘atthi nu kho, bhante, añño koci mayā upaṭṭhākataro’ti?

‘‘‘Atthi, mahārāja, vegaḷiṅgaṃ nāma gāmanigamo. Tattha ghaṭikāro nāma kumbhakāro; so me upaṭṭhāko aggupaṭṭhāko. Tuyhaṃ kho pana, mahārāja, na me kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho adhivāseti bārāṇasiyaṃ vassāvāsanti attheva atthi (sī. pī.) aññathattaṃ, atthi domanassaṃ. Tayidaṃ ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa ghaṭikāre kumbhakāre (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) natthi ca na ca bhavissati. Ghaṭikāro kho, mahārāja, kumbhakāro buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gato, dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gato, saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gato. Ghaṭikāro kho, mahārāja, kumbhakāro pāṇātipātā paṭivirato, adinnādānā paṭivirato, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato, musāvādā paṭivirato, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato. Ghaṭikāro kho, mahārāja, kumbhakāro buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato, saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato, ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato. Ghaṭikāro kho, mahārāja, kumbhakāro dukkhe nikkaṅkho, dukkhasamudaye nikkaṅkho, dukkhanirodhe nikkaṅkho, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya nikkaṅkho. Ghaṭikāro kho, mahārāja, kumbhakāro ekabhattiko brahmacārī sīlavā kalyāṇadhammo. Ghaṭikāro kho, mahārāja, kumbhakāro nikkhittamaṇisuvaṇṇo apetajātarūparajato . Ghaṭikāro kho, mahārāja, kumbhakāro pannamusalo na sahatthā pathaviṃ khaṇati kumbhakāro na musalena na sahatthā paṭhaviṃ khaṇati (syā. kaṃ. pī.), kumbhakāro na musalena sahatthā pathaviñca khaṇati (ka.). Yaṃ hoti kūlapaluggaṃ vā mūsikukkaro mūsikukkuro (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) vā taṃ kājena āharitvā bhājanaṃ karitvā evamāha – ‘‘ettha yo icchati taṇḍulapaṭibhastāni taṇḍula pabhivattāni (sī. pī.) vā muggapaṭibhastāni vā kaḷāyapaṭibhastāni vā nikkhipitvā yaṃ icchati taṃ haratū’’ti. Ghaṭikāro kho, mahārāja, kumbhakāro andhe jiṇṇe mātāpitaro poseti. Ghaṭikāro kho, mahārāja, kumbhakāro pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā.

atthi (sī. pī.) ghaṭikāre kumbhakāre (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) kumbhakāro na musalena na sahatthā paṭhaviṃ khaṇati (syā. kaṃ. pī.), kumbhakāro na musalena sahatthā pathaviñca khaṇati (ka.) mūsikukkuro (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) taṇḍula pabhivattāni (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
288. Then, Ānanda, the Blessed One Kassapa, the worthy one, the fully enlightened one, having dressed in the morning, taking his bowl and robe, went to the dwelling of Kiki, the King of Kāsi; having gone there, he sat down on the prepared seat, together with the Sangha of monks.

Then, Ānanda, Kiki, the King of Kāsi, with his own hands, satisfied and served the Sangha of monks, with the Buddha at its head, with delicious food, both hard and soft.

Then, Ānanda, Kiki, the King of Kāsi, after Kassapa, the Blessed One, the worthy one, the fully enlightened one, had finished eating and had removed his hand from the bowl, took a low seat and sat down to one side.

Having sat down to one side, Ānanda, Kiki, the King of Kāsi, said to Kassapa, the Blessed One, the worthy one, the fully enlightened one: ‘May the Blessed One accept from me a rainy season residence in Vārāṇasī; such support will be for the Sangha.’

‘Enough, great king.

My rainy season residence has already been provided for.’

A second time, Ānanda… A third time, Ānanda, Kiki, the King of Kāsi, said to Kassapa, the Blessed One, the worthy one, the fully enlightened one: ‘May the Blessed One accept from me a rainy season residence in Vārāṇasī; such support will be for the Sangha.’

‘Enough, great king.

My rainy season residence has already been provided for.’

Then, Ānanda, Kiki, the King of Kāsi, [thought]: ‘The Blessed One Kassapa, the worthy one, the fully enlightened one, does not accept a rainy season residence in Vārāṇasī from me,’ and he felt disappointment and sadness.

Then, Ānanda, Kiki, the King of Kāsi, said to Kassapa, the Blessed One, the worthy one, the fully enlightened one: ‘Is there, venerable sir, anyone else more supportive than me?’

‘There is, great king, a village named Vegaḷiṅga.

There, there is a potter named Ghaṭikāra; he is my supporter, my chief supporter.

But you, great king, [think]: “The Blessed One Kassapa, the worthy one, the fully enlightened one, does not accept a rainy season residence in Vārāṇasī from me,” and there is indeed difference [in your mind], there is sadness.

But this, for Ghaṭikāra the potter, does not exist, nor will it exist.

Ghaṭikāra, great king, the potter, has gone for refuge to the Buddha, has gone for refuge to the Dharma, has gone for refuge to the Sangha.

Ghaṭikāra, great king, the potter, abstains from killing living beings, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from sexual misconduct, abstains from false speech, abstains from liquor, wine, and intoxicants, the basis of negligence.

Ghaṭikāra, great king, the potter, is endowed with unwavering faith in the Buddha, is endowed with unwavering faith in the Dharma, is endowed with unwavering faith in the Sangha, is endowed with the virtues loved by the noble ones *(ariyas)*.

Ghaṭikāra, great king, the potter, is without doubt about suffering (*duḥkha*), without doubt about the origin of suffering (*duḥkhasamudaya*), without doubt about the cessation of suffering (*duḥkhanirodha*), without doubt about the path leading to the cessation of suffering (*duḥkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā*).

Ghaṭikāra, great king, the potter, eats only one meal a day, observes celibacy, is virtuous, of good character.

Ghaṭikāra, great king, the potter, has put aside jewels and gold, is without silver made of refined gold.

Ghaṭikāra, great king, the potter, using a plowshare, does not dig the earth with his own hands.

Whatever is a broken bank or a rat’s hill.
kaṃ.
pī.
What is left over from embankments, he brings home in a carrier, having made a pot, he says: “Let anyone who likes set down some selected rice or selected beans or selected lentils, and let him take away whatever he likes.”
The potter Ghaṭikāra, O great king, supports his blind and aged parents.
The potter Ghaṭikāra, O great king, through the destruction of the five lower fetters (*orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā*), has arisen spontaneously (*opapātiko*), and will come to final cessation (*parinibbāyī*) in that very place, not liable to return (*anāvattidhammo*) from that world (*tasmā lokā*).

commentary_pali:
288.Adhivuṭṭho meti kiṃ sandhāya vadati? Vegaḷiṅgato nikkhamanakāle ghaṭikāro attano santike vassāvāsaṃ vasanatthāya paṭiññaṃ aggahesi, taṃ sandhāya vadati. Ahudeva aññathattaṃ ahu domanassanti temāsaṃ dānaṃ dātuṃ, dhammañca sotuṃ, iminā ca niyāmena vīsati bhikkhusahassāni paṭijaggituṃ nālatthanti alābhaṃ ārabbha cittaññathattaṃ cittadomanassaṃ ahosi, na tathāgataṃ ārabbha. Kasmā? Sotāpannattā. So kira pubbe brāhmaṇabhatto ahosi. Athekasmiṃ samaye paccante kupite vūpasamanatthaṃ gacchanto uracchadaṃ nāma dhītaramāha – ‘‘amma amhākaṃ deve mā pamajjī’’ti. Brāhmaṇā taṃ rājadhītaraṃ disvā visaññino ahesuṃ. Ke ime cāti vutte tumhākaṃ bhūmidevāti. Bhūmidevā nāma evarūpā hontīti niṭṭhubhitvā pāsādaṃ abhiruhi. Sā ekadivasaṃ vīthiṃ olokentī ṭhitā kassapassa bhagavato aggasāvakaṃ disvā pakkosāpetvā piṇḍapātaṃ datvā anumodanaṃ suṇamānāyeva sotāpannā hutvā ‘‘aññepi bhikkhū atthī’’ti pucchitvā ‘‘satthā vīsatiyā bhikkhusahassehi saddhiṃ isipatane vasatī’’ti ca sutvā nimantetvā dānaṃ adāsi.

Rājā paccantaṃ vūpasametvā āgato. Atha naṃ paṭhamatarameva brāhmaṇā āgantvā dhītu avaṇṇaṃ vatvā paribhindiṃsu. Rājā pana dhītu jātakāleyeva varaṃ adāsi. Tassā ‘‘satta divasāni rajjaṃ dātabba’’nti varaṃ gaṇhiṃsu. Athassā rājā satta divasāni rajjaṃ niyyātesi. Sā satthāraṃ bhojayamānā rājānaṃ pakkosāpetvā bahisāṇiyaṃ nisīdāpesi. Rājā satthu anumodanaṃ sutvāva sotāpanno jāto. Sotāpannassa ca nāma tathāgataṃ ārabbha āghāto natthi. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘na tathāgataṃ ārabbhā’’ti.

Yaṃ icchati taṃ haratūti so kira bhājanāni pacitvā kayavikkayaṃ na karoti, evaṃ pana vatvā dārutthāya vā mattikatthāya vā palālatthāya vā araññaṃ gacchati. Mahājanā ‘‘ghaṭikārena bhājanāni pakkānī’’ti sutvā parisuddhataṇḍulaloṇadadhitelaphāṇitādīni gahetvā āgacchanti. Sace bhājanaṃ mahagghaṃ hoti, mūlaṃ appaṃ, yaṃ vā taṃ vā datvā gaṇhāmāti taṃ na gaṇhanti. Dhammiko vāṇijo mātāpitaro paṭijaggati, sammāsambuddhaṃ upaṭṭhahati, bahu no akusalaṃ bhavissatīti puna gantvā mūlaṃ āharanti. Sace pana bhājanaṃ appagghaṃ hoti, ābhataṃ mūlaṃ bahu, dhammiko vāṇijo, amhākaṃ puññaṃ bhavissatīti yathābhataṃ gharasāmikā viya sādhukaṃ paṭisāmetvā gacchanti. Evaṃguṇo pana kasmā na pabbajatīti. Rañño vacanapathaṃ pacchindanto andhe jiṇṇe mātāpitaro posetīti āha.

Yaṃ icchati taṃ haratū
commentary_english:
288. "adhivuṭṭho me" —what is he referring to when he speaks thus? At the time of departing from Vegaḷiṅga, the potter Ghaṭikāra made a promise to stay for the rainy season near him; he is referring to that.

"ahudeva aññathattaṃ ahu domanassaṃ" —[this means that] he could not give a three-month donation, nor hear the Dharma, nor care for twenty thousand monks in this manner. Because he could not obtain [these things], he had a change of heart and sadness, not because of the *tathāgata*.

Why? Because he was a stream-enterer (*sotāpanna*).

It seems that previously he was a Brāhmanical devotee.

Then, one time, when quelling a rebellion in a border region, he said to his daughter named Uracchadā: "Mother, do not be heedless of our gods."

The Brahmins, having seen that royal daughter, became unconscious.

When it was said, "Who are these?", [they replied,] "They are your earth deities (bhūmideva)."

Having spat, [saying,] "These are what earth deities are like!", he ascended to the palace.

She, one day, standing and looking at the street, having seen the chief disciple of the Blessed Kassapa, having had him summoned, having given alms-food and rejoicing in the approval, became a stream-enterer, and having asked, "Are there other monks?", and having heard, "The teacher dwells in Ṛṣipatana with twenty thousand monks," having invited [them], she gave alms.

The king, having quelled the border region, returned. Then, immediately, the Brahmins, having come and spoken ill of his daughter, destroyed [her reputation].

The king, however, gave a boon at the time of his daughter's birth.

They took the boon that the kingdom should be given to her for seven days: *satta divasāni rajjaṃ dātabba*.

Then the king gave her the kingdom for seven days: *satta divasāni rajjaṃ niyyātesi*.

She, while feeding the teacher, had the king summoned and had him sit outside the curtain.

The king, having heard the teacher's approval, became a stream-enterer.

For a stream-enterer, there is no hatred towards the *tathāgata*.

Therefore it was said: "There is no hatred towards the *tathāgata*."

"yaṃ icchati taṃ haratū" —he does not do buying and selling after cooking pots; thus having said, he goes to the forest for wood or clay or straw.

The multitude of people, having heard that "the potter has cooked the pots," take pure rice, salt, yogurt, oil, sugar, etc., and come.

If the pot is expensive, the price is small, or having given whatever [they have], [they say,] "We will take [it]," they do not take it.

The righteous merchant cares for his parents, attends upon the *sammāsambuddha*; thinking, "Much unwholesome [karma] will come to us," having gone again, they bring the price.

If, however, the pot is cheap, the price brought is high, [they think,] "The righteous merchant, *dhammiko vāṇijo*, merit will come to us," having returned it well, like householders, they go.

Why does such a virtuous one not renounce?

He said, cutting off the king's path of speech, "He supports his blind, old parents."

"yaṃ icchati taṃ haratū"

mula_pali: 289. ‘‘‘Ekamidāhaṃ , mahārāja, samayaṃ vegaḷiṅge nāma gāmanigame viharāmi. Atha khvāhaṃ, mahārāja, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa mātāpitaro tenupasaṅkamiṃ; upasaṅkamitvā ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa mātāpitaro etadavocaṃ – ‘‘handa, ko nu kho ayaṃ bhaggavo gato’’ti? ‘‘Nikkhanto kho te, bhante, upaṭṭhāko antokumbhiyā odanaṃ gahetvā pariyogā sūpaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjā’’ti. Atha khvāhaṃ, mahārāja, kumbhiyā odanaṃ gahetvā pariyogā sūpaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṃ pakkāmiṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī.). Atha kho, mahārāja, ghaṭikāro kumbhakāro yena mātāpitaro tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mātāpitaro etadavoca – ‘‘ko kumbhiyā odanaṃ gahetvā pariyogā sūpaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkanto’’ti? ‘‘Kassapo, tāta, bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho kumbhiyā odanaṃ gahetvā pariyogā sūpaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkanto’’ti? Atha kho, mahārāja, ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa etadahosi – ‘‘lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yassa me kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho evaṃ abhivissattho’’ti. Atha kho, mahārāja, ghaṭikāraṃ kumbhakāraṃ aḍḍhamāsaṃ pītisukhaṃ na vijahati na vijahi (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), sattāhaṃ mātāpitūnaṃ.
mula_english:
289. Once, O great king (mahārāja), I was dwelling at a town named Vebhalinga (vegaḷiṅge nāma gāmanigame). Then, O great king, having dressed in the morning, taking my bowl and robe, I approached the parents of the potter Ghaṭikāra; having approached, I said this to the parents of the potter Ghaṭikāra: “Come, where has this Bhaggava gone?” “Venerable sir (bhante), your attendant has gone out, taking porridge (odanaṃ) from inside the vessel (antokumbhiyā), taking sauce (sūpaṃ) from the saucepan (pariyogā), and consuming it.”

Then, O great king, I, taking porridge (odanaṃ) from the vessel (kumbhiyā), taking sauce (sūpaṃ) from the saucepan (pariyogā), consuming it, rose from my seat and departed.

Then, O great king, the potter Ghaṭikāra approached his parents; having approached, he said this to his parents: “Who, taking porridge (odanaṃ) from the vessel (kumbhiyā), taking sauce (sūpaṃ) from the saucepan (pariyogā), consuming it, has risen from his seat and departed?” “Kāśyapa (kassapo), father (tāta), the Blessed One (bhagavā), the worthy one (arahaṃ), the perfectly enlightened one (sammāsambuddho), taking porridge (odanaṃ) from the vessel (kumbhiyā), taking sauce (sūpaṃ) from the saucepan (pariyogā), consuming it, has risen from his seat and departed.” Then, O great king, this occurred to the potter Ghaṭikāra: “It is a gain for me, it is a great gain for me, that the Blessed One (bhagavā) Kāśyapa (kassapo), the worthy one (arahaṃ), the perfectly enlightened one (sammāsambuddho), is so intimate with me (abhivissattho).”

Then, O great king, rapture and happiness (pītisukhaṃ) did not leave the potter Ghaṭikāra for half a month (aḍḍhamāsaṃ), nor his parents for a week (sattāhaṃ).
commentary_pali: 289.Ko nu khoti kuhiṃ nu kho. Kumbhiyāti ukkhalito. Pariyogāti sūpabhājanato. Paribhuñjāti bhuñja. Kasmā panete evaṃ vadanti? Ghaṭikāro kira bhattaṃ pacitvā sūpaṃ sampādetvā mātāpitaro bhojetvā sayampi bhuñjitvā bhagavato vaḍḍhamānakaṃ bhattasūpaṃ paṭṭhapetvā āsanaṃ paññapetvā ādhārakaṃ upaṭṭhapetvā udakaṃ paccupaṭṭhapetvā mātāpitūnaṃ saññaṃ datvā araññaṃ gacchati. Tasmā evaṃ vadanti. Abhivissatthoti ativissattho. Pītisukhaṃna vijahatīti na nirantaraṃ vijahati, atha kho rattibhāge vā divasabhāge vā gāme vā araññe vā yasmiṃ yasmiṃ khaṇe – ‘‘sadevake nāma loke aggapuggalo mayhaṃ gehaṃ pavisitvā sahatthena āmisaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjati, lābhā vata me’’ti anussarati, tasmiṃ tasmiṃ khaṇe pañcavaṇṇā pīti uppajjati. Taṃ sandhāya evaṃ vuttaṃ.
commentary_english:
289. “Where now?” means where indeed.
“From the pot” means overflowed.
“From the bowl” means from the soup bowl.
“Enjoy” means partake.
Why do they say this? It is said that the potter, having cooked the rice and prepared the soup, and having fed his parents, and himself having eaten, and having presented the venerable one with an increasing rice-soup portion, and having prepared a seat, and having set out a support, and having offered water, and having given the sign to his parents, gives and goes to the forest.
Therefore, they say this.
“Extremely confident” means very confident.
"Joy and happiness"
“Does not forsake” means does not forsake without interruption; but rather, whether at nighttime or daytime, whether in the village or in the forest, at whatever moment – “The foremost individual in the world, named Sadevaka, having entered my house, takes the meat with his own hand and partakes, truly, it is a gain for me,” he recollects, at that very moment, five-colored joy arises.
With reference to that, this was said.

mula_pali: 290. ‘‘‘Ekamidāhaṃ, mahārāja, samayaṃ tattheva vegaḷiṅge nāma gāmanigame viharāmi. Atha khvāhaṃ, mahārāja, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa mātāpitaro tenupasaṅkamiṃ; upasaṅkamitvā ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa mātāpitaro etadavocaṃ – ‘‘handa, ko nu kho ayaṃ bhaggavo gato’’ti? ‘‘Nikkhanto kho te, bhante, upaṭṭhāko anto kaḷopiyā kummāsaṃ gahetvā pariyogā sūpaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjā’’ti. Atha khvāhaṃ, mahārāja, kaḷopiyā kummāsaṃ gahetvā pariyogā sūpaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṃ. Atha kho, mahārāja, ghaṭikāro kumbhakāro yena mātāpitaro tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mātāpitaro etadavoca – ‘‘ko kaḷopiyā kummāsaṃ gahetvā pariyogā sūpaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkanto’’ti? ‘‘Kassapo, tāta, bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho kaḷopiyā kummāsaṃ gahetvā pariyogā sūpaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkanto’’ti. Atha kho, mahārāja, ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa etadahosi – ‘‘lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yassa me kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho evaṃ abhivissattho’’ti. Atha kho, mahārāja, ghaṭikāraṃ kumbhakāraṃ aḍḍhamāsaṃ pītisukhaṃ na vijahati, sattāhaṃ mātāpitūnaṃ.
mula_english:
290. ‘“On one occasion, great king, I was dwelling at the village near Vegaḷiṅga.

Then, great king, having dressed in the morning, taking my bowl and robe, I went to the parents of the potter Ghaṭikāra; having gone, I said to the parents of the potter Ghaṭikāra: “Well, who has gone off having broken the pot?” “Your attendant has gone forth, venerable sir, having taken porridge from inside the *kalopiya* vessel and sauce from the *pariyoga*.”

Then, great king, having taken porridge from the *kalopiya* vessel and sauce from the *pariyoga*, I ate and, rising from my seat, departed.

Then, great king, the potter Ghaṭikāra went to his parents and, having gone, said to his parents: “Who has taken porridge from the *kalopiya* vessel and sauce from the *pariyoga*, eaten, and departed from his seat?” “Kassapa, dear, the Blessed One, the worthy, fully enlightened one, has taken porridge from the *kalopiya* vessel and sauce from the *pariyoga*, eaten, and departed from his seat.”

Then, great king, the potter Ghaṭikāra thought: “It is a gain for me, it is a great gain for me that the Blessed One Kassapa, the worthy, the fully enlightened one, relies on me thus!”

Then, great king, rapture and happiness did not leave Ghaṭikāra, the potter, for half a month, or his parents for a week.
commentary_pali: 290.Kaḷopiyāti pacchito. Kiṃ pana bhagavā evamakāsīti. Paccayo dhammiko, bhikkhūnaṃ patte bhattasadiso, tasmā evamakāsi. Sikkhāpadapaññattipi ca sāvakānaṃyeva hoti, buddhānaṃ sikkhāpadavelā nāma natthi. Yathā hi rañño uyyāne pupphaphalāni honti, aññesaṃ tāni gaṇhantānaṃ niggahaṃ karonti, rājā yathāruciyā paribhuñjati, evaṃsampadametaṃ. Parasamuddavāsītherā pana ‘‘devatā kira paṭiggahetvā adaṃsū’’ti vadanti.
commentary_english:
290. *kaḷopiyā* thus is last.

What, however, did the Blessed One do thus?

The cause is righteous, like food in the bowl of the monks, therefore he did thus.

The establishment of the precepts is for the disciples alone, for the Buddhas, there is no time for precepts.

Just as in the park of a king there are flowers and fruits, others are prevented from taking them, the king enjoys them as he pleases, this is such an accomplishment.

However, the elders dwelling beyond the sea say, "The deities, having received [it], gave [it]."

mula_pali: 291. ‘‘‘Ekamidāhaṃ, mahārāja, samayaṃ tattheva vegaḷiṅge nāma gāmanigame viharāmi. Tena kho pana samayena kuṭi gandhakuṭi (sī.) ovassati. Atha khvāhaṃ, mahārāja, bhikkhū āmantesiṃ – ‘‘gacchatha, bhikkhave, ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa nivesane tiṇaṃ jānāthā’’ti. Evaṃ vutte, mahārāja, te bhikkhū maṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘natthi kho, bhante, ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa nivesane tiṇaṃ, atthi ca khvāssa āvesane āvesanaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) tiṇacchadana’’ navacchadanaṃ (sī.) nti. ‘‘Gacchatha, bhikkhave, ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa āvesanaṃ uttiṇaṃ karothā’’ti. Atha kho te, mahārāja, bhikkhū ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa āvesanaṃ uttiṇamakaṃsu. Atha kho, mahārāja, ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa mātāpitaro te bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – ‘‘ke āvesanaṃ uttiṇaṃ karontī’’ti? ‘‘Bhikkhū, bhagini, kassapassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa kuṭi ovassatī’’ti. ‘‘Haratha, bhante, haratha, bhadramukhā’’ti. Atha kho, mahārāja, ghaṭikāro kumbhakāro yena mātāpitaro tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mātāpitaro etadavoca – ‘‘ke āvesanaṃ uttiṇamakaṃsū’’ti? ‘‘Bhikkhū, tāta, kassapassa kira bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa kuṭi ovassatī’’ti. Atha kho, mahārāja, ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa etadahosi – ‘‘lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yassa me kassapo bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho evaṃ abhivissattho’’ti. Atha kho, mahārāja ghaṭikāraṃ kumbhakāraṃ aḍḍhamāsaṃ pītisukhaṃ na vijahati, sattāhaṃ mātāpitūnaṃ. Atha kho, mahārāja, āvesanaṃ sabbantaṃ temāsaṃ ākāsacchadanaṃ aṭṭhāsi, na devotivassi na cātivassi (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). Evarūpo ca, mahārāja, ghaṭikāro kumbhakāro’ti. ‘Lābhā, bhante, ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa, suladdhā, bhante, ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa yassa bhagavā evaṃ abhivissattho’’’ti.
mula_english:
291. ‘“On one occasion, great king, I was staying at the village near the market town called Vebhalinga.

At that time, my hut leaked.

Then I addressed the monks thus: “Go, monks, and find out if there is any grass at the potter Ghaṭikāra’s house.”

When this was said, great king, those monks told me, “There is no grass at the potter Ghaṭikāra’s house, but there is a grass roof on his workshop.”

“Go, monks, and remove the grass from the potter Ghaṭikāra’s workshop.”

Then those monks did so.

Then the potter Ghaṭikāra’s parents asked the monks: “Who is removing the grass from the workshop?” “Sister, the hut of the Blessed One, the worthy, fully awakened Buddha, Kashyapa is leaking.”

“Take it, venerable sirs, take it and bless you!”

Then the potter Ghaṭikāra went to his parents and asked: “Who has removed the grass from the roof?” “Monks, dear, the hut of the Blessed One, the worthy, fully awakened Buddha, Kashyapa, is leaking.”

Then the potter Ghaṭikāra thought: “It is a gain for me, it is a great gain for me that the Blessed One Kashyapa, the worthy, fully awakened Buddha, relies on me thus!”

And the rapture and happiness never left the potter Ghaṭikāra for a half-month or his parents for a week.

Then that house remained three whole months with the sky for a roof, and yet no rain came in.

Such is the potter Ghaṭikāra.’

‘It is a gain for the potter Ghaṭikāra, venerable sir, it is a great gain for the potter Ghaṭikāra that the Blessed One relies on him thus.’"
commentary_pali:
291.Haratha, bhante, haratha bhadramukhāti amhākaṃ putto ‘‘kuhiṃ gatosī’’ti vutte – ‘‘dasabalassa santika’’nti vadati, kuhiṃ nu kho gacchati, satthu vasanaṭṭhānassa ovassakabhāvampi na jānātīti putte aparādhasaññino gahaṇe tuṭṭhacittā evamāhaṃsu.

Temāsaṃ ākāsacchadanaṃ aṭṭhāsīti bhagavā kira catunnaṃ vassikānaṃ māsānaṃ ekaṃ māsaṃ atikkamitvā tiṇaṃ āharāpesi, tasmā evamāha. Ayaṃ panettha padattho – ākāsaṃ chadanamassāti ākāsacchadanaṃ. Na devotivassīti kevalaṃ nātivassi, yathā panettha pakatiyā ca nibbakosassa udakapātaṭṭhānabbhantare ekampi udakabindu nātivassi, evaṃ ghanachadanagehabbhantare viya na vātātapāpi ābādhaṃ akaṃsu, pakatiyā utupharaṇameva ahosi. Aparabhāge tasmiṃ nigame chaḍḍitepi taṃ ṭhānaṃ anovassakameva ahosi. Manussā kammaṃ karontā deve vassante tattha sāṭake ṭhapetvā kammaṃ karonti. Yāva kappuṭṭhānā taṃ ṭhānaṃ tādisameva bhavissati. Tañca kho pana na tathāgatassa iddhānubhāvena, tesaṃyeva pana guṇasampattiyā. Tesañhi – ‘‘sammāsambuddho kattha na labheyya, amhākaṃ nāma dvinnaṃ andhakānaṃ nivesanaṃ uttiṇaṃ kāresī’’ti na tappaccayā domanassaṃ udapādi – ‘‘sadevake loke aggapuggalo amhākaṃ nivesanā tiṇaṃ āharāpetvā gandhakuṭiṃ chādāpesī’’ti pana tesaṃ anappakaṃ balavasomanassaṃ udapādi. Iti tesaṃyeva guṇasampattiyā idaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ jātanti veditabbaṃ.

Temāsaṃ ākāsacchadanaṃ aṭṭhāsī ākāsacchadanaṃ. Na devotivassī
commentary_english:
“Take, O venerable one, take [it], O auspicious-faced ones!” Our son, when asked, “Where have you gone?” replies, “To the presence of the Ten-Powered One.” Where, indeed, does he go? He does not even know the sheltering place of the Teacher.” Thus, with delighted hearts, [and] regarding [their] sons as offenders in [this] matter, they spoke thus.

“For three months there was a covering of the sky” means that the Blessed One, after one month had passed of the four months of the rains, had grass brought. Therefore, he spoke thus.
Here the meaning of the word is this: the sky is a covering for it, therefore, "a sky-covering."

“It did not rain divinely” means that it merely did not over-rain. Just as in this case, even a single drop of water did not over-rain in the interior of the well-sheltered water-place. Thus, as in the interior of a house with a dense covering, neither wind nor heat caused discomfort; by nature, there was only seasonal comfort.

Even when that town was abandoned in the latter part, that place was still without rain.

People, while doing work, put cloths there while the gods rained.
As long as the aeon lasts, that place will be just like that.

And that is not through the miraculous power of the *tathāgata*, but through the perfection of the qualities of those [beings] themselves.

For to them [occurred the thought], “Where might one not obtain a fully enlightened Buddha? He has made a dwelling for two blind men!” Due to that cause, sadness did not arise. [But] “The foremost individual in the world with the gods is causing grass to be brought to our dwelling and is covering the *gandhakuṭi*!” So a considerable joy arose for them.

Thus, it should be understood that this miracle occurred through the very perfection of the qualities of those [beings].

“For three months there was a covering of the sky" [means] "a sky-covering."

“It did not rain divinely.”

mula_pali:
292. ‘‘Atha kho, ānanda, kikī kāsirājā ghaṭikārassa kumbhakārassa pañcamattāni taṇḍulavāhasatāni pāhesi paṇḍupuṭakassa sālino tadupiyañca sūpeyyaṃ. Atha kho te, ānanda, rājapurisā ghaṭikāraṃ kumbhakāraṃ upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – ‘imāni kho, bhante, pañcamattāni taṇḍulavāhasatāni kikinā kāsirājena pahitāni paṇḍupuṭakassa sālino tadupiyañca sūpeyyaṃ. Tāni, bhante, paṭiggaṇhathā’ti patiggaṇhātūti (sī. pī.), paṭiggaṇhātūti (syā. kaṃ.). ‘Rājā kho bahukicco bahukaraṇīyo. Alaṃ me! Raññova hotū’ti. Siyā kho pana te, ānanda, evamassa – ‘añño nūna tena samayena jotipālo māṇavo ahosī’ti. Na kho panetaṃ, ānanda, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ahaṃ tena samayena jotipālo māṇavo ahosi’’nti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā ānando bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Ghaṭikārasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.
mula_english:
Then, Ānanda, King Kiki of Kasi dispatched to the potter Ghaṭikāra five hundred cartloads of red rice stored in the sheaf, and also sauce materials to go with it.

Then the king’s men went to the potter Ghaṭikāra and told him: ‘Venerable sir, there are five hundred cartloads of red rice stored in the sheaf, and also sauce materials to go with it, dispatched to you by King Kiki of Kasi;

‘Venerable Sir, please accept them.’

‘The king is very busy and has much to do. Enough for me! Let it be the King’s!’

“Now, Ānanda, it may be that you think thus: ‘Certainly, someone else was the brahmin student Jotipāla on that occasion.’

But it should not be regarded thus. I was the brahmin student Jotipāla on that occasion.”

The Blessed One spoke thus. The venerable Ānanda was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.

The Ghaṭikāra Sutta is finished, the first.
commentary_pali:
292.Taṇḍulavāhasatānīti ettha dve sakaṭāni eko vāhoti veditabbo. Tadupiyañca sūpeyyanti sūpatthāya tadanurūpaṃ telaphāṇitādiṃ. Vīsatibhikkhusahassassa temāsatthāya bhattaṃ bhavissatīti kira saññāya rājā ettakaṃ pesesi. Alaṃ me raññova hotūti kasmā paṭikkhipi? Adhigataappicchatāya. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘nāhaṃ raññā diṭṭhapubbo, kathaṃ nu kho pesesī’’ti. Tato cintesi – ‘‘satthā bārāṇasiṃ gato, addhā so rañño vassāvāsaṃ yāciyamāno mayhaṃ paṭiññātabhāvaṃ ārocetvā mama guṇakathaṃ kathesi, guṇakathāya laddhalābho pana naṭena naccitvā laddhaṃ viya gāyakena gāyitvā laddhaṃ viya ca hoti. Kiṃ mayhaṃ iminā, kammaṃ katvā uppannena mātāpitūnampi sammāsambuddhassapi upaṭṭhānaṃ sakkā kātu’’nti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Ghaṭikārasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
292. *taṇḍulavāhasatānī*: Here, it should be understood as "two carts, one load."
*tadupiyañca sūpeyya*: That which is suitable for soup, such as oil, molasses, etc.
Thinking that "food will be provided for twenty thousand monks for three months," the king sent that much.
Why did he refuse, saying, "*alaṃ me raññova hotū* (enough of the king)?" Because he had attained the state of desiring little.
Thus it occurred to him: "I have never been seen by the king before, how could he send [this]?"
Then he thought: "The teacher has gone to Vārāṇasī; indeed, while being requested for the rainy season residence by the king, he announced to him that I am pledged [to serve him], and he told the story of my virtues. The gain obtained through the story of virtues is like that obtained by a dancer having danced by an actor, or like that obtained by a singer having sung by a singer. What [is the use] to me of this, having done work, I am able to attend to my mother and father, and even to the perfectly enlightened Buddha."
The rest is clear throughout.

The commentary on the Ghaṭikārasutta is finished.

mula_pali: 293. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kurūsu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena thullakoṭṭhikaṃ thūlakoṭṭhikaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) nāma kurūnaṃ nigamo tadavasari. Assosuṃ kho thullakoṭṭhikā thūlakoṭṭhitakā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) brāhmaṇagahapatikā – ‘‘samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito kurūsu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ thullakoṭṭhikaṃ anuppatto. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. So imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti. So dhammaṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāseti. Sādhu kho pana tathārūpānaṃ arahataṃ dassanaṃ hotī’’ti. Atha kho thullakoṭṭhikā brāhmaṇagahapatikā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā appekacce bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce bhagavato santike nāmagottaṃ sāvetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu; appekacce tuṇhībhūtā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho thullakoṭṭhike brāhmaṇagahapatike bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi.
mula_english:
293. THUS HAVE I HEARD. On one occasion the Blessed One was wandering in the Kuru country with a large *saṃgha* of *bhikkhus*, and eventually he arrived at a Kuru town named Thullakoṭṭhika.

The *brāhmaṇa* householders of Thullakoṭṭhika heard: “The recluse Gotama, the son of the Sakyans who went forth from a Sakyan clan, has been wandering in the Kuru country with a large *saṃgha* of *bhikkhus* and has come to Thullakoṭṭhika.

concerning whom a good report has been spread about: “This Blessed Lord is an *arahaṃ*, a fully-enlightened *buddha*, perfected in knowledge and conduct (*vijjācaraṇasampanno*), a Well-Farer (*sugato*), Knower of the worlds (*lokavidū*), unequalled Trainer of men to be tamed (*anuttaro purisadammasārathi*), Teacher (*satthā*) of gods and humans (*devamanussānaṃ*), a *Buddha*, a Blessed Lord (*bhagavā*)”.

He proclaims this world with its gods (*deva*), *Māras*, and *Brahmās*, this generation with its ascetics (*samaṇa*) and *brāhmaṇas*, its princes and its people, which he has himself realised by direct knowledge (*abhiññā*).

He teaches the *dharma* that is good at the beginning, good in the middle, and good at the end, in the spirit and in the letter (*sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ*); he reveals the spiritual life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) that is utterly perfect and pure (*kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ*).

“It is good to see such *arahats*.”

Then the *brāhmaṇa* householders of Thullakoṭṭhika went to the Blessed One. Some paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down at one side; some exchanged greetings with him, and when this courteous and amiable talk was finished, sat down at one side; some extended their hands in reverential salutation towards the Blessed One and sat down at one side; some pronounced their name and clan in the Blessed One’s presence and sat down at one side; some kept silent and sat down at one side.

When they were seated, the Blessed One instructed, urged, roused, and encouraged them with talk on the *Dharma*.
commentary_pali: 293.Evaṃme sutanti raṭṭhapālasuttaṃ. Tattha thullakoṭṭhikanti thullakoṭṭhaṃ paripuṇṇakoṭṭhāgāraṃ. So kira janapado niccasasso sadā bījabhaṇḍaṃ nikkhamati, khalabhaṇḍaṃ pavisati. Tena tasmiṃ nigame koṭṭhā niccapūrāva honti. Tasmā so thullakoṭṭhikanteva saṅkhaṃ gato.
commentary_english:
293. Thus have I heard (evaṃ me suta): the Raṭṭhapāla Sutta.

There, *thullakoṭṭhika* means a full granary (thullakoṭṭhaṃ paripuṇṇakoṭṭhāgāraṃ). It is said that in that region, seeds and goods always went out, and harvested goods came in. Therefore, the granaries in that town were always full. Therefore, it was known as Thullakoṭṭhika.

mula_pali: 294. Tena kho pana samayena raṭṭhapālo nāma kulaputto tasmiṃyeva thullakoṭṭhike aggakulassa aggakulikassa (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) putto tissaṃ parisāyaṃ nisinno hoti. Atha kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa etadahosi – ‘‘yathā yathā khvāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā yathā kho bhagavā dhammaṃ deseti (sī.), nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ ekantaparisuddhaṃ saṅkhalikhitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajeyya’’nti. Atha kho thullakoṭṭhikā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkamiṃsu. Atha kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto acirapakkantesu thullakoṭṭhikesu brāhmaṇagahapatikesu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘yathā yathāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ ekantaparisuddhaṃ saṅkhalikhitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ. Icchāmahaṃ, bhante, kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ. Labheyyāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampadaṃ. Pabbājetu maṃ bhagavā’’ti ettha ‘‘labheyyāhaṃ…pe… upasampadaṃ’’ti vākyadvayaṃ sabbesupi mūlapotthakesu dissati, pārājikapāḷiyaṃ pana sudinnabhāṇavāre etaṃ natthi. ‘‘pabbājetu maṃ bhagavā’’ti idaṃ pana vākyaṃ marammapotthake yeva dissati, pārājikapāḷiyañca tadeva atthi. ‘‘Anuññātosi pana tvaṃ, raṭṭhapāla, mātāpitūhi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā’’ti? ‘‘Na khohaṃ, bhante, anuññāto mātāpitūhi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā’’ti. ‘‘Na kho, raṭṭhapāla, tathāgatā ananuññātaṃ mātāpitūhi puttaṃ pabbājentī’’ti. ‘‘Svāhaṃ, bhante, tathā karissāmi yathā maṃ mātāpitaro anujānissanti agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā’’ti.
mula_english:
294. At that time, a clansman named Raṭṭhapāla, the son of the leading clan in that same Thullakoṭṭhita, was sitting in that assembly.

Then the thought occurred to Raṭṭhapāla, the clansman: “As I understand the *Dhamma* taught by the Blessed One, it’s not easy, living at home, to practice the holy life (brahmacariya) totally perfect, totally pure, a polished shell. What if I were to shave off my hair & beard, put on the ochre robes (*kāsāya*), and go forth from the household life into homelessness?”

Then the *brāhmaṇas* and householders of Thullakoṭṭhika, having been shown, inspired, uplifted, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a talk on the *Dhamma*, delighted in and approved of the Blessed One’s words. Rising from their seats, worshipping and circumambulating the Fortunate One, they went away.

Then Raṭṭhapāla, the clansman, not long after the *brāhmaṇas* and householders of Thullakoṭṭhika had left, approached the Blessed One. After paying homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side.

Sitting to one side, Raṭṭhapāla, the clansman, said this to the Blessed One: “As I understand the *Dhamma* taught by the Blessed One, it is not easy while living in a home to lead the holy life (*brahmacariya*), utterly perfect and pure as a polished shell. I wish, venerable sir, to shave off my hair and beard, put on the yellow robes (*kāsāya*), and go forth from the home life into homelessness. May I receive the going forth (*pravrajyā*) in the Blessed One’s presence? May I receive the full admission (*upasampadā*)?"

“Let the Blessed One ordain me!”

“Raṭṭhapāla, have you been permitted by your mother and father to go forth from the household life into homelessness?”

“No, venerable sir, I have not been permitted by my mother and father to go forth from the household life into homelessness.”

“Raṭṭhapāla, the *Tathāgatas* do not give the going forth to anyone who does not have his parents’ permission.”

“Venerable sir, I shall see to it that my parents permit me to go forth from the home life into homelessness.”
commentary_pali:
294.Raṭṭhapāloti kasmā raṭṭhapālo? Bhinnaṃ raṭṭhaṃ sandhāretuṃ pāletuṃ samatthoti raṭṭhapālo. Kadā panassetaṃ nāmaṃ uppannanti. Padumuttarasammāsambuddhakāle. Ito hi pubbe satasahassakappamatthake vassasatasahassāyukesu manussesu padumuttaro nāma satthā uppajjitvā bhikkhusatasahassaparivāro lokahitāya cārikaṃ cari, yaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ –

‘‘Nagaraṃ haṃsavatī nāma, ānando nāma khattiyo;

Sujātā nāma janikā, padumuttarassa satthuno’’ti. (bu. vaṃ. 12.19);

Padumuttare pana anuppanne eva haṃsavatiyā dve kuṭumbikā saddhā pasannā kapaṇaddhikayācakādīnaṃ dānaṃ paṭṭhapayiṃsu. Tadā pabbatavāsino pañcasatā tāpasā haṃsavatiṃ anuppattā. Te dvepi janā tāpasagaṇaṃ majjhe bhinditvā upaṭṭhahiṃsu. Tāpasā kiñcikālaṃ vasitvā pabbatapādameva gatā. Dve saṅghattherā ohīyiṃsu. Tadā tesaṃ te yāvajīvaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ akaṃsu. Tāpasesu bhuñjitvā anumodanaṃ karontesu eko sakkabhavanassa vaṇṇaṃ kathesi, eko bhūmindharanāgarājabhavanassa.

Kuṭumbikesu eko sakkabhavanaṃ patthanaṃ katvā sakko hutvā nibbatto, eko nāgabhavane pālitanāgarājā nāma. Taṃ sakko attano upaṭṭhānaṃ āgataṃ disvā nāgayoniyaṃ abhiramasīti pucchi. So nābhiramāmīti āha. Tena hi padumuttarassa bhagavato dānaṃ datvā imasmiṃ ṭhāne patthanaṃ karohi, ubho sukhaṃ vasissāmāti. Nāgarājā satthāraṃ nimantetvā bhikkhusatasahassaparivārassa bhagavato sattāhaṃ mahādānaṃ dadamāno padumuttarassa dasabalassa puttaṃ uparevataṃ nāma sāmaṇeraṃ disvā sattame divase buddhappamukhassa saṅghassa dibbavatthāni datvā sāmaṇerassa ṭhānantaraṃ patthesi. Bhagavā anāgataṃ oloketvā – ‘‘anāgate gotamassa nāma buddhassa putto rāhulakumāro bhavissatī’’ti disvā ‘‘samijjhissati te patthanā’’ti kathesi. Nāgarājā tamatthaṃ sakkassa kathesi. Sakko tassa vacanaṃ sutvā tatheva sattāhaṃ dānaṃ datvā bhinnaṃ raṭṭhaṃ sandhāretuṃ pāletuṃ samatthakule nibbattitvā saddhāpabbajitaṃ raṭṭhapālaṃ nāma kulaputtaṃ disvā – ‘‘ahampi anāgate lokasmiṃ tumhādise buddhe uppanne bhinnaṃ raṭṭhaṃ sandhāretuṃ pāletuṃ samatthakule nibbattitvā ayaṃ kulaputto viya saddhāpabbajito raṭṭhapālo nāma bhaveyya’’nti patthanamakāsi. Satthā samijjhanakabhāvaṃ ñatvā imaṃ gāthamāha –

‘‘Sarājikaṃ cātuvaṇṇaṃ, posetuṃ yaṃ pahossati;

Raṭṭhapālakulaṃ nāma, tattha jāyissate aya’’nti. –

Evaṃ padumuttarasammāsambuddhakāle tassetaṃ nāmaṃ uppannanti veditabbaṃ.

Etadahosīti kiṃ ahosi? Yathā yathā khotiādi. Tatrāyaṃ saṅkhepakathā – ahaṃ kho yena yena kāraṇena bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, tena tena me upaparikkhato evaṃ hoti – ‘‘yadetaṃ sikkhattayabrahmacariyaṃ ekadivasampi akhaṇḍaṃ katvā carimakacittaṃ pāpetabbatāya ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ caritabbaṃ, ekadivasampi ca kilesamalena amalīnaṃ katvā carimakacittaṃ pāpetabbatāya ekantaparisuddhaṃ, saṅkhalikhitaṃ vilikhitasaṅkhasadisaṃ dhotasaṅkhasappaṭibhāgaṃ katvā caritabbaṃ, nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā agāramajjhe vasantena ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ…pe… carituṃ, yaṃnūnāhaṃ kesañca massuñca ohāretvā kāsāyarasapītatāya kāsāyāni brahmacariyaṃ carantānaṃ anucchavikāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā nikkhamitvā anagāriyaṃ pabbajeyya’’nti.

Etadahosī Yathā yathā kho

Acirapakkantesu thullakoṭṭhikesu brāhmaṇagahapatikesu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamīti raṭṭhapālo anuṭṭhitesu tesu na bhagavantaṃ pabbajjaṃ yāci. Kasmā? Tatthassa bahū ñātisālohitā mittāmaccā santi, te – ‘‘tvaṃ mātāpitūnaṃ ekaputtako, na labbhā tayā pabbajitu’’nti bāhāyampi gahetvā ākaḍḍheyyuṃ, tato pabbajjāya antarāyo bhavissatīti saheva parisāya uṭṭhahitvā thokaṃ gantvā puna kenaci sarīrakiccalesena nivattitvā bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamma pabbajjaṃ yāci. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘atha kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto acirapakkantesu thullakoṭṭhikesu…pe… pabbājetu maṃ bhagavā’’ti. Bhagavā pana yasmā rāhulakumārassa pabbajitato pabhuti mātāpitūhi ananuññātaṃ puttaṃ na pabbājeti, tasmā naṃ pucchi anuññātosi pana tvaṃ, raṭṭhapāla, mātāpitūhi…pe… pabbajjāyāti.

Acirapakkantesu thullakoṭṭhikesu brāhmaṇagahapatikesu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamī anuññātosi pana tvaṃ, raṭṭhapāla, mātāpitūhi…pe… pabbajjāyā
commentary_english:
294. "Why is he called *raṭṭhapāla*?" Because he is capable of maintaining and protecting a fractured kingdom, therefore he is called *raṭṭhapāla*. When did this name arise? In the time of Padumuttara, the Perfectly Awakened Buddha. Long ago, one hundred thousand aeons ago, among humans with a lifespan of one hundred thousand years, a teacher named Padumuttara arose, surrounded by a hundred thousand monks. He travelled for the welfare of the world. With reference to this, it was said: "The city was named Haṃsavatī, the *khattiya* was named Ānanda; Sujātā was the mother, of Padumuttara, the teacher." (bu. vaṃ. 12. 19); However, even before Padumuttara appeared, two families in Haṃsavatī, full of faith, had established almsgiving to the wretched, the poor, beggars, and so on. At that time, five hundred ascetics dwelling in the mountains arrived in Haṃsavatī. Those two people attended to the group of ascetics in the middle. Having lived there for a short time, the ascetics went to the foot of the mountain. Two elder monks of the *saṃgha* declined. Then they attended to them for as long as they lived. While the ascetics were enjoying [the alms] and expressing their approval, one described the beauty of Śakra's palace, and the other described the palace of Bhūmindhara, the Nāga king. One of the families, having made a wish for Śakra's palace, was reborn as Śakra. The other was [reborn] in the Nāga realm as a Nāga king named Pālitanāgarāja. Śakra, seeing him come to his attendance, asked, "Do you find delight in the Nāga womb?" He said, "I do not find delight." "Then, having given alms to Padumuttara, the Blessed One, make a wish in this place. Both of us will live happily." The Nāga king, having invited the Teacher, Padumuttara, the Blessed One, along with a retinue of one hundred thousand monks, gave a great alms-gift for a week. Seeing the *sāmaṇera* (novice) Uparevata, the son of Padumuttara, the possessor of ten powers, on the seventh day, having given divine cloths to the *saṃgha* with the Buddha at its head, he wished for the state of that *sāmaṇera*. The Blessed One, looking to the future, seeing that "In the future, the son of the Buddha named Gotama will be Rāhula," said, "Your wish will be fulfilled." The Nāga king told that matter to Śakra. Śakra, hearing his words, having given alms for seven days in the same way, and having been reborn in a family capable of maintaining and protecting a fractured kingdom, seeing a son of good family named Raṭṭhapāla, who had gone forth in faith, [wished]: "May I also, in the future, in this world, when Buddhas like you have arisen, having been reborn in a family capable of maintaining and protecting a fractured kingdom, be a Raṭṭhapāla, who has gone forth in faith, like this son of good family." The Teacher, knowing the nature of fulfillment, spoke this verse: "A kingdom... that is able to nourish the four castes; a Raṭṭhapāla family by name, there this one will be born." Thus, it should be understood that this name arose in the time of Padumuttara, the Perfectly Awakened Buddha. What was "This came to be"? What does "However, as ... " mean? Here is a summary of the story: I, from whatever cause I understand the *dharma* taught by the Blessed One, from that cause this occurs to me, being examined: "This threefold training (*śikṣā*), the *brahmacarya*, should be practiced entirely perfectly, even for one day, in order to attain the final state of mind; and it should be entirely pure, even for one day, having made [it] unpolluted by the impurities of defilements in order to attain the final state of mind, having made it like a conch shell written on, like a conch shell scrubbed clean, like a cleansed conch shell, it should be practiced. This is not easy for one dwelling in a house, living in the midst of a house, to practice entirely perfectly... to practice. What if I were to shave off my hair and beard, and having dressed in robes suitable for those practicing the *brahmacarya*, dyed in the juice of *kāsāya*, having gone forth from the house, were to go forth into homelessness?" "This came to be. However, as ...": "When the stout householders, *brāhmaṇas*, and householders had departed, Raṭṭhapāla approached the Blessed One." Among those who had not yet arisen, he did not ask the Blessed One for ordination. Why? Because there were many relatives, blood relations, friends, and associates there. They would seize [him] even by the arm and pull [him back, saying]—"You are the only son of your mother and father; it is not possible for you to go forth." Therefore, there would be an obstacle to ordination. Having risen together with the assembly, having gone a little way, and then having returned, troubled by some bodily exertion, he approached the Blessed One and asked for ordination. Therefore it was said: "Then, the noble Raṭṭhapāla, after the Thullakoṭṭhika people had recently departed... asked the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One ordain me.'" But since the Blessed One, from the time he had the prince Rāhula ordained, did not ordain a son without the permission of his parents, therefore he asked him: "Have you been permitted, Raṭṭhapāla, by your parents…to go forth?"

After the Thullakoṭṭhika *brāhmaṇa* householders had recently departed, he approached the Blessed One. Have you been permitted, Raṭṭhapāla, by your parents…to go forth?

mula_pali: 295. Atha kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā yena mātāpitaro tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mātāpitaro etadavoca – ‘‘ammatātā, yathā yathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ ekantaparisuddhaṃ saṅkhalikhitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ. Icchāmahaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ. Anujānātha maṃ agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā’’ti. Evaṃ vutte, raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa mātāpitaro raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘tvaṃ khosi, tāta raṭṭhapāla, amhākaṃ ekaputtako piyo manāpo sukhedhito sukhaparibhato sukhaparihato (syā. kaṃ. ka.) (ehi tvaṃ tāta raṭṭhapāla bhuñja ca piva ca paricāre hi ca, bhuñjanto pivanto paricārento kāme paribhuñjanto puññāni karonto abhiramassu, na taṃ mayaṃ anujānāma agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya,) sabbattha dissati, sudinnakaṇḍe pana natthi, aṭṭhakathāsupi na dassitaṃ. Na tvaṃ, tāta raṭṭhapāla , kassaci dukkhassa jānāsi. Maraṇenapi te mayaṃ akāmakā vinā bhavissāma. Kiṃ pana mayaṃ taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissāma agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā’’ti? Dutiyampi kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto…pe… tatiyampi kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto mātāpitaro etadavoca – ‘‘ammatātā, yathā yathāhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ ekantaparisuddhaṃ saṅkhalikhitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ. Icchāmahaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ. Anujānātha maṃ agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā’’ti. Tatiyampi kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa mātāpitaro raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘tvaṃ khosi, tāta raṭṭhapāla, amhākaṃ ekaputtako piyo manāpo sukhedhito sukhaparibhato. Na tvaṃ, tāta raṭṭhapāla, kassaci dukkhassa jānāsi. Maraṇenapi te mayaṃ akāmakā vinā bhavissāma. Kiṃ pana mayaṃ taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissāma agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā’’ti?
mula_english:
Then the clansman Raṭṭhapāla rose from his seat, and after paying homage to the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ), he departed, keeping him on his right. He went to his parents and told them: “Mother and father, as I understand the *dharma* taught by the Blessed One (bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ), it is not easy while living in a home (agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā) to lead the holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*), utterly perfect (*ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ*) and pure (*ekantaparisuddhaṃ*), like a polished shell.

I want to cut off my hair and beard (kesamassuṃ ohāretvā), put on the ocher robes (kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā), and go forth from home (*agārasmā*) into homelessness (*anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ*).

Please give me permission to go forth (*anujānātha maṃ agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya*)".

When this was said, Raṭṭhapāla’s parents said to him, “Raṭṭhapāla, dear, you are our only son (ekaputtako), dear and appealing (*piyo manāpo*), raised in comfort (*sukhedhito*), brought up in comfort (*sukhaparibhato*).

You know nothing of suffering (*dukkhassa jānāsi*).

Even in the case of your death we would lose you unwillingly (*maraṇenapi te mayaṃ akāmakā vinā bhavissāma*).

Why, then, would we allow you to go forth alive from home to homelessness (*agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya*)?"

For the second time…For the third time the clansman Raṭṭhapāla said to his parents: “Mother and father, as I understand the *dharma* taught by the Blessed One (bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ), it is not easy while living in a home (*agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā*) to lead the holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*), utterly perfect (*ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ*) and pure (*ekantaparisuddhaṃ*), like a polished shell.

I want to cut off my hair and beard (kesamassuṃ ohāretvā), put on the ocher robes (kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā), and go forth from home (*agārasmā*) into homelessness (*anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ*).

Please give me permission to go forth (*anujānātha maṃ agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya*)".

For the third time Raṭṭhapāla’s parents said to him, “Raṭṭhapāla, dear, you are our only son (ekaputtako), dear and appealing (*piyo manāpo*), raised in comfort (*sukhedhito*), brought up in comfort (*sukhaparibhato*).

You know nothing of suffering (*dukkhassa jānāsi*).

Why, then, would we allow you to go forth alive from home to homelessness (*agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya*)?"
commentary_pali: 295.Ammatātāti ettha ammāti mātaraṃ ālapati, tātāti pitaraṃ. Ekaputtakoti ekova puttako, añño koci jeṭṭho vā kaniṭṭho vā natthi. Ettha ca ekaputtoti vattabbe anukampāvasena ekaputtakoti vuttaṃ. Piyoti pītijanako. Manāpoti manavaḍḍhanako. Sukhedhitoti sukhena edhito, sukhasaṃvaḍḍhitoti attho. Sukhaparibhatoti sukhena paribhato, jātakālato pabhuti dhātīhi aṅkato aṅkaṃ āharitvā dhāriyamāno assakarathakādīhi bālakīḷanakehi kīḷayamāno sādurasabhojanaṃ bhojayamāno sukhena parihaṭo. Na tvaṃ, tāta raṭṭhapāla, kassaci dukkhassa jānāsīti tvaṃ , tāta raṭṭhapāla appamattakampi kalabhāgaṃ dukkhassa na jānāsi na sarasīti attho. Maraṇenapi te mayaṃ akāmakā vinā bhavissāmāti sacepi tava amhesu jīvamānesu maraṇaṃ bhaveyya, tena te maraṇenapi mayaṃ akāmakā anicchakā na attano ruciyā vinā bhavissāma, tayā viyogaṃ pāpuṇissāmāti attho. Kiṃ pana mayaṃ tanti evaṃ sante kiṃ pana kiṃ nāma taṃ kāraṇaṃ, yena mayaṃ taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissāma. Atha vā kiṃ pana mayaṃ tanti kena pana kāraṇena mayaṃ taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissāmāti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo.
commentary_english: 295. ammatātā: Here, ammā means addressing the mother ( *mātaram*), and tātā means addressing the father ( *pitaram*). ekaputtako: *ekova puttako*, means only one son, there is no other, neither elder (*jeṭṭho*) nor younger (*kaniṭṭho*). Here, instead of saying *ekaputto*, "one son," it is said *ekaputtako* due to compassion (*anukampāvasena*). piyo: *pītijanako*, the one who generates joy. manāpo: *manavaḍḍhanako*, the one who increases the mind. sukhedhito: *sukhena edhito*, *sukhasaṃvaḍḍhitoti attho*: grown up in happiness, *sukhasaṃvaḍḍhito*, means that. sukhaparibhato: *sukhena paribhato*, fostered in happiness; from the time of birth (*jātakālato*) onwards, having been taken and held by nurses (*dhātīhi*) from lap (*aṅkato*) to lap (*aṅkaṃ*) , being played with by toys such as horses and chariots (*assakarathakādīhi bālakīḷanakehi*), being fed tasty and delicious food (*sādurasabhojanaṃ*), *sukhena parihaṭo*, indulged in happiness. na tvaṃ, tāta raṭṭhapāla, kassaci dukkhassa jānāsī: "You, dear (*tāta*) Raṭṭhapāla, do not know (*jānāsī*) any suffering (*dukkhassa*)," means, you, dear Raṭṭhapāla, do not know even a small portion (*appamattakampi kalabhāgaṃ*) of suffering (*dukkhassa*), you do not experience it; that is the meaning (*attho*). maraṇenapi te mayaṃ akāmakā vinā bhavissāmā: Even by death (*maraṇena*), we will be separated from you against our will (*akāmakā vinā bhavissāmā*)," means, even if death (*maraṇaṃ*) should occur to you while we are living (*jīvamānesu*), even by that death (*maraṇenapi*), we, unwilling (*akāmakā*), not desiring (*anicchakā*), will be separated (*vinā bhavissāma*) not by our own choice (*na attano ruciyā*), we will experience separation (*viyogaṃ pāpuṇissāmāti*); that is the meaning. kiṃ pana mayaṃ ta: "What then, we...?" means, in this situation (*evaṃ sante*), what (*kiṃ*) then, what (*kiṃ*) indeed (*nāma*) is that reason (*kāraṇaṃ*), by which we would permit (*anujānissāma*) you, while living (*jīvantaṃ*)? Or, kiṃ pana mayaṃ ta: "By what (*kena*) reason (*kāraṇena*) would we permit (*anujānissāma*) you, while living (*jīvantaṃ*)?" Thus, in this regard (*evamettha*), the meaning (*attho*) should be understood (*daṭṭhabbo*).

mula_pali: 296. Atha kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto – ‘‘na maṃ mātāpitaro anujānanti agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā’’ti tattheva anantarahitāya bhūmiyā nipajji – ‘‘idheva me maraṇaṃ bhavissati pabbajjā vā’’ti. Atha kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto ekampi bhattaṃ na bhuñji, dvepi bhattāni na bhuñji, tīṇipi bhattāni na bhuñji, cattāripi bhattāni na bhuñji, pañcapi bhattāni na bhuñji, chapi bhattāni na bhuñji, sattapi bhattāni na bhuñji. Atha kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa mātāpitaro raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘tvaṃ khosi, tāta raṭṭhapāla, amhākaṃ ekaputtako piyo manāpo sukhedhito sukhaparibhato. Na tvaṃ, tāta raṭṭhapāla, kassaci, dukkhassa jānāsi ‘‘maraṇenapi te…pe… pabbajjāyā’’ti vākyadvayaṃ sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. potthakesu dutiyaṭṭhāne yeva dissati, pārājikapāḷiyaṃ pana paṭhamaṭṭhāne yeva dissati. tasmā idha dutiyaṭṭhāne punāgataṃ adhikaṃ viya dissati. Maraṇenapi te mayaṃ akāmakā vinā bhavissāma. Kiṃ pana mayaṃ taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissāma agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya. Uṭṭhehi, tāta raṭṭhapāla, bhuñja ca piva ca paricārehi ca; bhuñjanto pivanto paricārento kāme paribhuñjanto puññāni karonto abhiramassu. Na taṃ mayaṃ anujānāma agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya ‘‘maraṇenapi te…pe… pabbajāyā’’ti vākyadvayaṃ sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. potthakesu dutiyaṭṭhāne yeva dissati, pārājikapāḷiyaṃ pana paṭhamaṭṭhāne yeva dissati. tasmā idha dutiyaṭṭhāne punāgataṃ adhikaṃ viya dissati. Maraṇenapi te mayaṃ akāmakā vinā bhavissāma. Kiṃ pana mayaṃ taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissāma agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā’’ti? Evaṃ vutte, raṭṭhapālo kulaputto tuṇhī ahosi. Dutiyampi kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa mātāpitaro raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ…pe… dutiyampi kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto tuṇhī ahosi. Tatiyampi kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa mātāpitaro raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘tvaṃ khosi, tāta raṭṭhapāla, amhākaṃ ekaputtako piyo manāpo sukhedhito sukhaparibhato. Na tvaṃ, tāta raṭṭhapāla, kassaci dukkhassa jānāsi. Maraṇenapi te mayaṃ akāmakā vinā bhavissāma, kiṃ pana mayaṃ taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissāma agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya. Uṭṭhehi, tāta raṭṭhapāla, bhuñja ca piva ca paricārehi ca; bhuñjanto pivanto paricārento kāme paribhuñjanto puññāni karonto abhiramassu. Na taṃ mayaṃ anujānāma agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya. Maraṇenapi te mayaṃ akāmakā vinā bhavissāma . Kiṃ pana mayaṃ taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissāma agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā’’ti? Tatiyampi kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto tuṇhī ahosi.
mula_english:
296. Then the clansman Raṭṭhapāla thought: "My parents do not permit me to go forth from the household life into homelessness." So he lay down right there on the bare ground, resolving: "Here I will either die or attain the going forth."

Then the clansman Raṭṭhapāla did not eat a single meal, nor did he eat two, three, four, five, six, or seven meals.

Then Raṭṭhapāla's parents said to Raṭṭhapāla: "Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you are our only son, dear and beloved, raised in comfort and luxury. You know nothing of suffering."
[Note: "Even with your death... the going forth" this pair of sentences is found in the Sī.
Syā.
Kaṃ.
Pī.

Therefore, here it appears as extra, having returned to the second place.]
"Even if you die, we would not want to lose you. How then could we permit you, while you are still alive, to go forth from the household life into homelessness? Get up, dear Raṭṭhapāla, eat, drink, enjoy yourself, indulge in sensual pleasures, perform meritorious deeds, and be happy!"

"We do not permit you to go forth from the household life into homelessness." [Note: "Even with your death... the going forth" this pair of sentences is found in the Sī.
Syā.
Kaṃ.
Pī.
