Therefore, here it appears as extra, having returned to the second place.]
"Even if you die, we would not want to lose you. How then could we permit you, while you are still alive, to go forth from the household life into homelessness?" When this was said, the clansman Raṭṭhapāla remained silent.

For the second time, Raṭṭhapāla's parents said to him.... and for the second time, the clansman Raṭṭhapāla remained silent.

For the third time, Raṭṭhapāla's parents said to the clansman Raṭṭhapāla: "Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you are our only son, dear and beloved, raised in comfort and luxury. You know nothing of suffering. Even if you die, we would not want to lose you. How then could we permit you, while you are still alive, to go forth from the household life into homelessness? Get up, dear Raṭṭhapāla, eat, drink, enjoy yourself, indulge in sensual pleasures, perform meritorious deeds, and be happy!"

"We do not permit you to go forth from the household life into homelessness. Even if you die, we would not want to lose you. How then could we permit you, while you are still alive, to go forth from the household life into homelessness?" For the third time, the clansman Raṭṭhapāla remained silent.
commentary_pali:
296.Tatthevāti yattha naṃ ṭhitaṃ mātāpitaro nānujāniṃsu, tattheva ṭhāne. Anantarahitāyāti kenaci attharaṇena anatthatāya. Paricārehīti gandhabbanaṭanāṭakādīni paccupaṭṭhapetvā tattha sahāyakehi saddhiṃ yathāsukhaṃ indriyāni cārehi sañcārehi, ito cito ca upanehīti vuttaṃ hoti. Atha vā paricārehīti gandhabbanaṭanāṭakādīni paccupaṭṭhapetvā sahāyakehi saddhiṃ laḷa upalaḷa rama, kīḷassūtipi vuttaṃ hoti. Kāme paribhuñjantoti attano puttadārehi saddhiṃ bhoge bhuñjanto. Puññāni karontoti buddhañca dhammañca saṅghañca ārabbha dānappadānādīni sugatimaggasaṃsodhakāni kusalakammāni karonto. Tuṇhī ahosīti kathānuppabandhavicchedanatthaṃ nirālāpasallāpo ahosi.

Athassa mātāpitaro tikkhattuṃ vatvā paṭivacanampi alabhamānā sahāyake pakkosāpetvā ‘‘esa vo sahāyako pabbajitukāmo, nivāretha na’’nti āhaṃsu. Tepi taṃ upasaṅkamitvā tikkhattuṃ avocuṃ, tesampi tuṇhī ahosi. Tena vuttaṃ – atha kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa sahāyakā…pe… tuṇhī ahosīti. Athassa sahāyakānaṃ tikkhattuṃ vatvā etadahosi – ‘‘sace ayaṃ pabbajjaṃ alabhamāno marissati, na koci guṇo labbhati. Pabbajitaṃ pana naṃ mātāpitaropi kālena kālaṃ passissanti, mayampi passissāma, pabbajjāpi ca nāmesā bhāriyā, divase divase mattikāpattaṃ gahetvā piṇḍāya caritabbaṃ, ekaseyyaṃ ekabhattaṃ brahmacariyaṃ atidukkaraṃ, ayañca sukhumālo nāgarikajātiyo, so taṃ carituṃ asakkonto puna idheva āgamissati, handassa mātāpitaro anujānāpessāmā’’ti. Te tathā akaṃsu. Mātāpitaropi naṃ ‘‘pabbajitena ca pana te mātāpitaro uddassetabbā’’ti imaṃ katikaṃ katvā anujāniṃsu. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘atha kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa sahāyakā yena raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa mātāpitaro…pe… anuññātosi mātāpitūhi…pe… uddassetabbā’’ti. Tattha uddassetabbāti uddhaṃ dassetabbā, yathā taṃ kālena kālaṃ passanti, evaṃ āgantvā attānaṃ dassetabbā.

atha kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa sahāyakā…pe… tuṇhī ahosī uddassetabbā
commentary_english:
296.
" *Tatthevā*ti:" meaning in that very place where his mother and father did not give permission for him to stay, in that very place.
"*Anantarahitāyā*ti:" meaning without any intervening mattress or without any benefit.
" *Paricārehī*ti:" meaning, having arranged for music, singing, acting, plays, and so forth, and having reveled together with friends, according to one's pleasure, allowing the sense faculties to roam and wander, and indulging in them in this way and that; so it is said.
Or else, "*paricārehī*ti:" meaning, having arranged for music, singing, acting, plays and so forth, and together with friends, *laḷa upalaḷa rama*, play! So it is said.
"*Kāme paribhuñjanto*ti:" meaning enjoying possessions together with his own sons and wives.
"*Puññāni karonto*ti:" meaning, having undertaken generosity, and so forth, with regard to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the *saṃgha*, doing meritorious actions that purify the path to a good destination.
"*Tuṇhī ahosī*ti:" meaning, there was cessation of continuous talk for the purpose of cutting off speech.

Then, his mother and father, having spoken three times, and not obtaining any reply, had their friends summoned, saying, "This friend of yours wants to renounce [the world]; prevent him!"
They too approached him and spoke three times, but he remained silent (*tuṇhī ahosi*).
Therefore it was said: "*Atha kho Raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa sahāyakā...pe... tuṇhī ahosī*ti."

Then his friends, having spoken three times, it occurred to them: "If this man dies without obtaining ordination, there will be no merit to gain.
But if he is ordained, his mother and father will see him from time to time; we too will see him. And also, this ordination is indeed a heavy burden; day after day, having taken an alms bowl made of clay, one must wander for alms; solitary lodging, a single meal, celibacy, are extremely difficult. And this one is tender, of the *nāgarika* class; being unable to do that, he will come back here again. Come, let us persuade his mother and father."
They did likewise (*te tathā akaṃsu*).
His mother and father too gave their permission, having made this agreement, "And your mother and father must be shown respect by one who has gone forth (*pabbajitena*)."
Therefore it was said: "*Atha kho Raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa sahāyakā yena Raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa mātāpitaro...pe... anuññātosi mātāpitūhi...pe... uddassetabbā*ti."
There, "*uddassetabbā*ti" means they must be shown respect, so that they see him from time to time; thus, having come, he must show himself.

*Atha kho Raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa sahāyakā…pe… tuṇhī ahosī*.
*Uddassetabbā*.

mula_pali: 297. Atha kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa sahāyakā yena raṭṭhapālo kulaputto tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘tvaṃ khosi tvaṃ kho (sī. pī.), samma raṭṭhapāla, mātāpitūnaṃ ekaputtako piyo manāpo sukhedhito sukhaparibhato. Na tvaṃ, samma raṭṭhapāla, kassaci dukkhassa jānāsi. Maraṇenapi te mātāpitaro akāmakā vinā bhavissanti. Kiṃ pana te taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissanti agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya. Uṭṭhehi, samma raṭṭhapāla, bhuñja ca piva ca paricārehi ca; bhuñjanto pivanto paricārento kāme paribhuñjanto puññāni karonto abhiramassu. Na taṃ mātāpitaro anujānissanti anujānanti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya. Maraṇenapi te mātāpitaro akāmakā vinā bhavissanti. Kiṃ pana te taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissanti agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā’’ti? Evaṃ vutte, raṭṭhapālo kulaputto tuṇhī ahosi. Dutiyampi kho… tatiyampi kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa sahāyakā raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘tvaṃ khosi, samma raṭṭhapāla, mātāpitūnaṃ ekaputtako piyo manāpo sukhedhito sukhaparibhato, na tvaṃ, samma raṭṭhapāla, kassaci dukkhassa jānāsi, maraṇenapi te mātāpitaro akāmakā vinā bhavissanti. Kiṃ pana te taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissanti agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya? Uṭṭhehi, samma raṭṭhapāla, bhuñja ca piva ca paricārehi ca, bhuñjanto pivanto paricārento kāme paribhuñjanto puññāni karonto abhiramassu. Na taṃ mātāpitaro anujānissanti agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya, maraṇenapi te mātāpitaro akāmakā vinā bhavissanti. Kiṃ pana te taṃ jīvantaṃ anujānissanti agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā’’ti? Tatiyampi kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto tuṇhī ahosi.
mula_english:
Then the clansman Raṭṭhapāla's friends went to Raṭṭhapāla; and having approached Raṭṭhapāla, the clansman, said this to him: "You, friend Raṭṭhapāla, are your mother and father's only son, dear and beloved, raised in comfort, cherished in comfort. You know nothing of suffering, friend Raṭṭhapāla. Even in death, your parents would unwillingly lose you. Why would they permit you, while living, to go forth from home to homelessness, to ordination ( *pravrajyā*)? Get up, friend Raṭṭhapāla, eat, drink, and be merry; while eating, drinking and being merry, enjoying sensual pleasures, making merit, delight!" Your parents will not permit you to go forth from home to homelessness, to ordination. Even in death, your parents would unwillingly lose you. Why would they permit you, while living, to go forth from home to homelessness, to ordination?" When this was said, Raṭṭhapāla, the clansman, was silent.

A second time... A third time the clansmen Raṭṭhapāla's friends said this to Raṭṭhapāla: "You, friend Raṭṭhapāla, are your mother and father's only son, dear and beloved, raised in comfort, cherished in comfort. You know nothing of suffering, friend Raṭṭhapāla. Even in death, your parents would unwillingly lose you. Why would they permit you, while living, to go forth from home to homelessness, to ordination? Get up, friend Raṭṭhapāla, eat, drink, and be merry; while eating, drinking and being merry, enjoying sensual pleasures, making merit, delight!" Your parents will not permit you to go forth from home to homelessness, to ordination. Even in death, your parents would unwillingly lose you. Why would they permit you, while living, to go forth from home to homelessness, to ordination?" A third time Raṭṭhapāla, the clansman, was silent.

mula_pali: 298. Atha kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa sahāyakā yena raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa mātāpitaro tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa mātāpitaro etadavocuṃ – ‘‘ammatātā, eso raṭṭhapālo kulaputto tattheva anantarahitāya bhūmiyā nipanno – ‘idheva me maraṇaṃ bhavissati pabbajjā vā’ti. Sace tumhe raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ nānujānissatha agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya, tattheva tatthevassa (sī.) maraṇaṃ āgamissati. Sace pana tumhe raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ anujānissatha agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya, pabbajitampi naṃ dakkhissatha. Sace raṭṭhapālo kulaputto nābhiramissati agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya, kā tassa kā cassa (sī.) aññā gati bhavissati? Idheva paccāgamissati. Anujānātha raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā’’ti. ‘‘Anujānāma, tātā, raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya. Pabbajitena ca pana pana te (syā. kaṃ. ka.) mātāpitaro uddassetabbā’’ti. Atha kho raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa sahāyakā yena raṭṭhapālo kulaputto tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘uṭṭhehi, samma raṭṭhapāla ‘‘tvaṃ khosi samma raṭṭhapāla mātāpitūnaṃ ekaputtako piyo manāpo sukhedhito sukhaparihato, na tvaṃ samma raṭṭhapāla kassaci dukkhassa jānāsi, uṭṭhehi samma raṭṭhapāla bhuñja ca piva ca paricārehi ca, bhuñjanto pivanto paricārento kāme paribhuñjanto puññāni karonto abhiramassu, (sī. pī. ka.), anuññātosi mātāpitūhi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya. Pabbajitena ca pana te mātāpitaro uddassetabbā’’ti.
mula_english:
Then, the friends of Raṭṭhapāla, the clansman, went to Raṭṭhapāla’s parents, and upon arriving, they said this to Raṭṭhapāla’s parents: “Mother and Father, this Raṭṭhapāla, the clansman, is lying right there on the bare ground, [thinking,] ‘Right here, either my death or my going forth (*pabbajjā*) will occur.’ If you do not permit Raṭṭhapāla, the clansman, to go forth from the householder’s life into the homeless state (*anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya*), right there his death will occur. But if you permit Raṭṭhapāla, the clansman, to go forth from the householder’s life into homelessness, you will see him even after he has gone forth. If Raṭṭhapāla, the clansman, does not delight in going forth from the householder’s life into homelessness, where else will he go? He will return right here. Please permit Raṭṭhapāla, the clansman, to go forth from the householder’s life into homelessness.”

“We permit, dears, Raṭṭhapāla, the clansman, to go forth from the householder’s life into homelessness. And after he has gone forth, his parents must be visited.”

Then, the friends of Raṭṭhapāla, the clansman, went to Raṭṭhapāla, the clansman, and upon arriving, they said this to Raṭṭhapāla, the clansman: “Get up, friend Raṭṭhapāla, you have been permitted by your parents to go forth from the householder’s life into homelessness. And after he has gone forth, his parents must be visited.”

mula_pali:
299. Atha kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto uṭṭhahitvā balaṃ gāhetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘anuññāto ahaṃ, bhante, mātāpitūhi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya. Pabbājetu maṃ bhagavā’’ti. Alattha kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampadaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā acirūpasampanne āyasmante raṭṭhapāle aḍḍhamāsūpasampanne thullakoṭṭhike yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena sāvatthi tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena sāvatthi tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro kho panāyasmā raṭṭhapālo arahataṃ ahosi.

Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘icchāmahaṃ, bhante, mātāpitaro uddassetuṃ, sace maṃ bhagavā anujānātī’’ti. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa cetasā ceto paricca cetoparivitakkaṃ (sī. pī.) manasākāsi. Yathā yadā (sī. pī.) bhagavā aññāsi – ‘‘abhabbo kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattitu’’nti, atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ raṭṭhapālaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘yassadāni tvaṃ, raṭṭhapāla, kālaṃ maññasī’’ti. Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā senāsanaṃ saṃsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena thullakoṭṭhikaṃ tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena thullakoṭṭhiko tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ āyasmā raṭṭhapālo thullakoṭṭhike viharati rañño korabyassa migacīre. Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya thullakoṭṭhikaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Thullakoṭṭhike sapadānaṃ piṇḍāya caramāno yena sakapitu nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa pitā majjhimāya dvārasālāya ullikhāpeti. Addasā kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa pitā āyasmantaṃ raṭṭhapālaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna etadavoca – ‘‘imehi muṇḍakehi samaṇakehi amhākaṃ ekaputtako piyo manāpo pabbājito’’ti . Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo sakapitu nivesane neva dānaṃ alattha na paccakkhānaṃ; aññadatthu akkosameva alattha. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa ñātidāsī ābhidosikaṃ kummāsaṃ chaḍḍetukāmā hoti. Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo taṃ ñātidāsiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sacetaṃ, bhagini, chaḍḍanīyadhammaṃ, idha me patte ākirā’’ti. Atha kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa ñātidāsī taṃ ābhidosikaṃ kummāsaṃ āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa patte ākirantī hatthānañca pādānañca sarassa ca nimittaṃ aggahesi.

cetoparivitakkaṃ (sī. pī.) yadā (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
Then Ratthapala, a clansman, got up and, regaining his strength, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he bowed down to the Blessed One and sat to one side.

Sitting to one side, Ratthapala, the clansman, said this to the Blessed One: "I have been permitted, venerable sir, by my parents to go forth from the house life into homelessness. May the Blessed One grant me the going forth!"

Then Ratthapala, the clansman, received the going forth in the presence of the Blessed One and received the full ordination ( *upasampadā*).

Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Thullakotthita as long as he pleased, after the venerable Ratthapala had been fully ordained for a short time, a half-month after his full ordination, set out to wander towards Savatthi. Wandering by stages, he eventually arrived at Savatthi. There the Blessed One stayed in Savatthi, in Jeta's Grove, Anathapindika's monastery.

Then the venerable Ratthapala, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute, before long—for the sake of which young men of good family rightly go forth from home into homelessness—realized for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life, and having attained it, he remained there, knowing: "Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more coming to any state of being." And the venerable Ratthapala became another one of the *arahants*.

Then the venerable Ratthapala approached the Blessed One; having approached, he bowed down to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the venerable Ratthapala said this to the Blessed One: "I wish, venerable sir, to visit my parents, if the Blessed One permits me."

Then the Blessed One, encompassing the mind of the venerable Ratthapala with his own mind, understood: "Ratthapala, the clansman, is incapable of renouncing the training and returning to the lower life." Then the Blessed One said this to the venerable Ratthapala: "Now is the time, Ratthapala, for you to do as you think fit."

Then the venerable Ratthapala, rising from his seat, bowed down to the Blessed One, circumambulated him, set his lodging in order, and taking his bowl and robe, departed to wander towards Thullakotthita. Wandering by stages, he arrived at Thullakotthita. There the venerable Ratthapala stayed in Thullakotthita, in the Migacira park of King Koravya.

Then, in the morning, the venerable Ratthapala, having dressed, took his bowl and robe and entered Thullakotthita for alms. While wandering for alms in Thullakotthita from house to house, he approached his own father's house.

At that time, the father of the venerable Ratthapala was having his hair combed in the central door-hall. The father of the venerable Ratthapala saw the venerable Ratthapala coming from afar. Having seen him, he said this: "It was by these shaven-headed ascetics that our only son, dear and beloved, was made to go forth!"

Then the venerable Ratthapala obtained neither alms nor a refusal at his own father's house; he obtained only abuse.

At that time, a slave woman of the venerable Ratthapala's relatives was about to throw away some day-old porridge. Then the venerable Ratthapala said this to the slave woman: "Sister, if that is to be thrown away, pour it into my bowl here."

Then, as the slave woman of the venerable Ratthapala's relatives was pouring that day-old porridge into the venerable Ratthapala's bowl, she recognized the signs of his hands, his feet, and his voice.

commentary_pali:
299.Balaṃ gahetvāti sappāyabhojanāni bhuñjanto ucchādanādīhi ca kāyaṃ pariharanto kāyabalaṃ janetvā mātāpitaro vanditvā assumukhaṃ ñātiparivaṭṭaṃ pahāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami…pe… pabbājetu maṃ, bhante, bhagavāti. Bhagavā samīpe ṭhitaṃ aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantesi – ‘‘tena hi bhikkhu raṭṭhapālaṃ pabbājehi ceva upasampādehi cā’’ti. Sādhu, bhanteti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato paṭissutvā raṭṭhapālaṃ kulaputtaṃ jinadattiyaṃ saddhivihārikaṃ laddhā pabbājesi ceva upasampādesi ca. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘alattha kho raṭṭhapālo kulaputto bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampada’’nti.

Pahitattoviharantoti dvādasa saṃvaccharāni evaṃ viharanto. Neyyapuggalo hi ayamāyasmā, tasmā puññavā abhinīhārasampannopi samāno ‘‘ajja ajjeva arahatta’’nti samaṇadhammaṃ karontopi dvādasame vasse arahattaṃ pāpuṇi.

Pahitatto viharanto

Yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamīti mayhaṃ mātāpitaro pabbajjaṃ anujānamānā – ‘‘tayā kālena kālaṃ āgantvā amhākaṃ dassanaṃ dātabba’’nti vatvā anujāniṃsu, dukkarakārikā kho pana mātāpitaro, ahañca yenajjhāsayena pabbajito, so me matthakaṃ patto, idāni bhagavantaṃ āpucchitvā attānaṃ mātāpitūnaṃ dassessāmīti cintetvā āpucchitukāmo upasaṅkami. Manasākāsīti ‘‘kiṃ nu kho raṭṭhapāle gate koci upaddavo bhavissatī’’ti manasi akāsi. Tato ‘‘bhavissatī’’ti ñatvā ‘‘sakkhissati nu kho raṭṭhapālo taṃ madditu’’nti olokento tassa arahattasampattiṃ disvā ‘‘sakkhissatī’’ti aññāsi. Tena vuttaṃ – yathā bhagavā aññāsi…pe… kālaṃ maññasīti.

Yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamī Manasākāsī yathā bhagavā aññāsi…pe… kālaṃ maññasī

Migacīreti evaṃnāmake uyyāne. Tañhi raññā – ‘‘akāle sampattapabbajitānaṃ dinnameva idaṃ, yathāsukhaṃ paribhuñjantū’’ti evamanuññātameva ahosi, tasmā thero – ‘‘mama āgatabhāvaṃ mātāpitūnaṃ ārocessāmi, te me pādadhovanauṇhodakapādamakkhanatelādīni pesissantī’’ti cittampi anuppādetvā uyyānameva pāvisi. Piṇḍāya pāvisīti dutiyadivase pāvisi.

Migacīre Piṇḍāya pāvisī

Majjhimāyāti sattadvārakoṭṭhakassa gharassa majjhime dvārakoṭṭhake. Ullikhāpetīti kappakena kese paharāpeti. Etadavocāti – ‘‘ime samaṇakā amhākaṃ piyaputtakaṃ pabbājetvā corānaṃ hatthe nikkhipitvā viya ekadivasampi na dassāpenti, evaṃ pharusakārakā ete puna imaṃ ṭhānaṃ upasaṅkamitabbaṃ maññanti, ettova nikaḍḍhitabbā ete’’ti cintetvā etaṃ ‘‘imehi muṇḍakehī’’tiādivacanaṃ avoca. Ñātidāsīti ñātakānaṃ dāsī. Ābhidosikanti pārivāsikaṃ ekarattātikkantaṃ pūtibhūtaṃ. Tatthāyaṃ padattho – pūtibhāvadosena abhibhūtoti abhidoso, abhidosova ābhidosiko. Ekarattātikkantasseva nāmasaññā esā yadidaṃ ābhidosikoti, taṃ ābhidosikaṃ. Kummāsanti yavakummāsaṃ. Chaḍḍetukāmā hotīti yasmā antamaso dāsakammakārānaṃ gorūpānampi aparibhogāraho, tasmā naṃ kacavaraṃ viya bahi chaḍḍetukāmā hoti. Sacetanti sace etaṃ. Bhaginīti ariyavohārena attano dhātiṃ ñātidāsiṃ ālapati. Chaḍḍanīyadhammanti chaḍḍetabbasabhāvaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – ‘‘bhagini etaṃ sace bahi chaḍḍanīyadhammaṃ nissaṭṭhapariggahaṃ, idha me patte ākirāhī’’ti. Kiṃ pana evaṃ vattuṃ labbhati , viññatti vā payuttavācā vā na hotīti. Na hoti. Kasmā? Nissaṭṭhapariggahattā. Yañhi chaḍḍanīyadhammaṃ nissaṭṭhapariggahaṃ, yattha sāmikā anālayā honti, taṃ sabbaṃ ‘‘detha āharatha ākirathā’’ti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Teneva hi ayamāyasmā aggaariyavaṃsiko samānopi evamāha.

Majjhimāyā Ullikhāpetī Etadavocā Ñātidāsī Ābhidosika ābhidosikaṃ. Kummāsa Chaḍḍetukāmā hotī Saceta Bhaginī Chaḍḍanīyadhammanti

Hatthānanti bhikkhāgahaṇatthaṃ pattaṃ upanāmayato maṇibandhato pabhuti dvinnampi hatthānaṃ. Pādānanti nivāsanantato paṭṭhāya dvinnampi pādānaṃ. Sarassāti sace taṃ bhaginīti vācaṃ nicchārayato sarassa ca. Nimittaṃ aggahesīti hatthapiṭṭhiādīni olokayamānā – ‘‘puttassa me raṭṭhapālassa viya suvaṇṇakacchapapiṭṭhisadisā imā hatthapādapiṭṭhiyo, haritālavaṭṭiyo viya suvaṭṭitā aṅguliyo, madhuro saro’’ti gihikāle sallakkhitapubbaṃ ākāraṃ aggahesi sañjāni sallakkhesi. Tassa hāyasmato dvādasavassāni araññāvāsañceva piṇḍiyālopabhojanañca paribhuñjantassa aññādiso sarīravaṇṇo ahosi, tena naṃ sā ñātidāsī disvāva na sañjāni, nimittaṃ pana aggahesīti.

Hatthāna Pādāna Sarassā Nimittaṃ aggahesī
commentary_english:
299. <hi rend="bold">balaṃ gahetvā</hi>ti: Taking strength, eating suitable foods, caring for the body with rubbing with oil and so forth, generating physical strength, having paid homage to his mother and father, having left behind the weeping circle of relatives, he went to where the Bhagavān was…pe… “May the Bhagavān ordain me, venerable sir."
The Bhagavān addressed a certain monk standing nearby: “Then, monk, ordain Raṭṭhapāla and also grant him full admission."
"Good, venerable sir," that monk, having promised the Bhagavān, having obtained Raṭṭhapāla, a clansman, Jinadattiya, a fellow resident, ordained him and also granted him full admission.
Therefore it was said: “Raṭṭhapāla, a clansman, obtained the going forth in the presence of the Bhagavān, he obtained full admission."

<hi rend="bold">pahitatto viharanto</hi>ti: Living diligently, thus living for twelve years.
This venerable one was a person capable of being guided, therefore, being meritorious, endowed with aspiration, though practicing the ascetic life, thinking, “Today, this very day, [I will attain] arahantship,” he attained arahantship in the twelfth year.

<hi rend="bold">yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamī</hi>ti: "He went to where the Bhagavān was," because my mother and father, allowing my going forth, said, "You must come from time to time to give us a glimpse,” having said this, they permitted [me]. But, mothers and fathers are hard to treat, and the purpose for which I went forth, that has reached its peak for me. Now, having taken leave of the Bhagavān, I will show myself to my mother and father,” thinking thus, desiring to take leave, he approached.
<hi rend="bold">manasākāsī</hi>ti: He considered, “What misfortune might befall Raṭṭhapāla once he has gone?”
Then, having known "There will be," contemplating "Will Raṭṭhapāla be able to subdue it?", having seen his attainment of arahantship, he knew "He will be able."
Therefore it was said: <hi rend="bold">yathā bhagavā aññāsi…pe… kālaṃ maññasī</hi>ti: “As the Bhagavān knew…pe… you think it is the time."

<hi rend="bold">yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamī manasākāsī yathā bhagavā aññāsi…pe… kālaṃ maññasī</hi>
<hi rend="bold">migacīre</hi>ti: In a park called Migacīra.
For that was given by the king to those ascetics who had arrived out of season, [saying,] "Let them enjoy it as they please," thus it was indeed permitted. Therefore, the elder thought, "I will announce my arrival to my mother and father, they will send me foot-washing water, hot water, oil for anointing the feet, and so forth," without even producing this thought, he entered the park.
<hi rend="bold">piṇḍāya pāvisī</hi>ti: He entered for alms on the second day.

<hi rend="bold">migacīre piṇḍāya pāvisī</hi>
<hi rend="bold">majjhimāyā</hi>ti: In the middle doorway of a house with seven door chambers.
<hi rend="bold">ullikhāpetī</hi>ti: He has his hair cut by a barber.
<hi rend="bold">etadavocā</hi>ti: He said this - "These ascetics, having ordained our dear son, do not show him even for a single day, as if they had deposited him in the hands of thieves. Thus, these harsh-doers think that this place is fit to be approached again, they should be dragged away from here," having thought thus, he spoke this saying beginning "by these shavelings."
<hi rend="bold">ñātidāsī</hi>ti: A slave of relatives.
<hi rend="bold">ābhidosika</hi>nti: A pārivāsika, having remained out for one night, being putrid.
There, this is the meaning of the word: Because he is overcome by the fault of putridity, he is abhidosa, and abhidosa is ābhidosika.
Indeed, the name-designation for one who has remained out for one night is ābhidosika, that <hi rend="bold">ābhidosikaṃ.</hi>
<hi rend="bold">kummāsa</hi>nti: Barley groats.
<hi rend="bold">chaḍḍetukāmā hotī</hi>ti: Because she is desirous of throwing [it] away, since it is unworthy of being used even by servants and laborers who are cowherds, therefore, she is desirous of throwing it away like trash <pb ed="v" n="3.
0210"/> hoti.
<hi rend="bold">saceta</hi>nti: If that is so.
<hi rend="bold">bhaginī</hi>ti: With noble speech, she addresses her wet nurse, a slave of relatives.
<hi rend="bold">chaḍḍanīyadhammanti</hi>: The nature of being thrown away.
This is what was said: "Sister, if this is something to be thrown away, something relinquished, sprinkle it in my bowl here."
But is it proper to say this, or is it not a communication or a speech that is employed?
It is not.
Why? Because of being relinquished.
For whatever is something to be thrown away, something relinquished, where the owners are without attachment, all that is "Give, bring".
It is proper to say "ākirathā".

Indeed, this venerable one, even though of the Aggaariyavaṃsa lineage, spoke thus.

Majjhimāyā, ullikhāpetī, etadavocā, ñātidāsī, ābhidosika, ābhidosikaṃ.

Kummāsa, being desirous of discarding, hotī, pb ed="v" n="3.

Saceta, bhaginī, chaḍḍanīyadhammanti, pb ed="p" n="3.

pb ed="m" n="3.

hatthāna means regarding the hands, from the wrist up to where the alms bowl is offered for the purpose of receiving alms, dvinnampi hatthānaṃ.

pādāna means regarding the feet, from the end of the garment upwards, dvinnampi pādānaṃ.

sarassā means, if one utters the speech, "she is a sister," sarassa ca.

nimittaṃ aggahesī means while looking at the back of the hands etc., "the backs of the hands and feet are like the back of a golden tortoise of my son Raṭṭhapāla, the fingers are well-rounded like orpiment rolls, the voice is sweet," she took up the form previously observed and recognized in the householder's time.

To that venerable one who had lived in the forest for twelve years, partaking of alms food, the color of his body was different. Therefore, that relative slave woman, having seen [him], did not recognize [him], but she grasped the sign.

hatthāna, pādāna, sarassā, nimittaṃ aggahesī

mula_pali: 300. Atha kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa ñātidāsī yenāyasmato raṭṭhapālassa mātā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa mātaraṃ etadavoca – ‘‘yaggheyye, jāneyyāsi – ‘ayyaputto raṭṭhapālo anuppatto’’’ti. ‘‘Sace, je, saccaṃ bhaṇasi, adāsiṃ taṃ karomī’’ti saccaṃ vadasi, adāsī bhavasīti (sī. pī.), saccaṃ vadasi, adāsī bhavissasi (ka.). Atha kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa mātā yenāyasmato raṭṭhapālassa pitā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa pitaraṃ etadavoca – ‘‘yagghe, gahapati, jāneyyāsi – ‘raṭṭhapālo kira kulaputto anuppatto’’’ti? Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā raṭṭhapālo taṃ ābhidosikaṃ kummāsaṃ aññataraṃ kuṭṭamūlaṃ kuḍḍaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) nissāya paribhuñjati. Atha kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa pitā yenāyasmā raṭṭhapālo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ raṭṭhapālaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘atthi nāma, tāta raṭṭhapāla, ābhidosikaṃ kummāsaṃ paribhuñjissasi? Nanu, tāta raṭṭhapāla, sakaṃ gehaṃ gantabba’’nti? ‘‘Kuto no, gahapati, amhākaṃ gehaṃ agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitānaṃ? Anagārā mayaṃ, gahapati. Agamamha kho te, gahapati, gehaṃ, tattha neva dānaṃ alatthamha na paccakkhānaṃ; aññadatthu akkosameva alatthamhā’’ti. ‘‘Ehi, tāta raṭṭhapāla, gharaṃ gamissāmā’’ti. ‘‘Alaṃ, gahapati, kataṃ me ajja bhattakiccaṃ’’. ‘‘Tena hi, tāta raṭṭhapāla, adhivāsehi svātanāya bhatta’’nti. Adhivāsesi kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa pitā āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa adhivāsanaṃ viditvā yena sakaṃ nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mahantaṃ hiraññasuvaṇṇassa puñjaṃ kārāpetvā kilañjehi paṭicchādetvā āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa purāṇadutiyikā āmantesi – ‘‘etha tumhe, vadhuyo, yena alaṅkārena alaṅkatā pubbe raṭṭhapālassa kulaputtassa piyā hotha manāpā tena alaṅkārena alaṅkarothā’’ti.
mula_english:
Then, the venerable Raṭṭhapāla's slave-girl went to Raṭṭhapāla's mother and said: "Please know, lady, your master-son Raṭṭhapāla has arrived."

"If, indeed, you speak the truth, I will make you a free woman!"

Then Raṭṭhapāla's mother went to Raṭṭhapāla's father and said: "Please know, householder, that Raṭṭhapāla, the son of a good family, has arrived."

Now at that time, the venerable Raṭṭhapāla was eating day-old gruel, leaning against a certain wall.

Then Raṭṭhapāla's father went to Raṭṭhapāla and said: "What is this, dear Raṭṭhapāla, that you are eating day-old gruel? Come now, dear Raṭṭhapāla, shouldn't you go to your own house?"

"Where is there a house for us, householder, who have gone forth from household life into the homeless life (*anagāriya*)? We are homeless ascetics (*anagāra*), householder. We went to your house, householder, but we received neither alms (*dāna*) nor a polite refusal there; instead we only received abuse."

"Come, dear Raṭṭhapāla, let's go to the house."

"Enough, householder, my meal for today is finished."

"Then, dear Raṭṭhapāla, consent to accept tomorrow's meal."

The venerable Raṭṭhapāla consented in silence.

Then, knowing that the venerable Raṭṭhapāla had consented, Raṭṭhapāla's father went back to his own house, had a great heap of gold and silver coins made, covered it with mats, and then addressed Raṭṭhapāla's former wives: "Come, ladies, adorn yourselves with the ornaments with which you were formerly dear and pleasing to Raṭṭhapāla, the son of a good family."
commentary_pali:
300.Raṭṭhapālassa mātaraṃ etadavocāti therassa aṅgapaccaṅgāni saṇṭhāpetvā thaññaṃ pāyetvā saṃvaḍḍhitadhātīpi samānā pabbajitvā mahākhīṇāsavabhāvappattena sāmiputtena saddhiṃ – ‘‘tvaṃ nu kho, me bhante, putto raṭṭhapālo’’tiādivacanaṃ vattuṃ avisahantī vegena gharaṃ pavisitvā raṭṭhapālassa mātaraṃ etadavoca. Yaggheti ārocanatthe nipāto. Saceje saccanti ettha jeti ālapane nipāto. Evañhi tasmiṃ dese dāsijanaṃ ālapanti, tasmā ‘‘tvañhi, bhoti dāsi, sace saccaṃ bhaṇasī’’ti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo.

Upasaṅkamīti kasmā upasaṅkami? Mahākule itthiyo bahi nikkhamantā garahaṃ pāpuṇanti, idañca accāyikakiccaṃ, seṭṭhissa naṃ ārocessāmīti cinteti. Tasmā upasaṅkami. Aññataraṃ kuṭṭamūlanti tasmiṃ kira dese dānapatīnaṃ gharesu sālā honti, āsanāni cettha paññattāni honti, upaṭṭhāpitaṃ udakakañjiyaṃ. Tattha pabbajitā piṇḍāya caritvā nisīditvā bhuñjanti . Sace icchanti, dānapatīnampi santakaṃ gaṇhanti. Tasmā tampi aññatarassa kulassa īdisāya sālāya aññataraṃ kuṭṭamūlanti veditabbaṃ. Na hi pabbajitā kapaṇamanussā viya asāruppe ṭhāne nisīditvā bhuñjantīti.

Upasaṅkamī Aññataraṃ kuṭṭamūla

Atthināma tātāti ettha atthīti vijjamānatthe, nāmāti pucchanatthe maññanatthe vā nipāto. Idañhi vuttaṃ hoti – atthi nu kho, tāta raṭṭhapāla, amhākaṃ dhanaṃ, nanu mayaṃ niddhanāti vattabbā, yesaṃ no tvaṃ īdise ṭhāne nisīditvā ābhidosikaṃ kummāsaṃ paribhuñjissasi. Tathā atthi nu kho, tāta raṭṭhapāla, amhākaṃ jīvitaṃ, nanu mayaṃ matāti vattabbā, yesaṃ no tvaṃ īdise ṭhāne nisīditvā ābhidosikaṃ kummāsaṃ paribhuñjissasi. Tathā atthi maññe, tāta raṭṭhapāla, tava abbhantare sāsanaṃ nissāya paṭiladdho samaṇaguṇo, yaṃ tvaṃ subhojanarasasaṃvaḍḍhitopi imaṃ jigucchaneyyaṃ ābhidosikaṃ kummāsaṃ amatamiva nibbikāro paribhuñjissasīti. So pana gahapati dukkhābhitunnatāya etamatthaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ katvā vattumasakkonto – ‘‘atthi nāma, tāta raṭṭhapāla, ābhidosikaṃ kummāsaṃ paribhuñjissasī’’ti ettakameva avaca. Akkharacintakā panettha idaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ vadanti – anokappanāmarisanatthavasenetaṃ atthisadde upapade ‘‘paribhuñjissasī’’ti anāgatavacanaṃ kataṃ. Tassāyamattho – ‘‘atthi nāma…pe… paribhuñjissasi, idaṃ paccakkhampi ahaṃ na saddahāmi na marisayāmī’’ti. Idaṃ ettakaṃ vacanaṃ gahapati therassa pattamukhavaṭṭiyaṃ gahetvā ṭhitakova kathesi. Theropi pitari pattamukhavaṭṭiyaṃ gahetvā ṭhiteyeva taṃ pūtikummāsaṃ paribhuñji sunakhavantasadisaṃ pūtikukkuṭaṇḍamiva bhinnaṭṭhāne pūtikaṃ vāyantaṃ. Puthujjanena kira tathārūpaṃ kummāsaṃ paribhuñjituṃ na sakkā. Thero pana ariyiddhiyaṃ ṭhatvā dibbojaṃ amatarasaṃ paribhuñjamāno viya paribhuñjitvā dhamakaraṇena udakaṃ gahetvā pattañca mukhañca hatthapāde ca dhovitvā kuto no gahapatītiādimāha.

Atthi nāma tātā atthī nāmā kuto no gahapatī

Tattha kuto noti kuto nu. Neva dānanti deyyadhammavasena neva dānaṃ alatthamha. Na paccakkhānanti ‘‘kiṃ, tāta raṭṭhapāla, kacci te khamanīyaṃ, kaccisi appakilamathena āgato, na tāva tāta gehe bhattaṃ sampādiyatī’’ti evaṃ paṭisanthāravasena paccakkhānampi na alatthamha. Kasmā pana thero evamāha? Pitu anuggahena. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘yathā esa maṃ vadati , aññepi pabbajite evaṃ vadati maññe. Buddhasāsane ca pattantare padumaṃ viya bhasmāchanno aggi viya pheggupaṭicchanno candanasāro viya suttikāpaṭicchannaṃ muttaratanaṃ viya valāhakapaṭicchanno candimā viya mādisānaṃ paṭicchannaguṇānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anto natthi, tesupi na evarūpaṃ vacanaṃ pavattessati, saṃvare ṭhassatī’’ti anuggahena evamāha.

kuto no Neva dāna Na paccakkhāna

Ehi tātāti tāta tuyhaṃ gharaṃ mā hotu, ehi gharaṃ gamissāmāti vadati. Alanti thero ukkaṭṭhaekāsanikatāya paṭikkhipanto evamāha. Adhivāsesīti thero pana pakatiyā ukkaṭṭhasapadānacāriko svātanāyabhikkhaṃ nāma nādhivāseti, mātu anuggahena pana adhivāsesi. Mātu kirassa theraṃ anussaritvā mahāsoko uppajji, rodaneneva pakkakkhi viya jātā, tasmā thero ‘‘sacāhaṃ taṃ apassitvā gamissāmi, hadayampissā phāleyyā’’ti anuggahena adhivāsesi. Kārāpetvāti ekaṃ hiraññassa, ekaṃ suvaṇṇassāti dve puñje kārāpetvā. Kīvamahantā pana puñjā ahesunti. Yathā orato ṭhito puriso pārato ṭhitaṃ majjhimappamāṇaṃ purisaṃ na passati, evaṃmahantā.

Ehi tātā Ala Adhivāsesī Kārāpetvā
commentary_english:
300. "raṭṭhapālassa mātaraṃ etadavocā": Having arranged the limbs of the elder, having given breast milk, like a wet nurse who had raised him, having renounced [the world], with her master-son who had attained the state of a great *khīṇāsava*, not daring to say the words beginning with "Are you, venerable sir, my son Raṭṭhapāla?", she entered the house quickly and said this to Raṭṭhapāla's mother. "yagghe": is a particle in the sense of imparting information. "sace je sacca": Here, *jeti* is a particle in the sense of addressing. For in that country they address a slave woman thus, therefore, the meaning here should be understood thus: "Indeed, woman slave, if you speak the truth." "upasaṅkamī": Why did she approach? In a great family, women going outside receive censure, and this is an urgent matter, [she] thinks "I will announce it to the wealthy man." Therefore, she approached. "aññataraṃ kuṭṭamūla": It seems that in that country, in the houses of donors there are halls, and here seats are arranged, water pots are set up. There, the renunciates, having wandered for alms, sit down and eat. If they wish, they take what belongs to the donors. Therefore, that too should be understood as the corner of a wall in such a hall of another family. For the renunciates do not eat sitting in an unsuitable place like wretched people. upasaṅkamī aññataraṃ kuṭṭamūla "atthi nāma tātā": Here, "atthi" is in the sense of existence, "nāma" is a particle in the sense of questioning or supposing. For this is what is said: "Is there indeed, dear Raṭṭhapāla, wealth for us? Are we not to be called impoverished, for whom you, sitting in such a place, will partake of stale gruel? Likewise, is there indeed, dear Raṭṭhapāla, life for us? Are we not to be called dead, for whom you, sitting in such a place, will partake of stale gruel? Likewise, I suppose, dear Raṭṭhapāla, you have recovered the qualities of a *samaṇa* relying on the teaching within you, that even though you were raised on delicious flavors, you will partake of this disgusting stale gruel without disgust, as if it were nectar." But that householder, unable to say this matter completely because of being oppressed by suffering, said only this much: "Is there indeed, dear Raṭṭhapāla, will you partake of stale gruel?" But the grammarians here state this characteristic: In the *atthisadde* (*atthi* word) used in the sense of unreflectiveness and impatience, the future tense "paribhuñjissasi" ("you will partake") is used. Its meaning is this: "Is there indeed... will you partake... I do not believe or tolerate even this directly." This much was spoken by the householder standing holding the edge of the elder's bowl. The elder too, while his father was standing holding the edge of the bowl, partook of that rotten gruel, like a rotten chicken egg smelling foul in a broken place, similar to a dog's vomit. It seems it is not possible for an ordinary person to partake of such gruel. But the elder, standing in the divine power, having partaken as if enjoying divine food, ambrosial taste, and having taken water with a water pot, and having washed the bowl, mouth, hands and feet, said "kuto no gahapatī" etc. atthi nāma tātā atthī nāmā kuto no gahapatī There, "kuto no" means "kuto nu" (why not?). "neva dāna": Because of the law of giving, we did not receive any gift. "na paccakkhāna": "What, dear Raṭṭhapāla, is it bearable for you? Have you come without hardship? Is food not being prepared in the house, dear?" We did not receive even a greeting in the manner of such hospitality. But why did the elder say this? Out of favor for his father. It seems it occurred to him thus: "As he speaks to me, I think he speaks thus to other renunciates as well. And in the Buddha's teaching, there is no end to monks whose hidden qualities are like a lotus in another's bowl, like fire covered with ashes, like the heartwood of sandalwood covered with bark, like a jewel covered with cloth, like the moon covered with clouds. He will not utter such words to those ones either, he will stand in restraint," out of favor he said this. kuto no neva dāna na paccakkhāna 0212"/> 0299"/> 0207"/>

ehi tātā means, "Daddy, don't let your house be [this way]. Come, daddy, let's go home," he says. ala means, the elder, rejecting the practice of eating a single meal while sitting in an austere manner, said this. adhivāsesī means, the elder, by nature a strict alms-seeker who goes from place to place, did not accept the discretionary alms, but he accepted them due to the favor of his mother. Remembering the elder Kirassa, great sorrow arose in his mother, and she became like someone who had her wings broken by crying. Therefore, the elder accepted it out of kindness, saying, "If I leave without seeing you, it would break her heart." kārāpetvā means, having made two heaps, one of silver ( *hirañña*) and one of gold (*suvaṇṇa*). How large were the heaps? Just as a man standing on this side cannot see a man of average height standing on the far side, so great were they.

ehi tātā ala adhivāsesī kārāpetvā

mula_pali: 301. Atha kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa pitā tassā rattiyā accayena sake nivesane paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa kālaṃ ārocesi – ‘‘kālo, tāta raṭṭhapāla, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta’’nti. Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena sakapitu nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa pitā taṃ hiraññasuvaṇṇassa puñjaṃ vivarāpetvā āyasmantaṃ raṭṭhapālaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘idaṃ te, tāta raṭṭhapāla, mātu mattikaṃ dhanaṃ, aññaṃ pettikaṃ, aññaṃ pitāmahaṃ. Sakkā, tāta raṭṭhapāla, bhoge ca bhuñjituṃ puññāni ca kātuṃ. Ehi tvaṃ, tāta raṭṭhapāla raṭṭhapāla sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya (sabbattha), hīnāyāvattitvā bhoge ca bhuñjassu puññāni ca karohī’’ti. ‘‘Sace me tvaṃ, gahapati, vacanaṃ kareyyāsi, imaṃ hiraññasuvaṇṇassa puñjaṃ sakaṭe āropetvā nibbāhāpetvā majjhegaṅgāya nadiyā sote opilāpeyyāsi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Ye uppajjissanti hi te, gahapati, tatonidānaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā’’ti. Atha kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa purāṇadutiyikā paccekaṃ pādesu gahetvā āyasmantaṃ raṭṭhapālaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘kīdisā nāma tā, ayyaputta, accharāyo yāsaṃ tvaṃ hetu brahmacariyaṃ carasī’’ti? ‘‘Na kho mayaṃ, bhaginī, accharānaṃ hetu brahmacariyaṃ carāmā’’ti. ‘‘Bhaginivādena no ayyaputto raṭṭhapālo samudācaratī’’ti tā tattheva mucchitā papatiṃsu. Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo pitaraṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sace, gahapati, bhojanaṃ dātabbaṃ, detha; mā no viheṭhethā’’ti. ‘‘Bhuñja, tāta raṭṭhapāla, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta’’nti. Atha kho āyasmato raṭṭhapālassa pitā āyasmantaṃ raṭṭhapālaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi.
mula_english:
Then, the venerable Raṭṭhapāla's father, as the night was ending, had exquisite staple and non-staple foods (*paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ*) prepared in his own house and had the time announced to the venerable Raṭṭhapāla: “It is time, dear Raṭṭhapāla, the meal is ready (*kālo, tāta raṭṭhapāla, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta*).”

Then, the venerable Raṭṭhapāla, early in the morning, having dressed, taking his bowl and outer robe, went to his own father’s house and sat down on the seat made ready.

Then his father, revealing the heap of gold and silver (*hiraññasuvaṇṇassa puñjaṃ*), said to the venerable Raṭṭhapāla, “This, my dear Raṭṭhapāla, is your maternal fortune (*mātu mattikaṃ dhanaṃ*); your paternal fortune is another, and your ancestral fortune is yet another.

Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you can enjoy the wealth and make merit (*bhoge ca bhuñjituṃ puññāni ca kātuṃ*).

Come then, dear Raṭṭhapāla, abandon the training and return to the low life, enjoy the wealth and make merit (*hīnāyāvattitvā bhoge ca bhuñjassu puññāni ca karohī*)!”

“Householder, if you would follow my advice, then have this pile of gold and silver (*hiraññasuvaṇṇassa puñjaṃ*) loaded on carts and carried away to be dumped midstream in the river Ganges.

Why is that? Because, householder, sorrows, lamentations, suffering, sadness, and despair will arise from that as the cause.”

Then, clasping each of his feet, the venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s former wives said to him, “What are they like, dear master-son, those nymphs (*accharāyo*) for whose sake you lead the holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ carasī*)?” “We do not lead the holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ carāmā*) for the sake of nymphs (*accharānaṃ*), sisters.”

“Our lord’s son Raṭṭhapāla calls us ‘sisters,’” they cried and right there they fainted.

Then the venerable Raṭṭhapāla said to his father, “Householder, if there is food to be given (*bhojanaṃ dātabbaṃ*), then give it. Do not harass us.”

“Eat then, dear Raṭṭhapāla, the meal is ready (*niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta*)!”

Then the venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s father served and satisfied the venerable Raṭṭhapāla with his own hands with exquisite staple and non-staple foods (*paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi*).
commentary_pali:
301.Idaṃ te tātāti kahāpaṇapuñjañca suvaṇṇapuñjañca dassento āha. Mattikanti mātito āgataṃ, idaṃ te mātāmahiyā mātu imaṃ gehaṃ āgacchantiyā gandhamālādīnaṃ atthāya dinnaṃ dhananti attho. Aññaṃ pettikaṃ aññaṃ pitāmahanti yaṃ pana te pitu ca pitāmahānañca santakaṃ, taṃ aññaṃyeva, nihitañca payuttañca ativiya bahu. Ettha ca ‘‘pitāmaha’’nti taddhitalopaṃ katvā vuttanti veditabbaṃ. ‘‘Petāmaha’’nti vā pāṭho. Sakkātatonidānanti dhanahetu dhanapaccayā. Taṃ taṃ dhanaṃ rakkhantassa ca rājādīnaṃ vasena dhanaparikkhayaṃ pāpuṇantassa kassaci uppajjamānasokādayo sandhāya evamāha. Evaṃ vutte seṭṭhi gahapati – ‘‘ahaṃ imaṃ uppabbājessāmīti ānesiṃ, so dāni me dhammakathaṃ kātuṃ āraddho, ayaṃ na me vacanaṃ karissatī’’ti uṭṭhāya gantvā assa orodhānaṃ dvāraṃ vivarāpetvā – ‘‘ayaṃ vo sāmiko, gacchatha yaṃ kiñci katvā naṃ gaṇhituṃ vāyamathā’’ti uyyojesi. Suvaye ṭhitā nāṭakitthiyo nikkhamitvā theraṃ parivārayiṃsu , tāsu dve jeṭṭhakitthiyo sandhāya purāṇadutiyikātiādi vuttaṃ. Paccekaṃ pādesu gahetvāti ekekamhi pāde naṃ gahetvā.

Kīdisānāma tā ayyaputta accharāyoti kasmā evamāhaṃsu? Tadā kira sambahule khattiyakumārepi brāhmaṇakumārepi seṭṭhiputtepi mahāsampattiyo pahāya pabbajante disvā pabbajjāguṇaṃ ajānantā kathaṃ samuṭṭhāpenti ‘‘kasmā ete pabbajantī’’ti. Athaññe vadanti ‘‘devaccharādevanāṭakānaṃ kāraṇā’’ti. Sā kathā vitthārikā ahosi. Taṃ gahetvā sabbā evamāhaṃsu. Atha thero paṭikkhipanto na kho mayaṃ bhaginītiādimāha. Samudācaratīti voharati vadati. Tattheva mucchitā papatiṃsūti taṃ bhaginivādena samudācarantaṃ disvā ‘‘mayaṃ ajja āgamissati, ajja āgamissatī’’ti dvādasa vassāni bahi na nikkhantā, etaṃ nissāya no dārakā na laddhā, yesaṃ ānubhāvena jīveyyāma, ito camhā parihīnā aññato ca. Ayaṃ loko nāma attanova cintesi, tasmā tāpi ‘‘idāni mayaṃ anāthā jātā’’ti attanova cintayamānā – ‘‘anatthiko dāni amhehi ayaṃ, so amhe pajāpatiyo samānā attanā saddhiṃ ekamātukucchiyā sayitadārikā viya maññatī’’ti samuppannabalavasokā hutvā tasmiṃyeva padese mucchitā papatiṃsu, patitāti attho.

Kīdisā nāma tā ayyaputta accharāyo na kho mayaṃ bhaginī Samudācaratī Tattheva mucchitā papatiṃsū

Mā no viheṭhethāti mā amhe dhanaṃ dassetvā mātugāme ca uyyojetvā viheṭhayittha, vihesā hesā pabbajitānanti. Kasmā evamāha? Mātāpitūnaṃ anuggahena. So kira seṭṭhi – ‘‘pabbajitaliṅgaṃ nāma kiliṭṭhaṃ, pabbajjāvesaṃ hāretvā nhāyitvā tayo janā ekato bhuñjissāmā’’ti maññamāno therassa bhikkhaṃ na deti. Thero – ‘‘mādisassa khīṇāsavassa āhārantarāyaṃ katvā ete bahuṃ apuññaṃ pasaveyyu’’nti tesaṃ anuggahena evamāha.

Mā no viheṭhethā
commentary_english:
301. “*Idaṃ te tātā*”: he said, showing a heap of *kahāpaṇas* and a heap of gold.

"*Mattika*": [means] that which came from the mother; this is the meaning: the money given by your maternal grandmother to your mother, who was coming to this house, for the sake of perfumes, garlands, and so on.

"*Aññaṃ pettikaṃ aññaṃ pitāmaha*": that which belongs to your father and your grandfathers is something different; it is indeed very much, deposited and utilized.

Here, it should be understood that “*pitāmaha*” is said after dropping the *taddhita*.

Or, “*petāmaha*” is a reading.

"*Tatonidāna*": because of wealth, due to wealth.

Having in mind the sorrows and so on that arise for someone who is protecting that wealth, and whose wealth meets with destruction due to kings and so on, he said thus.

When this was said, the wealthy householder [thought], “I brought him thinking, ‘I will have him renounce,’ now he has started to give me a *dhamma* talk; this one will not do my bidding,” and getting up, going, having opened the door of his harem, he urged [them on], “This is your master, go, do whatever you can, and strive to seize him.”

The actresses, standing in a good condition, went out and surrounded the *thera*, and having in mind those two elder actresses, he said “*purāṇadutiyikā*” and so on.

"*Paccekaṃ pādesu gahetvā*": having seized him by each foot.

“*Kīdisā nāma tā ayyaputta accharāyo*”: why did they say thus? At that time, seeing many Kṣatriya youths, Brāhmin youths, and sons of wealthy men renouncing, abandoning great wealth, and not knowing the good qualities of renunciation, how did they come to the conclusion, “Why are these ones renouncing?”

Others say, “Because of the celestial nymphs and celestial dramas.”

That talk became extensive.

Having taken him, all said thus.

Then the *thera*, rejecting [them], said, “*Na kho mayaṃ bhaginī*” and so on.

"*Samudācarati*": speaks, says.

"*Tattheva mucchitā papatiṃsū*": seeing him treat them with sisterly affection, [thinking,] “He will come today, he will come today,” they did not go outside for twelve years; depending on this, we did not get children, by whose power we might live, and from this we are diminished and from elsewhere too.

This world is named *attanova cintesi*, therefore those ones too, thinking, “Now we have become helpless,” — “This one is now without benefit for us; he considers us, being co-wives, like young girls sleeping in the same womb with himself,” — having become full of strong sorrow, in that very place they fainted and fell down, that is the meaning of fallen.

*Kīdisā nāma tā ayyaputta accharāyo na kho mayaṃ bhaginī samudācaratī tattheva mucchitā papatiṃsū mā no viheṭhethā*: "Do not harass us," [meaning] having shown wealth and having urged on the women, do not harass us; harassment is for those who have gone forth.

Why did he say thus? Because of the favor of his mother and father.

It is said that the wealthy man [thought], “The sign of a renunciate is defiled; having removed the garb of a renunciate, having bathed, we three people will eat together,” and thinking this, he did not give alms to the *thera*.

The *thera* [thought], “Having created an obstruction to the food of one like me, a *khīṇāsava*, these ones would generate much demerit,” and out of favor for them, he said thus.

*Mā no viheṭhethā*

mula_pali:
302. Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo bhuttāvī onītapattapāṇī ṭhitakova imā gāthā abhāsi –

‘‘Passa cittīkataṃ bimbaṃ, arukāyaṃ samussitaṃ;

Āturaṃ bahusaṅkappaṃ, yassa natthi dhuvaṃ ṭhiti.

‘‘Passa cittīkataṃ rūpaṃ, maṇinā kuṇḍalena ca;

Aṭṭhi tacena onaddhaṃ, saha vatthebhi sobhati.

‘‘Alattakakatā pādā, mukhaṃ cuṇṇakamakkhitaṃ;

Alaṃ bālassa mohāya, no ca pāragavesino.

‘‘Aṭṭhāpadakatā kesā, nettā añjanamakkhitā;

Alaṃ bālassa mohāya, no ca pāragavesino.

‘‘Añjanīva navā añjanīvaṇṇavā (ka.) cittā, pūtikāyo alaṅkato;

añjanīvaṇṇavā (ka.)

Alaṃ bālassa mohāya, no ca pāragavesino.

‘‘Odahi migavo pāsaṃ, nāsadā vākaraṃ migo;

Bhutvā nivāpaṃ gacchāma gacchāmi (syā. ka.), kandante migabandhake’’ti.

gacchāmi (syā. ka.)

Atha kho āyasmā raṭṭhapālo ṭhitakova imā gāthā bhāsitvā yena rañño korabyassa migacīraṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi.
commentary_pali:
302.Gāthā abhāsīti gāthāyo abhāsi. Tattha passāti santike ṭhitajanaṃ sandhāya vadati. Cittanti cittavicittaṃ. Bimbanti attabhāvaṃ. Arukāyanti navannaṃ vaṇamukhānaṃ vasena vaṇakāyaṃ. Samussitanti tīṇi aṭṭhisatāni navahi nhārusatehi bandhitvā navahi maṃsapesisatehi limpitvā samantato ussitaṃ. Āturanti jarāturatāya rogāturatāya kilesāturatāya ca niccāturaṃ. Bahusaṅkappanti paresaṃ uppannapatthanāsaṅkappehi bahusaṅkappaṃ . Itthīnañhi kāye purisānaṃ saṅkappā uppajjanti, tesaṃ kāye itthīnaṃ. Susāne chaḍḍitakaḷevarabhūtampi cetaṃ kākakulalādayo patthayantiyevāti bahusaṅkappo nāma hoti. Yassa natthidhuvaṃ ṭhitīti yassa kāyassa māyāmarīcipheṇapiṇḍa udakapupphuḷādīnaṃ viya ekaṃseneva ṭhiti nāma natthi, bhijjanadhammatāva niyatā.

Tacena onaddhanti allamanussacammena onaddhaṃ. Saha vatthebhi sobhatīti gandhādīhi maṇikuṇḍalehi ca cittakatampi rūpaṃ vatthehi saheva sobhati, vinā vatthehi jegucchaṃ hoti anolokanakkhamaṃ.

Tacena onaddha Saha vatthebhi sobhatī

Alattakakatāti alattakena rañjitā. Cuṇṇakamakkhitanti sāsapakakkena mukhapīḷakādīni nīharitvā loṇamattikāya duṭṭhalohitaṃ viliyāpetvā tilapiṭṭhena lohitaṃ pasādetvā haliddiyā vaṇṇaṃ sampādetvā cuṇṇakagaṇḍikāya mukhaṃ paharanti, tenesa ativiya virocati. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ.

Cuṇṇakamakkhita

Aṭṭhāpadakatāti rasodakena makkhitvā nalāṭapariyante āvattanaparivatte katvā aṭṭhapadakaracanāya racitā. Añjanīti añjananāḷikā.

Aṭṭhāpadakatā Añjanī

Odahīti ṭhapesi. Pāsanti vākarājālaṃ. Nāsadāti na ghaṭṭayi. Nivāpanti nivāpasutte vuttanivāpatiṇasadisabhojanaṃ. Kandanteti viravamāne paridevamāne. Imāya hi gāthāya thero mātāpitaro migaluddake viya katvā dassesi, avasesañātake migaluddakaparisaṃ viya, hiraññasuvaṇṇaṃ vākarājālaṃ viya, attanā bhuttabhojanaṃ nivāpatiṇaṃ viya, attānaṃ mahāmigaṃ viya katvā dassesi. Yathā hi mahāmigo yāvadatthaṃ nivāpatiṇaṃ khāditvā pānīyaṃ pivitvā gīvaṃ ukkhipitvā disaṃ oloketvā ‘‘imaṃ nāma ṭhānaṃ gatassa sotthi bhavissatī’’ti migaluddakānaṃ paridevantānaṃyeva vākaraṃ aghaṭṭayamānova uppatitvā araññaṃ pavisitvā ghanacchāyassa chattassa viya gumbassa heṭṭhā mandamandena vātena bījayamāno āgatamaggaṃ olokento tiṭṭhati, evameva thero imā gāthā bhāsitvā ākāseneva gantvā migacīre paccupaṭṭhāsi.

Odahī Pāsa Nāsadā Nivāpa Kandante

Kasmā pana thero ākāsena gatoti. Pitā kirassa seṭṭhi sattasu dvārakoṭṭhakesu aggaḷaṃ dāpetvā malle āṇāpesi – ‘‘sace nikkhamitvā gacchati , hatthapādesu naṃ gahetvā kāsāyāni haritvā gihivesaṃ gaṇhāpethā’’ti. Tasmā thero – ‘‘ete mādisaṃ mahākhīṇāsavaṃ hatthe vā pāde vā gahetvā apuññaṃ pasaveyyuṃ, taṃ nesaṃ mā ahosī’’ti cintetvā ākāsena agamāsi. Parasamuddavāsittherānaṃ pana – ‘‘ṭhitakova imā gāthā bhāsitvā vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā rañño korabyassa migacīre paccupaṭṭhāsī’’ti ayaṃ vācanāmaggoyeva.
commentary_english:
302. “*Gāthā abhāsī*” means *gāthāyo abhāsi*.

There, “*passā*" means he speaks in reference to the person standing nearby.

"*Citta*" means *cittavicittaṃ*.

"*Bimba*" means *attabhāvaṃ*.

"*Arukāya*" means, on page 3.0302, *navannaṃ vaṇamukhānaṃ vasena vaṇakāyaṃ*.

"*Samussita*" means it is raised up all around, having bound three hundred bones with nine hundred tendons, and having smeared [it] with nine hundred muscle fibers.

"*Ātura*" means constantly afflicted because of the affliction of old age, the affliction of disease, and the affliction of defilements.

"*Bahusaṅkappa*" means much intention through the intentions of others’ arisen desires, on page 3.0209.

Indeed, in the body of women, intentions arise for men; in the body of those, [intentions arise] for women.

Even this corpse discarded in a cemetery is desired by crows, vultures, and others; therefore, it is called much intention.

"*Yassa natthi dhuvaṃ ṭhitī*" means, on page 3.0214, because the body is like a magic mirage foam ball, it has no stability whatsoever like water bubbles, its nature is just to break apart, [therefore] it is impermanent.

"*Tacena onaddha*" means it is covered with fresh human skin.

"*Saha vatthebhi sobhatī*" means even a form that is decorated with fragrances and so forth, with jeweled earrings and so forth, is beautiful together with clothes; without clothes, it is disgusting and not fit to be looked at.

"*Tacena onaddha saha vatthebhi sobhatī*"

"*Alattakakatāti*" means it is dyed with lac.

"*Cuṇṇakamakkhita*" means having removed the pimples and so forth on the face with mustard paste, having dissolved the impure blood with salt clay, having purified the blood with sesame flour, having produced color with turmeric, they strike the face with powdered perfume; therefore, it shines exceedingly.

This was said with reference to him.

"*Cuṇṇakamakkhita*"

"*Aṭṭhāpadakatā*" means, on page 3.0303, having smeared [it] with flavored water, having made whirling turns at the forehead boundary, it is arranged by the arrangement of an *aṣṭāpada*.

"*Añjanī*" means an eyeliner tube.

"*Aṭṭhāpadakatā añjanī*"

"*Odahī*" means [he] placed [it].

"*Pāsa*" means a net of traps.

"*Nāsadā*" means he did not strike.

"*Nivāpa*" means food similar to the *nivāpa tiṇa* spoken of in the *nivāpa sutta*.

"*Kandante*" means while crying and lamenting.

Indeed, in this verse, the elder showed his mother and father as like deer hunters, he showed the remaining relatives as like the deer hunter's retinue, he showed gold and silver as like a net of traps, he showed his own eaten food as like *nivāpa tiṇa*, and he showed himself as like a great deer.

Just as a great deer, having eaten *nivāpa tiṇa* as much as it wanted, having drunk water, having raised its neck, having looked around in the directions, thinking “safety will come for one who has gone to such and such a place,” without even touching the trap of the deer hunters who are lamenting, having jumped up, having entered the forest, fanned by the gentle wind beneath the cluster of bushes like a thick-shaded parasol, stands watching the path it came from; just so, the elder, having spoken these verses, just as through the sky, having gone, stood before King Korabya’s deer pen.

"*Odahī pāsa nāsadā nivāpa kandante*"

Why then did the elder go through the sky?

His father, a wealthy man, having fastened the bolts on the seven gate chambers, on page 3.0215, having made [them] be given, ordered the wrestlers, "If he goes out, on page 3.0210, on page 3.0304, having seized him by the hands and feet, having taken away the monastic robes, make him take the householder’s dress.”

Therefore, the elder, thinking, “These might incur demerit by seizing someone like me, a great *khīṇāsava*, by the hands or feet; may that not happen to them," went through the sky.

However, to the elders dwelling by the Para Sea, “Just as he stood, having spoken these verses, having ascended into the sky, he stood before King Korabya’s deer pen," this itself is the traditional reading.
