Imehi pañcahi padhāniyaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu tathāgataṃ vināyakaṃ labhamāno – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyya cha rattindivāni… pañca rattindivāni… cattāri rattindivāni… tīṇi rattindivāni… dve rattindivāni… ekaṃ rattindivaṃ. Tiṭṭhatu, rājakumāra, eko rattindivo. Imehi pañcahi padhāniyaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu tathāgataṃ vināyakaṃ labhamāno sāyamanusiṭṭho pāto visesaṃ adhigamissati, pātamanusiṭṭho sāyaṃ visesaṃ adhigamissatī’’ti. Evaṃ vutte, bodhi rājakumāro bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘aho buddho, aho dhammo, aho dhammassa svākkhātatā! Yatra hi nāma sāyamanusiṭṭho pāto visesaṃ adhigamissati, pātamanusiṭṭho sāyaṃ visesaṃ adhigamissatī’’ti!
mula_english:
345. “Prince, when a *bhikkhu* who possesses these five factors of striving finds a *Tathāgata* to discipline him, for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness, he might dwell seven years until by realizing for himself with direct knowledge, he here and now enters upon and abides in that supreme goal of the holy life (*brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ*).

Let alone seven years, prince.

When a *bhikkhu* who possesses these five factors of striving finds a *Tathāgata* to discipline him, for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness, he might dwell six years…five years…four years…three years…two years…one year.

Let alone one year, prince.

When a *bhikkhu* who possesses these five factors of striving finds a *Tathāgata* to discipline him, for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness, he might dwell seven months.

Let alone seven months, prince.

When a *bhikkhu* who possesses these five factors of striving finds a *Tathāgata* to discipline him, for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness, he might dwell six months…five months…four months…three months…two months…one month…half a month.

Let alone half a month, prince.

When a *bhikkhu* who possesses these five factors of striving finds a *Tathāgata* to discipline him, for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness, he might dwell within seven days and nights.

Let alone seven days and nights, prince.

When a *bhikkhu* who possesses these five factors of striving finds a *Tathāgata* to discipline him, for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness, he might dwell six days and nights…five days and nights… four days and nights…three days and nights…two days and nights…one day and night.

Let alone one day and night, prince.

When a *bhikkhu* who possesses these five factors of striving finds a *Tathāgata* to discipline him, then being instructed in the evening, he might arrive at distinction in the morning; being instructed in the morning, he might arrive at distinction in the evening.”

When this was said, the Bodhi prince said this to the Blessed One: “Oh, Buddha! Oh, Dharma! Oh, well proclaimed is the Dharma! Where indeed, being instructed in the evening, he might arrive at distinction in the morning; being instructed in the morning, he might arrive at distinction in the evening!”
commentary_pali: 345.Sāyamanusiṭṭhopāto visesaṃ adhigamissatīti atthaṅgate sūriye anusiṭṭho aruṇuggamane visesaṃ adhigamissati. Pātamanusiṭṭho sāyanti aruṇuggamane anusiṭṭho sūriyatthaṅgamanavelāyaṃ. Ayañca pana desanā neyyapuggalavasena vuttā. Dandhapañño hi neyyapuggalo sattahi divasehi arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, tikkhapañño ekadivasena, sesadivase majjhimapaññāvasena veditabbaṃ. Aho buddho aho dhammo aho dhammassa svākkhātatāti yasmā buddhadhammānaṃ uḷāratāya dhammassa ca svākkhātatāya pāto kammaṭṭhānaṃ kathāpetvā sāyaṃ arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti, tasmā pasaṃsanto evamāha. Yatra hi nāmāti vimhayatthe nipāto.
commentary_english:
345. Having been instructed in the evening, "he will attain a distinction in the morning," he is instructed at sunset, he will attain a distinction at dawn.

Having been instructed in the morning, in the evening, he is instructed at dawn, at the time of sunset.

Moreover, this teaching is spoken in terms of a person who needs to be guided.

For a person of slow wisdom (dandhapañño), it takes seven days to attain arhatship; for a person of sharp wisdom (tikkhapañño), it takes one day; for the remaining days, it should be understood in terms of a person of middling wisdom (majjhimapaññāvasena).

"Oh, Buddha! Oh, Dharma! Oh, the well-proclaimed nature of the Dharma! (dhammassa svākkhātatā)" because by the greatness of the Buddha and the teachings, and by the well-proclaimed nature of the Dharma, having had a meditation topic (kammaṭṭhānaṃ) spoken about in the morning, he attains arhatship in the evening, therefore, praising, he says thus.

"Where, indeed, by name (yatra hi nāmā)!" is a particle in the sense of astonishment (vimhayatthe nipāto).

mula_pali:
346. Evaṃ vutte, sañjikāputto māṇavo bodhiṃ rājakumāraṃ etadavoca – ‘‘evameva panāyaṃ bhavaṃ bodhi – ‘aho buddho, aho dhammo, aho dhammassa svākkhātatā’ti ca vadeti vadesi (sī.), pavedeti (syā. kaṃ.); atha ca pana na taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchati dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañcā’’ti. ‘‘Mā hevaṃ, samma sañjikāputta, avaca; mā hevaṃ, samma sañjikāputta, avaca. Sammukhā metaṃ, samma sañjikāputta, ayyāya sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ’’. ‘‘Ekamidaṃ, samma sañjikāputta, samayaṃ bhagavā kosambiyaṃ viharati ghositārāme. Atha kho me ayyā kucchimatī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho me ayyā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘yo me ayaṃ, bhante, kucchigato kumārako vā kumārikā vā so bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchati dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ taṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata’nti. Ekamidaṃ, samma sañjikāputta, samayaṃ bhagavā idheva bhaggesu viharati susumāragire bhesakaḷāvane migadāye. Atha kho maṃ dhāti aṅkena haritvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho maṃ dhāti bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘ayaṃ , bhante, bodhi rājakumāro bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchati dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ taṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata’nti. Esāhaṃ, samma sañjikāputta, tatiyakampi bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata’’nti.

Bodhirājakumārasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.
mula_english:
346. When this was said, the brahmin student Sañjikāputta said to Prince Bodhi: “Master Bodhi says: ‘Oh the Buddha! Oh the *Dharma*! Oh, how well proclaimed is the *Dharma*!’ But he does not go to the esteemed Gotama for refuge, nor to the *Dharma*, nor to the *Saṃgha* of monks.”

“Do not say that, dear Sañjikāputta, do not say that. I have heard this directly from my mother, face to face, well received.”

“On one occasion, dear Sañjikāputta, the Blessed One (*Bhagavā*) was staying at Kosambi in Ghosita’s Park. Then my mother Kucchimati went to the Blessed One; having gone, she paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, my mother said this to the Blessed One: ‘The boy or girl in my womb, venerable sir (*bhante*), goes to the Blessed One for refuge, and to the *Dharma*, and to the *bhikkhu-saṃgha*. May the Blessed One remember him/her as a lay follower (*upāsaka*) who has gone for refuge from this day forth, for as long as life lasts.’”

“On another occasion, dear Sañjikāputta, the Blessed One was staying here in the country of the Bhaggas at Sumsumāragira in the Bhesakala Grove, the Deer Park. Then my nurse, taking me on her hip, went to the Blessed One; having gone, she paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, my nurse said this to the Blessed One: ‘This Prince Bodhi, venerable sir (*bhante*), goes to the Blessed One for refuge, and to the *Dharma*, and to the *bhikkhu-saṃgha*. May the Blessed One remember him as a lay follower (*upāsaka*) who has gone for refuge from this day forth, for as long as life lasts.’”

“So I, dear Sañjikāputta, for the third time go to the Blessed One for refuge, and to the *Dharma*, and to the *bhikkhu-saṃgha*. May the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower (*upāsaka*) who has gone for refuge from this day forth, for as long as life lasts.”

The Bodhirājakumāra Sutta, the fifth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
346.Kucchimatīti āpannasattā. Yo me ayaṃ, bhante, kucchigatoti kiṃ panevaṃ saraṇaṃ gahitaṃ hotīti. Na hoti. Acittakasaraṇagamanaṃ nāma natthi, ārakkho panassa paccupaṭṭhitova hoti. Atha naṃ yadā mahallakakāle mātāpitaro, – ‘‘tāta, kucchigatameva taṃ saraṇaṃ gaṇhāpayimhā’’ti sārenti, so ca sallakkhetvā ‘‘ahaṃ saraṇaṃ gato upāsako’’ti satiṃ uppādeti, tadā saraṇaṃ gahitaṃ nāma hoti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Bodhirājakumārasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
346. *Kucchimatī* means one who is pregnant (*āpannasattā*).

"Who is this that is in my womb (*kucchigato*)?" What kind of refuge (*saraṇaṃ*) is taken in this way?

It is not [a refuge].

There is no such thing as an unthinking refuge, but protection (*ārakkho*) is present.

Then, when her parents remind her in old age, "Dear, we had you take refuge (*saraṇaṃ*) while you were still in the womb (*kucchigataṃ eva*)", and she reflects and generates mindfulness, "I am a lay follower (*upāsako*) who has gone for refuge (*saraṇaṃ gato*)”, then it is said to be refuge taken (*saraṇaṃ gahitaṃ nāma hoti*).

The rest is clear throughout (*sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti*).

This concludes the commentary on the Bodhirājakumāra Sutta in the *Papañcasūdanī*, a commentary on the *Majjhimanikāya*.

mula_pali: 347. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena rañño pasenadissa kosalassa vijite coro aṅgulimālo nāma hoti luddo lohitapāṇi hatapahate niviṭṭho adayāpanno pāṇabhūtesu. Tena gāmāpi agāmā katā, nigamāpi anigamā katā, janapadāpi ajanapadā katā. So manusse vadhitvā vadhitvā aṅgulīnaṃ mālaṃ dhāreti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto senāsanaṃ saṃsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena coro aṅgulimālo tenaddhānamaggaṃ paṭipajji. Addasāsuṃ kho gopālakā pasupālakā kassakā pathāvino bhagavantaṃ yena coro aṅgulimālo tenaddhānamaggapaṭipannaṃ. Disvāna bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘mā, samaṇa, etaṃ maggaṃ paṭipajji. Etasmiṃ, samaṇa, magge coro aṅgulimālo nāma luddo lohitapāṇi hatapahate niviṭṭho adayāpanno pāṇabhūtesu. Tena gāmāpi agāmā katā, nigamāpi anigamā katā, janapadāpi ajanapadā katā. So manusse vadhitvā vadhitvā aṅgulīnaṃ mālaṃ dhāreti. Etañhi, samaṇa, maggaṃ dasapi purisā vīsampi purisā tiṃsampi purisā cattārīsampi purisā paññāsampi purisā saṅkaritvā saṅkaritvā saṃharitvā saṃharitvā (sī. pī.), saṅgaritvā (syā. kaṃ.) paṭipajjanti. Tepi corassa aṅgulimālassa hatthatthaṃ gacchantī’’ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhagavā tuṇhībhūto agamāsi. Dutiyampi kho gopālakā…pe… tatiyampi kho gopālakā pasupālakā kassakā pathāvino bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘mā, samaṇa, etaṃ maggaṃ paṭipajji, etasmiṃ samaṇa magge coro aṅgulimālo nāma luddo lohitapāṇi hatapahate niviṭṭho adayāpanno pāṇabhūtesu, tena gāmāpi agāmā katā, nigamāpi anigamā katā, janapadāpi ajanapadā katā. So manusse vadhitvā vadhitvā aṅgulīnaṃ mālaṃ dhāreti. Etañhi samaṇa maggaṃ dasapi purisā vīsampi purisā tiṃsampi purisā cattārīsampi purisā paññāsampi purisā saṅkaritvā saṅkaritvā paṭipajjanti. Tepi corassa aṅgulimālassa hatthatthaṃ gacchantī’’ti.
mula_english:
347. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapindika’s monastery.

And at that time, in King Pasenadi of Kosala's realm, there was a bandit named Aṅgulimāla, who was brutal, bloody-handed, devoted to killing and slaying, and showed no mercy to living beings.

He had turned villages into non-villages, towns into non-towns, settled countrysides into unsettled countrysides.

Having repeatedly killed human beings, he wore a garland of fingers (aṅgulīmāla).

Then, in the morning, having dressed, the Blessed One took his bowl and robe and entered Sāvatthī for alms.

Having wandered for alms in Sāvatthī, and returning from his alms round after his meal, he set his lodging in order. Carrying his bowl and robe, he went along the road to where the bandit Aṅgulimāla was staying.

Cowherds, shepherds, farmers, and travelers saw the Blessed One going along the road to where the bandit Aṅgulimāla was staying.

Having seen the Blessed One, they said this to him: "Don't go along that road, *samaṇa* (ascetic).

On that road, *samaṇa*, is the bandit Aṅgulimāla, who is brutal, bloody-handed, devoted to killing and slaying, and shows no mercy to living beings.

He has turned villages into non-villages, towns into non-towns, and settled countrysides into unsettled countrysides.

Having repeatedly killed human beings, he wears a garland of fingers.

Indeed, *samaṇa*, groups of ten, twenty, thirty, forty, even fifty men have gone along this road,

and even they have fallen into the hands of the bandit Aṅgulimāla."

When this was said, the Blessed One kept going in silence.

A second time... A third time, cowherds, shepherds, farmers, and travelers said this to the Blessed One: "Don't go along that road, *samaṇa*. On that road, *samaṇa*, is the bandit Aṅgulimāla, who is brutal, bloody-handed, devoted to killing and slaying, and shows no mercy to living beings. He has turned villages into non-villages, towns into non-towns, and settled countrysides into unsettled countrysides. So manusse vadhitvā vadhitvā aṅgulīnaṃ mālaṃ dhāreti.

Having repeatedly killed human beings, he wears a garland of fingers.

Indeed, *samaṇa*, groups of ten, twenty, thirty, forty, even fifty men have gone along this road,

and even they have fallen into the hands of the bandit Aṅgulimāla."
commentary_pali:
347.Evaṃme sutanti aṅgulimālasuttaṃ. Tattha aṅgulīnaṃ mālaṃ dhāretīti kasmā dhāreti? Ācariyavacanena. Tatrāyaṃ anupubbikathā –

Ayaṃ kira kosalarañño purohitassa mantāṇiyā nāma brāhmaṇiyā kucchismiṃ paṭisandhiṃ aggahesi. Brāhmaṇiyā rattibhāge gabbhavuṭṭhānaṃ ahosi. Tassa mātukucchito nikkhamanakāle sakalanagare āvudhāni pajjaliṃsu, rañño maṅgalasakuntopi sirisayane ṭhapitā asilaṭṭhipi pajjali. Brāhmaṇo nikkhamitvā nakkhattaṃ olokento coranakkhattena jātoti rañño santikaṃ gantvā sukhaseyyabhāvaṃ pucchi.

Rājā ‘‘kuto, me ācariya, sukhaseyyā? Mayhaṃ maṅgalāvudhaṃ pajjali, rajjassa vā jīvitassa vā antarāyo bhavissati maññe’’ti. Mā bhāyi, mahārāja, mayhaṃ ghare kumāro jāto, tassānubhāvena na kevalaṃ tuyhaṃ nivesane, sakalanagarepi āvudhāni pajjalitānīti. Kiṃ bhavissati ācariyāti? Coro bhavissati mahārājāti. Kiṃ ekacorako, udāhu rajjadūsako coroti? Ekacorako devāti. Evaṃ vatvā ca pana rañño manaṃ gaṇhitukāmo āha – ‘‘māretha naṃ devā’’ti. Ekacorako samāno kiṃ karissati? Karīsasahassakhette ekasālisīsaṃ viya hoti, paṭijaggatha nanti. Tassa nāmaggahaṇaṃ gaṇhantā sayane ṭhapitamaṅgalaasilaṭṭhi, chadane ṭhapitā sarā, kappāsapicumhi ṭhapitaṃ tālavaṇṭakaraṇasatthakanti ete pajjalantā kiñci na hiṃsiṃsu, tasmā ahiṃsakoti nāmaṃ akaṃsu. Taṃ sippuggahaṇakāle takkasīlaṃ pesayiṃsu.

ahiṃsako

So dhammantevāsiko hutvā sippaṃ paṭṭhapesi. Vattasampanno kiṃkārapaṭissāvī manāpacārī piyavādī ahosi. Sesaantevāsikā bāhirakā ahesuṃ. Te – ‘‘ahiṃsakamāṇavakassa āgatakālato paṭṭhāya mayaṃ na paññāyāma, kathaṃ naṃ bhindeyyāmā’’ti? Nisīditvā mantayantā – ‘‘sabbehi atirekapaññattā duppaññoti. Na sakkā vattuṃ, vattasampannattā dubbattoti. Na sakkā vattuṃ, jātisampannattā dujjātoti na sakkā vattuṃ, kinti karissāmā’’ti? Tato ekaṃ kharamantaṃ mantayiṃsu ‘‘ācariyassa antaraṃ katvā naṃ bhindissāmā’’ti tayo rāsī hutvā paṭhamaṃ ekacce ācariyaṃ upasaṅkamitvā vanditvā aṭṭhaṃsu. Kiṃ tātāti? Imasmiṃ gehe ekā kathā suyyatīti. Kiṃ tātāti? Ahiṃsakamāṇavo tumhākaṃ antare dubbhatīti maññāmāti. Ācariyo santajjetvā – ‘‘gacchatha vasalā, mā me puttaṃ mayhaṃ antare paribhindathā’’ti niṭṭhubhi. Tato itare, atha itarehi tayopi koṭṭhāsā āgantvā tatheva vatvā – ‘‘amhākaṃ asaddahantā upaparikkhitvā jānāthā’’ti āhaṃsu.

Ācariyo sinehena vadante disvā ‘‘atthi maññe santhavo’’ti paribhijjitvā cintesi ‘‘ghātemi na’’nti. Tato cintesi – ‘‘sace ghātessāmi ‘disāpāmokkho ācariyo attano santikaṃ sippuggahaṇatthaṃ āgate māṇavake dosaṃ uppādetvā jīvitā voropetī’ti. Puna koci sippuggahaṇatthaṃ na āgamissati, evaṃ me lābho parihāyissati, atha naṃ sippassa pariyosānupacāroti vatvā jaṅghasahassaṃ ghātehīti vakkhāmi. Avassaṃ ettha eko uṭṭhāya taṃ ghātessatī’’ti.

Atha naṃ āha – ‘‘ehi tāta jaṅghasahassaṃ ghātehi, evaṃ te sippassa upacāro kato bhavissatī’’ti. Mayaṃ ahiṃsakakule jātā, na sakkā ācariyāti. Aladdhupacāraṃ sippaṃ phalaṃ na deti tātāti. So pañcāvudhaṃ gahetvā ācariyaṃ vanditvā aṭaviṃ paviṭṭho. Aṭaviṃ pavisanaṭṭhānepi aṭavimajjhepi aṭavito nikkhamanaṭṭhānepi ṭhatvā manusse ghāteti. Vatthaṃ vā veṭhanaṃ vā na gaṇhāti. Eko dveti gaṇitamattameva karonto gacchati, gaṇanampi na uggaṇhāti. Pakatiyāpi paññavā esa, pāṇātipātino pana cittaṃ na patiṭṭhāti, tasmā anukkamena gaṇanampi na sallakkhesi, ekekaṃ aṅguliṃ chinditvā ṭhapeti. Ṭhapitaṭṭhāne aṅguliyo vinassanti, tato vijjhitvā aṅgulīnaṃ mālaṃ katvā dhāresi, teneva cassa aṅgulimāloti saṅkhā udapādi. So sabbaṃ araññaṃ nissañcāramakāsi, dāruādīnaṃ atthāya araññaṃ gantuṃ samattho nāma natthi.

Rattibhāge antogāmampi āgantvā pādena paharitvā dvāraṃ ugghāteti. Tato sayiteyeva māretvā eko ekoti gahetvā gacchati. Gāmo osaritvā nigame aṭṭhāsi, nigamo nagare. Manussā tiyojanato paṭṭhāya gharāni pahāya dārake hatthesu gahetvā āgamma sāvatthiṃ parivāretvā khandhāvāraṃ bandhitvā rājaṅgaṇe sannipatitvā – ‘‘coro, te deva, vijite aṅgulimālo nāmā’’tiādīni vadantā kandanti. Bhaggavo ‘‘mayhaṃ putto bhavissatī’’ti ñatvā brāhmaṇiṃ āha – bhoti aṅgulimālo nāma coro uppanno, so na añño, tava putto ahiṃsakakumāro. Idāni rājā taṃ gaṇhituṃ nikkhamissati, kiṃ kattabbanti? Gaccha sāmi, puttaṃ me gahetvā ehīti. Nāhaṃ bhadde ussahāmi, catūsu hi janesu vissāso nāma natthi, coro me purāṇasahāyoti avissāsanīyo, sākhā me purāṇasanthatāti avissāsanīyā, rājā maṃ pūjetīti avissāsanīyo, itthī me vasaṃ gatāti avissāsanīyāti. Mātu hadayaṃ pana mudukaṃ hoti. Tasmā ahaṃ pana gantvā mayhaṃ puttaṃ ānessāmīti nikkhantā.

Taṃdivasañca bhagavā paccūsasamaye lokaṃ volokento aṅgulimālaṃ disvā – ‘‘mayi gate etassa sotthi bhavissati. Agāmake araññe ṭhito catuppadikaṃ gāthaṃ sutvā mama santike pabbajitvā cha abhiññā sacchikarissati. Sace na gamissāmi, mātari aparajjhitvā anuddharaṇīyo bhavissati, karissāmissa saṅgaha’’nti pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā piṇḍāya pavisitvā katabhattakicco taṃ saṅgaṇhitukāmo vihārā nikkhami. Etamatthaṃ dassetuṃ ‘‘atha kho bhagavā’’tiādi vuttaṃ.
commentary_english:
347. Thus have I heard. This is the Aṅgulimāla Sūtra. Therein, regarding "he wears a garland of fingers," why does he wear [it]? Because of his teacher's instruction. This is the sequential story: It is said that he took rebirth in the womb of a Brāhmaṇī woman named Mantāṇī, the chief queen of King Kosala. In the night, the Brāhmaṇī experienced a stirring in her womb. At the time of his birth from his mother's womb, weapons blazed in the entire city, and the king's auspicious bird, which had been placed on the royal bed, also blazed. The Brahmin, having gone out, while looking at the constellation, [saw that he] was born under a robber constellation. So he went to the king and asked about [his] happiness and rest. The king [asked], "Where is happiness, teacher? My auspicious weapons are blazing; I think there will be an obstacle to the kingdom or to life." [The Brāhmin replied,] "Do not fear, great king; a boy has been born in my house. By the power of his merit, not only in your palace, but also in the entire city weapons are blazing." "What will he become, teacher?" "He will become a thief, great king." "Will he be a lone thief, or a thief who harms the kingdom?" "He will be a lone thief, deva." Having spoken thus, wishing to grasp the king's mind, he said, "Kill him, deva!" "Being a lone thief, what will he do? He will be like a single rice stalk in a field of a thousand *karīsa*s. Guard him!" While they were taking his name, the auspicious sword-stick that had been placed on the bed, the arrows that had been placed on the roof, and the razor for making *tālavaṇṭa*s that had been placed in the cotton [all] blazed. These, while blazing, did no harm. Therefore they gave him the name *Ahiṃsaka* (Non-Harmer). At the time for receiving instruction in the arts, they sent him to Takkasīla. *Ahiṃsaka*, having become a resident of the Dharma, began his training in the arts. He was accomplished in his vows, quick to respond to what needed to be done, pleasant in his conduct, and sweet in his speech. The other residents became hostile. They [thought], "From the time Ahiṃsaka-youth arrived, we are not known [or, visible]. How can we break him?" Sitting down, they planned, "Having made a separation between the teacher, we will break him." Becoming three groups, first some approached the teacher, bowed, and stood [before him]. "What is it, tāta?" "In this house a story is heard." "What is it, tāta?" "We think that Ahiṃsaka-youth is ruining [you] among yourselves." The teacher, scolding, said, "Go away, *vasala*s! Do not destroy my son among yourselves!" And he spat [at them]. Then the others, and then those three groups also, having come and having spoken in the same way, said, "Not believing us, examine and know [for yourselves]!" The teacher, having seen them speaking with affection, thinking "There must be attachment," considered, "Should I kill him or not?" Then he thought, "If I kill him, [people will say] 'The teacher, the leader of the region, having created an offense, deprives of life the youth who has come to his presence to receive instruction in the arts.'" Again, no one will come to receive instruction in the arts; thus my gain will be diminished." Then, [thinking] "He is no longer of use for the arts," I will say, "Kill a thousand men!" Surely one will rise up here and kill him. 0228"/> Then he said to him: “Come, dear father, kill a thousand men, thus proper respect will be shown to your craft ( *śippa* , skill).” “We are born in a family that does not harm living beings, it is not possible, teacher.” “A craft ( *śippa* , skill) without proper respect does not give fruit, dear father.” He took the five weapons, paid homage to his teacher, and entered the forest. Even at the place of entering the forest, even in the middle of the forest, even at the place of exiting the forest, having stood, he would kill people. He would not take clothing or wrapping. Counting only “one, two,” he goes, he does not even learn counting. Even by nature, he is wise, but his mind does not settle because he is a slayer of living beings. Therefore, unsystematically, he does not even consider counting, having cut off each finger, he sets it aside. The fingers rot in the place where they are set aside; therefore, having pierced [them], having made a garland of fingers, he wore it. Because of that, the designation "Aṅgulimāla" (garland of fingers) arose in him. He made the entire forest devoid of movement; there was no one by name who was able to go to the forest for the sake of wood and so on.

In the night part even having come to a village, having struck the door with his foot, he would knock it down. Then, having killed [people] even in their sleep, taking “one, one,” he goes. The village moved away [to another place], it stayed in a market town; the market town [moved] to a city. People, starting from three *yojanas* away, abandoning their houses, taking their children in their hands, having come, surrounding Sāvatthī, having built a camp, having gathered in the royal courtyard, said: "A thief, Aṅgulimāla by name, is in your majesty's conquered territory," and so on, speaking, they wept. Bhaggava, knowing that "He will be my son," said to the *brāhmaṇī*: “Lady, a thief named Aṅgulimāla has arisen; he is none other than your son, Ahimsakakumāra (the harmless youth)." Now the king will go out to seize him. What should be done?" "Go, husband, take my son and come here." "I am not able, noble lady, for indeed, there is no trust in four types of people: a thief is untrustworthy because he is my old friend; a branch (of a tree) is untrustworthy because it is my old resting place; a king is untrustworthy because he reveres me; a woman is untrustworthy because she has come under my control." But a mother’s heart is tender. Therefore, having decided, "I myself will go and bring my son," she departed.

On that day, the Blessed One, at dawn, looking at the world, seeing Aṅgulimāla, [thought:] "If I go, there will be well-being for him. Having stood in a forest without a village, having heard a four-lined verse, having gone forth in my presence, he will realize the six *abhiññās* (supernormal knowledges)." "If I do not go, having offended his mother, he will be irredeemable; I will make an act of grace towards him," having dressed in the early morning, having entered [the village] for alms, having finished his meal, desiring to favor him, he departed from the *vihāra*. To show this meaning, "Then, indeed, the Blessed One," and so on, was said.

mula_pali: 348. Atha kho bhagavā tuṇhībhūto agamāsi. Addasā kho coro aṅgulimālo bhagavantaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvānassa etadahosi – ‘‘acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho! Imañhi maggaṃ dasapi purisā vīsampi purisā tiṃsampi purisā cattārīsampi purisā paññāsampi purisā saṅkaritvā saṅkaritvā paṭipajjanti. Tepi mama hatthatthaṃ gacchanti. Atha ca panāyaṃ samaṇo eko adutiyo pasayha maññe āgacchati. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ samaṇaṃ jīvitā voropeyya’’nti. Atha kho coro aṅgulimālo asicammaṃ gahetvā dhanukalāpaṃ sannayhitvā bhagavantaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhi. Atha kho bhagavā tathārūpaṃ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkhāsi abhisaṅkhāresi (syā. kaṃ. ka.) yathā coro aṅgulimālo bhagavantaṃ pakatiyā gacchantaṃ sabbathāmena gacchanto na sakkoti sampāpuṇituṃ. Atha kho corassa aṅgulimālassa etadahosi – ‘‘acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho! Ahañhi pubbe hatthimpi dhāvantaṃ anupatitvā gaṇhāmi, assampi dhāvantaṃ anupatitvā gaṇhāmi, rathampi dhāvantaṃ anupatitvā gaṇhāmi, migampi dhāvantaṃ anupatitvā gaṇhāmi; atha ca panāhaṃ imaṃ samaṇaṃ pakatiyā gacchantaṃ sabbathāmena gacchanto na sakkomi sampāpuṇitu’’nti! Ṭhitova bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘tiṭṭha, tiṭṭha, samaṇā’’ti. ‘‘Ṭhito ahaṃ, aṅgulimāla, tvañca tiṭṭhā’’ti. Atha kho corassa aṅgulimālassa etadahosi – ‘‘ime kho samaṇā sakyaputtiyā saccavādino saccapaṭiññā. Atha panāyaṃ samaṇo gacchaṃ yevāha – ‘ṭhito ahaṃ, aṅgulimāla, tvañca tiṭṭhā’ti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ samaṇaṃ puccheyya’’nti.
mula_english:
348. Then the Blessed One, remaining silent, went on.

The thief Aṅgulimāla saw the Blessed One coming in the distance.

Seeing him, he thought: “It is wonderful, truly amazing! Groups of ten, twenty, thirty, forty, and fifty men go along this road, struggling along.

And even they fall into my hands. But now this ascetic comes attacking, as it were, alone and without a companion.

Why don’t I rob this ascetic of his life?”

Then the thief Aṅgulimāla, taking up his sword and shield, buckling on his bow and quiver, followed right behind the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One worked such a feat of psychic power that Aṅgulimāla, though running with all his might, could not catch up with the Blessed One walking at normal pace.

Then this thought occurred to the thief Aṅgulimāla: “It is wonderful, truly amazing! In the past I could catch even a running elephant, a running horse, a running chariot, a running deer. But now, though running with all my might, I cannot catch up with this ascetic walking at normal pace!” He stopped and said this to the Blessed One: “Stop, stop, ascetic!”

“I have stopped, Aṅgulimāla. You stop.”

Then this thought occurred to the thief Aṅgulimāla: “These ascetics, sons of the Śākyans, are speakers of the truth, asserters of the truths. But this ascetic, even while walking, says, ‘I have stopped, Aṅgulimāla. You stop.’ Why don’t I question this ascetic?”
commentary_pali:
348.Saṅkaritvā saṅkaritvāti saṅketaṃ katvā vaggavaggā hutvā. Hatthatthaṃ gacchantīti hatthe atthaṃ vināsaṃ gacchanti. Kiṃ pana te bhagavantaṃ sañjānitvā evaṃ vadanti asañjānitvāti? Asañjānitvā. Aññātakavesena hi bhagavā ekakova agamāsi. Coropi tasmiṃ samaye dīgharattaṃ dubbhojanena ca dukkhaseyyāya ca ukkaṇṭhito hoti. Kittakā panānena manussā māritāti? Ekenūnasahassaṃ. So pana idāni ekaṃ labhitvā sahassaṃ pūressatīti saññī hutvā yameva paṭhamaṃ passāmi, taṃ ghātetvā gaṇanaṃ pūretvā sippassa upacāraṃ katvā kesamassuṃ ohāretvā nhāyitvā vatthāni parivattetvā mātāpitaro passissāmīti aṭavimajjhato aṭavimukhaṃ āgantvā ekamantaṃ ṭhitova bhagavantaṃ addasa. Etamatthaṃ dassetuṃ ‘‘addasā kho’’tiādi vuttaṃ.

Iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkhāsīti mahāpathaviṃ ummiyo uṭṭhapento viya saṃharitvā aparabhāge akkamati, orabhāge valiyo nikkhamanti, aṅgulimālo sarakkhepamattaṃ muñcitvā gacchati. Bhagavā purato mahantaṃ aṅgaṇaṃ dassetvā sayaṃ majjhe hoti, coro ante. So ‘‘idāni naṃ pāpuṇitvā gaṇhissāmī’’ti sabbathāmena dhāvati. Bhagavā aṅgaṇassa pārimante hoti, coro majjhe. So ‘‘ettha naṃ pāpuṇitvā gaṇhissāmī’’ti vegena dhāvati. Bhagavā tassa purato mātikaṃ vā thalaṃ vā dasseti, etenupāyena tīṇi yojanāni gahetvā agamāsi. Coro kilami, mukhe kheḷo sussi, kacchehi sedā mucciṃsu. Athassa ‘‘acchariyaṃ vata bho’’ti etadahosi. Migampīti migaṃ kasmā gaṇhāti? Chātasamaye āhāratthaṃ. So kira ekaṃ gumbaṃ ghaṭṭetvā mige uṭṭhāpeti. Tato cittaruciyaṃ migaṃ anubandhanto gaṇhitvā pacitvā khādati. Puccheyyanti yena kāraṇenāyaṃ gacchantova ṭhito nāma , ahañca ṭhitova aṭṭhito nāma, yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ samaṇaṃ taṃ kāraṇaṃ puccheyyanti attho.

Iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkhāsī Migampī Puccheyya
commentary_english:
348. "Having combined, having combined," means having made a sign, having become groups of groups.
"Going to ruin in the hand," means they go to ruin, destruction, in the hand.
Why then do they speak thus, knowing or not knowing the Blessed One? Not knowing.
Indeed, the Blessed One, with an unrecognisable appearance, went alone.
The thief too, at that time, was distressed by the long night, and by bad food, and by a painful bed.
How many men were killed by him? One less than a thousand.
He, thinking, "Having obtained one now, I will complete a thousand," thinking "whomever I see first, having killed him, having completed the count, having made an offering for the craft, having shaved off the hair and beard, having bathed, having exchanged the clothes, I will see [my] mother and father," having come from the middle of the forest to the edge of the forest, he saw the Blessed One standing alone.
To show this meaning, "He saw" etc. was said.

"Having intentionally prepared, he prepared," means having gathered together the great earth like raising waves, he steps in another part, folds come out in this part, Aṅgulimāla, having released [himself] for just the time of a snap of the fingers, goes.
The Blessed One, having shown a great courtyard in front, himself stays in the middle, the thief [stays] at the edge.
He, thinking "Having reached him now, I will seize him", runs with all [his] strength.
The Blessed One is at the edge of the courtyard, the thief in the middle.
He, thinking "Having reached him here, I will seize him," runs with speed.
The Blessed One shows either a mat or a flat surface in front of him, by this means he went, having taken three *yojanā*s.
The thief was exhausted, saliva dried in [his] mouth, sweat flowed from [his] armpits.
Then this thought occurred to him: "Isn't it amazing, indeed!"
"*Migampī*," means why does he seize a deer? For the sake of food at the time of hunger.
He, they say, having struck a bush, makes the deer get up.
Then, following a deer in Cittaruciya, having seized [it], having cooked [it], he eats [it].
"*Puccheyya*," means why is it that this one, while going, stands, and I, although standing, [am] not standing. The meaning is, "Why should I not ask that ascetic this reason?"

"Having intentionally prepared, he prepared"
*Migampī*
*Puccheyya*

mula_pali:
349. Atha kho coro aṅgulimālo bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

‘‘Gacchaṃ vadesi samaṇa ṭhitomhi,

Mamañca brūsi ṭhitamaṭṭhitoti;

Pucchāmi taṃ samaṇa etamatthaṃ,

Kathaṃ ṭhito tvaṃ ahamaṭṭhitomhī’’ti.

‘‘Ṭhito ahaṃ aṅgulimāla sabbadā,

Sabbesu bhūtesu nidhāya daṇḍaṃ;

Tuvañca pāṇesu asaññatosi,

Tasmā ṭhitohaṃ tuvamaṭṭhitosī’’ti.

‘‘Cirassaṃ vata me mahito mahesī,

Mahāvanaṃ pāpuṇi saccavādī mahāvanaṃ samaṇoyaṃ paccupādi (sī.), mahāvanaṃ samaṇa paccupādi (syā. kaṃ.);

mahāvanaṃ samaṇoyaṃ paccupādi (sī.), mahāvanaṃ samaṇa paccupādi (syā. kaṃ.)

Sohaṃ carissāmi pahāya pāpaṃ sohaṃ cirassāpi pahāssaṃ pāpaṃ (sī.), sohaṃ carissāmi pajahissaṃ pāpaṃ (syā. kaṃ.),

sohaṃ cirassāpi pahāssaṃ pāpaṃ (sī.), sohaṃ carissāmi pajahissaṃ pāpaṃ (syā. kaṃ.)

Sutvāna gāthaṃ tava dhammayuttaṃ’’.

Itveva coro asimāvudhañca,

Sobbhe papāte narake akiri;

Avandi coro sugatassa pāde,

Tattheva naṃ pabbajjaṃ ayāci.

Buddho ca kho kāruṇiko mahesi,

Yo satthā lokassa sadevakassa;

‘Tamehi bhikkhū’ti tadā avoca,

Eseva tassa ahu bhikkhubhāvoti.
commentary_pali:
349.Nidhāyāti yo vihiṃsanatthaṃ bhūtesu daṇḍo pavattayitabbo siyā, taṃ nidhāya apanetvā mettāya khantiyā paṭisaṅkhāya avihiṃsāya sāraṇīyadhammesu ca ṭhito ahanti attho. Tuvamaṭṭhitosīti pāṇesu asaññatattā ettakāni pāṇasahassāni ghātentassa tava mettā vā khanti vā paṭisaṅkhā vā avihiṃsā vā sāraṇīyadhammo vā natthi, tasmā tuvaṃ aṭṭhitosi, idāni iriyāpathena ṭhitopi niraye dhāvissasi, tiracchānayoniyaṃ pettivisaye asurakāye vā dhāvissasīti vuttaṃ hoti.

Tato coro – ‘‘mahā ayaṃ sīhanādo, mahantaṃ gajjitaṃ, na idaṃ aññassa bhavissati, mahāmāyāya puttassa siddhatthassa samaṇarañño etaṃ gajjitaṃ, diṭṭho vatamhi maññe tikhiṇacakkhunā sammāsambuddhena, saṅgahakaraṇatthaṃ me bhagavā āgato’’ti cintetvā cirassaṃ vata metiādimāha. Tattha mahitoti devamanussādīhi catupaccayapūjāya pūjito. Paccupādīti cirassaṃ kālassa accayena mayhaṃ saṅgahatthāya imaṃ mahāvanaṃ paṭipajji. Pahāya pāpanti pajahitvā pāpaṃ.

cirassaṃ vata me mahito Paccupādī Pahāya pāpa

Itvevāti evaṃ vatvāyeva. Āvudhanti pañcāvudhaṃ. Sobbheti samantato chinne. Papāteti ekato chinne. Naraketi phalitaṭṭhāne. Idha pana tīhipi imehi padehi araññameva vuttaṃ. Akirīti khipi chaḍḍesi.

Itvevā Āvudha Sobbhe Papāte Narake Akirī

Tamehibhikkhūti tadā avocāti bhagavato imaṃ pabbājento kuhiṃ satthakaṃ labhissāmi, kuhiṃ pattacīvaranti pariyesanakiccaṃ natthi, kammaṃ pana olokesi. Athassa pubbe sīlavantānaṃ aṭṭhaparikkhārabhaṇḍakassa dinnabhāvaṃ ñatvā dakkhiṇahatthaṃ pasāretvā – ‘‘ehi bhikkhu svākkhāto dhammo, cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā’’ti āha. So saha vacaneneva iddhimayapattacīvaraṃ paṭilabhi. Tāvadevassa gihiliṅgaṃ antaradhāyi, samaṇaliṅgaṃ pāturahosi.

Tamehi bhikkhūti tadā avocā

‘‘Ticīvarañca patto ca, vāsi sūci ca bandhanaṃ;

Parissāvanena aṭṭhete, yuttayogassa bhikkhuno’’ti. –

Evaṃ vuttā aṭṭha parikkhārā sarīrapaṭibaddhāva hutvā nibbattiṃsu. Eseva tassa ahu bhikkhubhāvoti esa ehibhikkhubhāvo tassa upasampannabhikkhubhāvo ahosi, na hi ehibhikkhūnaṃ visuṃ upasampadā nāma atthi.

Eseva tassa ahu bhikkhubhāvo
commentary_english:
349. *Nidhāya* means that one should put aside the rod of violence that should be wielded against beings for the purpose of harming them. Having removed it, the meaning is that one stands in loving-kindness (*maitrī*), patience (*kṣānti*), reflection (*pratisaṃkhyā*), non-violence (*avihiṃsā*), and the practices that bring about mindfulness (*sāraṇīyadharma*).

*Tuvamaṭṭhitosī* means because of your lack of restraint towards beings, you, who have caused the slaughter of so many thousands of living beings, have no loving-kindness, patience, reflection, non-violence or mindfulness practices. Therefore, you are unsteady. Now, even standing in the posture [of a human], you will run to hell (*niraya*); it is said that you will run to the animal realm (*tiracchānayoni*), the realm of the departed spirits (*pretaviṣaya*), or the body of an *asura*.

Then the thief thought, "This is a great lion's roar, a great thunder! This will not belong to another. This thunder is from the *śramaṇa* king Siddhārtha, the son of Mahāmāyā. I think I have been seen by the perfectly awakened one (*samyaksambuddha*) with sharp eyes. The Blessed One (*bhagavān*) has come to me for the sake of gathering [me in]," and having thought, he spoke, beginning with *cirassaṃ vata me*.
There, *mahito* means honored with the four requisites of worship (*catupaccayapūjā*) by gods, humans, and so on.
*Paccupādī* means he approached this great forest (*mahāvana*) for my benefit after a long time [and] the passing of time.
*Pahāya pāpa* means having abandoned evil (*pāpa*).

*Cirassaṃ vata me mahito paccupādī pahāya pāpa itvevā* means just having spoken thus.
*Āvudha* means five weapons (*pañcāvudha*).
*Sobbhe* means cut off all around (*samantataḥ chinne*).
*Papāte* means cut off on one side (*ekataḥ chinne*).
*Narake* means in a place that bears fruit (*phalitaṭṭhāne*).
Here, however, the forest (*araṇya*) itself is described by these three terms.
*Akirī* means he threw and discarded (*khipi chaḍḍesi*).

*Itvevā ādudha sobbe papāte narake akirī tamehi bhikkhūti tadā avocā* means when the Blessed One (*bhagavān*) ordained him, [he] wondered, "Where will I obtain a knife? Where [will I obtain] a bowl and robe?" There was no task of seeking these things, but he looked at his own karma (*karma*).
Then, knowing that he had previously been given the state of possessing the eight requisites (*aṣṭaparikṣārabhaṇḍaka*) by virtuous ones, he stretched out his right hand and said, "Come, monk (*bhikṣu*)! The *dharma* is well-proclaimed (*svākkhāta*). Practice the pure life (*brahmacarya*) for the complete ending of suffering (*duḥkha*)!"
Together with the utterance, he obtained a bowl and robe made of miraculous power (*ṛddhimaya*).
Immediately, his householder's marks disappeared, and the marks of a *śramaṇa* became manifest.

*Tamehi bhikkhūti tadā avocā* "The three robes, the bowl, the razor, the needle, and the belt; these eight are with the monk who is engaged in yoga (*yoga*)."
In this way, the eight requisites, having become bound to his body, arose.
*Eseva tassa ahu bhikkhubhāvo* means that this very state of being a monk (*bhikkhubhāva*) was his state of being a fully ordained monk (*upasampannabhikkhubhāva*). Indeed, there is no separate ordination (*upasampadā*) for those who are "come, monk" (*ehi-bhikkhu*).

*Eseva tassa ahu bhikkhubhāvo*

mula_pali:
350. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmatā aṅgulimālena pacchāsamaṇena yena sāvatthi tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena sāvatthi tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena rañño pasenadissa kosalassa antepuradvāre mahājanakāyo sannipatitvā uccāsaddo mahāsaddo hoti – ‘‘coro te, deva, vijite aṅgulimālo nāma luddo lohitapāṇi hatapahate niviṭṭho adayāpanno pāṇabhūtesu. Tena gāmāpi agāmā katā, nigamāpi anigamā katā, janapadāpi ajanapadā katā. So manusse vadhitvā vadhitvā aṅgulīnaṃ mālaṃ dhāreti. Taṃ devo paṭisedhetū’’ti.

Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo pañcamattehi assasatehi sāvatthiyā nikkhami divā divassa. Yena ārāmo tena pāvisi. Yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi yānena gantvā yānā paccorohitvā pattikova yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho rājānaṃ pasenadiṃ kosalaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘kiṃ nu te, mahārāja, rājā vā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro kupito vesālikā vā licchavī aññe vā paṭirājāno’’ti? ‘‘Na kho me, bhante, rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro kupito, nāpi vesālikā licchavī, nāpi aññe paṭirājāno. Coro me, bhante, vijite aṅgulimālo nāma luddo lohitapāṇi hatapahate niviṭṭho adayāpanno pāṇabhūtesu. Tena gāmāpi agāmā katā, nigamāpi anigamā katā, janapadāpi ajanapadā katā. So manusse vadhitvā vadhitvā aṅgulīnaṃ mālaṃ dhāreti. Tāhaṃ, bhante, paṭisedhissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Sace pana tvaṃ, mahārāja, aṅgulimālaṃ passeyyāsi kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitaṃ, virataṃ pāṇātipātā, virataṃ adinnādānā, virataṃ musāvādā, ekabhattikaṃ, brahmacāriṃ, sīlavantaṃ, kalyāṇadhammaṃ, kinti naṃ kareyyāsī’’ti? ‘‘Abhivādeyyāma vā, bhante, paccuṭṭheyyāma vā āsanena vā nimanteyyāma, abhinimanteyyāma vā naṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārehi, dhammikaṃ vā assa rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṃ saṃvidaheyyāma. Kuto panassa, bhante, dussīlassa pāpadhammassa evarūpo sīlasaṃyamo bhavissatī’’ti?

Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā aṅgulimālo bhagavato avidūre nisinno hoti. Atha kho bhagavā dakkhiṇaṃ bāhuṃ paggahetvā rājānaṃ pasenadiṃ kosalaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘eso, mahārāja, aṅgulimālo’’ti. Atha kho rañño pasenadissa kosalassa ahudeva bhayaṃ, ahu chambhitattaṃ, ahu lomahaṃso. Atha kho bhagavā rājānaṃ pasenadiṃ kosalaṃ bhītaṃ saṃviggaṃ lomahaṭṭhajātaṃ viditvā rājānaṃ pasenadiṃ kosalaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘mā bhāyi, mahārāja, natthi te ito bhaya’’nti. Atha kho rañño pasenadissa kosalassa yaṃ ahosi bhayaṃ vā chambhitattaṃ vā lomahaṃso vā so paṭippassambhi. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo yenāyasmā aṅgulimālo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ aṅgulimālaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘ayyo no, bhante, aṅgulimālo’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ, mahārājā’’ti. ‘‘Kathaṃgotto ayyassa pitā, kathaṃgottā mātā’’ti? ‘‘Gaggo kho, mahārāja, pitā, mantāṇī mātā’’ti. ‘‘Abhiramatu, bhante, ayyo gaggo mantāṇiputto. Ahamayyassa gaggassa mantāṇiputtassa ussukkaṃ karissāmi cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārāna’’nti.
mula_english:
Then the Blessed One set out wandering toward Sāvatthī with Venerable Aṅgulimāla as his attendant monk.

Wandering by stages, he eventually arrived at Sāvatthī.

There he lived in Jeta’s Wood, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.

Now at that time a large crowd of people, loud & noisy, had gathered at the gates to King Pasenadi Kosala’s inner palace, calling out, “There is a bandit in your realm, sire, named Aṅgulimāla: brutal, bloody-handed, devoted to killing & slaying, showing no mercy to living beings.

He turned villages into non-villages, towns into non-towns, settled countryside into unsettled countryside.

Having repeatedly killed human beings, he wears a garland made of fingers.

The king must stamp him out!”

Then King Pasenadi Kosala, with a cavalry of roughly 500 horsemen, drove out of Sāvatthī during the day.

and entered the monastery.

Going in his vehicle as far as there was ground for a vehicle, getting down from his vehicle, he approached the Blessed One on foot. On arrival, he bowed down and sat to one side.

As he was sitting there, the Blessed One said to him, “What is it, great king? Has King Seniya Bimbisara of Magadha provoked you, or have the Licchavis of Vesali or some other hostile king?” “No, lord, King Seniya Bimbisara of Magadha has not provoked me, nor have the Licchavis of Vesali, nor any other hostile king.

There is a bandit in my realm, lord, named Aṅgulimāla: brutal, bloody-handed, devoted to killing & slaying, showing no mercy to living beings.

He turned villages into non-villages, towns into non-towns, settled countryside into unsettled countryside.

Having repeatedly killed human beings, he wears a garland made of fingers.

I am going to stamp him out.”

“Great king, suppose you were to see Aṅgulimāla with his hair & beard shaved off, wearing the ochre robe, having gone forth from the home life into homelessness, refraining from killing living beings, refraining from taking what is not given, refraining from telling lies, living the holy life on one meal a day, virtuous & of fine character: what would you do to him? “We would bow down to him, lord, stand up for him, invite him to be seated, accept his invitation for robes, almsfood, lodgings, & medicinal requisites for curing illness, and arrange for his lawful protection and safety.”

“But where would such self-restraint & virtue come from in an immoral person of evil character?”

Now at that time Ven. Aṅgulimāla was sitting not far from the Blessed One.

So the Blessed One, pointing with his right arm, said to King Pasenadi Kosala, “That, great king, is Aṅgulimāla.”

Then King Pasenadi Kosala was frightened, terrified, his hair standing on end.

So the Blessed One, sensing the king’s fear & hair-raising awe, said to him, “Don’t be afraid, great king. He poses no danger to you.”

Then the king’s fear, his terror, his hair-standing-on-end subsided.

He went over to Ven. Aṅgulimāla and said, “Are you really Aṅgulimāla, lord? “Yes, great king.”

“What is your father’s clan? What is your mother’s clan?” “My father is a Gagga, great king, and my mother is a Mantāṇī.”

“Then may Master Gagga Mantāṇiputta delight in staying here.

I will be responsible for your robes, almsfood, lodgings, & medicinal requisites for curing illness.”

commentary_pali:
350.Pacchāsamaṇenāti bhaṇḍaggāhakena pacchāsamaṇena, teneva attano pattacīvaraṃ gāhāpetvā taṃ pacchāsamaṇaṃ katvā gatoti attho. Mātāpissa aṭṭhausabhamattena ṭhānena antaritā, – ‘‘tāta, ahiṃsaka kattha ṭhitosi, kattha nisinnosi, kuhiṃ gatosi? Mayā saddhiṃ na kathesi tātā’’ti vadantī āhiṇḍitvā apassamānā ettova gatā.

Pañcamattehiassasatehīti sace corassa parājayo bhavissati, anubandhitvā naṃ gaṇhissāmi. Sace mayhaṃ parājayo bhavissati, vegena palāyissāmīti sallahukena balena nikkhami . Yena ārāmoti kasmā ārāmaṃ agamāsi? So kira corassa bhāyati, cittena gantukāmo na gacchati, garahābhayena nikkhami. Tenassa etadahosi – ‘‘sammāsambuddhaṃ vanditvā nisīdissāmi, so pucchissati ‘kasmā balaṃ gahetvā nikkhantosī’ti. Athāhaṃ ārocessāmi, bhagavā hi maṃ na kevalaṃ samparāyikeneva atthena saṅgaṇhāti, diṭṭhadhammikenapi saṅgaṇhātiyeva. So sace mayhaṃ jayo bhavissati, adhivāsessati. Sace parājayo bhavissati ‘kiṃ te, mahārāja, ekaṃ coraṃ ārabbha gamanenā’ti vakkhati. Tato maṃ jano evaṃ sañjānissati – ‘rājā coraṃ gahetuṃ nikkhanto, sammāsambuddhena pana nivattito’ti’’ garahamokkhaṃ sampassamāno agamāsi.

Pañcamattehi assasatehī Yena ārāmo

Kuto panassāti kasmā āha? Api nāma bhagavā tassa upanissayaṃ oloketvā taṃ ānetvā pabbājeyyāti bhagavato parigaṇhanatthaṃ āha. Raññoti na kevalaṃ raññoyeva bhayaṃ ahosi, avasesopi mahājano bhīto phalakāvudhāni chaḍḍetvā sammukhasammukhaṭṭhāneva palāyitvā nagaraṃ pavisitvā dvāraṃ pidhāya aṭṭālake āruyha olokento aṭṭhāsi. Evañca avoca – ‘‘aṅgulimālo ‘rājā mayhaṃ santikaṃ āgacchatī’ti ñatvā paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā jetavane nisinno, rājā tena gahito, mayaṃ pana palāyitvā muttā’’ti. Natthi te ito bhayanti ayañhi idāni kunthakipillikaṃ jīvitā na voropeti, natthi te imassa santikā bhayanti attho.

Kuto panassā Rañño Natthi te ito bhaya

Kathaṃ gottoti? Kasmā pucchati? Pabbajitaṃ dāruṇakammena uppannanāmaṃ gahetvā voharituṃ na yuttaṃ, mātāpitūnaṃ gottavasena naṃ samudācarissāmīti maññamāno pucchi. Parikkhārānanti etesaṃ atthāya ahaṃ ussukkaṃ karissāmīti attho. Kathentoyeva ca udare baddhasāṭakaṃ muñcitvā therassa pādamūle ṭhapesi.

Kathaṃ gotto Parikkhārāna
commentary_english:
350 " *pacchāsamaṇenā* ti": *pacchāsamaṇa* by the receiver of goods, by that very one having caused his own bowl and robe to be taken, having made him *pacchāsamaṇa*, is the meaning of "gone."

His mother was separated by a place eight *usabha*s in extent, and saying, "Dear *ahiṃsaka*, where are you standing, where are you sitting, where have you gone? You do not speak with me, dear," wandering about and not seeing him, she went just there.

" *pañcamattehi* ": " *assasatehī* " means, "If there will be defeat of the thief, having followed, I will seize him."

If there will be defeat of me, having quickly fled, "I will go out with light strength," he went out.

" *yena ārāmo* ti": Why did he go to the garden? It is said that he is afraid of the thief, he does not go willingly in his mind, he went out due to fear of reproach.

To him this occurred, "Having worshipped the perfectly awakened Buddha, I will sit down, he will ask, 'Why have you gone out having taken strength?'

Then I will announce, indeed the Blessed One does not only embrace me with a future benefit, but he embraces me even with a visible benefit."

If there will be victory of me, he will accept.

If there will be defeat, he will say, "What is it to you, great king, by going concerning one thief?"

Then people will recognize me thus, "The king went out to seize a thief, but he was turned back by the perfectly awakened Buddha," foreseeing release from reproach, he went.

" *pañcamattehi* "

" *assasatehī* "

" *yena ārāmo* "

" *kuto panassā* ti": Why did he say? It is said that the Blessed One, having looked at his support, having brought him, would ordain him, he spoke for the purpose of acceptance by the Blessed One.

" *rañño* ti": Not only to the king was there fear, but also the remaining great crowd, being frightened, having thrown away their shield-weapons, having fled just from face to face, having entered the city, having closed the door, having climbed up to the tower, he stood looking out.

And he said thus, "Aṅgulimāla, having known that 'The king is coming to my presence,' having come earlier, is sitting in Jeta Grove, the king was seized by him, but we, having fled, are freed."

" *natthi te ito bhaya* nti": Indeed, he does not now deprive a kunthakipillika of life, there is not fear to you from him, is the meaning.

" *kuto panassā* "

" *rañño* "

" *natthi te ito bhaya* "

" *kathaṃ gotto* ti": Why does he ask? It is not fitting to address an ordained one with a name arising from cruel action, thinking, "I will address him by the lineage of his mother and father," he asked.

" *parikkhārāna* nti": The meaning is, "For the sake of these, I will make effort."

Just as he was speaking, having released the tied cloth in his belly, he placed it at the foot of the elder.

" *kathaṃ gotto* "

" *parikkhārāna* "

mula_pali:
351. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā aṅgulimālo āraññiko hoti piṇḍapātiko paṃsukūliko tecīvariko. Atha kho āyasmā aṅgulimālo rājānaṃ pasenadiṃ kosalaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘alaṃ, mahārāja, paripuṇṇaṃ me cīvara’’nti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante! Yāvañcidaṃ, bhante, bhagavā adantānaṃ dametā, asantānaṃ sametā, aparinibbutānaṃ parinibbāpetā. Yañhi mayaṃ, bhante, nāsakkhimhā daṇḍenapi satthenapi dametuṃ so bhagavatā adaṇḍena asattheneva asatthena (syā. kaṃ.) danto. Handa ca dāni handa dāni (syā. kaṃ. pī.) mayaṃ, bhante, gacchāma; bahukiccā mayaṃ bahukaraṇīyā’’ti. ‘‘Yassadāni, mahārāja, kālaṃ maññasī’’ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

Atha kho āyasmā aṅgulimālo pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Addasā kho āyasmā aṅgulimālo sāvatthiyaṃ sapadānaṃ piṇḍāya caramāno aññataraṃ itthiṃ mūḷhagabbhaṃ vighātagabbhaṃ visātagabbhaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.). Disvānassa etadahosi – ‘‘kilissanti vata, bho, sattā; kilissanti vata, bho, sattā’’ti! Atha kho āyasmā aṅgulimālo sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā aṅgulimālo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘idhāhaṃ, bhante, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pāvisiṃ. Addasaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, sāvatthiyaṃ sapadānaṃ piṇḍāya caramāno aññataraṃ itthiṃ mūḷhagabbhaṃ vighātagabbhaṃ’’. Disvāna mayhaṃ etadahosi – ‘‘kilissanti vata , bho, sattā; kilissanti vata, bho, sattā’’ti!

visātagabbhaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.)

‘‘Tena hi tvaṃ, aṅgulimāla, yena sā itthī tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ itthiṃ evaṃ vadehi – ‘yatohaṃ, bhagini, jāto bhagini jātiyā jāto (sī.) nābhijānāmi sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropetā, tena saccena sotthi te hotu, sotthi gabbhassā’’’ti.

bhagini jātiyā jāto (sī.)

‘‘So hi nūna me, bhante, sampajānamusāvādo bhavissati. Mayā hi, bhante, bahū sañcicca pāṇā jīvitā voropitā’’ti. ‘‘Tena hi tvaṃ, aṅgulimāla, yena sā itthī tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ itthiṃ evaṃ vadehi – ‘yatohaṃ, bhagini, ariyāya jātiyā jāto, nābhijānāmi sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropetā, tena saccena sotthi te hotu, sotthi gabbhassā’’’ti.

‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā aṅgulimālo bhagavato paṭissutvā yena sā itthī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ itthiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘yatohaṃ, bhagini, ariyāya jātiyā jāto, nābhijānāmi sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropetā, tena saccena sotthi te hotu, sotthi gabbhassā’’ti. Atha khvāssā itthiyā sotthi ahosi, sotthi gabbhassa.

Atha kho āyasmā aṅgulimālo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. ‘Khīṇā jāti vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro kho panāyasmā aṅgulimālo arahataṃ ahosi.
mula_english:
At that time, Venerable Aṅgulimāla was a forest dweller, one who lived on alms, wore robes made of discarded cloth, and possessed only three robes.

Then Venerable Aṅgulimāla said to King Pasenadi of Kosala, "Enough, great king, my robe is complete."

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala went to where the Blessed One was. Having approached, he bowed down to the Blessed One and sat down to one side.

Sitting to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the Blessed One, "It's amazing, lord! It's astounding, lord! Indeed, the Blessed One is the tamer of those who are untamed, the pacifier of those who are unpacified, and the one who brings to nirvāṇa those who have not attained nirvāṇa.

For what we could not tame even with the rod or with weapons, the Blessed One has tamed without the rod or weapons.

"And now, venerable sir, we must depart. We are busy and have much to do."

"Now is the time, great king, to do as you think fit."

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala got up from his seat, bowed down to the Blessed One, circumambulated him, and departed.

Then, in the morning, Venerable Aṅgulimāla, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

There, Venerable Aṅgulimāla saw a certain woman in Sāvatthī suffering from a difficult and complicated pregnancy while he was going for alms from house to house.

Seeing her, he thought: "Living beings truly suffer! Living beings truly suffer!" Then, after the meal, Venerable Aṅgulimāla, returning from his alms round in Sāvatthī, went to where the Blessed One was. Having approached, he bowed down to the Blessed One and sat down to one side.

Sitting to one side, Venerable Aṅgulimāla said to the Blessed One: "Here, lord, this morning, having dressed and taken my bowl and robe, I entered Sāvatthī for alms.

There, lord, I saw a certain woman in Sāvatthī suffering from a difficult and complicated pregnancy while I was going for alms from house to house."

Seeing her, I thought: "Living beings truly suffer! Living beings truly suffer!"

"Then, Aṅgulimāla, go to that woman, and having approached her, say to her: 'Sister, since I was born, I do not recall intentionally depriving any living being of life. By this truth, may you be well, may your baby be well!'"

"But lord, surely that would be a conscious lie for me."
“For I, venerable sir (bhante), have intentionally killed many living beings.”

“Then in that case, Aṅgulimāla, go to that woman, and having approached her, say this to her: ‘Sister (bhagini), since I was born in the noble birth (ariyāya jātiyā jāto), I do not recall intentionally killing a living being. Through this truth (tena saccena) may there be wellbeing (sotthi) for you, wellbeing (sotthi) for your fetus (gabbhassā).’”

“So be it, venerable sir (bhante),” the venerable Aṅgulimāla replied to the Blessed One (bhagavato), and he approached that woman. Having approached her, he said this to her: “Sister (bhagini), since I was born in the noble birth (ariyāya jātiyā jāto), I do not recall intentionally killing a living being. Through this truth (tena saccena) may there be wellbeing (sotthi) for you, wellbeing (sotthi) for your fetus (gabbhassā).”

Then there was wellbeing (sotthi) for that woman, wellbeing (sotthi) for her fetus (gabbhassa).

Then the venerable Aṅgulimāla, dwelling alone, secluded, heedful, ardent, and resolute, before long attained in this very life, having directly known and realized it for himself through his own super-knowledge (abhiññā), that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life (brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ) for which clansmen rightly go forth from home into homelessness, and he lived possessing it.

“Destroyed is birth, the holy life (brahmacariyaṃ) has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of being this or that.”

And the venerable Aṅgulimāla became another one of the worthy ones (arahataṃ).
commentary_pali:
351.Āraññikotiādīni cattāri dhutaṅgāni pāḷiyaṃ āgatāni. Therena pana terasapi samādinnāneva ahesuṃ, tasmā alanti āha. Yañhi mayaṃ, bhanteti kiṃ sandhāya vadati? ‘‘Hatthimpi dhāvantaṃ anubandhitvā gaṇhāmī’’ti āgataṭṭhāne raññā pesitahatthādayo so evaṃ aggahesi. Rājāpi – ‘‘hatthīhiyeva naṃ parikkhipitvā gaṇhatha, asseheva, rathehevā’’ti evaṃ anekavāraṃ bahū hatthādayo pesesi. Evaṃ gatesu pana tesu – ‘‘ahaṃ are aṅgulimālo’’ti tasmiṃ uṭṭhāya saddaṃ karonte ekopi āvudhaṃ parivattetuṃ nāsakkhi, sabbeva koṭṭetvā māresi. Hatthī araññahatthī, assā araññaassā, rathāpi tattheva bhijjantīti idaṃ sandhāya rājā evaṃ vadati.

Piṇḍāya pāvisīti na idaṃ paṭhamaṃ pāvisi. Itthidassanadivasaṃ sandhāya panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Devasikampi panesa pavisateva, manussā ca naṃ disvā uttasantipi palāyantipi dvārampi thakenti, ekacce aṅgulimāloti sutvāva palāyitvā araññaṃ vā pavisanti, gharaṃ vā pavisitvā dvāraṃ thakenti. Palāyituṃ asakkontā piṭṭhiṃ datvā tiṭṭhanti . Thero uḷuṅgayāgumpi kaṭacchubhikkhampi na labhati, piṇḍapātena kilamati. Bahi alabhanto nagaraṃ sabbasādhāraṇanti nagaraṃ pavisati. Yena dvārena pavisati, tattha aṅgulimālo āgatoti kūṭasahassānaṃ bhijjanakāraṇaṃ hoti. Etadahosīti kāruññappattiyā ahosi. Ekena ūnamanussasahassaṃ ghātentassa ekadivasampi kāruññaṃ nāhosi, gabbhamūḷhāya itthiyā dassanamatteneva kathaṃ uppannanti? Pabbajjābalena, pabbajjābalañhi etaṃ.

Piṇḍāya pāvisī Etadahosī

Tena hīti yasmā te kāruññaṃ uppannaṃ, tasmāti attho. Ariyāya jātiyāti, aṅgulimāla, etaṃ tvaṃ mā gaṇhi, nesā tava jāti. Gihikālo esa, gihī nāma pāṇampi hananti, adinnādānādīnipi karonti. Idāni pana te ariyā nāma jāti. Tasmā tvaṃ ‘‘yato ahaṃ, bhagini, jāto’’ti sace evaṃ vattuṃ kukkuccāyasi, tena hi ‘‘ariyāya jātiyā’’ti evaṃ visesetvā vadāhīti uyyojesi.

Tena hī Ariyāya jātiyā

Taṃ itthiṃ etadavocāti itthīnaṃ gabbhavuṭṭhānaṭṭhānaṃ nāma na sakkā purisena upasaṅkamituṃ. Thero kiṃ karosīti? Aṅgulimālatthero saccakiriyaṃ katvā sotthikaraṇatthāya āgatoti ārocāpesi. Tato te sāṇiyā parikkhipitvā therassa bahisāṇiyaṃ pīṭhakaṃ paññāpesuṃ. Thero tattha nisīditvā – ‘‘yato ahaṃ bhagini sabbaññubuddhassa ariyāya jātiyā jāto’’ti saccakiriyaṃ akāsi, saha saccavacaneneva dhamakaraṇato muttaudakaṃ viya dārako nikkhami. Mātāputtānaṃ sotthi ahosi. Imañca pana parittaṃ na kiñci parissayaṃ na maddati, mahāparittaṃ nāmetanti vuttaṃ. Therena nisīditvā saccakiriyakataṭṭhāne pīṭhakaṃ akaṃsu. Gabbhamūḷhaṃ tiracchānagatitthimpi ānetvā tattha nisajjāpenti, tāvadeva sukhena gabbhavuṭṭhānaṃ hoti. Yā dubbalā hoti na sakkā ānetuṃ, tassā pīṭhakadhovanaudakaṃ netvā sīse siñcanti, taṅkhaṇaṃyeva gabbhavuṭṭhānaṃ hoti, aññampi rogaṃ vūpasameti. Yāva kappā tiṭṭhanakapāṭihāriyaṃ kiretaṃ.

Taṃ itthiṃ etadavocā mahāparittaṃ

Kiṃ pana bhagavā theraṃ vejjakammaṃ kārāpesīti? Na kārāpesi. Therañhi disvā manussā bhītā palāyanti. Thero bhikkhāhārena kilamati, samaṇadhammaṃ kātuṃ na sakkoti. Tassa anuggahena saccakiriyaṃ kāresi. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘idāni kira aṅgulimālatthero mettacittaṃ paṭilabhitvā saccakiriyāya manussānaṃ sotthibhāvaṃ karotīti manussā theraṃ upasaṅkamitabbaṃ maññissanti, tato bhikkhāhārena akilamanto samaṇadhammaṃ kātuṃ sakkhissatī’’ti anuggahena saccakiriyaṃ kāresi. Na hi saccakiriyā vejjakammaṃ hoti. Therassāpi ca ‘‘samaṇadhammaṃ karissāmī’’ti mūlakammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā rattiṭṭhānadivāṭṭhāne nisinnassa cittaṃ kammaṭṭhānābhimukhaṃ na gacchati, aṭaviyaṃ ṭhatvā manussānaṃ ghātitaṭṭhānameva pākaṭaṃ hoti. ‘‘Duggatomhi, khuddakaputtomhi, jīvitaṃ me dehi sāmīti maraṇabhītānaṃ vacanākāro ca hatthapādavikāro ca āpāthaṃ āgacchati, so vippaṭisārī hutvā tatova uṭṭhāya gacchati, athassa bhagavā taṃ jātiṃ abbohārikaṃ katvāvāyaṃ vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā arahattaṃ gaṇhissatīti ariyāya jātiyā saccakiriyaṃ kāresi. Eko vūpakaṭṭhotiādi vatthasutte (ma. ni. 1.80) vitthāritaṃ.

Eko vūpakaṭṭho
commentary_english:
351. The *āraññika*, etc., are four ascetic practices that have come down in the Pāḷi texts. However, the elder had taken upon himself thirteen of these practices, therefore he said, “Enough!”

“When we, venerable sir,” what does he say with reference to what? The king's messengers and others, who were sent by the king to the place where he arrived, “I will seize even an elephant that is running by following it,” this is how he seized them.

The king also [said] – “Surround him completely with elephants, seize him! With horses, with chariots!” Thus, many times he sent many elephants and so forth.

When they had thus gone, however, as he rose up among them and made the sound – “I am Aṅgulimāla, you fools!” – not even one was able to turn back his weapon. Having knocked them all down, he killed them.

Elephants are forest elephants, horses are forest horses, even chariots are destroyed right there—the king speaks thus with reference to this.

“Having entered for alms,” this is not the first time he entered. This was said with reference to the day he saw the woman.

Even to this day, he enters for alms. People, seeing him, are terrified and flee, or they close the door. Some, having heard that he is Aṅgulimāla, flee and enter the forest, or enter their house and close the door.

Unable to flee, they stand having turned their backs.

The elder does not obtain even *uḷuṅgayāgu* gruel or a spoonful of food. He is exhausted by [seeking] alms. Unable to obtain [food] outside, he enters the city, thinking, “It is open to all.”

By whichever door he enters, there is a cause for the destruction of hundreds of thousands of houses, [because people say,] “Aṅgulimāla has come!”

“This happened” means this happened through the attainment of compassion.

He did not have compassion even for one day for [the sake of] one less than a thousand human beings he had killed. How did it arise merely from seeing a woman suffering from being with child? Because of the power of renunciation. This, indeed, is the power of renunciation.

Having entered for alms... This happened...

“Therefore,” the meaning is, “Since compassion arose for you, therefore…”

“By an *ariya* birth,” Aṅgulimāla, do not take this [to heart]. That is not your birth.

This is the time of a householder. Householders, by name, even kill living beings. They also commit stealing and so forth. Now, your birth is called an *ariya* birth.

Therefore, if you are worried to say, “Since I, sister, was born,” then having distinguished it thus, “by an *ariya* birth,” speak thus, he urged her.

“Therefore,” “by an *ariya* birth,” “to that woman he said this,” it is not possible for a man to approach a place for women where they give birth.

“What are you doing, elder?” Aṅgulimāla, the elder, proclaimed, “Having performed an act of truth, I have come to bring well-being.”

Then they surrounded him with a curtain and arranged a seat for the elder outside the curtain.

The elder, having sat down there, – “Since I, sister, from the time I was born into the *ariya* birth of the all-knowing Buddha,” – performed an act of truth. Together with the utterance of the act of truth, like water released from a dam, the child came forth.

Well-being came to the mother and child.

Moreover, this protective formula does not dispel even a little danger. It is said to be named the “Great Protective Formula.”

The elder, having sat down, made a seat at the place where he performed the act of truth.

They even brought a pregnant woman of animal birth and made her sit there. In that very moment, there is easy childbirth.

She who is weak is not able to be brought. Having brought water for washing the seat for her, they sprinkle it on her head. In that very moment, there is childbirth. It also quells any other disease.

It is said that this miracle lasts as long as the aeon.

“To that woman he said this,” “Great Protective Formula...”
Is the Blessed One having the elder perform medical work? He is not having [him] perform [it].

Because, having seen the elder, people, being frightened, flee.

The elder is exhausted by alms food, he is not able to do the ascetic's duty ( *śramaṇadharma*).

Through his favor, he had an act of truth (*satyakriya*) performed.

Thus, it occurred to him: "Now, having obtained loving-kindness (*maitrīcitta*), the Elder Aṅgulimāla, by [performing] an act of truth (*satyakriya*), makes the people's welfare (*sotthibhāva*). People will think the elder should be approached. Then, not being exhausted by alms food, he will be able to do the ascetic's duty (*śramaṇadharma*)." Through his favor, he had an act of truth (*satyakriya*) performed.

For an act of truth (*satyakriya*) is not medical work.

And also for the elder, taking the fundamental basis of meditation (*mūlakammaṭṭhāna*), thinking "I will do the ascetic's duty (*śramaṇadharma*)", the mind of one seated in the night and day dwelling does not go towards the object of meditation (*kammaṭṭhānābhimukhaṃ*); having stood in the forest (*aṭavī*), only the place where people have been killed becomes evident.

"I am in a bad state (*duggato'smi*), I am a little son (*khuddakaputto'smi*), give me life, lord!" Both the manner of speech and the change of hands and feet of those frightened by death come into view. He, becoming remorseful, gets up from there and leaves. Then the Blessed One, having made that birth unserviceable, and having developed insight (*vipaśyanā*), will grasp Arhatship (*arahattaṃ*)." He had an act of truth (*satyakriya*) performed with a noble birth (*āriyāya jātiyā*).

352. Atha kho āyasmā aṅgulimālo pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Tena kho pana samayena aññenapi leḍḍu khitto āyasmato aṅgulimālassa kāye nipatati, aññenapi daṇḍo khitto āyasmato aṅgulimālassa kāye nipatati, aññenapi sakkharā khittā āyasmato aṅgulimālassa kāye nipatati. Atha kho āyasmā aṅgulimālo bhinnena sīsena, lohitena gaḷantena, bhinnena pattena, vipphālitāya saṅghāṭiyā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ aṅgulimālaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna āyasmantaṃ aṅgulimālaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘adhivāsehi tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, adhivāsehi tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa. Yassa kho tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, kammassa vipākena bahūni vassāni bahūni vassasatāni bahūni vassasahassāni niraye pacceyyāsi tassa tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, kammassa vipākaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme paṭisaṃvedesī’’ti. Atha kho āyasmā aṅgulimālo rahogato paṭisallīno vimuttisukhaṃ paṭisaṃvedi; tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

‘‘Yo pubbeva yo ca pubbe (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) pamajjitvā, pacchā so nappamajjati;

yo ca pubbe (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)

Somaṃ so imaṃ (sī.) lokaṃ pabhāseti, abbhā muttova candimā.

so imaṃ (sī.)

‘‘Yassa pāpaṃ kataṃ kammaṃ, kusalena pidhīyati pithīyati (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.);

pithīyati (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)

Somaṃ lokaṃ pabhāseti, abbhā muttova candimā.

‘‘Yo have daharo bhikkhu, yuñjati buddhasāsane;

Somaṃ lokaṃ pabhāseti, abbhā muttova candimā.

‘‘Disā hi me dhammakathaṃ suṇantu,

Disā hi me yuñjantu buddhasāsane;

Disā hi me te manujā bhajantu,

Ye dhammamevādapayanti santo.

‘‘Disā hi me khantivādānaṃ, avirodhappasaṃsīnaṃ;

Suṇantu dhammaṃ kālena, tañca anuvidhīyantu.

‘‘Na hi jātu so mamaṃ hiṃse, aññaṃ vā pana kiñci naṃ kañci naṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), kañcanaṃ (?);

kañci naṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), kañcanaṃ (?)

Pappuyya paramaṃ santiṃ, rakkheyya tasathāvare.

‘‘Udakañhi nayanti nettikā, usukārā namayanti damayanti (ka.) tejanaṃ;

damayanti (ka.)

Dāruṃ namayanti tacchakā, attānaṃ damayanti paṇḍitā.

‘‘Daṇḍeneke damayanti, aṅkusehi kasāhi ca;

Adaṇḍena asatthena, ahaṃ dantomhi tādinā.

‘‘Ahiṃsakoti me nāmaṃ, hiṃsakassa pure sato;

Ajjāhaṃ saccanāmomhi, na naṃ hiṃsāmi kiñci naṃ kañci naṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), kañcanaṃ (?).

kañci naṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), kañcanaṃ (?)

‘‘Coro ahaṃ pure āsiṃ, aṅgulimāloti vissuto;

Vuyhamāno mahoghena, buddhaṃ saraṇamāgamaṃ.

‘‘Lohitapāṇi pure āsiṃ, aṅgulimāloti vissuto;

Saraṇagamanaṃ passa, bhavanetti samūhatā.

‘‘Tādisaṃ kammaṃ katvāna, bahuṃ duggatigāminaṃ;

Phuṭṭho kammavipākena, aṇaṇo bhuñjāmi bhojanaṃ.

‘‘Pamādamanuyuñjanti, bālā dummedhino janā;

Appamādañca medhāvī, dhanaṃ seṭṭhaṃva rakkhati.

‘‘Mā pamādamanuyuñjetha, mā kāmarati santhavaṃ;

Appamatto hi jhāyanto, pappoti vipulaṃ paramaṃ (ka.) sukhaṃ.

paramaṃ (ka.)

‘‘Svāgataṃ sāgataṃ (sī. pī.) nāpagataṃ nāma sagataṃ (ka.), nayidaṃ dummantitaṃ mama;

sāgataṃ (sī. pī.) nāma sagataṃ (ka.)

Saṃvibhattesu suvibhattesu (syā. kaṃ.), savibhattesu (sī. ka.), paṭibhattesu (pī.) dhammesu, yaṃ seṭṭhaṃ tadupāgamaṃ.

suvibhattesu (syā. kaṃ.), savibhattesu (sī. ka.), paṭibhattesu (pī.)

‘‘Svāgataṃ nāpagataṃ, nayidaṃ dummantitaṃ mama;

Tisso vijjā anuppattā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsana’’nti.

Then venerable Aṅgulimāla, early in the morning, having dressed, taking his bowl and outer robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms. Now at that time, a clod thrown by someone hit venerable Aṅgulimāla's body; a stick thrown by someone hit venerable Aṅgulimāla's body; a potsherd thrown by someone hit venerable Aṅgulimāla's body. Then venerable Aṅgulimāla, his head broken, blood dripping, his bowl broken, his outer robe ripped to shreds, approached the Blessed One. The Blessed One saw venerable Aṅgulimāla coming from afar. Seeing venerable Aṅgulimāla, he said this: “Endure, *brāhmaṇa*, endure, *brāhmaṇa*. "The result of the *karma* that would have caused you to suffer in hell for many years, many hundreds of years, many thousands of years, you are now experiencing in this very life, *brāhmaṇa*!” Then venerable Aṅgulimāla, in seclusion, withdrawn, experienced the bliss of liberation. At that time he uttered this exclamation: “He who formerly was heedless, but later is not heedless, brightens the world like the moon freed from clouds. He whose evil-done action is covered by skillful [action], brightens the world like the moon freed from clouds. He who is a young *bhikkhu*, applies himself to the Buddha’s teaching, brightens the world like the moon freed from clouds.” “Let all regions hear my teaching on the Dharma, Let all regions apply themselves to the Buddha’s teaching, Let all regions honor those men, who, being peaceful, cause others to understand the Dharma.” “Let the regions hear my words of patience, praising non-opposition; Let them in due time hear the Dharma, and practice accordingly. “For surely he would never harm me, or anyone else; ), *kañcanaṃ* (?);

*kañci naṃ* (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. ), *kañcanaṃ* (?) Having attained the supreme peace, one should protect those who are trembling and steadfast. The irrigators lead the water, the arrow-makers bend the arrow, the carpenters bend the wood, and the wise subdue themselves. Some are subdued with a stick, with a hook, and with whips; I am subdued by the one who is without a stick and without a weapon. "Non-harming" was my name, formerly, as a doer of harm; today I am one whose name is truth, I do not harm anyone at all. Formerly, I was a thief, known as Aṅgulimāla; swept away by the great flood, I went for refuge to the Buddha. Formerly, I was one with a bloody hand, known as Aṅgulimāla; behold the going for refuge, the craving for existence is eradicated. Having done such deeds, leading to much suffering, touched by the result of karma, without debt, I eat my food. Fools, those of poor wisdom, pursue negligence; but the wise protect diligence as the best treasure. Do not pursue negligence, do not [pursue] association with sensual delight; for the diligent one, meditating, attains abundant bliss. Welcome, not departed, this is not ill-considered by me; in conditions of being well divided ka. ), *paṭibhattesu* (pī. ) *dhammesu*, *yaṃ seṭṭhaṃ tadupāgamaṃ*.

*suvibhattesu* (syā. kaṃ. ), *savibhattesu* (sī. ka. ), *paṭibhattesu* (pī. ) ‘‘*svāgataṃ nāpagataṃ*, *nayidaṃ dummantitaṃ mama*; *tisso vijjā anuppattā*, *kataṃ buddhassa sāsana’’nti*.

352.Aññenapi leḍḍu khittoti kākasunakhasūkarādīnaṃ paṭikkamāpanatthāya samantā sarakkhepamatte ṭhāne yena kenaci disābhāgena khitto āgantvā therasseva kāye patati. Kittake ṭhāne evaṃ hoti? Gaṇṭhikaṃ paṭimuñcitvā piṇḍāya caritvā paṭinivattetvā yāva gaṇṭhikapaṭimukkaṭṭhānaṃ āgacchati, tāva hoti. Bhinnena sīsenāti mahācammaṃ chinditvā yāva aṭṭhimariyādā bhinnena.

Brāhmaṇāti khīṇāsavabhāvaṃ sandhāya āha. Yassa kho tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, kammassa vipākenāti idaṃ sabhāgadiṭṭhadhammavedanīyakammaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Kammañhi kariyamānameva tayo koṭṭhāse pūreti. Sattasu cittesu kusalā vā akusalā vā paṭhamajavanacetanā diṭṭhadhammavedanīyakammaṃ nāma hoti. Taṃ imasmiṃyeva attabhāve vipākaṃ deti. Tathā asakkontaṃ ahosikammaṃ, nāhosi kammavipāko, na bhavissati kammavipāko, natthi kammavipākoti imassa tikassa vasena ahosikammaṃ nāma hoti. Atthasādhikā sattamajavanacetanā upapajjavedanīyakammaṃ nāma. Taṃ anantare attabhāve vipākaṃ deti. Tathā asakkontaṃ vuttanayeneva taṃ ahosikammaṃ nāma hoti. Ubhinnamantare pañcajavanacetanā aparāpariyavedanīyakammaṃ nāma hoti. Taṃ anāgate yadā okāsaṃ labhati, tadā vipākaṃ deti. Sati saṃsārappavattiyā ahosikammaṃ nāma na hoti. Therassa pana upapajjavedanīyañca aparāpariyavedanīyañcāti imāni dve kammāni kammakkhayakarena arahattamaggena samugghāṭitāni, diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ atthi . Taṃ arahattappattassāpi vipākaṃ detiyeva. Taṃ sandhāya bhagavā ‘‘yassa kho tva’’ntiādimāha. Tasmā yassa khoti ettha yādisassa kho tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, kammassa vipākenāti evaṃ attho veditabbo.

Brāhmaṇā Yassa kho tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, kammassa vipākenā diṭṭhadhammavedanīyakammaṃ ahosikammaṃ upapajjavedanīyakammaṃ aparāpariyavedanīyakammaṃ yassa kho
