Na hi jātu so mamaṃ hiṃseti yo mayhaṃ diso, so maṃ ekaṃseneva na hiṃseyya. Aññaṃ vā pana kiñci nanti na kevalaṃ maṃ, aññampi pana kañci puggalaṃ mā hiṃsantu mā viheṭhentu. Pappuyya paramaṃ santinti paramaṃ santibhūtaṃ nibbānaṃ pāpuṇitvā. Rakkheyya tasathāvareti tasā vuccanti sataṇhā, thāvarā nittaṇhā. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – yo nibbānaṃ pāpuṇāti, so sabbaṃ tasathāvaraṃ rakkhituṃ samattho hoti. Tasmā mayhampi disā nibbānaṃ pāpuṇantu, evaṃ maṃ ekaṃseneva na hiṃsissantīti. Imā tisso gāthā attano parittaṃ kātuṃ āha.

Na hi jātu so mamaṃ hiṃse Aññaṃ vā pana kiñci na Pappuyya paramaṃ santi Rakkheyya tasathāvare tasā thāvarā

Idāni attanova paṭipattiṃ dīpento udakañhi nayantinettikāti āha. Tattha nettikāti ye mātikaṃ sodhetvā bandhitabbaṭṭhāne bandhitvā udakaṃ nayanti. Usukārāti usukārakā. Namayantīti telakañjikena makkhetvā kukkuḷe tāpetvā unnatunnataṭṭhāne namentā ujuṃ karonti. Tejananti kaṇḍaṃ. Tañhi issāso tejaṃ karoti, parañca tajjeti, tasmā tejananti vuccati. Attānaṃ damayantīti yathā nettikā ujumaggena udakaṃ nayanti, usukārā tejanaṃ, tacchakā ca dāruṃ ujuṃ karonti, evamevaṃ paṇḍitā attānaṃ damenti ujukaṃ karonti nibbisevanaṃ karonti.

udakañhi nayanti nettikā nettikā Usukārā Namayantī Tejana Attānaṃ damayantī

Tādināti iṭṭhāniṭṭhādīsu nibbikārena – ‘‘pañcahākārehi bhagavā tādī, iṭṭhāniṭṭhe tādī, vantāvīti tādī, cattāvīti tādī, tiṇṇāvīti tādī, tanniddesāti tādī’’ti (mahāni. 38; 192) evaṃ tādilakkhaṇappattena satthārā. Bhavanettīti bhavarajju, taṇhāyetaṃ nāmaṃ. Tāya hi goṇā viya gīvāya rajjuyā, sattā hadaye baddhā taṃ taṃ bhavaṃ nīyanti, tasmā bhavanettīti vuccati. Phuṭṭhokammavipākenāti maggacetanāya phuṭṭho. Yasmā hi maggacetanāya kammaṃ paccati vipaccati ḍayhati, parikkhayaṃ gacchati, tasmā sā kammavipākoti vuttā. Tāya hi phuṭṭhattā esa aṇaṇo nikkileso jāto, na dukkhavedanāya aṇaṇo. Bhuñjāmīti cettha theyyaparibhogo iṇaparibhogo dāyajjaparibhogo sāmiparibhogoti cattāro paribhogā veditabbā. Tattha dussīlassa paribhogo theyyaparibhogo nāma. So hi cattāro paccaye thenetvā bhuñjati. Vuttampi cetaṃ ‘‘theyyāya vo, bhikkhave, raṭṭhapiṇḍo bhutto’’ti (pārā. 195). Sīlavato pana apaccavekkhaṇaparibhogo iṇaparibhogo nāma. Sattannaṃ sekkhānaṃ paribhogo dāyajjaparibhogo nāma. Khīṇāsavassa paribhogo sāmiparibhogo nāma. Idha kilesaiṇānaṃ abhāvaṃ sandhāya ‘‘aṇaṇo’’ti vuttaṃ. ‘‘Aniṇo’’tipi pāṭho. Sāmiparibhogaṃ sandhāya ‘‘bhuñjāmi bhojana’’nti vuttaṃ.

Tādinā Bhavanettī Phuṭṭho kammavipākenā aṇaṇo Bhuñjāmī

Kāmaratisanthavanti duvidhesupi kāmesu taṇhāratisanthavaṃ mā anuyuñjatha mā karittha. Nayidaṃ dummantitaṃ mamāti yaṃ mayā sammāsambuddhaṃ disvā pabbajissāmīti mantitaṃ, taṃ mama mantitaṃ na dummantitaṃ. Saṃvibhattesu dhammesūti ahaṃ satthāti evaṃ loke uppannehi ye dhammā saṃvibhattā, tesu dhammesu yaṃ seṭṭhaṃ nibbānaṃ, tadeva ahaṃ upagamaṃ upagato sampatto, tasmā mayhaṃ idaṃ āgamanaṃ svāgataṃ nāma gatanti. Tisso vijjāti pubbenivāsadibbacakkhuāsavakkhayapaññā. Kataṃbuddhassa sāsananti yaṃ buddhassa sāsane kattabbakiccaṃ atthi, taṃ sabbaṃ mayā kataṃ. Tīhi vijjāhi navahi ca lokuttaradhammehi desanaṃ matthakaṃ pāpesīti.

Kāmaratisanthava Nayidaṃ dummantitaṃ mamā Saṃvibhattesu dhammesū Tisso vijjā Kataṃ buddhassa sāsana

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Aṅgulimālasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
352. "When another clod is thrown": In order to ward off crows, dogs, pigs, etc., someone throws [a clod] in all directions around the immediate vicinity; [then,] having come, it falls on the body of the Elder.

How far does this happen? Having untied the knot, having gone for alms, having returned, as far as the place where the knot was untied, it happens that far.

"With a broken head": Having cut through the large skin, [it is broken] up to the limit of the bone.

"Brāhmaṇas": He says this referring to the state of having destroyed the āsavas.

"Due to whose karma, Brāhmaṇa, as a result": This was said referring to karma experienced as pleasant in the immediate present.

For karma, when being done, fills up three sections.

In the seven consciousnesses, whether wholesome or unwholesome, the first impulsive consciousness is called karma experienced as pleasant in the immediate present ( *dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyakarma*).

It gives its result in this same selfhood.

Likewise, if it is unable to do so, it is called lapsed karma ( *ahosikamma*): “There has been karma, there has been no karma-result, there will be no karma-result, there is no karma-result,” according to this triad.

The seventh impulsive consciousness that accomplishes the aim is called karma ripening in the next existence (*upapajjavedanīyakamma*).

It gives its result in the next selfhood.

Likewise, if it is unable to do so, it is called lapsed karma ( *ahosikamma*) in the way already described.

The five impulsive consciousnesses in between are called karma ripening in subsequent existences (*aparāpariyavedanīyakamma*).

It gives its result in the future when it gets the opportunity.

As long as the round of rebirths continues, it never becomes lapsed karma ( *ahosikamma*).

But for the Elder, these two karmas—karma ripening in the next existence and karma ripening in subsequent existences—have been uprooted by the path of arahantship, which destroys karma; karma experienced as pleasant in the immediate present still exists.

It continues to give its result even to one who has attained arahantship.

Referring to that, the Blessed One said, “Due to whose [karma], Brāhmaṇa?” etc.

Therefore, "Due to whose": here, the meaning should be understood thus: “Due to whose karma, Brāhmaṇa, as a result?"

"Brāhmaṇas," "Due to whose karma, Brāhmaṇa, as a result," "Karma experienced as pleasant in the immediate present ( *dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyakamma*)," "Lapsed karma (*ahosikamma*)," "Karma ripening in the next existence (*upapajjavedanīyakamma*)," "Karma ripening in subsequent existences (*aparāpariyavedanīyakamma*),"

"Freed from the clouds": This is just the beginning of the teaching. Here, the moon freed from defilements, namely clouds, mist, smoke, dust, and Rāhu, is intended.

Just as the moon, untainted in this way, illuminates the world, so too a monk who is mindful, free from negligence and defilements, illuminates this world of his aggregates, sense bases, and elements, and dispels the darkness of defilements.

"Freed from the clouds," "Is covered by the wholesome": It is covered by the wholesome path, it is made without rebirth.

"Engages in the Buddha’s teaching": He lives engaged and intent on the Buddha’s teaching with body, speech, and mind.

These three are called the Elder's verses of elation ( *udānagāthā*).

"Is covered by the wholesome," "Engages in the Buddha’s teaching," "The directions are mine": It seems that the Elder said this while making a protection for himself.

There, "The directions are mine" means my opponents.

Those who reproach me thus: “Just as we experience suffering because of the relatives killed by Aṅgulimāla, may Aṅgulimāla also experience [suffering]!”—may they listen to my discourse on the four noble truths, is the meaning.

"May they engage": May they live engaged and intent with body, speech, and mind.

“Those who introduce only the Dhamma”: Those noble persons who are at peace, who only introduce, encourage, and teach the Dhamma, may those people, my opponents, attend to, respect, and wait upon [me], is the meaning.

"The directions are mine," "The directions are mine," "May they engage," "Those who introduce only the Dhamma," "Are at peace," "Not praising opposition."
Avirodho is called *mettā*, its meaning is to praise *mettā*.
Listen to the Dharma at the proper time, listen to the Dharma that brings about patience, loving-kindness, reflection, and mindfulness at every moment.
And follow that, imitate and fulfill that Dharma.

A person who praises non-opposition.
Listen to the Dharma at the proper time, and follow that. "For surely he wouldn’t harm me," whoever is my enemy, he would not harm me at all.
"Or anyone else," not only me, but anyone else.
Let them not harm or injure any person.
"Having attained supreme peace," having attained *nirvāṇa*, which is the essence of supreme peace.
"One should protect those who tremble and are firm," the "trembling" are said to be those with craving, the "firm" are those without craving.
This is what is said: whoever attains *nirvāṇa* is able to protect all that trembles and is firm.
Therefore, may my enemies also attain *nirvāṇa*, in this way they will not harm me at all.
These three verses were spoken by himself to create protection.

"For surely he wouldn’t harm me," "Or anyone else."
"Having attained supreme peace," "One should protect those who tremble and are firm," the "trembling", the "firm". Now, revealing his own practice, "indeed, they lead the water."
He said, "nettikā".
There, nettikā are those who purify the water channel, bind it in a place where it should be bound, and lead the water.
usukārā means arrow makers.
namayantī means after smearing [the arrow] with oil-resin and heating it in embers, they bend [the arrow] at the elevated places and make it straight.
tejana means shaft.
For the drawing [of the bow] makes the arrow sharp, and furthermore it makes [the target] tremble, therefore it is called tejana.
attānaṃ damayantī means just as the nettikā lead the water along a straight path, the usukārā [straighten] the arrow, and carpenters make the wood straight, just so, wise people tame themselves, make [themselves] straight, and make [themselves] without attachment.

Indeed, they lead the water.
nettikā, nettikā, usukārā, namayantī, tejana, attānaṃ damayantī. tādinā means without change in desirable or undesirable things, etc. – “The Blessed One is stable in five ways, stable in desirable and undesirable things, a vomiter, a renouncer, one who has crossed over, his instruction is stable" (Mahāniddeśa.
38; 192) thus, by the Teacher who has attained the characteristics of stability.
bhavanettī means the rope of existence, this is a name for craving (*tṛṣṇā*).
For just as cows are led by a rope around their necks, beings are bound in their hearts and led to that and that existence, therefore it is called bhavanettī.
phuṭṭho kammavipākena means touched by the fruition of karma (*karmavipāka*).
Because karma (*karma*) ripens, matures, burns, and reaches its end through the consciousness of the path (*mārgacetanā*), therefore it is called the fruition of karma.
Because he is touched by that, he becomes unindebted, without defilements, not indebted to painful feeling.
bhuñjāmī means here, four kinds of enjoyment should be understood: enjoyment by theft, enjoyment by debt, enjoyment by inheritance, and enjoyment by ownership.
There, the enjoyment of an immoral person is called enjoyment by theft.
For he enjoys [the requisites] after stealing the four conditions.
And this was said, "Monks, you eat the alms-food of the country by theft" (Pārājika.
195).
But the enjoyment of a virtuous person who does not reflect is called enjoyment by debt.
The enjoyment of the seven learners is called enjoyment by inheritance.
The enjoyment of one whose outflows are destroyed is called enjoyment by ownership.
Here, referring to the absence of debt of defilements, it is said "debtless" (aṇaṇo).
"Without debt" (aniṇo) is also a reading.
Referring to partaking of wealth, it is said, "I eat food" (bhuñjāmi bhojana).

Touched by such craving for existence (bhavanettī) through the results of actions (kammavipākenā), [one is] debtless (aṇaṇo) and enjoys (bhuñjāmi).

"Association with sensual pleasure" (kāmaratisanthava): In both kinds of sensual pleasures, do not pursue or engage in attachment and delight in craving.

"This was not a bad decision of mine" (nayidaṃ dummantitaṃ mamā): The thought I had, seeing the Perfectly Awakened Buddha, that I would go forth, that thought of mine was not a bad decision.

"Amongst the divided qualities" (saṃvibhattesu dhammesū): Among the qualities that have arisen in the world, saying "I am the teacher" (ahaṃ satthāti), that which is the best, nirvāṇa (nibbāna), that itself I approached, attained, and reached. Therefore, this coming of mine is named "welcome" (svāgataṃ), gone (gatanti).

"Three knowledges" (tisso vijjā): Knowledge of former abodes (pubbenivāsa), divine eye (dibbacakkhu), and knowledge of the destruction of the outflows (āsavakkhayapaññā).

"The Buddha's teaching has been done" (kataṃ buddhassa sāsana): Whatever duties should be done in the Buddha's teaching, all that has been done by me.

Through the three knowledges (tīhi vijjāhi) and the nine supramundane qualities (lokuttaradhammehi), the teaching has been brought to its highest point.

Association with sensual pleasure (kāmaratisanthava), this was not a bad decision of mine (nayidaṃ dummantitaṃ mamā), amongst the divided qualities (saṃvibhattesu dhammesū), three knowledges (tisso vijjā), the Buddha's teaching has been done (kataṃ buddhassa sāsana).

The Aṅgulimālasuttavaṇṇanā, commentary to the Aṅgulimāla Sutta in the Papañcasūdanī, commentary to the Majjhima Nikāya, is finished.

mula_pali: 353. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa gahapatissa ekaputtako piyo manāpo kālaṅkato hoti. Tassa kālaṃkiriyāya neva kammantā paṭibhanti na bhattaṃ paṭibhāti. So āḷāhanaṃ gantvā kandati – ‘‘kahaṃ, ekaputtaka, kahaṃ, ekaputtakā’’ti! Atha kho so gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho taṃ gahapatiṃ bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘na kho te, gahapati, sake citte ṭhitassa indriyāni, atthi te indriyānaṃ aññathatta’’nti. ‘‘Kiñhi me, bhante, indriyānaṃ nāññathattaṃ bhavissati; mayhañhi, bhante, ekaputto piyo manāpo kālaṅkato. Tassa kālaṃkiriyāya neva kammantā paṭibhanti, na bhattaṃ paṭibhāti. Sohaṃ āḷāhanaṃ gantvā kandāmi – ‘kahaṃ, ekaputtaka, kahaṃ, ekaputtakā’’’ti! ‘‘Evametaṃ, gahapati, evametaṃ, gahapati evametaṃ gahapati (pī. sakideva), evameva (sī. sakideva)! Piyajātikā hi, gahapati, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā piyappabhavikā’’ti. ‘‘Kassa kho kissa nu kho (sī.) nāmetaṃ, bhante, evaṃ bhavissati – ‘piyajātikā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā piyappabhavikā’ti? Piyajātikā hi kho, bhante, ānandasomanassā piyappabhavikā’’ti. Atha kho so gahapati bhagavato bhāsitaṃ anabhinanditvā paṭikkositvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthi in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapindika’s monastery.

Now on that occasion, a certain householder’s ( *gahapati* ) dear and beloved only son had died.

After his death (*kālaṃkiriyāya*), he had no more desire to work or to eat.

He went to the charnel ground (*āḷāhanaṃ*) and cried: “Where, my only child (*ekaputtaka*)? Where, my only child?” Then that householder approached the Blessed One; after approaching, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side.

The Blessed One said this to the householder who was sitting to one side: “Householder, your faculties are not those of one in control of his own mind. Your faculties are deranged (*aññathattaṃ*).”

“How could my faculties not be deranged, venerable sir (*bhante*)? For my dear and beloved only son has died.

After his death, he had no more desire to work or to eat.

I go to the charnel ground and cry: ‘Where, my only child, where, my only child?’” “That is so, householder, that is so, householder! For sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair are born from what is beloved (*piyappabhavikā*).”

“But venerable sir, why should it be that joy and happiness (*ānandasomanassā*) are born from what is beloved?”

Then that householder, displeased and disapproving of the Blessed One’s words, rose from his seat and left.
commentary_pali: 353.Evaṃme sutanti piyajātikasuttaṃ. Tattha neva kammantā paṭibhantīti na sabbena sabbaṃ paṭibhanti, pakatiniyāmena pana na paṭibhanti. Dutiyapadepi eseva nayo. Ettha ca na paṭibhātīti na ruccati. Āḷāhananti susānaṃ. Aññathattanti vivaṇṇatāya aññathābhāvo. Indriyāni nāma manoviññeyyā dhammā, patiṭṭhitokāsaṃ pana sandhāya idaṃ vuttaṃ. Piyajātikāti piyato jāyanti. Piyappabhāvikāti piyato pabhavanti.
commentary_english:
Thus have I heard: the discourse on those born of affection.

There, *neva kammantā paṭibhantī* means they do not appear in every way in every respect, but they do not appear in the natural order.

And the same method applies to the second phrase as well.

And here, *na paṭibhātī* means it is not pleasing.

*Āḷāhana* means a cemetery (śmaśāna).

*Aññathatta* means alteration due to discoloration, an altered state.

*Indriyāni* (faculties) means mental cognizable things, but this is said with reference to an established opportunity.

*Piyajātikā* means they are born of affection (*priya*).

*Piyappabhāvikā* means they arise from affection (*priya*).

mula_pali: 354. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā akkhadhuttā bhagavato avidūre akkhehi dibbanti. Atha kho so gahapati yena te akkhadhuttā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā akkhadhutte etadavoca – ‘‘idhāhaṃ, bhonto, yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkamiṃ; upasaṅkamitvā samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho maṃ, bhonto, samaṇo gotamo etadavoca – ‘na kho te, gahapati, sake citte ṭhitassa indriyāni, atthi te indriyānaṃ aññathatta’nti. Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhonto, samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘kiñhi me, bhante, indriyānaṃ nāññathattaṃ bhavissati; mayhañhi, bhante, ekaputtako piyo manāpo kālaṅkato. Tassa kālaṃkiriyāya neva kammantā paṭibhanti, na bhattaṃ paṭibhāti . Sohaṃ āḷāhanaṃ gantvā kandāmi – kahaṃ, ekaputtaka, kahaṃ, ekaputtakā’ti! ‘Evametaṃ, gahapati, evametaṃ, gahapati! Piyajātikā hi, gahapati, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā piyappabhavikā’ti. ‘Kassa kho nāmetaṃ, bhante, evaṃ bhavissati – piyajātikā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā piyappabhavikā? Piyajātikā hi kho, bhante, ānandasomanassā piyappabhavikā’ti. Atha khvāhaṃ, bhonto, samaṇassa gotamassa bhāsitaṃ anabhinanditvā paṭikkositvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkami’’nti. ‘‘Evametaṃ, gahapati, evametaṃ, gahapati! Piyajātikā hi, gahapati, ānandasomanassā piyappabhavikā’’ti . Atha kho so gahapati ‘‘sameti me akkhadhuttehī’’ti pakkāmi. Atha kho idaṃ kathāvatthu anupubbena rājantepuraṃ pāvisi.
mula_english:
354. Now on that occasion some gamblers were playing with dice not far from the Blessed One.

Then the householder went to those gamblers and said: “Just now, sirs, I went to the *śramaṇa* Gotama; and after paying homage to the *śramaṇa* Gotama, I sat down at one side.

When I had done so, the *śramaṇa* Gotama said to me: Householder, your faculties (*indriyāṇi*) are not those of one in control of his own mind. Your faculties (*indriyāṇi*) are deranged."

When this was said, I said to the *śramaṇa* Gotama: "But, sir (*bhante*), why should my faculties (*indriyāṇi*) not be deranged? Sir (*bhante*), my only son, dear and appealing, is dead.

Since his death, I have no pleasure in work, nor does food taste good.

So I go to the charnel ground and cry: Where is my only son, where is my only son!‘ That’s how it is, householder, that’s how it is, householder! For sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and despair are born from those we love.’

‘But whose life, sir (*bhante*), would it not be like this – that sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and despair are born from those we love? For joy and happiness are born from those we love.’

Then, displeased with the words of the *śramaṇa* Gotama, disapproving of them, I rose from my seat and left."

“That’s how it is, householder, that’s how it is, householder! For joy and happiness are born from those we love."

Then the householder left thinking: “I agree with the gamblers.”

Eventually this story reached the king’s palace.

mula_pali: 355. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo mallikaṃ deviṃ āmantesi – ‘‘idaṃ te, mallike, samaṇena gotamena bhāsitaṃ – ‘piyajātikā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā piyappabhavikā’’’ti. ‘‘Sacetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā bhāsitaṃ, evameta’’nti. ‘‘Evameva panāyaṃ mallikā yaññadeva samaṇo gotamo bhāsati taṃ tadevassa abbhanumodati’’. ‘‘Sacetaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavatā bhāsitaṃ evametanti. Seyyathāpi nāma, yaññadeva ācariyo antevāsissa bhāsati taṃ tadevassa antevāsī abbhanumodati – ‘evametaṃ, ācariya, evametaṃ, ācariyā’’’ti. ‘‘Evameva kho tvaṃ, mallike, yaññadeva samaṇo gotamo bhāsati taṃ tadevassa abbhanumodasi’’. ‘‘Sacetaṃ, mahārāja , bhagavatā bhāsitaṃ evameta’’nti. ‘‘Carapi, re mallike, vinassā’’ti. Atha kho mallikā devī nāḷijaṅghaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ehi tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandāhi, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ puccha – ‘mallikā, bhante, devī bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchatī’ti. Evañca vadehi – ‘bhāsitā nu kho, bhante, bhagavatā esā vācā – piyajātikā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā piyappabhavikā’ti . Yathā te bhagavā byākaroti taṃ sādhukaṃ uggahetvā mama āroceyyāsi. Na hi tathāgatā vitathaṃ bhaṇantī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhotī’’ti kho nāḷijaṅgho brāhmaṇo mallikāya deviyā paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho nāḷijaṅgho brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘mallikā, bho gotama, devī bhoto gotamassa pāde sirasā vandati; appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchati; evañca vadeti – ‘bhāsitā nu kho, bhante, bhagavatā esā vācā – piyajātikā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā piyappabhavikā’’’ti.
mula_english:
Then King Pasenadi of Kosala told Queen Mallika: "This was spoken by the *śramaṇa* Gotama: ‘Sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are born from those who are dear, arise from those who are dear.’"

"If that has been said by the Blessed One (*bhagavatā*), sire (*mahārāja*), then it is so."

"So too, Mallika, no matter what the *śramaṇa* Gotama says, you applaud it thus."

"If that has been said by the Blessed One, sire, then it is so."

Just as a teacher (*ācariya*) says to a pupil (*antevāsi*), and the pupil applauds whatever his teacher says to him, saying: ‘So it is, teacher, so it is!’"

"So too, Mallika, no matter what the *śramaṇa* Gotama says, you applaud it thus."

"If that has been said by the Blessed One, sire, then it is so."

"Be off, Mallika, away with you!"

Then Queen Mallika addressed the *brāhmaṇa* Nāḷijaṅgha: "Come, *brāhmaṇa*, go to the Blessed One; and having gone, pay homage in my name with your head at the Blessed One’s feet, and ask whether he is free from illness and affliction and is healthy, strong, and abiding in comfort, saying: ‘Mallika, venerable sir (*bhante*), the queen (*devī*) pays homage with her head at the Blessed One’s feet and asks whether he is free from illness…and abiding in comfort.’ And say this: ‘Venerable sir, have these words been spoken by the Blessed One: “Sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are born from those who are dear, arise from those who are dear”?’

"And whatever the Blessed One declares to you, keep it well in mind and inform me. For *Tathāgatas* do not speak untruth."

"Even so, lady," replied the *brāhmaṇa* Nāḷijaṅgha to Queen Mallika, and then he went to where the Blessed One was; and having gone, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One.

Having exchanged greetings of friendliness and courtesy, he sat down at one side.

Having sat down at one side, the *brāhmaṇa* Nāḷijaṅgha said to the Blessed One: "Mallika, Master Gotama, the queen pays homage with her head at Master Gotama ‘s feet and asks whether he is free from illness…and abiding in comfort. And she says this: ‘Venerable sir, have these words been spoken by the Blessed One: “Sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are born from those who are dear, arise from those who are dear”?’"
commentary_pali: 355.Sace taṃ, mahārājāti tassa atthaṃ asallakkhayamānāpi satthari saddhāya evaṃ vadati. Cara pireti apehi amhākaṃ pare, anajjhattikabhūteti attho. Atha vā cara pireti parato gaccha, mā idha tiṭṭhātipi attho.
commentary_english: 355. sace taṃ, mahārājāti, even without considering its meaning, she speaks thus to the teacher with faith. cara pireti—the meaning is: "go away, you are foreign to us, you are not internal." Or, alternatively, cara pireti—the meaning is: "go away from here, do not stay here."

mula_pali:
356. ‘‘Evametaṃ, brāhmaṇa, evametaṃ, brāhmaṇa! Piyajātikā hi, brāhmaṇa, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā piyappabhavikāti. Tadamināpetaṃ, brāhmaṇa, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ yathā piyajātikā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā piyappabhavikā. Bhūtapubbaṃ, brāhmaṇa, imissāyeva sāvatthiyā aññatarissā itthiyā mātā kālamakāsi. Sā tassā kālakiriyāya ummattikā khittacittā rathikāya rathikaṃ rathiyāya rathiyaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāha – ‘api me mātaraṃ addassatha addasatha (sī. pī.), api me mātaraṃ addassathā’ti? Imināpi kho etaṃ, brāhmaṇa, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ yathā piyajātikā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā piyappabhavikāti.

‘‘Bhūtapubbaṃ , brāhmaṇa, imissāyeva sāvatthiyā aññatarissā itthiyā pitā kālamakāsi… bhātā kālamakāsi… bhaginī kālamakāsi… putto kālamakāsi… dhītā kālamakāsi… sāmiko kālamakāsi. Sā tassa kālakiriyāya ummattikā khittacittā rathikāya rathikaṃ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāha – ‘api me sāmikaṃ addassatha, api me sāmikaṃ addassathā’ti? Imināpi kho etaṃ, brāhmaṇa, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ yathā piyajātikā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā piyappabhavikāti.

‘‘Bhūtapubbaṃ , brāhmaṇa, imissāyeva sāvatthiyā aññatarassa purisassa mātā kālamakāsi. So tassā kālakiriyāya ummattako khittacitto rathikāya rathikaṃ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāha – ‘api me mātaraṃ addassatha, api me mātaraṃ addassathā’ti ? Imināpi kho etaṃ, brāhmaṇa , pariyāyena veditabbaṃ yathā piyajātikā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā piyappabhavikāti.

‘‘Bhūtapubbaṃ, brāhmaṇa, imissāyeva sāvatthiyā aññatarassa purisassa pitā kālamakāsi… bhātā kālamakāsi… bhaginī kālamakāsi… putto kālamakāsi… dhītā kālamakāsi… pajāpati kālamakāsi. So tassā kālakiriyāya ummattako khittacitto rathikāya rathikaṃ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāha – ‘api me pajāpatiṃ addassatha, api me pajāpatiṃ addassathā’ti? Imināpi kho etaṃ, brāhmaṇa, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ yathā piyajātikā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā piyappabhavikāti.

‘‘Bhūtapubbaṃ, brāhmaṇa, imissāyeva sāvatthiyā aññatarā itthī ñātikulaṃ agamāsi. Tassā te ñātakā sāmikaṃ sāmikā (sī.) acchinditvā aññassa dātukāmā. Sā ca taṃ na icchati. Atha kho sā itthī sāmikaṃ etadavoca – ‘ime, maṃ mama (syā. kaṃ. pī.), ayyaputta, ñātakā tvaṃ tayā (sī.), taṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī.) acchinditvā aññassa dātukāmā. Ahañca taṃ na icchāmī’ti. Atha kho so puriso taṃ itthiṃ dvidhā chetvā attānaṃ upphālesi uppāṭesi (sī. pī.), ophāresi (ka.) – ‘ubho pecca bhavissāmā’ti. Imināpi kho etaṃ, brāhmaṇa, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ yathā piyajātikā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā piyappabhavikā’’ti.

mula_english:
356. “So it is, Brahmin, so it is, Brahmin! Sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are born from those who are dear, arise from those who are dear. It can be understood from this, Brahmin, how sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are born from those who are dear, arise from those who are dear. Once in this same Śrāvastī, there was a certain woman whose mother died. Owing to her mother’s death, she went mad, lost her mind, and wandered from street to street and from crossroad to crossroad, saying: ‘Have you seen my mother? Have you seen my mother?’” And it can also be understood from this how sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are born from those who are dear, arise from those who are dear. “Once in this same Śrāvastī, there was a certain woman whose father died…whose brother died…whose sister died…whose son died…whose daughter died…whose husband died. Owing to her husband’s death, she went mad, lost her mind, and wandered from street to street and from crossroad to crossroad, saying: ‘Have you seen my husband? Have you seen my husband?’” And it can also be understood from this how sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are born from those who are dear, arise from those who are dear. “Once in this same Śrāvastī, there was a certain man whose mother died. Owing to her death, he went mad, lost his mind, and wandered from street to street and from crossroad to crossroad, saying: ‘Have you seen my mother? Have you seen my mother?’” And it can also be understood from this, Brahmin, how sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are born from those who are dear, arise from those who are dear. “Once in this same Śrāvastī, there was a certain man whose father died…whose brother died…whose sister died…whose son died…whose daughter died…whose wife died. Owing to her death, he went mad, lost his mind, and wandered from street to street and from crossroad to crossroad, saying: ‘Have you seen my wife? Have you seen my wife?’” And it can also be understood from this, Brahmin, how sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are born from those who are dear, arise from those who are dear. “Once in this same Śrāvastī, there was a certain woman who went to her relatives’ family. Her relatives wanted to divorce her from her husband and give her to another, whom she did not want. Then that woman said this to her husband: ‘These relatives of mine, dear son, want to divorce you from me and give me to another, but I do not want that.’” Then the man cut the woman in two and committed suicide. 0110"/> He uprooted uprooted (sī. pī. ), removed (ka. ) – ‘We both will be in the state of having departed.’ And it can also be understood from this how sorrow (śoka), lamentation (parideva), pain (duḥkha), grief (daumanasya), and despair (upāyāsa) are born from those who are dear (priya), arise from those who are dear (priyaprabhavika).

Mistress (sāmikā) (sī. ) Mine (mama) (syā. kaṃ. pī. ) By you (tayā) (sī. ), that (taṃ) (syā. kaṃ. pī. ) uprooted (uppāṭesi) (sī. pī. ), removed (ophāresi) (ka. )
commentary_pali: 356.Dvidhāchetvāti asinā dve koṭṭhāse karonto chinditvā. Attānaṃupphālesīti teneva asinā attano udaraṃ phālesi. Yadi hi tassa sā appiyā bhaveyya, idāni aññaṃ mātugāmaṃ gaṇhissāmīti attānaṃ na ghāteyya. Yasmā panassa sā piyā ahosi, tasmā paralokepi tāya saddhiṃ samaṅgibhāvaṃ patthayamāno evamakāsi.
commentary_english:
356. *dvidhā*: having cut ( *chetvā*) means having divided by making two parts with a sword (*asinā*).
*attānaṃ* *upphālesī* means he split his own belly (*udaraṃ*) with that very sword (*asinā*).
If she were displeasing (*appiyā*) to him, he would not have killed himself (*attānaṃ na ghāteyya*), thinking, "Now I will take another woman (*mātugāmaṃ gaṇhissāmi*)."
Because she was dear (*piyā*) to him, therefore, desiring a harmonious state (*samaṅgibhāvaṃ patthayamāno*) with her even in the next world (*paraloka*), he did this (*evamakāsi*).

mula_pali:
357. Atha kho nāḷijaṅgho brāhmaṇo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena mallikā devī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā yāvatako ahosi bhagavatā saddhiṃ kathāsallāpo taṃ sabbaṃ mallikāya deviyā ārocesi. Atha kho mallikā devī yena rājā pasenadi kosalo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rājānaṃ pasenadiṃ kosalaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, piyā te vajirī kumārī’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ, mallike, piyā me vajirī kumārī’’ti. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, vajiriyā te kumāriyā vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā uppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā’’ti? ‘‘Vajiriyā me, mallike, kumāriyā vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā jīvitassapi siyā aññathattaṃ, kiṃ pana me na uppajjissanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā’’ti? ‘‘Idaṃ kho taṃ, mahārāja, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sandhāya bhāsitaṃ – ‘piyajātikā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā piyappabhavikā’ti.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, piyā te vāsabhā khattiyā’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ, mallike, piyā me vāsabhā khattiyā’’ti. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, vāsabhāya te khattiyāya vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā uppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā’’ti? ‘‘Vāsabhāya me, mallike, khattiyāya vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā jīvitassapi siyā aññathattaṃ, kiṃ pana me na uppajjissanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā’’ti? ‘‘Idaṃ kho taṃ, mahārāja, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sandhāya bhāsitaṃ – ‘piyajātikā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā piyappabhavikā’ti.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, piyo te viṭaṭūbho viḍūḍabho (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) senāpatī’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ , mallike, piyo me viṭaṭūbho senāpatī’’ti. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, viṭaṭūbhassa te senāpatissa vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā uppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā’’ti? ‘‘Viṭaṭūbhassa me, mallike, senāpatissa vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā jīvitassapi siyā aññathattaṃ , kiṃ pana me na uppajjissanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā’’ti? ‘‘Idaṃ kho taṃ, mahārāja, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sandhāya bhāsitaṃ – ‘piyajātikā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā piyappabhavikā’ti.

viḍūḍabho (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, piyā te aha’’nti? ‘‘Evaṃ, mallike, piyā mesi tva’’nti. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, mayhaṃ te vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā uppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā’’ti? ‘‘Tuyhañhi me, mallike, vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā jīvitassapi siyā aññathattaṃ, kiṃ pana me na uppajjissanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā’’ti? ‘‘Idaṃ kho taṃ, mahārāja, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sandhāya bhāsitaṃ – ‘piyajātikā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā piyappabhavikā’ti.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, piyā te kāsikosalā’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ, mallike, piyā me kāsikosalā. Kāsikosalānaṃ, mallike, ānubhāvena kāsikacandanaṃ paccanubhoma, mālāgandhavilepanaṃ dhāremā’’ti. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, kāsikosalānaṃ te vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā uppajjeyyuṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā’’ti? ‘‘Kāsikosalānañhi, mallike , vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā jīvitassapi siyā aññathattaṃ, kiṃ pana me na uppajjissanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā’’ti? ‘‘Idaṃ kho taṃ, mahārāja, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sandhāya bhāsitaṃ – ‘piyajātikā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā piyappabhavikā’’’ti.

‘‘Acchariyaṃ, mallike, abbhutaṃ, mallike! Yāvañca so bhagavā paññāya ativijjha maññe paṭivijjha paññāya (ka.) passati. Ehi, mallike, ācamehī’’ti ācāmehīti (sī. pī.). Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā tikkhattuṃ udānaṃ udānesi – ‘‘namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa, namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa, namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassā’’ti.

paṭivijjha paññāya (ka.) ācāmehīti (sī. pī.)

Piyajātikasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.
mula_english:
Then, the brahmin Nāḷijaṅgha, delighting and rejoicing in the Blessed One’s words, rose from his seat and went to Queen Mallikā; having gone there, he reported to Queen Mallikā his entire conversation with the Blessed One.

Then, Queen Mallikā went to King Pasenadi of Kosala; having gone there, she said to King Pasenadi of Kosala: “What do you think, great king? Is Princess Vajirī dear to you?” “Yes, Mallikā, Princess Vajirī is dear to me.”

“What do you think, great king? If change and alteration were to take place in Princess Vajirī, would sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise in you?” “If change and alteration were to take place in Princess Vajirī, Mallikā, even my life would be different; why would sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair not arise in me?” “Great king, this is what the Blessed One, knowing, seeing, worthy, and perfectly enlightened, said with a purpose: ‘Sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are born from those who are dear, they originate from those who are dear.’”

“What do you think, great king? Is the noble Queen Vāsabhā dear to you?” “Yes, Mallikā, the noble Vāsabhā is dear to me.”

“What do you think, great king? If change and alteration were to take place in the noble Vāsabhā, would sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise in you?” “If change and alteration were to take place in the noble Vāsabhā, Mallikā, even my life would be different; why would sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair not arise in me?” “Great king, this is what the Blessed One, knowing, seeing, worthy, and perfectly enlightened, said with a purpose: ‘Sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are born from those who are dear; they originate from those who are dear.’”

“What do you think, great king? “What do you think, great king? Am I dear to you?” “Yes, Mallikā, you are dear to me.”

“What do you think, great king? If change and alteration were to take place in me, would sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise in you?” “If change and alteration were to take place in you, Mallikā, even my life would be different; why would sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair not arise in me?” “Great king, this is what the Blessed One, knowing, seeing, worthy, and perfectly enlightened, said with a purpose: ‘Sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are born from those who are dear; they originate from those who are dear.’”

“What do you think, great king? Are Kāsi and Kosala dear to you?” “Yes, Mallikā, Kāsi and Kosala are dear to me. By the power of Kāsi and Kosala, Mallikā, we enjoy Kāsi sandalwood and wear garlands, scents, and unguents.”

“What do you think, great king? If change and alteration were to take place in Kāsi and Kosala, would sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise in you?” “If change and alteration were to take place in Kāsi and Kosala, Mallikā, even my life would be different; why would sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair not arise in me?” “Great king, this is what the Blessed One, knowing, seeing, worthy, and perfectly enlightened, said with a purpose: ‘Sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are born from those who are dear; they originate from those who are dear.’”

“Wonderful, Mallikā, amazing, Mallikā! The Blessed One sees so deeply with wisdom. Come, Mallikā, drink!”

commentary_pali:
357.Piyā te vajirīti evaṃ kirassā ahosi – ‘‘sacāhaṃ, ‘bhūtapubbaṃ, mahārāja, imissāyeva sāvatthiyaṃ aññatarissā itthiyā’tiādikathaṃ katheyyaṃ, ‘ko te evaṃ akāsi, apehi natthi eta’nti maṃ paṭisedheyya, vattamāneneva naṃ saññāpessāmī’’ti cintetvā evamāha. Vipariṇāmaññathābhāvāti ettha maraṇavasena vipariṇāmo, kenaci saddhiṃ palāyitvā gamanavasena aññathābhāvo veditabbo.

Vāsabhāyāti vāsabhā nāma rañño ekā devī, taṃ sandhāyāha.

Vāsabhāyā

Piyāte ahanti kasmā sabbapacchā āha? Evaṃ kirassā ahosi – ‘‘ayaṃ rājā mayhaṃ kupito, sacāhaṃ sabbapaṭhamaṃ ‘piyā te aha’nti puccheyyaṃ, ‘na me tvaṃ piyā, cara pire’ti vadeyya, evaṃ sante kathā patiṭṭhānaṃ na labhissatī’’ti kathāya patiṭṭhānatthaṃ sabbapacchā pucchi. Kāsikosalesu chaḍḍitabhāvena vipariṇāmo, paṭirājūnaṃ hatthagamanavasena aññathābhāvo veditabbo.

Piyā te aha Kāsikosalesu

Ācamehīti ācamanodakaṃ dehi. Ācamitvā hatthapāde dhovitvā mukhaṃ vikkhāletvā satthāraṃ namassitukāmo evamāha. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Ācamehī

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Piyajātikasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
357. *Piyā te vajirī* [is said]. Thus, it occurred to him: "If I were to speak the introductory words, 'Formerly, O great king, in this very Sāvatthī, regarding a certain woman,' he might reject me, saying, 'Who did that to you? Go away, there is nothing here.' I will convince him with what is happening now," thinking thus, he said:

*Vipariṇāmaññathābhāvā:* Here, *vipariṇāma* is due to death, and *aññathābhāva* should be understood as due to going away, having fled with someone.

*Vāsabhāyā:* *Vāsabhā* is the name of a certain queen of the king; referring to her, he said.

*Vāsabhāyā piyā te aha:* Why did he say [this] at the very end? Thus, it occurred to him: "This king is angry with me. If I were to ask 'Are you fond of me?' at the very beginning, he might say, 'You are not dear to me, go away!' Thus, the story would not gain a footing." For the sake of the story gaining a footing, he asked at the very end.

*Kāsikosalesu:* *Vipariṇāma* is due to the state of being thrown away in the Kāsi and Kosala countries, and *aññathābhāva* should be understood as due to going into the hands of enemy kings.

*Piyā te aha kāsikosalesu:* *Ācamehī:* Give me water for rinsing [the mouth].

Having rinsed his mouth, washed his hands and feet, cleansed his face, and desiring to greet the Teacher, he spoke thus.

The rest is clear throughout.

*Ācamehī.*

The commentary to the *Papañcasūdanī Majjhimanikāya*,

The explanation of the *Piyajātikasutta* is complete.

mula_pali: 358. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āyasmā ānando pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena pubbārāmo migāramātupāsādo tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāya. Tena kho pana samayena rājā pasenadi kosalo ekapuṇḍarīkaṃ nāgaṃ abhiruhitvā sāvatthiyā niyyāti divā divassa. Addasā kho rājā pasenadi kosalo āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna sirivaḍḍhaṃ mahāmattaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘āyasmā no eso, samma sirivaḍḍha, ānando’’ti . ‘‘Evaṃ, mahārāja, āyasmā eso ānando’’ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ehi tvaṃ, ambho purisa, yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena āyasmato ānandassa pāde sirasā vandāhi – ‘rājā, bhante, pasenadi kosalo āyasmato ānandassa pāde sirasā vandatī’ti. Evañca vadehi – ‘sace kira, bhante, āyasmato ānandassa na kiñci accāyikaṃ karaṇīyaṃ, āgametu kira, bhante, āyasmā ānando muhuttaṃ anukampaṃ upādāyā’’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, devā’’ti kho so puriso rañño pasenadissa kosalassa paṭissutvā yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho so puriso āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘rājā, bhante, pasenadi kosalo āyasmato ānandassa pāde sirasā vandati; evañca vadeti – ‘sace kira, bhante, āyasmato ānandassa na kiñci accāyikaṃ karaṇīyaṃ, āgametu kira, bhante, āyasmā ānando muhuttaṃ anukampaṃ upādāyā’’’ti. Adhivāsesi kho āyasmā ānando tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo yāvatikā nāgassa bhūmi nāgena gantvā nāgā paccorohitvā pattikova yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho rājā pasenadi kosalo āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sace, bhante, āyasmato ānandassa na kiñci accāyikaṃ karaṇīyaṃ , sādhu, bhante, āyasmā ānando yena aciravatiyā nadiyā tīraṃ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṃ upādāyā’’ti. Adhivāsesi kho āyasmā ānando tuṇhībhāvena.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī (Śrāvastī) in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapindika’s Park.

Then, in the morning, the venerable Ānanda, having dressed, taking his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

Having wandered for alms in Sāvatthī and having returned from his alms round, after his meal he went to the Eastern Park, to the Palace of Migāra’s Mother, for the day’s abiding.

Now at that time, King Pasenadi of Kosala, having mounted the elephant Ekapundarika, was riding out from Sāvatthī at midday.

King Pasenadi of Kosala saw the venerable Ānanda coming in the distance.

Having seen him, he addressed Sirivaḍḍha, the high official: “That is the venerable Ānanda, Sirivaḍḍha.”

“Yes, your majesty, that is the venerable Ānanda.”

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala told a certain man: “Come, good man, go to the venerable Ānanda and, having approached him, pay homage with your head at the feet of the venerable Ānanda in my name, saying: ‘The king, venerable sir, Pasenadi of Kosala, pays homage with his head at the feet of the venerable Ānanda.’

And say this: ‘If, venerable sir, the venerable Ānanda has no urgent business, may the venerable Ānanda come for a moment, out of compassion.’”

“Yes, sire,” the man replied to King Pasenadi of Kosala, and he went to the venerable Ānanda; having approached, he paid homage to the venerable Ānanda and stood at one side.

Standing to one side, that man said to the venerable Ānanda: “The king, venerable sir, Pasenadi of Kosala, pays homage with his head at the feet of the venerable Ānanda; and he says this: ‘If, venerable sir, the venerable Ānanda has no urgent business, may the venerable Ānanda come for a moment, out of compassion.’”

The venerable Ānanda consented in silence (tuṇhībhāvena).

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala went by elephant as far as the elephant could go, and then, dismounting from the elephant and going on foot, he approached the venerable Ānanda; having approached, he paid homage to the venerable Ānanda and stood at one side.

Standing to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the venerable Ānanda: “If, venerable sir, the venerable Ānanda has no urgent business, it would be good if the venerable Ānanda would go to the bank of the Aciravatī (Ajiaravati) River, out of compassion.”

The venerable Ānanda consented in silence (tuṇhībhāvena).
commentary_pali: 358.Evaṃme sutanti bāhitikasuttaṃ. Tattha ekapuṇḍarīkaṃ nāganti evaṃnāmakaṃ hatthiṃ. Tassa kira phāsukānaṃ upari tālaphalamattaṃ paṇḍaraṭṭhānaṃ atthi , tenassa ekapuṇḍarīkoti nāmaṃ akaṃsu. Sirivaḍḍhaṃ mahāmattanti paccekahatthiṃ abhiruhitvā kathāphāsukatthaṃ saddhiṃ gacchantaṃ evaṃnāmakaṃ mahāmattaṃ. Āyasmānoti ettha noti pucchāya nipāto. Mahāmatto therassa saṅghāṭipattadhāraṇākāraṃ sallakkhetvā ‘‘evaṃ, mahārājā’’ti āha.
commentary_english:
358. Thus, I heard: the Bāhitika Sutta.

There, " *ekapuṇḍarīkaṃ nāga* " means an elephant of such a name.

It is said that above its ribs, there was a white spot the size of a palm fruit; therefore they gave it the name *ekapuṇḍarīka*.

"*sirivaḍḍhaṃ mahāmatta*" means a great minister of such a name, who, having ascended his own elephant, was going along together to a place suitable for conversation.

"*āyasmāno* " here, " *no* " is a particle of questioning.

The great minister, having considered the manner in which the elder was wearing his *saṅghāṭī* robe and bowl, said, "Yes, Great King!"

mula_pali:
359. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena aciravatiyā nadiyā tīraṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo yāvatikā nāgassa bhūmi nāgena gantvā nāgā paccorohitvā pattikova yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho rājā pasenadi kosalo āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘idha, bhante, āyasmā ānando hatthatthare nisīdatū’’ti. ‘‘Alaṃ, mahārāja. Nisīda tvaṃ; nisinno ahaṃ sake āsane’’ti. Nisīdi kho rājā pasenadi kosalo paññatte āsane. Nisajja kho rājā pasenadi kosalo āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘kiṃ nu kho, bhante ānanda, so bhagavā tathārūpaṃ kāyasamācāraṃ samācareyya, yvāssa kāyasamācāro opārambho samaṇehi brāhmaṇehī’’ti brāhmaṇehi viññūhīti (sabbattha) aṭṭhakathā ṭīkā oloketabbā? ‘‘Na kho, mahārāja, so bhagavā tathārūpaṃ kāyasamācāraṃ samācareyya, yvāssa kāyasamācāro opārambho samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhī’’ti.

‘‘Kiṃ pana, bhante ānanda, so bhagavā tathārūpaṃ vacīsamācāraṃ…pe… manosamācāraṃ samācareyya, yvāssa manosamācāro opārambho samaṇehi brāhmaṇehī’’ti brāhmaṇehi viññūhīti (sabbattha) aṭṭhakathā ṭīkā oloketabbā? ‘‘Na kho, mahārāja, so bhagavā tathārūpaṃ manosamācāraṃ samācareyya, yvāssa manosamācāro opārambho samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhī’’ti.

‘‘Acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante! Yañhi mayaṃ, bhante, nāsakkhimhā pañhena paripūretuṃ taṃ, bhante, āyasmatā ānandena pañhassa veyyākaraṇena paripūritaṃ. Ye te, bhante, bālā abyattā ananuvicca apariyogāhetvā paresaṃ vaṇṇaṃ vā avaṇṇaṃ vā bhāsanti, na mayaṃ taṃ sārato paccāgacchāma; ye pana ye ca kho (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) te, bhante , paṇḍitā viyattā byattā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) medhāvino anuvicca pariyogāhetvā paresaṃ vaṇṇaṃ vā avaṇṇaṃ vā bhāsanti, mayaṃ taṃ sārato paccāgacchāma’’.

ye ca kho (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) byattā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)
mula_english:
359. Then venerable Ānanda went to the bank of the river Aciravatī (अचिरवती); after going there, he sat down on a prepared seat at the root of a certain tree.

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala went by elephant as far as the elephant could go, and dismounting from the elephant, he proceeded on foot to where venerable Ānanda was; after approaching, he paid homage to venerable Ānanda and stood to one side.

Standing to one side, King Pasenadi Kosala said this to venerable Ānanda: "Here, venerable sir (bhante), may venerable Ānanda be seated on this elephant rug."

"Enough, great king (mahārāja). You sit down; I am sitting on my own seat."

King Pasenadi of Kosala sat down on the prepared seat.

Having sat down, King Pasenadi Kosala said this to venerable Ānanda: "What kind of bodily conduct (kāyasamācāraṃ), venerable Ānanda, would the Blessed One (bhagavā) engage in, such that his bodily conduct would be criticized by ascetics (samaṇehi) and Brahmins (brāhmaṇehi)?"

"No, great king, the Blessed One would not engage in such bodily conduct that his bodily conduct would be criticized by ascetics and Brahmins."

"And what kind of verbal conduct (vacīsamācāraṃ)... or mental conduct (manosamācāraṃ), venerable Ānanda, would the Blessed One engage in, such that his mental conduct would be criticized by ascetics and Brahmins?"

"No, great king, the Blessed One would not engage in such mental conduct that his mental conduct would be criticized by ascetics and Brahmins."

"Amazing, venerable sir, astonishing, venerable sir! For what we were unable to fully answer with a question, venerable sir, has been fully answered by venerable Ānanda with an explanation of the question.

Those who, venerable sir, are foolish (bālā), unskilled (abyattā), without investigating (ananuvicca), without careful examination (apariyogāhetvā), speak praise or dispraise of others, we do not accept that as essential. But those who, venerable sir, are wise (paṇḍitā), skilled (viyattā), intelligent (medhāvino), having investigated, having carefully examined, speak praise or dispraise of others, we accept that as essential."
commentary_pali: 359.Opārambhoti upārambhaṃ dosaṃ āropanāraho. Kiṃ pucchāmīti rājā pucchati. Sundarivatthusmiṃ uppannamidaṃ suttaṃ, taṃ pucchāmīti pucchati. Yañhi mayaṃ, bhanteti, bhante, yaṃ mayaṃ viññūhīti idaṃ padaṃ gahetvā pañhena paripūretuṃ nāsakkhimhā, taṃ kāraṇaṃ āyasmatā evaṃ vadantena paripūritaṃ.
commentary_english:
359. *Opārambho* means someone deserving to be reproached for their fault.

"What shall I ask?" the king asked.

"This *sutta* arose concerning Sundarī; I will ask about that," he asked.

"Indeed, venerable sir (*bhante*)," meaning, "venerable sir, what we should understand," having taken this word (*padam*) and being unable to complete [the question] with the question, that reason (*kāraṇaṃ*) was completed by the venerable one (*āyasmatā*) speaking thus.

mula_pali:
360. ‘‘Katamo pana, bhante ānanda, kāyasamācāro opārambho samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhī’’ti? ‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro akusalo’’.

‘‘Katamo pana, bhante, kāyasamācāro akusalo’’? ‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro sāvajjo’’.

‘‘Katamo pana, bhante, kāyasamācāro sāvajjo’’? ‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro sabyābajjho’’ sabyāpajjho (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), sabyāpajjo (ka.).

sabyāpajjho (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), sabyāpajjo (ka.)

‘‘Katamo pana, bhante, kāyasamācāro sabyābajjho’’? ‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro dukkhavipāko’’.

‘‘Katamo pana, bhante, kāyasamācāro dukkhavipāko’’? ‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro attabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati tassa akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyanti; evarūpo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro opārambho samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhī’’ti.

‘‘Katamo pana, bhante ānanda, vacīsamācāro…pe… manosamācāro opārambho samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhī’’ti? ‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro akusalo’’.

‘‘Katamo pana, bhante, manosamācāro akusalo’’? ‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro sāvajjo’’.

‘‘Katamo pana, bhante, manosamācāro sāvajjo’’? ‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro sabyābajjho’’.

‘‘Katamo pana, bhante, manosamācāro sabyābajjho’’? ‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro dukkhavipāko’’.

‘‘Katamo pana, bhante, manosamācāro dukkhavipāko’’? ‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro attabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati tassa akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyanti; evarūpo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro opārambho samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhī’’ti.

‘‘Kiṃ nu kho, bhante ānanda, so bhagavā sabbesaṃyeva akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānaṃ vaṇṇetī’’ti? ‘‘Sabbākusaladhammapahīno kho, mahārāja, tathāgato kusaladhammasamannāgato’’ti.
mula_english:
360. “Now, venerable Ānanda, what kind of bodily behaviour is censured by wise *śrāmaṇas* (samaṇa) and *brāhmaṇas* (brāhmaṇa)?” “Any bodily behaviour that is unwholesome, great king.”

“Now, venerable sir, what kind of bodily behaviour is unwholesome?” “Any bodily behaviour that is blameworthy, great king.”

“Now, venerable sir, what kind of bodily behaviour is blameworthy?” “Any bodily behaviour that brings affliction, great king.”

“Now, venerable sir, what kind of bodily behaviour brings affliction?” “Any bodily behaviour that has painful results, great king.”

“Now, venerable sir, what kind of bodily behaviour has painful results?” “Any bodily behaviour, great king, that leads to one’s own affliction (*ātmavyābādhāya*), or to the affliction of others (*paravyābādhāya*), or to the affliction of both (*ubhayavyābādhāya*), and on account of which unwholesome states (*akuśalā dharma*) increase (*abhivaḍḍhanti*) and wholesome states (*kuśalā dharma*) diminish (*parihāyanti*). Such bodily behaviour is censured by wise *śrāmaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas*, great king.”

“Now, venerable Ānanda, what kind of verbal behaviour…pe… mental behaviour is censured by wise *śrāmaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas*?” “Any mental behaviour that is unwholesome, great king.”

“Now, venerable sir, what kind of mental behaviour is unwholesome?” “Any mental behaviour that is blameworthy, great king.”

“Now, venerable sir, what kind of mental behaviour is blameworthy?” “Any mental behaviour that brings affliction, great king.”

“Now, venerable sir, what kind of mental behaviour brings affliction?” “Any mental behaviour that has painful results, great king.”

“Now, venerable sir, what kind of mental behaviour has painful results?” “Any mental behaviour, great king, that leads to one’s own affliction, or to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both, and on account of which unwholesome states increase and wholesome states diminish. Such mental behaviour is censured by wise *śrāmaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas*, great king.”

“Now, venerable Ānanda, does the Blessed One (*bhagavān*) commend the abandoning of all unwholesome states?” “The *Tathāgata* (*tathāgata*) has abandoned all unwholesome states and is endowed with wholesome states, great king.”
commentary_pali:
360.Akusaloti akosallasambhūto. Sāvajjoti sadoso. Sabyābajjhoti sadukkho. Dukkhavipākoti idha nissandavipāko kathito. Tassāti tassa evaṃ attabyābādhādīnaṃ atthāya pavattakāyasamācārassa.

Sabbākusaladhammapahīno kho, mahārāja, tathāgato kusaladhammasamannāgatoti ettha sabbesaṃyeva akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānaṃ vaṇṇetīti. Āma vaṇṇetīti vutte yathā pucchā, tathā attho vutto bhaveyya. Evaṃ byākaraṇaṃ pana na bhāriyaṃ. Appahīnaakusalopi hi pahānaṃ vaṇṇeyya, bhagavā pana pahīnākusalatāya yathākārī tathāvādīti dassetuṃ evaṃ byākāsi. Sukkapakkhepi eseva nayo.

Sabbākusaladhammapahīno kho, mahārāja, tathāgato kusaladhammasamannāgato
commentary_english:
"Akusalo" means arising from unskillfulness. "Sāvajjo" means with fault. "Sabyābajjho" means with suffering. "Dukkhavipāko" means here the result flowing [from it] is spoken of. "Tassā" means of that bodily conduct which occurs for the purpose of harm to self, etc.

"sabbākusaladhammapahīno kho, mahārāja, tathāgato kusaladhammasamannāgato" means here it praises the abandoning of all unwholesome things.

"Yes, it praises," when said thus, the meaning would be spoken according to the question. However, this explanation is not weighty. Even one who has not abandoned the unwholesome might praise abandonment, but the Blessed One, because of having abandoned the unwholesome, is a speaker in accordance with his actions, thus he explained. And the same rule applies in the case of the bright side.

"sabbākusaladhammapahīno kho, mahārāja, tathāgato kusaladhammasamannāgato"

mula_pali:
361. ‘‘Katamo pana, bhante ānanda, kāyasamācāro anopārambho samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhī’’ti? ‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro kusalo’’.

‘‘Katamo pana, bhante, kāyasamācāro kusalo’’? ‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro anavajjo’’.

‘‘Katamo pana, bhante, kāyasamācāro anavajjo’’? ‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro abyābajjho’’.

‘‘Katamo pana, bhante, kāyasamācāro abyābajjho’’? ‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro sukhavipāko’’.

‘‘Katamo pana, bhante, kāyasamācāro sukhavipāko’’?

‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro nevattabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, na parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, na ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati tassa akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti; evarūpo kho, mahārāja, kāyasamācāro anopārambho samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhī’’ti.

‘‘Katamo pana, bhante ānanda, vacīsamācāro…pe… manosamācāro anopārambho samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhī’’ti? ‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro kusalo’’.

‘‘Katamo pana, bhante, manosamācāro kusalo’’? ‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro anavajjo’’.

‘‘Katamo pana, bhante, manosamācāro anavajjo’’? ‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro abyābajjho’’.

‘‘Katamo pana, bhante, manosamācāro abyābajjho’’? ‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro sukhavipāko’’.

‘‘Katamo pana, bhante, manosamācāro sukhavipāko’’? ‘‘Yo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro nevattabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, na parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, na ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati. Tassa akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti. Evarūpo kho, mahārāja, manosamācāro anopārambho samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhī’’ti.

‘‘Kiṃ pana, bhante ānanda, so bhagavā sabbesaṃyeva kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadaṃ vaṇṇetī’’ti? ‘‘Sabbākusaladhammapahīno kho, mahārāja, tathāgato kusaladhammasamannāgato’’ti.
mula_english:
361. “Now, venerable Ānanda, what kind of bodily behaviour is uncensured by wise renunciates, *brāhmaṇas*, and the intelligent?” “Any bodily behaviour, great king, that is skillful.”

“Now, venerable sir, what kind of bodily behaviour is skillful?” “Any bodily behaviour, great king, that is blameless.”

“Now, venerable sir, what kind of bodily behaviour is blameless?” “Any bodily behaviour, great king, that is free from affliction.”

“Now, venerable sir, what kind of bodily behaviour is free from affliction?” “Any bodily behaviour, great king, that has pleasant results.”

“Now, venerable sir, what kind of bodily behaviour has pleasant results?”

“Any bodily behaviour, great king, that does not lead to one’s own affliction, or to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both, and on account of which unwholesome *dharmas* diminish and wholesome *dharmas* increase. Such bodily behaviour, great king, is uncensured by wise renunciates, *brāhmaṇas*, and the intelligent.”

“Now, venerable Ānanda, what kind of verbal behaviour…pe…mental behavior is uncensured by wise renunciates, *brāhmaṇas*, and the intelligent?” “Any mental behaviour, great king, that is skillful.”

“Now, venerable sir, what kind of mental behaviour is skillful?” “Any mental behaviour, great king, that is blameless.”

“Now, venerable sir, what kind of mental behaviour is blameless?” “Any mental behaviour, great king, that is free from affliction.”

“Now, venerable sir, what kind of mental behaviour is free from affliction?” “Any mental behaviour, great king, that has pleasant results.”

“Now, venerable sir, what kind of mental behaviour has pleasant results?” “Any mental behaviour, great king, that does not lead to one’s own affliction, or to the affliction of others, or to the affliction of both, and on account of which unwholesome *dharmas* diminish and wholesome *dharmas* increase.
Such mental behaviour, great king, is uncensured by wise renunciates, *brāhmaṇas*, and the intelligent.”

“But venerable Ānanda, does that Blessed One commend the attainment of all skillful *dharmas*?” “The *Tathāgata*, great king, has abandoned all unskillful *dharmas* and possesses skillful *dharmas*.”

mula_pali:
362. ‘‘Acchariyaṃ , bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante! Yāva subhāsitaṃ cidaṃ subhāsitamidaṃ (sī.), bhante, āyasmatā ānandena. Iminā ca mayaṃ, bhante, āyasmato ānandassa subhāsitena attamanābhiraddhā. Evaṃ attamanābhiraddhā ca mayaṃ , bhante, āyasmato ānandassa subhāsitena. Sace, bhante, āyasmato ānandassa hatthiratanaṃ kappeyya, hatthiratanampi mayaṃ āyasmato ānandassa dadeyyāma. Sace, bhante, āyasmato ānandassa assaratanaṃ kappeyya, assaratanampi mayaṃ āyasmato ānandassa dadeyyāma. Sace, bhante, āyasmato ānandassa gāmavaraṃ kappeyya, gāmavarampi mayaṃ āyasmato ānandassa dadeyyāma. Api ca, bhante, mayampetaṃ mayameva taṃ (sī.), mayampanetaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) jānāma – ‘netaṃ āyasmato ānandassa kappatī’ti. Ayaṃ me, bhante, bāhitikā raññā māgadhena ajātasattunā vedehiputtena vatthanāḷiyā chattanāḷiyā (syā. kaṃ. pī.) pakkhipitvā pahitā soḷasasamā āyāmena, aṭṭhasamā vitthārena . Taṃ, bhante, āyasmā ānando paṭiggaṇhātu anukampaṃ upādāyā’’ti. ‘‘Alaṃ, mahārāja, paripuṇṇaṃ me ticīvara’’nti.

‘‘Ayaṃ , bhante, aciravatī nadī diṭṭhā āyasmatā ceva ānandena amhehi ca. Yadā uparipabbate mahāmegho abhippavuṭṭho hoti, athāyaṃ aciravatī nadī ubhato kūlāni saṃvissandantī gacchati; evameva kho, bhante, āyasmā ānando imāya bāhitikāya attano ticīvaraṃ karissati. Yaṃ panāyasmato ānandassa purāṇaṃ ticīvaraṃ taṃ sabrahmacārīhi saṃvibhajissati. Evāyaṃ amhākaṃ dakkhiṇā saṃvissandantī maññe gamissati. Paṭiggaṇhātu, bhante, āyasmā ānando bāhitika’’nti. Paṭiggahesi kho āyasmā ānando bāhitikaṃ.

Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘handa ca dāni mayaṃ, bhante ānanda, gacchāma; bahukiccā mayaṃ bahukaraṇīyā’’ti. ‘‘Yassadāni tvaṃ, mahārāja, kālaṃ maññasī’’ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo āyasmato ānandassa bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.
mula_english:
362. Wonderful, venerable sir, amazing, venerable sir! How well that has been expressed by the venerable Ānanda!

And we are satisfied and pleased by what has been so well expressed by the venerable Ānanda.

Venerable sir, we are so satisfied and pleased with what has been so well expressed by the venerable Ānanda.

that if the elephant-treasure (*hatthiratana*) were allowed to the venerable Ānanda, we would give the elephant-treasure (*hatthiratana*) to him;

if the horse-treasure (*assaratana*) were allowed to the venerable Ānanda, we would give the horse-treasure (*assaratana*) to him;

if the boon of a village (*gāmavara*) were allowed to the venerable Ānanda, we would give the boon of a village (*gāmavara*) to him.

But we know that these are not allowable for the venerable Ānanda.

But there is this cloak (*bāhitikā*) of mine, venerable sir, which was sent to me packed in a royal umbrella case by King Ajātasattu of Magadha, sixteen hands long and eight hands wide.

Let the venerable Ānanda accept it out of compassion.

“It is not necessary, great king. My triple robe (*ticīvara*) is complete.”

“Venerable sir, this river Aciravati has been seen both by the venerable Ānanda and by ourselves.

when a great cloud has rained heavily on the mountains; then this river Aciravati overflows both its banks. So too, venerable sir, the venerable Ānanda can make a triple robe (*ticīvara*) for himself out of this cloak (*bāhitikā*),

and he can share out his old triple robe (*ticīvara*) among his companions in the holy life.

In this way, our offering (*dakkhiṇā*) will overflow.

Venerable sir, let the venerable Ānanda accept the cloak (*bāhitika*).”

So the venerable Ānanda accepted the cloak (*bāhitikaṃ*).

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the venerable Ānanda: “And now, venerable sir, Ānanda, we depart. We are busy and have much to do.”

“Do whatever seems fit, great king.”

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala, having delighted and rejoiced in the venerable Ānanda’s words, rose from his seat, and after paying homage to the venerable Ānanda, keeping him on his right, he departed.
commentary_pali: 362.Bāhitikāti bāhitiraṭṭhe uṭṭhitavatthassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Soḷasasamā āyāmenāti āyāmena samasoḷasahatthā. Aṭṭhasamā vitthārenāti vitthārena samaaṭṭhahatthā.
commentary_english:
*bāhitikā* means this name is for a cloth that originated in the country of Bāhiti.

*soḷasasamā āyāmena* means sixteen hands in length.

*aṭṭhasamā vitthārena* means eight hands in width.

mula_pali:
363. Atha kho āyasmā ānando acirapakkantassa rañño pasenadissa kosalassa yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando yāvatako ahosi raññā pasenadinā kosalena saddhiṃ kathāsallāpo taṃ sabbaṃ bhagavato ārocesi. Tañca bāhitikaṃ bhagavato pādāsi. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘lābhā, bhikkhave, rañño pasenadissa kosalassa, suladdhalābhā, bhikkhave, rañño pasenadissa kosalassa; yaṃ rājā pasenadi kosalo labhati ānandaṃ dassanāya, labhati payirupāsanāyā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Bāhitikasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.
mula_english:
Then, soon after venerable Ānanda had departed from King Pasenadi of Kosala, he approached the Blessed One (bhagavā). Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side (ekamantaṃ nisīdi).

Seated to one side (ekamantaṃ nisinno), venerable Ānanda reported to the Blessed One everything that had been discussed with King Pasenadi of Kosala.

And he presented the cloak (bāhitikaṃ) to the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One addressed the monks (bhikkhū): "It is a gain (lābhā), monks (bhikkhave), for King Pasenadi of Kosala; it is a great gain (suladdhalābhā), monks (bhikkhave), for King Pasenadi of Kosala, that King Pasenadi of Kosala has the opportunity of seeing Ānanda, and the opportunity of paying respect."

The Blessed One said this (idamavoca bhagavā).

Satisfied (attamanā), the monks (bhikkhū) rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words (bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti).

The Bāhitika Sutta, the eighth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
363.Bhagavatopādāsīti bhagavato niyyātesi. Datvā ca pana gandhakuṭiyaṃ vitānaṃ katvā bandhi. Tato paṭṭhāya gandhakuṭi bhiyyosomattāya sobhi. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānameva. Neyyapuggalassa pana vasena ayaṃ desanā niṭṭhitāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Bāhitikasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
Bhagavato pādāsīti, he offered it to the Blessed One. Furthermore, having given it, he erected a canopy in the Gandhakuti and fastened it. From then on, the Gandhakuti shone all the more. The rest is clear throughout. This teaching is concluded according to the capacity of the person to be guided.

The Bāhitikasuttavaṇṇanā is concluded in the Papañcasūdanī, commentary on the Majjhimanikāya.

mula_pali: 364. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati medāḷupaṃ metaḷūpaṃ (sī.), medaḷumpaṃ (pī.) nāma sakyānaṃ nigamo. Tena kho pana samayena rājā pasenadi kosalo nagarakaṃ anuppatto hoti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo dīghaṃ kārāyanaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘yojehi, samma kārāyana, bhadrāni bhadrāni yānāni, uyyānabhūmiṃ gacchāma subhūmiṃ dassanāyā’’ti subhūmidassanāyāti (dī. ni. 2.43). ‘‘Evaṃ, devā’’ti kho dīgho kārāyano rañño pasenadissa kosalassa paṭissutvā bhadrāni bhadrāni yānāni yojāpetvā rañño pasenadissa kosalassa paṭivedesi – ‘‘yuttāni kho te, deva, bhadrāni bhadrāni yānāni. Yassadāni kālaṃ maññasī’’ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhadraṃ yānaṃ abhiruhitvā bhadrehi bhadrehi yānehi nagarakamhā niyyāsi mahaccā rājānubhāvena. Yena ārāmo tena pāyāsi. Yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi yānena gantvā yānā paccorohitvā pattikova ārāmaṃ pāvisi. Addasā kho rājā pasenadi kosalo ārāme jaṅghāvihāraṃ anucaṅkamamāno anuvicaramāno rukkhamūlāni pāsādikāni pasādanīyāni appasaddāni appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni manussarāhaseyyakāni (sī. pī.) paṭisallānasāruppāni. Disvāna bhagavantaṃyeva ārabbha sati udapādi – ‘‘imāni kho tāni rukkhamūlāni pāsādikāni pasādanīyāni appasaddāni appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni paṭisallānasāruppāni, yattha sudaṃ mayaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ payirupāsāma arahantaṃ sammāsambuddha’’nti.
mula_english:
364. Thus I have heard: At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyas at Medāḷupa, a Sakyan town.

Now on that occasion King Pasenadi of Kosala had arrived at Nagaraka for some business or other.

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala addressed Dīgha Kārāyana: “Dear Kārāyana, have the state carriages prepared. Let us go to the pleasure garden (**uyyānabhūmi**) to see a pleasing spot.”

“Yes, sire,” replied Dīgha Kārāyana to King Pasenadi of Kosala. When the state carriages (**bhadrāni bhadrāni yānāni**) were prepared, he informed King Pasenadi of Kosala: “Sire, the state carriages (**bhadrāni bhadrāni yānāni**) are ready for you. Now is the time, sir, to do as you think fit.”

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala mounted a state carriage (**bhadraṃ yānaṃ**), and accompanied by the other carriages (**bhadrehi bhadrehi yānehi**), he drove out from Nagaraka with the full pomp of royalty.

He proceeded towards the park (**ārāma**).

He went by chariot as far as possible, then dismounted from his carriage (**yānā**), and entered the park (**ārāmaṃ**) on foot.

King Pasenadi of Kosala saw in the park (**ārāme**) the roots of trees (**rukkhamūlāni**) that were lovely, inspiring, quiet and undisturbed by voices, with an atmosphere of seclusion, remote from people, favourable for retreat (**paṭisallānasāruppāni**).

The sight of these reminded him of the Blessed One thus: “These roots of trees (**rukkhamūlāni**) are lovely and inspiring, quiet and undisturbed by voices, with an atmosphere of seclusion, remote from people, favourable for retreat (**paṭisallānasāruppāni**), like the places where we used to pay respect to the Blessed One, the Arhat, the Fully Enlightened One (**sammāsambuddha**).”
commentary_pali:
364.Evaṃme sutanti dhammacetiyasuttaṃ. Tattha medāḷupanti nāmetaṃ tassa, tassa hi nigamassa medavaṇṇā pāsāṇā kirettha ussannā ahesuṃ, tasmā medāḷupanti saṅkhaṃ gataṃ. Senāsanaṃ panettha aniyataṃ, tasmā na taṃ vuttaṃ. Nagarakanti evaṃnāmakaṃ sakyānaṃ nigamaṃ. Kenacideva karaṇīyenāti na aññena karaṇīyena, ayaṃ pana bandhulasenāpatiṃ saddhiṃ dvattiṃsāya puttehi ekadivaseneva gaṇhathāti āṇāpesi, taṃdivasañcassa bhariyāya mallikāya pañcahi bhikkhusatehi saddhiṃ bhagavā nimantito, buddhappamukhe bhikkhusaṅghe gharaṃ āgantvā nisinnamatte ‘‘senāpati kālaṅkato’’ti sāsanaṃ āharitvā mallikāya adaṃsu. Sā paṇṇaṃ gahetvā mukhasāsanaṃ pucchi. ‘‘Raññā ayye senāpati saddhiṃ dvattiṃsāya puttehi ekappahāreneva gahāpito’’ti ārocesuṃ. Mahājanagataṃ mā karitthāti ovaṭṭikāya paṇṇaṃ katvā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ parivisi. Tasmiṃ samaye ekā sappicāṭi nīharitā, sā ummāre āhacca bhinnā, taṃ apanetvā aññaṃ āharāpetvā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ parivisi.

Satthā katabhattakicco kathāsamuṭṭhāpanatthaṃ – ‘‘sappicāṭiyā bhinnapaccayā na cintetabba’’nti āha. Tasmiṃ samaye mallikā paṇṇaṃ nīharitvā bhagavato purato ṭhapetvā – ‘‘bhagavā imaṃ dvattiṃsāya puttehi saddhiṃ senāpatino matasāsanaṃ, ahaṃ etampi na cintayāmi, sappicāṭipaccayā kiṃ cinteyyāmī’’ti āha. Bhagavā – ‘‘mallike, mā cintayi, anamatagge saṃsāre nāma vattamānānaṃ hoti eta’’nti aniccatādipaṭisaṃyuttaṃ dhammakathaṃ katvā agamāsi. Mallikā dvattiṃsasuṇisāyo pakkosāpetvā ovādaṃ adāsi. Rājā mallikaṃ pakkosāpetvā ‘‘senāpatino amhākaṃ antare bhinnadoso atthi natthī’’ti pucchi. Natthi sāmīti. So tassā vacanena tassa niddosabhāvaṃ ñatvā vippaṭisārī balavadomanassaṃ uppādesi. So – ‘‘evarūpaṃ nāma adosakārakaṃ maṃ sambhāvayitvā āgataṃ sahāyakaṃ vināsesi’’nti tato paṭṭhāya pāsāde vā nāṭakesu vā rajjasukhesu vā cittassādaṃ alabhamāno tattha tattha vicarituṃ āraddho. Etadeva kiccaṃ ahosi. Idaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘‘kenacideva karaṇīyenā’’ti.

Dīghaṃkārāyananti dīghakārāyano nāma bandhulasenāpatissa bhāgineyyo ‘‘etassa me mātulo adosakārako nikkāraṇena ghātito’’ti raññā senāpatiṭṭhāne ṭhapito. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Mahaccā rājānubhāvenāti mahatā rājānubhāvena , dharaṇitalaṃ bhindanto viya sāgaraṃ parivattento viya vicittavesasobhena mahatā balakāyenāti attho. Pāsādikānīti dassaneneva saha rañjanakāni. Pasādanīyānīti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Atha vā pāsādikānīti pasādajanakāni. Appasaddānīti nissaddāni. Appanigghosānīti avibhāvitatthena nigghosena rahitāni. Vijanavātānīti vigatajanavātāni. Manussarāhasseyyakānīti manussānaṃ rahassakammānucchavikāni, rahassamantaṃ mantentānaṃ anurūpānīti attho. Paṭisallānasāruppānīti nilīyanabhāvassa ekībhāvassa anucchavikāni. Yattha sudaṃ mayanti na tena tattha bhagavā payirupāsitapubbo, tādisesu pana payirupāsitapubbo, tasmā yādisesu sudaṃ mayanti ayamettha attho.

Dīghaṃ kārāyana Mahaccā rājānubhāvenā Pāsādikānī Pasādanīyānī pāsādikānī Appasaddānī Appanigghosānī Vijanavātānī Manussarāhasseyyakānī Paṭisallānasāruppānī Yattha sudaṃ maya

Atthi, mahārājāti paṇḍito senāpati ‘‘rājā bhagavantaṃ mamāyatī’’ti jānāti, so sace maṃ rājā ‘‘kahaṃ bhagavā’’ti vadeyya, adandhāyantena ācikkhituṃ yuttanti carapurise payojetvā bhagavato nivāsanaṭṭhānaṃ ñatvāva viharati. Tasmā evamāha. Ārāmaṃ pāvisīti bahinigame khandhāvāraṃ bandhāpetvā kārāyanena saddhiṃ pāvisi.

Atthi, mahārājā Ārāmaṃ pāvisī
commentary_english:
364. Thus I have heard: the Dhammacetiya Sutta.

There, *medāḷupa* means that this was the name of that place. For there, in that town, stones of *meda* color were uplifted. Therefore it went to the designation of *medāḷupa*.

The lodgings there were unregulated, therefore this was not said.

*nagaraka* means a town of the Sakyas with such a name.

*kenacideva karaṇīyenā* means not by any other doing. But he ordered Bandhula, the general, "Go with thirty-two sons and seize [them] in one day!" On that very day, the Blessed One was invited by Mallikā, the wife of him, together with five hundred monks. Having come to the house in the Sangha headed by the Buddha, as soon as they were seated, they brought the message "The general has died" and gave it to Mallikā.

She took the letter and asked for the verbal message.

"General, together with thirty-two sons, has been seized by the king in a single strike, O lady!" they announced.

"Lest it become associated with a great crowd," having made a letter with an *ovaṭṭika*, she served the Sangha of monks.

At that time, a pot of ghee was brought forth. It broke, having struck the threshold. Having removed that and having had another brought, she served the Sangha of monks.

The Teacher, having finished the meal, for the purpose of starting a conversation, said, "One should not be concerned about the broken condition of the ghee pot."

At that time, Mallikā, having brought forth a letter, having placed it before the Blessed One, said, "Blessed One, this is the message of the general's death, together with thirty-two sons. I do not even consider this. Why should I consider [the breaking of] the ghee pot?"

The Blessed One said, "Mallikā, do not be concerned, this happens to those who are wandering in the round of rebirths which has no known beginning." Having made a Dhamma talk connected with impermanence and so on, he departed.

Mallikā, having had thirty-two daughters-in-law summoned, gave an exhortation.

The king, having had Mallikā summoned, asked, "Is there any offense different among us of the general?"

"There is no lord," [she said].

He, knowing the state of being without offense of him by her word, produced remorse, a strong grief.

He, "Having considered me a friend who does no wrong, he has destroyed a helper who had come," from then on, not obtaining enjoyment of the mind in palaces or in dramas or in royal pleasures, began to wander here and there.

This very thing became the duty.

This was said with reference to that: "By some doing."

Dīghaṃ Kārāyana means that Dīghakārāyana, by name, was the nephew of Bandhula, the general. "This maternal uncle of mine, a doer of no wrong, has been killed for no reason," he was placed by the king in the general's position.

This was said with reference to him.

*mahaccā rājānubhāvenā* means by a great royal power, breaking the surface of the earth, as if overturning the ocean, with the splendor of varied attire, with a great army, this is the meaning.

*pāsādikānī* means delighting together with the very sight.

*pasādanīyānī* means that very word.

Or, *pāsādikānī* means producing delight.

*appasaddānī* means without sound.

*appanigghosānī* means without noise, by the fact of being indistinct.

*vijanavātānī* means without the winds of people.

*manussarāhasseyyakānī* means fitting for the secret deeds of humans, suitable for those who are pondering a secret *mantra*, this is the meaning.

*paṭisallānasāruppānī* means suitable for the state of seclusion, for the state of oneness.

*yattha sudaṃ maya* means, "Not by him was the Blessed One attended there before, but by such ones was he attended before." Therefore, "Of which sort, indeed, am I?" this is the meaning here.
dīghaṃ kārāyana mahaccā rājānubhāvenā pāsādikānī pasādanīyānī pāsādikānī appasaddānī appanigghosānī vijanavātānī manussarāhasseyyakānī paṭisallānasāruppānī yattha sudaṃ maya atthi, mahārājā ti paṇḍito senāpati ‘‘rājā bhagavantaṃ mamāyatī’’ti jānāti, so sace maṃ rājā ‘‘kahaṃ bhagavā’’ti vadeyya, adandhāyantena ācikkhituṃ yuttanti carapurise payojetvā bhagavato nivāsanaṭṭhānaṃ ñatvāva viharati. tasmā evamāha. ārāmaṃ pāvisī ti bahinigame khandhāvāraṃ bandhāpetvā kārāyanena saddhiṃ pāvisi.
atthi, mahārājā ārāmaṃ pāvisī

mula_pali: 365. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo dīghaṃ kārāyanaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘imāni kho, samma kārāyana, tāni rukkhamūlāni pāsādikāni pasādanīyāni appasaddāni appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni paṭisallānasāruppāni, yattha sudaṃ mayaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ payirupāsāma arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ. Kahaṃ nu kho, samma kārāyana, etarahi so bhagavā viharati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho’’ti? ‘‘Atthi, mahārāja, medāḷupaṃ nāma sakyānaṃ nigamo. Tattha so bhagavā etarahi viharati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho’’ti. ‘‘Kīvadūre kīvadūro (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) pana, samma kārāyana , nagarakamhā medāḷupaṃ nāma sakyānaṃ nigamo hotī’’ti? ‘‘Na dūre, mahārāja; tīṇi yojanāni; sakkā divasāvasesena gantu’’nti. ‘‘Tena hi, samma kārāyana, yojehi bhadrāni bhadrāni yānāni, gamissāma mayaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya arahantaṃ sammāsambuddha’’nti. ‘‘Evaṃ, devā’’ti kho dīgho kārāyano rañño pasenadissa kosalassa paṭissutvā bhadrāni bhadrāni yānāni yojāpetvā rañño pasenadissa kosalassa paṭivedesi – ‘‘yuttāni kho te, deva, bhadrāni bhadrāni yānāni. Yassadāni kālaṃ maññasī’’ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhadraṃ yānaṃ abhiruhitvā bhadrehi bhadrehi yānehi nagarakamhā yena medāḷupaṃ nāma sakyānaṃ nigamo tena pāyāsi. Teneva divasāvasesena medāḷupaṃ nāma sakyānaṃ nigamaṃ sampāpuṇi. Yena ārāmo tena pāyāsi. Yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi yānena gantvā yānā paccorohitvā pattikova ārāmaṃ pāvisi.
mula_english:
Then King Pasenadi of Kosala addressed Dīgha Kārāyana: "Indeed, friend Kārāyana, these are tree roots, inspiring, delightful, quiet, without noise, with breezes blowing through deserted spots, hidden from people, suitable for retreat, where we might attend to the Blessed One, the **arhat**, the Fully Awakened One (**sammāsambuddha**)."

"But where, friend Kārāyana, is that Blessed One (**bhagavantaṃ**), the **arhat**, the Fully Awakened One (**sammāsambuddhaṃ**) dwelling now?"

"There is, your majesty, a town of the Sakyans named Medāḷupa."

"There the Blessed One (**bhagavā**), the **arhat**, the Fully Awakened One (**sammāsambuddho**) is dwelling now."

"How far is Medāḷupa, the town of the Sakyans, from Nagaraka?"

"Not far, your majesty; three *yojanas*; it is possible to reach it by the end of the day."

"Then, friend Kārāyana, have fine state carriages prepared. We will go to see that Blessed One (**bhagavantaṃ**), the **arhat**, the Fully Awakened One (**sammāsambuddhaṃ**)."
