"Yes, your majesty," replied Dīgha Kārāyana to King Pasenadi of Kosala. Having had fine state carriages prepared, he informed King Pasenadi of Kosala: "The fine state carriages are ready for you, your majesty. Now is the time to do as you think fit."

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala mounted a fine state carriage, and accompanied by fine state carriages, set out from Nagaraka towards Medāḷupa, the town of the Sakyans.

He arrived at Medāḷupa, the town of the Sakyans, by the end of the day.

He proceeded towards the park.

As far as the ground was suitable for carriages, he went by carriage; then, alighting from the carriage, he entered the park on foot.

mula_pali: 366. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū abbhokāse caṅkamanti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca – ‘‘kahaṃ nu kho, bhante, etarahi so bhagavā viharati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho? Dassanakāmā hi mayaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddha’’nti. ‘‘Eso, mahārāja, vihāro saṃvutadvāro. Tena appasaddo upasaṅkamitvā ataramāno āḷindaṃ pavisitvā ukkāsitvā aggaḷaṃ ākoṭehi. Vivarissati bhagavā te dvāra’’nti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo tattheva khaggañca uṇhīsañca dīghassa kārāyanassa pādāsi. Atha kho dīghassa kārāyanassa etadahosi – ‘‘rahāyati kho dāni rājā mahārājā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), idheva tenidheva (sī.) dāni mayā ṭhātabba’’nti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo yena so vihāro saṃvutadvāro tena appasaddo upasaṅkamitvā ataramāno āḷindaṃ pavisitvā ukkāsitvā aggaḷaṃ ākoṭesi. Vivari bhagavā dvāraṃ. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo vihāraṃ pavisitvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavato pādāni mukhena ca paricumbati, pāṇīhi ca parisambāhati, nāmañca sāveti – ‘‘rājāhaṃ, bhante, pasenadi kosalo; rājāhaṃ, bhante, pasenadi kosalo’’ti.
mula_english:
366. At that time, a large number of monks were doing walking meditation in the open.

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala approached those monks and said to them, “Where, venerable sirs, is the Blessed One ( *bhagavā*), the perfected one ( *arahaṃ*), the fully enlightened Buddha ( *sammāsambuddho*) residing now? For we wish to see that Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully enlightened Buddha.”

“That, great king ( *mahārāja*), is his dwelling ( *vihāro*), with the closed door. Go up to it quietly, without hurrying, enter the porch ( *āḷindaṃ*), clear your throat, and tap on the panel ( *aggaḷaṃ*). The Blessed One will open the door ( *dvāraṃ*) for you.”

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala handed over his sword ( *khaggañca*) and turban ( *uṇhīsañca*) to Dīgha Kārāyana then and there.

Then Dīgha Kārāyana thought: “So the king is going into secret session now! And I have to wait here alone now!”

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala went quietly up to the dwelling ( *vihāro*) with the closed door, entered the porch ( *āḷindaṃ*), cleared his throat, and tapped on the panel ( *aggaḷaṃ*). The Blessed One opened the door ( *dvāraṃ*).

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala entered the dwelling ( *vihāraṃ*) and prostrated himself with his head at the Blessed One’s feet, he covered the Blessed One’s feet with kisses and caressed them with his hands, pronouncing his name: “I am King Pasenadi of Kosala, venerable sir; I am King Pasenadi of Kosala.”
commentary_pali:
366.Vihāroti gandhakuṭiṃ sandhāyāhaṃsu. Āḷindanti pamukhaṃ. Ukkāsitvāti ukkāsitasaddaṃ katvā. Aggaḷanti kavāṭaṃ. Ākoṭehīti agganakhena īsakaṃ kuñcikacchiddasamīpe koṭehīti vuttaṃ hoti. Dvāraṃ kira atiupari amanussā, atiheṭṭhā dīghajātikā koṭenti. Tathā akoṭetvā majjhe chiddasamīpe koṭetabbaṃ, idaṃ dvārakoṭṭakavattanti dīpentā vadanti. Tatthevāti bhikkhūhi vuttaṭṭhāneyeva. Khaggañca uṇhīsañcāti desanāmattametaṃ,

Vālabījanimuṇhīsaṃ, khaggaṃ chattañcupāhanaṃ;

Oruyha rājā yānamhā, ṭhapayitvā paṭicchadanti. –

Āgatāni pana pañcapi rājakakudhabhaṇḍāni adāsi. Kasmā pana adāsīti. Atigaruno sammāsambuddhassa santikaṃ uddhatavesena gantuṃ na yuttanti ca, ekakova upasaṅkamitvā attano rucivasena sammodissāmi cāti. Pañcasu hi rājakakudhabhaṇḍesu nivattitesu tvaṃ nivattāti vattabbaṃ na hoti, sabbe sayameva nivattanti. Iti imehi dvīhi kāraṇehi adāsi. Rahāyatīti rahassaṃ karoti nigūhati. Ayaṃ kirassa adhippāyo ‘‘pubbepi ayaṃ rājā samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ catukkaṇṇamantaṃ mantetvā mayhaṃ mātulaṃ saddhiṃ dvattiṃsāya puttehi gaṇhāpesi, idānipi catukkaṇṇamantaṃ mantetukāmo, kacci nu kho maṃ gaṇhāpessatī’’ti. Evaṃ kopavasenassa etadahosi.

Rahāyatī

Vivaribhagavā dvāranti na bhagavā uṭṭhāya dvāraṃ vivari, vivaratūti pana hatthaṃ pasāresi. Tato – ‘‘bhagavā tumhehi anekesu kappakoṭīsu dānaṃ dadamānehi na sahatthā dvāravivaraṇakammaṃ kata’’nti sayameva dvāraṃ vivaṭaṃ. Taṃ pana yasmā bhagavato manena vivaṭaṃ, tasmā ‘‘vivari bhagavā dvāra’’nti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Vihāraṃ pavisitvāti gandhakuṭiṃ pavisitvā. Tasmiṃ pana paviṭṭhamatteyeva kārāyano pañca rājakakudhabhaṇḍāni gahetvā khandhāvāraṃ gantvā viṭaṭūbhaṃ āmantesi ‘‘chattaṃ samma ussāpehī’’ti. Mayhaṃ pitā kiṃ gatoti? Pitaraṃ mā puccha, sace tvaṃ na ussāpesi, taṃ gaṇhitvā ahaṃ ussāpemīti. ‘‘Ussāpemi sammā’’ti sampaṭicchi. Kārāyano rañño ekaṃ assañca asiñca ekameva ca paricārikaṃ itthiṃ ṭhapetvā – ‘‘sace rājā jīvitena atthiko, mā āgacchatū’’ti viṭaṭūbhassa chattaṃ ussāpetvā taṃ gahetvā sāvatthimeva gato.

Vivari bhagavā dvāra Vihāraṃ pavisitvā
commentary_english:
366. *Vihāro* means they referred to the *gandhakuṭi*.

*Āḷinda* means the front.

*Ukkāsitvā* means having made a coughing sound.

*Aggaḷa* means a door panel.

*Ākoṭehī* means, "tap near the keyhole with the tip of your fingernail," it is said.

It is said that non-humans knock on the door very high up, and long-lived beings very low down.

Having tapped thus, one should tap in the middle near the hole; they say, indicating that this is the door-knocking custom.

*Tatthevā* means in the very place spoken of by the monks.

*Khaggañca uṇhīsañcā*—this is merely the extent of the teaching.

vālabījanimuṇhīsaṃ, khaggaṃ chattañcupāhanaṃ;

oruyha rājā yānamhā, ṭhapayitvā paṭicchadanti.

However, he gave the five royal emblems that had arrived.

Why did he give [them]?

Because it was not fitting to go to the greatly compassionate, perfectly enlightened Buddha (*sammāsambuddha*) in a haughty manner, and also, "Having approached alone, I will converse in accordance with my own liking."

Indeed, when the five royal emblems have been returned, it is not necessary to say, "You, turn back!"; all turn back of their own accord.

Thus, he gave [them] for these two reasons.

*Rahāyatī* means he makes it secret, he hides [it].

This was his intention: "Previously also, this king, having conferred in private (*catukkaṇṇamantaṃ*) with the *śramaṇa* Gotama, had my maternal uncle seized, together with thirty-two sons; even now, he intends to confer in private, and I wonder whether he will have me seized!"

Thus it occurred to him because of the power of anger.

*Rahāyatī* *vivari*

*Bhagavā dvāra* means the Blessed One did not get up and open the door, but he stretched out his hand, [saying,] "Let it be opened!"

Then – "The Blessed One, while giving alms for many hundreds of thousands of *kappa*s, has not personally done the work of opening the door" – of its own accord the door was opened.

Since that was opened by the mind of the Blessed One, therefore it is fitting to say, "*Vivari bhagavā dvāra*."

*Vihāraṃ pavisitvā* means having entered the *gandhakuṭi*.

However, as soon as he had entered there, Kārāyana, having taken the five royal emblems, went to the camp and addressed Viṭaṭūbha, saying, "Raise the umbrella, friend!"

"Where has my father gone?" "Do not ask about [your] father; if you do not raise [it], having seized you, I will raise [it]!"

"I will raise [it], friend!" he assented.

Kārāyana, having left one horse and sword and just one female attendant for the king – [saying,] "If the king is desirous of life, let him not come!" – having had Viṭaṭūbha raise the umbrella, having taken it, he went to Śrāvastī (*sāvatthi*) itself.

*Vivari Bhagavā dvāra Vihāraṃ pavisitvā*

mula_pali: 367. ‘‘Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, mahārāja, atthavasaṃ sampassamāno imasmiṃ sarīre evarūpaṃ paramanipaccakāraṃ karosi, mittūpahāraṃ cittūpahāraṃ (sī.) upadaṃsesī’’ti? ‘‘Atthi kho me, bhante, bhagavati dhammanvayo – ‘hoti sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho’ti. Idhāhaṃ, bhante, passāmi eke samaṇabrāhmaṇe pariyantakataṃ brahmacariyaṃ carante dasapi vassāni, vīsampi vassāni, tiṃsampi vassāni, cattārīsampi vassāni. Te aparena samayena sunhātā suvilittā kappitakesamassū pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitā samaṅgībhūtā paricārenti. Idha panāhaṃ, bhante, bhikkhū passāmi yāvajīvaṃ āpāṇakoṭikaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carante. Na kho panāhaṃ, bhante, ito bahiddhā aññaṃ evaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ samanupassāmi. Ayampi kho me, bhante, bhagavati dhammanvayo hoti – ‘sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho’’ti.
mula_english:
“But, great king, what reason do you see for doing such supreme honour to this body and for showing such friendship?”

“Venerable sir, I infer according to *dharma* about the Blessed One: ‘The Blessed One is fully enlightened (*sammāsambuddho bhagavā*), the *dharma* is well proclaimed by the Blessed One (*svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo*), the *Sangha* of the Blessed One’s disciples is practising the good way (*suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho*.’

Now, venerable sir, I see some recluses and *brahmins* leading a limited holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ carante*) for ten years, twenty years, thirty years, or forty years, and then on a later occasion I see them well groomed and well anointed, with trimmed hair and beards, enjoying themselves provided and endowed with the five cords of sensual pleasure (*pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitā samaṅgībhūtā paricārenti*).

But here I see *bhikkhus* leading the perfect and pure holy life (*paripuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carante*) as long as life and breath last. Indeed, I do not see any other holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) elsewhere as perfect and pure as this.

This too, venerable sir, is why I infer according to *dharma* about the Blessed One: ‘The Blessed One is fully enlightened (*sammāsambuddho bhagavā*), the *dharma* is well proclaimed by the Blessed One (*svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo*), the *Sangha* of the Blessed One’s disciples is practising the good way (*suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho*.’"
commentary_pali: 367.Dhammanvayoti paccakkhañāṇasaṅkhātassa dhammassa anunayo anumānaṃ, anubuddhīti attho. Idāni yenassa dhammanvayena ‘‘sammāsambuddho bhagavā’’tiādi hoti, taṃ dassetuṃ idha panāhaṃ, bhantetiādimāha. Tattha āpāṇakoṭikanti pāṇoti jīvitaṃ, taṃ mariyādaṃ anto karitvā, maraṇasamayepi carantiyeva, taṃ na vītikkamantīti vuttaṃ hoti. ‘‘Apāṇakoṭika’’ntipi pāṭho, ājīvitapariyantanti attho. Yathā ekacce jīvitahetu atikkamantā pāṇakoṭikaṃ katvā caranti, na evanti attho. Ayampi kho me, bhanteti buddhasubuddhatāya dhammasvākkhātatāya saṅghasuppaṭipannatāya ca etaṃ evaṃ hoti, evañhi me, bhante, ayaṃ bhagavati dhammanvayo hotīti dīpeti. Eseva nayo sabbattha.
commentary_english:
367. "Dhammanvayo" means: Anunaya and anumāna are terms for the Dhamma that is described as direct knowledge (paccakkhañāṇa), the meaning is anubuddhi.

Now, to show that through which Dhammanvaya, "sammāsambuddho bhagavā," etc., comes to be, he said, "Here now, venerable sir (bhante)."

There, "āpāṇakoṭika" means: life (jīvitaṃ) is breath (pāṇoti), having made that a limit (mariyādaṃ anto karitvā), even while moving at the time of death (maraṇasamayepi carantiyeva), it is said that they do not transgress that (taṃ na vītikkamantīti vuttaṃ hoti).

"Apāṇakoṭika" is also a reading, the meaning is: until the end of life (ājīvitapariyantanti attho).

Just as some, for the sake of life (jīvitahetu), transgressing, make the limit of life (pāṇakoṭikaṃ katvā caranti), it is not so, is the meaning.

"Ayampi kho me, bhante" means: this is so for me through the good awakening of the Buddha (buddhasubuddhatāya), through the Dhamma being well-proclaimed (dhammasvākkhātatāya), and through the Sangha being of good conduct (saṅghasuppaṭipannatāya); in this way, venerable sir (bhante), this Dhammanvaya in the Blessed One (bhagavati dhammanvayo hotīti dīpeti) is revealed.

This is the same principle everywhere (eseva nayo sabbattha).

mula_pali: 368. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhante, rājānopi rājūhi vivadanti, khattiyāpi khattiyehi vivadanti, brāhmaṇāpi brāhmaṇehi vivadanti, gahapatayopi gahapatīhi vivadanti, mātāpi puttena vivadati, puttopi mātarā vivadati, pitāpi puttena vivadati, puttopi pitarā vivadati, bhātāpi bhaginiyā vivadati , bhaginīpi bhātarā vivadati, sahāyopi sahāyena vivadati. Idha panāhaṃ, bhante, bhikkhū passāmi samagge sammodamāne avivadamāne khīrodakībhūte aññamaññaṃ piyacakkhūhi sampassante viharante. Na kho panāhaṃ, bhante, ito bahiddhā aññaṃ evaṃ samaggaṃ parisaṃ samanupassāmi. Ayampi kho me, bhante, bhagavati dhammanvayo hoti – ‘sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho’ti.
mula_english:
Again, venerable sir, kings quarrel with kings (rājānopi rājūhi vivadanti), nobles with nobles (khattiyāpi khattiyehi vivadanti), brahmins (brāhmaṇāpi brāhmaṇehi vivadanti) with brahmins, householders (gahapatayopi gahapatīhi vivadanti) with householders; a mother (mātāpi puttena vivadati) disputes with her offspring, an offspring (puttopi mātarā vivadati) with their mother, a father (pitāpi puttena vivadati) with his offspring, an offspring (puttopi pitarā vivadati) with their father; a brother (bhātāpi bhaginiyā vivadati) with his sister, a sister (bhaginīpi bhātarā vivadati) with her brother, a friend (sahāyopi sahāyena vivadati) with their friend.

Here, however, venerable sir, I see monks (bhikkhū passāmi) living in concord, rejoicing (sammodamāne), without quarreling (avivadamāne), mingled like milk and water (khīrodakībhūte), regarding each other with affectionate eyes (piyacakkhūhi sampassante viharante).

Indeed, venerable sir, I do not see any other assembly (parisaṃ samanupassāmi) elsewhere with such concord.

This too, venerable sir, is why I infer according to Dhamma (dhammanvayo hoti) about the Blessed One (bhagavati): ‘The Blessed One (bhagavā) is fully enlightened (sammāsambuddho), the Dhamma (dhammo) is well proclaimed (svākkhāto) by the Blessed One (bhagavatā), the Sangha (sāvakasaṅgho) of the Blessed One’s (bhagavato) disciples is practising the good way (suppaṭipanno).’

mula_pali: 369. ‘‘Puna caparāhaṃ, bhante, ārāmena ārāmaṃ, uyyānena uyyānaṃ anucaṅkamāmi anuvicarāmi. Sohaṃ tattha passāmi eke samaṇabrāhmaṇe kise lūkhe dubbaṇṇe uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajāte dhamanisanthatagatte, na viya maññe cakkhuṃ bandhante janassa dassanāya. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘addhā ime āyasmanto anabhiratā vā brahmacariyaṃ caranti, atthi vā tesaṃ kiñci pāpaṃ kammaṃ kataṃ paṭicchannaṃ; tathā hi ime āyasmanto kisā lūkhā dubbaṇṇā uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajātā dhamanisanthatagattā, na viya maññe cakkhuṃ bandhanti janassa dassanāyā’ti. Tyāhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadāmi – ‘kiṃ nu kho tumhe āyasmanto kisā lūkhā dubbaṇṇā uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajātā dhamanisanthatagattā, na viya maññe cakkhuṃ bandhatha janassa dassanāyā’ti? Te evamāhaṃsu – ‘bandhukarogo no paṇḍukarogino (ka.), mahārājā’ti. Idha panāhaṃ, bhante, bhikkhū passāmi haṭṭhapahaṭṭhe udaggudagge abhiratarūpe pīṇindriye pīṇitindriye (sī. pī.) appossukke pannalome paradattavutte migabhūtena cetasā viharante. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘addhā ime āyasmanto tassa bhagavato sāsane uḷāraṃ pubbenāparaṃ visesaṃ jānanti; tathā hi ime āyasmanto haṭṭhapahaṭṭhā udaggudaggā abhiratarūpā pīṇindriyā appossukkā pannalomā paradattavuttā migabhūtena cetasā viharantī’ti. Ayampi kho me, bhante, bhagavati dhammanvayo hoti – ‘sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho’ti.
mula_english:
“Again, venerable sir, in the afternoon, I walked and wandered from park to park, and from garden to garden.

There I saw some ascetics and Brahmins who were lean, wretched, unsightly, jaundiced, with veins standing out on their limbs, such that people would not want to look at them again.

Then, venerable sir, it occurred to me: ‘Surely these venerable ones are leading the holy life in discontent, or they have done some evil deed and are concealing it; for these venerable ones are lean, wretched, unsightly, jaundiced, with veins standing out on their limbs, such that people would not want to look at them again.’

Then I approached them and said this: ‘Why, venerable sirs, are you lean, wretched, unsightly, jaundiced, with veins standing out on your limbs, such that people would not want to look at you again?’ They replied thus: ‘It is our family sickness, great king.’

Here, however, venerable sir, I see monks who are joyful and delighted, uplifted, with senses pleased, without anxiety, with plumage shed, nourished by what others give, abiding with mind like a wild deer.

Then, venerable sir, it occurred to me: ‘Surely these venerable ones perceive successive states of lofty distinction in the Blessed One’s Dispensation, since these venerable ones are joyful and delighted, uplifted, with senses pleased, without anxiety, with plumage shed, nourished by what others give, abiding with mind like a wild deer.’

This too, venerable sir, is how I infer according to the *dharma* about the Blessed One: ‘The Blessed One is a *sammāsambuddha* (perfectly enlightened one), the *dharma* is well proclaimed by the Blessed One, the *saṅgha* (community) of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way.’"
commentary_pali: 369.Naviya maññe cakkhuṃ bandhanteti cakkhuṃ abandhante viya. Apāsādikañhi disvā puna olokanakiccaṃ na hoti, tasmā so cakkhuṃ na bandhati nāma. Pāsādikaṃ disvā punappunaṃ olokanakiccaṃ hoti, tasmā so cakkhuṃ bandhati nāma. Ime ca apāsādikā, tasmā evamāha. Bandhukarogo noti kularogo. Amhākaṃ kule jātā evarūpā hontīti vadanti. Uḷāranti mahesakkhaṃ. Pubbenāparanti pubbato aparaṃ visesaṃ. Tattha kasiṇaparikammaṃ katvā samāpattiṃ nibbattento uḷāraṃ pubbe visesaṃ sañjānāti nāma, samāpattiṃ padaṭṭhānaṃ katvā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā arahattaṃ gaṇhanto uḷāraṃ pubbato aparaṃ visesaṃ sañjānāti nāma.
commentary_english:
369. I think it is as if the eye is bound, as if the eye is unbound.

Having seen something unpleasing, there is no further need to look back; therefore, he does not bind the eye, it is said.

Having seen something pleasing, there is a repeated need to look back; therefore, he binds the eye, it is said.

These are unpleasing, therefore he says thus.

"Is it a *bandhuka* disease or not?" [It is] a family disease.

They say, "Those born in our family are of this nature."

"*Uḷāra* means great power."

"*Pubbenāpara*" means a distinction from before.

There, having performed the preliminary work on the *kasiṇa*, bringing forth attainment (*samāpatti*), he discerns a great distinction before, it is said. Having made attainment the basis, developing insight (*vipaśyanā*), taking hold of arhatship (*arahatta*), he discerns a great distinction from before, it is said.

mula_pali: 370. ‘‘Puna caparāhaṃ, bhante, rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto; pahomi ghātetāyaṃ vā ghātetuṃ, jāpetāyaṃ vā jāpetuṃ, pabbājetāyaṃ vā pabbājetuṃ . Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, aḍḍakaraṇe nisinnassa antarantarā kathaṃ opātenti. Sohaṃ na labhāmi – ‘mā me bhonto aḍḍakaraṇe nisinnassa antarantarā kathaṃ opātetha opātentu (sī.) upariselasutte pana ‘‘opātethā’’tiyeva dissati, kathāpariyosānaṃ me bhonto āgamentū’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, antarantarā kathaṃ opātenti. Idha panāhaṃ, bhante, bhikkhū passāmi; yasmiṃ samaye bhagavā anekasatāya parisāya dhammaṃ deseti, neva tasmiṃ samaye bhagavato sāvakānaṃ khipitasaddo vā hoti ukkāsitasaddo vā. Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhante, bhagavā anekasatāya parisāya dhammaṃ deseti. Tatraññataro bhagavato sāvako ukkāsi. Tamenaṃ aññataro sabrahmacārī jaṇṇukena ghaṭṭesi – ‘appasaddo āyasmā hotu, māyasmā saddamakāsi; satthā no bhagavā dhammaṃ desetī’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho! Adaṇḍena vata kira, bho, asatthena evaṃ suvinītā parisā bhavissatī’ti! Na kho panāhaṃ, bhante, ito bahiddhā aññaṃ evaṃ suvinītaṃ parisaṃ samanupassāmi. Ayampi kho me, bhante, bhagavati dhammanvayo hoti – ‘sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho’ti.
mula_english:
370. Furthermore, venerable sir, the king, a noble anointed one, is capable of ordering someone to be killed or killing someone himself, ordering someone to be made to win or making someone win himself, ordering someone to be expelled or expelling someone himself.

Yet when I am sitting in council, venerable sir, they break in and interrupt me.

Though I say: ‘Gentlemen, do not break in and interrupt me when I am sitting in council; wait till the end of my speech,’

still they break in and interrupt me.

But here I see *bhikkhus* while the Blessed One is teaching the Dhamma to an assembly of several hundred followers and then there is not even the sound of a disciple of the Blessed One coughing or clearing his throat.

Once the Blessed One was teaching the Dhamma to an assembly of several hundred followers.

and there a disciple of his cleared his throat.

Thereupon one of his companions in the holy life nudged him with his knee to indicate: “Be quiet, venerable sir, make no noise; the Blessed One, the Teacher, is teaching us the Dhamma.”

I thought: ‘It is wonderful, it is marvellous! Without a stick, without a weapon, how well-disciplined this assembly will be!’ I do not see another assembly as well-disciplined as this outside of this one.

This too, venerable sir, is why I infer according to Dhamma about the Blessed One: ‘The Blessed One is fully enlightened, the *Dhamma* is well proclaimed by the Blessed One, the *Saṃgha* of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way.’
commentary_pali: 370.Ghātetāyaṃ vā ghātetunti ghātetabbayuttakaṃ ghātetuṃ. Jāpetāyaṃ vā jāpetunti dhanena vā jāpetabbayuttakaṃ jāpetuṃ jānituṃ adhanaṃ kātuṃ. Pabbājetāyaṃ vā pabbājetunti raṭṭhato vā pabbājetabbayuttakaṃ pabbājetuṃ.
commentary_english:
370.
"ghātetāyaṃ vā ghātetu" means fit to be killed, to kill.
"jāpetāyaṃ vā jāpetu" means by means of wealth, fit to cause to win, to cause to win, to know, to make without wealth.
"pabbājetāyaṃ vā pabbājetu" means from the country, fit to be banished, to banish.

mula_pali: 371. ‘‘Puna caparāhaṃ, bhante, passāmi idhekacce khattiyapaṇḍite nipuṇe kataparappavāde vālavedhirūpe. Te bhindantā vobhindantā (sī.) maññe caranti paññāgatena diṭṭhigatāni. Te suṇanti – ‘samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo amukaṃ nāma gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā osarissatī’ti. Te pañhaṃ abhisaṅkharonti – ‘imaṃ mayaṃ pañhaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ upasaṅkamitvā pucchissāma. Evaṃ ce no puṭṭho evaṃ byākarissati, evamassa mayaṃ vādaṃ āropessāma; evaṃ cepi no puṭṭho evaṃ byākarissati, evampissa mayaṃ vādaṃ āropessāmā’ti. Te suṇanti – ‘samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo amukaṃ nāma gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā osaṭo’ti. Te yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamanti. Te bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṃseti . Te bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā na ceva bhagavantaṃ pañhaṃ pucchanti, kuto vādaṃ āropessanti? Aññadatthu bhagavato sāvakā sampajjanti. Ayampi kho me, bhante, bhagavati dhammanvayo hoti – ‘sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho’ti.
mula_english:
371. “Again, venerable sir (bhante), I see here certain learned nobles (khattiyapaṇḍite) who were clever (nipuṇe), knowledgeable about the doctrines of others (kataparappavāde), as sharp as hairsplitting marksmen (vālavedhirūpe).

They, as it were (maññe), wander about (caranti) demolishing (bhindantā) the views (diṭṭhigatāni) of others with their sharp wits (paññāgatena).

When they hear (te suṇanti): ‘The recluse (samaṇo) Gotama (gotamo) will visit (osarissati) such and such a village (gāmaṃ vā) or town (nigamaṃ vā),’

they formulate (abhisaṅkharonti) a question (pañhaṃ) thus: ‘We will go (upasaṅkamitvā) to the recluse (samaṇaṃ) Gotama (gotamaṃ) and ask him (pucchissāma) this question (imaṃ pañhaṃ).

If he is asked (puṭṭho) like this (evaṃ), he will answer (byākarissati) like this (evaṃ), and so (evamassa) we will refute (āropessāma) his doctrine (vādaṃ) in this way (mayaṃ); and even if (cepi) he is asked (puṭṭho) like that (evaṃ), he will answer (byākarissati) like that (evaṃ), and so (evampissa) we will refute (āropessāmā’ti) his doctrine (vādaṃ) in that way (mayaṃ).’

They hear (te suṇanti): ‘The recluse (samaṇo) Gotama (gotamo) has come to visit (osaṭo) such and such a village (gāmaṃ vā) or town (nigamaṃ vā).’

They go (tenupasaṅkamanti) to the Blessed One (bhagavā).

The Blessed One (bhagavā) instructs (sandasseti), urges (samādapeti), rouses (samuttejeti), and encourages (sampahaṃseti) them with a talk on the Dhamma (dhammiyā kathāya).

Having been instructed (sandassitā), urged (samādapitā), roused (samuttejitā), and encouraged (sampahaṃsitā) by the Blessed One (bhagavatā) with a talk on the Dhamma (dhammiyā kathāya), they do not (na ceva) so much as ask (pucchanti) the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ) a question (pañhaṃ), so how (kuto) should they refute (āropessanti) his doctrine (vādaṃ)? Instead (aññadatthu), they become (sampajjanti) disciples (sāvakā) of the Blessed One (bhagavato).

Venerable sir (bhante), I infer (dhammanvayo hoti) according to Dhamma (bhagavati): ‘The Blessed One (bhagavā) is fully enlightened (sammāsambuddho), the Dhamma (dhammo) is well proclaimed (svākkhāto) by the Blessed One (bhagavatā), the Sangha (sāvakasaṅgho) of the Blessed One’s (bhagavato) disciples is practising the good way (suppaṭipanno).’

mula_pali: 372. ‘‘Puna caparāhaṃ, bhante, passāmi idhekacce brāhmaṇapaṇḍite…pe… gahapatipaṇḍite…pe… samaṇapaṇḍite nipuṇe kataparappavāde vālavedhirūpe. Te bhindantā maññe caranti paññāgatena diṭṭhigatāni. Te suṇanti – ‘samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo amukaṃ nāma gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā osarissatī’ti. Te pañhaṃ abhisaṅkharonti – ‘imaṃ mayaṃ pañhaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ upasaṅkamitvā pucchissāma. Evaṃ ce no puṭṭho evaṃ byākarissati, evamassa mayaṃ vādaṃ āropessāma; evaṃ cepi no puṭṭho evaṃ byākarissati, evampissa mayaṃ vādaṃ āropessāmā’ti. Te suṇanti – ‘samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo amukaṃ nāma gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā osaṭo’ti. Te yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamanti. Te bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṃseti. Te bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā na ceva bhagavantaṃ pañhaṃ pucchanti, kuto vādaṃ āropessanti? Aññadatthu bhagavantaṃyeva okāsaṃ yācanti agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāya. Te bhagavā pabbājeti. Te tathāpabbajitā samānā ekā vūpakaṭṭhā appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharantā nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti. Te evamāhaṃsu – ‘manaṃ vata, bho, anassāma; manaṃ vata, bho, panassāma’. Mayañhi pubbe assamaṇāva samānā samaṇāmhāti paṭijānimhā, abrāhmaṇāva samānā brāhmaṇāmhāti paṭijānimhā, anarahantova samānā arahantāmhāti paṭijānimhā. ‘Idāni khomha samaṇā, idāni khomha brāhmaṇā, idāni khomha arahanto’ti. Ayampi kho me, bhante, bhagavati dhammanvayo hoti – ‘sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho’ti.
mula_english:
“Furthermore, venerable sir, I see here certain learned *brāhmaṇas*…pe… learned householders…pe… learned ascetics, who are clever, skilled in refuting the doctrines of others, and like hairs split by an arrow.

They wander about, as it were, demolishing the views of others with their sharp wits (*prajñā*).

They hear: ‘The *śramaṇa* Gotama will visit such and such a village or town.’

They formulate a question thus: ‘We will go to the *śramaṇa* Gotama and ask him this question.

If he is asked like this, he will answer like this, and so we will refute his doctrine (*vāda*) in this way; and if he is asked like that, he will answer like that, and so we will refute his doctrine in that way.’

They hear: ‘The *śramaṇa* Gotama has come to visit such and such a village or town.’

They go to the Blessed One (*bhagavā*).

The Blessed One (*bhagavā*) instructs, urges, rouses, and encourages them with a talk on the Dharma (*dhammiyā kathāya*).

After they have been instructed, urged, roused, and encouraged by the Blessed One (*bhagavatā*) with a talk on the Dharma (*dhammiyā kathāya*), they do not so much as ask him the question, so how should they refute his doctrine (*vāda*)? Instead, they only request the opportunity from the Blessed One (*bhagavantaṃyeva*) to go forth from the house life (*agārasmā*) into homelessness (*anagāriyaṃ*) in the *pravrajya*.

The Blessed One (*bhagavā*) gives them the going forth (*pabbājeti*).

Not long after they have thus gone forth (*tathāpabbajitā*), dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute, by realizing for themselves with direct knowledge they here and now enter upon and abide in that supreme goal of the holy life (*brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ*) for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life (*agārasmā*) into homelessness (*anagāriyaṃ*) (*pabbajanti*).

They say thus: ‘We were very nearly lost, we very nearly perished.’

For formerly we claimed that we were *śramanas* though we were not really *śramanas*; we claimed that we were *brāhmaṇas* though we were not really *brāhmaṇas*; we claimed that we were *arhats* though we were not really *arhats*.

But now we are *śramanas*, now we are *brāhmaṇas*, now we are *arhats*.’

This too, venerable sir (*bhante*), is why I infer according to Dharma (*dhammanvayo*) about the Blessed One (*bhagavati*): ‘The Blessed One (*bhagavā*) is a fully enlightened one (*sammāsambuddho*), the Dharma (*dhammo*) is well proclaimed by the Blessed One (*bhagavatā*), the Sangha (*saṅgho*) of the Blessed One’s (*bhagavato*) disciples (*sāvaka*) is practising the good way.’"

mula_pali: 373. ‘‘Puna caparāhaṃ, bhante, ime isidattapurāṇā thapatayo mamabhattā mamayānā, ahaṃ nesaṃ jīvikāya jīvitassa (sī.), jīvikaṃ (sī. aṭṭha.), jīvitaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) dātā, yasassa āhattā; atha ca pana no tathā mayi nipaccakāraṃ karonti yathā bhagavati. Bhūtapubbāhaṃ, bhante, senaṃ abbhuyyāto samāno ime ca isidattapurāṇā thapatayo vīmaṃsamāno aññatarasmiṃ sambādhe āvasathe vāsaṃ upagacchiṃ. Atha kho, bhante, ime isidattapurāṇā thapatayo bahudeva rattiṃ dhammiyā kathāya vītināmetvā, yato ahosi bhagavā assosuṃ kho bhagavantaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) tato sīsaṃ katvā maṃ pādato karitvā nipajjiṃsu. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho! Ime isidattapurāṇā thapatayo mamabhattā mamayānā, ahaṃ nesaṃ jīvikāya dātā, yasassa āhattā; atha ca pana no tathā mayi nipaccakāraṃ karonti yathā bhagavati. Addhā ime āyasmanto tassa bhagavato sāsane uḷāraṃ pubbenāparaṃ visesaṃ jānantī’ti. Ayampi kho me, bhante, bhagavati dhammanvayo hoti – ‘sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho’ti.
mula_english:
Again, venerable sir, Isidatta and Purāṇa, my two inspectors, eat my food and use my carriages; I provide them with a livelihood (*jīvikā*) and bring them fame. Yet in spite of this, they are less respectful towards me than they are towards the Blessed One (*bhagavat*).

Once, venerable sir, when I was on a military campaign, while considering these two inspectors, Isidatta and Purāṇa, I approached lodging in a crowded rest house. Then these two inspectors, Isidatta and Purāṇa, after spending much of the night in talk on the *dharma*, lay down with their heads in the direction where they had heard the Blessed One (*bhagavat*) was staying and with their feet towards me.

Then, venerable sir, it occurred to me: ‘It is wonderful, truly amazing! These two inspectors, Isidatta and Purāṇa, eat my food and use my carriages; I provide them with a livelihood (*jīvikā*) and bring them fame. Yet in spite of this, they are less respectful towards me than they are towards the Blessed One (*bhagavat*). Surely these good people perceive successive states of lofty distinction in the Blessed One’s (*bhagavat*) Dispensation.’

This too, venerable sir, is why I infer according to *dharma* about the Blessed One (*bhagavat*): ‘The Blessed One (*bhagavat*) is fully enlightened (*sammāsambuddha*), the *dharma* is well proclaimed by the Blessed One (*bhagavat*), the *saṅgha* of the Blessed One’s (*bhagavat*) disciples is practising the good way.’
commentary_pali: 373.Isidattapurāṇāti isidatto ca purāṇo ca. Tesu eko brahmacārī, eko sadārasantuṭṭho. Mamabhattāti mama santakaṃ bhattaṃ etesanti mamabhattā. Mamayānāti mama santakaṃ yānaṃ etesanti mamayānā. Jīvikāya dātāti jīvitavuttiṃ dātā. Vīmaṃsamānoti upaparikkhamāno. Tadā kira rājā niddaṃ anokkantova okkanto viya hutvā nipajji. Atha te thapatayo ‘‘katarasmiṃ disābhāge bhagavā’’ti pucchitvā ‘‘asukasmiṃ nāmā’’ti sutvā mantayiṃsu – ‘‘yena sammāsambuddho, tena sīse kate rājā pādato hoti. Yena rājā, tena sīse kate satthā pādato hoti, kiṃ karissāmā’’ti? Tato nesaṃ etadahosi – ‘‘rājā kuppamāno yaṃ amhākaṃ deti, taṃ acchindeyya. Na kho pana mayaṃ sakkoma jānamānā satthāraṃ pādato kātu’’nti rājānaṃ pādato katvā nipajjiṃsu. Taṃ sandhāya ayaṃ rājā evamāha.
commentary_english:
373. *Isidattapurāṇā* means Isidatta and Purāṇa.

Among them, one was a celibate (*brahmacārī*), the other content with his own wife (*sadārasantuṭṭho*).

*Mamabhattā* means my own food (*mama santakaṃ bhattaṃ*). These are *mamabhattā*.

*Mamayānā* means my own vehicle (*mama santakaṃ yānaṃ*). These are *mamayānā*.

*Jīvikāya dātā* means the giver of livelihood (*jīvitavuttiṃ dātā*).

*Vīmaṃsamāno* means examining (*upaparikkhamāno*).

Then, it seems the king, as if sleep had not come upon him, lay down having the appearance of one who was asleep.

Then those stewards, having asked, "In which direction is the Blessed One (*bhagavā*)?" and having heard, "In such and such a place," conferred, "When the Perfectly Awakened One (*sammāsambuddho*) is at the head, the king is at the feet.

When the king is at the head, the teacher (*satthā*) is at the feet, what shall we do?" Then this occurred to them: "The king, being angry, might take back what he gives to us.

Surely, we are not able, knowingly, to place the teacher (*satthāraṃ*) at the feet," and they lay down having placed the king at the head.

With reference to that, this king said thus.

mula_pali:
374. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhante, bhagavāpi khattiyo, ahampi khattiyo; bhagavāpi kosalo, ahampi kosalo; bhagavāpi āsītiko, ahampi āsītiko. Yampi, bhante, bhagavāpi khattiyo ahampi khattiyo, bhagavāpi kosalo ahampi kosalo, bhagavāpi āsītiko ahampi āsītiko; imināvārahāmevāhaṃ imināpāhaṃ (ka.), bhante, bhagavati paramanipaccakāraṃ kātuṃ, mittūpahāraṃ upadaṃsetuṃ. Handa, ca dāni mayaṃ, bhante, gacchāma; bahukiccā mayaṃ bahukaraṇīyā’’ti. ‘‘Yassadāni tvaṃ, mahārāja, kālaṃ maññasī’’ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkantassa rañño pasenadissa kosalassa bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘eso, bhikkhave, rājā pasenadi kosalo dhammacetiyāni bhāsitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkanto. Uggaṇhatha, bhikkhave, dhammacetiyāni; pariyāpuṇātha, bhikkhave , dhammacetiyāni; dhāretha, bhikkhave, dhammacetiyāni. Atthasaṃhitāni, bhikkhave, dhammacetiyāni ādibrahmacariyakānī’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Dhammacetiyasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.
mula_english:
“Furthermore, venerable sir, the Blessed One is also a noble (*kṣatriya*), and I am also a noble; the Blessed One is also a Kosalan, and I am also a Kosalan; the Blessed One is eighty years old, and I am eighty years old.

Since that is so, venerable sir, I think it is proper to do such supreme honor (*paramanipaccakāra*) to the Blessed One and to show such friendship (*mittūpahāra*).

And now, venerable sir, we depart. We are busy and have much to do.”

“Do whatever seems fit, great king (*mahārāja*).”

Then King Pasenadi Kosala got up from his seat, bowed down to the Blessed One, and keeping him to his right, departed.

Then, soon after King Pasenadi of Kosala had left, the Blessed One addressed the *bhikkhus* thus: “*Bhikkhus*, this King Pasenadi of Kosala, having spoken of the monuments to the Dharma (*dharmacetiyāni*), rose from his seat and departed.

Learn the monuments to the Dharma (*dharmacetiyāni*), *bhikkhus*; master the monuments to the Dharma (*dharmacetiyāni*); remember the monuments to the Dharma (*dharmacetiyāni*).

The monuments to the Dharma (*dharmacetiyāni*) are beneficial (*atthasaṃhitāni*), *bhikkhus*, and they belong to the fundamentals of the holy life (*ādibrahmacariyakāni*).”

The Blessed One spoke thus.

Elated, those *bhikkhus* delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The *Dhammacetiyasutta* is finished, the ninth.
commentary_pali:
374.Pakkāmīti gandhakuṭito nikkhamitvā kārāyanassa ṭhitaṭṭhānaṃ gato, taṃ tattha adisvā khandhāvāraṭṭhānaṃ gato, tatthāpi aññaṃ adisvā taṃ itthiṃ pucchi. Sā sabbaṃ pavattiṃ ācikkhi. Rājā – ‘‘na idāni mayā ekakena tattha gantabbaṃ, rājagahaṃ gantvā bhāgineyyena saddhiṃ āgantvā mayhaṃ rajjaṃ gaṇhissāmī’’ti rājagahaṃ gacchanto antarāmagge kaṇājakabhattañceva bhuñji, bahalaudakañca pivi. Tassa sukhumālapakatikassa āhāro na sammā pariṇāmi. So rājagahaṃ pāpuṇantopi vikāle dvāresu pihitesu pāpuṇi. ‘‘Ajja sālāyaṃ sayitvā sve mayhaṃ bhāgineyyaṃ passissāmī’’ti bahinagare sālāya nipajji. Tassa rattibhāge uṭṭhānāni pavattiṃsu, katipayavāre bahi nikkhami. Tato paṭṭhāya padasā gantuṃ asakkonto tassā itthiyā aṅke nipajjitvā balavapaccūse kālamakāsi. Sā tassa matabhāvaṃ ñatvā – ‘‘dvīsu rajjesu rajjaṃ kāretvā idāni parassa bahinagare anāthasālāya anāthakālakiriyaṃ katvā nipanno mayhaṃ sāmi kosalarājā’’tiādīni vadamānā uccāsaddena paridevituṃ ārabhi. Manussā sutvā rañño ārocesuṃ. Rājā āgantvā disvā sañjānitvā āgatakāraṇaṃ ñatvā mahāparihārena sarīrakiccaṃ karitvā ‘‘viṭaṭūbhaṃ gaṇhissāmī’’ti bheriṃ carāpetvā balakāyaṃ sannipātesi. Amaccā pādesu patitvā – ‘‘sace, deva, tumhākaṃ mātulo arogo assa, tumhākaṃ gantuṃ yuttaṃ bhaveyya, idāni pana viṭaṭūbhopi tumhe nissāya chattaṃ ussāpetuṃ arahatiyevā’’ti saññāpetvā nivāresuṃ.

Dhammacetiyānīti dhammassa cittīkāravacanāni. Tīsu hi ratanesu yattha katthaci cittīkāre kate sabbattha katoyeva hoti, tasmā bhagavati cittīkāre kate dhammopi katova hotīti bhagavā ‘‘dhammacetiyānī’’ti āha. Ādibrahmacariyakānīti maggabrahmacariyassa ādibhūtāni, pubbabhāgapaṭipattibhūtānīti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Dhammacetiyānī Ādibrahmacariyakānī

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Dhammacetiyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
374. "Having departed ( *pakkāmī*)," [means that] having left the Perfumed Chamber, he went to Kārāyana's dwelling place. Not seeing him there, he went to the encampment; even there, not seeing another person, he asked that woman.
She told him everything, the whole story (*pavattiṃ ācikkhi*).
The king [thought]: "Now I must not go there alone. Having gone to Rājagaha, having come back together with my nephew, I will take my kingdom (*rajjaṃ gaṇhissāmī*)." As he was going to Rājagaha, on the road, he ate some *kaṇājaka* food and also drank a lot of water.
The food did not digest well in him, accustomed as he was to delicate nourishment.
Though he reached Rājagaha, he arrived at an improper time, when the gates were shut.
"Today, having slept in the hall, tomorrow I will see my nephew (*bhāgineyyaṃ passissāmī*)," he thought and lay down in the hall outside the city.
In the night, he had to get up many times; a few times he went outside.
From then on, unable to go on foot, having lain down in that woman's lap, at the break of dawn, he died (*kālamakāsi*).
She, having realized that he was dead, lamenting, said: "Having had kingship done in two kingdoms, now in another's hall outside the city, having done a death without protection, lies my lord, the Kosala king (*kosalarājā*)," and so forth, and began to lament loudly (*uccāsaddena paridevituṃ ārabhi*).
The people heard and announced it to the king (*rañño ārocesuṃ*).
The king, having come, having seen, having recognized, having understood the reason for his coming, having performed the last rites with great ceremony, proclaimed (*bheriṃ carāpetvā*): "I will seize Viṭaṭūbha (*viṭaṭūbhaṃ gaṇhissāmī*)," and assembled his army.
The ministers, having fallen at his feet, said: "If, your majesty, your maternal uncle were healthy, it would be fitting for you to go. But now, Viṭaṭūbha too, relying on you, is able to raise the umbrella," and having made him understand, they prevented him.

"*Dhammacetiyānī* " means words honoring the Dhamma.
Since, when honor is done to any one of the three jewels, honor is done to all, therefore, when honor is done to the Blessed One, honor is also done to the Dhamma, so the Blessed One said "*dhammacetiyānī*."
"*Ādibrahmacariyakānī*" means the first elements of the path of holy life, the preliminary practices.
The rest is clear throughout.

*Dhammacetiyānī*, *ādibrahmacariyakānī*.
The Dhammacetiyasutta's explanation in the Papañcasūdanī, commentary to the Majjhimanikāya, is finished.

mula_pali: 375. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā uruññāyaṃ ujuññāyaṃ (sī. pī.), udaññāyaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) viharati kaṇṇakatthale migadāye. Tena kho pana samayena rājā pasenadi kosalo uruññaṃ anuppatto hoti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ehi tvaṃ, ambho purisa, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandāhi, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ puccha – ‘rājā, bhante, pasenadi kosalo bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchatī’ti. Evañca vadehi – ‘ajja kira, bhante, rājā pasenadi kosalo pacchābhattaṃ bhuttapātarāso bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissatī’’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, devā’’ti kho so puriso rañño pasenadissa kosalassa paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so puriso bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘rājā, bhante, pasenadi kosalo bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchati; evañca vadeti – ‘ajja kira bhante, rājā pasenadi kosalo pacchābhattaṃ bhuttapātarāso bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissatī’’’ti. Assosuṃ kho somā ca bhaginī sakulā ca bhaginī – ‘‘ajja kira rājā pasenadi kosalo pacchābhattaṃ bhuttapātarāso bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissatī’’ti. Atha kho somā ca bhaginī sakulā ca bhaginī rājānaṃ pasenadiṃ kosalaṃ bhattābhihāre upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – ‘‘tena hi, mahārāja, amhākampi vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandāhi, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ puccha – ‘somā ca, bhante, bhaginī sakulā ca bhaginī bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchatī’’’ti.
mula_english:
375. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Ujunna (Uruññā), in the Kannakatthala Deer Park.

Now on that occasion King Pasenadi of Kosala had arrived at Ujunna for some business or other.

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala addressed a certain man: “Come, good man, go to the Blessed One and pay homage in my name with your head at his feet, and ask whether he is free from illness and affliction, and is healthy, strong, and abiding in comfort, saying: ‘Venerable sir, King Pasenadi of Kosala pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet, and he asks whether the Blessed One is free from illness…and abiding in comfort.’

And say this: ‘Venerable sir, today King Pasenadi of Kosala will come to see the Blessed One after he has had his breakfast.’”

“Yes, sire,” the man replied, and he went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side.

Sitting at one side, the man said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, King Pasenadi of Kosala pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet, and he asks whether he is free from illness and affliction, and is healthy, strong, and abiding in comfort; and he says this: ‘Venerable sir, today King Pasenadi of Kosala will come to see the Blessed One after he has had his breakfast.’”

The sisters Soma and Sakula heard: “Today King Pasenadi of Kosala will go to see the Blessed One after he has had his breakfast.”

Then the sisters Soma and Sakula went to King Pasenadi of Kosala while the meal was being served, and said to him: “Sire, pay homage in our name with your head at the Blessed One’s feet, and ask whether he is free from illness and affliction, and is healthy, strong, and abiding in comfort, saying: ‘Venerable sir, the sisters Soma and Sakula pay homage with their heads at the Blessed One’s feet, and they ask whether he is free from illness…and abiding in comfort.’”
commentary_pali: 375.Evaṃme sutanti kaṇṇakatthalasuttaṃ. Tattha uruññāyanti uruññāti tassa raṭṭhassapi nagarassapi etadeva nāmaṃ, bhagavā uruññānagaraṃ upanissāya viharati. Kaṇṇakatthale migadāyeti tassa nagarassa avidūre kaṇṇakatthalaṃ nāma eko ramaṇīyo bhūmibhāgo atthi, so migānaṃ abhayatthāya dinnattā migadāyoti vuccati, tasmiṃ kaṇṇakatthale migadāye. Kenacideva karaṇīyenāti na aññena, anantarasutte vuttakaraṇīyeneva. Somā ca bhaginī sakulā ca bhaginīti imā dve bhaginiyo rañño pajāpatiyo. Bhattābhihāreti bhattaṃ abhiharaṇaṭṭhāne. Rañño bhuñjanaṭṭhānañhi sabbāpi orodhā kaṭacchuādīni gahetvā rājānaṃ upaṭṭhātuṃ gacchanti, tāpi tatheva agamaṃsu.
commentary_english:
375. Thus, "Thus I have heard" is the Kaṇṇakatthala Sutta.

Therein, "to Uruññā" means Uruññā is the name of both that district and city. The Blessed One dwelt near the city of Uruññā.

"At Kaṇṇakatthala in the Deer Park" means not far from that city, there is a delightful region called Kaṇṇakatthala, which is called Deer Park ( *migadāya* ) because it was given for the safety of the deer. [He dwelt] at that Kaṇṇakatthala in the Deer Park.

"By some duty" means not by another, but just by the duty stated in the immediately preceding sutta.

"Somā was a sister, and Sakulā was a sister" means these two sisters were the king's consorts (*pajāpatiyo*).

"*Bhattābhihāre*" means at the place of bringing food (*bhattaṃ abhiharaṇaṭṭhāne*).

Indeed, when the king is eating (*rañño bhuñjanaṭṭhānañhi*), all the harem women, taking spoons etc. (*kaṭacchuādīni gahetvā*), go to wait upon the king; they too went in that way (*tāpi tatheva agamaṃsu*).

mula_pali: 376. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo pacchābhattaṃ bhuttapātarāso yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘somā ca, bhante, bhaginī sakulā ca bhaginī bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati vandanti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchatī’’ti pucchantīti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). ‘‘Kiṃ pana, mahārāja, somā ca bhaginī sakulā ca bhaginī aññaṃ dūtaṃ nālatthu’’nti? ‘‘Assosuṃ kho, bhante, somā ca bhaginī sakulā ca bhaginī – ‘ajja kira rājā pasenadi kosalo pacchābhattaṃ bhuttapātarāso bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissatī’ti. Atha kho, bhante, somā ca bhaginī sakulā ca bhaginī maṃ bhattābhihāre upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – ‘tena hi, mahārāja, amhākampi vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandāhi, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ puccha – somā ca bhaginī sakulā ca bhaginī bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchatī’’’ti. ‘‘Sukhiniyo hontu tā, mahārāja, somā ca bhaginī sakulā ca bhaginī’’ti.
mula_english:
Then, King Pasenadi of Kosala, after having finished his meal, approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side.

Seated to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said this to the Blessed One: "The sisters Somā and Sakulā, venerable sir, pay homage with their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, and ask whether you are free from affliction, free from sickness, in good health, strong, and living comfortably."

"Great king, could not the sisters Somā and Sakulā have found another messenger?"

"Venerable sir, the sisters Somā and Sakulā heard: 'Today King Pasenadi of Kosala, after having finished his meal, will approach the Blessed One to see him.'

Then, venerable sir, the sisters Somā and Sakulā came to me while the meal was being served, and said this: 'Therefore, great king, in our name pay homage with your head at the feet of the Blessed One, and ask whether he is free from affliction, free from sickness, in good health, strong, and living comfortably—the sisters Somā and Sakulā pay homage with their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, and ask whether he is free from affliction, free from sickness, in good health, strong, and living comfortably.'"

"May they be happy, great king, the sisters Somā and Sakulā."
commentary_pali: 376.Kiṃ pana, mahārājāti kasmā evamāha? Rañño garahaparimocanatthaṃ. Evañhi parisā cinteyya – ‘‘ayaṃ rājā āgacchamānova mātugāmānaṃ sāsanaṃ āroceti, mayaṃ attano dhammatāya bhagavantaṃ daṭṭhuṃ āgatoti maññāma, ayaṃ pana mātugāmānaṃ sāsanaṃ gahetvā āgato, mātugāmadāso maññe, esa pubbepi imināva kāraṇena āgacchatī’’ti. Pucchito pana so attano āgamanakāraṇaṃ kathessati, evamassa ayaṃ garahā na uppajjissatīti garahamocanatthaṃ evamāha.
commentary_english:
“Why does he say, ‘What now, great king?’ (kiṃ pana, mahārājā)” It is to absolve the king of reproach.

For in this way, the assembly would think: “This king, as he comes, announces the message of women. We think that we have come to see the Blessed One by our own righteousness, but this one has come having taken the message of women. He seems to be a slave to women. He comes even formerly for this same reason.”

But if he is asked, he will tell the reason for his coming. In this way, this reproach will not arise for him. He says it to remove the reproach.

mula_pali: 377. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante, samaṇo gotamo evamāha – ‘natthi so samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yo sabbaññū sabbadassāvī aparisesaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paṭijānissati, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti. Ye te, bhante, evamāhaṃsu – ‘samaṇo gotamo evamāha – natthi so samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yo sabbaññū sabbadassāvī aparisesaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paṭijānissati, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti; kacci te, bhante, bhagavato vuttavādino, na ca bhagavantaṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhanti, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākaronti, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchatī’’ti? ‘‘Ye te, mahārāja, evamāhaṃsu – ‘samaṇo gotamo evamāha – natthi so samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yo sabbaññū sabbadassāvī aparisesaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paṭijānissati, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti; na me te vuttavādino, abbhācikkhanti ca pana maṃ te asatā abhūtenā’’ti.
mula_english:
Then King Pasenadi of Kosala said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, I have heard that the *śramaṇa* Gotama says thus: 'There is no *śramaṇa* or *brāhmaṇa* who is all-knowing (*sarvajñū*) and all-seeing (*sarvadarśāvī*), who claims to have complete knowledge and vision (*apariśeṣaṃ jñānadarśanaṃ*); that is not possible.'

Venerable sir, do those who say this say what was said by the Blessed One—'The *śramaṇa* Gotama says, there is no *śramaṇa* or *brāhmaṇa* who is all-knowing (*sarvajñū*) and all-seeing (*sarvadarśāvī*), who claims to have complete knowledge and vision (*apariśeṣaṃ jñānadarśanaṃ*); that is not possible'—and not misrepresent the Blessed One with what is untrue? Do they explain the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma*, so that no co-religious argument leads to a justifiable cause for reproach?"

"Great King, those who say, 'The *śramaṇa* Gotama says, there is no *śramaṇa* or *brāhmaṇa* who is all-knowing (*sarvajñū*) and all-seeing (*sarvadarśāvī*), who claims to have complete knowledge and vision (*apariśeṣaṃ jñānadarśanaṃ*); that is not possible,' do not say what I have said. They misrepresent me with what is false and untrue."

mula_pali: 378. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo viṭaṭūbhaṃ senāpatiṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ko nu kho, senāpati, imaṃ kathāvatthuṃ rājantepure abbhudāhāsī’’ti? ‘‘Sañjayo, mahārāja, brāhmaṇo ākāsagotto’’ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ehi tvaṃ , ambho purisa, mama vacanena sañjayaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ ākāsagottaṃ āmantehi – ‘rājā taṃ, bhante, pasenadi kosalo āmantetī’’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, devā’’ti kho so puriso rañño pasenadissa kosalassa paṭissutvā yena sañjayo brāhmaṇo ākāsagotto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā sañjayaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ ākāsagottaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘rājā taṃ, bhante, pasenadi kosalo āmantetī’’ti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘siyā nu kho, bhante, bhagavatā aññadeva kiñci sandhāya bhāsitaṃ, tañca jano aññathāpi paccāgaccheyya paccāgaccheyyāti, abhijānāmi mahārāja vācaṃ bhāsitāti (sī.). Yathā kathaṃ pana, bhante, bhagavā abhijānāti vācaṃ bhāsitā’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ kho ahaṃ, mahārāja, abhijānāmi vācaṃ bhāsitā – ‘natthi so samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yo sakideva sabbaṃ ñassati, sabbaṃ dakkhiti, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’’’ti. ‘‘Heturūpaṃ, bhante, bhagavā āha; saheturūpaṃ, bhante, bhagavā āha – ‘natthi so samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yo sakideva sabbaṃ ñassati, sabbaṃ dakkhiti, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’’’ti. ‘‘Cattārome, bhante, vaṇṇā – khattiyā, brāhmaṇā, vessā, suddā. Imesaṃ nu kho, bhante, catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ siyā viseso siyā nānākaraṇa’’nti? ‘‘Cattārome, mahārāja, vaṇṇā – khattiyā, brāhmaṇā, vessā, suddā. Imesaṃ kho, mahārāja, catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ dve vaṇṇā aggamakkhāyanti – khattiyā ca brāhmaṇā ca – yadidaṃ abhivādanapaccuṭṭhānaañjalikammasāmīcikammānī’’ti sāmicikammānanti (sī.). ‘‘Nāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ diṭṭhadhammikaṃ pucchāmi; samparāyikāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ pucchāmi. Cattārome, bhante, vaṇṇā – khattiyā, brāhmaṇā, vessā, suddā. Imesaṃ nu kho, bhante, catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ siyā viseso siyā nānākaraṇa’’nti?
mula_english:
Then King Pasenadi of Kosala addressed General Viṭaṭūbha: “General, who introduced this story into the palace?” “Sañjaya, great king, the *brāhmaṇa* of the Ākāsa clan.”

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala told a man: “Come, good man, in my name tell Sañjaya, the *brāhmaṇa* of the Ākāsa clan: ‘Venerable sir, King Pasenadi of Kosala calls you.’”

“Yes, sire,” the man replied. He went to Sañjaya, the *brāhmaṇa* of the Ākāsa clan, and told him: “Venerable sir, King Pasenadi of Kosala calls you.”

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, could something else have been said by the Blessed One referring to that, and the person understood it wrongly?”

“How, venerable sir, does the Blessed One recall having made the utterance?” “I recall having actually made the utterance in this way, great king: ‘There is no *śramaṇa* or *brāhmaṇa* who knows all, who sees all, simultaneously; that is not possible.’”

“What the Blessed One has said appears reasonable, what the Blessed One has said appears to be supported by reason: ‘There is no *śramaṇa* or *brāhmaṇa* who knows all, who sees all, simultaneously; that is not possible.’”

“There are these four castes, venerable sir: the nobles (*kṣatriya*), the *brāhmaṇas*, the merchants (*vaiśya*), and the workers (*śūdra*). Is there any distinction or difference among them?” “There are these four castes, great king: the nobles (*kṣatriya*), the *brāhmaṇas*, the merchants (*vaiśya*), and the workers (*śūdra*). Of these four castes, great king, two castes are called foremost: the nobles (*kṣatriya*) and the *brāhmaṇas*—namely, these acts of greeting, rising, reverential salutation with joined palms (*añjalikamma*), and proper behavior.”

“Venerable sir, I was not asking about this present life; I was asking about the life to come. There are these four castes, venerable sir: the nobles (*kṣatriya*), the *brāhmaṇas*, the merchants (*vaiśya*), and the workers (*śūdra*). Is there any distinction or difference among them?”
commentary_pali: 378.Abbhudāhāsīti kathesi. Sakidevasabbaṃ ussati sabbaṃ dakkhitīti yo ekāvajjanena ekacittena atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ sabbaṃ ussati vā dakkhiti vā, so natthīti attho. Ekena hi cittena atītaṃ sabbaṃ jānissāmīti āvajjitvāpi atītaṃ sabbaṃ jānituṃ na sakkā, ekadesameva jānāti. Anāgatapaccuppannaṃ pana tena cittena sabbeneva sabbaṃ na jānātīti. Esa nayo itaresu. Evaṃ ekacittavasenāyaṃ pañho kathito. Heturūpanti hetusabhāvaṃ kāraṇajātikaṃ. Saheturūpanti sakāraṇajātikaṃ. Samparāyikāhaṃ, bhanteti samparāyaguṇaṃ ahaṃ, bhante, pucchāmi.
commentary_english:
378.
"Abbhudāhāsī" means he related (kathesi).
"Sakideva sabbaṃ ussati sabbaṃ dakkhitī" means the meaning (attho) is that there is no one (natthi) who, with a single attention (ekāvajjanena), with a single thought (ekacittena), can exert (ussati) or see (dakkhiti) everything (sabbaṃ) – past (atīta), future (anāgata), and present (paccuppanna) (sabbaṃ ussati vā dakkhiti vā).
Indeed (hi), with a single thought (ekena cittena), even having turned the mind (āvajjitvāpi) thinking, "I will know (jānissāmi) all the past (atītaṃ sabbaṃ)," it is not possible (na sakkā) to know (jānituṃ) all the past (atītaṃ sabbaṃ); one knows (jānāti) only a part (ekadesameva).
Moreover (pana), with that thought (tena cittena), one does not know (na jānāti) everything (sabbaṃ) entirely (sabbeneva) concerning the future and present (anāgatapaccuppannaṃ).
This (esa) is the method (nayo) for the rest (itaresu).
Thus (evaṃ) this question (pañho) has been discussed (kathito) based on a single thought (ekacittavasenāyaṃ).
"Heturūpa" means having the nature of a cause (hetusabhāvaṃ), being of the nature of a cause (kāraṇajātikaṃ).
"Saheturūpa" means being with a cause (sakāraṇajātikaṃ).
"Samparāyikāhaṃ, bhante" means, "Venerable Sir (bhante), I (ahaṃ) ask (pucchāmi) about the quality (guṇaṃ) related to the future (samparāya)."

mula_pali: 379. ‘‘Pañcimāni, mahārāja, padhāniyaṅgāni. Katamāni pañca? Idha, mahārāja, bhikkhu saddho hoti, saddahati tathāgatassa bodhiṃ – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti; appābādho hoti appātaṅko samavepākiniyā gahaṇiyā samannāgato nātisītāya nāccuṇhāya majjhimāya padhānakkhamāya; asaṭho hoti amāyāvī yathābhūtaṃ attānaṃ āvikattā satthari vā viññūsu vā sabrahmacārīsu; āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu; paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammādukkhakkhayagāminiyā – imāni kho, mahārāja, pañca padhāniyaṅgāni. Cattārome, mahārāja, vaṇṇā – khattiyā, brāhmaṇā, vessā, suddā. Te cassu imehi pañcahi padhāniyaṅgehi samannāgatā ; ettha pana nesaṃ assa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā’’ti. ‘‘Cattārome, bhante, vaṇṇā – khattiyā, brāhmaṇā, vessā, suddā . Te cassu imehi pañcahi padhāniyaṅgehi samannāgatā; ettha pana nesaṃ, bhante, siyā viseso siyā nānākaraṇa’’nti? ‘‘Ettha kho nesāhaṃ, mahārāja, padhānavemattataṃ vadāmi. Seyyathāpissu, mahārāja, dve hatthidammā vā assadammā vā godammā vā sudantā suvinītā, dve hatthidammā vā assadammā vā godammā vā adantā avinītā. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, ye te dve hatthidammā vā assadammā vā godammā vā sudantā suvinītā, api nu te dantāva dantakāraṇaṃ gaccheyyuṃ, dantāva dantabhūmiṃ sampāpuṇeyyu’’nti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Ye pana te dve hatthidammā vā assadammā vā godammā vā adantā avinītā, api nu te adantāva dantakāraṇaṃ gaccheyyuṃ, adantāva dantabhūmiṃ sampāpuṇeyyuṃ, seyyathāpi te dve hatthidammā vā assadammā vā godammā vā sudantā suvinītā’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Evameva kho, mahārāja, yaṃ taṃ saddhena pattabbaṃ appābādhena asaṭhena amāyāvinā āraddhavīriyena paññavatā taṃ vata taṃ tathā so (ka.) assaddho bahvābādho saṭho māyāvī kusīto duppañño pāpuṇissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’’ti.
mula_english:
379. “Great king, there are these five factors of striving.

What are the five? Here, great king, a *bhikkhu* has faith *śraddhā*, he places his faith in the *Tathāgata’s* enlightenment *bodhi* thus: ‘The Blessed One *bhagavā* is accomplished *arahaṃ*, fully enlightened *sammāsambuddho*, perfect in true knowledge *vidyā* and conduct *caraṇa*, sublime *sugato*, knower of worlds *lokavidū*, incomparable leader *anuttaro* of persons to be tamed *purisadammasārathi*, teacher *satthā* of gods *deva* and humans *manussānaṃ*, enlightened *buddho*, blessed *bhagavā*.’ Then he is free from illness *appābādho* and affliction, possessing a good digestion *samavepākiniyā gahaṇiyā samannāgato* that is neither too cool *nātisītāya* nor too warm *nāccuṇhāya* but medium *majjhimāya* and able to bear the strain of striving *padhānakkhamāya*. Then he is honest *asaṭho* and sincere *amāyāvī*, and reveals his true self *yathābhūtaṃ attānaṃ āvikattā* to the Teacher *satthari* or to his wise *viññūsu* fellow *sabrahmacārīsu*; he dwells with energy aroused *āraddhavīriyo viharati* for abandoning *pahānāya* unwholesome *akusalānaṃ* things *dhammānaṃ*, for attaining *upasampadāya* wholesome *kusalānaṃ* things *dhammānaṃ*, powerful *thāmavā*, firm in his effort *daḷhaparakkamo*, not giving up the burden *anikkhittadhuro* in wholesome *kusalesu* things *dhammesu*; he is wise *paññavā*, possessing wisdom *paññāya* that leads to the cessation of existence *udayatthagāminiyā*, endowed with noble *ariyāya* penetrative *nibbedhikāya* wisdom that leads to the complete destruction of suffering *sammādukkakkhayagāminiyā*. These, great king, are the five factors of striving *pañca padhāniyaṅgāni*.

There are these four castes *vaṇṇā*, great king: the nobles *khattiyā*, the Brahmins *brāhmaṇā*, the merchants *vessā*, and the workers *suddā*.

They are endowed with these five factors of striving; here there might be a difference or a distinction among them.

"Here, great king, I speak of the inequality of striving.

Suppose, great king, there were two tamable elephants *hatthidammā*, or tamable horses *assadammā*, or tamable oxen *godammā* that were well tamed *sudantā* and well disciplined *suvinītā*, and two tamable elephants *hatthidammā* or tamable horses *assadammā* or tamable oxen *godammā* that were untamed *adantā* and undisciplined *avinītā*.

What do you think, great king? Would the two tamable elephants *hatthidammā* or tamable horses *assadammā* or tamable oxen *godammā* that were well tamed *sudantā* and well disciplined *suvinītā*, being tamed, acquire the behavior of the tamed, would they arrive at the grade of the tamed?" "Yes, venerable sir."

"But would the two tamable elephants *hatthidammā* or tamable horses *assadammā* or tamable oxen *godammā* that were untamed *adantā* and undisciplined *avinītā*, being untamed, acquire the behavior of the tamed, would they arrive at the grade of the tamed, like the two tamable elephants *hatthidammā* or tamable horses *assadammā* or tamable oxen *godammā* that were well tamed *sudantā* and well disciplined *suvinītā*?" "No, venerable sir."

"So too, great king, it is not possible that what can be achieved by one who has faith *saddhā*, who is free from illness *appābādhena*, who is honest *asaṭhena* and sincere *amāyāvinā*, who is energetic *āraddhavīriyena*, and who is wise *paññavatā*, can be achieved by one who has no faith *assaddho*, who has much illness *bahvābādho*, who is fraudulent *saṭho* and deceitful *māyāvī*, who is lazy *kusīto*, and who is not wise *duppañño*."
commentary_pali:
379.Pañcimānīti imasmiṃ sutte pañca padhāniyaṅgāni lokuttaramissakāni kathitāni. Kathinaṅgaṇavāsīcūḷasamuddatthero pana ‘‘tumhākaṃ, bhante, kiṃ ruccatī’’ti vutte ‘‘mayhaṃ lokuttarānevāti ruccatī’’ti āha. Padhānavemattatanti padhānanānattaṃ. Aññādisameva hi puthujjanassa padhānaṃ, aññādisaṃ sotāpannassa, aññādisaṃ sakadāgāmino, aññādisaṃ anāgāmino, aññādisaṃ arahato, aññādisaṃ asītimahāsāvakānaṃ, aññādisaṃ dvinnaṃ aggasāvakānaṃ, aññādisaṃ paccekabuddhānaṃ, aññādisaṃ sabbaññubuddhānaṃ. Puthujjanassa padhānaṃ sotāpannassa padhānaṃ na pāpuṇāti…pe… paccekabuddhassa padhānaṃ sabbaññubuddhassa padhānaṃ na pāpuṇāti. Imamatthaṃ sandhāya ‘‘padhānavemattataṃ vadāmī’’ti āha. Dantakāraṇaṃ gaccheyyunti yaṃ akūṭakaraṇaṃ, anavacchindanaṃ , dhurassa acchindananti dantesu kāraṇaṃ dissati, taṃ kāraṇaṃ upagaccheyyunti attho. Dantabhūminti dantehi gantabbabhūmiṃ. Assaddhotiādīsu puthujjanasotāpannasakadāgāmianāgāmino cattāropi assaddhā nāma. Puthujjano hi sotāpannassa saddhaṃ appattoti assaddho, sotāpanno sakadāgāmissa, sakadāgāmī anāgāmissa, anāgāmī arahato saddhaṃ appattoti assaddho, ābādho arahatopi uppajjatīti pañcapi bahvābādhā nāma honti. Ariyasāvakassa pana saṭho māyāvīti nāmaṃ natthi. Teneva thero – ‘‘pañca padhāniyaṅgāni lokuttarāni kathitānīti mayhaṃ ruccatī’’ti āha. Assakhaḷuṅkasuttante pana – ‘‘tayo ca, bhikkhave, assakhaḷuṅke tayo ca purisakhaḷuṅke desessāmī’’ti (a. ni. 3.141) ettha ariyasāvakassāpi sambodhināmaṃ āgataṃ , tassa vasena lokuttaramissakā kathitāti vuttaṃ. Puthujjano pana sotāpattimaggavīriyaṃ asampatto…pe… anāgāmī arahattamaggavīriyaṃ asampattoti kusītopi assaddho viya cattārova honti, tathā duppañño.

Evaṃ panettha opammasaṃsandanaṃ veditabbaṃ – adantahatthiādayo viya hi maggapadhānarahito puggalo. Dantahatthiādayo viya maggapadhānavā. Yathā adantā hatthiādayo kūṭākāraṃ akatvā avicchinditvā dhuraṃ apātetvā dantagamanaṃ vā gantuṃ dantabhūmiṃ vā pattuṃ na sakkonti, evamevaṃ maggapadhānarahito maggapadhānavatā pattabbaṃ pāpuṇituṃ nibbattetabbaṃ guṇaṃ nibbattetuṃ na sakkoti. Yathā pana dantahatthiādayo kūṭākāraṃ akatvā avicchinditvā dhuraṃ apātetvā dantagamanaṃ vā gantuṃ dantabhūmiṃ vā pattuṃ sakkonti , evamevaṃ maggapadhānavā maggapadhānavatā pattabbaṃ pāpuṇituṃ nibbattetabbaṃ guṇaṃ nibbattetuṃ sakkoti. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – ‘‘sotāpattimaggapadhānavā sotāpattimaggapadhānavatā pattokāsaṃ pāpuṇituṃ nibbattetabbaṃ guṇaṃ nibbattetuṃ sakkoti…pe… arahattamaggapadhānavā arahattamaggapadhānavatā pattokāsaṃ pāpuṇituṃ nibbattetabbaṃ guṇaṃ nibbattetuṃ sakkotī’’ti.
commentary_english:
379. "The five" means, in this *sutta*, the five factors of striving (*padhāniyaṅga*) mixed with the supramundane (*lokuttara*) have been spoken of.

The Elder Cūḷasamudda, who dwells in the Kathina enclosure, said, "What is pleasing to you, venerable sir?" He said, "The supramundane is pleasing to me."

"Difference in striving" means difference in striving.

For the striving of an ordinary person (*puthujjana*) is of one kind, that of a stream-enterer (*sotāpanna*) is of another kind, that of a once-returner (*sakadāgāmin*) is of another kind, that of a non-returner (*anāgāmin*) is of another kind, that of an *arhat* is of another kind, that of the eighty great disciples is of another kind, that of the two chief disciples is of another kind, that of the *pratyekabuddhas* is of another kind, that of the all-knowing Buddhas is of another kind.

The striving of an ordinary person does not reach the striving of a stream-enterer...pe... the striving of a *pratyekabuddha* does not reach the striving of an all-knowing Buddha.

Referring to this meaning, he said, "I will speak of the difference in striving."

"One might go for a tooth cause" means that which is not a false cause, not an interruption, in the teeth a cause is seen, that cause one might approach, is the meaning.

"Tooth-ground" means a ground to be gone to with teeth.

In "[one who is] faithless" etc., ordinary persons, stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, all four are called faithless.

For an ordinary person, not having attained the faith of a stream-enterer, is faithless, a stream-enterer [not having attained the faith] of a once-returner, a once-returner [not having attained the faith] of a non-returner, a non-returner [not having attained the faith] of an *arhat* is faithless, an affliction arises even for an *arhat*, therefore all five are called "having many afflictions."

For a noble disciple, the name "deceitful, fraudulent" does not exist.

Therefore that Elder said, "The five factors of striving, the supramundane, have been spoken of. This is pleasing to me."

In the Assakhaḷuṅka Sutta, however, "I will teach, monks, three horse-whips and three person-whips" (A.
Ni.
3.
141) Here, for a noble disciple, the name "awakening" has come, by reason of that, mixed with the supramundane has been spoken, it is said.

But an ordinary person has not attained the energy of the path of stream-entry...pe... a non-returner has not attained the energy of the path of *arhatship*, therefore even one who is lazy is like one who is faithless, all four are, and likewise one who is unwise.

Thus, here, the connection of simile should be understood - an individual without the striving of the path is like elephants without tusks etc.

Those with the striving of the path are like elephants with tusks etc.

Just as elephants without tusks etc., without making a false shape, without cutting off, without dropping the burden, are not able to go to the going of teeth or reach the ground of teeth, just so one without the striving of the path is not able to attain that which should be attained by those with the striving of the path, to produce that quality which should be produced.

Just as elephants with tusks etc., making a false shape, cutting off, dropping the burden, are able to go to the going of teeth or reach the ground of teeth, just so one with the striving of the path, by those with the striving of the path, is able to attain that which should be attained, to produce that quality which should be produced.

This has been said - "One with the striving of the path of stream-entry, by those with the striving of the path of stream-entry, is able to attain the opportunity that has been attained, to produce that quality which should be produced...pe... one with the striving of the path of *arhatship*, by those with the striving of the path of *arhatship*, is able to attain the opportunity that has been attained, to produce that quality which should be produced."

mula_pali: 380. ‘‘Heturūpaṃ, bhante, bhagavā āha; saheturūpaṃ, bhante, bhagavā āha. Cattārome, bhante, vaṇṇā – khattiyā, brāhmaṇā, vessā , suddā. Te cassu imehi pañcahi padhāniyaṅgehi samannāgatā te cassu sammappadhānā; ettha pana nesaṃ, bhante, siyā viseso siyā nānākaraṇa’’nti? ‘‘Ettha kho ettha kho pana (sī.) nesāhaṃ, mahārāja, na kiñci nānākaraṇaṃ vadāmi – yadidaṃ vimuttiyā vimuttiṃ. Seyyathāpi, mahārāja, puriso sukkhaṃ sākakaṭṭhaṃ ādāya aggiṃ abhinibbatteyya, tejo pātukareyya ; athāparo puriso sukkhaṃ sālakaṭṭhaṃ ādāya aggiṃ abhinibbatteyya, tejo pātukareyya; athāparo puriso sukkhaṃ ambakaṭṭhaṃ ādāya aggiṃ abhinibbatteyya, tejo pātukareyya; athāparo puriso sukkhaṃ udumbarakaṭṭhaṃ ādāya aggiṃ abhinibbatteyya, tejo pātukareyya. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, mahārāja, siyā nu kho tesaṃ aggīnaṃ nānādāruto abhinibbattānaṃ kiñci nānākaraṇaṃ acciyā vā acciṃ, vaṇṇena vā vaṇṇaṃ, ābhāya vā ābha’’nti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’. ‘‘Evameva kho, mahārāja, yaṃ taṃ tejaṃ vīriyā nimmathitaṃ padhānābhinibbattaṃ viriyaṃ nippharati, taṃ pacchābhinibbattaṃ (sī.), nāhaṃ tattha kiñci nānākaraṇaṃ vadāmi – yadidaṃ vimuttiyā vimutti’’nti. ‘‘Heturūpaṃ, bhante, bhagavā āha; saheturūpaṃ, bhante, bhagavā āha. Kiṃ pana, bhante, atthi devā’’ti? ‘‘Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, mahārāja, evaṃ vadesi – ‘kiṃ pana, bhante, atthi devā’’’ti? ‘‘Yadi vā te, bhante, devā āgantāro itthattaṃ yadi vā anāgantāro itthattaṃ’’? ‘‘Ye te, mahārāja, devā sabyābajjhā te devā āgantāro itthattaṃ, ye te devā abyābajjhā te devā anāgantāro itthatta’’nti.
mula_english:
“What the Blessed One has said appears reasonable, venerable sir; what the Blessed One has said appears to be supported by reason.

There are these four castes, venerable sir: the nobles (*kṣatriya*), the brahmins (*brāhmaṇa*), the merchants (*vaiśya*), and the workers (*śūdra*).

Now if they possessed these five factors of striving, and if their striving was right, would there be any difference among them in that respect?” “Here, great king, in this respect I say that among them there is no difference, that is, between the deliverance of one and the deliverance of the others (*vimukti*).

Suppose a man took dry *śāka* wood, lit a fire, and produced heat; and then another man took dry *sāla* wood, lit a fire, and produced heat; and then another man took dry mango wood (*āmrakaṣṭha*), lit a fire, and produced heat; and then another man took dry *udumbara* wood, lit a fire, and produced heat.

What do you think, great king? Would there be any difference among these fires lit with different kinds of wood, that is, between the flame of one and the flames of the others, or between the color of one and the colors of the others, or between the radiance of one and the radiances of the others?” “No, venerable sir.”

“So too, great king, when a fire is kindled by energy, lit by striving, there is, I say, no difference, that is, between the deliverance of one and the deliverance of the others (*vimukti*).”

“What the Blessed One has said appears reasonable, venerable sir; what the Blessed One has said appears to be supported by reason.

“Now, venerable sir, are there gods (*deva*)?” “Why do you ask that, great king, saying, ‘Now, venerable sir, are there gods (*deva*)?’” “Are those gods (*deva*), venerable sir, coming to this state, or are they not coming to this state?” “Those gods (*deva*), great king, who are afflicted, are coming to this state; those gods (*deva*) who are unafflicted are not coming to this state.”
commentary_pali: 380.Sammappadhānāti maggapadhānena sammappadhānā. Na kiñci nānākaraṇaṃ vadāmi yadidaṃ vimuttiyā vimuttinti yaṃ ekassa phalavimuttiyā itarassa phalavimuttiṃ ārabbha nānākaraṇaṃ vattabbaṃ siyā, taṃ na kiñci vadāmīti attho. Acciyā vā accinti acciyā vā accimhi. Sesapadadvayepi eseva nayo, bhummatthe hi etaṃ upayogavacanaṃ. Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, mahārājāti, mahārāja, kiṃ tvaṃ? ‘‘Santi devā cātumahārājikā, santi devā tāvatiṃsā…pe… santi devā paranimmitavasavattino, santi devā tatuttari’’nti evaṃ devānaṃ atthibhāvaṃ na jānāsi, yena evaṃ vadesīti. Tato atthibhāvaṃ jānāmi, manussalokaṃ pana āgacchanti nāgacchantīti idaṃ pucchanto yadi vā te, bhantetiādimāha. Sabyābajjhāti sadukkhā, samucchedappahānena appahīnacetasikadukkhā. Āgantāroti upapattivasena āgantāro. Abyābajjhāti samucchinnadukkhā. Anāgantāroti upapattivasena anāgantāro.
commentary_english:
380. *Sammappadhānā* means *sammappadhānā* by way of the path.

*"Na kiñci nānākaraṇaṃ vadāmi yadidaṃ vimuttiyā vimutti"* means that there is no variation concerning the liberation of one in relation to the liberation of the other, in relation to the fruit of liberation; this is the meaning.

*"Acciyā vā acci"* means either in the flame or in the fire.

The same method applies to the remaining two words; for the meaning of "earth," this is a statement of use.

*"Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, mahārājā"* means, great king, what are you? "There are gods of the heaven of the Four Great Kings, there are gods of the heaven of the Thirty-three...pe...there are gods who have power over the creations of others, there are gods beyond that" - do you not know of the existence of the gods, that you speak thus?

"Then I know of the existence, but do they come to the human world or not come?" Asking this, he said, "*Yadi vā te, bhante*," etc.

*"Sabyābajjhā"* means with suffering, suffering of mental factors not abandoned by eradication.

*"Āgantāro"* means those who come by way of rebirth.

*"Abyābajjhā"* means those whose suffering is completely cut off.

*"Anāgantāro"* means those who do not come by way of rebirth.

mula_pali:
381. Evaṃ vutte, viṭṭūbho senāpati bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘ye te, bhante, devā sabyābajjhā āgantāro itthattaṃ te devā, ye te devā abyābajjhā anāgantāro itthattaṃ te deve tamhā ṭhānā cāvessanti vā pabbājessanti vā’’ti?

Atha kho āyasmato ānandassa etadahosi – ‘‘ayaṃ kho viṭaṭūbho senāpati rañño pasenadissa kosalassa putto; ahaṃ bhagavato putto. Ayaṃ kho kālo yaṃ putto puttena manteyyā’’ti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando viṭaṭūbhaṃ senāpatiṃ āmantesi – ‘‘tena hi, senāpati, taṃ yevettha paṭipucchissāmi; yathā te khameyya tathā naṃ byākareyyāsi. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, senāpati, yāvatā rañño pasenadissa kosalassa vijitaṃ yattha ca rājā pasenadi kosalo issariyādhipaccaṃ rajjaṃ kāreti, pahoti tattha rājā pasenadi kosalo samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā puññavantaṃ vā apuññavantaṃ vā brahmacariyavantaṃ vā abrahmacariyavantaṃ vā tamhā ṭhānā cāvetuṃ vā pabbājetuṃ vā’’ti? ‘‘Yāvatā, bho, rañño pasenadissa kosalassa vijitaṃ yattha ca rājā pasenadi kosalo issariyādhipaccaṃ rajjaṃ kāreti, pahoti tattha rājā pasenadi kosalo samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā puññavantaṃ vā apuññavantaṃ vā brahmacariyavantaṃ vā abrahmacariyavantaṃ vā tamhā ṭhānā cāvetuṃ vā pabbājetuṃ vā’’ti.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, senāpati, yāvatā rañño pasenadissa kosalassa avijitaṃ yattha ca rājā pasenadi kosalo na issariyādhipaccaṃ rajjaṃ kāreti, tattha pahoti rājā pasenadi kosalo samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā puññavantaṃ vā apuññavantaṃ vā brahmacariyavantaṃ vā abrahmacariyavantaṃ vā tamhā ṭhānā cāvetuṃ vā pabbājetuṃ vā’’ti? ‘‘Yāvatā, bho, rañño pasenadissa kosalassa avijitaṃ yattha ca rājā pasenadi kosalo na issariyādhipaccaṃ rajjaṃ kāreti, na tattha pahoti rājā pasenadi kosalo samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā puññavantaṃ vā apuññavantaṃ vā brahmacariyavantaṃ vā abrahmacariyavantaṃ vā tamhā ṭhānā cāvetuṃ vā pabbājetuṃ vā’’ti.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, senāpati, sutā te devā tāvatiṃsā’’ti? ‘‘Evaṃ, bho. Sutā me devā tāvatiṃsā. Idhāpi bhotā raññā pasenadinā kosalena sutā devā tāvatiṃsā’’ti. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, senāpati, pahoti rājā pasenadi kosalo deve tāvatiṃse tamhā ṭhānā cāvetuṃ vā pabbājetuṃ vā’’ti? ‘‘Dassanampi, bho, rājā pasenadi kosalo deve tāvatiṃse nappahoti, kuto pana tamhā ṭhānā cāvessati vā pabbājessati vā’’ti? ‘‘Evameva kho, senāpati, ye te devā sabyābajjhā āgantāro itthattaṃ te devā, ye te devā abyābajjhā anāgantāro itthattaṃ te deve dassanāyapi nappahonti; kuto pana tamhā ṭhānā cāvessanti vā pabbājessanti vā’’ti?
mula_english:
381. Thus addressed, General Viṭṭūbha said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, those gods who are troubled, who return to this human state, and those gods who are not troubled, who do not return to this human state – can they remove or banish those gods from that place?"

Then it occurred to the venerable Ānanda: "This General Viṭaṭūbha is the son of King Pasenadi of Kosala; I am the son of the Blessed One. This is the time for one son to talk with the other."

Then the venerable Ānanda said to General Viṭaṭūbha: "In that case, General, I shall ask you a question in return. Answer it as you see fit. What do you think, General? As far as King Pasenadi of Kosala's realm extends, where King Pasenadi of Kosala exercises lordship and sovereignty, can King Pasenadi of Kosala remove or banish from that place a *śramaṇa* or a *brāhmaṇa*, a meritorious person or an unmeritorious person, one who leads the holy life or one who does not?"

"As far as King Pasenadi of Kosala's realm extends, where King Pasenadi of Kosala exercises lordship and sovereignty, King Pasenadi, can remove or banish from that place a *śramaṇa* or a *brāhmaṇa*, a meritorious person or an unmeritorious person, one who leads the holy life or one who does not."

"What do you think, General? As far as King Pasenadi of Kosala's realm does not extend, where King Pasenadi of Kosala does not exercise lordship and sovereignty, can King Pasenadi of Kosala remove or banish from that place a *śramaṇa* or a *brāhmaṇa*, a meritorious person or an unmeritorious person, one who leads the holy life or one who does not?"

"As far as King Pasenadi of Kosala's realm does not extend, where King Pasenadi of Kosala does not exercise lordship and sovereignty, King Pasenadi Kosala cannot remove or banish from that place a *śramaṇa* or a *brāhmaṇa*, a meritorious person or an unmeritorious person, one who leads the holy life or one who does not."

"What do you think, General? Have you heard of the gods of the *Tāvatiṃsa* heaven?"

"Yes, sir. I have heard of the gods of the *Tāvatiṃsa* heaven. Here too, the King Pasenadi of Kosala has heard of the gods of the *Tāvatiṃsa* heaven."

"What do you think, General? Can King Pasenadi of Kosala remove or banish the gods of the *Tāvatiṃsa* heaven from that place?"
