Then the Blessed One addressed the Brahmin Brahmāyu with these verses (gāthāhi paccabhāsi):

“Those thirty-two marks of a Great Man (dvattiṃsa-mahāpurisalakkhaṇā), all of them are present in my body (kāyasmiṃ), do not doubt (mā te kaṅkhāhu), O Brahmin.

That which should be known (abhiññeyyaṃ), I have known (abhiññātaṃ); that which should be developed (bhāvetabbaṃ), I have developed (bhāvitaṃ); that which should be abandoned (pahātabbaṃ), I have abandoned (pahīnaṃ me), therefore, I am awakened (buddhosmi), O Brahmin.

For the sake of benefit in this very life (diṭṭhadhammahitatthāya), and for the sake of happiness in the life to come (samparāyasukhāya ca), ask whatever (yaṃ kiñci) you desire (abhipatthita), opportunity has been made.”

mula_pali:
393. Atha kho brahmāyussa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi – ‘‘katāvakāso khomhi samaṇena gotamena. Kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ puccheyyaṃ – ‘diṭṭhadhammikaṃ vā atthaṃ samparāyikaṃ vā’’’ti. Atha kho brahmāyussa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi – ‘‘kusalo kho ahaṃ diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ atthānaṃ. Aññepi maṃ diṭṭhadhammikaṃ atthaṃ pucchanti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ samparāyikaṃyeva atthaṃ puccheyya’’nti. Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

‘‘Kathaṃ kho brāhmaṇo hoti, kathaṃ bhavati vedagū;

Tevijjo bho kathaṃ hoti, sotthiyo kinti vuccati.

‘‘Arahaṃ bho kathaṃ hoti, kathaṃ bhavati kevalī;

Muni ca bho kathaṃ hoti, buddho kinti pavuccatī’’ti.
mula_english:
Then the brahmin Brahmāyus thought: “Permission has been granted to me by the renunciate Gotama.
Which should I ask the renunciate Gotama about: good in this life (*dṛṣṭadhārmika artha*) or good in the lives to come (*samparāyika artha*)?”
Then the brahmin Brahmāyus thought: “I am skilled in the good of this life (*dṛṣṭadhārmikānaṃ arthānaṃ*).
And others too ask me about good in this life (*dṛṣṭadhārmikaṃ arthaṃ*).
Why shouldn’t I ask the renunciate Gotama only about good in the lives to come (*samparāyikaṃ eva arthaṃ*)?”
Then the brahmin Brahmāyu addressed the Blessed One in verses:

“How does one become a *brāhmaṇa*, how does one become a knower of the Vedas (*vedagū*);
How does one become a *tevijjo* (possessor of the three knowledges), how is one called a *sotthiyo*?”

“How does one become an *arahaṃ*, how does one become a *kevalī*;
And how does one become a *muni*, how is one called a *buddha*?”
commentary_pali: 393.Kevalīti sakalaguṇasampanno.
commentary_english: [p.393] *kevalī* (kaivalya) means endowed with all perfect qualities (*sakalaguṇasampannaḥ*).

mula_pali:
394. Atha kho bhagavā brahmāyuṃ brāhmaṇaṃ gāthāhi paccabhāsi –

‘‘Pubbenivāsaṃ yo vedi, saggāpāyañca passati;

Atho jātikkhayaṃ patto, abhiññā vosito muni.

‘‘Cittaṃ visuddhaṃ jānāti, muttaṃ rāgehi sabbaso;

Pahīnajātimaraṇo, brahmacariyassa kevalī;

Pāragū sabbadhammānaṃ, buddho tādī pavuccatī’’ti.

Evaṃ vutte, brahmāyu brāhmaṇo uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavato pādāni mukhena ca paricumbati, pāṇīhi ca parisambāhati, nāmañca sāveti – ‘‘brahmāyu ahaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇo; brahmāyu ahaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇo’’ti. Atha kho sā parisā acchariyabbhutacittajātā ahosi – ‘‘acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho! Yatra hi nāmāyaṃ brahmāyu brāhmaṇo ñāto yasassī evarūpaṃ paramanipaccakāraṃ karissatī’’ti. Atha kho bhagavā brahmāyuṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘alaṃ, brāhmaṇa, uṭṭhaha nisīda tvaṃ sake āsane yato te mayi cittaṃ pasanna’’nti. Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo uṭṭhahitvā sake āsane nisīdi.
commentary_pali:
394.Paccabhāsīti ekappahārena pucchite aṭṭha pañhe byākaronto patiabhāsi. Yo vedīti yo vidati jānāti, yassa pubbenivāso pākaṭo. Saggāpāyañca passatīti dibbacakkhuñāṇaṃ kathitaṃ. Jātikkhayaṃpattoti arahattaṃ patto. Abhiññā vositoti taṃ arahattaṃ abhijānitvā vosito vosānappatto. Munīti arahattañāṇamoneyyena samannāgato.

Visuddhanti paṇḍaraṃ. Muttaṃ rāgehīti kilesarāgehi muttaṃ. Pahīnajātimaraṇoti jātikkhayappattattā pahīnajātiko, jātipahāneneva pahīnamaraṇo. Brahmacariyassa kevalīti yaṃ brahmacariyassa kevalī sakalabhāvo, tena samannāgato, sakalacatumaggabrahmacariyavāsoti attho. Pāragū sabbadhammānanti sabbesaṃ lokiyalokuttaradhammānaṃ abhiññāya pāraṃ gato, sabbadhamme abhijānitvā ṭhitoti attho. Pāragūti vā ettāvatā pariññāpāragū pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ, pahānapāragū sabbakilesānaṃ , bhāvanāpāragū catunnaṃ maggānaṃ, sacchikiriyāpāragū nirodhassa, samāpattipāragū sabbasamāpattīnanti ayamattho vutto. Puna sabbadhammānanti iminā abhiññāpāragū vuttoti. Buddho tādī pavuccatīti tādiso chahi ākārehi pāraṃ gato sabbākārena catunnaṃ saccānaṃ buddhattā buddhoti pavuccatīti.

Visuddha Muttaṃ rāgehī Pahīnajātimaraṇo Brahmacariyassa kevalī Pāragū sabbadhammāna Pāragū sabbadhammāna Buddho tādī pavuccatī

Kiṃ pana ettāvatā sabbe pañhā vissajjitā hontīti? Āma vissajjitā, cittaṃ visuddhaṃ jānāti, muttaṃ rāgehīti iminā tāva bāhitapāpattā brāhmaṇoti paṭhamapañho vissajjito hoti. Pāragūti iminā vedehi gatattā vedagūti dutiyapañho vissajjito hoti. Pubbenivāsantiādīhi imāsaṃ tissannaṃ vijjānaṃ atthitāya tevijjoti tatiyapañho vissajjito hoti. Muttaṃ rāgehi sabbasoti imināva nissaṭattā pāpadhammānaṃ sottiyoti catutthapañho vissajjito hoti. Jātikkhayaṃ pattoti iminā pana arahattasseva vuttattā pañcamapañho vissajjito hoti. Vositoti ca brahmacariyassa kevalīti ca imehi chaṭṭhapañho vissajjito hoti. Abhiññā vosito munīti iminā sattamapañho vissajjito hoti. Pāragū sabbadhammānaṃ, buddho tādī pavuccatīti iminā aṭṭhamapañho vissajjito hoti.
commentary_english:
394. *Paccabhāsī* means he replied, explaining the eight questions asked with a single strike.

*Yo vedī* means he knows, he understands, for whom previous abodes are evident.

*Saggāpāyañca passatī* means the divine eye knowledge is spoken of.

*Jātikkhayaṃ patto* means attained to arhatship.

*Abhiññā vosito* means having known that arhatship, he is finished, he has reached the end.

*Munī* means endowed with the knowledge of arhatship and silence.

*Visuddha* means white.

*Muttaṃ rāgehī* means freed from the defilement of passion.

*Pahīnajātimaraṇo* means having attained the destruction of birth, he has abandoned birth; by the abandonment of birth alone, he has abandoned death.

*Brahmacariyassa kevalī* means he is endowed with the entirety of the holy life, meaning he dwells in the entirety of the fourfold path of the holy life.

*Pāragū sabbadhammāna* means he has gone to the far shore of knowledge of all mundane and supramundane things, he abides having understood all things.

Or, *pāragū* means, to this extent, he has reached the limit of understanding of the five aggregates, the limit of abandoning all defilements, the limit of developing the four paths, the limit of realizing cessation, the limit of attaining all attainments—this meaning is stated.

Again, by *sabbadhammāna*, the limit of knowledge is stated.

*Buddho tādī pavuccatī* means such a one is called a Buddha because he has gone to the far shore in six ways and is awakened to the four noble truths in every way.

*Visuddha muttaṃ rāgehī pahīnajātimaraṇo brahmacariyassa kevalī pāragū sabbadhammāna pāragū sabbadhammāna buddho tādī pavuccatī*

But are all the questions answered merely by this much? Yes, they are answered. By "he knows the mind is pure, freed from passion," the first question, "a brahmin who has banished evil," is answered.

By *pāragū*, the second question, "one who has gone to the Vedas, a knower of the Vedas," is answered because he has gone to the Vedas.

By *pubbenivāsa*, etc., the third question, "possessing the three knowledges," is answered because of the existence of these three knowledges.

By "freed from passion in every way," the fourth question, "one who has cast off evil qualities, a sotthiya," is answered because he is rid of evil qualities.

By "attained the destruction of birth," the fifth question is answered, since it speaks of arhatship.

By "vosito" and "brahmacariyassa kevalī," the sixth question is answered.

By "abhiññā vosito munī," the seventh question is answered.

By "pāragū sabbadhammānaṃ, buddho tādī pavuccatīti," the eighth question is answered.

mula_pali:
395. Atha kho bhagavā brahmāyussa brāhmaṇassa anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ, sīlakathaṃ, saggakathaṃ; kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Yadā bhagavā aññāsi brahmāyuṃ brāhmaṇaṃ kallacittaṃ muducittaṃ vinīvaraṇacittaṃ udaggacittaṃ pasannacittaṃ, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā taṃ pakāsesi – dukkhaṃ, samudayaṃ, nirodhaṃ, maggaṃ. Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, evameva brahmāyussa brāhmaṇassa tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – ‘‘yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma’’nti. Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo diṭṭhadhammo pattadhammo viditadhammo pariyogāḷhadhammo tiṇṇavicikiccho vigatakathaṃkatho vesārajjappatto aparappaccayo satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama! Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti – evamevaṃ bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gataṃ. Adhivāsetu ca me bhavaṃ gotamo svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā’’ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi . Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo tassā rattiyā accayena sake nivesane paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – ‘‘kālo, bho gotama, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta’’nti.

Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena brahmāyussa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo sattāhaṃ buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi. Atha kho bhagavā tassa sattāhassa accayena videhesu cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Atha kho brahmāyu brāhmaṇo acirapakkantassa bhagavato kālamakāsi. Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘brahmāyu, bhante, brāhmaṇo kālaṅkato. Tassa kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo’’ti? ‘‘Paṇḍito, bhikkhave, brahmāyu brāhmaṇo paccapādi dhammassānudhammaṃ, na ca maṃ dhammādhikaraṇaṃ vihesesi. Brahmāyu, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇo pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko hoti, tattha parinibbāyī, anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā’’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Brahmāyusuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.
mula_english:
Then the Blessed One gave Brahmāyu the Brahmin a graduated talk, that is to say: talk on giving (dānakathā), talk on virtue (sīlakathā), talk on heaven (saggakathā); he revealed the danger (ādīnava), degradation (okāra), and defilement (saṃkilesa) in sensual pleasures (kāmānaṃ), and the blessing (ānisaṃsaṃ) of renunciation (nekkhamme).

When the Blessed One knew that the mind of Brahmāyu the Brahmin was ready (kallacittaṃ), receptive (muducittaṃ), free from hindrances (vinīvaraṇacittaṃ), elated (udaggacittaṃ), and confident (pasannacittaṃ), he then revealed the teaching special to the Buddhas (buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā): suffering (dukkhaṃ), its origin (samudayaṃ), its cessation (nirodhaṃ), and the path (maggaṃ).

Just as a clean cloth with all marks removed would take dye evenly, so too, while the brahmin Brahmāyu sat there, the spotless immaculate vision of the Dhamma (dhammacakkhuṃ) arose in him: “All that is subject to arising (samudayadhammaṃ) is subject to cessation (nirodhadhammaṃ).”

Then the brahmin Brahmāyu, having seen the Dhamma (diṭṭhadhammo), attained the Dhamma (pattadhammo), understood the Dhamma (viditadhammo), fathomed the Dhamma (pariyogāḷhadhammo), having crossed beyond doubt (tiṇṇavicikiccho), having done away with perplexity (vigatakathaṃkatho), having gained intrepidity (vesārajjappatto), and having become independent of others (aparappaccayo) in the Teacher’s Dispensation (satthusāsane), said this to the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ): “Magnificent (abhikkantaṃ), Master Gotama (bho Gotama), Magnificent (abhikkantaṃ), Master Gotama (bho Gotama)! Just as, Master Gotama (bho Gotama), one might set upright what was overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or show the way to one who was lost, or hold up a lamp in the dark so that those with eyes might see forms, just so has the Dhamma (dhammo) been made clear in many ways (anekapariyāyena) by Master Gotama (Gotamena).

I go to the Blessed One Gotama (bhavantaṃ Gotamaṃ) for refuge (saraṇaṃ gacchāmi), and to the Dhamma (dhammañca), and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus (bhikkhusaṅghañca).

May the revered Gotama (bhavaṃ Gotamo) remember me (maṃ dhāretu) as a lay follower (upāsakaṃ) who has gone for refuge (saraṇaṃ gataṃ) from this day forth (ajjatagge), as long as life shall last (pāṇupetaṃ).

May the revered Gotama (bhavaṃ Gotamo) consent (adhivāsetu) to accept tomorrow’s meal (svātanāya bhattaṃ) from me (me), together with the Sangha of bhikkhus (saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā'ti).”

The Blessed One (bhagavā) consented by maintaining silence (tuṇhībhāvena).

Then, knowing that the Blessed One (bhagavato) had consented (adhivāsanaṃ viditvā), the brahmin Brahmāyu rose from his seat (uṭṭhāyāsanā), and after paying homage to the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā), keeping him on his right (padakkhiṇaṃ katvā), he departed (pakkāmi).

Then, when the night had ended (tassā rattiyā accayena), the brahmin Brahmāyu had good food (paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ) of various kinds prepared (paṭiyādāpetvā) in his residence (sake nivesane), and he had the time announced (kālaṃ ārocāpesi) to the Blessed One (bhagavato): “It is time (kālo), Master Gotama (bho Gotama), the meal (bhattaṃ) is ready (niṭṭhitaṃ).”

Then, it being morning (pubbaṇhasamayaṃ), the Blessed One (bhagavā) dressed (nivāsetvā), and taking his bowl and outer robe (pattacīvaramādāya), he went (upasaṅkami) with the Sangha of bhikkhus (saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena) to the brahmin Brahmāyu’s residence (brahmāyussa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṃ) and sat down (nisīdi) on the seat made ready (paññatte āsane).

Then the brahmin Brahmāyu, for a week (sattāhaṃ), with his own hands (sahatthā), served and satisfied (santappesi sampavāresi) the Sangha of bhikkhus (bhikkhusaṅghaṃ) headed by the Buddha (buddhappamukhaṃ) with various kinds of good food (paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena).

Then, at the end of that week (tassa sattāhassa accayena), the Blessed One (bhagavā) set out to wander (cārikaṃ pakkāmi) in the country of the Videhans (videhesu).

Soon after he had gone (acirapakkantassa), the brahmin Brahmāyu died (kālamakāsi)

Then a number of bhikkhus (sambahulā bhikkhū) went (upasaṅkamiṃsu) to the Blessed One (bhagavā); having approached (upasaṅkamitvā), having greeted the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā), they sat down (nisīdiṃsu) at one side (ekamantaṃ).

As they were sitting at one side (ekamantaṃ nisinnā), those bhikkhus (te bhikkhū) said this (etadavocuṃ) to the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ): “Brahmāyu (Brahmāyu), venerable sir (bhante), the brahmin (brāhmaṇo) has died (kālaṅkato). What is his destiny (kā gati), what is his future state (ko abhisamparāyo)?” “Wise (paṇḍito), bhikkhus (bhikkhave), Brahmāyu the brahmin (brahmāyu brāhmaṇo) practiced (paccapādi) the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma (dhammassānudhammaṃ), and he did not harass me (na ca maṃ vihesesi) in matters of the Dhamma (dhammādhikaraṇaṃ).

Brahmāyu (Brahmāyu), bhikkhus (bhikkhave), the brahmin (brāhmaṇo), with the destruction (parikkhayā) of the five lower fetters (pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ), has reappeared spontaneously (opapātiko hoti), and there (tattha) he will attain final Nibbāna (parinibbāyī), never to return (anāvattidhammo) from that world (tasmā lokā).”

This (idaṃ) the Blessed One (bhagavā) said (avoca).

Elated (attamanā), those bhikkhus (te bhikkhū) delighted (abhinandunti) in the Blessed One’s statement (bhagavato bhāsitaṃ).

The Brahmāyusutta is finished, the first.
commentary_pali:
395.Dānakathantiādīni heṭṭhā sutte vitthāritāneva. Paccapādīti paṭipajji. Dhammassānudhammanti imasmiṃ sutte dhammo nāma arahattamaggo, anudhammo nāma heṭṭhimā tayo maggā tīṇi ca sāmaññaphalāni, tāni paṭipāṭiyā paṭilabhīti attho. Na ca maṃ dhammādhikaraṇaṃ vihesesīti mañca dhammakāraṇā na kilamesi, na punappunaṃ kathāpesīti vuttaṃ hoti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānameva. Tattha parinibbāyīti pana padena desanāya arahatteneva kūṭaṃ gahitanti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Brahmāyusuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
395. *dānakathā* etc. were already extensively explained in the sutta below. *paccapādī* means he undertook. *dhammassānudhammaṃ* means in this sutta, *dhamma* is the path of Arhatship, *anudhammo* means the lower three paths and the three fruits of the ascetic life; the meaning is that he attained them in order. *na ca maṃ dhammādhikaraṇaṃ vihesesī* means he did not weary me because of the Dhamma, he did not make me speak again and again. The rest is clear throughout. However, with the word *tattha parinibbāyī*, it is as if the peak was seized by the Dhamma through Arhatship.

The Brahmāyu Sutta Commentary in the Papañcasūdanī, Commentary to the Middle Length Discourses, is finished.

mula_pali:
396. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā aṅguttarāpesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ aḍḍhateḷasehi bhikkhusatehi yena āpaṇaṃ nāma aṅguttarāpānaṃ nigamo tadavasari. Assosi kho keṇiyo jaṭilo – ‘‘samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito aṅguttarāpesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ aḍḍhateḷasehi bhikkhusatehi āpaṇaṃ anuppatto. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. So imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti. So dhammaṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāseti. Sādhu kho pana tathārūpānaṃ arahataṃ dassanaṃ hotī’’’ti.

Atha kho keṇiyo jaṭilo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho keṇiyaṃ jaṭilaṃ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi . Atha kho keṇiyo jaṭilo bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘adhivāsetu me bhavaṃ gotamo svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā’’ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhagavā keṇiyaṃ jaṭilaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘mahā kho, keṇiya, bhikkhusaṅgho aḍḍhateḷasāni bhikkhusatāni, tvañca brāhmaṇesu abhippasanno’’ti. Dutiyampi kho keṇiyo jaṭilo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘kiñcāpi kho, bho gotama, mahā bhikkhusaṅgho aḍḍhateḷasāni bhikkhusatāni, ahañca brāhmaṇesu abhippasanno; adhivāsetu me bhavaṃ gotamo svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā’’ti. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā keṇiyaṃ jaṭilaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘mahā kho, keṇiya, bhikkhusaṅgho aḍḍhateḷasāni bhikkhusatāni, tvañca brāhmaṇesu abhippasanno’’ti. Tatiyampi kho keṇiyo jaṭilo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘kiñcāpi kho, bho gotama, mahā bhikkhusaṅgho aḍḍhateḷasāni bhikkhusatāni, ahañca brāhmaṇesu abhippasanno; adhivāsetu me bhavaṃ gotamo svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā’’ti . Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho keṇiyo jaṭilo bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena sako assamo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mittāmacce ñātisālohite āmantesi – ‘‘suṇantu me bhonto, mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā; samaṇo me gotamo nimantito svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Yena me kāyaveyyāvaṭikaṃ kāyaveyāvaṭṭikaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.), kāyaveyyāvatikaṃ (ka.) kareyyāthā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bho’’ti kho keṇiyassa jaṭilassa mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā keṇiyassa jaṭilassa paṭissutvā appekacce uddhanāni khaṇanti, appekacce kaṭṭhāni phālenti, appekacce bhājanāni dhovanti, appekacce udakamaṇikaṃ patiṭṭhāpenti, appekacce āsanāni paññapenti. Keṇiyo pana jaṭilo sāmaṃyeva maṇḍalamālaṃ paṭiyādeti.

kāyaveyāvaṭṭikaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.), kāyaveyyāvatikaṃ (ka.)
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was wandering in the country of the Aṅguttarāpas with a large *saṅgha* of *bhikkhus*, with twelve hundred and fifty *bhikkhus*, and eventually he arrived at a town of the Aṅguttarāpas named Āpaṇa.

The matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya heard: “The recluse Gotama, the son of the Sakyans who went forth from a Sakyan clan, has been wandering in the country of the Aṅguttarāpas with a large *saṅgha* of *bhikkhus*, with twelve hundred and fifty *bhikkhus*, and he has come to Āpaṇa.

Now a good report of Master Gotama has been spread to this effect: ‘The Blessed One is an *arahaṃ*, a *sammāsambuddha*, accomplished in knowledge and conduct (*vijjācaraṇasampanno*), sublime (*sugato*), knower of the world (*lokavidū*), incomparable (*anuttaro*), leader of persons to be tamed (*purisadammasārathi*), teacher of gods and humans (*satthā devamanussānaṃ*), a Buddha (*buddho*), blessed (*bhagavā*)’.

He, having realized it by his own super-knowledge, proclaims this world with its gods (*devas*), *Māras*, and *Brahmās*, this generation with its ascetics (*ssamaṇas*) and *brāhmaṇas*, its princes and its people, which he has himself realised by direct knowledge (*abhiññā sacchikatvā*).

He teaches the *Dhamma*, which is lovely in its beginning (*ādikalyāṇaṃ*), lovely in its middle (*majjhekalyāṇaṃ*), lovely in its ending (*pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ*), in the spirit (*sātthaṃ*) and in the letter (*sabyañjanaṃ*), and displays the fully-perfected and purified holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*).

“It is good to see such a worthy one.”

Then the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya went to where the Blessed One was, and exchanged greetings with him.

After exchanging courteous greetings and polite conversation, he sat down at a distance.

As he was sitting there, the Blessed One instructed, urged, roused, & encouraged Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic with a *Dhamma* talk.

Then, having been instructed, urged, roused, and encouraged by the Blessed One with a talk on the *Dhamma*, the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya said to the Blessed One: “Let Master Gotama together with the *Saṅgha* of *bhikkhus* consent to accept tomorrow’s meal from me.”

When this was said, the Blessed One told him: “The *Saṅgha* of *bhikkhus* is large, Keṇiya, consisting of twelve hundred and fifty *bhikkhus*, and you place full confidence in the *brāhmaṇas*.”

A second time the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya said to the Blessed One: “Although the *Saṅgha* of *bhikkhus* is large, Master Gotama, consisting of twelve hundred and fifty *bhikkhus*, and although I place full confidence in the *brāhmaṇas*, still let Master Gotama, together with the *Saṅgha* of *bhikkhus*, consent to accept tomorrow’s meal from me.”

A second time the Blessed One told him: “The *Saṅgha* of *bhikkhus* is large, Keṇiya, consisting of twelve hundred and fifty *bhikkhus*, and you place full confidence in the *brāhmaṇas*.”

A third time the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya said to the Blessed One: “Although the *Saṅgha* is large, Master Gotama…still let Master Gotama together with the *Saṅgha* of *bhikkhus* consent to accept tomorrow’s meal from me.”

The Lord signified his acceptance by silence (*tuṇhībhāvena*).

Then, knowing that the Blessed One had consented, the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya rose from his seat and went to his own hermitage where he addressed his friends and companions, his kinsmen and relatives thus: “Hear me, sirs, my friends and companions, my kinsmen and relatives. The recluse Gotama has been invited by me for tomorrow’s meal together with the *Saṅgha* of *bhikkhus*.

Therefore, you should help me.”

“Yes, sir,” they replied, and some dug out ovens, some chopped wood, some washed dishes, some set out water jugs, some prepared seats,

while the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya himself set up a pavilion (*maṇḍalamālaṃ*).
commentary_pali:
396.Evaṃme sutanti selasuttaṃ. Tattha aṅguttarāpesūtiādi potaliyasutte vitthāritameva. Aḍḍhateḷasehīti aḍḍhena teḷasehi, dvādasahi satehi paññāsāya ca bhikkhūhi saddhinti vuttaṃ hoti. Te pana sāvakasannipāte sannipatitā bhikkhūyeva sabbe ehibhikkhupabbajjāya pabbajitā khīṇāsavā. Keṇiyoti tassa nāmaṃ, jaṭiloti tāpaso. So kira brāhmaṇamahāsālo, dhanarakkhaṇatthāya pana tāpasapabbajjaṃ samādāya rañño paṇṇākāraṃ datvā bhūmibhāgaṃ gahetvā tattha assamaṃ kāretvā vasati pañcahi sakaṭasatehi vaṇijjaṃ payojetvā kulasahassassa nissayo hutvā, assamepi cassa eko tālarukkho divase divase ekaṃ sovaṇṇamayaṃ tālaphalaṃ muñcatīti vadanti. So divā kāsāyāni dhāreti, jaṭā ca bandhati, rattiṃ kāmasampattiṃ anubhavati. Dhammiyā kathāyāti pānakānisaṃsapaṭisaṃyuttāya dhammiyā kathāya. Ayañhi keṇiyo tucchahattho bhagavato dassanāya gantuṃ lajjāyamāno – ‘‘vikālabhojanā viratānampi pānakaṃ kappatī’’ti cintetvā susaṅkhatabadarapānaṃ pañcahi kājasatehi gāhāpetvā agamāsi. Evaṃ gatabhāvo cassa – ‘‘atha kho keṇiyassa jaṭilassa etadahosi kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ samaṇassa gotamassa harāpeyya’’nti bhesajjakkhandhake (mahāva. 300) pāḷiāruḷhoyeva.

Dutiyampi kho bhagavāti kasmā punappunaṃ paṭikkhipi? Titthiyānaṃ paṭikkhepapasannatāya, akāraṇametaṃ, natthi buddhānaṃ paccayahetu evarūpaṃ kohaññaṃ. Ayaṃ pana aḍḍhateḷasāni bhikkhusatāni disvā ettakānaṃyeva bhikkhaṃ paṭiyādessati, sveva selo tīhi purisasatehi saddhiṃ pabbajissati. Ayuttaṃ kho pana navake aññato pesetvā imeheva saddhiṃ gantuṃ, ime vā aññato pesetvā navakehi saddhiṃ gantuṃ. Athāpi sabbe gahetvā gamissāmi, bhikkhāhāro nappahossati. Tato bhikkhūsu piṇḍāya carantesu manussā ujjhāyissanti – ‘‘cirassāpi keṇiyo samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ nimantetvā yāpanamattaṃ dātuṃ nāsakkhī’’ti, sayampi vippaṭisārī bhavissati. Paṭikkhepe pana kate ‘‘samaṇo gotamo punappunaṃ ‘tvañca brāhmaṇesu abhippasanno’ti brāhmaṇānaṃ nāmaṃ gaṇhātī’’ti cintetvā brāhmaṇepi nimantetukāmo bhavissati, tato brāhmaṇe pāṭiyekkaṃ nimantessati , te tena nimantitā bhikkhū hutvā bhuñjissanti. Evamassa saddhā anurakkhitā bhavissatīti punappunaṃ paṭikkhipi. Kiñcāpi kho, bhoti iminā idaṃ dīpeti, – ‘‘bho gotama, kiṃ jātaṃ yadi ahaṃ brāhmaṇesu abhippasanno, adhivāsetu bhavaṃ gotamo, ahaṃ brāhmaṇānampi dātuṃ sakkomi tumhākampī’’ti.

Dutiyampi kho bhagavā Kiñcāpi kho, bho

Kāyaveyyāvaṭikanti kāyaveyyāvaccaṃ. Maṇḍalamāḷanti dussamaṇḍapaṃ.

Kāyaveyyāvaṭika Maṇḍalamāḷa
commentary_english:
396. Thus, "have I heard," is the Sela Sutta. There, "Aṅguttarāpesū," etc., is explained in detail in the Potaliya Sutta. "Aḍḍhateḷasehī" means half of thirteen, twelve hundred. And with fifty monks, it is said that there was faith. Those monks, gathered in the assembly of disciples, were all those who had gone forth by the "Come, monk" ordination, [and were] those who had destroyed the āsavas (influxes). "Keṇiyo" is his name, "Jaṭilo" is the ascetic. It is said that he was a great brahmin, who, for the purpose of protecting wealth, took the ascetic life, gave a gift to the king, took a share of the land, built a hermitage there, lived by engaging in trade with five hundred carts, and having become a refuge for a thousand families, a single palm tree in his hermitage would drop one golden palm fruit each day. He wears reddish-brown robes during the day, ties up his matted hair, and experiences the pleasures of the senses at night. "Dhammiyā Kathāyā" means in accordance with the Dhamma, connected with the benefits of the drink. This Keṇiyo, ashamed to go empty-handed to the Blessed One, thinking, "Drink is suitable even for those who are abstaining from untimely meals," had a well-prepared badara drink obtained with five hundred kārṣāpaṇas (a type of coin) and went. Thus was his state of being – "Then it occurred to Keṇiyo the ascetic, 'What should I offer to Gotama the Samaṇa (recluse)?'" – in the Bhesajjakkhandhaka (Mahāvagga. 300) it is clearly stated in the Pāli.

Again, why did the Blessed One repeatedly reject [his invitation]? Because of the Titthiyas' inclination to reject [him]. This is not a reason; there is no such ignorance among the Buddhas as to have a reason for their belief. But this one, having seen the thirteen and a half hundred monks, will provide alms for only so many. Sela himself will go forth with three hundred men. It is not fitting to send the new ones elsewhere and go with these, or to send these elsewhere and go with the new ones. But if I take all of them, there will not be enough alms food. Then people will criticize the monks who are wandering for alms – "Even after a long time, Keṇiyo, having invited Gotama the Samaṇa, was not able to give even enough for sustenance," and he himself will be remorseful. But when [his invitation] has been rejected, thinking, "Gotama the Samaṇa repeatedly takes the name of the Brahmins and is attached to the Brahmins," he will want to invite the Brahmins as well. Then he will invite each of the Brahmins separately, and those monks invited by him will eat. Thus, his faith will be protected, so he repeatedly rejected [his invitation]. "Kiñcāpi kho, bho" (Even though, sir) indicates this, – "Sir Gotama, what has happened if I am attached to the Brahmins? May Gotama accept [my invitation], I am able to give to the Brahmins as well as to you."

Again, the Blessed One. "Kāyaveyyāvaṭika" means physical assistance. "Maṇḍalamāḷa" means a cloth pavilion.

Physical assistance, cloth pavilion.

mula_pali:
397. Tena kho pana samayena selo brāhmaṇo āpaṇe paṭivasati tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ pāragū sanighaṇḍukeṭubhānaṃ sākkharappabhedānaṃ itihāsapañcamānaṃ , padako, veyyākaraṇo, lokāyatamahāpurisalakkhaṇesu anavayo, tīṇi ca māṇavakasatāni mante vāceti. Tena kho pana samayena keṇiyo jaṭilo sele brāhmaṇe abhippasanno hoti. Atha kho selo brāhmaṇo tīhi māṇavakasatehi parivuto jaṅghāvihāraṃ anucaṅkamamāno anuvicaramāno yena keṇiyassa jaṭilassa assamo tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho selo brāhmaṇo keṇiyassa jaṭilassa assame appekacce uddhanāni khaṇante, appekacce kaṭṭhāni phālente, appekacce bhājanāni dhovante, appekacce udakamaṇikaṃ patiṭṭhāpente, appekacce āsanāni paññapente, keṇiyaṃ pana jaṭilaṃ sāmaṃyeva maṇḍalamālaṃ paṭiyādentaṃ. Disvāna keṇiyaṃ jaṭilaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘kiṃ nu bhoto keṇiyassa āvāho vā bhavissati vivāho vā bhavissati mahāyañño vā paccupaṭṭhito, rājā vā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro nimantito svātanāya saddhiṃ balakāyenā’’ti? ‘‘Na me, bho sela, āvāho bhavissati napi vivāho bhavissati napi rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro nimantito svātanāya saddhiṃ balakāyena; api ca kho me mahāyañño paccupaṭṭhito. Atthi, bho, samaṇo gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito aṅguttarāpesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ aḍḍhateḷasehi bhikkhusatehi āpaṇaṃ anuppatto. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. So me nimantito svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā’’ti.

‘‘Buddhoti – bho keṇiya, vadesi’’?

‘‘Buddhoti – bho sela, vadāmi’’.

‘‘Buddhoti – bho keṇiya, vadesi’’?

‘‘Buddhoti – bho sela, vadāmī’’ti.
mula_english:
397. At that time, Sela the *brāhmaṇa* was living in Apana. He had mastered the three Vedas, with their *nighaṇḍu* (glossaries), *keṭubha* (commentaries), and systems of phonology, as well as the *itihāsa* (tradition) as a fifth subject. He was skilled in *padaka* (grammar) and *veyyākaraṇa* (etymology), and was not deficient concerning the characteristics of the *lokāyata* and the great man. He had three hundred students recite *mantras*.

At that time, Keniya the ascetic had full confidence in Sela the *brāhmaṇa*.

Then Sela the *brāhmaṇa*, while walking and wandering for exercise attended by his three hundred brahmin students, came to the hermitage of Keniya the ascetic.

Sela the *brāhmaṇa* saw at the hermitage of Keniya the ascetic some men digging out ovens, some chopping wood, some washing dishes, some setting out water jugs (*udakamaṇikaṃ*), some preparing seats, while the ascetic Keniya himself was setting up a pavilion (*maṇḍalamālaṃ*).

Seeing Keniya the ascetic, he said this: “Friend Keniya, are you holding a marriage (*āvāho*)? Or a wedding (*vivāho*)? Or is a great sacrifice (*mahāyañño*) being prepared? Or has King Seniya Bimbisara of Magadha been invited for tomorrow’s meal together with a large retinue (*balakāyena*)?”

“No, Master Sela, I am not holding a marriage, nor a wedding, nor has King Seniya Bimbisara of Magadha been invited for tomorrow’s meal together with a large retinue; but a great sacrifice is being prepared for me."

“Sir, the *samaṇa* Gotama, the son of the Sakyans who went forth from a Sakyan clan, has been wandering in the country of the Anguttarapas with a large *saṅgha* of *bhikkhus*, with twelve hundred and fifty *bhikkhus*, and has come to Apana.”

And of that master Gotama this fine reputation has spread: ‘He is indeed a Blessed One (*bhagavā*), a Worthy One (*arahaṃ*), a Fully Enlightened One (*sammāsambuddho*), consummate in clear-knowing and conduct (*vijjācaraṇasampanno*), Well-Gone One (*sugato*), an expert with regard to the cosmos (*lokavidū*), unexcelled trainer of people fit to be tamed (*anuttaro purisadammasārathi*), teacher of gods and human beings (*satthā devamanussānaṃ*), awakened (*buddho*), blessed (*bhagavā*)’."

"He has been invited by me for tomorrow’s meal together with the *saṅgha* of *bhikkhus*.”

“Do you say, ‘Buddha’—friend Keniya?”

“‘Buddha’—friend Sela, I say.”

“Do you say, ‘Buddha’—friend Keniya?”

“‘Buddha’—friend Sela, I say.”
commentary_pali: 397.Āvāhoti kaññāgahaṇaṃ. Vivāhoti kaññādānaṃ. So me nimantitoti so mayā nimantito. Atha brāhmaṇo paripakkopanissayattā buddhasaddaṃ sutvāva amatenevābhisitto pasādaṃ āvikaronto buddhoti, bho keṇiya, vadesīti āha. Keṇiyo yathābhūtaṃ ācikkhanto buddhoti, bho sela, vadāmīti āha. Tato naṃ punapi daḷhīkaraṇatthaṃ pucchi, itaropi tatheva ārocesi.
commentary_english:
397. *Āvāha* means the acceptance of a maiden (*kaññāgrahaṇaṃ*).
*Vivāha* means the giving of a maiden (*kaññādānaṃ*).
"*So me nimantito*" means he was invited by me.
Then, the *brāhmaṇa*, because of the maturity of his supporting conditions, having heard the word of the Buddha and being as if sprinkled with *amṛta*, revealing joy, said, "*Buddhoti*, bho Keṇiya, *vadesi*."
Keṇiya, declaring the truth, said, "*Buddhoti*, bho Sela, *vadāmī*."
Then he asked him again for the sake of strengthening [his conviction], and the other also declared it in the same way.

mula_pali:
398. Atha kho selassa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi – ‘‘ghosopi kho eso dullabho lokasmiṃ – yadidaṃ ‘buddho’ti yadidaṃ buddho buddhoti (ka.). Āgatāni kho panamhākaṃ mantesu dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇāni, yehi samannāgatassa mahāpurisassa dveyeva gatiyo bhavanti anaññā. Sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā cāturanto vijitāvī janapadatthāvariyappatto sattaratanasamannāgato. Tassimāni satta ratanāni bhavanti, seyyathidaṃ – cakkaratanaṃ, hatthiratanaṃ, assaratanaṃ, maṇiratanaṃ, itthiratanaṃ, gahapatiratanaṃ, pariṇāyakaratanameva sattamaṃ. Parosahassaṃ kho panassa puttā bhavanti sūrā vīraṅgarūpā parasenappamaddanā. So imaṃ pathaviṃ sāgarapariyantaṃ adaṇḍena asatthena dhammena abhivijiya ajjhāvasati. Sace pana agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati, arahaṃ hoti sammāsambuddho loke vivaṭṭacchado’’.

‘‘Kahaṃ pana, bho keṇiya, etarahi so bhavaṃ gotamo viharati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho’’ti? Evaṃ vutte, keṇiyo jaṭilo dakkhiṇaṃ bāhuṃ paggahetvā selaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘yenesā, bho sela, nīlavanarājī’’ti. Atha kho selo brāhmaṇo tīhi māṇavakasatehi saddhiṃ yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami. Atha kho selo brāhmaṇo te māṇavake āmantesi – ‘‘appasaddā bhonto āgacchantu pade padaṃ pāde pādaṃ (sī.) nikkhipantā; durāsadā dūrasaddā (ka.) hi te bhagavanto sīhāva ekacarā. Yadā cāhaṃ, bho, samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ manteyyaṃ, mā me bhonto antarantarā kathaṃ opātetha. Kathāpariyosānaṃ me bhavanto āgamentū’’ti. Atha kho selo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho selo brāhmaṇo bhagavato kāye dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇāni samannesi.

pāde pādaṃ (sī.) dūrasaddā (ka.)

Addasā kho selo brāhmaṇo bhagavato kāye dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇāni, yebhuyyena ṭhapetvā dve. Dvīsu mahāpurisalakkhaṇesu kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati – kosohite ca vatthaguyhe, pahūtajivhatāya ca. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – ‘‘passati kho me ayaṃ selo brāhmaṇo dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇāni, yebhuyyena ṭhapetvā dve. Dvīsu mahāpurisalakkhaṇesu kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati – kosohite ca vatthaguyhe, pahūtajivhatāya cā’’ti. Atha kho bhagavā tathārūpaṃ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkhāsi, yathā addasa selo brāhmaṇo bhagavato kosohitaṃ vatthaguyhaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā jivhaṃ ninnāmetvā ubhopi kaṇṇasotāni anumasi paṭimasi; ubhopi nāsikasotāni anumasi paṭimasi; kevalampi nalāṭamaṇḍalaṃ jivhāya chādesi. Atha kho selassa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi – ‘‘samannāgato kho samaṇo gotamo dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇehi paripuṇṇehi, no aparipuṇṇehi; no ca kho naṃ jānāmi buddho vā no vā. Sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ vuddhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘ye te bhavanti arahanto sammāsambuddhā te sake vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attānaṃ pātukarontī’ti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ sammukhā sāruppāhi gāthāhi abhitthaveyya’’nti.
mula_english:
398. Then the brāhmaṇa Sela thought: "Even the sound 'Buddha' is rare in the world. The thirty-two marks of a great man [mahāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇa] have come down to us in the mantras, and for a great man endowed with them, there are only two possible destinies. If he lives the household life, he becomes a Wheel-turning Monarch (cakravartin), a righteous king who rules by the Dhamma, master of the four quarters, all-victorious, who has stabilised his country and possesses the seven treasures. These are his seven treasures: the wheel-treasure (cakra-ratana), the elephant-treasure (hasti-ratana), the horse-treasure (aśva-ratana), the jewel-treasure (maṇi-ratana), the woman-treasure (strī-ratana), the steward-treasure (gṛhapati-ratana), and the counsellor-treasure (pariṇāyaka-ratana) as the seventh. He has more than a thousand sons who are heroes, of heroic stature, conquerors of the hostile army. Over this earth bounded by the ocean, he rules without a rod, without a weapon, by means of the Dhamma. But if he goes forth from the home life into homelessness, then he will become an *arhat*, a fully-enlightened Buddha (sammā-sambuddha), one who draws back the veil from the world."

"Where, Keṇiya, is the venerable Gotama, the *arhat*, the Fully Enlightened Buddha, residing at present?" When this was said, the ascetic Keṇiya raised his right arm and said to the brāhmaṇa Sela, "That, Sela, is the line of blue forest."

Then the brāhmaṇa Sela went with three hundred brahmin students to the Blessed One (bhagavān). Then the brāhmaṇa Sela addressed the brahmin students: "Come quietly, sirs, tread carefully; for these Blessed Ones are difficult to approach, they wander alone like lions. When I am speaking with the *śramaṇa* Gotama, do not break in and interrupt me, but wait until our talk is finished."

Then the brāhmaṇa Sela went to the Blessed One; having gone there, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. Having concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down at one side. Seated at one side, the brāhmaṇa Sela examined the Blessed One’s body for the thirty-two marks of a great man [mahāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇa].

The brāhmaṇa Sela saw the thirty-two marks of a great man on the Blessed One’s body, except for two, more or less. He doubted and was uncertain about two marks of a great man, he was not decided, he was not confident – the sheathed genitals (*koso-hite*) and the extensive tongue (*pahūtajivhatā*).

Then the Blessed One thought: "This brahmin Sela sees the thirty-two marks of a great man on me, except for two, more or less. He doubts and is uncertain about two marks of a great man, he is not decided, he is not confident – the sheathed genitals and the extensive tongue."

Then the Blessed One performed such a feat of supernormal power that the brāhmaṇa Sela saw that the Blessed One’s male organ was enclosed in a sheath. Then the Blessed One, having extended his tongue, touched and rubbed both ear-holes; he touched and rubbed both nostril-holes; he covered his entire forehead with his tongue.

Then the brāhmaṇa Sela thought: "The *śramaṇa* Gotama is endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man, complete, not incomplete; but I do not know whether he is a Buddha or not. I have heard that when the praise of those who are *arhats*, Fully Enlightened Buddhas, is spoken, they reveal themselves in their true form."

"Suppose I extol the *śramaṇa* Gotama to his face with fitting verses."
commentary_pali: 398. Athassa kappasatasahassehipi buddhasaddasseva dullabhabhāvaṃ sampassato. Etadahosīti. Etaṃ ‘‘ghosopi kho’’tiādi ahosi. Nīlavanarājīti nīlavaṇṇarukkhapanti. Pade padanti padappamāṇe padaṃ. Accāsanne hi atidūre vā pāde nikkhipamāne saddo uṭṭhāti, taṃ paṭisedhento evamāha. Sīhāva ekacarāti gaṇavāsī sīho sīhapotakādīhi saddhiṃ pamādaṃ āpajjati, ekacaro appamatto hoti. Iti appamādavihāraṃ dassento ekacarasīhena opammaṃ karoti. Mā me bhontoti ācāraṃ sikkhāpento āha. Ayañhettha adhippāyo – sace tumhe kathāvāraṃ alabhitvā mama kathāya antare kathaṃ pavesessatha, ‘‘antevāsike sikkhāpetuṃ nāsakkhī’’ti mayhaṃ garahā uppajjissati, tasmā okāsaṃ passitvā manteyyāthāti. No ca kho naṃ jānāmīti vipassīpi bodhisatto caturāsītisahassattherapabbajitaparivāro satta māsāni bodhisattacārikaṃ cari, buddhuppādakālo viya ahosi. Amhākampi bodhisatto chabbassāni bodhisattacārikaṃ cari. Evaṃ paripuṇṇasarīralakkhaṇehi samannāgatāpi buddhā na honti. Tasmā brāhmaṇo ‘‘no ca kho naṃ jānāmī’’ti āha.
commentary_english:
398. Then, as he was contemplating the difficulty of encountering a Buddha, even after hundreds of thousands of eons, the following occurred to him.

This was the beginning of "Even the sound..."

*Nīlavanarājī* means a row of blue-colored trees.

*Pade pada* means a foot [placed] at the measure of a foot.

When a foot is placed very close or very far away, a sound arises; thus, preventing it, he said as follows.

*Sīhāva ekacarā* means that a lion that dwells in a group falls into negligence together with lion cubs, etc.; a solitary one is mindful.

Thus, showing the dwelling of mindfulness, he makes a comparison to a solitary lion.

*Mā me bhonto* means teaching conduct, he said.

Herein lies the intention: If you, without obtaining a chance to speak, insert a word in the middle of my speech, the criticism will arise against me that "he was not able to train his disciples"; therefore, having seen an opportunity, you should speak.

*No ca kho naṃ jānāmī* means Vipassī Bodhisattva, surrounded by a retinue of eighty-four thousand elder renunciates, practiced the Bodhisattva conduct for seven months; it was like the time of a Buddha's arising.

Also, our Bodhisattva practiced the Bodhisattva conduct for six years.

Thus, even Buddhas who are endowed with fully complete bodily characteristics do not [necessarily] exist.

Therefore, the *brāhmaṇa* said, "*No ca kho naṃ jānāmī*."

mula_pali:
399. Atha kho selo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ sammukhā sāruppāhi gāthāhi abhitthavi –

‘‘Paripuṇṇakāyo suruci, sujāto cārudassano;

Suvaṇṇavaṇṇosi bhagavā, susukkadāṭhosi vīriyavā viriyavā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.).

viriyavā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)

‘‘Narassa hi sujātassa, ye bhavanti viyañjanā;

Sabbe te tava kāyasmiṃ, mahāpurisalakkhaṇā.

‘‘Pasannanetto sumukho, brahā brahmā (syā. kaṃ. ka.) uju patāpavā;

brahmā (syā. kaṃ. ka.)

Majjhe samaṇasaṅghassa, ādiccova virocasi.

‘‘Kalyāṇadassano bhikkhu, kañcanasannibhattaco;

Kiṃ te samaṇabhāvena, evaṃ uttamavaṇṇino.

‘‘Rājā arahasi bhavituṃ, cakkavattī rathesabho;

Cāturanto vijitāvī, jambusaṇḍassa jambumaṇḍassa (ka.) issaro.

jambumaṇḍassa (ka.)

‘‘Khattiyā bhogirājāno, anuyantā anuyuttā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) bhavantu te;

anuyuttā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)

Rājābhirājā manujindo, rajjaṃ kārehi gotama’’.

‘‘Rājāhamasmi selāti, dhammarājā anuttaro;

Dhammena cakkaṃ vattemi, cakkaṃ appaṭivattiyaṃ’’.

‘‘Sambuddho paṭijānāsi, dhammarājā anuttaro;

‘Dhammena cakkaṃ vattemi’, iti bhāsasi gotama.

‘‘Ko nu senāpati bhoto, sāvako satthuranvayo;

Ko te tamanuvatteti, dhammacakkaṃ pavattitaṃ’’.

‘‘Mayā pavattitaṃ cakkaṃ, (selāti bhagavā dhammacakkaṃ anuttaraṃ;

Sāriputto anuvatteti, anujāto tathāgataṃ.

‘‘Abhiññeyyaṃ abhiññātaṃ, bhāvetabbañca bhāvitaṃ;

Pahātabbaṃ pahīnaṃ me, tasmā buddhosmi brāhmaṇa.

‘‘Vinayassu mayi kaṅkhaṃ, adhimuccassu brāhmaṇa;

Dullabhaṃ dassanaṃ hoti, sambuddhānaṃ abhiṇhaso.

‘‘Yesaṃ ve dullabho loke, pātubhāvo abhiṇhaso;

Sohaṃ brāhmaṇa sambuddho, sallakatto anuttaro.

‘‘Brahmabhūto atitulo, mārasenappamaddano;

Sabbāmitte vasī katvā, modāmi akutobhayo’’.

‘‘Imaṃ bhonto nisāmetha, yathā bhāsati cakkhumā;

Sallakatto mahāvīro, sīhova nadatī vane.

‘‘Brahmabhūtaṃ atitulaṃ, mārasenappamaddanaṃ;

Ko disvā nappasīdeyya, api kaṇhābhijātiko.

‘‘Yo maṃ icchati anvetu, yo vā nicchati gacchatu;

Idhāhaṃ pabbajissāmi, varapaññassa santike’’.

‘‘Etañce evañce (syā. kaṃ.) ruccati bhoto, sammāsambuddhasāsanaṃ sammāsambuddhasāsane (katthaci suttanipāte);

evañce (syā. kaṃ.) sammāsambuddhasāsane (katthaci suttanipāte)

Mayampi pabbajissāma, varapaññassa santike’’.

‘‘Brāhmaṇā tisatā ime, yācanti pañjalīkatā;

Brahmacariyaṃ carissāma, bhagavā tava santike’’.

‘‘Svākkhātaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, (selāti bhagavā sandiṭṭhikamakālikaṃ;

Yattha amoghā pabbajjā, appamattassa sikkhato’’ti.

Alattha kho selo brāhmaṇo sapariso bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampadaṃ.
mula_english:
399. Then Sela the *brāhmaṇa*, facing the Blessed One, praised him with fitting verses:

"Perfect in body, of good appearance, well-born, charming to behold;

Of golden hue, O Blessed One, with exceedingly white teeth, O energetic one.

[Considering the case] when the body of a well-born man is tolerant of all medicines,

All those marks of a great man are in your body.

With a serene eye, with a beautiful face, Brahma, upright, powerful;

In the midst of the *śramaṇa* assembly, you shine like the sun.

O *bhikṣu* of auspicious appearance, with skin like gold;

What is the point of your *śramaṇa* state, O one of such excellent color?

You deserve to be a king, a wheel-turning monarch, a leader of chariots;

A conqueror of the four quarters, lord of Jambusaṇḍa.

Kṣatriyas, enjoying kings, followers, let them be yours;

King of kings, lord of men, rule the kingdom, Gotama."

"I am a king, Sela, a righteous king, unsurpassed;

By the Dharma I turn the wheel, a wheel that cannot be turned back."

"You acknowledge yourself as the Awakened One, a righteous king, unsurpassed;

'By the Dharma I turn the wheel,' so you say, Gotama.

Who is your general, a disciple following the teacher;

Who conforms to you, [so that] the wheel of Dharma is set in motion?"
"The wheel has been set in motion by me," said the Blessed One, "the unsurpassed wheel of the Dharma; Sāriputta turns it, born after the Thus-Gone One (Tathāgata)."

"What should be directly known has been directly known, and what should be developed has been developed; what should be abandoned has been abandoned by me; therefore, Brahmin, I am a Buddha."

"Brahmin, dispel your doubt in me, be convinced! Rare is the sight of fully awakened Buddhas."

"He whose appearance in the world is very rare, I am that awakened Buddha, Brahmin, the unsurpassed surgeon."

"Having become Brahman-like, without equal, the destroyer of the army of Māra, having made all enemies subject, I rejoice, fearless from anywhere."

"Listen to this, good sirs, how the one with vision speaks; the surgeon, the great hero, roars like a lion in the forest."

"Having become Brahman-like, without equal, the destroyer of the army of Māra, who, even though of outcast birth, would not be pleased upon seeing [him]?"

"Whoever wishes [to follow] me, let him come; whoever does not wish [to follow], let him go; here I will renounce [the world] in the presence of the one with excellent wisdom."

"If the dispensation of the truly awakened Buddha pleases you, we also will renounce [the world] in the presence of the one with excellent wisdom."

"These three hundred Brahmins, with hands joined in reverence, request; we will live the holy life, Blessed One, in your presence."

"Well-proclaimed is the holy life," said the Blessed One, "visible here and now, timeless; where the going forth is not in vain, for one who is heedful and learning."

Then the Brahmin Sela, together with his followers, received the going forth in the presence of the Blessed One, and he received the higher ordination (upasampadā).
commentary_pali:
399.Paripuṇṇakāyoti lakkhaṇehi paripuṇṇatāya ahīnaṅgatāya ca paripuṇṇasarīro. Surucīti sundarasarīrappabho. Sujātoti ārohapariṇāhasampattiyā saṇṭhānasampattiyā ca sunibbatto. Cārudassanoti sucirampi passantānaṃ atittijanako manoharadassano. Suvaṇṇavaṇṇoti suvaṇṇasadisavaṇṇo. Susukkadāṭhoti suṭṭhu sukkadāṭho. Mahāpurisalakkhaṇāti paṭhamaṃ vuttabyañjanāneva vacanantarena nigamento āha.

Idāni tesu lakkhaṇesu attano cittarucitāni gahetvā thomento pasannanettotiādimāha. Bhagavā hi pañcavaṇṇapasādasampattiyā pasannanetto, puṇṇacandasadisamukhatāya sumukho, ārohapariṇāhasampattiyā brahā, brahmujugattatāya uju, jutimantatāya patāpavā. Yampi cettha pubbe vuttaṃ, taṃ ‘‘majjhe samaṇasaṅghassā’’ti iminā pariyāyena thomayatā puna vuttaṃ. Ediso hi evaṃ virocati. Uttaragāthāyapi eseva nayo. Uttamavaṇṇīnoti uttamavaṇṇasampannassa. Rathesabhoti uttamasārathi. Jambusaṇḍassāti jambudīpassa. Pākaṭena issariyaṃ issaro hoti.

pasannanetto pasannanetto, sumukho, brahā, uju, patāpavā Uttamavaṇṇīno Rathesabho Jambusaṇḍassā

Khattiyāti jātikhattiyā. Bhogīti bhogiyā. Rājānoti ye keci rajjaṃ kārentā. Rājābhirājāti rājūnaṃ pūjanīyo, adhirājā hutvā, cakkavattīti adhippāyo. Manujindoti manussādhipati paramissaro hutvā.

Khattiyā Bhogī Rājāno Rājābhirājā Manujindo

Evaṃ vutte bhagavā – ‘‘ye te bhavanti arahanto sammāsambuddhā, te sakavaṇṇe bhaññamāne attānaṃ pātukarontī’’ti imaṃ selassa manorathaṃ pūrento rājāhamasmītiādimāha. Tatrāyamadhippāyo – yaṃ maṃ tvaṃ sela ‘‘rājā arahasi bhavitu’’nti yācasi, ettha appossukko hoti rājāhamasmi. Sati ca rājatte yathā añño rājā yojanasataṃ vā anusāsati yojanasahassaṃ vā, cakkavattī hutvāpi catudīpapariyantamattaṃ vā, nāhamevaṃ paricchinnavisayo, ahañhi dhammarājā anuttaro bhavaggato avīcipariyantaṃ katvā tiriyaṃ appamāṇalokadhātuyo anusāsāmi. Yāvatā hi apadadvipadādibhedā sattā, ahaṃ tesaṃ aggo. Na hi me koci sīlena vā…pe… vimuttiñāṇadassanena vā paṭibhāgo atthi, svāhaṃ evaṃ dhammarājā anuttaro anuttareneva catusatipaṭṭhānādibhedena dhammena cakkaṃ vattemi. Idaṃ pajahatha, idaṃ upasampajja viharathāti āṇācakkaṃ, idaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ ariyasaccantiādinā pariyattidhammena dhammacakkameva vā. Cakkaṃ appaṭivattiyanti yaṃ cakkaṃ appaṭivattiyaṃ hoti samaṇena vā…pe… kenaci vā lokasminti.

rājāhamasmī rājāhamasmi dhammarājā anuttaro dhammena cakkaṃ vattemi Cakkaṃ appaṭivattiya

Evaṃ attānaṃ āvikarontaṃ bhagavantaṃ disvā pītisomanassajāto selo puna daḷhīkaraṇatthaṃ sambuddho paṭijānāsīti gāthādvayamāha. Tattha ko nu senāpatīti rañño bhoto dhammena pavattitassa cakkassa anupavattako senāpati ko nūti pucchi.

sambuddho paṭijānāsī ko nu senāpatī

Tena ca samayena bhagavato dakkhiṇapasse āyasmā sāriputto nisinno hoti suvaṇṇapuñjo viya siriyā sobhamāno, taṃ dassento bhagavā mayā pavattitanti gāthamāha. Tattha anujāto tathāgatanti tathāgataṃ hetuṃ anujāto, tathāgatena hetunā jātoti attho. Apica avajāto anujāto atijātoti tayo vuttā. Tesu avajāto dussīlo, so tathāgatassa putto nāma na hoti. Atijāto nāma pitarā uttaritaro, tādisopi tathāgatassa putto natthi. Tathāgatassa pana eko anujātova putto hoti, taṃ dassento evamāha.

mayā pavattita anujāto tathāgata

Evaṃ ‘‘ko nu senāpatī’’ti pañhaṃ byākaritvā yaṃ selo āha ‘‘sambuddho paṭijānāsī’’ti, tatra naṃ nikkaṅkhaṃ kātukāmo ‘‘nāhaṃ paṭiññāmatteneva paṭijānāmi, apicāhaṃ iminā kāraṇena buddho’’ti ñāpetuṃ abhiññeyyanti gāthamāha. Tatra abhiññeyyanti vijjā ca vimutti ca. Bhāvetabbaṃ maggasaccaṃ. Pahātabbaṃ samudayasaccaṃ. Hetuvacanena pana phalasiddhito tesaṃ phalāni nirodhasaccadukkhasaccānipi vuttāneva honti. Evaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ pariññātabbaṃ pariññātanti idampettha saṅgahitanti catusaccabhāvanāphalañca vimuttiñca dassento ‘‘bujjhitabbaṃ bujjhitvā buddho jātosmī’’ti yuttahetunā buddhabhāvaṃ sādheti.

abhiññeyya abhiññeyya Bhāvetabbaṃ Pahātabbaṃ

Evaṃ nippariyāyena attānaṃ āvikatvā attani kaṅkhāvitaraṇatthaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ aticāriyamāno vinayassūti gāthattayamāha. Tattha sallakattoti rāgādisallakantano. Anuttaroti yathā bāhiravejjena vūpasamitarogo imasmiññevattabhāve kuppati, na evaṃ. Mayā vūpasamitassa pana rogassa bhavantarepi uppatti natthi, tasmā ahaṃ anuttaroti attho. Brahmabhūtoti seṭṭhabhūto. Atituloti tulaṃ atīto, nirupamoti attho. Mārasenappamaddanoti kāmā te paṭhamā senāti evaṃ āgatāya mārasenāya pamaddano. Sabbāmitteti khandhakilesābhisaṅkhāramaccudevaputtamārasaṅkhāte sabbapaccatthike. Vasīkatvāti attano vase vattetvā. Akutobhayoti kutoci abhayo.

vinayassū sallakatto Anuttaro Brahmabhūto Atitulo Mārasenappamaddano Sabbāmitte Vasīkatvā Akutobhayo

Evaṃ vutte selo brāhmaṇo tāvadeva bhagavati sañjātapasādo pabbajjāpekkho hutvā imaṃ bhontoti gāthattayamāha. Tattha kaṇhābhijātikoti caṇḍālādinīcakule jāto. Tato tepi māṇavakā pabbajjāpekkhā hutvā evañce ruccati, bhototi gāthamāhaṃsu. Atha selo tesu māṇavakesu tuṭṭhacitto te ca dassento pabbajjaṃ yācanto ‘‘brāhmaṇā’’ti gāthamāha.

imaṃ bhonto kaṇhābhijātiko evañce ruccati, bhoto ‘‘brāhmaṇā’’

Tato bhagavā yasmā selo atīte padumuttarassa bhagavato sāsane tesaṃyeva tiṇṇaṃ purisasatānaṃ gaṇaseṭṭho hutvā tehi saddhiṃ pariveṇaṃ kāretvā dānādīni puññāni katvā tena kammena devamanussasampattiṃ anubhavamāno pacchime bhave tesaṃyeva ācariyo hutvā nibbatto, tañca tesaṃ kammaṃ vimuttiparipākāya paripakkaṃ ehibhikkhubhāvassa ca upanissayabhūtaṃ, tasmā te sabbeva ehibhikkhupabbajjaṃ pabbājento svākkhātanti gāthamāha. Tattha sandiṭṭhikanti sayameva daṭṭhabbaṃ paccakkhaṃ. Akālikanti maggānantaraphaluppattiyā na kālantaraṃ pattabbaphalaṃ. Yattha amoghāti yasmiṃ maggabrahmacariye appamattassa sikkhattayapūraṇena sikkhato pabbajjā amoghā hoti, saphalāti attho. Evañca vatvā ‘‘etha bhikkhavo’’ti bhagavā avoca. Te sabbe pattacīvaradharā hutvā ākāsenāgantvā vassasatikattherā viya suvinītā bhagavantaṃ abhivādayiṃsu. Evamimaṃ tesaṃ ehibhikkhubhāvaṃ sandhāya ‘‘alattha kho selo’’tiādi vuttaṃ.

svākkhāta sandiṭṭhika Akālika Yattha amoghā
commentary_english:
399. *Paripuṇṇakāyo* means having a fully developed body, complete with all auspicious marks and without any deficient bodily parts, thus a perfect body.

*Surucī* means having a beautiful bodily radiance.

*Sujāto* means being well-born, having excellent height, circumference and a well-formed constitution.

*Cārudassano* means having a pleasing appearance, never satiating those who gaze upon him, and possessing an enchanting form.

*Suvaṇṇavaṇṇo* means having a complexion like that of gold.

*Susukkadāṭho* means having very white teeth.

*Mahāpurisalakkhaṇā* means the previously mentioned characteristics of a great man, summarized in different words.

Now, having taken those characteristics that are pleasing to his own mind from among those marks, he praises [the Buddha], saying, "*pasannanetto*," and so forth.

Indeed, the Blessed One, through the perfection of the fivefold radiance of purity, is *pasannanetto* (clear-eyed); through having a face like a full moon, he is *sumukho* (having a beautiful face); through the perfection of height and circumference, he is *brahā* (great); through having the uprightness of Brahmā, he is *uju* (upright); and through possessing splendor, he is *patāpavā* (powerful).

And that which was previously said here, that same thing is said again by way of praise, with this expression: "In the midst of the community of *śramaṇas*."

Such a one shines forth in this way.

The same method [applies] also in the subsequent verse.

*Uttamavaṇṇīno* means possessing the best complexion.

*Rathesabho* means being the best charioteer.

*Jambusaṇḍassā* means [being the lord] of Jambudvīpa (rose-apple island).

Through manifest sovereignty, he is *īśvara* (lord).

*Pasannanetto, pasannanetto, sumukho, brahā, uju, patāpavā, uttamavaṇṇīno, rathesabho, jambusaṇḍassā.*

*Khattiyā* means a noble by birth.

*Bhogī* means wealthy.

*Rājāno* means those who cause kingdoms to be ruled [justly].

*Rājābhirājā* means worthy of being honored by kings, having become a sovereign, the idea [is] a *cakravartin* (wheel-turning monarch).

*Manujindo* means lord of men, having become the supreme lord.

*Khattiyā, bhogī, rājāno, rājābhirājā, manujindo.*

Having spoken thus, the Blessed One, fulfilling the aspiration of Sela, said, "*rājāhamasmī*," and so forth: "Those who become *arhats*, perfectly awakened ones, reveal themselves in every way."

There, this is the meaning: "That which you, Sela, ask of me, 'You deserve to be a king,' in this, there is little desire," [for] "*rājāhamasmi*," I am a king!

And while kingship exists, just as another king rules a hundred *yojanas* or a thousand *yojanas*, or even having become a *cakravartin*, [his dominion extends] only to the limit of the four continents; I am not one whose domain is thus limited. I, indeed, am a *dharmarājā* (righteous king), unsurpassed, having reached the highest existence, having made [my realm] extend to the limit of Avīci [hell], and across the world systems that are immeasurable.

As far as there are beings of different kinds, such as footless ones and bipeds, I am the foremost among them.

Indeed, for me there is no equal in virtue, or…in the knowledge and vision of liberation; therefore, I, as a righteous king, unsurpassed, by that very unsurpassed Dharma, set in motion the Wheel of Dharma.

"Abandon this; attain this and abide," [this is] the Wheel of Command; and, "This, indeed, *bhikṣus*, is suffering, the noble truth," and so forth, by means of the Dharma of instruction, it is indeed the Wheel of Dharma.

*Cakkaṃ appaṭivattiya* means the wheel that cannot be turned back, which is not able to be turned back by a *śramaṇa*, or…by anyone in the world.

*Rājāhamasmī, rājāhamasmi, dhammarājā anuttaro, dhammena cakkaṃ vattemi, cakkaṃ appaṭivattiya.*

Having seen the Blessed One revealing himself in this way, Sela, born of joy and gladness, in order to strengthen [his faith], said these two verses, "*sambuddho paṭijānāsī*": "You declare yourself to be the Awakened One!"
Therein, *ko nu senāpatī* means, "Who is the general who continues the wheel, rolling on in accordance with the Dhamma, of the Blessed Lord, the King?" Thus he asked.

*Sambuddho paṭijānāsī, ko nu senāpatī:* At that time, the venerable Sāriputta was seated on the Blessed One's right side, shining with glory like a heap of gold. Showing him, the Blessed One spoke this verse, *mayā pavattita*.

Therein, *anujāto tathāgata* means that he is born after the cause, the *tathāgata*; that is, he is born from the *tathāgata* as cause.

Moreover, there are said to be three types: *avajāto*, *anujāto*, and *atijāto*.

Of these, the *avajāto* is immoral; he is not called a son of the *tathāgata*.

The *atijāto* is superior to his father; even such a one is not a son of the *tathāgata*.

But the *tathāgata* has only one kind of son, the *anujāto*; showing him, he said this:

*Mayā pavattita, anujāto tathāgata:* Thus, having answered the question, "Who is the general?", Sela said, "You claim to be a fully enlightened one ( *sambuddho paṭijānāsī*)." There, wishing to make him free from doubt, [the Buddha], to make it known that "I do not claim [enlightenment] merely by making a claim, but I am enlightened by this reason," spoke this verse, *abhiññeyya*.

Therein, *abhiññeyya* means knowledge ( *vijjā*) and liberation (*vimutti*).

The truth of the path (*maggasacca*) is to be developed (*bhāvetabbaṃ*).

The truth of the origin (*samudayasaccaṃ*) is to be abandoned (*pahātabbaṃ*).

By the statement of the cause, however, from the accomplishment of the fruit, their fruits, the truth of cessation (*nirodhasacca*) and the truth of suffering (*dukkhasacca*), are indeed stated.

Thus, showing that "It is to be realized (*sacchikātabbaṃ*), it is realized (*sacchikataṃ*), it is to be fully known (*pariññātabbaṃ*), it is fully known (*pariññātaṃ*)," this too is included here, the fruit of the development of the four truths and liberation,

Showing [this], "It is to be understood (*bujjhitabbaṃ*), having understood, I am born enlightened (*buddho jātosmī*)," by a fitting reason, he demonstrates Buddhahood.

*Abhiññeyya, abhiññeyya, bhāvetabbaṃ, pahātabbaṃ*

Thus, without a break, having revealed himself, and while [Sela] was approaching him, wishing to dispel doubt in himself, he spoke these three verses, *vinayassū*.

Therein, *sallakatto* means the cutter of the dart of craving, and so on.

*Anuttaro* means that just as a disease subdued by an external physician flares up again in this very existence, it is not so [with me].

But for the disease subdued by me, there is no arising even in another existence; therefore, I am *anuttaro*. Such is the meaning.

*Brahmabhūto* means he has become the best.

*Atitulo* means he has gone beyond measure; he is incomparable. Such is the meaning.

*Mārasenappamaddano* means that he is the destroyer of the army of Māra, which has come thus, with desires as its first army.

*Sabbāmitte* means all enemies, reckoned as the aggregates, defilements, *abhisaṅkhāra*, death, the *devaputta* Māra—all adversaries.

*Vasīkatvā* means having brought [them] under his control.

*Akutobhayo* means without fear from anywhere.

*Vinayassū, sallakatto, anuttaro, brahmabhūto, atitulo, mārasenappamaddano, sabbāmitte, vasīkatvā, akutobhayo*

Thus spoken, Sela the brahmin, with faith arisen in the Blessed One, seeking ordination, spoke these three verses, *imaṃ bhonto*.

Therein, *kaṇhābhijātiko* means born in a low family, a *caṇḍāla*, and so on.

Then those youths too, seeking ordination, spoke this verse, *evañce ruccati, bhoto*.

Then Sela, with his mind pleased with those youths, showing them too, asking for ordination, spoke this verse, *‘‘brāhmaṇā’’*.

*Imaṃ bhonto, kaṇhābhijātiko, evañce ruccati, bhoto, ‘‘brāhmaṇā’’*

Then, since the Blessed One, in the past, in the dispensation of the Blessed Padumuttara, having been the chief of the group of those very three hundred men, having had a monastery built together with them, and having performed meritorious deeds such as giving, was experiencing the prosperity of gods and humans by that deed, and in the last existence, he was born as their teacher, and that deed of theirs was ripe for the maturation of liberation and was the basis for the state of "Come, *bhikkhu*," therefore, ordaining all of them with the "Come, *bhikkhu*" ordination, he spoke this verse, *svākkhāta*.

Therein, *sandiṭṭhika* means visible by oneself, directly.

*Akālika* means the fruit to be attained is not at another time, but with the arising of the fruit immediately after the path.

*Yattha amoghā* means that in whatever path-brahmacariya the going forth of one who is diligent, with the fulfillment of the three trainings, is not in vain, it is fruitful. Such is the meaning.

Having said this, the Blessed One said, "Come, *bhikkhus* (*etha bhikkhavo*)."

All of them, having become holders of bowl and robe, coming through the sky, like elders of a hundred years, well-trained, saluted the Blessed One.
Thus, with reference to their state of becoming a *ehibhikṣu* (a monk who is told "come!"), it is said, "Sela obtained...", and so forth.

svākkhāta, sandiṭṭhika, akālika, and yattha amoghā

mula_pali:
400. Atha kho keṇiyo jaṭilo tassā rattiyā accayena sake assame paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – ‘‘kālo, bho gotama, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta’’nti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena keṇiyassa jaṭilassa assamo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho keṇiyo jaṭilo buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi, sampavāresi. Atha kho keṇiyo jaṭilo bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ aññataraṃ nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho keṇiyaṃ jaṭilaṃ bhagavā imāhi gāthāhi anumodi –

‘‘Aggihuttamukhā yaññā, sāvittī chandaso mukhaṃ;

Rājā mukhaṃ manussānaṃ, nadīnaṃ sāgaro mukhaṃ.

‘‘Nakkhattānaṃ mukhaṃ cando, ādicco tapataṃ mukhaṃ;

Puññaṃ ākaṅkhamānānaṃ, saṅgho ve yajataṃ mukha’’nti.

Atha kho bhagavā keṇiyaṃ jaṭilaṃ imāhi gāthāhi anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

Atha kho āyasmā selo sapariso eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro kho panāyasmā selo sapariso arahataṃ ahosi. Atha kho āyasmā selo sapariso yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ cīvaraṃ katvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

‘‘Yaṃ taṃ saraṇamāgamma, ito aṭṭhami cakkhumā;

Sattarattena anuttarena (ka.) bhagavā, dantamha tava sāsane.

anuttarena (ka.)

‘‘Tuvaṃ buddho tuvaṃ satthā, tuvaṃ mārābhibhū muni;

Tuvaṃ anusaye chetvā, tiṇṇo tāresimaṃ pajaṃ.

‘‘Upadhī te samatikkantā, āsavā te padālitā;

Sīhova anupādāno, pahīnabhayabheravo.

‘‘Bhikkhavo tisatā ime, tiṭṭhanti pañjalīkatā;

Pāde vīra pasārehi, nāgā vandantu satthuno’’ti.

Selasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.
mula_english:
Then, Keṇiya the Jaṭila (matted-hair ascetic), at the end of that night, in his own hermitage, having had exquisite staple and non-staple food prepared, had the time announced to the Blessed One, "It is time, Master Gotama, the meal is ready."

Then the Blessed One, early in the morning, having dressed, taking his bowl and outer robe, went to the hermitage of Keṇiya the Jaṭila; on arrival, he sat down on the prepared seat together with the Saṅgha of monks.

Then Keṇiya the Jaṭila, with his own hands, served and satisfied the Saṅgha of monks, with the Buddha at its head, with exquisite staple and non-staple food.

Then Keṇiya the Jaṭila, after the Blessed One had finished eating and had withdrawn his hand from the bowl, taking a low seat, sat down on one side.

The Blessed One, being seated to one side, approved of Keṇiya the Jaṭila with these verses:

"The fire sacrifice is the chief of sacrifices; the Sāvitrī is the chief of meters;

The king is the chief of human beings; the ocean is the chief of rivers.

The moon is the chief of stars; the sun is the chief of things that shine;

The Saṅgha is the chief of those who yearn for merit when offering sacrifice."

Then the Blessed One, having expressed his appreciation to Keṇiya the Jaṭila with these verses, got up from his seat and departed.

Then, not long after, the venerable Sela with his following, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute, by realizing for themselves with direct knowledge, here and now entered upon and abided in that supreme goal of the holy life for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness.

He directly knew: “Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more coming to any state of being.”

Then the venerable Sela with his following became arahants.

Then the venerable Sela with his assembly went to the Blessed One. Having arranged his upper robe on one shoulder, extending his hands in reverential greeting towards the Blessed One, he addressed the Blessed One with these stanzas:

"That refuge to which I have come, you are the eighth, O Cakkhumā (one with vision);

In seven nights, O Blessed One, we have been tamed in your teaching.

You are the Buddha, you are the teacher, you are the sage who has conquered Māra;

You, having cut off tendencies, having crossed over, carry this population across.

Your defilements are transcended, your āsavas (cravings) are destroyed;

Like a lion, unattached, you have abandoned fear and dread.

These monks, three hundred in number, stand with joined palms;

Extend your feet, O hero, may the Nāgas (elephants; noble ones) pay homage to the teacher."

The Selasutta is finished, the second.
commentary_pali:
400.Imāhīti imāhi keṇiyassa cittānukūlāhi gāthāhi. Tattha aggiparicariyaṃ vinā brāhmaṇānaṃ yaññābhāvato ‘‘aggihuttamukhā yaññā’’ti vuttaṃ. Aggihuttaseṭṭhā aggijuhanappadhānāti attho. Vede sajjhāyantehi paṭhamaṃ sajjhāyitabbato, sāvittī, ‘‘chandaso mukha’’nti vutto. Manussānaṃ seṭṭhato rājā ‘‘mukha’’nti vutto. Nadīnaṃ ādhārato paṭisaraṇato ca sāgaro ‘‘mukha’’nti vutto. Candayogavasena ‘‘ajja kattikā ajja rohiṇī’’ti saññāṇato ālokakaraṇato sommabhāvato ca ‘‘nakkhattānaṃ mukhaṃ cando’’ti vuttaṃ. Tapantānaṃ aggattā ādicco ‘‘tapataṃ mukha’’nti vutto. Dakkhiṇeyyānaṃ pana aggattā visesena tasmiṃ samaye buddhappamukhaṃ saṅghaṃ sandhāya ‘‘puññaṃ ākaṅkhamānānaṃ, saṅgho eva yajataṃ mukha’’nti vuttaṃ. Tena saṅgho puññassa āyamukhanti dasseti.

Yaṃ taṃ saraṇanti aññaṃ byākaraṇagāthamāha. Tassattho – pañcahi cakkhūhi cakkhumā bhagavā yasmā mayaṃ ito aṭṭhame divase taṃ saraṇaṃ āgatamhā, tasmā attanā tava sāsane anuttarena damathena dantāmhā, aho te saraṇassa ānubhāvoti.

saraṇa

Tato paraṃ bhagavantaṃ dvīhi gāthāhi thometvā tatiyāya vandanaṃ yācanto bhikkhavo tisatā imetiādimāhāti.

bhikkhavo tisatā ime

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Selasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
400. *imāhī* thus.

 imāhi keṇiyassa cittānukūlāhi gāthāhi.
Therein, without the tending of fire, because of the absence of the Brahmins' sacrifice, it is said, "The *agni-hotra* is the mouth of sacrifices."
*aggihuttaseṭṭhā aggijuhanappadhānāti*—this is the meaning.
Because it is to be recited first by those reciting the Veda, the *sāvitrī*, is said to be "the mouth of the *chandas*."
Among humans, the king is the best; thus, he is said to be "the mouth."
Because the ocean is the support and refuge of rivers, it is said to be "the mouth."
Because of the force of lunar conjunctions, from the recognition that "today is *kārttikā*, today is *rohiṇī*," and because it makes light and has a pleasing nature, it is said that "the moon is the mouth of the *nakṣatras*."
Because the sun is the chief among those that are hot, it is said that "the sun is the mouth of those that are hot."
Moreover, because it is chief among those worthy of offerings, with special regard to the Saṃgha, with the Buddha at its head, at that time, it is said, "For those desiring merit (*puṇya*), the Saṃgha is indeed the mouth of those sacrificing."
Therefore, [the text] shows that the Saṃgha is the entrance-mouth (*āyamukha*) of merit (*puṇya*).

That which is *saraṇa*, another grammatical verse says.
Its meaning [is as follows]: “Because we, on the eighth day from here, have come to that *saraṇa*, the Blessed One (bhagavān), who has vision with five eyes (*cakṣūhi*), have been tamed by the unsurpassed *damatha* in your *śāsana*, O you, of your *saraṇa*, what *ānubhāva*!”

*saraṇa*
Then, after praising the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ) with two verses (*gāthāhi*) and asking for reverence (*vandanaṃ*) with a third, [he] says, "*bhikkhavo tisatā ime*," and so forth.

*bhikkhavo tisatā ime*
The *papañcasūdanī* commentary to the *majjhimanikāya*

The *selasuttavaṇṇanā* is finished.

mula_pali:
401. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena nānāverajjakānaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ pañcamattāni brāhmaṇasatāni sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasanti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Atha kho tesaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ etadahosi – ‘‘ayaṃ kho samaṇo gotamo cātuvaṇṇiṃ suddhiṃ paññapeti. Ko nu kho pahoti samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ asmiṃ vacane paṭimantetu’’nti? Tena kho pana samayena assalāyano nāma māṇavo sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasati daharo, vuttasiro, soḷasavassuddesiko jātiyā, tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ pāragū sanighaṇḍukeṭubhānaṃ sākkharappabhedānaṃ itihāsapañcamānaṃ, padako, veyyākaraṇo, lokāyatamahāpurisalakkhaṇesu anavayo. Atha kho tesaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ etadahosi – ‘‘ayaṃ kho assalāyano māṇavo sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasati daharo, vuttasiro, soḷasavassuddesiko jātiyā, tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ pāragū…pe… anavayo. So kho pahoti samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ asmiṃ vacane paṭimantetu’’nti.

Atha kho te brāhmaṇā yena assalāyano māṇavo tenupaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā assalāyanaṃ māṇavaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘ayaṃ, bho assalāyana , samaṇo gotamo cātuvaṇṇiṃ suddhiṃ paññapeti. Etu bhavaṃ assalāyano samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ asmiṃ vacane paṭimantetū’’ti paṭimantetunti (pī. ka.).

paṭimantetunti (pī. ka.)

Evaṃ vutte, assalāyano māṇavo te brāhmaṇe etadavoca – ‘‘samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo dhammavādī; dhammavādino ca pana duppaṭimantiyā bhavanti. Nāhaṃ sakkomi samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ asmiṃ vacane paṭimantetu’’nti. Dutiyampi kho te brāhmaṇā assalāyanaṃ māṇavaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘ayaṃ, bho assalāyana, samaṇo gotamo cātuvaṇṇiṃ suddhiṃ paññapeti. Etu bhavaṃ assalāyano samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ asmiṃ vacane paṭimantetu paṭimantetuṃ (sī. pī. ka.). Caritaṃ kho pana bhotā assalāyanena paribbājaka’’nti. Dutiyampi kho assalāyano māṇavo te brāhmaṇe etadavoca – ‘‘samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo dhammavādī; dhammavādino ca pana duppaṭimantiyā bhavanti . Nāhaṃ sakkomi samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ asmiṃ vacane paṭimantetu’’nti. Tatiyampi kho te brāhmaṇā assalāyanaṃ māṇavaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘ayaṃ, bho assalāyana, samaṇo gotamo cātuvaṇṇiṃ suddhiṃ paññapeti. Etu bhavaṃ assalāyano samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ asmiṃ vacane paṭimantetu paṭimantetuṃ (sī. pī. ka.). Caritaṃ kho pana bhotā assalāyanena paribbājakaṃ. Mā bhavaṃ assalāyano ayuddhaparājitaṃ parājayī’’ti.

paṭimantetuṃ (sī. pī. ka.) paṭimantetuṃ (sī. pī. ka.)

Evaṃ vutte, assalāyano māṇavo te brāhmaṇe etadavoca – ‘‘addhā kho ahaṃ bhavanto na labhāmi. Samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo dhammavādī; dhammavādino ca pana duppaṭimantiyā bhavanti. Nāhaṃ sakkomi samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ asmiṃ vacane paṭimantetunti. Api cāhaṃ bhavantānaṃ vacanena gamissāmī’’ti.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard:

On one occasion the Blessed One (bhagavā) was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jetavana, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park (ārāma).

At that time, a great number of Brahmins (brāhmaṇānam) from various districts, some five hundred, were residing in Sāvatthī, due to some particular business.

Then those Brahmins (brāhmaṇānam) had this thought: “This ascetic Gotama (gótamo) proclaims purification (śuddhiṃ) for all four castes (cātuvaṇṇiṃ).

Who now is capable of disputing with the ascetic Gotama (gótamo) about this assertion (vacane)?”

At that time, there was a brahmin student (māṇavo) named Assalāyana residing in Sāvatthī, a young man with shaven head, sixteen years of age, who by birth (jātiyā) was a master of the three Vedas (vedānaṃ), with their vocabularies, liturgy, phonology and etymology, and the histories as a fifth; skilled in philology and grammar; fully versed in natural philosophy (lokāyata) and in the marks of a great man (mahāpurisalakkhaṇesu).

Then those Brahmins (brāhmaṇānam) had this thought: "This Brahmin student (māṇavo) Assalāyana is staying in Sāvatthī, young, with shaven head, sixteen years of age by birth (jātiyā), a master of the three Vedas (vedānaṃ)… and fully versed in natural philosophy (lokāyata)."

"He is capable of disputing with the ascetic Gotama (gótamo) regarding this statement (vacane)."

Then the Brahmins (brāhmaṇā) went to where the Brahmin student (māṇavo) Assalāyana was; having gone there, they said this to the Brahmin student (māṇavaṃ) Assalāyana: "This ascetic (samaṇo) Gotama (gotamo) proclaims purification (śuddhiṃ) for the four castes (cātuvaṇṇiṃ).

Let Master (bhavaṃ) Assalāyana come and dispute with the ascetic Gotama (gotamena) about this assertion (vacane)."

When this was said, the brahmin student (māṇavo) Assalāyana said this to those Brahmins (brāhmaṇe): "The ascetic (samaṇo) Gotama (gotamo), is one who speaks about the *dharma* (dhammavādī); and those who speak about the *dharma* (dhammavādino) are difficult to dispute with.

I am not capable of disputing with the ascetic Gotama (gotamena) about this assertion (vacane)."

A second time those Brahmins (brāhmaṇā) said this to the Brahmin student (māṇavaṃ) Assalāyana: "This ascetic (samaṇo) Gotama (gotamo) proclaims purification (śuddhiṃ) for the four castes (cātuvaṇṇiṃ).

Let Master (bhavaṃ) Assalāyana come and dispute with the ascetic Gotama (gotamena) about this assertion (vacane). The training of a wanderer (paribbājaka) has been completed by Master Assalāyana."

A second time the Brahmin student (māṇavo) Assalāyana said this to those Brahmins (brāhmaṇe): "The ascetic (samaṇo) Gotama (gotamo) speaks about the *dharma* (dhammavādī); and those who speak about the *dharma* (dhammavādino) are difficult to dispute with.

I am not capable of disputing with the ascetic Gotama (gotamena) about this assertion (vacane)."

A third time those Brahmins (brāhmaṇā) said this to the Brahmin student (māṇavaṃ) Assalāyana: "This ascetic (samaṇo) Gotama (gotamo) proclaims purification (śuddhiṃ) for the four castes (cātuvaṇṇiṃ).

Let Master (bhavaṃ) Assalāyana come and dispute with the ascetic Gotama (gotamena) about this assertion (vacane). The training of a wanderer (paribbājakaṃ) has been completed by Master Assalāyana.

Let not Master (bhavaṃ) Assalāyana be defeated without a fight."
When this was said, the brahmin student Assalāyana said to those brahmins: “Indeed, sirs, I am unable to refute you. The *śramaṇa* Gautama, sirs, is one who speaks on the *dharma*; and those who speak on the *dharma* are difficult to dispute with. I am not able to dispute with the *śramaṇa* Gautama about this assertion. Still, sirs, at your bidding I will go.”
commentary_pali:
401.Evaṃme sutanti assalāyanasuttaṃ. Tattha nānāverajjakānanti aṅgamagadhādīhi nānappakārehi verajjehi āgatānaṃ, tesu vā raṭṭhesu jātasaṃvaḍḍhānantipi attho. Kenacidevāti yaññupāsanādinā aniyamitakiccena. Cātuvaṇṇinti catuvaṇṇasādhāraṇaṃ. Mayaṃ pana nhānasuddhiyā bhāvanāsuddhiyāpi brāhmaṇāva sujjhantīti vadāma, ayuttampi samaṇo gotamo karotīti maññamānā evaṃ cintayiṃsu. Vuttasiroti vāpitasiro.

Dhammavādīti sabhāvavādī. Duppaṭimantiyāti amhādisehi adhammavādīhi dukkhena paṭimantitabbā honti. Dhammavādino nāma parājayo na sakkā kātunti dasseti. Paribbājakanti pabbajjāvidhānaṃ, tayo vede uggahetvā sabbapacchā pabbajantā yehi mantehi pabbajanti, pabbajitā ca ye mante pariharanti, yaṃ vā ācāraṃ ācaranti, taṃ sabbaṃ bhotā caritaṃ sikkhitaṃ. Tasmā tuyhaṃ parājayo natthi, jayova bhavissatīti maññantā evamāhaṃsu.

Dhammavādī Duppaṭimantiyā Paribbājaka
commentary_english:
401.
Thus, "Thus have I heard the Assalāyana Sūtra."
There, *nānāverajjakāna* means those who have come from various kinds of foreign territories, such as Aṅga and Magadha, or it means that they were born and raised in those districts.
*kenacidevā* means through irregular activities such as sacrifice and worship.
*cātuvaṇṇi* means common to the four castes (cāturvarṇyasādhāraṇam).
We, however, say that Brahmins are purified by purification through bathing and also by purification through meditation. The *samaṇa* Gotama does even unsuitable things, so thinking, they considered thus.
*vuttasiro* means shaved head.

*dhammavādī* means asserting the nature.
*duppaṭimantiyā* means that they are to be answered with difficulty by us, the assertors of non-dharma, with suffering.
It shows that there is no way to defeat the *dhammavādino*.
