*paribbājaka* means the procedure for ordination (pravrajyāvidhānam): having learned the three Vedas, those who ordain last of all, with which mantras they ordain, and also which mantras the ordained recite, or whatever conduct they practice, all that is learned conduct by the venerable one.
Therefore, there is no defeat for you, only victory will occur, so thinking, they said thus.

*dhammavādī*, *duppaṭimantiyā*, *paribbājaka*

mula_pali: 402. Atha kho assalāyano māṇavo mahatā brāhmaṇagaṇena saddhiṃ yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho assalāyano māṇavo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘brāhmaṇā, bho gotama, evamāhaṃsu – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo; brāhmaṇova sukko vaṇṇo, kaṇho añño vaṇṇo; brāhmaṇova sujjhanti, no abrāhmaṇā; brāhmaṇāva brahmuno puttā orasā mukhato jātā brahmajā brahmanimmitā brahmadāyādā’ti. Idha bhavaṃ gotamo kimāhā’’ti? ‘‘Dissanti dissante (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) kho pana, assalāyana, brāhmaṇānaṃ brāhmaṇiyo utuniyopi gabbhiniyopi vijāyamānāpi pāyamānāpi. Te ca brāhmaṇiyonijāva samānā evamāhaṃsu – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo; brāhmaṇova sukko vaṇṇo, kaṇho añño vaṇṇo; brāhmaṇāva sujjhanti, no abrāhmaṇā; brāhmaṇāva brahmuno puttā orasā mukhato jātā brahmajā brahmanimmitā brahmadāyādā’’’ti. ‘‘Kiñcāpi bhavaṃ gotamo evamāha, atha khvettha brāhmaṇā evametaṃ maññanti – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo…pe… brahmadāyādā’’’ti.
mula_english:
Then, Assalāyana the youth, together with a large group of Brahmins, went to where the Blessed One was; on arrival, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One.

When this courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side.

Seated to one side, Assalāyana the youth said to the Blessed One: “Brahmins, Master Gotama, say thus: ‘Only Brahmins are the highest caste (varṇa), any other caste is inferior; only Brahmins are the fairest caste, any other caste is dark; only Brahmins are purified, not non-Brahmins; Brahmins alone are the true children of Brahmā, born from his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.’

What does the esteemed Gotama say about this?”

“Now, Assalāyana, Brahmin women are seen having their periods, becoming pregnant, giving birth, and giving suck.

And yet those who are born from the wombs of Brahmin women say thus: ‘Only Brahmins are the highest caste, any other caste is inferior; only Brahmins are the fairest caste, any other caste is dark; only Brahmins are purified, not non-Brahmins; Brahmins alone are the true children of Brahmā, born from his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.’“

“Although the esteemed Gotama says this, still the Brahmins think thus: ‘Only Brahmins are the highest caste…heirs of Brahmā.’“
commentary_pali: 402.Dissanti kho panātiādi tesaṃ laddhibhindanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tattha brāhmaṇiyoti brāhmaṇānaṃ puttapaṭilābhatthāya āvāhavivāhavasena kulā ānītā brāhmaṇiyo dissanti . Tā kho panetā aparena samayena utuniyopi honti, sañjātapupphāti attho. Gabbhiniyoti sañjātagabbhā. Vijāyamānāti puttadhītaro janayamānā. Pāyamānāti dārake thaññaṃ pāyantiyo. Yonijāva samānāti brāhmaṇīnaṃ passāvamaggena jātā samānā. Evamāhaṃsūti evaṃ vadanti. Kathaṃ? Brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo…pe… brahmadāyādāti. Yadi pana nesaṃ saccavacanaṃ siyā, brāhmaṇīnaṃ kucchi mahābrahmuno uro bhaveyya, brāhmaṇīnaṃ passāvamaggo mahābrahmuno mukhaṃ bhaveyya, ettāvatā ‘‘mayaṃ mahābrahmuno ure vasitvā mukhato nikkhantā’’ti vattuṃ mā labhantūti ayaṃ mukhato jātacchedakavādo vutto.
commentary_english:
402. "Dissanti kho panā," etc., was spoken to break their views.

There, "brāhmaṇiyo" means brāhmaṇas’ wives brought from families by means of marriage in order to obtain sons.

Furthermore, after some time, these become "utuniyopi," the meaning is having flowers.

"Gabbhiniyo" means having conceived.

"Vijāyamānā" means generating sons and daughters.

"Pāyamānā" means those who cause infants to drink milk.

"Yonijāva samānā" means being born the same from the brāhmaṇīs’ urinary tract.

"Evamāhaṃsū" means thus they say.

How? "brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo…pe… brahmadāyādā."

If their statement were true, the brāhmaṇīs’ womb would be the chest of Mahābrahmā, the brāhmaṇīs’ urinary tract would be the mouth of Mahābrahmā; to that extent, they should not obtain to say, "We, dwelling in the chest of Mahābrahmā, emerged from the mouth"; this is the statement of cutting off birth from the mouth.

mula_pali: 403. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, assalāyana, sutaṃ te – ‘yonakambojesu aññesu ca paccantimesu janapadesu dveva vaṇṇā – ayyo ceva dāso ca; ayyo hutvā dāso hoti, dāso hutvā ayyo hotī’’’ti ? ‘‘Evaṃ, bho, sutaṃ taṃ me – ‘yonakambojesu aññesu ca paccantimesu janapadesu dveva vaṇṇā – ayyo ceva dāso ca; ayyo hutvā dāso hoti, dāso hutvā ayyo hotī’’’ti. ‘‘Ettha, assalāyana, brāhmaṇānaṃ kiṃ balaṃ, ko assāso yadettha brāhmaṇā evamāhaṃsu – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo…pe… brahmadāyādā’’’ti? ‘‘Kiñcāpi bhavaṃ gotamo evamāha, atha khvettha brāhmaṇā evametaṃ maññanti – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo…pe… brahmadāyādā’’’ti.
mula_english:
“What do you think, Assalāyana? Have you heard that in Yona and Kamboja and in other outland countries there are only two classes (*vaṇṇa*), masters (*ayya*) and slaves (*dāsa*), and that masters become slaves and slaves masters?"

“So I have heard, sir.”

“Here, Assalāyana, what is the power (*bala*) of the Brahmins (*brāhmaṇa*), what is their comfort, that the Brahmins declare: ‘The Brahmin class (*vaṇṇa*) is the best; any other class is inferior… Brahmins are the heirs of Brahmā’?”

“Even though Master Gotama says this, here the Brahmins still think this: ‘The Brahmin class (*vaṇṇa*) is the best; any other class is inferior… Brahmins are the heirs of Brahmā.’”
commentary_pali: 403.Ayyo hutvā dāso hoti, dāso hutvā ayyo hotīti brāhmaṇo sabhariyo vaṇijjaṃ payojento yonakaraṭṭhaṃ vā kambojaraṭṭhaṃ vā gantvā kālaṃ karoti, tassa gehe vayappatte putte asati brāhmaṇī dāsena vā kammakarena vā saddhiṃ saṃvāsaṃ kappeti. Ekasmiṃ dārake jāte so puriso dāsova hoti, tassa jātadārako pana dāyajjasāmiko hoti. Mātito suddho pitito asuddho so vaṇijjaṃ payojento majjhimapadesaṃ gantvā brāhmaṇadārikaṃ gahetvā tassā kucchismiṃ puttaṃ paṭilabhati, sopi mātitova suddho hoti pitito asuddho. Evaṃ brāhmaṇasamayasmiññeva jātisambhedo hotīti dassanatthametaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiṃbalaṃ, ko assāsoti yattha tumhe dāsā hontā sabbeva dāsā hotha, ayyā hontā sabbeva ayyā hotha, ettha vo ko thāmo, ko avassayo, yaṃ brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇoti vadathāti dīpeti.
commentary_english: 403. The brāhmaṇa, with his wife, engaging in trade, [saying,] "Having been a master, he becomes a slave; having been a slave, he becomes a master," goes to the Yona country or the Kamboja country and makes time; when there is no son in his house who has reached adulthood, the *brāhmaṇī* engages in cohabitation with a slave or a hired laborer. When a child is born to one, that man is just like a slave; his son born of her, however, is the owner of the inheritance. He is pure from the mother, impure from the father; engaging in trade, he goes to the Middle Country, takes a *brāhmaṇa* maiden, and obtains a son in her womb; he also is pure from the mother, impure from the father. Thus, it is shown that even in the time of Brahmins, there is a mixture of castes. What strength ( *balaṃ*), what refuge ( *ko assāso*) is there, where you all, being slaves, are all slaves, being masters, are all masters? Here, what is your power ( *ko thāmo*), what is your support ( *ko avassayo*)? He reveals that you say that only a *brāhmaṇa* is the best caste.

mula_pali: 404. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, assalāyana, khattiyova nu kho pāṇātipātī adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī pisuṇavāco pharusavāco samphappalāpī abhijjhālu byāpannacitto micchādiṭṭhi kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjeyya, no brāhmaṇo? Vessova nu kho…pe… suddova nu kho pāṇātipātī adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī pisuṇavāco pharusavāco samphappalāpī abhijjhālu byāpannacitto micchādiṭṭhi kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjeyya, no brāhmaṇo’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama. Khattiyopi hi, bho gotama, pāṇātipātī adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī pisuṇavāco pharusavāco samphappalāpī abhijjhālu byāpannacitto micchādiṭṭhi kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjeyya. Brāhmaṇopi hi, bho gotama…pe… vessopi hi, bho gotama…pe… suddopi hi, bho gotama…pe… sabbepi hi, bho gotama, cattāro vaṇṇā pāṇātipātino adinnādāyino kāmesumicchācārino musāvādino pisuṇavācā pharusavācā samphappalāpino abhijjhālū byāpannacittā micchādiṭṭhī kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjeyyu’’nti. ‘‘Ettha, assalāyana, brāhmaṇānaṃ kiṃ balaṃ, ko assāso yadettha brāhmaṇā evamāhaṃsu – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo…pe… brahmadāyādā’’’ti? ‘‘Kiñcāpi bhavaṃ gotamo evamāha, atha khvettha brāhmaṇā evametaṃ maññanti – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo…pe… brahmadāyādā’’’ti.
mula_english:
404. "What do you think, Assalāyana? Suppose a noble (khattiya) were to kill living beings (pāṇātipātī), take what is not given (adinnādāyī), misconduct himself in sensual pleasures (kāmesumicchācārī), speak falsely (musāvādī), speak maliciously (pisuṇavāco), speak harshly (pharusavāco), gossip (samphappalāpī), be covetous (abhijjhālu), have a mind of ill will (byāpannacitto), and hold wrong view (micchādiṭṭhi). On the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), would only he be likely to reappear in a state of deprivation (apāyaṃ), in an unhappy destination (duggatiṃ), in perdition (vinipātaṃ), even in hell (nirayaṃ) - and not a *brāhmaṇa*? Suppose a merchant (vessa)…pe… a worker (sudda) were to kill living beings (pāṇātipātī), take what is not given (adinnādāyī), misconduct himself in sensual pleasures (kāmesumicchācārī), speak falsely (musāvādī), speak maliciously (pisuṇavāco), speak harshly (pharusavāco), gossip (samphappalāpī), be covetous (abhijjhālu), have a mind of ill will (byāpannacitto), and hold wrong view (micchādiṭṭhi). On the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā) after death (paraṃ maraṇā), would only he be likely to reappear in a state of deprivation (apāyaṃ), in an unhappy destination (duggatiṃ), in perdition (vinipātaṃ), even in hell (nirayaṃ) - and not a *brāhmaṇa*?”

"No, indeed, Venerable Gotama."

"Surely, Venerable Gotama, a noble (khattiyopi hi, bho gotama), kills living beings (pāṇātipātī), takes what is not given (adinnādāyī), misconducts himself in sensual pleasures (kāmesumicchācārī), speaks falsely (musāvādī), speaks maliciously (pisuṇavāco), speaks harshly (pharusavāco), gossips (samphappalāpī), is covetous (abhijjhālu), has a mind of ill will (byāpannacitto), and holds wrong view (micchādiṭṭhi) and on the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), he reappears in a state of deprivation (apāyaṃ), in an unhappy destination (duggatiṃ), in perdition (vinipātaṃ), even in hell (nirayaṃ).

Surely, Venerable Gotama, a *brāhmaṇa*…pe… Surely, Venerable Gotama, a merchant (vessa)…pe… Surely, Venerable Gotama, a worker (sudda)…pe… Surely, Venerable Gotama, all four castes (cattāro vaṇṇā) kill living beings (pāṇātipātino), take what is not given (adinnādāyino), misconduct themselves in sensual pleasures (kāmesumicchācārino), speak falsely (musāvādino), speak maliciously (pisuṇavācā), speak harshly (pharusavācā), gossip (samphappalāpino), are covetous (abhijjhālū), have minds of ill will (byāpannacittā), and hold wrong views (micchādiṭṭhī), and on the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), they reappear in a state of deprivation (apāyaṃ), in an unhappy destination (duggatiṃ), in perdition (vinipātaṃ), even in hell (nirayaṃ)."

"In this matter, Assalāyana, what strength (balaṃ) do the *brāhmaṇas* have, what is their consolation (assāso) that the *brāhmaṇas* declare thus: '*Brāhmaṇas* are the best caste (seṭṭho vaṇṇo), other castes are inferior (hīno añño vaṇṇo)…pe… descendants of Brahmā (brahmadāyādā)?"

"Even though Venerable Gotama says this, still, in this matter, the *brāhmaṇas* consider it thus: '*Brāhmaṇas* are the best caste (seṭṭho vaṇṇo), other castes are inferior (hīno añño vaṇṇo)…pe… descendants of Brahmā (brahmadāyādā)."
commentary_pali: 404.Khattiyova nu khotiādayo suttacchedakavādā nāma honti.
commentary_english: khattiyova nu kho and other such suttacchedakavādā are so called.

mula_pali: 405. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, assalāyana, brāhmaṇova nu kho pāṇātipātā paṭivirato adinnādānā paṭivirato kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato musāvādā paṭivirato pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato samphappalāpā paṭivirato anabhijjhālu abyāpannacitto sammādiṭṭhi kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyya, no no ca (ka.) khattiyo no vesso, no suddo’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama! Khattiyopi hi, bho gotama, pāṇātipātā paṭivirato adinnādānā paṭivirato kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato musāvādā paṭivirato pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato samphappalāpā paṭivirato anabhijjhālu abyāpannacitto sammādiṭṭhi kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyya. Brāhmaṇopi hi, bho gotama…pe… vessopi hi, bho gotama…pe… suddopi hi, bho gotama…pe… sabbepi hi, bho gotama, cattāro vaṇṇā pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā adinnādānā paṭiviratā kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā musāvādā paṭiviratā pisuṇāya vācāya paṭiviratā pharusāya vācāya paṭiviratā samphappalāpā paṭiviratā anabhijjhālū abyāpannacittā sammādiṭṭhī kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyyu’’nti. ‘‘Ettha, assalāyana , brāhmaṇānaṃ kiṃ balaṃ, ko assāso yadettha brāhmaṇā evamāhaṃsu – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo…pe… brahmadāyādā’’’ti? ‘‘Kiñcāpi bhavaṃ gotamo evamāha, atha khvettha brāhmaṇā evametaṃ maññanti – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo…pe… brahmadāyādā’’’ti.
mula_english:
“What do you think, Assalāyana? Suppose a *brāhmaṇa* were to abstain from killing living beings (*prāṇātipātā paṭivirato*), from taking what is not given (*adinnādānā paṭivirato*), from misconduct in sensual pleasures (*kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato*), from false speech (*musāvādā*), from malicious speech (*pisuṇāya vācāya*), from harsh speech (*pharusāya vācāya*), and from gossip (*samphappalāpā*), and were to be uncovetous (*anabhijjhālu*), to have a mind without ill will (*abyāpannacitto*), and to hold right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*). On the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*paraṃ maraṇā*), would only he be likely to reappear in a happy destination (*sugatiṃ*), even in the heavenly world (*saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyya*) - and not a noble (*khattiyo*) , or a merchant (*vesso*), or a worker (*suddo*)?”

“No indeed, venerable Gotama! Whether it be a noble (*khattiyopi hi, bho gotama*), or a *brāhmaṇa*, or a merchant (*vessopi hi, bho gotama*), or a worker (*suddopi hi, bho gotama*) - those of all four castes (*sabbepi hi, bho gotama, cattāro vaṇṇā*) who abstain from killing living beings (*pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā*)...and hold right view (*sammādiṭṭhī kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyyu*)”.

“Here, Assalāyana, what is the power (*kiṃ balaṃ*) of the *brāhmaṇas*, what is their consolation (*ko assāso*) that the *brāhmaṇas* say thus: '*Brāhmaṇas* are the highest caste (*brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo*), other castes are inferior (*hīno añño vaṇṇo*)…heirs of Brahma (*brahmadāyādā*)'?”

“Although venerable Gotama says this, still the *brāhmaṇas* think thus: '*Brāhmaṇas* are the highest caste (*brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo*), other castes are inferior (*hīno añño vaṇṇo*)…heirs of Brahma (*brahmadāyādā*)'.”

mula_pali: 406. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, assalāyana, brāhmaṇova nu kho pahoti asmiṃ padese averaṃ abyābajjhaṃ mettacittaṃ bhāvetuṃ, no khattiyo, no vesso no suddo’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama! Khattiyopi hi, bho gotama, pahoti asmiṃ padese averaṃ abyābajjhaṃ mettacittaṃ bhāvetuṃ; brāhmaṇopi hi, bho gotama… vessopi hi , bho gotama… suddopi hi, bho gotama… sabbepi hi, bho gotama, cattāro vaṇṇā pahonti asmiṃ padese averaṃ abyābajjhaṃ mettacittaṃ bhāvetu’’nti. ‘‘Ettha, assalāyana, brāhmaṇānaṃ kiṃ balaṃ, ko assāso yadettha brāhmaṇā evamāhaṃsu – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo…pe… brahmadāyādā’’’ti? ‘‘Kiñcāpi bhavaṃ gotamo evamāha, atha khvettha brāhmaṇā evametaṃ maññanti – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo…pe… brahmadāyādā’’’ti.
mula_english:
406. “What do you think, Assalāyana? Is only a *brāhmaṇa* capable of developing a mind of loving-kindness (*mettacitta*) towards a certain region, without hostility (*averaṃ*) and without ill will (*abyābajjhaṃ*), and not a noble (*khattiyo*), or a merchant (*vesso*), or a worker (*suddo*)?”

“No, indeed, sir Gotama! Whether it be a noble (*khattiyo*), or a *brāhmaṇa*, or a merchant (*vesso*), or a worker (*suddo*) - those of all four castes (*cattāro vaṇṇā*) are capable of developing a mind of loving-kindness (*mettacittaṃ*) towards a certain region, without hostility (*averaṃ*) and without ill will (*abyābajjhaṃ*).”

“In this matter, Assalāyana, what is the power (*balaṃ*) of the *brāhmaṇas*, what is their consolation, that the *brāhmaṇas* say thus: ‘The *brāhmaṇa* is the best caste (*vaṇṇo*), other castes are inferior (*hīno añño vaṇṇo*)… heirs of Brahmā’?”

“Even though venerable Gotama says thus, yet here the *brāhmaṇas* think thus: ‘The *brāhmaṇa* is the best caste (*vaṇṇo*), other castes are inferior (*hīno añño vaṇṇo*)… heirs of Brahmā’.”

mula_pali: 407. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, assalāyana, brāhmaṇova nu kho pahoti sottisināniṃ ādāya nadiṃ gantvā rajojallaṃ pavāhetuṃ, no khattiyo, no vesso, no suddo’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama! Khattiyopi hi, bho gotama, pahoti sottisināniṃ ādāya nadiṃ gantvā rajojallaṃ pavāhetuṃ, brāhmaṇopi hi, bho gotama… vessopi hi, bho gotama… suddopi hi, bho gotama… sabbepi hi, bho gotama, cattāro vaṇṇā pahonti sottisināniṃ ādāya nadiṃ gantvā rajojallaṃ pavāhetu’’nti. ‘‘Ettha, assalāyana, brāhmaṇānaṃ kiṃ balaṃ, ko assāso yadettha brāhmaṇā evamāhaṃsu – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo…pe… brahmadāyādā’’’ti? ‘‘Kiñcāpi bhavaṃ gotamo evamāha, atha khvettha brāhmaṇā evametaṃ maññanti – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo…pe… brahmadāyādā’’’ti.
mula_english:
“So what do you think, Assalāyana? Is it only a *brāhmaṇa* who is able to take bath powder and go to the river to wash off the dust and dirt? Not a noble, not a merchant, not a worker?”

“No, Gotama! A noble is also able, Gotama, to take bath powder and go to the river to wash off the dust and dirt; a *brāhmaṇa* is also able, Gotama… a merchant is also able, Gotama… a worker is also able, Gotama… those of all four *varṇas* are able, Gotama, to take bath powder and go to the river to wash off the dust and dirt.”

“In this regard, Assalāyana, what strength (*balam*) do the *brāhmaṇas* have, what is their consolation (*assāso*) that the *brāhmaṇas* say thus: ‘Only a *brāhmaṇa* is the best *varṇa*, other *varṇas* are inferior… and they are the descendants of Brahmā’?”

“Even though venerable Gotama says thus, yet the *brāhmaṇas* think thus: ‘Only a *brāhmaṇa* is the best *varṇa*, other *varṇas* are inferior… and they are the descendants of Brahmā.’”

mula_pali:
408. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, assalāyana, idha rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto nānājaccānaṃ purisānaṃ purisasataṃ sannipāteyya – ‘āyantu bhonto ye tattha khattiyakulā brāhmaṇakulā rājaññakulā uppannā, sākassa vā sālassa vā uppannā sālassa vā (sī. pī.) salaḷassa vā candanassa vā padumakassa vā uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya, aggiṃ abhinibbattentu, tejo pātukarontu. Āyantu pana bhonto ye tattha caṇḍālakulā nesādakulā venakulā veṇakulā (sī. pī.), veṇukulā (syā. kaṃ.) rathakārakulā pukkusakulā uppannā, sāpānadoṇiyā vā sūkaradoṇiyā vā rajakadoṇiyā vā eraṇḍakaṭṭhassa vā uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya, aggiṃ abhinibbattentu, tejo pātukarontū’ti.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, assalāyana, yo evaṃ nu kho so yo ca nu kho (syā. kaṃ. ka.) khattiyakulā brāhmaṇakulā rājaññakulā uppannehi sākassa vā sālassa vā salaḷassa vā candanassa vā padumakassa vā uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya aggi abhinibbatto, tejo pātukato, so eva nu khvāssa aggi accimā ceva ca (sī. pī.) vaṇṇavā vaṇṇimā (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) ca pabhassaro ca, tena ca sakkā agginā aggikaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ; yo pana so caṇḍālakulā nesādakulā venakulā rathakārakulā pukkusakulā uppannehi sāpānadoṇiyā vā sūkaradoṇiyā vā rajakadoṇiyā vā eraṇḍakaṭṭhassa vā uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya aggi abhinibbatto, tejo pātukato svāssa aggi na ceva accimā na ca vaṇṇavā na ca pabhassaro, na ca tena sakkā agginā aggikaraṇīyaṃ kātu’’nti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama! Yopi hi so yo so (sī. pī.), bho gotama, khattiyakulā brāhmaṇakulā rājaññakulā uppannehi sākassa vā sālassa vā salaḷassa vā candanassa vā padumakassa vā uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya aggi abhinibbatto, tejo pātukato svāssa so cassa (sī. pī.), sopissa (syā. kaṃ.) aggi accimā ceva vaṇṇavā ca pabhassaro ca, tena ca sakkā agginā aggikaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ; yopi so caṇḍālakulā nesādakulā venakulā rathakārakulā pukkusakulā uppannehi sāpānadoṇiyā vā sūkaradoṇiyā vā rajakadoṇiyā vā eraṇḍakaṭṭhassa vā uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya aggi abhinibbatto, tejo pātukato, svāssa aggi accimā ceva vaṇṇavā ca pabhassaro ca, tena ca sakkā agginā aggikaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ. Sabbopi hi, bho gotama, aggi accimā ceva vaṇṇavā ca pabhassaro ca, sabbenapi sakkā agginā aggikaraṇīyaṃ kātu’’nti. ‘‘Ettha, assalāyana, brāhmaṇānaṃ kiṃ balaṃ, ko assāso yadettha brāhmaṇā evamāhaṃsu – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo; brāhmaṇova sukko vaṇṇo, kaṇho añño vaṇṇo; brāhmaṇāva sujjhanti, no abrāhmaṇā; brāhmaṇāva brahmuno puttā orasā mukhato jātā brahmajā brahmanimmitā brahmadāyādā’’’ti? ‘‘Kiñcāpi bhavaṃ gotamo evamāha, atha khvettha brāhmaṇā evametaṃ maññanti – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo…pe… brahmadāyādā’’’ti.

yo ca nu kho (syā. kaṃ. ka.) ca (sī. pī.) vaṇṇimā (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) yo so (sī. pī.) so cassa (sī. pī.), sopissa (syā. kaṃ.)
mula_english:
408. What do you think, Assalāyana? Suppose a noble king, anointed on the head, were to assemble here a hundred men of different births and say: 'Come, sirs, let those who are born into a noble family (kṣatriyakula), a Brahman family (brāhmaṇakula), or a royal family (rājaññakula), take an upper fire-stick (uttarāraṇi) made of *sāka* wood, *sāla* wood, *salaḷa* wood, sandalwood (candana), or *padumaka* wood, light a fire (agni), and produce heat (tejas). Let those who are born into an outcaste family (caṇḍālakula), a hunter's family (nesādakula), a wicker-worker's family (venakula), a cartwright's family (rathakārakula), or a scavenger's family (pukkusakula), take an upper fire-stick made of dog-trough wood (sāpānadoṇiyā), pig-trough wood (sūkaradoṇiyā), washerman's trough wood (rajakadoṇiyā), or *eraṇḍaka* wood, light a fire (agni), and produce heat (tejas).'

What do you think, Assalāyana? When a fire (agni) is produced and heat (tejas) is generated by those born into a noble family (kṣatriyakula), a Brahman family (brāhmaṇakula), or a royal family (rājaññakula), taking an upper fire-stick made of *sāka* wood, *sāla* wood, *salaḷa* wood, sandalwood (candana), or *padumaka* wood, would that fire (agni) alone have a flame (accimā), color (vaṇṇavā), and radiance (pabhassaro), and could things be done with that fire (agni) that should be done with fire? And when a fire (agni) is produced and heat (tejas) is generated by those born into an outcaste family (caṇḍālakula), a hunter's family (nesādakula), a wicker-worker's family (venakula), a cartwright's family (rathakārakula), or a scavenger's family (pukkusakula), taking an upper fire-stick made of dog-trough wood (sāpānadoṇiyā), pig-trough wood (sūkaradoṇiyā), washerman's trough wood (rajakadoṇiyā), or *eraṇḍaka* wood, would that fire (agni) not have a flame (accimā), color (vaṇṇavā), and radiance (pabhassaro), and could things not be done with that fire (agni) that should be done with fire?" "No, Master Gotama! Any fire (agni) at all, Master Gotama, whether produced by those born into a noble family (kṣatriyakula), a Brahman family (brāhmaṇakula), or a royal family (rājaññakula), taking an upper fire-stick made of *sāka* wood, *sāla* wood, *salaḷa* wood, sandalwood (candana), or *padumaka* wood, or by those born into an outcaste family (caṇḍālakula), a hunter's family (nesādakula), a wicker-worker's family (venakula), a cartwright's family (rathakārakula), or a scavenger's family (pukkusakula), taking an upper fire-stick made of dog-trough wood (sāpānadoṇiyā), pig-trough wood (sūkaradoṇiyā), washerman's trough wood (rajakadoṇiyā), or *eraṇḍaka* wood—any fire (agni) at all that is produced and whose heat (tejas) is generated has flame (accimā), color (vaṇṇavā), and radiance (pabhassaro), and things can be done with any fire (agni) that should be done with fire."

"On what strength (bala), Assalāyana, on what assurance (assāso) do these Brahmans (brāhmaṇā) say: 'Only Brahmans (brāhmaṇā) are the best class (vaṇṇo); other classes (vaṇṇo) are inferior. Only Brahmans (brāhmaṇā) are the fair class (vaṇṇo); other classes (vaṇṇo) are dark. Only Brahmans (brāhmaṇā) are purified, not non-Brahmans (abrāhmaṇā). Brahmans (brāhmaṇā) are the legitimate (orasā) sons of Brahmā, born from his mouth (mukhato jātā), born of Brahmā (brahmajā), created by Brahmā (brahmanimmitā), heirs of Brahmā (brahmadāyādā)'?" "Though the esteemed Gotama says this, here the Brahmans (brāhmaṇā) think thus: 'Only Brahmans (brāhmaṇā) are the best class (vaṇṇo); other classes (vaṇṇo) are inferior…heirs of Brahmā (brahmadāyādā).'"
pī.

commentary_pali: 408. Idāni cātuvaṇṇisuddhiṃ dassento idha rājātiādimāha. Sāpānadoṇiyāti sunakhānaṃ pivanadoṇiyā. Aggikaraṇīyanti sītavinodanaandhakāravidhamanabhattapacanādi aggikiccaṃ. Ettha assalāyanāti ettha sabbasmiṃ aggikiccaṃ karonte.
commentary_english:
Now, showing the purification of the four castes, he said, "Here [is] the king," and so forth.

"*Sāpānadoṇiyā*" means a drinking trough for dogs.

"*Aggikaraṇīya*" means the fire-business, such as dispelling cold, providing amusement, dispelling darkness, and cooking food.

"*Ettha assalāyanā*" means here, while doing all the fire-business.

mula_pali:
409. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, assalāyana, idha khattiyakumāro brāhmaṇakaññāya saddhiṃ saṃvāsaṃ kappeyya, tesaṃ saṃvāsamanvāya putto jāyetha; yo so khattiyakumārena brāhmaṇakaññāya putto uppanno, siyā so mātupi sadiso pitupi sadiso, ‘khattiyo’tipi vattabbo ‘brāhmaṇo’tipi vattabbo’’ti? ‘‘Yo so, bho gotama, khattiyakumārena brāhmaṇakaññāya putto uppanno, siyā so mātupi sadiso pitupi sadiso, ‘khattiyo’tipi vattabbo ‘brāhmaṇo’tipi vattabbo’’ti.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, assalāyana, idha brāhmaṇakumāro khattiyakaññāya saddhiṃ saṃvāsaṃ kappeyya, tesaṃ saṃvāsamanvāya putto jāyetha; yo so brāhmaṇakumārena khattiyakaññāya putto uppanno, siyā so mātupi sadiso pitupi sadiso, ‘khattiyo’tipi vattabbo ‘brāhmaṇo’tipi vattabbo’’ti? ‘‘Yo so, bho gotama, brāhmaṇakumārena khattiyakaññāya putto uppanno, siyā so mātupi sadiso pitupi sadiso, ‘khattiyo’tipi vattabbo ‘brāhmaṇo’tipi vattabbo’’ti.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, assalāyana idha vaḷavaṃ gadrabhena sampayojeyyuṃ saṃyojeyya (ka.), tesaṃ sampayogamanvāya kisoro jāyetha; yo so vaḷavāya gadrabhena kisoro uppanno, siyā so mātupi sadiso pitupi sadiso, ‘asso’tipi vattabbo ‘gadrabho’tipi vattabbo’’ti? ‘‘Kuṇḍañhi so vekurañjāya hi so (sī. pī.), so kumāraṇḍupi so (syā. kaṃ.), vekulajo hi so (?), bho gotama, assataro hoti. Idaṃ hissa , bho gotama, nānākaraṇaṃ passāmi; amutra ca panesānaṃ na kiñci nānākaraṇaṃ passāmī’’ti.

saṃyojeyya (ka.) vekurañjāya hi so (sī. pī.), so kumāraṇḍupi so (syā. kaṃ.), vekulajo hi so (?)

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, assalāyana, idhāssu dve māṇavakā bhātaro saudariyā, eko ajjhāyako upanīto eko anajjhāyako anupanīto. Kamettha brāhmaṇā paṭhamaṃ bhojeyyuṃ saddhe vā thālipāke vā yaññe vā pāhune vā’’ti? ‘‘Yo so, bho gotama, māṇavako ajjhāyako upanīto tamettha brāhmaṇā paṭhamaṃ bhojeyyuṃ saddhe vā thālipāke vā yaññe vā pāhune vā. Kiñhi, bho gotama, anajjhāyake anupanīte dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ bhavissatī’’ti?

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, assalāyana, idhāssu dve māṇavakā bhātaro saudariyā, eko ajjhāyako upanīto dussīlo pāpadhammo, eko anajjhāyako anupanīto sīlavā kalyāṇadhammo. Kamettha brāhmaṇā paṭhamaṃ bhojeyyuṃ saddhe vā thālipāke vā yaññe vā pāhune vā’’ti? ‘‘Yo so, bho gotama, māṇavako anajjhāyako anupanīto sīlavā kalyāṇadhammo tamettha brāhmaṇā paṭhamaṃ bhojeyyuṃ saddhe vā thālipāke vā yaññe vā pāhune vā. Kiñhi, bho gotama, dussīle pāpadhamme dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ bhavissatī’’ti?

‘‘Pubbe kho tvaṃ, assalāyana, jātiṃ agamāsi; jātiṃ gantvā mante agamāsi; mante gantvā tape agamāsi; tape gantvā mante gantvā tametaṃ tvaṃ (sī. pī.), mante gantvā tameva ṭhapetvā (syā. kaṃ.) cātuvaṇṇiṃ suddhiṃ paccāgato, yamahaṃ paññapemī’’ti. Evaṃ vutte, assalāyano māṇavo tuṇhībhūto maṅkubhūto pattakkhandho adhomukho pajjhāyanto appaṭibhāno nisīdi.

mante gantvā tametaṃ tvaṃ (sī. pī.), mante gantvā tameva ṭhapetvā (syā. kaṃ.)
mula_english:
409. “What do you think, Assalāyana? Suppose a noble (*kṣatriya*) youth were to cohabit with a *brāhmaṇa* girl, and a son was born from their cohabitation. Should a son born from a noble youth and a *brāhmaṇa* girl be called a noble after the father or a *brāhmaṇa* after the mother?” “The son born from a noble youth and a *brāhmaṇa* girl would resemble both his mother and father and should be called both a noble and a *brāhmaṇa*, Master Gotama.”

“What do you think, Assalāyana? Suppose a *brāhmaṇa* youth were to cohabit with a noble girl, and a son were to be born from their cohabitation. Should the son born from a *brāhmaṇa* youth and a noble girl be called a noble after the mother or a *brāhmaṇa* after the father?” “The son born from a *brāhmaṇa* youth and a noble girl would resemble both his mother and father and should be called both a noble and a *brāhmaṇa*, Master Gotama.”

“What do you think, Assalāyana? Suppose they were to mate a mare with a donkey, and a foal were born from their mating. Should a foal born from a mare and a donkey be called a horse or a donkey?” “Since he is a hybrid,” Master Gotama, “he is a mule. This, Master Gotama, is what I see as a distinction; but I see no distinction there among those lords.”

“What do you think, Assalāyana? Suppose there were two brahmin students who were brothers, born of the same mother, one studious and initiated, and one neither studious nor initiated. Which of them would *brāhmaṇas* feed first at a funeral feast, or at a ceremonial milk-rice offering, or at a sacrifice, or at a feast for guests?” “The *brāhmaṇa* student who is studious and initiated, Master Gotama. For why, Master Gotama? Because what is given to one who is unstudious and uninitiated is not of great fruit.”

“What do you think, Assalāyana? Suppose there were two brahmin students who were brothers, born of the same mother, one studious and initiated, but immoral and of bad character, and one neither studious nor initiated, but virtuous and of good character. Which of them would *brāhmaṇas* feed first at a funeral feast, or at a ceremonial milk-rice offering, or at a sacrifice, or at a feast for guests?” “The brahmin student who is unstudious and uninitiated, but virtuous and of good character, Master Gotama. For why, Master Gotama? Because what is given to one who is immoral and of bad character is not of great fruit.”

“Formerly, Assalāyana, you went to the *jāti*; having gone to the *jāti* you went to the *mantras*; having gone to the *mantras*, you went to austerity; having gone to austerity, you have come to claim that purity is based on the four social classes, which I reject.” When this was said, the brahmin student Assalāyana sat silent and dismayed, with shoulders drooping and head down, glum, and without response.
)
commentary_pali:
409. Idāni yadetaṃ brāhmaṇā cātuvaṇṇisuddhīti vadanti, ettha cātuvaṇṇāti niyamo natthi. Pañcamo hi pādasikavaṇṇopi atthīti saṃkhittena tesaṃ vāde dosadassanatthaṃ idha khattiyakumārotiādimāha. Tatra amutra ca panesānanti amusmiñca pana purimanaye etesaṃ māṇavakānaṃ kiñci nānākaraṇaṃ na passāmīti vadati. Nānākaraṇaṃ pana tesampi atthiyeva. Khattiyakumārassa hi brāhmaṇakaññāya uppanno khattiyapādasiko nāma, itaro brāhmaṇapādasiko nāma, ete hīnajātimāṇavakā.

Evaṃ pañcamassa vaṇṇassa atthitāya cātuvaṇṇisuddhīti etesaṃ vāde dosaṃ dassetvā idāni puna cātuvaṇṇisuddhiyaṃ ovadanto taṃ kiṃ maññasītiādimāha. Tattha saddheti matakabhatte. Thālipāketi paṇṇākārabhatte. Yaññeti yaññabhatte. Pāhuneti āgantukānaṃ katabhatte. Kiṃ hīti kiṃ mahapphalaṃ bhavissati, no bhavissatīti dīpeti.

taṃ kiṃ maññasī saddhe Thālipāke Yaññe Pāhune Kiṃ hī
commentary_english:
409. Now, the Brāhmaṇas say, "the purification of the four classes," but here, there is no restriction to just four classes.

Since there is a fifth class, the pādasikavaṇṇa, he said, in brief, in order to show the fault in their argument, "here [is] a *kṣatriya*-*kumāra*," etc.

There, "and elsewhere, sir," he says, "in that previous method, I do not see any differentiation of these youths."

But there is indeed a differentiation for them.

Indeed, the *kṣatriya*-*kumāra* born of a Brāhmaṇa maiden is called a *kṣatriyapādasika*, the other is called a *brāhmaṇapādasika*; these [are] youths of low birth.

Thus, having shown the fault in their argument that there is a purification of the four classes due to the existence of the fifth class, now again, advising on the purification of the four classes, he said, "what do you think?" etc.

There, *saddhe* means in [the case of] a meal for the dead.

*thālipāke* means in [the case of] a meal in the form of leaves.

*yaññe* means in [the case of] a sacrifice meal.

*pāhune* means in [the case of] a meal made for guests.

*kiṃ hī* means "will there be great fruit, or will there not be?" he indicates.

What do you think? *saddhe*, *thālipāke*, *yaññe*, *pāhune*, *kiṃ hī*.

mula_pali: 410. Atha kho bhagavā assalāyanaṃ māṇavaṃ tuṇhībhūtaṃ maṅkubhūtaṃ pattakkhandhaṃ adhomukhaṃ pajjhāyantaṃ appaṭibhānaṃ viditvā assalāyanaṃ māṇavaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘bhūtapubbaṃ, assalāyana, sattannaṃ brāhmaṇisīnaṃ araññāyatane paṇṇakuṭīsu sammantānaṃ vasantānaṃ (sī.) evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo…pe… brahmadāyādā’ti. Assosi kho , assalāyana, asito devalo isi – ‘sattannaṃ kira brāhmaṇisīnaṃ araññāyatane paṇṇakuṭīsu sammantānaṃ evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo…pe… brahmadāyādā’ti. Atha kho, assalāyana, asito devalo isi kesamassuṃ kappetvā mañjiṭṭhavaṇṇāni dussāni nivāsetvā paṭaliyo aṭaliyo (sī. pī.), agaliyo (syā. kaṃ.) upāhanā āruhitvā jātarūpamayaṃ daṇḍaṃ gahetvā sattannaṃ brāhmaṇisīnaṃ patthaṇḍile pāturahosi. Atha kho, assalāyana, asito devalo isi sattannaṃ brāhmaṇisīnaṃ patthaṇḍile caṅkamamāno evamāha – ‘handa, ko nu kho ime bhavanto brāhmaṇisayo gatā gantā (syā. kaṃ. ka.); handa, ko nu kho ime bhavanto brāhmaṇisayo gatā’ti? Atha kho, assalāyana, sattannaṃ brāhmaṇisīnaṃ etadahosi – ‘ko nāyaṃ gāmaṇḍalarūpo viya sattannaṃ brāhmaṇisīnaṃ patthaṇḍile caṅkamamāno evamāha – ‘handa, ko nu kho ime bhavanto brāhmaṇisayo gatā; handa, ko nu kho ime bhavanto brāhmaṇisayo gatāti? Handa, naṃ abhisapāmā’ti. Atha kho, assalāyana, satta brāhmaṇisayo asitaṃ devalaṃ isiṃ abhisapiṃsu – ‘bhasmā, vasala vasalī (pī.), vasali (ka.), capalī (syā. kaṃ.), hohi; bhasmā, vasala, hohī’ti bhasmā vasala hohīti abhisapavacanaṃ sī. pī. potthakesu sakideva āgataṃ. Yathā yathā kho, assalāyana, satta brāhmaṇisayo asitaṃ devalaṃ isiṃ abhisapiṃsu tathā tathā asito devalo isi abhirūpataro ceva hoti dassanīyataro ca pāsādikataro ca. Atha kho, assalāyana, sattannaṃ brāhmaṇisīnaṃ etadahosi – ‘moghaṃ vata no tapo, aphalaṃ brahmacariyaṃ. Mayañhi pubbe yaṃ abhisapāma – bhasmā, vasala, hohi; bhasmā, vasala, hohīti bhasmāva bhavati ekacco. Imaṃ pana mayaṃ yathā yathā abhisapāma tathā tathā abhirūpataro ceva hoti dassanīyataro ca pāsādikataro cā’ti. ‘Na bhavantānaṃ moghaṃ tapo, nāphalaṃ brahmacariyaṃ. Iṅgha bhavanto, yo mayi manopadoso taṃ pajahathā’ti. ‘Yo bhavati manopadoso taṃ pajahāma. Ko nu bhavaṃ hotī’ti? ‘Suto nu bhavataṃ – asito devalo isī’ti? ‘Evaṃ, bho’. ‘So khvāhaṃ, bho, homī’ti. Atha kho, assalāyana, satta brāhmaṇisayo asitaṃ devalaṃ isiṃ abhivādetuṃ upakkamiṃsu.
mula_english:
Then, the Blessed One, knowing that the young man Assalāyana was silent, confused, shoulders drooping, face downcast, and without ready wit, said this to the young man Assalāyana: "Formerly, Assalāyana, this kind of evil view arose in seven brahmin seers who were gathered in leaf huts in a forest retreat: 'Only *brāhmaṇas* are the best class, other classes are inferior... heirs of *Brahma*.'

Assalāyana, Asita Devala ṛṣi heard: 'This kind of evil view arose in seven brahmin seers who were gathered in leaf huts in a forest retreat: "Only *brāhmaṇas* are the best class... heirs of *Brahma*."'

Then, Assalāyana, Asita Devala ṛṣi, having had his hair and beard cut, having put on garments of ochre color, having put on stout sandals, and having taken a staff made of gold, appeared in the courtyard of the seven brahmin seers.

Then, Assalāyana, Asita Devala ṛṣi, while walking up and down in the courtyard of the seven brahmin seers, said thus: 'Come now, where have these worthy brahmin seers gone; come now, where have these worthy brahmin seers gone?'

Then, Assalāyana, this thought occurred to the seven brahmin seers: 'Who is this, like a village fool, walking up and down in the courtyard of the seven brahmin seers, saying thus: "Come now, where have these worthy brahmin seers gone; come now, where have these worthy brahmin seers gone?" Come now, let us curse him!'

Then, Assalāyana, the seven brahmin seers cursed Asita Devala ṛṣi: 'Be ashes, vile one, be ashes; be ashes, vile one, be ashes!'

Assalāyana, just as the seven brahmin seers cursed Asita Devala ṛṣi, so did Asita Devala ṛṣi become even more beautiful, more handsome, and more pleasing.

Then, Assalāyana, this thought occurred to the seven brahmin seers: 'Our asceticism is truly in vain, our holy life is fruitless. For formerly, whomever we cursed - "Be ashes, vile one, be ashes," - some one would become ashes. But as much as we curse him, so much more beautiful, handsome and pleasing does he become.'

'Your asceticism is not in vain, worthy ones, your holy life is not fruitless. Come now, worthy ones, abandon your malice towards me.'

'We abandon that malice which arises. Who are you, sir?' 'Have you heard of Asita Devala ṛṣi?' 'Yes, sir.'

'I am he, sirs.'

Then, Assalāyana, the seven brahmin seers approached Asita Devala ṛṣi to pay homage.
commentary_pali: 410.Bhūtapubbanti assalāyana pubbe mayi jātiyā hīnatare tumhe seṭṭhatarā samānāpi mayā jātivāde pañhaṃ puṭṭhā sampādetuṃ na sakkhittha, idāni tumhe hīnatarā hutvā mayā seṭṭhatarena buddhānaṃ sake jātivādapañhaṃ puṭṭhā kiṃ sampādessatha? Na ettha cintā kātabbāti māṇavaṃ upatthambhento imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha asitoti kāḷako. Devaloti tassa nāmaṃ, ayameva bhagavā tena samayena. Paṭaliyoti gaṇaṅgaṇupāhanā. Patthaṇḍileti paṇṇasālapariveṇe. Ko nu khoti kahaṃ nu kho. Gāmaṇḍalarūpo viyāti gāmadārakarūpo viya. So khvāhaṃ, bho, homīti so ahaṃ, bho, asitadevalo homīti vadati. Tadā kira mahāsatto koṇḍadamako hutvā vicarati. Abhivādetuṃ upakkamiṃsūti vandituṃ upakkamaṃ akaṃsu. Tato paṭṭhāya ca vassasatikatāpasopi tadahujātaṃ brāhmaṇakumāraṃ avandanto koṇḍito hoti.
commentary_english:
410. *Bhūtapubba* means Assalāyana, formerly, though you were superior, because of my inferior birth, you were not able to resolve the question I asked regarding caste. Now that you are inferior, having become [such] because of me, who am superior, what will you resolve when asked a question regarding caste by the Awakened Ones? No thought should be given to this.” Supporting the young man, he began this teaching.

There, *Asito* means black.

*Devalo* means his name, this very Blessed One at that time.

*Paṭaliyo* means footwear covering the ankles.

*Patthaṇḍile* means in the leaf-hut enclosure.

*Ko nu kho* means where now?

*Gāmaṇḍalarūpo viyā* means like a village boy.

*So khvāhaṃ, bho, homī* means "I am, sir, Asitadevala," he says.

Then, it seems, the great being, having become Koṇḍadamaka, wandered about.

*Abhivādetuṃ upakkamiṃsū* means they began to venerate.

From then on, even the ascetic of a hundred years, not venerating the Brāhmaṇa boy born that day, became Koṇḍita.

mula_pali:
411. ‘‘Atha kho, assalāyana, asito devalo isi satta brāhmaṇisayo etadavoca – ‘sutaṃ metaṃ, bho, sattannaṃ kira brāhmaṇisīnaṃ araññāyatane paṇṇakuṭīsu sammantānaṃ evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ – brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīno añño vaṇṇo; brāhmaṇova sukko vaṇṇo , kaṇho añño vaṇṇo; brāhmaṇāva sujjhanti, no abrāhmaṇā; brāhmaṇāva brahmuno puttā orasā mukhato jātā brahmajā brahmanimmitā brahmadāyādā’ti. ‘Evaṃ, bho’.

‘‘‘Jānanti pana bhonto – yā janikā mātā janimātā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) brāhmaṇaṃyeva agamāsi, no abrāhmaṇa’nti? ‘No hidaṃ, bho’.

janimātā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)

‘‘‘Jānanti pana bhonto – yā janikāmātu janimātu (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) mātā yāva sattamā mātumātāmahayugā brāhmaṇaṃyeva agamāsi, no abrāhmaṇa’nti? ‘No hidaṃ, bho’.

janimātu (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)

‘‘‘Jānanti pana bhonto – yo janako pitā janipitā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) brāhmaṇiṃyeva agamāsi, no abrāhmaṇi’nti? ‘No hidaṃ, bho’.

janipitā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)

‘‘‘Jānanti pana bhonto – yo janakapitu janipitu (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) pitā yāva sattamā pitupitāmahayugā brāhmaṇiṃyeva agamāsi, no abrāhmaṇi’nti? ‘No hidaṃ, bho’.

janipitu (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)

‘‘‘Jānanti pana bhonto – yathā gabbhassa avakkanti hotī’ti na mayaṃ jānāma bho yathā gabbhassa avakkanti hotīti. yathā kathaṃ pana bho gabbhassa avakkanti hotīti. (ka.)? ‘Jānāma mayaṃ, bho – yathā gabbhassa avakkanti hoti na mayaṃ jānāma bho yathā gabbhassa avakkanti hotīti. yathā kathaṃ pana bho gabbhassa avakkanti hotīti. (ka.). Idha mātāpitaro ca sannipatitā honti, mātā ca utunī hoti, gandhabbo ca paccupaṭṭhito hoti; evaṃ tiṇṇaṃ sannipātā gabbhassa avakkanti hotī’ti.

na mayaṃ jānāma bho yathā gabbhassa avakkanti hotīti. yathā kathaṃ pana bho gabbhassa avakkanti hotīti. (ka.) na mayaṃ jānāma bho yathā gabbhassa avakkanti hotīti. yathā kathaṃ pana bho gabbhassa avakkanti hotīti. (ka.)

‘‘‘Jānanti pana bhonto – taggha yagghe (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), so gandhabbo khattiyo vā brāhmaṇo vā vesso vā suddo vā’ti? ‘Na mayaṃ, bho, jānāma – taggha so gandhabbo khattiyo vā brāhmaṇo vā vesso vā suddo vā’ti. ‘Evaṃ sante, bho, jānātha – ke tumhe hothā’ti? ‘Evaṃ sante, bho , na mayaṃ jānāma – ke mayaṃ homā’ti. Te hi nāma, assalāyana, satta brāhmaṇisayo asitena devalena isinā sake jātivāde samanuyuñjīyamānā samanuggāhīyamānā samanubhāsīyamānā na sampāyissanti; kiṃ pana tvaṃ etarahi mayā sakasmiṃ jātivāde samanuyuñjīyamāno samanuggāhīyamāno samanubhāsīyamāno sampāyissasi, yesaṃ tvaṃ sācariyako na puṇṇo dabbigāho’’ti.

yagghe (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)

Evaṃ vutte, assalāyano māṇavo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata’’nti.

Assalāyanasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.
mula_english:
Then, Āssalāyana, Asita Devala Ṛṣi said this to the seven Brahmins: 'I have heard that when these seven Brahmin seers were staying in leaf huts in the forest, such an evil view arose in them: “Only the *brāhmaṇa* is the best *varṇa* (caste), other *varṇas* (castes) are inferior; only the *brāhmaṇa* is the fairest *varṇa* (caste), other *varṇas* (castes) are dark; only *brāhmaṇas* are purified, not non-*brāhmaṇas*; only *brāhmaṇas* are the sons of Brahmā, born from his mouth, his direct descendants, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā."' 'That is so, sir.' 'Do you know if the mother who bore you only went with *brāhmaṇas*, and not with non-*brāhmaṇas*?' 'No, sir.' 'Do you know if your mother's mother, back to the seventh generation of maternal grandmothers, only went with *brāhmaṇas*, and not with non-*brāhmaṇas*?' 'No, sir.' 'Do you know if the father who begot you only went with a *brāhmaṇī*, and not with a non-*brāhmaṇī*?' 'No, sir.' 'Do you know if your father's father, back to the seventh generation of paternal grandfathers, only went with *brāhmaṇīs*, and not with non-*brāhmaṇīs*?' 'No, sir.' kaṃ. pī. )

‘‘‘Do you know, sirs, how conception occurs in a womb?’ti We do not know, sir, how conception occurs in a womb. How, sir, does conception occur in a womb? (ka. )? ‘We know, sir, how conception occurs in a womb We do not know, sir, how conception occurs in a womb. How, sir, does conception occur in a womb? (ka. ). Here the mother and father come together, and it is the mother’s season, and the *gandhabba* is present; thus, through the union of these three, conception occurs in a womb.’

We do not know, sir, how conception occurs in a womb. How, sir, does conception occur in a womb? (ka. ) We do not know, sir, how conception occurs in a womb. How, sir, does conception occur in a womb? (ka. )

‘‘‘Do you know, sirs— truly indeed (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. )—whether that *gandhabba* is a noble, a *brāhmaṇa*, a merchant, or a worker?’ ‘No, sir, we do not know—truly whether that *gandhabba* is a noble, a *brāhmaṇa*, a merchant, or a worker.’ ‘That being so, sirs, do you know who you are?’ ‘That being so, sirs , we do not know who we are.’ Indeed, Assalāyana, those seven *brāhmaṇa* seers, being questioned, cross-examined, and interrogated by Asita Devala the seer on their own birth-based doctrine, were unable to maintain it; how then can you, being questioned, cross-examined, and interrogated by me now on your own birth-based doctrine , be able to maintain it, you whose knowledge depends on your teachers and who are not even a spoon-holder like Puṇṇa?’’

indeed (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. )

When this was said, Assalāyana the young man said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, Master Gotama…pe… may the esteemed Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from today for as long as I live.”

The Assalāyana Sutta, the third, is finished.
commentary_pali:
411.Janikā mātāti yāya tumhe janitā, sā vo janikā mātā. Janikāmātūti janikāya mātu. Yo janakoti yo janako pitā. ‘‘Yo janiko pitāteva’’ vā pāṭho.

Asitenāti pañcābhiññena asitena devalena isinā imaṃ gandhabbapañhaṃ puṭṭhā na sampāyissanti. Yesanti yesaṃ sattannaṃ isīnaṃ. Na puṇṇo dabbigāhoti tesaṃ sattannaṃ isīnaṃ dabbiṃ gahetvā paṇṇaṃ pacitvā dāyako puṇṇo nāma eko ahosi, so dabbigahaṇasippaṃ jānāti. Tvaṃ sācariyako tesaṃ puṇṇopi na hoti, tena ñātaṃ dabbigahaṇasippamattampi na jānāsīti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Asitenā Yesa Na puṇṇo dabbigāho

Ayaṃ pana assalāyano saddho ahosi pasanno, attano antonivesaneyeva cetiyaṃ kāresi. Yāvajjadivasā assalāyanavaṃse jātā nivesanaṃ kāretvā antonivesane cetiyaṃ karontevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Assalāyanasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
411.
*janikā*, *mātā* means: she by whom you are born, she is your mother, *janikā mātā*.
*janikāmātū* means the mother of the one who gives birth.
*yo janako* means he who begets, the father ( *pitā*).
‘‘yo janiko pitāteva’’ or a reading.

*asitenā* means by Asita, by the seer Asita Devala, possessing the five superknowledges; they will not approve this question of the Gandharva.
*yesa*nti to those seven seers.
*na puṇṇo dabbigāho* means: Dabbigāha was not complete: having taken a ladle for those seven seers and having cooked leaves, the giver was called Puṇṇa, one; he knew the art of ladle-taking.
You, with your teacher, are not equal to that Puṇṇa; therefore, it is known that you do not even know a little bit about the art of ladle-taking.
The rest is clear throughout.

*asitenā* *yesa* *na puṇṇo dabbigāho* This Assalāyana, however, was full of faith and serene; he had a shrine built in his own inner residence.
As long as those born in the lineage of Assalāyana have had a dwelling built, they have been building a shrine in the inner residence.

The Assalāyana-sutta commentary in the Papañcasūdanī, commentary on the Majjhima Nikāya, is finished.

mula_pali:
412. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā udeno bārāṇasiyaṃ viharati khemiyambavane. Tena kho pana samayena ghoṭamukho brāhmaṇo bārāṇasiṃ anuppatto hoti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Atha kho ghoṭamukho brāhmaṇo jaṅghāvihāraṃ anucaṅkamamāno anuvicaramāno yena khemiyambavanaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā udeno abbhokāse caṅkamati. Atha kho ghoṭamukho brāhmaṇo yenāyasmā udeno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā udenena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā āyasmantaṃ udenaṃ caṅkamantaṃ anucaṅkamamāno evamāha – ‘‘ambho samaṇa, ‘natthi dhammiko paribbajo’ paribbājo (sī. pī.) – evaṃ me ettha hoti. Tañca kho bhavantarūpānaṃ vā adassanā, yo vā panettha dhammo’’ti.

Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā udeno caṅkamā orohitvā vihāraṃ pavisitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Ghoṭamukhopi kho brāhmaṇo caṅkamā orohitvā vihāraṃ pavisitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ kho ghoṭamukhaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ āyasmā udeno etadavoca – ‘‘saṃvijjanti saṃvijjante (bahūsu) kho, brāhmaṇa, āsanāni. Sace ākaṅkhasi, nisīdā’’ti. ‘‘Etadeva kho pana mayaṃ bhoto udenassa āgamayamānā (na) nisīdāma. Kathañhi nāma mādiso pubbe animantito āsane nisīditabbaṃ maññeyyā’’ti? Atha kho ghoṭamukho brāhmaṇo aññataraṃ nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho ghoṭamukho brāhmaṇo āyasmantaṃ udenaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘ambho samaṇa, ‘natthi dhammiko paribbajo’ – evaṃ me ettha hoti. Tañca kho bhavantarūpānaṃ vā adassanā, yo vā panettha dhammo’’ti. ‘‘Sace kho pana me tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, anuññeyyaṃ anujāneyyāsi, paṭikkositabbañca paṭikkoseyyāsi; yassa ca pana me bhāsitassa atthaṃ na jāneyyāsi, mamaṃyeva tattha uttari paṭipuccheyyāsi – ‘idaṃ, bho udena, kathaṃ, imassa kvattho’ti? Evaṃ katvā siyā no ettha kathāsallāpo’’ti. ‘‘Anuññeyyaṃ khvāhaṃ bhoto udenassa anujānissāmi, paṭikkositabbañca paṭikkosissāmi; yassa ca panāhaṃ bhoto udenassa bhāsitassa atthaṃ na jānissāmi, bhavantaṃyeva tattha udenaṃ uttari paṭipucchissāmi – ‘idaṃ, bho udena, kathaṃ, imassa kvattho’ti? Evaṃ katvā hotu no ettha kathāsallāpo’’ti.

saṃvijjante (bahūsu)
mula_english:
THUS HAVE I HEARD. On one occasion the venerable Udena was living at Benares in the Khemiya Mango Grove.

Now on that occasion the brahmin Ghotamukha had arrived in Benares for some business or other.

As he was walking and wandering for exercise, he came to the Khemiya Mango Grove.

At the time the venerable Udena was walking up and down in the open.

Then the brahmin Ghotamukha went up to the venerable Udena and exchanged greetings with him.

When this courteous and amiable talk was finished, still walking up and down with the venerable Udena, he said this: “Worthy recluse, there is no wanderers’ life that accords with the *dharma*: so it seems to me here, and that may be because I have not seen such venerable ones as yourself or because I have not seen the *dharma* here.”

When this was said, the venerable Udena stepped down from the walk and went into his dwelling, where he sat down on a seat made ready.

And Ghotamukha too stepped down from the walk and went into the dwelling, where he stood at one side.

Then the venerable Udena said to him: “There are seats, brahmin, sit down if you wish.”

“We did not sit down because we were waiting for Master Udena to speak. How could someone like me presume to sit on a seat without being invited?” Then the brahmin Ghotamukha took a low seat, sat down at one side, and said to the venerable Udena: “Worthy recluse, there is no wanderers’ life that accords with the *dharma*: so it seems to me here, and that may be because I have not seen such venerable ones as yourself or because I have not seen the *dharma* here.”

“Brahmin, if you think any statement of mine is to be agreed with, then agree with it; if you think any statement of mine is to be argued against, then argue against it; and if you do not understand the meaning of any statement of mine, ask me to clarify it thus: ‘How is this, Master Udena? What is the meaning of this?’ In that way we could have a conversation here.”

“I will agree with any statement of Master Udena that is to be agreed with, and I will argue against any statement that is to be argued against; and if I do not understand the meaning of any statement of Master Udena, I will ask you to clarify it thus: ‘How is this, Master Udena? What is the meaning of this?’ In that way let us have a conversation here.”
commentary_pali: 412.Evaṃme sutanti ghoṭamukhasuttaṃ. Tattha khemiyambavaneti evaṃnāmake ambavane. Dhammiko paribbajoti dhammikā pabbajjā. Adassanāti tumhādisānaṃ vā paṇḍitānaṃ adassanena. Yo vā panettha dhammoti yo vā pana ettha dhammo sabhāvo, tasseva vā adassanena. Iminā ‘‘amhākaṃ kathā appamāṇaṃ, dhammova pamāṇa’’nti dasseti. Tato thero ‘‘navauposathāgāre viya bahunā kammena idha bhavitabba’’nti cintetvā caṅkamā oruyha paṇṇasālaṃ pavisitvā nisīdi. Taṃ dassetuṃ evaṃ vuttetiādi vuttaṃ.
commentary_english:
412. "Thus I have heard," the Ghoṭamukha Sutta.

There, *khemiyambavane* means in an mango grove named thus. *dhammiko paribbajo* means, Dhāmmikā entered the monastic life. *adassanā* means, by the non-seeing of those like you or learned individuals. *yo vā panettha dhammo* means, or whatever Dharma, the nature, that is here; or, by the non-seeing of that itself. By this, he shows, "Our talk is not the measure; the Dharma itself is the measure."

Then the elder, thinking, "There must be much work here, like in a new uposatha hall," descended from the cloister, entered the leaf hut, and sat down. To show that, *evaṃ vutte* etc. was stated.

mula_pali:
413. ‘‘Cattārome, brāhmaṇa, puggalā santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ. Katame cattāro? Idha, brāhmaṇa, ekacco puggalo attantapo hoti attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto. Idha pana, brāhmaṇa, ekacco puggalo parantapo hoti paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto. Idha pana, brāhmaṇa, ekacco puggalo attantapo ca hoti attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto parantapo ca paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto. Idha pana, brāhmaṇa , ekacco puggalo nevattantapo hoti nāttaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto, na parantapo na paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto. So anattantapo aparantapo diṭṭheva dhamme nicchāto nibbuto sītībhūto sukhappaṭisaṃvedī brahmabhūtena attanā viharati. Imesaṃ, brāhmaṇa, catunnaṃ puggalānaṃ katamo te puggalo cittaṃ ārādhetī’’ti?

‘‘Yvāyaṃ, bho udena, puggalo attantapo attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto ayaṃ me puggalo cittaṃ nārādheti; yopāyaṃ, bho udena, puggalo parantapo paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto ayampi me puggalo cittaṃ nārādheti; yopāyaṃ, bho udena, puggalo attantapo ca attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto parantapo ca paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto ayampi me puggalo cittaṃ nārādheti; yo ca kho ayaṃ, bho udena, puggalo nevattantapo nāttaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto na parantapo na paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto so anattantapo aparantapo diṭṭheva dhamme nicchāto nibbuto sītībhūto sukhappaṭisaṃvedī brahmabhūtena attanā viharati. Ayameva me puggalo cittaṃ ārādhetī’’ti.

‘‘Kasmā pana te, brāhmaṇa, ime tayo puggalā cittaṃ nārādhentī’’ti? ‘‘Yvāyaṃ, bho udena, puggalo attantapo attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto so attānaṃ sukhakāmaṃ dukkhapaṭikkūlaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti; iminā me ayaṃ puggalo cittaṃ nārādheti. Yopāyaṃ , bho udena, puggalo parantapo paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto so paraṃ sukhakāmaṃ dukkhapaṭikkūlaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti; iminā me ayaṃ puggalo cittaṃ nārādheti. Yopāyaṃ, bho udena, puggalo attantapo ca attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto parantapo ca paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto so attānañca parañca sukhakāmaṃ dukkhapaṭikkūlaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti; iminā me ayaṃ puggalo cittaṃ nārādheti. Yo ca kho ayaṃ, bho udena, puggalo nevattantapo nāttaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto na parantapo na paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto so anattantapo aparantapo diṭṭheva dhamme nicchāto nibbuto sītībhūto sukhappaṭisaṃvedī brahmabhūtena attanā viharati, so attānañca parañca sukhakāmaṃ dukkhapaṭikkūlaṃ neva ātāpeti na paritāpeti; iminā me ayaṃ puggalo cittaṃ ārādhetī’’ti.
mula_english:
413. “Brāhmaṇa, there are these four types of individuals to be found existing in the world.

What four? Here, brāhmaṇa, a certain individual torments himself and is devoted to the practice of torturing himself ( *attantapo*).

Here, brāhmaṇa, a certain individual torments others and is devoted to the practice of torturing others ( *parantapo*).

Here, brāhmaṇa, a certain individual torments himself and is devoted to the practice of torturing himself, and also torments others and is devoted to the practice of torturing others.

Here, brāhmaṇa, a certain individual neither torments himself nor is he devoted to the practice of torturing himself, neither torments others nor is he devoted to the practice of torturing others.

Neither tormenting himself nor tormenting others, he dwells in the here & now free of hunger, unbound, cooled, sensitive to happiness with a Brahma-like mind ( *brahmabhūtena attanā viharati*).

Of these four individuals, brāhmaṇa, which individual satisfies your mind?”

“That individual, Master Udena, who torments himself and is devoted to the practice of torturing himself, that individual does not satisfy my mind. That individual, Master Udena, who torments others and is devoted to the practice of torturing others, that individual also does not satisfy my mind. That individual, Master Udena, who torments himself and is devoted to the practice of torturing himself, and also torments others and is devoted to the practice of torturing others, that individual also does not satisfy my mind. But that individual, Master Udena, who neither torments himself nor is devoted to the practice of torturing himself, neither torments others nor is he devoted to the practice of torturing others; who—neither tormenting himself nor tormenting others—dwells in the here & now free of hunger, unbound, cooled, sensitive to happiness with a Brahmā-like mind.

That very individual satisfies my mind.”

“But why, brāhmaṇa, do these three individuals not satisfy your mind?” “That individual, Master Udena, who torments himself and is devoted to the practice of torturing himself, torments and tortures himself though he desires pleasure and recoils from pain; that is why this individual does not satisfy my mind.

That individual, Master Udena, who torments others and is devoted to the practice of torturing others, torments and tortures others who desire pleasure and recoil from pain; that is why this individual does not satisfy my mind.

That individual, Master Udena, who torments himself and is devoted to the practice of torturing himself, and who also torments others and is devoted to the practice of torturing others, torments and tortures himself and others, both of whom desire pleasure and recoil from pain; that is why this individual does not satisfy my mind.

But that individual, Master Udena, who neither torments himself nor is devoted to the practice of torturing himself, neither torments others nor is he devoted to the practice of torturing others; who—neither tormenting himself nor tormenting others—dwells in the here & now free of hunger, unbound, cooled, sensitive to happiness with a Brahmā-like mind; he does not torment and torture either himself or others, both of whom desire pleasure and recoil from pain. That is why this individual satisfies my mind.”
commentary_pali: 413.Cattārome brāhmaṇāti therassa kira etadahosi – ‘‘ayaṃ brāhmaṇo ‘dhammikaṃ pabbajjaṃ upagato samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā natthī’ti vadati. Imassa cattāro puggale dve ca parisā dassetvā ‘catutthaṃ puggalaṃ katarāya parisāya bahulaṃ passasī’ti pucchissāmi, jānamāno ‘anāgāriyaparisāya’nti vakkhati. Evametaṃ sakamukheneva ‘dhammiko paribbajo atthī’ti vadāpessāmī’’ti imaṃ desanaṃ ārabhi.
commentary_english:
413. *cattārome brāhmaṇā* [Four Brahmans]: It occurred to the Elder (thera) thus: “This Brahman, having adopted an unrighteous (adharmika) ordination (pabbajja), says, ‘There is no *śramaṇa* or *brāhmaṇa*.’

Having shown this person four individuals (puggala) and two assemblies (parisā), I will ask, ‘In which assembly do you see the fourth individual most?’ Knowing, he will say, ‘In the homeless (anāgāriya) assembly.’

Thus, through his own mouth (sakamukhena), I will make him say, ‘There is a righteous wanderer (dhammiko paribbajo).’” Thus, he began this discourse (desana).

mula_pali:
414. ‘‘Dvemā, brāhmaṇa, parisā. Katamā dve? Idha, brāhmaṇa, ekaccā parisā sārattarattā maṇikuṇḍalesu puttabhariyaṃ pariyesati, dāsidāsaṃ pariyesati, khettavatthuṃ pariyesati, jātarūparajataṃ pariyesati.

‘‘Idha pana, brāhmaṇa, ekaccā parisā asārattarattā maṇikuṇḍalesu puttabhariyaṃ pahāya, dāsidāsaṃ pahāya, khettavatthuṃ pahāya, jātarūparajataṃ pahāya, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā. Svāyaṃ, brāhmaṇa, puggalo nevattantapo nāttaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto na parantapo na paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto. So anattantapo aparantapo diṭṭheva dhamme nicchāto nibbuto sītībhūto sukhappaṭisaṃvedī brahmabhūtena attanā viharati. Idha katamaṃ tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, puggalaṃ katamāya parisāya bahulaṃ samanupassasi – yā cāyaṃ parisā sārattarattā maṇikuṇḍalesu puttabhariyaṃ pariyesati dāsidāsaṃ pariyesati khettavatthuṃ pariyesati jātarūparajataṃ pariyesati, yā cāyaṃ parisā asārattarattā maṇikuṇḍalesu puttabhariyaṃ pahāya dāsidāsaṃ pahāya khettavatthuṃ pahāya jātarūparajataṃ pahāya agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā’’ti?

‘‘Yvāyaṃ , bho udena, puggalo nevattantapo nāttaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto na parantapo na paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto so anattantapo aparantapo diṭṭheva dhamme nicchāto nibbuto sītībhūto sukhappaṭisaṃvedī brahmabhūtena attanā viharati; imāhaṃ puggalaṃ yāyaṃ parisā asārattarattā maṇikuṇḍalesu puttabhariyaṃ pahāya dāsidāsaṃ pahāya khettavatthuṃ pahāya jātarūparajataṃ pahāya agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā imissaṃ parisāyaṃ bahulaṃ samanupassāmī’’ti.

‘‘Idāneva kho pana te, brāhmaṇa, bhāsitaṃ – ‘mayaṃ evaṃ ājānāma – ambho samaṇa, natthi dhammiko paribbajo, evaṃ me ettha hoti. Tañca kho bhavantarūpānaṃ vā adassanā, yo vā panettha dhammo’’’ti. ‘‘Addhā mesā, bho udena, sānuggahā vācā bhāsitā. ‘Atthi dhammiko paribbajo’ – evaṃ me ettha hoti. Evañca pana maṃ bhavaṃ udeno dhāretu. Ye ca me bhotā udenena cattāro puggalā saṃkhittena vuttā vitthārena avibhattā, sādhu me bhavaṃ, udeno ime cattāro puggale vitthārena vibhajatu anukampaṃ upādāyā’’ti. ‘‘Tena hi, brāhmaṇa, suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bho’’ti kho ghoṭamukho brāhmaṇo āyasmato udenassa paccassosi. Āyasmā udeno etadavoca –
mula_english:
414. “Brahmin, there are these two kinds of assembly.

What are the two? Here, brahmin, a certain assembly is consumed by passion and seeks jewels and earrings, wives and children, men and women slaves, fields and land, gold and silver.

But here, brahmin, a certain assembly, not consumed by passion, having abandoned jewels and earrings, wives and children, men and women slaves, fields and land, gold and silver, has gone forth from the household life into homelessness.

Now, brahmin, this person neither torments himself nor pursues the practice of torturing himself, and he neither torments others nor pursues the practice of torturing others.

Since he torments neither himself nor others, he dwells in the here and now free of hunger, extinguished, cooled, sensitive to happiness, with a mind that has become like Brahmā.

Here, brahmin, in which of these two kinds of assembly do you most often see this person—in the assembly that is consumed by passion and seeks jewels and earrings, wives and children, men and women slaves, fields and land, gold and silver, or in the assembly that is not consumed by passion, having abandoned jewels and earrings, wives and children, men and women slaves, fields and land, gold and silver, [and] has gone forth from the home life into homelessness?"

, Master Udena, this person neither torments himself nor pursues the practice of torturing himself, and he neither torments others nor pursues the practice of torturing others. Since he torments neither himself nor others, he dwells in the here and now free of hunger, extinguished, cooled, sensitive to happiness, with a mind that has become like Brahmā; I usually see this person in the assembly that is not consumed by passion, having abandoned jewels and earrings, wives and children, men and women slaves, fields and land, gold and silver, [and] has gone forth from the home life into homelessness.”

“Just now, brahmin, you said: ‘We understand thus: “Worthy samaṇa, there is no wanderer’s life that accords with the *dharma,* thus it seems to me here. And that is because I have not seen venerable ones like yourself, or because I have not seen the *dharma* here.’”

“Certainly, Master Udena, those words were spoken to elicit a response. ‘There is a wanderer’s life that accords with the *dharma*’—thus it seems to me here.

And may Master Udena remember me [as having spoken] thus.

And it would be good if, out of compassion, Master Udena would expound to me in detail those four kinds of persons he mentioned in brief.”

“Then, brahmin, listen and pay careful attention, I shall speak.”

“Yes, sir,” the brahmin Ghotamukha replied to the Venerable Udena.

The Venerable Udena said this:
commentary_pali: 414. Tattha sārattarattāti suṭṭhu rattarattā. Sānuggahā vācā bhāsitā sakāraṇā vācā bhāsitā. Vuttañhetaṃ mayā ‘‘amhākaṃ kathā appamāṇaṃ, dhammova pamāṇa’’nti.
commentary_english:
414.
There, *sārattarattā* means exceedingly reddened.

*Sānuggahā vācā bhāsitā* means speech that is accompanied by favor, and *sakāraṇā vācā bhāsitā* means speech that is accompanied by reason.

This was said by me, "Our conversation is immeasurable, the *dharma* is the measure."

mula_pali: 415. ‘‘Katamo ca, brāhmaṇa, puggalo attantapo attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto? Idha, brāhmaṇa, ekacco puggalo acelako hoti muttācāro hatthāpalekhano naehibhaddantiko natiṭṭhabhaddantiko, nābhihaṭaṃ na uddissakataṃ na nimantanaṃ sādiyati. So na kumbhimukhā paṭiggaṇhāti, na kaḷopimukhā paṭiggaṇhāti, na eḷakamantaraṃ, na daṇḍamantaraṃ, na musalamantaraṃ, na dvinnaṃ bhuñjamānānaṃ, na gabbhiniyā, na pāyamānāya , na purisantaragatāya, na saṅkittīsu, na yattha sā upaṭṭhito hoti, na yattha makkhikā saṇḍasaṇḍacārinī, na macchaṃ na maṃsaṃ, na suraṃ na merayaṃ na thusodakaṃ pivati. So ekāgāriko vā hoti ekālopiko, dvāgāriko vā hoti dvālopiko…pe… sattāgāriko vā hoti sattālopiko; ekissāpi dattiyā yāpeti, dvīhipi dattīhi yāpeti…pe… sattahipi dattīhi yāpeti; ekāhikampi āhāraṃ āhāreti, dvīhikampi āhāraṃ āhāreti…pe… sattāhikampi āhāraṃ āhāreti – iti evarūpaṃ addhamāsikaṃ pariyāyabhattabhojanānuyogamanuyutto viharati. So sākabhakkho vā hoti, sāmākabhakkho vā hoti, nīvārabhakkho vā hoti, daddulabhakkho vā hoti , haṭabhakkho vā hoti, kaṇabhakkho vā hoti, ācāmabhakkho vā hoti, piññākabhakkho vā hoti, tiṇabhakkho vā hoti, gomayabhakkho vā hoti, vanamūlaphalāhāro yāpeti pavattaphalabhojī. So sāṇānipi dhāreti, masāṇānipi dhāreti, chavadussānipi dhāreti, paṃsukūlānipi dhāreti, tirīṭānipi dhāreti, ajinampi dhāreti, ajinakkhipampi dhāreti, kusacīrampi dhāreti, vākacīrampi dhāreti, phalakacīrampi dhāreti, kesakambalampi dhāreti, vāḷakambalampi dhāreti, ulūkapakkhampi dhāreti; kesamassulocakopi hoti kesamassulocanānuyogamanuyutto , ubbhaṭṭhakopi hoti āsanapaṭikkhitto, ukkuṭikopi hoti ukkuṭikappadhānamanuyutto, kaṇṭakāpassayikopi hoti kaṇṭakāpassaye seyyaṃ kappeti; sāyatatiyakampi udakorohanānuyogamanuyutto viharati – iti evarūpaṃ anekavihitaṃ kāyassa ātāpanaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto viharati. Ayaṃ vuccati, brāhmaṇa, puggalo attantapo attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto.
mula_english:
415.  Furthermore, brāhmaṇa, what kind of person is one who torments himself and is devoted to the practice of torturing himself? Here, brāhmaṇa, a certain person goes naked, rejecting conventions, licking his hands, not coming when asked, not stopping when asked; he does not accept food brought, food specially made, or an invitation to a meal.

He does not accept food from a pot, from a bowl, across a threshold, across a stick, across a pestle, from two eating together, from a pregnant woman, from a woman giving suck, from a woman living with a man, from where food is advertised to be distributed, from where a dog is waiting, from where flies are buzzing; he accepts no fish or meat, he drinks no liquor, wine, or fermented brew.

He is a one-house man or a one-morsel man, a two-house man or a two-morsel man… he is a seven-house man or a seven-morsel man; he lives on one saucerful a day, on two saucerfuls a day…on seven saucerfuls a day; he eats food once a day, once every two days…once every seven days—thus in such a variety of ways he dwells pursuing the practice of taking food at stated intervals every half month.

He is an eater of greens or millet or wild rice or hide-parings or moss or rice bran or rice-scum or sesamum flour or grass or cow dung. He lives on forest roots and fruits; he feeds on fallen fruits.

He wears coarse hemp or mixed material, shrouds from corpses, rags from the dust-heap, garments of bark-fibre, antelope-skins, grass, bark, shavings, blankets of human hair or horse-hair, the wings of owls. He is one who pulls out hair and beard, pursuing the practice of pulling out hair and beard; he is one who stands continuously, rejecting seats; he is one who squats continuously, devoted to maintaining the squatting position; he is one who uses a mattress of spikes; he makes a mattress of spikes his bed; he dwells pursuing the practice of bathing in water three times daily including the evening—thus in such a variety of ways he dwells pursuing the practice of tormenting and mortifying the body.

This, brāhmaṇa, is called a person who torments himself and is devoted to the practice of torturing himself ( *attantapo 'ttaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto* ).

mula_pali: 416. ‘‘Katamo ca, brāhmaṇa, puggalo parantapo paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto? Idha, brāhmaṇa, ekacco puggalo orabbhiko hoti sūkariko sākuṇiko māgaviko luddo macchaghātako coro coraghātako goghātako bandhanāgāriko – ye vā panaññepi keci kurūrakammantā. Ayaṃ vuccati, brāhmaṇa, puggalo parantapo paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto.
mula_english:
Here, brahmin, what sort of person is a tormentor of others, one who is devoted to torturing others? Here, brahmin, a certain individual is a butcher of sheep (*orabbhika*), a butcher of pigs (*sūkarika*), a fowler (*sākuṇika*), a trapper (*māgavika*), a hunter (*ludda*), a fisherman (*macchaghātaka*), a thief (*cora*), an executioner (*coraghātaka*), a cattle-slaughterer (*goghātaka*), a prison warden (*bandhanāgārika*), or anyone who follows any other such cruel occupation (*kurūrakammantā*).

This, brahmin, is called a person who torments others and is devoted to the practice of torturing others. (*puggalo parantapo paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto*)

mula_pali: 417. ‘‘Katamo ca, brāhmaṇa, puggalo attantapo ca attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto, parantapo ca paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto? Idha, brāhmaṇa, ekacco puggalo rājā vā hoti khattiyo muddhāvasitto, brāhmaṇo vā mahāsālo. So puratthimena nagarassa navaṃ santhāgāraṃ kārāpetvā kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kharājinaṃ nivāsetvā sappitelena kāyaṃ abbhañjitvā magavisāṇena piṭṭhiṃ kaṇḍuvamāno navaṃ santhāgāraṃ pavisati saddhiṃ mahesiyā brāhmaṇena ca purohitena. So tattha anantarahitāya bhūmiyā haritupalittāya seyyaṃ kappeti. Ekissāya gāviyā sarūpavacchāya yaṃ ekasmiṃ thane khīraṃ hoti tena rājā yāpeti, yaṃ dutiyasmiṃ thane khīraṃ hoti tena mahesī yāpeti, yaṃ tatiyasmiṃ thane khīraṃ hoti tena brāhmaṇo purohito yāpeti, yaṃ catutthasmiṃ thane khīraṃ hoti tena aggiṃ juhati, avasesena vacchako yāpeti. So evamāha – ‘ettakā usabhā haññantu yaññatthāya, ettakā vacchatarā haññantu yaññatthāya, ettakā vacchatariyo haññantu yaññatthāya, ettakā ajā haññantu yaññatthāya’, ettakā urabbhā haññantu yaññatthāya, ettakā assā haññantu yaññatthāya, ettakā rukkhā chijjantu yūpatthāya, ettakā dabbhā lūyantu barihisatthāyā’ti. Yepissa te honti ‘dāsā’ti vā ‘pessā’ti vā ‘kammakarā’ti vā tepi daṇḍatajjitā bhayatajjitā assumukhā rudamānā parikammāni karonti. Ayaṃ vuccati, brāhmaṇa, puggalo attantapo ca attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto , parantapo ca paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto.
mula_english:
417. "And which, *brāhmaṇa*, is the individual who torments himself and is devoted to the practice of torturing himself, [and] who torments others and is devoted to the practice of torturing others? Here, *brāhmaṇa*, some person is a head-anointed noble king (*rājā*), or a well-to-do *brāhmaṇa*.

Having had a new sacrificial temple (*santhāgāraṃ*) built to the east of the city, and having shaved off his hair and beard, dressed himself in rough hide (*kharājinaṃ*), and greased his body with ghee and oil, scratching his back with a deer’s horn, he enters the new sacrificial temple (*santhāgāraṃ*) together with his chief queen (*mahesī*) and his *brāhmaṇa* high priest (*purohitena*).

There he lies down on the bare ground with the grass on it.

The king lives on the milk in the first teat of a cow (*gāviyā*) with a calf of the same color (*sarūpavacchāya*) while the chief queen (*mahesī*) lives on the milk in the second teat and the *brāhmaṇa* high priest (*purohito*) lives on the milk in the third teat; the milk in the fourth teat they pour onto the fire (*aggiṃ juhati*), and the calf lives on what is left.

He says thus: ‘Let so many bulls (*usabhā*) be slaughtered for sacrifice (*yaññatthāya*), let so many bullocks (*vacchatarā*) be slaughtered for sacrifice (*yaññatthāya*), let so many heifers (*vacchatariyo*) be slaughtered for sacrifice (*yaññatthāya*), let so many goats (*ajā*) be slaughtered for sacrifice (*yaññatthāya*), let so many sheep (*urabbhā*) be slaughtered for sacrifice (*yaññatthāya*), let so many horses (*assā*) be slaughtered for sacrifice (*yaññatthāya*), let so many trees (*rukhā*) be felled for the sacrificial posts (*yūpatthāya*), let so much grass (*dabbhā*) be cut for the sacrificial grass (*barihisatthāyā*).’

And then his slaves (*dāsā*), messengers (*pessā*), and servants (*kammakarā*) make preparations, weeping with tearful faces, being spurred on by threats of punishment and by fear.

This is called the kind of person who torments himself (*attantapo*) and pursues the practice of torturing himself (*attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto*) and who torments others (*parantapo*) and pursues the practice of torturing others (*paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto*)."

mula_pali:
418. ‘‘Katamo ca, brāhmaṇa, puggalo nevattantapo nāttaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto, na parantapo na paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto; so anattantapo aparantapo diṭṭheva dhamme nicchāto nibbuto sītībhūto sukhappaṭisaṃvedī brahmabhūtena attanā viharati? Idha, brāhmaṇa, tathāgato loke uppajjati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā. So imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti. So dhammaṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāseti. Taṃ dhammaṃ suṇāti gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā aññatarasmiṃ vā kule paccājāto. So taṃ dhammaṃ sutvā tathāgate saddhaṃ paṭilabhati. So tena saddhāpaṭilābhena samannāgato iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘sambādho gharāvāso rajopatho abbhokāso pabbajjā. Nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ ekantaparisuddhaṃ saṅkhalikhitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajeyya’nti. So aparena samayena appaṃ vā bhogakkhandhaṃ pahāya mahantaṃ vā bhogakkhandhaṃ pahāya, appaṃ vā ñātiparivaṭṭaṃ pahāya mahantaṃ vā ñātiparivaṭṭaṃ pahāya, kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati. So evaṃ pabbajito samāno bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāsājīvasamāpanno pāṇātipātaṃ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho lajjī dayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharati.

‘‘Adinnādānaṃ pahāya adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti dinnādāyī dinnapāṭikaṅkhī. Athenena sucibhūtena attanā viharati.

‘‘Abrahmacariyaṃ pahāya brahmacārī hoti ārācārī virato methunā gāmadhammā.

‘‘Musāvādaṃ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato hoti saccavādī saccasandho theto paccayiko avisaṃvādako lokassa.

‘‘Pisuṇaṃ vācaṃ pahāya pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti; ito sutvā na amutra akkhātā imesaṃ bhedāya, amutra vā sutvā na imesaṃ akkhātā amūsaṃ bhedāya. Iti bhinnānaṃ vā sandhātā sahitānaṃ vā anuppadātā, samaggārāmo samaggarato samagganandī samaggakaraṇiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti.

‘‘Pharusaṃ vācaṃ pahāya pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti. Yā sā vācā nelā kaṇṇasukhā pemanīyā hadayaṅgamā porī bahujanakantā bahujanamanāpā tathārūpiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti.

‘‘Samphappalāpaṃ pahāya samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, kālavādī bhūtavādī atthavādī dhammavādī vinayavādī, nidhānavatiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā kālena sāpadesaṃ pariyantavatiṃ atthasaṃhitaṃ.

‘‘So bījagāmabhūtagāmasamārambhā paṭivirato hoti . Ekabhattiko hoti rattūparato virato vikālabhojanā. Naccagītavāditavisūkadassanā paṭivirato hoti. Mālāgandhavilepanadhāraṇamaṇḍanavibhūsanaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti. Uccāsayanamahāsayanā paṭivirato hoti. Jātarūparajatapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti. Āmakadhaññapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti. Āmakamaṃsapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti. Itthikumārikapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti. Dāsidāsapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti. Ajeḷakapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti. Kukkuṭasūkarapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti. Hatthigavassavaḷavapaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti. Khettavatthupaṭiggahaṇā paṭivirato hoti. Dūteyyapahiṇagamanānuyogā paṭivirato hoti. Kayavikkayā paṭivirato hoti. Tulākūṭakaṃsakūṭamānakūṭā paṭivirato hoti. Ukkoṭanavañcananikatisāciyogā paṭivirato hoti. Chedanavadhabandhanaviparāmosaālopasahasākārā paṭivirato hoti.

‘‘So santuṭṭho hoti kāyaparihārikena cīvarena, kucchiparihārikena piṇḍapātena. So yena yeneva pakkamati samādāyeva pakkamati. Seyyathāpi nāma pakkhī sakuṇo yena yeneva ḍeti sapattabhārova ḍeti, evameva bhikkhu santuṭṭho hoti kāyaparihārikena cīvarena, kucchiparihārikena piṇḍapātena. So yena yeneva pakkamati samādāyeva pakkamati. So iminā ariyena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato ajjhattaṃ anavajjasukhaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti.
mula_english:
418. “And what, brahmin, is the individual who is neither devoted to self-mortification nor to the practice of torturing oneself, neither devoted to the mortification of others nor to the practice of torturing others; being not a self-mortifier, nor a mortifier of others, is cool, quenched, and has become peaceful in this very life, experiencing pleasure, abiding with a self that has become like Brahmā? Here, brahmin, a *Tathāgata* appears in the world, accomplished, fully enlightened, perfect in true knowledge and conduct, sublime, knower of worlds, incomparable leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, enlightened, blessed.

He, having realised it by his own super-knowledge, proclaims this world with its gods, *Māras,* and *Brahmās,* its princes and people.

He preaches the *Dharma,* which is lovely in its beginning, lovely in its middle, lovely in its ending, in the spirit and in the letter, and displays the fully-perfected and purified holy life.

A householder or householder’s son or one born in some other clan hears that *Dharma.*

Having heard this *Dharma,* he gains faith in the *Tathāgata.*

Possessing that faith, he considers thus: ‘Household life is crowded and dusty; life gone forth is wide open.

It is not easy while living in a home to lead the holy life utterly perfect and pure as a polished shell.

What if I were to shave off my hair & beard, put on the ochre robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness?’

On a later occasion, abandoning a small or a large fortune, abandoning a small or a large circle of relatives, he shaves off his hair and beard, puts on the yellow robe, and goes forth from the home life into homelessness.

Having thus gone forth and possessing the *bhikkhus'* training and way of life, abandoning the killing of living beings, he abstains from killing living beings; with rod and weapon laid aside, gentle and kindly, he abides compassionate to all living beings.

“Abandoning stealing, he abstains from stealing; he takes only what is given, and expects only what is given.
By not stealing he abides in purity.
