commentary_pali: 426.Opātetīti paveseti. Saṃpurekkharontīti puttamattanattamattampi samānaṃ purato katvā vicaranti.
commentary_english:
Thus opātetī.
paveseti.
saṃpurekkharontī, having placed their children equally in front, they wander around.

mula_pali:
427. Atha kho kāpaṭikassa māṇavassa etadahosi – ‘‘samannāharati kho maṃ samaṇo gotamo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ pañhaṃ puccheyya’’nti. Atha kho kāpaṭiko māṇavo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘yadidaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇānaṃ porāṇaṃ mantapadaṃ itihitihaparamparāya piṭakasampadāya, tattha ca brāhmaṇā ekaṃsena niṭṭhaṃ gacchanti – ‘idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’nti. Idha bhavaṃ gotamo kimāhā’’ti? ‘‘Kiṃ pana, bhāradvāja, atthi koci brāhmaṇānaṃ ekabrāhmaṇopi yo evamāha – ‘ahametaṃ jānāmi, ahametaṃ passāmi. Idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’’’nti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’. ‘‘Kiṃ pana, bhāradvāja, atthi koci brāhmaṇānaṃ ekācariyopi , ekācariyapācariyopi, yāva sattamā ācariyamahayugāpi, yo evamāha – ‘ahametaṃ jānāmi, ahametaṃ passāmi. Idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’’’nti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’. ‘‘Kiṃ pana, bhāradvāja, yepi te brāhmaṇānaṃ pubbakā isayo mantānaṃ kattāro mantānaṃ pavattāro yesamidaṃ etarahi brāhmaṇā porāṇaṃ mantapadaṃ gītaṃ pavuttaṃ samihitaṃ tadanugāyanti tadanubhāsanti bhāsitamanubhāsanti vācitamanuvācenti seyyathidaṃ – aṭṭhako vāmako vāmadevo vessāmitto yamataggi aṅgīraso bhāradvājo vāseṭṭho kassapo bhagu, tepi evamāhaṃsu – ‘mayametaṃ jānāma, mayametaṃ passāma. Idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’’’nti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’.

‘‘Iti kira, bhāradvāja, natthi koci brāhmaṇānaṃ ekabrāhmaṇopi yo evamāha – ‘ahametaṃ jānāmi, ahametaṃ passāmi. Idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’nti; natthi koci brāhmaṇānaṃ ekācariyopi ekācariyapācariyopi, yāva sattamā ācariyamahayugāpi, yo evamāha – ‘ahametaṃ jānāmi, ahametaṃ passāmi. Idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’nti; yepi te brāhmaṇānaṃ pubbakā isayo mantānaṃ kattāro mantānaṃ pavattāro yesamidaṃ etarahi brāhmaṇā porāṇaṃ mantapadaṃ gītaṃ pavuttaṃ samihitaṃ tadanugāyanti tadanubhāsanti bhāsitamanubhāsanti vācitamanuvācenti seyyathidaṃ – aṭṭhako vāmako vāmadevo vessāmitto yamataggi aṅgīraso bhāradvājo vāseṭṭho kassapo bhagu, tepi na evamāhaṃsu – ‘mayametaṃ jānāma, mayametaṃ passāma. Idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’nti.
mula_english:
Then the brahmin student Kāpaṭhika thought: “The recluse Gotama has turned towards me. Suppose I ask the recluse Gotama a question.”

Then the brahmin student Kāpaṭhika said this to the Blessed One: “Master Gotama, in regard to the ancient brahmanic *mantra* verses of the Brahmins that have come down through oral transmission and in the scriptural collections (*piṭakasampadāya*), the Brahmins come to the definite conclusion: ‘Only this is true, anything else is wrong.’ What does the esteemed Gotama say about this?”

“How then, Bhāradvāja, among the Brahmins is there even a single Brahmin who says thus: ‘I know this, I see this: only this is true, anything else is wrong’?”

“No, Master Gotama.”

“How then, Bhāradvāja, among the Brahmins is there even a single teacher, or a single teacher’s teacher back to the seventh generation of teachers (*ācariyamahayugāpi*), who says thus: ‘I know this, I see this: only this is true, anything else is wrong’?”

“No, Master Gotama.”

“How then, Bhāradvāja, about those ancient *ṛṣis* of the Brahmins, the creators of the *mantras*, the composers of the *mantras*, whose ancient *mantra* verses that were formerly chanted, uttered, and compiled, the Brahmins nowadays still chant and repeat, repeating what was spoken and reciting what was recited - that is, Aṭṭhaka, Vāmaka, Vāmadeva, Vessāmitta, Yamataggi, Aṅgīrasa, Bhāradvāja, Vāseṭṭha, Kassapa, and Bhagu – did even these say thus: ‘We know this, we see this: only this is true, anything else is wrong’?”

“No, Master Gotama.”

“So, Bhāradvāja, it seems that among the Brahmins there is not even a single Brahmin who says thus: ‘I know this, I see this: only this is true, anything else is wrong.’ And among the Brahmins there is not even a single teacher or a single teacher’s teacher back to the seventh generation of teachers, who says thus: ‘I know this, I see this: only this is true, anything else is wrong.’ And the ancient *ṛṣis* of the Brahmins, the creators of the *mantras*, the composers of the *mantras*, whose ancient *mantra* verses that were formerly chanted, uttered, and compiled, the Brahmins nowadays still chant and repeat, repeating what was spoken and reciting what was recited - that is, Aṭṭhaka, Vāmaka, Vāmadeva, Vessāmitta, Yamataggi, Aṅgīrasa, Bhāradvāja, Vāseṭṭha, Kassapa, and Bhagu – even these ancient seers did not say thus: ‘We know this, we see this: only this is true, anything else is wrong.’”
commentary_pali: 427.Mantapadanti mantāyeva mantapadaṃ, vedoti attho. Itihitiha paramparāyāti evaṃ kira evaṃ kirāti paramparabhāvena āgatanti dīpeti. Piṭakasampadāyāti pāvacanasaṅkhātasampattiyā. Sāvittiādīhi chandabandhehi ca vaggabandhehi ca sampādetvā āgatanti dasseti. Tattha cāti tasmiṃ mantapade. Pavattāroti pavattayitāro. Yesanti yesaṃ santakaṃ. Mantapadanti vedasaṅkhātaṃ mantameva. Gītanti aṭṭhakādīhi dasahi porāṇakabrāhmaṇehi padasampattivasena sajjhāyitaṃ. Pavuttanti aññesaṃ vuttaṃ, vācitanti attho. Samihitanti samupabyūḷhaṃ rāsikataṃ, piṇḍaṃ katvā ṭhapitanti attho. Tadanugāyantīti etarahi brāhmaṇā taṃ tehi pubbe gītaṃ anugāyanti anusajjhāyanti vādenti. Tadanubhāsantīti taṃ anubhāsanti, idaṃ purimasseva vevacanaṃ. Bhāsitamanubhāsantīti tehi bhāsitaṃ sajjhāyitaṃ anusajjhāyanti. Vācitamanuvācentīti tehi aññesaṃ vācitaṃ anuvācenti. Seyyathidanti te katameti attho. Aṭṭhakotiādīni tesaṃ nāmāni, te kira dibbena cakkhunā oloketvā parūpaghātaṃ akatvā kassapasammāsambuddhassa bhagavato pāvacanena saha saṃsandetvā mante ganthesuṃ, aparāpare pana brāhmaṇā pāṇātipātādīni pakkhipitvā tayo vede bhinditvā buddhavacanena saddhiṃ viruddhe akaṃsu.
commentary_english:
427. *Mantapada* means just mantra-words, *veda*, is the meaning.

*Itihitiha paramparāyā* means thus, it is said, thus it is said, it indicates that it came about through successive transmission.

*Piṭakasampadāyā* means possessing the collection of teachings.

It shows that it came about by bringing together meters and verse structures, etc.

*Tattha cā* means in that mantra-word.

*Pavattāro* means the instigators.

*Yesa* means belonging to whom.

*Mantapada* means mantra which is known as the Veda.

*Gīta* means that it was recited with the possession of words by the ancient Brahmins, such as Aṭṭhaka and others.

*Pavutta* means spoken by others; the meaning is "recited".

*Samihita* means heaped up together, made into a mass, having made a lump it was established, this is the meaning.

*Tadanugāyantī* means nowadays Brahmins sing that which was formerly sung by them, they recite it, they perform it.

*Tadanubhāsantī* means they speak that; this is a synonym of the former.

*Bhāsitamanubhāsantī* means that which was spoken by them, they recite it, they repeat it.

*Vācitamanuvācentī* means they cause to recite that which was recited to others by them.

*Seyyathida* means what are those? This is the meaning.

*Aṭṭhako* and the others are their names; it is said that they, having looked with divine eyes, not doing harm to others, having brought together the teachings of the Blessed One, Kassapasammāsambuddha, composed the mantras. But other Brahmins, having inserted things such as killing living beings, having broken the three Vedas, made things contradictory with the words of the Buddha.

mula_pali: 428. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, bhāradvāja, andhaveṇi paramparāsaṃsattā purimopi na passati majjhimopi na passati pacchimopi na passati; evameva kho, bhāradvāja, andhaveṇūpamaṃ maññe brāhmaṇānaṃ bhāsitaṃ sampajjati – purimopi na passati majjhimopi na passati pacchimopi na passati. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, bhāradvāja , nanu evaṃ sante brāhmaṇānaṃ amūlikā saddhā sampajjatī’’ti? ‘‘Na khvettha, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā saddhāyeva payirupāsanti, anussavāpettha brāhmaṇā payirupāsantī’’ti. ‘‘Pubbeva kho tvaṃ, bhāradvāja, saddhaṃ agamāsi, anussavaṃ idāni vadesi. Pañca kho ime, bhāradvāja, dhammā diṭṭheva dhamme dvedhā vipākā. Katame pañca? Saddhā, ruci, anussavo, ākāraparivitakko, diṭṭhinijjhānakkhanti – ime kho, bhāradvāja , pañca dhammā diṭṭheva dhamme dvedhā vipākā. Api ca, bhāradvāja, susaddahitaṃyeva hoti, tañca hoti rittaṃ tucchaṃ musā; no cepi susaddahitaṃ hoti, tañca hoti bhūtaṃ tacchaṃ anaññathā. Api ca, bhāradvāja , surucitaṃyeva hoti…pe… svānussutaṃyeva hoti…pe… suparivitakkitaṃyeva hoti…pe… sunijjhāyitaṃyeva hoti, tañca hoti rittaṃ tucchaṃ musā; no cepi sunijjhāyitaṃ hoti, tañca hoti bhūtaṃ tacchaṃ anaññathā. Saccamanurakkhatā, bhāradvāja, viññunā purisena nālamettha ekaṃsena niṭṭhaṃ gantuṃ – ‘idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’’’nti.
mula_english:
428. Suppose, Bharadvaja, there was a file of blind men, each in touch with the next: the first one does not see, the middle one does not see, and the last one does not see. So too, Bharadvaja, in my opinion, the talk of these *brāhmaṇas* is like a file of blind men: the first one does not see, the middle one does not see, and the last one does not see.

What do you think, Bharadvaja, is it not the case that in this way, the *brāhmaṇas'* faith becomes groundless?

"No, Master Gotama, the *brāhmaṇas* do not adhere to it simply out of faith, but rather, the *brāhmaṇas* adhere to it through oral tradition."

"Bharadvaja, first you took your stand on faith, now you speak of oral tradition.

There are five things, Bharadvaja, that may turn out in two different ways here and now.

Which five? They are: *śraddhā* (faith), *ruci* (approval), *anussava* (oral tradition), *ākāraparivitarka* (reasoned cogitation), and *dṛṣṭinijjhānakkhanti* (reflective acceptance of a view). These five things, Bharadvaja, may turn out in two different ways here and now.

Furthermore, Bharadvaja, something may be fully accepted out of faith, yet it may be empty, hollow, and false; but something else may not be fully accepted out of faith, yet it may be factual, true, and unmistaken.

Again, Bharadvaja, something may be fully approved of… may be well reflected upon, yet it may be empty, hollow, and false; but something else may not be well reflected upon, yet it may be factual, true, and unmistaken.

Under these conditions it is not proper for a wise man who preserves truth, Bharadvaja, to come to the definite conclusion: ‘Only this is true, anything else is wrong.’“
commentary_pali:
428.Andhaveṇīti andhapaveṇī. Ekena hi cakkhumatā gahitayaṭṭhiyā koṭiṃ eko andho gaṇhāti, taṃ andhaṃ añño, taṃ aññoti evaṃ paṇṇāsa saṭṭhi andhā paṭipāṭiyā ghaṭitā andhaveṇīti vuccati. Paramparāsaṃsattāti aññamaññaṃ laggā, yaṭṭhiggāhakenapi cakkhumatā virahitāti attho. Eko kira dhutto andhagaṇaṃ disvā ‘‘asukasmiṃ nāma gāme khajjabhojjaṃ sulabha’’nti ussāhetvā tehi ‘‘tattha no sāmi nehi, idaṃ nāma te demā’’ti vutte lañjaṃ gahetvā antarāmagge maggā okkamma mahantaṃ gacchaṃ anuparigantvā purimassa hatthena pacchimassa kacchaṃ gaṇhāpetvā ‘‘kiñci kammaṃ atthi, gacchatha tāva tumhe’’ti vatvā palāyi. Te divasampi gantvā maggaṃ avindamānā ‘‘kahaṃ, bho, cakkhumā kahaṃ maggo’’ti paridevitvā maggaṃ avindamānā tattheva mariṃsu. Te sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘‘paramparāsaṃsattā’’ti. Purimopīti purimesu dasasu brāhmaṇesu ekopi. Majjhimopīti majjhe ācariyapācariyesu ekopi. Pacchimopīti idāni brāhmaṇesu ekopi.

Pañcakhoti pāḷiāgatesu dvīsu aññepi evarūpe tayo pakkhipitvā vadati. Dvedhāvipākāti bhūtavipākā vā abhūtavipākā vā. Nālametthāti, bhāradvāja, saccaṃ anurakkhissāmīti paṭipannena viññunā ‘‘yaṃ mayā gahitaṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’’nti ettha ekaṃseneva niṭṭhaṃ gantuṃ nālaṃ na yuttanti upari pucchāya maggaṃ vivaritvā ṭhapesi.

Pañca kho Dvedhāvipākā Nālametthā
commentary_english:
428. *Andhaveṇī* means a procession of the blind.

Indeed, one blind person grasps the end of a stick held by a sighted person, and another blind person [grasps] that blind person, and another [grasps] that one. Thus, fifty or sixty blind people, arranged in a line, are called a *andhaveṇī*.

*Paramparāsaṃsattā* means connected one to another, lacking even a sighted person to hold the stick. This is the meaning.

It is said that a rogue, having seen a crowd of blind people, encouraged them, saying, "In such-and-such village, food and snacks are easily available." Persuading them [in this way], they said to him, "There, sir, lead us! We will give you this much!" Having taken the bribe, he left the path in the middle of the road, went around a large thicket, caused the hand of the first [blind man] to grasp the back of the last one, and saying, "There is some work [to be done], go on for a while, you all!" he fled.

Having gone even a day's journey without finding the way, lamenting, "Where, sir, is the sighted person? Where is the way?" and not finding the way, they died right there.

With reference to that, it was said, "*paramparāsaṃsattā*."

*Purimopī* means even one of the first ten Brahmins.

*Majjhimopī* means even one in the middle of the teachers and sub-teachers.

*Pacchimopī* means even one among the present-day Brahmins.

*Pañca*...

*Kho* means having inserted three more of this type into the two that came from the Pāḷi, he speaks.

*Dvedhāvipākā* means either having results that are real, or having results that are unreal.

*Nālametthā*, Bharadvāja, by the wise person who has undertaken, "I will protect the truth," [believing] "That which is grasped by me, this alone is the truth, other [teachings] are vain," it is not fitting to go to a conclusion with certainty in this matter. He revealed the path by questioning further, [saying] "It is not right."

*Pañca*... *Kho* *dvedhāvipākā* *Nālametthā*

mula_pali: 429. ‘‘Kittāvatā pana, bho gotama, saccānurakkhaṇā hoti, kittāvatā saccamanurakkhati? Saccānurakkhaṇaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā’’ti. ‘‘Saddhā cepi, bhāradvāja, purisassa hoti; ‘evaṃ me saddhā’ti – iti vadaṃ saccamanurakkhati evameva sijjhatīti iti vā, taṃ saccamanurakkhati (ka.), natveva tāva ekaṃsena niṭṭhaṃ gacchati – ‘idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’nti ( ) (ettāvatā kho bhāradvāja saccānurakkhaṇā hoti, ettāvatā saccamanurakkhati, ettāvatā ca mayaṃ saccānurakkhaṇaṃ paññāpema, na tveva tāva saccānubodho hoti) (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). Ruci cepi, bhāradvāja, purisassa hoti…pe… anussavo cepi, bhāradvāja, purisassa hoti…pe… ākāraparivitakko cepi, bhāradvāja, purisassa hoti…pe… diṭṭhinijjhānakkhanti cepi, bhāradvāja, purisassa hoti; ‘evaṃ me diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantī’ti – iti vadaṃ saccamanurakkhati, natveva tāva ekaṃsena niṭṭhaṃ gacchati – ‘idameva saccaṃ, moghamañña’nti. Ettāvatā kho, bhāradvāja, saccānurakkhaṇā hoti, ettāvatā saccamanurakkhati, ettāvatā ca mayaṃ saccānurakkhaṇaṃ paññapema; na tveva tāva saccānubodho hotī’’ti.
mula_english:
429. “But how, venerable Gotama, is there preservation of truth? How does one preserve truth? We ask the venerable Gotama about the preservation of truth.”

“If, Bhāradvāja, a person has faith (saddhā); he preserves truth by saying, ‘Thus is my faith (saddhā).’

, but he does not yet come to the definite conclusion: ‘This alone is the truth, (all) else is foolish.’”

“If, Bhāradvāja, a person has approval…pe… If, Bhāradvāja, a person has oral tradition…pe… If, Bhāradvāja, a person has reasoned cogitation…pe… If, Bhāradvāja, a person has reflective acceptance of a view; he preserves truth by saying, ‘Thus is my reflective acceptance of a view,’ but he does not yet come to the definite conclusion: ‘This alone is the truth, (all) else is foolish.’

In this way, Bhāradvāja, there is the preservation of truth; in this way he preserves truth; in this way we describe the preservation of truth. But as yet there is no discovery of truth.”

mula_pali: 430. ‘‘Ettāvatā, bho gotama, saccānurakkhaṇā hoti, ettāvatā saccamanurakkhati, ettāvatā ca mayaṃ saccānurakkhaṇaṃ pekkhāma. Kittāvatā pana, bho gotama, saccānubodho hoti, kittāvatā saccamanubujjhati? Saccānubodhaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā’’ti. ‘‘Idha idha kira (syā. kaṃ. ka.), bhāradvāja, bhikkhu aññataraṃ gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā upanissāya viharati. Tamenaṃ gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā upasaṅkamitvā tīsu dhammesu samannesati – lobhanīyesu dhammesu, dosanīyesu dhammesu, mohanīyesu dhammesu. Atthi nu kho imassāyasmato tathārūpā lobhanīyā dhammā yathārūpehi lobhanīyehi dhammehi pariyādinnacitto ajānaṃ vā vadeyya – jānāmīti, apassaṃ vā vadeyya – passāmīti, paraṃ vā tadatthāya samādapeyya yaṃ paresaṃ assa dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyāti? Tamenaṃ samannesamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘natthi kho imassāyasmato tathārūpā lobhanīyā dhammā yathārūpehi lobhanīyehi dhammehi pariyādinnacitto ajānaṃ vā vadeyya – jānāmīti, apassaṃ vā vadeyya – passāmīti, paraṃ vā tadatthāya samādapeyya yaṃ paresaṃ assa dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya dukkhāyāti (sabbattha). Tathārūpo tathā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) kho panimassāyasmato kāyasamācāro tathārūpo tathā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) vacīsamācāro yathā taṃ aluddhassa. Yaṃ kho pana ayamāyasmā dhammaṃ deseti, gambhīro so dhammo duddaso duranubodho santo paṇīto atakkāvacaro nipuṇo paṇḍitavedanīyo; na so dhammo sudesiyo luddhenā’’’ti.
mula_english:
430. “In that way, Master Gotama, there is the preservation of truth; in that way one preserves truth; in that way we recognise the preservation of truth.

But to what extent, Master Gotama, is there the final arrival at truth; to what extent does one finally arrive at truth? We ask the honorable Gotama about the final arrival at truth.”

“Here, Bharadvaja, a *bhikkhu* may be living in dependence on some village or town.

Then a householder or a householder's son approaches him and examines him with regard to three things: with regard to states based on greed (*lobhanīyesu dhammesu*), with regard to states based on aversion (*dosanīyesu dhammesu*), with regard to states based on delusion (*mohanīyesu dhammesu*).

‘Are there in this venerable one any states based on greed (*lobhanīyā dhammā*) such that, with his mind obsessed by those states (*lobhanīyehi dhammehi pariyādinnacitto*), while not knowing he might say, “I know,” or while not seeing he might say, “I see,” or he might urge others to act in a way that would lead to their harm and suffering for a long time?’ As he investigates him, he comes to know: “There are no such states based on greed in this venerable one such that, with his mind obsessed by those states, while not knowing he might say, ‘I know,’ or while not seeing he might say, ‘I see,’ or he might urge others to act in a way that would lead to their harm and suffering for a long time.”

‘Furthermore, is the bodily conduct (*kāyasamācāro*) of this venerable one of such a kind… is the verbal conduct (*vacīsamācāro*) of such a kind that it accords with one who is without greed (*aluddhassa*)?

And the Dharma (*dhammaṃ*) that this venerable one teaches, is profound, difficult to see, difficult to understand, peaceful, excellent, beyond the reach of logic, subtle, to be experienced by the wise; this Dharma (*dhammo*) cannot easily be taught by one affected by greed.’”
commentary_pali: 430.Idha, bhāradvāja, bhikkhūti jīvakasutte (ma. ni. 2.51 ādayo) viya mahāvacchasutte (ma. ni. 2.193 ādayo) viya ca attānaññeva sandhāya vadati. Lobhanīyesu dhammesūti lobhadhammesu. Sesapadadvayepi eseva nayo.
commentary_english:
Here, Bharadvaja, *bhikkhū* in the Jīvaka Sutta (Ma.
Ni.
2.
51 *ādayo*) as in the Mahāvaccha Sutta (Ma.
Ni.
2.
193 *ādayo*) and referring to himself, he speaks.
"*Lobhanīyesu dhammesū*" means in the *lobhadhammesu*.
And so with the other two remaining *pada*s.

mula_pali: 431. ‘‘Yato naṃ samannesamāno visuddhaṃ lobhanīyehi dhammehi samanupassati tato naṃ uttari samannesati dosanīyesu dhammesu. Atthi nu kho imassāyasmato tathārūpā dosanīyā dhammā yathārūpehi dosanīyehi dhammehi pariyādinnacitto ajānaṃ vā vadeyya – jānāmīti, apassaṃ vā vadeyya – passāmīti, paraṃ vā tadatthāya samādapeyya yaṃ paresaṃ assa dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyāti? Tamenaṃ samannesamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘natthi kho imassāyasmato tathārūpā dosanīyā dhammā yathārūpehi dosanīyehi dhammehi pariyādinnacitto ajānaṃ vā vadeyya – jānāmīti, apassaṃ vā vadeyya – passāmīti, paraṃ vā tadatthāya samādapeyya yaṃ paresaṃ assa dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya. Tathārūpo kho panimassāyasmato kāyasamācāro tathārūpo vacīsamācāro yathā taṃ aduṭṭhassa. Yaṃ kho pana ayamāyasmā dhammaṃ deseti, gambhīro so dhammo duddaso duranubodho santo paṇīto atakkāvacaro nipuṇo paṇḍitavedanīyo; na so dhammo sudesiyo duṭṭhenā’’’ti.
mula_english:
431. “When he has investigated him and has seen that he is purified from states based on greed (lobhanīyehi dhammehi), he next investigates him in regard to states based on hate (dosanīyesu dhammesu).

‘Are there in this venerable one any states based on hate (dosanīyā dhammā) such that, with his mind obsessed by those states…he might urge others to act in a way that would lead to their harm and suffering for a long time? As he investigates him, he comes to know: ‘There are no such states based on hate (dosanīyā dhammā) in this venerable one…he might urge others to act in a way that would lead to their harm and suffering for a long time.

The bodily behaviour (kāyasamācāro) and the verbal behaviour (vacīsamācāro) of this venerable one are not those of one affected by hate (aduṭṭhassa).

And the Dharma (dhammaṃ) that this venerable one teaches is profound… to be experienced by the wise (paṇḍitavedanīyo). This Dharma (dhammo) cannot easily be taught by one affected by hate (duṭṭhenā).’

mula_pali:
432. ‘‘Yato naṃ samannesamāno visuddhaṃ dosanīyehi dhammehi samanupassati , tato naṃ uttari samannesati mohanīyesu dhammesu. Atthi nu kho imassāyasmato tathārūpā mohanīyā dhammā yathārūpehi mohanīyehi dhammehi pariyādinnacitto ajānaṃ vā vadeyya – jānāmīti, apassaṃ vā vadeyya – passāmīti, paraṃ vā tadatthāya samādapeyya yaṃ paresaṃ assa dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyāti? Tamenaṃ samannesamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘natthi kho imassāyasmato tathārūpā mohanīyā dhammā yathārūpehi mohanīyehi dhammehi pariyādinnacitto ajānaṃ vā vadeyya – jānāmīti, apassaṃ vā vadeyya – passāmīti, paraṃ vā tadatthāya samādapeyya yaṃ paresaṃ assa dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya. Tathārūpo kho panimassāyasmato kāyasamācāro tathārūpo vacīsamācāro yathā taṃ amūḷhassa. Yaṃ kho pana ayamāyasmā dhammaṃ deseti, gambhīro so dhammo duddaso duranubodho santo paṇīto atakkāvacaro nipuṇo paṇḍitavedanīyo; na so dhammo sudesiyo mūḷhenā’’’ti.

‘‘Yato naṃ samannesamāno visuddhaṃ mohanīyehi dhammehi samanupassati ; atha tamhi saddhaṃ niveseti, saddhājāto upasaṅkamati, upasaṅkamanto payirupāsati, payirupāsanto sotaṃ odahati, ohitasoto dhammaṃ suṇāti, sutvā dhammaṃ dhāreti, dhatānaṃ dhāritānaṃ (ka.) dhammānaṃ atthaṃ upaparikkhati, atthaṃ upaparikkhato dhammā nijjhānaṃ khamanti, dhammanijjhānakkhantiyā sati chando jāyati, chandajāto ussahati, ussahitvā tuleti, tulayitvā padahati, pahitatto samāno kāyena ceva paramasaccaṃ sacchikaroti paññāya ca naṃ ativijjha passati. Ettāvatā kho, bhāradvāja, saccānubodho hoti, ettāvatā saccamanubujjhati, ettāvatā ca mayaṃ saccānubodhaṃ paññapema; na tveva tāva saccānuppatti hotī’’ti.

dhāritānaṃ (ka.)
mula_english:
432. "When he has investigated him and has seen that he is purified from states based on hate ( *dosanīyehi dhammehi*), he next investigates him in regard to states based on delusion (*mohanīyesu dhammesu*).

‘Are there in this venerable one (*ayasmato*) any states based on delusion (*mohanīyā dhammā*) such that, with his mind obsessed by those states, while not knowing he might say, “I know (*jānāmīti*),” or while not seeing he might say, “I see (*passāmīti*),” or he might urge others to act in a way that would lead to their harm and suffering for a long time (*dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya*)? ’ As he investigates him, he comes to know: “There are no such states based on delusion in this venerable one. The bodily behaviour (*kāyasamācāro*) and the verbal behaviour (*vacīsamācāro*) of this venerable one are not those of one affected by delusion (*amūḷhassa*).

And the *dharma* that this venerable one teaches is profound (*gambhīro*)...to be experienced by the wise (*paṇḍitavedanīyo*). This *dharma* cannot easily be taught by one affected by delusion (*mūḷhena*).”

"When he has investigated him and has seen that he is purified from states based on delusion (*mohanīyehi dhammehi*), then he places faith (*saddhaṃ*) in him; filled with faith (*saddhājāto*) he visits him and pays respect to him; having paid respect to him, he gives ear; when he gives ear, he hears the *dharma*; having heard the *dharma*, he memorises it; he examines the meaning (*atthaṃ*) of the teachings (*dhammānaṃ*) he has memorised; when he examines their meaning, he gains a reflective acceptance (*nijjhānaṃ khamanti*) of those teachings; when he has gained a reflective acceptance of those teachings, zeal (*chando*) springs up in him; when zeal has sprung up, he applies his will (*ussahati*); having applied his will, he weighs things up (*tuleti*); having weighed things up, he makes an effort (*padahati*), being one who has made effort, he realizes the ultimate truth (*paramasaccaṃ sacchikaroti*) with his body and sees it piercingly with wisdom (*paññāya ativijjha passati*).

In this way, Bhāradvāja, there is the discovery of truth (*saccānubodho*); in this way one discovers truth (*saccamanubujjhati*); in this way we describe the discovery of truth (*saccānubodhaṃ paññapema*). But as yet there is no final arrival at truth (*saccānuppatti*)."
commentary_pali: 432.Saddhaṃ nivesetīti okappaniyasaddhaṃ niveseti. Upasaṅkamatīti upagacchati. Payirupāsatīti santike nisīdati. Sotanti pasādasotaṃ odahati. Dhammanti desanādhammaṃ suṇāti. Dhāretīti paguṇaṃ katvā dhāreti. Upaparikkhatīti atthato ca kāraṇato ca vīmaṃsati. Nijjhānaṃ khamantīti olokanaṃ khamanti, idha sīlaṃ kathitaṃ, idha samādhīti evaṃ upaṭṭhahantīti attho. Chandoti kattukamyatā chando. Ussahatīti vāyamati. Tuletīti aniccādivasena tīreti. Padahatīti maggapadhānaṃ padahati. Kāyena ceva paramasaccanti sahajātanāmakāyena ca nibbānaṃ sacchikaroti, paññāya ca kilese nibbijjhitvā tadeva vibhūtaṃ pākaṭaṃ karonto passati.
commentary_english:
432.
"He establishes faith ( *saddhāṃ niveseti* )" means he establishes faith that is based on conviction ( *okappaniyasaddhaṃ niveseti*).
"He approaches ( *upasaṅkamati* )" means he goes near ( *upagacchati* ).
"He attends ( *payirupāsatī* )" means he sits nearby ( *santike nisīdati* ).
"A stream ( *sota* )" means he directs a stream of serenity ( *pasādasotaṃ odahati*).
"The teaching ( *dhamma* )" means he hears the teaching of the Dhamma ( *desanādhammaṃ suṇāti*).
"He retains ( *dhāretī* )" means having made it skillful, he retains it ( *paguṇaṃ katvā dhāreti*).
"He investigates ( *upaparikkhatī* )" means he examines in terms of meaning and cause ( *atthato ca kāraṇato ca vīmaṃsati*).
"They are patient with contemplation ( *nijjhānaṃ khamantī* )" means they are patient with looking; here, virtue (*śīla*) is spoken of; here, concentration (*samādhi*); thus, its meaning is that they attend.
"Desire ( *chando* )" means the desire to do, desire ( *kattukamyatā chando*).
"He strives ( *ussahatī* )" means he makes an effort ( *vāyamati*).
"He weighs ( *tuletī* )" means he crosses over by way of impermanence ( *aniccādivasena tīreti*).
"He applies ( *padahatī* )" means he applies effort to the path ( *maggapadhānaṃ padahati*).
"With the body and truly supreme (*kāyena ceva paramasacca*)" means with the body named co-emergent ( *sahajātanāmakāyena ca*) he realizes *nirvāṇa* (*nibbānaṃ sacchikaroti*), and having pierced the afflictions (*kleśa*) with wisdom (*prajñā*), he sees that very thing, making the expanded evident.

mula_pali: 433. ‘‘Ettāvattā, bho gotama, saccānubodho hoti, ettāvatā saccamanubujjhati, ettāvatā ca mayaṃ saccānubodhaṃ pekkhāma. Kittāvatā pana, bho gotama, saccānuppatti hoti, kittāvatā saccamanupāpuṇāti? Saccānuppattiṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā’’ti. ‘‘Tesaṃye , bhāradvāja, dhammānaṃ āsevanā bhāvanā bahulīkammaṃ saccānuppatti hoti. Ettāvatā kho, bhāradvāja, saccānuppatti hoti, ettāvatā saccamanupāpuṇāti, ettāvatā ca mayaṃ saccānuppattiṃ paññapemā’’ti.
mula_english:
“In that way, Master Gotama, there is the discovery of truth; in that way one discovers truth; in that way we recognise the discovery of truth.

But in what way, Master Gotama, is there the final arrival at truth; in what way does one finally arrive at truth? We ask you, Master Gotama, about the final arrival at truth.”

“Through the repeated association, development and cultivation of those things, Bharadvaja, there is the final arrival at truth.

In this way, Bharadvaja, there is the final arrival at truth; in this way one finally arrives at truth; in this way we describe the final arrival at truth.”
commentary_pali:
433.Saccānubodhoti maggānubodho. Saccānuppattīti phalasacchikiriyā. Tesaṃyevāti heṭṭhā vuttānaṃ dvādasannaṃ, evaṃ dīghaṃ maggavādaṃ anulometi, tasmā nāyamattho. Ayaṃ panettha attho – tesaṃyevāti tesaṃ maggasampayuttadhammānaṃ. Padhānanti maggapadhānaṃ. Tañhi phalasacchikiriyasaṅkhātāya saccānuppattiyā bahukāraṃ, magge asati phalābhāvatoti. Iminā nayena sabbapadesu attho veditabbo. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Caṅkīsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
433. *Saccānubodho* means path-understanding (*maggānubodho*). *Saccānuppattī* means the realization of the fruit (*phalasacchikiriyā*). *Tesaṃyevā* refers to the twelve mentioned below; thus, it conforms to a lengthy path-doctrine, therefore this is not the meaning. But here this is the meaning: *Tesaṃyevā* means of those path-associated states (*maggasampayuttadhammānaṃ*). *Padhāna* means path-exertion (*maggapadhānaṃ*). For that is very helpful for the truth-attainment consisting of the realization of the fruit, because without the path there is no obtaining of the fruit. In this way the meaning should be understood in all passages. The rest is clear throughout (*sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti*).

The commentary on the Caṅkī Sutta in the Papañcasūdanī, commentary to the Middle Length Discourses (Majjhimanikāya), is finished.

mula_pali:
434. ‘‘Ettāvatā, bho gotama, saccānuppatti hoti, ettāvatā saccamanupāpuṇāti, ettāvatā ca mayaṃ saccānuppattiṃ pekkhāma. Saccānuppattiyā pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Saccānuppattiyā bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā’’ti. ‘‘Saccānuppattiyā kho, bhāradvāja, padhānaṃ bahukāraṃ. No cetaṃ padaheyya, nayidaṃ saccamanupāpuṇeyya. Yasmā ca kho padahati tasmā saccamanupāpuṇāti. Tasmā saccānuppattiyā padhānaṃ bahukāra’’nti.

‘‘Padhānassa pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Padhānassa bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā’’ti. ‘‘Padhānassa kho, bhāradvāja, tulanā bahukārā. No cetaṃ tuleyya, nayidaṃ padaheyya. Yasmā ca kho tuleti tasmā padahati. Tasmā padhānassa tulanā bahukārā’’ti.

‘‘Tulanāya pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Tulanāya bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā’’ti. ‘‘Tulanāya kho, bhāradvāja, ussāho bahukāro. No cetaṃ ussaheyya, nayidaṃ tuleyya. Yasmā ca kho ussahati tasmā tuleti. Tasmā tulanāya ussāho bahukāro’’ti.

‘‘Ussāhassa pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Ussāhassa bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā’’ti. ‘‘Ussāhassa kho, bhāradvāja, chando bahukāro. No cetaṃ chando jāyetha, nayidaṃ ussaheyya. Yasmā ca kho chando jāyati tasmā ussahati. Tasmā ussāhassa chando bahukāro’’ti.

‘‘Chandassa pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro ? Chandassa bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā’’ti. ‘‘Chandassa kho, bhāradvāja, dhammanijjhānakkhanti bahukārā. No cete dhammā nijjhānaṃ khameyyuṃ, nayidaṃ chando jāyetha. Yasmā ca kho dhammā nijjhānaṃ khamanti tasmā chando jāyati. Tasmā chandassa dhammanijjhānakkhanti bahukārā’’ti.

‘‘Dhammanijjhānakkhantiyā pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Dhammanijjhānakkhantiyā bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā’’ti. ‘‘Dhammanijjhānakkhantiyā kho, bhāradvāja, atthūpaparikkhā bahukārā. No cetaṃ atthaṃ upaparikkheyya, nayidaṃ dhammā nijjhānaṃ khameyyuṃ. Yasmā ca kho atthaṃ upaparikkhati tasmā dhammā nijjhānaṃ khamanti. Tasmā dhammanijjhānakkhantiyā atthūpaparikkhā bahukārā’’ti.

‘‘Atthūpaparikkhāya pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Atthūpaparikkhāya bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā’’ti. ‘‘Atthūpaparikkhāya kho, bhāradvāja, dhammadhāraṇā bahukārā. No cetaṃ dhammaṃ dhāreyya, nayidaṃ atthaṃ upaparikkheyya. Yasmā ca kho dhammaṃ dhāreti tasmā atthaṃ upaparikkhati. Tasmā atthūpaparikkhāya dhammadhāraṇā bahukārā’’ti.

‘‘Dhammadhāraṇāya pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Dhammadhāraṇāya bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā’’ti. ‘‘Dhammadhāraṇāya kho, bhāradvāja, dhammassavanaṃ bahukāraṃ. No cetaṃ dhammaṃ suṇeyya, nayidaṃ dhammaṃ dhāreyya. Yasmā ca kho dhammaṃ suṇāti tasmā dhammaṃ dhāreti. Tasmā dhammadhāraṇāya dhammassavanaṃ bahukāra’’nti.

‘‘Dhammassavanassa pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Dhammassavanassa bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā’’ti . ‘‘Dhammassavanassa kho, bhāradvāja, sotāvadhānaṃ bahukāraṃ . No cetaṃ sotaṃ odaheyya, nayidaṃ dhammaṃ suṇeyya. Yasmā ca kho sotaṃ odahati tasmā dhammaṃ suṇāti. Tasmā dhammassavanassa sotāvadhānaṃ bahukāra’’nti.

‘‘Sotāvadhānassa pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Sotāvadhānassa bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā’’ti. ‘‘Sotāvadhānassa kho, bhāradvāja, payirupāsanā bahukārā. No cetaṃ payirupāseyya, nayidaṃ sotaṃ odaheyya. Yasmā ca kho payirupāsati tasmā sotaṃ odahati. Tasmā sotāvadhānassa payirupāsanā bahukārā’’ti.

‘‘Payirupāsanāya pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Payirupāsanāya bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā’’ti. ‘‘Payirupāsanāya kho, bhāradvāja, upasaṅkamanaṃ bahukāraṃ. No cetaṃ upasaṅkameyya, nayidaṃ payirupāseyya. Yasmā ca kho upasaṅkamati tasmā payirupāsati. Tasmā payirupāsanāya upasaṅkamanaṃ bahukāra’’nti.

‘‘Upasaṅkamanassa pana, bho gotama, katamo dhammo bahukāro? Upasaṅkamanassa bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ pucchāmā’’ti. ‘‘Upasaṅkamanassa kho, bhāradvāja, saddhā bahukārā. No cetaṃ saddhā jāyetha, nayidaṃ upasaṅkameyya. Yasmā ca kho saddhā jāyati tasmā upasaṅkamati. Tasmā upasaṅkamanassa saddhā bahukārā’’ti.
mula_english:
434. “In that way, Master Gotama, there is the final arrival at truth; in that way one finally arrives at truth; in that way we recognise the final arrival at truth. “But what, Master Gotama, is most helpful for the final arrival at truth? We ask Master Gotama about the thing most helpful for the final arrival at truth.” “Striving (*pradhāna*) is most helpful for the final arrival at truth, Bharadvaja. If one does not strive, one will not finally arrive at truth; but because one strives, one does finally arrive at truth. That is why striving is most helpful for the final arrival at truth.” “But what, Master Gotama, is most helpful for striving (*pradhāna*)? We ask Master Gotama about the thing most helpful for striving.” “Scrutiny (*tulanā*) is most helpful for striving, Bharadvaja. If one does not scrutinise, one will not strive; but because one scrutinises, one strives. That is why scrutiny is most helpful for striving.” “But what, Master Gotama, is most helpful for scrutiny (*tulanā*)? We ask Master Gotama about the thing most helpful for scrutiny.” “Application of the will (*utsāha*) is most helpful for scrutiny, Bharadvaja. If one does not apply one’s will, one will not scrutinise; but because one applies one’s will, one scrutinises. That is why application of the will is most helpful for scrutiny.” “But what, Master Gotama, is most helpful for application of the will (*utsāha*)? We ask Master Gotama about the thing most helpful for application of the will.” “Zeal (*chanda*) is most helpful for application of the will, Bharadvaja. If one does not arouse zeal, one will not apply one’s will; but because one arouses zeal, one applies one’s will. That is why zeal is most helpful for application of the will.” “But what, Master Gotama, is most helpful for zeal (*chanda*)? We ask Master Gotama about the thing most helpful for zeal.” “A reflective acceptance of the teachings (*dhammanijjhānakkhanti*) is most helpful for zeal, Bharadvaja. If one does not gain a reflective acceptance of the teachings, zeal will not spring up; but because one gains a reflective acceptance of the teachings, zeal springs up. That is why a reflective acceptance of the teachings is most helpful for zeal.” “But what, Master Gotama, is most helpful for a reflective acceptance of the teachings (*dhammanijjhānakkhanti*)? We ask Master Gotama about the thing most helpful for a reflective acceptance of the teachings.” “Examination of the meaning (*atthūpaparikkhā*) is most helpful for a reflective acceptance of the teachings, Bharadvaja. If one does not examine their meaning, one will not gain a reflective acceptance of the teachings; Therefore, examination of the meaning (*attha-ūpaparikkhā*) is most helpful for a reflective acceptance of the teachings ( *dhamma-nijjhāna-khanti*)."

“But Master Gotama, which phenomenon (*dharma*) is most helpful for the examination of the meaning (*attha-ūpaparikkhā*)? We ask you, Master Gotama, which phenomenon (*dharma*) is most helpful for the examination of the meaning (*attha-ūpaparikkhā*)?” “For the examination of the meaning (*attha-ūpaparikkhā*), Bhāradvāja, memorising the teachings (*dhamma-dhāraṇā*) is most helpful. If one does not memorise a teaching (*dhamma*), one will not examine its meaning (*attha*); but because one memorises a teaching (*dhamma*), one examines its meaning (*attha*). Therefore, for examination of the meaning (*attha-ūpaparikkhā*), memorising the teachings (*dhamma-dhāraṇā*) is most helpful.”

“But Master Gotama, which phenomenon (*dharma*) is most helpful for memorising the teachings (*dhamma-dhāraṇā*)? We ask you, Master Gotama, which phenomenon (*dharma*) is most helpful for memorising the teachings (*dhamma-dhāraṇā*)?” “For memorising the teachings (*dhamma-dhāraṇā*), Bhāradvāja, hearing the Dharma (*dhamma-savana*) is most helpful. If one does not hear the Dharma (*dhamma*), one will not memorise the teachings (*dhamma*); but because one hears the Dharma (*dhamma*), one memorises the teachings (*dhamma*). Therefore, for memorising the teachings (*dhamma-dhāraṇā*), hearing the Dharma (*dhamma-savana*) is most helpful.”

“But Master Gotama, which phenomenon (*dharma*) is most helpful for hearing the Dharma (*dhamma-savana*)? We ask you, Master Gotama, which phenomenon (*dharma*) is most helpful for hearing the Dharma (*dhamma-savana*)?” “For hearing the Dharma (*dhamma-savana*), Bhāradvāja, giving ear (*sotāvadhāna*) is most helpful. If one does not give ear (*sota*), one will not hear the Dharma (*dhamma*); but because one gives ear (*sota*), one hears the Dharma (*dhamma*). Therefore, for hearing the Dharma (*dhamma-savana*), giving ear (*sotāvadhāna*) is most helpful.”

“But Master Gotama, which phenomenon (*dharma*) is most helpful for giving ear (*sotāvadhāna*)? We ask you, Master Gotama, which phenomenon (*dharma*) is most helpful for giving ear (*sotāvadhāna*)?” “For giving ear (*sotāvadhāna*), Bhāradvāja, paying respect (*payirupāsanā*) is most helpful. If one does not pay respect (*payirupāsanā*), one will not give ear (*sota*); but because one pays respect (*payirupāsanā*), one gives ear (*sota*). That is why paying respect (*payirupāsanā*) is most helpful for giving ear (*sotāvadhāna*).”

“But Master Gotama, which phenomenon (*dharma*) is most helpful for paying respect (*payirupāsanā*)? We ask you, Master Gotama, which phenomenon (*dharma*) is most helpful for paying respect (*payirupāsanā*)?” “For paying respect (*payirupāsanā*), Bhāradvāja, visiting (*upasaṅkamana*) is most helpful. If one does not visit (*upasaṅkamana*), one will not pay respect (*payirupāsanā*); but because one visits (*upasaṅkamana*), one pays respect (*payirupāsanā*). That is why visiting (*upasaṅkamana*) is most helpful for paying respect (*payirupāsanā*).”

“But Master Gotama, which phenomenon (*dharma*) is most helpful for visiting (*upasaṅkamana*)? We ask you, Master Gotama, which phenomenon (*dharma*) is most helpful for visiting (*upasaṅkamana*)?” “For visiting (*upasaṅkamana*), Bhāradvāja, faith (*saddhā*) is most helpful. If faith (*saddhā*) does not arise, one will not visit (*upasaṅkamana*); but because faith (*saddhā*) arises, one visits (*upasaṅkamana*). That is why faith (*saddhā*) is most helpful for visiting (*upasaṅkamana*).”

mula_pali:
435. ‘‘Saccānurakkhaṇaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ apucchimha, saccānurakkhaṇaṃ bhavaṃ gotamo byākāsi; tañca panamhākaṃ ruccati ceva khamati ca tena camha attamanā. Saccānubodhaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ apucchimha, saccānubodhaṃ bhavaṃ gotamo byākāsi; tañca panamhākaṃ ruccati ceva khamati ca tena camha attamanā. Saccānuppattiṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ apucchimha, saccānuppattiṃ bhavaṃ gotamo byākāsi; tañca panamhākaṃ ruccati ceva khamati ca tena camha attamanā . Saccānuppattiyā bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ apucchimha, saccānuppattiyā bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ bhavaṃ gotamo byākāsi; tañca panamhākaṃ ruccati ceva khamati ca tena camha attamanā. Yaṃyadeva ca mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ apucchimha taṃtadeva bhavaṃ gotamo byākāsi; tañca panamhākaṃ ruccati ceva khamati ca tena camha attamanā. Mayañhi, bho gotama, pubbe evaṃ jānāma – ‘ke ca muṇḍakā samaṇakā ibbhā kaṇhā bandhupādāpaccā, ke ca dhammassa aññātāro’ti? Ajanesi vata me bhavaṃ gotamo samaṇesu samaṇapemaṃ, samaṇesu samaṇapasādaṃ, samaṇesu samaṇagāravaṃ. Abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata’’nti.

Caṅkīsuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.
mula_english:
435. “We asked Master Gotama about the preservation of truth ( *saccānurakkhaṇaṃ* ), and Master Gotama answered about the preservation of truth; we approve of and accept that answer, and so we are satisfied. We asked Master Gotama about the discovery of truth (*saccānubodhaṃ*), and Master Gotama answered about the discovery of truth; we approve of and accept that answer, and so we are satisfied. We asked Master Gotama about the final arrival at truth (*saccānuppattiṃ*), and Master Gotama answered about the final arrival at truth; we approve of and accept that answer, and so we are satisfied. We asked Master Gotama about the thing most helpful for the final arrival at truth (*saccānuppattiyā bahukāraṃ dhammaṃ*), and Master Gotama answered about the thing most helpful for the final arrival at truth; we approve of and accept that answer, and so we are satisfied. Whatever we asked Master Gotama about, that he has answered us; we approve of and accept that answer, and so we are satisfied. Formerly, Master Gotama, we used to think: ‘Who are these bald-pated recluses (*muṇḍakā samaṇakā*), these swarthy menial offspring of the Kinsman’s feet, that they would understand the *Dhamma*? Master Gotama has engendered in me affection for recluses (*samaṇapemaṃ*), serenity towards recluses (*samaṇapasādaṃ*), and respect for recluses (*samaṇagāravaṃ*).’ Excellent, Master Gotama! … Let Master Gotama accept me as a lay follower (*upāsakaṃ*) who from today has gone for refuge for life.”

The Caṅkī Sutta, the fifth, is finished.

mula_pali: 436. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho esukārī brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho esukārī brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘brāhmaṇā, bho gotama, catasso pāricariyā paññapenti – brāhmaṇassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti, khattiyassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti, vessassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti, suddassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti. Tatridaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti – ‘brāhmaṇo vā brāhmaṇaṃ paricareyya, khattiyo vā brāhmaṇaṃ paricareyya, vesso vā brāhmaṇaṃ paricareyya, suddo vā brāhmaṇaṃ paricareyyā’ti. Idaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti. Tatridaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā khattiyassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti – ‘khattiyo vā khattiyaṃ paricareyya, vesso vā khattiyaṃ paricareyya, suddo vā khattiyaṃ paricareyyā’ti. Idaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā khattiyassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti. Tatridaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā vessassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti – ‘vesso vā vessaṃ paricareyya, suddo vā vessaṃ paricareyyā’ti. Idaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā vessassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti . Tatridaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā suddassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti – ‘suddova suddaṃ paricareyya. Ko panañño suddaṃ paricarissatī’ti? Idaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā suddassa pāricariyaṃ paññapenti. Brāhmaṇā, bho gotama, imā catasso pāricariyā paññapenti. Idha bhavaṃ gotamo kimāhā’’ti?
mula_english:
436.

Thus have I heard: On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī (Śrāvastī), in the Jeta Grove (Jetavana), Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park (Anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme).

Then the *brāhmaṇa* (Brahmin) Esukārī approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him. Having concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side.

Seated to one side, the *brāhmaṇa* Esukārī said to the Blessed One: " *Brāhmaṇas*, Master Gotama, prescribe four levels of service (*pāricariyā*): the level of service to a *brāhmaṇa*, the level of service to a *khattiya* (noble), the level of service to a *vessa* (merchant), and the level of service to a *sudda* (worker).

Therein, Master Gotama, *brāhmaṇas* prescribe this as the level of service towards a *brāhmaṇa*: 'A *brāhmaṇa* may serve a *brāhmaṇa*, a *khattiya* may serve a *brāhmaṇa*, a *vessa* may serve a *brāhmaṇa*, and a *sudda* may serve a *brāhmaṇa*.'

That, Master Gotama, is the level of service towards a *brāhmaṇa* that *brāhmaṇas* prescribe.

Therein, Master Gotama, *brāhmaṇas* prescribe this as the level of service towards a *khattiya*: 'A *khattiya* may serve a *khattiya*, a *vessa* may serve a *khattiya*, and a *sudda* may serve a *khattiya*.'

That, Master Gotama, is the level of service towards a *khattiya* that *brāhmaṇas* prescribe.

Therein, Master Gotama, *brāhmaṇas* prescribe this as the level of service towards a *vessa*: 'A *vessa* may serve a *vessa*, and a *sudda* may serve a *vessa*.'

That, Master Gotama, is the level of service towards a *vessa* that *brāhmaṇas* prescribe.

Therein, Master Gotama, *brāhmaṇas* prescribe this as the level of service towards a *sudda*: 'Only a *sudda* may serve a *sudda*.

Who else would serve a *sudda*?' That, Master Gotama, is the level of service towards a *sudda* that *brāhmaṇas* prescribe.

*Brāhmaṇas*, Master Gotama, prescribe these four levels of service.

What does Master Gotama say about this?"

mula_pali: 437. ‘‘Kiṃ pana, brāhmaṇa, sabbo loko brāhmaṇānaṃ etadabbhanujānāti – ‘imā catasso pāricariyā paññapentū’’’ti paññapentīti (sī. ka.)? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, puriso daliddo daḷiddo (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) assako anāḷhiyo. Tassa akāmassa bilaṃ olaggeyyuṃ – ‘idaṃ te, ambho purisa, maṃsaṃ khāditabbaṃ, mūlañca anuppadātabba’nti. Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, brāhmaṇā appaṭiññāya tesaṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ, atha ca panimā catasso pāricariyā paññapenti. Nāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘sabbaṃ paricaritabba’nti vadāmi; nāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘sabbaṃ na paricaritabba’nti vadāmi. Yaṃ hissa, brāhmaṇa, paricarato pāricariyāhetu pāpiyo assa na seyyo, nāhaṃ taṃ ‘paricaritabba’nti vadāmi; yañca khvāssa, brāhmaṇa, paricarato pāricariyāhetu seyyo assa na pāpiyo tamahaṃ ‘paricaritabba’nti vadāmi. Khattiyaṃ cepi, brāhmaṇa, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘yaṃ vā te paricarato pāricariyāhetu pāpiyo assa na seyyo, yaṃ vā te paricarato pāricariyāhetu seyyo assa na pāpiyo; kamettha paricareyyāsī’ti, khattiyopi hi, brāhmaṇa , sammā byākaramāno evaṃ byākareyya – ‘yañhi me paricarato pāricariyāhetu pāpiyo assa na seyyo, nāhaṃ taṃ paricareyyaṃ; yañca kho me paricarato pāricariyāhetu seyyo assa na pāpiyo tamahaṃ paricareyya’nti. Brāhmaṇaṃ cepi, brāhmaṇa…pe… vessaṃ cepi, brāhmaṇa…pe… suddaṃ cepi, brāhmaṇa, evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘yaṃ vā te paricarato pāricariyāhetu pāpiyo assa na seyyo, yaṃ vā te paricarato pāricariyāhetu seyyo assa na pāpiyo; kamettha paricareyyāsī’ti, suddopi hi, brāhmaṇa, sammā byākaramāno evaṃ byākareyya – ‘yañhi me paricarato pāricariyāhetu pāpiyo assa na seyyo, nāhaṃ taṃ paricareyyaṃ; yañca kho me paricarato pāricariyāhetu seyyo assa na pāpiyo tamahaṃ paricareyya’nti. Nāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘uccākulīnatā seyyaṃso’ti vadāmi, na panāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘uccākulīnatā pāpiyaṃso’ti vadāmi; nāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘uḷāravaṇṇatā seyyaṃso’ti vadāmi, na panāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘uḷāravaṇṇatā pāpiyaṃso’ti vadāmi; nāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘uḷārabhogatā seyyaṃso’ti vadāmi, na panāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘uḷārabhogatā pāpiyaṃso’ti vadāmi.
mula_english: 437. “Well, brahmin, has all the world authorised the *brāhmaṇas* to prescribe these four levels of service (catasso pāricariyā)?” “No, Master Gotama.” “Just as, brahmin, a man is poor, wretched, and destitute. If they were to force a cut of meat upon that unwilling man and tell him: ‘Good man, you must eat this meat and pay for it.’ So too, brahmin, without the consent of those other *śramaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas*, the *brāhmaṇas* nevertheless prescribe those four levels of service (catasso pāricariyā). I do not say, brahmin, that all are to be served (sabbaṃ paricaritabba), nor do I say that none are to be served (sabbaṃ na paricaritabba). For if, when serving someone, one becomes worse and not better because of that service, then I say that he should not be served (paricaritabba). And if, when serving someone, one becomes better and not worse because of that service, then I say that he should be served (paricaritabba). “If they were to ask a noble thus: ‘Which of these should you serve - one in whose service you become worse and not better when serving him, or one in whose service you become better and not worse when serving him?’ Answering rightly, a noble would answer thus: ‘I should not serve the one in whose service I become worse and not better when serving him; I should serve the one in whose service I become better and not worse when serving him.’ “If they were to ask a *brāhmaṇa*…to ask a merchant…to ask a worker…answering rightly, a worker would answer thus: ‘I should not serve the one in whose service I become worse and not better when serving him; I should serve the one in whose service I become better and not worse when serving him.’ “I do not say, brahmin, that one is better because one is from an aristocratic family (uccākulīnatā), nor do I say that one is worse because one is from an aristocratic family (uccākulīnatā). I do not say that one is better because one is of great beauty (uḷāravaṇṇatā), nor do I say that one is worse because one is of great beauty (uḷāravaṇṇatā). I do not say that one is better because one is of great wealth (uḷārabhogatā), nor do I say that one is worse because one is of great wealth (uḷārabhogatā).
commentary_pali: 437.Evaṃme sutanti esukārīsuttaṃ. Tattha bilaṃ olaggeyyunti koṭṭhāsaṃ laggāpeyyuṃ, iminā satthadhammaṃ nāma dasseti. Satthavāho kira mahākantārapaṭipanno antarāmagge goṇe mate maṃsaṃ gahetvā sabbesaṃ satthikānaṃ ‘‘idaṃ khāditvā ettakaṃ mūlaṃ dātabba’’nti koṭṭhāsaṃ olaggeti, goṇamaṃsaṃ nāma khādantāpi atthi akhādantāpi, mūlaṃ dātuṃ sakkontāpi asakkontāpi. Satthavāho yena mūlena goṇo gahito, tassa nikkhamanatthaṃ sabbesaṃ balakkārena koṭṭhāsaṃ datvā mūlaṃ gaṇhāti, ayaṃ satthadhammo. Evamevaṃ brāhmaṇāpi lokassa paṭiññaṃ aggahetvā attanova dhammatāya catasso pāricariyā paññapentīti dassetuṃ evameva khotiādimāha. Pāpiyo assāti pāpaṃ assa. Seyyo assāti hitaṃ assa. Atha vā pāpiyoti pāpako lāmako attabhāvo assa. Seyyoti seṭṭho uttamo. Seyyaṃsoti seyyo. Uccākulīnatāti uccākulīnattena seyyo. Pāpiyaṃsoti pāpiyo. Uccākulīnatā ca dvīsu kulesu vaḍḍheti khattiyakule brāhmaṇakule ca, uḷāravaṇṇatā tīsu. Vessopi hi uḷāravaṇṇo hoti. Uḷārabhogatā catūsupi. Suddopi hi antamaso caṇḍālopi uḷārabhogo hotiyeva.
commentary_english:
437. Thus, "I have heard" is the Esukārī Sutta.

There, "they would hang up a portion" means they would fix a share. By this, he shows what is called "the doctrine of the caravan."

A caravan leader, it seems, having set out on a great desert journey, when an ox dies on the way, takes the meat and hangs up a share for all the members of the caravan, saying, "Having eaten this, such and such a price must be paid." There are those who eat the ox meat and those who do not eat it, those who are able to pay the price and those who are not able to pay it.

The caravan leader, having forcibly given a share to all and taken the price for which the ox was taken, for the purpose of release, this is the doctrine of the caravan.

Just as the Brahmins, without accepting a pledge from the world, propound four services according to their own nature, to show this, he said, "Just so, indeed," and so forth.

"Worse would be" means evil would be.

"Better would be" means benefit would be.

Or, "worse" means an evil, wretched state of existence would be.

"Better" means the best, the highest.

"Of better lineage" means better by high lineage.

"Of worse lineage" means worse.

High lineage increases in two families, in the Khattiya family and in the Brahmin family, and excellent complexion in three.

Even a Vessa has an excellent complexion.

Excellent prosperity is in all four.

Even a Sudda, even a Caṇḍāla, has excellent prosperity.

mula_pali: 438. ‘‘Uccākulīnopi hi, brāhmaṇa, idhekacco pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, pisuṇāvāco hoti, pharusāvāco hoti, samphappalāpī hoti, abhijjhālu hoti , byāpannacitto hoti, micchādiṭṭhi hoti. Tasmā ‘na uccākulīnatā seyyaṃso’ti vadāmi. Uccākulīnopi hi, brāhmaṇa, idhekacco pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, anabhijjhālu hoti, abyāpannacitto hoti, sammādiṭṭhi hoti. Tasmā ‘na uccākulīnatā pāpiyaṃso’ti vadāmi.
mula_english:
“438. Furthermore, brahmin, here some person of high birth may be one who kills living beings (*pāṇātipātī*), takes what is not given (*adinnādāyī*), engages in sexual misconduct (*kāmesumicchācārī*), speaks falsely (*musāvādī*), speaks malicious words (*pisuṇāvāco*), speaks harsh words (*pharusāvāco*), engages in idle chatter (*samphappalāpī*), is covetous (*abhijjhālu*), has a mind of ill will (*byāpannacitto*), and holds wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhi*).

Therefore, I do not say that being of high birth (*uccākulīnatā*) is superior.

Furthermore, brahmin, here some person of high birth may be one who abstains from killing living beings (*pāṇātipātā paṭivirato*), abstains from taking what is not given (*adinnādānā paṭivirato*), abstains from sexual misconduct (*kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato*), abstains from false speech (*musāvādā paṭivirato*), abstains from malicious speech (*pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato*), abstains from harsh speech (*pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato*), abstains from idle chatter (*samphappalāpā paṭivirato*), is uncovetous (*anabhijjhālu*), has a mind without ill will (*abyāpannacitto*), and holds right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*).

Therefore, I do not say that being of high birth (*uccākulīnatā*) is inferior.

mula_pali: 439. ‘‘Uḷāravaṇṇopi hi, brāhmaṇa…pe… uḷārabhogopi hi, brāhmaṇa, idhekacco pāṇātipātī hoti…pe… micchādiṭṭhi hoti. Tasmā ‘na uḷārabhogatā seyyaṃso’ti vadāmi. Uḷārabhogopi hi, brāhmaṇa, idhekacco pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhi hoti. Tasmā ‘na uḷārabhogatā pāpiyaṃso’ti vadāmi. Nāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘sabbaṃ paricaritabba’nti vadāmi, na panāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ‘sabbaṃ na paricaritabba’nti vadāmi. Yaṃ hissa, brāhmaṇa, paricarato pāricariyāhetu saddhā vaḍḍhati, sīlaṃ vaḍḍhati, sutaṃ vaḍḍhati, cāgo vaḍḍhati, paññā vaḍḍhati, tamahaṃ ‘paricaritabba’nti (vadāmi. Yaṃ hissa, brāhmaṇa, paricarato pāricariyāhetu na saddhā vaḍḍhati, na sīlaṃ vaḍḍhati, na sutaṃ vaḍḍhati, na cāgo vaḍḍhati, na paññā vaḍḍhati, nāhaṃ taṃ ‘paricaritabba’nti) ( ) etthantare pāṭho sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. potthakesu natthi vadāmī’’ti.
mula_english:
“Here, brahmin, one of great beauty…one of great wealth may kill living beings…and hold wrong view.

Therefore I say that one is not better because one is of great wealth.

But also, brahmin, one of great beauty…of great wealth may abstain from killing living beings…and hold right view.

Therefore I do not say that one is worse because one is of great wealth.

“I do not say, brahmin, that all are to be served, nor do I say that none are to be served.

For if, when serving someone, one’s faith (saddhā), virtue (sīla), learning (suta), generosity (cāga), and wisdom (prajñā) increase in his service, then I say that he should be served.”

For if, when serving someone, one’s faith does not increase, nor virtue, nor learning, nor generosity, nor wisdom, then I do not say that he should be served.

mula_pali: 440. Evaṃ vutte, esukārī brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘brāhmaṇā, bho gotama, cattāri dhanāni paññapenti – brāhmaṇassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti, khattiyassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti, vessassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti, suddassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti. Tatridaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti bhikkhācariyaṃ; bhikkhācariyañca pana brāhmaṇo sandhanaṃ atimaññamāno akiccakārī hoti gopova adinnaṃ ādiyamānoti. Idaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti. Tatridaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā khattiyassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti dhanukalāpaṃ; dhanukalāpañca pana khattiyo sandhanaṃ atimaññamāno akiccakārī hoti gopova adinnaṃ ādiyamānoti. Idaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā khattiyassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti. Tatridaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā vessassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti kasigorakkhaṃ; kasigorakkhañca pana vesso sandhanaṃ atimaññamāno akiccakārī hoti gopova adinnaṃ ādiyamānoti. Idaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā vessassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti. Tatridaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā suddassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti asitabyābhaṅgiṃ; asitabyābhaṅgiñca pana suddo sandhanaṃ atimaññamāno akiccakārī hoti gopova adinnaṃ ādiyamānoti. Idaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā suddassa sandhanaṃ paññapenti. Brāhmaṇā, bho gotama, imāni cattāri dhanāni paññapenti. Idha bhavaṃ gotamo kimāhā’’ti?
mula_english:
When this was said, the *brāhmaṇa* Esukārī said this to the Blessed One: "Master Gotama, the *brāhmaṇas* describe four kinds of wealth (*dhanāni*). They describe the wealth of a *brāhmaṇa*, the wealth of a *kṣatriya*, the wealth of a *vaiśya*, and the wealth of a *śūdra*.

"And therein, Master Gotama, the *brāhmaṇas* describe the wealth (*sandhanaṃ*) of a *brāhmaṇa* as the practice of begging for alms (*bhikkhācariyaṃ*); but a *brāhmaṇa* who despises that wealth (*sandhanaṃ*), the practice of begging for alms (*bhikkhācariyaṃ*), is an idler, like a herdsman who takes what is not given. That, Master Gotama, is what the *brāhmaṇas* describe as the wealth (*sandhanaṃ*) of a *brāhmaṇa*.

"And therein, Master Gotama, the *brāhmaṇas* describe the wealth (*sandhanaṃ*) of a *kṣatriya* as the bow and quiver (*dhanukalāpaṃ*); but a *kṣatriya* who despises that wealth (*sandhanaṃ*), the bow and quiver (*dhanukalāpaṃ*), is an idler, like a herdsman who takes what is not given. That, Master Gotama, is what the *brāhmaṇas* describe as the wealth (*sandhanaṃ*) of a *kṣatriya*.

"And therein, Master Gotama, the *brāhmaṇas* describe the wealth (*sandhanaṃ*) of a *vaiśya* as farming and cattle-raising (*kasigorakkhaṃ*); but a *vaiśya* who despises that wealth (*sandhanaṃ*), farming and cattle-raising (*kasigorakkhaṃ*), is an idler, like a herdsman who takes what is not given. That, Master Gotama, is what the *brāhmaṇas* describe as the wealth (*sandhanaṃ*) of a *vaiśya*.

"And therein, Master Gotama, the *brāhmaṇas* describe the wealth (*sandhanaṃ*) of a *śūdra* as the sickle and carrying pole (*asitabyābhaṅgiṃ*); but a *śūdra* who despises that wealth (*sandhanaṃ*), the sickle and carrying pole (*asitabyābhaṅgiṃ*), is an idler, like a herdsman who takes what is not given. That, Master Gotama, is what the *brāhmaṇas* describe as the wealth (*sandhanaṃ*) of a *śūdra*.

"Master Gotama, these are the four kinds of wealth (*dhanāni*) that the *brāhmaṇas* describe. What does Master Gotama say about this?"
commentary_pali:
440.Bhikkhācariyanti koṭidhanenapi hi brāhmaṇena bhikkhā caritabbāva, porāṇakabrāhmaṇā asītikoṭidhanāpi ekavelaṃ bhikkhaṃ caranti. Kasmā? Duggatakāle carantānaṃ idāni bhikkhaṃ carituṃ āraddhāti garahā na bhavissatīti. Atimaññamānoti yo bhikkhācariyavaṃsaṃ haritvā sattajīvakasikammavaṇijjādīhi jīvikaṃ kappeti, ayaṃ atimaññati nāma. Gopo vāti yathā gopako attanā rakkhitabbaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ thenento akiccakārī hoti, evanti attho. Iminā nayena sabbavāresu attho veditabbo. Asitabyābhaṅginti tiṇalāyanaasitañceva kājañca. Anussaratoti yattha jāto, tasmiṃ porāṇe mātāpettike kulavaṃse anussariyamāneti attho. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Esukārīsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
440. *Bhikkhācariya:* Even a *brāhmaṇa* with wealth of a *koṭi* should still go begging for alms. Ancient *brāhmaṇas* with wealth of eighty *koṭis* would go for alms once a day. Why? So that when they go begging in times of poverty, there will be no criticism that they have only started begging now.

*Atimaññamāno:* This is someone who abandons the tradition of going for alms and makes a living through the crafts, trades, commerce, etc., that sustain life. This is what is called *atimaññati*.

*Gopo vā:* Just as a herdsman who steals goods that he should protect is one who does what should not be done; this is the meaning. In this way, the meaning should be understood in all instances.

*Asitabyābhaṅgi:* <pb ed="p" n="3. 0429"/> Both the *asita* made of *tiṇalāyana* and the *kāja*.

*Anussarato:* That is, remembering the ancient maternal and paternal family lineage in which he was born; this is the meaning.

The rest is clear throughout.

The commentary on the Esukārī Sutta in the Papañcasūdanī, the commentary to the *Majjhimanikāya*, is complete.

mula_pali:
441. ‘‘Kiṃ pana, brāhmaṇa, sabbo loko brāhmaṇānaṃ etadabbhanujānāti – ‘imāni cattāri dhanāni paññapentū’’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, puriso daliddo assako anāḷhiyo. Tassa akāmassa bilaṃ olaggeyyuṃ – ‘idaṃ te, ambho purisa, maṃsaṃ khāditabbaṃ, mūlañca anuppadātabba’nti. Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, brāhmaṇā appaṭiññāya tesaṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ, atha ca panimāni cattāri dhanāni paññapenti. Ariyaṃ kho ahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, lokuttaraṃ dhammaṃ purisassa sandhanaṃ paññapemi. Porāṇaṃ kho panassa mātāpettikaṃ kulavaṃsaṃ anussarato yattha yattheva attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti tena teneva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Khattiyakule ce attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti ‘khattiyo’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; brāhmaṇakule ce attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti ‘brāhmaṇo’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; vessakule ce attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti ‘vesso’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; suddakule ce attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti ‘suddo’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, yaṃyadeva paccayaṃ paṭicca aggi jalati tena teneva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Kaṭṭhañce paṭicca aggi jalati ‘kaṭṭhaggi’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; sakalikañce paṭicca aggi jalati ‘sakalikaggi’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; tiṇañce paṭicca aggi jalati ‘tiṇaggi’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; gomayañce paṭicca aggi jalati ‘gomayaggi’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Evameva kho ahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, ariyaṃ lokuttaraṃ dhammaṃ purisassa sandhanaṃ paññapemi. Porāṇaṃ kho panassa mātāpettikaṃ kulavaṃsaṃ anussarato yattha yattheva attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti tena teneva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati.

‘‘Khattiyakule ce attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti ‘khattiyo’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; brāhmaṇakule ce attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti ‘brāhmaṇo’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; vessakule ce attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti ‘vesso’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati; suddakule ce attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti ‘suddo’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati.

‘‘Khattiyakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, abrahmacariyā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, anabhijjhālu hoti, abyāpannacitto hoti, sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

‘‘Brāhmaṇakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

‘‘Vessakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

‘‘Suddakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.
mula_english:
“Well, brahmin, has all the world authorised the *brāhmaṇas* to prescribe these four types of wealth?” “No, Gotama.”

“Just as, brahmin, they were to force a cut of meat upon a poor, resourceless, and helpless man and tell him: ‘Good man, you must eat this meat and pay for it’; so too, brahmin, without the consent of those other recluses and *brāhmaṇas*, the *brāhmaṇas* nevertheless prescribe these four types of wealth. I, brahmin, declare the noble supramundane *Dhamma* as a person’s own wealth (*ariyaṃ kho ahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, lokuttaraṃ dhammaṃ purisassa sandhanaṃ paññapemi*). But recollecting his ancient maternal and paternal family lineage, he is reckoned according to wherever he is reborn. If he is reborn in a clan of nobles (*khattiyakule*), he is reckoned as a noble (*khattiyo’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati*); if he is reborn in a clan of *brāhmaṇas*, he is reckoned as a *brāhmaṇa* (*brāhmaṇakule ce attabhāvassa abhinibbatti hoti ‘brāhmaṇo’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati*); if he is reborn in a clan of merchants (*vessakule*), he is reckoned as a merchant (*vesso’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati*); if he is reborn in a clan of workers (*suddakule*), he is reckoned as a worker (*suddo’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati*). Just as fire is reckoned by the particular condition dependent on which it burns – when fire burns dependent on logs, it is reckoned as a log fire (*kaṭṭhaggi’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati*); when fire burns dependent on faggots, it is reckoned as a faggot fire (*sakalikaggi’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati*); when fire burns dependent on grass, it is reckoned as a grass fire (*tiṇaggi’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati*); when fire burns dependent on cowdung, it is reckoned as a cowdung fire (*gomayaggi’tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati*) - so too, brahmin, I declare the noble supramundane *Dhamma* as a person’s own wealth. But recollecting his ancient maternal and paternal family lineage, he is reckoned according to wherever he is reborn.

“If he is reborn in a clan of nobles, he is reckoned as a noble; if he is reborn in a clan of *brāhmaṇas*, he is reckoned as a *brāhmaṇa*; if he is reborn in a clan of merchants, he is reckoned as a merchant; if he is reborn in a clan of workers, he is reckoned as a worker.

“If, brahmin, anyone from a clan of nobles goes forth from the home life into homelessness, and after encountering the *Dhamma* and Discipline proclaimed by the *Tathāgata*, he abstains from killing living beings (*pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti*), from taking what is not given (*adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti*), from incelibacy (*abrahmacariyā paṭivirato hoti*), from false speech (*musāvādā paṭivirato hoti*), from malicious speech (*pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti*), from harsh speech (*pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti*), and from gossip (*samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti*), and is uncovetous (*anabhijjhālu hoti*), has a mind without ill will (*abyāpannacitto hoti*), and holds right view (*sammādiṭṭhi hoti*), he is one who is accomplishing the true way, the *Dhamma* that is wholesome (*ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ*).

“If, brahmin, anyone from a clan of *brāhmaṇas* goes forth from the home life into homelessness, and after encountering the *Dhamma* and Discipline proclaimed by the *Tathāgata*, he abstains from killing living beings…and holds right view, he is one who is accomplishing the true way, the *Dhamma* that is wholesome.

“If, brahmin, anyone from a clan of merchants goes forth from the home life into homelessness, and after encountering the *Dhamma* and Discipline proclaimed by the *Tathāgata*, he abstains from killing living beings…and holds right view, he is one who is accomplishing the true way, the *Dhamma* that is wholesome.

“If anyone from a clan of workers goes forth from the home life into homelessness, and after encountering the *Dhamma* and Discipline proclaimed by the *Tathāgata*, he abstains from killing living beings…and holds right view, he is one who is accomplishing the true way, the *Dhamma* that is wholesome.

mula_pali:
442. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, brāhmaṇa, brāhmaṇova nu kho pahoti asmiṃ padese averaṃ abyābajjhaṃ mettacittaṃ bhāvetuṃ, no khattiyo no vesso no suddo’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama. Khattiyopi hi, bho gotama, pahoti asmiṃ padese averaṃ abyābajjhaṃ mettacittaṃ bhāvetuṃ; brāhmaṇopi hi, bho gotama… vessopi hi, bho gotama… suddopi hi, bho gotama… sabbepi hi, bho gotama, cattāro vaṇṇā pahonti asmiṃ padese averaṃ abyābajjhaṃ mettacittaṃ bhāvetu’’nti. ‘‘Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, khattiyakulā cepi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

‘‘Brāhmaṇakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa… vessakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa… suddakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.
mula_english:
442. “What do you think, brahmin? Is only a brahmin capable of developing a mind of loving-kindness ( *mettacittaṃ*) towards a certain region, without hostility (*averaṃ*) and without ill will (*abyābajjhaṃ*), and not a noble (*khattiyo*), or a merchant (*vesso*), or a worker (*suddo*)?”

“No, indeed, sir (*bho*), Gotama. Whether it be a noble (*khattiyo*), sir (*bho*), Gotama, they are capable of developing a mind of loving-kindness (*mettacittaṃ*) towards a certain region, without hostility (*averaṃ*) and without ill will (*abyābajjhaṃ*); or a brahmin (*brāhmaṇo*), sir (*bho*), Gotama… or a merchant (*vesso*), sir (*bho*), Gotama… or a worker (*suddo*), sir (*bho*), Gotama… indeed all four castes (*cattāro vaṇṇā*), sir (*bho*), Gotama, are capable of developing a mind of loving-kindness (*mettacittaṃ*) towards a certain region, without hostility (*averaṃ*) and without ill will (*abyābajjhaṃ*).”

“So too, brahmin, if anyone from a clan of nobles (*khattiyakulā*) goes forth from the home life (*agārasmā*) into homelessness (*anagāriyaṃ*), and after encountering the *Dhamma* and Discipline (*dhammavinayaṃ*) proclaimed by the *Tathāgata*, he abstains from killing living beings (*pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti*)…and holds right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*), he is one who is accomplishing (*ārādhako hoti*) the true way (*ñāyaṃ*), the *Dhamma* (*dhammaṃ*) that is wholesome (*kusalaṃ*).

“If, brahmin, anyone from a clan of brahmins (*brāhmaṇakulā*)… or a clan of merchants (*vessakulā*), brahmin… or a clan of workers (*suddakulā*), brahmin, goes forth from the home life (*agārasmā*) into homelessness (*anagāriyaṃ*), and after encountering the *Dhamma* and Discipline (*dhammavinayaṃ*) proclaimed by the *Tathāgata*, he abstains from killing living beings (*pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti*)…and holds right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*), he is one who is accomplishing (*ārādhako hoti*) the true way (*ñāyaṃ*), the *Dhamma* (*dhammaṃ*) that is wholesome (*kusalaṃ*).

mula_pali:
443. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, brāhmaṇa, brāhmaṇova nu kho pahoti sottisināniṃ ādāya nadiṃ gantvā rajojallaṃ pavāhetuṃ, no khattiyo no vesso no suddo’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama . Khattiyopi hi, bho gotama, pahoti sottisināniṃ ādāya nadiṃ gantvā rajojallaṃ pavāhetuṃ; brāhmaṇopi hi, bho gotama… vessopi hi, bho gotama … suddopi hi, bho gotama… sabbepi hi, bho gotama, cattāro vaṇṇā pahonti sottisināniṃ ādāya nadiṃ gantvā rajojallaṃ pavāhetu’’nti. ‘‘Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, khattiyakulā cepi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

‘‘Brāhmaṇakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa… vessakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa… suddakulā cepi , brāhmaṇa, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.
mula_english:
“What do you think, brahmin? Is only a *brāhmaṇa* capable of taking a loofah and bath powder, going to the river, and washing off dust and dirt, and not a *kṣatriya*, or a *vaiśya*, or a *śūdra*?”

“Whether it be a *kṣatriya*, a *brāhmaṇa*, a *vaiśya*, or a *śūdra* — all four *varṇas* are capable of taking a loofah and bath powder, going to the river, and washing off dust and dirt.”

“So too, brahmin, if anyone from a clan of *kṣatriyas* goes forth from the home life into homelessness, and after encountering the *dharma-vinaya* proclaimed by the *Tathāgata*, he abstains from killing living beings…and holds right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*), he is one who is accomplishing the true way (*ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ*).”

“If, brahmin, anyone from a clan of *brāhmaṇas*, a clan of *vaisyas*, or a clan of *śūdras* goes forth from the home life into homelessness, and after encountering the *dharma-vinaya* proclaimed by the *Tathāgata*, he abstains from killing living beings…and holds right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*), he is one who is accomplishing the true way (*ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ*).”

mula_pali:
444. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, brāhmaṇa, idha rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto nānājaccānaṃ purisānaṃ purisasataṃ sannipāteyya – ‘āyantu bhonto ye tattha khattiyakulā brāhmaṇakulā rājaññakulā uppannā sākassa vā sālassa vā salaḷassa vā candanassa vā padumakassa vā uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya aggiṃ abhinibbattentu, tejo pātukarontu; āyantu pana bhonto ye tattha caṇḍālakulā nesādakulā venakulā rathakārakulā pukkusakulā uppannā sāpānadoṇiyā vā sūkaradoṇiyā vā rajakadoṇiyā vā eraṇḍakaṭṭhassa vā uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya aggiṃ abhinibbattentu, tejo pātukarontū’’’ti?

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, brāhmaṇa, yo evaṃ nu kho so khattiyakulā brāhmaṇakulā rājaññakulā uppannehi sākassa vā sālassa vā salaḷassa vā candanassa vā padumakassa vā uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya aggi abhinibbatto tejo pātukato so eva nu khvāssa aggi accimā ceva vaṇṇavā ca pabhassaro ca tena ca sakkā agginā aggikaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ; yo pana so caṇḍālakulā nesādakulā venakulā rathakārakulā pukkusakulā uppannehi sāpānadoṇiyā vā sūkaradoṇiyā vā rajakadoṇiyā vā eraṇḍakaṭṭhassa vā uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya aggi abhinibbatto tejo pātukato svāssa aggi na ceva accimā na ca vaṇṇavā na ca pabhassaro na ca tena sakkā agginā aggikaraṇīyaṃ kātu’’nti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama. Yopi hi so, bho gotama, khattiyakulā brāhmaṇakulā rājaññakulā uppannehi sākassa vā sālassa vā salaḷassa vā candanassa vā padumakassa vā uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya aggi abhinibbatto tejo pātukato svāssa aggi accimā ceva vaṇṇavā ca pabhassaro ca tena ca sakkā agginā aggikaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ; yopi so caṇḍālakulā nesādakulā venakulā rathakārakulā pukkusakulā uppannehi sāpānadoṇiyā vā sūkaradoṇiyā vā rajakadoṇiyā vā eraṇḍakaṭṭhassa vā uttarāraṇiṃ ādāya aggi abhinibbatto tejo pātukato svāssa aggi accimā ceva vaṇṇavā ca pabhassaro ca tena ca sakkā agginā aggikaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ. Sabbopi hi, bho gotama, aggi accimā ceva vaṇṇavā ca pabhassaro ca sabbenapi sakkā agginā aggikaraṇīyaṃ kātu’’nti.

‘‘Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, khattiyakulā cepi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ. Brāhmaṇakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa… vessakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa… suddakulā cepi, brāhmaṇa, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so ca tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ āgamma pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, abrahmacariyā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, anabhijjhālu hoti, abyāpannacitto hoti, sammādiṭṭhi hoti, ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusala’’nti.

Evaṃ vutte, esukārī brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata’’nti.

Esukārīsuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.
mula_english:
“What do you think, brahmin? Suppose a noble king, a head-anointed one, were to assemble here a hundred men of different births, saying: ‘Let those who are born in noble families ( *kṣatriyakulā* ), Brahmin families ( *brāhmaṇakulā* ), or royal families ( *rājaññakulā* )—whether from teak, *sāla*, *salaḷa*, sandalwood *candana*, or *padmaka* wood—bring an upper fire-stick (*uttarāraṇiṃ*) and kindle a fire, produce heat. But let those who are born in outcaste (*caṇḍāla*) families, hunter (*nesāda*) families, *veṇa* families, chariot-maker (*rathakāra*) families, or *pukkusa* families—whether using a dog’s feeding bowl, a pig’s feeding bowl, a dyer’s bowl, or an castor-oil plant wood—bring an upper fire-stick (*uttarāraṇiṃ*) and kindle a fire, produce heat’?”

“What do you think, brahmin? When a fire is kindled and heat produced by those born in noble families ( *kṣatriyakulā* ), Brahmin families ( *brāhmaṇakulā* ), or royal families ( *rājaññakulā* )—whether from teak, *sāla*, *salaḷa*, sandalwood (*candana*), or *padmaka* wood—would that fire alone have a flame, color, and radiance, and only that fire could be used for the purposes of fire? And when a fire is kindled and heat produced by those born in outcaste (*caṇḍāla*) families, hunter (*nesāda*) families, *veṇa* families, chariot-maker (*rathakāra*) families, or *pukkusa* families—whether using a dog’s feeding bowl, a pig’s feeding bowl, a dyer’s bowl, or castor-oil plant wood—would that fire not have a flame, color, and radiance, and could that fire not be used for the purposes of fire?”

“No, Master Gotama.”

“So too, Master Gotama, when a fire is kindled and heat produced by those born in noble families (*khattiyakulā*), Brahmin families (*brāhmaṇakulā*), or royal families (*rājaññakulā*)—whether from teak, *sāla*, *salaḷa*, sandalwood (*candana*), or *padmaka* wood—that fire would have a flame, color, and radiance, and could be used for the purposes of fire. And when a fire is kindled and heat produced by those born in outcaste (*caṇḍāla*) families, hunter (*nesāda*) families, *veṇa* families, chariot-maker (*rathakāra*) families, or *pukkusa* families—whether using a dog’s feeding bowl, a pig’s feeding bowl, a dyer’s bowl, or castor-oil plant wood—that fire too would have a flame, color, and radiance, and could be used for the purposes of fire. For all fire, Master Gotama, has a flame, color, and radiance, and all fire can be used for the purposes of fire.”

“Just so, brahmin, if anyone from a clan of nobles (*khattiyakulā*) goes forth from the home life into homelessness, and after encountering the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the *tathāgata* , he abstains from killing living beings…and holds right view, he is one who is accomplishing the true way, the Dhamma that is wholesome. If anyone from a clan of Brahmins (*brāhmaṇakulā*), or merchants (*vessakulā*) or workers (*śuddakulā*) goes forth from the home life into homelessness, and after encountering the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the *tathāgata* , he abstains from killing living beings, from taking what is not given, from celibacy, from false speech, from malicious speech, from harsh speech, and from gossip, and is uncovetous, has a mind without ill will, and holds right view, he is one who is accomplishing the true way, the Dhamma that is wholesome.”

When this was said, the Brahmin Esukari said to the Blessed One (*bhagavant*): “Magnificent, Master Gotama! Magnificent, Master Gotama! …From today let Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone to him for refuge for life.”
