The Esukari Sutta, the sixth, is finished.

mula_pali: 445. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā sāriputto dakkhiṇāgirismiṃ cārikaṃ carati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu rājagahe vassaṃvuṭṭho vassaṃvuttho (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) yena dakkhiṇāgiri yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho taṃ bhikkhuṃ āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca – ‘‘kaccāvuso, bhagavā arogo ca balavā cā’’ti? ‘‘Arogo cāvuso, bhagavā balavā cā’’ti. ‘‘Kacci panāvuso, bhikkhusaṅgho arogo ca balavā cā’’ti? ‘‘Bhikkhusaṅghopi kho, āvuso, arogo ca balavā cā’’ti. ‘‘Ettha, āvuso, taṇḍulapālidvārāya dhanañjāni dhānañjāni (sī. pī.) nāma brāhmaṇo atthi. Kaccāvuso , dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo arogo ca balavā cā’’ti? ‘‘Dhanañjānipi kho, āvuso, brāhmaṇo arogo ca balavā cā’’ti. ‘‘Kacci panāvuso, dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo appamatto’’ti? ‘‘Kuto panāvuso, dhanañjānissa brāhmaṇassa appamādo? Dhanañjāni, āvuso, brāhmaṇo rājānaṃ nissāya brāhmaṇagahapatike vilumpati, brāhmaṇagahapatike nissāya rājānaṃ vilumpati . Yāpissa bhariyā saddhā saddhakulā ānītā sāpi kālaṅkatā; aññāssa bhariyā assaddhā assaddhakulā ānītā’’. ‘‘Dussutaṃ vatāvuso, assumha, dussutaṃ vatāvuso, assumha; ye mayaṃ dhanañjāniṃ brāhmaṇaṃ pamattaṃ assumha. Appeva ca nāma mayaṃ kadāci karahaci dhanañjāninā brāhmaṇena saddhiṃ samāgaccheyyāma, appeva nāma siyā kocideva kathāsallāpo’’ti?
mula_english:
THUS HAVE I HEARD.

On one occasion the Blessed One (bhagavā) was living at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove (veḷuvana), the Squirrels’ Sanctuary (kalandakanivāpe).

Now at that time the venerable Sāriputta was wandering in the Southern Hills (dakkhiṇāgiri) with a large Saṃgha of monks (bhikkhusaṅgha).

Then a certain monk (bhikkhu) who had spent the Rains at Rājagaha went to the venerable Sāriputta in the Southern Hills, and exchanged greetings with him (sammodi). Having exchanged greetings of friendliness and courtesy (sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā), he sat down at one side (ekamantaṃ nisīdi).

The venerable Sāriputta said to the monk who was sitting to one side (ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ): “Is the Blessed One (bhagavā) well and strong, friend (āvuso)?”

“The Blessed One (bhagavā) is well and strong, friend (āvuso).”

“Is the Saṃgha of monks (bhikkhusaṅgho) well and strong, friend (āvuso)?”

“The Saṃgha of monks (bhikkhusaṅghopi) is well and strong, friend (āvuso).”

“Here, friend (āvuso), at Taṇḍulapālidvāra, there is a Brahmin (brāhmaṇo) named Dhanañjāni.”

“Is that Brahmin (brāhmaṇo) Dhanañjāni well and strong, friend (āvuso)?”

“That Brahmin (brāhmaṇo) Dhanañjāni is also well and strong, friend (āvuso).”

“Is that Brahmin (brāhmaṇo) Dhanañjāni diligent, friend (āvuso)?”

“How could that Brahmin (brāhmaṇassa) Dhanañjāni be diligent, friend (āvuso)? That Brahmin (brāhmaṇo) Dhanañjāni, friend (āvuso), relying on the king (rājānaṃ nissāya), robs the Brahmins (brāhmaṇagahapatike), and relying on the Brahmins (brāhmaṇagahapatike nissāya), robs the king (rājānaṃ vilumpati).

His wife, who had faith (saddhā) and came from a clan with faith (saddhakulā ānītā), has died (kālaṅkatā) and he has taken another wife (bhariyā), a woman without faith (assaddhā) who comes from a clan without faith (assaddhakulā ānītā).”

“This is bad news that we hear, friend (āvuso), it is bad news that we hear. The Brahmin (brāhmaṇaṃ) Dhanañjāni has become negligent (pamattaṃ). Perhaps sometime or other we might meet the Brahmin (brāhmaṇena) Dhanañjāni and have some conversation with him (kathāsallāpo).”
commentary_pali: 445.Evaṃme sutanti dhanañjānisuttaṃ. Tattha dakkhiṇāgirisminti girīti pabbato, rājagahaṃ parikkhipitvā ṭhitapabbatassa dakkhiṇadisābhāge janapadassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Taṇḍulapālidvārāyāti rājagahassa kira dvattiṃsamahādvārāni catusaṭṭhikhuddakadvārāni, tesu ekaṃ taṇḍulapālidvāraṃ nāma, taṃ sandhāyevamāha. Rājānaṃ nissāyāti ‘‘gaccha manusse apīḷetvā sassabhāgaṃ gaṇhāhī’’ti raññā pesito gantvā sabbameva sassaṃ gaṇhāti, ‘‘mā no, bhante, nāsehī’’ti ca vutte – ‘‘rājakule vuttaṃ mandaṃ, ahaṃ raññā āgamanakāleyeva evaṃ āṇatto, mā kanditthā’’ti evaṃ rājānaṃ nissāya brāhmaṇagahapatike vilumpati. Dhaññaṃ yebhuyyena attano gharaṃ pavesetvā appakaṃ rājakule paveseti. Kiṃ brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṃ na pīḷaṃ akāsīti ca vutto – ‘‘āma, mahārāja, imasmiṃ vāre khettāni mandasassāni ahesuṃ, tasmā apīḷentassa me gaṇhato na bahuṃ jāta’’nti evaṃ brāhmaṇagahapatike nissāya rājānaṃ vilumpati.
commentary_english:
445.
evaṃ me sutanti Dhanañjānisuttaṃ.

tattha dakkhiṇāgirisminti girīti pabbato, rājagahaṃ parikkhipitvā ṭhitapabbatassa dakkhiṇadisābhāge janapadassetaṃ nāmaṃ.

taṇḍulapālidvārāyāti rājagahassa kira dvattiṃsamahādvārāṇi catusaṭṭhikhuddakadvārāṇi, tesu ekaṃ taṇḍulapālidvāraṃ nāma, taṃ sandhāyevamāha.

rājānaṃ nissāyāti "gaccha manusse apīḷetvā sassabhāgaṃ gaṇhāhī"ti raññā pesito gantvā sabbameva sassaṃ gaṇhāti, "mā no, bhante, nāsehī"ti ca vutte – "rājakule vuttaṃ mandaṃ, ahaṃ raññā āgamanakāleyeva evaṃ āṇatto, mā kanditthā"ti evaṃ rājānaṃ nissāya brāhmaṇagahapatike vilumpati.

dhaññaṃ yebhuyyena attano gharaṃ pavesetvā appakaṃ rājakule paveseti.

kiṃ brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṃ na pīḷaṃ akāsīti ca vutto – "āma, mahārāja, imasmiṃ vāre khettāni mandasassāni ahesuṃ, tasmā apīḷentassa me gaṇhato na bahuṃ jāta''nti evaṃ brāhmaṇagahapatike nissāya rājānaṃ vilumpati.

mula_pali: 446. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto dakkhiṇāgirismiṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena rājagahaṃ tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena rājagahaṃ tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ āyasmā sāriputto rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi . Tena kho pana samayena dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo bahinagare gāvo goṭṭhe duhāpeti. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto rājagahe piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘ito, bho sāriputta, payo, pīyataṃ tāva bhattassa kālo bhavissatī’’ti. ‘‘Alaṃ, brāhmaṇa. Kataṃ me ajja bhattakiccaṃ. Amukasmiṃ me rukkhamūle divāvihāro bhavissati. Tattha āgaccheyyāsī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bho’’ti kho dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosi. Atha kho dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo pacchābhattaṃ bhuttapātarāso yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho dhanañjāniṃ brāhmaṇaṃ āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca – ‘‘kaccāsi, dhanañjāni, appamatto’’ti? ‘‘Kuto, bho sāriputta, amhākaṃ appamādo yesaṃ no mātāpitaro posetabbā, puttadāro posetabbo, dāsakammakarā posetabbā, mittāmaccānaṃ mittāmaccakaraṇīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, ñātisālohitānaṃ ñātisālohitakaraṇīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, atithīnaṃ atithikaraṇīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, pubbapetānaṃ pubbapetakaraṇīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, devatānaṃ devatākaraṇīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, rañño rājakaraṇīyaṃ kātabbaṃ, ayampi kāyo pīṇetabbo brūhetabbo’’ti?
mula_english:
Then, the venerable Śāriputta, having stayed at Dakṣiṇāgiri for as long as he pleased, set out to wander towards Rājagṛha.

Wandering by stages, he eventually arrived at Rājagṛha.

There, the venerable Śāriputra was staying at Rājagṛha in the Veḷuvana, the Kalandakanivāpa (Squirrel Sanctuary).

Then, in the morning, the venerable Śāriputra, having dressed, taking his bowl and robe, entered Rājagṛha for alms.

Now at that time, the brahmin Dhanañjāni was having his cows milked in a cowshed outside the city.

Then, the venerable Śāriputra, having wandered for alms in Rājagṛha, and having returned from his alms round after his meal, went to the brahmin Dhanañjāni.

The brahmin Dhanañjāni saw the venerable Śāriputta coming in the distance.

Seeing him, he went to the venerable Śāriputta; having approached, he said to the venerable Śāriputta: "Come, sir Śāriputta, drink some milk, it will soon be time for the meal."

"Enough, brahmin.

I have finished my meal for today.

I will spend the day at the root of a certain tree.

Come there."

"Yes, sir," the brahmin Dhanañjāni replied to the venerable Śāriputta.

Then, the brahmin Dhanañjāni, after his morning meal, went to the venerable Śāriputta; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the venerable Śāriputra.

Having concluded their courteous and amiable talk, he sat down at one side.

The venerable Śāriputra said this to the brahmin Dhanañjāni, who was sitting to one side: "Are you diligent, Dhanañjāni?" "How can we be diligent, sir Śāriputra, when we have to support our parents, our wife and children, and our slaves, servants and workers; when we have to do our duty towards our friends and companions, towards our kinsmen and relatives, towards our guests, towards our departed ancestors, towards the deities, and towards the king; and when this body must also be refreshed and nourished?"
commentary_pali: 446.Payo pīyatanti taruṇakhīraṃ pivatu. Tāva bhattassāti yāva khīraṃ pivitvā nisīdissatha, tāvadeva bhattassa kālo bhavissati. Idheva hi no pātarāsabhattaṃ āharissantīti dasseti. Mātāpitarotiādīsu mahallakā mātāpitaro mudukāni attharaṇapāvuraṇāni sukhumāni vatthāni madhurabhojanaṃ sugandhagandhamālādīni ca pariyesitvā posetabbā. Puttadhītānaṃ nāmakaraṇamaṅgalādīni sabbakiccāni karontena puttadāro posetabbo. Evañhi akariyamāne garahā uppajjatīti iminā nayena attho veditabbo.
commentary_english:
446. " *payo pīyata* " means let him drink *taruṇakhīraṃ* (fresh milk).
" *tāva bhattassā* " means until you drink the milk and sit down, that will be the time for the meal.
It indicates that they will bring breakfast here.
"*mātāpitaro* " etc., elderly parents should be cared for by seeking soft bedding and coverings, fine clothes, sweet food, fragrant garlands, and so on.
By one who performs all duties, such as naming ceremonies and auspicious rites for sons and daughters, the wife and children should be supported.
Thus, if it is not done, blame arises; the meaning should be understood in this way.

mula_pali:
447. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco mātāpitūnaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho mātāpitūnaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti , mātāpitaro vā panassa labheyyuṃ ‘eso kho amhākaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosi, mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ’’.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco puttadārassa hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho puttadārassa hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti, puttadāro vā panassa labheyya ‘eso kho amhākaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosi mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ’’.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco dāsakammakaraporisassa hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho dāsakammakaraporisassa hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti, dāsakammakaraporisā vā panassa labheyyuṃ ‘eso kho amhākaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosi, mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ’’.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco mittāmaccānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho mittāmaccānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti, mittāmaccā vā panassa labheyyuṃ ‘eso kho amhākaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosi, mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ’’.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco ñātisālohitānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho ñātisālohitānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti, ñātisālohitā vā panassa labheyyuṃ ‘eso kho amhākaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosi, mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ’’.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco atithīnaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho atithīnaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti, atithī vā panassa labheyyuṃ ‘eso kho amhākaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosi, mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ’’.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco pubbapetānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho pubbapetānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti, pubbapetā vā panassa labheyyuṃ ‘eso kho amhākaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosi, mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ’’.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco devatānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho devatānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti, devatā vā panassa labheyyuṃ ‘eso kho amhākaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosi, mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ’’.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco rañño hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho rañño hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti, rājā vā panassa labheyya ‘eso kho amhākaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosi, mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ’’.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, idhekacco kāyassa pīṇanāhetu brūhanāhetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, tamenaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu nirayaṃ nirayapālā upakaḍḍheyyuṃ. Labheyya nu kho so ‘ahaṃ kho kāyassa pīṇanāhetu brūhanāhetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosiṃ, mā maṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’ti, pare vā panassa labheyyuṃ ‘eso kho kāyassa pīṇanāhetu brūhanāhetu adhammacārī visamacārī ahosi, mā naṃ nirayaṃ nirayapālā’’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho sāriputta. Atha kho naṃ vikkandantaṃyeva niraye nirayapālā pakkhipeyyuṃ’’.
mula_english:
447. “What do you think, Dhananjani? Suppose someone here were to behave contrary to the *Dhamma*, to behave unrighteously for the sake of his parents, and then because of such behavior the wardens of hell would drag him off to hell. Would he be able to free himself by pleading thus: ‘It was for the sake of my parents that I behaved contrary to the *Dhamma*, that I behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag me off to hell’? Or would his parents be able to free him by pleading thus: ‘It was for our sake that he behaved contrary to the *Dhamma*, that he behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag him off to hell’?” “No, Master *Śāriputta*. Then, even while he was crying out, the wardens of hell would fling him into hell.”

“What do you think, Dhananjani? Suppose someone here were to behave contrary to the *Dhamma*, to behave unrighteously for the sake of his wife and children, and then because of such behavior the wardens of hell would drag him off to hell. Would he be able to free himself by pleading thus: ‘It was for the sake of my wife and children that I behaved contrary to the *Dhamma*, that I behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag me off to hell’? Or would his wife and children be able to free him by pleading thus: ‘It was for our sake that he behaved contrary to the *Dhamma*, that he behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag him off to hell’?” “No, Master *Śāriputta*. Even while he was crying out, the wardens of hell would fling him into hell.”

“What do you think, Dhananjani? Suppose someone here were to behave contrary to the *Dhamma*, to behave unrighteously for the sake of his slaves, workers and servants, and then because of such behavior the wardens of hell would drag him off to hell. Would he be able to free himself by pleading thus: ‘It was for the sake of my slaves, workers and servants that I behaved contrary to the *Dhamma*, that I behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag me off to hell’? Or would his slaves, workers and servants be able to free him by pleading thus: ‘It was for our sake that he behaved contrary to the *Dhamma*, that he behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag him off to hell’?” “No, Master *Śāriputta*. Even while he was crying out, the wardens of hell would fling him into hell.”

“What do you think, Dhananjani? Suppose someone here were to behave contrary to the *Dhamma*, to behave unrighteously for the sake of his friends and colleagues, and then because of such behavior the wardens of hell would drag him off to hell. Would he be able to free himself by pleading thus: ‘It was for the sake of my friends and colleagues that I behaved contrary to the *Dhamma*, that I behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag me off to hell’? Or would his friends and colleagues be able to free him by pleading thus: ‘It was for our sake that he behaved contrary to the *Dhamma*, that he behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag him off to hell’?” “No, Master *Śāriputta*. Even while he was crying out, the wardens of hell would fling him into hell.”

“What do you think, Dhananjani? Suppose someone here were to behave contrary to the *Dhamma*, to behave unrighteously for the sake of his relatives and blood-relations, and then because of such behavior the wardens of hell would drag him off to hell. Would he be able to free himself by pleading thus: ‘It was for the sake of my relatives and blood-relations that I behaved contrary to the *Dhamma*, that I behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag me off to hell’? Or would his relatives and blood-relations be able to free him by pleading thus: ‘It was for our sake that he behaved contrary to the *Dhamma*, that he behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag him off to hell’?” “No, Master *Śāriputta*. Even while he was crying out, the wardens of hell would fling him into hell.”

“What do you think, Dhananjani? Suppose someone here were to behave contrary to the *Dhamma*, to behave unrighteously for the sake of his guests, and then because of such behavior the wardens of hell would drag him off to hell. Would he be able to free himself by pleading thus: ‘It was for the sake of my guests that I behaved contrary to the *Dhamma*, that I behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag me off to hell’? Or would his guests be able to free him by pleading thus: ‘It was for our sake that he behaved contrary to the *Dhamma*, that he behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag him off to hell’?” “No, Master *Śāriputta*. Even while he was crying out, the wardens of hell would fling him into hell.”

“What do you think, Dhananjani? Suppose someone here were to behave contrary to the *Dhamma*, to behave unrighteously for the sake of his departed ancestors, and then because of such behavior the wardens of hell would drag him off to hell. Would he be able to free himself by pleading thus: ‘It was for the sake of my departed ancestors that I behaved contrary to the *Dhamma*, that I behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag me off to hell’? Or would his departed ancestors be able to free him by pleading thus: ‘It was for our sake that he behaved contrary to the *Dhamma*, that he behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag him off to hell’?” “No, Master *Śāriputta*. Even while he was crying out, the wardens of hell would fling him into hell.”

“What do you think, Dhananjani? Suppose someone here were to behave contrary to the *Dhamma*, to behave unrighteously for the sake of the deities, and then because of such behavior the wardens of hell would drag him off to hell. Would he be able to free himself by pleading thus: ‘It was for the sake of the deities that I behaved contrary to the *Dhamma*, that I behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag me off to hell’? Or would the deities be able to free him by pleading thus: ‘It was for our sake that he behaved contrary to the *Dhamma*, that he behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag him off to hell’?” “No, Master *Śāriputta*. Even while he was crying out, the wardens of hell would fling him into hell.”
“What do you think, Dhananjani? Suppose someone here were to behave contrary to the *dharma*, to behave unrighteously for the sake of the king… for that unrighteous conduct, would the wardens of hell drag him off to hell (*niraya*)?
Would he be able to free himself by pleading thus: ‘It was for the sake of the king that I behaved contrary to the *dharma*, that I behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag me off to hell (*niraya*)’? Or would the king be able to free him by pleading thus: ‘It was for our sake that he behaved contrary to the *dharma*, that he behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag him off to hell (*niraya*)’?”
“No, revered Sāriputta.”
“Even while he was crying out, the wardens of hell (*nirayapālā*) would fling him into hell (*niraya*).”

“What do you think, Dhananjani? Suppose someone here were to behave contrary to the *dharma*, to behave unrighteously for the sake of refreshing and nourishing this body (*kāyassa pīṇanāhetu brūhanāhetu*)… for that unrighteous conduct, would the wardens of hell drag him off to hell (*niraya*)?
Would he be able to free himself by pleading thus: ‘It was for the sake of refreshing and nourishing this body (*kāyassa pīṇanāhetu brūhanāhetu*) that I behaved contrary to the *dharma*, that I behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag me off to hell (*niraya*)’? Or would others be able to free him by pleading thus: ‘It was for the sake of refreshing and nourishing this body (*kāyassa pīṇanāhetu brūhanāhetu*) that he behaved contrary to the *dharma*, that he behaved unrighteously, so let not the wardens of hell drag him off to hell (*niraya*)’?”
“No, revered Sāriputta.”
“Even while he was crying out, the wardens of hell (*nirayapālā*) would fling him into hell (*niraya*).”
commentary_pali: 447.Adhammacārīti pañca dussīlyakammāni vā dasa dussīlyakammāni vā idha adhammo nāma. Upakaḍḍheyyunti pañcavidhabandhanādikammakaraṇatthaṃ taṃ taṃ nirayaṃ kaḍḍheyyuṃ.
commentary_english:
Adhammacārī: Here, *adhamma* refers to either five types of immoral conduct (*pañca dussīlyakammāni*) or ten types of immoral conduct (*dasa dussīlyakammāni*).

Upakaḍḍheyyu: They drag each and every being to that hell for the purpose of performing actions such as the five kinds of bonds (*pañcavidhabandhanādikammakaraṇatthaṃ*).

448. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, yo vā mātāpitūnaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, yo vā mātāpitūnaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa; katamaṃ seyyo’’ti? ‘‘Yo hi, bho sāriputta, mātāpitūnaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, na taṃ seyyo; yo ca kho, bho sāriputta, mātāpitūnaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa, tadevettha seyyo. Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi, bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo’’ti. ‘‘Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā kammantā, yehi sakkā mātāpitaro ceva posetuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjituṃ.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, yo vā puttadārassa hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, yo vā puttadārassa hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa; katamaṃ seyyo’’ti? ‘‘Yo hi, bho sāriputta, puttadārassa hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, na taṃ seyyo; yo ca kho, bho sāriputta, puttadārassa hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa, tadevettha seyyo. Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi, bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo’’ti. ‘‘Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā kammantā yehi sakkā puttadārañceva posetuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjituṃ.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, yo vā dāsakammakaraporisassa hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, yo vā dāsakammakaraporisassa hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa; katamaṃ seyyo’’ti? ‘‘Yo hi, bho sāriputta, dāsakammakaraporisassa hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, na taṃ seyyo; yo ca kho, bho sāriputta, dāsakammakaraporisassa hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa, tadevettha seyyo. Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi, bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo’’ti. ‘‘Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā kammantā, yehi sakkā dāsakammakaraporise ceva posetuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjituṃ.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, yo vā mittāmaccānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, yo vā mittāmaccānaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa; katamaṃ seyyo’’ti? ‘‘Yo hi , bho sāriputta, mittāmaccānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, na taṃ seyyo; yo ca kho, bho sāriputta, mittāmaccānaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa, tadevettha seyyo. Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi, bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo’’ti. ‘‘Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā kammantā, yehi sakkā mittāmaccānañceva mittāmaccakaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjituṃ.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, yo vā ñātisālohitānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, yo vā ñātisālohitānaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa; katamaṃ seyyo’’ti? ‘‘Yo hi, bho sāriputta, ñātisālohitānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, na taṃ seyyo; yo ca kho, bho sāriputta, ñātisālohitānaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa, tadevettha seyyo. Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi, bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo’’ti. ‘‘Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā kammantā, yehi sakkā ñātisālohitānañceva ñātisālohitakaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjituṃ.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, yo vā atithīnaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, yo vā atithīnaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa; katamaṃ seyyo’’ti? ‘‘Yo hi, bho sāriputta, atithīnaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, na taṃ seyyo; yo ca kho, bho sāriputta, atithīnaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa, tadevettha seyyo. Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi, bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo’’ti. ‘‘Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā kammantā, yehi sakkā atithīnañceva atithikaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjituṃ.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, yo vā pubbapetānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, yo vā pubbapetānaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa; katamaṃ seyyo’’ti? ‘‘Yo hi, bho sāriputta, pubbapetānaṃ hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, na taṃ seyyo; yo ca kho, bho sāriputta, pubbapetānaṃ hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa, tadevettha seyyo. Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi , bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo’’ti. ‘‘Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā kammantā, yehi sakkā pubbapetānañceva pubbapetakaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjituṃ.

Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi, bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo’’ti. ‘‘Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā kammantā, yehi sakkā devatānañceva devatākaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjituṃ.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, yo vā rañño hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, yo vā rañño hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa; katamaṃ seyyo’’ti? ‘‘Yo hi, bho sāriputta, rañño hetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, na taṃ seyyo; yo ca kho, bho sāriputta, rañño hetu dhammacārī samacārī assa, tadevettha seyyo. Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi, bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo’’ti. ‘‘Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā kammantā, yehi sakkā rañño ceva rājakaraṇīyaṃ kātuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjituṃ.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, yo vā kāyassa pīṇanāhetu brūhanāhetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, yo vā kāyassa pīṇanāhetu brūhanāhetu dhammacārī samacārī assa; katamaṃ seyyo’’ti? ‘‘Yo hi, bho sāriputta, kāyassa pīṇanāhetu brūhanāhetu adhammacārī visamacārī assa, na taṃ seyyo; yo ca kho, bho sāriputta, kāyassa pīṇanāhetu brūhanāhetu dhammacārī samacārī assa, tadevettha seyyo. Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhi, bho sāriputta, dhammacariyāsamacariyā seyyo’’ti. ‘‘Atthi kho, dhanañjāni, aññesaṃ hetukā dhammikā kammantā , yehi sakkā kāyañceva pīṇetuṃ brūhetuṃ, na ca pāpakammaṃ kātuṃ, puññañca paṭipadaṃ paṭipajjitu’’nti.

448. “What do you think, Dhananjani? Who is the better, one who for the sake of his parents behaves contrary to the *Dhamma*, behaves unrighteously, or one who for the sake of his parents behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously?”

“Master Sariputta, the one who for the sake of his parents behaves contrary to the *Dhamma*, behaves unrighteously, is not the better; but the one who for the sake of his parents behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously, is the better.

The one who for the sake of unrighteous conduct and uneven conduct, behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously, is the better.”

“Dhananjani, there are other kinds of work, profitable and in accordance with the *Dhamma*, by means of which one can support one’s parents and at the same time both avoid doing evil and practise merit.

“What do you think, Dhananjani? Who is the better, one who for the sake of his wife and children behaves contrary to the *Dhamma*, behaves unrighteously, or one who for the sake of his wife and children behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously?”

“Master Sariputta, the one who for the sake of his wife and children behaves contrary to the *Dhamma*, behaves unrighteously, is not the better; but the one who for the sake of his wife and children behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously, is the better.

The one who for the sake of unrighteous conduct and uneven conduct, behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously, is the better.”

“Dhananjani, there are other kinds of work, profitable and in accordance with the *Dhamma*, by means of which one can support one’s wife and children and at the same time both avoid doing evil and practise merit.

“What do you think, Dhananjani? Who is the better, one who for the sake of his servants, workers and men behaves contrary to the *Dhamma*, behaves unrighteously, or one who for the sake of his servants, workers and men behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously?”

“Master Sariputta, the one who for the sake of his servants, workers and men behaves contrary to the *Dhamma*, behaves unrighteously, is not the better; but the one who for the sake of his servants, workers and men behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously, is the better.

The one who for the sake of unrighteous conduct and uneven conduct, behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously, is the better.”

“Dhananjani, there are other kinds of work, profitable and in accordance with the *Dhamma*, by means of which one can support one’s servants, workers and men and at the same time both avoid doing evil and practise merit.

“What do you think, Dhananjani? Who is the better, one who for the sake of his friends and companions behaves contrary to the *Dhamma*, behaves unrighteously, or one who for the sake of his friends and companions behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously?”

“Master Sariputta, the one who for the sake of his friends and companions behaves contrary to the *Dhamma*, behaves unrighteously, is not the better; but the one who for the sake of his friends and companions behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously, is the better.

The one who for the sake of unrighteous conduct and uneven conduct, behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously, is the better.”

“Dhananjani, there are other kinds of work, profitable and in accordance with the *Dhamma*, by means of which one can support one’s friends and companions and do what is proper for friends and companions, and at the same time both avoid doing evil and practise merit.

“What do you think, Dhananjani? Who is the better, one who for the sake of his relatives and blood relations behaves contrary to the *Dhamma*, behaves unrighteously, or one who for the sake of his relatives and blood relations behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously?”

“Master Sariputta, the one who for the sake of his relatives and blood relations behaves contrary to the *Dhamma*, behaves unrighteously, is not the better; but the one who for the sake of his relatives and blood relations behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously, is the better.

The one who for the sake of unrighteous conduct and uneven conduct, behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously, is the better.”

“Dhananjani, there are other kinds of work, profitable and in accordance with the *Dhamma*, by means of which one can support one’s relatives and blood relations and do what is proper for relatives and blood relations, and at the same time both avoid doing evil and practise merit.

“What do you think, Dhananjani? Who is the better, one who for the sake of his guests behaves contrary to the *Dhamma*, behaves unrighteously, or one who for the sake of his guests behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously?”

“Master Sariputta, the one who for the sake of his guests behaves contrary to the *Dhamma*, behaves unrighteously, is not the better; but the one who for the sake of his guests behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously, is the better.

The one who for the sake of unrighteous conduct and uneven conduct, behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously, is the better.”

“Dhananjani, there are other kinds of work, profitable and in accordance with the *Dhamma*, by means of which one can support one’s guests and do what is proper for guests, and at the same time both avoid doing evil and practise merit.

“What do you think, Dhananjani? Who is the better, one who for the sake of his deceased ancestors behaves contrary to the *Dhamma*, behaves unrighteously, or one who for the sake of his deceased ancestors behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously?”

“Master Sariputta, the one who for the sake of his deceased ancestors behaves contrary to the *Dhamma*, behaves unrighteously, is not the better; but the one who for the sake of his deceased ancestors behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously, is the better.

The one who for the sake of unrighteous conduct and uneven conduct, behaves according to the *Dhamma*, behaves righteously, is the better.”

“Dhananjani, there are other kinds of work, profitable and in accordance with the *Dhamma*, by means of which one can support one’s deceased ancestors and do what is proper for deceased ancestors, and at the same time both avoid doing evil and practise merit.
“What do you think, Dhananjani? Which is better – one who, for the sake of the gods, behaves unrighteously and improperly, or one who, for the sake of the gods, behaves righteously and properly?”

“Which is better?”

“Indeed, Master Sāriputta, the one who for the sake of the gods behaves unrighteously and improperly is not the better; and indeed, Master Sāriputta, the one who for the sake of the gods behaves according to the Dhamma and righteously, that is the better.

The one who behaves according to the *dharma* and equitably, is the better.”

“Dhananjani, there are other kinds of work, profitable and in accordance with the *dharma*, by means of which one can perform what is to be done for the gods, and at the same time both avoid doing evil and practice merit (*puṇya*).

“What do you think, Dhananjani? Which is better – one who, for the sake of the king, behaves unrighteously and improperly, or one who, for the sake of the king, behaves righteously and properly?”

“Indeed, Master Sāriputta, the one who for the sake of the king behaves unrighteously and improperly is not the better; and indeed, Master Sāriputta, the one who for the sake of the king behaves according to the *dharma* and equitably, that is the better.

The one who behaves according to the *dharma* and equitably, is the better.”

“Dhananjani, there are other kinds of work, profitable and in accordance with the *dharma*, by means of which one can perform what is to be done for the king, and at the same time both avoid doing evil and practice merit (*puṇya*).

“What do you think, Dhananjani? Which is better – one who, for the sake of refreshing and nourishing the body, behaves unrighteously and improperly, or one who, for the sake of refreshing and nourishing the body, behaves according to the *dharma* and properly?”

“Indeed, Master Sāriputta, the one who for the sake of refreshing and nourishing the body behaves unrighteously and improperly is not the better; and indeed, Master Sāriputta, the one who for the sake of refreshing and nourishing the body behaves according to the *dharma* and equitably, that is the better.

The one who behaves contrary to the *dharma* and unrighteously, the one who behaves according to the *dharma* and equitably, is the better.”

“Dhananjani, there are other kinds of work, profitable and in accordance with the *dharma*, by means of which one can refresh and nourish this body, and at the same time both avoid doing evil and practice merit (*puṇya*).”
commentary_pali:
448.Dhammacārīti dhammikasivavijjādikammakārī. Paṭikkamantīti osaranti parihāyanti. Abhikkamantīti abhisaranti vaḍḍhanti. Seyyoti varataraṃ. Hīneti nihīne lāmake. Kālaṅkato ca sāriputtāti idaṃ bhagavā ‘‘tatrassa gantvā desehī’’ti adhippāyena theramāha. Theropi taṃkhaṇaṃyeva gantvā mahābrahmuno dhammaṃ desesi, tato paṭṭhāya cātuppadikaṃ gāthaṃ kathentopi catusaccavimuttaṃ nāma na kathesīti.

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Dhanañjānisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
448. *Dhammacārī* means one who performs meritorious acts of Dharma such as sewing robes and dispensing knowledge.
*Paṭikkamantī* means they decline and diminish.
*Abhikkamantī* means they approach and increase.
*Seyyo* means superior.
*Hīne* means inferior and wretched.
"*Kālaṅkato ca sāriputtā*," the Bhagavān said to the elder with the intention, "Go there and teach."
The elder then went that very moment and taught the Dharma to Mahābrahmā, but from then on, even when reciting a verse of four lines, he did not speak of the Four Noble Truths and liberation.

The commentary on the *Dhanañjānisutta* is concluded.

mula_pali: 449. Atha kho dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo āyasmato sāriputtassa bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Atha kho dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo aparena samayena ābādhiko ahosi dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. Atha kho dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ehi tvaṃ, ambho purisa , yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandāhi – ‘dhanañjāni, bhante, brāhmaṇo ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’ti. Yena cāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena āyasmato sāriputtassa pāde sirasā vandāhi – ‘dhanañjāni, bhante, brāhmaṇo ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So āyasmato sāriputtassa pāde sirasā vandatī’ti. Evañca vadehi – ‘sādhu kira, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto yena dhanañjānissa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṃ upādāyā’’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ , bhante’’ti kho so puriso dhanañjānissa brāhmaṇassa paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so puriso bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘dhanañjāni, bhante, brāhmaṇo ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’’ti. Yena cāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so puriso āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘dhanañjāni, bhante, brāhmaṇo ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So āyasmato sāriputtassa pāde sirasā vandati, evañca vadeti – ‘sādhu kira, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto yena dhanañjānissa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṃ upādāyā’’’ti. Adhivāsesi kho āyasmā sāriputto tuṇhībhāvena.
mula_english:
Then, the brahmin Dhanañjāni, having delighted and rejoiced in the venerable Sāriputta’s words, rose from his seat and departed.

On a later occasion, the brahmin Dhanañjāni became afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill.

Then the brahmin Dhanañjāni told a man: “Come, good man, go to the Blessed One (bhagavā), pay homage in my name with your head at his feet, and say: ‘Venerable sir (bhante), the brahmin Dhanañjāni is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill; he pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet.’

Then go to the venerable Sāriputta, pay homage in my name with your head at his feet, and say: ‘Venerable sir (bhante), the brahmin Dhanañjāni is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill; he pays homage with his head at the venerable Sāriputta’s feet.’

Then say thus: ‘It would be good, venerable sir (bhante), if the venerable Sāriputta would come to the residence (nivesanaṃ) of the brahmin Dhanañjāni, out of compassion (anukampaṃ) .’“

“Yes, venerable sir (bhante),” the man replied, and he went to the Blessed One (bhagavā), and after paying homage to the Blessed One, he sat down at one side.

As he was sitting there he said, “Venerable sir (bhante), the brahmin Dhanañjāni is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill; he pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet.”

Then he went to the venerable Sāriputta and after paying homage to the venerable Sāriputta, he sat down at one side.

As he was sitting there he said, “Venerable sir (bhante), the brahmin Dhanañjāni is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill; he pays homage with his head at the venerable Sāriputta’s feet.” Then he said, “It would be good, venerable sir (bhante), if the venerable Sāriputta would come to the residence (nivesanaṃ) of the brahmin Dhanañjāni, out of compassion (anukampaṃ).”

The Venerable Sāriputta consented by silence (tuṇhībhāvena).

mula_pali: 450. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena dhanañjānissa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho āyasmā sāriputto dhanañjāniṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘kacci te, dhanañjāni, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ? Kacci dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti, no abhikkamanti? Paṭikkamosānaṃ paññāyati , no abhikkamo’’ti? ‘‘Na me, bho sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti. Abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi, bho sāriputta , balavā puriso tiṇhena sikharena muddhani muddhānaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) abhimattheyya; evameva kho , bho sāriputta, adhimattā vātā muddhani ca ūhananti. Na me, bho sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ, na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti. Abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi, bho sāriputta, balavā puriso daḷhena varattakkhaṇḍena varattabandhanena (sī. pī.) sīse sīsaveṭhaṃ dadeyya; evameva kho, bho sāriputta, adhimattā sīse sīsavedanā. Na me, bho sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti. Abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi, bho sāriputta, dakkho goghātako vā goghātakantevāsī vā tiṇhena govikantanena kucchiṃ parikanteyya; evameva kho, bho sāriputta, adhimattā vātā kucchiṃ parikantanti. Na me, bho sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ, na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti. Abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo. Seyyathāpi, bho sāriputta, dve balavanto purisā dubbalataraṃ purisaṃ nānābāhāsu gahetvā aṅgārakāsuyā santāpeyyuṃ samparitāpeyyuṃ; evameva kho, bho sāriputta, adhimatto kāyasmiṃ ḍāho. Na me, bho sāriputta, khamanīyaṃ na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti. Abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati , no paṭikkamo’’ti.
mula_english:
Then the venerable **Śāriputra**, having dressed, taken his bowl and outer robe, went to the residence of the brahmin **Dhanañjāni**, and sat down on the prepared seat.

Seated, the venerable **Śāriputra** said this to the brahmin **Dhanañjāni**: "Are you getting better, **Dhanañjāni**? Are you comfortable? Are your painful feelings subsiding, and not increasing? Is their subsiding apparent, and not their increasing?"

"Master **Śāriputra**, I am not getting well, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are greatly increasing, not decreasing. Their increase is apparent, not their decrease. Just as if a strong man were rubbing my head with a sharp potsherd, so too, Master **Śāriputra**, violent winds are pounding in my head. I am not getting well, Master **Śāriputra**, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are greatly increasing, not decreasing. Their increase is apparent, not their decrease. Just as if a strong man were tightening a tough leather strap around my head as a headband, so too, Master **Śāriputra**, there are violent pains in my head. I am not getting well, Master **Śāriputra**, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are greatly increasing, not decreasing. Their increase is apparent, not their decrease. Just as if a skilled butcher or his apprentice were to carve up an ox’s belly with a sharp butcher’s knife, so too, Master **Śāriputra**, violent winds are carving up my belly. I am not getting well, Master **Śāriputra**, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are greatly increasing, not decreasing. Their increase is apparent, not their decrease. Just as if two strong men were to seize a weaker man by both arms and roast him over a pit of hot coals, so too, Master **Śāriputra**, there is a violent burning in my body. I am not getting well, Master **Śāriputra**, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are greatly increasing, not decreasing. Their increase is apparent, not their decrease."

mula_pali:
451. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, katamaṃ seyyo – nirayo vā tiracchānayoni vā’’ti? ‘‘Nirayā, bho sāriputta, tiracchānayoni seyyo’’ti. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, katamaṃ seyyo – tiracchānayoni vā pettivisayo vā’’ti? ‘‘Tiracchānayoniyā, bho sāriputta, pettivisayo seyyo’’ti. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, katamaṃ seyyo – pettivisayo vā manussā vā’’ti? ‘‘Pettivisayā, bho sāriputta, manussā seyyo’’ti. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni , katamaṃ seyyo – manussā vā cātumahārājikā cātummahārājikā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) vā devā’’ti? ‘‘Manussehi , bho sāriputta, cātumahārājikā devā seyyo’’ti. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, katamaṃ seyyo – cātumahārājikā vā devā tāvatiṃsā vā devā’’ti? ‘‘Cātumahārājikehi, bho sāriputta, devehi tāvatiṃsā devā seyyo’’ti. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, katamaṃ seyyo – tāvatiṃsā vā devā yāmā vā devā’’ti? ‘‘Tāvatiṃsehi, bho sāriputta, devehi yāmā devā seyyo’’ti. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, katamaṃ seyyo – yāmā vā devā tusitā vā devā’’ti? ‘‘Yāmehi, bho sāriputta, devehi tusitā devā seyyo’’ti. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, katamaṃ seyyo – tusitā vā devā nimmānaratī vā devā’’ti? ‘‘Tusitehi, bho sāriputta, devehi nimmānaratī devā seyyo’’ti. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, katamaṃ seyyo – nimmānaratī vā devā paranimmitavasavattī vā devā’’ti? ‘‘Nimmānaratīhi , bho sāriputta, devehi paranimmitavasavattī devā seyyo’’ti. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, dhanañjāni, katamaṃ seyyo paranimmitavasavattī vā devā brahmaloko vā’’ti? ‘‘‘Brahmaloko’ti bhavaṃ sāriputto āhāti, katamaṃ sāriputto āha brahmalokoti. (ka.) – bhavaṃ sāriputto āha; ‘brahmaloko’ti – bhavaṃ sāriputto āhā’’ti bhavaṃ sāriputto āhāti, katamaṃ sāriputto āha brahmalokoti. (ka.).

Atha kho āyasmato sāriputtassa etadahosi – ‘‘ime kho brāhmaṇā brahmalokādhimuttā. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ dhanañjānissa brāhmaṇassa brahmānaṃ sahabyatāya maggaṃ deseyya’’nti. ‘‘Brahmānaṃ te, dhanañjāni, sahabyatāya maggaṃ desessāmi; taṃ suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bho’’ti kho dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosi. Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca – ‘‘katamo ca, dhanañjāni, brahmānaṃ sahabyatāya maggo? Idha, dhanañjāni, bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ; iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharati. Ayaṃ kho, dhanañjāni, brahmānaṃ sahabyatāya maggo’’.
mula_english:
451. “What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—hell or the animal realm?” “Hell, Venerable Sāriputta, the animal realm is better.”
“What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—the animal realm or the realm of ghosts?” “Compared to the animal realm, Venerable Sāriputta, the realm of ghosts is better.”
“What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—the realm of ghosts or human beings?” “Compared to the realm of ghosts, Venerable Sāriputta, human beings are better.”
“What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—human beings or the gods of the heaven of the Four Great Kings (Cātumahārājika)?” “Compared to human beings, Venerable Sāriputta, the gods of the heaven of the Four Great Kings are better.”
“What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—the gods of the heaven of the Four Great Kings or the gods of the heaven of the Thirty-three (Tāvatiṃsa)?” “Compared to the gods of the heaven of the Four Great Kings, Venerable Sāriputta, the gods of the heaven of the Thirty-three are better.”
“What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—the gods of the heaven of the Thirty-three or the Yama gods?” “Compared to the gods of the heaven of the Thirty-three, Venerable Sāriputta, the Yama gods are better.”
“What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—the Yama gods or the gods of the Tusita heaven?” “Compared to the Yama gods, Venerable Sāriputta, the gods of the Tusita heaven are better.”
“What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—the gods of the Tusita heaven or the gods who delight in creating (Nirmāṇaratī)?” “Compared to the gods of the Tusita heaven, Venerable Sāriputta, the gods who delight in creating are better.”
“What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—the gods who delight in creating or the gods who wield power over others’ creations (Paranimmitavasavattī)?” “Compared to the gods who delight in creating, Venerable Sāriputta, the gods who wield power over others’ creations are better.”
“What do you think, Dhanañjāni, which is better—the gods who wield power over others’ creations or the Brahmā world (Brahmaloka)?” “'The Brahmā world,' Venerable Sāriputta said; 'The Brahmā world,' Venerable Sāriputta said.”

Then the venerable Sāriputta thought: “These Brahmins are devoted to the Brahmā-world (Brahmaloka). Suppose I show the Brahmin Dhanañjāni the path to the company of Brahmā (Brahmā).”
“Dhanañjāni, I shall show you the path to the company of Brahmā (Brahmā); listen and carefully attend to what I shall say.”
“Yes, sir,” replied the Brahmin Dhanañjāni to the venerable Sāriputta.
The venerable Sāriputta said this: “And what, Dhanañjāni, is the path to the company of Brahmā (Brahmā)? Here, Dhanañjāni, a *bhikkhu* abides pervading one direction with a mind imbued with loving-kindness (*mettā*), likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth; so above, below, around, and everywhere, and to all as to himself, he abides pervading the all-encompassing world with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility and without ill will.
This, Dhanañjāni, is the path to the company of Brahmā (Brahmā).”

mula_pali: 452. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, dhanañjāni, bhikkhu karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ; iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharati. Ayaṃ kho, dhanañjāni, brahmānaṃ sahabyatāya maggo’’ti. Tena hi, bho sāriputta, mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandāhi – ‘dhanañjāni , bhante, brāhmaṇo ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’ti. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto dhanañjāniṃ brāhmaṇaṃ sati uttarikaraṇīye hīne brahmaloke patiṭṭhāpetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Atha kho dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo acirapakkante āyasmante sāriputte kālamakāsi, brahmalokañca upapajji.
mula_english:
“Again, Dhanañjāni, a *bhikkhu* abides pervading one quarter with a mind imbued with compassion (*karuṇāsahagatena cetasā*)…pe… with a mind imbued with appreciative joy (*muditāsahagatena cetasā*)… with a mind imbued with equanimity (*upekkhāsahagatena cetasā*), likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth; so above, below, around, and everywhere, and to all as to himself, he abides pervading the all-encompassing world with a mind imbued with equanimity, abundant, exalted (*mahaggatena*), immeasurable (*appamāṇena*), without hostility (*averena*) and without ill will (*abyābajjhena*).

This, Dhanañjāni, is the way (*maggo*) to union with Brahmā (*brahmānaṃ sahabyatāya*’ti).

“Well then, venerable Sāriputta (*bho sāriputta*), would you please pay homage with your head at the Blessed One's (*bhagavato pāde sirasā vandāhi*) feet in my name and say, ‘Dhanañjāni, venerable sir (*bhante*), the *brāhmaṇa* is afflicted (*ābādhiko*), suffering (*dukkhito*), and very sick (*bāḷhagilāno*). He pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet (*so bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’ti*.’"

Then the venerable Sāriputta (*āyasmā sāriputto*), having established the *brāhmaṇa* Dhanañjāni in the inferior Brahma-world (*hīne brahmaloke*), rose from his seat (*uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi*) and departed.

Soon after the venerable Sāriputta had left, the *brāhmaṇa* Dhanañjāni died (*kālamakāsi*) and reappeared in the Brahma-world (*brahmalokañca upapajji*).

mula_pali:
453. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘eso, bhikkhave, sāriputto dhanañjāniṃ brāhmaṇaṃ sati uttarikaraṇīye hīne brahmaloke patiṭṭhāpetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkanto’’ti. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi, ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘dhanañjāni, bhante, brāhmaṇo ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno, so bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’’ti. ‘‘Kiṃ pana tvaṃ sāriputta dhanañjāniṃ brāhmaṇaṃ sati uttarikaraṇīye hīne brahmaloke patiṭṭhāpetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkanto’’ti? ‘‘Mayhaṃ kho, bhante, evaṃ ahosi – ‘ime kho brāhmaṇā brahmalokādhimuttā, yaṃnūnāhaṃ dhanañjānissa brāhmaṇassa brahmānaṃ sahabyatāya maggaṃ deseyya’nti. ‘‘Kālaṅkatoca kālaṅkatova (syā. kaṃ. ka.), sāriputta, dhanañjāni brāhmaṇo, brahmalokañca upapanno’’ti.

Dhanañjānisuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.
mula_english:
Then the Blessed One addressed the *bhikkhus* thus: "Bhikkhus, Sāriputta, having established the *brāhmaṇa* Dhananjani in the inferior Brahma-world, rose from his seat and departed while there was still more to be done."

Then the venerable Sāriputta went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side and said: "Venerable sir, the *brāhmaṇa* Dhananjani is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill; he pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet."

"But, Sāriputta, did you establish the *brāhmaṇa* Dhananjani in the inferior Brahma-world when there was still more to be done, [and then rise from your seat and depart]?" "Venerable sir, I thought thus: ‘These *brāhmaṇas* are devoted to the Brahma-world. Suppose I show the *brāhmaṇa* Dhananjani the path to the company of Brahmā.’"

"Sāriputta, the *brāhmaṇa* Dhananjani has died and has reappeared in the Brahma-world."

The Dhananjāni Sutta, the seventh, is finished.

mula_pali: 454. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā icchānaṅgale icchānaṅkale (sī. pī.) viharati icchānaṅgalavanasaṇḍe. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā abhiññātā abhiññātā brāhmaṇamahāsālā icchānaṅgale paṭivasanti, seyyathidaṃ – caṅkī brāhmaṇo, tārukkho brāhmaṇo, pokkharasāti brāhmaṇo, jāṇussoṇi jāṇussoṇī (pī.), jāṇusoṇī (ka.) brāhmaṇo, todeyyo brāhmaṇo, aññe ca abhiññātā abhiññātā brāhmaṇamahāsālā. Atha kho vāseṭṭhabhāradvājānaṃ māṇavānaṃ jaṅghāvihāraṃ anucaṅkamantānaṃ anuvicarantānaṃ anucaṅkamamānānaṃ anuvicaramānānaṃ (sī. pī.) ayamantarākathā udapādi – ‘‘kathaṃ, bho, brāhmaṇo hotī’’ti? Bhāradvājo māṇavo evamāha – ‘‘yato kho, bho, ubhato sujāto mātito ca pitito ca saṃsuddhagahaṇiko yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā akkhitto anupakkuṭṭho jātivādena – ettāvatā kho, bho, brāhmaṇo hotī’’ti. Vāseṭṭho māṇavo evamāha – ‘‘yato kho, bho, sīlavā ca hoti vattasampanno vatasampanno (pī.) ca – ettāvatā kho, bho, brāhmaṇo hotī’’ti. Neva kho asakkhi bhāradvājo māṇavo vāseṭṭhaṃ māṇavaṃ saññāpetuṃ, na pana asakkhi vāseṭṭho māṇavo bhāradvājaṃ māṇavaṃ saññāpetuṃ. Atha kho vāseṭṭho māṇavo bhāradvājaṃ māṇavaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ayaṃ kho, bho bhāradvāja, samaṇo gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito icchānaṅgale viharati icchānaṅgalavanasaṇḍe. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. Āyāma, bho bhāradvāja, yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkamissāma; upasaṅkamitvā samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ etamatthaṃ pucchissāma. Yathā no samaṇo gotamo byākarissati tathā naṃ dhāressāmā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bho’’ti kho bhāradvājo māṇavo vāseṭṭhassa māṇavassa paccassosi.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling near Icchānaṅgala in the Icchānaṅgala jungle thicket.

Now on that occasion a number of well-known, well-to-do *brāhmaṇas* were staying at Icchānaṅgala, that is, the *brāhmaṇa* Caṅki, the *brāhmaṇa* Tārukkha, the *brāhmaṇa* Pokkharasāti, the *brāhmaṇa* Jāṇussoṇi, the *brāhmaṇa* Todeyya, and other well-known, well-to-do *brāhmaṇas*.

Then, while the students Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja were walking and wandering for exercise, this discussion arose between them: "How, sir, does one become a *brāhmaṇa*?" The student Bhāradvāja said: "When one is well-born on both sides, of pure maternal and paternal descent seven generations back, unassailable and impeccable in respect of birth, then, sir, one is a *brāhmaṇa*."

The student Vāseṭṭha said: "When one is virtuous and fulfills the observances, then, sir, one is a *brāhmaṇa*."

But the *brāhmaṇa* student Bhāradvāja could not convince the *brāhmaṇa* student Vāseṭṭha, nor could the *brāhmaṇa* student Vāseṭṭha convince the *brāhmaṇa* student Bhāradvāja.

Then the student Vāseṭṭha addressed the student Bhāradvāja: “Sir, the *śramaṇa* Gotama, the son of the Śākyans, who went forth from a Śākyan clan, is living at Icchānaṅgala, in the wood near Icchānaṅgala.

Now a good report of Master Gotama has been spread to this effect: ‘That Blessed One is an Arhat, a fully-enlightened Buddha (*sammāsambuddha*), perfected in knowledge (*vijjā*) and conduct (*caraṇa*), a Well-Farer (*sugata*), Knower of the worlds (*lokavidū*), unequalled Trainer of men to be tamed (*purisadammasārathi*), Teacher (*satthā*) of gods (*deva*) and humans (*manussa*), a Buddha, a Blessed Lord (*bhagavā*)’.”

Come, Bhāradvāja, let us go to the *śramaṇa* Gotama and ask him about this matter.

As the *śramaṇa* Gotama will explain it to us, so we will remember it."

"Just so, dear friend," the student Bhāradvāja replied to the student Vāseṭṭha.
commentary_pali: 454.Evaṃme sutanti vāseṭṭhasuttaṃ. Tattha icchānaṅgalavanasaṇḍeti icchānaṅgalagāmassa avidūre vanasaṇḍe. Caṅkīti ādayo pañcapi janā rañño pasenadissa kosalassa purohitā eva. Aññe ca abhiññātāti aññe ca bahū abhiññātā brāhmaṇā. Te kira chaṭṭhe chaṭṭhe māse dvīsu ṭhānesu sannipatanti. Yadā jātiṃ sodhetukāmā honti, tadā pokkharasātissa santike jātisodhanatthaṃ ukkaṭṭhāya sannipatanti. Yadā mante sodhetukāmā honti, tadā icchānaṅgale sannipatanti. Imasmiṃ kāle mantasodhanatthaṃ sannipatiṃsu. Ayamantarā kathāti yaṃ attano sahāyakabhāvānurūpaṃ kathaṃ kathentā anuvicariṃsu, tassā kathāya antarā ayamaññā kathā udapādi. Sīlavāti guṇavā. Vattasampannoti ācārasampanno.
commentary_english:
454. Thus have I heard (evaṃ me suta), namely, the Vāseṭṭha Sutta.

There, "in the Icchānaṅgala grove" (icchānaṅgalavanasaṇḍe) means in a grove not far from the village of Icchānaṅgala.

Caṅkī and the others, even five people, were the family priests (purohita) of King Pasenadi Kosala.

"Other well-known (brāhmins)" (aññe ca abhiññātā) means many other well-known *brāhmaṇas* (brāhmaṇā).

It seems every six months (chaṭṭhe chaṭṭhe māse) they would assemble in two places (dvīsu ṭhānesu sannipatanti).

When they want to purify their lineage (jātiṃ sodhetukāmā honti), then they assemble near Pokkharasāti for the purpose of purifying the lineage (jātisodhanatthaṃ) at Ukkaṭṭhā.

When they want to purify the *mantras* (mante sodhetukāmā honti), then they assemble in Icchānaṅgala (icchānaṅgale sannipatanti).

At this time (imasmiṃ kāle) they had assembled for the purpose of completely purifying the mantras (mantasodhanatthaṃ sannipatiṃsu).

"This intervening talk" (ayamantarā kathā) means the talk they were going on with, relating it to their friendly relationship; in between that talk (kathāya antarā) there arose another talk (ayam aññā kathā udapādi).

"Virtuous" (*śīlavā*) means possessed of good qualities (guṇavā).

"Accomplished in conduct" (vattasampanno) means accomplished in behavior (*ācārasampanno*).

455. Atha kho vāseṭṭhabhāradvājā māṇavā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vāseṭṭho māṇavo bhagavantaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

‘‘Anuññātapaṭiññātā, tevijjā mayamasmubho;

Ahaṃ pokkharasātissa, tārukkhassāyaṃ māṇavo.

mula_english:
Then Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja, the students, went to the Blessed One; having gone, they exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. After exchanging courteous greetings and an amiable talk, they sat down on one side.

While seated on one side, the student Vāseṭṭha addressed the Blessed One in verses:

“We are both known as acknowledged experts in the three Vedas ( *tevijja* );

I am [a student] of Pokkharasāti, and this student is of Tārukkha."

“Among those skilled in the three Vedas, we are known as the foremost;

versed in the [Vedic] texts, skilled in grammar, disciples like our teachers;

We have a dispute, Gotama, regarding the doctrine of caste (*jāti*).

Bhāradvāja declares that a *brāhmaṇa* is [such] by birth (*jāti*),

while I say [he is such] by deeds (*kamma*). Know this, O clear-sighted one.

We are unable to convince each other, both of us;

We have come to ask you, who are known as the enlightened one ( *sambuddha* ).

Just as people, after [the moon] has passed beyond the clouds, with joined palms,

worship and pay homage to Gotama in the world,

We ask you, Gotama, the eye arisen in the world:

Is a *brāhmaṇa* [such] by birth (*jāti*), or does he become [such] by deeds (*kamma*)?

Explain it to us who do not know, so that we may understand a *brāhmaṇa*.”

“Then I will explain to you, Vāseṭṭha,” said the Blessed One,

“in due order, as it really is;

the classification of beings according to their different births (*jāti*).

Know that even in the case of grasses and trees, [though] they are not aware,

there is a mark of their species (*jāti*): their species are different.

Then, among insects and moths, as far as ants,

there is a mark of their species (*jāti*): their species are different.

Know that even among quadrupeds, both small and large,

there is a mark of their species (*jāti*): their species are different.

Know that even among those that move on their chests, snakes with long backs,

there is a mark of their species (*jāti*): their species are different."
Then know that fish, too, in water have their dwelling;
Their birth is their distinctive mark; For many are the kinds of birth.

Then know that birds, too, moving in the sky, have their flight;
Their birth is their distinctive mark; For many are the kinds of birth.

Just as among these births, their birth is their distinctive mark;
Even so among humans, there is no distinctive mark based on birth.

Not in the hairs, nor in the head, nor in the ears, nor in the eyes;
Nor in the mouth, nor in the nose, nor in the lips, nor the brows.

Nor in the shoulders or the neck Nor in the belly or the back;
Nor in the buttocks nor in the breast, nor in private parts nor in sexual intercourse.

Nor with the hands, nor with the feet, nor with fingers, nor with nails;
Nor with the shanks, nor with the thighs, nor with colour, nor with voice;
Their birth is not their distinctive mark, as it is in other births.

Moreover, in bodies, this is not found among humans;
And vocations among humans are designated by convention.

Whoever among humans makes a living by cattle-breeding;
Thus, Vāseṭṭha, know that he is a farmer, not a *brāhmaṇa*.

Whoever among humans lives by various crafts;
Thus, Vāseṭṭha, know that he is a craftsman, not a *brāhmaṇa*.

Whoever among humans makes a living by trade;
Thus, Vāseṭṭha, know that he is a merchant, not a *brāhmaṇa*.

Whoever among humans makes a living by serving others;
Thus, Vāseṭṭha, know that he is a servant, not a *brāhmaṇa*.

Whoever among humans makes a living by taking what is not given;
Thus, Vāseṭṭha, know that he is a thief, not a *brāhmaṇa*.

Whoever among humans makes a living by archery;
Thus, Vāseṭṭha, know that he is a soldier, not a *brāhmaṇa*.

Whoever among humans makes a living as a chaplain;
Thus, Vāseṭṭha, know that he is a priest, not a *brāhmaṇa*.

Whoever among humans enjoys a village and a kingdom;
Thus, Vāseṭṭha, know that he is a king, not a *brāhmaṇa*.

I do not call a *brāhmaṇa* one born from a womb;
kaṃ.
)</note> His name it would be, if he were acquisitive.

bhovādī (syā.
kaṃ.
)</note>
But the one who has nothing, who takes nothing: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

458
Having cut all fetters, he trembles not;

Who has overcome all ties, detached: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

Having cut the thong, the strap, the rope, together with its appurtenances,

Whose shaft is lifted, the awakened one: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

Though reviled, abused, and bound, he patiently endures, not angered;

Patience is his strength, an army his might: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

He is without anger, is dutiful, virtuous, free from craving,

Subdued, bearing his final body: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

Like water on a lotus leaf, a mustard seed on the tip of an awl,

He who clings not to sensual pleasures: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

He who knows, even here, the end of his suffering,

With burden lowered, and detached: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

With wisdom deep, intelligent, skilled in discerning the right and wrong path,

And has attained the goal supreme: Him do I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

Unassociated is he with householders and likewise with the homeless;

And wanders about with no fixed abode and but few wants — him do I call a holy man.

Having renounced the rod for beings trembling or firm,

Who neither harms nor causes to harm: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

He is not hostile among the hostile, is calm among those who wield the rod,

He clings not among those who cling: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

Whose passion, hatred, pride, and envy are shed,

Like a mustard seed from the point of an awl: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

459
Gentle, instructive, truthful is his speech;

Which does not damage anyone: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

He who takes nothing in the world that is not given, be it long or short, small or large, good or bad:

Him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

He who wants nothing of either this world or the next,

Who lives unyearning and detached: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.
He in whom no cravings are found, who is free from perplexity through understanding, has attained the Deathless Sphere: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

He who has transcended both merit and demerit, who is free from sorrow, stainless, and pure: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

Like the moon, stainless, pure, serene, and clear, with craving and being both destroyed: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

He who has passed beyond this treacherous, difficult path, this wandering, this delusion, who has crossed over, gone beyond, is meditative, unperturbed, and free from doubt, who, without clinging, has attained *nirvāṇa*: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

He who has slain sensual pleasures, and wanders without a home, with craving for sensual existence destroyed: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

He who has slain craving, and wanders without a home, with craving for existence destroyed: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

He who has abandoned human attachment, and has transcended divine attachment, detached from all bonds everywhere: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

He who has abandoned both delight and aversion, is cool, without defilements, the hero who has overcome the whole world: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

He who knows the passing away and rebirth of beings, and is unattached, the Well-gone One, awakened in every way: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

He whose destiny is unknown to gods, spirits, and humans, the one with eradicated influxes, a worthy one: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

He in whom there is nothing at all, before, after, or in the middle, who has nothing and is unattached: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*. (akiñcanaṃ anādānaṃ, tamahaṃ brūmi brāhmaṇaṃ)

The bull, the excellent, the hero, the great seer, the conqueror, unwavering, bathed, awakened: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

He who knows his former dwelling, and sees heaven and woe, and has attained the destruction of birth: him I call a *brāhmaṇa*.

These designations, name and lineage, are assigned in the world, conventionally arisen, assigned here and there.

Those who do not know, given to slumber for a long time, ignorant of what is right, declare: ‘One is a *brāhmaṇa* by birth.’

Not by birth is one a *brāhmaṇa*, not by birth is one a non-*brāhmaṇa*.

The farmer is such through action, the artisan is such through action;

The merchant is such through action, the messenger is such through action.

The thief is such through action, the soldier is such through action;

The sacrificer is such through action, the king is also such through action.

Thus, as it really is, the wise see action;

Beings are bound by action, like a chariot wheel that moves.
