commentary_pali:
455.Anuññātapaṭiññātāti sikkhitā tumheti evaṃ ācariyehi anuññātā, āma ācariya sikkhitamhāti evaṃ sayañca paṭiññātā. Asmāti bhavāma. Ahaṃ pokkharasātissa, tārukkhassāyaṃ māṇavoti ahaṃ pokkharasātissa jeṭṭhantevāsī aggasisso, ayaṃ tārukkhassāti dīpeti.

Tevijjānanti tivedānaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ. Yadakkhātanti yaṃ atthato ca byañjanato ca ekaṃ padampi akkhātaṃ. Tatra kevalinosmaseti taṃ sakalaṃ jānanato tattha niṭṭhāgatamhāti attho. Idāni taṃ kevalibhāvaṃ āvikaronto padakasmātiādimāha. Tattha jappe ācariyasādisāti kathanaṭṭhāne mayaṃ ācariyasadisāyeva.

Tevijjāna Yadakkhāta Tatra kevalinosmase padakasmā jappe ācariyasādisā

Kammunāti dasakusalakammapathakammunā. Ayañhi pubbe sattavidhaṃ kāyavacīkammaṃ sandhāya ‘‘yato kho, bho, sīlavā hotī’’ti āha, tividhaṃ manokammaṃ sandhāya ‘‘vattasampanno’’ti. Tena samannāgato hi ācārasampanno hoti. Cakkhumāti pañcahi cakkhūhi cakkhumantabhāvena bhagavantaṃ ālapati.

Kammunā Cakkhumā

Khayātītanti ūnabhāvaṃ atītaṃ, paripuṇṇanti attho. Peccāti upagantvā. Namassantīti namo karonti.

Khayātīta Peccā Namassantī

Cakkhuṃ loke samuppannanti avijjandhakāre loke taṃ andhakāraṃ vidhamitvā lokassa diṭṭhadhammikādiatthadassanena cakkhu hutvā samuppannaṃ.

Cakkhuṃ loke samuppanna
commentary_english:
455. *Anuññātapaṭiññātā* means: "Trained by you, having been thus permitted by the teachers, and having self-acknowledged, 'Yes, I am trained, teacher.'" *Asmā* means: "We are." *Ahaṃ pokkharasātissa, tārukkhassāyaṃ māṇavo* means: "I am Pokkharasāti's senior pupil and foremost student; this is Tārukkha," thus he indicates.

*Tevijjāna* means: "Of the three Vedas, of the Brahmins." *Yadakkhāta* means: "Whatever even one word has been declared, in meaning and in expression." *Tatra kevalinosmase* means: "In knowing that entire [Veda], we are consummate in it," is the meaning. Now, revealing that consummation, he says beginning with *padakasmā*. There, *jappe ācariyasādisā* means: "In speaking, we are just like the teachers."

*Kammunā* means: "According to deeds," according to the ten wholesome courses of action (*dasa-kusala-kammapatha*). For earlier, referring to the seven kinds of bodily and verbal action, he said, "Because, good sir, he is virtuous," and referring to the three kinds of mental action, "accomplished in observances." For, being endowed with that, he is accomplished in conduct (*ācārasampanno*). *Cakkhumā* means: He addresses the Blessed One with the quality of being endowed with the five eyes (*pañcacakkhū*).

*Khayātīta* means: "Having transcended the state of deficiency, it is full," is the meaning. *Peccā* means: "Having approached." *Namassantī* means: "They do homage" (*namo* *karonti*).

*Cakkhuṃ loke samuppanna* means: "The eye (*cakṣus*) arose in the world of the darkness of ignorance (*avidyā*), having dispelled that darkness, having become the eye (*cakṣus*) for the world by showing the benefit of visible Dharma etc."

mula_pali:
461. Evaṃ vutte, vāseṭṭhabhāradvājā māṇavā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama! Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti – evamevaṃ bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Ete mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāma dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsake no bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gate’’ti.

Vāseṭṭhasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.
mula_english:
461. Thus, when this was said, the youths Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable Gotama, excellent! Just as, venerable Gotama, one might set upright what has been overturned, or uncover what is concealed, or show the way to one who is lost, or hold up a lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes may see forms, in the same way the Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by venerable Gotama.

We go to venerable Gotama for refuge, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of monks.

From today, may venerable Gotama remember us as lay followers who have gone to him for refuge for life.”

The Vāseṭṭha Sutta, the eighth, is finished.

mula_pali: 462. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena subho māṇavo todeyyaputto sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasati aññatarassa gahapatissa nivesane kenacideva karaṇīyena. Atha kho subho māṇavo todeyyaputto yassa gahapatissa nivesane paṭivasati taṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sutaṃ metaṃ, gahapati – ‘avivittā sāvatthī arahantehī’ti. Kaṃ nu khvajja samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā payirupāseyyāmā’’ti? ‘‘Ayaṃ, bhante, bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Taṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ payirupāsassū’’ti. Atha kho subho māṇavo todeyyaputto tassa gahapatissa paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho subho māṇavo todeyyaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘brāhmaṇā, bho gotama, evamāhaṃsu – ‘gahaṭṭho ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ, na pabbajito ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusala’nti. Idha bhavaṃ gotamo kimāhā’’ti?
mula_english:
Thus have I heard:

Once the Blessed One (bhagavā) was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapindika’s Park (jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme).

At that time, Subha, the student of Todeyya, was residing at the house of a certain householder in Sāvatthī for some particular reason.

Then Subha, the student of Todeyya, said to that householder in whose residence he was staying: “Householder, I have heard it said that Sāvatthī is not devoid of *arhats* (arahantehī).”

“Which *śramaṇa* (samaṇaṃ) or *brāhmaṇa* (brāhmaṇaṃ) should we visit today?”

“Venerable sir (*bhante*), the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) is staying in Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapindika’s Park.

Venerable sir (*bhante*), you should visit that Blessed One (*bhagavantam*).”

Then Subha, the student of Todeyya, assented to that householder and went to where the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) was; having gone there, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One (*bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi*).

Having concluded their conversation of courteous greetings, he sat down at one side (ekamantaṃ nisīdi).

Seated to one side (ekamantaṃ nisinno), Subha, the student of Todeyya, said this to the Blessed One (*bhagavantaṃ etadavoca*): “Brahmins (*brāhmaṇā*), Master Gotama (*bho gotama*), say thus: ‘The householder (*gahaṭṭho*) is one who accomplishes the true way (*ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ*), the *dharma*, that is wholesome; the renunciate (*pabbajito*) is not one who accomplishes the true way, the *dharma*, that is wholesome.’”

“What does Master Gotama (*bhavaṃ gotamo kimāha*) say about this?”
commentary_pali: 462.Evaṃme sutanti subhasuttaṃ. Tattha todeyyaputtoti tudigāmavāsino todeyyabrāhmaṇassa putto. Ārādhako hotīti sampādako hoti paripūrako. Ñāyaṃ dhammanti kāraṇadhammaṃ. Kusalanti anavajjaṃ.
commentary_english: Thus have I heard: the Subha-sutta. There, *todeyyaputto* means the son of the Todeyya brahmin who lived in Tudigama. *ārādhako hoti* means he is the accomplisher, he is the perfecter. *ñāyaṃ dhamma* means the causal Dharma. *kusala* means faultless.

mula_pali:
463. ‘‘Vibhajjavādo kho ahamettha, māṇava; nāhamettha ekaṃsavādo. Gihissa vāhaṃ, māṇava, pabbajitassa vā micchāpaṭipattiṃ na vaṇṇemi. Gihī vā hi , māṇava, pabbajito vā micchāpaṭipanno micchāpaṭipattādhikaraṇahetu na ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ. Gihissa vāhaṃ, māṇava, pabbajitassa vā sammāpaṭipattiṃ vaṇṇemi. Gihī vā hi, māṇava, pabbajito vā sammāpaṭipanno sammāpaṭipattādhikaraṇahetu ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusala’’nti.

‘‘Brāhmaṇā, bho gotama, evamāhaṃsu – ‘mahaṭṭhamidaṃ mahākiccaṃ mahādhikaraṇaṃ mahāsamārambhaṃ gharāvāsakammaṭṭhānaṃ mahapphalaṃ hoti; appaṭṭhamidaṃ appakiccaṃ appādhikaraṇaṃ appasamārambhaṃ pabbajjā kammaṭṭhānaṃ appaphalaṃ hotī’ti. Idha bhavaṃ gotamo kimāhā’’ti.

‘‘Etthāpi kho ahaṃ, māṇava, vibhajjavādo; nāhamettha ekaṃsavādo. Atthi, māṇava, kammaṭṭhānaṃ mahaṭṭhaṃ mahākiccaṃ mahādhikaraṇaṃ mahāsamārambhaṃ vipajjamānaṃ appaphalaṃ hoti; atthi, māṇava, kammaṭṭhānaṃ mahaṭṭhaṃ mahākiccaṃ mahādhikaraṇaṃ mahāsamārambhaṃ sampajjamānaṃ mahapphalaṃ hoti; atthi, māṇava, kammaṭṭhānaṃ appaṭṭhaṃ appakiccaṃ appādhikaraṇaṃ appasamārambhaṃ vipajjamānaṃ appaphalaṃ hoti; atthi, māṇava, kammaṭṭhānaṃ appaṭṭhaṃ appakiccaṃ appādhikaraṇaṃ appasamārambhaṃ sampajjamānaṃ mahapphalaṃ hoti. Katamañca, māṇava , kammaṭṭhānaṃ mahaṭṭhaṃ mahākiccaṃ mahādhikaraṇaṃ mahāsamārambhaṃ vipajjamānaṃ appaphalaṃ hoti? Kasi kho, māṇava, kammaṭṭhānaṃ mahaṭṭhaṃ mahākiccaṃ mahādhikaraṇaṃ mahāsamārambhaṃ vipajjamānaṃ appaphalaṃ hoti. Katamañca, māṇava, kammaṭṭhānaṃ mahaṭṭhaṃ mahākiccaṃ mahādhikaraṇaṃ mahāsamārambhaṃ sampajjamānaṃ mahapphalaṃ hoti? Kasiyeva kho, māṇava, kammaṭṭhānaṃ mahaṭṭhaṃ mahākiccaṃ mahādhikaraṇaṃ mahāsamārambhaṃ sampajjamānaṃ mahapphalaṃ hoti. Katamañca, māṇava, kammaṭṭhānaṃ appaṭṭhaṃ appakiccaṃ appādhikaraṇaṃ appasamārambhaṃ vipajjamānaṃ appaphalaṃ hoti? Vaṇijjā kho, māṇava, kammaṭṭhānaṃ appaṭṭhaṃ appakiccaṃ appādhikaraṇaṃ appasamārambhaṃ vipajjamānaṃ appaphalaṃ hoti. Katamañca māṇava, kammaṭṭhānaṃ appaṭṭhaṃ appakiccaṃ appādhikaraṇaṃ appasamārambhaṃ sampajjamānaṃ mahapphalaṃ hoti? Vaṇijjāyeva kho, māṇava, kammaṭṭhānaṃ appaṭṭhaṃ appakiccaṃ appādhikaraṇaṃ appasamārambhaṃ sampajjamānaṃ mahapphalaṃ hoti.
mula_english:
463. “Here, student, I am one who speaks after making an analysis (vibhajjavādo); I do not speak one-sidedly (ekaṃsavādo).

I do not praise the wrong way of practice (micchāpaṭipatti) on the part either of a householder (gihissa) or one gone forth (pabbajitassa);

for whether it be a householder (gihī) or one gone forth (pabbajito), one who has entered on the wrong way of practice (micchāpaṭipanno), by reason of his wrong way of practice (micchāpaṭipattādhikaraṇahetu), is not accomplishing the true way, the Dhamma that is wholesome (kusalaṃ).

I praise the right way of practice (sammāpaṭipattiṃ) on the part either of a householder (gihissa) or one gone forth (pabbajitassa);

for whether it be a householder (gihī) or one gone forth (pabbajito), one who has entered on the right way of practice (sammāpaṭipanno), by reason of his right way of practice (sammāpaṭipattādhikaraṇahetu), is accomplishing the true way, the Dhamma that is wholesome.”

“Master Gotama, the *brāhmaṇas* (brāhmaṇā) say this: ‘Since the work of the household life (*gharāvāsakammaṭṭhānaṃ*) involves a great deal of activity (*mahaṭṭhaṃ*), great functions (*mahākiccaṃ*), great engagements (*mahādhikaraṇaṃ*), and great undertakings (*mahāsamārambhaṃ*), it is of great fruit (*mahapphalaṃ*). Since the work of those gone forth (*pabbajjā kammaṭṭhānaṃ*) involves a small amount of activity (*appaṭṭhaṃ*), small functions (*appakiccaṃ*), small engagements (*appādhikaraṇaṃ*), and small undertakings (*appasamārambhaṃ*), it is of small fruit (*appaphalaṃ*).’

What does Master Gotama say about that?”

“Here too, student, I am one who speaks after making an analysis (vibhajjavādo); I do not speak one-sidedly (ekaṃsavādo).

There is work (kammaṭṭhānaṃ) involving a great deal of activity (*mahaṭṭhaṃ*), great functions (*mahākiccaṃ*), great engagements (*mahādhikaraṇaṃ*), and great undertakings (*mahāsamārambhaṃ*), which, when it fails (vipajjamānaṃ), is of small fruit (appaphalaṃ). There is work (kammaṭṭhānaṃ) involving a great deal of activity (*mahaṭṭhaṃ*), great functions (*mahākiccaṃ*), great engagements (*mahādhikaraṇaṃ*), and great undertakings (*mahāsamārambhaṃ*), which, when it succeeds (sampajjamānaṃ), is of great fruit (mahapphalaṃ). There is work (kammaṭṭhānaṃ) involving a small amount of activity (*appaṭṭhaṃ*), small functions (*appakiccaṃ*), small engagements (*appādhikaraṇaṃ*), and small undertakings (*appasamārambhaṃ*), which, when it fails (vipajjamānaṃ), is of small fruit (appaphalaṃ). There is work (kammaṭṭhānaṃ) involving a small amount of activity (*appaṭṭhaṃ*), small functions (*appakiccaṃ*), small engagements (*appādhikaraṇaṃ*), and small undertakings (*appasamārambhaṃ*), which, when it succeeds (sampajjamānaṃ), is of great fruit (mahapphalaṃ).

And what, student, is that work (kammaṭṭhānaṃ) involving a great deal of activity (*mahaṭṭhaṃ*), great functions (*mahākiccaṃ*), great engagements (*mahādhikaraṇaṃ*), and great undertakings (*mahāsamārambhaṃ*), which, when it fails (vipajjamānaṃ), is of small fruit (appaphalaṃ)? Agriculture (kasi), student, is that work (kammaṭṭhānaṃ) involving a great deal of activity (*mahaṭṭhaṃ*), great functions (*mahākiccaṃ*), great engagements (*mahādhikaraṇaṃ*), and great undertakings (*mahāsamārambhaṃ*), which, when it fails (vipajjamānaṃ), is of small fruit (appaphalaṃ).

And what, student, is that work (kammaṭṭhānaṃ) involving a great deal of activity (*mahaṭṭhaṃ*), great functions (*mahākiccaṃ*), great engagements (*mahādhikaraṇaṃ*), and great undertakings (*mahāsamārambhaṃ*), which, when it succeeds (sampajjamānaṃ), is of great fruit (mahapphalaṃ)? Agriculture (kasi), student, is that work (kammaṭṭhānaṃ) involving a great deal of activity (*mahaṭṭhaṃ*), great functions (*mahākiccaṃ*), great engagements (*mahādhikaraṇaṃ*), and great undertakings (*mahāsamārambhaṃ*), which, when it succeeds (sampajjamānaṃ), is of great fruit (mahapphalaṃ).

And what, student, is that work (kammaṭṭhānaṃ) involving a small amount of activity (*appaṭṭhaṃ*), small functions (*appakiccaṃ*), small engagements (*appādhikaraṇaṃ*), and small undertakings (*appasamārambhaṃ*), which, when it fails (vipajjamānaṃ), is of small fruit (appaphalaṃ)? Trade (vaṇijjā), student, is that work (kammaṭṭhānaṃ) involving a small amount of activity (*appaṭṭhaṃ*), small functions (*appakiccaṃ*), small engagements (*appādhikaraṇaṃ*), and small undertakings (*appasamārambhaṃ*), which, when it fails (vipajjamānaṃ), is of small fruit (appaphalaṃ).

And what, student, is that work (kammaṭṭhānaṃ) involving a small amount of activity (*appaṭṭhaṃ*), small functions (*appakiccaṃ*), small engagements (*appādhikaraṇaṃ*), and small undertakings (*appasamārambhaṃ*), which, when it succeeds (sampajjamānaṃ), is of great fruit (mahapphalaṃ)? Trade (vaṇijjā), student, is that work (kammaṭṭhānaṃ) involving a small amount of activity (*appaṭṭhaṃ*), small functions (*appakiccaṃ*), small engagements (*appādhikaraṇaṃ*), and small undertakings (*appasamārambhaṃ*), which, when it succeeds (sampajjamānaṃ), is of great fruit (mahapphalaṃ).
commentary_pali:
463.Micchāpaṭipattinti aniyyānikaṃ akusalapaṭipadaṃ. Sammāpaṭipattinti niyyānikaṃ kusalapaṭipadaṃ.

Mahaṭṭhantiādīsu mahantehi veyyāvaccakarehi vā upakaraṇehi vā bahūhi attho etthāti mahaṭṭhaṃ. Mahantāni nāmaggahaṇamaṅgalādīni kiccāni etthāti mahākiccaṃ. Idaṃ ajja kattabbaṃ, idaṃ sveti evaṃ mahantāni adhikārasaṅkhātāni adhikaraṇāni etthāti mahādhikaraṇaṃ. Bahūnaṃ kamme yuttappayuttatāvasena pīḷāsaṅkhāto mahāsamārambho etthāti mahāsamārambhaṃ. Gharāvāsakammaṭṭhānanti gharāvāsakammaṃ. Evaṃ sabbavāresu attho veditabbo. Kasikamme cettha naṅgalakoṭiṃ ādiṃ katvā upakaraṇānaṃ pariyesanavasena mahaṭṭhatā, vaṇijjāya yathāṭhitaṃyeva bhaṇḍaṃ gahetvā parivattanavasena appaṭṭhatā veditabbā. Vipajjamānanti avuṭṭhiativuṭṭhiādīhi kasikammaṃ, maṇisuvaṇṇādīsu acchekatādīhi ca vaṇijjakammaṃ appaphalaṃ hoti, mūlacchedampi pāpuṇāti. Vipariyāyena sampajjamānaṃ mahapphalaṃ cūḷantevāsikassa viya.

Mahaṭṭha mahaṭṭhaṃ mahākiccaṃ mahādhikaraṇaṃ mahāsamārambhaṃ. Gharāvāsakammaṭṭhāna Vipajjamāna
commentary_english:
463. *micchāpaṭipatti* means unwholesome practice that does not lead out [of suffering]. *sammāpaṭipatti* means wholesome practice that leads out [of suffering].

In *mahaṭṭha* etc., because there is much benefit/meaning (*attha*) here through great assistants (*veyyāvaccakara*) or implements (*upakaraṇa*), [it is called] *mahaṭṭhaṃ*.

Because there are great undertakings (*kicca*) here, such as naming ceremonies (*nāmaggahaṇamaṅgala*) etc., [it is called] *mahākiccaṃ*.

Because there are great authoritative decisions (*adhikaraṇa*) here, consisting of "This should be done today, this tomorrow," [it is called] *mahādhikaraṇaṃ*.

Because there is a great undertaking (*mahāsamārambho*) consisting of oppression (*pīḷā*) due to the state of being connected and unconnected (*yuttappayuttatāvasena*) to many actions (*kamme*), [it is called] *mahāsamārambhaṃ*.

*gharāvāsakammaṭṭhāna* means household occupation (*gharāvāsakammaṃ*).

Thus, the meaning (*attha*) should be understood in all instances (*sabbavāresu*).

Here, in agriculture (*kasikamme*), *mahaṭṭhatā* [is] due to the search (*pariyesana*) for implements (*upakaraṇa*) with the ploughshare (*naṅgalakoṭiṃ*) as the beginning (*ādiṃ katvā*); in trade (*vaṇijjāya*), *appaṭṭhatā* [is] due to the exchange (*parivattanavasena*) after taking goods (*bhaṇḍaṃ*) just as they are placed (*yathāṭhitaṃyeva*). This should be understood (*veditabbā*).

*vipajjamāna* means that agriculture (*kasikammaṃ*) [suffers] from lack of rain, excessive rain, etc. (*avuṭṭhiativuṭṭhiādīhi*), and trade (*vaṇijjakammaṃ*) [suffers] from dishonesty, etc. (*acchekatādīhi*) in jewels, gold, etc. (*maṇisuvaṇṇādīsu*); [thus] there is little fruit (*appaphalaṃ hoti*), and even the root is destroyed (*mūlacchedampi pāpuṇāti*).

Conversely (*vipariyāyena*), flourishing (*sampajjamānaṃ*) yields great fruit (*mahapphalaṃ*), like a junior resident disciple (*cūḷantevāsikassa viya*).

*mahaṭṭha*, *mahaṭṭhaṃ*, *mahākiccaṃ*, *mahādhikaraṇaṃ*, *mahāsamārambhaṃ*.
*gharāvāsakammaṭṭhāna*, *vipajjamāna*.

mula_pali:
464. ‘‘Seyyathāpi, māṇava, kasi kammaṭṭhānaṃ mahaṭṭhaṃ mahākiccaṃ mahādhikaraṇaṃ mahāsamārambhaṃ vipajjamānaṃ appaphalaṃ hoti; evameva kho, māṇava, gharāvāsakammaṭṭhānaṃ mahaṭṭhaṃ mahākiccaṃ mahādhikaraṇaṃ mahāsamārambhaṃ vipajjamānaṃ appaphalaṃ hoti. Seyyathāpi, māṇava, kasiyeva kammaṭṭhānaṃ mahaṭṭhaṃ mahākiccaṃ mahādhikaraṇaṃ mahāsamārambhaṃ sampajjamānaṃ mahapphalaṃ hoti; evameva kho, māṇava, gharāvāsakammaṭṭhānaṃ mahaṭṭhaṃ mahākiccaṃ mahādhikaraṇaṃ mahāsamārambhaṃ sampajjamānaṃ mahapphalaṃ hoti. Seyyathāpi, māṇava, vaṇijjā kammaṭṭhānaṃ appaṭṭhaṃ appakiccaṃ appādhikaraṇaṃ appasamārambhaṃ vipajjamānaṃ appaphalaṃ hoti; evameva kho, māṇava, pabbajjā kammaṭṭhānaṃ appaṭṭhaṃ appakiccaṃ appādhikaraṇaṃ appasamārambhaṃ vipajjamānaṃ appaphalaṃ hoti. Seyyathāpi, māṇava, vaṇijjāyeva kammaṭṭhānaṃ appaṭṭhaṃ appakiccaṃ appādhikaraṇaṃ appasamārambhaṃ sampajjamānaṃ mahapphalaṃ hoti; evameva kho , māṇava, pabbajjā kammaṭṭhānaṃ appaṭṭhaṃ appakiccaṃ appādhikaraṇaṃ appasamārambhaṃ sampajjamānaṃ mahapphalaṃ hotī’’ti.

‘‘Brāhmaṇā , bho gotama, pañca dhamme paññapenti puññassa kiriyāya, kusalassa ārādhanāyā’’ti. ‘‘Ye te, māṇava, brāhmaṇā pañca dhamme paññapenti puññassa kiriyāya, kusalassa ārādhanāya – sace te agaru – sādhu te pañca dhamme imasmiṃ parisati bhāsassū’’ti. ‘‘Na kho me, bho gotama, garu yatthassu bhavanto vā nisinno bhavantarūpo vā’’ti nisinnā bhavantarūpā vāti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). ‘‘Tena hi, māṇava, bhāsassū’’ti. ‘‘Saccaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā paṭhamaṃ dhammaṃ paññapenti puññassa kiriyāya, kusalassa ārādhanāya. Tapaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā dutiyaṃ dhammaṃ paññapenti puññassa kiriyāya, kusalassa ārādhanāya. Brahmacariyaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā tatiyaṃ dhammaṃ paññapenti puññassa kiriyāya, kusalassa ārādhanāya. Ajjhenaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā catutthaṃ dhammaṃ paññapenti puññassa kiriyāya, kusalassa ārādhanāya. Cāgaṃ kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā pañcamaṃ dhammaṃ paññapenti puññassa kiriyāya, kusalassa ārādhanāya. Brāhmaṇā, bho gotama, ime pañca dhamme paññapenti puññassa kiriyāya, kusalassa ārādhanāyāti. Idha bhavaṃ gotamo kimāhā’’ti?

nisinnā bhavantarūpā vāti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)
mula_english:
464. “Just as, student (māṇava), agriculture is a work (kammaṭṭhānaṃ) that involves a great deal of activity (mahaṭṭhaṃ), great functions (mahākiccaṃ), great engagements (mahādhikaraṇaṃ), and great undertakings (mahāsamārambhaṃ), but is of small fruit (appaphalaṃ) when it fails (vipajjamānaṃ), so too, student (māṇava), the work of the household life (gharāvāsakammaṭṭhānaṃ) involves a great deal of activity (mahaṭṭhaṃ), great functions (mahākiccaṃ), great engagements (mahādhikaraṇaṃ), and great undertakings (mahāsamārambhaṃ), but is of small fruit (appaphalaṃ) when it fails (vipajjamānaṃ).

Just as, student (māṇava), agriculture itself is a work (kammaṭṭhānaṃ) that involves a great deal of activity (mahaṭṭhaṃ), great functions (mahākiccaṃ), great engagements (mahādhikaraṇaṃ), and great undertakings (mahāsamārambhaṃ), and is of great fruit (mahapphalaṃ) when it succeeds (sampajjamānaṃ), so too, student (māṇava), the work of the household life (gharāvāsakammaṭṭhānaṃ) involves a great deal of activity (mahaṭṭhaṃ), great functions (mahākiccaṃ), great engagements (mahādhikaraṇaṃ), and great undertakings (mahāsamārambhaṃ), and is of great fruit (mahapphalaṃ) when it succeeds (sampajjamānaṃ).

Just as, student (māṇava), trade is a work (kammaṭṭhānaṃ) involving a small amount of activity (appaṭṭhaṃ), small functions (appakiccaṃ), small engagements (appādhikaraṇaṃ), and small undertakings (appasamārambhaṃ), and is of small fruit (appaphalaṃ) when it fails (vipajjamānaṃ), so too, student (māṇava), the work of those gone forth (pabbajjā kammaṭṭhānaṃ) involves a small amount of activity (appaṭṭhaṃ), small functions (appakiccaṃ), small engagements (appādhikaraṇaṃ), and small undertakings (appasamārambhaṃ), and is of small fruit (appaphalaṃ) when it fails (vipajjamānaṃ).

Just as, student (māṇava), trade itself is a work (kammaṭṭhānaṃ) involving a small amount of activity (appaṭṭhaṃ), small functions (appakiccaṃ), small engagements (appādhikaraṇaṃ), and small undertakings (appasamārambhaṃ), and is of great fruit (mahapphalaṃ) when it succeeds (sampajjamānaṃ), so too, student (māṇava), the work of those gone forth (pabbajjā kammaṭṭhānaṃ) involves a small amount of activity (appaṭṭhaṃ), small functions (appakiccaṃ), small engagements (appādhikaraṇaṃ), and small undertakings (appasamārambhaṃ), and is of great fruit (mahapphalaṃ) when it succeeds (sampajjamānaṃ).”

“Master Gotama (bho gotama), the Brahmins (brāhmaṇā) prescribe five things (pañca dhamme) for the performance of merit (puññassa kiriyāya), for accomplishing the wholesome (kusalassa ārādhanāya).”

“Those five things (pañca dhamme), student (māṇava), that the Brahmins (brāhmaṇā) prescribe for the performance of merit (puññassa kiriyāya), for accomplishing the wholesome (kusalassa ārādhanāya)—if it is not troublesome (sace te agaru)—please state (bhāsassū) those five things (pañca dhamme) to this assembly (imasmiṃ parisati).”

“It is not troublesome (garu) for me, Master Gotama (bho gotama), when such venerable ones (bhavanto) as yourself are sitting (nisinno) in the assembly.”

“Then state them (bhāsassū), student (māṇava).”

“Master Gotama (bho gotama), truth (saccaṃ) is the first thing (paṭhamaṃ dhammaṃ) that the Brahmins (brāhmaṇā) prescribe for the performance of merit (puññassa kiriyāya), for accomplishing the wholesome (kusalassa ārādhanāya).

Asceticism (tapaṃ) is the second thing (dutiyaṃ dhammaṃ)...

Celibacy (brahmacariyaṃ) is the third thing (tatiyaṃ dhammaṃ)...

Study (ajjhenaṃ) is the fourth thing (catutthaṃ dhammaṃ)...

Generosity (cāgaṃ) is the fifth thing (pañcamaṃ dhammaṃ) that the Brahmins (brāhmaṇā) prescribe for the performance of merit (puññassa kiriyāya), for accomplishing the wholesome (kusalassa ārādhanāya).

Master Gotama (bho gotama), the Brahmins (brāhmaṇā) prescribe these five things (ime pañca dhamme) for the performance of merit (puññassa kiriyāya), for accomplishing the wholesome (kusalassa ārādhanāya).”

“What does Master Gotama (bhavaṃ gotamo) say here (idha)?”
commentary_pali:
464.Evameva khoti yathā kasikammaṭṭhānaṃ vipajjamānaṃ appaphalaṃ hoti, evaṃ gharāvāsakammaṭṭhānampi. Akatakalyāṇo hi kālaṃ katvā niraye nibbattati. Mahādattasenāpati nāma kireko brāhmaṇabhatto ahosi, tassa maraṇasamaye nirayo upaṭṭhāsi. So brāhmaṇehi ‘‘kiṃ passasī’’ti vutto? Lohitagharanti āha. Brahmaloko bho esoti. Brahmaloko nāma bho kahanti? Uparīti. Mayhaṃ heṭṭhā upaṭṭhātīti. Kiñcāpi heṭṭhā upaṭṭhāti , tathāpi uparīti kālaṃ katvā niraye nibbatto. ‘‘Iminā amhākaṃ yaññe doso dinno’’ti sahassaṃ gahetvā nīharituṃ adaṃsu. Sampajjamānaṃ pana mahapphalaṃ hoti. Katakalyāṇo hi kālaṃ katvā sagge nibbattati. Sakalāya guttilavimānakathāya dīpetabbaṃ. Yathā pana taṃ vaṇijjakammaṭṭhānaṃ vipajjamānaṃ appaphalaṃ hoti, evaṃ sīlesu aparipūrakārino anesanāya yuttassa pabbajjākammaṭṭhānampi. Evarūpā hi neva jhānādisukhaṃ na saggamokkhaṃ labhati. Sampajjamānaṃ pana mahapphalaṃ hoti. Sīlāni hi pūretvā vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhento arahattampi pāpuṇāti.

Brāhmaṇā, bho gotamoti idha kiṃ pucchāmīti pucchati? Brāhmaṇā vadanti – ‘‘pabbajito ime pañca dhamme pūretuṃ samattho nāma natthi, gahaṭṭhova pūretī’’ti. Samaṇo pana gotamo – ‘‘gihissa vā ahaṃ māṇava pabbajitassa vā’’ti punappunaṃ vadati, neva pabbajitaṃ muñcati, mayhameva pucchaṃ maññe na sallakkhetīti cāgasīsena pañca dhamme pucchāmīti pucchati. Sace te agarūti sace tuyhaṃ yathā brāhmaṇā paññapenti, tathā idha bhāsituṃ bhāriyaṃ na hoti, yadi na koci aphāsukabhāvo hoti, bhāsassūti attho. Na kho me, bhoti kiṃ sandhāyāha? Paṇḍitapaṭirūpakānañhi santike kathetuṃ dukkhaṃ hoti, te pade pade akkhare akkhare dosameva vadanti. Ekantapaṇḍitā pana kathaṃ sutvā sukathitaṃ pasaṃsanti, dukkathite pāḷipadaatthabyañjanesu yaṃ yaṃ virujjhati, taṃ taṃ ujuṃ katvā denti. Bhagavatā ca sadiso ekantapaṇḍito nāma natthi, tenāha ‘‘na kho me, bho gotama, garu, yatthassu bhavanto vā nisinno bhavantarūpo vā’’ti. Saccanti vacīsaccaṃ. Tapanti tapacariyaṃ. Brahmacariyanti methunaviratiṃ. Ajjhenanti mantagahaṇaṃ. Cāganti āmisapariccāgaṃ.

Brāhmaṇā, bho gotamo Sace te agarū Na kho me, bho Sacca Tapa Brahmacariya Ajjhena Cāga
commentary_english:
464. Just as agriculture that is poorly managed yields little fruit, so too is the management of household life.

A person who has not done good deeds, upon dying, is reborn in hell.

There was a general named Mahādatta, a devotee of Brahmins. At the time of his death, hell appeared before him.

The Brahmins asked him, "What do you see?" He replied, "A house of blood."

"It is the Brahmā world, sir."

"Where is the Brahmā world, sir?" "It is above."

"He attends to me from below."

Even though he attends from below, having died thinking "it is above," he was reborn in hell.

"By this, our sacrifice has been ruined!" Taking a thousand [coins], they gave [it] to be taken away.

But when it succeeds, it is of great fruit.

A person who has done good deeds, upon dying, is reborn in heaven.

The entire story of the Guttila celestial mansion should be illuminated.

Just as trade that is poorly managed yields little fruit, so too is the renunciate life of one who is intent on unsought things and does not fulfill the precepts.

Such a person neither gains the happiness of meditative absorption, and so on, nor attains heaven or liberation.

But when it succeeds, it is of great fruit.

Having fulfilled the precepts, developing insight, one attains even arahantship.

Brahmins, Gotama! What should I ask here?" he asks. The Brahmins say, "A renunciate is not capable of fulfilling these five qualities, only a householder can fulfill them."

The ascetic Gotama says repeatedly, "Whether for a householder or a renunciate, O student," but he does not release the renunciate. "I think he does not consider my question, but I will ask about the five qualities with a mind of generosity," he asks.

"If it is not burdensome to you," meaning if it is not difficult for you to speak here as the Brahmins proclaim, if there is no discomfort, speak, is the meaning.

"It is not easy for me, sir," what is the reason for saying this? It is difficult to speak in the presence of those who are mere semblances of scholars, for they find fault with every word and every letter.

But how do true scholars, having heard something well-spoken, praise it? In poorly spoken [words], they straighten out whatever is contradictory in the Pali words, meanings, and expressions and give [the correct interpretation].

There is no one like the Blessed One, a true scholar. Therefore, he says, "It is not easy for me, O Gotama, for you are either sitting or in the form of a being."

*Satya* means truthfulness of speech.

*Tapas* means the practice of austerity.

*Brahmacarya* means abstinence from sexual activity.

*Adhyayana* means the recitation of mantras.

*Tyāga* means the renunciation of material things.

Brahmins, Gotama! If it is not burdensome to you, it is not easy for me, sir. Satya, tapas, brahmacarya, adhyayana, tyāga.

mula_pali:
465. ‘‘Kiṃ pana, māṇava, atthi koci brāhmaṇānaṃ ekabrāhmaṇopi yo evamāha – ‘ahaṃ imesaṃ pañcannaṃ dhammānaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā vipākaṃ pavedemī’’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’. ‘‘Kiṃ pana, māṇava, atthi koci brāhmaṇānaṃ ekācariyopi ekācariyapācariyopi yāva sattamā ācariyamahayugāpi yo evamāha – ‘ahaṃ imesaṃ pañcannaṃ dhammānaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā vipākaṃ pavedemī’’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’. ‘‘Kiṃ pana, māṇava, yepi te brāhmaṇānaṃ pubbakā isayo mantānaṃ kattāro mantānaṃ pavattāro yesamidaṃ etarahi brāhmaṇā porāṇaṃ mantapadaṃ gītaṃ pavuttaṃ samihitaṃ tadanugāyanti tadanubhāsanti bhāsitamanubhāsanti vācitamanuvācenti, seyyathidaṃ – aṭṭhako vāmako vāmadevo vessāmitto yamataggi aṅgīraso bhāradvājo vāseṭṭho kassapo bhagu, tepi evamāhaṃsu – ‘mayaṃ imesaṃ pañcannaṃ dhammānaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā vipākaṃ pavedemā’’’ti? ‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’.

‘‘Iti kira, māṇava, natthi koci brāhmaṇānaṃ ekabrāhmaṇopi yo evamāha – ‘ahaṃ imesaṃ pañcannaṃ dhammānaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā vipākaṃ pavedemī’ti; natthi koci brāhmaṇānaṃ ekācariyopi ekācariyapācariyopi yāva sattamā ācariyamahayugāpi yo evamāha – ‘ahaṃ imesaṃ pañcannaṃ dhammānaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā vipākaṃ pavedemī’ti; yepi te brāhmaṇānaṃ pubbakā isayo mantānaṃ kattāro mantānaṃ pavattāro, yesamidaṃ etarahi brāhmaṇā porāṇaṃ mantapadaṃ gītaṃ pavuttaṃ samihitaṃ, tadanugāyanti tadanubhāsanti bhāsitamanubhāsanti vācitamanuvācenti, seyyathidaṃ – aṭṭhako vāmako vāmadevo vessāmitto yamataggi aṅgīraso bhāradvājo vāseṭṭho kassapo bhagu. Tepi na evamāhaṃsu – ‘mayaṃ imesaṃ pañcannaṃ dhammānaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā vipākaṃ pavedemā’ti.

‘‘Seyyathāpi, māṇava, andhaveṇi paramparāsaṃsattā purimopi na passati majjhimopi na passati pacchimopi na passati; evameva kho, māṇava, andhaveṇūpamaṃ maññe brāhmaṇānaṃ bhāsitaṃ sampajjati – purimopi na passati majjhimopi na passati pacchimopi na passatī’’ti.
mula_english:
465. “How then, student, is there even a single *brāhmaṇa* among the *brāhmaṇas* who says thus: ‘I declare the result of these five *dharmas*, having realised them myself with direct knowledge’?”

“No, good Gotama.”

“How then, student, is there even a single teacher or a teacher’s teacher back to the seventh generation of teachers among the *brāhmaṇas* who says thus: ‘I declare the result of these five *dharmas*, having realised them myself with direct knowledge’?”

“No, good Gotama.”

“How then, student, the ancient *brāhmaṇa* seers, the creators of the *mantras*, the composers of the *mantras*, whose ancient *mantra* verses that were formerly chanted, uttered, and compiled the *brāhmaṇas* nowadays still chant, repeat, and recite—that is, Aṭṭhaka, Vāmaka, Vāmadeva, Vessāmitta, Yamataggi, Aṅgīrasa, Bhāradvāja, Vāseṭṭha, Kassapa, and Bhagu—did even these ancient *brāhmaṇa* seers say thus: ‘We declare the result of these five *dharmas*, having realised them ourselves with direct knowledge’?”

“No, good Gotama.”

“Thus indeed, student, there is no *brāhmaṇa* among the *brāhmaṇas* who says thus: ‘I declare the result of these five *dharmas*, having realised them myself with *abhiññā* direct knowledge’. There is no teacher or teacher’s teacher back to the seventh generation of teachers among the *brāhmaṇas* who says thus: ‘I declare the result of these five *dharmas*, having realised them myself with direct knowledge’. The ancient *brāhmaṇa* seers, the creators of the *mantras*, the composers of the *mantras*, whose ancient *mantra* verses that were formerly chanted, uttered, and compiled the *brāhmaṇas* nowadays still chant, repeat, and recite—that is, Aṭṭhaka, Vāmaka, Vāmadeva, Vessāmitta, Yamataggi, Aṅgīrasa, Bhāradvāja, Vāseṭṭha, Kassapa, and Bhagu—even they did not say thus: ‘We declare the result of these five *dharmas*, having realised them ourselves with direct knowledge.’”

“Just as, student, a file of blind men are linked together, the first one does not see, the middle one does not see, and the last one does not see; just so, student, I consider the speech of the *brāhmaṇas* to be like a file of blind men: the first one does not see, the middle one does not see, and the last one does not see.”

mula_pali:
466. Evaṃ vutte, subho māṇavo todeyyaputto bhagavatā andhaveṇūpamena vuccamāno kupito anattamano bhagavantaṃyeva khuṃsento bhagavantaṃyeva vambhento bhagavantaṃyeva vadamāno – ‘samaṇo gotamo pāpito bhavissatī’ti bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘brāhmaṇo, bho gotama, pokkharasāti opamañño subhagavaniko evamāha – ‘evameva panidhekacce panimeke (sabbattha) samaṇabrāhmaṇā uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ paṭijānanti. Tesamidaṃ bhāsitaṃ hassakaṃyeva sampajjati, nāmakaṃyeva sampajjati, rittakaṃyeva sampajjati, tucchakaṃyeva sampajjati. Kathañhi nāma manussabhūto uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ ñassati vā dakkhati vā sacchi vā karissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’’’ti?

‘‘Kiṃ pana, māṇava, brāhmaṇo pokkharasāti opamañño subhagavaniko sabbesaṃyeva samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajānātī’’ti? ‘‘Sakāyapi hi, bho gotama, puṇṇikāya dāsiyā brāhmaṇo pokkharasāti opamañño subhagavaniko cetasā ceto paricca na pajānāti, kuto pana sabbesaṃyeva samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajānissatī’’ti?

‘‘Seyyathāpi, māṇava, jaccandho puriso na passeyya kaṇhasukkāni rūpāni, na passeyya nīlakāni rūpāni, na passeyya pītakāni rūpāni, na passeyya lohitakāni rūpāni, na passeyya mañjiṭṭhakāni rūpāni, na passeyya samavisamaṃ, na passeyya tārakarūpāni, na passeyya candimasūriye. So evaṃ vadeyya – ‘natthi kaṇhasukkāni rūpāni, natthi kaṇhasukkānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī; natthi nīlakāni rūpāni, natthi nīlakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī; natthi pītakāni rūpāni, natthi pītakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī; natthi lohitakāni rūpāni, natthi lohitakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī; natthi mañjiṭṭhakāni rūpāni, natthi mañjiṭṭhakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī; natthi samavisamaṃ, natthi samavisamassa dassāvī; natthi tārakarūpāni, natthi tārakarūpānaṃ dassāvī; natthi candimasūriyā, natthi candimasūriyānaṃ dassāvī. Ahametaṃ na jānāmi, ahametaṃ na passāmi; tasmā taṃ natthī’ti. Sammā nu kho so, māṇava, vadamāno vadeyyā’’ti?

‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama. Atthi kaṇhasukkāni rūpāni, atthi kaṇhasukkānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī; atthi nīlakāni rūpāni, atthi nīlakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī; atthi pītakāni rūpāni, atthi pītakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī; atthi lohitakāni rūpāni, atthi lohitakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī; atthi mañjiṭṭhakāni rūpāni, atthi mañjiṭṭhakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī; atthi samavisamaṃ, atthi samavisamassa dassāvī; atthi tārakarūpāni, atthi tārakarūpānaṃ dassāvī ; atthi candimasūriyā, atthi candimasūriyānaṃ dassāvī. ‘Ahametaṃ na jānāmi, ahametaṃ na passāmi; tasmā taṃ natthī’ti; na hi so, bho gotama, sammā vadamāno vadeyyā’’ti.

‘‘Evameva kho, māṇava, brāhmaṇo pokkharasāti opamañño subhagavaniko andho acakkhuko. So vata uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ ñassati vā dakkhati vā sacchi vā karissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati’’.
mula_english:
466. When this was said, the brahmin student Subha, Todeyya’s son, was angry and displeased with the simile of the file of blind men, and he reviled, disparaged, and censured the Blessed One, saying: “The recluse Gotama will be worsted.” Then he said to the Blessed One: “Master Gotama, the brahmin Pokkharasati of the Upamanna clan, lord of the Subhaga Grove, says thus: ‘Some recluses and *brāhmaṇas* here claim superhuman states (*uttarimanussadhammā*), distinctions in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones (*alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ*). What they say turns out to be ridiculous; it turns out to be mere words, empty and hollow. How could a human being know, see, or realize a superhuman state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones? This is impossible!’”

“But what, *māṇava*, does the *brāhmaṇa* Pokkharasati of the Upamanna clan, lord of the Subhaga Grove, know the minds of all recluses and *brāhmaṇas* with his mind?”

“Master Gotama, the *brāhmaṇa* Pokkharasati of the Upamanna clan, lord of the Subhaga Grove, does not even know the mind of his own servant Puṇṇikā with his mind, how could he know the minds of all recluses and *brāhmaṇas* with his mind?”

“Suppose, *māṇava*, there was a man born blind who could not see dark and light forms (*kaṇhasukkāni rūpāṇi*), who could not see blue forms (*nīlakāni rūpāṇi*), who could not see yellow forms (*pītakāni rūpāṇi*), who could not see red forms (*lohitakāni rūpāṇi*), who could not see pink forms (*mañjiṭṭhakāni rūpāṇi*), who could not see what was even and uneven (*samavisamaṃ*), who could not see the stars (*tārakarūpāṇi*), or the sun and moon (*candimasūriye*). He might say thus: ‘There are no dark and light forms (*kaṇhasukkāni rūpāṇi*), and no one who sees dark and light forms (*kaṇhasukkānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī*); there are no blue forms (*nīlakāni rūpāṇi*), and no one who sees blue forms (*nīlakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī*); there are no yellow forms (*pītakāni rūpāṇi*), and no one who sees yellow forms (*pītakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī*); there are no red forms (*lohitakāni rūpāṇi*), and no one who sees red forms (*lohitakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī*); there are no pink forms (*mañjiṭṭhakāni rūpāṇi*), and no one who sees pink forms (*mañjiṭṭhakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī*); there is nothing even and uneven (*samavisamaṃ*), and no one who sees anything even and uneven (*samavisamassa dassāvī*); there are no stars (*tārakarūpāṇi*), and no one who sees stars (*tārakarūpānaṃ dassāvī*); there is no sun or moon (*candimasūriyā*), and nobody who can see them (*candimasūriyānaṃ dassāvī*). I do not know these, I do not see these, therefore these do not exist.’ Would he be speaking rightly, *māṇava*, in so speaking?”

“No, Reverend Gotama. There are dark and light forms (*kaṇhasukkāni rūpāṇi*), and those who see dark and light forms (*kaṇhasukkānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī*); there are blue forms (*nīlakāni rūpāṇi*), and those who see blue forms (*nīlakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī*); there are yellow forms (*pītakāni rūpāṇi*), and those who see yellow forms (*pītakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī*); there are red forms (*lohitakāni rūpāṇi*), and those who see red forms (*lohitakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī*); there are pink forms (*mañjiṭṭhakāni rūpāṇi*), and those who see pink forms (*mañjiṭṭhakānaṃ rūpānaṃ dassāvī*); there is something even and uneven (*samavisamaṃ*), and those who see anything even and uneven (*samavisamassa dassāvī*); there are the stars (*tārakarūpāṇi*), and those who see stars (*tārakarūpānaṃ dassāvī*); there is a sun and a moon (*candimasūriyā*), and those who see the sun and the moon (*candimasūriyānaṃ dassāvī*). Saying, ‘I do not know these, I do not see these, therefore these do not exist,’ he would not be speaking rightly.”

“So too, *māṇava*, the *brāhmaṇa* Pokkharasati of the Upamanna clan, lord of the Subhaga Grove, is blind and visionless. That he could know or see or realise a superhuman state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones - this is impossible.”
commentary_pali: 466.Pāpito bhavissatīti. Ajānanabhāvaṃ pāpito bhavissati. Etadavocāti bhagavatā andhaveṇūpamāya niggahito taṃ paccāharituṃ asakkonto yathā nāma dubbalasunakho migaṃ uṭṭhapetvā sāmikassa abhimukhaṃ katvā sayaṃ apasakkati, evamevaṃ ācariyaṃ apadisanto evaṃ ‘‘brāhmaṇo’’tiādivacanaṃ avoca. Tattha pokkharasātīti idaṃ tassa nāmaṃ, ‘‘pokkharasāyī’’tipi vuccati. Tassa kira kāyo setapokkharasadiso devanagare ussāpitarajatatoraṇaṃ viya sobhati, sīsaṃ panassa kāḷavaṇṇaindanīlamayaṃ viya, massupi candamaṇḍale kāḷamegharāji viya khāyati, akkhīni nīluppalasadisāni, nāsā rajatapanāḷikā viya suvaṭṭitā suparisuddhā, hatthapādatalāni ceva mukhañca katalākhārasaparikammaṃ viya sobhati. Ativiya sobhaggappatto brāhmaṇassa attabhāvo. Arājake ṭhāne rājānaṃ kātuṃ yuttamimaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ, evamesa sassiriko, iti naṃ pokkharasadisattā ‘‘pokkharasātī’’ti sañjānanti, pokkhare pana so nibbatto, na mātukucchiyanti iti naṃ pokkhare sayitattā ‘‘pokkharasāyī’’tipi sañjānanti. Opamaññoti upamaññagotto. Subhagavanikoti ukkaṭṭhāya subhagavanassa issaro. Hassakaṃyevāti hasitabbakaññeva. Nāmakaṃyevāti lāmakaṃyeva. Tadeva taṃ atthābhāvena rittakaṃ. Rittakattā ca tucchakaṃ. Idāni naṃ bhagavā sācariyakaṃ niggaṇhituṃ kiṃ pana māṇavātiādimāha.
commentary_english:
466.
He will be caused to reach [a state of] ignorance.
He will be caused to reach [a state of] ignorance.
"Thus he spoke": rebuked by the Blessed One with the simile of the blind bamboo, unable to retract that, just as a weak dog, having roused a wild animal, retreats towards its master, having done <pb ed="m" n="3. 0304"/> that itself, in the same way, declaring the teacher, thus he spoke the statement beginning with "brāhmaṇa."
There, "Pokkharasātī": this is his name; he is also called "Pokkharasāyī."
His body shines like a white lotus in a city of gods, like a raised silver archway, but his head is like an indigo-colored one made of dark blue, his beard appears like a dark cloud in the lunar sphere, his eyes are like blue lotuses, his nose is well-rounded and very pure like a silver pipe, and his palms and soles of his feet and his face are like <pb ed="v" n="3. 0314"/> a well-prepared red lacquered surface.
The Brāhmaṇa's essence is extremely endowed with beauty.
In a kingless place, it is fitting to make this Brāhmaṇa king; thus he is glorious, thus they recognize him as "Pokkharasātī" because of his lotus-like nature, <pb ed="p" n="3. 0447"/> but he was born in a lotus, not in a mother's womb, thus they recognize him as "Pokkharasāyī" because he rests in a lotus.
"Opamañño" means of the Opamañña *gotra* (clan).
"Subhagavaniko" means the lord of the fortunate forest (*subhagavana*) due to excellence (*ukkaṭṭhāya*).
"Hassakaṃyevā" means just to be laughed at.
"Nāmakaṃyevā" means just contemptible.
That itself is empty (*rittakaṃ*) due to the absence of meaning (*atthābhāvena*).
And due to being empty (*rittakattā*), [it is] void (*tucchakaṃ*).
Now, the Blessed One, in order to refute him along with his teacher, said the following, beginning with "*kiṃ pana māṇavā*."

mula_pali:
467. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, māṇava, ye te kosalakā brāhmaṇamahāsālā, seyyathidaṃ – caṅkī brāhmaṇo tārukkho brāhmaṇo pokkharasāti brāhmaṇo jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo pitā ca vā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) te todeyyo, katamā nesaṃ seyyo seyyā (syā. kaṃ.), yaṃ vā te sammuccā sammusā (sī. pī.) vācaṃ bhāseyyuṃ yaṃ vā asammuccā’’ti? ‘‘Sammuccā, bho gotama’’.

‘‘Katamā nesaṃ seyyo, yaṃ vā te mantā vācaṃ bhāseyyuṃ yaṃ vā amantā’’ti? ‘‘Mantā, bho gotama’’.

‘‘Katamā nesaṃ seyyo, yaṃ vā te paṭisaṅkhāya vācaṃ bhāseyyuṃ yaṃ vā appaṭisaṅkhāyā’’ti? ‘‘Paṭisaṅkhāya, bho gotama’’.

‘‘Katamā nesaṃ seyyo, yaṃ vā te atthasaṃhitaṃ vācaṃ bhāseyyuṃ yaṃ vā anatthasaṃhita’’nti? ‘‘Atthasaṃhitaṃ, bho gotama’’.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, māṇava, yadi evaṃ sante, brāhmaṇena pokkharasātinā opamaññena subhagavanikena sammuccā vācā bhāsitā asammuccā’’ti asammusā vāti (pī.) evamitarapañhattayepi vāsaddena saha dissati? ‘‘Asammuccā, bho gotama’’.

asammusā vāti (pī.) evamitarapañhattayepi vāsaddena saha dissati

‘‘Mantā vācā bhāsitā amantā vā’’ti? ‘‘Amantā, bho gotama’’.

‘‘Paṭisaṅkhāya vācā bhāsitā appaṭisaṅkhāyā’’ti? ‘‘Appaṭisaṅkhāya, bho gotama’’.

‘‘Atthasaṃhitā vācā bhāsitā anatthasaṃhitā’’ti? ‘‘Anatthasaṃhitā, bho gotama’’.

‘‘Pañca kho ime, māṇava, nīvaraṇā. Katame pañca? Kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ, byāpādanīvaraṇaṃ, thīnamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ uddhaccakukkuccanīvaraṇaṃ, vicikicchānīvaraṇaṃ – ime kho, māṇava, pañca nīvaraṇā. Imehi kho māṇava, pañcahi nīvaraṇehi brāhmaṇo pokkharasāti opamañño subhagavaniko āvuto nivuto ophuṭo ovuto (sī.), ophuto (syā. kaṃ. pī.) pariyonaddho. So vata uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ ñassati vā dakkhati vā sacchi vā karissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

ovuto (sī.), ophuto (syā. kaṃ. pī.)
mula_english:
467. “What do you think, student (māṇava)? Those well-to-do Kosala brahmins (brāhmaṇamahāsālā) such as the brahmin (brāhmaṇo) Canki (caṅkī), the brahmin (brāhmaṇo) Tarukkha (tārukkho), the brahmin (brāhmaṇo) Pokkharasāti (pokkharasāti), the brahmin (brāhmaṇo) Janussoni (jāṇussoṇi), or your father (pitā), Todeyya (todeyyo), which is better for them, that the statements (vācaṃ) they make accord with worldly convention (sammuccā) or flaunt worldly convention (asammuccā)?” “That they accord with worldly convention (sammuccā), Master Gotama (bho gotama).”

“Which is better for them, that the statements (vācaṃ) they make be thoughtful (mantā) or thoughtless (amantā)?” “Thoughtful (mantā), Master Gotama (bho gotama).”

“Which is better for them, that they make their statements (vācaṃ) after reflecting (paṭisaṅkhāya) or without reflecting (appaṭisaṅkhāyā)?” “After reflecting (paṭisaṅkhāya), Master Gotama (bho gotama).”

“Which is better for them, that the statements (vācaṃ) they make be beneficial (atthasaṃhitaṃ) or unbeneficial (anatthasaṃhitaṃ)?” “Beneficial (atthasaṃhitaṃ), Master Gotama (bho gotama).”

“What do you think, student (māṇava)? If that is so, was the statement (vācā) spoken by the brahmin (brāhmaṇena) Pokkharasāti (pokkharasātinā), Opamañña (opamaññena), Subhagavanika (subhagavanikena) in accordance with worldly convention (sammuccā) or not in accordance with worldly convention (asammuccā)?” “Not in accordance with worldly convention (asammuccā), Master Gotama (bho gotama).”

“Was the statement (vācā) spoken thoughtful (mantā) or thoughtless (amantā)?” “Thoughtless (amantā), Master Gotama (bho gotama).”

“Was the statement (vācā) spoken after reflecting (paṭisaṅkhāya) or without reflecting (appaṭisaṅkhāyā)?” “Without reflecting (appaṭisaṅkhāya), Master Gotama (bho gotama).”

“Was the statement (vācā) spoken beneficial (atthasaṃhitā) or unbeneficial (anatthasaṃhitā)?” “Unbeneficial (anatthasaṃhitā), Master Gotama (bho gotama).”

“Now there are these five hindrances (pañca nīvaraṇā), student (māṇava). What are these five (katame pañca)? The hindrance of sensual desire (kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ), the hindrance of ill will (byāpādanīvaraṇaṃ), the hindrance of sloth and torpor (thīnamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ), the hindrance of restlessness and remorse (uddhaccakukkuccanīvaraṇaṃ), and the hindrance of doubt (vicikicchānīvaraṇaṃ). These are the five hindrances (pañca nīvaraṇā). The brahmin (brāhmaṇo) Pokkharasāti (pokkharasāti), Opamañña (opamañño), Subhagavanika (subhagavaniko) is obstructed (āvuto), hindered (nivuto), blocked (ophuṭo), and enveloped (pariyonaddho) by these five hindrances (pañcahi nīvaraṇehi). That he could know or see or realise a superhuman state (uttarimanussadhammā), a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones (ariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ) - this is impossible (netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati).
commentary_pali: 467. Tattha katamā nesaṃ seyyoti katamā vācā tesaṃ seyyo, pāsaṃsataroti attho. Sammuccāti sammutiyā lokavohārena. Mantāti tulayitvā pariggaṇhitvā. Paṭisaṅkhāyāti jānitvā. Atthasaṃhitanti kāraṇanissitaṃ. Evaṃ santeti lokavohāraṃ amuñcitvā tulayitvā jānitvā kāraṇanissitaṃ katvā kathitāya seyyabhāve sati. Āvutoti āvarito. Nivutoti nivārito. Ophuṭoti onaddho. Pariyonaddhoti paliveṭhito.
commentary_english:
467.
Therein, *katamā nesaṃ seyyo* means "which speech is better for them, [which is] more praiseworthy," that is the meaning.
*sammuccā* means by convention ( *sammutiyā*), by worldly usage (*lokavohārena*).
*mantā* means having weighed ( *tulayitvā*), having grasped (*pariggaṇhitvā*).
*paṭisaṅkhāyā* means having known (*jānitvā*).
*atthasaṃhita* means dependent on reason (*kāraṇanissitaṃ*).
*evaṃ sante* means "while worldly usage is not abandoned, having weighed, having known, having made [it] dependent on reason, when there is a better state of what has been spoken."
*āvuto* means covered (*āvarito*).
*nivuto* means warded off (*nivārito*).
*ophuṭo* means bound (*onaddho*).
*pariyonaddho* means surrounded (*paliveṭhito*).

mula_pali:
468. ‘‘Pañca kho ime, māṇava, kāmaguṇā. Katame pañca? Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā, sotaviññeyyā saddā…pe… ghānaviññeyyā gandhā… jivhā viññeyyā rasā… kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā – ime kho, māṇava, pañca kāmaguṇā. Imehi kho, māṇava, pañcahi kāmaguṇehi brāhmaṇo pokkharasāti opamañño subhagavaniko gathito mucchito ajjhopanno anādīnavadassāvī anissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati. So vata uttarimanussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ ñassati vā dakkhati vā sacchi vā karissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, māṇava, yaṃ vā tiṇakaṭṭhupādānaṃ paṭicca aggiṃ jāleyya yaṃ vā nissaṭṭhatiṇakaṭṭhupādānaṃ aggiṃ jāleyya, katamo nu khvāssa aggi accimā ceva vaṇṇavā ca pabhassaro cā’’ti? ‘‘Sace taṃ, bho gotama, ṭhānaṃ nissaṭṭhatiṇakaṭṭhupādānaṃ aggiṃ jāletuṃ, svāssa aggi accimā ceva vaṇṇavā ca pabhassaro cā’’ti. ‘‘Aṭṭhānaṃ kho etaṃ, māṇava, anavakāso yaṃ nissaṭṭhatiṇakaṭṭhupādānaṃ aggiṃ jāleyya aññatra iddhimatā. Seyyathāpi, māṇava, tiṇakaṭṭhupādānaṃ paṭicca aggi jalati tathūpamāhaṃ, māṇava, imaṃ pītiṃ vadāmi yāyaṃ pīti pañca kāmaguṇe paṭicca. Seyyathāpi, māṇava, nissaṭṭhatiṇakaṭṭhupādāno nissaṭṭhatiṇakaṭṭhupādānaṃ paṭicca (sī. pī. ka.) aggi jalati tathūpamāhaṃ, māṇava , imaṃ pītiṃ vadāmi yāyaṃ pīti aññatreva kāmehi aññatra akusalehi dhammehi.

nissaṭṭhatiṇakaṭṭhupādānaṃ paṭicca (sī. pī. ka.)

‘‘Katamā ca, māṇava, pīti aññatreva kāmehi aññatra akusalehi dhammehi? Idha, māṇava, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayampi kho, māṇava, pīti aññatreva kāmehi aññatra akusalehi dhammehi. Puna caparaṃ, māṇava, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayampi kho, māṇava, pīti aññatreva kāmehi aññatra akusalehi dhammehi.
mula_english:
468. “Now there are these five cords of sensual pleasure, student. What are the five? Forms cognizable by the eye that are wished for, desired, agreeable, and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust; sounds cognizable by the ear… smells cognizable by the nose… tastes cognizable by the tongue… tangibles cognizable by the body that are wished for, desired, agreeable, and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust. These are the five cords of sensual pleasure. The *brāhmaṇa* Pokkharasāti is tied to these five cords of sensual pleasure, infatuated with them and utterly committed to them; he enjoys them without seeing the danger in them or understanding the escape from them. That he could know or see or realise a superhuman state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones - this is impossible.”

“What do you think, student? Which of these two fires would have a better flame, colour, and radiance - a fire that might burn in dependence on fuel, such as grass and wood, or a fire that might burn independent of fuel, such as grass and wood?" “If it were possible, Master Gotama, for a fire to burn independent of fuel, such as grass and wood, that fire would have a better flame, colour, and radiance.”

“It is impossible, student, it cannot happen that a fire could burn independent of fuel such as grass or wood except through the exercise of supernormal power. Like the fire that burns dependent on fuel such as grass and wood, I say, is the rapture that is dependent on the five cords of sensual pleasure.

Like the fire that burns independent of fuel such as grass and wood, I say, is the rapture that is apart from sensual pleasures, apart from unwholesome states."

“And what is the rapture that is apart from sensual pleasures, apart from unwholesome states? Here, student, quite secluded from sensual pleasures… a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the first *jhāna* (first meditative absorption). This is a rapture apart from sensual pleasures, apart from unwholesome states. Again, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought… a *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the second *jhāna* (second meditative absorption). This is a rapture apart from sensual pleasures, apart from unwholesome states.
commentary_pali: 468.Gadhitotiādīni vuttatthāneva. Sace taṃ, bho gotama, ṭhānanti sace etaṃ kāraṇamatthi. Svāssāti dhūmachārikādīnaṃ abhāvena so assa aggi accimā ca vaṇṇimā ca pabhassaro cāti. Tathūpamāhaṃ māṇavāti tappaṭibhāgaṃ ahaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – yatheva hi tiṇakaṭṭhupādānaṃ paṭicca jalamāno aggi dhūmachārikaṅgārānaṃ atthitāya sadoso hoti , evamevaṃ pañca kāmaguṇe paṭicca uppannā pīti jātijarābyādhimaraṇasokādīnaṃ atthitāya sadosā. Yathā pana pariccattatiṇakaṭṭhupādāno dhūmādīnaṃ abhāvena parisuddho, evamevaṃ lokuttarajjhānadvayasampayuttā pīti jātiādīnaṃ abhāvena parisuddhāti attho.
commentary_english:
468. *gadhito* etc. [are to be understood] only in the places where [they were] spoken.

"*sace taṃ, bho gotama, ṭhāna*," [means] if this is the reason, [then it] exists.

"*svāssā*," due to the absence of smoke, ashes, etc., that fire is without flame, color, and luminosity.

"*tathūpamāhaṃ māṇavā*," I [make] that comparison.

This is what was said: Just as a blazing fire, on account of depending on the fuel of grass and wood, is faulty due to the existence of smoke, ashes, and embers, so too, the joy that arises from depending on the five sensual qualities is faulty due to the existence of birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, and so on.

However, just as [a fire] freed from the fuel of grass and wood is pure due to the absence of smoke and so on, so too, the joy associated with the two transcendental meditative states is pure due to the absence of birth and so on. This is the meaning.

mula_pali:
469. ‘‘Ye te, māṇava, brāhmaṇā pañca dhamme paññapenti puññassa kiriyāya kusalassa ārādhanāya, katamettha kamettha (ka. sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) brāhmaṇā dhammaṃ mahapphalataraṃ paññapenti puññassa kiriyāya kusalassa ārādhanāyā’’ti? ‘‘Yeme, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā pañca dhamme paññapenti puññassa kiriyāya kusalassa ārādhanāya, cāgamettha brāhmaṇā dhammaṃ mahapphalataraṃ paññapenti puññassa kiriyāya kusalassa ārādhanāyā’’ti.

‘‘Taṃ ki maññasi, māṇava, idha aññatarassa brāhmaṇassa mahāyañño paccupaṭṭhito assa. Atha dve brāhmaṇā āgaccheyyuṃ – ‘itthannāmassa brāhmaṇassa mahāyaññaṃ anubhavissāmā’ti. Tatrekassa tatthekassa (pī.) brāhmaṇassa evamassa – ‘aho vata! Ahameva labheyyaṃ bhattagge aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍaṃ, na añño brāhmaṇo labheyya bhattagge aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍa’nti. Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, māṇava , vijjati yaṃ añño brāhmaṇo labheyya bhattagge aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍaṃ, na so brāhmaṇo labheyya bhattagge aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍaṃ. ‘Añño brāhmaṇo labhati bhattagge aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍaṃ, nāhaṃ labhāmi bhattagge aggāsanaṃ aggodakaṃ aggapiṇḍa’nti – iti so kupito hoti anattamano. Imassa pana, māṇava, brāhmaṇā kiṃ vipākaṃ paññapentī’’ti? ‘‘Na khvettha, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā evaṃ dānaṃ denti – ‘iminā paro kupito hotu anattamano’ti. Atha khvettha brāhmaṇā anukampājātikaṃyeva anukampajātikaṃyeva (syā. kaṃ. ka.) dānaṃ dentī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ sante, kho, māṇava, brāhmaṇānaṃ idaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ puññakiriyavatthu hoti – yadidaṃ anukampājātika’’nti. ‘‘Evaṃ sante, bho gotama, brāhmaṇānaṃ idaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ puññakiriyavatthu hoti – yadidaṃ anukampājātika’’nti.

tatthekassa (pī.) anukampajātikaṃyeva (syā. kaṃ. ka.)

‘‘Ye te, māṇava, brāhmaṇā pañca dhamme paññapenti puññassa kiriyāya kusalassa ārādhanāya, ime tvaṃ pañca dhamme kattha bahulaṃ samanupassasi – gahaṭṭhesu vā pabbajitesu vā’’ti? ‘‘Yeme, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā pañca dhamme paññapenti puññassa kiriyāya kusalassa ārādhanāya, imāhaṃ pañca dhamme pabbajitesu bahulaṃ samanupassāmi appaṃ gahaṭṭhesu. Gahaṭṭho hi, bho gotama, mahaṭṭho mahākicco mahādhikaraṇo mahāsamārambho, na satataṃ samitaṃ saccavādī hoti; pabbajito kho pana, bho gotama, appaṭṭho appakicco appādhikaraṇo appasamārambho, satataṃ samitaṃ saccavādī hoti. Gahaṭṭho hi, bho gotama, mahaṭṭho mahākicco mahādhikaraṇo mahāsamārambho na satataṃ samitaṃ tapassī hoti… brahmacārī hoti… sajjhāyabahulo hoti… cāgabahulo hoti; pabbajito kho pana, bho gotama, appaṭṭho appakicco appādhikaraṇo appasamārambho satataṃ samitaṃ tapassī hoti… brahmacārī hoti… sajjhāyabahulo hoti… cāgabahulo hoti. Yeme, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā pañca dhamme paññapenti puññassa kiriyāya kusalassa ārādhanāya, imāhaṃ pañca dhamme pabbajitesu bahulaṃ samanupassāmi appaṃ gahaṭṭhesū’’ti.

‘‘Ye te, māṇava, brāhmaṇā pañca dhamme paññapenti puññassa kiriyāya kusalassa ārādhanāya cittassāhaṃ ete parikkhāre vadāmi – yadidaṃ cittaṃ averaṃ abyābajjhaṃ tassa bhāvanāya. Idha, māṇava, bhikkhu saccavādī hoti. So ‘saccavādīmhī’ti labhati atthavedaṃ, labhati dhammavedaṃ, labhati dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ. Yaṃ taṃ kusalūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ, cittassāhaṃ etaṃ parikkhāraṃ vadāmi – yadidaṃ cittaṃ averaṃ abyābajjhaṃ tassa bhāvanāya. Idha, māṇava, bhikkhu tapassī hoti…pe… brahmacārī hoti…pe… sajjhāyabahulo hoti…pe… cāgabahulo hoti. So ‘cāgabahulomhī’ti labhati atthavedaṃ, labhati dhammavedaṃ, labhati dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ. Yaṃ taṃ kusalūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ, cittassāhaṃ etaṃ parikkhāraṃ vadāmi – yadidaṃ cittaṃ averaṃ abyābajjhaṃ tassa bhāvanāya. Ye te māṇava, brāhmaṇā, pañca dhamme paññapenti puññassa kiriyāya kusalassa ārādhanāya, cittassāhaṃ ete parikkhāre vadāmi – yadidaṃ cittaṃ averaṃ abyābajjhaṃ tassa bhāvanāyā’’ti.
mula_english:
469. “Of those, student, the *brāhmaṇas* who propound five qualities for performing merit, for accomplishing the wholesome, which of these, here, <note>which here (ka.
sī.
syā.
kaṃ.
pī.
)</note> do the *brāhmaṇas* propound as the most fruitful *dharma* for performing merit, for accomplishing the wholesome?”

“Of those, Master Gotama, the *brāhmaṇas* who propound five qualities for performing merit, for accomplishing the wholesome, <pb ed="v" n="2. 0428"/> the *brāhmaṇas* here propound generosity (*cāga*) as the most fruitful *dharma* for performing merit, for accomplishing the wholesome.”

“What do you think, student? Here, for some *brāhmaṇa*, a great sacrifice (*mahāyañña*) might be prepared. Then two *brāhmaṇas* might come, thinking, ‘We will partake in the great sacrifice (*mahāyañña*) of that *brāhmaṇa* named so-and-so.’ For one there, <note>for one there (pī.)</note> this might occur to the *brāhmaṇa*: ‘Oh, that only I might obtain the best seat, the best water, the best almsfood in the refectory (*bhatta-agga*). May no other *brāhmaṇa* obtain the best seat, the best water, the best almsfood in the refectory (*bhatta-agga*)!’ This is indeed a possibility, student <pb ed="t" n="2. 0661"/>, that another *brāhmaṇa* might obtain the best seat, the best water, the best almsfood in the refectory (*bhatta-agga*), while that *brāhmaṇa* does not obtain the best seat, the best water, the best almsfood in the refectory (*bhatta-agga*). ‘Another *brāhmaṇa* obtains the best seat, the best water, the best almsfood in the refectory (*bhatta-agga*), but I do not obtain the best seat, the best water, the best almsfood in the refectory (*bhatta-agga*)’ – thus he <pb ed="p" n="2. 0205"/> becomes angry (*kupito*), displeased (*anattamano*). But what result (*vipāka*) do the *brāhmaṇas* propound for this, student?”

“Indeed, Master Gotama, the *brāhmaṇas* do not give alms (*dāna*) thus: ‘Through this, may another become angry (*kupito*), displeased (*anattamano*)!’ But rather, the *brāhmaṇas* give alms (*dāna*) solely out of compassion (*anukampājātika*) here.” <note>solely out of compassion (syā.
kaṃ.
ka.)</note>

“That being so, student, this is the sixth basis for performing merit (*puṇyakriyāvastu*) for the *brāhmaṇas*: that is, being of a compassionate nature (*anukampājātika*).”

“That being so, Master Gotama, this is the sixth basis for performing merit (*puṇyakriyāvastu*) for the *brāhmaṇas*: that is, being of a compassionate nature (*anukampājātika*).”

<note>for one there (pī.)</note> <pb ed="t" n="2. 0661"/> <pb ed="p" n="2. 0205"/> <note>solely out of compassion (syā.
kaṃ.
ka.)</note>

“Those five qualities that the *brāhmaṇas* propound for performing merit, for accomplishing the wholesome, where do you mostly see these five qualities, student – among householders (*gahaṭṭha*) or among those gone forth (*pravrajita*)?”

“Those five qualities that the *brāhmaṇas* propound for performing merit (*puṇya*), for accomplishing the wholesome (*kuśala*), I mostly see these five qualities among those gone forth (*pravrajita*) <pb ed="m" n="2. 0421"/>, and rarely among householders (*gahaṭṭha*). For the householder (*gahaṭṭha*) has a great deal of activity (*mahaṭṭha*), great functions (*mahākicca*), great engagements (*mahādhikaraṇa*), and great undertakings (*mahāsamārambha*); he is not constantly and invariably truthful (*satyavādī*) <pb ed="t" n="2. 0662"/>; but one gone forth (*pravrajita*) has a small amount of activity (*alpaṭṭha*), small functions (*alpakicca*), small engagements (*alpādhikaraṇa*), and small undertakings (*alpasamārambha*); he is constantly and invariably truthful (*satyavādī*). For the householder (*gahaṭṭha*) has a great deal of activity (*mahaṭṭha*), great functions (*mahākicca*), great engagements (*mahādhikaraṇa*), and great undertakings (*mahāsamārambha*); he is not constantly and invariably an ascetic (*tapasvī*)… celibate (*brahmacārī*)… devoted to study (*svādhyāyabahula*)… generous (*tyāgabahula*). But one gone forth (*pravrajita*) has a small amount of activity (*alpaṭṭha*), small functions (*alpakicca*), small engagements (*alpādhikaraṇa*), and small undertakings (*alpasamārambha*); he is constantly and invariably an ascetic (*tapasvī*)… celibate (*brahmacārī*)… devoted to study (*svādhyāyabahula*)… generous (*tyāgabahula*) <pb ed="v" n="2. 0429"/>. Those five qualities that the *brāhmaṇas* propound for performing merit, for accomplishing the wholesome, I mostly see these five qualities among those gone forth (*pravrajita*), and rarely among householders (*gahaṭṭha*).”
