“Those five qualities that the *brāhmaṇas* propound for performing merit, for accomplishing the wholesome, I say that these requisites of the mind (*citta*), student, are
I declare this to be an equipment of the mind, namely, a mind that is without hatred and without malice, for its cultivation.
Here, student, a *bhikkhu* is a speaker of truth ( *saccavādī*).
Thinking, ‘I am a speaker of truth,’ he gains inspiration in the meaning (*atthavedaṃ*), gains inspiration in the Dhamma (*dhammavedaṃ*), gains gladness connected with the Dhamma (*dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ*).
I declare that gladness connected with the wholesome (*kusalūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ*) to be an equipment of the mind, namely, a mind that is without hatred and without malice, for its cultivation.
Here, student, a *bhikkhu* is an ascetic…one who is celibate…one who engages in study…one who engages in generosity.
Thinking, ‘I am one who engages in generosity,’ he gains inspiration in the meaning (*atthavedaṃ*), gains inspiration in the Dhamma (*dhammavedaṃ*), gains gladness connected with the Dhamma (*dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ*).
I declare that gladness connected with the wholesome (*kusalūpasaṃhitaṃ pāmojjaṃ*) to be an equipment of the mind, namely, a mind that is without hatred and without malice, for its cultivation.
Those, student, are the five things that the Brahmins prescribe for the performance of merit, for accomplishing the wholesome, for the sake of reverence. I call these the equipment of the mind, namely, a mind that is without hatred and without malice, for its cultivation.
commentary_pali:
469. Idāni ye te brāhmaṇehi cāgasīsena pañca dhammā paññattā, tepi yasmā pañceva hutvā na niccalā tiṭṭhanti, anukampājātikena saddhiṃ cha āpajjanti. Tasmā taṃ dosaṃ dassetuṃ ye te māṇavātiādimāha. Tattha anukampājātikanti anukampāsabhāvaṃ.

Kattha bahulaṃ samanupassasīti idaṃ bhagavā yasmā – ‘‘esa ime pañca dhamme pabbajito paripūretuṃ samattho nāma natthi, gahaṭṭho paripūretī’’ti āha, tasmā – ‘‘pabbajitova ime pūreti, gahaṭṭho pūretuṃ samattho nāma natthī’’ti teneva mukhena bhaṇāpetuṃ pucchati.

Kattha bahulaṃ samanupassasī

Na satataṃ samitaṃ saccavādītiādīsu gahaṭṭho aññasmiṃ asati vaḷañjanakamusāvādampi karotiyeva, pabbajitā asinā sīse chijjantepi dve kathā na kathenti. Gahaṭṭho ca antotemāsamattampi sikkhāpadaṃ rakkhituṃ na sakkoti, pabbajito niccameva tapassī sīlavā tapanissitako hoti. Gahaṭṭho māsassa aṭṭhadivasamattampi uposathakammaṃ kātuṃ na sakkoti, pabbajitā yāvajīvaṃ brahmacārino honti. Gahaṭṭho ratanasuttamaṅgalasuttamattampi potthake likhitvā ṭhapeti, pabbajitā niccaṃ sajjhāyanti. Gahaṭṭho salākabhattampi akhaṇḍaṃ katvā dātuṃ na sakkoti, pabbajitā aññasmiṃ asati kākasunakhādīnampi piṇḍaṃ denti, bhaṇḍaggāhakadaharassapi patte pakkhipantevāti evamattho daṭṭhabbo. Cittassāhametenti ahaṃ ete pañca dhamme mettacittassa parivāre vadāmīti attho.

Na satataṃ samitaṃ saccavādī Cittassāhamete
commentary_english:
469. Now, those five *dharmas* that have been designated by the *brāhmaṇas* along with Cāgasīsa, since they are just five and do not remain stable, but rather, together with one who is of the nature of compassion (*anukampājātika*), they undergo six [conditions]. Therefore, in order to show that fault, he says, "Those young men," and so forth. There, *anukampājātika* means the nature of compassion (*anukampāsabhāvaṃ*).

Where do you often observe?" This is what the Blessed One said, because "It is not possible that a renunciate does not fulfill these five *dharmas*, but a householder does fulfill them." Therefore, he asks, "Only the renunciate fulfills these, it is not possible that a householder is able to fulfill them," in that very way causing [them] to speak.

Where do you often observe?

Not always united, a speaker of truth," and so forth. A householder, when there is something else not available, even commits deceptive false speech, while renunciates, even when their heads are being cut off with a sword, do not speak two words. And a householder is not able to protect even just a training rule (*śikṣāpada*) for the duration of two or three months, while a renunciate is always an ascetic, virtuous, and relies on austerity (*tapanissitako*). A householder is not able to perform the *uposatha* observance even for eight days of a month, while renunciates are celibates (*brahmacārino*) for as long as they live. A householder, even just the auspicious Ratana Sūtra (*ratanasuttam*)-Maṅgala Sūtra (*maṅgalasuttam*) writes [them] in a book and keeps [it], while renunciates constantly recite [them]. A householder is not able to give even alms-food (*salākabhatta*) unbroken, while renunciates, when there is something else not available, even give a morsel of food (*piṇḍaṃ*) to crows, dogs, and so forth, even when a young distributor of food (*bhaṇḍaggāhaka*) throws [it] into [their] bowls. Thus, this meaning is to be understood. These are of my mind means "I speak these five *dharmas* in the retinue of a mind of loving-kindness (*mettacittassa*)," this is the meaning.

Not always united, a speaker of truth These are of my mind

mula_pali:
470. Evaṃ vutte, subho māṇavo todeyyaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘sutaṃ metaṃ, bho gotama – ‘samaṇo gotamo brahmānaṃ sahabyatāya maggaṃ jānātī’’’ti.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, māṇava, āsanne ito naḷakāragāmo, na yito dūre naḷakāragāmo’’ti?

‘‘Evaṃ, bho, āsanne ito naḷakāragāmo , na yito dūre naḷakāragāmo’’ti.

‘‘Taṃ, kiṃ maññasi māṇava, idhassa puriso naḷakāragāme jātavaddho jātavaḍḍho (syā. kaṃ. ka.); tamenaṃ naḷakāragāmato tāvadeva avasaṭaṃ apasakkaṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.) naḷakāragāmassa maggaṃ puccheyyuṃ; siyā nu kho, māṇava, tassa purisassa naḷakāragāme jātavaddhassa naḷakāragāmassa maggaṃ puṭṭhassa dandhāyitattaṃ vā vitthāyitattaṃ vā’’ti?

jātavaḍḍho (syā. kaṃ. ka.) apasakkaṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.)

‘‘No hidaṃ, bho gotama’’.

‘‘Taṃ kissa hetu’’?

‘‘Amu hi, bho gotama, puriso naḷakāragāme jātavaddho. Tassa sabbāneva naḷakāragāmassa maggāni suviditānī’’ti. ‘‘Siyā nu kho, māṇava, tassa purisassa naḷakāragāme jātavaddhassa naḷakāragāmassa maggaṃ puṭṭhassa dandhāyitattaṃ vā vitthāyitattaṃ vāti, na tveva tathāgatassa brahmalokaṃ vā brahmalokagāminiṃ vā paṭipadaṃ puṭṭhassa dandhāyitattaṃ vā vitthāyitattaṃ vā. Brahmānañcāhaṃ, māṇava, pajānāmi brahmalokañca brahmalokagāminiñca paṭipadaṃ; yathāpaṭipanno ca brahmalokaṃ upapanno tañca pajānāmī’’ti .

‘‘Sutaṃ metaṃ, bho gotama – ‘samaṇo gotamo brahmānaṃ sahabyatāya maggaṃ desetī’ti. Sādhu me bhavaṃ gotamo brahmānaṃ sahabyatāya maggaṃ desetū’’ti.

‘‘Tena hi, māṇava, suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi, bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ bho’’ti kho subho māṇavo todeyyaputto bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
470. When this was said, the brahmin student Subha, the son of Todeyya, said this to the Blessed One: “Master Gotama, I have heard it said that the ascetic Gotama knows the path to the company of Brahmā (brahmānaṃ sahabyatāya maggaṃ jānātī).”

“What do you think, young man? Is the village of Naḷakāra near here, or is the village of Naḷakāra far from here?”

“Yes, sir, the village of Naḷakāra is near here, not far from here.”

“What do you think, young man? Suppose there was a man born and raised in the village of Naḷakāra; if people were to ask him, just after he had left Naḷakāra, about the path to the village of Naḷakāra, would that man who was born and raised in the village of Naḷakāra, when asked about the path to the village of Naḷakāra, be slow or confused?”

“No, Reverend Gotama.”

“Why is that?”

“Because, Reverend Gotama, a man born and raised in the village of Naḷakāra would know all the paths to the village of Naḷakāra well.”

“Young man, a man born and raised in the village of Naḷakāra might be slow or confused if asked about the path to the village of Naḷakāra, but the Tathāgata, when asked about the world of Brahmā (brahmalokaṃ) or the path leading to the world of Brahmā (brahmalokagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ), would never be slow or confused. I know Brahmā, young man, and I know the world of Brahmā, and I know the path leading to the world of Brahmā; and I know how one who has practiced accordingly is reborn in the world of Brahmā.”

“Master Gotama, I have heard it said that the ascetic Gotama teaches the path to the company of Brahmā (brahmānaṃ sahabyatāya maggaṃ desetī). It would be good if Master Gotama would teach me the path to the company of Brahmā.”

“Then listen, young man, pay close attention, and I will speak.”

“Yes, sir,” replied the brahmin student Subha, the son of Todeyya, to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this:
commentary_pali:
470.Jātavaddhoti jāto ca vaḍḍhito ca. Yo hi kevalaṃ tattha jātova hoti, aññattha vaḍḍhito, tassa samantā gāmamaggā na sabbaso paccakkhā honti, tasmā jātavaddhoti āha. Jātavaddhopi hi yo ciraṃ nikkhanto, tassa na sabbaso paccakkhā honti, tasmā tāvadeva avasaṭanti āha, taṃkhaṇameva nikkhantanti attho. Dandhāyitattanti ‘‘ayaṃ nu kho maggo ayaṃ na nu kho’’ti kaṅkhāvasena cirāyitattaṃ. Vitthāyitattanti yathā sukhumaṃ atthajātaṃ sahasā pucchitassa kassaci sarīraṃ thaddhabhāvaṃ gaṇhāti, evaṃ thaddhabhāvagahaṇaṃ. Natvevāti iminā sabbaññutaññāṇassa appaṭihatabhāvaṃ dasseti. Tassa hi purisassa mārāvaṭṭanādīnaṃ vasena siyā ñāṇassa paṭighāto, tena so dandhāyeyya vā vitthāyeyya vā, sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ pana appaṭihataṃ, na sakkā tassa kenaci antarāyo kātunti dīpeti.

Seyyathāpi māṇava balavā saṅkhadhamoti ettha balavāti balasampanno. Saṅkhadhamoti saṅkhadhamako. Appakasirenāti akicchena adukkhena. Dubbalo hi saṅkhadhamako saṅkhaṃ dhamantopi na sakkoti catasso disā sarena viññāpetuṃ, nāssa saṅkhasaddo sabbaso phari. Balavato pana vipphāriko hoti, tasmā balavāti āha. Mettāya cetovimuttiyāti ettha mettāyāti vutte upacāropi appanāpi vaṭṭati, cetovimuttiyāti vutte pana appanāva vaṭṭati. Yaṃ pamāṇakataṃ kammanti pamāṇakataṃ kammaṃ nāma kāmāvacaraṃ vuccati, appamāṇakataṃ kammaṃ nāma rūpārūpāvacaraṃ. Tesupi idha brahmavihārakammaññeva adhippetaṃ. Tañhi pamāṇaṃ atikkamitvā odhisakaanodhisaka disāpharaṇavasena vaḍḍhetvā katattā appamāṇakatanti vuccati. Na taṃ tatrāvasissati, na taṃ tatrāvatiṭṭhatīti taṃ kāmāvacarakammaṃ tasmiṃ rūpārūpāvacarakamme na ohīyati na tiṭṭhati. Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti? Kāmāvacarakammaṃ tassa rūpārūpāvacarakammassa antarā laggituṃ vā ṭhātuṃ vā rūpārūpāvacarakammaṃ pharitvā pariyādiyitvā attano okāsaṃ gahetvā patiṭṭhātuṃ vā na sakkoti, atha kho rūpārūpāvacarakammameva kāmāvacaraṃ mahogho viya parittaudakaṃ pharitvā pariyādiyitvā attano okāsaṃ gahetvā tiṭṭhati, tassa vipākaṃ paṭibāhitvā sayameva brahmasahabyataṃ upanetīti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Seyyathāpi māṇava balavā saṅkhadhamo balavā Saṅkhadhamo Appakasirenā Mettāya cetovimuttiyā mettāyā cetovimuttiyā Yaṃ pamāṇakataṃ kamma Na taṃ tatrāvasissati, na taṃ tatrāvatiṭṭhatī

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Subhasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
470. *Jātavaddho* means both born and raised there. For one who is only born there, but raised elsewhere, the village paths all around are not entirely clear. Therefore, he said *jātavaddho*. But even for one born and raised there, if he has left for a long time, they are not entirely clear. Therefore, he said *tāvadeva avasaṭa*, meaning he left just at that moment. *Dandhāyitatta* means slowness due to doubt, thinking, "Is this the path, or is it not?". *Vitthāyitatta* means rigidity, just as the body of someone suddenly asked about a subtle point becomes stiff. *Natvevā*—by this, he shows the unimpeded nature of the wisdom of the all-knowing one. For that person, there might be an impediment to knowledge due to things like the whirl of Māra, so he might be slow or rigid. But the wisdom of the all-knowing one is unimpeded; it is not possible for anyone to cause an obstruction for him, this is what he indicates.

As in, "Just as a strong trumpeter, young man"—here, *balavā* means possessing strength. *Saṅkhadhamo* means a trumpeter. *Appakasirenā* means without difficulty, without suffering. For a weak trumpeter, even blowing the trumpet, is not able to make the four directions known with the sound; the sound of his trumpet does not spread everywhere. But for a strong one, it is extensive. Therefore, he said *balavā*. In *mettāya cetovimuttiyā*, when *mettāyā* is said, both approach (*upacāra*) and attainment (*appanā*) are suitable, but when *cetovimuttiyā* is said, only attainment is suitable. *Yaṃ pamāṇakataṃ kamma*—*pamāṇakataṃ kamma* is said to be related to the desire realm (*kāmāvacara*), *appamāṇakataṃ kamma* is said to be related to the form and formless realms (*rūpārūpāvacara*). Even among those, here, only *brahmavihāra* karma is intended. For that, having exceeded measure, having been done by increasing it in terms of radiating the directions with limit and without limit, it is called *appamāṇakata*. *Na taṃ tatrāvasissati, na taṃ tatrāvatiṭṭhatī*—that *kāmāvacara* karma does not subside, does not remain in that *rūpārūpāvacara* karma. What is said? *Kāmāvacara* karma is not able to latch on or stand in between that *rūpārūpāvacara* karma, or to pervade and consume the *rūpārūpāvacara* karma, or to take its opportunity and establish itself. But rather, the *rūpārūpāvacara* karma itself, like a great flood, pervading and consuming the limited water of the *kāmāvacara*, taking its opportunity, stands, repelling its fruition, itself bringing about companionship with Brahmā.

The rest is clear throughout.

Just as a strong trumpeter, young man.
Strong trumpeter. Without difficulty. With loving-kindness, liberation of mind. Loving-kindness. Liberation of mind. Whatever karma is done with measure. It does not remain there, it does not stand there.

The Subha Sutta Commentary, from the Papañcasūdanī, Commentary on the Middle Length Discourses, is finished.

mula_pali: 471. ‘‘Katamo ca, māṇava, brahmānaṃ sahabyatāya maggo? Idha, māṇava, bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ; iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharati. Evaṃ bhāvitāya kho, māṇava, mettāya cetovimuttiyā yaṃ pamāṇakataṃ kammaṃ na taṃ tatrāvasissati, na taṃ tatrāvatiṭṭhati. Seyyathāpi, māṇava, balavā saṅkhadhamo appakasireneva cātuddisā viññāpeyya evameva kho māṇava evaṃ bhāvitāya mettāya (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. dī. ni. 1.556) tathāpi idha pāṭhoyeva upamāya saṃsandiyamāno paripuṇṇo viya dissati; evameva kho, māṇava…pe… evaṃ bhāvitāya kho, māṇava, mettāya evameva kho māṇava evaṃ bhāvitāya mettāya (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. dī. ni. 1.556) tathāpi idha pāṭhoyeva upamāya saṃsandiyamāno paripuṇṇo viya dissati cetovimuttiyā yaṃ pamāṇakataṃ kammaṃ na taṃ tatrāvasissati, na taṃ tatrāvatiṭṭhati. Ayampi kho, māṇava, brahmānaṃ sahabyatāya maggo. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, māṇava, bhikkhu karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā…pe… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ; iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyābajjhena pharitvā viharati. Evaṃ bhāvitāya kho, māṇava, upekkhāya cetovimuttiyā yaṃ pamāṇakataṃ kammaṃ na taṃ tatrāvasissati, na taṃ tatrāvatiṭṭhati. Seyyathāpi, māṇava, balavā saṅkhadhamo appakasireneva cātuddisā viññāpeyya; evameva kho, māṇava…pe… evaṃ bhāvitāya kho, māṇava, upekkhāya cetovimuttiyā yaṃ pamāṇakataṃ kammaṃ na taṃ tatrāvasissati, na taṃ tatrāvatiṭṭhati. Ayampi kho, māṇava, brahmānaṃ sahabyatāya maggo’’ti.
mula_english:
471. What, young man, is the path to the company of Brahmā? Here, young man, a *bhikṣu* abides pervading one quarter with a mind imbued with loving-kindness (*mettā*), likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth; so above, below, around, and everywhere, and to all as to himself, he abides pervading the all-encompassing world with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, abundant, exalted, immeasurable (*appamāṇena*), without hostility (*averena*), and without ill will (*abyābajjhena*).

When the deliverance of mind (*cetovimuttiyā*) by loving-kindness is developed in this way, young man, no limiting action (*kammaṃ*) remains there, none persists there.

Just as a vigorous trumpeter could make himself heard without difficulty in the four quarters, so too, young man... when the deliverance of mind by loving-kindness is developed in this way, young man, no limiting action remains there, none persists there.

This too, young man, is the path to the company of Brahmā.

Again, young man, a *bhikṣu* abides pervading one quarter with a mind imbued with compassion (*karuṇā*)...with a mind imbued with appreciative joy (*muditā*)...with a mind imbued with equanimity (*upekkhā*), likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth; so above, below, around, and everywhere, and to all as to himself, he abides pervading the all-encompassing world with a mind imbued with equanimity, abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, and without ill will.

When the deliverance of mind by equanimity is developed in this way, young man, no limiting action remains there, none persists there.

Just as a vigorous trumpeter could make himself heard without difficulty in the four quarters; so too, young man... when the deliverance of mind by equanimity is developed in this way, young man, no limiting action remains there, none persists there.

This too, young man, is the path to the company of Brahmā.

mula_pali:
472. Evaṃ vutte, subho māṇavo todeyyaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama! Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti – evamevaṃ bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gataṃ. Handa, ca dāni mayaṃ, bho gotama, gacchāma; bahukiccā mayaṃ bahukaraṇīyā’’ti. ‘‘Yassadāni tvaṃ, māṇava, kālaṃ maññasī’’ti. Atha kho subho māṇavo todeyyaputto bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

Tena kho pana samayena jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo sabbasetena vaḷavābhirathena vaḷabhīrathena (sī.) sāvatthiyā niyyāti divā divassa. Addasā kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo subhaṃ māṇavaṃ todeyyaputtaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna subhaṃ māṇavaṃ todeyyaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘handa, kuto nu bhavaṃ bhāradvājo āgacchati divā divassā’’ti? ‘‘Ito hi kho ahaṃ, bho , āgacchāmi samaṇassa gotamassa santikā’’ti. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, bhavaṃ bhāradvājo, samaṇassa gotamassa paññāveyyattiyaṃ paṇḍito maññeti’’? ‘‘Ko cāhaṃ, bho, ko ca samaṇassa gotamassa paññāveyyattiyaṃ jānissāmi? Sopi nūnassa tādisova yo samaṇassa gotamassa paññāveyyattiyaṃ jāneyyā’’ti. ‘‘Uḷārāya khalu, bhavaṃ bhāradvājo, samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ pasaṃsāya pasaṃsatī’’ti. ‘‘Ko cāhaṃ, bho, ko ca samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ pasaṃsissāmi? Pasatthapasatthova so bhavaṃ gotamo seṭṭho devamanussānaṃ. Ye cime, bho, brāhmaṇā pañca dhamme paññapenti puññassa kiriyāya kusalassa ārādhanāya; cittassete samaṇo gotamo parikkhāre vadeti – yadidaṃ cittaṃ averaṃ abyābajjhaṃ tassa bhāvanāyā’’ti.

vaḷabhīrathena (sī.)

Evaṃ vutte, jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo sabbasetā vaḷavābhirathā orohitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā udānaṃ udānesi – ‘‘lābhā rañño pasenadissa kosalassa, suladdhalābhā rañño pasenadissa kosalassa yassa vijite tathāgato viharati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho’’ti.

Subhasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.
mula_english:
472. When this was said, Subha, the brahmin student, Todeyya’s son, said this to the Blessed One: “Magnificent, Master Gotama! Magnificent, Master Gotama! Just as, Master Gotama, one might set upright what had been overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or point out the path to one who was lost, or hold up an oil lamp in the dark so that those with eyes might see forms, in the same way, the Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by Master Gotama. I go to the revered Gotama for refuge, and to the Dhamma, and to the *bhikkhu-saṃgha* (community of monks). May the revered Gotama remember me as a lay follower (*upāsaka*) who has gone to him for refuge for life. And now, Master Gotama, we must go; we have much to do, many responsibilities." "Now is the time, student (*māṇava*), to do as you think fit." Then Subha, the brahmin student, Todeyya’s son, having delighted and rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words, rose from his seat, and after paying homage to the Blessed One, keeping him on his right, he departed.

At that time, the brahmin Jāṇussoṇi was going out from Sāvatthi in an all-white chariot drawn by mares, during the day. The brahmin Jāṇussoṇi saw Subha, the brahmin student, Todeyya’s son, coming from afar. Seeing Subha, the brahmin student, Todeyya’s son, he said this: “Well, from where is Master Bhāradvāja coming during the day?” “I am coming from the presence of the ascetic Gotama.” “What do you think, Master Bhāradvāja, is the ascetic Gotama wise in his lucidity of wisdom?” “Who am I, sir, who am I to know the ascetic Gotama’s lucidity of wisdom? Surely, one would have to be his equal to know the ascetic Gotama’s lucidity of wisdom.” “Master Bhāradvāja praises the ascetic Gotama with high praise indeed!” “Who am I, sir, who am I to praise the ascetic Gotama? The revered Gotama is praised by those who are praised; he is the best of gods and humans. Those five things that these brahmins prescribe for the performance of merit, for accomplishing the wholesome, the ascetic Gotama calls equipment of the mind, that is, for developing a mind that is without hostility and without ill will."

When this was said, the brahmin Jāṇussoṇi got down from his all-white chariot drawn by mares, and after arranging his upper robe on one shoulder, he extended his hands in reverential salutation towards the Blessed One and uttered this exclamation: “It is a gain for King Pasenadi of Kosala, it is a great gain for King Pasenadi of Kosala that the *Tathāgata*, the worthy one, the perfectly enlightened one, lives in his realm.”

The Subha Sutta, the ninth, is finished.

mula_pali:
473. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosalesu cārikaṃ carati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ. Tena kho pana samayena dhanañjānī dhānañjānī (sī. pī.) nāma brāhmaṇī cañcalikappe maṇḍalakappe (sī.), paccalakappe (syā. kaṃ.), caṇḍalakappe (pī.) paṭivasati abhippasannā buddhe ca dhamme ca saṅghe ca. Atha kho dhanañjānī brāhmaṇī upakkhalitvā tikkhattuṃ udānaṃ udānesi – ‘‘namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa. Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa. Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassā’’ti .

Tena kho pana samayena saṅgāravo nāma māṇavo cañcalikappe paṭivasati tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ pāragū sanighaṇḍukeṭubhānaṃ sākkharappabhedānaṃ itihāsapañcamānaṃ , padako, veyyākaraṇo, lokāyatamahāpurisalakkhaṇesu anavayo. Assosi kho saṅgāravo māṇavo dhanañjāniyā brāhmaṇiyā evaṃ vācaṃ bhāsamānāya. Sutvā dhanañjāniṃ brāhmaṇiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘avabhūtāva ayaṃ avabhūtā cayaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) dhanañjānī brāhmaṇī, parabhūtāva ayaṃ parābhūtā cayaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) dhanañjānī brāhmaṇī, vijjamānānaṃ (tevijjānaṃ) ( ) sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. potthakesu natthi brāhmaṇānaṃ, atha ca pana tassa muṇḍakassa samaṇakassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsissatī’’ti bhāsatīti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī). ‘‘Na hi pana tvaṃ, tāta bhadramukha, tassa bhagavato sīlapaññāṇaṃ jānāsi. Sace tvaṃ, tāta bhadramukha, tassa bhagavato sīlapaññāṇaṃ jāneyyāsi, na tvaṃ, tāta bhadramukha, taṃ bhagavantaṃ akkositabbaṃ paribhāsitabbaṃ maññeyyāsī’’ti. ‘‘Tena hi, bhoti, yadā samaṇo gotamo cañcalikappaṃ anuppatto hoti atha me āroceyyāsī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhadramukhā’’ti kho dhanañjānī brāhmaṇī saṅgāravassa māṇavassa paccassosi.

avabhūtā cayaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) parābhūtā cayaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) ( ) sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. potthakesu natthi bhāsatīti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī)

Atha kho bhagavā kosalesu anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena cañcalikappaṃ tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā cañcalikappe viharati todeyyānaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ ambavane. Assosi kho dhanañjānī brāhmaṇī – ‘‘bhagavā kira cañcalikappaṃ anuppatto, cañcalikappe viharati todeyyānaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ ambavane’’ti. Atha kho dhanañjānī brāhmaṇī yena saṅgāravo māṇavo tenupasaṅkami ; upasaṅkamitvā saṅgāravaṃ māṇavaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘ayaṃ, tāta bhadramukha, so bhagavā cañcalikappaṃ anuppatto, cañcalikappe viharati todeyyānaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ ambavane. Yassadāni, tāta bhadramukha, kālaṃ maññasī’’ti.
mula_english:
473. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was wandering among the Kosalans with a large community of monks.

At that time, a *brāhmaṇī* named Dhanañjānī, firmly trusting in the Buddha, the *Dharma*, and the *Saṃgha*, was living in Cañcalikappa.

Then the *brāhmaṇī* Dhanañjānī, having stumbled, exclaimed three times this solemn utterance: "Homage to that Blessed One, the *Arhat*, the perfectly enlightened Buddha! Homage to that Blessed One, the *Arhat*, the perfectly enlightened Buddha! Homage to that Blessed One, the *Arhat*, the perfectly enlightened Buddha!"

At that time, a youth named Saṅgārava, who was versed in the three Vedas, with their *nighaṇḍu*, *keṭubha*, and systems of *akkhara*, and was familiar with the *itihāsa* as a fifth subject, was living in Cañcalikappa; he was skilled in *padaka*, grammar, and *lokāyata* and the characteristics of a great man.

Saṅgārava the youth heard Dhanañjānī the *brāhmaṇī* speaking thus.

Having heard Dhanañjānī the *brāhmaṇī*, he said this: "This Dhanañjānī the *brāhmaṇī* is ruined! This Dhanañjānī the *brāhmaṇī*, while there are *brāhmaṇas* who maintain the Vedas (threefold knowledge), she will praise that shaveling ascetic!"

"Indeed, dear sir, you do not know the virtue and wisdom (*śīlapaññāṇaṃ*) of that Blessed One. If you knew the virtue and wisdom of that Blessed One, you would not think of abusing and reviling him."

"Then, lady, when the ascetic Gotama arrives at Cañcalikappa, you should inform me."

"Yes, dear sir," replied Dhanañjānī the *brāhmaṇī* to Saṅgārava the youth.
0425"/> <note>avabhūtā cayaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)</note> <note>parābhūtā cayaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)</note> <note>( ) sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. potthakesu natthi</note> <note>bhāsatīti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī)</note> <pb ed="t" n="2.0668"/>

Then the Blessed One, wandering by stages in the Kosala country, arrived at Cañcalikappa. There the Blessed One lived in Cañcalikappa, in the Mango Grove of the Todeyya Brahmins.

Dhanañjānī the *brāhmaṇī* heard that the Blessed One had arrived at Cañcalikappa and was living in Cañcalikappa, in the Mango Grove of the Todeyya Brahmins.

Then Dhanañjānī the *brāhmaṇī* went to the *brāhmaṇa* student Saṅgārava; having gone, she said this to Saṅgārava the student: "This, dear sir, is that Blessed One who has arrived at Cañcalikappa, and is living in Cañcalikappa, in the Mango Grove of the Todeyya Brahmins. Now is the time, dear sir, to do as you think fit."
commentary_pali:
473.Evaṃme sutanti saṅgāravasuttaṃ. Tattha cañcalikappeti evaṃnāmake gāme. Abhippasannāti aveccappasādavasena pasannā. Sā kira sotāpannā ariyasāvikā bhāradvājagottassa brāhmaṇassa bhariyā. So brāhmaṇo pubbe kālena kālaṃ brāhmaṇe nimantetvā tesaṃ sakkāraṃ karoti. Imaṃ pana brāhmaṇiṃ gharaṃ ānetvā abhirūpāya mahākulāya brāhmaṇiyā cittaṃ kopetuṃ asakkonto brāhmaṇānaṃ sakkāraṃ kātuṃ nāsakkhi. Atha naṃ brāhmaṇā diṭṭhadiṭṭhaṭṭhāne – ‘‘nayidāni tvaṃ brāhmaṇaladdhiko, ekāhampi brāhmaṇānaṃ sakkāraṃ na karosī’’ti nippīḷenti. So gharaṃ āgantvā brāhmaṇiyā tamatthaṃ ārocetvā – ‘‘sace, bhoti ekadivasaṃ mukhaṃ rakkhituṃ sakkuṇeyyāsi, brāhmaṇānaṃ ekadivasaṃ bhikkhaṃ dadeyya’’nti āha. Tuyhaṃ deyyadhammaṃ ruccanakaṭṭhāne dehi, kiṃ mayhaṃ etthāti. So brāhmaṇe nimantetvā appodakaṃ pāyāsaṃ pacāpetvā gharañca sujjhāpetvā āsanāni paññāpetvā brāhmaṇe nisīdāpesi. Brāhmaṇī mahāsāṭakaṃ nivāsetvā kaṭacchuṃ gahetvā parivisantī dussakaṇṇake pakkhalitvā ‘‘brāhmaṇe parivisāmī’’ti saññampi akatvā āsevanavasena sahasā satthārameva anussaritvā udānaṃ udānesi.

Brāhmaṇā udānaṃ sutvā ‘‘ubhatopakkhiko esa samaṇassa gotamassa sahāyo, nāssa deyyadhammaṃ gaṇhissāmā’’ti kupitā bhojanāni chaḍḍetvā nikkhamiṃsu. Brāhmaṇo – ‘‘nanu paṭhamaṃyeva taṃ avacaṃ ‘ajjekadivasaṃ mukhaṃ rakkheyyāsī’ti, ettakaṃ te khīrañca taṇḍulādīni ca nāsitānī’’ti ativiya kopavasaṃ upagato – ‘‘evameva panāyaṃ vasalī yasmiṃ vā tasmiṃ vā tassa muṇḍakassa samaṇassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, idāni tyāhaṃ vasali tassa satthuno vādaṃ āropessāmī’’ti āha. Atha naṃ brāhmaṇī ‘‘gaccha tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, gantvā vijānissasī’’ti vatvā ‘‘na khvāhaṃ taṃ, brāhmaṇa, passāmi sadevake loke…pe… vādaṃ āropeyyā’’tiādimāha. So satthāraṃ upasaṅkamitvā –

‘‘Kiṃsu chetvā sukhaṃ seti, kiṃsu chetvā na socati;

Kissassu ekadhammassa, vadhaṃ rocesi gotamā’’ti. (saṃ. ni. 1.187) –

Pañhaṃ pucchi. Satthā āha –

‘‘Kodhaṃ chetvā sukhaṃ seti, kodhaṃ chetvā na socati;

Kodhassa visamūlassa, madhuraggassa brāhmaṇa;

Vadhaṃ ariyā pasaṃsanti, tañhi chetvā na socatī’’ti. (saṃ. ni. 1.187) –

Pañhaṃ kathesi. So pabbajitvā arahattaṃ patto. Tasseva kaniṭṭhabhātā akkosakabhāradvājo nāma ‘‘bhātā me pabbajito’’ti sutvā bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā akkositvā bhagavatā vinīto pabbajitvā arahattaṃ patto. Aparo tassa kaniṭṭho sundarikabhāradvājo nāma. Sopi bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā pañhaṃ pucchitvā vissajjanaṃ sutvā pabbajitvā arahattaṃ patto. Aparo tassa kaniṭṭho piṅgalabhāradvājo nāma. So pañhaṃ pucchitvā pañhabyākaraṇapariyosāne pabbajitvā arahattaṃ patto. Saṅgāravomāṇavoti ayaṃ tesaṃ sabbakaniṭṭho tasmiṃ divase brāhmaṇehi saddhiṃ ekabhattagge nisinno. Avabhūtāvāti avaḍḍhibhūtā avamaṅgalabhūtāyeva. Parabhūtāvāti vināsaṃ pattāyeva. Vijjamānānanti vijjamānesu. Sīlapaññāṇanti sīlañca ñāṇañca na jānāsi.

Saṅgāravo māṇavo Avabhūtāvā Parabhūtāvā Vijjamānāna Sīlapaññāṇa
commentary_english:
473. Thus have I heard: the Saṅgārava Sutta.

There, *cañcalikappe* means in a village of that name.

*Abhippasannā* means delighted by way of unwavering faith.

She, it is said, was a stream-enterer, a noble female disciple, the wife of a brahman of the Bhāradvāja clan.

That brahman formerly, at the right time, invited brahmans, and offered them honor.

But having brought this *brāhmaṇī* home, being unable to upset the mind of a beautiful, high-born *brāhmaṇī*, he was unable to offer honor to the brahmans.

Then the brahmans, in every place they saw him, pressed him, saying, "Now you are not a brahman-benefactor; you do not even offer a single day's honor to the brahmans."

He, having come home, told that matter to the *brāhmaṇī*, saying, "If, lady, you were able to guard your face for one day, I would give alms to the brahmans for one day."

Give your alms-duty in a pleasant place; what is it to me here?

He invited the brahmans, had thin rice-gruel cooked, and having cleaned the house and set out seats, he seated the brahmans.

The *brāhmaṇī*, having put on a great cloak, taking a ladle and serving, spilling it on the edge of the cloth, without even making the notion, "I will serve the brahmans," suddenly recollecting the Teacher by force of habit, uttered an exclamation.

The brahmans, having heard the exclamation, saying, "This is one sided with the ascetic Gotama, we will not accept alms-duty from him," angered, threw away the food and departed.

The brahman – "Surely I told you beforehand, 'Guard your face for just this one day!' So much of your milk, rice, and so on has been ruined!" – exceedingly overcome by the power of anger – "Just so, this outcast praises the qualities of that shaven ascetic wherever he goes. Now I, you outcast, will bring a charge against that Teacher!" he said.

Then the *brāhmaṇī* said to him, "Go you, brahman, having gone, you will know," saying, "I do not see him, brahman, in the world with the *devas*... bring a charge," and so on.

He, having approached the Teacher –

"What cutting does one sleep happily, what cutting does one not grieve;

Of which single thing, Gotama, do you approve of the killing?"

(Saṃ.

Ni.

187) –

asked a question.

The Teacher said –

"Cutting off anger one sleeps happily, cutting off anger one does not grieve;

The killing of anger with its poisoned root and honeyed tip, O brahman;

The noble ones praise, for having cut that off one does not grieve."

(Saṃ.

Ni.

187) –

He declared the question.

He went forth and attained *arhatship*.

His younger brother, named Akkosakabhāradvāja, having heard, "My brother has gone forth," having approached the Blessed One, having abused [him], being trained by the Blessed One, having gone forth, attained *arhatship*.

Another of his younger brothers was named Sundarikabhāradvāja.

He too, having approached the Blessed One, having asked a question, having heard the explanation, having gone forth, attained *arhatship*.

Another of his younger brothers was named Piṅgalabhāradvāja.

He, having asked a question, at the end of the question and answer, having gone forth, attained *arhatship*.
saṅgārava māṇavo: This one, the youngest of them all, sat on that day with the *brāhmaṇas* at a single meal.
avabhūtāvā: one who has become underdeveloped, one who has become inauspicious.
parabhūtāvā: having attained destruction.
vijjamānāna: in those existing.
sīlapaññāṇa: you do not know morality (*śīla*) and wisdom (*jñāna*).
